Huh???   the service:  like i said, we were warmly welcomed and seated right away.   the waiter was attentive, but didn't seem to know some key information about sides that come with main dishes and what beer was available where.   when the bill came, we paid half with cash, half on a card.  i asked that he use the cash first and put the balance on the card.  he didn't do that and seem to take tip out of the cash we gave him first before running any amount on the card.  it was really strange.   it was my first time there, and i may go back because it is a great atmosphere with great views and i'd like to try some of the other other items on the menu.  I probably won't get the blue crabs again unless i'm just dying for some crab. i also hope, optimistically, that some of the issues with the wait staff knowing the menu better get worked out.

I would really like to write a review for the food but I can't since I've now trekked out here TWICE and haven't even been able to eat. Strike 1: We come out around 9pm and are told the wait is about 2 hours and we wouldn't get in before the kitchen closed. We went to Red Hook Lobster pound and had a great meal. Strike 2: We call the place to find out what time they open. According to the voicemail it opens at 12. We go out there at 12:30 and are told by incredibly annoyed staff that only the bar is open and the kitchen doesnt open until 3pm. Not only is that a really bad idea (a bar full of hungry people who havent eaten all day?) but they could at least list it somewhere. When we tried to ask if maybe the raw bar was open or if we could get anything to nibble on we were actually ignored. Straight up ignored. Again we went to Red Hook Lobster Pound and again it is amazing. Strike 3: Before going the first time I thought it would be a great place to throw my boyfriend's birthday party. The website says they dont take reservations YET, but to email with any questions. The email I sent over 2 weeks ago is still unanswered. This place will definitely be closed by 2013.

The food is great. The service is excellent. The problem is, arriving before the sun is down and your group gets a table on the roof. The sun is really hot and the experience was destroyed by the sun on the roof.  There is a usually an hour wait for a table.  There is a bottom section and they serve a cold and raw menu.   The section is cooler than the top section and the bar is all cash in this bottom section. The roof  section allows credit cards.  If I return to this place I will stay on the bottom section. The prices are cheaper and the food is spicy.

Ok quality za... Never have had delivery not be less the 60 min.. $45~ for two 14" specialty pizzas (buffalo chicken & vegetable) Only thing this place has going is the Cal-Mungo, a crazy 5 lb calzone that you need to finish in 45 min. That's the American dream, food challenges.

Solid dinner tonight at Il Pittore.  I look forward to heading back their way in a few weeks.  There are kinks to work out for sure; mostly service oriented.  Th interior is charming and I will most definitely head to the bar (first floor) next time.  Living in the neighborhood, I could see this being a regular spot for a quick pasta fix.  The formality with the white table linens is charming, but a little cumbersome with anxious service staff monitoring every stain, covering them with white napkins. The staff and management are all amazingly friendly. I have to compare the food to other italian eateries of similar price point.  Really, not up to par with the heavy hitters that come to mind.   I'll be back and expect to add a star or two.

Well done. This well hyped new Starr white tablecloth Italian restaurant id not disappoint. From the dining room, the quality of the staff and the food quality it was all top shelf. I ate upstairs with a great space with large skylights. I asked my waiter, Kevin, to provide recommendations. Not overly hungry and wanted to sample some dishes. Started with the Polpo Brasato which was a grilled octopus dish with potato and some type of pesto. Perfectly cooked and a great fusion of both flavor and texture. Next I had the special pasta of the night, Ametriciana. It was a long pasta, perfectly cooked al dente, in a spicy red sauce with pork cheeks. Great flavor and satisfying. Bread included sticks, ciabatta and a flatbread. All fantastic and served with fresh salted butter. Portions are not huge. It's not South Philly Italian. More refined Northern Italian fare. Met both the sommelier and manager. Both very friendly and eager for feedback. A great first impression. Will absolutely be back soon.

Thursday night with a good friend at ll Pittore.  The Mexigroni mixed by Derek the bartender was unbelievable.  The service was good but over-attentive which seems to be the prevailing trend now.  We ordered the salted cod which was a perfectly portioned small plate and was delicious; it was topped with octopus and a delicate pickled onion that balanced the dish with its acidity. The Cacio peppe was al dente and very good as well. I am looking forward to going back!

I cannot say enough good things about Tisserie. A new pasttime these past few weekend mornings has been to relax with a house coffee (they brew Stumptown!), one of their assortment of incredible pastries (likely a blueberry muffin or scone), and marvel at the folks who bypass this place and head to the (incredibly crowded) starbucks next door. Kidding aside though, Tisserie offers an incredible selection of fresh baked pastries, properly made coffee and espresso, freshly squeezed juices, and quiches I can't stop thinking about. Do yourself a favor, skip the nearby chains, and go.

They are efficient! At 2/2:30 am, they were getting people through the queue quickly. But when they decide to close, that's it. Saw many disappointed people come by a few minutes later. The plain cheese slice was awesome, and I wasn't even drunk.

I'll be quick and brief with this survey. The pizza was some of the best I've had in this particular area. They have the best crust that just hits the spot. The sauce and toppings were great as well. Absolutely love the pizza.
I have live in this neighborhood for 45 yrs and have never tasted a better pizza! I go once a week and refuse to try anything else.

Prince st pizza has taken over my number 2 spot for the best pizzeria in NYC! We got the margarita and the Sicilian both of which were amazing fresh out of the oven extra crispy topped with peppers and cheese! I used to love SUPREMA by penn station on 8ave but prince st has definitely taken over this spot. Will come over more often.

How did I live in NYC and only discover this place AFTER moving to LA? FML! The owner is authentic, from Sicily & you can taste it on the pizza! If you order anything but the deep dish pepperoni , you are CRAY! Pizza was beyond epic! Small, crowded but don't let the line scare you... It's worth the wait!

BEST PIZZA EVER!!! I've been to many pizza spots in New York and this most recent trip I decided to check out Prince St. Pizza. It's by the slice, so I got a Margharita slice. So amazing, words cannot even describe it! I HAD to get a 2nd. You must come here to eat!!!

Went here for first time today. Things were slow as they are still working out some kinks with the opening (they ran out of squash and I had to wait), but the food was worth it! Sooo much more flavor than Chipolte or Qdoba and more vegetarian and 'toppings' options. I will definitely be back and hope to be able to upgrade my review. Would be great if they could do brown rice for the whole grain fans...

This place is awesome. If you are sick of Chipotle and want a delicious meal, this is the place. I went here yesterday and it was amazing. The smoked brisket burrito was one of the tastiest burritos Ive ever had. This place just opened a few days ago but I will definitely be back there again
Excellent pork burrito. This place replaced a great neighborhood pizza joint, but that's OK. Move over Chiptole....

Wow. Finally somewhere i can get a vegetarian burrito that actually has some flavor, depth, and is more than just some rice and beans thrown at you.   The Grilled Corn is perfectly cooked, packed with flavor, and has just the right right balance of sweet and acidic. They also offer roasted chiptole squash (a unique and thoroughly welcome menu addition) along with two kinds of rice and two kinds of beans (one of each is made vegetarian). The black beans were delicious, and the arroz verde was light, fluffy, and packed with flavor. The restaurant itself was very cool, with spray painted walls, barn board, and great music. I cant wait till they have beer! Overall, one of the sleekest, tastiest new Mexican/Texan joints in the city. If you havent tried it yet, get over to 22nd and 6th and take a taste for yourself.

finally a goddamn quick service burrito that offers chicken BREAST as an option (glaring in your direction, chipolte) not only that, but it was super flavorful and delicious! as were all the other toppings. this is now my go-to burrito fix. BUT...i'll most likely order the bowl option... i didn't rate 5 stars because while the 'bowl' was plentiful and generous with the fillings, the burrito (with exact same ingredients ordered) was pretty substantially skimped out on and when more was requested, the staff had a bit of an attitude about it. even after that, there was still more tortilla left over for nearly an entire second burrito. kind of lame. they need to ditch the dainty squeeze bottles when it comes to sauces and sour cream.

Even though the line might seem like a sure sign of a quality establishment, this place falls short of its competitors. While the cuisine is interesting enough, and the concept is all right, the service isn't quite great. And after a long line the least I would expect is warm food, but that seems to be a bit too much to ask. Overall I wouldn't bother during heavy lunch hours as you might be disappointed by the temperature of your food. I recommend this place at its low traffic time. Maybe its better then?

meh. Overhyped the place around the corner on 23 and 6th that looks like a bodega will give you better tacos for cheaper plus they're open late. This is a simple case of a restaurant that spent $$ to look amazing on the outside but in reality its just a taco dressed up in overpriced mediocrity. Guac was bland. Chicken was room temp. pico de gallo was ok but you'd find the same at any of the existing taco-restaurants in the area. The one thing I did kind of enjoy way the doughnut. The doughnut itself was a little stale (maybe made the day before?) but the smoked sugar and caramel filling was delicious!

After living outside of Philadelphia for several years and trying many different cheesesteak places, this place did not disappoint at all. It might seem like a tourist trap in the middle of old city, but the cheesesteak was amazingly juicy and flavorful. I ordered the original with beef, fried onions and cheez wiz.
Had the cheesesteak hoagie and onion rings. All I can say is that both were awesome. Place was a mix of locals and tourists.

The service is absolutely the worst, the lady took our order was extremely rude and did not take our orders and kept us waiting and did not bother to tell us what kind of cheese we want and said we can read from the board...  almost walked out of the door, but based on the reviews we stayed. The sandwich was so so and there are a plenty of places have better choices.

So happy we stopped here on our roadtrip up the coast! After waiting 30+ minutes in line, we were finally able to place our orders. The girl taking our orders was clearly having a terrible day and denied us the huge golden onion rings that we kept seeing everyone walk by with...but the fries we got instead (almost) made up for it. By far the best cheesesteak I've had to date in Philly. Beef with Onions with Cheese...what can go wrong (actually, a lot can...), especially when you top it off with spicy peppers?! Yes, it's oily, but what do you expect? Tons of goodness in the juice that drips into perfect sandwich bread. I'm a fan!

This place is ok. It's more for the tourists. If you're looking for a legitimate cheesesteak place that locals go to, it's ishkabibbles on South St. If I'm ever in Old City, I go to Campo's instead. It's family owned and their cheesesteaks are insanely delicious.

Worst food ever. They seem like they just reheat stale food. To top it off there was a roach on our table. And customer service is HORRIBLE.  They can't speak or understand English and they act like they are doing you a favor by serving you. Don't ever eat here if you care about your stomach.

Really good authentic food. If you want a great experience of the Asian culture, you will be captivated by the decor and the staff is awesome. They will stay open even after closing hours to accommodate diners. Thanks for the referral Emzee .

As someone who frequents the Asian Grill, I can truly say what a great place it is to go and a great place to eat.  As I read some of these reviews I see that I am not alone.  It is a rare find to have a nice sit down chinesefood dinner in this area.  The staff is attentive, the food is excellent and the quality is good.  In the years that I have been going, I have never had a problem with either the staff or the food.  It is nice to go into a place where most of the staff knows you from previous visits.  I am a bid fan of shrimp and the variety of shrimp dishes offered gives me a sometimes tough choice.  Grand Marnier Shrimp is a must to try!     I also read the negative remarks written on 9/14/14.  I want to say that this guy must have had a bad day or maybe an off day at the restaurant.  But I do not think that is the case.  Formerly a service worker, I know that a long day is tiring and people want to go home.  I also walked in to this restaurant late and had a meal.  I had no problems with the staff or management but I was also respectful of the fact that the staff has most likely worked long hours and want to go home to finally relax.  Most people who go into any place late, do not realize or even care about what the employees went through that day or how long they have been there.  Even though I walked in late with my friend, we were welcome.      So trust me, as a man who likes to eat and a man who likes a relaxing sit down meal, this is the place to try.  Hopefully you won't run into a miserable person who wants his butt kissed instead of enjoying the little things in life!!

Based on the reviews, we stopped in here for lunch since we were in the neighborhood for work related reasons.  I ordered the pork (any style) off the lunch menu and decided to go with the Pepper Salted Pork Chops.  The lunch also came with a choice of soup and appetizer.  Asian Grill accommodated our request, and we ordered the egg drop-wonton soup, and got dumplings for appetizer.  Both tasted great, and had a great balance of spices and herbs.  It wasn't too salty (soy sauce), and the ratio of stuffing to dumpling wrapper was perfect.  Definitely not something you experience at your local pickup/ delivery Chinese restaurant.  As for the pork chops, they were amazing.  They were fried with a light batter, and topped with minced garlic, jalapenos, and onions.  The food here is definitely closer to real Chinese food, versus your typical Americanized-Chinese food.  If you're looking to experience real Chinese/ Asian food, give this restaurant a try, but be adventurous with the menu and don't go with your typical General Tso/ Sesame chicken.  You won't be upset.

Can only say about take out order I got today. Live kinda far away but was in area  & thought I'd try cuz of yelp.Heard great food reviews about Cantonese roast chicken and saw Peking duck on menu. Got both to try. Flavor was good but chicken was overdone & dry... Glad I got the duck , otherwise our dinner would have been ruined. Also got two sushi rolls which were tasty. Disappointed but maybe because it was a take out order.

I am finally getting around to review Asian Grill. I have enjoyed this restaurant at least a dozen times and have never been disappointed.  The sushi is fresh with real wasabi. Spicy yellow tail roll is my favorite.  Satay, ribs, dumplings are always spot on. Main courses such as Mango chicken, orange chicken, shrimp in chili sauce are all time favorites.  Service and food are always consistent.
Liked: - Good service -- the host and waiter were great - Meat stuffed olives - Pork sausage Wish were different: - Porchetta tasted like turkey from the Walmart deli - Food service was pretty slow!

Wow this is one of my new favorite spots now!...Outstanding. Great ambiance! This is THE BEST Italian dining in Astoria now !!... I felt like I was actually in Italy! The servers were all very nice, the owners speak in Italians, service was fantastic and I loved how laid back they were, never once felt pressure to pay the bill and leave. The place is small, but very busy, which it's okay to wait a little bit, (coz the crowd is really cool ) as the food was fantastic!..Very cool Bar/Crowd to ..!!..nice Prosecco !! All the pastas are cooked perfectly.Quality, old-school Italian! The seating is comfortable and the tables are not on top of each other. Great location, the vibe and atmosphere were amazing!. Worth checking it out. I definitely recommend Vite Vinosteria for a taste of real Italy. I would definitely come back and recommend this place to anyone looking for good food and great atmosphere  that doesn't get sticker shock. Tiramisu' Vite & Mousse di Popcorn with Brandy-sorbetto were out of this world !! I love the Bar ambience !...and their bartenders : very friendly and gorgeous !! Read this review on : "ASTORIA POST " Two former Cipriani employees open Italian restaurant in Astoria astoriapost.com/2014/07/…

Genuine Italian cuisine is prepared by the chef and he has yet to disappoint. The food reminds me if being in Italy. I have been twice and both times a left totally satisfied and the price is right. I've had the filet of sole which was perfectly seasoned and cooked. Also the mussels were so good we had to get more bread to finish the sauce. The tiramisu is perfection as well as any of the other desserts they offer. The place is a cozy gem in the middle of Astoria with all of the other imitation Italian restaurants in the neighborhood this should be your Italian go to without question.
Not the most authentic Japanese food, but really tasty sushi. Good location and food is served very quickly.

I had Kobeyaki for dinner on Saturday night.  Long story short, it wasn't completely amazing, but it was good enough that I would have it again.  My boyfriend had the grilled chicken bowl with brown rice (he wasn't a huge fan, but I tried it and thought it was pretty good) and I had the tuna tataki salad, which I definitely enjoyed.  We ordered a could of sushi rolls to share as well.  The California roll was standard and the salmon volcano roll was just okay.  The sashimi roll, however, was quite tasty - I would definitely order it again.
This place has the touch of soul for whoever is homesick. Excellent customer service and everything from the drinks to cornbread is on point... If ur in new haven definitely check this place out

Sandra's Next Generation soul food is the truth.   My friends and I made our way here for lunch this past weekend, and it was a food adventure from beginning to end.  I'm not sure if it was our wide eyes and excited discussions over what to order, or the fact that the three of us ordered as many different things as possible because we wanted to try everything, but multiple members of the staff - including Sandra herself - came out and asked us if it was our first time here (it was) and checked on us regularly to make sure that we were having a good experience (we were).  Everyone who worked here was super sweet, and the warm and welcoming atmosphere just added to the comfort/soul food experience.   I ordered the "Go Green" chicken, which was one of the specials for the day, and my friends had a creole shrimp special and BBQ ribs, respectively.  We each decided to go with a "church plate," which comes with four sides.  You can get a plate with two sides, but the sides are really good, so I would recommend getting two additional sides for just $2 more.  There are several regular menu items, plus a wide variety of specials that aren't available everyday, and they range from fried chicken and BBQ (there's a smoker out back), to chitterlings and oxtails.  The "Go Green" chicken was excellent - tender and juicy baked chicken covered in green herbs and spices, bursting with flavor.  Sandra said that G. Garvin tried the "Go Green" chicken when he stopped in to feature the restaurant on his Cooking Channel show, and they've had a lot more customers since the show aired.  The TV appearance and new customers are well-deserved.  The collard greens and fried okra were the best I've ever had, and I loved the Caribbean rice, fried plantains, and potato salad I had along with my chicken.  I was able to try some of my friends' shrimp, ribs, and mac 'n cheese, and everything was top-notch.   Along with the wide variety of entrees and sides, Sandra's also has a great dessert selection (there's a Yelp check-in offer for a free dessert right now), and an impressive variety of refreshing drinks.  My friends and I decided to order the watermelon mint green tea, which came in a container the size of a large Chinese takeout order of soup, and which went perfectly with our amazing lunches.  We were glad we made our way over to this place, and we will definitely be back again.

I really wanted to like this place after reading the reviews and viewing the pictures of the food. My family and I arrived on a Saturday and the restaurant was empty, but there were people outside in the back of the restaurant. The server greeted and seated us promptly inside. I attempted to order oxtails but they were out of them along with a few of their side dishes. We order fried chicken, fried fish, smothered pork chops, collards greens, yams, Mac & cheese, black eye peas, grits, and fried okra. The fried fish was not seasoned, and the grits were cold. I understand that some soul food items must be prepared in advanced due to how long it takes to cook, but it seemed as if our food was taken out of the refrigerator and microwaved. I know it's hard to find a soul food restaurant in Connecticut yet alone a good one. However, I will not be returning to this restaurant, and I can't recommend this restaurant to others.

Wow! This is the word you'll be saying after anything you eat at Sandra's. My son and I came here last week for the first time. We both ordered the lunch special for $8.50 a person. This included an entree selection with two sides and a buttery piece of cornbread. My son had the fried chicken. After his first bite, he went into a perfectly seasoned fried chicken joyous food coma. Basically, he couldn't speak because it was the best fried chicken he had ever tasted. The white meat was moist and seasoned. Sandra's obviously seasons there chicken for at least two days. The skin was crispy, but not greasy. He also had corn and there mac and cheese, which  I can only describe as made from scratch cheesy love. I had the ribs with a smear of BBQ glaze that was slightly spicy, but not overwhelmingly sweet. My collard greens were perfection. This restaurant knows how to spice  food and cook "low and slow."  The greens were tender, slightly sweet with a hint of bitterness, and the yams were melt in your mouth yum! Sooooo! We came back this week. We just couldn't stay away. Besides...today is mashed potato day. What can be so special about mashed potatoes ? Well when Sandra has a food special on a specific day, you know it must be awesome. My son had the potatoes for one of his sides. Did I mention that he's a twelve year old foodie. He said the potatoes were smooth, creamy with some seasoning that brought it all together. I'm a culinary teacher, part-time caterer and personal chef on the side.... so we know good food and good service. This time, I also had the chicken. This brings me back to the beginning of this review....WOW! Did I tell you would hear this word again. I also need to mention the fantastic gigantic iced-tea or lemonade that comes in huge Chinese size soup container served over ice if you eat in. Lets talk about the service. Sandra was there during both of our visits and she came over to talk to my son and myself on both  occasions. Sandra checked on our food and service, and then just had a nice chat with us that made our lunch so enjoyable. It's so nice when the owner is visible and attentive to their customers. Her staff were also just as attentive and  warm with customers that came in for take-out orders.  It was as if I was I was eating in my own kitchen. Do not pass up the opportunity to eat and enjoy the experience at Sandra's
The Food Is Good.

Came here for lunch on a Sunday and Sandra's did not disappoint! We ordered the oxtail special with sides of collards and green beans along with a separate order of BBQ ribs- the portions came with golden sweet cornbread and were super generous. Oxtail was full of flavor and nicely stewed; ribs were deliciously sweet and tender. Sandra was so kind and welcoming and we couldn't resist her recommendation for dessert - banana pudding cake with pineapple, showered with copious amounts of nilla wafer crumbles. We could barely stand up after our meal but it was well worth it! I will be back to try their pulled pork and sweet potato pie..

The hype is real! With great reviews and high expectations visiting Sandra's for the first time, it would have been exceptionally easy for it to fall short. Sandra's met expectations and then quickly exceeded them with perfectly cooked food bursting with flavor. Everything I tasted was outstanding. Not only that, but the service was some of the best I've ever experienced - personal, caring and attentive.
Decent Happy Hour. Their wings here are pretty damn good. The mussels looked awesome, I will be getting them next. Nice little atmosphere.

North Star Bar, what can I say.... Highly unprofessional, one of the most unreliable establishments I can think of in the Philadelphia area. The MGMT cancelled gigs for FOUR BANDS tonight. These musicians could have scheduled other gigs, lessons, rehearsals etc.. had the MGMT not cut them out at the last minute. Time is something you can never get back and bonin' hardworking, incredibly talented artists out of a gig/time in this manner will not go unnoticed!!!! DON'T BOOK YOUR GIGS HERE... -"The B-Man"

I am the band leader of one of the bands that was supposed to play last night at North Star Bar. My band plays frequently in Philadelphia and has NEVER dealt with a venue that acted as unprofessionally as this establishment did tonight. The show had been planned for a couple of months, and I know many people were planning on attending. However, according to a rude bartender, since not all of the bands were present EXACTLY at the load in time, they decided to cancel the show. VIA A FACEBOOK NOTIFICATION. Not even a call was made to the headlining band who was there loading in right at 6 pm and briefly left to pick up more equipment. In other words, the people in charge of sound/the show had something better to do with their night and apparently left around 6:30 (2.5 hours before the show even started). North Star Bar made an awful and stupid decision, losing a lot of money and respect from musicians and show-goers alike. I do not recommend this venue to anyone, especially musicians looking for a respectful and dependable venue to share their music with.

BEST DARN GRILLED CHEESE EVER! The Melter Skelter... Thick white bread, slathered with butter and drizzled with garlic oil, loaded with Valley Shepherd "Melter Skelter," a Raclette style cheese, pickled green tomatoes, jalapeño, BBQ potato chips (Yes, inside the sandwich!) and watercress. Whomever thought up this bad boy is a GENIUS! The bbq chips turn into something like bbq mashed potatoes because of the super high temperature they put this piece of art through on a glass bottom Electrolux sandwich press. It's served with your choice of sea salt or dill pickle flavored chips. A fact that makes this place even cooler, is they use as many of the ingredients as they can from within Reading Terminal Market. The guys and gals behind the counter are also uber cool. One guy, Zeke, was exceptionally friendly and held up a good conversation about Philly as I awaited my Melter Skelter. Do NOT miss this place!

Best grilled cheese I've ever had in my life! They have many different kinds of meats you can put inside (i went with bacon duh) and also several different rubs to cook it in. Their tomato soup, you can tell was homemade as well strongly recommend if your in the mood for a grilled cheese

As I was considering my usual options on a RTM run, I walked passed this unusual new kid on the block. The extensive olive bar heaven first caught my eye...then the woman behind the glass windows making fresh cheese. I know, you're thinking...great, another cheese joint in RTM. Well, this isn't your Grandma's cheese place (if it is, I'm very sorry for offending your Grandmother). The mozzarella is made fresh on the premises, the breads are fresh, crusty and delicious, and they source most of their ingredients straight from other places in the market. I decided on their Classic Mozz (FRESH AS SH*T mozzarella, roasted tomatoes, and I opted in for sopressata served on a delicious baguette). It came with some delightful, perfectly cooked, dill-kissed-magic potato chips. The sandwich was amazing. Great flavors, fresh ingredients, and left us completely satiated. Some people sitting next to us even asked where we got our sandwiches and we recommended them right away. I've read others had long waits, but I did not run into that problem. The sandwich was ready in minutes (room temp. so no toasting), and the service was excellent; the people who helped us were super friendly. I'm eager to make my way back to try some of their other mouth watering offerings. I got my eye on the Brielle (Brie, cranberry chutney, caramelized onions and pine nuts)! Not everything at RTM is excellent, but MeltKraft is a welcomed newcomer and I think business will be booming good long while. They will certainly be seeing my business again very soon.

First off the lady that runs this joint is so friendly and welcoming! She does a very good job running the place and makes you feel at ease. The free chips and salsa as you wait for your meal is a good plus and they are cooked very well. A friend and I ordered out and he got the mariachi trio tacos and loved them. Said they were well done and they filled him up just fine he couldn't even eat all his rice and beans after. I got the mariachi platter and man was it big. Several different mexican dished combined on one platter for a huge and filling delicious feast. No complaints here, the food was excellent the service was warm and the pricing was good. Stop by if you're in the area!

I started working nearby about a year ago and realized quickly that there weren't too many options for lunch until I found out that the restaurant my friend always raved about had a location right up the street!  I probably average about once a week here for lunch and sometimes even grab dinner on my way home at night.  Mexican is my favorite food and this restaurant doesn't disappoint!  I usually get the surf n' turf (steak and shrimp) burrito either in a container (if I'm trying to be good) or in the tortilla and it's always delicious.  I brought one home for my husband and as he was eating it he told me it was the best burrito he ever had and if I brought him one every day, it would change his life!  Considering he hates other chain burrito places, this is quite the compliment!  The mild salsa (I don't do spicy) is also amazing and if they were to bottle it, I'd buy it!  The woman in charge is always very pleasant when she takes my order over the phone and also when I go to pick up.  I love this place and I'll continue going back!  This is the kind of authentic, delicious, local place that needs to be frequented and cherished amongst all the crappy food (in both quality and taste) that's out there.

Heard alot about this restaurant, went with friends the service was so-so, the food literal;ly sucked,  appetizers were over-rated; all the dinners came out cold and over cooked, the lobster was cold and tasteless, fish was cold all-in-all dinner was over-priced and not worth the trip to this place anyone who thinks it is great knows nothing about food.   NEVER WILL GO BACK OR RECOMMEND TO ANYONE THAT I LIKE.

I was stupid not to make reservations for New Years Eve but Fernandes pulled through for me. I was in the mood for Rodizio and most places around Ferry Street were doing a NYE package for the night. Since I was only interested in dinner and making other plans later, this worked out. Food was delicious!  Every meat brought out was full of flavor and cooked perfect. Lots of side items and the servers were on top of everything. Salad bar and desserts were only average so stick to the meats if you visit for Rodizio.

This is a lovely restaurant, if you only judge by what's on your table.  Ultimately the food is what really matters, but decor and atmosphere should contribute to the overall dining experience at this price point.  The colors here are only found on the plates, the rest of the restaurant must be what it feels like after your psychiatrist doubles the dosage of your Bipolar disorder medication. If you bring a date here, her first instinct might be to kick off her heels and flee the scene in fear of being mugged, as you are more likely to happen upon a trashcan bonfire than a first-rate restaurant at this location.  However, if she's draped head-to-toe in items from a Talbots catalog, then she might love the decor here if you manage to usher her down the desolate street into the restaurant.   Having said that, the staff provides outstanding service here.  They always manage to be timely while being careful not to intrude, which could be easy to do as the dining room is usually only half full.   But, most importantly, the food here is terrific, especially under the current format where you can order protein for as many courses as you want.  I've stretched it to five in a couple of 6-course tastings, thus far nobody has come out of the kitchen to yell at me, so I don't think it's frowned upon to do so.

This restaurant was a pleasant surprise. We ordered the 4 course meal. We weren't sure about what we ordered but each course was amazing. Even better we got about 8 samples of tastes before we even started the meal. The chef is creative and the tastes are fun. Everything was beautifully presented as well. The service is also worth a mention. Attentive with a sense of humor. Expensive but well worth it.

Just  back from opening day at Lcal 44 - it was FANTASTC!  What a fabulous beer list, you cannot find a better one in the city - or a more fairly priced one.  The kitchen brought out some complementary morsels:  juicy batter-coated chicken wings, rich tasting potato cakes, hearty Cuban-style sandwiches (I don't think the kitchen is presently using a plancha, the sandwich press that gives the the cubano its caramelized grilled edge, but it was tasty none the less).  In any case, while it is too early to judge the kitchen, its early menu complements the great beer list perfectly.  The West Philly neighborhood now boasts a terrific bar and in Leigh and Brendan it could not have found more gracious and knowledgeable hosts.  Happy New Year indeed.

My first time eating here was with my husband and two kids.  They were friendly, accommodating of our gluten free buns (they are getting their own soon), and had a very clean place.  The burgers were seasoned well and delicious.  The fries?  Also seasoned well and wonderful!  Loved it!!  We have gluten and corn allergies and had no problems eating here!

Went here last night and had a very good dinner.  It was half price wine night so we got a 32 dollar bottle of Riesling for only 16.  The wine was amazing.  For an appetizer we got calamari which was ok.  My dinner was a Greek salad.  I added blackened salmon and for $4 extra for a full fillet of salmon you would have to be stupid not to.  Salad was excellent.  My fiancée got the flounder stuffed which crab.  She said the fish was very good, but the sauce was to die for.  Dessert menu looked great, but I didn't have room.  Service was exceptional.

We went here the other night for a nice dinner.  We had previously only been to the underground bar which is ehh... Since upstairs is amazing, it makes up for the sub par pub downstairs. If you're going for good food in a nice setting, the restaurant is highly recommended.  I'm very excited for the patio to open up!  And I'm totally looking forward to Octoberfest this year!! If you're looking for a good bar near Hillsborough, keep looking... the look and feel of the bar in the basement is nothing to write home about..

We went in there on a Friday night and it was dead, that should of been our first clue. The restaurant is pretty inside and almost has this "fine dining" ambiance about it. They had two tvs inside that was on CNN instead of sports or something not as depressing. The bartender came over to take our drink order and I ordered a lemon drop martini. It was really bitter and tasted dirty, I couldn't drink it. The bartender and waitress were both nice though. We placed an order for appetizer mac and cheese and egg roll. We ordered a filet for the entree. While we were waiting for our food they brought out scallops to another table that smelled like rancid rotten fish and instantly made me nauseous. It was the most putrid thing I've ever smelled. Shortly after they brought out our apps. I took one bite of the mac and cheese and almost had to spit it out. The cheese tasted and smelled like sweaty gym socks. I was so disgusted that I cancelled the rest of our order and asked for the check. The waitress asked if we wanted a box for the food and I told her no. They still didn't get that it was because the food was awful. She was really nice so I didn't want to be rude and just paid for what I didn't eat and couldn't get out of there fast enough. I have never had an experience like that before in my life. I got really sick after I left the restaurant from eating 2 bites. I wouldn't wish this restaurant on my worst enemy. Not sure how they passed their health inspection or how it's even possible to charge what they do for that so called food.

We are regulars at Slate, and have been for the 6 years or so they've been open.  This is one of our go to places, and we've never had a bad meal here.  Last night, I had the mixed greens salad, and the mussels, which is the only place in the city that I feel has great mussels.  My husband had the hangar steak, which was done to perfection, and very tender (he gave me a bite).  The drinks are generous, as are the food portions,  Good job Slate!
Best burger in the city. Beats Good Stuff and Village Whisky for me. Can't wait until they can serve beer too.

While waiting for the "Book of Mormon" lottery the past few days we have been watching them put the finishing touches on this new burger joint. R told me it was open and I was craving a burger so off we went. We ordered fries and rings. The onion rings were delicious, but the fries were mushy and not crisp or crunchy. The sauces and the ketchup weren't our cup of tea. The smoke sauce is best, but smuggle in your own Heinz. I also think it's sort of weird that they don't have a soda fountain or gun. It's all bottled soda. With fries/burgers I always want something carbonated and generally a troth of it. I am American after all! So, the burgers come. The buns are bigger than the burger. The buns have these weird seeds on them. Flax? Uncertain. My beef burger doesn't even taste like ground beef. The texture is bizarre. I ate half. I just didn't feel like complaining or I would have. The pickles however are delicious! I had a side of sweet pickles and dill pickles on my burger. The stout onions were good as well. R had the bean burger and said it had no taste or seasonings. The guac on it she said tasted heavily of raw onion. She was not impressed. She also ordered a vanilla milkshake, but said it was lackluster. Our bill was 44! Ridiculous we didn't even have cocktails or a dessert. Definitely not returning and hope you will get your burger on elsewhere!

Love this new place!  Fantastic new spot with many gluten-free and vegan options as well as exotic, sustainable meats for carnivorous foodies. Many salads and sides in addition to burgers.  Best of all- organic everything.  Service was fantastic and ambiance is fun.

For a to-go burger (I'll explain later), the SoCal was amazing.  The turkey was juicy and flavorful, and the guac, sprouts, and lettuce were all high quality and super fresh.  One of the best burgers I've had here.  Some of the other options on the menu looked really intriguing......anyone like Ostrich?  I think I'll have to try that next time. The reason I don't give this place five stars is their business model.  My burger was pretty pricey (around 12 dollars), which I wouldn't mind paying for a great product, but, I don't want to pay a tip on top of that.  I just don't understand why they made their restaurants full service.  I didn't expect to walk into a restaurant specializing in burgers and have to be seated, served, and thus pay a tip, which is why I ordered mine to-go.  By the time you get fries, a burger, and pay a tip, you could easily be looking at 20 bucks.  On Manhattan, maybe, but in Philly, I'm not so sure......

Our server, Carlos, was delightful.  We were greeted and seated promptly for lunch.  Complimentary water in a glass jug for the table is a nice touch.  They have a great selection of exotic meats like elk, wild boar, goat, and bison.  I went with the Southern Caviar burger because I'm a sucker for pimiento cheese and it was great.  I thought the prices were fairly reasonable for the quality of the items.  The seats were comfy and I very much enjoyed the entire experience.  I'm excited to go back and try some of the other burgers!

I have to agree with many of the reviews here.  I liked the flavors of the burgers (my wife had the socal and I had the goat), the onion rings (and the awesome dipping sauces!), and the sweet potato fries.  Both patties were extremely overcooked and dry, though.  And the sweet potato fries were practically cold.  But again, the ingredients themselves tasted really good.  I appreciated the quality. Most importantly, though, these guys just really need to work out the kinks in their operations.  We had to wait 15 minutes to sit down, another 15 minutes before a server took our order, and a whopping 45 minutes before we got our food.  It was pretty ridiculous, especially for a burger joint. Our server also didn't really seem like he knew what he was doing - he was working hard, but he was just doing a lot of walking back and forth with a bewildered look on his face (wasn't bringing food or taking orders). So.  Good food.  A pretty bad experience.  3 stars, it is. This place shows promise, if they can get their act straightened out.  I'll give them another try a few months later, just to see if they worked out all their service issues.

Fantastic location!  Staff were awesome, quick and very welcoming.  We are always looking for organic, humanely raised food that is also cooked properly.  This place hit it out of the park!  Great appetizers followed by some great burgers and finished with a snicker doodle ice cream sandwich.  If we didn't live so far away this would be a regular spot for us.

Was walking by and noticed them open for business but i was by myself and wasn't really in the mood to eat alone so i made plans with my girlfriend to come here during the weekend. We arrive around 8pm on a saturday and it was packed but we were greeted right away and luckily we got a table the moment we walked in. Our server Ron was awesome!! he gave us a breakdown right away and described everything properly! I got the Grindhouse with the elk and it was so good! my girlfriend got The Hudson Salad and she loved it. We shared a fries and onion ring combo and i loved the sauces that came with it ! i highly recommend the Special sauce!!!! We were too full to get desert but i will def get the Flourless chocolate cake. It was so good i came in 3 days later during the week adn got the lunch special with the standard, french fries and Draft soda. it was only 11.85$ before taxes! what a great deal with such good burgers! I highly recommend this place to anyone who wants a good burger!
More vegan options than I expected. The collard green wrapped farmstead was hardier than expected.
Great organic turkey burgers...use to frequent the one in Brooklyn...so glad they are in Philly now

I've eaten here six times.  They finally got their cooking times correct.  Now medium IS medium.  Get your damn liquor license problem resolved or make it byob in the meantime!  The place is too brightly lit!  And the servers are a bit too casual.  But I love the place!  Best Elk burger!  Great Boar!  Goat!  Bison!  It's all good.  Best fries, sweet and French, around!  Get some liquor!

My friend from the hood took me here. New joint on the block next to the Tuck Shop and Ten Degrees (love 'em both). Great stuff and great prices! Fresh, delicious meats. I had the pork and spicy chorizo tacos, my friend had some veggie stuff (darn vegetarians and their vegetables n stuff) and she loved it. Beer is super cheap (4 bucks like the old days in the East Village), rockin' music, nice fella behind the counter. Hey, its a great lil' taco joint! What more can you ask for?

Last week my friend and I were tackling her bucket list of must try eateries in Manhattan.  That coupled with my New Years resolution to expand my list of go to restaurants in my neighborhood brought us upon this amazing little nook.  The restaurant we intended to go to was packed, which led us to Five Tacos. My girlfriend and I sat at the bar of this spotless little joint and decided to have a drink and try the tacos. The food was incredible and the different sauces complemented the tacos perfectly.  I am very big on service, and the staff was very attentive and accommodating. Definitely a must go!

I have eaten here many times now and have not been disappointed. I have tried something new each time and everything has been exceptional. With the inexpensive beers, and the friendly staff, this place will keep me coming back for more.

We loved the wings when we visited the original Pok Pok in Portland. They're still amazing at this location, but the wait system is ridiculous. So bad that it warranted this review. They send people across the street to have a drink instead of waiting near the restaurant. Because of this, we sat and stared at three open tables for about 15 minutes of our 30 minute wait instead of being sat because the people were across the street taking their time and finishing their drinks. The reasons the wait times are long here is completely Pok Pok's own doing so that they can make more money at their Whiskey Soda Lounge location. The fact that they wouldn't seat our tiny party of 2 in one of the THREE open tables, even at the bar, while we waited for couples to drink and eat appetizers across the street is TERRIBLE customer service.
Fish sauce wings!!   This place came from Portland, OR before ending up in NYC.

A great place to dine with a small group. I arrived with a party of four on a Sunday evening, around 6pm. There was no wait to dine outside, though, it was about 65* outside, it was a little chilly for outdoor dining. The food is phenomenal. We opted for several noodle dishes but the standouts were the chicken wings and the prawns. When they say SPICY, you bet your ass its spicy. I highly recommend getting sticky rice with your meal to cool your mouth. The service is friendly but slow. The restrooms were clean. I would come back and order a bowl of the prawns just for myself.
A very lovely dinner! Everything was amazing even the affogato! I am def coming back and maybe grabbing a Pok Pok gift card!

Overpriced, small portions.  If they're charging these prices the rice should be free, they charge $3 per scoop.  Four people need to order 5-6 dishes for lunch plus several orders of rice.  The sticky rice was dry and on the hard side.  The wings were tasty; they were very garlicky sweet.  The flank steak salad was good, but each order lasts about 4-5 bites.

Maybe it was off night, because not many reviewers seem to mention this, but the noise level in this wine bar / restaurant was throught the ROOF one Thursday a few weeks ago. Granted, darling M and I are both relatively soft-spoken chicklets. But I found myself doing that thing you do in a nightclub or concert setting: Getting right up in someone's face and kind of shouting, then deciding if it made more sense for her to shout back directly in my ear, or in front of my face, so I could so a little lip-reading, too. The flatbread pizzas are nice. That's about all I'll say for those. We also ordered some appetizer that involved fresh pear and Brie, and that was delicious (and it inspired my next homemade pizza). When I arrived, I happened to sit down next to a woman who sold wine to the bar; she'd done her pitch and was now eating dinner. She had a whole big bottle of a beautiful Argentine rose in front of her that they'd been tasting and she was still drinking. She generously shared with us. Aside from seeing my dear friend who I hadn't been out with in months, that might have been the highlight. TYC 13

Great little wine bar for the neighborhood.  We stopped in for a few drinks before dinner and were pleasantly surprised.  The wine list was pretty decent and they had some good beers on tap.  The guys at the bar were super friendly, and the one guy definitely knew his wines.   Will stop in again soon.

Despite the number of wine bars I have visited in the Upper West Side or nearby Hells Kitchen, this one is by far my favorite. I have brought friends here many times and have never left disappointed with the food, wine or prices. My only gripe  is the unreliable service. There appear to be enough servers but on my last two visits we had to consistently wait half an hour to 45 minutes before anyone checked on us for a refill - very frustrating. Regardless, I'm going to attribute this to two off nights and will def. visit the bar again for the wine and food.

This is a staple of UPenn. The Cheesesteaks in general are always a good bet when in Philly, but the key to taste lies with the bread. Fresh Italian style rolls are the best and Abner's does a good job. They have been around since 1930, so I guess they are doing something right. The cook is sassy and will make your cheese steak just the way you want it. You want onions? You want cheese? What kind: American, Provolone, Whiz? You want Mayo? Ketchup? As you can see by the questioning if you don't know how you want it they will walk you through the process and you will end up with a cheese steak the way you want it, not the way they think you will like it. I'm pretty boring; steak, onions, and whip on a great tasting Italian roll. The prices are good and the place has plenty of seating. Not fancy, but more like that worn college hangout feel.
HUGE SERVING SIZES My Stromboli could have fed 3 people. The cheesesteaks are pretty big too. The food is good but not great. Pretty average.

1. Cheesesteaks 2. Cheesy 3. Southern diner style I've never been to southern diner, but this is what I'd imagine it look like. Lol. Yeah, I tried their cheesesteak with my parents who were visiting from out of town. I liked that the meat wasn't too dry and it was decently flavorful. Cheesesteaks aren't my favorite, but if I were ever craving one, I'd probably come here again.

Nicolas used to be my favorite restaurant in the area. Unfortunately, since they moved from Hawthorne the food has gone down hill. We ordered chicken Marcela tonight and the sauce was like water. No flavor at all and the mushrooms appeared to be canned. My daughter would not even eat the water soaked chicken. Perhaps today was a really off day, but we will not be returning for overpriced boiled chicken.
Over priced 3 of us had veal & the other 2 had chicken & sausage.  When dinner was done we all said it sucked.  There has to be better places to eat in Totowa,NJ.

Wow! Easy to find- cheap parking- amazing food!!!!! Wonderful service- fancy but not too fancy- burgers are incredible! The bison meat (it was my first time trying it) was very tasty.  Julie was very attentive- manager came by and made sure everything was good- highly recommended-

Great atmosphere. Bison is lower fat so I was worried that the filet would be dry, asked the waitress about it and she assured me it was NOT dry, yup it's dry. Try the Kansas City cut instead. I would come back again.

I was just walking home when I noticed a new storefront awning. It was called Absolute Thai Restaurant and I love Thai food so I walked in. I told them Ive been living in this neighborhood now for 14 yrs and never noticed this place. They said they just opened 3 days ago. It's a take out only restaurant so without looking at the menu i just asked for my favorite dish which is Pad Khee Mao with mixed seafood. When I opened up the bag I was blown away by the dish it's was chock full of seafood and for the first time i had mussels included as well. Once i tasted it i was impressed as well. It was, as i say, Thai spicy which was fine for me. it was so great that I had to call the take out place and pay my compliments to the chef. I wish this new Thai place all the best and hope they are successful in Spanish Harlem. Welcome to the neighborhood.

Food was tasty; service was good;  however too pricey for the area and location;   in addition, menu was limited and they did not serve any fresh bread or rolls which I consider a negative when ordering a salad or soup;  though I rated the restaurant 3-star, I doubt the restaurant will last as it caters to a select crowd and not to a general public;

Horrible!!! We wanted to enjoy some cocktails at Pure, which claims to be open until 2 a.m., but they were closing a little after 11, and the manager was very rude to us. IMPURE!!!! IMPURE!!!! IMPURE!!!!!

Oof... my recent experience wasn't good. Once again, I looked to American Retro to satisfy my love of tater tots.  My friends ordered the Jalapeño Poppers, Chicken Sandwich, and beef chili.  This time, I felt they gave us less tater tots and they were over-fried. Worst of all, my friend felt horrible the next day.  She had stomach pain all day from the food.  I still recommend American Retro for the tater tots (like I do in my original review), but this confirms my strategy of not eating anything else from them.  At least don't get the poppers or chicken sandwich, judging by how miserable she was.
What a nice find! Cozy ambiance, Great food, nice friendly service, great value for all the above. We are definitively be back every time we are in NY.

I had the restaurant dinner menu, the butternut squash soup, the braised short ribs, and the chesapeake spring roll. The soup was a little to sweet, but the ribs and cheesecake was amazing. The waiter was helpful and provided great service.

3.5 Stars I came here for restaurant week. Overall, the food is good, with dessert the worst part. Food: Solid bread basket Baby beets and goat cheese salad - pretty good but the goat cheese was fried Braised beef short rib - pretty good and meat crumbles easily Cheesecake spring roll - decent Panna cotta - not great
Great bakery! Love their breads, always nice and fresh. Stopped buying bread anywhere else as fresh and daily baked breads are available there.
My daughter had worked in the bakery for years when she was a teenager. Only ate in the restaurant once or twice but the food was very good.

While Baoburg is a newcomer to the neighborhood, Chef Bao Bao is no stranger to N. 6th St. with experience at both Ramen Yebisu and Chai Thai next door. However, Baoburg brings her cooking skills to the next level in a very intimate venue. I decided to try out the new spot with a friend and we shared several different dishes (all affordably priced as well!). Definitely try the Seared Duck Breast Noodle with perfectly cooked duck and an amazing, rich broth. I would also recommend the Chicken Pate dish, which was not on the menu but definitely showcased an Asian fusion style with the spring roll-like serving. The side of Roasted Brussels Sprouts was also amazing, with a blend of potatoes and apple slices as well. Finally, the oysters and Roasted Octopus Legs rounded out the meal nicely. Just be aware that this location is cash only for now!

Been here a few times for brunch and dinner, this place is a hidden gem!   Amazing delicate tastes in every dish we tried.  Spaghetti anchovy was my fav dinner, the eggs Benedict is great brunch dish.  The cuisine is French with a thai/asian flair. Highly recommended.
Must try Duck noodles, Short ribs ramen, Wings, Gambas al Ajillo, Coconuts mussel, Baked cod, Bacon wrapped prunes,Pork belly and Brussels sprouts:) don't miss it!!!

The place appears small in size but surely is big in its passion for serving great food. Everything I tried here was yummy, presented with attention to detail and artistic touch. Outstanding quality for a reasonable price. The gentle background music adds to a memorable experience. A friendly chat with the staff and a charming Chef Bao Bao is a bonus.

When I took a trip up to Jersey recently , I was searching for somewhere casual for lunch. I was pointed in the direction of Hapgoods. The deli's atmosphere was Clean and appealing. The meal delivered was just as enjoyable as the friendly service. I felt very comfortable and at home at Hapgoods , and I am looking forward to eating there again on my next trip up.

GOOD food!!!!! horrible service... they do not know how to hire the right people.. everytime Ive gone the service has been horrible.. HIRE PEOPLE WITH EXPERIENCE!! other then the service the food is yummy!!

Awesome everything! The food is fresh and delicious. I had the blueberry pancakes with the pouched pears....OMG. The pancake batter is the chef's secret recipe! The next day.... Yes I went back...I had the fresh vegetable soup! Amazing!  The staff is so friendly and the owners are awesome! They all are huge supporters of the military and veterans which is A++ in my book! Would totally recommend this family friendly atmosphere.
i've only tried a few things, but their summer rolls are MUCH better than any other vietnamese restaurant in jersey city, by far. prices are great. they're fast, too.

Had lunch today with a friend. OCabanon is a really cool, down-town'esk french bistro, in area without a lot (maybe any?) good restaurants.  Don't be put off by the block (W29th, bet. 7th-8th) which is garment district, commercial looking.  Cabano is worth the trip. My guess is that they are ahead of the curve on the neighborhood, which is beeing taken over by young companies and condos.   We shared Charcuterie plate, frisee salad and the steak sandwich special.  All food was excellent.  Service very attentive, making a real effort. Ended up speaking with the owner/chef Michael who is really great. (from Le Bernardin).  Gave us a tour of the space which he renovated himself: kind of industrial chic, lots of welded metal, distressed wood, cool overhead light in the back.   I am definitely coming back and recommending to friends.   Want to try the rest of the menu and what looks like a cool, eclectic wine list

Yummy French food and an even more awesome atmosphere.  This place recently opened but I think once word starts buzzing this place will be packed.  They have lots of seating - so great place for a group of friends.  Great wine selection and a very friendly and attentive staff.  Food was yummy - started with the chicken wings and oysters.  I had a salmon special and my husband had the French stew with mashed potatoes. Dessert we had an ice creamy thing of nougat which was delicious.  We don't eat a ton of French food but we might have to start since we will be coming back here.  Also great since it's closer to path.
Very casual and variety of wines, but too many servers made feel a bit uncomfortable. Sigh.

I simply love this place. We went there already several times (and this in NYC!) and were never disappointed. Great food, great wines and always a valuable recommendation from the servant. My personal favorite is the bagel with foie gras with a glas of champagne, but I also tried other dishes as the tuna tartare, the cheese selection or the little sweets with an espresso - all very delicious and highly recommended to be tried. Thanks to Mike and his team, you really created a place with great food and a great atmosphere. Thanks for the hospitality tonight.  We had all we need for a great evening amongst friends.
Mediocre food and terrible service - 40 minutes for a simple lunch order, one item didn't come, and another was wrong. Do not eat here.
Pretty decent pizza with a nice, crunchy crust. I loved it. Went for an after-class get-together in the outdoor seating area and it's definitely got a nice atmosphere.

We ate there last night and had a very good experience. The food was good to very good, prices reasonable (entrees around $15) and the staff very helpful. We shared the mussels mariniere  as an appetizer ($12) and they were excellent. We had the rainbow trout served with vegetables baked in a bag and the scallop/shrimp dish...both very good. Will definitely return (and try the brunch for $10). And , yes, they took Amex.

When I saw the menu on Thrillist, I knew that this was the kind of food my partner loved -- simple old-fashioned non-trendy French bourgeois fare.   Three of us went for Brunch on Sunday and loved it; we all had terrific oysters to start, followed by either Steak Tartare (for 2 of us) and Mussles Mariniere (for the 3rd).  All were excellent; great flavor and a really good value for the price.  Our waiter couldn't have been nicer, and recommended an excellent reasonably priced French wine. We will definitely be going back!

Service here is great, even if the seating is a little cramped they make the meal very pleasant. The starter portions are very generous. My steak tartare was perfectly seasoned, and could have been a meal itself. There was also a ton of mussels, which were quite good (go with mariniere, classics seem to be the best here) The bread is a little dry/stale, better for dipping into the mussels sauce than it is on its own. The duck comes two ways, crispy confit which is a little dry/salty and a really good breast in pan sauce, with a mound of fantastic comfort food(mushroom, potato and garlic). The beef bourguignon (saturday special) is very good, and its sauces drip all over the mushroom risotto base. Nothing disappointing with a few real standouts, it's nice to have a really good standby restaurant for the area.

YAAAAAAAAAAAASSSSSS!!!! I took my boyfriend here because I read the reviews and I'm new to the Buswick/Williamsburg area. We went on a night that was pretty packed so waited for a couple minutes. NBD, they asked us if we wanted to put in a drink order so I ordered a Dark and Stormy while the boyfriend ordered the Old Fashioned... FIRST OF ALL- This place puts so much care into their drinks, you can imagine how much care they put into their food. Their D&S is bottled and carbonated on site, their Campari is aged in a french oak barrel. These things make such a difference in the taste and experience of drinks and I wish more people cared this much. Needless to say, we didn't order just one of these delicious drinks... we ordered... several. Everything here is made for sharing, which makes it an amazing date spot or a place for 3-5 friends to gather. Since it's a little more intimate, I think anymore than 5 is uncomfortable. Oh, I should also mention that we went back exactly a week after our date with some friends. I just HAD to. On to the meal(s)- Brocoli Rabe- This was something everyone told us we could not miss. The rabe was accompanied by anchovies, parmesean, and eggs. The combination sounds odd but the bitter rabe, with the salty anchovies and parmesean, was perfectly balanced with the creaminess of a medium boiled egg. This is the dish that has me coming back because I feel like I'm eating something relatively healthy but incredibly delicious at the same time. Patatas Bravas- We went to Barcelona and enjoyed several versions of this dish- It's basically fried potatoes with Mayo and Sriracha, although in Barcelona we wished it was this spicy. As delicious as it was, it was my least favorite because I kept accidentally eating the paper that was on the bottom...WHAT!? It looked like potato skin... -_- Creamy Polenta- And creamy indeed it is. I don't think it needed the pork ragu at all. Both were amazing together, but they would have definitely help up on their own. We licked the bowls clean and wished we had more. Grilled Octopus- The boyfriend and I had some delicious Octopus in Europe and we were taken back to those amazing moments once we tasted this one. Although it was a pretty small portion for the price, the meat was tender and there was a great char to it. Another dish I wish we had more of. Steamed Mussels- Spicy, tangy, garlicky, aMAHzingness- that's all I remember of that but it was yummy. Try it! Tagliatelle- My friends thought it was a bit salty but I love that so I didn't mind. For some of these items we got them from a tasting menu. I think I would have chosen to order it anyways. I wish that the noodles were handmade because I think that a fresh pasta would have held up better to the flavorful sauce. Roasted Organic Chicken- This was another thing off the tasting menu. I don't typically order Chicken because it's something I make a lot of at home. However, this chicken was such comfort food. The garlic jus it came with was a game changer. It was tender, moist, and well seasoned. Something I would easily order again. Tiramisu- Have you ever had a dessert that just blew your mind? (cue explosion sound effects). How can something be so decadent yet light, satisfying yet not heavy? Please meet TSA's Tiramisu. It has all the elements of boring tiramisu with a twist. I think the most important element of their tiramisu was the Espresso Granita. Instead of soaking the lady fingers in that, they top the dessert with this and it makes it cool, light, and refreshing. It's the perfect thing to end a meal with. I should know because I had it end my meals twice. Summary- Go there. You won't be disappointed. If you take a girl there, you will definitely score some points. Get the drinks, get the broccoli rabe, get the tiramisu. You won't be disappointed.
Love this place. The oysters, salumi and broccoli rabe were all great, the patatas bravas are just ridiculously good, and service is excellent.

HM.  This was one of those reviews that I wanted to process thoroughly before writing. I had decided on The Saint Austere for my birthday dinner way in advance, just a nice and small gathering of good friends.  I contacted the business via Yelp, and immediately got a response from Jacqueline.  She was very accommodating with my party size and dietary restrictions, 3 in my party are lactose intolerant.  We worked on a menu; I pretty much chose whatever fellow Yelpers had tried and recommended in their reviews.  I had been abroad for close to a month, and when I returned, I also received a follow-up on my reservation.  I was pleased with the attention paid to my reservation. The night I arrived at the restaurant, I was a bit shocked to discover that 9 of us would end up on one table with 4 on the other, whilst sharing a table with another party.  This was a major miscommunication error.  When I was informed that there would be tables next to each other via email, I was not aware the tables would be parallel to each other, and not adjacent.  I have had other restaurants warn me of separate tables, but they would be in the same line of sight, just separated by a gap.  Because of this, a few of my guests were immediately put off and didn't feel like they were part of the celebration.  This made my night of hosting a little more difficult as I was constantly maneuvering between the tables to make sure my guests felt welcomed; it was a small restaurant, and at times, I got in the way of the serving staff. Moving on to the food, as I had mentioned, was an 'All-Stars' $40 prix fixe menu based on reviews: Broccoli Rabe Creamy Polenta Grilled Octopus Steamed Mussels Pappardelle with meat sauce Roasted Organic Chicken Tiramisu I added the meat & cheese boards for an additional $9/person.  I was thoroughly satisfied with the various cuts of meat and pate.  I disliked almost all of the cheese selection, which I was very surprised by since I am an avid fan of cheese. We also decided on 3 dozen oysters- I thought the oysters were small, but passable. Based on my own personal preferences and my guests', I found that the food was a mixed bag.  Some people liked items that I thought were poor executions, others disliked the dishes I preferred.  Only a few thought all the dishes were pretty decent.  The ones I liked included the polenta, broccoli rabe, and organic chicken.  The octopus was tender, but tiny- we had to split 2 tentacles between 4 people.  I did not like the fennel and onion sauce that accompanied the mussels, which were also small.  The pappardelle meat sauce was too subtle- I needed more of the veal & pork to come through.  The chicken was where we had issues.  The chicken I had was tender and juicy; I typically don't order chicken at restaurants because they err on the dry side.  I took a chance on it because of its rave reviews.  I was not disappointed in its texture.   I was then told by guests on the other end of my table that their chicken was still alive and "bucking away."  One of my guests was pretty disgusted by the fact that it was bleeding onto her plate.  Jacqueline took my friend's dish away.  Since I didn't see the chicken with my own eyes, I wasn't going to review it here.  However, because I don't waste food, I brought the leftover pasta and chicken home.  While I was reheating the chicken, the bones were revealed to be almost ENTIRELY red. This really got me annoyed.  I was annoyed that my guests were unable to eat it, and annoyed that the whole chicken was not removed and recooked to the proper temperature.  In this day and age of food-borne illnesses, I don't see how any restaurant can afford to serve under-cooked chicken.   Lastly was the dessert- I cannot even tell you how many tiramisus I've had in my life- from small bakeries to homemade to various Italian restaurants to places that offered a twist.  The tiramisu I had here ranked the lowest on my list.  And I will explain why.  It's made with a dulce de leche and fit into a mason jar with espresso granita sprinkled on top.  I didn't mind the mixture so much, but it did lack a balance between the cream and pastry.  The granita was poorly done; since the chef chose to make the granita more on the icy side, they really had to highlight a stronger espresso taste.  It didn't happen because it wasn't consistent; some icy bits had a slight espresso taste, while others were just comprised of plain water.  It was quite the disappointment. This was the most controversial dining experience of my life- I have never had so many people disagree on the quality of food here.  If I judged solely based on service, I would probably give it a 4.5 rating.  I never saw any of the waitstaff slacking; they worked extremely hard the whole night. And so these 3 stars are really for their effort to provide for our tables.  The rating really suffered in the food department; I can see the potential, but the food definitely needs more TLC.

++++ - That polenta, you cannot leave without having this dish +++ - House made tiramisu, its very delicious. I wasn't a fan of the icy topping though. The rest of the dish made up for it. - Drinks; The homemade bottled dark and stormy was the perfect sweet/alcohol drink without overdoing it on either side ++ - Broccoli rabe, it has egg, but not that strong - The mussels get a thumbs up, although I wish there were a bit more - Service. We wanted for nothing. They were constantly coming around, cleaning tables, asking f we needed anything, replacing plates, everything. They should run a waiter school. + - Scialatelli was alright, I should have ordered another polenta though - - Negative TIPS: - Be careful, those cheap plates add up

This place is awesome!! Menu is complete with all things cheese... from traditional mac n cheese to nutella grilled cheese. They have lactose and gluten free options so it's perfect for just about everyone. Staff is super friendly, answered all my questions and gave great recommendations. Anyone in the Montclair area should do themselves a favor and stop in!
This place is awesome. Mac and cheese deliciousness all around. The sandwiches and desserts are great too. The owner was great and gave good recommendations, definitely give it a try it's worth it!

Im a fry kind of a guy and I must say I had some good FRENCH forts in my life but this place really takes it.. golden crispy, had all the right stuff.... AND THAT WAS JUST THE REGULAR FRIES!!!!.. this really became my regular spot and I hope you guys take this review and take mac attack into consideration it's a cool place cool people... alot of cheese on the menu that'll leave smiling for more... take a visit you'll love it get addicted ..its the cheesest place in montclair.. I always leave wanting more and hope your time there will leave you wanted more and they'll have plenty to give.... check it out

I sooo wanted to like this place, we were excited for it to open forever, but it was a huge letdown. I got the Southwest Mac, $10.00, and an appetizer of peppers with aioli, $7.00. I didn't think the flavors were bad, but the portion sizes were insanely small for what they are charging! (3 tiny piquillo peppers for $7.00 is way too much, even for Montclair, and the mac and cheese container was only a quarter full). I'd go to Cars for mac and cheese before returning, better portions and less money, but I'd be willing to give them another shot if I start to see the reviews improving. I did go the first day they opened so I'm hoping they just need to work out some kinks.

AMAZING!! For a quick bite, I would definitely recommend Mac Attack. The staff is incredibly friendly. They made sure that everything in our order was perfect and we were satisfied. I recommend the Reuben Mac and the Smoked Chicken Mac. If you're looking for grilled cheese, the Manchego and Apple was super tasty. I will definitely be back!!

Love this place! The staff is very friendly and helpful and the food is delicious! What is there not to like about cheese! The traditional grilled cheese- with three different kinds of cheese is AMAZING and the reuben mac and cheese is a unique and delicious take on mac and cheese This is a great place for take out or to sit with friends for a quick casual dinner. Looking forward to going back.

The concept of this - restaurant? - is amazing, and the idea of a grilled mac and cheese made me visibly excited while ordering. Unfortunately, my boyfriend and I found Mac Attack not quite worth our original excitement. My grilled mac and cheese - essentially mac and cheese between toast - wasn't really flavorful at all and was actually pretty bland. I am a carb girl at heart and I found that this sandwich wasn't worth the splurge. My boyfriend got the Philly Mac, which is mac and cheese with steak, peppers and onions. This was very good, and the portion size was huge. The prices are I guess typical Montclair prices, however we felt that the food really wasn't worth the cost. As for the place itself - I was confused. I loved the color scheme and style but there was definitely not enough seating. The choice of couches in the front windows is trendy, but not practical during a lunch rush. There is a ton of unused space. Overall, I probably wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again, especially when I can make better mac and cheese at home.
I loved this place! The food tasted high quality and the service was great! The staff was super friendly and owners are cool. I will definitely be back!

Anybody who tried this place around the time they opened needs to go back!!  I can't attest to the decor because I get delivery.  But the portions have seen a vast improvement in the past few weeks.  They are using the same containers, but instead of being half full or less, they are packed.  I'm eating Philly Mac right now and having a lover affair with it. It's a new place and things are clearly in flux.  Don't write them off because of these reviews, many of them were written around the time of their opening.  Not that they're wrong per se, but things have definitely improved. I'm rooting for you Mac Attack!

If you love Comfort food Mac Attack is the place for you. Anything you order their is AMAZING. The have the Best French fries. Creamy and stringy mozzarella sticks that are to die for. Grilled Cheese that has great texture and great taste. The Mac and cheese is made unconventionally but will be the best you have ever tasted. They even have. Great kids meal. The staff are on of the most friendly people. And the owners are also really awesome. I would 101% recommend Mac Attack.

Mac Attack is literally the greatest place ever. I went in there last weekend after failed planning ruined my night and had a grilled cheese and thats when I knew that my night had changed for the better. Not only is Mac Attack's menu filled with all things cheesy goodness, but they have a Nutella Grilled Cheese (which I cannot wait to try!). AND for all the lazys out there like me that are too lazy to get up and drive 5 minutes, THEY HAVE FREE DELIVERY!!! I know what I'm having for dinner! PLUS my friend and I met the owner and the manager and they are both AMAZING! New best friends, seriously. So go get drunk at the bar and then go to Mac Attack because what else could you possibly want after a night of drinking?? CHEESE!

My boyfriend and I went there a couple of weeks ago. Decor looks a lot like 5 guys-minimalistic. Hipster behind the counter was unenthusiastic. My boyfriend had the Traditional Mac and Cheese. The cheese was fair but the mac was WAY over cooked which is unforgivable. I had the Manchego and Apple grilled cheese. It was okay but I should have known the basil would not work. It feels like an afterthought, thankfully it peeled off easily enough. There was some dijon type of spread on it which enhanced the taste. Overall-fair, high priced for mediocre food. I won't be back.

I don't get the bad reviews. The food was fantastic, I got buffalo chicken mac and it was great. my buddy got cheeseburger mac and he loved it. We both agreed the portion size was great, I almost couldn't finish mine (but I powered through it) because I was so full. In comparison, this place blows the NYC mac and cheese places out of the water in price and taste. This is not a gourmet restaurant, but it's delicious.
