Oh and the staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable. Jeez people. edit: Crystal M., what the hell were you expecting? a 5 star restaurant? double edit: is there anyway I can give this place more than 5 stars?

Very good experience, I'm not sure where all the hate is coming from (although I have an idea...).  Came in with my family and John, one of the owners was behind the counter.  He was friendly and very helpful in making recommendations.  I had the buffalo chicken mac (special), my wife had the carbonara mac and my daughter had the mac bites.  All were very good.  Also I had the tomato soup, seemed "homemade", was hot and delicious.  Service was quick and even though it's counter service, we had people check on us a couple of times to make sure everything was OK. I like to evaluate based on what I would expect at a comparable restaurant.  Meaning I'm not comparing this to Culinariane down road, but like I would a diner or other "fast food" type of place.  That being said the food was great, the portions were plentiful (anyone saying else wise, I have no idea what you were expecting), service was friendly and quick.  What more can you want at an avg. price of $10-$12. The only area I can ding them is an ambiance.  Very bright overhead lighting and with the colors on the wall, the room practically glows.  I like a "darker room", but that's my bias I guess.  Also could use more (and more comfortable) seating and additional decor.  But overall, you should try this place.   I know we'll be back.

My wife and I love this place. We moved from NYC to CT and REALLY missed our favorite restaurants. That said Star of India is hands down our favorite Indian food restaurant. Even better than Jackson Diner (it's true) this place does not disappoint. The chicken Korma is amazing. The lunch buffet is to die for, and prices are good. I don't generally write reviews but this place is seriously the best Indian in CT (best Indian anywhere frankly.)

Loved this place! My boyfriend and I decided to go to this place as a last-minute Valentine's day dinner. Lucky for us, it was about 8:45 pm and the place was fairly empty - the server said we came in just after the v-day rush. We had such a good experience (minus the weird couple next to us who were clearly on their first date, after meeting online... I know this because their conversation was so freaking loud). The food came out in a timely fashion, the servers were attentive and friendly, they kept our water re-filled, and when there was food left over (because the servings were huge) he bagged our left overs up, and added more rice so we could eat it for lunch tomorrow! One server that I have to point out was pretty awesome was the older gentleman; don't know his name.. but he was super attentive and very friendly :) My only complaint is that when I wanted to finish my meal off with an Indian Chai from their menu, he told me they weren't able to make it that night... but I understand... it's busy and whatnot, I just got a black tea instead. One thing I should also point out is that my boyfriend is a Rican who was not introduced to Indian food until we started dating. Up until now, he has been very "ehhh"-ish about Indian food, and has basically eaten it to humor me. However, after dining at Star of India, my boyfriend came home from work today and stated that he wanted to order delivery from this place because he was craving the sauce from his Chicken Tikki Masala. That right there says a whole lot to how delish this place is! Also, this place is a bit cheaper then the other places I have been around her (I usually frequent Sitar or Kamal). Every single dish is a few dollars cheaper, which is nice :) I will definitely go back!
Good beer, horrible service. Waitress tried to rip me off of twice! Never coming back to this dump.

I must say, I really do not understand the negative comment about the Makris.  I try to get there every weekend, because my kids love the place, and so do I.  We have almost exclusively gone for breakfast, but I have had a few lunches there as well.  No matter what meal I go for, I never leave feeling anything less than fully satisfied. Breakfast is our favorite.  I have had everything from omelets to the Monte Cristo, and all have been fabulous.  My oldest always gets chocolate chip wheat pancakes, and is never disappointed.  My youngest has various food allergies, and the folks at the Makris have always either cooked her something special, or cooked the special waffles or oatmeal I bring myself.  No other diner or restaurant has done this for us, and it really shows what a special place the Makris is. In addition to the great food and wonderful, personal attention we are paid while dining at the Makris, I have to comment on the atmosphere.  Unlike certain other diners or restaurants in the area (the Olympia and the rebuilt McDonald's come immediately to mind), the Makris actually looks and feels genuine- probably because it is.  The Makris is clean and fittingly updated, but remains an old-school diner without the fake, over-the-top "nostalgia" of those other places.  From the shining diner car exterior to the single-table juke boxes, the Makris oozes small town diner charm.   Unlike the Olympia, which tries really hard but just can't pull off the genuine atmosphere and incredible food, the Makris does so with ease. Basically, your choice is to visit the Olympia once and leave wanting, or visit the Makris and feel as if you never want to leave.

4 Stars because: + Friendly and prompt service + GREAT coffee/espresso - By JRene - a CT micro roaster + Large portions (I'm a big eater on the weekend after a long night out.) + Great location, ample Parking (in back), lots of seating, and easy to access I cant give it a 5 because they are not open 24 hours and only server Breakfast and Lunch so at 1:30am when I'm leaving the bar I have to go to either Goldrock, Dennie's, or Olympia... and frankly given those choices Id rather go home thank drink burnt water which they claim to be coffee.

We used to go to their first restaurant particularly for the veal. Then that place changed owners and the quality went down and the price went up. We were happy when we saw the familiar faces at RigaTony's and were even happier to find out that they still care about the quality of their food and once again, the veal is outstanding.

I've been there 5 or 6 times since they opened  & everything I've tried has been awesome. The Penne Vodka is the best I've ever had and the prices are very reasonable. Even though it's a new place, you can tell the owners really know what they're doing. Overall, a great experience dine-in or take-out
Food was excellent and the service was excellent! I'll definitely be back.
kalbi was awesome and very well marinaded. this place was very clean and staffs were very knowledgeable about the menu and friendly.. no doubt this would be another great place to dine out!

Going to a restaurant in its first week of operation is always a gamble because the staff is still trying to figure out the work groove.  Therefore, as a patron, you are expected to have some hiccups in service.  However, I see a lot of potential in this place. Despite being new, I really wanted to try this restaurant ASAP.  When I saw the first reviews on Yelp, I knew that I had to drag my fiancé.  After all, I drive by it everyday to work (both jobs) and was anxious to try it! Though located in a crummy strip mall, the location near Westfarms Mall and the interior décor are both perfect.  When we walked in, lots of tables were occupied and the kitchen was chaotic.  We were walked to our table/grill immediately, but were not acknowledged until ten minutes after we were seated.  Our waitress was very nervous and appeared to be new to waiting on tables, but gave her the benefit of the doubt because the restaurant was new and it was busy.  She was hesitant when she was cooking our meat on the grill. The menu had lots and lots of choices; Korean bbq, noodle dishes, soups, and sushi.  We were surprised that it was not cheap.  The Korean bbq was in the $20 and above range and it was a two-person minimum.  Since we never had a Jewish Christmas on Christmas, we splurged on the BBQ and ordered the Chadol-Baegi (beef brisket that is not marinated) and Daeji-Bulgogi (spicy pork collar, more like paprika pork collar).  Both were very good, but I liked the beef brisket.  You got a lot of food and it was like a Korean hibachi.  As Jason M. reviewed, if you get the BBQ, you don't need to get anything else because it comes with a bunch of different mini appetizers; some were good and others were misses. What was cool was that they didn't have a liquor license so we got a bottle of wine from CT Bev Mart next door, so we saved money on drinks.  The manager walked around and asked about our experiences.  There are little rooms for those who want a private party. Definitely be back, but to try a soup or noodle dish.  Good to see non-chain restaurants open in the West Farms area.

We went back and tried the BBQ.  We made reservations and were seated promptly in one of there rooms.  Service was adequate considering how busy they were.  They did forget about us at the end of our meal.  And yes like most korean BBQ, u need to have at least two to BBQ at your table.  Tons of banchan.  Complimentary tea.  But a bit expensive for the area, almost as expensive as Queens.  We will definitely be going back to curb my Korean cravings.

I went there on New Year's Day after I heard some Korean friends raving about the place, and I can see why. The ambience in the restaurant is nice and cozy, don't take the latter too literally though, since as other reviewers have pointed out the place can be a bit cold because of the vent hoods. We got the BBQ combo for 5 (you get 14 sides with that, most of which were various types of kimchi and salads) and one person in my party ordered sushi. The food was delicious; the parts of the meat that were marinated were just right and the sides were nice and authentic. The experience of cooking meat on a grill on my own table was new to me - and totally fun! Their sushi got good reviews as well. Prices are a bit high, but not too unreasonable considering the quality. My friends noticed that some items disappeared from the menu since the last time they went to the restaurant, so I guess the restaurant still needs some time to get to run really well. Still, the food came super fast and the staff we interacted with was very nice.

We have been trying to find a good Korean restaurant in CT since we left Hawaii 10 years ago. This place is it!  We had reservations and upon arrival we were immediately seated. Our initial waiter was good, but virtually all of the wait staff goes around the restaurant to attending to all patrons, which was great.  The food....oh my goodness, it was so good.  My only "complaint" would be that it wasn't spicy enough for me.  We had the boneless kalbi and seasoned pork belly to grill at our table.  The 14 little plates of vegetables were delicious (although not spicy enough).  I asked for some steamed egg and was pleasantly surprised when it was made and brought to our table..delicious!  It's not on the menu though.  We didn't know that it was BYOB so next time we will bring our own.  We were pleasantly surprised and extremely happy with the food (plenty of choices on the menu), the wait staff, and the owners.  This is great place to eat...even if it took us over an hour to drive there!  I would have enjoyed a refreshing cold cinnamon drink at the end of the meal.  Perhaps they will add that to the menu!  We will definitely go back....soon!
Love the place, it was clean, good food. Great servers, quick and kind. Recommend the place if you are around Midtown looking for good not expensive food.
I love everything from this place, nice decor, nice staff, excellent food.. I have the pad see ewe, spring rolls and foil salmon...
Food is great. You get great lunch deals. Best Thai food Ive ever had.

The food here is excellent. We came here for a couple of drinks, but decided to stay for dinner after eating some appetizers and loving the food. They have wonderful martinis. I especially love the lychee Martini. We had the pad udon, spicy pad kee Mao, basil fried rice with roasted duck, and kow mun Kai tod. Every meal was expertly prepared. The flavors were excellent and and spices were perfect. I would  definitely go back next time I'm in NYC.

5 stars for their lunch special - which is your typical everyday Thai food lunch special BUT it comes with an awesome beverage - Thai Iced Tea! (I think you have other choices for beverage too, but I don't remember). However, I once came here right when they first opened on a Sunday (at noon) and the woman didn't seem too excited to see me. Also, when I took out my credit card to pay for my little lunch special, the lady said they had a $10 card minimum. But then I made a sad face, so she swiped it anyways. Future husband also once saw that they had accidentally overcharged him on his credit card statement (mixed him up with another bill). However, when he went over with the receipt, they changed it for him. But 3 stars for service for all things related to credit card. Everything else rounds out to a nice 4 stars. Dinners are typical usual prices. Since it first opened (I think last fall/winter), they have downgraded a little bit, but the quality is pretty decent. Future husband and I come here quite often since it's right around the corner from his place. Is it better than the gazilion Thai places in the area? Probably on-par, but not out of the park better by any means. BUT if you like a free Thai Iced Tea with your lunch special, come here! PROS: Thai Iced Tea with lunch special, cheap lunch deals, nice decor (if you like dark and neon lights) CONS: credit card issues/minimum, some people are not happy
Came at 11:30p. Website said midnight.  Told us they were closed. Went to Bea's which was great.

Pauline's was wonderful! The food was superb! My husband had salmon and I had a chicken dish and they were both excellent. The service was wonderful as well. My husband asked for a recommendation on a local beer, and the server was knowledgeable and gave a great suggestion. The prices were a little on the high side, but we didn't mind paying it for what we got.

I loved my visit to the Americana.. Our server was very polite and extra friendly (not fake friendly) I had the "little bit of everything" and it was so good!! It came with 2 pancakes, eggs, bacon and sausage.. The maple syrup was warm and awesome!!! You must go there!! I will visit again when back in NJ!!!

The restaurant gets very busy.  Especially during peak hours, which is when you want to go.  You will wait a few minutes before being seated.  But we have never waited longer than 5 minutes.  During these times the parking lot can be challenging on your nerves.  As the traffic light at the outlet backs up the exiting vehicles within the lot.  Wait area can get cramped.  But again, you shouldn't be there for very long. Those expecting and looking for a more "diner" theme, should be cautious when entering.  Although Americana calls itself a "diner", the restaurant is one white tablecloth & candle stick away from being "fine dining".  There is a definite diner feel to the front, and the menu is vast, but that's about where the dining aspect ends.  The restaurant will certainly have an option for everybody.  As your eyes begin to wander overlooking the menu, you will be sure to notice the price.  Americana sells above average food, at an expensive price.  Service is always decent.  Again, the food is above average in quality.  Portions will be much smaller than what you would anticipate at any other "diner".  And the plates are put together for more aesthetic purposes. Also attached to the restaurant is a bar.  During the week nights, it is indeed a nice place to meet with somebody.  But again, can add up quick. *** 1/2 *

First and foremost:  This is not a diner.  I repeat -- not a diner. so if you came here for some comfort food, to stuff yourself silly, have enough leftovers for two more meals, and walk out for under $10 a person -- this is not it. I had heard that they had changed, but we forgot before walking in the door and seeing that the entire menu is a piece of paper/placemat. Their burgers and sandwiches (limited) come with nothing and are $12.  However, that comes with a $3 "credit" towards a side -- where you can, indeed, get fries.  They have some really interesting other sides, some $3, some $4, some $5. The veggie burger was okay; hubby got mexicali burger, son got a reuben.  All just okay.  The three sides were onion rings, polenta "chips" and quinoa salad.  Um, okay.  Everything was just okay.  no leftovers, all food consumed, and we were hungry, so it was backtracking to DQ for ice cream. Bill was $50 for 3, no drinks. Sigh.

been going here for years before it got upscale and I enjoyed it either way. But the food quality has gone down but their servers are great and fast they monitor your drinks and are attentive. The manager is clueless and they change too much management get your management together the food overall though I have to say is good but sometime bland and overly priced

This place is my go to hibachi spot. The Food is reasonably priced and you get a lot for your money. The hibachi shrimp is my favorite of any hibachi place I have tried (over aprx 15 shrimp you get).   Their ginger dressing is awesome and i always ask for extra. The sushi is pretty good and reasonably priced you are expecting "awesome sushi" go to a SUSHI restaurant, not a hibachi steakhouse. I always order a spicy tuna or salmon roll with my hibachi dinner. They also offer you  ice cream that included in the price of your hibachi dinner.  Not many places do that. Also they give you a LOT of any meat you order , especially the chicken. Their was a rumor that the health department found a CAT carcass in the freezer?? i dont believe it but i thought it was funny.  If it was a cat, it tasted pretty damn good.

I came here once earlier this year late night.. our bartender was very friendly , down to earth and just overall pleasant. It was laid back and casual. I must say I had way too much to drink and at $25 a shot.. I should of known better .. lol

The food gets 5 stars. Seriously delicious stuff that I crave if I've gone too long without it. If you like New Orleans eating, you'll find a happy home here. The bar service gets 2 stars. I haven't experienced a whiff of hospitality on any visit.

We had a good experience at Bluebird.  Not mind-blowing, but good.  They were out of clams, which knocked an appetizer and a main dish off the menu.  They were out of the rabbit "saddle," which I only learned about after I had ordered (who doesn't want to try a rabbit "saddle?).  I also overheard the waiter say they were out of Bombay Sapphire gin.  So, I'm wondering what is going on with the ordering here.  They have a pretty tight menu, meaning, it's not huge, and there were no specials, so I would expect they should be able to do better inventory control.   Nevertheless, I had a slow-cooked flatiron, which was excellent.  Super tender, with mashed potatoes and roasted carrots.  The carrots were a tiny bit undercooked, but not terribly so.  My wife had an oyster-stuffed filet of sole, which she loved.  It's not often you get a piece of stuffed fish that isn't way heavy on the breading.   For dessert, I had a cranberry cake, which was very tasty.  She had something called an "affogatto," which was ice cream with a piece of cooked dough.  The dough was tough and chewy, so it wasn't winning any awards.   We have been here before for brunch and it was good.  There was barely anyone there at 6pm, but by 6:30, the place was hopping, and the atmosphere was nice.  We'll go back.  Rabbit saddle?

As soon as I sat down, I knew this was going to be a treat! The smoked salmon appetizer was seriously good and the rabbit saddle and leg saddled me with joy! I thought that my main course was good! But boy was I in for a treat....literally! The affogato cake knocked me off my feet! I would go here again and again!

The Bluebird Tavern changed my life... I started out as a lowly cubicle jockey, my job was monotonous, I couldn't find a girlfriend, and my car got 7 miles to the gallon on a good day, but that was before I started eating at the tavern... The second I took my first bite of rabbit "saddle" I could feel my mind expanding and taking in experiences I never before dreamed possible. I could see the whole cosmos laid out before me, nebula and galaxies spun before my vision. When I came to I was sitting in my garage looking at my car. The hood was open and all of my power tools lay scattered on the floor, when I sat in the driver's seat I noticed that my car is now a paddle shifter and now a week later I have yet to need to fill up on gas. Since that day, I have eaten the tavern's rabbit "saddle" everyday and my salary has increased by two orders of magnitude, I have a penthouse office in a fortune 500 company, and I go helli-skiing on the weekends... I still can't find a girlfriend, but hey I make enough to eat rabbit saddle at every meal now so I'm sure I don't have long to wait.

A few days ago I was strolling down St. Paul Street and the enticing aroma of glorious honeysuckle grabbed hold of me. Before I knew it, I was purchasing a Cranberry Duff Cake from one of stunning waiters. If I hadn't been exhausted from working in the tobacco fields all week, I would have gotten on one knee in a jiffy. I proceeded to enjoy my moist piece of cake. Before long I was hovering above the ground with joy. Let me be clear: that previous sentence was not a figure of speech. From the moment I took my first bite, I literally started to grow tiny blue wings, weird enough, not unlike the wings of a bluebird. I am still fluttering my wings this very moment. I am not entirely sure if they are permanent, but score! Overall, a lovely tavern with desserts that are the bomb-diggity. Fair warning though: the Duff Cake may or may not grant you the gift of flight. So those of you with a fear of heights, proceed with caution. Bizz Twinkling Stars out of Bizz.

Little Pete's is a great, simple, unpretentious place for a good meal.  The prices are great and the food is always good.   They have lunch specials on weekdays that include a great cup of soup and a drink with your meal.  The service is always fast and helpful.   If you're in the mood for a casual meal you should give it a shot!  I'd especially recommend coming for lunch or weekend brunch.

The closest thing to a diner Fairmount has to offer. The food is consistent, and for better or worse, so is the service.   What I mean to say is this: don't go if you're in a rush, don't go if you want warm and friendly servers, don't go if you don't want to eat elbow to elbow with perpetually fussy senior citizens. On the other hand, I keep returning because I know exactly what I'm going to get at Little Pete's.  And the chicken burger is the best I've had in the city. One final tip: if you don't like your potatoes on the raw side at breakfast, ask for them extra crispy or well done.

**Note to the uninitiated like myself: The address of this place is a tad misleading -- it's NOT on the Pennsylvania side of the building, but rather on the Fairmount side. So, if you're say, a tourist visiting Eastern State Penn, this makes Little Pete's an optimal spot to grab a bite just before or after.** This is a solid 3.5, but more to the 4 side than the 3. Be still my Jersey heart - Little Pete's is a straight up Greek diner, and for the Mister and me, it was the ideal spot for a quasi-brunch on a windy, cold holiday-week morning. Service took a minute to get off the ground, but once it did, it was quick. Yes, it's a haven for fussy seniors, but most good and affordable diners are. The coffee was okay... nothing stellar, but decent enough. I had the Eggs Benedict, which other Yelpers recommended with good reason -- nice portion size, eggs poached to yolky perfection and the hollandaise is delicious, with a tangy, mustardy kick. The home fries were sort of bland, but there was just enough hollandaise left in the gratin dish to where I was able to plop the taters in, coat them in the sauce and relish my concoction. The Mister opted for a grilled cheese with bacon on whole wheat and a couple of eggs over light (accompanied by those ubiquitous potatoes). He's a tough customer to please, but he admitted that while the eggs were standard, the grilled cheese was among the best he's had -- crisp, melty and just plain good. We received the lunch specials menu, and they didn't look bad at all... maybe next time!

So refreshing to have a different place to order from for lunch at work, ordered chicken Caesar salad and it was really, really  good, the chicken was super moist and tasty, their clementine soda is really good too, can't wait to try everything else, and prices are very reasonable for this area! Hope they stay that way !
Truly lovely people, atmosphere, and thankfully (!!) comforting, delicious food. Best of luck - looking forward to stopping in for a home cooked meal again soon.

I am thrilled about finding this restaurant. The food is amazing. I went here for the first time just a few minutes ago and was very impressed. The owners are very friendly and focused on customer service while the food is just out of this world. I had the half chicken with a side of ratatouille and spinach. I will be back here as often as possible and would highly recommend it to friends.

4.5 stars. Fabulous little place with cute ambience, great ingredients,  friendly husband+wife team, and great value on food. They are known for their tender rotisserie chicken. Definitely get something with rotisserie chicken. Portions ate large so i would recommend small sizes rather than large unless you are sharing. They get their produce and chicken fresh every day. I would come here for lunch all of the time if I worked nearby.
Order takeout half chicken & 2 sides. So good! And so fast!  Chicken is very juicy. Vegis are fresh and well prepared. Side salad had a nice, light dressing. Owner/employees are very nice.

Thanks to Salinas, I died and went to Basque food heaven for a while last night.   My husband and I were impressed with the sexy décor, the friendly yet unobtrusive staff and the fantastic, delicious food. The dining room is all flickering lights, dark wood, relaxation and romance, a wonderful relaxing environment, a perfect place to have a great dining experience. Got started with some sangria which was excellent -- not too sweet, not too dry, with tons of fresh  fruit.  We chose the quail wrapped in bacon and short rib croquettas  to start.  Both were really tasty and well presented.   We had some more sangria and then tackled a large dish of paella which was perfectly cooked and looked and tasted exactly like its wonderful counterpart that I enjoyed while visiting the Basque some years ago. Unfortunately, I could not stay and try the desserts as we were on the babysitting clock...but that's just another good reason to eat here again.   Salinas, yo te amo demasiado!

Why haven't I been here before?! What an incredibly sexy place for dinner! The atmosphere is dark and cozy. Candlelight every where! There is a small bar and waiting area in the front, where I believe you can order from the menu if you can't get a table. The service is absolutely outstanding. The hostess greeted us immediately and warmly. Our coats were checked in, and we were brought back to our table with little to no wait at all on a fairly busy evening. There are not a whole lot of tables back there, but I did see them put together a few tables to accommodate a large group. It drove the noise level up significantly, but that's probably the most negative thing I can say about this restaurant. The chef sent us a small sampling of their tapas, or an amuse bouche. We got the the tostas de boqueron (marinated anchovies on toast) and brandada y hongos (catalan codfish, wild mushroom compote on toast). Two bites for each of us. They were delicious! We ordered the panceta con calabaza (pork belly and squash) and the codorniz con membrillo (bacon wrapped quail). We devoured everything. And these plates came out looking like small works of art! For our entrees, we went with the fish of the day (and for the life of me can't remember what it was, but it was fantastic and light) and the Porcella (suckling pig). I am Filipina and I know a thing or two about suckling pig. This was melt-in-your-mouth, fall off the bone divine! It was flavored beautifully and the skin was crispy enough. The micro greens and watercress that accompanies these dishes are perfect compliments to the proteins. The sauces were flavorful and strong without overpowering the entire dish. I can't say enough fabulous things about this spot. It's a hidden gem that was quite busy on a cold Tuesday night. Will I be back? Let's just put it this way; if a date happens to take me there for dinner, chances are they are in for a very satisfying night! (I'm talking about the food, of course!)  ;-)

Salinas is a mecca for traditional Basque and Catalan fare. When entering into the restaurant, I was immediately struck by the dimly lit cavernous feeling of the place-- it was romantic and intimate but also super trendy.  Dimpled velvet couches were as comfortable as they were attractive. Tapas and cocktails were definitely the highlight of the meal.  I had the hido en sidecar and my date had the new amsterdam. Both were strong and very good.  The tapas were also quite delicious-- especially the grilled country bread, tomato and boquerones, and the bacon wrapped quail with mushrooms and shallots. The entrees were a bit less impressive-- We split the suckling pig and rosejat rapida. Despite rave reviews of the "fideo" (spanish style pasta), I was certainly partial to the former.   Service was IMPECCABLE. Chef Bollo even made an appearance to give us a rundown of the menu. Definitely worth a visit!

This restaurant is the most delicious Spanish restaurant that I have been to thus far. The service was excellent. We were promptly greeted when we entered the restaurant. The ambiance was really cozy and memorable. The servers were very attentive, but not overwhelming. It was a great experience. Overall, I would give this a 4.5 stars out of 5. I forgot the names of the drinks I ordered but they were both very delicious. 5/5 Appetizers: Montadito- lamb meatballs with cucumbers. The spices added were a perfect blend with the lamb and cucumbers. 5/5 Cordorniz Con Manzanas- quail wrapped with bacon with pan seared apple and mushrooms. This also tasted very good. 4/5 Main Course: Pescado Del Dia- fish of the day over sliced potatoes. The fish was perfectly cooked and the potatoes were a wonderful addition. Super delicious. 5/5 Pollo Campero- local chicken with beans, mushrooms and greens. Although the chicken tasted good, this is a more mediocre dish. 3/5 Dessert: Nuestro Flan- the flan is very rich and flavorful. I would recommend sharing this. 4/5 We really enjoyed dining at Salinas, the food, the ambiance and the service were great.

The atmosphere is exquisite, really beautiful and rich; it's the kind of place you'll want to just take your time in because you don't want to leave. There's a back garden area behind the restaurant, and in the  summer the roof retracts. I'll certainly be back for tapas and drinks to experience this. The service was really top-notch as well, everyone was really friendly. The manager came over before and after our meals to introduce herself, and was very friendly. Onto the drinks! The sangria was excellent. It was really sweet but with fruit, not sugar. It tasted like a fruity red-wine candy (uh-oh =D). They've also got a heavy pour, which I like. I opted for a tequila cocktail, I beleive called the Duente. I don't see it on their online menu now, but it was a great combination of a Spanish fruit, thyme, and egg white. All of the cocktails looked really artful and good quality. For the food, we each ordered a tapa and an entree. I got the gambas al ajillo, which had mushrooms in them along with your standard gambas set-up. I thought it needed some salt. My friend Courtney got the quail, which was served crispy, wrapped in bacon, and with sauteed apples in balsamic reduction. Those were the best thing that we ate. Onto the entree, we each ordered the Porcella (aka suckling pig). The day after I ate at Salinas, I took a look online to try to explain to a friend what I had eaten. I googled "Salinas Pork," because I had forgotten the name, and the first thing that popped up was a write-up from NY Magazine that Salinas was in fact the best Suckling Pig in the city. The pork itself was in fact really delcious. The inside was super tender and flavorful, topped with a thin later of inevitable fat, and then a crispy and delicious skin that was actually out of this world. The only minus is I think it needed sides that held up better to the weight of the pork.

I recently went to Acacia on a date due to a recommendation by a friend.  The food and service was excellent.  Our waitress Lauren was extremely friendly and personable and had extensive knowledge of the menu which made our experience that much better.  As far as food, I had the duck which was out of this world.  Also, the ambiance is very quaint and comfortable while still being fancy to allow for a great night out.  I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the area.

I cannot say enough nice things about this place.  I have been here two times and both times have been terrific.  I had the crab cakes both times and they are the best.  My boyfriend has gotten daily specials and enjoyed them.  Every entree there is complemented by original sides and sauces making for great dishes.  The service and ambiance are excellent.  It is a little overpriced but overall worth it.

Is the pizza great? Not really. But the sandwiches really hit the spot! Their chicken salad is also amazing. It's PACKED with tons of different veggies and a generous portion of grilled chicken and a side of bread and butter. So take it for what it is, a quick spot to grab a bite.

I live right around the corner and saw this place being built for a while, so when i saw it was open, i figured i had to try one of their cheesesteaks.  I was hoping i wouldnt have to drive out to delassandro's or down to john's roast pork anymore, but i was very disappointed with this place.  the roll was great, but the meat was not sliced thin, and it wasnt chopped up like it should be, also the cheese should be mixed with the meat instead of just placed on the roll.  also, places like delassandro's give you plenty of meat, this place, the meat didnt even come close to covering the whole roll.  the decor is nice and its clean, and dont know about  the other food, but there cheesesteaks need tons of improvement.

Extremely disappointed. We were looking forward to checking out this new place in the neighborhood.  Placed an order for delivery and waited for over an hour before we called to inquire about our status. They had not recorded our order and could not recall me even ordering.  Best of luck, but we will not be attempting to try this place again.

Blue is my go to place for special occasions or for date night with the hubby.  They also offer weekly pre fixe menus with a nice variety of items to choose from.  The owners of Blue also own Bayou (trying that next) and Beso which I love love love....  You won't go wrong at Blue.

This was my second time at this restaurant. The first time was during the week and the food was good. However, it was a little noisy and the table was so wide that we could not carry on a conversation. We tried it again but this time on a Saturday night. We were seated at the same wide table. When I asked for another table, I was told that there was none available for our party of 6. First the food: nothing special. The samosas were flavorless and mushy and my friend's were burnt. They ran out of the halibut special and substituted tuna. Some pieces were cooked well, others were overcooked. The rice that was supposed to be included in the dish was absent. When we asked about it, we received an apology and were given a plate of overcooked watery rice. Next the service: we waited a long time for our drinks to be served and a long time for our main dishes. We were asked by the busboy to give him our dishes. After our appetizer dishes were taken away, we were never given  silverware for our main course. The busboy came with 4 dishes and called out "who gets the shrimp, who gets the chicken etc. rather than knowing who got what. Then we waited for the other 2 dishes to arrive. My friend had to ask 3 times for an additional drink. The busboy passed dishes across people instead of serving them from behind each person. After our main course was done, the busboy yelled across the table "can you hand me that plate" to my husband and my friend. Although she tried to control the chaos, our server became involved with a party and could not give us the attention we deserved and kept making excuses for the poor service. We waited 20 minutes for our check and 10 minutes for it to be processed. And the worst thing: the noise level. We should have left when we realized we could not have a conversation across the wide table or even with the person next to me. But, you can be sure we will not return.

2 stars or 1, really not sure.  Tried pork taco, chicken- both seemed way overly cooked and dried out.  Flavorless, not juicy as a taco should be.  The tortilla though actually had some flavor to it. What did look amazing? The huge nachos platter served next to us.  Now that might be very good!

I'm not a huge fan of Mexican food, but this place has definitely changed me. It's better than Chipotle and any of those other chain restaurants, which was why I made the trip from the UWS to the East Village, transfers and the possibility of missing my bus back to NJ included. Both times I've came, I've had the steak burrito and it is seriously foodgasmic. The steak inside is so tender and the rice and beans only add more depth to the flavor. I typically hate beans, but this place has made me come to love them with my burritos. I've ordered carnitas tacos here before too for a friend, who told me she loved them, but the steak taco will forever be my go to. It's pricier than those chain restaurants, but you can't compensate for the amazing food that this place puts out. I LOVE TAQUERIA DIANA!

This was my experience at Taqueria Diana tonight.  It is more about the atmosphere which was so shitty, I couldn't really enjoy my food. There was one person in line in front of me, so I thought I would get two tacos to tide me over until a late dinner.  I placed my order and was waved down.  I got to a table where the previous people had failed to bus their tray.  I bused their shit for them.  I sat next to a table where two young women were also eating.  On the other side two men sat down who ordered behind me.  30 minutes go by. The line of people waiting for their food is extremely long. The two dudes and I check in with each other about what the hell is going on that two tacos would take this long. I get up to see what's happening with the food and the ladies next to me leave, also not bussing their trays.  A young, super rich but ultra cheesy couple sits down.  As I come back to the table they have placed the dirty dishes left by the women on my tiny table near all of my stuff which is touching their table.  Just be aware--the seating area is super tiny there.  Basically their actions were like putting someone else's dirty dishes in my lap instead of taking, literally, three steps and putting the plates at the bussing station. They have their food, despite ordering AFTER everyone and whip out their phones and other little camera (THREE in total) to take many pictures of their food.  I stare at them incredulous (which is stupid of ME.  Duh, this is the East Village where young, rich, mean kids go to be young, rich, and mean). I sit down with my tacos pissed.  And then this couple starts browsing their phones for places to stay in Ibiza.  "Do you think a three step stairway down to the beach is too far?" F.U.C.K. Y.O.U.  I got my shit and moved to the little counter literally a few steps away and dropped my phone, because FUCK, I wanted to get away from these people, and the cook laughed at me.   And you know what, joke IS on me. This place charges $5 a taco.  THAT IS CRAZY when a good taco truck charges a buck.  When you go to a place where people will cough money for something that usually costs a buck, be prepared to be stomped on so that Mr. and Mrs. Rich East Village Couple can take awesome photos of their food which I'm sure they'll expell with laxatives later to show their backstabbing friends in Ibiza. For. Real.

This is my go to place to grab food and then catch a game at Standings. The tacos are solid.  A little messy, but worth it.  The Al Pastor taco was delicious. They really don't skimp on the meat in these tacos either - two tacos was plenty of food for me.   However, the guacamole was disappointing. It was a creamy guac, and I prefer a very chunky and spicy guac.

Very good nachos. I didn't eat here but took it to a bar nearby because I needed to be able to wash it all down with a cold beer.  I got the chicken nachos and let me say, the portion was obscene.  The bag weighed a couple pounds, easy.  Definitely enough for two hungry people.  Tons of pulled roasted chicken on here.  I asked for creme and didn't get it but at least they gave me the guac, and it was substantial.  Also, it was loaded with cheese.  There was distinctly smokey flavor in the chicken.  Next time I will want to eat there because what it lacked was HOT sauce.  Still, even without crema and hot sauce it tops my best ever nacho list (I can't even think of any that come close to even being memorable).  I will be back for more if I am in the area.  My friend had the chicken burrito which was also amazing.

Definitely the best "classic" (e.g. not overtly fusion ala Tres Carnes) taco I've had in New York.  I liked the ample helpings of flavorful meat, along with the opportunity to really layer on extras like guac, crema and cheese, which I think some purists might be averse to.   So why four stars? Because the operations and real estate could use some serious work: the assembly line seems unspecialized and the store understaffed.  I am not from California, but on recent visits to a few San Francisco taquerias, lines out the door were handled from start to food in about five minutes.  I had to wait twenty minutes for two tacos and had a heck of a time getting to order even though there was only one person in front of me.  I'm not saying that Taqueria Diana needs to change everything, but I do think that getting an operational specialist to advise them might help a bit.  (Along with re-arranging the layout if there's ever the funding.)

Came here on a Thursday night for a two stop taco night and this was the second stop (went to Otto's Taco first). This is my friends favorite taco joint so of course I had to see what the hype was all about. My friend had the Al Pastor taco (split roast pork) and I had the Pollo taco (chicken). We shared the nachos which we added steak to (Carne Asada nachos). The tacos were good (chicken was NOT DRY), but the nachos were...lets just say ORGASMIC! YES, SO GOOD that we were both very full but still trying to scarf it down. The nachos are a must!! I wish I wasn't so full from my first taco stop, otherwise I would come back here just for the nachos and the portions are HUGE!!

We went for lunch today.  So FREEKKIN YUMMY.  Small, tiny, hole in the wall!! I love a hole in the wall.  Fancy Smansy places that are expensive and not yummy ANNOY THE CRAP OUTTA ME!!! Very Fresh, A family owns it I think.  They were so sweet...One of our dishes was the Mushroom Quesadia, so so good. My husband and I were so overjoyed that everything was not crazy salty, as we are in training and try to eat healthy.   People are really unable to grasp that healthy food is the least processed and has the fewest ingredients....Resulting in a fresh taste of the ACTUAL INGREDIENTS...GO  FIGURE  Why go to a tiny tiny place if you want lightning fast service.  We actually waited a while too...But I cannot explain how happy I was at the freshness of our food, that had not been sitting in a freezer...premade for six months. Go to Houlis, Red Lobster or Bonefish for food that is quick and prepared in a factory and shipped across country. The food has few ingredients...whatever meat you order...some cilantro, fresh or fried onion and peppers...frankly I would liken it to close to health food....So if you want some super salty, preservative laden eats...this is not the place for you.
Been there 4 times now. The salmon with mustard sauce is delicious and consistant each time.   I will definitely go again and again.

I love that both of the historic Taft spaces have now been restored (the other being Roia in the ballroom). And both show much care and respect in their restoration. This place has a great atmosphere and a feel that's unique to New Haven. It definitely has a bit of a LES/Williamsburg vibe - joining the ranks of Firehouse 12 and 116 Crown as another preferred hipster watering hole. Prices are good, drink menu is interesting, beer choices are solid, service is good. Haven't tried the cheese/charcuterie/savory pies yet, but I trust it's all top quality coming from Mr. Cheese himself. It gets 5 stars on appearance alone. The back room is especially awesome, a comfortable place to hang out and relax as the Richter's moose surveys his domain.

Great drinks at reasonable prices; beautiful dark wood bar, warm atmosphere.  The Ordinary is something New Haven has been missing. Glad it's here now. Minus one star though for the wooden sporks and, especially, the fast-food style paper baskets that the pies come in. Give us real forks and plates!

A cute place to eat right on the Passaic river.  The staff is very friendly and professional. The prices are reasonable. Unfortunately the food isn't that great, it's not that bad but not great. Over all experience is fair and I'd suggest giving it a try. What doesn't taste great for me might be for you. Enjoy!

Came upon this little place thanks to Yelp. Great surprise! Food was nicely prepared, service charming and, added bonus for the first warm day of the year, garden in the back with heating lamps. Dinner on the terrace with guests from wintery Québec, memorable!

Chop Shop is very tasty! This place doesn't look like much from the outside, but once you step inside you are greeted with cute decor and a friendly staff. Though small, the outdoor seating in the back is lovely. The food here is very tasty. I came with friends and we ordered the Fried Rice, Pork Belly Buns, Kung Pao Chicken (a special that night) and the Spicy Drunken Noodle. We all enjoyed our dishes very much! I ordered the Spicy Drunken Noodle and asked for a vegetarian option with tofu instead of shrimp and they were very accommodating. It was delicious!   Chop Shop is small, so its probably best to make a reservation. Our server was excellent. I would definitely return to Chop Shop!

I just found a brand new deli and it is AMAZING.  It's not your typical deli.  This is by far the best deli I have ever been to in NYC.  If you are looking for a deli that is not ordinary by any means, this is the place to go.  They offer sandwiches, salads, hot food, cold food, pasta, ready-made and for-order sushi, pasta station, pho, udon, and a whole section of gourmet cookies/snacks.   I highly recommend anything in this place.  I love love love how spacious it is and the seating area upstairs gives you a birds eye view of the whole deli. Check it out if you're looking for food that tastes like home cooking.  You won't regret it!

Very good place to go for breakfast or lunch. The neighborhood lacks food locations that have this many options in one place. Not your typical NYC deli. Not only is the food great but the interior space is designed well and very clean.

The man who said this is the best diner in New Jersey made me laugh so hard I felt like throwing myself in front of a bus. Maybe yeaaaaars ago this was a good diner, but get serious. For breakfast, you probably have your best shot cause there is less to screw up. Lunch 50/50 and by the time you get to dinner, well, you know where this is going. I had the soup which basically was a cup of salt. (No intention to insult salt). Marilyn is a terrific waitress, and has always been. That's why I give this 2 stars, instead of one. But, it is obvious the owners put very little effort or concern into this place, because they have the other restaurant which gets their attention. Oh well.

It's so simple: hands down the best pasta I have tried in New York. Best tiramisu too. I have been going to other Italian places trying to find a good Italian meal. Most of them more expensive than Ciccio, none could compare to it. Service is excellent at Ciccio's too, genuine smiles all over.

I came here because of the great yelp ratings, and the only reason I'm giving 2 out of 5 is because the waitress was nice. I came with 5 guests and our meal came in 5 parts, one at a time, with each dish coming out 15-20 minutes apart. The last friend to eat his dish got his meal an hour and 15 minutes after the first friend finished his meal. I felt the pasta was subpar and I had one of the worst dining experiences of my life.

This place finally opened up a few weeks ago just a few blocks from my apartment in the location of the former Marius Cafe, and tonight my boyfriend and I stopped in to try it out! We're both vegetarian so we had somewhat limited options with their current menu, but I ordered and loved the Frisse Salad (mixed greens with sliced parmesan topped with a fried egg) and my boyfriend ordered and equally enjoyed some kind of cheese sandwich with vegetables and spiced mayonnaise.  The side of fries we shared was super delicious!  At the start of the meal we enjoyed fried plantains with a very tasty cliantro dip on the house, which was a nice touch!   The atmosphere was really nice- I loved the new floorplan compared to that of Marius Cafe and the school chairs and wood accents gave the place a relaxed and cool (but not TOO cool) kind of vibe. The staff seemed very nice too. I can definitely see coming down here many more evenings for dinner or just to enjoy some drinks at the bar.  And I can't wait until they start serving brunch (my top favorite meal of the day!).  I'd love to see this place do well, so stop in some time!

Been waiting to try Bar Bruno since its opening two weeks ago. Stopped in on a very heavy and 3-bag trek to the subway before the hurricane hit, and I'm so glad I did. Fantastic chateau de roquefort rosé on special, delicious ceviche tostadas at the bar. Great buzz, cool decor, much-needed nighttime spot in this little area. Can't wait to come back!

I was very excited to try this place, but I left disappointed. The service was bizarre - granted our waitress was 'in training' but she was super weird - staring at us, awkward silences - and the food was not great. The space, however, is very nice and I could see it being a good place to go for drinks and maybe appetizers but I will not come back to eat again. Don't get me wrong, the food is edible, but there are much much better options available within walking distance. If you must eat here, avoid the super bland sandwiches. I really hope they get it together and improve the food, the place has a lot of potential and would be a great addition to the neighborhood...

Beco is one of my favorite brunch places for three reasons: 1- I'm Brazilian 2- I live quite close 3- the food is good and the price is fair: 16 bucks for a dish + coffee + one drink is good enough for me. If you're looking for the delicious Brazilian caipirinhas or caipiroskas this place unfortunately is not for you: they are not made with fresh fruit, but bottled juices. SAD. But the Bloody Mary is super yum. Bife a cavalo is def my favorite. The steak is always soft, the eggs taste fresh and the beans are not from cans... Fantastic. Pão de queijo is a must if your need an appetizer. The staff is usually pretty happy and helpful. I had a little attitude from a Brazilian server today, that coincidently (or not) started when I asked her in Portuguese to trade my guava mimosa for a caju mimosa, the one I had ordered. Anyways I always have a good meal there. Lovely when soccer games are on!
Been here many many times and have gotten most of the food on the menu.  Cheese balls, salada de roca, rice and beans, granola, eggs benedict are to die for.  Cheap, tasty and fun.

I'm infatuated with this place and have been my whole life!! Such good food, I don't even know where to begin! Everything is amazing, from the pizza to their entrees... Their grandma slices are heaven, their focaccia sammies are to die for, and their bowties with sausage and broccoli is my favorite meal of all time. Also, their catering prices are reasonable and the food was nothing less than the amazingess I'm used to. I literally eat here 2-3 times a week!

We went there on Friday night around 6. The place was pretty packed, but we got seated within 10 minute waiting. Based on the reviews and its name, you can tell the restaurant is famous for self made tofu. We ended up having spicy rice cake, seafood soup and bibimbap with tofu and beef. Rice cake was more like a soup and a bit too sweet. I personally more into traditional style. Other two dishes were good. The restaurant truly makes tasty tofu.

Great food, and VERY fast versus some of the other restaurants in the area. Just for two, we came in at noon and got seated instantly. There are 3 floors, top floor is least busy I suppose, first floor was the noisest. I'm always not sure about soup, 'cause sometimes the broth lacks flavour. But BCD Tofu House knows their broth! Great flavor and variety, you won't be disappointed. We got the lunch combo (for two) (L1, BBQ ribs) and the rice cakes as an appetizer. It was $19, despite their site saying a lesser price. Appetizers came in fast, and the rice cake. Loved the fried fish, it was still warm when we got it, I don't always see that in some appetizers. And this was more than enough to fill two people. Side note-- appetizers come per person ordered. I think some restaurants do it by # of people at a table. So we only got a set of one appetizer since we only got on entree. Rice cakes: I loved the spicy broth!! It was so much! There weren't rice cakes, but also fried dumpling and roll and tofu skin/curd. Very filling! The broth was sweet too. I really loved it. BBQ ribs: the marinade was pretty good. It wasn't that oily or greasy. Really generous amount of meat and fatty cuts. At the bottom there were also grilled onions, a lot of them. Assorted Soondubu: Combination of beef, mussels and shrimp. I'm usually skeptical of soup, but the broth was very flavorful and subtle, hardly salty. Don't forget to add the egg! The only thing that sucks about this place is sometimes it's hard to grab a waitress' attention. Like it took more than 10 mins to get our server's attention to reheat our soup cause the egg was still uncooked。 They are always prompt to give you the check though haha.

BCD's second incarnation exceeds its first in flavors and magnitude. An expansive k-town restaurant, BCD stands out amongst a sea of competitors for its best in class soon dubu (Korean stew) offerings. Having tried the seafood, beef and kimchi varieties, I have yet to be disappointed. The ban chan (free appetizer) offerings are up there with the best, including a whole small fish (per person!) are the cherry atop the cake. Just dont arrive hungry; expect 30-60 minute waits during busy times (and a no reservation policy).
The seafood tofu is amazing. The food came in a short period of time, esp for a busy resturant.The service was very organized, but my waitress wasn't very helpful.
best seafood tofu ever!

We were totally messed up because of their bad service. We arrived there after midnight yesterday I can't remember exact time. We waited about half an hour, and it was not bad because we knew it was rushed time. I had a flight schedule so I had to be  hurried. After we were seated, the meal was okay, but the service made us fully uncomfortable. We sat around the restroom but one guy told me that I had to use another one in down stairs, but he didn't explain why. That's uncomfortable. The servers didn't see if the customers need something at all. They just served food with frowned faces. That's it. Some customers had to be waited 20 minutes for asking just a glass of water.  Ridiculously, they put tips about 18% automatically without any notices or any explains. Anyway, we are not gonna visit that place again.
Great spot for Korean food! They are fast and delicious! Get their seafood tofu soup and their number 6 which is their bibimbap which also comes with soup. Their side dishes are also great!

Good dogs, good people, good location. Some creative menu choices put a nice spin on the traditional wiener. All of their tubesteaks are served on a real roll, not a cheap bun and are prepared just for you. I reccomend the classic coney as well as any variation of the mac and cheese dog. The owners are very courteous and always happy to see us return. They even give our friends dog a "Henry Dog" (no bun or toppings wrapped in foil). I really enjoy making The Dapper Dog a weekend stop when I am in the area. Also, keep an eye out for them around philly at different events, they are mobile.

Dapper Dog is amazing.  It is just what you need at 2AM when the bars are closed and you are hungry as hell.  The hot dogs are delicious.... my favorites are the Mac dog (a hot dog with delicious mac and cheese on top) as well as the Chicago dog with onions, mustard, peppers and a pickle spear.  The Coney Island dog with chili, peppers and cheese is also pretty damn good.

Great selection, and they're here for you after you stumble out onto 2nd street drunk as a skunk.  I may not have ever eaten at the Dapper Dog sober, but who cares? They're great. The guys that run the cart are pretty cute too.

visited this place yesterday afternoon for lunch..after a nite of drinking, idli-dosa with yum sambhar is just the tonic i needed. Buffet was decent, good mix of south indian dishes and some north indian too... Ordered plain dosa, which was ok...a little too small for my appetite, most south indian place have the huge paper dosa on the menu. of the folks in our group ordered buttermilk, which she was raving about. all in all, decent place for decent price, the dosas came quickly which was much appreciated by everyone famished by the afternoon time.
Great food and friendly service. Reminded me of some of the dishes my mother made for me when I was a child. Give this place a try.

My favorite place for takeout. I love the gyros and the ribs, they have so many great things on the menu. Love the souvlaki on the stick as well. The service is great as well. Food is always ready in about 10 to 15 minutes and I never have to wait at the counter when I pick it up.

After reading some reviews here on Yelp, apparently Marabella had been opened for months but I've only discovered it the week past. The store is so low key that one would hardly know there's such an establishment in the area unless one happens to look in that direction when walking on that particular sidewalk. Knowing there's a meatball establishment in my neck of wood, I've decided to try it out this past Sunday. Its interior is kinda a red and white sleek design with rustic wooden tables, playing vibey lounge music. All suggesting it to be a trendy spot, which is an awkwardly huge contrast with the older staff and supposedly homey food of the place. The matriarch figure of the place gave me and my boyfriend a detailed "tour" of the menu. Marabella is in fact meatball central. Four kinds of meatballs on long rolls, round rolls, sliders, on pastas, on crustinis... different kinds of sauces and cheeses, one could almost be confused and overwhelmed. But wanting to try them all, I've gotten the 3-sliders Morso deal and trying different cheeses, sauce and meatballs on each. The boyfriend has gotten a traditional chicken meatballs alfredo with gorgonzola, while the alfredo is creamy and I deeply enjoy the tanginess of gorgonzola, the flavor of the chicken meatballs were completely lost. The beef marinara is also quite generic even though the matriarch insisted that this is the right combination, I've never had Piave Vecchio before and it was good. The veggie meatballs are pretty good, good enough to satisfy any vegetarian, pairing up with tomato sauce and fontina gives it a nice bite. My favorite is the pork meatballs here, they are really nicely seasoned, I guess the pork fat perfumes the meat better, I also adore the creamy mushroom sauce, provolone is good but next time I'll try it with the piave vecchio since it seems to be the best cheese. With two bottles of beverage it comes to $26 for the two of us, price is a tiny, tiny bit on the high end but the service is quite friendly. I would love if they serve mac and cheese or some side dish like fries. A meatball place is great but I think it's just a sometimes food for me.

I ate here on a Saturday night while in Philly on biz.   It seems this place has been open for months... from the looks of the yelp reviews.  However, there was a remark on the chalkboard that made it look like the place had only been open a week.  ???  I was at this spot... Mid March 2011.  Beyond wondering how new this place is to the area.... I am sure I found this place to be an average place for dinner. The place is kinda cute... the staff was very helpful.   It has a nice vibe in the joint. As for the food... I started with a Caesar salad.  It had way too much dressing on it.  It was good but the leaves were swimming in dressing.   I then had a chicken meatball pasta dish.  The pasta was ok... nothing special... the chicken meatball was tasty but then again nothing I will remember a month from now.   Would I eat here again... sure.  Will I crave something from this spot?  No.

I have only had the dim sum at noodle chu.  I am a huge fan of dim sum but I've mostly had just mediocre dim sum in the US.  This restaurant is the same, mediocre dim sum but it will satisfy my cravings.   The service is typical for dim sum; not particularly warm nor friendly.  However, when I go for dim sum I'm not looking for 5-star service.

I accidentally stumbled upon this place late on valentines day. My bf at the time didn't even want to go inside, he said it reminded him of a nursing-home. I guess it was because most couples there were over 50 w/a few exceptions. I dragged him anyway. He was right in a sense, there is nothing glam, trendy or pretentious about this establishment. Instead, it is an old-fashioned french classic, warm, cozy and welcoming. We both walked out most impressed. Food is fantastic, regardless of your preference. It's been 7 years and I don't think I've ever had a bad meal. The owner/manager always greets us with a smile. I tend to see familiar faces every time I'm there and staff has not changed much, that says a lot about the way they run their business. Good bartender as well. Some of my favorites are; monk fish, mushroom or carrot/ginger soup, lobster risotto, tuna steak and seared scallops. The flour-less chocolate cake w/hazelnut ice cream takes about 20min but totally worth it. One of my favorite restaurants. I will continue coming here with my family and friends.

Bistro Les Amis was introduce to us by our niece who was graduating from NYU.   This place was amazing.  It was a crazy busy day and I just needed a place to unwind. I had a mint lemonade with a spike of vodka which was refreshing and a tuna nicoise. The tuna was cooked to perfection with a pepper coating.  Got to sit back and watch the sites.  Great place to people watch.  The waitress was sincere and funny.  Plus I got to practice my French.  Merci!
Best sandwiches. Thin chicken cutlets. Great margherita pie. Buffalo balls unreal. Pay 4 what u get. Good shizzle here.

Nice patio/setting area was very nice with many heaters. They even have outside speaker and TV (which was on ESPN). They have small dishes for antipasto, we ere able to choose combinations which was great since we were 3 of us and we got to try different things (we had rice ball, portebello mashroom topped with stuff - I had server choose 4) Overall good. Then we ordered some pasta dishes. I got lobster ravioli which was good. It has taste of real lobster. And others ordered some chicken and shrimp pasta dishes. Overall food was okay. We finished off with funnel fries with ice cream which was best part of the meal. Also server did us a favor, by given us half order of the desert since it was so large as whole order (he mentioned one order can serve 5-6 people and he was right half order was enough for 3). Services were okay. I believe manager came out couple times to greet people and had friendly conversations.

I HEART Gena's.  I should have reviewed her months ago, but after reuniting this afternoon on my lunch break I made a mental note to give up her overdue props.   While this isn't a place you're going to meet a friend(s) for lunch as there are like 2 tables and a small counter, it is IDEAL for takeout.  It's super quick, super inexpensive, and super delicious.  I've had the shrimp in garlic sauce, the tostones, the stewed chicken, and the yellow rice and beans here as well as the batido de papaya (YUM).  All of it has been delicious.  This is Latin American comfort food at it's best.  My go-to lunch is the stewed chicken with rice and beans washed down with the batido and it is beyond filling and less than $10.  SO damn good.  I love you Gena xoxo

Best deli in the area!  Service is great. Sandwiches are reasonably priced.  And they have a  ton of options. (too long to list).  They also have fresh whole wheat, multi grain and regular italian bread served daily.   You really can't go wrong with anything here. I recommend trying their homemade ravioli.  Enjoy!

I was so happy to hear of another new restaurant in the neighborhood and Humo didn't disappoint. Yes, they are new and still figuring our some stuff but, the pulled pork was amazing, as was the brisket and the sausage. Also loved the black beans. Their menu has a "Veggie" on it, but they were out when we went. I hope they start making veggies more regularly. It's a simple place, on the model of Fette Sau in Williamsburg, but simpler and without the hipter attitude. They were super duper nice. FYI, for now it's BYOB. And, they deliver!

I went here for the first time with a friend, and I have never gone to another soul food restaurant since then. When people are looking for a good place to eat i always recommend them here. It is the best soul food in New Haven. The ambiance is amazing and the staff is super friendly. Sabrina is AMAZING! She is so nice and is so accommodating. If you're looking for good food, a friendly staff and a nice environment this is where you need to go.

I order at least two times per month from Rice Bowl. The food is delicious. My wife likes the fried bean curd and broccoli. My children always want the cheese wonton. I enjoy the General Tso's chicken--it's whole, gigantic pieces of white chicken meat. The staff provides excellent service. The establishment is well kept. The price is affordable. I believe they can be more generous with the shrimp servings, otherwise this is my favorite Chinese food location in Central Jersey.

Our first visit was much more successful than this weekends.  There is a "grazing menu". Which is a tasting of various dishes.  You can choose 3, 4 or 5 (including a sweet course).  Prices ranging from $70-$120 per person.  The waiter informed us they were bigger than appetizer portions but smaller than dinner portions. We had a 7PM seating and they had already run out of 2 of the main protein options which were  closer to main dishes and we were left able to select smaller options, which were considered more as appetizers.  The waitron forgot to mention that those plates would be smaller and not as filling.  We ended up spending over $200 per couple and my wife and all guests were still quite hungry after the meal ended.  We did tell the manager and he did say that the waiter should have told us and should have known to recommend the larger 4 course tasting.... It's a relatively small restaurant with limited seating, so I am not sure how they ran out that quickly.  Poor planning on their part.  Also, the flavors of the dishes were not as good as I did recall. We were also quite disappointed that no one informed us of the closing if the wine store....  Luckily other couples brought wine but half the fun used to be having the ability to go into the wine store, tasting and selecting a new bottle to try with your meal. It could have been an off night because we did enjoy it so much the first time but the second visit was such a disappointment , especially for the price point.  I am not opposed to spending the money but this visit was way off of expectations. I believe this will be our last visit here.

Party of 6. Only 2 people spoke spanish, the rest of us had such a hard time. The waiter charged us for 4 sodas when we got 2. They charged $2 for Coke and $1.50 for Sprite. That's a joke right? Food in Passaic at Noches tastes better. You also get more for the money.  They also charged us a ridiculous 19% service charge on a dead Sunday night where they barely did anything, but mess up. Not coming back here, I'll go to Passaic.

Food = Great Price = Reasonable for the quality People = ... Hold on for a second, let me talk about the people who work here. Every single person I have ever encountered here, including the busboys (actually, ESPECIALLY the busboys) are INCREDIBLY friendly. Being that this is a self-serve restaurant, they really have no reason to interact with you as they're just taking trays and plates back to the kitchen -- but they THANK me for putting my tray up! They also continuously wipe down tables (I once spent about 8 hours there doing work and I lost count of how many times I saw them wiping down the tables). The people who serve you the food also give very generous portions, and sometimes sneak you an extra piece (or two) of the gluten free bread. I don't know if it's the food or what, but everyone here seems to actually not hate their jobs, which is rare to see in "fast food" Manhattan restaurants.

Breakfast- delicious mash bar (Banana, almond butter, cashew cream and kiwis), the coffee is good and they have homemade nut milks which are amazing to add into your bevs. As with any GF paleo place the prices are a bit high but when you want to indulge in a healthy start to your day, its the only choice really. Lunch- havent tried it yet but the menu is varied but you can also grab a pre-made side or salad when you pick up your breakfast. ie: Kale, chickpeas, quinoa etc

Damn I like this place! Love how simple yet delicious everything is and totally guilt free. I've eaten at a lot of breakfast/brunch places in NYC and have tried many of their "healthy" dishes, but NOTHING has been as satisfying as this place. The Burritos are HUGE and so filling, but all the ingredients are so healthy and tasty. And best of all, they deliver...and quick!!! Bravo! NYC needs this!!!

Spent $11.50 on a 1/4 organic roasted chicken and a generous side of broccoli for dinner tonight. I was frugal so I opted for no drink.While it may sound a little pricey for a pay then sit establishment, I thought it was worth it, especially since Hu is on Fifth Ave bw 13/14th. Pros: -Healthy variety -Actual plates and silverware, and the cashier offered me a glass (not plastic) for filtered serve yourself water -Ample seating, stylish decor and dim lightning. Nice ambiance -Staff was very polite and kept the place tidy Cons: -none that i spotted this time around

You have an appetite like a raven and this is the place.Goat biriyani - I eat till the last grain.Their service especially through Victor is phenomenal,he pays personal attention to your tastes.Buffet spread is also worth the try for the price they offer.

I have been going to Indian Hut for some time now. I am really impressed with the breads here like Keema Naan. I also never had Indian Chinese food before coming here. The Gobi Manchurian and Chicken Manchurian are sublime.

Went with my wife for our anniversary on 7/25/14 and the shrimp, scallops and lobster with cappellini special was so good that I ordered and ate two of them!! The server had a great personality as well!! We will be going back!!

I just can't say anything bad about this way cool joint!  The drinks are so hot, you'll want to try them all - yikes!  The small plates of food are absolutely divine!  I nearly fell over backwards for the deviled eggs!  If you are feeling light and airy, hang out upstairs and enjoy the setting sun and BillyBurg street vibe.  Feeling dark and sexy?  Wander downstairs to blend into the shadows while surrounded by stunning peeps.  You will not be disappointed.  It's even worth the trip over the Willy B Bridge!

Went for a drink late on Saturday night with a couple of friends. Had a very chill, sophisticated, but not pretentious vibe (unlike some other wine bars). The bartenders and staff were very friendly and knowledgeable about wine and beer.  The space downstairs looked like a good place to get cozy with a date, but I sat at one of the large tables in the main room, where we enjoyed our beers.   I believe there was music in the background, but it was nice to go someplace where you can talk to people without shouting. Since I already ate, I did not try any of the food, which I must do next time. Definitely, a welcome addition to the neighborhood and B-burg bar/restaurant scene.

I was so impressed with this place that I broke down and signed up for Yelp. I don't head to Williamsburg often, but will be coming back here. This place was well-executed from the menu to the design. Open airy corner space w/tables on ground level and a spacious downstairs bar. Could be great for a large group or party. I spent a few hours downstairs on Thursday - all the cocktails that I tried were delicious and the bartender was very helpful attentive and friendly. He could tell what you liked and was able to improvise some off-the-menu cocktails. They also had a quality playlist going. Didn't really try the food except for the croutons (which were great), but will be back to get through the menu. I was surprised there weren't more people there on a Thursday night, but this place will become more popular through the summer as word gets out.
Nice place, good atmosphere, beer selection, cocktails and food. Truly abysmal service - we were ignored by waitress, order forgotten.
The food was awesome.  I had a grilled chicken with mango chutney on a chibatta roll.  So delicious.

I've had salads from many places but this is definitely up there and although a bit much, worth the money. The portion is generous and the ingredients taste insanely fresh. I ordered their cranberry quinoa salad with chicken and added avocado- it was on point! I came across it when doing a search for good sandwich places in midtown east, so was not expecting them to also have good salads. Definitely plan on going back to try one of their sandwiches!

Kimchee Burger wasn't as good as expected!The Meat was well done instead of medium! It is just some a little Portion of Bulgogi beef wirhout a lot of flavour and some kimchee...pretty dry Burger! The Classic Burger was much better and fresher!
Best place in Ny!! Love it! Especially they have special meatball that we came for it! Owners are so friendly i definetly recommend this place!

I just made a reservation here for New Year Eve, I have been impressed with my previous dining experiences. This is a nice place suited for celebrations and romantic evenings out or any time you want to treat yourself. The food is incredible and beautifully presented. I feel comfortable ordering pretty much anything off the menu and knowing it will be well prepared. The portions are reasonably sized so you get to enjoy multiple courses without feeling overly full. I ordered venison, the special for the night, and my friend ordered salmon. Venison came with black trumpet mushrooms which were out of this world good. Salmon was moist with a crispy skin, with a side of roasted beet salad that really captures the sweetness of beets. The wine we had was also incredibly and I will be ordering it again.
Always friendly, excellent servers, fresh seasonal locally grown veggies and locally procured meats, beautiful atmosphere, and not terribly expensive.  What's not to love?

This was by far the greatest experience I had ever had in a restaurant.  Not only was the food perfectly prepared, but the service was above and beyond.   My wife had brought my for my birthday and we had planned our trip to Brooklyn around eating here.  We arrived early and enjoyed a few drinks on the rooftop deck which has great ambiance.  The drink prices were inline for NY and the though the drink menu is limited upstairs, the addition of the Orleans Slushie made up for that. It was a warm day in Brooklyn so the slushie was the perfect relief for the heat.   When we arrived to eat in the dinning room, we received perfect service and everything we ordered was explained to us and then brought out one plate at a time.  We started off with the Broccoli which paired the heat from the chili and the subtle malt vinegar flavor perfectly and it was a fresh take on boring old broccoli.   Next we went onto the Grilled Shishitos, which while we weren't sure what we getting into we were very excited once we had them in front of us.  Again there was the perfect blend of heat and flavor on the shishitos and the portion was again perfect for two.   The third plate we shared was the Pickled Mussels. We were both intrigued into how this would taste as we had not had mussels prepared like this before.  The flavor again was again perfect and the proportions great for sharing.   Finally we rounded out our parade of shared dinner plates with the Hanger Steak and Mad Onions.  The steak was perfectly cooked and the being cooked over the wood-fire grill gave it a distinct flavor that pared perfectly with the "mad onions." The onions which are a variety of onions prepared in different ways, give the steak a perfect group of companions. After those four dishes we weren't overly full and had we not had tickets to see a show in the city, we could have stayed their for hours trying everything on the menu.  But we did squeeze in one final dish from the "Sweet" section of the menu.  We had the Sticky Toffee Pudding with ice cream.   Again the flavor was perfect and the proportions were perfect to share. To top off the night, I was able to meet Ilan Hall who was not only very polite but you could tell that the positive energy that the staff had starts with him.   If you are in Brooklyn or even just a subway ride away from Brooklyn I would highly recommend that you stop by The Gorbals.
