You could either sit on the rooftop deck of grab a romantic dinner. While you might feel a bit weird eating in a restaurant in the middle of an Urban Outfitters, do not judge this book by the cover. As soon as you sit down you will forget that you are in the middle of New York and you will feel welcomed by this great staff and served the best food in NY.

OK GUYS, This is rare. 5 stars, this is simply because the food is amazing. So amazing, I went on Friday, told some other friends about it, so they wanted me to go with them a few days later. First of all, sitting in the restaurant it feels like you are in a pop-up.  You can see the store through cracks, its a little weird, but forgotten as soon as you start eating.  I was surprised that both times I dined here it was not packed.  I suggest going with at least 3 more people so you can have a little bit of EVERYTHING. What I ate: First Time around: Broccoli, soy, chilis - idk if its grilled or broiled or what but its light and fluffy and tangy, this is amazing. LOVE Lamb ribs - this is super fatty, tender and delicious, the candied ginger is definitely a special treat....i also ate this the 2nd time around Banh mi poutine - O M GAH. so good we ordered two rounds this time, and again the second time i came.  the pulled meat, and sauce on top of fries. DEAD. WHOLE ROASTED PIGS HEAD - it says its for 2. they lie. we were a group of 4. it was so much. so good, meaty, fatty, roasted. Gribenes - OK. HOW DO YOU PRONOUNCE this word?  however it is, its like their take on a BLT but the gribenes is fried chicken skin.  do i need to say more? Matzoh balls - i dont remember eating this...so i guess it was ok? Mussels - this was good, the sauce was light not too heavy. Sticky toffee pudding - no comment. this was weird. had to return it.  i think this should be warm?   OK 2nd time around - Broccoli again... Lamb ribs....again... Banh mi poutine....again Corn with smoked butter - this was good, but not a corn fan period. Grilled shishitos - they said this was extra spicy. its not. its really really good, i think the peppers should be a little more grilled. but it was great anyway. Falafel crusted veal sweetbread - SO SO SO good. i still dont get what a sweetbread is, because i couldnt hear the server explain. but it was amazing. Beef marrow - SO FATTY. SO GOOD. MARROW? HELLO! Lamb neck - so they said this takes about 45mins to prep. it didnt. its so tender, and it looks like it would be very rich in flavor.  its not. its just right. AMAZING. Octopus - this is a whole leg or arm ....OH TENTACLE?  grilled, the sauce with pinenuts didnt really do anything for me.  but it was fresh, and cooked perfectly. Chicken schnitzel - i was extremely full when this came out....so i cant really describe it. i had a bite. it was good. Brownie with caramelized onions - sounds weird?  extremely amazing.  its perfect because i'm not a sweet person but the onions on it were perfect. OK - so i basically almost had the whole menu.  And I sound like a fatass.... I hope more people come here because i'd like to see it stay open....i'll be back soon after i FAST for a month. HIGH FIVE TO THE CHEF. and another high five for your playlist.

The staff was rude, condescending, and obnoxious.  The food was marginal at best, but The Gorbals has questionable standards in cleanliness.  It was filthy.  I would NEVER recommend this establishment to my worst enemy.

I was skeptical about eating in an urban outfitters and the fact that the sign is barely visible almost had me miss this place all together. Im glad i didn't. After we were promptly seated and poured our water, we were told the chef recommended sharing. We complied. Our server was extremely knowledgable about the menu and was able to answer all the questions we fired at him. The first item we had was the fermented celery broth. sounds strange, but the flavors totally work. Although i thought the dish was missing something (couldn't put my finger on it), i would recommend it. Next was the bacon wrapped matzoh balls. A must order. They were better than my grandmothers, but then again, she wouldn't wrap hers in bacon. After that we had the beef tongue. This blew my mind. The tongue was melt in your mouth tender, the tomato romesco sauce tangy, and the croutons crunchy and citrus-y. I debated to my self if i would come back alone the next day to have it again. For our final course, we had the lamb neck with risotto oats. Although the portion size was huge, we could not finish it, and it was quite a heavy dish, it was impeccably cooked. The oats were super creamy, and the finish of mint added the slight lightness it need to not be too heavy. We liked everything so much, we decided to truck through one dessert. We opted for the chocolate brownie with onions. Although strange (my two companions enjoyed it more then i did), it was good. The stand out being the charred scallion ice cream. In short: Great service, great cocktails, great food. Highly recommended. Im glad this was my first Yelp review

Whoa!!! I mean whoa I had a sandwich from here and it was pretty tasty but today I tried the grits!  WOW! Idk if they put cocaine in the grits lol but I finished them before I left the block and had to talk myself out of going back for more.  Easily top 2 best grits I have ever tasted in my life and I have had lots of grits.

I had dinner here recently and woke up the next morning fondly recalling one of the best dining experiences of my life. The seafood entrees, including the hamachi crudo and tuna pica, are incredibly flavorful. Braised octopus, a cooked dish in this den of raw seafood, is a particular standout. Both the cocktails and wines pair extraordinarily well with the seafood. The vegetarian dishes I tried, including the kale panzanella and a expertly plated grilled mushroom dish, are as unique as the seafood. My vegetarian guest felt there were a multitude of options to choose from. Getting there from Manhattan was quick and painless. This restaurant is sure to become a destination.

I dined here with a friend recently and am very impressed.  I am a big fan of raw fish and had a hard time deciding what to order.  I went with the fluke, himachi, and salmon.  The razor clams were awesome...as well as the grilled mushrooms!  Once I tasted the mushrooms..I did not want to share anymore.  There was not a morsel left. We ordered one of the "toasts" as an appetizer. i didn't know what to expect from a cauliflower toast..but it was really, really good. The cocktails are unique and strong...and there are many to choose from.  I went with the Agave Orchard (a tequila cocktail. strong!).  Atmosphere is cozy and I enjoyed the background music.  I will definitely go back again soon.

This restaurant was nothing like what I assumed it would be from the outside. Quasi-sushi type small plates and nice cocktails in a wood and tile atmosphere. It's somewhat hard to describe. I'm not doing it justice. The drinks are nice, but the seafood out shines everything. The flavor combinations are innovative and delicious. As others have mentioned, the fluke is wonderful. My personal favorite was the octopus--not even a hint of chewy, just so meaty and tender. I cannot wait to come back. This is a hidden gem.

I went to Bergen Hill and found the Char No. 8 to be my favorite cocktail bar none.  It pairs great with my personal favorite, the hamachi, although some prefer it with the octopus or the hen of the woods mushroom dish.  The service was impeccable, and that sealed the deal for my return.  I felt that it was a welcome reprieve from what I was used to when it comes to cocktail bars.  Likewise, I noticed the ample terrace space and couldn't help but think that it will be a great place to enjoy on a balmy summer evening.
Great place to spot after a workout in Kelly drive!!!! You can park your bike and enjoy a nice meal!!

We absolutely LOVED In Riva! Everything was excellent. Food was super flavorful and a lot of knowledge and passion went into it. Our server was terrific. The atmosphere was fun (we sat outside on the patio on a Saturday night). The bartender at the outside bar made an excellent Mojito. I told him lower on the syrup and he nailed it. Highly recommend this place. You wont be let down. I look forward to going again soon. Great job to everyone here.
We use Sandwich Theory for our firm luncheons and their food is always delicious! You have to try their potato salad...YUM!!!!

I've been to The Pines a few times and it's always been great. The food is outstanding and so creative. The staff are super friendly and nice and can answer any questions you have about the menus. The bar is a nice spot to sit and eat or get a drink. The atmosphere is chill and casual and the decor is perfectly Brooklyn. I love that you can see the kitchen. I would definitely recommend!

4.5, but I'm rounding up.  My wife and I went to the Pines in summer of this year and were really impressed.  I remember having an uni dish with puffed amaranth, a wagyu steak with kimchi, and a foie gras dish.  The portions are incredibly generous, beautifully plated, and creative.  We just went again last night and I feel compelled to write a review as it was better than our first visit.  The service was warm and friendly and the food was some of the best I've had in recent months--and we are avid foodies.  Although our waiter suggested five plates, three or four probably would have sufficed.  We started with the bread and cultured butter which came with about five large hunks of bread and a generous pat of delicious butter, that almost had a cheesy quality to it.  Next was braised cabbaged, boar belly, delicious maitake mushrooms, and a scallion cream.  Beautiful, gorgeous, and inspired.  Maybe a bit on the salty side, but the dish was absolutely pure bliss!  Then we had the crispy veal sweetbreads, honey mushrooms, escarole, and butternut squash cream.  So good.  The ingredients are treated with such care and finesse, the final product is so wonderful.  We ended with the agnolotti filled with ricotta and parsnip, in a broth of its own whey, topped with black truffles.  Such a subtle dish--the creamy sweet ricotta paired with teh sourness of the whey was wonderful.  The five dishes, with a glass of wine, at $110.  Seriously, not bad at all considering the quality and quantity they give you.  We hope to be back sooner rather than later.

I took my brother here for his birthday two years in a row and both times it was an amazing experience.  The vibe and décor are unpretentious and inviting.  The wait staff is attentive and friendly as well, and the bartenders are some of my favorite around.  They know the food and the menu, and make a captivating assortment of delicious drinks. Oh and did I mention that the food is incredible?  I love that the menu changes often so I can always look forward to a new exciting dish when I come, accompanied by some of my favorite staples.  Everything was extremely well seasoned throughout our entire meal, and we ate a nice variety of vegetables, protein, and desserts.  The cabbage dish blew me away.  Who knew a plate of cabbage, mushrooms, and cauliflower could taste so good?  You can really taste the love that goes into their house made pasta, and it's always accompanied by original, interesting ingredients. The bread is delicious as well and the desserts really push the envelope, in a good way.  They make you think twice about combining sweet and savory flavors, and somehow they always make it work.  You are left wondering how something that sounds so out of the box, tastes so amazing! By the end of both my meals, I left feeling happy, full, and excited to return again in the near future.

I never write reviews, but my wife and I had such amazing food here I had to take the time to do so.  From our well crafted and unique cocktails and every beautiful plate that was brought out to us, each item wonderfully delicious.  We loved it so much that it was the first place we both thought of when we picked a place for a Valentine's day dinner.  I highly recommend The Pines for a date or dinner with friends or family.

This is the second time that I've been here and I'm going to keep coming back cause I haven't tried everything on the menu yet.  The food is incredibly playful, mixing ingredients I would never imagine to pair together and it works really, really well.  I wish there was more vegetarian stuff for my friend, but the waiter made it possible to make some of the dishes vegetarian and still tasted great.  The service was knowledgable and nice.  Not stuffy at all.  The food seems like it should be in a stuffy restaurant, but it's in a comfortable wooden setting with friendly servers having a good time with you.  My only complaint was a lot of ice cream for dessert in the dead of winter.  Not interested in ice cream in the dead of winter.  Other than that, 5 stars, easy.

Wow! Where am I eating dinner...Gowanus?!? I was so pleasantly surprised with the food and service in this hidden gem in Brooklyn. Admittedly, I went there only after ignoring the hype of friends who had gone before me and raved about the food. Finally, I needed to go for myself and I was AMAZED! My cocktail was expertly prepared by a very friendly bartender who I had mistakenly called Phil all night due to the blasting hip hop music. Volume withstanding the drink, the Quincy's Jam, was delicious with a touch of tart and plenty of booze. It is served in a vintage coupe glass that made me feel like I had traveled through time to the days when a bartender cared about his customer and did not try to rush dinner to get the next table seated.  For the record the bartender's name was Will and he is very very easy on the eyes! Onto dinner, after handsome Will thoroughly explained the menu items and ingredients, I was drooling and ready to gorge on everything! I settled on the bread which was a medley of fresh baked wheat baguette, seeded brioche, and some type of Italian deliciousness I can't remember-all served with this blend of cheese and butter. CHEESE AND BUTTER people and it was so good I nearly ate the entire batch alone. Next, I had a Sweet Potato plate with Brussels sprouts and pork fat with a touch of buttercream. The perfect sweet and savory combination. Oh I just remembered the bread had an olive oil drizzle and sea salt sprinkle...so tasty! Lastly, Will recommended the Duck Cappalacchi. I am positive I misspelled this dish but it is a delicious dumpling like pasta stuffed with braised duck meat in a scrumptious broth topped with mustard greens. Hands down the best meal I have had in Brooklyn by far, including Williamsburg-for all the food snobs out there on YELP, there is better food in BK than Wburg. My only regret was I did not save room for dessert. I saw a couple of gelato looking desserts pass my way, but after 3 drinks and a million questions about the menu, it was time for me to go. In sum, check this place out if you want a delicious meal, superior service, and some eye candy while you digest your meal. Better yet go there if you are tired of rude waiters or overcrowded small spaces and want an exquisite dining experience. One more shout out to the host or manager, Anthony, for providing me with a space to have dinner without a reservation. He was very accommodating and another piece of eye candy!

I went here for Brunch when it first started and I must say the food was excellent. I ended up getting the Chorizo and the eggs. The Chorizo was just what I needed to hit the spot. I ended up taking the rest of my eggs home because I couldn't finish everything, but that tasted great as a leftover. I would recommend the bloody mary. It's hand made and has a nice kick to it to start your day.

My friends and I came in on Friday night and had the best dining experience we had in a long time! They sat us right away and quickly brought us bread to start that was delicious! The service was incredible, we started with appetizers (muscles, arugula salad, Cesar salad) and everyone was raving about their food. The timing was perfect and as soon as we finished they took our plates and brought out delicious meals! The grilled chicken with tomato pesto, palenta, and brussel sprouts was incredible as was the mahi mahi and the penne alla vodka! I can't say enough about the exceptional service and delicious authentic food! The ambience was perfect and made us feel like we were right at home with our family and friends! We all can't wait to come back! Thank you for the best dining experience! Also it's a BYOB and our dinner was so affordable! A must visit!

It's a tiny little gem. About $20/entree... Frikkin delish. They had quite a few specials for the evening and I chose to start with one of the salad specials. It was definitely large enough to share with another person because they also bring out bread and oil. I had the lobster ravioli and was pleased that the pasta was al dente and there was enough lobster inside that I actually had to chew. Really good. A bit oily but very flavorful. My date had the eggplant & ricotta penne. Again perfectly cooked pasta. Great flavor. We both had leftovers so I'd say portion size is adequate for even a big eater. Service was terrific (and easy on the eyes). They leave you be and allow you to enjoy your meal, wine, and company. Can't wait to take some friends and try more dishes. Larger groups will likely need reservations as this place is small.
Impressive!  Small and old world. Reminds me of the restaurants in the north end of Boston.

Excellent red sangria.  The white, not so good.   Try the shrimp, bacon and avocado arepa (La Fresquita).  The octopus one and the veggie are excellent too. Stay away from the greasy empanadas.  Very friendly Dominican waitress.

Guayoyo has the best cachapa I've had outside of the heavily Venezuelan neighborhood of Doral in Miami. The service was fantastic and friendly, the brunch menu is delicious and reasonable, and the mango juice was just beautiful. Since moving to the neighborhood this is my first and favorite brunch spot.
One of my favorite local spots. Arepas are amazing here. Along with some guac and sangria and I'm a very happy camper.
The arepas are amazing, as are the empanadas. The happy hour special is pretty good. The wait staff is friendly and the service is good. Everything is very reasonably priced.

Bruno's is in a strip mall off of 46 a short distance after the Paterson exits, so if you don't keep an eye out you might miss it; it is towards the eastern side of that mall.  I sure did!  Inside it is rather dumpy with a diner-bar setup and booths in front with more seating in the back.  There is a waitress here that won an award for being the best pizzeria waitress in NJ, but I did not get to meet her (poor me).  They have a full menu, but by popular consensus the Sicilian slice is the thing to get here: it is consistently rated as one of the best in NJ, often compared to a place named Mr. Bruno's in Lyndhurst--no relation that I am aware of.   The Sicilian slice I got was very big and heavy.  It was also cheap at only $2!  Because of its size, it reheated awkwardly at best.  Part of my slice didn't rise very well, which left half of it to get that great fried dough texture--the hallmark of a good sicilian--and the other half to be a sloppy messy under the weight of the toppings.  The tomato sauce was aggresively herbed, but the tomatoes they used were good enough that they held up; it was  a bit sweet though.  Mozzarella was used sparingly, which i appreciated.  All said this was a very aggressive, unbalanced slice that packed good flavor, but didn't really live up to its reputation.  I can definitely see why people love it though.   If I'm in the area again and I don't want to hit Pizzatown USA for some reason--ie: I get into a fight with one of the sisters--then I'll give this another shot.  But for me, Mr. Bruno's in Lyndhurst wins the battle of the NJ sicilians hands down here.

The pizza is good, but the owner's attitude sucks!  I was rushing tonight and when i left the restaurant I  forgot my pie.  We went shopping and when I called back he said he had just thrown it out.  I asked for another and he told me to forget about it!  I fussed and then he agreed to give me singles that he had lying around.  He tossed loose singles in a dirty pizza box and threw slices of cold pepperoni on the slices.   We will never go back!  I will suggest that our school orders pizza from someone else and with all of the good pizzerias in Jersey, you need to have an owner with a positive attitude.
We had such a great time! The place has a ton of character and if you are lucky to sit by the bar, the man behind was very knowledgable and friendly. I would definitely go back.

Really small and a bit hard to find- great for a one on one catchup meal or drinks. The octopus dish is DELICIOUS. Kale and squash risotto was very good as well. Some dishes (kale, pork belly) are too salty. Overall, great vibe and excellent food. Because it is so small, I would not recommend more than two people at a time.

To sum it up: excellent food, great beer selection (and prices!) and HORRIBLY SLOW service. I came to Race Street Cafe last Wednesday as part of a group of 8 people around 7PM. We were celebrating my friend's birthday. It was not busy at all when we sat down, maybe 3 other tables were occupied, all 2 tops. The server, a young lady, greeted us promptly upon sitting down and took some drink orders. When I saw how long it took for the drinks to come, I knew we were in trouble. When she finally came back to take food orders, I ordered the gazpacho to start, the po' boy and a spanish burger for my husband. Someone please tell me why it would take 18 minutes (I was timing) for a gazpacho to come out?? It's freakin' gazpacho! Anyway, my frustration quicly dwindled when I tasted it. It was really delicious- bright and acidic with a silky mouthfeel, but still chunky enough to satisfy. About a year later, our entrees came out, except for one member of our party who's order the server admittedly forgot about. The food was definitely excellent. I could tell that the po' boy I ate was a very well thought out sandwich. I loved the contrast of the shrimp and the crabmeat salad, the crunch of the cornmeal breading, the subtle, pleasant heat of the chipotle sauce and the refreshing crunch of the lettuce. I was in heaven for the entire 3 minutes it took to scarf it down. I also had a bite of hubby's spanish burger, which was also very good. My only concern was that I felt that the onions got a little lost in the sandwich, probably overpowered by the jalapenos and maybe even the chorizo. I think throwing a couple more on there would solve that problem. The server never once came over to our table to ask how we were enjoying our meals, and was not very apologetic about forgetting my friend's order. She didn't even offer to comp it, even though he had to wait another half hour to receive his food. The beer selection was also quite impressive. I'm a bit of a connoisseur and was still able to find beers that I hadn't tried yet, all at an average price of $4. Overall, I'd say the dining experience was good, except for the service. I mean, I usually don't complain about this, but it was downright terrible. Just God awful. I may not return because of this. The one thing that baffles me is that I see countless reviews complaining of the service, and no changes have been made. It's like the owner of this establishment is intentionally trying to take a good thing and run it into the ground. Race Street Cafe owner(s): Do something about the service in your restaurant or you will not have customers to serve!

I walked in here early on a weekend evening with a group of four.  There were two high tops available and one regular table available, but the latter was overrun by another larger group sitting next to it and was not an option for us.  The two high tops were next to each other, so my group pushed them together.  We were brashly informed that it was against the restaurant policy to do so, even though we were not blocking any aisles and would have been, in fact, freeing up central floor space for wait staff to maneuver.  We were not given any logic behind the decision, but the bartender was insistent.  As one member of my party was expecting and we could not wait for a proper table to free up, we were forced to leave, and the restaurant lost the sale.  It is a shame, because I had been so looking forward to trying their great draft selection and sampling their food upon others' recommendations, but instead now, they have lost a customer due to poor customer service--which seems to be a recurring theme on other Yelp reviews.  What a shame, but perhaps I have been saved an overall negative experience by only scratching the surface of the staff's personality.

I've been to Race Street on multiple occasions and never once had an issue with the service, food or drinks.  Every time I go I always find something new on the menu that I love!  When available I would recommend the Shepards Pie.  The best in Olde City!!! As for the previous reviews regarding service, I find this hard to believe.  Unlike other restaurants I've been too in the city, the servers at Race Street have always been attentive to us.
Race Street Cafe is a great place to mingle and eat great food with friends. The staff is friendly and the food is fantastic.

Just spent the week in Princeton for a conference...ate lunch at Nassau Seafood EVERY DAY!! Had each of the following; Shrimp Po Boy, Oyster Po Boy, Firecracker Shrimp w/chips, Fish Tacos, Ceviche Taco, Shrimp Taco and Oyster Po Boy again...all of it fantastic! DO NOT be discouraged by the modest appearance, but DO get the cornbread for a side Wish they had a 30 star rating, this place would get it from me.
consistently delicious

It seems like they might be sensitive about how long their food prep takes, but this place is so much better than every other Middle Eastern option in the neighborhood... Everything from the falafel to the fatoush salad to the hummus to the french fries to the juice is great--this is really a fail-safe place to frequent if you live or work nearby.

i heared so many good things about this place and i couldn`t believe it till i had my own experience and my friends were right,the food is delicious,also i liked so much the restaurant atmosphere  and how  everything  is sparkling clean.i definitely will go back.

On my way home and craving sushi, I Googled my Droid to see where Glastonbury's Japanese restaurants were and wound up here. It was a Sunday afternoon and I sat at the sushi bar. The chef was very friendly. The sushi was really delicious; I had a special spicy tuna roll. I would definitely go back and hope to have the same experience. I felt very welcomed.
Super Clean, casual and fun. They have great coffee and sandwiches. A must if you are in Greenpoint.
Aside from the staff and owner being extremely helpful and friendly, ETC's cappuccino and delicious selection of sandwiches keep me coming back for more.
I agree that this place is a great addition to the neighborhood. The coffee is good, the decor is great, and the sandwiches and soups are great - simple, fresh, and not over the top.

Sushi Village is actually the same thing as Sushi Palace and holds the exact same menu.  Environment is kind of cute, completely unassuming if you're looking in from outside.   Prices are perfect at only $21pp on weekends.  That's just incredibly hard to beat for AYCE sushi and appetizers.  Our favorites were: Appetizer Favorites - Grilled Squid - Calamari - Salmon Teriyaki - Spicy Seaweed Salad Sushi Menu Favorites - Dragon Roll - Passaic - Shrimp Tempura - Soft Shell Crab - Eel Sushi The salmon sushi was iffy in terms of freshness.  Some pieces were great, but then others were not fresh at all.  Avoid the white tuna from this location.   Parking is readily available and they do have a private lot.  Staff isn't overly helpful, but majority of the interaction happens between you and the paper and pen for ordering.

Lunch AYCE is half the price of dinner for a couple of reasons: - Absolutely NO sashimi or sushi available - just some hot kitchen items and rolls - No AYCE ice cream Aside from that, we were majorly disappointed with this Sushi Village for a couple of reasons. - Average rolls (spicy tuna lacked tempura flakes, very mushy, average fish quality) - Majorly under-staffed - ONE waitress and 1 waiter/manager during prime lunch hours - Incomplete AYCE request - we had to ask three times  for a bowl of miso soup. Mushroom soup and another hot kitchen order never came. We waited another 20 mins for them to finally bring us our complete order - Tea was never refilled - Once service got busy, we never got our complimentary dessert (two tiny wedges of orange which we saw served to other tables) Not coming back here again. At least, not for lunch.

Went the other night during the Soft Opening and had a great chopped salad, a white pie with sliced tomatoes and basil and a red pie with mushroom and sausage. We discovered the great tasting cheese is from Liuzzis (keeping it local makes me a fan) and the sauce is the same as the Brooklyn recipe. The crust was not too too thick and not too too thin- That's all I'm saying about the dough. The white pie was very good. The red was also good but I expect things to improve as the feedback comes in.  The slices are large on purpose that's their style. There will be some that say it doesn't compare to New Haven pizza and it shouldn't --the Grimaldi's are famous in Brooklyn and opening up here is a good game changer to the pizza "wars". There are a large number (something like thousands and thousands) of pizza places in New Haven County and some are great and some are not so great-everyone likes their pizza a certain way but you may like this pie for a change of pace from the Wooster St./Crown St./State St. gangs. The owner/partners were there and personally introduced themselves to everyone-offered FREE desserts and espressos (My husband and I were most impressed-The cannolis were BETTER than any cannoli I've had in a LONG, LONG time (and I have family that worked at two fairly famous pastry/ bakeries in New Haven area) Teramisu could have had a little more flavor-but all in all very good "dulce" offerings to complete the meal! The Server was Samantha and she was great! Oh, and a good wine selection from the bar area-Place was packing them in so I hope for a long history in Woodbridge for this Abeetza Place!
Pizza OK, but at $22 for a small w/ 2 toppings, overpriced for the product. I'll stick w/ the usual on Wooster St
Excited to have another alternative to all the new haven style pizza places in this area. Excellent crisp but airy crust and fresh mozz.

Yummmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm The rosemary chicken wings could cure polio The pizza is definitely worth the trip and the tomato sauce had the perfect amount of sweetness For stamford folks, this is an absolute gem and I highly highly highly recommend

Montana's reminds me of Disneyland, Cracker barrel and TGIF - Generically birthed with a heavy dose of gentrification and pretension. The atmosphere is played out and predictable - corny stuff like taxidermy and americana that looks like a stylist picked it out.  Aesthetic aside, the food we had was barely passable, unambitious, small portioned, and too expensive. The $18 fried chicken was two bland pieces of meat and a handful of kale. The thimble full of sauce on the side reminded me of the familiar reddish goo that comes with spring rolls at any take out place. My friend had the brisket - it tasted ok but was very tiny and the edible meat portion was dwarfed by hunks of fat (for $23).  We spent about a $100 with tip, and left wondering what the hell had happened in there. The experience was surreal and sad.
horribly over priced food

Favorite restaurant in Brooklyn. Top 5 favorites in all of NYC. The fried chicken is served perfectly scolding hot, crispy, seasoned amazingly. The potatoes are next level. The Grits are perfect. Mustard Greens A+++ The Brisket was not like anything i've ever tasted before. I didn't even need a knife to get into it. The service was insane. Super friendly, fast, helpful. I honestly couldn't believe how awesome our waitress was. We ended up trying every cocktail on the menu and couldn't say one bad thing about a single one. Everything is fresh and original  - food - drinks - wait staff - atmosphere. You name it it was perfect. I can't even wait to go back. I want to have my birthday here.

I've lived in NYC since January and finally found a restaurant compares with my favorites in LA. Everything was superb. I love this style of food, classic but with flavors that make me forget I've ever had the dish before. We ordered the fried chicken veggie plate, mussels, and brisket. Everything was excellent. I loved that the veggies were full of wonder even though we bought them as the healthy counterpart to our duck fat and butter laden other dishes. Also, try the switchel cocktail if you like ginger and sour things. Oh my god so good. I was floored by how original and delightful this place is. Beautiful environment, service and impeccable food.
get a flight of bud

The food is excellent and the staff is very friendly.  I've eaten in the restaurant a couple of times, but mostly get take-out.  The food has always been fresh and I always get greeted warmly when I go in to pick up my order.   Love their garlic naan.  Try their mutter panir.  The cheese just melts in your mouth. The atmosphere in the restaurant is great.  I took a friend there once for lunch and she loved it too.  Said it was the best Indian food she had tasted in the area. I highly recommend it.

My wife and I have eaten here several times and I also regularly meet a friend for lunch at Cross Culture. The food is always excellent, service top notch, and the atmosphere quite pleasant. Let's start with lunch. Cross Culture does not have a buffet, but the lunch specials menu absolutely makes up for it. Choose basically any entree you want (even if it's not on the list) and it is served with unlimited rice, dal, and naan. Also included for an appetizer are pakoras which are excellent. Lunches average around $12 and for what you get it's a bargain. Dinner is excellent as well. We're not new to Indian cuisine and even if something is not on the menu the staff are more than willing to accommodate. I would classify the prices as more than fair for the portion size. The food is top notch, well seasoned, and extremely fresh. The biggest positive  about Cross Culture food is the consistency. Unlike many other Indian restaurants in the area, this one does not suffer from the constant change of chefs and kitchen staff. The food is always spot on and has been great from the first time we went. Been visiting regularly for about a year and a half and it's just great every time. The owner is a very nice guy and really gets involved and engages the customers. Overall, we love Cross Culture and highly recommend.

Very good indian food for an awesoome price. We tried the chicken tikka masala, lamb curry and two other chicken and lamb dishes. I can't remember the names. The rice was perfectly cooked and the Naan bread was excellent! I would go back again for sure.

This review is for the breakfast - it's pretty simple with large portions of egg, toast, or oatmeal, whatever you order. It will definitely keep you full throughout the morning. I'd give it a higher rating due to the great affordability and friendly service, but there's really nothing special about the food (spinach omelet) itself.

This local "hole in the wall" was a three block or so walk from the Marriott. They were open early on a Saturday so it was an easy choice. Nothing fancy here. You order at the counter and then have a seat. Plastic knives and forks. But for $7.77 I got more than I could eat and it was pretty darn good. Two eggs with chess, three BIG strips of turkey bacon, rye toast, GRITS, and milk. Can't beat that. Highly recommend.

Eh, overrated. Well, to be honest, we only had two things..the jalapeño and deviled egg starters. Not really a fan, but it does have potential. They are really creative with their ingredients, which I really respect, but it didn't really come together for me. The back patio was super cute and I do wish them luck. It just didn't pop for me.

Ladies and gents, we have a winner and it's Do or Dine in Bed-Stuy.  The reviews in the NYTimes and Tasting Table were totally on-point.  This place takes food and service seriously and the vibe is spot-on.  We went last night and the place was packed.  Eating at the bar with the neighborhood folks was a pleasure and the staff/owners were amazing (and cute).  Eggs with baby octopus - amazing.  Chicken with roasted corn - even better.  The AC wasn't super cold, but whatever.  I'm totally supporting this place and you should, too!  Peace out.

My husband and I were a little put off by the owners keeping the old restaurant sign (a la Pianos), a bittersweet reminder that Do or Dine is selling gentrification almost as much as fine food. But we love great food, and the reviews (and proximity to home!) drew us to have my birthday dinner at Do or Dine. When we walked in, no host showed us to a seat or let us know the wait time. Instead, the chef himself shouted from the kitchen, "I think there's a bit of a wait... look for the guy on the floor who's crazy busy." That guy never materialized, but a pleasant enough server (in an awesome polka-dotted apron) came through to let us know we'd be waiting around 15 minutes and got us openers for our beer. We sat around by the bar and agreed that the atmosphere was a little disorienting (super clubby music, disco ball); the whole place seems to be trying very very hard, which is admirable, but can be a little discomfiting. We were, indeed, seated well within 15 minutes and the chef came by our table (and all the customers') making recommendations and brief small talk. He recommended the Nippon Nachos, clever dumplings stuffed with nacho fillings, that didn't taste nearly as unique as they looked. He also recommended the fatty lamb breast, apparently a dish that is loved by tons of customers. It was our least favorite of the things we ordered, overly salty and limey, with none of the promised cumin flavor and skin that was hard to chew (though the lamb meat itself was beautifully tender). The infamous foie gras donut, though, lived up to the hype. I haven't been a huge foie gras fan in the past, but prepared this way, it was amazing. I've been thinking about it for days. The salmon was also beautifully prepared. The service, in general, was strange. I wasn't sure just who our server was, and I was not super pleased to see tons of beautifully prepared plates sitting on the kitchen ledge, waiting minutes to be delivered to tables. Still, it was busy, and the place is finding it's footing. We'll try it again and hope that the food becomes more consistent and the service more expedient.

Remember when you were young and you thought you had great taste in clothes and music (especially to impress your friends or date), but you have no money to supplement those tastes?   Now that we're grown up, we still think we have great taste; especially in food, via fine restaurants, but we have trouble finding economical avenues to correctly show off our sophisticated sense of culture. Do or Dine fixes this.  It has a great ambiance, the food knocks your socks off, and the service is casual but sophisticated- which is probably how you describe yourself on OKCupid.   If I ever get a date (which occurs once every leap year), and I want to knock it out of the park; I'm taking her here.  She'll basically have to.

Absolutely horrendous service. We sat for 20 minutes before being acknowledged by anyone. The bartender was clearly drunk or hungover or something. I ordered a "bottomless" Bloody Mary. The bartender served me ONE and then disappeared for about 30 mins. I ended up having to ask a server to give me my bill... 45 mins later. While I'll admit the food was pretty good, it was certainly not worth the awful service that came with it.

Come here for brunch! The food is super unique and super tasty! I love the box trash Bennie because there is nothing like a poached egg over dressed fries. The bottomless mimosas help too. Overall the place is super fun and well priced. The only regret is when I have gone a few times to have brunch and they weren't open for whatever reason.

Great beer selection, tasty food, warm and welcoming ambiance, and friendly service. What more could you want from a neighborhood restaurant and bar. I love this place so hard! They KNOW beer, have interesting selections (particularly Belgian-style heavy when I was there, and that's not my taste, but I don't mind! At least they have a perspective!) They also were featuring the Queens brewery Singlecut which was awesome beer. Basically, this is a great local place. I will be becoming a regular for sure. Tip: Their "tasting" tapas brunch is a dream come true for pepole like me who always want a little savory a little sweet. YOu can get a generous "single" portion of Duck confit hash w/ a poached egg, one potato pankcake, and one piece french toast for like $13!  And if you like boozy brunch, add unlimited bloodies or mimosas for $19... total. This place is a gem. I'm going back for brunch for the pistachio pancakes... and then again for dinner to try their delicious looking tapas. I normally hate tapas because i always end up feeling like i don't eat enough, but Open Door's portions are generous. All in all, I love this place and would recommend to any friend looking to dine well in LIC.

Delicious dinner - perfect portions. We had the beef stew and the 1/2 roasted chicken.  Our waiter was super friendly - relaxed yet attentive. Great beer list and music playlist. We were in for an early dinner and were one of two couples in the restaurant - don't let the lack of crowds deter you - this place was perfect. We will definitely be back.

Very nice service, lovely decor, but inconsistent food. Chorizo Tart - triangles of puff pastry stuffed with ground chorizo mixture. Pastry was soggy. stuffing was mushy. Trio of Croquettes - tastes reheated and stale... In plain tomato sauce. Rather underwhelming. 1/2 roasted chicken - size of a pigeon. a half pigeon. Kid you not. Gnocchi - mushy. Pretty tasty cilantro pesto, though. Maybe i'll come back for brunch and give it another go? It IS so close and convenient...

Perfect. Not just the food but the dining experience. Wanted to enjoy an evening of quality food and some nice drinks and Open Door exceeded all expectations. Cheese plate-amazing. Fish Tacos-Superb. Pumpkin tart- WOW. We ordered incrementally and the food was always quick and fresh. Nick and Gerard were fantastic and topped off the experience. Also try Tuesdays for Half off Bottles of wine on a very competent list.

My friend and our bfs met up at this place primarily for the AYCD mimosas and bloodies. It was kind of a trek for us to go out to LIC from Manhattan but for the additional $5 buckaroos you're promised bottomless drinks with purchase of brunch. I was like hey hey! That's a super sweet deal! The bf and I went for bloodies first, then by the second glass realized it was a tad salty. So we opt out for mimosa. The mimosa were easy to drink, cuz it was rather watered down in my opinion. It was like drinking OJ with a splash of champagne - a couple times we even notice a few ice chunks floating on top of our drinks! I can't remember if I've ever had a mimosa served with ice...To top that off, the server wasn't the greatest or the most attentive. Let's just say our water glasses and beverage glasses remained empty more than we'd like it to be. Half the time she was siting at the bar chit chatting with friends. However, the food was surprising acceptable for this bar/diner. I had the Eggs Benedict ($14) - they let you chose 2 different types of eggs or the same. I tried the Cured Salmon and the Confetti Duck Eggs Benedict. Both are served with hollandaise sauce. The bf tried the Steak and Eggs ($15) - which wasn't really a steak...but more like a short rib. It was nice and juicy, but still not a steak. The taste was acceptable. But nothing to rave about.
A staple of Hamilton as long as I can remember. 30 years ago it was our High School lunch place of choice. It was good than and just as good today.

My friends and I get a pizza from Brother's every Friday night. The owners always seem to be working and are very friendly to us and the rest of the customers. The place gets pretty busy on the weekends, but the staff doesn't ever seem overwhelmed. The food is always pretty quick. I'm a big fan of the pizza, but their hot subs are also delicious. I've had almost every kind, and I highly recommend them. I've yet to have anything bad from Brother's. I don't dine in there much, but it seems like a decent place to do so. The waitresses seem alright, and the place always looks clean and welcoming. Brother's is awesome. Go get some grub.

Brother's is a great place to go for pizza or sandwiches. The food is consistently good and the atmosphere is very comfortable. They don't deliver, but their conveniently in the heart of Hamilton, so picking it up yourself isn't much of a problem. The service is okay, and the prices are great. I can't stress enough how much I love their pies and subs. I highly recommend Brother's for lunch or dinner.

This place has been open a week people need to realize that But I must say. We had a 730 reservation and were sat within 15 minutes. Places was jammed solid. They were very accommodating with our sons stroller. Our waitresses came over within minutes to get us drinks and appetizers. Appetizers came out hot And fresh. Short rib tacos are a must. Big Mac sliders were great and a huge portion. Our main course did not come out on top of the appetizers. They were spaced out perfectly. I expected to wait a while considering how busy they were. But it eded up being perfect. Everyone was happy with there main courses. I had the Italian steak sandwich which I always get in nutley and it was just as good. I tasted my friends sizzling steak and it was cooked perfect. Great beer selection. Especially the tap beers. TVs are huge you can see them from anywhere in the restaurant. Prices are great. We needed a place like this in that area. Can't wait to go back been craving the tacos already.

I have not been to Franklin Steakhouse yet, but I plan to since I pass by it everyday on my way home from work.  I have been to the steakhouse in Nutley and like it a lot.  I could understand having problems the first couple of weeks any restuarant opens, even one that was already established at another location.  That is why when I read the first 2 comments, I could believe the problems, but the customers have to give it a little more time to develop. What I do find hard to believe is the post from Joseph C. in Riverdale.  Is this guy a sales rep for the place or what?  Or is he one of the owners or managers?  In less than 24 hours he had a completely different description of everything about the restuarant.  He describes the place and menu like he is on an infomercial.  5 star rating right after 2 people give it 2 stars?  Rome was not built in a day. I am sure this will be a great place in the very near future, lets just be realistic and not try to sell the world on it until more people can check it out themselves.

I came here the other night with my husband. We ordered a sandwich and sliders. They weren't too bad except the buns for my sliders were hard and my husband found a black HAIR in his sandwich. When we brought it to our servers attention, she took the plate into the kitchen and when she returned she said that she told the chef about the hair and asked if we wanted a new plate of fries. We saw no management what so ever and were in no way compensated for finding such a disgusting thing in our meal. Also, we found the food was overpriced, especially for such a hairy meal. YUCK!

My family went here to celebrate my brother's birthday and we had a HORRIBLE dinner experience. Everything was extremely unorganized and the manager lacked the ability or interest in rectifying any of the errors that were made.  Four out of six orders were incorrect (i.e. the wrong steak sandwich, two filets were well done when ordered medium and medium rare, completely opposite sides from what was ordered... the list goes on and on).   When we called the manager over to our table to make him aware, we actually just stared at us and then turned around and walked away without even saying anything.  Also, the wait staff stopped at our table three times with appetizers that were not ours and then seemed to be lost when trying to determine where the food should go. I will never go here again.

Meh.. I do realize that they just opened, but it's not like there new at the business. Served my table of 4, had only 3 of the dinners, every one was finished by the time I got mine,20 minutes later (just a steak with mashed potatoes) Waitress did what she could, manager was rude, non-caring and dressed like the maintenance man. Would I go back, maybe I'll give it a year.

Oh, this poor, poor establishment. I get it, been open a few weeks. I've been to restaurants open a day that had their sh** together better than this place, and this is their second time around the block. I went here with a group of about 6 friends. We all had very specific dietary needs.... we wanted meat and vegetables. What better place to go for meat, than, well...a steakhouse...the veggie part should kinda be a given. Walked in to an empty establishment around 5:00pm, the hostess asked if we had reservations. We said no, looked at the bar and saw there were 6 seats...said we were willing to take those if it was an issue. We were hungry,. We would have eaten sitting on the floor. Hostess ended up sitting us at a nice comfy table in the corner of the restaurant. I would say, it took the server 10-15 to approach us (in-case you missed it, the place was dead at that time). Our drink order was taken...took about a good 15-20 minutes for us to get a bottle of wine, and three other drinks (place is still pretty slow, picking up though). By the time everyone got their drinks, we were ravenous and wanted meat...and veggies. We all ordered some type of meat, and a veggie or two for a side (mainly steamed broccoli)...We did not get that...at all. We got potatoes, and broccoli rabe. AND, we waited pretty much over an hour, EASY, for our food. Again, buy this time it was about 6:30ish. It had picked up but, it wasn't overwhelming. I'll focus on my dish, well, because I'm writing this. I ordered a Filet, 10oz,  Medium Rare, and steamed broccoli. Totally willing to pay the $29-ish for a good piece of filet and non-mushy broccoli. I got broccoli rabe (mushy), a medium-well filet, that tasted mediocre, and mashed potatoes. I could live with the miscommunication about the veggies...However, if I'm paying almost $30.00 for a steak, and drinking like a fish, I expect it to come out how I requested it. Especially, from a steakhouse. We all ordered pretty significantly priced dishes. One of my friends got the hibachi steak and also asked for it medium rare, it came out like a brick. We sent that one back. Of course I asked for the manager. I'm not a complain-to-the-manager-to-get-a-free-meal-person. However, I most definitely, absolutely, hands-down in funky town, will tell a manager that my $30.00 steak was over cooked, that our food took almost a hour and a half to come out, that none of our simple requests were answered, and that we all grew grey hair while waiting for our drinks. Which, we drank a lot. The Manager, John I think, was super friendly, and used the 'we just opened line'. I said I get it, but it doesn't excuse that fact that I got a hockey puck for filet. He asked if we drank, and said he would take care of us. We got the bill, and held to his word... The waitress appreciated him that day...all I have to say. Do your self a favor, if you want a good steak in the area, go to one of the Bonefish Grills...they're consistent, and the meat is amazing (ironic). At least, until Franklin is operating in full swing.

Went in anticpation of a great burger. Host seated us and that was the last time we spoke to him. Ordered the lobster bisque (only on Fri and Sat) they should call it sea leg soup. No lobster and it was 10 bucks. Ordered a cheeseburger and it was the most tasteless meal I have ever had. The lettuce was wilted and the tomatoe mealy. The manager walked through a number of times, never spoke to a patron, he changed the channel on the TV and spoke to the staff. We told our waitress of our displeasure and she said"sorry". No one came to our table after that. We left and the manager still did not speak to us and the waitress he was talking to said good night. Not a good experience for a place that just opened . I will not go back. Food lacking in taste and freshness, no management to care about the customers, and should be false advertising to say lobster bisque, charge 10 bucks and have fake sea legs.  DON'T GO HERE!!
Very poor. Service week .Food below average. it should not be called steakhouse. 5-6 steak choices only.

Excellent South-Indian Vegetarian Food that has an authentic and delicious taste. There are a wide range of options including a variety of Dosas, Uttapams, Vadas, Idlis and deserts. These are accompanied by great chutneys and Sambhar. Overall, We *love* the food and service here. We especially recommend  Tuesday and Friday nights which are the "All you can eat" buffet nights with different South-Indian and other regional foods (such as North Indian Chat and Pani-Puri). The owners are very attentive to the needs of the customers and the service is prompt and very courteous. We highly recommend this restaurant.

I have eaten here several times as I choose to stay at the Hampton whenever I can. My meals have always been rich in flavor and the servers have always been attentive.  I recently stayed over visiting family for Easter. Instead of everyone cooking this year we decided to do the Easter Buffet (8 people).  I will have to say nicely done!!!! Keep in mind you have to make reservations ahead of time because they are swamped. They have different seating times, that way you are assured the buffet is always fresh. The manager who I have conversed with in my past stays (I believe his name is Tom) welcomed me back and even remembered my name (the reservations weren't under my name). The food was amazing, however I accidentally took the octopus. I am not a fan of tentacles as one of the other reviewers is. (yes it had tentacles). They had Turkey and Roast Beef carving stations, along with chicken dishes, leg of lamb, and  many other numerous selections. The prices are reasonable and the service is good. Quite honestly anyone that writes that the food is cheap in a restaurant only encourages the establishment to raise them.  I highly recommend this restaurant!

The Calandra's Mediterranean Grill is a true Italian restaurant.  There is a piano player a few times a week at night there, and it really sets the ambiance.  The kids get pizza dough and on Sundays there is even a magician!  They have a little bit of everything to eat here so no one is ever unhappy.  The wait staff is extremely helpful and always ready to jump and if you need anything.  As with all the Calandra's restaurants, the amount of food on your plate is overwhelming, so I take it home and eat it the next day with the free loaf of bread you get at the door on your way out.  What a great place, two nights of no cooking!
Service is bad, Veg food tasted ok...Non Veg was bad...

Food was delicious as usual at Topaz.  Thai restaurants in the area are all consistently good.  On our last visit to Topaz we brought a bottle of wine (BYOB).  Even though we ordered a full 3 course meal of appetizers, entrees, and desserts we were still charged $4.50 corkage fee.   I respect establishment's BYOB fee policy but there are other great Thai places in the immediate area that do not charge for bringing your own wine.

My girlfriend and I went here for Valentine's Day and it was fantastic - we quite literally ate everything they gave us and then some. The spring rolls to start were great, and we split the duck and pad see ew for dinner. Honestly they were the best examples of either one I have ever had. Then we ordered one of the homemade desserts mostly just to try, but wound up eating the whole thing! Needless to say, after eating all that we were stuffed but very happy. Will certainly go back again

Very good, small homestyle Thai. Everything is good and it has a modern spin. The chef varies the menu with the season ad there are certain specials which are to quite addictive. If you happen to be there in the fall, be advised that this chef works wonders with pumpkin - in curries, entrees and even pumpkin custard with sticky rice for dessert. Small, charming artisan restaurant that is worth a trip!

I have been coming here since it opened and was struggling. The food, but more importantly Momma and her wonderful personality has kept me coming back. The best Thai in North Jersey - bar none. Everything is exceptional. Prices are reasonable and Byob makes it that much better.

I really wanted to like this place (mom/pop shop, straightforward cooking, etc.), and after reading the previous reviews, I ventured past the familiar brunch spots on FDB to try this out. I'm not familiar with brunch spots north of here so maybe it's good for the neighborhood, but there are just much better options south of 135th St, like Maison Harlem, Harlem Tavern, Amy Ruth's, even Jimbo's. The bang for the buck just isn't there: $12 for a breakfast sandwich on a mini biscuit? They're $4 from the bodega and taste better. Biscuit was too dense, grits were clumpy, eggs were over cooked, and the potatoes were lukewarm. Service was friendly and personable, but not very present. I wish I lived closer so I could have another opportunity to see what the hype is about, but the food will not bring me back.
AMAZING pancakes!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! and outstanding service. I cannot wait to go back!

Came here for brunch and the good and coffee were both very good.  The space itself is beautiful, with exposed brick and great lighting.  I had the Frittata and my friend had the French Toast.  Both were excellent and good portions.  The service was earnest, if a little inexperienced.  The only critique is that brunch was pretty expensive for the area - $20 a person not including alcohol.

Such a cute spot for brunch with friends and family! Bright, spacious, close to the 137th-City College stop on the 1 train. The staff is attentive and the owner is very friendly. The challah french toast was delicious with yogurt and strawberries, and I had a few bites of the frittata and turkey sausage and everyone in my party was happy with their meal!  The coffee is also delicious-- the staff whipped up the half and half cream which was pretty wonderful!

We came for a late brunch here on Saturday and LOVED it. I had griddle cakes with berries, and homemade chicken apple sausage - both were RIDICULOUSly delicious. My boyf had sausage egg and cheese on a biscuit and swore it was the best biscuit he's ever eaten. It was comfortable, cool and cozy. We were there at a weird time so it wasn't crazy busy, and we had a great time chatting with the hostess and servers. Donna, the owner, even came over to make we were happy. One thing: Google will tell you that it's on Fred Doug Blvd but it's NOT, it's on Amsterdam. Luckily it was totally worth the hike!

Meh. In 14 minutes you could walk from Testo to Il Passatore.  The menu & underwhelming food would be the same at both places. The Caprese con Mozzarella di Bufala ($10) was really disappointing.  The tomato wasn't ripe, the cheese was dry & the garnish was ONE basil leaf.  The plate needed a healthy drizzle of olive oil.  Where was the waiter to bring this?  Outside, smoking.  Rip off. The entrees were fine.  The handmade pasta in the ragu was great.  The sauce itself was thin & kinda like the sauce in Chef Boyardee.  Once upon a time, Chef Boyardee was a great champion of Italian cuisine. I wasn't surprised that my steak was overcooked.  The poor thing was dry & gristle-pocked, but the garnishes made it more enjoyable.  The caramelized onions atop the steak were the best part of my meal, really delicious. The small space & atmosphere are charming, i expect to see a lot of traffic here.  Though i walked away feeling "meh" about my meal, if you stick to the pasta selections you won't have completely wasted your time & money. Cash Only.  No alcohol, no BYOB. No AC. PS, AVOID the seafood pasta unless you like the taste of freezer burn

Went for the Taste of Hartford and a friend's birthday recently.  Not bad at all, but really nothing outstanding either.  I had a strip steak that may have come from the local Stop and Shop - a cheap, grizzly cut.  All of the other items, though, were very good.  The service was odd - it seemed to consist of a kind of team of three people.  That would have been fine, but 2 spoke no English at all.  Finally, we asked that our check be split in half among to credit cards.  We received the slips to sign, and there was about a $20 disparity between the the two.  Weird.
One of the best pizzerias in town! They have a good selection of specialty pizzas. Delivery is very slow on weekends so it's better to do take-out.

All I have to say is AMAZING! OMG! No matter what dish you order, you will be satisfied! A must to order is their Salmon Panini. I was in awe while I bit into it and I told the waitress how great it was and she told me the paper wrote them up just on that panini alone! They loved it so much that an article was written up about it. Simply amazing! I go as often as I can!

As part of the 5BBC  (five borough bike club) we stopped by during a friday evening ride led by Bill M. The ride was fine, we zig zagged through the beautiful neighborhoods of Brooklyn from Grand Army Plaza. The ride made a stop at Panino Rustico and WOW WOW WOW.. this place blew my socks off. The breads were perfectly toasted and the ingredients were all excellent. The prices were fair (not Bánh mì cheap but not hipster expensive) 8-9 bucks is average. The gelato is 3 bucks a scoop (little pricey but very nice). In both cases I split the sandwich with someone else and both halves were AMAZING. When the Bill M. announced another Brooklyn ride with a stop here, I was the first in line. And again the 2 paninis I shared (different this time but I forget which) were delicious. I think the only downside is its location, it's in a mostly residential neighborhood in Bensonhurst (which is far for me). But since I have a car, a motorcycle, a bicycle.. I'll drive to avoid hipsters, no problem. Also the lines CAN get long if this place gets a flood of people (no thanks to the 20+ bicyclist) but I'd rather it be made with care than to be rushed. The owner is friendly. The servers and waitresses are pretty (probably there for the summer). What's not to like?

We had lunch there the other day. Two adults, two children. We had NO appetizers, no alcohol, no dessert.  The bill was  $87.09. to make sure that you you read that correct  $87.09.  There is no lunch that is worth 87.09. the waiter had personality, however not $87.09. I said something to the manager. She said that they were "fine dining".  There is no place in the upper valley that is fine dining. I also informed her that fine dining requires a dress code and it is not blue jeans and a sweat shirt. They are a FAR CRY from fine dining. I will NEVER EVER return to Koto's in West Lebanon NH. Not for a lunch for 2 adults and 2 children for $87.09. Unless you have more money than you know what to do with than I suggest any of the other restaraunts in the upper valley that has faster service, better prices and FREE refills on drinks.   It won't let me post this with out giving one star they deserve 0 stars !!!!!!!!!

We decided to try this place when we came to check out the neighborhood of our new apartment. It was great to see an unexpected restaurant like this right around the corner. It's small and charming. I don't think I've ever tried Indonesian food, but the flavors, though a bit new were strong but not overwhelming. We tried the bluefish dish and the stewed beef dish, both were really good. It's also BYOB with a wine/liquor store very close by, so that's definitely a plus.

Excellent food and service. Definitely worth the trip! The nasi goreng was a perfect blend of flavors. I could eat it every day. I also loved the bluefish, which came with an assortment of accompaniments (bok choi, roti, chutneys) that worked perfectly together. I'd love to see a similarly inventive and well-balanced set of desserts--a ginger-peppercorn ice cream, maybe...?
I ordered delivery. Came very fast. The good was good but not unique like I've never had before. I always order from Ekta but wanted to try something different.

Went in with my girlfriend Friday afternoon with the 15 for 30 groupon...only to find a buffet with a delicious assortment from the menu, something for all tastes.  And it was only like 9 bucks a person.  Sweetest lunch deal in the City.  Coming back here once a week.  Food was awesome and served with rice and naan.

You have to really want to get to Mood Indian Restaurant because the approach is a challenge. When 95 South was jammed south of Girard, I was able to jump off, zigzag my way to Spring Garden, make a left on N.4th, and start looking for my destination.  There it was, but at first view it seemed to be behind bars.  Fences and security everywhere.  Reminded of prison gates.  Quickly realized all that parking was for residents, and the street meters were the only nearby option.  At 12 minutes for .25 on a Saturday night, I fished out all my quarters and fed the hungry metal mouth. Then located the narrow opening in the fence and the walkway leading to the resto.  I hoped I had all the necessary credentials to get through customs. The boss was squeegeeing his front windows as I walked up to the door.  I was impressed that he had not delegated the work, but took pride in his shop's appearance, knowing that first impressions are so important.  Stepping inside after confirming I had arrived with Ali, I was taken by the crispness of the white linen tablecloths and red napkins.  The space had high industrial ceilings, giving an open sensation.  I was shown to the table and sat down to await the arrival of my friends.  I was alone there at 6 pm; thinking that Indians/Pakistanis prefer late dinners.  I liked the vibe as I perused the menu and took in the details.   After V & M arrived, we ordered several dishes to get a cross section of the kitchen fare.  Samosa Chaat, Chicken Malabar for apps; Salmon Tandoori, Chicken Makhani, Baingan Bharta(Eggplant), a Bread Basket mix, and Basmati Rice as entrees.   Mango Lassi for me, and Sweet Lassi for M.   All were good to excellent. Most memorable were the Chicken Malabar which was grilled and breaded with Coconut, the Samosa Chaat, which had all the ingredients of a Samosa, but reformulated into an open dish full of Potato, Peas, various crunchy chips and spices. Additionally, the Baingan Bharta was very well done with a complementary heat/sweet texture, and the Makhani was tender in a Tomato base curry that was requested hot spiced and delivered fully.  The Salmon Tandoori was the most colorful dish (see photo), but the fish was a tad dry and the veggies and spices so overpoweringly good, that the mild taste of the Salmon was somewhat hidden by its pushy roommates. All in all, a very good meal in a pleasant environment.  By the time we left around 8, the room was full, along with our stomachs.  We ended up taking a large portion home with us.   I will definitely return once they let me out on parole.

I'm a huge fan of any place BYOB and Zizi tops my list. It's rare to find an intimate setting with delicious food that also allows you to bring in your own wine or beer. The food is very reasonably priced and the wait staff extremely polite. Great for date night!

4.5 stars for dinner.  We came in late on a rainy Friday night and the place was packed!  Thankfully we scooped up the last table and probably the last seating of the night.  The servers were very attentive and friendly, the atmosphere is charming but the real winners are the food.  Every thing we tasted that night was delicious.  We started off with the Crazy Baba, Shisito Peppers and Falafels.  Everything was perfectly balanced and the different textures played well together.  The only complaint I'd have is there could have been more pita bread served with the Crazy Baba (only 2 triangles for a plate full).  For an entree we split the stuffed root vegetables.  Everything about this dish was excellent.  It was warm and cozy but felt refreshing as well with the yogurt sauce and sprigs of fresh cilantro.  For dessert we had the semolina cake with ice cream and the baklava.  Holy moly on the semolina cake!  It was the perfect end to the meal and we left the place wanting to try everything on the menu. Since we were such big fans, we came back 2 days later for brunch.  Brunch here was just ok and I'd give it 3 stars.  Service was pretty slow this time around and food was nothing to write home about.  For brunch we started with the Gravlax Limona and the Home Fries Armada.  Both were fine but not as good as the small plates during our previous visit.  The Gravlax was sliced a little thick for my liking and the yogurt sauce reminded me more of mayo.  It could have used a couple squirts of lemon.  The home fries were very tasty but there was too much mayo dolloped all over it.  For entrees I had the Hummus Masabacha and my friends had the Cowshuka and Shakshuka.  Although the hummus was good, it looked very blah when it came out.  It was a giant pool of hummus with a sliced hard boiled egg on top.  The colors, textures and flavors were very monotonous and I really couldn't eat more than a few bites.  This would've been much better served with a salad or any type of green.  I wouldn't recommend this dish as a meal (better as an appetizer).  The Cowshuka and Shakshuka my friends had though were delicious.  The steak was perfectly cooked and good flavors in both dishes. Overall, this place is great.  Brunch needs a few tweaks but dinner is sooooo good.  It's inventive middle eastern food that is executed very well.  Will definitely be back.

I ate here last night and the food is so flavorful.  I ordered the vegetable/beef stock stew and then the stuffed root vegetables with lamb.   I haven't been to such an authentic Mediterranean restaurant in Brooklyn and I will be coming back often.  It looks like the have good lunch specials as well. The waitress was pleasant and recommended a great wine to pair with the meal. I also like that they have a specialty store within the restaurant with things like tea, raw tahini (bought it and already made amazing hummus with it, it's very fresh), spices and other regional specialties.

Have mixed feelings about this place. The space is great, very homely yet not too rustic, just the perfect blend to make one feel comftable. The food thou, is another thing. Knowing this cuisine, it's just outright lying, calling menu items what they are. I ordered Hummus Masabacha, and after thousands of those in the past, all around the world, this is NOT a hummus masabach. It was tasty, just not hummus. This also goes for the Shakshuka other people in my table ordered, or the Fatush. It wasnt a veriation of the plate, just something very different. I felt disappointed

Love at first meal. I've been lucky enough to try a good portion of their menu over 4 visits and I've never been disappointed. If I had to pick, I'd recommend the Hummus Masabacha. The service is usually excellent (unless you get sat at the bar on a busy night). But, even then, it's not bad. Complimentary Tahini and hot grilled pita make the whole experience a win from the time you sit down until you leave. It quickly became my favorite spot in Williamsburg and judging by the increased popularity and occasional 10-20 minute wait, I'm not alone! If you're nearby and hungry... check it out!
This place is amazing!

Had a nice quiet brunch here. The shakshuka was pretty damn tasty, especially with the texture of the tahini. Also, to Omer H. This is Williamsburg, Brooklyn. AKA - Home of creativity. Sorry the food isn't exactly what you grew up eating. Get over it. Also, I had a book with pictures of Marlon Brando in it. So, I was basically just horny the whole time, which made the experience pleasant.

I first learned of Joey Thai from a show on The Cooking Channel and since I love Thai food and it's very close to go and try it out.  Boy am I glad I went!!  Took my folks who never tried Thai food out for a late lunch.  We met Joey, the owner and chef, who was the most gracious host.  We learned that his mother began teaching him how to cook when he was just 6 years old.  Astounding!!!  When we mentioned that we heard of the restaurant on TV, he said thank you so much for coming and we made small talk while deciding what to start off with.  We went with the Crabmeat Balls which came with a delicious sweet and sour sauce and Thai Spare Ribs with garlic and pepper with a sauce that was excellent but I forgot to ask what was in it.  Appetizers were quickly polished off and we were ready for the main course.  Since I love Thai food and have had it a lot, I made suggestions for my folks which I think they would enjoy. My mother chose the Pad Singapore Noodle (stir-fried vermicelli rice noodles, jumbo shrimp, egg, mixed vegetables and curry powder) and my father chose the Pad See-ew with chicken (stir-fried flat rice noodles with egg, broccoli and soy sauce). I usually go with a Spicy Basil Fried Rice, a curry dish, or a Pad Thai but I wanted to try something new.  Since it's so hard for me to pick from the menu because I like everything I knew I had to make a choice and ultimately went for the Duck Garlic (sliced boneless crispy duck with onion, garlic and bell peppers).  Needless to say, I was pleased with my choice as were my parents.  The rich and vibrant flavors in all our dishes were absolutely popping and so tasty.  Joey did a great job in making everything. For dessert we went with the Fried Ice Cream (vanilla ice cream inside a tempura shell with chocolate syrup on top) which was delicious and Taro custard (I love Taro bubble tea) which I've never had but glad I tried it.  The custard was served warm and had a similar consistency to flan and full of the taro flavor.  It was a hit with me and we enjoyed both items together. I'm going to bring my friends here and tell everyone I know to come and experience  for themselves some of the best Thai cuisine I've ever had.  I'm glad he sailed across the Hudson to bring us some truly wonderful food.  KUDOS!!!

I don't know what I loves more the delicious food or the friendly staff! We were in town for the weekend and looking for something yummy and we found it- the group had omelets, pancakes, and breakfast sandwiches and everyone was happy!

Delicious breakfast.   The atmosphere was homey and we felt almost like a regular.   The staff was very welcoming and the food was great!  My husband and teenaged son complained of being "too full" a high never happens.   My short stack of blueberry pancakes with Vermont maple syrup was fantastic.   Great value and great atmosphere.
The food is always excellent and a great value!

I have been coming to Geronimo's for years and I could go on and on about how delicious the food is and how nice the ambiance is, however, what makes Geronimo's special to me is the people who work there.  Hugo, the waiter, is the reason why I have recommended the restaurant to so many people.  He is extremely friendly and professional.  At most restaurants you will typically find that the employees are usually one or the other, but Hugo greeted my table with a very authentic hello and smile.  He was extremely attentive to our big group even though the restaurant was crowded.  Whenever anybody wanted to order more food or drinks he was right behind us ready to serve.  His knowledge for the menu is also top notch.  I absolutely love all of his recommendations.

Great margaritas, attentive service, awesome music, outdoor seating, and a big heaping serving of guacamole. I approve and will absolutely be back soon to hopefully experience more options than just the delicious margarita selection!

I want to really like this place, and I like it but not for the food. Every time I let time lapse and go for some dinner and drinks I get disappointed. Great atmosphere in the summer with an outdoor bar and patio for which to enjoy a warm breeze and the characters of new haven, but the food for me falls short. I ordered a chicken burrito filled with choAxica (sp?) cheese, grilled veggies, avocado and mole and it was bland and had more the taste of charred veggies than anything else. Yucca fries were good and sprinkled with a chipotle seasoning. Prior to the main entree we had the table side guacamole.  which we ordered as medium intensity- it was HOT! So Much so that it killed my taste buds which is maybe in part why I didn't enjoy my meal. Whoever it was made it-not table side but came back with it and literally there were 1/4in pieces of jalapeño in it. Now I'm not into the display of people making guac, I think it's a bit ridiculous, but if you're going to ask $14 for it, make it tableside or better yet, just offer it out of the kitchen for less cost. Even my husband who loves hot stuff said it was mucho caliente for medium. I got a glass of their white sangria which was overpowered by grapefruit and lime- just not my thing. My husband got the shredded bison tacos and I found it to be very gamey and I usually like bison. Oh well, I'm sure the place will again lure us back for more in due time with its atmospheric charms but for now I won't be making plans for soon.

I really enjoy the atmosphere (the outdoor seating is pretty solid), and the margaritas are pretty great. Honestly, I go back for Hugo, who is the man. He has got to be the best waiter I've ever seen, and I've seen many. He remembers us every time, he brings us free drinks and food, and he's just generally pleasant and upbeat. Great, great guy. The food here is good - you will enjoy whatever you get. I think it is moderately overpriced, but not so much to deter me from going there quite often.
Great burgers n fries. Delicious chicken salad. Friendly service. The kitchen was somewhat slow at midday on Monday.

I'm a Fatty McFatty and even I can't finish a plate of their awesomeness in one sitting.  Food out your ears.  Everything tastes fresh - you can see the meats cooked / prepared right there - and there is a wealth of sides to choose from to dress up your plate, bowl, pita, or flatbread.  Hummus is smooth and delicious - and in addition to your sides, you get a bunch of freebies you can toss on top / in whatever it is you're gearing to chow down on.  Good luck with that, btw!  You'll need 2 stomachs.  Everything sits great in the tum, and the service is expedient a-la-Chipotle assembly line.  Nom nom nom nom nom.
