This place has become quite possibly my favorite place to eat. It all started one day my gf and I were walking by to get a free slurpee at 7-11 because of the free slurpee day. Hummus, Pita & Co were giving out free samples of their falafel and pita bread. We tasted it and fell in love with it. A few days later we returned to eat a full meal there. Falafel on pita bread in combo with soda and french fries. The service is incredibly friendly, you feel welcomed to eat there. The food comes out fast and the fries are taken to your table when they're done. The food is phenomenal. The taste, the texture, to me it's perfect. The french fries, nice and crispy, not overly greasy nor overly salty, just about perfect. We went for a second visit and tried the sweet potato fries instead. It was even better than the french fries. The place has free wifi and student discount, so this is an ideal place for a college student, as a matter of fact I saw quite a few students studying and doing homework there on their macbooks and laptops as they ate, so a great place for students or a writer looking for a spot to do some writing. Great food, fantastic service, I look forward to going again and again.

So delish!! I always get the falafel bowl. I keep telling myself to try something new but I just can't resist the amazing falafel. So crispy on the outside and soft inside, not to mention they're so flavorful! Big portions of yummy food for a great price... What's not to love? Plus the staff is super great and it's always very clean. My go to spot for something quick and delicious... Highly recommend

Went to Hot Tomato's yesterday for lunch. This is one of my favorite places!! Was greeted at the door by Carrie who seated us promptly.  Our server was there immediately to take our drink order and let us know about the specials. We both decided to get salads and they came out quickly which is wonderful when you have to get back to work. My chopped salad was great!! I suggest it with the burger in the grass!! The atmosphere is cool even at lunch. The dining room was full of people there for lunch or working lunches. I will be back!! "KC"

I'm ecstatic that there's a coffee place south of Tasker that isn't filled with jerk know-it-alls who started their barista careers working at Starbucks - and it's good, real good. Not perfect, but that's expected for a place that just opened up (last week? the week before?) I stumbled in here with some friends over the weekend for breakfast. I'm so attracted to comfortable (and level) outdoor seating, so we stopped in. Mind you, I noticed the place that was in the same spot before, something 'croissant,' but I never felt welcomed to come in and get something. Chhaya, using the same space, was able to get me in there. I'm not a Yelp aficionado who tries millions of spots, I generally only frequent the same spots that I adore, but this is definitely a spot to try. I love the 'let's put anything and everything on top of a waffle and it will be DELICIOUS!' Holy fucking yes! Chili? Eggs benedict? Check, Check... and now I hear of chicken curry? On a waffle?! I CAN'T WAIT TO TRY IT!

What a neat little spot. When I first heard about Mook's, I figured "a sandwich shop is a sandwich shop", but these guys really do offer a unique menu. Their sandwich options are kind of like bahn-mi meets NYC deli, and they all look fantastic. They also offer a few side dishes, soups, wraps and fresh juice mixes (which look delicious). I tried the miso braised beef sandwich. One of the best sandwiches I've had in NYC so far. As far as I'm aware, it's only been a few weeks since they've opened, but they are already doing it right. Definitely worth checking out.
Really delicious sandwiches. I had the PBLT full, it's really big and probably enough for two. Really nice addition to the neighborhood.

Very tasty! This was a very good value for the quality of food. I live in kips bay and besides incredible Indian food there's not much else out here. What a nice surprise to find this small place randomly!
wonderful food and staff! love their special drink!!!
I absolutely love this place very good service and awesome food . Waiter gave us a complementary appetizer since it was our first time coming here . Glassed pork was amazing !
If you a re looking for a great place to eat with great food and service ten this is the place for you. My only complaint is that I eat to much and don't want to have to drive home.

Love when Im traveling out of this terminal.. Great place to eat before your flight.. I had a crispy chicken wrap and it was delicious..   came with fries and they were just your regular fries but good! My husband had eggs over easy with bacon and he enjoyed them.. Service was good and its inexpensive for airport food!

This place was horrible. Service was slow. Had to ask multiple times for drinks. Took forever to get our food. Medium rare steak came out more than well done. Other items missing from order. Avoid this place.

Al's has been doing it right forever. Double cheese, quart of fries, and a corn dog if your extra hungry. This place would be on my short list of 3 if I could only choose 3 restaurants to eat at for the rest of my life.

I'll keep this one simple. Eat the fries, and you'll be glad you did. Eat anything else, and you'll feel sick for two days. The fries are absolutely the best. They are the only reason Al's gets three stars. The burgers are paper thin and use the lowest quality meat imaginable. Think gristle. Another major issue is that they don't take credit cards. Like NONE. In the event that you forgot to bring cash, there's an ATM next to the door which is convenient except you've got to pay a service fee ($2.75, I think) that equals about 30% of your meal. The creemees are a great addition in the summer time. Honestly, my memories of this place are way better than the reality.

Second time and it was equally good. Love the octopus. It's so tender. Tried the falafel which was good and both greasy at all!  Tried the Branzino this time which was good but love the dorado more. I love the kunefe!!  U just have to get it to end ur meal. Sweet, salty, crunchy and creamy.  Will be back. The yelp deal is awesome. The device is great too. They are all so friendly and so accommodating.
Great place. Recommend grilled bass and trout. We definitely will come back will friends.

When I came in, I feel it's a very comfortable place to hang out with friends and family. The atmosphere is really relaxing. The food is really good!!! We have St. Peter, black sea surf and turf. The fish is tender and the lamb is very tender also juicy. The dessert is also excellent!!! Love this place!

My go to spot for the best bronzina fish in town. Only Turkish know how to make fish this way, and Black Sea knows it well! Tonight I had the bronzina butterfly cut and it was cooked just right, squeeze a little lemon over it and ahh, enjoy!
we loved this place!  the waitor is absolutely great.  the fallafel is very good, has a kick of spice, not oily at all.  the mixed grill of lamb is tenderandjuicy.  the sea bass is very fresh.
Service was great and food was fresh and delicious!!!! Must come back :) highly recommend the octopus salad and the rice pudding for dessert. The waitress Katya was excellent!!!

I love visiting neighborhood favorites such as Blacksea Fish & Grill. After a quick look around the restaurant, it was easy to see that tables were filled with regular customers who were warmly greeted by the staff and knew exactly what to order.   As for the two of us, we relied on the wonderful Yelp reviews and photos to determine what to order. For appetizers, we ordered the calf's liver and the fish patties. For entree, we ordered the best grilled fish in Queens, the St. Peter Fish. The calf's liver had a nice texture but lacked flavor. The fish patties didn't taste as homemade as I hoped. Since we didn't see many positive reviews on appetizers, I would say that I wasn't too disappointed about the two that we ordered. However, the expectation we had for the St. Peter Fish was much higher. The St. Peter Fish turned out to be worthy of all the wonderful praises it received. Before even taking a bite, I was so pleased to see how huge the fish was and how nice the grill marks came out. As I was cutting into the skin of the fish, I couldn't contain my excitement as I listened to the cracking of the crispy skin. It was love at first bite... at second bite, at third bite, and so on. I was amazed at how juicy and flavorful the flesh turned out. The fish alone was worth three stars! The Turkish coffee we ordered at the end of our meal paired nicely with our rice pudding dessert. Without the coffee, the rice pudding would've been too plain for me. My fourth star for Blacksea is given to the friendly and professional staff. Keep up the good work!

The restaurant is in an old store of Winooski.  Very casual and yes, I would have to agree with the person who said that it is a "little" dusty and service can be slow but the pasta's are pretty good and pizza is same for the price you can't complain they even have specials where you can get 50% off one entree when buying another.

For someone who is used to super expensive rodizio places in NY this place is a breathe of fresh air! They serve all the good cuts of meat- namely, picanha, and they also have a great buffet which has feijoada, rice, and all that other good stuff. SO you get to have bbq AND pork stew, all at the same time. I was a happy camper. Not the best rodizio ever, but pretty good, and well priced!

I was craving Brazilian BBQ so badly, and Boi Na Brasa hit the spot. I was chary when I walked into the restaurant because it's the type of interior decoration that Chef Ramsey would strike down in an instant, but once I sat down and the meat started coming out, I forgot about my surroundings, and it was just about the meat and me. They have enough varieties of meat to keep you happy and full, but be prepared for a bit of saltiness. The ONLY thing that I was disappointed about was that they didn't serve Pao de Queijo (Brazilian Cheese Bread), but the Sangria sort of made up for it. The service was great, and the price for all-you-can-eat dinner is fair if you come with an appetite. Don't show up and eat only 3 pieces of meat! I'd definitely go here again to get my fill of Brazilian BBQ. I don't like to be overwhelmed with salty meats, so I stayed away from the bacon wrapped meats, but I definitely had my fair share of top sirloin, which was my favorite by far. So juicy and tender. Mmm.

Really enjoyed my visit to the Tria Taproom. Like most, I'm a huge fan of Tria in general and make it to their Rittenhouse location about once every two weeks. I'm also a fan of cider, so when I heard the taproom would be a combination of Tria and rare ciders on tap I was in! Boyfriend and I went on Friday night of opening week and while it was busy (40 minute wait for 2) we were able to sneak to the seats in the back and cut that wait to 2 minutes! His beer was kicked just as he ordered it, so they gave him a sample of the last of it and comped his next beer -- really great service. The iPad based menu wasn't my favorite. Innovative, yes, but maybe a little disorganized and took a long time to look through. Working at a company that designs multitouch applications, it felt painful to navigate -- but kudos to them for trying something new -- though I'm under the impression if it's not broken why fix it. The food was really tasty. I started with the 3 cheeses for $12, which were smaller in size than the traditional Tria and were served with something like a flatbread cracker? It was still tasty and I felt a good deal, but not as filling as I expected. I also got the black bean puree which was spicy and came with soft, grilled flatbread that was tasty. I was happy with these two, some people may prefer 3 items. My boyfriend got the cobb salad and it was amazing. Smoky, salty, bacon-y. They grill the romain and have a house made dressing. I'm not a cobb fan but would definitely order this one if I went back. Overall was really happy with the meal, the service, and the addition to my neighborhood. I'll probably still frequent Tria more often as I like the food options more, but I'll definitely be back to the taproom, especially if they get a happy hour!

I like the concept of having the Ipads when for ordering your beer even though I'm not sure it's completely needed.  I am surprised that the menu isn't just right on the Ipad too; it's just the beer.  Regardless, I think it's cool, but this review is about the food.  We tried the ribs, the octopus, salads, and a flat-bread.  Luckily, I had the ribs to my self, as I am a bit protective over my rib rights.  My wife enjoyed her  Kennett Square flatbread along eventually switching over to wine, which also was set up on tap.  It was packed in here on a Saturday night, but we had no problem waiting a few minutes until the bar opened up.  I have always been a fan of Tria and I think the taproom fits well into the family.
Beautiful beer list, delicious flatbreads...very nice (All that needs to change is the bad music)!

Great place!  Delicious flatbreads and fun atmosphere.  Very crowded when we went (~7:30pm on a Thursday night), but we were seated within 15 minutes.  May be tricky with larger groups, but a fun place to go on a date or with a friend.

Small dive bar with no parking lot, but great dive bar food. No nonsense service but they could use more than just one server in the entire bar.   Wings and clam were delicious. We had the Thai chili and Maryland wings. Maryland wings were soooo good as they were covered with Old Bay seasoning. Who knew? Prices are reasonable. Happy hour specials are great, but you have to eat in to get happy hour prices or you end up with a surcharge of 10 cents per wing for takeout (at least according to their sign). If subpar service annoys you, best to get takeout and enjoy those wings & clams at home.

Great date night! Felt like I was whisked away to a bistro in Paris. Sat the bar and had a late dinner and drinks while listing to live music. It's dimmly lit and the ambiance is just perfect for a date. The waitress/bartender was very friendly and explained to us that the vintage fridge they use for beers/wine etc they got from monastary (fun fact!). The cocktails were great and the food even better. It was sort of frnech food but more american style bistro a little of everything. I had the pork bun and my friend had the eggplant bun and both were very very good. They were on like a ciabatta bread and the pork was so flavorful all these different spices and sauces something sweet something spicey I was having flavor explosions in my mouth. Don't know what the bad reviews were about, it could be hit or miss depending on the service.

Not only are their cheesecakes amazing but their food is too.  I try to go to Anthony's for lunch as many times as I can.  You get really good, fresh food for a reasonable price.  Their menu changes everyday so I always get to try something different every time I go in.  You can write down your email address and they'll email you their menu daily.  I definitely recommend trying this place out, you"ll definitely get hooked.

This place is pretty cool. The bartenders are all friendly and attentive. They have your typical bar fare and they have a few extra specials. The pizza is fab! However the drinks are a tad expensive but overall it's a good time so no complaints here!

I like 381 main bar & grill very much! I like the TVs, the food is good  especially  the pizza,  best margherita  pizza I have ever eaten, thin crispy crust amazing !!!!!!!!!!!!!!   The drinks are good !
the place is awesome just way too crowded! very hard to get a drink

I had to try this place seeing how many amazing reviews it has - Chop Chop doesn't disappoint! I was tossing up between the french toast and the duck confit sandwich but the guy at the register told me to go for the latter. It did not disappoint! The duck confit sandwich is served up on a buttery brioche bun, with a fried egg and roquette, with a lovely portion of hand-cut fries and salad on the side. The owners are super friendly and kind. Oh and try their blueberry and ginger lemonade, it's a treat!

I've been a customer here since they opened and I have to say they've never disappointed!! Malcolm and his staff are warm and inviting as well as professional. he's a truly talented chef! I've lived in the neighborhood for the past 3 and a half years and this place is truly a breath of fresh air! My favorite dishes are the rib eye steak with parmesan cauliflower, and the Cajun club with perfectly seasoned fries! Had brunch with my mom on mother's day and we had the lobster omelette which she was thoroughly impressed with. All around great service, food and atmosphere! I plan to be a regular for many years to come! Oh and definitely say YES to the NoBurger! you'll be glad you did :-)

I've eaten here several times and each time has been delicious! The Duck Torte & the Lobster Roll were delicious! Staff was friendly and fast. A little on the pricy side, but understandable for the quality of the food (duck & lobster ain't cheap!). I will definitely be back again.

If you want delivery, stay away from this place. I live 5 mins away and ordered and waited 2 hours for my food and never got it. I called the store after an hour of waiting and the lady told me my order had just left the store. After another 50 mins of waiting, I called the store and found out they closed. You just lost a customer. I will not be returning.

I usually try to avoid going here because it's expensive and not super high quality, but if I need a meal on the go and don't have time to go farther, it's a good place to go. The hot food is ok, not as good as it looks, but they have some nice products you won't find in other places in town. Another big benefit is that it's open in the middle of the night. They're not super friendly, but it's nice to have somewhere to go after a night out for a snack and some water, even if they do jack up their prices.

Your buffet food sucks. You don't label it. Nobody that works there ever knows what is in it. It always tastes like shit. I take a break from you guys, come back a few months later...NOPE! STILL BLOWS! Now I've limited you to things a marsupial can make...like a sweet potato. I thought ceasar salad was simple, having only 3 ingredients but you manage to screw that up. Your tofu is in huge chunks and flavorless sauces. Your meats always look dry as hot August dog shit. Your deli sandwiches are decent. Your produce looks ok, despite not being organic. Beautiful flowers. Your market is ok, despite being pricey.
Best bagels period.  You will not find better .  Owner (s) are present and pleasant.  You may encounter long lines on the weekend, but it usually moves fairly quick.

This place did not need to market themselves by posting a groupon.  In my opinion, they make the best bagels in the area.  I live in cedar grove and have tried every place around eg. cedar grove, little falls, verona.  Far and away the best.  Always a hectic crowd inside on the weekend.  The groupon has only made it crazier inside to make your order.  They didn't need the marketing like most groupon eateries do.

The freshest sushi in Brooklyn! I'm in tummy love! A very welcome addition to the neighbourhood with consistency of great delicious, top quality food and friendly service making this gem a sure thing. Not yet visited? Do yourself a favour and make it a summer evening priority!

I've been terrified to try sushi in Crown Heights. I just don't think anyone is going to haul fresh fish this far in. But wait! They have! And holy crap this is amazing food. I've been to Japan twice, and my friend owns one of the most popular sushi shops in Hiroshima, and he would approve of this place (except the rolls were a tad loose). Anyway, we had two of their special rolls (a tuna something and a salmon something) a yellowtail scallion roll off the basic menu and one other. I can never eat more than two rolls usually. but after splitting this with my husband I was dying for more! We should have eaten there so we could keep ordering. The whole experience was lovely. it seems to be run and owned by Japanese people (they were saying Onegaishimasu every time they handed the chef an order). They are polite, and have beer if you like while you wait for your meal. Outside seating is limited but we got a space and had an Asahi in the sun while we waited. The very sweet waitress brought our food out with a smile. I LOVE THIS PLACE!!!

Great sushi! It is tiny inside but they have a nice outdoor seating area in front. The special rolls are quite large - we liked all of the rolls we tried (special salmon, macrobiotic were my favorites) and the hijiki salad was fantastic. I am definitely planning to come back to try one of the bowls. Fantastic addition to the neighborhood.

I was really excited when this place opened but I was disappointed with the rolls we ordered. Everything tasted over salted and I love salt. I don't think I will go back here again. There are better sushi restaurants that are cheaper, offer a greater variety and  deliver.

We used to like this place a lot, now its just OK The phone people taking the orders can be rude/aggressive at times and the pizza can be too oily or soggy or just warm (not hot). For that few extra dollars they charge it could be better. Its better to eat at location, that way you can let all the oil drip off before you eat it. We get the Margarita pizza a lot.
great pizza

Love this place.  Inventive, albeit pre-made sandwiches.  If you come late, they are occasionally sold out and the meat later in the day can at times be dry, but for the price you cannot beat it.  I have been there three times this week and expect to continue to go there often.

Tasty food, affordable prices, friendly service. _ Pad Se-Ew ($9): good. _ Pad Thai ($9): also good. _ Basil Fried Rice ($9): tasty with peppery kick _ Gai Toon noodle bowl ($9): also good. Have and will return.

Small place that's about only 15 feet wide but fully opens in good weather. Waiter staff are very friendly and sometimes there's a wait for a table. Try to avoid coming in large groups of around 6. Bar is good for eating solo or for two. On to the soups. Tom Yum soup was the best I ever had. They threw quite a spin on it with the lettuce, string beans, and broad noodles. The broth was so good. I tried also there Baa Mee, and the noodles in that soup are so tasty and don't taste like they were freeze dried. Beer and wine is served but expect to pay about $5 for a bottle of beer. Ambience is dim at night with some tea candles to light up the table. One wall is decorated with various bowls of different designs. Goes well with their soup menu.

What can I say? I love Noodies. Even though it is about 10 blocks from my office, it is worth the hike to get there.  The food is cheap and clean and did I say delicious?  Yes!  The restaurant is small, that is, it really is a railroad restaurant kind of deal, but the decor really makes up for the small footprint.  Not absolutely in love with the stools but I guess I can deal with them to eat such delicious food.  My favorite ther is the Pad-Se-Ew but I really should give other dishes a try...

I attended a dinner here last weekend with a large group, we have come here for several years in a row during a benefit weekend we are all in town for. Last weekend will be the last time I ever dine here, not only was food and service mediocre at best. But the owner was rude to my guests, right to their face.  They miscounted the table settings and hadn't had enough seatings ready for our guest count. One gentleman set at the head of the table which would've been fine. Except the owner Franco, told my him that this was not okay and he was "too big to be in this restaurant." As well another lady asked were was the best area, for an elderly lady, who was on a walker, to be sat... again the owner said just plop her corpse over here.  I was mortified. I was embarrassed for them. And had we not been a large party that otherwise couldn't just find easy accommodation for a Saturday night. I would have walked out. The owner knew he was wrong, and tried to joke with then both and pretend this is how South Philly is. I would beg you, you rude little ignorant man, to find some people on the streets, where my family grew up, who would even think what you did was humorous, let alone indicative of the people in this city. I dare you. I am livid at the fact I had to have my friends subjected to you and your small minded pitiful disrespect.  I will however be sure to tell everyone I know who dines there regularly, and make it a point to publicly tell this story on every social media or review site I can. You will quickly see how your mistake of talking to guests is going to cost you your business.  For an owner to even think of speaking to a guest like so is appalling. High Note Cafe has clearly hit an all time low. It has lost a customer. And likely any of my friends who I would have gladly introduced to it.  Never again.

This place gets 5 stars because I'm getting giddy just thinking about what I ate. But to keep it simple: get the oxtail and the coconut flan. It is so, so good. The lunch specials are also very reasonable - portions I believe are the same. Garlic-lovers like me out there will love this place. Service was friendly and lovely, and the space makes it a nice one for date-night.

I was truly disappointed by my experience at Puerto Viejo. My friend had come here before and really enjoyed the food, but the food was nothing special. We had some empanadas to start, then I had the pernil and maduros as a main. The pork was dry and a bit gristly (can meat actually be both of those things at once?), and the plantains were okay but overcooked/mushy and overly sweet. While it wasn't the worst meal I've ever had, it certainly wasn't worth twenty-some dollars. The empanadas were fine, though, and I can see how they'd be good if you're just getting quick drinks and snacks. However, I'd highly recommend against coming here for a full meal. Beyond the totally 'meh' food itself, the service was the worst I've had in my six years of living in Brooklyn. There didn't seem to be any logic or order in which the tables were served--we were served a full (and unbelievable) two hours and ten minutes after we arrived at the restaurant. We watched countless patrons who arrived after us receive their food first. The waitress who was helping us was helpful and efficient, but it seems like there are huge issues with the kitchen and management. There are great ways to linger over a meal, but not as a casual, not-particularly-atmospheric place like this one. We weren't able to eat and leave the restaurant until a full three hours after we arrived.
Got a good mixed sandwich of brisket and corned beef. Definitely a good sandwich but the prices are a bit high so it's tough to want to keep going back.

LIVE AT DAVES BRISKET!!! this place has great comedy acts and great live music. also amazing MEAT (although sometimes during strange hours it isn't warm enough). a true institution in the neighborhood.

I finally went to the very first David's Brisket House. I was greeted with the same kind of greeting I that I had when I went to the Bay Ridge shop. I had no idea that there was a second shop. I will be going back to both establishments. I say keep up the great work.  When I folks come to New York, you can best believe, we will be going to David's Brisket House. Thank you

Nachos. Nachos. Nachos. Good lord the nachos. I can't say enough great things about this place (and the nachos). Both times I've been have been during restaurant week in Center City so the place was pretty empty. Apparently it gets pretty busy during the week and it's not rare that the place will be filled with merriment and cheer when 90% of it is reserved for a big party. The waiter was attentive and twice has suggested some spot on delicious meals. He even let us choose the Pandora station to listen to! The food is incredible and it is very inexpensive. Second time I went everyone raved about their meal and their drinks (we brought tequila and they had the margarita mix ready for us). I had a the seafood soup and went for the optional pasta instead of the soup. The plate was bigger than my head and was brimming with deliciousness. I took it home and it fed me for 2 more meals! For 6 people the bill was just over $100 and this was after the nachos (remember me raving about that?), guac, and meals that could feed twice as many of us. Be warned it's a BYOB but they are more than happy to pour it for you. Believe me...*more* than happy. This is definitely a date night restaurant. Don't worry if neither of you speak Spanish -- the waiter is Italian and speaks English (ask him to tell you the story of how he got the job!) so that's not a problem. He does speak some Spanish from working there for a while so that isn't lost. All around a really great place to have a delicious meal and a laugh.

Just received a bistec (steak) burrito and tinga de pollo quesadilla from Iztaccihuatl, which I ordered via seamless tonight. First thoughts: it's just about midnight so I'm managing expectations. The steak burrito isn't "bad" but there wasn't an easy way to customize the ingredients. Not a fan of onions. Aside from that, it's a basic burrito, nothing special. The quesadilla tortilla on all three pieces was so stale and hard, it was arguably no longer edible. They used some type of cheese that resembles an abbazabba with shredded chicken. Essentially this choice sucked, I wouldn't order from this place ever again based on the lack of a quality control I witnessed tonight. I'm writing this review at approximately 12:18am the same night, in case I die of food poisoning in the night. Shame on you, Iztaccihuatl. God have mercy on my bowels.

I moved to Montclair back in March of 2013 and was always looking for a place with Middle Eastern food that was quality food and quality service.  I've been here a couple times, but tonight really stood out. I called around 7:00pm to place an order for one beef and one chicken shwarama, gave my name, and was told it'd be ready in 10 minutes.  However once I got there, I was told that somebody else with my exact name picked up the same exact order and that mine wasn't there.  They told me that they'd make the order again, but at that point I was pretty frustrated and left.  While I wasn't sure exactly how accurate that claim was, I was sure that I wouldn't ever come back. When I got home, I called to find out exactly what happened and hung up with the front lady even more frustrated.  What got me was that, the owner himself called me back a minute later and apologized for what happened. On top of that, he told me that he'd make a new order and have it delivered for no cost! I couldn't believe it! This was QUALITY service, and while other food places would simply act like it didn't happen, this guy made it a point that he didn't want to lose a customer and fixed the problem as best as he could. The order came and the food was as usual amazing, but tonight the quality of service is what stood out.  You guys are awesome, thanks for customer service that really cares!

I can't believe I haven't written a review for Falafel Hut! Let me tell you, the more and more I order from this place the more and more I grow to LOVE, not like it. The falafel sandwiches are no joke. They are packed with meat and flavor. Their ingredients are super fresh! Their tomatoes are super red! And the prices are just right. My favorite? The fattush salad with toasted pita croutons! The croutons are extra crunchy! Which makes me think now...its been a while since I've had anything from them. I must change that!
I love this place!

My coworkers and I will eat here for lunch sometimes.  The owner is super friendly and the place is inviting.  We always call in our order since we have a limited amount of time available and the food is always ready when we arrive.  There is ample street parking which is a plus.  I usually go with the super hut specials...the "zoom zoom" is a good mix of meat.  The "for pete's sake" is delicious if you like gyro (I do!).  I'm not a huge fan of the lamb kebabs--personal preference.  The platter comes with rice or fries, and salad.  It's a good sized portion and I usually have leftovers.  Unfortunately, once reheated, the leftovers aren't very appetizing.  Eat what you can while you are there! It's good stuff!

I attended a friends and family night at The Gander and was impressed by the quality of food and service that the restaurant provided from day one. Our server Koreen was very knowledgeable and personable. She suggested a nice Cotes du Rhone for me to start with and later stepped it up to a fuller, funkier Portuguese wine. I was dining with a vegan, and that wasn't a problem at all - they had a salad to start with, a trumpet mushroom entree, and a vegetable side for him. I had the trout tartare - tender small pieces of raw fish served with red caviar, spicy mustard seeds, chopped asparagus (I think), and a crunchy toast of something that looked like fish skin - inventive and delicious. My main course was the beet tortelli - round pouches with bright deep pink bellies of beety filling cooked to a perfect consistency, topped up with radish (I think) crisps and goat yogurt. Superb! Finally, for desert we had a strawberry rhubarb sorbet (for the vegan) and a creme brulee made with whisky, among other things, and served with bacon bits and hazelnuts. The rich creamy goodness was a perfect combination of sweet, salty and bitter, not to mention the pretty presentation. They also had a health inspector visit in the middle of the preview night, which made them stop serving for a bit. However, the staff handled the situation with grace and we loved them even more for it. Welcome and best of luck to this great new addition to the NYC contemporary American dining scene.

Having had an incredible meal at Recette a few years ago, I was excited to try this new follow-up from Chef Jesse Schenker. The apps and pastas were really great, but some of the entrees and desserts were disappointingly underwhelming. Dining here on the second night they were open, the staff was all still in the mode of very much aiming to please, and it made for a very pleasant experience. It's a beautiful space and is a nice place for a date night or a meal at the bar in the front area. We got a ton of food, which I regretted a bit upon seeing the steep bill at the end: - Parker House Rolls This is the complimentary bread they bring you to start, and it is an excellent way to begin the meal...and to enjoy throughout, as you will find it impossible to say no as they repeatedly ask you if you would like more. - Brisket Tots ($9) These were incredible and were definitely the best thing we had here. They are listed under the "Snacks" section of the menu, which the waitress described as tiny bites, but this was actually pretty substantial, and one of the most satisfying things we got for the price. These are like tater tots, but with brisket in the middle instead of potatoes. So good. These are the one thing here you must make sure to get. - Local Greens ($12) I tend to get salad sometimes lately to make myself feel better about ordering all fried foods and red meat otherwise. This one turned out to be a letdown, as although it did taste good and was very refreshing after the heavy tots, it just was not good enough to justify spending $12 on. It wasn't much more than could be done at home for a fraction of the price. - Casarecci with suckling pig ragu ($22) This was the best of the main dishes we got. The waitress advised us that the appetizer portion ($14) was quite tiny, so we used that as justification to get this as the entree size even though the two of us were already ordering two entrees. I'm glad we did, as this was much better than both entrees. There was a surprisingly generous amount of the delicious, juicy pork, along with some tasty, sweet tomatoes and the perfectly al dente pasta. This was a great choice if you are looking to have some pasta. - Pork Chop ($28) From here on out for the rest of the meal, everything we got was a lot more impressive looking than tasting. For the few bites of this small pork chop that there were, it was very good, but there was just too much fat and bone and not enough good meat. There also wasn't much else on the plate that was too tasty, with a few of the root vegetables scattered around. It looked really cool though. - Tasmanian Trout ($26) This one was actually very tasty, with chunks of chorizo and plenty of coco beans and leeks piled on top of the barely cooked fish. I didn't expect it to be served like this, but it was practically raw, which made it incredibly soft. It had a great flavor and was definitely a better choice over the pork chop. - French Fries with Bone Marrow Mayo ($9) It was just a side, but this was one of the things I was most excited for, and unfortunately most disappointed by. For a whopping $9, this was a smallish cup of incredibly greasy fries, which were mostly the small, crispy ends of the fries you get at the bottom of the batch. It was hard to find many where you could taste some actual potatoes. The gimmicky bone marrow mayo didn't really taste much different than most mayos or aiolis you get with fries at these types of places. - Angel Food Cake ($10) Billed as one of their "lighter" desserts, I should have stayed away from this as I like a rich, satisfying end to a good meal. This was mostly composed of fruit, with a couple of really tiny pieces of the impossibly light cake, which was the consistency and density of a light sponge. Again, this is a beautifully-plated dessert, but I would skip it. - Creme Brûlée Semifreddo ($10) This was the much better dessert, and looked really cool too. I didn't like the mix of the whiskey flavor, which could be avoided by staying away from those two dollops on the plate, but the rich, dense main part of the dish, the semifreddo, was delicious. The smoothness of it went great with the crunchy walnuts. This one is a good ending to the meal. Everything about the meal went smoothly, and they were impressive in that respect having only been open for a few days. Service was perfect and very attentive. A few of the food items were a bit disappointing, but perhaps I was expecting a bit too much after the deliciousness of Recette. Depending on what you get though, you can get a really satisfying, delicious meal here.

I love Recette and am a huge fan of Jesse's (hello? He won iron chef with plantains, and he hates plantains!) Note first - Chef loves the iceberg wedge! How did we not order this?? My friend and I did only snacks, appetizers and sides because we wanted to share: Fava Bean Crostini Fluke Crudo Lamb Pastrami Beef Tater Tots French Fries with Marrow Aoili Roasted Cauliflower with Anchovies Bangin' is all I have to say. The first four were perfect. The Aoili was so tasty but was very rich for two girls to clean of at the end of our meal. If it's a table of 3 or 4, definitely get an order to split all around! Then Dessert. If you don't know Christina lee you should! We had the banana parfait (tiny scrumptious chunks of banana and a little graham cracker with coconut cream on top). I dolloped the cream in my decaf americano. No? YES! We also got the creams brûlée with the nuts and bacon. Because, bacon. Drinks - the Goose Punch is a little namesake and throws back to their blood orange margarita at Recette. So refreshing as spring arrives! Great selection of dessert wines an aperitifs. We loved the marble bar, and stayed to drink more!

I wanted to LOOOOVE the Gander, the way I love Recette, but alas, that is not the case. 2 people shared the following snacks and apps.  We weren't really into any of the entrees. From best to worst: Brisket tots - Super original and tasty Buffalo Sweetbreads - Also super original and tasty Shimp au Jus - Perfect little bites, tasted good nothing original though Calamari salad - Tasted fine but nothing special... just fried calamari on romaine lettuce... Cauliflower side - It was good but  was sort of overpowered with some crazy spicy Fluke Crudo - Absolutely GROSS, the prawn was mushy and the fluke was stringy and the broth was crazy salty. Completely inedible. The service was "whatever", the waiter was nice enough when he actually came around which wasn't super frequently.  Mostly I was surprised that no one asked why we didn't finish any of our food (which i have experienced at many decent restaurants in manhattan). I noticed many other diners also didn't have clean plates soo.... I assume I am not the only one who felt this way...

I had an absolutely fabulous dining experience here. The staff was extremely friendly and attentive to everyone's needs and the food was amazing! We had the Fava Bean and Ricotta Crostini, Shrimp Toast au Jus, Crispy Calamari Salad, local Greens salad and Hamachi Crudo to start all of which was really good. I had the Arctic Char as my main course, which was perfectly cooked so it was just tender enough and very juicy. I also had a side of grits which were smoky and delicious. Lastly, we had the chocolate custard and chocolate mousse to finish which were decadent and smooth. For cocktails, I highly recommend the Gin Rhubarb Mule - yum!

I drove through again today and sit in the restaurant.  It is very comfortable and the food taste good! I like the food that is using 100% vegetable oil.  The spring roll is absolutely amazing! The vegetable is very fresh and the BBQ pork is definitely better than then ones in NY Chinatown.
Very good Chinese food in Bayonne. I like Boneless Spare Ribs.

Great Brazilian style BBQ. It's buffet, a you can eat but you pay by the pound. Great idea so you don't end up wasting food like in so many other buffet. Salad and side were tasty and there was plenty of variety. I really loved the squash with okra. For the meats, I had the chicken wrapped in bacon and lamb, both were seasoned well and excellent. My hubby and son had the beef and pork sausage. They both loved it. The place is in a small plaza type place, you have keep an eye out for the place but really nice inside. We are definitely going back.

This review is not of the food or drink at The Bahche Cafe, because, unfortunately, we were never given the opportunity to try it. This is a review of the management - and for anyone considering The Bahche Cafe for an event. My fiance and I were interested in checking out The Bahche Cafe. We stumbled upon the place and were struck by how beautiful it was. We went in right then to inquire about events. We were told they do events and left our number for Corina. She called the next day, and after the conversation she promised to send an email with pricing and package ideas. This e-mail never came. A week later, after seeing them posting on Twitter, I replied to a tweet asking why they don't reply to e-mails. That got their attention. We arranged a meeting with Corina for Friday, January 3 at 4pm. We made the hour-long trek from Harlem in shitty weather only to find that they were closed due to the snow. There was no call, no e-mail, nothing to let us know that no one would be in to show us the space. We are very disappointed. We think the space is beautiful and would've loved to consider it for our big day, but the communication has been inconsistent at best. They have been rude and unprofessional at every turn. I can only hope that they treat prospective couples in the future with more respect. It's sad that we are left with nothing nice to say about The Bahche Cafe.

Don't go in here if you're expecting an Eagles bar. Jets sound on during the Eagles Bucs game. Eagles game on a tv set to sling box that paused about every 5 minutes. Terrible bartender basically rooting against everyone in the bar cause he maybe bet 5 bucks on a game. 2 stars cause food decent but avoid this Shorty's location, uptown much better.

Place doesn't have their act together. One tv showing Eagles game which you would expect in NYC but they advertise as a "Philly bar". Picture grainy, no sound. They used the same line as this summer- "we are having trouble with satellite reception". Playing audio from the Jets game because as the server explained "the manager is a Jets fan" fair enough. As I was leaving the aforementioned manager came over to give us a hard time for trying to apply a couple of free drink tokens we were given because of the inconvenience.  We never were able to use them and can't see us ever using them now.

My family and I have been to Shogun, Sushi Palace, Sen's and Kanoko before it closed. We tried Sushi King and have gone back at least 6 more times since it opened. We found the food to be fresh and the staff very welcoming. The food is prepared quickly and the atmosphere is relaxing. The prices are right even for the all you can eat menu. If you are looking for good sushi at a good price I would highly recommend. We had no issue with the way the food was prepared. We were more concerned with taste and given the fact we have been back a number of times since then should say something about the foods overall quality. Sushi King is on par with Sushi Palace and more convenient to get to for us.
the best place on earth, the staff is friendly, we like to go there with our kids and this is their favorite spot, try the omelette ham and cheese for brunch, honestly the best in the world!!!!!

Food: really good Service: excellent Ambiance and decor: excellent all I can say is that this is a really cool but place with a really awesome laid back vibe. The staff is really outstanding and just kind of fit in with the feel of the place. We ordered bone marrow on toast and it was AWESOME, I also got a chance to try the sirloin tips which were really good, the fries were really great too. I will not recommend the shrimp croquettes because they were really salty and fishy. Overall will be back for sure.
I have been here before and loved it.  Beware though that yelp says it is open when it is not.  Call first.
This place is super cool, I have a hunch it's good for a lunch and a brunch.
The vegetarian pho was loaded with lots of good vegetables. Also they have amazing iced coffee! A great neighborhood place!!

I don't hate this place. Actually I kind of liked this place. Having never really explored New Haven before I don't have much to compare it to in the area but I did hear quite a bit of criticism about Anchor before going. It was a first date and it seemed I wasn't the only one as two other people asked if I was the person they were meeting (I must have seemed confused when I walked in and looked around). It's a small place, with the lights fully on so no hiding what you actually look like if it is a first date. There is a juke box, although I never saw someone pick a song and the music became very bad when it reached 11-12pm. There was only one bartender, nice fella, handling the crowd well. Good location and parking, good selection of bottled beers and a diverse crowd all seeming to enjoy themselves in personal conversations. Complaints: the bathrooms downstairs are adjacent to a sketchy, if not creepy, old possibly dance floor or gambling area in the basement, and something happened with the draft taps so couldn't order draft after 10pm. The guy I was with said something goes wrong with their booze supply, lights, servers, or music nearly every time he goes (but still comes back so I'm guessing no major issues). I was warned this was a 'Yale "tool" Bar' however I think it's a cool little hangout and fits well with the Dive Bar status it has here on yelp. In summary, I'd go back, but probably not until after exploring what the rest of New Haven has to offer first.

Mirabelles joins a growing list of solid brunch spots in Burlington. Of course, the popularity of this cafe and pastry shop comes with a long wait. The hostess tended to underestimate the wait time and they also ran out of a couple of specials so it would behoove you to arrive early. If you do end up waiting, the large display of cakes and pastries are sure to make you salivate. By the time we were seated, two of the specials were wiped off the board so I settled on the popover with herb-scrambled eggs and hash browns. The popovers run out quite frequently so get them while you can. These are Yorkshire pudding-like hollow rolls that are cut in half and stuffed with scrambled eggs. It was a little on the bland side and I wish it came with some sausage or bacon. I also tried a sausage, spinach, and mushroom omelet, which provided the savory flavor I was missing from my popover. The omelet came with your choice of toast (the baguette was amazing). I was most impressed with the hash browns here. They are cooked as a giant pancake and divided up into slices. The outer layers were perfected crispy with the inside mixed with sauteed onions. Each breakfast plate also came with fresh fruit, which left me feeling quite satisfied. If not for the wait, I would definitely be more inclined to come here more often for Sunday brunch. Their breakfast menu has a nice balance between sweet and savory and you leave feeling comfortably full.

I went to Mirabelles on a Saturday morning for brunch. The wait was only 15 minutes which, compared to the other brunch places in Burlington, was great. I ordered the breakfast scramble and basically modified everything which wasn't a problem at all. I ended up with an egg-white scramble with goat cheese, spinach, tomatoes, and avocado. It came with french baguette toast and fresh fruit. It was delicious! The french baguette was the best part, but I particularly liked that the eggs were not greasy and were delicious as well. The fruit selection was not that impressive, but I still appreciated the side of fruit. I also tried the banana walnut pancakes that came with walnuts and powdered sugar on top which were quite good as well. I really enjoyed my brunch here and I look forward to going back and trying something new. Another great thing about Mirabelles is that they have a delicious selection of pastries, so don't forget to stop by the pastry counter on your way out for dessert! They make delicious cakes and are definitely a place to consider when you are looking for a cake for a special occasion.

the most fantastic meal I've ever had in my 5 years in the city. Fully deserving 5 yelp stars, 2 michelin stars, should be given 3 instead 2 ny times stars. went for an anniversary dinner, and they gave us custom menus...it had the date and "Happy Anniversary" on the top of our menus. complimentary glass of champagne on top of that. AND, on our dessert, they wrote Happy Anniversary with the sauce. I mean... if that isn't top class service, I don't know what is. top notch the atmosphere is very upscale, almost traditional dining experience. nothing amazing, just very enjoyable now for the amazing food... I'm Korean, and I love my Korean food. I hate places like Danji or Hanjan that are trying this "fusion korean" - which in my opinion, is overly westernized to suite western taste buds and have lost the core essence of Korean cuisine. Jungsik, however, does the most amazing job at being Korean, but at the same time, making it completely different. We opted for the a la carte instead of the tasting menu. it was cheaper and i got to order what I wanted. I won't go for the specifics - just order whatever you want. we had 4-5 dishes I think, and every single one of them just completely blew my mind we ordered a dessert. as I mentioned above, they wrote Happy Anniversary on our plate. WHO DOES THAT THESE DAYS? Seriously, the best service I've had EVER in my life from a restaurant. If you're asian, and you want to celebrate whatever that needs celebrating, come here. Tell them what the special occasion is beforehand on the opentable message or call them beforehand. You won't be dissapointed

We were a group of 10 people and had a birthday dinner here. All of the appetizer are very  delicious x10s and the presentation is excellent. The bill came out so much but it's because we drank several bottle of wine... If I have VIP guests, def will take them here!
Exquisite! One of the best meals I've ever had. The short ribs are to die for. Phenomenal service! Great atmosphere. Great wine list! They made my husband's birthday extra special.

My favorite spot in Nyc, my nephew put me on to Pio Pio family style dining. I make a point of going here at least once a month. Best Calamari in the city, order the red Sangria by the pitcher, one glass is not enough. Seafood is great, I make sure I order the Matador Combo and another dish. Inexpensive and classy at the same time. Great staff and great atmosphere. And don't forget to order desert!

I had the pleasure of visiting this restaurant and I loved it. I must say when I first entered in it was not at all what I expected. It was a slow start it took about 5-10 minutes for them to seat us. The receptionist left and came back about 3 times before someone else sat us but once we did it was amazing. They lead us from the reception area through the bar area and from there the restaurant opens up and it is beautiful. The atmosphere in there is very great for a subtle lowkey date. My friend and I ordered the Juanita's Chicken which is a whole rotisserirre chicken meant to be shared (as told by our waiter). I got Saffron Rice and Red Beans and they got french fries and tostones. We also got a half of pitcher of sangria with no dessert and everything came out to $48! The chicken was very good, moist and well seasoned. The rice and beans reminded me of my grandmothers cooking and the tostones with the garlic sauce were, lack of a better word, poppin' (lol) Our waiter was very attentive as were the clean up crew. Our waiter kept an eye on us from a distance and would call people over to clean up what we finished. I do plan on coming here again. I loved it!

The restaurant is family style dining so the portions are HUGE. It was crowded Friday night when we went and the wait for a table was 30-50 minutes. The salchipapas (chopped hotdog and French fries) were good and the various sauces were amazing. The tostones y amarillo/maduros were good as well. The rice and beans, however, were not enough for one person let alone four! The empanadas were great to me- smaller than I'm used to, but thicker. My S.O. Did not like them because there were olives in them and he doesn't eat olives. All in all a great experience- be sure to go when it's less busy, because it's impossible to navigate between tables if you're larger than size 1.

What can I say about you PIO PIO except thank you for increasing my pant size with your seductive yumminess.  My gym treadmill thanks you. We came here for dinner a few times and I can honestly say I never get tired of the food. The portions are perfect for sharing - highly recommend the Matador Combo. If you plan on doing anything besides sleeping after this, then you can downsize to the Peruvian combo. This one has less sides. I have to say that the very first time I came to the restaurant and ordered the Matador Combo, I DID NOT (LORD HELP ME) expect such large plates. On another occasion, I went to dinner with some very dear friends and I let them order the Matador Combo just to see their faces get swollen with disbelief when the food came and they realized they were going to eat all that between the 2 of them... yeah, I should have warned them... but it was entertaining! Remember that you can always substitute the sides (I always switch out the french fries for sweet plantains). You can always order other things on the menu but since Pio Pio is famous for its chicken....that is what I eat. This particular location which is 604 Tenth Avenue (between 43rd & 44th Streets) has a good atmosphere. Very trendy as it is in the chic Hells Kitchen area.  There are several tables and booths overlook a large double-floor dining room underneath a ceiling made of thousands of randomly-woven tree branches.   Where this particular location gets 3 stars is the letter grade (non-newyorkers, this is the health inspection grade). It fluctuates between A and "grade pending" (aka, we got lower than a B, but don't want to show it)... way too often for my linking! All the other locations don't seem to have this problem, not sure what goes no here, but I refuse to eat there when its grade pending.

People loves this place and I just don't get it - I thought it was because I went to the murray hill location, and so last minute changes and instead of eating Fried Chicken and Waffles, I had to meet E all the way in HK and this location is definitely not like the other locations. The facade looks like a fine dining restaurant rather than Pio Pio. They sat us downstairs, and the interior looks cool and all, but the designer didn't think about the noise level that bounces off the walls covered in timber. It was super loud, I couldn't even hear anything that E was telling me here. E ordered us the following items: Ensalada De Avocado sliced avocado, fresh lettuce, tomatoes and vegetables, tossed in a homemade dressing. - seriously, I could have made this salad. Like nothing about this salad was hard or complicated.....bleh. Salchipapa sliced frankfurters & french fries - the frankfurters were the only thing that I didn't mind eating and that's not saying much Ceviche Mixto * fresh corvina, shrimp, octopus & calamari marinated in lime juice & mixed with red onions, cilantro and rocoto hot pepper, served with sweet potato and choclo corn - heavily breaded and just not good Juanita's Chicken one whole rotisserie chicken marinated in mama juanita's authentic recipe - eh, boring. You have to constantly dip this chicken into the green sauce just to make it semi good. I am sorry, but this dish is lame, why do people love this? I got hot green tea, because I don't eat this sort of food and I love how they serve you tea without a saucer, where in the hell am I going to put my used tea bag? I also got food poisoning here - seriously, been here once and now twice....never again. I am not a fan of this place and I still don't get the hype.

Price is double of what is advertised here. The staff or owner is not apologetic about it either. It's a kind of service that makes you question the entire approach of this restaurant. I won't recommend it
Great atmosphere.  Food was good.  Wait staff attentive.  I recommend it.

Went here for my 33rd birthday specifically for the interior architecture. But I must say the food did not disappoint. All of my friends had a real great time. The drinks were amazing and the food delicsh.

Im used to going to the original location on Northern blvd in Queens but decided on this location for lunch with a group of friends. The decor inside is really interesting. Definitely has a more upscale vibe than Northern blvd. And the service seems to be better as well. The bartender and our waiter were the best! Now the food was amazing. ..normally I get the Matador combo..but this time I ordered the Jalea. I ordered the small and Im glad I did. I shared this with a friend and we each had two full servings, and their were still leftovers.The seafood was fried perfectly and wasnt greasy. We also ordered the plantains and rice and beans and they great as well. Our group shared pitchers of sangria and that was very good too..a bit sweet for me but enjoyable. Will definitely return..

Amazing place to get lunch! The genius of  Jason Sobocinski (of Caseus Cheese) and Mike Farber (of Mikro). As noted on their online menu, it was created to supply smoked meats for their other restaurants. I had the grass fed beef brisket with crispy slaw over hand cut fries with the NC apple cider vinegar sauce and a side of mac and cheese. It was a great flavor bomb of a concoction, one that I will be ordering again soon! The best BBQ place in the area!

Fantastic place right on franklin and N 15th street. They have a big round bar and about 10 picnic tables inside. Waitress service for drinks. Up to the lithen window for food. Fries with dipping sauces are a great snack for drinking beer with. Perrogis too but less filling. A lot of the beers are made at the brewpub. The "Clifford Pl." is a can't go wrong APA made with Simcoe and Amarillo hops. Simply delicious. They also have a selection of house English and German beers. The mild and Witt beer are both enjoyable. The raichbier smoked beer is a bit too smoky for me, I like more subtlety. The piece de resistance is the Tupelo IPA. Dank tropical fruits and dangerously drinkable imperial IPA offering is seriously awesome. Worth coming just for it. Very reasonable prices. Fun atmosphere. Not kid unfriendly during the day for you parents that like to have a quiet beer with your family.
Place sucks!!!!! Bad food, bad drinks, not worth it unless you're having a quick beer with a group.
Loved the food. Loved the beer. But the crappy 90's themed "Applebee's" style music really made me question the aesthetics of this place. Fuck you Spin Doctors and Sugar Ray.

Decent beer, good food, horrible music.  Went on a Friday night, had the pork knuckles and the braised short ribs.  Short ribs - The meat was good, fall off the bone tender, but the sauce that it was 'braised' in was more like a thick red BBQ sauce.  The pork knuckle  was good, but again the gravy/sauce was eh. Would have stayed longer but the music drove us away.  At first it was a bad playlist from the early 90's then it went into horrible top 40 hits.

Loved this place.  Get there soon because once the word gets out, there will always be a long wait.  I went with a large group and so I was able to try a few dishes. Drinks The Louie Louie was outstanding.  Big crowd favorite Venitian Spritz - I loved it.  Would absolutely order it again.  Simple, just what I wanted. For appetizers, We had the Octopus.  Tasty, I'd order it again.  Good flavoring. Scallop - Very good, but there's only one scallop.  It was awesome though. Main Lasagna - awesome.  5/5.  I'd order it again.  Perfectly done pasta.   Taglioni Sasicca - I just had a bite of it but it was also very tasty.  Will try it next time I go.   We had the flan and some other crunchy dessert, both which were fabulous.   Ambiance, 5/5.  Great lighting, perfect volume, service outstanding. Of note, they have some options for open bar with big parties and I would highly recommend open bar.  They were generous with their drinks. Afterwards, we went to the bar/club downstairs.  Super cute and trendy.  Again, go soon and early because it's going to get busy.

Really good Italian food! Friendly & attentive staff and owner. The other reviews are correct - start with the squash blossom fritters then segue to he Chilean sea bass and / or wonderful penne bolognese. Small bar so arrive early. Bon Appetite!

This is a great place for any holiday or special occasion. So far Ive been to Mulberry Street for Christmas Eve, Valentines Day, Mothers Day, countless birthdays and any other excuse my family could come up with just to go back. We all agree, we love this place. Between my whole family and myself we have probably tried the entire menu and we have yet to taste anything bad. Everything always comes out delicious and in impeccable time. The only waiting Ive done at Mulberry Street is for the occasional table and its well worth it considering the house specials seem to be updated constantly with new meals you wont find anywhere else and unique twists on classic favorites. Regardless of when in the year you go there, your gonna find something on that menu you just love.

I had friends visiting from Michigan and we wanted Indian food. I used the navi system in my car and choose Karma. What and excellent choice!!! The service was Awesome (Shout Out to Michael) the food was the BEST I have had. We met one the of the owners, Bobby, personable, friendly and a pleasure to chat with. I will Absolutely be back to experience The Wonderful buffet as well.

Hubby and I took my bff here for her first experience with Indian food! She's slightly sheltered when it comes to worldly cuisines but was ready to try something new... Karma did not disappoint! Hubby asked for his "Lamb Vindaloo" spicy and the kitchen delivered. BFF had Chicken Tikka Masala which was fragrant and creamy- the chicken was perfectly done and not stewed to within an inch of its life. I had the Saag Paneer which was also fantastic. The service was also great! They seemed to work as a well oiled team with various servers and other staff attending to our needs- which were few and far between- nothing better than a water glass that is ALWAYS full! Overall, a relaxed, enjoyable dining experience with excellent service and yummy food- looking forward to leftovers!

Came here for drinks so I can't comment on the food.  The atmosphere was great.  It wasn't loud which was perfect since it was a first date.   I got the Clay-kiser which was just a little tart but no complaints.  The bartender was attentive.  I want to come here again to try the food.

I have found a new favorite breakfast/brunch place! It's so nice to find a restaurant that's so welcoming of patrons with all kinds of dietary preferences. RPH has vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options that are just as delicious and varied as everything else on the menu! Small touches like available soy milk for coffee and butter substitute made me feel like the restaurant owners really wants to make everyone happy. The service was friendly too! I ordered the popeye tofu scramble (tofu, spinach, mushrooms, avocado), which comes with a substantial amount of home fries and toast. I also split an order of the vegan pancakes because I really wanted to try them. I loved the scramble, but the vegan pancakes FLOORED me. They were light and tasty! I was excited to find out that RPH frequently make special vegan pancakes like tiramisu flavor. The wait (about 30 minutes) was annoying, but the food was definitely worth the trip. I will definitely be coming back here and recommending it to friends and family!
A great place for breakfast. Tried the Tiramasu pancakes on their special board. Very good. The staff is very attentive and always pleasant.

MY NEW BREAKFAST JOINT.  Why it took us so long to try RPH out is beyond me but we are hooked.  For one they have Gluten Free pancakes!!!  I had Blueberry pancakes with strawberries on top so amazing, granted a few were undercooked in the middle because of all the berries.  My fiancee had the eggs benedict, his eggs were a little over cooked, but he still liked it didn't love it like me.  Prices are reasonable.  No wait if you don't mind sitting at the counter.  Will be back in two weeks when I get back from a work trip!

Funny how Yelp reviews come about! Last week I had found out through my fellow yelpers (LOL love that term) about this place and saw pretty high marks for it. I decided that I would take my Dad and Mom( they are like Siamese twins lol) here for Father's Day since he had once told me about how much he despised the Ridgewood Pancake House and maybe this would cheer him up. I called to make a reservation on the premise that it would be packed since my dad like myself, does not like to wait and we would want an immediate table. I spoke with the owner named Rick who politely informed they don't take reservations because they tried that system once and it ended in disaster. I laughed and he said the best time to come was before 10:30 when the church crowd comes by and it gets packed. I said I appreciated the tip and said I would see him next week. Then out of the blue, he said the special next week would be red velvet pancakes. I thought that was very thoughtful and courteous and yet at the same time he sounded very routine and blasé about it This incidentally is a good way to describe the Rutherford Pancake House. Food: 3 stars: My Mom and Dad ordered a combo breakfast which came with pancakes, Eggs, Bacon, Sausage and Home fries ($10.95) that they were happy with although the pancakes were a little too cold. The Eggs, bacon Sausage and Home Fries were all cooked perfectly even though they were a little bland for my taste and could have used a bit more seasoning. As far as their namesake pancakes go, I ordered Blueberry Pancakes which came in a stack of 4 that the waitress said were huge along with 2 eggs. I was looking forward to hubcap sized pancakes. Instead I got pancakes slightly bigger than a compact disc. The blueberries were mixed in with the batter as opposed to just thrown on top. The Pancakes themselves were good and had a unique flavor which I think comes from some type of corn flour. They were good solid pancakes but not over the top good (I feel some blueberries or compote added on top would have helped). The Eggs were ok. Cooked right but bland A nice plus was they offered real 100% maple syrup with your pancakes as opposed to simply offering Aunt Jemima.( I'm serious the house syrup is Aunt Jemima LOL) While it cost $1.99 extra, it was a definite bonus. Service: 5 Stars:  Service was outstanding and professional. You can tell that this is a place that is used to being busy all the time and the staff is well-equipped to deal with the oncoming traffic. The waitress was friendly and efficient, taking our order in a timely manner. The entire wait staff runs like a Swiss watch. Coffee is constantly being refilled and everybody seems to function as if they are a well-oiled machine. Nobody is out of place or looking rushed or exacerbated even though they are busy and always in motion. Our waitress checked back to make sure we liked everything. Atmosphere: 4 stars: This place is a cross between an old-fashioned coffee shop and a diner. The place is very no-frills as far as décor goes. The noise level is reasonable even though it is packed. Tables and booths were standard. There were a lot of families here as well as slightly older people. Everybody seemed at ease even though it was busy. Verdict: This is an unusual place to categorize and rate. The food was average and at very reasonable prices but not so good that you just have to come back again. However, this is a place that I would come back to again but not necessarily come to on a regular basis. The service was extraordinarily efficient and polite but in more of an assembly-line manner as opposed to personality. I give the place 3 stars as opposed to 2 because the service as aforementioned was better than great, the pancakes are good and the owner took the time to be detailed with me on the phone. But something is missing here, its missing the WOW factor that makes it stand out. It's not a place that I would have suspected to be as busy as it is to be honest with you yet the owner said it was slow for a Father's day! Go figure. I think I was expecting better from this place than I thought, but overall it is a good solid no frills place that serves a variety of food in a timely manner. It's worth going to.  Try it out and hopefully you will get the WOW that I didn't get.
better than the diners

Friendly staff and great food, what else could you want for breakfast?!?!  Lots of options, starting with fresh squeezed OJ through steak and eggs.  They are more than happy to cater to various dietary restrictions.  Properly cooked eggs and tasty pancakes really start off the day on the right food.

LOVE this place!  I went two days in a row, in fact!  I adore both the spinach/bacon/goat cheese pizza and mushroom pizza.  My friend let me try a slice of her spicy shrimp pizza and that was excellent too!  Personal pizzas run from $10-12, which is a little pricey, but they're high quality and delicious, served with a little salad.Sandwiches look good too. This place it pretty tiny - seats around 30 people at max, so get there early and keep it to groups of 2!  We saw many disappointed groups of 4 walk in and find the place completely full.  The servers are very nice and gracious as well.   The cinnamon roll bread pudding is decent, but not as decadent as it sounds.  They serve it with a side bowl of extra whipped cream, which I think it hilarious.   Happy Hour runs from 4-7pm at the bar only and pizzas are $5!  I haven't attended yet to find out if they're giving you a full-size pizza, which would mean a 50-60% discount off the menu price.

Really pleased with this little restaurant. Went for lunch with a friend. The place was busy but we got a table right away. The lunch menu is so reasonably priced and the food is great! I shared the grilled pear salad and spinach, goat cheese, and bacon pizza with my friend. The portions were what lunch portions should look like, not huge but enough to leave the restaurant satisfied. The food was great, the service prompt and attentive, and the overall experience super pleasant. The restaurant has floor to ceiling windows for optimal people watching on West Broadway. I will be back again and again for lunch!

Very disappointing.  The food was OK but the service was poor.  I downloaded their app to get a $5 discount but it took them 15 minutes to decide that they couldn't do it.  THey shouldn't have an app which they encourage if they don't know how to use it and then make phone calls to the owner who still doesn't know how to use it.  They should have offered to take off the $5 or not charge for the coffee which they forgot to add on until we asked for the discount.

Word to the wise: Perhaps it's not such a good idea to visit a restaurant on their second day open. I learned this the hard way when I showed up at Rucola in Boerum Hill, Brooklyn. The anticipation of the opening of this new spot that touts northern-Italian cuisine was palpable when I arrived on Friday to a swarm of patrons outside the door. Probably because it's the baby of alums of the Prime Meats, Death & Co., and Cafe Boulud "restaurant titan trifecta." And I fell for it. I even waited for over two hours to be seated, which I would never do! This time was an exception, as the hours pass pleasantly when you have a friend who works at a bar down the street and you're not yet famished. Cut to us merrily merging forces and sitting at a table for three at 10:15 pm. With some trifecta power of our own and a short listed offering of 5 plates and 2 desserts, it was only natural to order the whole menu. Turns out even that was not enough and we wound up having to double up on items. It also would have been considerate if they had mentioned one minor  detail: They had no power! Excuse me? How could you confidently invite patrons to spend a pretty penny (yeah, it wasn't cheap) on what they think is a fully supported menu of food worth a 2-hour plus wait, and you don't have a functioning fridge and burner? Well it didn't go unnoticed, as our food left much to be desired - and we ordered everything! I will commend Rucola for the ambiance set by perfectly placed rustic wooden tables, romantic candle-lighting, and an extremely genial front of the house. Our server was genuinely bubbly and Julian Brizzi, managing partner and "name-taker" of the night, was all smiles and enthusiasm as he jotted our phone number and nonchalantly mentioned it's a 2-hour wait for 2 - which couldn't help beget the "don't call us, we'll call you" sentiment. If you still feel hungry after a meal out, there is a screw loose somewhere. I don't appreciate dishes overpriced for their portions, but can give a pass if the food is at the least thoughtful and tasty. But the leave-you- feeling-hungry, uninteresting, pricey fare doesn't jive with me. And this was Rucola in a nutshell. Two bottles of wine made this pill easier to swallow, but my party was still all too aware of our disappointment. We wound up with two meat and cheese plates - the second, one of those duplications that came at the end of the meal when we still needed more to put in our mouths. These were acceptably edible and as interesting as a charcuterie board might be, showcasing three of each, but in a portion that did not reflect the $19 a pop price. Move to the two salads on the menu that looked almost identical. One presented itself as an octopus salad, but had more tasteless arugula than the thread-thin fish. The other with radishes and dandelion greens was as robust and intricate as it sounds: not. Whatever else was in them to contribute some sort of flavor failed. It was unfortunate that the octopus was another repeat dish. But excitement abounded when the pasta plate approached, as surely this was fail-safe. We were so confident in this homemade fettuccine carbonara with ramps that we doubled up on this dish right from the start - only to be informed post-ordering they only had one left (hence the second, but unfulfilling helping of octopus salad.) Well, we found it wouldn't have been worth the carb consumption. A blessing in disguise? How do I know this pasta did not meet anyone's tongue in the kitchen? Because they would have dumped the whole batch had the overload of salt assaulted them as it did us. The resulting taste was akin to the all too familiar experience of merrily salting along when the loose cap of the shaker demonically flies off, a flood of salt crystals rushing out like a broken dam. When it comes to salting, a heavy hand can be a bad, bad thing - and it was. The only thing that was notable by comparison was the whole fish on the bone, decorated with clams and a simple lemon, oilve oil, and basil pesto. This was good as far as these things go, but nothing outstanding, as one might hope for with such a hefty price. An assorted cookie platter was not a comprehensive dessert by any stretch but the hodge podge sufficed as little sugary nibbles. The chocolate cake tasted like it was compliments of Betty Crocker, living up to the after-thought it probably was without an appearance menu. And the soupy rice pudding - ah, make that two. Oh right, hungry still - was the best of the three options, with a rhubarb compote that added a spruce of color if not a benign sweetness. Hunger plus mediocrity equals over $80 per person? So I guess we won't be doing that again - not unless I can be assured that all the electrical appliances are powered and there is a salt patrol on duty. Even with these things, the thought put into the dishes needs to be more deliberate, focused and creative. Not to mention better supported by substantial ingredients.

bleh - unfortunately all I can comment on the details of this experience. But I completely agree with all the other reviews giving it 1 star. Btw Frankie's is quite good, as is Daniel, Gilt and Gramercy. But the food here is nothing to match any of those places - it's hard to imagine veterans from those restaurants producing what is served here.
Wonderful food, great service, beautiful restaurant. We had appetizers, entrees and desserts and all was delicious. People were happy, babies were well treated, crowded and happy.

This is what I have to say 'bout Boerum Hill newcomer Rucola. I am super happy to have it in the neighborhood. It's exactly what we needed. Everyone that works there is outrageously friendly. Which stands out to me, especially given the hipster pedigree. The place is gorgeous. Sure, it's small, and a little loud. Who cares? The wine list is full of serious bargains, and the cocktail list is not messing around either. The food isn't quite there yet, but nothing was off to the point of mentioning it.
