I just think they haven't hit their stride in the kitchen, but I fully expect they will. Can't wait to see what they do for breakfast.

Rucola is perfect as a neighborhood restaurant, but not destination-worthy as of yet.  Solid drink menu with inventive and low-sugar cocktails, pleasant service, a cute if somewhat jammed space, and friendly staff.  The food just didn't blow any of my party of 4 away; I would not point to anything being particularly bad, but nothing was particularly great either.  The soft shell crab dish seemed oversalted and overbreaded; the chicken was oversalted, and my fish dish was somewhat bland.  Again, perfectly great spot if you're already in the neighborhood, but if you don't live around there, there are probably equally good places to go.   Nothing on the menu particularly wowed me to begin with, either... again, not bad in any particular way, just not particularly Italian, and not many things that grabbed me. At any rate, I'm pulling for them, as the people running the place seem very cool and friendly.  Considering it was packed when we ate there at 8 on a Wednesday, it looks like I don't have to pull for them too hard...

So I wanted Italian in the area and found this quaint little place at the corner of Bond and Dean...reminded me of Seersucker on Smith when I went in. Was early so I sat at the bar...bar stool was uncomfortable but oh well. Hooks underneath the bar for bags and coats. Seems like a neighborhood bar, the guy beside me was talking to staff and diners alike who all lived around the area! Friend came, we were sat promptly...host made sure to check in with us even though we had to wait 15 mins or so. I had that ear-shaped pasta with salt cod and broccoli rabe...LOVED it. I polished it off...was about to lick my plate. The broccoli rabe was amazing...not bitter at all. The salt cod was..interesting, wasn't too salty or overwhelming. Only complaint: TOO LITTLE (well, I am greedy so...) My gf had the baked pasta with cheese...same thing, amazingness in too little a portion. Prices were decent for the quality of food I must say...I wish there was more though! I cannot wait to come back again!!!! :) Tip-bits: Cash only...for now Gets busy so come early and wait at the bar Single unisex bathroom to the R in the back, by the kitchen 3 draft beers only for now Good for couples/dates/small groups Get loud when busy Couple of outdoor tables

Wow...one of my best mexican burrito experience... Fresh as ever tortillas made in front of your eyen and onto your plate with the taste you choose..!! ...delicious...already hungry for more... Finally a fresh mexican food place...!! A MUST COME ... MUST EAT

Panchero's is a welcome addition to the Hamilton community. Previously, to satisfy my burrito craving I would have to drive out of my way at least 20-30 minutes. The inside is very clean and nicely decorated, but not presumptuous. It is essentially a "fast food" place, but with attention to detail. I came around 8pm, it was not too busy, but the people making the food were still very efficient and attentive. They serve tacos, burritos, and quesadillas that are custom-made to your liking. The tortillas are fresh pressed and then stuffed with all the ingredients you would like. I ordered the steak burrito and got every topping imaginable in it (except guacamole, which I believe was the only thing extra anyway). My friend got the carnitas burrito, including guacamole, and my boyfriend got a chicken burrito. We all enjoyed our food, it was fresh and filling. The steak was on the medium side I would say, as to my liking. Also, I was very impressed with the chips, salsa, and guac. Very tasty. And the chips were blue corn chips, a very nice touch. The salsa was on the milder side in my opinion, but that will satisfy a broader audience. They have plenty of extra hot sauces around to add your desired level of spice to your meal. Price-wise, I would not consider this "cheap", but I would not call it unreasonable either, especially considering the quality and portion size that you get. Overall, I think this place is off to a very good start and I would definitely come again to see if there are any changes and to sample some of the other items. I have already recommended it to some of my friends.

Had a very nice dinner here.  The room is feels small, but it lends itself well to the experience.  Bar is a little crowded, but it does give the restaurant a busy and vibrant feel.  Our food (steak and pasta) was very good.  Mixed crowd of 30's - 60's.  High-energy, bustling feel to the place.

My gf and I ate valentines dinner here. The food was amazing and the service was even better. A bit crowded but worth the trip from north jersey. The waiter we had was incredible, he made us feel right at home.

Quite a surprise. They've only been open for 2 months. Saw a couple cops having dinner before their shift. Everyone knows local cops have the best knowledge about the best food places. Location is a bit tricky. They are located at the far end of the mall. Plenty of parking spaces. Ambiance is 3 out of 5. They've done some good renovations. Far East Asian theme. You can choose between bar, table/booth or hibachi.  We choose a table since we wanted sushi rolls. They were helpful and attentive. My guess since we were first timers and they want to word of mouth. Food is better than average. Decent presentation and proportions are appropriate. Prices are a bit more than the area normally offers. This is in Bayonne after all. But it's a good addition and should be tired. Not everyone will like it I think but it's an experience worth taking.

Wow, what a big, beautiful restaurant for this little town of Bayonne. The boyfriend & I got hibachi dinners- he got steak, I got shrimp. Both dinners came with fried rice AND noodles with grilled veggies and a shrimp appetizer and soup & salad. The food was so fresh oh my lord did they surprise me. And everything was just so delicious! Only downfall is that they don't have their liquor license yet but I will definitely be back when they do!

I've been here 3 times already, 1 for sushi, 1 for hibachi, and one for lunch take out. I really like this place. It is pretty close to the house so its easy for us to get to. Also the parking is a lot so you dont have to deal with the horror of Bayonne street parking. The hibachi was alot of fun and the chef was very funny. We enjoyed ourselves very much. You got ALOT of food for your dish. i have the shrimp and filet mignon dish. The only minus was that the food was a little too salty. Sushi was very wood too and not too pricey. Lunch special was decent. 2 rolls for $9 3 rolls for $11 with soup or salad. We will becoming regulars in no time!

New place on Astoria Blvd and one of the best in the neighborhood.  We had biscuits and gravy, dirty rice, and collard greens.  These were all amazing and portion size was great.  Also had beef brisket, which was excellent, but portion was a little weak.  Will be back very soon.  Great southern food with a great tasty twist.

Just moved in the neighborhood and I am really happy this place is around the corner! For sure, this is going to be my favorite burger place! I can't wait to eat the rest of the menu! The burger and the fries were absolutely delicious, very tasty and not greasy at all!! The place is also really soothing and well decorated!

This is one of our favorite restaurants! Kenny the owner and his wife are personable and the sushi is always fresh and delicious. Great food and reasonable prices! Great for a business lunch or family dinner! My family gives it 5 stars because we always have a delicious meal and good time and visit several times a week! We love Mizu - thank you for coming to West Windsor!

This isn't the 1st time I've eaten at Andrews, and won't be the last My favorite is his Falafel Sandwich which I can not have enough of. But today I ordered his Vegetarian Salad, which is out of this World. All fresh Ingredients and very tasty.  I would give this man a thumbs up for all the work he puts into all his cooking. His soups are excellent and all gluten free and creamy, Again I have a favorite of his soups. Butternut Squash, and before I started eating at Andrews, I never had this soup. It's simply delicious!!!!!!  This item alone I would give a 5 Star. I heard that he was Bill Clinton's private chef, I don't know how the man let this owner of this Cafe go. I agree with Riss H. He does deserve a Nobel Prize for his delicious gluten free healthy cooking.  His ideas are Fantastic!!!

Me and my friends were tried their soups and gourmet sandwiches, this is our favorite place and the Dinner specials was out standing we highly recommend any one who would like to eat healthy and the same time tasty food... this is the place in east no dough about that. they have fruit smoothies, MOST IMPORTANTLY we had enrage booster coffee It doesn't have any caffeine, it has over 200 minerals and vitamins, fast solo dillies we are coming again and again the bet ever we came a cross in east cost. Thank you to the person who run and the Owner !! your food are the Bet of every one and you are setting and example to every one in town! Bless your business and you!! we so your product it is real organic food the day we were their we sow the delivery you got from NY. wow we love your product and quality of produce you getting! and we are proud of you you should be get Nobel price for feeding healthy ! don't bother about who is Rich d.

Ordered 3 sandwiches earlier today for pickup. Had to throw all of them out unfortunately. Ordered the Rainforest for a vegan friend. 3 bites into it and she pulled out a piece of some sort of wrapper or plastic wrap the length of the sandwich with her teeth. The tofu was not even cooked. It seemed like it was taked out of the package and thrown onto it. Ordered the Vietnamese. Was entirely soaked in grease to the point that the foil it was wrapped in fell apart with the sandwich. The "steak" was cooked to the point it chewed like rubber and the fresh asian slaw that should have at least been crunchy was just as soggy as the rest from all the grease. Also ordered a portobello that lacked any type of flavor that could have been involved in it. I called the order in and was hung up on by whoever took the ordet without asking a name or anything. It's very hard to support local business when this is what you get. Horrible food for high prices and service to match.

If Union Bar & Kitchen does not have a full, over capacity, Happy Hour crowd by mid October, I would be very surprised. I don't even know where to begin with this place. I guess it helps that they aren't in a very heavily congested area in terms of foot traffic because the Happy Hour crowd around 5:15 was a bit light, but it was also to our advantage because we got to pig out on some deliciously shucked Blue Point Oysters for $1... Yes, a, dollar. We then ordered the fried oysters for $2 (happy hour pricing) and they were pretty delicious. They have some sort of tartar sauce underneath them which makes them even tastier. Finally, the pork belly sweet BBQ sliders ($2) were REALLY good. They have an incredible avocado slaw and the jalapeño gives it just the right touch. The chef came out personally to chat with everyone which was a nice touch. He's a little insane, but a little insane make a great dish, and like most artists, he takes pride in his work. Also, I forgot to mention that the Happy Hour draft beers were $4 and the $5 Sauvignon blanc was some of the best picked wine I've tasted for a Happy Hour. Like I said, if this place doesn't become impossible to get a seat at for Happy Hour, then New Yorkers are doing something very wrong.

We were there tonight for dinner the entrées were pretty good the chicken tacos were bland, service was a little slow and the side dishes like the rice and beans were bland but overall it is good not great Mexican food for the price.

5 Stars.....One for flavor, variety and overall crispy, flaky goodness.  One for Stella - you'll love her instantly.  One for low prices but high quality.  One for all those sides of homemade chimichurri or salsa sauce.  One for homemade flan.  Get some. I had or shared the following empanadas: mac & cheese (hands down my favorite), banana rum raisin (my second favorite), broccoli & cheddar, calabrese, spinach & mushroom, spinach & cheddar. I did not eat the following but feedback was that they were absolutely delicious: spicy chicken, beef & cheese. That's about half the flavors that Stella's actually offers.  Which means I have to go back there again soon and have a little empanada eating contest with myself.

I just want start by describing what I found in the water they gave me. I had a gnat floating in the water with the ice. I then asked for a new one and guess what they gave me, a unclean glass with avocado residue. I guess they do not clean their dishes carefully or notice that it was not clean. The place is small and get packed quick but the food was decent but it left me a bad taste in my mouth thing how all other dishes may not be clean. I usually order the egg roll vermicelli or the pork rice dish which is a Vietnamese standard dish.

My family and I recently ate here and I must say there service is slow and their plates and utensils are dirty.  I'd hate to imagine what their kitchen looks like.  Their priced increased and they reduced portion size as well.   I'm giving 2 stars for decent vietnamese food.  I wonder if its still under same ownership.  The place use to be clean, faster service and food tasted better.   Now, I'll add this onto my "do not dine list".

A random strip mall along Belleville ave.. Over the years it has been has been dominated by the East West Filipino/Asian grocery... And for 14 years tucked away in the corner... Hiding in plain sight is this hidden gem. Ordered takeout... Everything was packaged well and survived in a back pack... On a ride on a motorcycle ride home without a drop or morsel spilled.. great flavors and spices.. looking forward to winter and a warm bowl O'pho.

If you like craft beer and want to see what your local brewmaster has to offer, this is the place to go. And yes, NJ does have good beer! Lots of taps that get rotated regularly so you get great variety. You want to talk beer? Say hi to Jesse :-) Food is tasty- great burger, great steak, and my favorite the Reuben (although I am the weirdo that likes it with provolone cheese Lol) This is the spot to go for a friendly, "Cheers" kind of environment.

You can't fully appreciate Poor Henry's without understanding how much history it holds and how much its changed for the better.  For instance, you won't find a better craft beer selection in the area because the owner is passionate about reaching out to brewers throughout the state and beyond to bring a selection of IPAs, Porters, and random seasonal selections on tap that might not otherwise be available.  And with more taps added in the past month, expect the selection to change even more randomly. The salad bar is always well stocked and compliments any meal you get with daily specials that change as often as the beer selection does.  Become a regular and you might find yourself partaking in bottle shares, brew fests, beer pairing dinners, and bourbon beyond your wildest dreams.  Always packed for football games or drinking holidays, while equally popular with families who have been regulars for years, the decor is cozy, with history, unapologetic - Irish restaurant and pub.  Cheers!

This place was ok. It's clean, the food is decent, the drinks are pretty good. But was VERY overpriced for the quality of food you get. I don't mind dropping $120 for a fabulous meal, but it bothers me when what I get would cost me $75 anywhere else. I had the fresh Mozzarella and tomatoes which were just that. No balsamic, no basil. The tomatoes were tasteless and the Mozzarella was sloppily sliced, so the slices were too thick and not as good as they could have been. At $10 for the plate, I'd expect it to at least be done better. We got Calamari, it was ok. Not the best I've ever had, but not the worst either. My husband got the Gnocchi and it was very good. It was just an OK meal. Nothing exciting. DEFINITELY not worth the price.

great personalities, amazing good food quality.  only tip : was so saturatured with salt ( pastas, fish and my fathers chicken dish)   thought my racing heart wouldnt stop that night. i still give good ratings but we gotta cut back. keep the high levels of salt on the street for the winter ice not in the food. . .

I have eaten at the East Hanover diner every Sunday for the past month and the last two times have been terrible from a service perspective. Waited 45 minutes to be severed two weeks ago and 25 minutes today. Waitress staff is terrible and kitchen can not handle the rush. Owners are nice and food is good when you eventually get it. Maybe it would be better to go during a slower time.

I've had two experiences here but I've only eaten here once. We just moved in town and had no idea where to go. The whole experience was meh... The food was ok but nothing special. And we were sitting in what was going to be the band space and I can feel how they were anxiously waiting for us to leave.

We received a very warm greeting upon walking in. Service was friendly and attentive. I had the Hummus wrap and it was really good. The curly fries were also yummy. My boyfriend ordered the Texas BBQ burger. We couldn't believe the size of it! He loved it. The desserts were very tempting, but we were too full. Next time I'll make sure to leave some room to try them. Overall we had a great experience. The new owners have greatly improved the diner. We already look forward to going back.

It's been a while since I visited Ola. First I must say mango MOJITO'S was awesome. My husband had the Sea bass stuffed with  salad, which could of used a little more flavor, I had the seafood paella, good but little loose. Over all, I will visit this place again.
Great Food and presentation

Great atmosphere and excellent service even better food and drinks.  The food is unique and delicious.  The paella is incredible and save room for dessert.  The presentations of all food is sexy and appealing.  This is a must try!

I'm stuck in Newark for days eating crap until I found the gem of place that served delicious pizza & wonderful beer from bartender Lisa.   The beer was ice cold & really comforted this road warrior & the pizza was spectacular.

Came here for dinner a few weeks ago and forgot to review it in my flurry of positive emotions. First off, I want to say that the dining area is my future home's dream dining area--super high ceilings, floor to ceiling windows that let in lots of natural light, dark wood, glass, and steel everything for the modern yet cabiny feely, and lots of farm portraits to keep it oh-so-american. The feel here is upscale and the ambiance matches. We started the night off right with a bottle of Barbaresco Gaja 1991, really excellent! They changed their menu so I have to try to remember what I ordered from the top of my head, but I had a homemade thin-crust pizza as my entree (although it is regularly an appetizer) and tried some of my friends' pork belly dish and steak dish. The pizza was actually very large! Perfect for sharing or for one hungry girl, I would recommend it. The pork belly, while very excellently prepared, wasn't very memorable for me as many Asian restaurants actually prepare it better I think--more flavor. The steak was small but very tender and the side salad it came with was drenched in steak juice, which was amazing. For dessert we had 3 scoops of ice creeam/gelato, which were all very very flavorful without being too sweet. One of them actually didn't taste too different from vanilla, which we indicated on the comments card, and management came right over and comped the whole dish! I was so so so impressed by the care here at Colicchio & Sons that I have been recommending it to all my friends since. The only mishap was that we had to send the check in like 5 times because our server did not udnerstand how to split a credit card. But overall, amazing experience and will definitely come back--soon!
You've got to be kidding me.  Pretentious, inedible menu.  Ridiculous sauce-covered dogshit at $200/plate prices.  Stay away.

This was always a restaurant that's been on my to go list for a long time. I knew I had to come after falling in love with the food at Riverpark. I took my girlfriend here to celebrate her belated birthday and everything was AMAZING! First off the ambiance and decor was very nice. Semi-dark lighting gave the restaurant a very intimate vibe. Definitely good for a date night or to catch up over dinner with a close girlfriend. Secondly, the service was impeccable! Our waitress was very knowledgeable and patient. She had good recommendations for wine and cocktails. With every course that comes out, your plates and utensils are cleared and switched for new ones. This is great so the flavors from your appetizer doesn't mix with your entree and leaves your palette clean. The employees here were super attentive without intruding. 6 stars for service alone! Last but not least, the food was incredible too! I didn't expect any less from Tom Colicchio but the meal exceeded my expectations. First courses; 1. Burrata, sweet corn, heirloom tomatoes, & basil - burrata was creamy and wonderful.The sweet vegetables tasted very fresh and made for a great accompaniment. 2. Baked beau soleil oysters, chorizo, jalapeño & breadcrumbs - the topping was delicious. Crunchy goodness on the outside and perfectly cooked oyster on the inside 3. Chicken liver mousse, sunny side egg, & blueberries - I'm not a huge fan of mousse but this was the perfect consistency. Creamy and savory but not too heavy. The tartness from the blueberries cut the mousse very well. 4. Escargot, garlic confit, smoked bacon & sourdough - not much to say about this but it was delicious as well. If you love escargot and garlic, you will enjoy this dish. Main courses- 1. Skate, radish, citrus & lobster - probably the best skate I've ever had. The fish was cooked perfectly. I just used my fork to pick up a piece and it would flake apart on it's own. Perfection in every bite- the natural butteriness of the skate shined through while holding up it's firm texture. 2. Pork belly, spigarello, sweet corn & Manila clams - Oh. My. God. The most amazing pork belly In the world!!! This dish made every other pork belly dish I've ever tried look like garbage. The skin was super crunchy while the inside was fatty and juicy. Cooked to perfection. My mouth still waters thinking about this pork belly. This is a seasonal restaurant so all the ingredients are very fresh! The one bad thing I had to say is that I feel like there was corn involved in a lot of the dishes. Maybe due to it's seasonal availability at the time I went ... But it made some of the dishes taste very repetitive. Granted everything was cooked very well, I couldn't eat corn for at least a week after that and I am a corn lover. Must go! Definitely recommend!!!! They deserve 10 stars if possible! Don't forget to order the pork belly!

I had never been to a Tom Colicchio restaurant, and was looking forward to having dinner at my first. But overall, it was pretty underwhelming. We were here for a birthday celebration and had several dishes for the table to share. The ricotta, arugula, and farm egg pizza with white truffles was an interesting experience. The white truffle was presented to us from a fancy wooden box and shaved methodically at our table by the chef. The pizza itself however tasted like an average ricotta arugula pizza with some egg on top. The gala apple and rosemary pizza seemed very autumnal, but apples on pizza isn't really my thing. And the baked malpeque oysters tasted like nothing more than jalapeno and breadcrumbs. My favorite thing was probably the spice-rubbed brisket. It was tender, moist, and had a melt-in-your-mouth texture. We were told that the pork shoulder was cooked for 24 hours, and indeed it was tender and flavorful. I had the duck confit, the best of which was the perfect crispy skin. But overall, nothing was really impressive. While everything was done well, the flavor combinations on each plate just didn't work for me. And for a restaurant of this reputation, I was expecting more. Food aside - our server was friendly, and the restaurant was nice. Oh, and the complimentary to-go pumpkin shortbread cookie was gooood.

Craft Beers done right! The variety of craft beers is  extensive... constantly changing.  An all star line up on tap and plenty of  choices in bottle... that beez.in the trap is delicious! Beyond the craft beers, you got chicken and waffles that are airy. Fluffy, crunchy.. and glazed with a sauce your gonna be licking up.. corn.dip,brisket and mac and cheese that can't be beat! Chill out vibe, and simply good stuff!
Great place to hang out. Tvs are updated and the atmosphere is very laid back. Definitely coming back again!
By far best BBQ spot on staten island! Doesnt even feel like staten island inside. Hipster and trendy with an extensive beer list.

Food was awesome. Had chicken/waffels. Others had brisket, fried chicken, and a veggie burger. Sides were great service also great. Just can't say enough about craft house. Will definitely add to my "A" list.
Best selection of Craft Beers on Staten Island, hands down. Delicious comfort food and a friendly staff make this a place you have to try.
Good food.great atmosphere what else can you ask. Home like feeling makes this place special.

We stalked this place until it opened up, and we have never been displeased. The beer selection fantastic, the bartenders are knowledgeable,  and the food is delicious. I love the chicken and waffles, mac and cheese, corn dip and the burgers. The atmosphere is fantastic as well. The bar itself is beautiful and the music is always great!
BYOB. We love this place. Food is always good. I usually get the chicken enchiladas and my husband gets the steak fajitas. Never disappointed and the servers are always friendly and attentive.

Wasn't the  best Mexican place but wansnt the worst.  1 thing though..  Why isn't there queso fresco or creme on the tostada? If it had that would of been perfect.  The tamales were good.  Sadly my rice was hard and my beans weren't that cooked.  Also I'd say it's a tad over priced.  Other then that the service was good and the atmosphere was nice.  I'd come back but Def try something else.

Yelpers,this is the place to be. I've been living in Rahway for about 10 yrs and I'm so mad I didn't try this place sooner. My wife and I brought the kids for a family night out to try this place and I'm glad we did, it was great. They had a little play area for the kids with coloring books and toys so my wife and I talked and relaxed while keeping an eye on them. Chips came out hot and fresh and the salsa was probably the best I ever had. My wife had fish tacos that looked amazing. They came out with a slice of orange on top that I thought was a little different. I had the steak fajitas and I thinks my biggest complaint is that there was way to much. I wish we tried this place years ago. The service and food were awesome!!! Thanks to all see ya soon.

In Early July 2014, we were looking for a meaningful gift to give to our Aunt and Uncle for their 50th Wedding Anniversary and we have received Christmas presents from our niece from this bakery so when we were looking for a bakery to make a cookie cake, we decided to call Mozzicato's Bakery.in Hartford, Ct. We asked if it was possible to order a 15 pound cookie cake for a 50th anniversary and the person we spoke to said they usually only send out 5 or 0 pound cookie cakes, but that hey could do this and we ordered the cookie cake which was shipped to our home in Batavia,NY, When it arrived, we noticed that the cookies at the bottom of the cookie cake we cracked and crushed. It was too late to go out and get a replacement cookie cake so we called the Bakery and spoke to 2 people Gina and then Paulo who said to send photos of the cookie cake for them to see which we did. Paulo told us that he was very sorry for the crushed cookies and that he would replace the cookie cake, but would prefer we pick up the cookie cake instead of shipping it out. Since our daughter and son live in Boston, I asked Paulo if it would be possible for our daughter yo pick this up when she comes home for Christmas and he said this could be done and just to call the shop a few days before and they would get this ready for her. Today my daughter called the bakery to get the cookie cake done and Gina Mozzicato stated that she had no knowledge of an 15 pound cookie cake order and we needed to show the pictures, credit card receipt and email to this effect and either way she said they never make a 15 pound cookie cake and said she would not replace this. This person Gina was very unprofessional in he reply to my daughter and luckily we do have proof of the conversations and what was said to myself as well as my daughter.We are also planning on reporting this to the Better Business Bureau since Paulo made a verbal promise to me that the cookie cake would be replaced with no problem whenever we could arrange to pick it up. I am   a professional person and an Italian American and I would think that a verbal statement would be honored by this bakery and by Paulo instead of  Gina denying ever even making up and shipping this cookie cake to us. I had promised my Aunt and Uncle that I would bring over the cookie cake as soon as I got it and feel very bad that I will be disappointing them. I have 10 photos of the cookie cake which at least 75% of the cookies were crushed. I din't think this bakery deserves any stars and want you to know I signed up for yelp just to post this review,.

I bought several cookie trays for Christmas and not only are they some of the best cookies I have ever had.. the old school Italian's I gave them too were also extremely happy to enjoy the delicious cookies. They were so good, I went back on Christmas eve and picked up 2 more!  Easy in and out and I now have a new christmas tradition!! Thanks you! Buon Natale a tutti !
Excellent food, great pricing and a very friendly staff, my favorite place to eat dinner at now and love the fact its only a mile down the street from me.

Stopped here spur of the moment when on a road trip. Love! Love! Loved this place! I wish I lived closer. I would frequent it often. I had the stuffed plantain and it was amazing. My friends said their food was equally as good. If Im in the area this is the place I will stop.
Very good restaurant, with very hospitable servers. I would definitely recommend it to my friends and peers.

One of the best spots to get mexican food in the city. I'm mexican so my standards of how unique and true to my culture mexican food should be are satisfied in this restaurant. Besides the fact that the staff and place are great. Had de pleasure to met manager William and waitress Laura, both amazing. I definitely recommend this place.
Good option for Mexican in the West Village. Great cocktails and tacos.

One of the best happy hours in Manhattan! Its all week from 4-7. Good service, good food + AMAZING margaritas. They don't skimp on the alcohol even during happy hour. Can't say the same for many places! Love love this place!
Expensive.  Oddball menu. Nothing simple.  Food is very good tho.
Food is good but prices are high, although not completely foreign to the area.  I typically get a sandwich and don't have any complaints with that. Not much of a place to sit outside

Lucy's is a *real* find, tucked alongside a totally nondescript section of the state road. It is sparkly white- feels classy and cool with all that italian marble, and has tons of fresh pasta goods. its unclear to me why a place like this doesnt exist in walking distance to campus?

Phillips steaks taste great.  It's true they don't seem to have enough meat on them.  Their Hot sauce burns just as much going in as it does coming out.  Be that as it may, at 3:30 in the morning, you can't get a better cheese steak.

Being reluctant to try this place as a typical tourist to try Geno's .... we grabbed a wiz wit anyways. Wow! It was super good and greasy like a good steak should be. I was only suppose to eat half but you know ... Nice people working the counter not pretentious at all like the big tourist traps. Maybe a little more meat but it was gone in 30 secs so who's counting anyways?

Went there because they sent us BOGO coupon in Clipper magazine. Food was edible, but not good. I would be really upset if I have to pay full price for that food quality. Only ting they did great was the tandoor chicken. Close to real thing.

Mehek has the best indian food in town and great service to match!  Their chicken tikka masala is hardy, with sauce enough to eat with their perfect garlic naan.  Lunch buffet is great too -- and definitely cheap enough for a college student's budget.  It is without a doubt my go to spot in Princeton.

good  food  and  great   service   been   to this   few  time   in  winter  as  its  very  convinenet  to  walk  from  university  love  ther  chicken  tikka  masal  and  garli  naan. if  in mood  for spicy  try  out  there  devil naan ITS  REALLY  DEVIL

I am new to Cuban food and rum bars. Iwas looking for something diferent. I couldn't be more pleased. Zafra was everything the Hartford Courant said it would be. I had the pork and sampled several of the rums. The presentation was very nice and the service could not have been better. I will return and bring my friends.   Gary Koval

Went for lunch with 3 coworkers and we were all very happy with the food. I had the cubano, which maybe could have used a little more pickle, but it was still VERY tasty. The side of yuca fries were possibly even better than the sandwich, especially with that aioli. Friends got the veggie burger, chicken adobo sandwich, and a seafood chowder, a special that day. Portions were generous -- probably perfect for a guy. All us ladies had just a little left on our plates by time we determined that as good as it was, we just couldn't eat any more. Looking forward to going back for dinner and a drink.

There is a beautiful little outside seating which is really nice. We did not eat here but passing it, it looked lovely. The food however, is terrible. We typically do not mind bad service so long as the food is good... however, this was not the case. We had ordered on the phone for pick up. When asked if we could add chicken to the Penne a la Vodka and how much it would cost, the guy who answered asked what kind of chicken we wanted. He then proceeded to list the following: grilled chicken, bbq chicken, roasted chicken, etc. WHO PUTS BBQ CHICKEN INTO PENNE A LA VODKA????? Honestly, that was our first mistake... we did not specify that when we wanted chicken in our pasta, we wanted it mixed with the sauce. That we thought was a given.. but it was not. When asked how much it would cost to add chicken, he said that he does not know but that the total came to $42 + tax. Why would anyone be allowed to work at a place and not know how to read the pricing The food that was decent was the Chicken Parm and the garlic bread that comes with each entree. However, there was one pasta thrown into our Chicken Parm that was not the same as the other. The Penne a la Vodka had mushy pasta and the chicken we ordered was literally just white chicken on top of the pasta... bland and not worth the $3. We also ordered the Roasted Parmesan Potato Wedges which did not taste like it had cheese at all. We ended up adding our own cheese. Overall, not worth the high cost. Go to Paisano's in Plainsboro, NJ if you are looking for great Italian food. It's amazing and also byob.

Incredible tasting menu, every plate was memorable and delicious. Extra points for the lounge and service who treated me and my girlfriend extremely well during our anniversary dinner. Best plates of the evening were the King Crab, Sea Urchin, Hushpuppy, Smoked Mussels, and the Beet Jerky. That's five dishes that I can't choose between and there's still dishes left off that I completely loved. I was initially nervous about the 20(!) plates coming my way but the portions and pace were immaculate. The atmosphere of the dining room was beautiful and intimate, easily the nicest "Chef's Counter" set-up I've seen. I'll be back here in heartbeat.

Up Thai is a nice addition to a neighborhood that lacks good asian food. The menu is mostly classic Thai dishes, my favorite of which is the Pad See Ew. Although, everything I've had has been solid. The restaurant looks very nice on the inside and the service is very attentive, almost to the point of being overbearing, but not quite. I once showed up unannounced with a group of 10, and they helped us get seating and were very nice about it. This restaurant doesn't try to be inventive or innovative. They serve the classics and they do them well. And as long as the prices stay as reasonable as they are right now, it will be worth many more visits.

Yum Yum! really cute restaurant with good food. I had the up thai fried rice, it was really salty, but i still liked it a lot- probably due to the flavor was this familiar yummy taste that I had lodged back in my conscientiousness. A bite of it made me go into flavor heaven.  My friend had the crispy duck with the thick flat noodles. Its a pretty standard thai restaurant, from the look of the menu, but the decor of the restaurant looks very cute and cozy inside. The thai ice tea was delicious too :). Note- all parties need to be present to be seated, or else you can wait at the bar.

Great Lunch Options for $9-12 -Lunch salad: They use springs greens instead of just boring chopped romaine -Veg Spring Roll: Super flaky crunchy crust with the yummy sweet sauce -Massaman Curry: Delicious! Flavors are nicely balanced with hints of ginger and even licorice! But..... I really really really wanted to give them four stars. In the culinary desert of the UES, I was happy to find a thai place that had delicious and fresh food, cute/trendy ambiance and great lunch options. But I'm really not a fan of attitude. If I say my thank you's and please's and am polite with you, I kind of expect there not to be a problem- ESPECIALLY if you are the server! So I placed an order of mango sticky rice 'to go' at the end of my meal with the waitress. I guess there was a mix up and the dessert came out as an 'eat in' dish. Ok that's totally fine, let's just wrap it to go. When I kindly pointed out that the dessert was 'to go' the dude who brought it out gave me the most exasperated sigh of annoyance, rolled his eyes ALL THE WAY TO THE BACK OF HIS HEAD, and grabbed the plate to saunter unhappily back to the kitchen. Maybe he was having a bad day?
Great food and the variety is excellent. I have eaten in, gotten take-out and delivery, Service always great.

Best drunken noodles I have ever ate, spring rolls were also delicious and at a very reasonable price. I love the atmosphere too and my only complain was our waiter but the food was definitely was a top notch.
beautiful decoration inside with great relaxing atmosphere. The fried rice with thai tea is the best combo for me

There are so many Thai restaurants in this city, but this one for sure is one of the best I've ever been to. I got there around 3:00pm and was shocked that they even had a Lunch Special. I was so happy. In the lunch special came with a soup or salad, an appetizer, and a wide variety of courses to select from. I tried the Kee Mao with crispy duck. It was delicious. A little spicy but I had a thai iced tea to help soothe the spice. Awesome decor inside and the people that work there are so friendly. Nice Atmosphere and good food!
The good was amazing , especially the lunch special. They have food for vegans which was perfect for me. The service was great even during the lunch rush

I've been wanting to try Up Thai after reading the stellar reviews - I always see what's being rated highly in my neighborhood and make it a point to go! As us Upper East Siders know, there are a bunch of Thai restaurants to choose from - some pretty solid and others not so much. I've personally been looking for my replacement for Land since it closed down... Anyway, my friend and I came in around 7 last night and the place was crowded - always a good sign mid-week. We got seated in the front at the high top tables but the back looked really nicely decorated. To start, we got the summer rolls - they were ok - just your usual. For my meal I got my old faithful - kee mao with chicken. Kind of bizarre exchange I had with the waitress while ordering. I asked for no onions. Her response, "well, it's still the same price." Ok...I wasn't asking for you to bump the price down, I just despise onions. Just strange...I was reading some of the reviews on here about strange service and now I understand. That's neither here nor there at this point, because the dish was phenomenal - extremely, extremely spicy, but absolutely delicious. I'm weird about my chicken in that dish and this meat was cooked to absolute perfection. I will definitely be back. Oh, PS - super affordable - $34 total for two people? I'll take it.

cannot say anything negative about this place. have ordered out twice, eaten in once. everything i've ever gotten was amazing. up thai rolls are great! green curry and panang are some of the best i've had. service is fast. prices for lunch special are $10 and you get tons of food. decor of the restaurant is modern and intimate, also good for a date. i haven't tried their thai iced coffee or tea, but that's next on my list!

Small little restaurant in the walk of the piazza. Waiting for your fun is fun. You get to play games and eat popcorn! The waiter was the one of the nicest waiters I have ever had. The food was delicious! American cuisine! The have GREAT weekly features (or specials). Probably my favorite thing about this place

Suppa is this little room tucked away down near the end of The Walk at the Piazza at Schmidts.  Unless you are looking for it you will not likely happen upon this place.  This is a shame because it is totally worth the trip.  The menu is always fresh, seasonal, sustainable and most importantly, tasty.  The menu consists of fun twists on contemporary foods.  I occasionally go there for lunch and I have enjoyed every meal I've eaten there.

This quiet and small restaurant has so much to offer! The food here is sooo good! There is something for everyone on the menu and all of the entree's have their own little twist. I had the Tandori Fried Chicken with Collard Greens and it was so good! Also, this cute little restaurant is BYOB and they provide the mixers! They have games and trivia lying around while you are waiting for your food. That was a fun distraction although the food did not take long at all. The atmosphere is so fun for friends or cute dates and I felt so comfortable eating here that my boyfriend and I stayed for a while. All of the staff is very friendly and inviting making you feel like you've been a regular customer for years. I definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone cruising through Liberties Walk and looking for a bite to eat.

AWESOME!!!  From the Drinks to the food it was all very well done and of course having Jim Cramer running around doing everything from silverware to plates helps:) All kidding aside the drinks were special I had a Tequila infused with Jalapeno was fantasic. we started with the short rib tacos - tasty as can be.  Also had the guac and chips. For entree we both shared the chicken skewars and the lamb chops. Both cooked to perfection and very tasty. Really what a Yelp Five Star should be - and very reasonably Priced!

I waited anxiously for Bar San Miguel to open ever since I saw it under construction a few months ago. Everyday on the walk from my apartment to the subway, I watched the place come together - I love the open windows that practically take up the whole front wall, the grand and weathered looking metal door that looks like it belongs on a castle. I finally got to try Bar San Miguel last weekend, so could actually enjoy the décor from the inside too. The exposed brick walls are painted blue, cute pillows line the bench seating and the restaurant is lit with only the light of candles. Muy romantica. I'm from California, so when it comes to Mexican food I can be a tough critic. First off, I like to judge a Mexican place by how good their margaritas and guacamole are. Bar San Miguel didn't disappoint - the original margarita was made with real lime (none of that sour mix shit), nicely rimmed with salt and deviously strong. The guacamole was a little bit chunky, which I liked - I hate when places serve it goopy like the texture of sour cream. For the mains we shared cheese empanadas, beef empanadas, short rib enchiladas and chicken skewers. The chicken skewers were ehhh - a bit dry. The corn salsa it was served with was really nice and fresh though. I loved both empanadas - perfectly crispy and flaky dough envelopes filled with thick cheese or juicy ground beef. The short rib empanadas were a nice spin on the original. These tortillas were chock full of flavorful short rib, rolled up and smothered in sauce and cheese. All in all, this California girl was impressed even though I'm a purist and would call Bar San Miguel Mexican fusion. Either way, I will be back!

As far as French bistros go, this is not one of my favorites. I ordered the Chicken Chez Moi, which was drowning in a butter sauce. Too much for my liking. It came with fries that were pretty low grade - kind of flavorless, kind of scrawny, kind of homogeneous. The food wasn't necessarily bad, it was just kind of mediocre. I would rather spend my $17 on an entree somewhere else.

Great atmosphere and service. Decent food. Chez Moi is a really cute restaurant and fairly spacious. We stumbled upon this spot while we were trying to find a fairly quiet spot without a wait in the area on a Friday night. (We were actually at Bijan's first but it was so loud, we had to leave. My voice was gone and it was IMPOSSIBLE for me to hold a conversation in that atmosphere. Which was very unfortunate because Bijan's has some great food.) The atmosphere here was exactly what we were looking for that night. We were seated almost immediately after we arrived. We didn't even have a complete party and they were still very understanding. The service was great and the environment was cozy. We started with the country pate which was delicious. My main entree was the beet salad and sweet potato soup special for the day. I was incredibly disappointed. I wish someone had told me the beet salad wasn't really a salad but a full plate of ONLY beets. Don't get me wrong, I love beets but they served it extremely sweet and there was zero lettuce. The soup was okay, nothing too special. My friends' dishes all seemed better than mine but no one was really blown away. I think this spot might be worth coming back to for the atmosphere and drinks, but I wouldn't expect too much from the food. I may have to give this place another chance for brunch.

I love French bistro food and have had my fair share. Chez Moi was just OK. The pate was standard, but not as good as nearby Cafe Tabac, the risotto of the day was good, but the skate, and fish and chips (not standard French fare) was just ok. The ambience was nice, with a bar area and the service was competent if a little casual. and the mixologist was very good. If the prices were a bit more of a bargain, maybe I wouldn't have felt so disappointed. Maybe it was just an off night.

Great surprise when I discovered this little French restaurant. Me and my friend are real Parisian and very picky about food even more when it's French Food!! Everything was very good, food and cocktails were super tasty, the waitress was really nice and the manager even more. The restaurant is very cosy with little candle light at night and great music.   So if you want to have a great time you should definitely stop by "Chez Moi" ;)
Very busy at the bar for a Friday night so we went to the back for a table. Friends say the Cobb salad and veggie burger are great! Good music, vey busy and attentive staff!
Casual and friendly service at a decent price. Great atmosphere for getting together with a few friends or coworkers. Ann, our server was attentive and friendly. Would go back again.
Excellent service. Kudos to the bartender. Great beer selection too. Will definitely be back.

3.8 Stars! If you understand that this isn't "authentic" mexican cuisine you will have a nice experience. They often have deals where you can get 3 tacos for under 5 bucks! The salsas and condiments they offer are great, especially for a chain restaurant.  Give them a try if you are in the area for a filling non-expensive lunch!

Awesome spot. Chorizo, grilled fish, and carnita tacos are my favorites but there are many others that are good too. Guacamole and chips a staple. The cheese flautas and quesadillas  are simply delish. We frequent this place about once a week on average.

A really good underrated fast food place. Much better than your average Chipotle or Moe's. Probably costs about as much as Chipotle or Moe's but the quality is significantly better. I am sure you could get better Mexican food at a restaurant but this is still good food at a solid price. If this place was located by where I worked I would never go to Chipotle again.

What an absolutely amazing place. My girlfriend and I recently ate here. Born and bred in Louisiana to a Cajun chef father, I was a bit skeptical about any restaurant this far north touting "Creole" or "Soul" food. But the owners of Cast Iron Soul got it just right. The blackened catfish had the perfect blend of spices and "blackened" exterior while melting in your mouth. The candied yams and macaroni-n-cheese were out of this world. I returned today just to try dessert (which I was too full to try the first time). Upon recommendation I had the banana pudding cake and--of course--it was amazing. Hats off to the Cast Iron crew. They really made this Southerner incredibly happy.
Pretty good. No complaints. I enjoyed the fries a lot. My sandwich was good but nothing to write home about. The service was also good.

Okay Thai place in an area with a lot of Thai places. The ambience is definitely not distinctive at all, though the food was good and the price reasonable. Then again, the same can be said of many other similar places within a few square blocks.

This place is pretty legit... at least the larbs are. I got the beef larb delivered to my buddy's place who I was visiting. We are both pretty big fans of Thai food, been to Thailand and have pretty high expectations. So I felt pretty good ordering from here after he recommended it. You have to a pick a spice level from 1 through 5. If you are supremely confident about handling your spice, I would recommend a 3. I can handle eating raw thai chili peppers and for me 3 was a good level of spice.  Anything higher than this, and you risk a heavy session of a$$ burn the next morning or a case of heart burn immediately afterwards (if you can even get through your meal i.e.) Hopefully I'll get to try some of the other stuff on their menu.

How in the world did I ever miss this place?  Maybe because 9th Ave is like Sukhumvit Road?  Never we get into how I missed it, but now is now and I was HERE. Having lunch with a work friend and went here based on her recommendation.  She told me this place is special and different as they feature cuisines of Northern Thailand.   From their menu I had Kra Prao Moo Krob Over Rice Lunch Special, which is Stir-fried basil sauce with crispy pork, chili and garlic over rice.  It was simply amazing.  Crispy enough without being crunchy, fatty enough without being chewy and flavorful enough to dance with the basil garlic and chili.  And saucy enough to coat the rice just enough without soaking it.  Far and away some of the best Thai food I ever had in NY. I would have loved to have taken an order of this home but crispy anything doesn't travel too well, so I got an order of pad thai to take out.  The pad thai was also quite good.  Theirs was prepared really well in that it wasn't too oily, not too dry, aka just right, and was actually a tad sweet without being annoyingly sweet.   I WILL go back here, and I vow to try multiple dishes instead of my standby green curry chicken.  If they have it, I will try it, but not before I get into some of the other wonderful items on the menu.   Only 4 stars for now due to one visit under my belt, but soon enough I will have some more pork inside of my belt and this place will be 5.  Not 55555, but 5.  lol

I live on 9th Ave. in Hell's Kitchen, so I know the neighborhood's Thai. Pam's Real Thai used to be my favorite until I encountered Larb Ubol, and ironically, two blocks from my place. It is in that area of HK near the Port Authority that is kind of ignored, but you shouldn't ignore this restaurant. It is charming, the service is friendly, the wine and beer options are limited but good, and the food is on par with the best Thai in the City. I started with the Larb pork salad with mint, coriander, and peanuts over lettuce and cabbage. It was enough for a lite meal, but I also wanted to try the tilapia. I chose the fried filet with basil spicy sauce. It was incredibly tasty, though I wish I had chosen a more healthy option. The red snapper looked delicious and perfect for two. Larb just won some regular business from me.

Out of over 200 thai restaurant I've been to while I was traveling with my dad since 11 years old up until now, this has got to be the best restaurant I've ever been to. The restaurant has a casual setting. The seats were decorated with a fabric called pa karma (a traditional thai fabric which used as towels. The food was on point, delicious, fresh and authentic. I wish they have restaurant like this in Virginia.  I was in New York for 4 days. Went there all 4 days. Wish i could give this place more stars!
Tasty food with flavor. Great décor and customer service. Enjoyed our trip and plan to visit in the future.

Very disappointing experience.Went there for Hibachi. My server was nice and the Hibachi chef was very entertaining but my lobster hibachi dinner was pretty much tasteless and mediocre at best. I can't put my finger on it but there is just something cheesy about this place. It can't compare to Imperial 46.

Our family loves hibatchi style dining and we have been to every place in the surrounding area.  Our son's birthday was on the coldest day of the year and we didn't feel like traveling to our favorite place 20 minutes away so we tried Nikko.  It was amazing.  The food was delicious - very plentiful portions and extremely entertaining chef.  For our son's birthday they brought out a beautiful decorated plate with tempura ice cream and a personalized message in chocolate sauce at no charge.  The decor in this restaurant is very upscale and brand new.  There are a few private rooms with very large hibatchi tables.  Didn't try sushi yet but will for sure be back to try that!!  Prices were great too.

Saray is an absolute gem. Their food is incredible. The servers are exceedingly polite. It's BYOB. And they have a huge, well-lit, well-decorated space, so even when the restaurant is packed you'll never have a problem carrying on conversations. There's no better place to go when you want Turkish food. Every single dish that I've ever tried here has been delicious. For a first visit, I'd recommend starting with some combination of the cacik, imam bayildi, baba ganoush, and sigara boregi. For an entree, go with the iskender kebab or adana kebab. The iskender kebab is a heaping pile (enough for 2+ meals) of fall-apart tender lamb and chunks of pita topped with cooked tomatoes and a thick, tangy yogurt. The adana kebab is a skewer of beef that has been minced with an indescribably tasty blend of spices. You won't be disappointed by either. Most importantly, make sure to leave enough room for a Turkish coffee and the rice pudding. Both are so mind-blowingly good that the meal would just feel incomplete otherwise.

After 13 years in the restaurant industry myself, this is the first bad review I have written about a restaurant EVER. I have been to Rustica one time previously to this, ok experience:  not awful, not amazing.  However, I went to Rustica again recently and am determined not to return.   My biggest issue is the credit card fraud that they blatantly did after we left.  We had a $25 gift certificate to put toward the bill.  The server then put an 18% gratuity on the total bill, which was fine with me.  We then tipped ON TOP of the gratuity, bringing the server's total tip well above 25% of the total check, before the gift certificate was taken out.  You think that would be enough?  Well, after we left, an additional $15 was charged to our card, that we did not authorize.  This is illegal. For a two-top, we were a server's dream check:  2 apps, 1 salad, 2 expensive entrees, dessert, espresso, 25+% tip, didn't linger after dessert.  I would not have come here if I didn't already have a gift certificate, and I regret that I did. This alone does not make me want to return, however, on top of that, the portion sizes were miniscule compared to the first time I dined at Rustica.  The salmon entree had at best, 3oz of fish.  The steak entree was also on the small side.  The sides that came along with it were also extremely small.  EVERY plate we ordered (except the salad) was small in portion.  After the aforementioned 2 apps, 1 salad, 2 entrees and dessert, I left hungry.   Service:  we saw the server to take our order, drop the entrees, take the dessert order, and drop the check.  The bus staff is phenomenal though, incredibly attentive and amiable.  The bus staff is the only reason why I didn't rate this zero stars; they earned their star and then some.  The server also yanked the gift certificate out of my husband's hand extremely aggressively, which was incredibly rude.  I suggest counseling. In short:  I will not return.  I will continue to frequent places with incredible food and service, particularly Giotto.

My girlfriend and I have had two great experiences here. Food is great. I got chicken with prosciutto and fontina in a mushroom sauce. Flavors were well balanced and it is something I would definitely order again. My girlfriend got a tuna special with avocado salsa. She loved it. Service is good, not great. All around enjoyable experience and will continue to dine here.

We have been here twice and I wanted to write a review since we did not encounter the problems others mentioned in reviews. Both times one on a Sunday night and another on Saturday night no problem seating us - although we did wait about 10-15 minutes on Saturday despite having reservations. It was worth it as we got great seating corner bench table.Love able to bring your own wine. The place was reasonably full Sunday, and packed on Saturday. I got water replenished, and thought adequately attentive. every time we have gone we have enjoyed the food. The first time the shrimp with my husband's dish was a little light in quantity. Also the menu online and then when you go is slightly different - they have taken off the veal dishes. We will be coming back. I actually liked the charm of the place, its much better than other options in this neighborhood I have been to. We also got the cheese and meat plate, which the procuitto was very good, although could use more. We liked the bread they served.

I was looking for somewhere new to grab dinner and a beer when I'm too lazy to cook, and read about this new Fishtown spot via Twitter.  Suddenly what I really wanted was a burger and a scotch.  I decided to trek through the first snow/sleet/nastiness of the season to check it out. After reading up on the brand new bar, I was hoping for "Village Whiskey, Fishtown Edition" and that is exactly what I got.  No, they don't have 50 single malt scotches on the menu.  But the do have close to 10, at a big discount from Village Whiskey's prices.  And they have my personal favorite scotch -- Laphroaig 10yr -- which I enjoyed with an excellent burger. (It's not really fair to compare to the Village Whiskey burger, which is arguably the best burger in the city, so I won't.) Overall, my first visit was excellent, and I will most likely find myself there again every time someone I've shared a drink with at Village Whiskey is in my neighborhood.

I came in for the grand opening, and I've already been back numerous times. Food is phenomenal (I highly recommend the Texas Tommy), and the drinks selections are fantastic. It's great to finally have a bar in this part of the city that knows how to make a proper cocktail. Definitely had one of the best Manhattans of my life there, and the crew really know their stuff. Scott, Taylor, and Lloyd have really hit the nail on the head with this one!

Came last night for dinner with my boyfriend. Had to wait maybe 10 minutes for a table. From the inside, it could have been 1992. Noticed they have a booming "take out" business.  I think there were more brown to go bags of pick up orders coming out of the kitchen then there were plated dinners. Rib House is the place to go for always consistent ribs. Baby Back ones, get those. Also you can't go wrong with a half carafe of wine either.   There's a small dining room area and a separate lounge/bar side too. Even though the dining room only has a couple tables and booths, we didn't feel rushed at all, which was great. Can't wait to come back.
BBQ Chicken skin was like rubber, Ribs were like leather! Chili's all the way for ribs no contest !!
Completely average. I will probably be back as the ribs are pretty decent but other than that this is really nothing special.

Worst restaurant ever!! Too pricey for the quality of food they serve. Cold behari kebabs, hot lassi to go with the rude old lady behind the counter who seems to hate her job and taking her frustration out on the customers. They seriously need to fire her or else they will lose a lot more customers like me & will eventually close down. Paid more then $100 for that garbage food yet the lady had an attitude as if we were asking for free food. Highly not recommended!! You will regret it.

This restaurant is not good at all! I ate chicken biryani from here, and I ended up getting an upset stomach. I would not recommend this place. I have eaten other entrees from here, and I am less than impressed with each order. I don't like how they keep there food. They put everything in a glass display in the front of the place. It probably collects bacteria sitting there for so long! The service is bad too. People here are not good at communicating with customers. They seemed to be half listening to me when I was talking to them. I would recommend a different restaurant. I think this restaurant offers the buffet. I have eaten that in the past. I don't think I can recommend it now.

I Have been a loyal customer since it first opened. If you are looking for the most authentic Pakistani cuisine, this is it. They have the best chicken cheese kabobs. All of the dishes are very good, the food is for people that enjoy spicy dishes. The biryani is very delicious and all the tandoori nans are made fresh just like back home in Pakistan. This place is the closest thing to "food street" in Lahore. I would recommend them for all of your special event caterings (they even make it less spicy according to preference) or just to walk in and have a great lunch or dinner. If you have a sweet tooth they have so many different varieties of methai, and all of them look beautiful and taste delicious. All of my friends and family love this place, I give it 5 stars.

I was looking for another place while walking in. Simple decor ,nothing amazing but the food smelled great.Looks like a lot of locals come here. Lunch buffet has great dish choices and even has mango lassi and sweets without additional charge. Im going again soon.

I was so excited about this grand opening especially the fact that Bobby Flay will be there the whole day.  The hour + wait was more than worth it.  I had the Crunchburger and the Napa Valley Burger.  I have to lean toward the Napa Valley more so.  Both were cooked to medium so you definitely see some pink in the middle.  This made the burger very juicy and delicious.  The service was very friendly and attentive.  I however would NOT order the margarita.  It did not taste good at all to the point where I was not able to finish.  Next time I have to try the shakes.

Big fan of Bobby Flay's shows and food, not a fan of this restaurant. 45 minute wait, understandable. You know, celebrity chef's new restaurant in one of the BEST locations for a burger joint in Philly along with gorgeous weather, of course there's going to be a line. But why are half of the tables empty? This isn't a nightclub where long lines promote popularity. Ordered my L.A. Burger, sweet potato fries, and black and white shake, and a number was given to me to place on my table. I wasn't timing them because I was busy taking pictures and checking out the cool decor (which is definitely Bobby Flay style), but the food arrived fairly quick. The shake was OK, nothing special (Lee's black and white shakes are a different story!). Sweet potato fries were good and so was the honey mustard dipping sauce that came with it, but it was too runny and barely any would adhere to the fry. My burger came out and it looked delicious. They sure know how to make a pretty burger, with HAIR on it. Yes, my burger was topped with avocado relish, watercress, cheddar, and a strand of light brown hair. People make mistakes, fine. They brought my new hairless L.A. Burger out. The meat of the burger is actually pretty good. But the toppings were so so (more lime in the relish maybe?). I practically had to drench it in the sauces, mostly the jalapeno, on the side. Meal finished. I ordered a kid's meal to go for a friend of mine. Waited **20** minutes for it to come out. During the wait, we were asked about 20 times if we were done (not exaggerating) and if any of you have been there this week, you know what I'm talking about. No sauces came with it, not even ketchup packets. No compensation was offered for the hair incident, which I'm not going to make a big deal about. They did apologize, good enough. I'll give the place a second try, but I am not waiting in that ridiculous line.
i'm sure it's delicious based on the theme park lines, i'll revisit my stars when i actually have enough time (and a crossword puzzle in tote) to wait in line.  i'm sure it's worth it.

Good selection of various types of burgers (beef, turkey, chicken) *Be sure to tell them how you want it cooked, because most of the time they cook them medium-pink* Milkshakes are absolutely amazing. I recommend the COFFE shake. Fries are all handcut and come with very good dipping sauce. Food comes out very quickly. It has a COSI style service, i.e. order from the counter, they hand you number, and then food is brought out to you. Tends to get very busy around lunch since its on a college campus. Try getting there before 12 or after 2 to avoid the massive student rush. Prices are all fairly cheap - Burgers : $7.5 - $9 - Fries : $3.5

First let me say how much I love Bobby Flay. He made pumpkin soup with chocolate on Iron Chef and I instantly became a big fan. I have his books, I watch Throw Down, I even visited the Pop Shop because of the show. But his burger palace was a bit disappointing. His name is on the door but after that it is just another burger place. I traveled nearly thirty miles, got stuck in city traffic, and then waited an hour in line for pretty much the same burger I could have gotten from my local Ruby Tuesday. I think I was expecting food that tasted a little more chef prepared. The selections are unusual enough and definitely got my taste buds curious but basically this is chain food. LIkewise the sweet potato fries are also a good idea but the regular french fries were more like potato sticks. If I lived nearby I would go again but this really isn't was I was expecting. Maybe there was too much hype but I don't think I will be back.
Thought the food here was spicier than the majority of Indian restaurants I frequent in NYC! Be prepared to drink lots of water! Also, the chicken masala didn't come with rice so ask for it!

This is a great neighborhood Thai place. Good food, friendly service, and BYO too. The Red Curry I ordered was very tasty - very spicy but also very flavorful. With all the number of competitive Thai and Asian restaurants in the Bloomfiled/Montclair area, this place sits towards the top of the list.
Always super friendly and accommodating. As parents of very young children this is the go to place for take out. My two yr old loves their pad see ew(did I spell that right?!)

Came here the other night with my boyfriend for dinner. We were both in the mood for sushi so I Yelped for sushi in our area and stumbled on SK. We had tried other sushi places in town and thought it would nice to try another new place, after all we weren't married to any in town. Sushi Koshi was this tiny little place. It probably sat 30 people total, including the bar area. At almost every table there was a little poster advertising that you had the option to order either white, brown or black rice for you sushi rolls, and the benefits of ordering black rice. So in total my boyfriend and I tried two specialty rolls and three standard rolls, just get an idea of how to gauge them in comparison to all the other sushi places around. We ordered the California roll with black rice just to see how it would taste. Specialty roll or regular roll, the diameter is fairly the same for both so I thought that was a little disappointing since the specialty rolls are priced between $11 and $15.  The fish was fresh, the flavor was mellow yet present. The black rice was great! The texture was just like the white rice. In my mind I thought it would be similar to brown rice, but it wasn't the case. My boyfriend had ordered the "MAKI B" set which included the three rolls, salad and miso soup. He had noticed at the end of the meal that his soup and salad were never given to him. We immediately checked the menu to double check if he was right, told the staff and they were super apologetic about it. Overall I would have to say that I enjoyed my meal here. I wish a lot of their specialty rolls didn't include 'blueberry sauce' because its such a turn off when they add too much fruit into the sushi. It's so Americanized! I would definitely be back Sushi Koshi! The black rice option sold me well!

This is my third visit to Princeton soup and sandwich. I can now call myself a regular customer! WOW!!!!! I've never wrote a review on yelp before, but after the third time going I've figured it was time to give these guys there "kudos". The first couple times I came the food was awesome! Since I'm a vegetarian I decided to have the humus and avocado, I spoke to one of the employees and they said they make the hummus from scratch! Today I tried the soup combo with gazpacho sandwich and ten vegetable soup and there not kidding when they say ten vegetables. It's hard for me to find vegetarian food around here and it's really awesome to see a place like this actually have vegetarian options that are so delicious!!! The place is tiny and can get a little crazy at lunch, if your lucky enough you might just get a seat..maybe outside or at the counter. Staff is friendly and knowledgeable. Thank you Princeton soup and sandwich.

Being from Xi'an, my expectations for Xi'an food is understandably elevated. Xi'an Sizzling Woks comes close to meeting them. What's good: *The biang biang noodles are legit. Like super legit. *The liang pi is pretty good. I've never been a huge liang pi fan, but this is pretty authentic. *The service is friendlier/better than most places in Chinatown What keeps it from getting 5 stars is the flavor. It's just a bit weak on some of the dishes (such as the chicken spicy pot flavor). The cumin lamb was decent, but lacked the punch that I've come to expect, from comparable spots. This place is worth going to for the biang biang noodles alone. They need to spice it up a notch on the other stuff. If you're looking for authentic Xi'an food, this is as good as it gets in Philly.

Love love love this place! I'm a weird lacto-intolerant gal who can have goat chees for some strange reason... They have a goat Gouda wih bacon, avocado & chèvre that is to do die for. First legit (non-gross soy "fake cheese) grilled cheese in over a decade. I am one happy grateful camper.

I had the 3 cheese grille cheese with bacon, the crispy goat, spicy tomato soup, french fries, sweet potato tater tots, and to top it off the sweet grilled cheese with mascarpone, bananas, and nutella with ice cream. Service was awesome, owner is cool as hell. This is by far the best grilled cheese I have ever eaten. Sorry grandma. If your around check it best bang for your buck around here you won't be sorry!

Hands down..the best grilled cheese and spicy tomato soup I have ever had. I was informed that this place has been open since July of 2014..I can't tell you how many times I've walked past here and never noticed this place before. I am quite disappointed that I haven't had the pleasure of eating here sooner. The place is cozy --perfect place to just sit, order and relax. The interior is well decorated, extremely clean and colorful. The hospitality AMAZING. I tried the three cheese with bacon--let me tell you..it was to die for & super cheesy. I also had the crispy goat which happens to be one of their more popular grilled cheese sandwiches..totally satisfying. The thing I loved most on the menu: SWEET POTATO TOTS! They were perf! Side note: everything tastes better dipped in that amazing spicy tomato soup. I want to swim in a pool of that stuff. We had the banana for dessert..it's mascarpone, Nutella, and banana with ice cream on brioche..first off..NUTELLA, BANANA, ICE CREAM. Has there ever been a more perfect combination? It was delicious. In conclusion..totally recommend this place. If you pop in and Mike is there..I guarantee he'll add to the experience of the place. I can't wait to come back.

This is going to be the neighborhood go to place. Lovely little Italian restaurant and soon to come Enoteca. They are still waiting for their liquor license to get approved. They do accept credit cards now. They are the same owners of Candela that used to be on 16th street between Irving & park ave. The food is delicious and refined simple Italian food. The prices are fair for the quality of food you are getting. This neighborhood has been waiting for a great little place like this. I had the trout and the Arancini  (rice balls) and all the different cristini's and they were magical. The fish was cooked to perfection. The fennel was sweet and delicious. My husband had the eggplant parmigiana and said it was equally good. My son had the spaghetti and tomato sauce. It was one of the best sauces I have tasted. For those of you who have to have wine or liquor with your meal be patient it's coming soon. If you can have a meal with out the liquor then go now. It's worth trying.

This area has very few mid-priced cozy restaurants so I was looking forward to trying out La Follia. I noticed business was light the first few weeks they were open but once they got their liquor license the place seemed packed by 7:30 every night. Good sign, yay! La Follia is split up into 2 sections, a restaurant portion and a wine bar with high-top tables. Both areas are nicely decorated with dim lighting and candles on every table. The menu has a wide range of options from vegetarian to fish and meat dishes. The wine list is mostly Italian and there lots of affordable options by the glass, carafe and bottle. Based on what I tried the ingredients seemed fresh and dishes were well executed. I definitely want to go back and try more items on the menu. The stand-outs for me were the burrata crostini and tirimisu.

Tried the restaurant out as well.  Our waitress was very sweet and great.  The food is very well priced and decent.  I got a pasta with butternut squash and roasted cauliflower in oil/butter.  I also asked for broccoli rabe in it, which was a bit bitter.  It wasn't too oily which was a plus, but I do wish there were more veggies in it.  We had a caraffe of the locorosso which was great.  The tiramisu was just OK.  Overall with the great service and decent food, I would go back.

We enjoyed our evening here.  There was a bit of a wait for a table in the restaurant part on Friday evening around 9pm, so we had a glass of wine and some appetizers in the wine bar area first.  The service was very good and they really seemed to be hustling to make everyone happy.   As for the food, almost everything was very good.  The endive salad, salmon entree, and white bean bruschetta won top marks.  The penne with cauliflower and butternut squash could have been a bit better -- the squash was hard, it was nothing too special -- but with enough butter and cheese I enjoyed it thoroughly nonetheless.   Our waitress was really nice and a totally genuine seeming way.

The lunch special here is a great value. Half sandwich and fries for about $5.50. There is also a pasta + salad lunch special for about $6.50. The fries were a little soggy. The chicken parmesan was very good. They deliver. They also have free WiFi if you're ever in the mood.

The food is amazing. Great flavors! I love the coconut crusted fish! I would recommend to anyone. Its freshly made. And to top it off the owners are super nice!!!! Im so happy to have this cute little place next to my home.
Everything is delicious!

Let the Italian Angels shine their light on Eataly and sing down from above: "Hallelujah!" "Che bellissima!" "Si, si mangia!" And the Italian god of Pasta smiled and said "E 'bene." (It is good.) Eataly is a sight to behold-- a true mecca for all things that belong in a proper Italian kitchen.  With posh lighting, a variety of foodstuffs and samples aplenty, it's easy to be overwhelmed and still delighted in Mario Batali/Lidia Bastianach's latest venture.  There are rows and rows of beautifully shelved products imported straight from Italy and admiring the gorgeous packaging is enough to take up an entire afternoon's time.  There is a macelleria (butcher), formaggeria (cheese), salumeria, gelateria, two pasticcerias and even a food court unlike any you've seen before. Price-wise, there are items that are on-par with your typical NYC grocery store.  Dry pastas, canned sauces, etc.  Others, like the fresh meats and cheeses are a smidge pricier than what you'd see at a Whole Foods.  Nothing seemed exorbitant. Each counter seemed to be well staffed and I saw plenty of friendly Eataly employees (in their Batali inspired orange crocs, no less) running around the floor offering their aid.  Everything seemed to be running smoothly and I would definitely make a stop by here to pick up fancy ingredients for a special home-cooked meal.
