We weren't too thrilled with the waygu beef (too chewy but the vegies were amazing) and we didn't really dig the goats cheeze sorbet but we didn't care since the rest of the dishes and the experience made up for it in a totally big way. One thing we liked with almost all the dishes were that they never were what they appeared to be. For example, in the dashi there were these peas in a pod served with it but they weren't pees at all, they were cucumbers.. Many other examples of this playfulness for you to find on your own... We are definitely coming back to try the other things on the menu.

The good: nice décor, great concept, simple menu The bad: turkey burger was undercooked and mushy, greens of the mesclun salad wilted! The ugly: over thirty minutes wait for two burgers... on a Thursday night, and not that busy...Luckily we did not have to go to the movies... Our food server never came once by our table to let us know what was going on... I I understand it is a new restaurant so I will give it another try, because there is some serious potential there

Sat at the bar with only a short time before our movie was starting.  Ordered a lemon- cranberry Cosmo-- yum.  The bar menu is vodka-centric, featuring locally made and premium vodka drinks.  Fun idea.  The artichoke heart appetizers were excellent.  Another member if my party enjoyed his burger.  I ordered a quinoa-squash salad that was certainly edible, but it was so cold that I couldn't taste all the flavors.  I would recommend and would return.  Fun atmosphere for a quick bite.  Check it out if you are in Williston!

We celebrated a birthday at the hibachi and I have to say it was a big "meh".  The decor is a little overdone but impressive nonetheless, just wish they spent that kind of time on the food.   The hibachi chefs wear weird American/Texan uniforms with cowboy hats which sets a strange tone for the evening right away.  The highlight of our meal was definitely the scorpion bowl (available in several flavors) served with a floating, flaming shot of 151 in the middle.  The mushroom soup was musty, and the hibachi meal decidedly so-so.   I didn't get sushi, but glancing at the menu the rolls were priced tiny bit more than you would pay elsewhere. In my opinion, Hayama in Orange and Kampai in Branford, where the food outshines the show, are still the best hibachi options in the area.

I learned about this spot through a flyer I was handed on my way to work.  My first experience was through delivery since the flyer provided a 10% discount.  Ordered the Florida Fry  and the Friendly Apple Salad and both were AMAZING, but especially the fish sandwich.  Had I only ordered the sandwich or just the salad  I probably would have still been hungry, but the sandwich and salad together was almost too much food.  A sandwich/salad combo would be ideal.  Online ordering was a cinch. My second lunch happened today when  I ventured out to pick up my food directly from the shop.  If it wasn't for the helpful doorman at the strip club next door, I would have never found this place because there's NO SIGNAGE.  You walk through the red door of the restaurant next door and up a flight of stairs. There's also no seating,just a cash register in the kitchen.  I had the Chicken Pestolada (too salty for my taste) and the Cauliflower Bisque (vegan and delicious, though I wish it was served in cardboard container instead of plastic).   All sandwiches are served with pickle relish on the side and a chocolate chip cookie, which I'm pretty sure contains toffee bits, YUM!  If this spot was a tad cheaper, I would order from here multiple times a week.  Great spot to have cater office lunches.

always amazing!! seriously every single thing we ve tried has been SO good - every first bite we keep looking at one another like "how do they do that?!?"   ...and that tim is such a swell guy ;-) love your biggest fans amon & zaida at ny neurology downtown former employees at neuroasis ;-P
The flavor alone is just great I love the sauce here reminds me of pizza back home on Arthur Ave in the bronx

A quite little place that I happened into on a lonely, rainy Saturday afternoon whilst wandering Williamsburg. I was pleased at how friendly the server was, and I suspect he may be the owner. He greeted another customer by name, which always warms my opinion of an establishment. I ordered a chai - non-sugary - and a muffin. The muffin was beautiful; it was dainty, moist, healthy and delicious. Seriously wonderful.

Ignore the bad review.  It is amazing that someone would pan a brand new restaurant for bad service in the very first week the restaurant opened and because they do not like the food served at the restaurant -- meaning that they would pan a restaurant for serving a cuisine they do not like...would you pan a bagel place because you don't like bagels?   This is a great place.  The service was great - we waited after the first week - knowing how insane it would be.  Every new restaurant takes time to get the kinks out - which is why a newspaper like the Times would not review it during the first week.  Alas, the cruelty of sites like this one - that give people the chance to pan a brand new place. On to the cuisine.  The rolls were fine as was the miso soup, fried dumplings, etc. However, I would go for the bimbimbap and traditional Korean dishes.  A lot of great spicy food.  Yum. Staff are friendly and local - they own the nail salon around the corner. Good luck to them!

A little slice of Koreatown in the Jersey burbs. Great addition to the neighborhood!  Everything we had was delicious.  Bulgogi taco, bibimbap, japchae, mandoo...I'm getting hungry just thinking about it.  Haven't tried the bulgogi burger yet, but will do next time. They definitely had some service issues the first week, but seem to be figuring it out.  The owners are friendly and knew they had some kinks to work out.  Definitely recommended.

What a wonderful addition to the neighborhood!! Just had lunch there and found it totally delicious. They've worked out the kinks in opening week's issues. Food was freshly prepared and the service was very attentive, friendly and fast. highly recommend this place!!!

They should not do rolls.... Ingredients were not fresh and there were too much rice.  Sushi rice was not seasoned properly. In addition, all the rolls are over priced. They charge $2.99 for the miso soup that is only 1/3 portion of other places. One of the men who works there was wearing sweat pants with filp flops and his underwear was showing. They need some kind of uniform or need to wear neat looking cloths. That grossed me out and they did not look professional at all. The place was neat though since they just opened up. Maybe yes for Korean foods, but do not ever order rolls. Personally, I would not go back to this place.
Love love love this place!!! Great service & great food. I can't steer away from the French toast they are amazing. Of coarse I have to have a class if OJ!!

Oh I love this place...  I mean. What's not to love? Open kitchen concept with green walls, green plates, green cups, green bar chairs... 3-4 people working in the whole place ... Immediately walk into the smell of fried bacon and pancakes. Where can you get a burger (only burger- add a dollar for cheese) for $4 and breakfast (in general) for $7? I feel like I walked into a friend's house and her uncles and aunts decided to cook for us. Fresh squeezed OJ, yes please! Eggs over easy, yes please! blueberry pancakes, yes please! Everything I have tried is good and they are good portions. Not like the diner portions where you feel super stuffed or too little where you have to order multiple dishes. I only do that because I want to try them all... :) It is a small place but it never feels over-crowded. Just make sure they are open because the business hours are not regular restaurant hours. More like bagel shop hours? When you go I recommend: Fresh OJ, blueberry pancakes, and their turkish sausage on/with/in addition to anything.

hasn't been open too long, but great whiskey selection. and if they can keep the prices as low as they currently are, i would expect there to be lines out the door at all hours... i hear the food is good, but i can't speak to that yet. maybe when i return.....
Hey, I love this place! It's a mere half block from my apartment - I can see this getting ugly.

Went here late at night for a friends birthday and she got treated like a queen!  Kind staff, beautiful tables and photography, masculin rustic, great classic tunes fine fitting for whiskey drinking.  Try the pickled blackberrys!! I love it here.

Went here for happy hour after work with a bunch of coworkers. There was a good selection of maybe 20 beers on tap and lots of liquor. The happy hour price was decently cheap. The restaurant was big and there were plenty of big tables to sit at. I did not order any but many coworkers said the happy hour apps tasted like crap. The place was also kind of dingy and the table tops were sticky like they don't every wipe them down properly. I would not recommend this if you want food or a great dining experience, not bad for after work drinks perhaps.

Wow is all I have to say and its not a good wow.  It took 45 Min to get our food and it came out overcooked!  Needless.to.say we.ended up at McDonald's after a long hour of waiting and disappointment.  We did receive a drink on the house due to the wait, but we received a ton of excuses as well. Unfortunate. we won't be returning anytime soon, there are far too many great restaurants in Philly that do know how to handle a full seating and delivering great food.

I really like this place: it's kitschy and chill all at once.  The place is decorated in blues, oranges...well, many different colors - very vibrant.  I've only been for brunch, and the eats are ok, but not bad.  I've had the apple stuffed french toast, chocolate and banana pancakes, burger eggs benedict, and one of the frittatas..I forget which one.  The food is decent to good.  I mean, most breakfast/brunch is just that - unless the food is unique in some way, most breakfast foods fall in the okay range for me.  The owners work in the kitchen and occasionally take orders.  I've only met one of them, and he's pretty nice.   The restaurant is nice to hang out at for brunch or any other time of day.  They have an amazing list of microbrews that the one owner I met prides himself on.  Beers are listed with their grades, type, and alcohol content. Oddly enough, all the times I've been to the restaurant, it's been raining out so I've not gotten a chance to hang out on their colorful and spacious patio.  Repeat visits to the Llama Tooth are in my future.  Maybe one of these days, I'll talk the owner into gifting me with one of the cute llama artworks on the wall.

I was excited to go to brunch here today for the first time, and to sit outside. Arriving at noon, there was only one other table seated, but there were 18 of them. The kitchen clearly is not prepared to handle large parties. After almost an hour their food came out two at a time, over a half hour. After another 15 mins our food came out, was served to another couple by mistake, finally made its way over to us, with no apology for the delay. The food was good and reasonably priced, but no brunch is worth a 70 minute wait from the time I order. Cool patio and I still want to try dinner here so they get one more chance to redeem themselves.

We found this wonderful restaurant quite by accident.  Our rental car broke down right in front of the restaurant so we stopped in for something to eat.  The food was great, the drinks were free flowing and everyone was very friendly and helpful for two old, out-of-town tourists.  Philly truly is the city of brotherly love.  We loved the patio and the murals.  If my rental car ever breaks down again I hope it's in front of this lovely restaurant.

After eating the meatloaf at Llama Tooth, I have cravings for it. It is turkey meat with broccoli, green peppers & onions with a tangy barbecue sauce, MMMMM. The crab cakes and the ahi tuna salad are also delicious. The patio is so perfect  with the murals & tiki bar. I can't wait to try the brunch, on a september morning, on the patio !!!

Llama Tooth has one of the best outdoor dining spaces I've spent time in in Philly. At night, when seated on the patio, strings of lights flow across the table umbrellas and it's really a relaxing and fun setting to be enjoying your food and drink. This place has a great atmosphere inside and out, as the indoor dining room has a real cozy yet elegant feel to it. I had the ahi tuna and I can't stress enough how perfectly crafted this dish was. I was thoroughly satisfied. Also of note, the beer list is quite extensive and features notable brews from around the U.S. as well as real local gems. Impressive to say the least.  Craft lovers take notice! This is definitely a place not to be missed.
this place is great the food is just about what taste good ,and the owners are really nice especialy the cute old guy ,hes really funny .
place just opened, I was there on the opening night, good atmosphere and great food! I will defiantly come back.

We trekked out to Jackson Heights from the UWS specifically because Samudra had great Yelp reviews. Was worth the trip -- modest interior but very attentive and friendly service, delicious food, and excellent value. There were a ton of items on the menu that I'd now happily go back and try. Recommended!

I'm not a vegetarian, but I still had plenty of great options to choose from.  The samosas are some of the best I've ever had.  I really enjoyed the Palak Paneer, as well.  Dessert was fantastic as well. The service was very friendly, but my gripe is it was a bit rusty. It's a relatively new restaurant, so those kinks will work themselves out. Make sure you mention the Groupon ahead of time.
Was driving for a while and i saw this place and stopped in. Food was good and so was price. best thing about this diner was the portion size!

OK, first about the food - it was delicious.  The Chilled Poached Foie Gras was amazing.  The Escargot with green cauliflower in a parsley chicken sauce was very different from other snail dishes that I've tried and was also delicious. The Seared Artic Char was the "winner" of the evening, with the fish cooked perfectly and the skin seared to the point that it just slid off the fish, almost like a potato chip.  It was very very good.  I was a little disappointed in the rabbit dish, which had more foie gras than rabbit. I have to say I guess we're spoiled.  Most of the restaurants we go to in Philly are BYOB, which helps to reduce the sticker shock when you get the bill.  Le Cheri now has their liquor license, so if getting a bottle of wine with dinner (although there are other options), you know that the bill will be increased by at least around $50. The setting is a little more subdued (read elegant, dark, old world) than most of the restaurants in town, including Bibou, the other restaurant owned by the same couple running Le Cheri.  This shouldn't stop you from trying this beautiful location but we both thought we would return to Bibou before returning here, Before tip, with a bottle of wine and no dessert, we paid around $138.

We recently experienced an extraordinary epicurean evening at Le Cheri.  Every morsel and drop delightful!  From the special ravioli (filled with 2 fishes and garnished with flavorful oil and herbs) to the fresh fish for two served table side (perfectly cooked in a pastry shell) to the decadent desserts (chocolate bread pudding never tasted so good!) - the meal was amazing!  In addition, the wine pairings perfectly complimented our food and our tastes....Charlotte is a Wine Wizard! We are still glowing from our experience and will be sure to return soon!

We had Saturday reservations for 9pm. Since it was a lousy night outside we called to ask they had been any cancelations for a earlier time. Also , we're at the age where we are too young for early bird special, but 9pm dinner is a little late for us. They didn't have anything but said they would call if anything changed. And they did! We got in at 7pm. Perfect. We had the Salad Lyonaise, and the Ravoli cream cheese for starters. Both were very good, but the salad gets the nod for being different.  I had the short ribs which I'm always a sucker for. They were delicious, and my wife had something I could neither pronounce or remember, but she enjoyed greatly. Obviously, being French they have several bottles of wine to choose from, and a handful by the glass. I was pleasantly surprise with their unusual beer selection. I have a French triple that was very nice. The ambiance was ok.  The table were sat at was very close to the next table.
Everything is amazing here. the deli is quick and delicious, the pizza is great alternative for a fast lunch and their coffee is fresh and perfect for a pick-me-up!

As the other reviewers have stated this place is quite large with several different sections - restaurant, bakery and specialty packaged / grocery items.  Overall the quality of the food is quite high and portions are generous. If you are a fan of Calandra's, then you will likely appreciate that the Village offers everything they are famous for under one roof.

Been to Calandras many times in recent times due to reviews of their bakery and baked goods. Not overly impressed. Those giving it five stars clearly have not gone to te bakeries that truly offer the earth of fresh foods that leave you wanting more. Review is based on over ten or so visits. Parking is nothing short of a cluster.... Whoever designed the parking probably built that monstrosity next to MetLife stadium. No left turn out of parking lot. Setup is nice with restaurant and coffee shop but overall layout is messy. Ordered dozen rolls, two large dinner rolls, French bread and a basket of goods to go. All cold upon pick up and noted to manager that as a fresh bakery, that is not good enough. Gave them he benefit of the doubt but since this visit everything from counter front is cold to the touch. If you advertise fresh, serve fresh! Calandras has the reputation of the best in NJ. It just isn't. Not anymore. Lou has let standards drop over the last three years at this store. There is no doubt the rolls from supermarkets are good but they are loaded with preservatives....tasty (and rated the best). But, leave them in your bread bin for a couple of days and watch what happens. Sugar desserts are great! Servers are inexperienced with Italian bakery but that is to be expected....but again, if you advertise to be the best...I will rate based on that. A good place for a casual person wanting baked goods. If you want the best, avoid or at least get everything fresh or ask for it that way.

Went here for lunch during the week and I must say I was very impressed.  The atmosphere was great and the service was excellent. I like the idea of small plates.  Me and my guest ordered  5 plates to share they were all very good.  I was less impressed with the fried chicken dish I felt that is was a little bland and the breading didn't really stay on and the egg dish lacked seasoning.  Other then that all in all was a nice meal.

We were looking forward to trying this new restaurant in Princeton. The plus is that it is a BYOB and the food was delicious. We had the grilled octopus (delicious) and the grilled beet salad (excellent); I had the grilled skate (again delicious). Everyone seemed to like their dishes. Negatives - the small plates did not come out fast enough; one friend had to wait almost 45 minutes for his dish. Waiter tried to be helpful, but still the wait was too long. Also, the restaurant is so noisy that we could not hear ourselves talk. We do not have trouble hearing, but the noise level will keep us from returning. Go on a beautiful spring or summer evening when you can sit outdoors. MKF

I would give this place 5 stars for the Chef, the food, the service from the kitchen and the manager. As somebody else has mentioned.... a shame to loose a star because of lack of service. We had eight dishes and EVERYTHING was amazing. Were FINALLY seated at the bar after having been standing around  for 20 min looking at 6 EMPTY spots in the bar.  The hostess seemed overwhelmed. Smiling smiling and seemed to have the latest computer software to show her which seat was booked and which was open. It was super busy and there were plenty of " hands on deck"... still she would clear a glass here a plate there instead of concentrating on getting people seated. When finally seated we sat another 10 min...and NOTHING! Finally this sweet smiling young waitress came and opened our wine .... took our order.... but didn't think to give us wine glasses. After another good while I got up and got us the glasses myself. Water we had to ask for after another while. It was my husband's first time and he was getting desperate because of the poor service. I assured him the food was so worth waiting for. AND IT WAS! As soon as we were out of the grip of the hostess and our waitress everything runs like an orchestra.  What a delight. The chef calls out the orders ..and when dish is ready he calls " hands please "... a waiter is ready to serve the dish ... luckily NOT depending on your waitress because we would still have been waiting. The manager was helping where he saw the service "slipping" on the floor. He was outstanding .... but our waitress and the hostess needs to find a job with less pressure. Sweet and polite is wonderful but doesn't cut it.

Mmm delicious Saturday brunch.  My friends and I sampled about everything on the menu (between the 5 of us) and all of it was wonderful.  I'm Lebanese, so I know when I'm eating good Lebanese food, and this was definitely up to par.  I would recommend it to anyone who is interested in getting great food without spending too much money!

Birthplace of Phish.  Yay hippies! Awesome gravy fries.  Perfect snack after a night at the bars. Need I say more? This is a hidden gem venue, in the heart of Burlington, VT.  If you are in town, stop by for a drink or let your dreads down and catch a band jamming out.
a classic burlington spot, if you want to experience burlington you have to go here! good music, good drinks, good drinking food!
Always a treat! Consistent and wonderful burgers and the shakes are thick and creamy!

Khao Kang translates to rice and curry / stew/ soup.  A nice new addition to the Thai food scene.   They have a stream table with a variety of choices, choose two items for $7 or three for $7.50.  We've seen this before with the Chinese lunch boxes in Flushing and Elmhurst - this is similar, straightforward and simple, and this is Thai. There is no waitress here to seat you or take your order.  Walk inside the restaurant - and if you are dining in, scope out your seats.  There were 2 tables of 4 and one table that fits up to 10 - be ready to share your table and make some new friends.  Go up to the steam table and order your meal, pay at the register (cash only) and then settle down some home-style Thai cuisine. They don't make your food to order, if you don't like a particular dish then choose something else.  We had fish in yellow curry with sour bamboo shoots, pork basil, tom kha gai - chicken galangal soup, sweet pork, quail with bamboo, chili pork with thai eggplant and string beans.  You won't find many of these dishes in your typical Thai restaurant.  Everything we tried were tasty, comforting, and authentic- they used traditional ingredients such as coconut milk, galangal, coriander, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves (beware some of the choices were spicy).  If you need to further enhance your food, there is fish sauce with chili peppers on the table to kick it up a notch- but we found the food perfectly seasoned and didn't need to add anything. There were plenty of desserts to cool down the heat, as well as drinks (Thai iced tea/coffee, grass jelly, logan). You will only find this food in Thailand or in the kitchen of your favorite Thai host.  Come with a hungry stomach and open mind, you will leave satisfied and full.

This place rocks! Similar steam table setup as some  Chinese places BUT with a much cooler and modern decor. There is no question as to whether the food is authentic. You will notice a good portion of Thai diners from the neighborhood + everyone gets the same selection. I also tried one of their desserts which was really good too. You can tell there is NO watering down of flavors or "gringo" spicing, its the real deal and the food is great! To top it off you will only pay 7.50 for 3 choices of protein or veggie sides with rice in a hip, clean environment.  In a city full of mediocre, overpriced, watered down Thai food, this place stands out as a true gem!

Do you like home-cooked Thai food or you never had Thai dishes and just want to sample? Are you adventurous? Go visit Khao Kang. They have a Thai steam table with ten selections. You can get 2 items with rice ($7.00) or 3 items with rice ($7.50). You won't get fancy plates or rice molded in the shapes of stars and pyramids or flower garnishes. What you will get is close to homemade Thai food that is tasty. They only cook one level of spiciness so maybe spicy for some. Most of the others in my group felt it was a little too spicy for them. They took advantage of the free water with lemon. When I was there the place was packed with Thai folks enjoying the food. We also tried their Thai Ice Tea ($2)- it was very good. We tried two of their jelly desserts ($3 each)  too; a green and white multilayer Jelly and a tan colored jelly mini cups. Both good but the green & white layered squares are better. Seating at Khao Kang is limited; I counted only 16 table-chair spots. Parking on the street is not easy because of the Elmhurst Hospital a block away and the many other popular Thai restaurants on the same street.

Kaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaang!! (star trek fans knowattamean) Anyway...the food is fo'reals Thai....no Manhattan/Park-slope Gringo style watered down flavours.  This is what you'd get walking around in Thailand..really good selection that changes day to day...no menus...just point and eat up! They have desserts too (ok..smaller than other Thai spots)  I just wish theyd make some strictly Vegetarian dishes for my vegan "bunny" friends. PLEASE--Krup!!!

Don't expect this place to be like Spicy Shallot and Ayada because it's not. While Spicy Shallot offers everything from thai to sushi to asian fusion dishes, Khao Kang specializes in authentic Thai dishes.  There is no menu because they offer different dishes everyday. You choose between 8 0r 10 dishes to create a dish with 2 or 3 curries with a large heaping of rice. But I must say all three of my dishes were VERY spicy, so the faint of heart beware. I would definitely recommend this to others and cant wait to go back and try their other dishes.

Creative sushi and standard Hibachi. Decor is nice and modern. Staff is friendly and service is usually prompt. Plan B Burger, next store, often has a long wait. If you're in the mood for something Asian instead of beefy, check this place out.

The best sushi in the Hartford area--flavorful, fresh rolls. Great drinks, great appetizers, awesome friendly knowledgeable wait staff. I've been to most of the other highly rated sushi restaurants on here, and Ginza is my favorite hands down. Don't forget to ask about the specials that are not on the menu--they're usually the best things there!! Favorites: Paradise Roll, seasoned edamame, Asian Pear Cosmo :-)

Chinese owned Japanese restaurants are a dime a dozen, and the fool the unsuspected eye. To the trained eye, nothing can get passed you. Hence, when I checked out the menu for Ginza, I was pretty skeptical. A sushi place with hibachi, Chinese and Thai food, all mixed in with supposed Japanese food? This is a formula for epic fail. Nonetheless, when on a business trip, beggars cannot be choosers, and I'll take fake Japanese food over McDonald's any day. Ginza in Wethersfield is a pretty decently sized restaurant. They have a bar up in the front, and then numerous booths scattered throughout the floor. With that being said, I've only gotten take out so I can't speak to the service. As far as the food goes, after coming here a 2-3x, I've realized what is acceptable to get, and what you should steer away from. Right off the bat, the Tum Yum soup and seafood miso soup are both pretty bad. The tum yum soup tastes nothing like what it's supposed to taste and you should just avoid it at all costs. It's watery, and just does not have flavor. If you order the seafood miso soup, then be prepared for a bunch of imitation crab meat. With all those things mixed in, the miso flavor is lost and it just kind of tastes weird. With appetizers, there are some interesting ones, with the Peking duck roll being one of them. To be honest, it's actually not that bad, considering this place is Chinese owned. There's not too much hoison sauce and the duck is crispy enough to be tasty. Now if you plan to go with the dim sum deluxe, then be prepared for some microwaved frozen dim sum. The shu mai and har gaw look straight up pulled from the freezer, and at $13, there's no way you can justify the cost. What I've come to stick to are the uni sushi, toro sashimi, amaebi, and just for kicks, the dragon roll. The sashimi isn't the absolute best, but out of everything on the menu, it's by far the most amazing thing you can get. The uni tastes fresh enough, but the toro is hit or miss. Then again, I've learned that any toro is better than no toro. Out in Connecticut, there really isn't a great Japanese restaurant. Ginza is alright, considering the location, but that doesn't mean that you should be making this place your regular spot. The flavors are bland and generic, and there are just too many things on the menu for any one dish to be amazing. For business trips, it's acceptable, but otherwise, Chipotle doesn't sound half bad.

Boyfriend and I always get takeout from Kimchi Taco when we want something hearty but healthy (in comparison to other takeout places) and delicious and cheap. It's so good that writing this review is making me crave it! I suggest the spicy chicken kimchi bowl and the pulled chicken tostada. So so good!

I usually get the chicken burrito here although I've been tempted to order the chicken wings as well on many occasions. The chicken burrito is awesome! I get it with kimchi fried rice and that combined with the sauce on the chicken and cheese is just a great combination of flavors. I've tried the tacos as well which I didn't like as much because I'm more of a burrito person, but I will say that the korean fried chicken tacos are amazing. Definitely the best taco from their menu. Solid korean mexican fusion and a must try if you've never had korean burritos!
My food was delicious. Delivery service was great and polite! Thank you, Donna

I've been a big fan of their taco truck (Mexico Boulevard) for its delectable pork and pineapple taco and killer guac. But when it stopped coming to Ditmars, I sought out their new restaurant. The tacos I loved from the truck are there, though a bit pricier than they once were. But the quality is even better. So fair enough. We started our meal with the $8 guacamole and chips appetizer. The guac was outstanding, fresh and smooth with just the right spice. The chips were made on the spot! STILL WARM! We ordered the Al Pastor (pork & pineapple), Adobo (roasted pork), Tinga (chipotle chicken), Bistec En Pasilla (drunken beef), and Nopales (grilled cactus and panel cheese). All of the above where on the truck except for the cactus. All were lick the plate good. They also gave us samples of their new hot sauces, which had great flavor as well as HEAT! (Use sparingly, like drops.) They don't have their beer & wine license yet, but their sodas are a great compliment to the tacos. I suggest the grapefruit one, which doesn't taste like grapefruit. It tastes sweeter, less bitter, fruitier. The meals are great, the environment is bright, rustic and casual. The service is friendly, enthusiastic and well-informed about the menu. Basically, it's an outstanding addition to the neighborhood.

Chela & Garnacha is a perfect addition to 36 ave! Not to knock other small Astoria businesses, but if you're still going to Arepa Cafe (next door), you're doing it wrong. The tacos, specifically the tinga and al pastor are my favorite, but you should try them all. Super tasty and fresh ingredients, paired with different salsas of all heat levels. Not sure if tortillas are made in-house, but they are perfect size and softness for the amount of meat served on them. When they offer you crispy cheese for your tacos, say yes, you won't regret it. As for the other menu items, I've tried the ceviche + intrincadas, all delicious and fresh. Tacos are definitely the star of the menu, curious to see how it will expand once they incorporate brunch and lunch later in the year. I would've given this place 5 stars if they opened with their beer + liquor license, hopefully I'll see micheladas on the menu soon!

I've been ordering from here for about four and a half years. When we first found this place it was outstanding. But over the past year or so the quality of the service and food has been on a decline. I've asked for primarily the same thing every time. Two half sandwiches withe the bread toasted. One with Salami, Provolone, lettuce, onions, and oil and vinegar with EXTRA onions. Then Turkey, Swiss, Lettuce, Onion, Tomato, oil/vinegar with extra Mayo. Well this evening I've had it. I will post pictures so you can see. One that was supposed to have Extra onions. Had NO onions. The sandwich that was supposed to have extra Mayo. Had a smear of of Mayo. And had Provolone instead of Swiss. It's unfortunate that tonight we will be eating Joey's for the final time. At one point we ordered here every week without fail. Then it went to twice a month to every other month. But the last three times we've ordered it's been utter chaos. It's very sad.

It is a great place to hang around with friends. We love the music outside once in a while. Drinks are inexpensive.   burger with fries portion was humongous.   While some people think it is loud,  the place is lively. Friday and Saturday evenings on Summer days are nice when you get to sit outside.   Love it.

This review is for their burgers and wings only. Tavern has their wings night on Mon and burgers on Weds. Their wings are meaty and acceptably spicy for a Korean-American who loves flavorful heat. Their burgers are the best in the area -- hand-formed, large patties, good bun and great sweet potato fries or onion rings. They skimp on the lettuce, tomato and red onion, but you'll live. I also like their salmon burger when I want something slightly "healthier." I doubt the patty is house made, but I like the tzaziki sauce that comes with it. Also, their craft beer selection has improved immensely, which is a draw for me. Overall, it's a good option for a night of drinking any warm night on their outdoor patio by the lake. If you want a place to eat burgers or wings in Hightstown, come by on a Mon or Weds.

Great beer selection and good pricing. I recently moved to Hightstown and definitely see this as my main watering hole. I haven't eaten much of the food, but the Irish nachos were quite delicious. The bar atmosphere is a bit divey (which I personally enjoy), but the restaurant side has a nicer ambiance. There is also a lovely outdoor seating area by (you guessed it!) the lake.

let me start off with MARIO CART!!! and I was sold. also biggest TVs in Old city to watch all the games, and videos to every song that comes on. pretty cool place, great pitcher deals.. hot bartenders and awesome food! i happened to come in when it was taco tuesday, 2$ tacos that were gormet as fuck i will most definatly go back.

It's taken me too long to write a review about this restaurant but that in no way should suggest that this place is anything short of fantastic.  I've already eaten here three times with my girlfriend and each time we shared one of the larger meals that were enough for two. Cozido à portuguesa  -- on point, I loved all the pig parts just like my grandmother's. I'd only suggest a few more slices of farinheira please.  For those of you who aren't familiar with this dish, it's a traditional portuguese style boiled dinner with various meats, turnips, potatoes, cabbage, portuguese chouriço and farinheira which is a unique portuguese flour sausage with a nice tangy flavor. My only request is more farinheira please!   Still they execute this dish very nicely. Sardinhas Assadas --   Grilled Sardines, perfect on a summer day.  Accompanied with peppers roasted to perfection. Feijoada Brasileira -- The Brazilian classic, black beans and pork stewed to perfection, served with crisp collard greens, fluffy rice and orange slices.  The best I've had in Newark. The place is byob which makes for an all around cheaper meal.  One of my favorite spots in the Ironbound.

Every other review here that says the food is overpriced and sub-par is spot on. If you want to pay twice what you should for food that's mediocre at best, but are impressed by a couple canoes hanging from the ceiling and some leather couches, then this is your place. The bar is no better. If it's a busy night and you want to go to the bar and get a drink, budget 30 minutes for that task - it'll take you a good 15 minutes to get the bartender's attention, and then another 15 minutes after you've been given your drink until he'll come back and take your money.

This restaurant has really improved!! I've had lunch here several times in the past few months and am impressed by the improvement in food quality and lower seating density. It isn't as cramped as before. The noise level is a bit better, too. Lunch here is very civilized and pleasant. I've come to like this restaurant.

Lunch was just as disappointing as dinner.  I ordered the lamb pita and the lamb was chopped and loose with some yogurt sauce mixed in which was bizarre, I thought it would be chunks of meat or ground meat rolled into patties like kofta.   There was also not enough lamb especially since there was so much bread.  Very unbalanced meal.
Snobby and expensive,  bartenders only good thing about this joint

Went with the recommendations and had the cold appetizer platter and wow was it delicious. Fresh and flavorful but I should have listened to Yelpers...it truly is a meal within itself. I tried splitting it and even then I had no room for dinner.

Chicken tacos were like cold cardboard. This is NOT Mexican. Mexican food is defined by the freshness of the ingredients and the simplicity of the cooking style. My "Chicken Tacos" were cold, limp and inedible.  I had one bite and then left. I've had better Mexican food in Sweden.

Had a great meal tonight.  Ordered one of their specials, it came out in a timely manner.  The service was friendly and courteous.  The meal was made according to order and tasty.  Thanks for a great experience.
If you want real Mexican food, go elsewhere. The tamales were horribly salty and lack any real flavor. Head downtown to Madera's!.

Location is excellent - haven't tried any of the eats, but, service at the bar is top-notch an prices are reasonable. The ID guy at night is temporary to please the bitchy neighbors, so don't be offended by that- the place is brand new an well decorated. It just needs to be bigger to accommodate the local demand. Easier said than done though.

Walked by this afternoon with my roomie today, popped in just check it out but decided to stay for "a drink," which happened to be a "voodoo" bloody mary (which is basically a meal FYI). The lunch happy hour looks promising for future afternoon wanderings.

this is my favorite place in nyc. it only opened recently, but every time i'm in brooklyn i make sure to spend serious time there. the food is delicious--they have pretty reasonably priced appetizers and amazing po boys. their beers on tap are always changing and are always great choices. the bartenders are all really nice and helpful and the atmosphere is wonderful. it's really laid-back, and it feels like you've left nyc and gone to new orleans. i would recommend it to pretty much anyone

Catfish is my new local.  I've been there several times since they opened a few weeks ago.  I can't tell you how happy I am to have them as a new addition to the neighborhood.   DECOR: Really well-done with great attention to detail.  From the hand-laid tin near the entrance, to the counter-lever controlled sliding doors to the bathrooms and the televisions that can be hidden by unobtrusive panels that swing up and all but disappear when the tvs are in use, it's clear to me that the place was well-thought out and expertly executed.  Kudos to whoever decided to go with the Mrs. Meyers hand soap.   FOOD: I have had brunch there -- the grits were outstanding as was the tasso ham and the andouille sausage.  I have had dinner there -- the rattatouille is packed with flavor and served over rice.  What could have just been a de-facto vegetarian option just sings on the plate.  The Slow Cooked Beef Po' Boy is decadent and messy from the overflow of ingredients amassed on the bread.  Order this before you have a few drinks or you're likely to wear it.  But when you taste that slow-cooked beef, you might not care.   DRINKS:  The Voodoo Bloody Mary with crab meat and shrimp and topped with a wee bit of Guiness might just be the best bloody mary I've had in my life.  I tossed it back so quickly it frightened me.  But, for me, the beer program is the finest in the neighborhood and what truly sets it apart from the other restaurants in the area.  16 revolving taps of craft brew featuring some of the finest examples of styles by breweries such as Weyerbacher, Left Hand, Abita (natch), and their newest addition of Jolly Pumpkin Brewery's Maracaibo as an expansion of their sour beer selections.  I mean, sour beer on draft (as well as the classic example Monk's Sour in bottles) two blocks from my apartment?  There is nothing wrong with that last sentence. SERVICE: Service is excellent.  The bar staff is friendly without being intrusive, and are experts in connecting neighbors in conversation.  I'm more an "eat at the bar" kind of guy and we've only taken seats at a table a handful of times.  Each time the waitress was attentive without being overbearing.  A real chill vibe that starts with the seat yourself policy.   Each of the 3 owners make it a point to make rounds and connect with anyone willing to chat with them.  Their friendliness and passion for what they have created is a joy to experience.  Well done, guys.  Welcome to the neighborhood!  I'll try to make it in before last call tonight!

I love this place! It's got an amazing neighborhood bar feel, great personalities, cocktails, food (get the GUMBO!!) - I also hear they're planning to expand their menu soon- get to their brunch on the weekend (and make sure to get the cheddar grits!) Anyone that doesn't like Catfish needs to do some serious introspection! What a great addition to the expanding bar/restaurant scene in Crown Heights!
Brunch needs to happen everyday.

I started with a Bloody Mary super hot (I didn't order a Voodo - just asked for a Bloody Mary) and tasted of Old Bay seasoning for some reason.  Good beer selection, switched after being fried by the Bloody Mary.  Good oysters, had a couple different types.  Will not order the  beef Poboy, sloppy and fairly tasteless, hard to eat as a sandwich, maybe it was tasteless after the super over the top "taste" of the Bloody Mary?   I'll try something else next time, I'll be back. Service was good.

This club totally RULES. The gumbo is bangin' and so is the talent- oooooo boy. If Genny Cream aint your bag, don't worry, after ten shots of Old Overholt, you wont care. You want upcycled Vermont farm wood? Check. Bearded bartender with kissable lips? Check. Whiskey all day long? Check. Brunch? Everyone wants brunch. CHECK. BEST GRITS EVA. Can't wait to lounge in that back patio and talk about stuff and hang out with all of my favorite people. I LOVE YOU, CATFISH.

Not a memorable meal. Drinks so so only. 5 stars for service though. They even gave us a free round of drinks toward the end. Great location in Tribeca. Has potential, but food and drink needs to be better.

Decent neighbourhood food - nothing to travel for, but the staff were incredibly friendly.  We shared the mushrooms with aioli (best thing we ate), the chicken wings (pretty good, but not earth shattering), the watermelon salad, the roasted cauliflower (this was really good!). We also received complimentary oysters and garlic pickles from the chef - which was nice of them!  I'm not a pickle fan, so I'm not really in a position to comment. Would I go again - eh, probably not.  But if I was hungry and nearby, it does the job.  And it was pretty empty for a Friday night, so a good place to just walk-in.

Yum! Lovely atmosphere and great music (Beastie Boys!). Super attentive, friendly service. Unique, seriously tasty food. What we ordered: Started with the insane popcorn and awesome watermelon appetizer. Yum. Next came the mushrooms and garlic (amazing) and the cauliflower (good). My friend ordered the burger and tater tots and he seemed very happy. I tried the tater tots and thought they were the best I'd ever had...ever. Before checking this place out I emailed them and asked if they had any vegan options. The Sous Chef wrote me back personally and said they had plenty for me to choose from. I thought that was pretty nice of him. While the side dishes are unique and tasty (and large portions!), there were no proteins to choose from (beans, lentils, chick peas, etc.). To be fair, I think the broccoli side had peanuts on it, which I will order next time. They obviously take their menu very seriously, and with all their creative dishes, I think they could easily add one or two "mains" for vegans (soy-free please, tofu is gross). My friend ordered the s'mores for dessert and I tried them...pretty yummy and lovely presentation. BTW I saw some fantastic onion rings coming out of the kitchen like every 10 seconds. I will definitely try them next time. Outdoor seating also available.

Great friendly knowledgable service, delicious food (get the burger and the wings), beautiful space. Was still busy/every table full at 11pm in Tribeca - thats saying something. Speaking of which, its refreshingly nice to have something open late in Tribeca. I was impressed that the director of services(?) even came over to our table at the end of the meal to ask how everything was, ask for any suggestions and just made us feel welcome and appreciated. Will definitely come back!

I've only been here once so I'm going on that experience. My Dad took me here for lunch on a Wednesday. Pretty empty since it was 2pm. He woks downtown and says the restaurant is usually frequented by downtown lawyers etc. I ordered a salad with salmon. It was the most amazing thing I've ever eaten. Sounds lame, but holy God. The salmon was perfect and spiced perfect. The "salad" wasn't just greens...had lentils, mango, etc and overall was one of the best meals I've ever had. The portion was gigantic and I finished the whole thing. My Dad's shrimp salad was just as good but mine was better :) I will go back here

Wow. During our meal at the new Lea I thought to myself, "I need to write a yelp review for this place!" Our meal was great. We were a party of 4 and ordered three appetizers, the braised collards (delicious!), the lima bean crostino (super tasty!) and the risotto balls with pork and veal with melted mozzarella (lovely!). Our waiter was appropriately attentive and cute. The 1/2 carafe of wine was a great deal. And the meal itself (3 pizzas and a pasta dish) was very very good. We ordered dessert too and were really enjoying the whole experience. We got the check and dropped almost 200 well spent dollars...UNTIL... the bearded manager guy comes over a mere two minutes after we've signed the check and asks us to leave. I think the words he used were something like, "I don't mean to be passive aggressive but we have a 2 hour wait for tables..." I have never been a restaurant lingerer (full disclosure we were seated at the table for one hour forty minutes), also I was literally putting on my scarf when he approached the table, so I am kind of offended. It was very disappointing because up until that point it had been a really nice experience. We live in the neighborhood and enjoy going to all the great local spots. It's a shame that a good meal with friends and excellent service was undermined by this guy's anxiety. We may go back. We may not. But if there's ever a two hour wait for this place we would gladly go to the Farm (or Wheated, or Cinco de Mayo, or Mimi's, or Purple Yam, or Ox Cart, etc...) instead. **Please note, if we hadn't been asked to leave I would've given this place 4-5 stars.

I live in Brooklyn and work in midtown. I regularly take advantage of the best of culinary NYC. I went recently to the newly-opened Lea in a medium-sized group and we ordered a variety of dishes. The food was very good. We ordered several appetizers, pizzas, pastas, drinks, and desserts. The balances of tastes -- acids to starches to sweet -- were excellent. However, everything else made the experience unworthy. The service was middling to hostile, strangely, from the moment we stepped in to an empty space at opening time and asked for a table. The prices were completely overblown in relation to the serving sizes. Appetizers could be shared with 2 people at best but were priced for 3 or 4. Members of the party enjoyed the pizza, but the presentation and preparation was on par with every other fire-cooked pizza in the last 2-4 years and at double the price. The pasta was on par with Franny's both in taste and price, but in an incomparable neighborhood, in minuscule proportions, and with unfriendlier service. I do wonder at which demographic the owners are aiming. I have sampled almost every restaurant in the surrounding neighborhoods and many "best of" in Manhattan and Brooklyn. If San Remo (the local pizza slice joint in the nabe) stepped up its game and served more fresh pasta, the two restaurants would be comparable. Come to think of it, perhaps I'll go have a chat with them.  San Remo that is, since I will not be returning to nor recommending Lea again. Truly sorry to say so! I had such high hopes. Sad.
I went on a Friday night. Great service great food and great wine. If you are looking for a nice meal and laid back servers this is your place. I will be coming back very soon.

We went to Guacamole based on Yelp recommendations...and we weren't disappointed! We both had the Chicken Mole..and it's the best mole I've had. The owner told us his family owns a mole factory in Mexico..and that this was his grandmother's recipe. The guacamole was outstanding, also. It was $2.50 for a small dish..but it was good! The portions are hearty. the chicken mole dinner was just that...lots of sliced chicken, rice and refried beans with shredded lettuce and tomato. The place is casual and  small...seats about 15 people. The service is friendly and we were made to feel right at home. Two chicken mole dinners, 2 guacamole and chips, and two drinks were $24 and change. Tip jar is on the counter. While we were there folks came in for lots of take away. We'll be going back...

If your idea of a veggie burrito is nothing but rice and beans, this may be for you. If, on the other hand, you've had a veggie burrito from anywhere else in the world and have come to expect things such as cheese, sour cream, and guacamole, you will likely be disappointed.

Really good food. Tacos are the best, but the burritos aren't bad either. Love the guacamole. The Churros are the best I've ever had. The place is small and funky, but it's all about the food. Rodolfo, the guy behind the counter, is always nice and welcoming in an edgy hipster kind of way.

Half Price Bottle of wine Wendesday!?!?!  Situated beside the TLA, Redwood is a snazzy little addition to the South Street area.  The place was a bit quiet, and I really can't figure out why!  We dined alfresco and took advantage of many of the awesome specials they had.  First, my friend and I shared a cold bottle of pinot grigio on a warm summer day to celebrate her birthday.  We also split the margarita flat bread which was part of many $6 appetizer specials.  It was delicious with lots of fresh mozzarella and very tasty bread.  Our server was really friendly and outgoing and he really made our dining experience awesome.  He left us alone to hang out and catch up, but it was like he could read our minds to know when we wanted him to come back; a perfect balance.  For my 'entree' i had the tofu satay skewers which came with a pesto garlic sauce on them.  They were a hair salty, but mainly just delicious.  All in all, I really enjoyed this place, and for the price point, its a great deal!  I'll definitly return!

Me and my sister came here for a quick chill dinner. I got the mini 5 beers they offered for 5 bucks it was actually good except one tasted like dirty water which I didn't finish. They offer small plates so we got the oysters? Calamari and margarita flat bread. Oysters were ok, calamari was good and I liked the sauce but the flat bread sucked! The cheese came off right when I got a slice so I basically ate tomato sauce on bread. Te bartender was nice tho. Over all it was an OK experience doubt I'll go back again.

I was looking for a dish of pasta on a Friday night before catching the opening of the movie "Bad Teacher".  I found awesome pasta, can't say the same about the movie. My wife and I went to Roberto Cafe because it is a few blocks from our house and after living here a year we had not tried it yet.  I am sorry we didn't get to this place sooner.  Great little BYOB.  Very nice atmosphere, the waitstaff was so nice, and I am assuming they are the owners.  Most importantly the food was delicious.  We started with Mozzarella Affumicata (grilled mozzarella with radicchio, mushrooms and balsamic) and it was bread dipping good. For dinner I had the Veal Saltimbocca which was a little salty but overall good flavor.  I grabbed a side of penne in marinara and the sauce was good and spicy.  My wife had Spaghetti Tarantini (mussels, clams and calamari in a marinara sauce).  The dish was very good and the portions were large.  For dessert we had the Mascarpone Cheesecake.  A great choice, very creamy.  Overall this was a nice little BYOB and I will definitely go back (probably several times).

We started with a variety of appetizers that the restaurant suggested and provided to meet the needs of our group.  Cozze E Vongole (PEI Mussels) and the Smoked Mozzarella and Grilled Vegetables were both great. I ordered the Risotto, which was a hearty dish with the smoked mozzarella melted into the rice and a limited amount of sausage. While it was good, I had serious food envy with all the delicious pasta around me - I will just have to go back!

I really like to give this place 3.5 stars. When my brother was visiting I knew I had to take him to one our cheaper Italian byos to get the real Philadelphia dining experience. My roommate mentioned Roberto Cafe and was sold. I called around 2pm Saturday for a 7:15pm reservation for 6 people that evening and they were happy to accommodate (gotta love that!). Highlights from the meal: Food arrived very quickly! All the pasta dishes were very authentic (everyone enjoyed their meal) Things that can be improved: The air conditioning situation (In their defense it was during the middle of heat wave on one of the hottest days of the year, but they only have one ac unit and a ceiling fan for the entire restaurant. We were also right by the door.) Our waiter was condescending and patronizing at times I definitely need to come back when it is nice weather and even try out the patio. Since we were eating hot food in a hot restaurant we were somewhat uncomfortable, but we can't penalize the restaurant for the weather. But the conditions didn't make for the best dining experience. I will return and be sure to update my review.

my favorite margarita in the whole city!  i know...big statement but i have tested it, tasted it, this is my conclusion and I am sticking to it...for now. only wish that parking around that area isn't such a biatch tho.

While waiting in line for Grimaldi's decided to see what my fellow Yelpers said about Juliana's and was pleasantly surprised. Since I've been to Grimaldi's decided to check out Juliana's and I'm really glad I did. The staff and decor makes for a great setting to enjoy pizza! Decided on the traditional pie and did half fennel sausage as well. The sauce is so great and overall was impressed! As a person that loves pizza and has been to most of the best pizza places in the city I definitely would put this up there on my list! Enjoy!

My daughter have this place a 5 before she even tried the pizza! The pizza is excellent, skip the long line at Grimadli's & come here where Patsy Grimaldi himself was seating guests. He is charming, even gave my daughter a pen for when she starts school! The pizza is perfectly cooked, with a wonderful taste. We had the red pizza with pepperoni & sweet sausage and a white pizza. The leftovers where carefully packaged up which I appreciated since we were walking around a bit before taking the train home. I love the decor, the acoustics in the restaurant aren't the best so if it is busy night and you are hoping to have an intimate dinner where you can chat this might not be the place. However, come for the food and then walk around DUMBO afterwards for a conversation!

Overall - A Service - A (Tiffany was ourwaitress and she was outstanding. Came to the table the right amount of times to check on us and overall very good) Pizza - A+ (we got the Margherita and Pepperoni pizzas. Amazing pizza that isn't too doughy and has the right amount of sauce) Wait time - B+ - less than 30 mins but shorter than Grimaldi's Overall this is the original Grimaldi's. Grimaldi's (next door) seems to be a major tourist trap.

Pretty disappointing. Pretty average tasting, there's definitely better places around here. Came here with a group of 7 and everyone agreed it was nothing special. Service & staff are very cold. They put about 2 pieces of basil on our margherita pizza & when we asked for extra basil on the side, they said they can't give us any for whatever odd reason. So we ordered extra basil on the next pizza & they put about 3 pieces. Maybe basil is a rare item around here? Wouldn't really come here again.

Best coal fired pizza we have had in New York!  Excellent wait staff, quick friendly service.  Located under the Brooklyn Bridge. This pizza place is owned by the original Grimaldi's owner, Patsy Grimaldi.  Ironically the store Patsy sold, along with his name, is still operating next door, providing a choice of pizzeria's under the bridge..

My coworkers and I ordered take out from this little Brooklyn gem, and we were all blown away by the taste profile and quality of the pizza. We ordered two specialty pies--the No.1 and the No.4. The No. 1 was a complete showstopper--house-made mozzarella, Scamorza (difficult to find in your run-of-the-mill pizza joint), salty pancetta, scallions and white truffles all on a crust that was the perfect combination of soft and crispy. The No. 4 was also absolutely delicious (especially the prosciutto), although not quite as inventive as the other pie. Prices are steep when compared to surrounding pizza places (specialty pies run around $30 each), but 2 pizzas ended up feeding five of us just fine. We didn't get to experience the service or the line (which often gets a little long, I've heard), but the food certainly speaks for itself!

Delicious pizza. Always great service. Very quick service. I have been here twice and both times have been wonderful. It is a great NY pizza place in a beautiful location. Fair prices as well. Can't wait to come back and try the cheesecake.
Perfect crust, delicious sauce, homemade mozzarella all baked in a coal fired oven, much, much better than the Grimaldi's next door!

I do not understand the long lines for the restaurant next door. Yes, it's got a bigger name, but Juliana's has better pizza, service and ambiance.   Everyone in my party of three thought the pizza rocked our world.  We shared a No. 4 (Tomato, mozzarella, arugula and prosciutto) and it was fresh and delicious. Service was prompt and efficient without being rushed.  And unlike the popular spot next door, Juliana's serves alcohol.   Hands down, this is the place to go for pizza if you're in the Brooklyn Bridge area in Brooklyn.  You'll have a wait to get into Juliana's, but it is worth it (and will likely be half the wait time as the spot next door.)

I was going to be in the area whale hunting (tracking down a rare beer), so I did a quick search on Bayonne to see what else might be worth visiting nearby.  El Aguila Dorada stuck out above all else.  I love Mexican taquerias; I have no clue why they aren't more prevalent in the NY metro area given the Mexican population.  This restaurant looks somewhat similar to a Mexican restaurant upstate (Cancun Inn) thanks to it's 2 room setup, but thankfully the food is much better.  Horchata was pretty good, although I prefer mine sans ice cubes.  Service was from a member of the owning family, and as you'd expect it was very good.  Given what I ate, I will be returning on subsequent whale hunting trips. The tortilla chips that came out were freshly made and tasty, and went well with a tangy tomato-based salsa.  I was a bit disappointed by the salsa verde, which while spicy was very basic otherwise.  Of all 3 salsas, the red chipotle salsa was the best; while it could've been spicier, there was a depth of flavor that wasn't present in the salsa verde.  I ordered the shrimp tacos, which included the 3 tacos with a hearty helping of baby shrimp on homemade tortillas, along with pico de gallo.  These tacos were pretty tremendous.  The tortillas were among the best I've had on this coast.  The shrimp were good, as was the pico de gallo.  A grilled scallion, radish, and a piece of cactus came on the side; the former 2 are typical at authentic taquerias like this, and the cactus was a nice touch even if it was just alright.  As a whole, this was pretty damn good lunch that scratched my itch for great Mexican food. You're lucky if you live by this place.  I want to go back and try some of the other taco varieties.  This was my first time in Bayonne, and I was surprised by the small town feel; in many ways, it's like I wish Jersey City was.  Regardless, this gives me a reason to come back eventually!

Definetly my go to place for authentic Mexican food in the Hudson county area. They deliver, but I recommend eating in instead because the food gets a little soggy in the containers. I've pretty much had every taco here from the tripe, to the roast pork, but my favorite is the beef tongue taco. The meat is flavorful and melts in your mouth. The gorditas are also solid, and the tortas are huge and filling. For the price i definitely would recommend coming here, instead of going to the usual chains that are more tex-mex than authentic Mexican

Cute place with good food. Sopas are fantastic. Mole chicken is good too. Only issue was how long it took for the food to come out. We ordered a quesadilla for our toddler and it seemed to take a loooong time. Servers were very nice.

I LOVE this place. I always joke with my husband that I think I was Mexican in another life because I'm always the first to try REAL Mexican restaurants. My best friend (who happens to be Mexican) came here once so I could show her that this is one of the few restaurants that cook real Mexican and she totally agreed! Reminded her of back home. Writing this is kinda making me hungry! Anyway, I can't wait to go back. I don't feel so bad about breaking my never ending diet for this place because it's really fresh and natural foods. From the looks of it almost all of their stuff is made on site. I have yet to try their tamales because im they usually run out by the time I get there. :( I'm a huge tamal fan! Yummy yummy!

Ok. First review EVER. I've came here twice in the last 2 weeks before deciding to write my thoughts on this place. I normally fucked with Taqueria in downtown if I need to get my taco fix but after Hurricane Sandy, that place just feels...different. Anyway. I come to this spot, which is much closer to where I live, after reading a few positive reviews on Yelp. A friend and I were seated and greeted with some complimentary chips and salsa. Cool. I order a few tacos (pork) and the chicken quesadilla (Mexican style, as they dub it). I also ordered the tamarind water for my drink. Food came out in a short time and I must say, they are very generous with the portions. Tacos were good but were definitely missing some flavor. It's dry in comparison to taqueria. The mexican style quesadillas were a pleasant surprise. It's basically a big ass taco, but the tortilla is fried so it's crispy.  The drink was also delicious, very balanced, sweet but not too sweet. I'm giving this place 4 stars, mainly cause it's cheap and I don't have to drive my ass to downtown just to get some "authentic" tacos. I will definitely hit this place more often.

A cold modelo and some bistec flautas will def hit the spot, glad they serve beer now :)  Overall the most authentic mexican you'll get in Bayonne/Jersey city.  I love their burritos, steak flautas, and the torta loca is huuuuge.  I think everything in this place is overall great

It is sad I have to write such a negative review because I had eaten in this place before and I believe the food is good.  But what happened last Sunday was EXTREMELY unpleasant! I made a reservation for 4 people and 2 of us arrived early.  We announced ourselves and we were asked if everybody was there already.  I said "no, they are coming", so we were invited to sit a the bar.  So far so good, it is pretty customary to wait for all the party to be present before sitting at the table. OK, no problem. Then other TWO parties arrived, just a couple of minutes before my other two friends, and BOTH of these parties were waiting for other people to arrive.  Well, BOTH of these parties were invited to sit at the table (even if the full party was not there, and without even asking us if we wanted to sit at the table as well) with the result that when my party was ready, we were not able to sit right away and they ended up offering us the most remote table inside the the room in a dark corner and far from the open window and the sun.  No one of my friends was happy about it, it was a beautiful day and we all would have preferred to sit closer to the window and fresh air.  But we were never even offered a choice.  I am sorry but we had our reservation and we arrived before.  We had the right of being offered the same service.  The lame excuse of the host was "sorry, we were under the impression you preferred to wait at the bar".  What? We were invited to wait at the bar, that was never our choice! This is definitely not the way to treat customers.  We ended up leaving Palma and eating somewhere else. Very sad for a good restaurant.

absolutely gorgeous restaurant with awesome bartender and great food. we had a reservation in the garden, and while they will not seat you until your entire party arrives, never mind that and have a drink at the bar. bartender swung a large ice cube around the wine glass for a minute, and the chardonnay was ice cold. great move! while the interior in general is beautiful, nothing beats sitting in the garden. they strung up white lights on the brick wall, and of course had globe lights strung across the top. pretty freaking magical overall sorry for writing a novel about it. next to barolo (rip), my second fav garden. the fettuccine ai funghi is a must-order. everything else e.g. fried artichokes, branzino, angus strip loin were all good, but the pasta dish was the most notable. how can you go wrong with white truffles?
This is by far one of the best hidden gems in the city. I was born and raised in NYC and this is a top 5 spot. Go early to sit in the garden.
classy italian joint with homemade dish tastiness in west village. garden is pretty and wine is yey! take a date or go with clients. :D
Definitely concerned with turnover on a Saturday night. Host is a little pushy on incomplete parties. Was better on a previous visit, but still one of the better Hibachi joints in Morris/Essex County

This place was good. Had the filet and chicken hibachi. Fun chief doing the standard hibachi tricks. Fried Rice good and noodles were a surprise. As with all Hibachi grills always too much food. The sushi isn't much to write home about. I ate a tuna hand roll and it was tuna and rice, no veggies. Pickled ginger was a little substandard. They did not have any brands of unfiltered sake. Service was great! Super friendly and as mentioned above the hibachi chief was entertaining.

This is a perfectly fine restaurant.  I live walking distance away and decided to go on a whim on a Sunday for lunch (they have lunch specials that go into the weekend as well).  It's a cozy little place with interesting decor.  The prices are also very attractive.  I had staple thai food (pad thai and a salad) and I was NOT disappointed.  I was on a first date and because I brought her here, I got pretty lucky.. heh heh.  Would you like to get lucky too?  Bring your date here.  Thank me later.  I will definitely be back.  Be warned though, spicy dishes are super spicy.  My date had curry with tofu in it, and I almost didn't get lucky because of the spiciness, but she quickly got over it.  And the Tofu was fried.  BE WARY BUT CARRY ON, THIS IS A GOOD RESTAURANT TO TRY.

Decor, wonderful with a subtle ambience. The wait staff is pleasant and helpful. The cuisine is fantastic, wonderful, delicious, and leaves you wanting more. They know how to do it right and by that I mean serve delicious Thai cuisine. We will continue to go back. My wife and I wish to thank everyone at Spice Thai Cuisine for allowing us to be a part of their gigantic dinner table where they serve the public each day. Kudos!

Nice thai spot that's local. It's very quaint and tiny but always packed. We didn't have reservations but they sat us quickly. I had the chicken basil dish. I asked for it to be mild because I didn't want a runny nose all night. They obliged me...However, I have to confess, it was just too bland. The portions were very reasonable and the brown rice was yummy. I had a coconut juice drink that was very tasty. The service was also excellent. Overall, I liked it here but probably wouldn't be inclined to rush back as the food was a little blah. Maybe I just need to try some other selections and be more specific about how I want the spice control to go down.

This is a small Thai place that most people would overlook. I have a co-worker, who never leads me to a bad restaurant, recommend it to me. It's a BYO, so head to the liquor store first. The staff is friendly and attentive. It is pretty small, so make reservations, or be prepared to wait some. The food was excellent. The only downside is that the table next to you will be very close, so you will hear each other's conversations.

I went there on a Tuesday Night and by the time we left there were no empty seats! The staff was attentive. I was in a party of two and we ordered the very delicious Thai Iced Tea (for me!) and Thai Iced Coffee. (They charge $1 extra for no ice in the drinks) We ate the Chicken Rama Curry - 'crispy chicken & broccoli with a peanut curry sauce and cocnut milk' and, Flat Noodle Thai Basil with chicken, chili, red pepper, onion, and basil. In both instances we were asked our preferences in terms of the spiceiness of the dish. I ordered low heat and my companion ordered medium heat --- because the server said medium was "very hot". While the food was delicious the spiceiness as we were advised did not deliver. I would definitely go back there!

I never let too much time pass between lunchtime visits to my homies at Melt Shop lol. Then again, I go there very often so they know me by name and face. The classic American grilled cheese sandwich with SHOP TOTS and a lemonade is the way to go. One thing to note, this place gets VERY busy - fortunately, I never wait long like the other suckers. I just order ahead on Seamless :)

Wow! Melt Shop tantalized my taste buds after a day of enjoying the city. My lady and I ordered the buffalo chicken and the classic turkey and we're very impressed. I would recommend melt shop to anyone in the area. Basically it takes your childhood grilled chesses and explodes it by 10x. Maurice at the window was helpful and suggested the sandwich to my liking...hats off to him and the staff. He even came out to ask how we enjoyed our dinner. A+
Seriously no joke. BEST GRILLED CHEESE SANDWHICH EVER!!!!!  I eat here literally all the time. Maurice and Dean are legit and will make it your sand which like you've never had it before.
Best grilled cheese I've had in a long time. the fried chicken was moist and tender. Tater tots were prefect

This is the place to go for hearty, grown-up versions of the grilled cheese sandwich.  My favorite is the Fried Chicken--it's exactly how it sounds with a healthy portion of red cabbage slaw and met sauce on sourdough bread.  The Maple Bacon is pretty good also, but unless you're eating for two I'd go for the Fried Chicken. The tots make a great side (with extra melt sauce), and the Oreo shake will put you over but is well worth it.  Melt closes at 9pm, but go before that; popular items like the Fried Chicken sell out quickly, or they might turn off the deep fryer early.
It was my first time at melt shop. Anthony and Maurice provided impeccable customer service and prepared my meal deliciously. I will deffinitely be returning!

Based on the food, atmosphere, and service, this place should be packed to the brim every second of every day. If it was next to Spicy Shallot, I swear it would put them out of business- Kitchen 79 is waaaaay better than the many other Thai places in the area (that I've tried). I have tried the spring rolls, summer rolls, dumplings, curry puffs, roti, pad Thai, and the tom yum soup. Everything is consistently fresh and delicious, but the spring rolls are a little small and the dumplings more closely resemble shui mai. I came in once and the service was sweet and swift but I mostly order delivery from here because my boyfriend lives three blocks away and the delivery is fast so my food is still super hot when it gets here. Apparently they deliver past 112th St. That's far as fuck but good for those of you who aren't in the area. I ordered soup to pick up once and I noticed it wasn't the soup I wanted when I got to my boyfriends, so I called them and they're sending over the right one. Problem solved. Love this place.

NICE! ..Since this area has at least 12 more Thai spots to compete with. I will say the food is very good..not great. but very good. Service is incredibly nice...but slow to exit the kitchen.  They have dishes not available in all other Thai spots..which is nice. Impressive!!..Not traditional Thai in decor (no foto of Thai King....no monk scripts by the register..no Buddha facing the door)..yes i know..i cant eat decor...but i felt like a vampire would jump out from the oddly demonic "art" piece facing the door (Fung Shui people be warned) Would i go back...sure..but only during daylight.(^_^)

Been here 4 times so far. Excellent service. Very friendly manager / owner (rudy I think is her name). Crab fried rice is awesome. Had it every time I went. Soft shell crab and whole fried fish are bomb. Don't worry, the food is better than I write. My brain lacks delicious adjectives.

I've been coming to this restaurant since it first opened. Firstly, the service is phenomenal, Rudy the owner I believe, is a sweetheart. My boyfriend and I go there frequently and Wee usually serves us, he is very nice and always treats us well. Now for the food, the food is amazing. I have been to many different thai restaurant and this is the best I have been to thus far. The food is FRESH. I usually go for the chicken pad Thai which and my boyfriend gets the phad ka pow. We usually visit this place at least once a week neither of us live or work anywhere around this neighborhood, that is how amazing it is! Definitely try it out.
Very good food,  and very authentic! A must try for typical indian (punjabi) food. And very friendly people.

Went back today to Risotteria Melotti, this time around for lunch. Again a sensational culinary experience and the lunch special - a choice of salad and a choice of risotto for $12.- is the best deal in town.  The salads are beautifully served, plentiful, and simply much more than a salad: a delicious combination of ingredients, a meal onto itself.   We are talking TOP QUALITY and AUTHENTICITY - making use of  seasonal ingredients. Perfectly executed risottos.  Top notch,  cannot recommend enough. Toasted rice cakes are addictive. Today I also found out it is the only 100 percent gluten free restaurant in NYC. And the staff is charming.   Go, and you will visit again and again.

Loved the service and authenticity of the food. Rice cakes and bread were amazing. Salads were simple, fresh and delectable. My friend's risotto tasted great with a hint of cinnamon. Mine was alright with the chicken; only complaint would be that the chicken was a tad dry and tough to chew. Quaint, affordable, sweet, delicious. I'll be coming back for dinner next time around!

Yup it is still a five star rating for me! They deserve it.  Celebrated my coworker bday this evening, I knew this place is perfect to do so.  I highly recommend it.  The food is fantastic.  We had the buratta: fresh Mozzarella and arugula with balsamic vinegrette, calamari, shrimp/crab/Lobster pasta in a red sauce (phenomenal), stuffed spinach ravioli in white wine sauce, osso bucco with spinach mash potatoes (would have liked the veal to be more flavorful), and for dessert: creme Bruleè and Tiramasu. Yum! :D

Went to dinner last night, busy restaurant , hostess did not even turn around to greet us, she was talking to us facing and talking to us by looking at the mirror. Appetizers were great: carpaccio and arancini. We ordered pasta: penne alla Norma e spaghetti alla chitarra. Penne had no seasoning, barely no eggplant nor ricotta, spaghetti were bland and seafood was not the best quality either. For an Italian restaurant, pasta should be their best dish but it is not. Prices are high, 2 apps and 2 pasta $90.
awesome quality mediterranian food------and an awesome time!!! high recommend
We were back this weekend and everything was excellent! We were very pleased with the food and the service was great! Labebe is going to be a new go-to spot for us!

Had an excellent night out with my family! The place is stunning, the staff was friendly and most importantly... THE FOOD! Is amazing. Drinks were flowing and unique. Coming from a middle eastern background I am very picky when it comes to middle eastern cuisine. I felt as if I was eating a home cooked meal only with a better presentation of course.
