Thank you Labebe  for the excellent experience! I will certainly be back and recommending this restaurant.

Ehhhhh. (Irish Accent) Wanted to go to an Irish bar today and get a good feel for the atmosphere and boy oh boy I did. Everyone was so rude I left. Not to mention it was hotter than hell in there. Pop a "Molly" a sweatin, right? The waitress kicked us out of our table because everyone there didn't order and appetizer. Sorry that no one wanted your mediocre $12 dollar "homemade" cheese sticks aka frozen Dyson products. So the waitress told us to move to the bar where there where no seats or room. She then proceeded to rudely tell us to stand next to the fireplace. It was 90 degrees in the bar sorry I didn't want to stand in the fire. I have been to Ireland in my life time and have never experienced a troll like the waitress we had at Molly's. That being said I did enjoy my one Guinness I was able to scarf down thanks to The Lord of the Rings troll. The saw dust on the floor would have been cool and unique except for the fact they STOLE IT FROM MCSORELYS.  I think my opinion will lead you to believe that I won't be going back to Molly's and that is true. The only reason this place got 2 stars was because I love Christmas and they had some killer lights. Not Rolf's but a good effort. So Molly... Merry Christmas you filthy animal and a happy new year.

We were in search of nice burgers- and we stomped upon this place via YELP.  Thank you- YELP. We've been here twice and both experiences were very nice and warm. First day of big snowstorm 2013 we popped in here noticing the saw dust on the floow and the whole, but small, pub lit up beautifully.  Our server was friendly- as we ordered a few beers (guiness and black/tan) both extremely fresh beers.   Once server- older woman - was a bit fiesty here and there- we were watching her and every so often she ran up to us almost trying to rush us even though she wasn't our server.  Possibly the manager trying to squeeze more people in and out. Anyways- we ordered bison and beef burgers- at first my bison was huge when it came out but then it wasn't cooked the way I like it so I sent it back.  When it came back it was a bit smaller- but still very good.  Fries and onion rings both fresh cut and yummy. Normal burger is a good size but bison a little small- price $13-14 Then we ordered mozz sticks- home-made and unbelievable.  Also a bit pricey but good. We came here again XMAS EVE and wow very lovely experience.  Beers are SUPER FRESH ON DRAUGHT! Young lady server who was also super nice.  Every place was dead except this place.  It really looked like XMAS- all lit up!

I went here on a Friday night recently with my girlfriend. It seemed like a good idea on the face of it -- the weather outside was cold and rainy and a bar with a fireplace would be a nice escape. It seems like this place is a victim of its own success though -- it was very crowded. It took a few minutes to a waitress to seat us, and the service thereafter was very slow -- 10-15 minutes to get the menu, 15 minutes to have our order taken, and another 10-15 to receive the order. She even screwed up my order of a salmon sandwich for a chicken sandwich. I didn't bother asking for my order, because it would've taken another 10-15 minutes and at that point, I just wanted to eat something and leave. I liked the vibe of the place though -- the wooden furniture, the sawdust (to minimize gross beer spills, BTW), the christmas lights -- it's just too crowded. Maybe this place is better to visit on a Tuesday night.

One of my favorite spots for lunch in New York. Always come here for the buffalo burger with fries and potato salad. It has a warm atmosphere, dark and cosy with booths, a fireplace and sawdust on the floor. As a bonus, the staff is actually Irish. Highly recommend!
Love this place! Love the fun, cute bartender and the potato chip nachos. Great half bottles of Sancerre, too.

I went to Swine for my second time this past weekend.  We went back because we first just had a few sides and loved them.  The food we had the second time around was equally good... however.... A MOUSE LITERALLY RAN UP MY LEG AT THE TABLE Yeah, I'm new to the city, but I can't imagine this is acceptable.  After the said mouse tried to run up my leg, I stomped it out and it lay dead on the floor.  At first the waiter and the owner didn't believe me, and then after much explanation, and making them look under the table at the dead mouse, they offered to comp. our meal.  As we were walking out the waiter asked if the service was okay... Yeah bro, the service was okay, aside from the mouse that attacked me, and you making me feel like I'm stupid for pointing it out. So, great food, cool spot, they have mice, or at least the had one, so enjoy that.  Best part, was the owner telling me all restaurants have mice at times, sweet, guess I'm cooking at home.

This kind of restaurant was seriously MEANT for people like me and the carnivorous love-of-my-life. I saw a quick blurb about this in a Yelp Weekly announcement, looked at the menu, and fell madly in love with what I saw. When we got there it had started to rain, so we put out umbrella's away in their little bins by the door and were promptly seated downstairs. The space is very...well, spacious. It's a split level as you come in, so there's a level up and a level down from the entrance way. The deocr is charming, with a feel of "dive" bar upstairs and rustic country mixed into urban deconstructed (I only say that because there is a partially finished wall down there, still looked cool though!). We were promptly greeted by our waiter Stephen, who was extremely chatty and great at describing some of the beers to us, recommending a newer and limited edition beer that they had on tap from the Bronx, which boyfriend HAD to try since he hails from there. Because our lovely waiter was extremely chatty to the point that he became lost in a conversation with another table, we also got Jackson to help us out with food and drink, recommending pairings and food, and even helping us plan how our food was to be brought out (in courses, which we hadn't thought of - of course being starving at this point we just wanted all the food, right then and there, baha!). For starters, we got the duck fat cashews (which had a grainier texture than I was expecting because it was sprinkled with cinnamon, but it was bursting with that flava flav), and then the potato chip nachoes, which had duck confit, cheese sauce, and house made potato chips and jalapeno's. Holy CRAP those were amazing - amazing to the point that I wish I hadn't been sharing them, haha! Following that we had the rabbit croquettes and the sock-eye salmon, and the croquette's were off the hook! I'd never had rabbit before, so it was a completely different flavor and the  aioli/mayo/something with it was major yum! The salmon was super fresh (like I just caught it with my hands out of the atlantic fresh), but with that it was raw as well. Since I'm huge on texture, raw is not something I do very well with. Boo and I split the Bone Marrow and Brisket Burger - again, another dish I wish I hadn't been sharing! It was tender, juicy, soooooo flavorful, and it was the highlight of the meal. With our two waiters contrasted beautifully with each other, Stephen being the buddy-buddy "let me tell you about the awesome people who have been here" type, and Jackson being the "this food is amazing because it's so fresh and wonderful" type. They seriously made the meal, almost more so than the food! And, of course, Bacon Ice Cream. Get it. If you love bacon, you will LOVE it!

Good xiao long bao. Everything else ranged from so so to terribad. Shengjianbao, the pan fried soup dumplings are too doughy with no soup. Bad. Do not order. Congyoubing, the scallion pancakes are okay but not great. At least it is a large serving size. The jiachangdoufu or homestyle tofu was a sorry excuse for the real deal. AND expensive. Three ladies, probably three orders of xlb is enough. Moral of story: only eat xlb here.
The only Chinese restaurant I order from! Love their pan fried noodles!

Was so excited to get to Chinatown on this visit to NYC and friends suggested Shanghai Asian Manor. It was EXCELLENT! The people couldn't have been nicer letting my husband and I sit & wait for our friends while sipping jasmine tea. Our friend did the ordering and we had Shanghai dumpling, crab dumplings, beef wonton, a tofu dish, another beef dish and the house special ribs. All was tastybut the Shanghai dumplings and ribs were my favorites. The sauce in the rib dish is thick, gingery, full of flavor and the rib meat tender and just falling off the bone. The place kept filling up and yet we were never rushed out of our seats. Great final night in NyC

I had the mock duck, which was pretty good. It was tofu skin stuffed with mushrooms. A little bland, but pretty tasty with soy sauce. It wasn't spectacular or anything, but was decent and reasonably priced. I will say, though, my non-vegan friends are in love with the fried tiny buns with pork, so definitely try those if you come here!

Please get on Seamless already! This gets 5 stars if you go there, and 2 stars if you order delivery.   The bad:  delivery takes forever and they have at least twice lost the order.  Sad panda face. The good:  the soup dumplings.  The crab and pork soup dumplings.  Happy panda face.  If it's winter, get a table away from the door.  I don't know why, but so many times it seems that the door stays open without closing.

Warning! Don't eat here for the love of God! The food is gross! If there was a 0 star option I would give it. Last time I was there with others I ordered the duck something and couldn't even eat it. The duck was hard and sauce was a glutenous red mess. I know good Asian food and this is laziness at its best. The place is super outdated but if the food was at least decent I would be able to forgive that. Not only is it in edible but its expensive. Not even alcohol helps and that is saying something. Only positive was that our server was a nice man but I couldn't understand a word he said and neither did the rest of the table. We just nodded lol. Oh and drinks were decent. Karaoke is a sham where the hosts sing most of the songs (old school mediocrity style) and make the rest wait. When you finally get to sing you can't hear anything because sound balance is nonexistent. How about getting a freaking monitor so singers don't sound like dying cats!!! In conclusion if you want to go somewhere where you can get trashed and make fun of people this is your spot. If you want a decent meal with friends, good drinks, and a fun karaoke experience this is not the place for you.

Great bar. We went here on our recent trip to NY and stopped in for lunch and a few beers. The bar tender was super friendly and  the service was prompt. We really enjoyed our burgers and the atmosphere. We'll definitely go back.

My husband and I were visiting New York from MA for a few days, and unfortunately decided to grab dinner at this restaurant. They market themselves as an Irish restaurant but they were far from it. They didn't even have the #1 Irish meal on the menu, shepherd's pie. Above our table was a speaker blasting the radio into our ears. Throughout the first 10 minutes of us sitting down, one of the staff members kept playing around with the stereo volume....up, down, up down, and so on. It was so annoying. When we got our food, the hamburger (ordered well done) was raw inside. I mean RED raw, it was disgusting. The cheese quesadillas were mediocre at best. The only good food were the onion rings. Then thank goodness I checked our bill because of our waitress had added another table's drinks to our tab. We ended up paying $70 for a meal that sucked. Would never recommend this place, ever.
One of my favorite tapas places in ny. Great sangria, cozy decor, delicious food. Perfect for dinner or drink and a snack.

One of the few sit down restaurants for dinner in St. George. Too bad it just as bad as the rest. We had the "special" pre fix menu and it started off nicely with a yummy chicken soup. The second course however, was a big disappointment: tilapia with a seriously salty olive and tomato sauce sitting next to a pile of yellow tasteless rice straight from a Goya box. They didn't even try to make it look appealing. And then for the desert course, there was a choice of ice cream or tres leches cake. We decided to go for the ice cream because you can't go wrong with ice cream right? Wrong. I'm not sure how they managed it, but my chocolate ice cream had freezer burn and the vanilla ice cream was the worst I have ever had. No joke. It didn't even taste like ice cream...more like frozen low fat milk with sugar and pectin. The waitress forgot to bring a glass of wine but I don't blame her. I would hate working there too and serving food made by cooks who couldn't care less.

I know that there's at least one other OBAO in the city, and I feel like they operate as different franchises or something because the one in Midtown East is... not to be visited again. This location though is really nice, and I really enjoyed the food and drinks--and the space itself is pretty. I can be a stickler about Vietnamese food, but I'd say OBAO lives up to the bar, even in its fusion style. And it's good prices! The vermicelli, laksa, and sugar cane skewers really stand out in my memory. What I really want to try next time is the clay pot catfish with rice.

1stly, the decor with the little bamboo lights (Looks like hovering faeries), so quaint & warm.....definitely a great spot for dinner. Romantic even! We had the Laksa & Vermicelli noodles with pork & shrimp. Yum! & a good amount of meat.....not the usual measly portions found in soups. The But it was the dessert that was the champ - that Jasmine pannacotta with blueberries & caramelised balsamic/soy reduction (or something like it) served with a refreshing mango sorbet. I know, sounds bizarre & like too much is going on, but OMG! The pannacotta was so delicate, smooth & creamy. & the sauce added just the right amount of tartness & that hint of bitter caramelization.....& the mango sorbet is like a palate cleanser but also enhances the Jasmine flavour of the dessert. It's like a "pretty-perfumy" dessert. Like nothing I've ever eaten before. OMG delicious!!!!

I love this place and its food!! I tried many thai places as it is my favorite food, but this one beats them all for price/quality! Delicious food, great ambient and cheap price for lunch (8$ for appetizers and big portion of entree). I am recommending it to everyone and will definitely go back!

This is not the first time I visit this place. all good experiences. This time I tried Sambal spiced calamari and Pho Bo. The Pho($11) came with stewed beef, beef brisket and round eye. it was so good!. The caramari. lightly battered caramari with a decent amount of sauce on it. soooo good! I also ordered coctail. Fig-a-tini. fig infused vodga

Service was on point, and the food was good, but there was nothing particularly eye-catching or brow-raising about the interior, service, or flavors. I didn't think there was anything special about the food... Maybe it's because I'm spoiled by being an LA native, but I felt like I'd tasted fresher, cleaner, tastier Thai food in LA.

OBAO has it down- excellent drinks, ambiance, and service...and most importantly- the food is kickass. Pros: * The decor is comfortable and eclectic- while they did use traditional elements such as bamboo and wooden lampshades, the ambiance still felt modern and trendy. * The food was awesome- recommend the Spare Ribs on Sugar Cane Skewer (perfectly marinated and tender), Salt & Pepper Shrimp (these flavorful popcorn shrimp are so addicting that I could have ordered 3 more), and Clay Pot Shrimp (huge portion, tons of flavor, and packed with shrimp and shitake mushrooms). The Pho Bo is probably the best bowl of pho you can get in Hell's Kitchen (Pho Grand still reigns). Cons: * Although delicious, the Spare Ribs on Sugar Cane Skewer should be called "Very Thin Pork Belly Wrapped around Cane Skewer" because of how little meat this dish actually had. Tips: * OBAO is popular and BUSY- best to make a reservation for any night, especially weekends. Luckily I made a reservation for Friday at 8PM- and we were seated right away.
very nice environment! the dishes were creative but delicious! most important, it was not expensive at all, what it offered worth for the money!

Obao is one of my favorite place in Hell's kitchen area. The atmosphere is very romantic. it is perfect for a date or just a casual meal with friends. my favorite item is Spareribs on sugarcane, Pho Bo , and Beef Luclak things to note- 1 The Portion of Pho Bo is very big. 2 spareribs on sugarcane is actually a thin slice of spareribs wrapped around sugarcane.3 you will need to make a reservation during the dinner time. It is always packed!
Delicious food, original recipes. try not to sit upstairs as service slow there. But wait staff friendly and accommodatting. Not too expensive.
Great food. The seafood pad pen was good and spicy!  Pad Thai was good. Loud and upbeat. Calamari appetizer was different but good too. Good choice for Hells Kitchen.

The restaurant has a delightful ambience. Cool servers with excellent service. Reasonable prices on the menu. Happy hour drinks and amazing house libations. I would recommend their OBAO drink. Gin and jalapeño with pineapple juice. They just took it to the next level. Its worth the try. Coming back again.

Came here with friends (party of 5) on Friday night. the place was packed highly recommended: Vietnamese Ice coffee, already sweet without the sweetener. Crispy pork belly appetizer, it has a crispy skin and juicy inside. Seafood Pad Ped, very delicious! Pad Thai and Basi fried rice were okay, not as unique as the appetizers. service was good. price was reasonable. if you don't make a reservation, be ready to wait, though.

At 5:30, OBAO was already kind of happening. It was a little busy for an earlier dinner in NY but understandably so. I went with a large party and got a bunch of appetizers: shrimp rolls, chicken satay, and calamari. All were good with no weak links. We then ordered our meals and they came out really quickly. Not even a 10 minute wait. We were impressed. My wife and I shared the lobster pad Thai($32 market price) and the chicken panaag curry ($14). Both were really good. The noodles of the pad Thai were particularly good and the curry was really creamy with a decent amount of chicken and vegetables. We were also fortunate to taste a friend's Claypot Catfish. Also a winner. For the size of the portions and for being a restaurant in NY this place was also rather affordable (yes, the lobster was pricey but it was LOBSTER) but everything else on the menu was around $13-16. Not bad. If you like Thai food, OBAO is worth a try.
Family owed business Nice place  food is is excellent. The pizza is always good.. The lunch buffet is a great deal and always fresh..

I had never had Indonesian food before, but was super impressed.  It is a mixture of Chinese and Thai flavors, but also unique in many ways.  It's really cheap (cash only, byob) and a bit of a hole in the wall, but totally worth the trip.  If you are adventurous, just ask them to recommend some dishes and you'll leave happy!
Really good place, i like the environment and the vibe, good service as well.

My husband and I were very excited to eat at Candelas because we had heard so much about it!  The whole restaurant is nothing short of top notch.  The food was delicious, served hot and fresh.  The waitstaff was fun and professional.  The owners were delightful, they stopped by making sure everything was perfect, and it was!!!!  We can't stop talking about how great it was.  We can't wait to go back!!!!

Unquestionably the best Thai place in New Haven, dare I say Connecticut. It would be tied for first even for the places I have been in NYC (Sripraphai). Very fresh. Super tasty yet not doused with peanut sauce or other flavors to over power the taste of the individual components of the meal. Feels light rather than a heavy meal. Favorite dish is Seafood Curry. Favorite appetizer is chicken puffs. Green curry chicken entree is really good too (and equally amazing as a left over - best left over I have had of any type of food). Decor simple. Service fine. Authentic Thai food (even an associate who owns a Thai restaurant said this was the closest thing to authentic Thai food in the area). Even NY Times rated it highly.

Sorry.  Have to join the ranks of the Shiki-bashers.  Have been ordering from Shikiwok for years and had never been disappointed.  The last two times we ordered it took over an hour for delivery (and I live in Bloomfield!)  The quality has gone way down.  I loved their DimSum, but they must have switched.  The noodles were thick, dry and gummy all at once.  The spare ribes were dry and chewy.  The only thing I still enjoyed was the jumbo fried shrimp, but it isn't worth it to remain a customer for one thing.  Looking for another Chinese restaurant.  :( BTW, their website is down today.   Not sure what kind of sign that is...

This place is weird because I don't think I'd ever go out of my way to come here but it's always really solid, the food is pretty fresh, they have a decent "traditional" menu and the service is good.  I feel like it could go 5 or 4, depending.  The menu is limited overall but I respect a place that doesn't take on more than it can handle so there's that. Stopped in yesterday because the new Shanghai Bun near Princeton Jct. train station hasn't opened yet and I was dying for Chinese food without going too far. They had the regular menu with Chinese American staples and then a second menu with some more Chinese type stuff on it.  We got an order of "chives box" which I think was called shrimp and chive pancake on their menu, but they're one of my favorite dim sum items ever, and then an order of the twice cooked pork and the Shanghai year cake.  I love year cake even though it sits in your stomach, but the ones here were nice and flavorful, stir-fried in a light sauce with ground pork, lots and lots of scallions and delicious mushroom.  Husband's twice cooked pork was good but kind of different than I'm used to seeing it at Sichuan places, it had slices of very dense tofu in it and those thin asian green peppers but less leeks than I'm used to seeing.  It was really tasty though, but kind of expensive for a small portion.  Delicious though, and all the ingredients were very high quality. The woman who took our order had the waiter bring us a small dish of cold cooked eggplant in a delicious soy sauce vinegar sauce that was slightly spicy with lots of fresh cilantro on top and that was crazy good.  I've never had anything like it before but it was a perfect summer type appetizer.

OMG... it made it's wait into Philly!!!!!!!!! And it landed a few blocks away from home!!! Was on our way to Shake Shack.. Car stopped at the red light, and I noticed the bright sign... BURGER FI... OMG... wat does that mean?? DETOURRRR!!!!! I was so excited like a lil kid going to a candy store!!! Hubby n I got the Brisket and the Cheeseburger, and an order of the Cry Fries (fries n onion rings)... It was a lil over 12min wait time... But it was well worth it when the food arrived... Burger was deeelicious!!! Patty was thick the cheese was gooey... LOVE.. We had the cajun spice to our side and it was o so good... Service was good.. I even saw (i think) the manager or owner going around asking tables how they thought of the food.. I'm sure this is because it's a grand new opening, and it won't last long, but it was nice to see... I'm so glad I don't have to make a trip to NY for this anymore...

I walk past this location from my home to the train station and back every day, so when I saw this place was being built I got really excited. Especially since we didnt have a nice burger joint in the area.  I went in today and here's my impression: As others reviews say, its pretty much a shake shack. They even have the "burgerfi sauce" a-la shake shack style. But man the burger I got was good! I inhaled it and had to order another one, and I swear I wasn't hungry. Didn't order fries, but had my good 'old Mexican coke, which I really appreciate. I sat by the bar to charge my phone and got a beer. There's something funny with the way their beers taste, probably the system is new? I dont know. But couldnt finish my overpriced yuenling. Regarding service... The girl in the counter was either having the worst day in her life, or after 7 days just found out she hates serving burgers... She might also have been dying yo go to the restrooms. Anyways, she had quite some attitude, only matched by the bartender, who received me with a face and voice tone that yelled "I'll hate you if you dont order a drink". Good think she dulcified her tone when I ordered a beer. Will I come back? Definitely, those burgers are tasty. Will I stay here to party and gave a good time? Nope. Will I gave a drink Herr? Only if there's another bartender. Cheers!

My new go to burger spot! Blows 5 guys out of the water and i have been a 5guys follower since they opened, a bit more expensive than the norm but it is not the norm! Cant wait to go back and have me some chilli cheese fries!

If I were rating the food only I would give 3 stars and say that its A-OK. The taste of the burgers is on par with five guys but much more expensive when you add the fact that many of their toppings cost money. I dont mind paying a buck for shrooms but you should give me more then 3 pathetic soggy little slivers. The deal breaker for me was .77 cents for vinegar for the fries. Seriously? That is a condiment not a topping and it should be free. Five guys does not charge for vinegar or mushrooms for that matter.

SO glad to see this place with such high reviews! They offer samples, but I recommend the blue corn... everything! The chips are a bit greasy but overwhelmingly awesome, the tortillas and so flavorful I dont always fill them, and that stack of warmth topped with their green salsa is like a beauitful mexican pancake stack. Be prepared cash in hand, and if you get there at the right time you might not need to wait. They sell their dough, too, just ask! Super duper cheap :) The best. Just say yes.
NOT a restaurant - merely an open room tortilla bakery that sells warm tortillas over the counter.

I went to San Roman thanks to the reviews on Yelp and it was awesome! I agree with others that this isn't a restaurant so much as it's a GREAT little shop. The tortillas are fantastic and the green salsa is my favorite. The red is SUPER hot, but good. Plus, for the quality, the price is totally reasonable. You would pay as much for a bag of toast it's as you would for their chips and these are better. Ya gotta go!!!! :)

This review is for their Dining Days "deal". Not for the food, mind you. Sadly, we did not opt to eat here. Their Dining Days menu has been on the internet for months. Lengthy lists of 3 delicious-sounding courses, including but not limited to crab mac n cheese, scallops, and pork tenderloin for just $30? It sounded too good to be true. Well apparently, it was. Upon being seated, we were puzzled to find that the menu gave us a mere two prix fixe options: chicken or salmon. Even the appetizer was just a choice between a salad and a gazpacho. Really? We were not willing to pay $30 (plus tax and tip!) for a chicken leg and some tomato soup, so we left. Before that happened though, a friend complained to the waiter and then asked to see the manager. We were fed a lot of bullshit (from both parties) about how the menus were posted in February and the prices of "locally sourced" produce and proteins had gone up since then, and they couldn't change the menu online (incidentally, a friend and I noticed several changes in Distrito's Dining Days menu no more than 2 weeks ago), but that it was on their own website (I just checked, it did ambiguously mention that "The Prix Fixe will be changing on a daily basis" but there was no mention of there only being two choices, or what those choices were. And "changing on a daily basis"? How is it that the one day we go, the "rotating" options just happen to be the two cheapest (and most boring) things on the menu? Suspicious.). They could've at least mentioned it when they called to confirm our reservation. But they said we were welcome to choose from the a la carte menu (which averaged $30 for entrees and $10 for appetizers, not even including dessert). Yeah, you'd like that, wouldn't you? Nope, sorry. Not what we signed up for. Look Marigold, if you don't want to suck it up for Dining Days and cut your losses, don't participate. Or, don't pretend to offer items you don't actually intend to serve at a pre-agreed upon price, and hope your patrons will just suck it up for you and not complain. It's as simple as that. It was a total bait-and-switch, something that has been happening a lot (at least to me) with the West Philly Dining Days. Sketchy. Very sketchy. I wish I could tell you the food was worth it, but I guess I wouldn't know.

DISHONEST BUSINESS PRACTICES!  FALSE ADVERTISING! Planned with a bunch of friends to dine here during the only available reservation time - 6pm on a Tuesday.  We were excited, because the posted menu included tantalizing options like crab mac n cheese, corn fritters, scallops, pork tenderloin, and 6 dessert options. Went here for Dining Days and they totally switched the menu.  Instead of having 4-5 options each for apps and entree according to the menu posted online, they minimized it to 2 options per (no dessert option/choice).  Funny because, the options listed on their new a la carte menu were some of the same dishes on the original online menu, but now no longer part the $30 prix fixe. When we realized this switcharoo, we asked to speak to the manager.  The hostess (who said she was also the manager) came to explain to us that we could still order the same items, just pay more for them!  No kidding Sherlock!  So you mean instead of paying $45 (including tax and tip) like we expected, we can get the same thing and pay $80+? SO WE LEFT AND I WOULD NEVER COME HERE AGAIN.

Please note: This review has absolutely nothing to do with the food served at Marigold. Marigold had a menu posted on the university city district's webpage for dining days offering 3 courses for $30. The menu listed 7 appetizers, 6 entrees & 3 desserts to choose from... AFTER making the reservations, with intentions of taking advantage of the dining days menu, my party (of 6) saw that Marigold changed their online dining days menu. The dining days menu now stated the following:  'Each day Chef Halpern will be selecting different appetizers, entrees and desserts as our Dining Days options'. To our dismay, calling Marigold the day we had the reservation (today), the dining days menu offered went from 7 appetizers to 2, 6 entrees to 2 & 3 desserts to 1. We opted to cancel our reservation, disappointed with the now-lacking-in-everything-delicious dining days menu. Even after Marigold falsely advertised the number of options offered for each course & even after they didn't tell us what they would be offering on today's dining days menu until 4:30PM, they still charged us $18 for cancelling our reservation. Absolutely absurd & downright creepy... the 'manager' claimed they were completely booked tonight (our reservation was for 8:30PM) even though their website lists them as closed Monday (today). Take from this what you will, but I doubt I will ever bring my business to Marigold.

Went for dining days and ordered off the a la carte menu. My scallops were large, and a bit salty. At ten dollars a scallop, 3 for $32, I thought they were overpriced. The presentation was beautiful, and the drizzle of foie gras was tasty, from what I could tell, but not worth the price. My $14 sweetbreads was microscopic but tasty. Believe me, I am not an "all you can eat buffet" type person, but these portions at these prices are insulting. What am I an idiot? Again, the presentations were lovely, so I guess I should consider them edible works of art, and we all know that art is priceless. We had a table of 12 which they seated directly against the air conditioner. The other side of the room would have accommodated that size table, so It did not seem well thought out to expect someone to be placed two inches in front of a blasting air conditioner. The bread was a major disappointment. It appeared to be prepackaged, dry,stale rolls. The butter came in an asian soup spoon to be shared with 4 people, and one knife we had to pass down with the spoon of butter. The other entrees did not appear more ample than mine. Less for more should be the motto. The gazpacho had one shrimp in it with the inedible tail still attached, which meant if you wanted to eat the whole shrimp, you had to stick your fingers in your soup to pull it out of the tail shell. Who's idea was this?  Again, the service was good, the presentation is attractive, but after that, forget about it. I think Marigold Kitchen is highly overrated.

Wow- I guess I'm not the only person who was disappointed with my UC Dining Days experience.  What a shame, as this a really cute restaurant on one of those beautiful, green West Philly streets.   For the record, I've been here before.  They're a little pricey- especially for West Philly- so I usually reserve my visits to Dining Days or when a parent visits.  I was always pleased that, despite the prix-fixe three course menu, you'd usually end up getting a couple little things in between meals- little sorbets as palate cleansers, a shot of soup, etc.  In addition, it used to be a chance to try really fancy things like foams and emulsions.  However, like others I was pretty disappointed to only see a choice of pretty standard soup or salad, chicken or salmon.  I, too thought it would be the lengthier menu featured on their website. Right off the bat, our visit seemed to be a bit off.  We walked into the vestibule to find no one in there.  There was no sign, but I remembered in the past there was a hostess that met you there, so we just kind of stood there awkwardly- not sure whether or not to go inside or keep waiting.  Eventually our hostess came to greet us. It was early in the middle of the week, so we did not make a reservation.  They stuck us upstairs, which was good enough- but I kind of got the impression that they put the younger people upstairs in the less attractive dining room. But hey, it gets busy during Dining Days.  Once we were seated, our waiter came by.  Again, he was good enough.  He was polite, but pretty stiff and curt. My main beef (hah) with Marigold was with the salmon.  I almost always choose salmon from a menu, so in addition to the salmon I cook at home, I end up eating a lot of it.  As soon as I stuck my fork into the salmon, I thought it looked a little undercooked. Extremely orange and translucent. I know tuna is served just seared on the outside, but I had never seen it with salmon before.  I thought maybe I'd just keep on eating, but I just didn't feel comfortable- the texture was just off for me undercooked like that- none of the flakiness I like from fish.  Because we were upstairs in a room with a curtain over it, my fiance was just about done with his entree before I could get my waiter's attention.  He said he would have another made, but also mentioned that the salmon was organic and that was probably why it "appeared" undercooked.  I didn't appreciate that- I felt like he basically told me I didn't know what I was talking about.  Maybe I don't know what I'm talking about, but I had never seen salmon served that undercooked and if I wasn't happy with it, I think it was unnecessary to quantify it. Lest I sound too picky, I should note that this is the first time I have ever sent food back in my life. Also, I really do think it was a fluke that they didn't want own up to, as I didn't see any other reviewers say anything about their fish appearing undercooked.  They did bring out a whole new fillet, perfectly cooked which was pretty tasty. Overall, this last visit just left something to be desired from start to finish.  It was almost a different restaurant from what I remembered in the past.

The Heath is a time machine. Taking you back to a bygone era of tuxedoed jazz ensembles and smoky chanteuses dripping in sequins. There is an impressive thoroughness of imagination at work here. An attention to detail that even includes vintage microphones and the subtle use of smoke to give the air a bit of atmosphere. The food is terrific. But what the Heath is really selling is complete sensorial teleportation. Actors in period attire mill about and have intrigues. But it never interferes with the totality of the illusion. As fantastical as it is delicious, The Heath is an experience like no other.

I went to Plan B last night for my birthday dinner on a glowing recommendation from a friend. It was busy for a Sunday night but my party of 9 was immediately accomodated. The waitress (do not remember her name) was very attentive and answered our endless questions with patience. The drinks were great (I had the John Daly - amazing!) and came out quickly. We were definitely impressed with the vast selection of beers and bourbons. I had the Blue Cheese burger and it was AMAZING. I normally do not like burgers, but this was without a doubt the best burger I have ever had in my life. My stomach is growling just thinking about it! Everyone's food came out quickly and everyone loved it! There was a lot of sampling each other's food, and there was not one thing we did not like! My friend ordered the shepard's pie, which came out in a huge pot - great portion sizes! Next time I will definitely upgrade to the parmesaen fries - they were delicious! Did not get to try the desserts as we were all stuffed. The prices were reasonable. The restaurant was a little loud and there was a speaker directly over our table. We were also seated right by the kitchen so there was a steady stream of waitstaff walking by our table with food. We are already planning our next trip there and I can't wait!

Meh. Great selection of burbon and beer. Though they sell burbon in "3 fingers" and it was only 2 of mine. Friendly, knowledgeable, and fun wait staff. The burger was bland. I just had a burger - nothing on it but lettuce tomato and ketchup. My wife's tasted better, but that was because of the blue cheese and carmelized onions not the beef. It's a big burger but I wouldn't go back. FYI people compare it to Prime 16. I'm underwhelmed by both.

Seriously, the place is gorgeous and sophisticated. The food is incredible and I've never even tried their burgers. There is so much to choose from: phenomenal  apps, homemade Mac and Cheese, great big salads, lots of all natural, local, and organic ingredients... And then there's BEER!! Only American, lots of local Craft beers, and each waiter/waitress I've encountered can explain them and make perfect recommendations. Really big bourbon selection too, the bottles go all the way up to the ceiling and the bartenders will climb up there to get them. Not really into Bourbon yet but this place is so cool that I just might start. As for the bad reviews, duh, the place is brand spanking new and is always packed, of course there will be some mistakes, give them some time. I think they serve food until last call too, so go when the dinner rush is over and see for yourself. Just make sure you save room for dessert.

First for all of the negative comments written comparing this to Prime 16, they're different restaurant one doesn't have to be better than the other they can both be great. I have been to Plan B now 3 times and each time it gets better and better.     There were a lot of growing pains when they first opened as far service, and waiting for a table. The service has improved considerably but it is still a bit of a wait for a table most times, I guess that speaks enough about how good the food is, and the word of mouth reviews that this restaurant has received. The beer is fantastic and always changing, each time I go the selection has changed but is always fantastic. I have only ever eaten burgers here but they are fantastic. The beef is natural, grass fed, chemical free,  and ground fresh daily. It has ruined burgers that i used to enjoy at other restaurants because I did not know what a burger truly could be until I ate here. I suggest everyone go once and try it for yourself

The burgers have been great each time I've come here, though I would probably stay away from the ground chicken. The draft beer is usually well picked (Captain Lawrence Kolsch & Big Eye IPA were flowing the last two times I went), and the bourbon selection is top notch. The wait on a busy Saturday night was an hour or more, but due to the ample room available in the bar area, we kept our palates wet and were comfortable doing so. Of special note: the "American nachos" were, at first sight, off-putting. Kettle-chips slathered with beans, meat, salsa, peppers, and cheese didn't seem like the Southern cuisine our slightly-tipsy tongues were craving. Rest assured: we were wrong. The nachos here were arguably the most surprising delight yet. Bottom line: Go. The burgers aren't legendary, but the atmosphere, waitstaff, other food, and bourbon selection are.

Went to Plan B for lunch, got a table in the bar instantly. Our server was very informative, really knew the menu and beer selection very well. We both had burgers and I had a beer! They offer half pints which I was very excited about! The burgers were delicious!!! Service was great, love the atmosphere and decor! Can't wait to go back!

Went on a spur of a moment rainy Thursday and it was packed so we had a drink and waited in the bar area for 20min until our was ready. Our server Damian was excellent and knew about everything on the menu. Had the wings/parmesan which were very crispy outside and tasty as hell inside. If you go here you better order a burger! i had the Baja burger with the chipolte spread on the side. It was very tasty and juicy. The avocado was fresh and the Jack cheese added a nice kick. If you like spicy this burger is for you! Overall the service and food was on point, give this place a visit. Always honest & objective reviews.

27 Mix is a happy find, my consistant choice when I am taking friends out to dinner in the neighborhood. It holds its own against very strong competition in the West Village. I enjoy it first for the food, but the front desk and wait staff are helpful, relaxed, and go out of their way to make an evening there pleasurable.

Always good vibes. This is a great place if you just looking for a bite and a great drink. I usually get the spring rolls. It is never too crowded, and even when it's a little full the crowd is always nice.I'm in love with the bartender. She is always nice and makes my drinks nice and strong the way I like them. This is the Martini 494 for the hipster with a job!

It's amazing that a burrito filled with pico de gallo, sour cream, guacamole, and cheese can be tasteless, but somehow they managed to do it.  Just strange and bland. The chips were among the worst I've tasted.  I liked the salsa bar and that was almost enough to bump this up to two stars, but no.
Every time I eat at this place I run to the bathroom. I will not return to this place now that chipotle is open!!!!

I LOVE this place! Pause Cafe of my new neighborhood hotspot! It's a Moroccan Cafe with a wonderful ambience! Every detail of this cafe was well thought out down to where the sugars are placed. A wonderful juice bar where you can get a "green detox juice" or a "purple detox juice" for $4 for a small, $5 for a medium and $6 for a large. Next to the juice bar is a small salad bar where you can get a combination of other fresh ingredients. Upon first entrance you are greeted by friendly Moroccan staff members that always say hi to their regulars. Breakfast is served all day, the sandwiches are fresh and their coffee is also wonderful! I would recommend trying a green detox juice with a grilled chicken avocado sandwich. Eat and enjoy freshness!
I do enjoy their pizza and salad. The wait times are usually pretty quick and the ambiance is nice! Menu is a little small.

Outstanding visit.  Our waitress Daniel  set the bar for great service and was friendly and attentive.  Pizza was great came in for a beer devoured an entire pizza.  Came in for the Conehead IPA which is one of the best IPAs I have had in a while and was going to go home with a growler of it until I tried the Burliner Weisse with raspberries.  For me a near perfect beer and based the the flavor profile was amazed it only came in at 2.9% ABV.  If you love craft beer you need to come.  Love pizza ever more reason.

Amazing pizzas, salads, and beers, and a great atmosphere. If it is nice weather, sit outside! All the ingredients taste super fresh and are from local farms. It is definitely a must visit for visitors and it seemed like a great place for locals as well. One tip...they get pretty busy during peak hours so try to plan ahead a bit.

We all know the pizza made with locally sourced ingredients is amazing and the beer selection hard to beat, and now they have a new outdoor patio expansion to boot! The Evolution pie was fantastic as usual and loved the meatball pizza special last night.
Great friendly service and even better pizza, a pity we only had a chance to eat one!
Go to zinburger. Bar stools short, and took 15 minutes to get a drink. They are new , but come on; my food was there 2 seconds after my drink.

Decided to give The Counter a try after seeing construction going on for a few months. The whole checklist/clipboard thing is way too gimmicky; excessive options for toppings and sauces, and I found myself using the eraser a lot...the whole process felt more like a scantron test than a menu.  Why can't I just tell the waitress what I want?  Why does it have to feel so clinical?  They do have "pre built" combinations if you don't want to feel like you're taking a midterm for lunch.  I made a scantron-related joke to the waitress and her response made it seem like they have already gotten a lot of comments about the whole process. The burger itself was good, cooked medium-rare like I ordered.  Fries were nice, not too soggy or greasy.  Waitress was great, very helpful.  Price was on par with the hipster gourmet-burger scene (elevation burger, zinburger, etc).  I was expecting a slightly more casual atmosphere like 5 guys or smashburger (between cafe and fast food) rather than a restaurant, but no complaints.   If you frequent chipotle in riverfront center, you know how bad that parking lot can get.  I see this place catching on, and making the whole strip mall a nightmare. Overall a 3/5, mostly because they are over-complicating a simple idea with a silly ordering method.  Also (not counting this in the score), I didn't see a "counter" anywhere besides the bar

I'm a burger lover so with that being said I enjoy trying new burger places.   The counter did not disappoint, but it as well did not wow me. Service was very slow (came here on a weekday night), however our waiter was very nice. I ordered the chili cheese fries to share with my fiancé. These fries were very flavorful and filling. My fiancé and I both decided to create our own burgers, which by the time you add extra toppings such as bacon, egg or avocado your burger comes out to $14.  I thought it was a bit expensive for the quality of burger you get.   Overall, good drinks (I ordered the margarita which was very strong and tasteful) and decent burgers.

Love me some burgers. That is a fact. So I was excited to see that The Counter opened up so close by. My husband and 5 month old son went on a Saturday for lunch. The place was really dead inside, which is surprising for a Saturday in such a busy shopping complex. But better for us as we were seated right away. With all of the menu options, I'm sure people will think less of me when I say that I just went with a basic cheeserburger. But seriously, that menu is overwhelming, in the best possible way. Plus, after having so many burgers in the area it only felt fair to go traditional in an effort to better compare it to its competition. The food: -Birthday cake milkshake was all sorts of awesome. I would love to go back sans baby and try some of their adult milkshakes. -The onion straws : crispy and delicious. So much salty, onion-y goodness -The burger - really liked the bun, and you could tell it was high quality beef. Enjoyed it for sure. The service: Top notch. Everyone was so accommodating and checked in on us continuously. Maybe this was because we were one of 4 tables in the restaurant, but still. It was nice. And we didn't have to wait long for our food, which was good as the baby was starting to get fussy (I think he was upset about lack of burger). The consensus: As we walked out, I told my husband that I liked it, but I don't think I would be back. It's overpriced - our lunch with tip was $50 - and I feel there are better burger joints around for half the cost. Sorry, wish I could give more than 3 stars...

Great Burgers, Great Beer. If your in the area and love a craft beer and a great burger then this place is a must do. It's not very often that I can order a medium rare burger and it comes out perfect, but it was spot on. Your able to create your own burgers with any toppings and sauces. If you are expecting a cheap $8 burger them go to Wendy's or Applebee's. The counter is well worth the extra $4 for a gourmet burger.

I got the LB burger which was cooked to perfection!! I would like to see more in the appetizer section but when you've got so many choices for your burger I can let that pass. The staff was very attentive and helpful, I'm definitely going back soon!!

My girlfriend and I came here for the first time on a Sunday night. Here were the highlights * Immediately upon arrival, the hostess was seating us at a requested booth when she was stopped (and subsequently so were we, you know, because we were following her) by a waitress who looked visibly upset by where she was bringing us, resulting in a mini argument on the floor. It's okay, want foood. * My girlfriend ordered a beer. About 20-25 minutes go by and still no beer. When I flag our waitress down and ask about the beer, she says "Shit. The other table was complaining too but I'll be honest, I had to go to the bathroom so bad and I forgot." Mmmm. Still hungry. * The burgers come out and they look great. Despite all the service gaffes, my girlfriend and I exclaim that we'd come here again.  About 3/4 through my burger, I bite into something very hard. And sharp. At first, I gave it the benefit of the doubt that it was bacon, but I'd never eaten bacon that could potentially pierce steel and I didn't check off "Wood Flake" or "Cow Bone" on the menu. I am no longer hungry. I flagged the waitress down and showed her the mystery item and she showed the manager. My girlfriend saw behind me that she showed the manager the mystery item and he walked into the kitchen. They both came back out maybe 10 minutes later and he asks "how is everything". (great!) I explain and he says something unintelligible and ends it with "what do you want us to do?" I got pretty peeved but the waitress assured me it was just a language barrier, and that he didn't mean to come off rude? Eventually, the manager comped the two meals, which I thought was the right gesture (except for the beer) * Half of my girlfriends burger was raw ground meat and the bartenders dropped metal objects of which the sound broke my ear drums and made me shit myself at least 2 times. All in all great place 5 stars

Just go and enjoy... the burgers and the service are great- better than Zinburger IMHO. There were a few glitches but they just opened...they will work that all out. Great staff and management. We all enjoyed our food and they now have happy hour drink  specials too. The menu can be a little confusing especially with the build your own burger part.

My friend and I went here for lunch last week, excited to try a new burger place.   We will definitley not be back! When we walked in the place looked really cool, however once we sat down it took about 15 minutes for a waitress to even come to our table.  Staff are all dressed in t-shirts and casual clothes, no uniform or even same color shirt so you have no idea who works there. The place wasn't that busy.  We each ordered a build your own burger, unfortunatley they were out of the pretzel rolls....odd for a burger place.  I see on other reviews that other diners also experienced the same issue of not having items in stock.   I wanted my burger well done, and was talked out of it by the waitress.  (again odd)     We ordered the fried pickles as an appetizer which were tasty, nothing out of this world.   Our burgers were ok, nothing special.  In fact we both commented that Smashburger was way better.   The price they are charging for these "gourmet" burgers is definitley not worth it.   Go to Smashburger or Five Guys for a great tasting burger at half the price.

Burger meat is great, menu is extensive, adult shakes are delicious, service is a little slow, prices are high. I would return. Burgers: My rare burger was pink but not as bloody as I'd like rare to be. The burger itself had a great flavor with a nice char, though my char/crust was a little too thick on the bottom. This is a good, thick burger, though. I got a Southwestern burger bowl and it was a good, low carb choice. The cheese was not as melted as I would have liked, but whatev. My partner built his own burger with fresh mozzarella on it. The mozz was good - soft, thick. The bun was just alright. We got no sides. Shakes: I got a strawberry shortcake shake with vodka, cake mix, strawberries, and icecream. It was good, and the whipped cream was great, but I couldn't taste the liquor. My partner's shake was out of this world. Bananas foster definitely had rum in it and a great burnt caramel flavor to go with the bananas. I could drink that forever. Our two burgers and two liquor shakes cost $50. You are paying for the cool factor. Service: We went at 8:15 on a Friday night. There was no wait. Our food was a little slow coming out, though. We left around 9:45. So, 2 people with two burgers and two shakes took an hour and a half. We also got our shakes after our food, so we were sitting around for awhile with nothing to eat or drink.

Initially I enjoyed this place when it first opened and then it has gone sour on me. Brunch is good and pretty solid but the dinner menu needs to be updated.   Don't get me wrong it's 'okay' food but I think it needs to be updated.  The last time I was there the fries were a greasy and soggy mess. The house lights were on so low I could barely see my food.  The pasta dish my friend ordered was so gummy and flavorless.  The waiter had to be chased down numerous times and the place was not packed.

I come here for the All You Can Eat Sushi (the special rolls are included!) It is sooooo yummy. I leave hardly able to move every time. Gluttonous I know =/ I have never really had problems with the service. Sometimes it is a little slow, but I tend to savor the extra time when I am stuffing my face with their delish fresh fish. The only things I've been disappointed with are the drinks. The Green Tea tasted more like hot dirty water to me and when I asked for iced tea they brought out cans of Nestle - yuck. I discovered private rooms in the back when I ventured to the bathroom last time. I want to sit back there next time!
Had Dinner with friends last night, Food was as good as it gets..service was good considering how busy they were! Chef Owner Joe Immordino made everybody feel at home. Tell your friends, enjoy!!!

Went in Friday night for the second time and was very happy to see how much was improved since my first visit.  I went the first time only because I drove by earlier and saw the name change and figured id come back to check it out.  Apparently that night was a "soft opening" but nothing was soft about it because it was mobbed and anyone come in. It seemed chaotic but that was expected.  Friday night was very buys but our service was great and the food was amazing.  I had ribs and they were huge and my girlfriend got a salmon dish and loved it.  glad to see its doing well.  Especially after reading some of the reviews posted before mine by morons.  One idiot said they charge for ice in drinks and he has no idea what he is talking about. . a "rocks" charge is because it goes in a rocks glass and has more liquor than a plain shot.  Also, anyone who complains about an experience at a soft opening should just not go out to eat at all.  Ill be going back

Went with friends for a weeknight dinner.  Restaurant less than half full.  Seated at a window table (no curtains or blinds) so that the traffic outside shone their headlights in my eyes throughout th emeal.  Dining room acoustics not good - - hogh celings and hard tile foors made for very noisy dining. Food was pretty good (3 extremely good, 3 good, 1 poor of 7 meals).  Mixed drinks were bad, and Service was terrible.  Waiter tried to force bottled water on us, and got huffy when we asked for tap water.  He then walked away in the middle of taking our order in order to pour (bottled)  water at a nearby table, then returned and resumed as if he had never been gone.  Told us that it was half price on a bottle of wine only after we had ordered several glasses of wine for cocktails, then brough us a merlot instead of the pinot noir ordered - - then tried to charge full price on the bill!  Yes we had sympathy, 3 of our party work in the restuarant business, but there was no excuse for this guy.  Then, after we left, he changed the tip on the credit card bill, adding $13 to his tip.  We liveless than 2 miles away, and will never go back!

This place is run by complete morons. My family made reservations for Saturday night. The restaurant didn't seem to be too busy which was weird for a Saturday night at 6:30. The server came up and told us the specials. 2 of the specials he didn't have. He had a special beer on tap. He didn't have that either. It took about a half hour to get our drinks. Our apps came out after an hour. Hour and a half later no food. Our waiter apologized and said he was sending over the manager. The manager walks right past us and comps another table. I was starving and we had our 4 year was tired and starving as well. We were ready to walk out and probably should have. The manager finally comes over and tells us that our food is on its way out. A half hour after that which was 2.5 hours after our apps came out our entrees come to the table. THEY WERE COLD. The only thing that was hot was my 4 year olds fish sticks which the server tells us to not let him touch because the plate was too hot. (You give a little kid a scolding hot plate?). Who knows how long our food was sitting there while we waited for the fishsticks. Any restaurant will bring the kids food out right away but no this place obviously does the opposite.  PLUS, We were told that my wife's side and my father's sides were out. They didn't even say anything until we pointed out that the sides weren't there. Way to screw up Bonefish This was the absolute worst experience I have ever had a restaurant. I will never take my family back to this place. It was a train wreck. Go to Blue Point Grill for seafood on nassau street in Princeton. Its 10 minutes away and blows this place away or go to Big Fish a mile up Route 1. Big Fish is ok but MUCH better then Bonefish. They at least know how to run a restaurant.

Sat at the bar on a Tuesday night.   Service was terrible -- asked for water, never came.  Bill had a drink on it I didn't order because someone apparently charged it to the wrong account.   Bartenders spent more time talking to each other than taking care of guests.   Guy next to me ordered shrimp tacos and got fish tacos.   Bartender just said,  "I didn't hear you correctly, sorry".   Didn't offer to replace it or discount it or anything.   I will NOT go here again.

This jam is the shizz-nizzle........`nuff said!!   Well, okay, maybe that's not enough.  See, no matter where you search throughout the slowly redeveloping dowtown area in Newark, the quality of food being offered will not compare with this "fresh as can be" locale owned and operated by the sweetest young lady this side of Raymond Boulevard (the freckles are what do me in, personally). For the cost incurred by an average visitor - say, about $10 - the quality and, usually, the portions are not only excellent, they satisfy more tastefully and more healthfully than anything else available nearby. Lastly, have you had the brownies?!  Holy sh*t......have the f*ckin' brownies, wouldja?  Seriously, man.  No joke. Now go!!

Harvest Table is a welcomed oasis in the middle of bustling Newark! It has a great location on Halsey Ave. near Raymond Blvd., which makes it convenient to the many office bldgs and schools in the area. The cafe itself is warm and inviting with eclectic decor, good lighting, ample seating, and free wi-fi. The staff is friendly, courteous, and competent. Now on to the best part, which is the food! Just like the name Harvest Table implies, it's all about fresh ingredients...from the produce, to the meats, to the cheeses, to the baked goods. The made to order salads and pannini cater to any taste, and they are put together right in front of you assuring the freshness of each combination. The baked goods are also to die for...HT has made quite a name for itself in the area with good ol', reliable favorites like brownies and chocolate chip cookies. Prices are very reasonable for the quality of food you get. In short, you've just got to have lunch at Harvest Table to see for yourself. You won't be disappointed.
I love Harvest Table-  I'm glad it's in Newark!

Pros: Large portions, fresh ingredients, flavorful, decent prices, good service Cons: The sweet crepe could be improved... I walked into this cute, casual, cafe-esque spot and got a So Florentine crepe, which was really good! Topped with fresh cherry tomatoes, filled with warm Swiss cheese and spinach, and wrapped in a thin, fluffy buckwheat-and-wheat crepe skin, the So Florentine was a healthy yet satisfying indulgence. I also ordered a sweet crepe for dessert --- the So Suzette. The crepe skin was tasty and aromatic, but the grainy veil of normal crystallized sugar on top was off-putting. Powdered or superfine sugar might have been a better touch for such a delicate, sweet crepe... 5 etoiles for the savory, 3 for the sweet. Hence, an average of 4 stars!

Such a great crepe! Best I've had so far (definitely beats the crepes at reading terminal market). Strawberry nutella crepe with fresh whipped creme...oh myyyyy!!! Crepe was delicious, fresh, and a nice portion (shared dessert). Friendly service and it's BYO. I have to go back and get as savory crepe sometime.
Fresh and delicious food. Relaxing atmosphere. Friendly staff and owners.

I'm a vegan, so I booked this venue for a party of 10 for my birthday.   The staff is friendly.  Food is delicious. I wouldn't be doing anybody any justice if I didn't recommend the eggplant in garlic sauce, watermelon juice and the scallion pancakes.  Those 3 items are to die for! Hope everyone enjoys this restaurant as much as I did!! :)

The ladies of 13th Street have done it once again.  It is no surprise that their newest venture is FABULOUS. We went last night for the first night open to the public and had a wonderful meal.   The menu is incredible.  Each dish tells a story and the wait staff is happy to answer any questions. I was very impressed with all the explanations of the menu and the wine / sherry list.  Our waitress was very well versed in all. We shared 4 smaller dishes and 2 larger ones and walked away very satisfied.  The pig tail bbq, warm dates, crispy rice and pate's were more than yummy.  We ended with the Seafood soup.  We were blown away with the mix of seafood and how each was cooked to perfection. The mixed flavors were heaven. Our only regret is that we had no room for dessert, but there is next time. Great location / Great food / Great prices !!!!

Jamonera is a fine addition to the Center City restaurant scene if you don't set your expectations too high. You will not find authentic Spanish cuisine or ambiance, but rather a modern American interpretation of traditional dishes. Having vacationed in Spain over the summer, I went to Jamonera seeking (mostly) some authentic jamon iberico and tapas. The tostas were delicious (pig's tail and friend oyster recommended) but were really only practical as appetizers, as the menu only offers 4 varieties. The larger raciones were also very well done (recommend the octopus and flank steak), but included peculiar garnishes like broccoli rabe and eggplant which detracted from the authentic flavors. The chocolate mousse desert was just mediocre. I was also a bit disappointed by the wine menu, which offered only a few riojas and even fewer by the glass (some bottles north of $100). Admittedly I did not try the cocktail or sherry menus, but in my opinion a larger, more accessible cross-section of Spain's fantastic wines would go a long way. The ambiance was modern with neon red lighting behind the bar and not a hint of Iberian flare. The musical selections were largely top 40 and a bit out of place. I must say, the physical space is very small and almost too cozy. At first my date and I were seated about 6 inches from the host's standing computer station, and when we asked to move a few tables over, ended up 12 inches from an awkward first date. This is primarily a date place and I would not recommend bringing a party larger than 4. The service was satisfactory, though it was a bit distracting to be constantly either ordering or receiving the next small platter (which is necessary to be satisfied) and to keep the paper menu under your dish for this purpose. I generally would recommend trying Jamonera if you are curious and seeking some echoes of Spanish cuisine, but I have left several other downtown restaurants far more satisfied for the price.

I was teetering between a three or four star, but I decided to give it a four star because of our waitress. I don't remember her name, but she was blond. She worked on a Saturday night. She was super passionate about the food and I loved the service and so I give a four star. My friend and I ordered the: Pigs Tail Toast - You can't tell it's pig's tail. It's a burst of flavors! I loved it. It was fantastic. It was my favorite dish of the night Jamon Iberico - $22 dish - it's only spanish ham - if you love ham, get it. i lived in spain for a summer and I loved their ham. brought me back to madrid. It would have been nice if they paired it with some olives. Olives were free in spain. Setas La Plancha - mushrooms with foie gras over toast. The mushrooms on their own were a bit salty. BUT when you pair a piece of the maple or honey flavored toast with some foie gras and mushrooms - it's an explosion in your mouth. I had to close my eyes. I loveeeeeed the foie gras. Pulpa y Ensilada Rusa - I got the octopus b/c i love the octopus dish at barbuzzo and i know the restaurants are connected. The octopus were cooked very tender which I love, however, the whole dish was so salty. The octopus was a bit salty which is fine but the garnish around it was even more salty. I know Spanish food is salty, but that was a bit much. We also got a special dish not on the regular menu - it was cheese and pair. The cheese was cooked too lumpy, and the pear flavor was drowned out. DESSERT: Spanish donuts - four donuts - plain but good. came hot and fresh. true to european styled donuts. i wish it paired with vanilla ice cream. wasn't a fan of the sauce that came with it, but my friend enjoyed it. we got a honey cake with vanilla ice cream and fig. it was okay. but again, my friend really enjoyed the dessert. i think i'm too simple to enjoy the flavorings of this dessert. she has a better palette.

I took a reporter to this cool lunch place in Union Square.   It's a small place.  It could probably be loud if it was full.   The menu tends towards Farm to Table.  It's a little bit 'twee', but it executes on its intentional pretensions.  Cheese plate very good.  Salads very good and substantial.  i had the burger without a bun and it hit the spot. If you are looking for a good place to take a client who appreciates wholesome but indulgent food, this is a good option north of Union Square.

Three of us came for dinner last night. I'm afraid our experience wasn't great. The appetizers were OK, although the beets had been prepared earlier and tuna seemed over dressed. My tagliatelle was oily and overladen with garlic, while the chicken was tasty, the mash seemed fussy. While the food approached competent, the service was the clanger, it was like amateur hour. The wait staff couldn't remember two specials without referring to her note pad, couldn't remember who ordered what, and kind of threw the food in front of us. The staff seemed careless and offhand, pity, as they have taken some pains on the decor and the menu. C minus County.

What a great restaurant. it very inexpensive and the food was terrific. I just moved here from d.c. and was worried that we wouldn't find a good sushi joint. The fish tasted fresh and the rice was great. The service was perfect and the girls where really nice. I love this BYOB and no corking fee... The decorations make the atmosphere perfect. In short, this is a great place with great food and great people. go here! p.s. in case you're wondering, my girl and I shared sushi and rolls. then we got a fried banana with green tea. it was a good cap to dinner :)

Oh man Oh man Oh man. Now it usually takes me a good 2+ weeks to even get a semblance of a review together for a place I've gone to. But this place is special. Now I came here today to celebrate my 90 days and to study. I was successful in one of the two. Since I had completed my 90 day probation and was officially hired at my first (over the table) job since graduation (CLAP FOR EM), I had decided that I was going to celebrate. And since I need to do some homework for my grad school classes (Oh she fancy), and can never do it while at work on my breaks, I figured going to a sit in lunch would be the perfect solution for the two. Well I was definitely able to celebrate but found myself unable to get past a paragraph of work since I was basically dying from the deliciousness of the food. Oh my sushi heaven. This place sure knows how to do it and do it well. No. Better than that. This place is 5 star superb. Okay, lets first start with what I got today. I went for the Tempura lunch box special for an extremely reasonable $9.95. It comes with a delicious miso soup, large and filling green salad (my only complaint is that there was a bit too much dressing, but I easily worked around that), and a bento full of duh.li.ciousness. The bento came with a california roll (which I ordered without avocado- gasp the horror!), gyoza which had this banging sauce, rice, and the tempura (2 shrimp and veggies). It was rolling-in-my-grave-if-i-was-dead delicious. The service was also fantastic and everyone is very friendly. I suggest getting extra gyoza sauce, because it was a perfect dip for the tempura and the rice. I couldn't finish it all and had to wrap it up, but I'm extremely happy to have an afternoon snack that is so good. I've also had the shrimp tempura maki ($6.75) here before and it is definitely the best tempura roll I've had in Philly. I can't really say much else other than this is going to be my go to lunch treat on payweek and that I will be bringing my friends here since its byob. So far so duh.li.cious!

When I lived in West Philly, I became addicted to cheap delivery sushi. Like, seriously addicted. The cute hipstery delivery guys knew me and always brought me extra spicy sauce. It was heaven. Then I moved. I was away from Philly for a while and when I came back I craved a change of pace and moved to the Loft District/Callowhill, where everything is under construction and nothing makes sense. I feared I may never enjoy the joy of spontaneous sushi delivered to my doorstep again. Then I found Kansai. It's slightly more expensive than what I used to get in West Philly, but it's also much better. And, oh man, the specialty rolls. I demand everyone that eats here and likes spicy things try the following chef specials: Kansai Roll: If a rainbow roll and a spicy tuna roll had a crunchy baby, this would be it. Spicy Girl Roll: Spicy salmon meets dragon roll meets tempura sprinkled with--wait for it--peanut powder. Sounds weird, tastes awesome. Halloween Roll: It has FRIED PUMPKIN, just shut up and eat it. Hopefully one day I will actually eat in the restaurant itself because it looks lovely and I've heard wonderful things. Until then I can only comment on the food. They deliver far and wide and an order over $15 means free delivery. Treat yo'self. Just, keep it to less than once a week. I think I have a problem.

I've ordered delivery from them a few times now and they've been solidy in the 4+ star range.  The prices are decent and everything I've gotten has been fresh and has been delivered really quickly.  I'll be trying them again -- maybe I'll even get there.

Outstanding. Food is fast, fresh, and very reasonably priced.  Picnic tables are fine on a nice night, too bad there's heavy traffic but it's part of the experience.  Someone should bring the guys from the new(ish) Lenny and Joes at Long Wharf here to show them what a great lobster roll is like.  Order the onion rings.  And the birch beer.

Sometimes what you really need on a Saturday night is to sit at home, watch tv, and order an astounding amount of sushi. This is what I did recently. I can only speak about the vegetarian items, as I do not eat fish. I liked everything I ordered (mango, oshinko, avocado, cucumber) except the avocado and peanut. There seemed to be too many peanuts in the roll and/or the peanuts were not chopped finely enough... something just wasn't right. A great addition to the neighborhood!

So nice to have a different option other than fast food near where I work.  The Chicken and Shrimp Teriyaki is good, but the sushi is great! My favorites are the Spicy Tuna, Spicy Salmon, and the Snow Ball rolls.  There's a good variety of food to pick from and the pricing is pretty good. Usually lunch/dinner runs me about about $4-5 for 8 pieces, not bad.  The place is clean inside, you can see the cook making your food, friendly staff, they do deliver, and the food tastes very fresh.

Randomly found Lolita while walking around with a friend looking for dinner.  Even though it was restaurant week we were able to find a seat right away.  Our server Alex was at our table right away to take our drink and appetizer orders.  We decided to go with the mango guacamole. We were both pleased because it was great!  For the main course we went for the hanger tip tacos and Spinnin On The Trompo.   Both dishes were great and filled with favor!   Overall the atmosphere was nice and relaxed... the food was fresh and filled with flavor and Alex was great.  She made sure we had everything we needed all night.  I am definitely going to be coming back to try more off the menu!

Beyond phenomenal from the drinks to dessert.  My love of mexican is always saddened by the lack of good dessert options but Lolita truly turned this notion around. I believe the dessert was my favorite part of the meal!  I also had a Cucumber Jalapeño margarita that was super tasty although it could have used a bit more booze. Definitely recommend heading here for some really delicious mexican and be sure to save room for dessert!
Forever tacos All the food I've had from here is amazing! I've only had food Togo, so I can't comment on the wait staff, but the food holds up well even for left overs the next day. So, they rule!

I went to Lolita for a resutaurant week lunch, and on the whole, I would say I was satisfied. I really like the area (it's right next to Barbuzzo now), and we sat outside and enjoyed the beautiful day. For my appetizer, I ordered the chicken taquitos. I enjoyed them - they were a good size, and on the whole, pretty tasty, especially with the sauce they had. I ordered the Carne de Trompo tacos. These were pretty good, but not outstanding - not much different from other pork/carnitas street tacos I've had (for much cheaper, might I add). I ordered the Mexican Tiramisu for dessert. There is really nothing Mexican about it, it's the same tiramisu that Barbuzzo serves, so that's a little awkward. It was pretty good, though some of it was too cakey, with not enough cream. Overall, it was pretty good, but I really do think you can find better Mexican food around for a better price. I don't think they quite meet up to the extravagant prices for what you could get at a good Mexican food truck.

I returned to Lolita for dinner last weekend and was not disappointed.  I was able to make a last minute 5:00 PM reservation on my phone with the open table app about an hour before the place opened.  When we arrived there were already quite a few people outside waiting to get in.  Once five rolled around everyone was quickly seated. Since I was disappointed in the margarita last time, we just ordered food this time.  My husband and I ordered a few appetizers to share and an order of tacos each. Fried squash blossoms stuffed with ricotta were on special, so I had to get those.  They were cripsy outside and delicate inside.  I loved the vegetables that were placed around them such as the sweet grilled corn, sliced cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced fresh jalapenos.  These along with the green salsa really added to the flavor of the squash blossoms.  My husband and I also shared the fried plantains with cheese and cream. I love plantains, and these were piping hot and delicious. For tacos I had the fish ones.  They are made with breaded mahi mahi, and you get three per order.  They were good, but not the best I've ever had.  The combination of textures was nice with the cabbage and other veggies they were served with, and they have just a little heat to them.  If you want seafood though, I recommend the shrimp tacos instead.  I had those previously at happy hour, and they were amazing!  My husband had the pork tacos.  I don't eat pork, so I didn't taste them, but he seemed satisfied with them. We had a train to catch, so even though I was tempted by the prickly pear sorbet, we had to call it a night after the tacos.  Lolita has some pretty tasty food, and the service is good as well.   A few things to note:   1.  The bathroom doors need a good push to open.  I thought someone was inside and waited for ten minutes before I figured out there was actually no one inside.  It was a bit embarrassing because a line had formed behind me.  Opps... 2.  They do have outdoor seating, but it's practically in the street with a narrow isle in the middle of the sidewalk for people to barely get through.  Not sure about you, but this isn't really the dining experience I want to have. Inside seating is great though.  We sat in a little alcove by the window.
