Great simple Italian restaurant. Awesome prices ($4 glass of house red) and tasty food. No reservations are taken for small groups so you have to wait in a small nook before being seated, which sometimes may last 15+ minutes. The mozzarella was great as was the pasta. Must come for a weeknight dinner.

Stopped in here for dinner Sunday night.   Shared the buffalo motz and prosciutto appetizer which was delicious.   The bf had the pasta and meatballs and I had pancetta and sausage with a cream sauce.   Both very good.  Would return.
Amazing. Went here while visiting NY. The closest to can get to Italy. For a moment I forgot I was in NY. Food also excellent.

My gf and I went here on a Wednesday night, and it was fantastic. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was due to the service being a bit slow (we also had a concert to catch). Food was more Northern Italy/Tuscany based, with some seafood dishes mixed in. Food/Vino: We ordered the "Good" wine 1/2 carafe ($17) of Montepulciano. I'm a big fan of Montepulciano's and this was a great one. Took a while for it to come, but it thats ok. Also, places that serve wine in the smaller glasses make me feel like I'm back in Tuscany, so thats an A+ for them. We started with one of the antipasti specials, Burrata with roasted peppers ($15). It was amazing, I would get this every time and hope they make it a staple. I ordered the Beef Short rib and gnocchi ($20), however they were out of the beef, and the waiter kindly offered me a lamb shank instead....uh yes I will gladly take that!! (it was the same price). The gnocchi was surprisingly not heavy, and the tomato sauce was very hearty and complemented the dish extremely well. The gf ordered an item off the special menu, a Fruta di Mare dish with a type of pasta that I can't remember the name of , but it was like spaghetti, cut up into small pieces. The octopus was the best cooked octopus I've ever had, it melted in your mouth. She's not a big fan of clams, but said they were amazing. And then the broth was all mopped up with the bread that came with it. For dessert we ordered the Nutella Tiramisu ($7). It was unreal, not too Nutella-y and the lady fingers were deliciously soaked in coffee. We were a bit surprised by how small it was (a small mason jar), but it was so good we overlooked that. Easily could have had one each. She finished up with an espresso ($2.50), which I'm sure was good. Overall, I would definitely come back. Only reason it was 4/5 stars was because our waiter was a bit slow and we had to ask them to come over, bring our wine, etc. I'd give it a 4.5/5 if I could.
Amazing spaghetti and and pappardelle with oxtail ragu. Good, laid back environment, no hard-selling from the curb (ugh....Little Italy) and really good service. Will be back often.

I first went into Era for the Arts Crawl or whatever it is they call it up there where all the hipsters, yuppies, and Afrocentric types get together and look at pretty pictures in Fairmount.   It's definitely an interesting space.  A real down home kind of place in the middle of a neighborhood that is quickly becoming too self important.  They've got cheap drinks and the food is very tasty.

Loses a star for time it takes to get food. They don't have a very good system and it crumbles under the pressure of large volume. To that I say thank you Rachel for looking for our order and the "knuckle sandwich" you whipped up for the kitchen! Beyond that, this is my kind of place. Authentic dive, cheap cheap cheap ass drink specials, and spicy food individually prepared with obvious love. It was a perfect environment for Aaron and Lori's announcement! Congrat's!

Been looking forward to this spot opening up in LIC for over a year. We need restaurant diversity! Service took forever.  The bar selection was a joke, but bartender said more types of tequila and wine and vodka were coming.  Come on Jose Cuervo?? Ceviche Mixto had so many fillers on the side it wasn't really Ceviche. (try Casa Enrique's Ceviche, it's perfect) Pulpo al Olivo which is supposed to be thin slices of Octopus has a thick mayonaise type of sauce that completely smothered it and oozed all over the plate.  It's octopus for goodness sakes! Aguadito de Pollo (Cilantro rice chicken soup) was very salty and the chicken was beyond fatty.  The broth was this yucky brown color.  Not what I expected. Chupe de Camarones (Shrimp Chowder. Lima Beans ,corn and Huacatay.  Fried Egg) It was just disgusting...  3 of 4 of us were completely perplexed. The Jalea (Crispy fish, squid, mussels and shrimp)  was actually tasty. Over all maybe I'll visit in a few months.  Only the first week it's been open but hasn't the owner's dad been in the same business for over 20 years? Total Waste of time and money...  Good luck on your visit!

I went to Jora last Wednesday and had a good time.  I had been walking past it pretty often on my way home, during the long, long time it took for them to open, so when I finally noticed they had open I couldn't wait to visit.  My expectation was moderate, as I know that sometimes food that is foreign to you may be a little shocking. My friend and I ordered the ceviche as a starter, and for our main courses I ordered the lamb shank and my friend ordered the skirt steak. Everything was delicious.  Truly, truly good.  The meat was so well seasoned and done perfectly.  The sides were very good too.  The people who served us were very, very polite and nice, and they didn't give me or my friend any looks or attitude because we didn't order drinks (we are not drinkers, and often we get a lot attitude from servers who think we are cheap or something, haha). The space was comfortable, spacious, and clean.  I am not a decoration snob, I barely pay attention to that, so won't comment too much on it.  I thought the ambiance was nice and relaxed. The menu is small, but interesting, and judging by how the meals we ordered were prepared, I would say they know how to cook there.  I liked the place.  I will bring my husband there soon, and I will probably push for my closest group of friends to have dinner there sometime.

Still a few things to work out, but a great start for a wonderful addition to LIC. Having gone to Peru last year, I was eagerly anticipating this restaurant's opening. The promise of pisco sours within walking distance of home was finally realized this week! The decor was simple, but casually elegant, featuring Peruvian pottery and other native art. The inviting interior also had a nice bar at the back, with it's own atmosphere different from the dining room. I think the pisco available in the US is not as strong as down in South America; that said, my pisco sour was very tasty, and as close to the real thing as I expect to find. My meal consisted of a shrimp chowder that was so big & full of shrimp, it could have been a main course. My actual main course was a huge braised lamb shank, accompanied by rice & beans and a small salad garnish. Very flavorful and filling. My partner had the skirt steak, which was cooked beautifully and topped with onion, peppers and roasted tomato. We finished the evening sharing a dessert of fried dough rings with a fig sauce to drizzle over them. While still not perfect (eager, but inexperienced wait staff; computers were down that night, too), JORA is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, and worthy of giving a try.

I had a really good meal at Jora. Very nice watstaff. I ordered appetizer the relleno, the stuffed pepper which was an excellent dish. Really gotta get that out there - it was delicious. Now a pepper stuffed with beef and cheese with potatoes on the bottom, not the lightest appy. But seriously it tasted great and felt worth it. It should taste out of this world if it's a heavier dish - they succeeded. The lomo saltado steak sauteed with tomatoes and onions, was a good dish. I enjoyed it. The steak was tender and flavorful, the rice was good. Also, their green sauce start with plantain chipis was very good too. I recommend this joint and I plan to return myself.

FINALLY!!!!! GOOD latin food in this area!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Visited this spot with the hubby on Friday night and I was very impressed with the service and food. This establishment just opened, so I know it will just keep getting better in time. I appreciate wait staff that are attentive and food plates that are big enough to get you full! Thank you Jora, we will be back!!

I've visited this establishment a few times since it's opened. The food has been great, drinks are excellent however, I was turned off by the manager Jessica and her untactful regards towards guests along with the staff members. She is rude and unprofessional. It is sad to say but I don't see this restaurant standing long-term in our up and coming neighborhood of Long Island City with someone like her running  this business. She will drive it to the ground.

First time Peruvian food eater over here- went to Jora not knowing what to expect. Left with a new favorite restaurant in LIC. This place is brand new and looks great on the inside- very clean, cozy, intimate.  Nice Peruvian decorations. They serve plantain chips with black mint sauce instead of bread. That green mint sauce is KILLER. I wish they bottled it and sold it. I would put it on literally everything I eat. Creamy, herby and a little spicy. It's perfection. We ordered the skewered veal hearts to start. Sounds pretty cruel but tastes pretty delicious. The meat tastes more like steak than internal organ. It's served medium rare and has a charcoal grill flavor. Very good. I decided on the Arroz con Pollo for dinner. Omg that rice. It's served green because it's infused with cilantro. So flavorful. It comes with pickled onion/tomatoes soaked in fresh lime juice on the side. All the flavors work so perfectly mixed together. The chicken itself is juicy and tender and has a crispy, seasoned skin. The dish is also served with an orange-tinted cream sauce on the side. I don't know what's in it but it's also really good. The Arroz con Pollo dish is great for Peruvian food first-timers or anyone who is picky or unsure of what to get. It's definitely a crowd pleaser. The service at Jora was pretty slow- the waiter kept coming over to apologize for the kitchen being backed up. I didn't mind one bit since the atmosphere was so pleasant and I was enjoying the company of friends. The staff is so friendly and kind (and refilled my water OFTEN)- I couldn't be mad at them! I can't wait to go back to Jora!

I've been to Maize a number of times.  I live in the area for law school, and due to the price, this is the usual place I bring the parents so they can pay for dinner.  The food is very good, a tasty Caesar salad, but $12 is a pretty ridiculous price for said salad (but again, I'm not paying).  Other entrees are more reasonable in the mid to high $20s / low $30s.  I've tried the paella and Alaskan king crab legs, both are very good, as is the coriander-encrusted salmon.  Most of the clientele are hotel guests, business people and some professors from the area universities.   I have to disagree with Susy H. about the prices being fairly cheap - Maize's prices are significantly more expensive than most Newark restaurants (see $12 Caesar salad).   Nice service, clean facilities and "posh" for Newark.  I keep coming back here with the 'rents and no complaints yet.
First time trying Indian food was great here

I arrived at my 5 star rating very scientifically. 1 star for the Boudain Balls (crawfish) 1 star for the Muffaletta 1 star for the oysters 1 star for the mac & cheese 1 star for the decor We went on Sunday night of their first official opening weekend.  It's true that the wait for the food is longer than usual.  So -1 star for that.  But then the owners and the chef and even the designer all checked on us to see how we were doing.  Super friendly!  So +100 for that, which means Sugar Freak gets 104 stars, but since Yelp only goes up to 5, I will give them 5. My rating system is flawless.  ;)
How can I count the ways that I love this place? CANT. I love the food, service, atmosphere and vibe!!!! bring on the Michelin stars baby!!!!

Like everyone else I've been dying to try this place. Finally, got a chance Saturday night. We sat at what they jokingly called the "Elvis" table. Wife had the spiked lemonade which she enjoyed. We ordered the crawfish boudain balls, and I think I found my new addiction. All I can say is WOW. Our entrees were both really good.  The fried chicken with mac and cheese was best I 've had in a  looong time, and the wife really enjoyed the blackened catfish. We were going to skip desert, but the waiter said something about dump cake ( yeah that's what they call it). With a name like that we had to try it. Another winner with cherry, pineapple and cake all mixed (dumped) together. And just as a side note, there's something about this place where you just feel welcome and comfortable, unlike other places on 30th ave. From the funky tables, stuff encased in the bar, and TV cabinet storage?!?!?   Someone really poured the love into this place. Really hope they stick around, because I found my new go to place. And to the whiney snob who gave the place one star because you couldn't get in. Go back to reviewing Wendy's

With the arrival of Sugar Freak, and William Hallet on the same block, 30th Ave is starting to rival our neighbors to the south, 31st ave (which has Pachanga Patterson and Il Bambino).   So, yeah, this place is pretty damn good.  Free corn bread appetizers, not too large, but very delicious, as is all the food.  I had the catfish platter with sweet potato fries ($12)--some of the best catfish I've ever had.  Probably won't have to go to Louisiana now.  The lady had a full muffaletta ($12), and it was way too big to take home.  A good complement to my meal, as I felt the portions of the platter were too small.     Only complaints are that a cocktail shouldn't be almost as much as your meal ($11--should have gotten an Abita, only 5-6 bucks on tap), and that it was a little too cold inside.   Definitely going back!

Amazing new Astoria destination! We just had a wonderful first experience at Sugarfreak! The decor is unbelievably cool. So much attention to detail and so charming, you feel like you are in the comforts of a Southern home. Also, the BEST Mac n cheese I've ever tasted! Can't wait to try the traditional Louisiana goods. Might I recommend adding a little Crystal hot sauce to the Mac n cheese, it brings out the multitude of delicious cheese flavors.  And the drinks! So delicious! Hibiscus lemonade and the Hurricane were my boyfriend's and my favorites. Go! Enjoy! Have fun! Cheers!

Southern/cajun food?  Yes please!!  Great experience.  The service, food, drinks and atmostphere are fantastic.  Check this place out if you love a little (lot) Americana in the city.  Making this joint a staple for sure.
I always stop by here for some iced milk tea, the best in Chinatown period!
Darling of a place - a hole in the wall place but quaint and nice.   We just had siphon coffee and tea.  Service was pleasant  and amiable.  I need to go back to check out the other stuff.

Their food is very good, freshly made when you order.  This is a family owned and run restaurant.  Very friendly atmosphere. It is not large, so I would not show up with a groups of people unless you go during an off hour.
We have been back 4 times the service get's better every time. The food has been great every time!!

I don't understand why some people are so negative about a place that just opened a few weeks ago! I am a lifetime Yardley resident and I personally am excited that we have a place now that isn't the Continental (even though I love the Conti) and doesn't serve pizza or Chinese food. It's something authentic and lovely and the food and service were great. I plan to go back many times. I am happy to support and lift the spirits of local hard working businesses, not put them down for every little thing that goes wrong. We had a great dining experience. It was a very pretty place and the food was great and the servers were helpful and friendly and this little gem is a great addition to a Main St of a town that has consisted of pizza places and realtors for ,y whole lifetime. Best of luck to them! I hope they will be around for a log time.

Ok...just ate there tonight. Plenty of wait staff...and pretty good at their jobs and very friendly. Decor...clean but sterile and horrible acoustics....we could barely hear ourselves talk, come on guys....get some fabrics up on the walls and real curtains to help deaden the noise. The food....pretty tasteless.....we started with the insulate misto which was excellent...very tasty and very fresh......bruschetta was ice cold out of the fridge and very boring, just some chopped tomatoes and a couple of pieces of red onion. The gf ordered the brasiola flank steak.....again very little flavour except for the generic tomato sauce that you can find at any diner within 500 miles. My pollo limone was completely tasteless, not even the tiniest hint of lemon flavour to it...totally boring and the veggies,green beans and potatoes were no better. We also split the tagliatelle pomodoro....again a boring ,tasteless,very generic tomato sauce with no seasonings...not one speck of basil in it. I ordered a tiramisu...which was very good. The bill for all that was $65.00 and we brought our own booze....so it's not expensive and the food isn't lousy....it's just tasteless. I'd probably give them a second chance in a couple of months......except the maybe not due to the horrific acoustics. We'll see in due course. The rest of you.....you've been warned.
made me a sushi- lover! highly recommended.

Awesome low key bar tucked right next to the Queensboro bridge.  There's an awesome craft beer selection and the food is definitely up to par.  I had the Jeffrey Rubenstein sandwich and the house made IPA mustard that came on it was awesome!  There's a decent sized outdoor beer garden area out back that looks great for groups! We didn't get to go out there because it was raining though.  Overall this is definitely a little gem and next time I'm uptown I'll be coming back.

Right on the border of Midtown East and the Upper East Side, this great little gastropub located on 60th street (in between 1st and 2nd ave) next to the Queensboro Bridge is something worth keeping a secret. I took four friends from out of town here on a random Friday (early) afternoon, and let me say we were all blown away with their beer selection. The place itself was awesome, laid back and cool and it complimented the quality and variety of beers offered.  All my friends loved their beers, but I can only speak about my own beer. In general, I love Belgium Ales, so I got the Alagash Tripel - a strong golden ale marked by passion fruit and herbal notes in the aroma, with suggestions of banana and honey in the complex palate (description from their website). It was 9% ABV and had a $10 price tag - well worth every penny. I would definitely come back again, and I plan on coming back - I liked this place. Next time, I want to get some of the delicious looking food that's been well yelped about... Charcuterie, pulled pork, meatballs, and pickled veggies, NOMZ.

(went here wednesday, april 2, 2014) great selection of beers on tap. a few of them are $4 or $5 during their happy hour. i tried their cucumber-basil gimlet which was tasty but for $14 i wish i tasted some alcohol. my buddies and i also got their homemade beef jerky, truffle popcorn and pretzels. i can't remember exactly which 2 we tried but they were both amazing. our waitresses were also incredibly friendly. i'll definitely be back but will stick to their beers.

They don't take reservations, but I called anyway. "Sure we'll hold a table for you." We got there... no table. Could have been a disaster... but it wasn't!!! Instead of the usual Screw You treatment, the manager went out of his way to find us something. Not only that, he treated the whole group to Jamison shots to thank us for waiting. So, reason one, this place is so popular: THEY'RE NICE!!! Reason two: the beer. The menu changes three times a day. I was looking forward to Rauch beer (tough to get in NYC... it's great... like drinking Barbecue)... but they didn't have it any more. They did have a very nice VOODOO beer, that was worth another (and another) glassful. The cheese plate was great to share, and the spicy nuts were also good for the crew. The crowd was a mix of tourists, students, and bridge and cable people. (It's right next to the Roosevelt Island Tram). Everyone was friendlier than vacuum cleaner salesmen. Great night thanks to a great well-run bar.

Completely relaxed, microbrew beer destination. With a long bar and simple seats, the service is friendly, if a bit slow, but the beers here can be very good. Long and skinny, garden in the back, and the second door goes past a coffee machine to the bathrooms more easily than walking around. Paper menus, they probably replace them a lot. The cheese/meat charcuterie is not bad, though they didn't give us a knife for the softer cheese. The roast beef sandwich had a bit of spice, which was good. The happy hour M-F is 11am, yes, AM, to 7pm. Lunch special is a Happy Hour beer + sandwich for $10. Not a bad deal at all! Overall, a great little place to eat a few snacks and grab a tasty beer or two. Too small for large groups, though. Easiest in a 2-3 sized group.

Came here with a group of 3 for late lunch and there was no issue with getting seated. It was a little strange that we walked in and had to seat ourselves. Nobody ever came to greet us until we sat down. Despite that, the service was good. The waitress was friendly and attentive. We ordered the roast beef, veggie, and BLT sandwiches with regular fries and truffle fries. Unfortunately I didn't get a chance to try the veggie sandwich but was told that it was good. The roast beef sandwich wasn't bad. It lacked some flavor but it was tender and not chewy at all. I thought the sandwich was a little dry as opposed to the BLT sandwich. It was flavorful. I like the dressing in it. It made it less dry and the bacon were in perfect sizes. The bread was toasted and the bread used was excellent. The salt from the bacon was a perfect balance to the sandwich. The truffle fries/chips weren't bad. First time having it but it was only a hint of truffle and the chips/fries were too oily. Extremely fried. In summary, I would actually give this place 3.5 stars. Food wasn't bad at all but could offer some improvements in taste in the roast beef sandwich and a tad better in the service. I wouldn't mind coming back here again just to hang out. They also have a great beer selection.

I think this place has everything. Great beer selection first of all, and they are clearly passionate and meticulous about this. The food was superb, except for the deviled eggs. Didn't enjoy. But the truffle popcorn and devils on horseback more than made up for it. The interior is all wooden tables and exposed brick. And they have an outdoor beer garden. Seriously, go here. You will not be disappointed.

We ate here over Labor Day weekend for the restaurant's soft opening.  The place is unbelievable.  From the decor to the service to the food (the food!) to the drinks, the team of CookNSolo has killed it once again.  Go, eat everything, you won't be disappointed - the food is delicious and inventive, unlike anything this city (or any city) has ever seen.  Book now, I predict this place will be mobbed every night from now until forever.

Had a good sampling at restaurant week.... For veggies had the borscht and carrots with Gouda.  Both delicious, borscht reminded me of the beets at Zahav.  Carrots were outstanding.    Fish had the sable and gefilite (sp?).  Both very good the latter a bit better but can't go wrong with either.   Meats had the veal schnitzel tacos, this was the star of the evening I won't go back without getting those.  Also ordered the lamb, which didn't bowl me over.    Dessert had the bacon and egg Creme, that was super good, rivals barbuzzos caramel bundido for best desserts around. Fantastic server and service was spot on

I don't like to just throw out 5-star ratings after one visit, but for a restaurant that just opened a week or two ago I was seriously impressed. Once I visit again, if everything is equal to or better than my first experience, I will change this to 5 stars and Abe Fisher will be my homeboy for life. First, the entire staff was great. I'm not even going to elaborate because if you've been to good restaurants before you will know what good service is. I will say that I appreciated that manager took a few moments to chat with us. Next, I thought just about all of the food was fantastic, including the presentation. After ordering our drinks we were offered three different types of savory rugelach (a rolled pastry with filling) and they were actually one of the highlights of the meal. We couldn't decide which flavor was best. The carrots are a must try. My S.O. didn't care for the Kasha varnishkes, but what does she know? That's right. She doesn't even know. I really enjoyed them. A lot of different textures going on, which I am always a fan of. One of the only things I didn't really care for was the marinated portion of the Raw and Marinated Bass - it reminded me a little too much of deli tunafish salad - which just isn't for me. The raw stuff was unbelievable, though. I'd order it again just for the raw bass. The sable was decent, but not remarkable. The veal schnitzel tacos are another must try. We also had the meatballs, which were great. All the dishes are intended for sharing and are more than enough for two people. Happy endings - the panna cotta (not on their online menu) was honestly a top 5 all-time dessert for me. I was only allowed to have a tiny bite of the black and white, but that seemed really great. The decor, ambiance, etc was all cool. It's a smallish place, so it can be a little loud, but that certainly didn't detract from anything. All in all this is a place you should try. I know that I will be back.

Another hit from Michael Solomonov! We dined at Zahav last year and were extremely pleased, so we decided to try Abe Fisher during restaurant week. No regrets. None. We shared 8 plates including dessert which left us feeling full and satisfied. The highlights of the meal, although every dish was delicious, were the borscht tartare, roasted salmon, veal schnitzel tacos and the Roumainian skirt steak. I could have easily listed each and every plate but that would defeat the purpose of the 'highlight'. Oh forget it, let me tell you what else we got; kasha varnishkes, sable cake, and the black and white cheesecake and apple strudel were our dessert plates. Like I said earlier, the food was delicious and perfectly prepared. Some of the best steak I've ever had. Thanks to restaurant week we were able to eat all of this for $35 each. I highly recommend Abe Fisher and hope to return here for another meal. *12/30/14: Restaurant critic Craig Laban awarded Abe Fisher's Montreal-smoked short ribs his "Feast of the year" for 2014. I am absolutely dying to try it.
Food was decent. ..not the best breakfast in the area. Priced very reasonable and fast service. Also not over crowded for a Sunday morning which is a plus.

Never disappointing whenever I'm here.  It's my favorite restaurant in LIC.  Everything on the menu is yummy.  Decor is just ok, but the food totally makes up the lack of character.  Try the Mole when you are here!  It is California standard!  Tacos, short ribs, lamb shank are all delicious!

Great Mexican spot in LIC, with a backyard garden patio as well. Went here on Monday night with a few friends for dinner and it was fantastic.  Even before coming here, a few of the LIC locals even mentioned that Casa Enrique is the place to go to for good food. The back patio was completely full, so we sat inside, but it was still a nice experience.  When you walk in, there's a bar to the left, and two rooms that are simple, with white paint, but have this elegance towards them.  There were also a fair amount of people inside. The waitress was extremely nice and recommended great drinks too.  I ended up getting one of the spicy jalapeno margaritas (they have two on their menu) and it was really good.  When you take a sip, you don't realize the spiciness, just taste a traditional margarita, and then the spice hits you on the aftertaste.  It was delicious. We ordered the guac and that was very good - no compaints there.  They also provide the table with these fried corn sticks, that were very addicting. For dinner, I got the Dona Blanca Enchiladas, which were amazing!  There were three enchiladas that were sitting in this delicious tomatillo sauce with crema fresca.  The enchiladas were stuffed with roasted chilies, black beans, onions, and lettuce, and topped with sliced avocados on top.  The whole meal was delicious and worked very well together.  It wasn't messy, didn't fall apart, and I ate the whole thing without feeling overly stuffed. If I'm back in LIC, I'll definitely come back to this place!

WAY WAY WAY overpriced. I paid $8 for the two tacos. The two tacos are HONESTLY 3 inches in DIAMETER. TINY  TINY TACOS. $14 for enchiladas - they were OK. If you do go here ,just pay the $7 for the tres leches cake. It is the best thing on the menu.

Easily some of the best Mexican food I've had in NYC. Impeccable service from start to finish. The servers paid close attention to detail and always offered fantastic recommendations. Each dish had several layers and the flavors are very fresh and authentic. Highly memorable dishes: Serrano pepper margarita (tasted like jalapeño with a hint of cucumber) Scallops with chorizo** I would've ordered several servings Sopecitos The salsa in the middle of the table (especially the salsa verde and mild sauce) Doña Blancas enchiladas Tres Leches

Dishonest people are in this restaurant. My wife and I went to the brunch on Sunday 8/10/2014 at Casa Enrique in LIC. We paid by credit card and we added 19% tip to the bill. When I reviewed my credit card statement, I found out that the charge is not the same as what I paid on the receipt. Apparently they decided to take 25% tip. The food was so so. Nothing special. We don't plan to dispute the charge because it is not worth it for a few dollars. But we will not go back there because the people working there are greedy dishonest people who would fraud your tip amount. Be careful if you are paying by credit card at Casa Enrique. Check your credit card statement.

As weird as it may sound I'm ok with receiving poor service if it's super busy and everyone is equally receiving poor service. It's another thing when I feel and see that poor service is received only by those of a different age group or a different race from that of the normal customer base. Today brunch was pretty terrible. Service was obviously better for some people when I see the curly haired waitress joking around and asking how everything was going for other tables. Yet she never once came to our table other than to take our order and bringing our check after having to flag her down. If your going to be bias please don't make it so obvious by being loud about it with the table across from us and then completely ignoring us the whole time. The eggs in the huevos chorizo were dry and flavorless. The mole in huevos mole was ok I guess. Nothing spectacular. One star for guac which was pretty good and a big portion and one star for the unbiased busboy who refilled our water. I guess I'll have to keep an eye on my statement since it seems like they like overcharging the tip we leave.
Small spot. Delicious draft beers, sausages & pretzels.
I love going here! Even though it takes us 30 minutes to get there it is so worth it! I'm looking forward to lunch today! :)

I used to love their sweets, for the last 20 years this was my family's favorite sweet shop in this country. Even 1.5 years ago their sweets were still excellent and made with quality ingredients. Then I went to their store last June and the quality was just gone. I thought it was a one time fluke, so I went back three separate times over the next two months hoping they would get back on track. But it was just a waste of $100. They started adulterating their rasamalais and rasagulas with flour and I have no idea what they did to everything else. Their parking lot  and store used to be packed. These days I never see more than 5 cars in their lot. I hope they bring back their quality. But I am beginning to doubt they will.

Cheap beer ($3 for Bud and Yuengling all day, for one) and a huge long bar filled with some of NYC's finest. They have food too, just never tried it before. Big highlight for me is the waitress who served us when we sat in a booth: literally looked like she was one of the survivors on the Titanic. Really nice and accommodating, though. One of the best bars in the Financial District.

It is definitely a unique experience having lunch at the White Horse Tavern.  You can't go wrong with having a soup & sandwich for 8.00 The staff is very nice, the food is very good, it almost feels like I went into a time warp.

The place is really good. I had a Falafel sandwich and it was amazing! They bring you the plate with the vegetables, tahini and falafel separate, so you can assemble it yourself. After seeing the Mammon's cook preparing a falafel sandwich with the same bare hands that he took my money, Kasbah is definitely my future choice for Falafel sanwhiches. The place has a beautiful terrace where you can eat when the weather is nice. We had a group dinner in the second floor and we had a wonderful time. There are many many couches where you can sit comfortably and the owner and the waitress make you feel like home. Really worth a visit

Kasbah Garden is a hidden gem. The food is scrumptiou and reasonably priced, the restaurant is cozy - featuring a fantastic loft and gorgeous garden - and the family who runs the place are delightful. I haven't yet been there in the summer, but I can't wait for their candlelit patio and bellydancing when the warm weather arrives. And no matter how full you are, do NOT pass up the baklava. it is inspirational.

Food is divine, family that runs it is amazing. Have been twice now and can't wait for warmer weather and nights out in the garden. Live music and belly dancing! Hookah is great, baklava even better (and the pieces are so big!) and Moroccan tea hits the spot every time. This place is the best!

My husband and I have been to this restaurant a few times in the past couple months and just can't get enough of it. The food is outstanding, service is great, and the restaurant itself is nice and clean. The naan is awesome, and prices for the amount of food you get is very reasonable. Our favorite entree is the Chicken Korma which is a cashew saffron sauce and it is just incredible with naan and rice. Everything we have tried here is great and flavorful.
Food was excellent . Our group tried a variety of dishes . Our waiter R (don't remember his full name) was knowledgeable and helpful. I will go again

I have nothing bad to say about this place. The food from the lunch buffet is excellent. The perfect amount of heat in every dish. They could have a few more options though. The service was great. The mango lassi is delicious! The atmosphere is OK, a tad too modern for my taste. Lunch buffet is 12.99. I will definitely come back.

Warning to people with food allergies: I've been to Tiny Thai a handful of times (pretty average Thai food compared to what you would find in any big city, above average for the area), but my experience I had the last time I ate there may be the last because of the inept waitstaff. When ordering, I mentioned I had a shellfish allergy and the waitstaff took note of that.  One of the items that I ordered was the Beef Nam Tok.  The ingredients listed on the menu for the dish seemed to preclude it from having shellfish in it, but the menu says that not all ingredients are listed on the menu - which is a good thing I think.   Upon bringing the Beef Nam Tok out as an appetizer, our waitstaff (will keep it ambiguous as to who it was) says "I don't know who ordered this [it was me, the allergic one] but the Beef Nam Tok has shellfish in it.  I just found out it has shellfish in it."   Umm ok - that's not really how it works.  You are: a) supposed to have prior knowledge of the dishes that could cause an allergic reaction and tell the customer when they order or b) if you don't know at the point of ordering, it's perfectly OK (it can be daunting to memorize all of that), but find out from someone who does know ***BEFORE*** you bring the dish out to the customer (not after) The waitstaff appeared dumbfounded after I asked them to take it back.  They made the situation extremely awkward sort of just holding the dish there - no immediate apology was given, nor did they offer to take it back, or take it off our bill.  Attempting to defuse the situation, the person I was with said she would just eat it.  The waitstaff did eventually apologize.   Train your waitstaff, food allergies are serious.

Great shop and very friendly service. The shop is small and clean, and they also sell some assorted, ethnic frozen foods (e.g. paratha, samosas, etc.) The surrounding neighborhood is quiet and nice, and there's a large grocery store (Square on Square?) a block away if you need other items. I didn't know what type of lamb to buy and the man behind the counter was very helpful in choosing the best type for an Indian curry and then cutting the pieces accordingly. The quality of both the lamb and the chicken that I bought were very good.

Cutest place ever!! It's a very small place in the heart of soho, but totally worth going to if you're looking for a quick bite to eat somewhere an need to relax. They do have outside seating, but mind you, this place doesn't really have air conditioning. Their decor to their table settings was absolutely adorable. I ordered the mashed avocado sandwich which came with a cherry tomato jam and pickled carrot slaw on top. Yum!!! I came back the next day to order it to go since I work right around the corner. Definitely a must-go next time you're in soho.

Best Brunch and Dinner in soho - super cute interior, cafe vibe. Staff is laid back yet attentive. Best brunch item - shakshuka. For dinner, make sure you try the cauliflower and specials! I guess we got lucky the first time we came in, and got seated with not too long of a wait. We have been there a few times now, and after the third time we already felt like regulars. The two owners are usually there and super nice and accommodating.

LOve love love Jack's wife Freda, the food is divine, affordable, light  and super tasty! the atmosphere is amazing, young, happening and laid back in the evening, great place for brunch with kids, great place to bring ppl who want to see what a real New York place feels like, love it, too bad im all the way uptown!!

wow. came in again for for dinner and had such an amazing time! as we opened the door i just knew i was gonna have a great time. great soundtrack, amazing food, and the warmest service. i had the burger with haloumi  cheese, the waitress recommended - and was quite delicious and my husband had the whole fish (dorade i think) with couscous - it was just like somewhere on the Mediterranean sea... will be back soon Jacks wife!

This place is one of the few restaurants in NYC that consistently offers what feels like a home cooked meal (yet never bores one's palette!). The ambiance deserves the same description as the wife and husband owners are almost always there and in their absence are qualified managers. The staff acts like one big family ready to welcome you to their brood. And for its location (the middle of posh Soho) such easy going friendliness is invaluable. I recommend the tuna salad for health conscious eaters (although you definitely don't feel like your sacrificing any satisfaction) or for the more glutinous try the burger or steak sandwich. There are also many in-between options, such as their delicious but not over indulgent starters. As a middle grounder, I order the tuna salad with a side of small fries, which their happy to accommodate. The fries are AMAZING. One of the best places in NYC!!!

I found myself sitting in the corner of Jack's Wife Freda after an evening of bocce ball in Brooklyn, soaking in the casual-trendy vibe the place illuminated. It's an endearing, simply decorated room with white walls, simple accents, and a communal table in majestically sitting the center of the room.  At night, it can be beyond dim.  The crowd can be a combination of Nolita youth and stumbling tourists. The food options are simple and after reading about the owners and discovering that they hail from Israel and South Africa, you could easily say the menu is influenced by this fun fact.   The peri-peri sweetbreads, which I indulged in brought back all the good thoughts of fried, fatty meat, or in this case less often eaten parts of an animal, floating in a delicious sweet and spicy sauce.  My prego roll, or in translation, well cooked and seasoned skirt steak with a nice pungent garlic butter on a roll, was simple and filling.  The wife's Bloody Mary mussels were just that.  Fresh mussels cooked in a spicy tomato broth.  The fries that came with both our meals was adequate. The best part was seeing our check.  Damn good cooking with some wine and beer, a Leffe Blonde for me as the selection was simple, totaled 75 before tax and tip. Casual, laid back, deliciousness in the heart of a not so laid back area.

By looking from the outside, much different then anything you would expect ... very original and awesome food!   usually a line out the door during lunch but the guys behind the counter are extremely quick & efficient.   I heard they are opening up a new store.. Does anyone know where the next location is going to be... hopefully in Hoboken, they would rake in tons of cash there! Great place overall

Decent food at reasonable prices.  I've had the cheesesteak which is pretty good.  As expected greasy and hearty.  The tacos and Mexcian however are a bit of a disappointment.  I believe the burritoes are premade and just warmed up because the inside wasn't that hot.  It's a good place if you are in the mood for greasy fast food.

There is a reason Scott has all 5/5 stars. He is awesome. And passionate. About pizza. I went with a group of people, including some people who were born and raised in New York. One of them who is a through and through NY pizza fanatic was introduced to his new favorite pizza place thanks to Scott. Now, I'm not a NY pizza fan. I don't like greasy or flavorless pizza (sorry to all you die hard New York pizza fans) but he actually brought us to places that had good NY style pizza. Before this tour I didn't think that good NY style pizza existed. Even better than realizing that not all NY pizza is totally inedible, he took us to a pizza place that has Napoli style pizza (my favorite kind). I have been to Naples, and the pizza place he took us to was almost as good as the pizza I had there. Yum... tasty, not greasy, and totally flavorful pizza....*drools a little*

Not only is the pizza on the tour some of the best you'll ever have (for all tastes), Scott is the best person you could ever eat with. He never infringes his own experiences and personal tastes impact any one else's. He is a huge pizza cheerleader spreading passion for the food, cooking process and industry. Where better to learn about pizza than in NY!?
good one

Ah, what can I say that hasn't been said over and over in these reviews?  Scott (and JoAnne) are passionate about pizza and their love is infectious.  We did the walking tour, which is an easy do for anyone who can walk a few blocks and then eat a slice.  Our tour ran the gamut from flour to coal (they'll have to explain it further!).  Knowledgeable, exciting, fun, and just a fantastic way to spend a NY afternoon.  Also, if you live anywhere other than NY and need a good pizza, Scott has probably been to your hometown and knows where to steer you.  Run, don't walk, to this tour...you will be a better person for it.  It's a few hours that can change your perspective on what NY is all about.  Pizza for peace!

**TOO CHEESY FOR ME** With all the rave reviews on Yelp, I expected it to be a WOW experience, but alas, it did not WOW me like the others. Granted, Scott was very passionate about pizzas, but a bit too nerdy for  me. There were three pizza parlor stops: Lombardi's, Joe's, and John's. We spoke to some neighborhood Italians on the way and they told us that these were not the best pizza places; just historical pizza landmarks. So if you expect the best pizza pie experience, you may be disappointed. We were not interested in visiting a pizza supply store, so we stopped by Ray's on Prince instead and ordered the Sicilian which was very good. Again, this was my personal take on the tour, it just wasn't for me.

Good, but not as great as I thought it would be. My meal of chicken salad and soup which was a special for around $6 was great but my husband got a spring mixwrap with barely any lettuce and green peppers vs red and cold cheese. Just not what we described. Kids meals were a good deal.  Very weak iced tea (I mean almost water!). Our waitress was very nice but the service was so slow. We were there 1.5 hours and it was meant to be a quick stop. I really don't think it was her fault I just think it tool forever to place the order and get it done. The kicker is everything we got aside from soup was cold!
I went in this past weekend and it was amazing. The food is delicious and the servers are friendly. Love it!

Great food very nice wait staff. So I arrived just as they were finishing up for the day , and the owner and chef welcomed me to come in and eat. I had the eggs benedict with potato wedges. Excellent flavor just the right amount od hollandaise sauce, eggs were cooked to perfection.. Served on a toasted english muffin with a bed of steamed spinach and sauteedred onions. I asked the chef to leave out the meat, which was not a problem.  I had the blueberry limeaid fusion, which was very good but a bit to tart for my taste. Over all it was a great dining experience and my 2nd time there. I will be going back again. Worth the trip across the bridge.

Based on my first meal here, I'm a fan. Seating was prompt, service was friendly, and the food was very good. I started with a spinach salad with beets, corn and peppers; while I'm not generally enthusiastic about corn, its sweetness and crunch complemented the other sweet veggies well. Also, the cherry tomatoes were sliced, which is unfortunately often not the case. Overall, a well-made and attractively presented salad and an auspicious start to the dining experience. I followed up with the eggs florentine, about which there's not much to say: they were good. The eggs were cooked right and, more importantly, so was the kale: it was neither cooked to death nor rough and raw. And yes, as others have pointed out, the breakfast potatoes were delicious and perfect for scraping up yolk. I hope this place finds its customers and survives, because I look forward to returning and exploring the menu further.

Stopped in for brunch this morning just before 11AM. I was surprised that we were seated immediately, then I learned that we made it just in time before the late morning rush. The specials are listed on a chalkboard on the wall, and our waitress described them to us and gave her recommendations. They all sounded amazing, but I already had in my mind that I wanted a carb heavy meal. I opted for the Amaretto French Toast. I was nervous because I feared it may be too sweet. I hate when I get a "sweet" breakfast item and then feel nauseated halfway through the meal because of the overabundance of sugar. This french toast was PERFECT. It was french toast with an almond crust on top, rather than slices of bread infused with sugar. The vanilla bean maple syrup was also a nice touch. The portion size was excellent. I was able to finish my meal, but didn't feel like I had a food baby erupting. Overall, I think this is an excellent spot for brunch. I'd recommend going earlier to avoid the wait. It also appeared that they took reservations (which is rare for brunch). I will definitely be returning, and possibly with a bottle of champagne for some mimosas (BYOB!).

Given the great reviews of this place we were clearly unlucky but a bad experience is a bad experience. The main chef wasn't in that night so the place was totally dead on a Sunday night. The guest chef was serving Filipino food but honestly I have lived in the Philippines and did not recognize most of the dishes listed. There was very little choice - most of which was entrails, tripe, snout.... i'm assuming you get the picture? And hey, I like my offal as much as the next girl, but usually just as one dish of many  - the many being the usually eaten animal body parts. The idea of eating an entire meal of offal in an entirely empty restaurant was needless to say - pretty unappealing so had one glass of wine and the only normal beef and egg dish of the menu. Gotta say tho - the beef was pretty tasty!

I was a bit surprised at the idea of Korean/Argentine fusion food but was pleasantly surprised at the results.  The atmosphere does not feel very Korean (I'm Korean) or Argentine nor does the menu really look like either I have to say.  I was feeling very skeptical but we ordered an appetizer of ugly dumplings.  My girlfriend was a fan but I wasn't really.  I'm not much for cheese in a dumpling and the chimichurri sauce was nothing like Argentine chimichurri sauce according to my girlfriend (she's from Argentina).  The entrees though really knocked it out of the park.  I got the Ugly Pork Belly which was pretty delicious.  The cabbage on the bottom was a bit soggy but still tasty.  My girlfriend got some sort of chicken dish which was fantastic.  The chicken was very tender and juicy and the sauce was tasty.  I would definitely want to go back to try the other dishes.

Ugly is right-- perfect description of bar, staff, and clientele. Lame music, high-priced drinks made by surly bartenders, stomach-turning food, a Mecca for grade A d-bags. How has the East Village gone so far down hill?

Was here with a bunch of friends and family on a Thursday night for some random drinks after dinner. It's a really cute place, not too intimate not too large, and plays great music. If you're deciding on a venue to celebrate a birthday with friends and still want to be able to talk to them, hang out, listen to music, Ugly Kitchen will be a great place.

NEED to write another review for the food! Came here for a quick dinner with a friend before a concert and the food was amazing!! There weren't many people inside since it was early (around 6:30/7pm?) and service was super fast. For appetizers, we got the fries and pork buns (of courrsee) and both were great. As I checked in on foursquare, I realized there was a promotion for a free ugly dumpling app and our server quickly brought that out for us happily. For entrees, I listened to the other reviews and got the pork belly entree and my friend got the spicy amatriciana pasta. Pork belly was great, just the right amount of fatty vs meaty parts and over some sort of fantastic puree. The amatriciana was great as well, really flavorful with chunks of sausage but a bit too heavy for my taste. (especially after downing the pork belly) Great service, great food!

I love this place. I'm sure I'll come back often if I'm in the area. It has a very homey ambiance as it's a small place where the kitchen and dining area are as connected as possible. While sitting, you can see beyond the counter in the kitchen where it looks like the staff is preparing your food as if you were sitting at the dining table in someone's home. The Yuzu chicken rice dish was delicious, light, simple, and exactly what I was going for at the time.

My friend and I went to Rooftop120 today and we were impressed. The entrance is quaint and very welcoming. I ordered a Rooftop Sunset and it was awesome. This was one of the best drinks that I've had in a while. Then I ordered the Short Rib Sliders which was tasty but I requested a side of ketchup and tobasco sauce. I needed an extra umph. I had a chance to enjoy drinks and some short rib sliders while enjoying an amazing view. The seats were comfortable and it began to get more crowded. The ambiance was classy, trendy and there were positive vibes. For a sweet ending I ordered a Tempura Fried Double Stuff Oreos with a cup of milk. This is a great place for young professionals, date or relax with some friends old and new.  It's a combination of South Beach and Las Vegas.   Also, the waitstaff was excellent and I had the best waiter. She was very personable and helpful.

We went to Rooftop last night because it was gorgeous out and we wanted to sit outside. We were a party of 5 but two came late. I had asked if the three of us (who were going to sit and order dinner) could be sat at a table. The host refused and told me that only once the entire party is here could we do that. Once everyone did show up it was an absolute chore to get our food and drinks transferred from the bar to the table. Nothing arrived on time and our waiter (who was still wearing his sunglasses at 9:00 at night) took forever to wait on us. Beers we ordered were never served, food came out super late, the waitstaff was rude when we were ordering, and to top it all off the bartender had charged us for $30 bucks for drinks that our party had never even ordered. We couldn't leave fast enough (figuratively and literally- because they were so slow in bringing out food!)
Good atmosphere.  Nice place to have a drink outside in the evening.  However parking is impossible.  Waitstaff was rude. A little courtesy would go along way.

The Chef Park has very unique character; pretty humble and also always in confidence, energetic. He seems very creative and scrupulous. Foods are awesome!!!! I tried almost every foods here! Cuz once i tried small portion of appetizer, my instinctive suspicion was disappeared. I'd love to visit this place more often if i live in Williamsburg. That's the my complaint lol. *Overall; greatest foods i've ever had b4, great one-on-one customer services, cozy and comfy atmosphere. Everything just perfect. Pretty reasonable price too!

On a Friday night, what could have been more romantic than a dinner with the boyfriend at Bistro Petit! The restaurant is cozy , seating 10 people inside on high bar tables and 3 small round tables outside. I really felt as if I was on vacation dining in a French restaurant with its cute classical decor, sipping a glass of wine and watching pedestrians walk by. Mental notes I took down: - Definitely make a reservation as this place is very small. - BYOB ! This restaurant focuses on French bistro cuisine, with an Asian/Korean influence. Keep an eye out on what is their specials for the day. We had the watermelon salad appetizer and it was extremely refreshing with a marriage of the sweet & juicy of the watermelon, sourness from the pickled watermelon rind, and savoriness from the grilled cheese. The entrees are reasonably priced for the amount and quality of food. I had the kimchi bouillabaisse, which is a caldron pot filled with mussels, scallop, shrimp, fish in a kimchi based sauce. Caution: If you can't take spicy food, you may want to stay away from it because it's a good type of spiciness that stays in your mouth and refuses to leave.... Always leave room for dessert. Bistro Petit is known for their donuts which are rather large in size (5 pieces) and comes freshly made with a googy eggy goodness inside.  One order is more than enjoy for 2 people - trust me , I made the mistake of ordering two orders because my eyes were bigger than my stomach!

This place has been mark on my list for long time. Last week, I finally had a chance to come to this lovely neighborhood again, and I cant let my dinner go down to other place. It' s fun, cuz I put a wrong image on the store, I told my friend there is a long wooden dinning table, how lovely. But the truth is NO. I am just dreaming... Anyway, It was pretty cool experience. I didnt make reservation at all. But i was lucky that night, I had an outdoor table. It was right next to the garbage... which really turn me off a lot. I will suggest you guys move the table away from the gully cover... Anyway, bon appetite!  I had my burger and risotto, and a kimchi mussel! I share foods okay;)  The burger is AMAZING. I love the bun and the beef taste absolutely juicy juicy and fresh! A little bit of avocado smooths everything! The risotto was gone when it is out on the table. We Love it! It's cheesy when I scoop it up. It is just what I like, light and delightful.
Great service, delicious food.  Loved the atmosphere and decor.  We will return for sure!

TOP NOTCH. CAN I SAY THAT AGAIN? TOP NOTCH. i felt like i was a celebrity. seriously. and the food - OMGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGG. BEST TOMATO SOUP I HAVE EVER HAD. and yes, i order tomato soup at a lot of places. also had the scallops and the duck. amazing.
food was decent, but waaaaay overpriced.  building and staff are gorgeous, however.

I was not pleased with my experience at bucos at all! The food was decent but the service was not. The waiters were so rude and I had to ask for them to bring out bread and water because they were too incompetent to bring it out on their own. My utensils were dirty. There are so many better quality Italian restaurants in the area that I would go to instead of this one. In fact, I probably would have received better service at the Olive Garden. So disappointed!

Very disappointed. The quality has decreased. Tofu Soup base is just plain water add kimchi. We ordered #2 seafood tofu bean curd, they only gave us 1 unfresh shrimp and 2 little calms, thats all. Ridiculous. Plus A LOT OF MSG!

I have been to China many times and have eaten lots of meals there. Of all of them about 3 were very good. Chengdu 46 is as good or better. The Peking duck was spectacular and the short ribs just brilliant.

I came here yesterday for a soft touch opening and was given a complimentary drink...I ordered the Malasian potatoes and it was awesome!!! The service was great!!! I really thought the bartenders were awesome!!! The reason why this place does not receive 5 stars is due to not having a LQ license...and the complimentary wine smelled great but tasted a bit off...I wish that the cocktails were available to give a full description! !! I will be back once the LQ license is approved!!! This place is a extension of Vedge! !! V street is an awesome and laid back place. .

Amazing, affordable, adventurous bites -- vegetarians (vegans, pescetarians, & omnivores) rejoice!  V Street has arrived! Under normal circumstances I'd hold off reviewing until after the grand opening (Sat 10/18), but V Street was so polished and ready for service I can't resist.*  My husband and I showed up around 30 minutes after V Street opened and were quickly seated at the ~6 seat chef's counter (there were also some high 2-top tables in the kitchen space as well).  The drooling commenced. We ordered 6 dishes to share -- Papadums and Green Beans ($5 each) from the snacks section to start, followed by Peruvian Fries ($7) and Carrot Choripan ($10), and finished off with Dan Dan Noodles ($12) and Korean Fried Tempeh Tacos ($10).  Our server Amy was friendly and well versed in the menu, answering all of our questions with ease and offering us two complimentary beverages since the liquor license wasn't in yet.   We would order every dish again, just as soon after we make our way through the rest of the menu.  Two dishes stood out above the others, merely based on personal preference.  The Peruvian Fries are the best vegan "cheese" fries ever, with tons of flavor and crunch.  The Korean Fried Tempeh Tacos were hands down the best pieces of tempeh we have ever eaten -- maybe because they were battered, fried, and slathered in gochujang glaze.   A note on portion: We happily waddled home with no regrets, but would recommend starting off with 4 to 5 dishes rather than 6 for a party of 2.  We were pleasantly surprised that each dish was easy to share -- 2 tacos, 2 choripanes, etc. Highly recommend! *Didn't snap any pics during our visit -- but check out vstreetfood on instagram!  We geeked out when Kate Jacoby snapped a pic of our dan dan noodles Thursday night :)

Yummy vegan goodness! V Street is a great place to try a variety of small plates. The portions are lightfor the most part, but the excitement and the flavors make up for it. The trumpet mushrooms were a favorite of the night, as well as the Dan Dan Noodles. Beware, they are real Szechuan-style hot! I'm still sweating a day later, I think. The ambiance is great, and we were surprised to find no wait for a table just three weeks after they opened, although the place was full and busy when we arrived. I think this will be a long-living restaurant on 19th street.

I was excited to try this new restaurant with my two vegetarian friends. The drink menu is very interesting - all aspects: the cocktails, beers and wine all include things you don't see often. My friend ordered the mustard gin cocktail, which is heavy on the mustard flavor, but she enjoyed it. My other friend ordered the japanese whiskey miso drink, which was strong and sweet. I played it safe with a double IPA. After googling a lot of the menu ingredients and ordering, we anxiously awaited our dishes. We split the piri piri tofu and harissa cauliflower to start, which were some of the most flavorful appetizers I've ever had anywhere. The pickled celery and marinade on the tofu is a perfect balance. Not in the mood for a sandwich or soup, all three of us decided to order the mushroom dan dan noodles. The sesame sauce was incredibly bold and spicy, a little too spicy for everyone to handle (with no warning from our server after asking how spicy the piri piri was). The mushrooms were delicious but the noodles were a little overcooked. Though we all loved the addition of some zucchini noodles on top. We didn't have intentions of ordering dessert, but when the server described the cranberry soft serve as an interpretation of a Good Humor bar, we decided to get a bowl with three spoons. It was tart and sweet sherbet-style with granola bits and dried cranberries crumbled on top. I hope the menu changes often. I'm excited to try other things!

Boloco is decidedly the black sheep of the Chipolte-Qdoba-Anna's Taqueria family. And oh how I wish little Hanover NH had any of the above. Please? The big challenge with Boloco is the consistency of its product. Go in one day and your server will roll you a fat, delicious burrito or wrap that is hard to argue with. Go in twice after that, and you'll wonder if you've set foot in a different establishment: skimpy protein servings, less tasty filling, and presto, a sad, skinny burrito that looks like it jogged off the set of The Biggest Loser. Their second challenge is price. Let's face it. Boloco charges a premium--almost $10--for a burrito, if you add in extras like guac. That same $10 would easily buy you about 30% more burrito at any of the above franchises. Or, here in Hanover, there are plenty of sit-down, table service lunch *meals* to be had for under $10. Boloco could get its act together. It has such promise but delivers the wrap of your dreams only when it feels like it. But given it's really the only game in town for wraps, and no competitors are pushing it to be better, it will probably continue to serve up mediocre creations in its own private, highly lucrative bubble.

Pitrucco pizza is delicious!  I am so happy they decided to join the food truck area at Love Park on certain weekdays.  I went yesterday around 11:40AM as to avoid lines.  It worked because we just walked up to the counter and ordered.   I ordered the eggplant pizza.  It is slightly pricey at $8, but then when you consider what you are getting for the money, it's all good.  You get a personal sized pizza that will fill you up for lunch.  The dough/crust is perfect, fluffy around the edges and crispy on the bottom.  The ingredients are fresh and delicious.   I actually like that they don't give you a box.  There definitely needs to be less unnecessary packaging in the world.  Plus you can start eating it on your way back to the office!   :)   The service is friendly and fast and you have to give them points for innovation - the brick oven on a truck!   I will be back to try all of the non-meat pizza varieties soon.

Great pizza starts with a great crust, and Pitruco makes a great crust. Thin, crisp at first bite followed by a good chew, blistered around the edges, this crust would make a great meal topped with nothing but a drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkling of grated Locatelli. But the toppings are so much more imaginative than that: from wilted raddichio with a balsamic glaze; to soppresata with chunks of locally made mozzarella and Pitruco's signature, sweet-salty tomato sauce; to chick peas bathed in the runny yolk of a fried egg (sounds weird I know but the rich starch-on-starch combination really works). Great crust, great toppings, great pizza -- from a truck no less!
Birthday dinner on a Friday night.  Food was great--service was great!  Can't wait to go back.

The food is pretty good, not amazing nor inedible, but perfect when you need a pasta or pizza night. My roommates and I found them early in the year when we moved here and loved them for the quick delivery. However, the last three times they have delivered, they have been significantly late (over an hour from when they said they would arrive) OR have forgotten something with the order (side salad, pasta dish etc.) In short, we initially loved them because while their food was nothing special, their delivery was good. But since their delivery has gotten worse, I infrequently order from them now.

For lunch today, I ordered the FGT salad (fried green tomatoes, fresh burrata, basil oil).  Things started off fairly well.  The server brought over complimentary hush puppies and bowl of boiled peanuts.  I've never heard of boiled peanuts before, but I really enjoyed the snack. The salad was underwhelming.  The main problem was that the greens were not fresh (I believe it was arugula, but the coloring was off -- many pieces were heading into yellow territory -- and I tasted not a hint of pepper). I should have sent the salad back for fresher lettuce, but today was a working lunch with colleagues and I did not want to create any issues.  But really, I don't see how any restaurant could send out such pitiful looking lettuce.

Very excited to try a new place in the neighborhood, the décor and vibe was perfect for a Friday night dinner with friends. The food was phenomenal! One could complain about the portion size but mainly because it tasted so good and you wanted more, but on the bright side that left room for dessert. The funnel cake was amazing and even though I am generally not a cheesecake fan, I would highly recommend it and go back for it again

I visited the restaurant as a walk-in on a Wednesday night. Despite being open for less than a month, their marketing on food blogs, such as Eater, had really paid off--the restaurant was full and vibrant. After only a short 20 minute wait, my friend and I were seated. The wait staff was attentive, but more importantly, the food was delicious. My friend and I each had a soup appetizer and split the fried chicken for 2. The meat was juicy and the breading was delicious--I would definitely recommend! The additional side of honey we requested really topped off the meal. Despite being full, we went ahead and ordered dessert (I'm convinced there's a separate stomach for the dessert course). The cheesecake cobbler was delicious and warm--worth getting a little extra stuffed for! In the quiet, residential neighborhood of the UES, this place is truly a gem!

EXCELLENT! Food, decor, service and ambience are all top notch. My boyfriend and I had the pan roasted cod, prime smoked brisket, and side of crispy sweet potatoes. All dishes were perfectly cooked and beyond delicious. The portions appear to be on the smaller side but ended up being the perfect proportions. The service was also among the best I've ever experienced. In sum, I highly recommend The Writing Room, and I can't wait to go back to try the rest of the menu! Be sure to check out the back room, which has super stylish and cozy seating for a more intimate experience.

My husband and I were finally able to try the Writing Room last night and we really enjoyed it. They have a fun wine list that is unique and the vibe is great. The food was good, my fish was a little small (the cod) but we had the shrimp & grits app (yummy!) to start so that helped! My husband had the chicken, it was a much larger portion and was good. We'll be back again for sure!

Everything about this place is spectacular except the food. I ordered veal meat loaf that couldn't hold a candle to the meat loaf I get at the Greek coffee shop a few blocks up for half the price. The waitress advised me to order a side since the mashed sweet potatoes that came with it was more of a garnish. So I ordered hand cut potatoes that came drenched in salt. Ugh. My wife had the rotisserie chicken that was okay, but nothing more. The best things were the shrimp appetizer and the apple pie dessert. I doubt we'll be back.

I have had the pleasure of having good food and good service numerous times, but never has these experiences moved me to write a review, until NOW! I was visiting NYC on business and pleasure, with my husband. After a day of meetings, site seeing, and running around, I was starving. My husband suggested a place called The Writing Room. Apparently, the concierge at our hotel (near there) told him it had recently opened and suggested we dine there. Upon entrance, I was already in love! The decor was intimate, modern and welcoming and the staff was accommodating even though we didn't have a reservation. After being seated, we were greeted by our waiter Nicoye. This young man IS an INCOMPARABLE server. He made our experience magnificent. Not only was he pleasant and very helpful, but he was extremely knowledgeable about the menu. I wanted a glass of wine, but was unfamiliar with the wines listed by the glass. He asked me two questions about my preferences and was able to select the perfect wine for me. And in case I was unsure of his ability, he provided me with a blind tasting. He hit the nail right on the head. And after the day I had, I appreciated him being amazing at what he does! My husband also loved the bourbon he selected for him. The service he provided was personalized. It's as if we went to a tailor to get suited for the perfect dining experience. He was charismatic and articulate with the ability to captivate you with simple yet colorful descriptions of varying menu items. Needless to say, we ate everything he suggested. And the icing on the cake was the dessert selection. He selected a Cheesecake Cobbler that was by far the best dessert I had ever eaten. He made great pairings of food and drinks while we were there, but my husband and both believe the BEST pairing is with The Writing Room and Nicoye! Amazing food, outstanding service!! WE WILL BE BACK!!

My wife an I made reservations here to celebrate our 6 year anniversary.  We both have never been here before and I decided to take a shot in the dark to suprise her with a romantic dinner here. I requested to be seated in their back dining area that looks like a library with a fire place. After looking at the pictures I was sold on the romantic type atmosphere of this area of the restaurant. I was not disappointed one bit! My wife was extremely surprised and loved it. Our waiter Dan was awesome.  He was extremely knowledgeable about what was on the menu and made many good recommendations on what to get. He recommended a great champagne which we decided to get a bottle of and also recommended their special for the night which was pork belly. I decided to get the pork belly and my wife gor the Rotisserie chicken entrée.  The pork belly was heavenly and had this melt in your mout goodness.  My wife said she loved her entrée as well. We also had the ribs appetizer which was fall off the bone goodness. We topped it all off with the orange creamsicles for dessert.  Everything was wonderful! I would highly recommend this spot for the most excellent service if not anything else. Thank you for making this night special for the both of us. We will be back!

Heidi's House is as close to a home as a restaurant gets. Small, tight and cozy, you're sometimes asked to shift around in order to make room for more people. The food is American comfort food elevated. It's also very rich and greasy, so come hungry. I tried the crab dip with tortilla chips and triscuits - the dip is incredibly rich. The mac and cheese comes in a little claypot, which ensures maximum crispiness around the edges. It was quite yummy, but again, incredibly rich. There was a little puddle of chorizo-tinted oil sitting at the bottom of my empty claypot. I highly recommend the burger, though. It's served on an English muffin, which was great because it didn't detract from the juicy and tender meat. I really enjoyed the warm and friendly atmosphere here. Great little gem in the Upper East side.

Heidi's House is great traditional American. It's small and cozy, and the food is good quality. The appetizer was a sort of crab fondue with some nice blue corn chips and some triscuits (insert opinion here). I split a burger and an order of mac & cheese with chorizo. The burger was rather tall, adorned with the usual onion, lettuce tomato, and sat on an english muffin. It was quite juicy and the meat has a nice flavor to it. The macaronic and cheese had a nice pasta to cheese ratio and the spice of the chorizo made things interesting. I was especially fond of being served it in a skillet with some hardened cheese on the top and bottom.

In NYC on business and get so, so tired of the places catering to out-of-towners. Found this on Yelp.  What a delightful discovery.  Was well worth the cab ride up there. Being older than the rest of the clientele (okay, may have been as old as most of the diners' parents) will tell you what mattered to us: - creative food & atmosphere - quiet music We could engage in conversation without shouting. - wonderful service - immaculate from floor to tables to restroom We both commented that this reminded us of one of our favorite restaurants which happens to be in Rocheport MO called Abigail's. We had pasta of the day and the Vietnamese beef salad which were both excellent.  This is such a teeny tiny negative, but the side salad with the pasta had only greens and a light dressing (quite yummy).  I think a couple bites of fruit on it would have added a lot. Took a long time to get our food, but it didn't matter.  The atmosphere was soooo friendly.  We just enjoyed feeling like we were not in let-us-rip-you-off Manhattan. Big disappointment that the date bread pudding was not available.  Server even apologized (apologized!!) and gave us the chocolate souffle.  Gee, a cold glass of milk would have been good with that. We were concerned we might not get in after reading the reviews of it being so small.  It is, but should that happen, there are many restaurants in the neighborhood.  Worth the wait if you have the time, though.

Heidi's House is a cute little restaurant/bar owned and operated by Heidi herself. Its' homey feel puts you at ease--that is until the crowds start rolling in and it becomes PACKED. A tiny joint like this can't handle more than 50 people, that's for sure. The food is good though. I had the crab dip (amazing, very cheesy), the shrimp tacos (just OK-a bit bland) and the lobster mac-n-cheese (divine, although hyped up by fellow Yelpers) Prices are reasonable. Heidi's House is def worth checking out if you're in the area.

I like this place a lot. In the wasteland of mediocrity that is the Upper East Side, places like this stand out. The appetizers were great. The wine was good and cheap. They fucked up my steak really badly... overcooked all the taste out of it. But they gave me a $7 discount for it, and a coupon for a free dessert. Very friendly people. Will definitely go back. I wish they would fix the lighting tho. Its too bright to be romantic.

Mmmm Malai Koftha.  Had it here first, and it is the standard by which I have judged all others.  None have come close.   The food is amazing. The lamb vindaloo was also excellently.It had very nice flavors . I've tried the chicken tikka masala (pretty good),some vegetable dish (pretty good), naan (really good, Recommend the Chana Masala and Chicken Tikka Masala, though I'll definitely try other things on the menu next time I go. Goat curry is also very good. Mango lassi was also excellent.i definitely go back

I am such a fan of this place.  The food is excellent.  The service is amazing and the restaurant is very clean and elegant. The food is very tasty and I have tried many dishes.  I really enjoy the daily buffet.

Just a quick one 'cause I'm in a rush to get back there: Get the Haloumi.  Just get it. Make sure someone in your group orders the Bastilla. Lamb Cous Cous is good but not great. The Moroccan Iced Tea will take you to Taste Town, USA.  Err... Morocco. Mango Martinis are pricey but damn good! Definitely check it out.  The canopy-ed backyard is a blast too.

Cafe Mogador has a certain ambiance that makes you feel at home. The entire place is set-up in a sort of recreated indoor garden.  Strategic seating and nice simple places to get comfy while waiting for a table. The service was right there, slightly understated and never intrusive. Cafe Mogador specializes in Moroccan cuisine and two things were absolutely standout, the pita and the hummus.  I had the Bastilla for my entree. It was filo stuffed with chicken, eggs and almonds with Moroccan spices and side salad. Overall it was a lovely evening.   My one concern is that reservations are not accepted here.  It is quite difficult to dine at a restaurant with a group of people without a reservation.
Possibly the best breakfast in NYC... Beautifully presented food, delicious and surprisingly affordable... Go for the Middle Eastern or Halloumi eggs! Great staff and always super friendly....
Yummy! Always always yummy. You could sit by a bathroom here and it would be worth it. MMMMMMMMMM. Order everything.

Get to the Chase: Pros: 1) Having been lucky enough to have visited Morocco, dining at Cafe Mogador was hands down the closest experience I had to being transported to that beautiful country with deliciously flavorful cuisine 2) Chose this place only a week before 2014 New Year's Eve and managed to snag my family a pre-fixe NYE reservation for 5!
