Awesome! 3) Quality to price is fair - even for you hangries with big appetites; $60 per person plus 20% gratuity for appetizer, entree and dessert with complimentary rose 4) Staff was attentive and friendly despite the chaos of a full house and eager celebratory diners (even saw one group giving attitude saying that they'd just wait at the door until they were seated...hello it's NYE and you did not make a reservation and the hostess politely told them they had no room to accommodate...staff did not cause a ruckus and kindly asked them again to leave in order to make room for other patrons who were waiting outside in the cold) 5) Delicious mango martinis 6) Thank the middle-earth gods for their chocolate cake and flourless orange almond cake! I could eat either one every day for the rest of my life. 7) Not only are their desserts to die for, but shut your your mouth because I want moar of the lamb chop, mezze platter, and filet steak! Cons: 1) None!

Loved this place!!!  I love the atmosphere although I wish it were bigger because I'm assuming on a weekend it's probably impossible to get a seat.  I went for lunch last Friday and it was packed.  We did get a seat right away at the big table though and had a great experience.  The staff is super friendly.  We had a margherita pizza, which was delish and exactly how I like it.   But the real stars were the rotolo and the calzone.  To die for!  I think this place would be so much fun to bring some friends after work one night and have some wine or even an inexpensive casual date night with my hubby.  Can't wait to go back for that calzone!!  YUM!

Got the Crudo (prosciutto) but with a red sauce since Im not as wild about white pizza. It would have been the best pizza I have ever eaten except for the bottom of the pie crust which was very well done ... mostly black. At times I could taste burnt crust. Im not a fan of carcinogens in my food. That being said, the thinly sliced super tasty prosciutto and ricotta/mozerrella cheeses with a light and flavorful crust were DIVINE. Definitely not a place to dine in as its super small inside with only a few tables outside. Its a shame because they have wonderful beers on tap but I couldnt partake since I was getting take out. Only other thing was the price was a bit expensive. With tax it was about $20 for a small to medium sized pizza. Would eat here more often if it was a tad cheaper.

The pizza was amazing. Got the 4 cheese one and the prosciutto one. Both were amazing. My husband is a meat water and enjoyed the prosciutto one over my 4 cheese. The dough was doughy on the inside and crunchy on the outside (just right)!! My husband is all about the crust at pizza places and this was his favorite. The rotolo was melt in your mouth good. The drink we got was the "americano" which was made up of vermouth. We would not get it again but we both drank it all. Service was great and everyone we sat next to was super nice.

went to pizzeria vetri the other day.... 1. smart interior, large chalkboard with menu, but not much seating 2. loud hip hop/ rap music (very annoying imo) 3. very good service 5. AMAZING pizza (best in the city, beats out nomad by far) fresh as you can get ingredients.  The 800deg wood oven is their X-factor, try it, you'll know what i mean. TIP: they have a kitchen bar surrounding the wood oven, sit there and you can watch how they cook all the pizzas.  some what entertaining.

Pizza was delish and it's worth going just for that. I had a special (fig and gorgonzola square pizza) and the Crudo and both were fantastic. The Crudo was a bit small for the price, but whatever it tasted fantastic. The crust was an appropriate mix of doughy and crunchy, and the cheese and other ingredients were top-notch. Also the food came out super quick and we were seated quickly on a Tuesday night at 7pm. The service and seating, however, I was less-than-happy about. The place is small on the inside and seating is mostly family-style on long tables, save for some outdoor tables and counter/stool seating. If you have a group of 4 or more, the long tables might work. If you are just 2 and want some romance, maybe don't sit at the long tables. It was really hard to hear my bf bc we were rubbing elbows with strangers and it was loud in the space, plus the people we were sitting next to weren't interested in being social (but of course that may not happen to you), so it was awkward. With the long tables, it also made serving awkward because servers had to reach over you to place dishes and clear them. Our waitress seemed off her game, which I'm hoping is just due to opening recently. She messed up a couple of orders around us, but always gave a freebie from the menu to make up for it. I'll be back for the pizza, but if it's just me and my bf we'll probably request counter seating.

Every time Vetri adds a new restaurant, I have to visit it as soon as possible so I can say I've eaten at and enjoyed them all.  Pizzeria Vetri was no exception to the excellence that Marc Vetri brings to all of his establishments.  My friend and I went at 7 pm on a Tuesday and snagged the last two counter seats.  The view overlooks the "pizza kitchen" and gigantic oven we've heard so much about, and our mouths were quickly watering over the pizza being made right in front of us.   My friend and I split the Wood-Fired Salad minus the prosciutto and it was absolutely amazing.  The salad is served warm and the vegetables have a nice crisp, and in some cases, a slight char that made them almost carmelized, but definitely excellent.  We also split the Melanzana pizza.  The taste was very good, but by the time I got to my final slice the pizza was a bit soggy.  It may have been that I took too long to eat it than the stracciatella allows for, and thus it is entirely my fault.  I paired my dinner with the Brooklyn Pumpkin Ale, which went quite well with our choices.  The beer selection is great, both draft and bottles, and I had a hard time deciding.  Our server was knowledgeable about the selections when I sought his advice, as most Vetri fans have come to expect.

Thoroughly enjoyed my dining experience at pizzeria Vetri. Then staff is extremely welcoming and friendly, and very attentive to their tables. It's a small pizza joint, but I appreciate the layout organized the way it is. Came with a small group and we sat at the pizza bar lining the back walk, directly in front of all the action! The chefs are whipping up pies and sliding them into the beautiful wood and gas fired oven. All of the ingredients are fresh and sitting front row  to watch your pizza'a creation adds another level to your dining experience. We ordered a margarita, sausage, white pie, and prosciutto and arugula. The pizza crusts were crispy and the pies were full of flavor. The salads on the menu are also delicious and recommended. We tried the arugula and roasted veggie salad. Both were a hit amongst our group. The beer selection is also pretty solid. I will definitely be back!

Came here early on a Friday night; it was not too crowded.  If you sit inside, the tables are communal so you may be tight on elbow room.  There are also counters.  We ordered the melanzana pizza and the italian caesar salad. The pizza was soggy. When you lifted a slice off by the crust (as you normally would when eating pizza) all the toppings slide off.  It was disappointing.  The flavors were good; but the sogginess of the pie made me wonder how come this place has gotten such rave reviews.  I looked around and the other diners appeared to have non-soggy pizza.  They were actually holding the crust and biting into the pizza, whereas we were scooping our toppings off the plate.  So perhaps it is just this style of pizza that needs help.  I don't know.  I suspect that the pizza was made beforehand; dough rolled out too thin.  The soggy part of the pizza was also cold.  I'm definitely not coming back and actually would have given this place 1 star, but the waiter was nice and when we mentioned they could improve their soggy pizza they offered us a complimentary soft serve.  That was delicious, but not enough to change my mind about coming back for the pizza.  Also, there were egg shells in our salad.  So overall I question the quality of the food here.

As someone who thought that the pizza at Osteria was among the best in town, I was expecting a lot more of this place. The menu options are fairly limited, and the atmosphere is kind of weird. It feels like you're in a pizza-by-the-slice place designed by Starbucks and Stephen Starr. Honestly, it seems like Vetri is stretching himself a little too thin with this latest offering.

Decidedly underwhelming, but still good. Here are the facts: 1. Communal seating only. 2. Two kinds of wine: "house" red and white. Outrageously priced at $8.50/glass. 3. If you're not into meat on your pizza, you don't have that many veggie options. It's Margherita, or eggplant, or lots of cheese. There ain't nothin' green round these parts. 4. If you like meat on your pie, there's no pepperoni, or soppresata. Sausage or prosciutto only. Flavors are standard. Quality cheese, sauce and crust. Service is fine. I wouldn't rush back...from Vetri, I expected better.
Pizza and wings are their specialty

I experienced the same "grit" in the falafel. It made the pita sandwich very unpleasant. I'm not sure what the source is--maybe unwashed, sandy parsley in the falafel batter?  Whatever it is, I really hope they read these two reviews and fix it soon (instantly would upgrade the place to 3-4 stars). If they get it right, this certainly has the potential to become a regular lunch stop for me. I really enjoyed the baguette sandwiches that they used to have at the restaurant. It'd be great if they brought that to the truck as well.

Wow... what can i say, this is perhaps one of the best food deals in the city.  And to be located right in the midst of the Universities among college students?  Such great value is almost unheard of. Located right where Locust Walk ends at 40th street, the bright yellow Marrakesh Express truck is easy to spot.  Brahim the owner is there whenever the window is open, and he is as friendly and happy as his food is delicious. The Beef & Lamb as well as the Falafel are easily my two favorite options, although i have never had a bad meal there.  The Chicken and the Fish are both well done, too.  There is even a "Philly Cheesteak" style of shawarma... and while many restaurants in the city offer such a choice simply as a nod to local culture, it's a really valid option here!  (His seasoned, shredded beef as a base makes it excellent like all the others) If you do nothing else, stop by at least for the Mint Tea whenever you're passing that area.  I have never had it made as well as Brahim's, even when traveling through the Middle East.  (Although now i suspect i will have to visit Morocco to be sure!) I like to walk with my food, so I don't often order the "platter" option... but you won't be sad if you choose to.  The fries are always crisp and seasoned in a way you're not likely to find anywhere else. I'm still working my way through the side dishes... the stuffed grape leaves were terrific and I'm eager to try the hummus.  In truth, you can sample everything on the menu in about a week's time and not break the bank... the prices are all just so outstanding, even while the portions are big and filling! (Also, you can always call or text Brahim once he knows who you are in order to have your order prepared and waiting when you arrive!  Since all food is made fresh to order, the sandwiches take about 10 to 15 minutes to cook... this option of calling ahead is wonderful and is just one more reason to choose Marrakesh Express whenever you're in University City!)
Very good sushi.  Good value and great service.

I read about Ward III in this amazing article in New York Times, and this place was on my mind for a very long time, and the reason behind it was: BESPOKE COCKTAILS. A story of three extraordinary men putting together an innovative concept of custom drinks came to life, and I was honored to experience it. High ceilings and dark walls with heavy velvet drapes look somewhat gothic. Music (a cool retro  mix) is playing super loud. The bar seats are always full, since everyone wants to witness the "bespoke" creations with their own eyes. So we sit in the lounge. On the menu, you choose the flavor, texture, fruit and spice, and your own concoction arrives in a wine glass (I wish that part was changed, as i would prefer mine to be served in a stemless martini glass). The loudness of music was beyond any human ear...It's a lounge,people need to talk, not scream at each other. So, the "bespoke" part was immaculate, however, the service was "mass produced" and far from custom. Let me just replay my bespoke experience, never mind the rest.

A relaxed atmosphere greeted us and made us feel right at home.  The bartender was easy going and knowledgeable.  Plenty of cocktails and beers on tap.  Plenty of elbow room.  No posers.  My one complaint was the $20 pour of bourbon.  That really took me by surprise.

I was searching for one thing, and one thing only in Tribeca; Bacon Wrapped Dates.  I typed my request into the search bar above - and da - da - da - Ward III! I work in this neighborhood from time to time, and needed a way to relax after a rather stressful day.  This place was perfect.  Their hand crafted drinks were delish, and the bartenders mixology talents were quite entertaining!  I went with the Pimm's Cup in honor of the Royal Wedding. We toasted them in style! Onto the dates.  Wow, were they amazing!  First - they are HUGE.  I'm used to the little dates, three to a toothpick, but these buddies barely fit one. The dates are wrapped in thick bacon (twice around) and stuffed with a mix of a few cheeses with a surprise crunch in the middle - a smoked almond! It took all my restraint to not say, "Bring me another round ... of dates!"  I'll be back for sure.  They rival some of the best I've had, and I love my bacon wrapped dates.
Love the salads. The sandwiches are good, especially the windy city. They could use a little more oomph in flavoring though. Overall, a wonderful addition to the neighborhood and great service.
Nice, homey hometown place.  Bread pudding rocks, salads are awesome

First.... the good. Great corner location,outdoor seating,ample parking,clean colorful decor. Good menu covering most of the traditional Jamaican favorites and priced correctly for the portions and area. The oxtail stew i ordered was excellent if a bit too sweet, Tails are difficult to cook properly and tend to get oily or greasy unless prepared and stewed by an expert and this chef really  knows his stuff. Rich,complex with the right amount of chew,you can taste the subtle hints of caramel from the browning and thyme,all spice and bay. I really enjoyed sucking on the bones. The rice ,stewed cabbage was also very good but the fried plantains were rather dry and lacked flavor,  the corn bread I just don't get...a bammie,some boiled cassava or breadfruit would have been far more welcomed to sop up that amazing ox tail gravy. The beef patty was one of the best I've had in many years,with a nice mild bite but be careful as the spicy filling is like molten lead when it comes to the table. Sodas both local and Jamaican is available. Now ....the Bad. The Achilles heel of this family run restaurant is the extraordinarily long waits to place an order and get served. I visited earlier in the week,sat outside and waited...and waited until I decided it was not worth it and left.. On a Sunny Saturday I arrived at 2.15pm and sat inside and it still took 15 minutes before I could order after the lone young lady who not only sat and gave me the menu finally asked if I had ordered...... Who from My Dear... you? "No I haven't ordered"...she was clearly overwhelmed taking all the orders from both inside and out while manning the register,phones and seemed unfamiliar with the menu and pricing. All the while all I hear is the chef repeating "coming right up" from the open kitchen.."Coming right up" as the filled restaurant waited patiently.He even made a hurried pass through the dining room to personally apologize to each table. After awhile it appeared the chef spent almost as much time apologizing as he did cooking "It's a small family business" was uttered time and again. But that's just it.... judging from the takeout orders and the filled tables this is no longer  just a small family business....word has got out how good the food is and they're woefully unprepared, understaffed ,untrained and overwhelmed both in the kitchen and on the floor for the kind of volume that they now enjoy. Both my patty and oxtails came to the table at 3.10. and there were some parties still not served who were seated before me. Patrons are kind and forgiving and most wait  {having grown up in the Caribbean I too am very used to the concept of " Island time" but there were at least 2 tables who up and left before ordering}  because the menu is great and the Chef/owner is hard working,talented and apologetic..... but that's not going to fly for too much longer and I for one would hate Morgan's Island Grill to fall victim to it's own success.
I ordered the BBQ jerk chicken. It was a huge portion and very tasty. Friend ordered the ribs, huge portion as well . I would definitely return. Friendly owner.

So. Delicious.  I had the BBQ jerk chicken and it was the best I've had.  And the corn bread!  Just good. Everything was so good. Even the cabbage and plantains. My friends usually hate plantains but they loved these.   But the best part was the ambience. This is a small business with a friendly, casual atmosphere.  There's no pretentious airs. The owner and chef is friendly and has a super warm personality.
Had the jerk ribs and chicken... great flavors and portions. . will definitely be back...

Went for dinner when they first opened.  The food and service were very good, but we were the only customers in the restaurant for most of our meal.  We went back on July 3rd.  We were again the only customers when we first got there, but the restaurant quickly got busier.  The staff was extremely  disorganized and unable to handle multiple tables at once.  The first visit, we were given pappadum and chutneys while we waited for our order.  The second trip, a large tray of pappadum sat on the unused buffet table and was never given to any customers.  People were seated, but did not get menus for 10+ minutes at some tables.  Another 20 minutes were spent by some customers waiting for staff to take orders.  When some tables started to get their food, some got one person's meal while others at the table just sat there waiting for their food.   Waiters kept walking past tables, saying they would be right back, but never came back.  The two stars is because the food tastes good, although asking for medium spice level was either ignored or their medium is very mild.  I am a very patient person.  My sister, not so much.  Even I got very annoyed when they took my credit card for payment and did not return with it for 20 minutes.  Getting our leftovers packed up took even longer (we would have done it ourselves if they brought out containers, but they took the plates back with them despite the request for containers.)  Good food does not make up for terrible service, so we will not be back.  This is a shame for me since I do not drive, and Krishna is on a very convenient bus route.  We will just have to stick with Montclair for our Indian food cravings :(

I came here on opening day, and though the food was great, the service was not.  I expressed my displeasure, and to their credit, the owners reached out to me and apologized and expressed a seemingly legitimate desire to keep me as a customer.  That goes a long way for me, so I decided to give Krishna another chance.  I've since been back for the buffet.  There was a nice variety of dishes available, and all of it was tasty.  The servers were much more attentive and friendly this time around.  I am still curious to see how long the wait is at dinner time, but I will definitely be back (and hopefully back again).
I had a great service here and enjoyed the food. It was a great experience coming here, its very open and fancy!

Was at Ocean Prime last night for restaurant week and can't say enougn about it.  The food was absolutely delicious.  We began with lobster bisque then crab cakes on a bed of corn,  These were not tiny portions as we all had doggie bags.  Also there specialty drink was a blackberry mule.  Also delicious.  Our server was Mike - very attentive.  Would I come back hell yeah !!!!!!  Oh I forgot the ten layer carrot cake - can't say enough about that either   Pat M

Amazing!! I went with a friend for restaurant week and since I was running late they were able to push our reservation back 30 minutes with out a problem. We sat at the bar until our table was ready and the bartender helped my friend choose a glass of wine and made me a wonderful dirty martini with blue cheese olives I love so much. Though the hostesses had some trouble finding us for our table and we ended up sitting 20 minutes late, they were very apologetic and we were fine, just hungry. Our waiter, Steve, was fantastic as well. He got us another round, and extra olives for me, and even sent out a complimentary appetizer of their tuna tartar (I think to make up for waiting for the table) which was incredibly tasty and I devoured most of it. We each got the lobster bisque which was poured table-side, who doesn't love that? She got the scallops with Parmesan risotto while I got the crab cakes with succotash and we split an order of the Parmesan truffle fries. We were so full from the appetizer, soups, bread, and drinks that we barely touched our food. Steven was find enough to wrap up everything, including the carrot cake for dessert, to go and split the fries between the 2 of us. Though we sat late, we were never rushed out and there were still plenty of tables sitting when we left. The meal was just as tasty the next day as leftovers and I would go back in a heart beat. Ask for Steve!

The bartenders are so fun and make a great drink. Went here for restaurant week and really enjoyed my meal. Our table was in a side room though and I would of enjoyed being In the main dining area more. Also, busers could be a bit more attentive in removing unused glasses and plates to create space. Had I not liked my food and cocktails so much, this rating would of been a 4.

My friend and I were so excited about the happy hour menu that we were dying to go. The happy hour hours were posted online but did not include the days. Many restaurants in the city have weekend happy hours so we called to confirm the days. The person who answered the phone, the hostess I presume, confirmed that the happy hour menu was available on Saturday. When we arrived at the bar, there was no happy hour. We told the bar tender what was told to us over the phone earlier and she said that person was wrong. Ok fine, people make mistakes. We ordered some wine and when the bill came, we were overcharged. I politely confronted the bar tender and she said that the bill was correct, even though I tripled checked the menu and she definitely overcharged us. I am not impressed with the service but will give it another chance because I really want to try the food. The decor was beautiful and the menu looks good. Service could definitely use some work.

Just came here for lunch after I voted today, and was greeted by the greatest restaurant staff member Jeanne! Someone who undoubtedly deserves a 30% tip whether you get 1 beer or 50. She mentioned a new addition to their menu, a country fried steak served with mashed potatoes and sautéed garlic broccoli. When I say I wanted to lick the plate, I actually did. Best pub in the city of New Haven!!

This place is like the Asian equivalent of the classic NJ diner -- you know, the one where the menu has 600 things on it, so you have no idea what the specialties are, and could probably have a 1- to 5-star meal depending on what you ordered. The decor is a little classier than the standard NJ diner, though -- it's sleek inside, though our booth was the one that was engineered to add a bit more seating in a space that should've probably been left empty -- the booth benches were just a few inches too close to the table, which made for a slightly awkward eating experience. Also, the place is dark, and the menu font is small. I had to light up the menu with my cell phone flashlight so my poor mom could read it. We were seated quickly on a Thursday evening. There seemed to be three servers for a lot of diners, and they seemed harried. A few diners at other tables had that impatient, hungry look, so that's always worrisome. There was a sign outside looking for a part-time server, so at least it seems like they're trying to fix it. Our server, when she did stop by, was super friendly. We ordered quite diverse things. For appetizers, scallion pancake (small portion, not scalliony enough); roasted duck salad (quite good with big chunks of fried duck, reasonable spice level, though the toothpick-sized pieces of ginger were a bit of a surprise when you expected them to be mango and they were actually ginger); tempura green beans (tasty). For entrees, two noodle dishes were serviceable. My eel roll portion was quite large, but it was over-sweet and not that balanced -- I also had an order of tamago, which was really disappointing. The rice was dry and bland, the egg was dry, the balance was off (too much egg, not enough rice). The sauce and everything else in the rolls clearly masks the quality of the rice, but it was sadly obvious in the sushi. The massaman curry had a decent flavor to the curry, but all the wrong veggies (onions, red and green peppers, baby corn, taro chips); the brown rice on the side was just okay. I also watched my sushi sit on the counter for about 15 minutes while the rest of the hot food was being prepared, so they need to work on communication between kitchen and sushi bar if the same table orders some items from each. Or at least hide the waiting sushi so that I don't have to know that it sat there, lonely and sad on a counter. Oh well -- it was worth a try, and if you're more a quantity and novelty vs quality person when it comes to sushi, you'll probably do okay here.

Great sushi place that my co-workers and I end up ordering from all the time. It is our favorite, albeit I think the only one that delivers to downtown Trenton. The lunch special is great-$8 for 2 rolls and a soup or salad.
Amazing food, really fresh and healthy. Great selection of vegetarian stuff like black bean & sweet potato burger-like-things. And delicious veggies! Plus, great service. This place wins.

Finally came here for dinner with my mum on a cold, rainy, Saturday night. I called 15 minutes in advance and asked if there were any seats available - they told me to get there as soon as I could because they cold only hold the seats for 20 minutes. So we made it in time. Mum got the wild salmon burger - and she loved it. This meant that it had to be good because my mum's a somewhat picky eater. I got the eggplant veggie & tofu lasagna - and it was SO good. Like I'm craving it right now so good - and it's really filling for a vegetarian/vegan dish. The best part was that I didn't need to fall into a food coma afterwards - I felt ready for a yoga class (and I ended up doing a bit at home). We also got the red beets, orange & kale salad with the optional goat cheese. I hadn't realized that my mum disliked goat cheese, so I ended up eating all of it - which made almost every bite of salad I had seem a bit too sour or too tangy. If I hadn't eaten all that goat cheese, I may have enjoyed the salad more (my mum certainly liked it) - but I did have all of it, and my taste buds were very mad at me whilst eating the salad. Overall, I'd definitely come back - it was a cute place and that lasagna was the perfect meal for a cold and rainy day. (Or just any day, really.)

Came here with a group of friends on a recommendation and we were told to leave because we hadn't ordered enough. We were happy to change our orders so we could stay but we were practically kicked out before we had the chance. Pretty negative treatment for a place that supposedly preaches positivity. I understand that some establishments need to enforce a minimum spend, but if that is the case, politely explaining this to customers should be the first step - not accusing them of purposely taking up a good table and wasting everyone's time, which is not at all what we had intended! In the end we changed our orders, spent about $5 more per person, but were left with a bad taste in our mouths. Worth it? The food was fine but we won't be back after that treatment.
Ah-mazing!!! The Frisco omelet was to die for! My friend spared a bite of her breakfast burrito for me to try, de-lish!!! One of the best breakfasts of my life!

My boyfriend and I were vacationing in VT and were eager to find a yummy breakfast spot as the breakfast at our hotel was not so hot. Found this place and am SO glad! The place is small so I can see how on busy days, it can be hard to get a seat, but luckily we were able to grab a window two-seater and had a great breakfast! I got huevos rancheros and they were DELICIOUS! I was so impressed with the flavor. The boyfriend got a breakfast burrito and it was bigger than his head! He accepted the challenge and loved it as well. We definitely plan to return when we go back to Vt for another vacation!

Old and dated. If you're under 60, stay the hell away. What a dump. Didn't try the food because the senior citizen line dancing started. Since Frank the manager contacted me and was interested in making improvements so that I would have a better visit, I am adding a second star just for that effort.

Honestly, with a name like "Whiskey Cafe", I had high hopes. They had a very small whiskey selection (the waitress didn't even know what they were), the food was not impressive at all, and they only offer bottled beers (more than half they were out of). The person that left the comment about the guy from Bar Rescue couldn't have been more dead on! This place needs an upgrade ASAP! The only thing good about this place was that they offered "Paint Nite" where an artist comes in & helps you paint & you can drink while doing so (this was soooo much fun!) I wouldn't go back again though.

The food is always great - love everything about this place.  Wish he wouldn't run out of Italian bread so quickly, as it is so good!  Hey Joe how about opening up a bakery?  We need bread, rolls, jelly donuts and pies!

good; very authentic Italian food.   This was not fancy or pretentious in any way, just extremely good food, superior service and delightful ambience. My only criticism was that it was rather noisy, but this was Saturday
The croissant hot from the oven, almond, chocolate...  Heaven!!!!!!!!!!!!
Food is good but received unfriendly response from the attendant. May be she is not in Christmas mood. Do not suggest for new peole

This was my first visit to Oak Haven since they opened.  I had previously been to the location when it was "Press."   I attended my first ever Yelp Elite event here on a Monday night and we had the whole place for our event, which was so nice.  I like the feel of the place...cozy, warm and inviting.  The staff were also wonderful--polite, attentive and available. It is an upscale bar/restaurant that has a few small tables when you walk in, a bar area with a few high top tables and a nice sized back room for larger groups.  There is also a small outdoor area for dining in the warmer weather. I tried some of their signature items and everything was delish...flatbread with onions/cheese/apples, endive spears, crostini (marinated sliced steak w/rye whiskey shallot marmalade), crab cakes, pork dumplings and an eggplant arancini with spinach.  I couldn't do justice to the food in my description...it is way better detailed on their menu, which appears to change depending on the season.   It is rare to find a restaurant that is pure quality ingredients--local and fresh.  Thumbs up in my opinion!

The plates look small but the food is really rich and filling. Also very tasty. Also, they had a creme brulee stout. And duck. And bacon. And our server was really friendly. We plan on going again soon. =)

Awesome restaurant! Great service. Staff is friendly and the food is consistent. The menu is exciting and love the selection of rotating whiskies. Was in the mood for a spicy drink and the spicy twist to an Old Fashioned blew me away. Highly recommend an old fashioned with habanero juice. The roasted duck...one of the best dishes, too. Fav spot in New Haven.

We have tried oak haven 4 times now. The first time, right after they opened, was wonderful -- great food and atmosphere. Ever since the food has been bad (weird and superfluous seasonings on everything!! Let the Brussels taste like brussels, people!!) The scallops are good, but served on weird undercooked vegetables. Almost everything we have had has been average and has had a bizarre twist on it. The atmosphere is poor, unless you are going specifically to sit at the bar and chat with the bartender who talks and tells jokes loudly the entire evening. The waitstaff are always good, but that's not enough for us to come back.

I tried Oak Haven when a friend brought me there for some drinks and brunch.  I'm not a huge brunch fan, but I will admit I was impressed.  Portion sizes were good, my omelet came with a side salad.  There is pancake, omelet, french toast of the day.  The server explained it's because of fresh ingredients and availability.  I ordered sausage hash, tasted like my grandmothers, which was an amazing nostalgic feeling for me.  I ordered several bloody marys, perhaps too many.  Neighborhood spots like this one are good because you can walk home after.  The fig bread was delicious and the butter spread that they brought over is not your typical butter.  I would like to check this out again, I'm only in town for another week so I have to make it over at least one more time to try their dinner.

Great addition to the Upper State Street dining scene. Space is cozy and modern and the service was great. The food comes across as high-end comfort food tapas. Much of it locally sourced. Standouts included the mini burgers, pretzel nubs, and a fantastic pork belly. Portions are very generous and it's a good value for the money. Will definitely return.

This review is for brunch only because I've been here for dinner and it's much better. We came here for brunch for the first time today and expected to wait awhile for a table for 4 because we knew how popular it was. We were told the wait would be between 15 and 40 minutes. The first 20-30 minutes went by quickly and they started to call people who got there when we did. After 50 minutes they started to call people who had gotten there after us. The host kept saying that we were soon and then they took 3 parties of 3 and we were still waiting. After an hour and 10 minutes we heard the host say he would hold a table for a party of 8 until the rest of them arrived, but no longer than 5 minutes. So I was pissed because usually this place doesn't do that. After another 7 minutes he seated them even though the whole party wasn't there. I asked him how much longer for a table and he said you're next. He comes back out and says party of 4 at the bar. Seriously?! After an hour and 20 minutes?! At the bar?! So we go in and are hoping that the food will be so delicious that it'll make it worth the wait...wrong again. Disco tots were mushy, cranberry captain crunch French toast wasn't fully cooked inside, chicken and waffles were poorly seasoned, just spice, not flavor. Four mediocre entrees and two sub par appetizers came to $103. Definitely not worth the wait, step up your game!

I've been here for several brunches and dinners. Great at all times! The staff is friendly and while the space is TIGHT the food is worth the squeeze. There is typically a wait for the brunch but the the guy outside is funny and tries to keep the people entertained. I haven't ever waited for dinner so maybe thats a better time to come. Be ready to eat as this is not the place for nibbling on your food but all out feasting.

I'm so disappointed and confused on how this place got perfect ratings. I wanted to like it so bad. I was so excited for my food and waited so long. I loved the staff, atmosphere, and music. But then the food came and it was such a let down. For bunch, one of the benedicts was just swimming in sauce and the Egg McRuffin was just a ton of cheese melted onto an english muffin with a runny egg. The presentation was awful and I swear I can cook something at home that tastes better. This place needs to rethink it's food. It doesn't have to be so gimmicky! Just have good food next time.

Came here randomly and it was delightful. The atmosphere is very laid back! They use an old record player which was really cool and played old time films. They don't offer alcohol however you can BYOB. I had the strawberry lemonade which was delicious and my friends ordered the fruit green tea and a regular sweet tea. I got the chicken and waffles which had a Tabasco glaze. It was very flavorful and for me a little too spicy, my friends got the "down by law" and the "lil dizzy. Out of everything we thought the lil dizzy was the best! We wish we had room for dessert!

I had been attempting to have brunch at Queens Comfort for about a year now...no joke. If the pressing decision of where to brunch were only up to me, I would have waited for a table on our first attempt. Usually everyone in my group are opposed to waiting 30-45 minutes for a seat..so down 30th ave we would go. This time, I took my parents with me and my moms a sucker for BYOB. The wait was maybe 35 minutes? The "Host" (or the man standing in front calling out names) was super friendly and entertaining. The place is SUPER small and all of the seats are right up next to one another. I like the BYOB aspect, but I think that they could accommodate this a little better. After waiting outside in the heat for 40 minutes, my dads beer and moms champagne were both warm- my father was curious if they could provide some sort of ice bucket, but they said they didn't do that (I can understand why not, there is hardly any room for the servers to get to and from tables...thirty ice buckets alongside the tables wouldn't help). The menu was different and I had a hard time deciding what to order. We ended up trying the disco tots which were AMAZING. I usually don't like tater tots, but this may be the only exception. I went with one of their variations of eggs benedict, but I cant remember the name. It was accompanied by a slice of bacon that was PECAN CRUSTED! It was great. I knew when ordering my dish, that I was taking a chance because of the spicy honey? that was included and I should have asked for it without it, because it didn't do anything for me. Aside from the honey, the food and atmosphere was great. Will be updating my review when I finally get try dinner here.....hopefully not in another year.
Good food, a little more than you want to put up, long wait.  But good employees and BYOB make it worth the try.

Awesome find :) extremely friendly service, our waiter was very enthusiastic and just seemed happy to be there. We thought it was so sweet when he told us the dessert we ordered was the chef's mother's recipe. Love the decor and the music was awesome, the owner was playing DJ and playing records (Crimson and Clover was playing when we went in, also caught some Zombies and the Doors), but it was a bit too loud. We could barely hear our server and vice versa, and it was difficult to carry on our conversation. For food, we shared a few apps for our meal. The cap'n crunch chicken fingers, atomic balls, and the bbq pork croquettes. Everything was great, but missing salt. The chicken fingers were a bit too sweet, as was the dipping sauce. The ratio was just a hair off. We got the smores icebox for dessert, MUST TRY. It doesn't look like anything special but he chocolate was fudgy and perfect and it was just amazing. Get it. Get seven of them.I can't wait to go back! Ps- cash only, BYOB!

Great brunch place! Good  food good atmosphere and the waiters are super friendly......either experience start from the moment you walk up and put you name on the list......the funny black guy is to cool and he gives you that welcome home feeling then once you do get inside they have theses old school toys all over the place that makes me feel like s kid again and comfy then the menu is different from any other place I been to they have the lots of tote that I knew I should t be eating but it looked sooooo good! Then they had fried sassage ball puff they I had to try lol and to top it off above all the place is byob!! I loved it! Can't wait to go back....place is small tho....and on the cramped side so I sat at the bar lol I'm a big dude but I would go back for sure

Went last night at the insistence of friends who live in East Falls and have eaten here a few times.  Got there around 9:15, outside tables were empty but inside was still bustling, most tables were full but wrapping up.  They have had rave reviews of the restaurant in the short time it's been open, and have been insisting that I come out to try it...I live in South Philadelphia, and am surrounded but amazing Italian places, but Franco seems to be a bit of a legend in these parts, so I thought I'd give it a try. We shared the grilled calamari - excellent!  So delish, with chopped tomatoes & arugula, lightly dressed.  Awesome.   We also shared a greek-inspired chopped romaine salad - olives capers red onion feta green peppers and halved tomatoes - good, but nothing special.  I could make this salad at home.  Tasty but next time I'll choose something else. I had the rigatoni with pancetta - AWESOME!  Savory and satisfying, with bite-sized slivers of tasty pancetta mixed in to the delicious red sauce.  The pasta was cooked to perfection... and there was just enough to take home for leftovers. My friend had the tilapia, which was questionable at best.  It was served with a side of green veg & carrots, and roasted potato half.  As she dug into her fish, her face scowled and she immediately commented that the filet tasted "like chemicals".  I was a bit shocked, and after tasting a small sliver myself, it did indeed taste a bit "off"...not spolied, but just not good at all, definitely a chemical/chlorinated-type of taste to it.  Definitely not something one would want to ingest AT ALL.  She mentioned it to our waiter, who promptly removed it from the table (and from our bill!), and a few minutes Franco came out to get her first-hand commentary.  He immediately apologized, thanked her for her valuable feedback, and said he would look into it (and the supplier) right away.   We decided to pass on dessert, but were served complimentary glasses of house made Limoncello for the fish flub. All in all, I think this place has a few growing pains to sort out, but it was a decent meal.  It seems like the starters and the pasta dishes are the way to go if you're going to try it out for the first time.  I would definitely try it again.
Average food, too expensive for the quality if the food. Doubt I will be coming back anytime soon.  Well priced wine

I first went to Mediterra last winter on a Tuesday night and ordered a squid ink pasta that was to die for.  If I had reviewed it then, I would have given it 5 stars.  I was highly anticipating my return and have been back several times since, but it seems as if that one trip was a fluke.  The food in general is fine.  Nothing special and most certainly overpriced.  The ambience is very much dependent on your seating.  Some seats are nice and private, while others aren't as special.   Overall, I wouldn't say this is a must see place, but if you are looking for a nice relaxing dinner and don't mind the price, this is an alright place to go.
Super expensive, small portions, and the pasta isn't even made in-house (I've asked). The steak is great, though!!! My favorite dish here by FAR.

I was very disappointed to see the quality of their croissant . It is the worse I ever eaten.The plain one has no taste or  color, the almond one, tasted stale. They claimed its fresh. The cappuccino is nice.

Over priced, food sounds interesting but not impressive at all. The rabbit dish had fat strings that were stuck in my tooth and had to be pulled out by hands (not pleasant during a meal!). House rolls were basically per-made rolls that were warmed up in the oven, nothing special. The house cured ham was not bad, but wouldn't come here again.

Incredible Perfect Service again. 3 Wins and it's a rave review. I live for their atmosphere and the seasonal menu. The rabbit is exquisite. The steak; divine! All of the starters are incredible, even the 5 dollar bread - we couldn't be happier. The price, you get what you pay for. Ambitious ingredients, and the most attentive staff in Vermont is worth every penny especially if you want to impress an out-of-towner. When I say the best service team in Vermont: I mean it.

One of the best meals I've had in a while. The space is beautiful, warm and inviting.  The service was mostly impeccable. The menu was exciting with plenty of great food and drink options. The menu is printed daily. On the evening we went we had an array of small plates. The dishes were all super fresh and delicious, all with local farm to table ingredients.  I think I could eat their grilled octopus every day. It was a busy night and the kitchen fell way behind, otherwise it was a perfect meal.

Daring small plates, impeccable service, and a perfectly styled dining room all earn Hen of the Wood's second location the title of a destination restaurant. Animal heads hang among artisanal light bulbs and endless slate and wood accents leading to an exposed kitchen with an open spit, a roaring grill, and a whole staging area to watch food get prepped for lucky diners. I am aware of the accolades heaped upon Hen's first location but, honestly, I was not expecting a 5-star experience when I came to this relatively new Burlington outpost. Well, I was wrong: A toast with hen of the woods mushrooms sauteed in butter and then topped with a shatteringly crisp rasher of bacon and a yolky egg. Nuts. These amazingly airy fried sticks of a polenta and potato mixture served with aioli. Nuts. Chicken roulades served with a blueberry reduction, fried green tomatoes, (!) and rich, creamed corn.  Nuts. Smoked fish pate with house made crackers. Nuts. A wildly decadent chocolate budino with peppermint granita and cookie crumble. Nuts. I also want to shout out to our waiter who was BY FAR the chillest waiter my girlfriend and I have had in years. So yeah, pretty much every course was absurd and the open kitchen was just absolutely awesome to watch. Our favorite thing by far were the chicken roulades with blueberry/corn/fried tomatoes. It was unfortunately a special, but that dish should be on the menu every night. Or in my stomach every night. Both.
Everything, and I mean everything, was excellent. Our waiter was a little weird but the food was amazing. It is very cold though so bring a jacket.

I don't know what took me so long to come here but I finally found the perfect occasion - the boyfriends birthed (woohoo!) I made a reservation for a Friday night and found parking right away, we entered and we were greeted quickly and politely and got to sit right away which was perfect. I loved the decor, exposed brick walls, small photos on the walls, jazz music, rustic 20's feeling and I really liked the fire place, they even had an outdoor seating area. Theres also a bar area that almost looked full which was nice. I could def.see this as a nice couples and date night. Our waiter was awesome he was polite, outgoing and very chill. He let us know the specials and what was really good to try and I liked that cause you know how anal I am when it comes to my service. The menu was basic but everything sounded so good from the chicken to steak and seafood they also offer daily specials. Our choice in menu we went with : - bottle of red wine (Cabernet Sauvignon which was excellent) nice little toast! - mussels which I loved how they came out so properly arraigned and sized on the plate it just wasn't like poured onto the bowl like usual. That was fancy! = salad with walnuts, craisens, pears, blue cheese crumble, and fruits which was fresh and a good start before entrees. - filet mignon with mashed potatoes and steamed veggies, the steak was nice and proportion and cooked just the way I like it which is seeing the pink inside ! - chicken breast which came with mango and avocado (LOVE LOVE) - side of asparagus - fruit fondue platter which is the only picture I added it was great, once again something different new and enjoyable and its great to share with others I just didn't get any marshmallows. Prices are reasonable.   I just loved how the menu mixed fruits with regular everyday veggies its just delicious and I'm a fruit fanatic but you don't find many places that combine the two much and that will stick with me as a good thing. You can also check the menu out online which the site it well done and helpful and plus I love hearing the music on it too! Towards the end of the night the owner Sam J. came over and introduced himself and it was a pleasure to meet a YELP friend also, he was very polite, professional and asked how our night was and even wished the bf a happy birthday! He complimented us with after dessert drink and CHEERS to you Sam J that was very nice of you and you have yourself a great place. I for sure will be back I wanna try the sangria which looked great and mojitos. I wanna bring some friends and family to come and try a new blend of a restaurant in the neighborhood and I hope this place sticks around!
Fabulous food & excellent service. This was our 2nd time, being a picky eater that's saying something!!! Highly recommended, I tell everyone how great it is!

This was such an amazing surprise as I got off the bolt bus and was starving.  There were at least 20 different options of amazing food.  I went with the salami panini from the salami specialty place although can't remember the name.  They had house salami and beer salami. They will let you try both to see which you like more. They grill the panini and have some specialty spreads such as an olive tapenade caramelized onions and pesto sauce. There were the arincini brothers selling rice balls which I've had in the past and are to die for. The artisanal cannolis were there and almost completely sold out. Tons of local beer options. Sliders, pulled pork, brisket, and so much more definitely check it out

So cute! Plenty if beer and bites. Perfect small outdoor area. Sigmund pretzels ($4) yummm garlic and parsley pretzel was Sooo soft and delicious. Needed just a bit of salt. Soul lee Korean had awesome $3 beef taco. Packed with flavor even though the soft taco shell sort of fell apart. There was a slider stand that was a bit pricey ($6 a slider)- bland. The original slider was okay, a bit dry though (not worth the price). Chicken and waffles slider was bland and dry.

A fun idea in a nightmare part of town.  Lots of tourists around here and finally some good food. Great vendors, some seating and booze!  The negatives are the price (on the expensive side) and the crowds.  Great foodie fun!

If you're craving the whole outdoor food festival thing but missed your chance at Madison Square Eats, head over to Broadway Bites for a November encore! Many of the usuals from Madison Square Eats also set up shop over here, including Asia Dogs, Mexicue, Roberta's, Arancini, and some more.  I tend to come here with a few other people, with each of us separating and ordering one "splittable" plate (some $3 tacos, mac & cheese, bibimbap, etc.), then sitting together and sharing it all Thanksgiving dinner-style!  Living in Midtown, it's a great way to try out a bunch of food from places you may not think to trek to. That being said, there are some places I just won't go to, simply because live near their actual storefront and can sample the goods whenever I want.  For example, Mayhem & Stout just opened up a shop across the street from my condo (sweet!) and Mason Jar has a full restaurant and bar literally three blocks away from the whole Broadway Bites setup, so I can just walk down the street to go there. Food is priced a tad (if at all) higher than similar items at their respective stores/carts, but you're really paying for the convenience of having so many options in one spot.  Again, in my opinion, the best bet is to snag small eats from a variety of "obscure" places...combined with the excellent options and delicious food from just about every stand, and you're guaranteed a terrific meal :)

i ate a panini. I waited for my meal for  15 minutes. The temperature was so cold. Price was $10. Although the meal was delicious, the value was not enough.we have many options at this place.the atmosphere was very good.Many sightseers visited this place. but honestly I was not satisfied enough.

I work near Herald Square, so when I saw that Broadway Bites would be here until November 24, I was so excited! I've been a few times for lunch, and so far I've tried a few different vendors: - Jicama NYC - "California street food" (according to their website description). I got their classic fall tacos (2 for $9, you can choose from pork, chicken, or veggie). They're not that big, so 2 tacos won't really fill you up for lunch, but they were tasty, with lots of onions and cilantro. The guy taking orders was also incredibly nice and gave me a small sample of the Mexican hot chocolate to try, which was just hot chocolate with a little bit of spicy, and really yummy. Note: cash only. (Update 11/17/13: Just kidding, they take credit card too, their machine just wasn't working the day I went). - Roberta's - The pizzas here are sized for individuals, and range from $9-12. I got the bee sting pizza ($12), which was SO SPICY. Like, I really really wanted to finish it because it was so good (the honey drizzled on top is a real winner), but I had to buy milk just so I could finish it. I don't know if my particular pizza just happened to be extra spicy, because my friend said hers wasn't spicy at all, but in any case it's worth a try. - Asiadog - I've tried their hot dogs several times (here, at Mad Sq Eats, and Smorgasburg), and they have interesting toppings such as Japanese curry, kimchi, and banh mi ingredients. I really like the concept, but for some reason always feel like the hot dog itself is over-grilled. - Bangkok Bar - Quick and freshly made Thai food. I tried the tofu pad thai ($10), and it was pretty standard pad thai, though a bit heavy on the scallions. - Seoul Lee Korean Barbeque - Tacos, burritos, and rice bowls with Korean barbequed meats like bulgogi, spicy pork, and shrimp. My bulgogi burrito ($10) came with bulgogi, scallions, spicy mayo, and kimchi, and was pretty filling for lunch. They made it quickly too - my food was ready in about 5 minutes. - Poffertjes Man - Mini pancakes coated in butter and powdered sugar. They're sinfully good, but also quite pricy for their size (5 for $5). - Bantam Bagels - Mini bagel balls filled with cream cheese on the inside. Tip: either ask for them to be toasted and then eat them on the spot, or heat them up later on... they taste way better when they're warm. They're 1 for $1.50 or 4 for $5, and with the variety of flavors, make a good snack.

Uncle Momo is definitely Uncle Nonooo!! - Food was reasonably tasty but service was horrible. The only "waiter" at the restaurant got our order mixed up, was rude, told us they ran out of water glasses, french fries, and the list goes on - The "waiter" complained to us about occupying too much "space" because we were there with a toddler - We ordered spinach pie and ended up getting a spinach salad and the "waiter" said we got our order mixed up and insisted he was right (bad customer service!!!) - We ordered a shish kabab sandwich which were supposed to come with fries (per the menu) but the "waiter" delivered a different order entirely. When we finally got the sandwich it was without fries because they were supposedly "super busy" before we got there. The fair guy with thick glasses who is presumably the owner proceeded to tell us that they could not make any more fries - We ordered the spinach pie which was served with a side order of plastic wire inside the pie

This place is amazing. First time finding a Lebanese Mediterranean brunch joint. Was super excited to check out. The Tunisian eggs took me back to childhood in North African homes, the fresh bread was outta this world. The French toast was extra bangin, because it's dipped in cream. The nas nas morrocan cappuccino was amazing too.
Came here for brunch, grass fed steak, with eggs was great along with hummus and light homemade fluffy pita! Will definitely come back!

This is a very good Lebanese restaurant.  I had the chicken shish kabob.  It was amazing!  The chicken was grilled to perfection.  It came with a very tasty lentil puree.   The restaurant has nice decor.  The staff are not the most attentive.
No doubt this place has the largest slices you've ever seen. It's easy to make huge slices, but hard to make them tasty too! The buffalo chicken salad is one of my favorites too.

I only came in for a couple of drinks with my girlfriends and I will definitely be going back to sample their menu. The decor is phenomenal and the drink selection is outstanding. The bartenders were very knowledgable and attentive.

I have been looking for Dim Sum in Connecticut for a little while.  This place fits the bill, and the best I've have recently. My wife and I arrived at the end of the service (10am to 3pm I believe) so we may have had what's left.   Traditional cart service.   It didn't matter My Wife, My 16 month old, and I had a great feast and when it was all done. . it ended up being less than 30 bucks.  So thank you great wall, we will be back. . Too bad my waist can't take Dim Sum every weekend! Next time I plan on asking for at least one dish that is really good, but what Caucasians never order!

As soon as I walked into Great Wall of China I knew something was off. The place was empty, none of the staff offered to help us, and 2 women were peeling a comically large pile of green beans on one of the dining tables and shouting at each other in Chinese. It is set up like a buffet but they serve you as you walk down the line of food where we were rushed into choosing things that we weren't even sure of what they were. The table we sat at was about a foot thick and impossible to cross your legs under. It was also awkwardly long so I was strangely far away from the person sitting across from me. Then there was the food. It was the worst Chinese food I ever had. We ordered 3 different things in which were all put into one container. They all mixed together. One item that we hastily selected was drenched in an odd brown watery goo which coated everything in the tray. That particular item was spongy and bland. We later found out that it was cow stomach. I also ordered hot and sour soup. I think someone urinated in the hot and sour soup. Overall my taste buds felt violated and my mouth raped. Great Wall of China raped me in the mouth.
Food was fab. Service was excellent. Music was delightful. Great drinks. Awesome vibe. I would def return. Like all the time. A+ :)
Love this place. No better spot to get a really great meal and a flawless cocktail while spending a minimal amount of money. And if you're feeling luxurious, go for the lobster- you won't regret it.

Grew up in Jamaica and the really good jerk chicken places are right off the side of the road. You pull up, get your jerked whatever wrapped in foil, a piece of hard-dough bread, some pepper sauce and that's heaven. Glady's is just like those roadside places...except really cutely designed, with great music, and real silverware. We had the jerked half chicken, oxtails, rice and peas and plantains. We came during lunch so maybe that's why we had to order at the counter and pick up our food on a tray cafeteria style? I assume they wait on you during dinner hours... Everything was delicious. Jerk chicken was juicy, smokey and well spiced (fear not, pepper-phobic friends, the spice level is tolerable and you can always add more heat with their table sauces); oxtails were tender and in this amazing rich sauce (a little different from my Grandma's); rice and peas were nice; and plantains, sweet and perfectly pan friend. We left full and happy. See you again, Glady's!
Our favorite place in the area, food is simple and on point. Cocktails are well thought out-try the painkiller and goat curry.

This is my first yelp review and I must say Cici's was AMAZING! Their pizza is great and they have so many different types of options/varieties. If there is a specific type of pizza that you want and you don't see it, the staff will happily make it for you. Can't really go wrong for endless salad, bread sticks, pizza, pasta, and dessert for about $6. Would definitely go back there with my family.

The food isn't five star, I will hand you that, but they really will make you anything you want. It's kid and family friendly and they have a pizza that actually tastes like cheeseburgers-delicious. I highly suggest that you at least try that creation.  Service is awesome.  Management is wonderful.  At least give it a try.  So, that's my two cents. Also, who can say no to endless salad bar?  :-)

First off I have to start with the owner Brian! He is just a gem, awesome, nice, smart & great cook! Sounds like the perfect man to me ;) HAHA but lets get to the food part. When you first enter this place is might not be as busy as you think and the decor isn't all that up to date, old school style but its kind of like your having a dinner at your friends house so makes it more personal and homey feeling. Brian was great introduced himself, gave us menus and told us specials and his favorite type of foods and what other customers seem to enjoy most. We started off with Mac & Cheez which was a rigatoni pasta with a nice alfredo sauce and parmesan cheese which was great and we had small pizzeta which was like a deep dish dough and lots of cheese and sauce it was good too. Entrees we had pumpkin raviolis, so creamy and thick just love pumpkin you can't go wrong with that then we had sausage and peppers which were grilled so nicely and just nice taste ager each bite, the pork parm. was so good I enjoyed that a lot and just so different then the typical chicken and the pasta linguini had lots of meat sauce I loved that, we also had meatballs and chicken franchise and everything was just really good! I could not complain about nothing at all! Brian was just a beyond cook and his partner! You couldn't believe this man can make this all fresh by hand in his little kitchen in the back! The best part of the ending also was the dessert he offered on the house which was super nice and it was a chocolate cake which was to die for, super creamy and extra sweet right up my alley and a warm danish with sweet fresh raspberry filling and that was so good too. Everything was just worth the dime! He says starting in May he will have live musicians and bands come and play great wonderful music from classical to jazz to soul which sounds interesting and something I would come back for which enjoying me a nice home cooked meal! This is a great addition to my hometown and something new and I hope more people come by and give this place a try they won't be disappointed & i will be back!

I needed a place to chill after clinic and before a meeting so I came in from the freezing wind cold to have a cup of coffee and a slice of marble cake.  The place has quite the charm.  The server was chilling and jamming on his guitar playing some sweet tunes.  I would definitely go back and also try the Italian food to give it a more fair rating.

Sushi Cafe is the best sushi around.  Once you try some of Paul's sushi (the owner) you will wonder what you were eating before.  His sushi is the best!!  The place is clean, service is friendly, and the food is YUM!!! YAAY PAUL!!!

We love this place and do  not eat sushi anywhere else.  Paul, the owner and sushi chef, has a large menu of inventive rolls and sauces that will please everyone.  The fish is always fresh, and the staff is friendly and accommodating.  Paul recently added a bento box lunch special (as well as delivery service).  AND it's bring your own bottle!! Rhona and Pat

Do you like what sushi in America has become? Do you think Mayonnaise, especially hot mayonnaise is delicious? The best SUSHI I have ever had has been fish on rice.... This place is not where you go for that.... Though I will say this place is one of the best roll manufacturer's I have consumed. If you are a roll fan go here. This place will teach you a lesson. If you like fish and it's subtle delicacies steer clear. The next step or even the last three won't be found here.

FINALLY!  Bodhi Coffee has opened (right next to Xochitl and Cafe Nola)!  Brewing Stumptown coffee that includes certified organic and direct trade beans, Bodhi Coffee brings the Headhouse Square neighborhood socially responsible coffee and tea. It seems as though they've thought of everything to support local businesses and minimize the carbon footprint involved in bringing coffee to you - repurposed glass made into light fixtures from Mount Airy, pastries from Artisan Boulanger Patissier in South Philly, cheeses from Hillacres Pride Farm, organic waste removed by Bennett Compost, tea from The House of Tea on 4th Street - I imagine the list goes on and on, but I stopped asking questions so the staff could take the time and care to brew my coffee.  I think they are even working on biodegradeable cups. Heck, you can bring your own mug to go even greener. Try the hand poured coffee with a bagel with spreadable fromage.   Getting a cuppa here (and some water for the pup) will complete my Sunday morning strolls through Headhouse Square Farmers Market.  Bodhi Coffee, you have made mine runneth over.

Me and my girlfriend dined here one Sunday and it was great! We loved the atmosphere of the backyard and the intimate setting. The whole set up is classy! We started with fried calamari for me of course - I am just a fried food person. My girlfriend who is on a HEALTHY ROAD had grilled calamari - it was good. I ordered the grilled pork chops with wild mushrooms  wine sauce with grilled julienne vegetables - DELICIOUS! My girlfriend started out with a fish special - she did not like - so the restaurant immediately switched it for her with no problems for the Salmon, pan seared with lemon, capers, sage, split string beans & extra virgin olive oil - She loved it! I also had the BABY SPINACH with crispy bacon, chickpeas & goat cheese - That was so DELICIOUS! AAAANNNNNNNNNNNND - Yes I had to have desert - let me tell it was good and straight to the point - ORGANIC ALL THE WAY! Happy Eating!

Came here twice with 7 people or more and they can accommodate well. Fresh pasta is a big draw and it's worth trying. The rest of the food is great too. Service is solid. Good cocktails, decent price. Third time here, will come back.

One of the best restaurants I have eaten food in NJ. The special chicken biryani and the vegetable biryani are amazing... only the normal chicken biryani is so so... Everytime I go to NJ, I always get food from this place.... Love it...

I am not a ramen fan. My boyfriend is a ramen fan and it was his birthday. That being said, Chuko made me a ramen fan. Seriously. We had the Brussels sprouts (sans tossed in fish sauce) and they were crispy without being overdone with the portion perfect for two maybe even three. I had the veggie ramen with the soft poached egg and it was phenomenal. Sort of buttery and rich with earthy tasting noodles and soft cabbage (I think it was cabbage), onions and carrots. SO GOOD. My bf had the sweet potato beer and really dug it. We had to sit at the bar and the waitress was delightful. I told her I was a vegetarian and she made sure anything we ordered (or tried to order) was veggie friendly. Total sweetheart and attentive without being overbearing. Only pain is that they're cash only and you'll probably have to wait for a seat if you get there at peak times, but totally worth it.

Bottom line, the food is very good, and if you're in the neighborhood there is no reason for you to not check it out. That being said, if you're from jersey like myself, its not really good enough to travel all the way to Brooklyn, there are places in jersey that are cheaper and just as good. Got an order of the miso ramen, gyoza, and brussel sprouts. Apparently the veggie ramen is all the rage, but im a miso guy. The noodles - really tasty, probably some of the best ive ever had. The broth on the other hand as a bit lacking, but still very tasty. Gyoza, was a little soft for my liking, im by no means terrible with chop sticks, but they're were a little difficult to pick up. The brussel sprouts though, let me tell you, I never in a million years would have thought that you could have brussel sprouts anything other than meh, but these were unfreaking believable. I believe they are roasted than sautéed with garlic. If i was just chilling, I would haven no issue casually eating them. And again, Im talking about brussel sprouts. Final Analysis Real solid joint, definitely check out if you're in the neighborhood. The place looks more like a hip joint that serves ramen, rather than a traditional restaurant. They dont take reservations, and theres normally an hour wait, so if you do want to go, get there early, and put your name and phone number down. - they'll call you when your table is ready

Can I just say how much I love The Soup Girl? Yes I can. And let me list the reasons why: 1) I'm obsessed with soup. I've searched far and wide for delicious soups around CT, and Soup Girl is by far the freshest, most innovative, and best-tasting. My absolute favorite is Lemon Chicken Orzo, but all of them are delicious. 2) The staff is so kind and welcoming everytime I walk in the door. They have even offered to text me when my favorite soups are made! I received a text today from Bri (who is awesome), and she asked if she could set any soup aside for me so I wouldn't miss out. Customer service at its best! 3) They sell delicious cupcakes. Can I live here? Perhaps it's a little crazy of me to visit this place almost every day, but when you find something good, you can't stay away!

The lunch buffet here is a great deal and is definitely my favorite Indian buffet in town.  The food is always delicious and hot. Food is consistently refilled when it's busy here so you don't have to miss out on anything. I like that they don't wimp out on the spice at the buffet like some other indian places do. Prices are a little steep for dinner - lunch buffet is the way to go.
Most delicious Indian food in New haven!. Vegetarian options are less but still worth the money.

Went on a quiet Friday afternoon. Did the pre fixe menu. Asparagus salad was divine. Wasn't a fan of the meatballs. Tiramisu was also great. The host was very friendly and inviting. Even brought around a tray of cookies! Great lunch!

Arrived with my family of 5, was crowded at the check in podium and it was quite disorganized. Once we got seated it was a great experience, Our waiter was amazing. If you go, you must order the chicken parm - pounded thin and larger than the plate!

Had dinner before a show at Carnegie Hall. Food was very good. Service was professional. The pricing is typically expensive for this neighborhood. Location is key for getting to the show at Carnegie Hall on time. Other than that, for the price we paid one expects great food and service and we were not disappointed.

Came in here unexpectedly.  We started off with an antipasta dish which had some delicious assorted grilled vegetables and stuffed peppers.  It was fantastic.  Next, was a few of their pizzas.  The sausage & peppers along with a margarhita pie were also excellent.  Then on to the main course........I usually don't order ravioli when I'm out, but our waiter highly recommended we give them a try.  I honestly think the meat filled ravioli with a bolagnese sauce was one of the best pasta dishes I've ever had.  We also couldn't resist the chicken cutlet parmesan topped with fresh mozzarella and sliced pepperoni.   It was a unique spin on an otherwise boring dish.  The pepperoni definitely brought it to the next level.  Finally, after stuffing our faces with all of the above,  the waiter was able to talk us into trying the cannolis.  Something else that I wouldn't normally order while dining out.......but damn, I'm sure glad we did.  The shell was light and crispy, the cannoli cream was lighter than most Italian bakeries and the homemade raspberry sauce it was served on top of all made for an absolutely phenomenal dessert. The service was also fantastic.  Our waiter was friendly, attentive and funny.  The manager also visited our table to make sure we were all satisfied.  Prices are fair for NYC.  I think it was as close to a 5 star review you can possibly get.  So I'm giving it a 5 star rating.  It was an excellent meal and I'll without a doubt be returning.

I was not at all impressed with this restaurant. The decor was unattractive. There seemed to be a fixation on noses by the pictures on the walls. We were a group and ordered from the pre fixe menu. Myself and other Italians I have asked never heard of ribollita. Apparently it's a soup. I ordered it as an appetizer. When the waitress brought the deep bowl, it looked more like a dish that had already been eaten. There was barely any soup in the bowl. For the entree I ordered spaghetti and meatballs. I didn't like the sauce. It looked and tasted like reheated sauce. I have definitely had better spaghetti and meatball dinners. Dessert was good but since it was gelato, they didn't make it. Lol Others in my group had the tiramisu; they were big slices and they did like it.

In the land of mediocrity, the restaurant which offers the largest portion sizes wins. Because that's all you really get for your money here. Average food in large quantities. The beer selection is good in the sense that it's not a craft beer bar. Yes, they have some microbrews. Almost all of them are exclusively in bottles. No, I don't care what the Craft Brewers Association says, Sam Adams is not a craft brewer. Doesn't mean they don't make decent beer, it's just not something that excites me when I see it on draft. This isn't 1994. They do have a lot of TVs, so if you want to watch a game here, it's good for that. And your buddy who hates life can still chug Bud Light while you drink something with flavor, all at the same time sharing a bunch of wings and rooting for your team. My wife loves it because she can root for the Pats and against the Jets (just to annoy me) at the same time. But, in comparison to the beer bars in New Haven County (Cask Republic, Delaney's, Prime 16, Mikro, and soon to be Plan B) Wood-n-Tap is last in both beer selection and food. Not saying it's a waste of your time to come here, especially if you're already on the Post Rd. It's still one of the better options in a land of chain restaurant hell. I'm just saying know what you're getting yourself into.

The sliders were really good, and there are tons of beer options. The portions are really large, if you're into that. Good service, too. Only downside is that the Cajun pasta was not spicy. Not a bad place overall, but not memorable either.

My husband and I LOVE the Wood N Tap.  We live in the Hartford area, and have been to most of the other ones.  I work in Milford, and visit this one often with co-workers for Happy Hour, which in my opinion is the best place to go for it.  They have great deals, and the food is awesome!!
I absolutely love this restaurant. All of the waiters are super friendly towards us every time we go! The food is always excellent and the service is great! i would highly recommend eating here.

We loved the atmosphere here and our waiter was awesome! He was making food and beer suggestions and I'd go back and ask for him he was that helpful! We went to watch some sports and have some good food and craft beer, what more could you ask for:-)

Whether you're looking for a bar or dining room atmosphere, Wood-n-Tap in Orange has it. The offer a large menu with something for everyone and the food (in my experiences) has been excellent. The only reason I didn't give this place 5 stars was the service. The staff was friendly and everything was correct but be prepared to wait a while for your food. Our Saturday night dinner lasted about 2hrs (not including the 30 minute wait). Overall, I will return here. They have a great rewards program (be sure to sign up for it) and the food/atmosphere is enjoyable.

I came here with a Groupon for dinner for two - quite possibly the best deal in NYC. For $23 ($29 Groupon with e20% discount), we got two drinks (choice of house sangria, house white/red wine, or any beer!), two entrees, and two desserts. I ordered the house white and my dining buddy got the red sangria. Both were more than serviceable. For entrees, we shared the lamb shank and the salmon fillet. The salmon was excellent and the lamb was fall-off-the-bone unbelievable. Portions were generous. Dessert was apple pie for me and the affogato for my friend. Both were great! And an unexpected addition: our meals came with a solid house salad and truly excellent crusty bread and butter. Service was great - we didn't feel like the cheapskates with the Groupon deal, as sometimes happens. The only catches? Not super convenient to the subway; cash only; and no reservations accepted (though we didn't need them, even at 8 pm on Saturday). Would return again in a heartbeat - even without a Groupon!

Food was very good and staff is very polite.  The manager, Rocco, was also very nice to us.  It's important to be treated well because it makes or breaks the entire experience.  Been here for Brunch too and the French Toast is sooooo good...Yumm yumm!

Basic. Plain. Boring. I do not enjoy writing mediocre reviews on YELP nor on Bonjourclem.com. But Iam straight on and Peeky about my food. The seating was fast. Only 5mns after we arrived we got seated. The staff is pretty good. Nothing amazing but nothing to complain about. The ambiance is very boring with a crazy level of noise at Brunch time, at least. I couldn't hear my date on the other side of the table. We ordered Texas French Toasts, Strawberry Compote Buttermilk Pancakes and Baked Eggs with Salmon. The portions are huge but quite uninteresting. The eggs were overloaded with dry cheap salmon and drowned in tasteless tomato sauce. The pancakes were topped with industrial strawberry jam and not cooked enough. The French Toasts just passable. Experience 3/10 bonjourclem.com @Bonjourclem Xoxo Clem

Came here with the groupon seeing that there were over 5,000+ bought and we were definitely not disappointed. The groupon included drinks, entrees, and desserts - WHAT A DEAL!
