Our waiter was very friendly and we were immediately greeted with complimentary bread and salads. We both ordered red wine sangrias (YUM!) and both got the lamb shank which our waiter recommended. The lamb shank was phenomenal and came with a lot of sauce. The lamb was tender, juicy, and just melt in your mouth good. We finished our meal with two desserts to share - a cannoli and a tiramisu cake. Not too impressed with the dessert, namely the small cannoli but the tiramisu was a great finishing touch to our meal. Overall, for $29, it was a whole lot of food and left us feeling perfectly satisfied! Will come back to try their brunch menu :)

Williamsburger is a pricey burger joint located in a remote part of Queens/Brooklyn 10 minute walk south from the subway stop.  The burgers run from $12 to $15, delicious but rather overpriced for the quaint size and limited fries that are included in the meal (sweet potato fries $1.50 extra).  When I spend $12 on a burger I want it to be larger than my face.   This is not the place to annihilate a burger with bare hands instead to enjoy a fine burger with silverware.  The burger consisted of a toasted bun, mild pink (medium-rare) patty, slice of lettuce, circular purple onions, and dill pickles.  The flavor was quite juicy, however I noticed an unusual amount of oil dripping from the back of the burger that soaked into the bun and made it soggy. The item to rave here about isn't the burger, but it's the milkshake- Salted Caramel Milkshake.  I tried it influenced by the positive tips and found it to be unbelievable, worth ordering in place of the burger. I planned to take a lactose pill to eat only a 1/4 of the shake, but ended up consuming the whole thing and ran home and popped another pill. Salted Caramel Milkshake.  Do it.
Good experience and a quiet establishment, a good place for a nice burger time!

Went out here on a Saturday night for dinner.  The service, food, and atmosphere were all excellent!  It was busy, but we didn't feel rushed, and were able to enjoy a wonderful meal.  The waitress was friendly and knowledgeable, and both of our meals were excellent.  This was our first time here, and we will definitely be back!

We really like this place.  Food is good and its pretty low-key.  The only gripe we have is that it seems really pricey for the neighborhood.  This isn't Manhattan.   However, we want to support local places that are worth spending time in so we go there a bit, but sometimes do happy hour to take the bite out of the experience. Unfortunately, we discovered that they're happy hour misers.  Even though we ordered and received all of our drinks and food before happy hour ended the barman decided that one of our drinks was ineligible for happy hour pricing.   They didn't even mention that but snuck it on the bill. So while we may go back, it will be less frequently and never when the bear bar man is tending bar. What would have been a 4 star review suffers from cheating the customer.  - 2 stars

I went back to Brooklyn to visit the lovely GREENPOINT HEIGHTS.  10x better then ever before. Coming from California, I feel at home here at Greenpoint. And trust me when I say try the GREENPOINT LEMONADE. TRY IT BEST drink ever!!!!!! I shall return. And YOU shall go.......APRIL LOVES THIS PLACE

Wanted to be stoked on this place as its closer than Matchless and Enids. The music was way too hipster dancey and the vibe was too cool-ish. We wanted to grab some quick wings and they were way too hot and the lime had no taste.. Also the tater tots were beyond over cooked. Didnt have a great first impression of this joint.

We watched everyone at the bar receive crappy service from Carlin, a very loud and obnoxious person. Don't get me wrong, if you are able to do your job properly while being loud, that's just fine. It's when you screw up not one, but two pizzas because you are not paying attention to the customer. That's when you become obnoxious. My wife ordered a white pizza. It came out with red sauce. We ordered the white pizza again, it came out with the wrong toppings on it. We watched the servers eat the first pizza in the server station while waiting for our second pizza. We had to ask for the free bread and oil. We had to ask for silverware. I won't go into details about the gossip we overheard from the "bartender" -let's just say it was pretty crude and loud. When we got the bill, we were charged for both pizzas. My wife tracked down a manager who quickly did the right thing and took care of it. 0 stars for the weakest link; Carlin 0 stars for the food because it wasn't what we ordered twice 3 stars for management for comping our pizzas that we didn't order however, 3 stars is generous seeing as you are responsible for training/hiring/scheduling staff.
Wonderful service. The waiters are incredibly nice, friendly, and accommodating. Unfortunately, the food was not heavily flavored and lacked pizzazz.
Like a flawless symphony there was not a bad note in this meal. Best restaurant experience I have had in New York City ever.

I really wanted to like place more than I did. The atmosphere was great and so was the service, but overall the food was just okay. The high point of the whole meal was the parker rolls glazed with duck fat. So delicious! I especially liked that after we finished off the first 4, the server offered to bring us more. Unfortunately, the rest of the food was not nearly as good.  My husband did enjoy his trout, but wasn't wowed and my risotto was under seasoned and little one note. I will say the shrimp was perfectly cooked though.

I don't usually write reviews but this place really had great food.  I chose it because it was 3 doors down from where we were staying at The Gotham Hotel.  There were plenty of open tables Saturday night but I don't think that will be for long so go now while you can get a reservation easily. Everything was delicious.  Our group of 8 almost tried everything on the entrée menu and no complaints at all.  I didn't realize the chef had worked at awesome Manhattan restaurants before here so it makes sense now.  Service was awesome as well.

We went here based on Yelp reviews when my boyfriend and I were looking for a good date night. HOLY COW! Absolutely 100% incredible. Excellent beer selection for IPA/hoppy beer lovers. The rolls are absolutely amazing. Words can't describe them! My boyfriend and I had 6 each. I'll probably dream about them. The server was more than happy to keep bringing more out to us. The meals are the perfect portion (after an appetizer and all those rolls). To start, we ordered the crispy pork belly. It was not overpowering for an appetizer. The tastes complement each other so well. I ordered the scallops...I wouldn't have changed a thing. Perfection. I went with the smaller portion so I could keep eating the rolls. My boyfriend ordered the duck breast and was extremely satisfied. The entree's different tastes all went together so well. We were extremely impressed. After dinner, they gave us mini cookies as a completementary dessert and a pastry to go for checking out coats. The restaurant has only been open since March and I expect great things to come. Great place for a work dinner, family dinner or date night. And it won't kill your wallet either!

Amazing! We had a group of 8 and made last minute reservations. Our table took a while to be ready so they bought each of us a drink and gave us free appetizers! The food was incredible. I had the duck, which is one of the best duck dishes I have had. The ricotta meatballs were amazing also as an appetizer! This place is definitely a must in NYC! The food is great and the service is unparalleled. Everyone was so friendly and accommodating. We will all be back!!

Hard to find any food on Broadway in south Williamsburg! Very excited when I saw this was opening across the street. Everything was fresh I've tried the Seoul sandwich and their steam buns. Amazing! Staff is friendly and quick service. So happy to have a new spot for good bites

A warm, welcoming space with delicious food. Everything was super fresh (do not skip the bimbimbap: it is the ultimate combination of spicy sauce, delectable vegetables, and crunchy rice bits) and yummy. Oh and the ICE CREAM dessert. Oh my god. Homemade purple yam ice cream?! Yes, please. The restaurant is clearly a labor of love, and it shows in the food and service! Will definitely be back to try everything else on the menu. :)

I gotta say this place had me logging in to Yelp and everything and updating my account info just now because I actually felt the need to write them a review. (I've been on this site since 2009 apparently and this is my first review for anything so  kudos, Dotory). First of, the bibimbap: on point. It came out on a nice, well-presented tray complete with some small side portions of kimchi, seaweed, and chili sauce. The dish itself was sizzling in a stone bowl, like how dolsot bibimbap should be. Plus all the veggies and ingredients were fresh and in equal proportions; not too much, not too little. Besides the signature Korean dishes, what I personally liked about their menu is the inclusion of some Filipino food like lumpia shanghai and chicken adobo, as well as ice cream from Purple Yam. I only tried the "Manila" sandwich but if you like Banh Mi's, and chicken adobo, this is basically a dream sandwich. The toasty hoagie bread with cilantro/veggies, plus the slight vinegary taste of the chicken adobo was a combo I've never had before and I honestly don't even know why it's taken this long for such a thing to exist, and for me to discover it. But my life has drastically improved now that I have. I don't venture out to the Williamsburg and Greenpoint area all that much so I haven't really been to any other Korean restaurants in this part of Brooklyn BUT! Dotory has got to be the best bibimbap and Korean food on a.) all of Broadway and b.) in the S. Williamsburg/Bushwick/Bedstuy area, by far. Nice little spot under the J train (coincidentally on the same corner a Kpop music video was shot) and a welcome addition to the area. I'll be coming back just for the "Manila" sandwich alone, and to try out the other sandwiches, and likely the rest of their menu. Also really nice and friendly owners! My new Korean food spot.

why did it take so long for nyc to get laduree?  i'm curious if there will always be queues. box of 6 is $20, bag of 6 is $18 (so the actual box costs $2 and they have 5-6 different designs you can choose from).  the macarons are shipped here once a week and a full cafe is expected next year some time.  right now the space is smallish, selling macarons, chocolate, candles, jelly, caramel, ice cream, sorbet.  i think it will take some time for the workers to get a hang of their job.  i asked for certain flavors and found out they put in the wrong flavors when i got home (the colors were close enough, i guess).  luckily you can't go wrong with any of the flavors. also, i wanted caramel ice cream and was almost given sorbet.  the caramel flavor was out anyway. so--perhaps a label gun would help out of the workers a lot.

As much as I would love to give Laduree 5 stars... I have to give it a solid 4.5 - too bad Yelp won't let me do it so it's getting a 5--keep reading for why.  I've lived in France and traveled all throughout Paris tasting some of the best macarons in the city so I've been to two of the Ladurée boutiques (as well as Pierre Herme) in Paris and this one looks similar to both, minus the Salon de Thé.  Beautiful boxes and ribbons adorn their signature green walls - with the stars of the show, their vibrantly colored macarons taking center stage.   I arrived early and a line was quickly forming behind me.... I picked up a box of 8 for a friend, another box for my husband and 2 individuals for myself--rose and fraise mentholée (strawberry mint). The rose was utterly divine!  It's the kind of cookie you take a bite of and put back down as you're enjoying it way too much to even think about taking another taste before you've thoroughly enjoyed what's already in your mouth. It has that slight crunch on the outer shell which gives way to a slight chew before reaching the creamy filling.  Laduree NYC - you nailed it!  And then... then, I tried the Strawberry Mint (Fraise Mentholée) and my excitement fizzled out.  The cookie itself was a soggy mushy mess.  The flavor was great but hard to enjoy as the texture of the cookie was awful.  I can't say much more about it.   Later that evening, I tried another bite of two other flavors from the hubby's stash and they redeemed themselves - the Fleur de Sel Caramel was outstanding in terms of texture and flavor, as was Cherry Almond.  When they nail it, they really hit it home... now if they can find a way to expand their patisserie selection and get their palmiers here - I think I might cry tears of joy! Total cost for 2 gift boxes of 8, and 2 individual macarons for my enjoyment:  $56.
Now I know why there are always long queues in Maison Ladurée. The macarons are to die for. I love the packaging as well.

Trekked here with my friend (and fellow Yelper) Dominique F. before she went home. The line took about 1 hr. That being said... 1. Service is very friendly, though the servers definitely were totally overwhelmed by people and gave my friend the wrong macarons. They also give you a snobby look when you ask for just a regular bag for the macarons and not one of their fancy, overpriced, gold-trimmed, French-imported, plushy bags. 2. Price is comparable to those elsewhere. 3. I got Rose, Strawberry/Mint, Salted Caramel, Green Apple. Rose was my favorite. It was so delicately and light -- lighter than its counterpart at La Maison du Macaron. Still wonderfully chewy! Green Apple was delightfully tangy, though tasted rather fake. Strawberry Mint was not good. Caramel was DENSE. This is not for people who like their fluffy, airy macarons. This was like true chewy caramel in its spectacular form, with the sweetness brought out even more with the salt. I liked it, but couldn't even finish it. 4. Macarons last in the fridge for 3 days! They taste just as good on Day 3! Will probably come back again, but not until the hype dies down.

Been to the French outpost of this patisserie, and all I can say is YUM!  It's like the 31 flavors of macarons!  I am looking forward to the opening of their full restaurant as they make DELICIOUS breakfasts.  Laduree is a decadent, totally worth-it sweet shop.  If you want a special, special treat, this is the place to go!

Love it! We went there earlier in the day and avoided the line.  At $2.70 it's costly but is worth it!  The macaroons are quite small but they are so light and tasty.  It might be a good thing it's expensive - otherwise I would easily eat 15 of them! I tried the Vanilla which was my safe choice and the rose.  They were both great but I really enjoyed the rose.  My friends had the pistachio which they also really enjoyed. The store is beautiful and elegant.  The colors of the macaroons, chocolates and boxes are very appealing and I'm a sucker for good marketing! I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 since it's costly.

The only thing more funny than hipsters and drunk lonely housewives are the French. I've been to France a few times, cigarettes, coffee, Nutella, a culture and language in retreat. But hey! Let's milk it while its still breathing. I'm a sucker for sweets. So I found myself here. Actually a quick sortie (that's french!) to get a gift for mom. I knew that there would be a line to deal with but it wasn't so bad, about a 45 min turnaround time. I was amazed by the sheer number of Asians at attendance. A massive iphone armed insanely polite horde. The girls behind the counter should be commended with a star and perhaps a few martinis for having to deal with those who simply have less than zero English skills. Every question was answered by a 'yes'. Gift box or regular box? Yes. You get the idea. A good place to get a tasty treat, especially a gift. Since Payard closed I've always been on the look out for good sweet spots. I'll add this to the list.

I think overall I was impressed most by the beautiful boxes and packaging (basically the branding) of Laduree. Gorgeous!! The line is annoying and sweaty, but the macarons were quite good. The fleur d'oranger was a floral explosion in my mouth. Citron was also delicately tart (not overwhelmingly so). The petale de rose at first tasted like I was eating perfume, but then after a few bites was quite good. Cassis was punchy and tart. Framboise was good but not that memorable.I'm not a fan of caramel macarons (but if you are, you should def try one here). Texture of the macarons are soft and melt in your mouth. But my cousin would like to add that these definitely did not taste like the ones in Paris because these were a bit soggy. I think I'll be more excited to try this place once they start baking them on site.

Ahhh Laduree...finally you have blessed Manhattan with your sweetness. Only sad part is...no cafe and no yummy hot cocoa.  :( I heard about the horrific hour wait, so I decided to play it smart and venture out during my lunch break on a Wednesday. I waited a mere 15 minutes. Pay the extra couple dollars for the adorably presh "Laudree New York" boxes. Tres chic! I had a mixture of 8 cookies stuffed into my little purple box, and each one was delish. Salted Caramel, Rose, Raspberry, Lemon....even the pistachio were all blissfully delicious. If only they had a cafe within the maison, I could then close my eyes and really feel as if I was in Paris.

Laduree je t'adore! Don't get me wrong about the 4 stars I do love Laduree, but seriously how can you have a laduree outpost without the tea room and without the pastries??? I spoke with the cashier however, and was assured that there is a salon de the in the works. Thank goodness because although biting into a rose macaron (please don't pronounce it macaroon... that is a desert made with coconut that has nothing to do with this) instantly transported my mind to paris, enjoying it with taxi-cabs driving by is not ideal. Once there is a tea-room I'm sure New Yorkers like me will finally be able to experience that Proustian moment while biting into a madeleine over a cup of the Laduree and imagine themselves, if only for a moment, sitting in the original Laduree tearoom up on the premier etage above the place de la madeleine.   Quel bonheur!

Oh you want a burger? But you think that food trucks are always rip offs with low quality product huh? Go to spot. Quality. Variety. Laughs and smiles. Aptly named, because this sure as hell is the spot!
Didn't have food here just drinks. But great vibe in West Village. Burgers looked amazing and awesome setting. Had a Cosmo which was fabulous. Definitely recommend for a hotspot in the area.

I don't really understand all of the hype... I mean it's good, but it's nothing special. I enjoyed my time there, but I wouldn't go back. The food seemed expensive for what it was. We had a drink at the bar while we were waiting for a table. This was my highlight as its a nice ambiance with a homely feel. The bartenders were kind of rude though. I loved the lady on front of house, she was a hoot.

I wanted to like this place a lot but unfortunately this fell far below expectations. The burger was decent but is basically just meat and bread.  They wouldnt even let me purchase some lettuce to put on it. They also made us wait 45 min to get seated even though they had space because we arrived at 4:45 when they change from brunch to dinner. I hope uou have better luck.
posted in error
Expect an awesome burger...and a long wait for a table.

Visited NYC recently and read a great deal about this place. It lived up to my expectations! I got a solid burger and my fiancé ordered the most ridiculous grilled cheese ever!! It is a typical trendy NY restaurant, where the food is outstanding you have to sit on top of one another and it's pricey. If it wasn't $100 for 2 bloody mary's a burger and grilled cheese this place is 5 star. I would absolutely recommend eating here if you in the west side of Manhattan and you can grab a seat, (it gets packed quick!)

My. favorite. burger. And I'm a burger connoisseur (I even was a founding member of a burger club - and yes, we're all skinny). The thing with their burger is you must love gorgonzola cheese, which is admittedly polarizing. I had to remove one star because I'm not in love with their shoe string fries - they're so little you kind of have to shovel in your mouth as a group or even eat with a fork - though they are nice and crunchy. This is a fantastic dark & cozy spot for when the weather turns cold (aka, now through March). See you there!
Great service, fantastic food. My date loved it. I will definitely be coming back!

Salt Alert Greeting- a women just stood there and smiled. I didn't know if she worked there or was hitting on me. The hipster behind the podium had nothing to say Vibe- Alice in wonderland meets the hobbit Price- expensive Bathroom- unisex - failure Service- friendly table turning bandits Parking- after six pm the street opens up Wine by the glass is a rip off. And the poor selections make this one of the worst wine by the glass choices in the city. $16 Beckman Cab Sav Food $21 burger with shoestring fries. The cheese overwhelms the burger. Poor choice of cheese. The bun is great, the beef is ordinarily tasty. It looks better than it tastes. Cross hatching on bun and an abundance of shoestring fries make this dish too pretty to eat. Dessert Banana toffee pie is too sweet. Flourless chocolate cake is a cliche WIGB? No Talk about over rated. This is it. You are packed in at cafe tables with mushroom stools to sit on.  The bar has a limited amount of stools. Why this place has global recognition I do not know. Anyone who waits to get i here is crazy. The burgers were so salty tonight that they would make a fish's lips shrivel. If you threw one of these burgers into the Hudson River it would turn into the Dead Sea. Another typical example of over salted restaurant food. We have sodium sickness. The famous reviews about this place are. Once again BS. $109 for two burgers, two glasses of wine,one beer and two slices of pie. Crazy!
This place has terrific burgers - it's not all pork!
very good food and good prices
yes.  Disappointed.  Nude gnocchi way too salty as were other dishes ordered by friends.

We are giving this place a 4.5 on food and service, but due to seating issues, we are docking half to four. The wait is long, so be prepared. We showed around 6:30 on a Friday and it was an hour to an hour and a half wait. Thankfully, they have a texting service, so went around the corner to the historic (cash only) White Horse Tavern for a drink while we waited. Located on the corner, the building is nondescript, so be on the lookout for a tiny pig hanging out over the doorway. Walk in and you are greeted and seated when your table is ready. The seating is a bit cramped, with my wife seated pretty closely and intimately to the table behind her. The service was good, though, and despite the volume, was quick. We started out with Devils on Horseback (prunes wrapped in bacon) and an unlisted beef medallions in a cheese sauce. Our friend got the Sheep's Milk Ricotta Gnudi with Brown Butter & Sage and my wife and I each for the Chargrilled Burger with Roquefort Cheese & Shoestring Fries. The gnudi was packed and was very tasty and the burgers were cooked perfectly with addictive shoestring fries. So aside from the cramped space we got shoved in to, this place was worth the wait. The food and service were both good. If you've got time, give the place a try.
Over priced but yummy
Best burger, period! Good drinks too.

Simple perfection, made with love, great service.... Had brunch, came back later to eat again. Always a nice crowd, people laughing, having a great time. Sit at the bar if Chris is bartending, Teresa is also a great server... Just good people with great hearts, an eye for detail, and amazing charisma. All around an excellent experience. Try the Dutch baby pancakes.... The burger... And work through the drink menu... All of it.
Exceptional services  Our service adviser ken Walter is phenomenal.
Without a doubt I am coming back again, They make delicious dishes and they are all worth trying. I really Enjoyed the meals.
Awesome burger.  Great spot.  Cool secret spot on third floor as well!

Chargrilled burger and shoestring fries are on point. The burger has a nice full meaty flavor and the cheese makes it a very dense bite. At times the flavors are almost too rich as it seems to be with every dish in this place often bordering on too salty when earn together. The gnocchi plate is among the best offerings here tasting very smooth and buttery and the chicken liver toast is also a delightful dish. The seating is a bit cramped but the atmosphere is definitely very hip and I saw Anja Rubik dining upstairs so don't be surprised to see supermodels dining here. It was packed even on a Monday night. Get here before 7 and you won't have to wait for a table. Also a bit of a pain of the ass to get here since there's no subway stops nearby.

Always packed at night and a long wait, but our large group was able to get in relatively quick with some name-dropping. Burgers are a must-have, as are the fries. Can't go wrong with many things on the menu!

I don't know why it took my friend from California to take ME here! I was glad she did. The food was amazing! The burger was SO good. And the shoestring fries! We also had the oysters and the devil's on horseback. The waiter was really good at making recommendations. Only went the one time for a late dinner but it was a good time. It was a little crowded, noisy and dark but other than that...super fun time. I don't drink so maybe I could not appreciate the alcohol part of it. Definitely worth checking out.
Always amazing. Most incredible vibe & ambiance. Go during off-hours so you don't have to wait or deal with annoying crowds. Burger is the best. Deviled eggs, mmmmm. Devils on horseback, a must.
Cozy restaurant, get there early for a table or be prepared to wait. Order Devils on Horseback as a starter and the burger, arguably one of the best in NYC.
Absolutely brilliant - warm welcome from the staff, prompt service, good beers and straw fries to die for.
Its casual and a neighborhood spot.. food is what its expected to be.. its a fun pub in the west village
For a gastrolounge its pretty fun. the burgers and fries are to die for. But when it gets really busy the service can be sacrificed at times so go on a week day.

It was about 4:30 pm when we were heading to another restaurant down the street but forgot that they didn't open until 5. So we checked our options and saw that Xochitl was up the block. They too didn't serve dinner until 5, but was able to sit at bar order drinks and some chips, salsa and guacamole. The staff was very friendly. The deco was very true to Mexican design with tiles, heavy wood and lanterns. And the food was excellent. They're not large potions, so you didn't feel full when the plate was put in front of you., like in some restaurants was just enough....to have dessert. I had the mushroom tamale and for dessert the flan...OMG, the flan! Yeah, you gotta check this place out.

On a tip from a friend, I dinned here last weekend and was very surprised. We were seated in the lower level which was full atmosphere...and candles. We had perfect, perfect margaritas that were just right. Our first course was a mouth watering tuna ceviche, followed by some mexican flat bread and juicy carnitis tacos, which were disappointing only because my wife wouldn't let me order a 2nd round of them.   For the main course we had the fried chicken dish and the snapper. The fried chicken was juicy, flavorful and delicious. The corn bread which a lot of restaurants do not put much effort into was fantastic. The snapper was different in a amazing sort of way.  Fresh as could be and seasoned oh so right. For dessert we had the doughnuts and dessert martini, both were delicious were the perfect end to our amazing night. The service was great, our server Wedge was thoughtful, calm and polite, even though the room was full. We will definitely return soon.

We went her Friday night, and we had an open table coupon.  It was really great.  The main entrees were a little spendy for our taste (mid to high 20's) but there was plenty else to choose from on the menu and it was all good and different.  We had the "build your own" guacamole and it was to die for.  I highly recommend getting the truffles in it.  Wow.  We also had tuna ceviche, tacos and a mushroom dish that was all so yummy we wanted to savor it.  The best part though, was a side dish of corn that my husband couldn't stop talking about.  The wait staff was really nice to.  We didn't have any drinks, so I can't speak to that, but we will certainly go back for the food.

Went back to Xochitl after a while to find out that its management, chef, and entire staff had changed.  Although the name is the same, it's definitely not the same restaurant. The food was very good but it doesn't match the incredible cuisine that the prior chef created.  Sadly their drinks have also changed: gone many of the unique concoctions that I loved (such as the El Fumador).  Both the food and drink menus are decidedly uninspired.  The margaritas are good but (i though) a bit over-sweetened.  I have no complaints about the blood orange martini, however.  As for the food, it was just okay - the guac is more modestly portioned than it used to be and the appetizers (at least the ones we got) were bland. The Pollo Frito, supposedly this restaurant's signature dish, was tasty but lacked that out-of-this-world taste that you'd expect for a nearly 30-dollar entree. Our service was also lacking and I'm willing to chalk it up to an "off night", but when you're just not served two dishes that you've ordered it warrants mentioning.  Other tables' food was also brought to ours.  We received a dessert dish in lieu of the missing appetizer, but nothing was removed from the bill (nor offered to be).  The manager promised to make it up to us "next time".  Sadly, I'm not sure there will be one.

I was really disappointed by my last experience at Xochitl. I hadn't been there for years and it has changed quite a bit, and not for the better. Pros: -Service was good. -They seated us on time. -Server was informative and not too overbearing (but he did seem to take it personally when it was obvious we didn't like our food). -Nice size portions (we went for restaurant week and it was a good amount of food for the $35). Cons: -Owner and menu have changed and that means NO MORE SOPA AZTECA!! That's the ONLY reason I wanted to go there! Huge disappointment. For some reason I was confusing the tortilla soup with Sopa Azteca. Well, that was dumb of me! -The food just fell short. We ordered the 4 cheese empanadas and they were just so heavily fried, seemed almost triple fried. I know that many empanadas are fried but these were just so heavy and well, I couldn't finish them. -My friend and I shared the adobo shrimp and pollo frito. The server was really pushing the pollo. It wasn't anything spectacular, trust! 'm glad that I didn't pay full price for that because $30 for a mediocre fried chicken would just be frustrating. -Dessert. Well by the time we ordered, one of the choices was removed because "something happened in the kitchen." We got the doughnuts and the flan. The flan stood out, it was good. Again, the doughnuts seemed like they were quadruple fried or something. I'm really, really bummed out about this because I so loved Xochitl the other times I've been. Needless to say, I won't be heading back anytime soon. Can someone please tell me where to find a killer Sopa Azteca!???

Walking around town on a Friday night looking for a place to eat with no reservations and it being restaurant week, I was sure we would be eating at a dive or heading home to make tacos.. Not the case! We stumbled upon Xochitl and my boyfriend remembered hearing good things about it so in we went. We barely waited 3 minutes before being seated. Pretty decent given the circumstances. As it was restaurant week, Xochitl had a fixed 4 course menu at $35 a person. The meal started off with a customizable guacamole (we added red onion, roasted garlic, and cilantro) so yummy and the tortilla chips were perfectly crisp with just enough saltiness. Then on to the first course: we chose the cheese filled empanadas and some type of flat bread with mushrooms and cheese. I must admit that though good, the first courses were a tad bland. For example the flat bread could have used a little squeeze of citrus. For main courses, I ordered the short rib (served with a potato gordita and roasted veggies) and bf ordered the pollo frito (served with cornbread and greens) at the waiter's recommendation. The short rib was fantastic, perfectly glazed and tender but the potato and veggies were alittle lacking. I can't comment on the pollo frito but the cornbread it was served with was the best I've had yet. For dessert, we ordered the flan and doughnuts (served with both chocolate and strawberry dipping sauces). Both were very good. I also cannot comment on the drinks but if I visit again, I will most definitely give them a try. If you haven't been to Xochitl, I recommend giving it a go.

This review is specific to the bar staff at Juniper. Due to multiple off-putting experiences, my husband and I do not intend to spend another dime at Juniper -- which leaves us now unlikely to book a weekend at Hotel Vermont. We have ample experience working for tips, and we understand the benefits of providing courteous customer service to every party. For whatever reason, the employees behind the bar seem selective about who gets attentive service, while other parties get ignored. To be clear, we are nice, and tip nicely. :-) We find being ignored at the bar very frustrating as we have been in their shoes. Also, the first time we were there, we ate at the bar, and found metal from a fry basket cooked into our food. Having worked in kitchens, we know things like this can happen by mistake. We were very cool about it. The bartender and barback seemed nonplussed. Yes, we got that item comped, but not with any apology. We chalked it up to a restaurant being new and working out kinks. Recently, we have both been back separately and found ourselves ignored for other parties at the bar -- at only moderately busy times. Now that the establishment has been open one year and this is still occurring, we are inclined to let people know Juniper is not living up to Hotel Vermont's stated vision. These employees act like Juniper is the only game in town. It is not! Spend your time and money at one of the other, wonderful Burlington restaurants, where every party is treated with equal attention!
We only had the pea soup for lunch but it was absolutely delicious! Very nice atmosphere, great music and friendly staff as well.

Junipers, the bar and restaurant within the Hotel Vermont, is a nice place to have some drinks or get a quick dinner with friends or business associates. They have a well stocked bar and a really nice assortment of wines and beers. Menu is a bit limited and a touch pricey but so are most places in Burlington. Having stayed at the hotel for a couple of months and dined at Junipers at least once a week, I have tried most of the items on the menu. Always pretty good.... but nothing Special.

Been going here every once in a while for years.  Recently went back with 2 others after the Peter McAndrews menu overhaul and had an amazing meal worthy of writing a review.  Part of menu consists of what I guess you could call "italian tapas", a bunch of 2-3 bite $3 plates like shimp bruschetta, or grilled octopus in red sauce.  We split a few small plates, an order of the red spicy mussels, then each got a half portion of one of the pasta dishes.  Was a great way to not over fill yourself and try out a bunch of stuff without breaking the bank.  I'm still craving more of the shrimp bruschetta days later, and the mussels were some of the best I ever had.   Previously I would go for the great beer list and cozy atmosphere, now I'll be going back for the food.

Went to Bridgid's on a busy Saturday night with my wife and 2 sisters after the flower show at the Convention center. One of my sisters lives right around the corner from this wonderful establishment and after a nice day in Philly we didn't feel like driving anywhere else. Glad we didn't!     We had a reservation for 6:15 and they were very accommodating when we wouldn't be able to get there until 6:30. We walked in to a very tight bar area and to the back where we were seated promptly.     Mark was our server and very knowledgeable about the menu and drinks.   My wife ordered a White Zinfandel and since they didn't have that Mark and another server talked her into trying a similar wine which she wrote down since she enjoyed it so much.  One of my sisters ordered a cider and my other sister and I ordered from their long beer / ale list.  The Philly ale was great.    Our appetizers included the fondue meatball, fried octopus and their homemade bread, all delicious and recommended .         Dinners included Lasagna, pasta with bolognese sauce,and steak skewers. If you order the broccolli rabe as a side, be prepared!  Very hot,with red pepper flakes on it. They warn you on the menu, though.     This is a new menu for them, they went Italian.  We would go back anytime to try more dishes. Give them a try!

Love the new Italian menu at Bridgid's.  Great, friendly place to grab a drink (great variety of beers) with delicious and affordable appetizers, or a full dinner.  Always a nice evening.  Looking forward to trying brunch there.
Loved the food here. Highly recommend.

After living in Manhattan and eating H&H bagels, no bagel in Jersey had come close to them. But Bagel Box is the closest to that big perfect H&H - big and crispy outside, soft inside.  Good flavor selection here, blueberry, choc. chip, Black Russian (Pumpernickel) some whole grains and even cheddar or jalapeno. They even have flavored cream cheeses and fish salads by the pound prepacked to go. They'll make you a sandwich of tuna, light tuna, coldcuts or chicken on a bagel of your choice. They have cold drinks or coffee as well. It's a small shop, so beware sometimes you may have a wait as other customers order  a bunch of sandwiches or salads to take out. I'm not sure if you can call in an order in advance, but that would be helpful.

I've had bagels from here for 30 years.  Parking is horrible and the place has gone way down.  Must be the new owners.   The bagels in the afternoon seem leftover from the morning.  I'm very disappointed. There is a great bagel place in wallington.  Long drive since I living in west orange but worth it. The employees not so nice. Cream cheese prices are very expensive.
We were here on 16th oct 2014.pleasant atmosphere,courteous service,hygienic ,homely,very tasteful ,reasonably priced food.whenever one is in Iselin he/she should visit this restaurant

I came here while exploring Oak Tree Road with a few friends. We came in at around 2 pm, and the place was empty. The service was very friendly and helped us decide what we would like. One thing to be cautious of are the small portions. I wouldn't go here for a big meal; however, their portions make this place great for a small lunch in the afternoon. I especially recommend the pav bhaji and mango lassi. Great place to socialize with friends.

I have been eating at talk of the town now for over a year. The quality of food and service is great and has only gotten better and better over time.  The place is clean all the time. The best thing is no foam plates are used here. I'm happy that this place is close to where I live and i don't have to drive a few miles. I have been and will continue to happily recommend this place to my friends. Good job 'Talk Of The Town', keep up the great job.

I've been to Le Virtu a few times and it's my favorite Italian in Philadelphia.  I've been to Amis, Monsu, and plenty of the gravy places in the city but Virtu is far and away my favorite and the best deal.  I really love their lamb shank and their rabbit ragu but you really can't go wrong with their menu.

Dinner Monday Evening -11Feb2013: We, had a wonderful dinner at Le Virtu with family Monday evening. We heard of all the mixed reviews (most good to excellent, some not so great), so we decided to check it out for ourselves. To start out, for a Monday the restaurant was full, including the entire bar. While waiting for the other guests, I sat at the bar and ordered a cocktail, an old fashioned. Though the bar did not have rye whiskey, Tree (sp?) the lovely bartender mixed a very nice stiff one made with Maker's Mark, I was content! Once all of us arrived, we were seated at our table (we had a party of 6). The server that evening was very friendly and she was very knowledgeable with the menu and the menu additions. As a table, we ordered a number of appetizers: Suppli al telefono (Fried rice balls, saffron, meat ragù and mozzarella) - lovely warm balls of rice enclosing creamy meat ragù ( 2 orders). Insalata di bietole -Red and yellow baby beets, endive, pine nuts, gorgonzola, red wine vinegar -if you are a fan of beets, I recommend this plate. My absolute favorite antipasto was definitely the Affettati misti which is a selection of Le Virtu's house-cured salumi and assorted antipasti.  For my primi course, I ordered a small portion of Taccozzelle all'aquilana Taccozzelle, house-made Abruzzese-style sausage, porcini, black truffle, Navelli saffron. Wow, first off, the portion substantial, the pasta was fresh perfectly cooked. The house made sausage and procini with black truffle navelli saffron sauce was absolutely incredible. (you can order a smaller portion of any of the pasta dishes-with exception to the Maccheroni alla mugnaia). For the secondi course I had the Brodetto a flavorful seafood stew, roasted red peppers, tomato broth- very well prepared - again, simple rustic preparation with incredible deep flavor.  Another great recommendation, not on the menu that evening was the shepherd's gnocchi lamb ragu. The texture of the pasta was not like gnocchi I've had before, it was dense with a definite "chew" to it. It was explained that this preparation of gnocchi is made without potatoes, just water and flour. A rustic simple preparation, with the lamb ragu, incredible rich, earthy flavor.  After  a round of cocktails and 5 bottles of wine, a superb dinner and dessert, our entire party had such a wonderful and great experience. We will definitely come back!

I liked this place.  I can't say that there is anything particularly unique to this place, compared to many other great Italian restaurants in the city, but its good.  The place is understated but clean and welcoming.  The staff was very nice.  I really look forward to going back in the summer and checking out their amazing outdoor space.  The appetizers were definitely the best part.  We got the beet salad with pine nuts and gorgonzola.  Probably the best beet salad I have ever had.  Ridiculous.  We also got the braising egg and cheese croquettes which were good but nothing special.  Our pastas were rich and the portion sizes were appropriate (not too big).  We got the Maccheroni alla mugnaia and the Taccozzelle all'aquilana (minus the sausage).  East Passyunk area is truly an amazing area of philly and this place fits right in.

I lived in Northern Italy last year, but I don't remember ever having a pasta dish as good as Le Virtu's agnolotti alla porchetta. The layers of flavor, savory and just a little sweet, were awesome. We ordered a range of other antipasti, primi, secondi, and dessert plates. Overall, it was all very good -- the N'duja appetizer (kind of like pate or charcuterie, but with more spice) and the orata (second-course fish, skinned table-side) were standouts. The crepes in broth appetizer and the panna cotta were less successful (the pears with panna cotta were flavorful, but the panna cotta texture was a bit off). Service, including the waitress and hostess, were solid. It's a nice restaurant with more of a classic/classy vibe, but the fact that it's in the cool East Passyunk neighborhood keeps it from feeling too stuffy.

WOW... the sushi here and the spring rolls are the best I've had.    Just don't forget that the Hondo (sushi chef) has his own personal tip cup. The chinese food is OK, good range of vegan options also.   Don't let the area scare you, you'll wonder what took you so long to come here.  It's mostly a take-out , so if you eat there , there's always a table ready.   Staff is polite and fast on their feet, too.

Great Sushi! This guy is not messing around. We've come in for take out a few times and have always enjoyed watching their sushi chef and his assistant kick out some really great rolls. I appreciate finding a place that takes its Sushi so seriously down here in South Philly. Dynamite roll and the Dragon roll are standouts.

Giving it 3 Stars but it should really be 2.5. I Really Really wanted to like this place so I went back multiple times and tried multiple menu items. First nothing is seriously bad about the place but I had a bad experience with the Beef Ribs and the peach cobbler.  The Beef ribs good luck finding the meat, I was handed a plate full of bones with almost no meat on them. It was a combo plate  and the chicken was ok, the mash potatoes were also ok. The one highlight was the hush puppies were good (the reason for the 3rd star). I also tried there chicken sandwich on another visit and it was OK, the macaroni and cheese was Horrible as it was inedible with all the oil that was in it. The desserts...Peach Cobbler...texture was OK..but covered in some super sweet syrup. The cakes were OK, but nothing special and overpriced. The Banana Pudding was OK, the first time I had it it was good, then I had it on a subsequent visit and they put pudding and bananas over some vanilla wafers, which is not how banana pudding is made. Very sloppy. The dining area is clean. Grandmother is fun, and super helpful, The Food for the most part is OK, but nothing special at all and overpriced for nothing special. There open 3 days a week, so you would expect the food to be top notch and it isn't. The problem in my opinion is they have to many menu items and it hurts them all. They should lower the number of items they offer so they can concentrate on a few very well done items. The owner needs to set standards for the people working there and the food the present. Overall - Its not good, Its not bad but its only OK, and there charging you a premium so it should be GOOD not just OK.

Food and baked goods are just awesome. Simply stated. Though I'm not a fan of the pumpkin bread or wheat veggie fish pattie, but literally everything else I've tasted was awesome. Organic eggplant pattie, Veggie chicken and veggie fish pattie (not the one in wheat flour), spare ribs, curry chicken, coconut bread so yummy in my tummy haha, pineapple cake and bread pudding, porridge and brown rice. I think I need to go to rehab for this place.
Best hibachi in by far, Benihana isnt nearly as good (but still decent) jason is the best chef, rice, noodles, and the filet all great with the ginger sauce
Consistent quality each time I've been here over the last 10 years or so.  Best hibachi as far as I'm concerned.   Always as for the soy sauce garlic mixture....you won't be disappointed!!

I think the hibachi service has fallen off a bit since the last time I was here. I wonder I they still offer the 2 for 1 coupon offer and are cutting corners. There wasn't much flavor except for a lot of burnt garlic. No spices. No egg in the fried rice. The ginger and mustard sauce was bland. Perhaps i hit an off night. It used to be quite good.

I always eat at masala grill, so I went to the restuarant with my friends and we ordered our food.  I was eating when suddenly I found a roach inside my chicken tikka masala.  i was grossed out so i called the waiter and I told him.  They have very bad customer service because no listened to us. I recommend to all the students not to eat there.  If I found a roach in my food imgaine how dirty and nasty is inside the restuarant.  i am never gtoing back again.

Really enjoyed our dinner at Masala Grill on Saturday night!  Friendly service, busy and comfortable restaurant.  We had the saag paneer, chicken vindaloo (4 level of hotness) and olive oil naan for dinner... followed by a vanilla ice cream dish for dessert which was delicious.  Only thing I disagreed with was the high prices for small dishes.  Otherwise a great meal!

Worst service ever! I waited by the door for 20 minutes without one person acknowledging us including the Manager looking gentleman behind the counter who was wearing worn out tennis shoes and shorts. I understand that it was busy due to a school function that had just gotten out but at least hostess to greet and take a tally of names to be seated. Everyone waiting for a seat just kept looking around waiting to be greeted without any help. Finally we stopped one of the waitresses and told her that we were waiting to be seated and she eventually sat us down at a table that was still dirty. The wait staff seems to be of high school age. The waiter didn't know the menu very well and had to check with the kitchen a few times to see if they had the food available. I ordered a steak and it was a frozen overpriced nasty piece of meat. Broccoli was super cold and tasteless. Never got a refill on our drinks. Finally the ice cream which I thought was the redeeming factor of this place. We ordered 3 ice creams and all 3 came out with frost and freezer burn ice chunks.

A.C. Petersen Farms absolutely hit the spot. It had everything I was looking for: great service, great atmosphere, and most importantly, GREAT food. Sitting outside on their patio on a cool summer night is just about as good as it gets. I started my evening off with a hot, creamy cup of delicious New England Clam Chowder, and followed it up with a perfectly cooked ACP Burger. After such a pleasant meal, I had high hopes for their much-hyped ice cream, and it did not disappoint. I had a two scoop sundae with one scoop of graham cracker and one scoop of cookie dough, and I can honestly say it was one of the best sundaes I've had in years. What made it great was the fantastic HAND WHIPPED whipped cream that was piled high above a warm river of rich hot fudge. All this combined with great service from our waitress, as well as relaxing, family friendly atmosphere, made my experience at ACP one to remember. I can't wait to go back for another meal.
What can I say? I like their ice cream - the rich taste, the many choices of flavors. I also love the hot fudge and the peanut butter sauce.

Ordered a corned beef and pastrami reuben the meat was so tender flavorful and delicious!  Grilled in the panini press and you have a 5 star sandwich. Can't recommend this place enough.  Just looking at them carving up that meat will make your mouth water all by itself. Amazing just amazing!  I want to take this place back home with me!

This place sums up a lot about Philly for me: flavorful, lots of personality, and consistent. Our friends who had moved here for a short time from Cali recommended it, and I am still so so thankful for that recommendation. We definitely come here at least once a month and you can never go wrong with the pastrami sandwich. The quality of the meat and the care they take to carve/fill up your fresh heaping sandwich really says a lot about them! I am grateful we don't have to go up to NYC Katz Deli to get our fill. Such a special place and the only place I recommend eating at in Reading Terminal as everything else there has been a little underwhelming. You definitely have to eat these fresh as it gets messy.

I found the restaurant when I was turning around to get back to Bloomfield Ave and thought it had a nice look. I thought the food was very good and I'm surprised at what others are saying about it. The thinny thin Pizza is fantastic and the chicken savoy is just about the closest I've had to the Belmont Tavern. Michael the host didn't know me from adam & couldn't have made me feel more welcomed. I have told friends and family about this new restaurant & I highly recommend.
Service and food was excellent ... Family run...pizza and pasta was some of the best in the area, very nice atmosphere ..will go back very soon

We are from California visiting Newark. By far Vonda's is one of the best eateries for soul food. We had a variety off of the menu from Grits, collard greens, mac n cheese, chicken, waffles, biscuits and gravy, and French toast. It was all delicious and filling! And it was the one place there was actually parking. The hospitality was great. Vonda is a great cook! Can't say enough. Gotta visit this place if you have never been. I grew up on soul food and it beats some of the places in California hands down.

First time at Vonda's Kitchen and I couldn't have been happier! The staff was welcoming, the atmosphere was bright and friendly and Vonda greeted us herself a minute after we were seated. I had the ox tail with rice and beans - my first time for ox tail and it was great. I'll definitely be going back soon.
Food was great! Service was good! Place was crowded, that's always a good sign. My daughters salad was huge! Great Mac and cheese! Will return!

Gotta Love Vonda's!!! My Aunt Told me about this place....and when SHE reccomends a place i know its official!! and THAT it is!! Awesome FOOD....Great MENU!! Service is Great as Well...everyone was so courteous. Two Thumbs Up!
O my the fried fish was delightful.  And the macaroni and cheese is out of this world.  Only thing was the service is slow.  Otherwise everthing was great.  cant wait to come back.

Spice 28 breaks out from the usual mode of chinese restaurant, gets the young & trendy vibe going on w/ the contemporary interior & lounge music - good for party, not for 1st date though.  food is quite good.  these were what we had: mini wonton - wonton are good but the sauce makes it great - yum-yum-yum duck crepe - mild but great flavor; duck is tender & nicely done - yum-yum tom yum soup - miso base??  taste good but not impressive Szechuan peppercorn chicken - hot,  spicy, crunchy & w/ great flavor - better than what i had in Shanghai -yum-yum-yum drunken chicken noodle - absolutely yummy ; the use of basil is refreshing- yum-yum-yum eggplant - garlic- & tasty- too big a portion as side dishes though-yum-yum The manager Ben was gracious & friendly. Waitress we got was however inexperienced, but I have to admit that I am comparing it to upper scale restaurant services.  I will definitely go back for more.

Went here with 7 of my college friends. The food was great, well-priced, and large portions and the servers were very friendly. They let us bring about 60 beers and some wine, gave us an ice bucket, and helped remove beer from the table. On top of that, they gave us free dessert. All in all a great experience

Go here immediately. Order anything. Thank me later. We got takeout here for the second time last night, ordered entirely different items to get a sense of their range, and everything we got was incredible. This time when I got to the place to pick it up there were no hiccups with our order and it was ready promptly. I met the owner, Ben, who was very personable and genuine. I'm rooting for these folks, they've got a good thing going here! Also, they will have their liquor license this weekend and will be serving at their bar by Monday. The bar is really cool, backlit marble. When the order was ready I asked for a separate bag for the blue crab avocado salad, so as not to have it get hot in there with everything else. So glad I did! That thing was a masterpiece. A half of a perfect, ripe avocado filled with heaps of perfect crab salad with a spicy kick, and fresh greens with a lovely vinaigrette. E demolished it. I went for the thai basil style chicken, no onion no garlic, spicy. I ate almost the whole thing (good thing this was after the gym!). The sauce was so flavourful and it was packed with tender, moist chicken and string beans and peppers. I want it again right now even though it's 8am. E got the shrimp pad thai, mild, and it was pad thai perfection. The noodles were firm and springy with a light tamarind and peanut sauce and all the right fixins. He wasn't crazy about the pickled radish bits but I liked them. The shrimp alone are worth a shout-out: huge, well-cleaned, perfectly cooked, and 7 to an order of pad thai. The tails were left on but pulled off with ease. I stole one, and a bite of the noodles. Then some more of the noodles later with bites of my chicken. I kept going back to the kitchen after I cleared the food to snack on cold leftovers. We will not ever order from Circles again- when I want some good Asian food it's going to be Spice 28 all the way.

I keep going back to try the different entrees  and have not been disappointed. Food is great and love the drunken noodles with chicken. Happy to see they finally received the green light to serve drinks. The bar is beautiful and the drinks are interesting and good.

My bf and I came here for lunch since the menu looked enticing and the reviews were very positive.  We are so glad we did so! We ordered the roasted tomato salad as an appetizer and it was one of the best salads I've ever had.  My bf and I literally devoured it within a minute.  You can tell they used fresh produce and ingredients in creating this salad.  We were pretty surprised that such a seemingly simple salad could taste so good.   For entrees, I ordered the pad thai with vegetables (spicy) and bf ordered the green curry with shrimp.  They gave a good variety of vegetables in my pad thai with just the right amount of spice.  We were both very satisfied with our dishes.   At the end of our meal, we received a complimentary dessert.  It was a type of sweet potato sticky pancake and this was also really good! Amazing food at reasonable prices.  Service was great as well.   I would definitely come back to try their other dishes.  This restaurant is a hidden gem in the heart of Philly!

This is a nice place to visit. We had a large crowd with us, and the wait staff was patient and helpful. They deserve a big applause. The food options were pretty good, but not exceptional.  We found a lot of vegetarian and vegan options.  Be careful of the spices, as a 1, 2 or 3 on the menu really does mean it will be a spicy item.  The location is perfect for a center city crowd, but unfortunately the layout of the restaurant and the lack of sound proofing system made it nearly impossible to hear our guests.

Pretty good food here, we had pretty traditional fare (dry pot beef, spicy cold potato, fried rice) so I can't comment on the "fusion"  concept here but nothing on the menu looked bad in my opinion. Ambiance is kinda cool, but it feels like it would be pretty loud on a busy night. Wait staff was attentive and pleasant. If you're craving hot szechuan food but also need to please some folks with a more tender palate, this place has a lot to offer in terms of variety. If you are like me and just need the hot stuff, this place would come in a close second to Han Dynasty. Well worth a try if you're in the area.

I am a huge fan of the iron bound in Newark. I am also a huge fan of Latin food. This is a really cool place to experience the other side of Latin cuisine. Not the fancy dishes with cloth napkin service and premium bar drinks, but the real, neighborhood style, corner restaurants that one would frequent on a more casual basis. This is definitely a great place to go for a lazy lunch or super late night to try and soak up whatever you've just poisoned your internals with. the variety is huge, the portion is huge and the prices are perfect. Our waitress was quiet, but very nice and friendly. They are pretty busy so , if you are expecting platinum customer service and attention , this is not the place to go. Really, it's a place to chill out, get some great food and either plan your day or try and put the pieces together of your night and stumble back home. My steak sandwhich was outstanding. The bread was soft on the inside and perfectly crusty on the outside. The steak was huge but maybe could have use just a pinch more seasoning. The sauces they offer are tasty and it's fun to mix and match.

Alright! Im back! Altas Horas is the place to go on a Friday or Saturday night after having a few drinks. The hamburgers are ridiculously huge. They have a healthy sandwich called the Fat Free, which is grilled chicken breast lettuce tomato on rye bread. Also, They have freshly squeezed juices. My favorite is pineapple with mint. The service is not so hot. Its hit or miss sometimes. Depending who you got and who wants to make that big tip at the table. 3 Stars For Me.

Best Brazilian Burgers in Newark. What makes this is best is more than just the crazy toppings. You can get that at a bunch of places around here.  What makes this place the best is the burgers are actually cooked well.  Take away the Brazilian toppings and you still have a good burger.  The patty has a sear and isn't cooked all the way through, meaning that it's still moist.  You can't find a regular burger patty cooked so well at any other Brazilian place around here. Try the X-Banana.  Yes. Bananas on the burgers.  The bananas are slightly caramelized and compliments the thick slice of mozzarella on the burger.  I never thought bananas belonged on a burger. I stand corrected.

Perfectly done sandwiches, they're steamy hot! Flavor is great! Not the type where you find them just warm because its been sitting there and serve late. I would definitely go back for seconds~ Whenever I order bubble tea I usually end up not liking them because the tapioca is too hard but there is nice and soft! As for the sandwiches again, I've tried the traditional, grilled chicken, and pork and I've gotta say, their so mothwatering so it really depends on what you're in the mood for because each have their unique taste. Each is delicious! Try it! FYI: summer roll with shrimp soo savory with their sesame/peanut sauce!

I was so excited to take my new neighbor, a professional chef, to introduce to this SI institution.  Sadly I come away ready to be institutionalized.    We waited a half hour for a table and asked the server if we could start a tab.  I got my orange soda.  My friend never got her Blue Moon.  I also got to witness a guy choking and one of the bar regulars give him the Heimlich.  Probably a sign of what was to come.  When we finally did get the high bar table in the freezing cold drafty  doorway we only had to wait another 15 minutes to order her beer.  When the waitress did show up, we ordered everything at once, and explained we were starving, so could we start with the cole slaw?  Isn't the whole point of a restaurant to sell you food and drink?  We were waiting so long I joked aobut ordering a pizza and was ready to leave.  To sit there hungry and thirsty for so long and be ignored???  Really?  After we got our potato skins, I asked her again for the extra sour cream I ordered.  She came back with the cole slaws.   I never did get the sour cream.   When we got our burgers, I just asked for the check. When she came back to take away the dishes I asked again for the check and a box.  Someone else dropped the box  off, and when we went back to the service area to pay our check we got to wait some more.  Finally the arrogant busboy/manager/host asked how everything was.  I told him I never tip that badly, but never had service that bad.  He told me someone had a seizure and messed them up.  Since I saw the whole thing go down, I don't understand how it could have messed them up when it was  bar customer who saved him.  They were very obviously understaffed and both of us are in the business.  For him to tell me to have a nice night and ignore everything we went through added insult to injury.  The burger I had boxed I left in the kitchen on the way out.  The attitude was so bad I wouldn't even feed it to my dog.  After I paid $50 for it!   You can get away with murder as long as people feel someone cares about them.  It was obvious this place is run to generate as much money for a tiny staff, and no concern to the customer.  I shouldn't have to leave my dirty plates stacked on the side of the table  waiting 15 minutes to get a refill while screaming bar customers yell about the French, English and Jews.  I am ashamed for you!  This is hospitality?????????

There are two things you need to know about this place- 1. If you don't try a Duffy Burger (with cheese) then you're out of your mind.  2. You have to get the waffle fries with the Duffy Burger.   It's just so delicious.  The best burger I've had in my whole life.  I live in the neighborhood and every time my family gets together and can't figure out what to eat we just go up to Duffy's. It's a homely bar that's good for families to get together and hang out and catch up.   If you don't feel like having the burger (which I don't know why you wouldn't) the Chili is also amazing.  For a pub you wouldn't think of that as the first option, but it's an excellent choice. The bar usually has the regulars sitting there, so it's not a place for anyone in their younger ages to go and have a good night at, but if you want to just relax and throw back a cold one, then this is indeed you're location.

The best word that comes to mind when describing this place is: Sunday. The place feels the way Sunday does. When you're too bored to commit to going anywhere so you wanna read the paper in a bright and sunny establishment with a delicious iced coffee and eggs. The Egyptian Poached Eggs were one of a kind and so delicious! They are served on a cutting board over fresh arugula and crushed walnuts. Palette is unusual for a brunch spot but chance is nice! Come here if you're tired of the usual eggs benedict!

2 months ago I would've given it 5 stars.  I came every weekend, but I haven't been in months now, because they got rid of their regular breakfast menu and changed it with a brunch menu on the weekends.  What's wrong with that, right?  I love brunch!   Except the brunch menu is not good.   Nothing we ordered from the brunch menu matched the description on the menu.  I got the kale salad with grilled haloumi, but it wasn't served with grilled haloumi.  Also, the kale was just raw cut up kale, perhaps the chef prefers it this way, but every kale salad I've ever ordered (or made) has had the kale oil-rubbed to soften it.  Not here.   The french toast is tasty, but the menu said it had walnuts, and it didn't. I miss the healthier breakfast options. The coffee is great, pastries are great, and the ambience is lovely (much better than the hideous-cave vibe at Qathra), but I ain't going back until they bring back the BREAKFAST TACOS.  Or seriously fix up the brunch menu.   They need egg dishes that aren't as polarizing as the egyptian eggs (tried them, not my thing) or the salmon omelet (I often do not wake up and want to eat fish in the morning, personally; how about some other omelet options?). TL;DR:  Great coffee, they ruined brunch, bring back my breakfast tacos. Thanks!
Amazing ambiance, great food. However, they only take cash. NIcest coffee shop in Brooklyn. Staff are really nice.

While the ambience was divine, the food was not so delicious. There was a steady stream of customers coming in and out while I was there, which is good for business but, along with the loud music, made it difficult to concentrate on my book. I would give milk and honey a second shot, but it's not anything to obsess over.

The coffee is absolutely amazing, I've tried only half of their menu and everything so far is delicious and more than what I've expected. I live in the neighborhood and I'm definitely happy this is close to my house My favorite dish is probably the turkey avocado sandwich. Trust me, I believe everyone should try it
Amazing!!! Food blew me away, wine, ill be back!!

I'm reluctant to review this place because I don't want the secret to get out. However, I feel like I owe it to the amazing cooks and staff at Martha to tell you how extraordinary the restaurant is. I have been to Martha multiple times for dinner and once for brunch. I've been with parties of six and parties of two...all times were fabulous. My personal favorites for dinner are the Brussels Sprouts, Cauliflower, and fried chicken. My husband dreams about the egg noodles and duck sausage. For brunch I had the cast iron pancake and Sunny Egg and Greens. The perfect balance of sweet and salty. The cocktails are also very inventive. Martha, thank you for bringing great goodness to my life.

WOW!!! So now America, with an open heart and an empty stomach, I say unto you in the words of my uncle: 'Allez cuisine!' Today's secret ingredient is....... SALT! Iron chef of the America, thank you very much for a very generous amount of 'salt' and passion into your cooking. Pass the water please! I'm afraid I might bite my tongue to end the suffering. take my words with a grain of salt (not pun intended) we left the restaurant with a bloated stomach, a lighter wallet and learned a bad attitude. Felt a decline in my moral for not finishing the food and lick the plates, there are starving kids out there. Visit again? Not even with my worst enemy.

This place looks amazing when you walk in.  We came in without a reservation and they said it would likely be around 30 minutes.  After an hour (At 10:30 PM) we asked if a table would be ready anytime soon.  3 managers or hosts stood around saying they would "discuss" if they could get a table for us.  There were 4-5 booths available, and when we asked them about them they said that they wanted to make sure the kitchen could handle an additional table.  What??  They asked us to wait more and they would get back to us.  The tall manager with curly grey hair stood there with his hands in his pockets for 10 minutes making no move to seat us.  After asking him 3 times if they were going to seat us at one of the 4 tables they were staring at they again just said they were "working it out."  Unreal.  They just refused to seat us when they clearly knew we were waiting and there were tables available.  Is this really a Bobby Flay restaurant?  Is it really a NY restaurant?  This guy (The manager) is not qualified to run a professional establishment.  I am sure the place is great, but they have no idea what they are doing in terms of service...

Bobby Flay was cooking my food on a Saturday night. Doesn't get any better than this. I could not believe he was actually in the restaurant, and cooking all night long. This guy doesn't mess around. I ordered the Halibut, AMAZING, some veggie options and the mushroom paella. Everything was above and beyond my expectations. I was thinking, oh, here we go, another celebrity chef place... I was wrong. Amazing experience with amazing food. I did not have a reservation and noticed they opened at 530pm, so I went there at 5:45 and all the bar spots and opening seating areas were full. Assuming people actually stand in a line for this place to open? It literally took an hour and a half for that first group to leave and for me to find a seat, but luckily, I was in no hurry and they have great drinks.

Had a great experience at Bobby Flays new restaurant, Gato! I called ahead and found out they were booked for the night, so we decided to show up uninvited when the doors opened (nothing was stopping us from trying this place).  So, good news...We got seats at the bar facing bobby in the kitchen! Sweet! We tried the bar menu and ordered the lamb, chorizo, and 7 layer potato (everything was money - if I had to pick my favorite I'd say the chorizo).  This all went great with a glass of red wine. Next, I had the charred beef, and my girlfriend had the kale and mushroom paella.  Both were on point.  However, I think we missed out on the potato side dish.  Apparently we were the only ones that didn't get that dish.  Excuse to go back??? I think so

So good. Soooo good. So good. The roasted octopus was the best I've tried. The carrots were awesome. The eggplant was a bit oily, the chorizo was eh, the eleven layer potato was awesome. The kale and mushroom paella was really good but was overly salted. The porkchop was juicy and delicious. But when I reached the bone it was raw. The waiters also wouldn't stop pouring water every 5 seconds. Would come back to try others.

I LOVE Gato! I read somewhere that they are purposely not filling the restaurant to capacity so that the kitchen doesn't get overwhelmed. I think this is pretty smart since most new places get a ton of bad reviews based solely on "new" kinks like food taking too long, service not great, etc. So yes, its hard to get a reservation. I came here for a work dinner and got to try most of the menu. Everything was delicious. I had the egg appetizer and it was amazing, creamy and cheesy and it came with bread for spreading.  I had the lobster risotto for an entree and it was fantastic as well. I tried the beef, the pork chop, both pizzas options,and 4 desserts everything was so good. My only complaint would be that the cocktails could have been stronger. We moved on to wine after one cocktail. Bobby Flay himself is in the kitchen and he was nice enough to take a picture with my group who are big fans and not from NYC. All in all this is the best of Bobby Flay in my opinion and I have been to all of his restaurants in New York.

I thought that my experience for a $300 dinner at a Bobby Flay restaurant would be much better than what we experienced Saturday night. Ambiance/Decor: The restaurant gives you the feeling of being in a tapas bar in Sevilla. The brick roof with the arch motif, reminded me of the striped arches in La Mezquita in Cordoba, Spain. The beautiful tiled floors had a Moorish-Spanish look to it. The din in the dining room was just enough that I could hear my dinner-mate across the table and I wasn't required to raise my voice for her to hear me. All in all, the energy was energizing. Service: Firstly, our server suggested we order from the 'bar' menu, an app, and an entree. We ended up ordering two apps, the spreads, a vegetable side, and an entree each and it was far too much food. Next, we were instructed to put our entire order in at once and that the kitchen will time when our food comes out. We ordered the spreads (3 spreads with pita), the lamb sausage pizza, and the grilled octopus as appetizers. All three were brought to our table at once. I'm not too sure about timing, by the time we would have finished our pizza, then the octopus would have been cold, or vice versa. Also, if we had started with our spread, then the two warm apps would have been cold. I would have expected the kitchen to have known to brought out our food in waves so that we could enjoy them as they are just coming out of the kitchen. As part of our entree course, we had ordered the crispy potatoes, which comes with a poached egg on top of it. When we received the potatoes, the egg on top looked more like a mangled egg that was dropped and the yolk left back in the kitchen. When we asked about it to our server, he explained at all of the yolk had probably seeped to the bottom of the dish, which made me wonder how long our plate was sitting waiting for it to be served. Food: All of the food was delicious. We ordered the following: - Lamb Sausage Pizza - Grilled Octopus - Gato Spreads (yogurt base, chickpea base, white bean base) - Crispy Potatoes - Rabbit with Fregula Sarda - Beef with blue cheese butter Everything was delicious and well cooked; my recommendation is the grilled octopus and the rabbit. I thought that the lamb pizza was overrated - it was a large app serving of pizza with few pieces of lamb sausage on it. Also, all of the spreads were standout Cleanliness: Gato has 3 restrooms for the entire restaurant. At one point in time, there was a line out in front, which I found very surprising. I don't recall seeing that too often at high end restaurants. If so, then I don't recall being able to see it from the dining room. When both me and my dinner-mate went to use the bathrooms, they were in terrible shape. I thought I was at a bar toilet around around last call - there was urine all over the seat, not to mention the floor. It was disgusting and I almost wanted to wait until I got home. Other than the food, everything else at the restaurant was poorly executed. I would expect that a new restaurant for a new chef might have some starting pains, but Bobby Flay is a brand with 6+ restaurants and I expected more. I recommend people should wait for the restaurant team to work out the kinks in operations before having a $300 meal, in order to spare them from the dismal experience we had at Gato.

Just got engaged last night there! So happy! The food was really good. We had the crab rossito and the halibut and was so good. Clarissa the pastry chef makes the best dessert in the world!!! Amazing!!

So, if you show up within the next few weeks, you actually get to see bobby flay (which is a pretty awesome) He'll be behind glass pane windows that everyone's ogling over and "working the line" making sure his plates come out flawless.   It was pretty intense for myself considering early that morning, he was grilling lamb sausage on cooking channels' "boy meets grill," only to later that night, serve me pizza with ofcourse, lamb sausage. Speaking of his plates, this is what I recommend.: -EGGPLANT MANCHEGO, OREGANO, BALSAMIC -ELEVEN LAYER POTATO CARAMELIZED SHALLOTS, FRIED SAGE -SCRAMBLED EGGS ALMOND ROMESCO, BOUCHERON CHEESE, TOMATO CONFIT TOAST -TARRAGON CHICKEN CRISPY POTATOES, GOAT CHEESE, DANDELION -KALE AND WILD MUSHROOM PAELLA CRISPY ARTICHOKES, EGG The first 2 are from the bar menu: they arrive with delicateness in mind and you have to cherish each bite, as they're only a few to be had. the eggplant was my favorite. The next one is THE way to go. you're thinking scrambled eggs? for dinner but they are most definitely the fluffiest eggs you'll eat in your life. I read somewhere that inmates on death row are requesting it as their last meal. yea, that good... Finally, my gf and I both found our entrees to be too salty. Her chicken enough to be sent back and changed.  My paella was delicious and the runny egg mixed table-side was a great touch but maybe the lack of protein got to me. Overall, a great date spot with chic décor and outstanding service. Nice work, Bobby.

Food: 10/10 recommendations are any sandwich, the chicken and chorizo empanadas, any coffee beverage especially espresso, and whatever pastry looks interesting to you. (I'm not huge on pastries) When to go: Breakfast, Lunch, or Brunch Size: small to medium for café Ambiance: Lively Spanish music, mostly merengue, bachata, salsa, and sometimes Spanish pop. Interior: Modern with Caribbean influence yellow walls and beautiful paintings that are actually for sale hung up on the walls. Restrooms: Yes, single room but clean so, fellas don't forget to clean up and ladies you too! I hate that people think they can leave public spaces dirty just because they assume someone else will clean it.
