What makes this place great: The fact that the theme is attractive, if they greet you in Spanish, it's on purpose and only serves to bring you more into a place of wonderful Cuban heritage and influence. You will enjoy this place and if you know Cuban Pete's in Montclair, this cafe is like it's little sister.
The food was excellent. Great coconut cupcake. Amazing ham croquet. The service was the best. Great place and highly recommend.
This was our first time here and we loved it! Great ambiance, salsa music playing in the background, cheery decor, and great pastries. Will return.

Went here for the first time recently. The Taiwanese beef noodle soup was amazing. Haven't had one this good in so long. The broth was rich and flavorful, the noodles were homemade and had a great chew and the bit of picked vegetables tied it together perfectly. Scallion pancakes were also excellent. Took some dumplings and 3 cups chicken home. Dumplings were so so. 3 cups chicken had a great sauce but be prepared for bones-it's basically thighs chopped into small pieces which Americans who are not used to chewing through things like us chinese may not be used to. Get the beef noodle soup, you will not be disappointed.

Came for brunch. For $15 (although they tried to charge me $18 contrary to the menu price), the steak and eggs was fine, arguably too salty although I enjoyed that aspect of it. My gf got the "eggs of New York" which tasted like poached eggs on top of plain tomato paste on top of polenta. I have no idea where they came up with that idea. The place was pretty dark for brunch and our waitress made limited appearances despite the place not being busy (surprisingly) on the first beautiful Sunday of 2014. The food was on the slow side. It was not expensive at all though (all in $20/pp), so I cannot complain too much.

I waited until I'd visited this place 4-5 times before writing a review. It was a rockier start but they finally found their pasta-making footing and I am quite pleased. The place is "just" busy enough to feel lively but not so busy you feel like screaming. Service is usually spot on and they run late night hours. Score. I would say their pastas are better than apps and meats though. Stick with me, you'll do well. You're welcome.
Good brunch - selection of classic brunch dishes with eggs and pastas.  Ricotta pancakes - were perfect.  Exceptional service.

We came here for brunch and had the most awful customer service experience. The waiter took forever to get us water (I had to ask her several times). She took forever and a day to get our orders (even though we kept trying to wave her down several times). And then she messed up all of our payments. This brunch took 3 hours for a party of 5 people. We had a wedding dress appointment after and we had to RUN to make it there on time. Also, there's only ONE stall for a bathroom -__- The ONLY reason I'm not giving this only one star because granted the food was great. I ordered a spaghetti bolognese which was delicious! So, pagani - please get your servicing right!

This place is officially my favorite Asian restaurant in the Princeton area. The atmospehere is beautiful and the staff is very courteous. I have been here twice so far and the only real down side to this place is that it's pretty pricey depending on what you order. It's definitely worth it if you want a nice night out. The sushi was incredibly fresh and everyone in my group loved their food. The three creme brulee dessert was surprising. Who knew coffee and green tea creme brulee could be so good? Overall this place was an amazing dining experience. I was pleasantly surprised considering its location. Definitely give it a try!

I would give 3.5 stars. I liked the place and it has a lot of potential. I didn't dislike anything we had but it seemed a little short of what it could be. We started off with miso soup and the lettuce wraps. Soup was very good and flavorful. The lettuce wraps were served with an awkward, stripped down piece of lettuce - cut to 4 strips of 2 inches by 5 inches or so. As with many places, this inevitably leaves a lot of filling left over. Also, they served with a very hot sirachi sauce rather than offering a variety. Most had sushi for the rest of the meal. Good taste, fresh and well formed. Only suggestion here is to not put the wasabi in a ball that looks a little odd - not the nice, light green color in a little pyramid like pile. Small but it really shows inexperience or lack of attention to detail. For desert, had the ice cream tempura. They lit it on fire which left a burnt taste on the pallet along with a little bit doughy in the inside. Would suggest being a bit more simplistic and just go for a nice chocolate sauce. Prices aren't unreasonable. Very nice Devore. But would say that Mizu on Clarksville is just as good on the food and I would end up paying 15-20% less. Still, I would recommend going and will go back myself. Hopefully, owners are looking and expecting feedback.

Really nice! The interior is gorgeous and unexpected. Something about the place gave me the impression that there would be a bar, but it doesn't look like there is one. Food was very good, a bit expensive. I tried the sushi, the fried rice and an appetizer. Two complaints: the tablecloths aren't anchored down to the table, so they slip and slide while you eat. Also, the coffee and tea was $4.50 a cup - way too expensive. The restaurant is across Meadow Road from MarketFair - it's a bit hard to see unless you're looking for it. The easiest way to get there is to turn onto Farber Rd from Route 1.

we always enjoy going to Kotos.  It's our daughter's birthday this week and this is the restaurant she has choosen for her special dinner.... much to our delight.  We always fine the food and staff wonderful!  And noticed the last time we went how nice it is to meet such wonderful people (including other guests) each time we go!
Excellent service and food. Great place to take my daughter when I visit her at Montclair state.

I went for my birthday last week and the food was really good. The staff is friendly and the server was attentive and nice. I ordered there filet mignon medium per the servers request and it was absolutely delicious!
The chicken stix, veggie crisps, lentil salad and Greek fries were amazing. Paired with a red Sangria and finished off with kataifi made for the most amazing meal ever.

My husband and I were looking for a casual place to eat before going to see a movie  sunday and walked into this place. We are always looking for healthy options as my husband is getting ready to run a marathon. The manager at the front- a delightful young woman- started chatting with us and told us that all of the food was organic. We ordered the spread symposium which came with whole wheat pita bread, tuna stix, chicken stix, and farmers blue cheese with organic veggies. The tuna was seared to perfection and the salad was delicious. My husband said that he will be back for lunch now too. Great food and friendly service.

Stix is a special kind of hopeless.  They are good at one thing, and one thing only - meat on a skewer.  Anything else - the soups, the salads, the sides, and the Stix that have more than one ingredient, like the chef's special stix, are anything from mediocre to inedible. I couldn't get more than one bite into the Chef's Special stix or the chicken soup.  The salad my companion and I shared was OK, but it was simply acceptable.  The pork stix were actually good, but they represented $3 of a bill that was over $50. The staff is both inattentive and pushy - I had a waiter suggesting half of the menu to me in an attempt to get a bigger sale, but when it came time to serve, the drinks took forever, and the entrees were brought out before the starters.  Speaking of the drinks, the drafts are about a half serving for full price - for $8, I expect a pint. No need to be this disappointed in this neighborhood.

I took my Greek friend here yesterday for a belated birthday brunch.  She had been talking about it for weeks as a place I needed to try, and I always take advice from someone who is a native. We were in heaven.  Rather than ordering from the brunch menu (that looked great) we decided to order a feast of different "stix" and sharing plates.  Everything was fantastic, and a few things stood out.  the veggie crisps,  spicy cheese spread, Greek fries, kataifi, and corsica cocktail were all delicious.  My absolute favorites were the tzatziki, which was so fresh with tiny chunks of cucumber, as well as the feta sauce that came with the sack of potatoes - just amazing.   The atmosphere was wonderful, and the staff was amazing.  I was quite impressed with the fact that the owner was not only present in the restaurant the entire meal, but he greeted each table many times.  Not just to ask how things were, but as if we were family.   I enjoyed myself so much that I changed the location for my meeting this evening from one of my other favorite places in the city to Stix.  Now if they figure out how to get saganaki on a stick, I'm never leaving!   Thank you for a wonderful time!

Wonderful personal service. Great food!! Priced well. Get the veggie chips app. Get it all, like we did. Great for groups! Nothing on the menu disappointed. The owner is the nicest most welcoming and affable man!! Five stars!
Everything was soooo delicious! Kale, fries, meat sticks.Wanna go back.

Woohoo, Mexican in Fairmount! We went into Calacas with high expectations. And for the most part they hit the spot. The fish tacos were solid, the carnitas tacos were pretty great, and the corn was delicious. And warm, endless chips. Yum. The staff was attentive and friendly, but really worked for the up-sell. My only major complaints were drink-related. The margaritas were mostly ice, unfortunately, and didn't feel worth the $7.50. To that end, when we arrived happy hour was going on for drinks ordered at the bar, but the deal didn't extend to the tables, which was kind of a bummer. These are minor issues, though, considering Tecate is $3. All in all, a good choice, and perhaps a new neighborhood staple.

I'm always happy when a new Mexican place opens up in the city so I went with some friends to check it out last night.  We had reservations for 7:30pm (note: they only take reservations for parties of 6 or more). The bar area is small and cramped and was packed.  Once we squeezed past that we were lead into a large, stylish dining room with big round booths to accommodate large groups. Our server was friendly and attentive, our waters were refilled multiple times without having to ask.  The food is delish.  I started out with an order of nachos split with a friend.  It's big enough to be an app for 2 people. I'd describe the nachos as fancy without being pretentious - fresh jalapenos, some other type of pepper, refried black beans, melted cheese with microgreens on top - and NO soggy chips!  The plantains were well seasoned and tasty.  I had the carnitas tacos which were divine with flavorful juicy tender pork.  I sampled my friend's campechano tlayuda (flatbread-like with shortrib, chorizo, beans & queso).  The flavor was good but the crust was too chewy.  I guess a thin and crispy crust isn't possible with all that stuff weighing it down. I had no complaints with my Feliz margaritas. Nice addition to the Fairmount area!

Great food, cute decor and friendly, fast service.  No free chips and salsa for the table though ;( Chorizo Fundido-  deilcious.  Then again, who doesn't love melted cheese and chorizo. Fish Tacos- 2 tacos with large fried , perfectly cooked pieces of tilapia over a pickled cabbabge slaw.  Only downfall- didn't come with salsa or guacamole, but delicious nonetheless. Pretty busy for a Thursday night, but we had reservations so were seated quickly.  Comfy semi-circle booth to accommodate 5 of us.  The bar area is pretty narrow though so it's not conducive to standing around.  Definitely will be back again!

The one time I was here I unfortunately was in a rush, but what I can say is that the Pizza with Prosciutto was excellent. They have a selection of italian craft beers including some larger format Baladins and others, which is great. They have an exposed hot water pipe in the bathroom with a clear sign warning that the pipe is hot. Upon not heeding that warning I was underwhelmed by the temperature of the pipe - minus .5 stars.
if there was an option to do half stars, I'd do 4 1/2... we had the Regginella, but we preferred the Popeye. the perfect start to a new year.

went back again this weekend.. The Laura pie is a thing of beauty.. Friendly service, they now have beer and wine.. The beer is interesting as it's all this crafted beer from Italy.. And while I love the idea and respect it, let's have some offerings that are not 15 bucks for a pint.  There is one 6 dollar offering which is nice but, they did not have any light beer, not even a crappy Peroni. Calzones remain delicious.

I went here for the lunch buffet and bit into a ball of spice in my curry that was 1 inch in diameter.  The spice on the inside started crumbling into the curry, as well as in my mouth.  Thus, the rest of my meal tasted like dirt.  I was very unhappy. For a place that serves curried spice balls, it's overpriced.

Delicious homemade lemonade. And BUFFALO CHICKEN SANDWICH is to die for. It comes on a huge roll, cut in half. I couldn't finish will all the bread but definitely eat every bite of the buffalo chicken, with buffalo sauce.  Comes with a side salad. Plain greens. Simply delicious.
LOVEEEEEE IT!!! Everything is delish!   Always packed. Be ready to wait for a seat for al least 45 minutes or so..

Great brunch menu + great staff + great location Chili - a bowl of chili with blue nachos! It's not the creamy chili I love but it was still good. I mixed it when my tofu scramble to get the perfect consistency and it was fabulous. A tad beany but hey, who would complain about more protein? Mozzarella sticks - WOAH I don't have to travel to long island for mozzarella sticks?!? These are so good! The bread crumbs that hold the cheese in place is super thin and the mozzarella is melted perfectly, creamy and thick. You'll get the cheese drag after biting into it. So addicting! And it doesn't have the fake cheese taste! Tofu Benedict - I never had egg benedict so I can't compare but if it tastes like this then I've been missing out for so many years! The yellow sauce tasted so familiar but I couldn't figure out what the ingredients were. The tofu looked and tasted like egg; it still amazes me how they do it. Then there's a fake meat, that looks and tastes like Canadian bacon! Woot woot. I loved Canadian bacon. The only downside to this dish was the biscuit. I'm not a fan of biscuits because it's usually super dry. I thought benedicts were on English muffins or is that just frozen breakfast packages? Tofu scramble - how do they make this!? I need to learn the recipe. The egg consistency is spot on! Love it. It doesn't have a strong tofu taste, you couldn't even tell it's tofu! This is legit tofu scramble. Half order of French toast- It's moist and soft inside, crisp on the outside with the perfect toast markings and color of French toast, and it's vegan! Say what?! Chocolate milkshake - not the thick milk shake consistency I was hoping for. It was basically chocolate soy milk. Pineapple coconut muffin - the first thought that came into my head was a corn muffin texture. Or you could think of this like a macaroon with dried sweetened pineapple. Cheesecake brownie - dry cheesecake on top of a mushy brownie. Coconut whoppie pie - sugar overload! I have a high tolerance for sweets unless it tastes like pure sugar and this did. Cinnamon bun - I wanted to try this for a few years now. I always called to see if they had it. What was the big deal with this? It's dry and the they put way too much frosting. I checked in on yelp for my free coffee and the waitress gave us two with almond milk!
Came back for breakfast the next day and it was equally as amazing. Great food!

Overall, the food is awesome (though there are some real duds on the menu), the service is really nice (but a little flaky), and sometimes it's a long wait to get a table. Highlights: the fish burrito, the philly cheesesteak, the chicken and biscuit, and the chicken and waffles. The food is insanely filling and really comforting, and the space is really cozy. Items to avoid: the banh mi has way too much bread and seems to be made a bit randomly depending on the particular cook. The breakfast burritos are all too carby and pale in comparison to the fish one. The fries used to be spiced way more (and tasted way better!). Wish they'd go back to that, but maybe I've just had the wrong cook a few times in a row now. Really reliable, very affordable, overall a great spot.
I like the potato breakfast bowl.

came here on saturday with my sister for my birthday. we only waited for a little while outside before someone brought us to a little table by the window. it's really small inside--but decorated real cute. like a cozy-classic-retro-punk-diner. or something. in a case up front, they have all their desserts displayed. yummy. i chose the build-your-own-burger with pulled pork, and made it a melt on sourdough for a total of 8.50 for the sandwich. oh my GOD it was so delicious!! i was worried that i wouldnt be full with just a salad, but believe me, it was enough. (and it was grilled/fried. i love that.) it was crowded, but our waitress was attentive, and was patient with us while we chose our desserts. for the desserts, i got a cheesecake brownie, and a slice of red velvet cake to go. the cheesecake brownie was ginormous. it was good, but not great--the cheesecake part was perfect, but the brownie was a bit dry and...not brownie-like. the red velvet cake, on the other hand, was AMAZING. super moist and rich and decadent, with delicious frosting. wow. also, bottomless cups of coffee are $2. YAY!

The mushroom burger is the star attraction of this place. I took a friend who likes conservative places and she went with a really negative attitude. She had the mushroom burger and said she wished she could lick her plate. (When she was finished, it look like she did.) The grass fed beef burger is also great, as are the fish tacos. If you like Margueritas, Duino makes them fresh. No mixer. Yes this is where the hipsters hang. I am not one, but I get a kick out of observing. The range of people who go to Duino from hipsters to oldsters like me is fun also. Varied music also, although tonight, the loud horns and drum solo made it impossible to hear. Drum solos and blaring horns are not a good choice for such a small establishment. Only problem with this place is the inconsistent service. Sometimes the food is amazingly fast, other times ridiculously slow, So don't plan on this place if you are short for time.

This is a great cafe right by Columbus Park with delicious coffee, baked goods, pastries, and sandwiches. Also, they take card which is less than most places besides the large chains can say. Everything I've had so far is super delicious and the baked goods are hot and fresh out of the oven whenever I walk in. I'd recommend this place to anyone and will never be going back to Dunkin Donuts or Starbucks.

Welcome back Mundo!  I was delighted to hear they are open again & I was looking forward to see what they've created. Menu was very similar to their old one with some favorite dishes available (red sonja, carrot dip, veggie wrap, etc) but I was actually hoping for a food more options. The other reason for only 4 stars is the portion sizes vary between tapas style & entrée and it's not very clear on the menu.  I loved everything we ordered but we needed to order side dishes to supplement.   Decor, Location,  Service...5 STARS! I will be back & I'm bringing friends to ensure they stay around for a long time! I truly wish Willy & the gang continued success as they aspire to give the neighborhood what it is lacking. Keep your eyes out for new dance nights for their large downstairs space!

I can't tell you how happy my family was with our recent Bar Mitzvah at Mundo.   We live in Manhattan and were looking for a unique environment for our celebration.  We looked at many locations in the city and in this neighborhood, but couldn't find a location that satisfied all of our needs.  When we first visited Mundo at the Paper Factory, we knew that this would be a perfect place for our party.   The manager and staff were amazingly accommodating and provided a great deal of support in regards to planning our party.  They provided us guidance regarding the decorations, food choices, organization of space, placement of entertainment, and helped manage the entire evening.   The decor at the Mundo and the Paper Factory are amazing.  We received great feedback from our guests in regard to the food and environment.  The Paper Factory and Mundo is a hotel that you would expect to see in Soho.   My family all stayed at the hotel, and were very happy. Thanks to all of the staff at Mundo and the Paper Factory for helping us put together an amazing and memorable evening.

So glad Mundo is back! We loved it in its old location and are so pleased to see them reopened in a beautiful new location. The food and service are just as wonderful, if not more so, and we had a fantastic time here a few weeks ago. Red Sonja, I've missed you! And the Zen cocktail is delicious. Go, enjoy! We can't wait to return.

Country looking spot great for a weekend brunch. The space is small and gets very crowded. They offer a text waiting list system that would alert you when your table is ready. The menu has creative and diverse options. The staff was very friendly and attentive. Be aware that there is only one Unisex bathroom and lines can also get long. I had the pastrami Hash, and it was served within few minutes of ordering. Overall, great place to enjoy breakfast and lunch (you know what I mean).

We went to this place because it was rated highly. It took half an hour to 45 minutes to get our food. Admittedly, it was pretty crowded but still, why does it take so long to make a sandwich and scrambled eggs? The sandwich (egg, avocado and bacon) was pretty tasty. The scrambled eggs came with super dry toast and extremely oily potatoes that were otherwise tasteless.

This place was really great! I read about it on yelp, and knew that there was going to be a bit of a wait for a Sunday brunch, so I was prepared when I put my name down and was told it was going to be about 40 minutes. The place is really small, but quaint, so I knew there wasn't a ton of room for seating. The host asked if I wanted to leave my cell phone number, and he'd text me when our table was ready. I thought that was a nice feature, since there wasn't a ton of room to wait around in, and this allowed you to come and go as you wanted without risk of losing your spot in line. The wait was pretty much spot-on and in 45 minutes we were offered a spot at a communal table. Not what I was expecting, but it was nice nonetheless. We ended up sitting next to this family that had just left B&H and was talking about cameras, and my dining parter was actually interested in the camera this guy had, so there were a few moments when we were all chatting together about camera. The people you meet in NYC... Anyway, we both had coffee and the BELT, bacon, egg, lettuce and tomato with an herbed aioli on sourdough. I added avocado to mine, my dining partner added caramelized onions and white pepperjack cheese. Mine was absolutely delicious, she said hers was too! We shared some of their homemade biscuits. The whole meal was pretty much a home run success! I didn't even really mind the wait because the food was so awesome. Wish they had a place like this in OKC! I'll be dreaming of that sandwich for a while!
Really good for GF people. The owner was there today, and said they have a separate fryer and use separate utensils.  The pastrami Reuben is outstanding.

We came here for brunch one Sunday afternoon and had a great time.  We loved that we could just put our name in with the hostess and get cocktails some place else, as the restaurant doesn't have room for it.  Once our table was ready, she texted us and we immediately came back to an open table!  Had the chicken and waffles and fried green tomatoes benedict.  Loved it all!  Great food and cocktails, and a fantastic farm to table with the freshest ingredients; we will be back.

BOTTOMLESS MIMOSA and brunch at mezetto is the best decision you'll ever make. For $16, you can sit there and drink different flavored mimosas (peach, pineapple, passion fruit, orange) for hours. It's one of the best mimosas I've ever had and the waiter is very quick to refill your glass. My friends got about 5 glasses each and the waiter didn't question us once. In fact, he gave me a free glass of mimosa on the house because I was the only one not drinking. He was super sweet and I really appreciated the thoughtful gesture. The brunch menu was great. I had the eggs benedict which was delicious. But my hats go off to the chef for the potatoes. They were the crispiest little gems ever. Perfectly flavored and tender on the inside while maintaing a crispy skin! My friends loved their dishes as well: baked eggs and french toast. The french toast was topped off with the sweetest figs. I had one and I could not stop raving about how good they were. The honey coating really blew them out the roof. The small details in each dish made me appreciate it even more. I would love to come back and try out their dinner menu. I saw the appetizers menu and they all sound amazing... I mean chorizo meatballs and chickpea crab cakes?! I WANT THEM ALL

I went there for brunch with 2 friends on Sunday.  We did not partake in the bottomless mimosas deal- but we were the odd ones out. Seemed like the majority of the restaurant was enjoying this deal Coffee was good - the tea, not so much. It took quite a while to get our food.  We had a mixup and the mistake was rectified quickly.   We ordered the steak hash and the pork belly Benedict.  Both were good, but the potatoes are a bit dry. Asked for hot sauce and got this amazing chili paste - yummy. :-) Tried a dessert with caramel and pistachios , can't remember the name- but it was delicious :-)

The food was very lack luster. No flavor and served lukewarm. The mimosa flavors are tasty (pomegranate, orange, passion fruit, peach), but are not worth the slow service and mediocre meal. Better brunches are out there!

Wanted to introduce my kids to Middle Eastern food, so we tried some take out from Aladdin Halal.  I drove in to the city and picked up some food while they were at soccer and it worked out great!  They loved the shawarma and the chicken kebabs.  Additionally, I thought the falafel and the tabbouleh were out of this world.   Looking forward to trying some other menu items. The only small problem was finding parking.  I ended up paying $5 to park in the adjacent lot after finding no street parking.  It was a small price to pay however for the great food.  Prices were pretty good - about $30 got us enough for three people for dinner, with a generous amount of leftovers.

Recently, I was asked to plan a very special surprise birthday dinner party for a very special lady. I knew I chose the perfect place from my first inquiry. I met with Jordanna, the Capital Grille sales manager, who could not have been more gracious and knowledgeable.  She customized the menu for our group of more than 20, so that  everyone would have many delicious choices.  The room was most attractive, and the waitstaff, Martha and Mark, were professional and efficient.  They anticipated our every need and made certain the party flowed seamlessly. The manager, Lee, was most welcoming...and a surprise visit to the birthday gal from Chef Nick was great fun. The food was beautifully presented, and the whole experience was as good as it gets. Don't wait for your next "special occasion" to dine at the Capital Grille.....life is too short !

ordered an arugula salad , and it came laces with literally spoonfuls of sugar - thought it was a prank and it wasnt!  need i say more. In one word , disgusting. only takes one terrible dish, and poor service (extremely long between courses) to spoil a meal. There's too many great restaurants in nyc to up tolerate a shocker dish.

Wow! Overall pretty impressed with presentation, taste, and service. I had the ahi tuna for an appetizer and it was delicious! The crunch that the chef put on the bottom was an outstanding compliment to the smooth-textured tuna. I also enjoyed the lobster orzotto. That was by far the best fish of the night and a must have if you ever go there. I love how they did a risotto out of the orzo rice, and the flavors of the sauce. JUST OUT IF GHIS WORLD. My waiter recommended the prawns and the whole fish for an entree and I must say I wish I could remember the name of the whole fish because it was delicious. It started with an L and was a sea bass but wow they nailed that one. I also was able to try the lamb. It was also delicious and wonderfully cooked. For the sides I ordered the feta mash potatoes, brussel sprouts, and this other very hard to remember name. Feta mash potatoes were delicious! Wow a must have. I cannot remember the name of the other side but it was delicious. It had eggplant and potatoe and cheese (my waiter described it as sort of like a lasagna but with out the noodle). It was so delicious! ALSO GET THE GREEK SALAD. A normal dish but wow the fresh tomatoes were so good! And the desert was amazing. I had this one custard desert. Very well prepared and delicious! Last, I must give a round of applause to the service. Usually you get the stuck up waiter recommending the most expensive meal so his tip can go up, but here everything the waiter recommended was amazing. I was impressed with the service and all of the amazing food that came with it. Definitely stop and check this place out of you ever visit nyc!

Tiny, but cute.  I like the fresh food market vibe, and its doesn't smell fishy like your typical fish market, so that's good.  Yummy wines and even yummier oysters!   I didn't think it was that expensive - i mean, would you eat raw oysters from some place that had cheap prices? YOu get what you pay for and the oysters were great and the descriptions were very good.. briny, sweet, meaty.. they all hit the mark.    It seemed to get crowded and there wasn't a lot of space but it didn't seem like people were waiting too long to get seated... Have to go back soon!

Hi my name is Katie, and i have a little problem (well one of many). So I tend to order mussels at all sorts of questionable places in this city,  many more times than I could possible count. My favorite place being Flex Mussels - seriously amazeballs. I suggest you have all your first dates there or just ask me to come with you anytime.  My least favorite being Ashton's bar, I went to a few weeks ago and tried to give myself food poisoning from ordering their Mussel Diablo.   Anyway the point of my rambling confession is - I like Prince Edward Island mussels (a lot) and can easily put away close to a pound of them. Which coincidentally is what Wild Edibles offers in addition to OLD BAY fries for 17 bucks. Given that I grew up in Maryland, I generally refer to old bay seasoning as crack. Honestly it should go on nearly everything non-dessert like. Minus one star because they have slow delivery and they stop taking orders around 8:30pm. Also if my company wasn't paying for it, I would say that they are tad too pricey. I will definitely order from them again and I need to try the oysters and fish given that is more what they are more well known for.... mmmm food.
I'll sum it up for you in one statement - food was good, but service sucked. Come on, one person and a bartender for serving people? Try somewhere else.

service wasn't great. I overheard the day shift bartender/server talking to the night shift person loudly that they wanted to scream at everyone walking in and he can see the "a**holes coming from a mile away". We ordered the oyster special with the pint of beer and the east coast oysters were so small they were barely edible. The Mahi Mahi we ordered was greasy and flavorless. Also the front serves as a fish market which is cute but customers sign there receipts at the bar which is where I happened to be sitting. I was really excited to try this place but left feeling ripped off and disappointed.

I went on 9-8-2013 with my son. We were seated right away. We received the coleslaw and pickles almost as we sat down.  We watched as others came and were seated.  We watched the waitresses going to other tables taking their drink orders. We just got back from a hike so we were very hungry and thirsty.  My son is 9 and wanted a drink badly.  I taught him good manners so he wasn't loud about it.  After people were seated next to us and got their drink orders, well you guess it, we left.  I will never, ever go back or tell anyone to go there. They put a VERY bad taste in my mouth without even trying the food.
OMG!!! The service and good has been excellent every time my wife and I have attended.
I came here with my girls and they loved it! Very relaxing atmosphere and at the same time, perfect to chit chat and eat quality food.

One of the best Italian food I've had after (genuine homemade Italian food). Much better than Olive Garden or some the chain restaurants. They start with bread topped with tomato sauce and then garlic bread. The food was so simple and fresh, felt like Nonna was in the kitchen preparing it. You want good Italian food this place is worth a try.

Splash is located on a floating dock ON lake champlain.  You really can't beat the location, especially when the afternoon sun is drifting over the lake.  The dock/bar is also home to some large yachts which make for great day dreaming.  While the drinks were pricey, $9 cocktails, I couldn't help but sit there with a big smile on my face, enjoying my drink, the view, and my fantasy of owning one of the large speed boats.

The drinks and food were both overpriced, and when I asked about freshness/local foods, my server told me the majority of food was premade/frozen from Sysco (Gross!) While sitting and trying to enjoy my mediocre (at best) food, it was hard to relax while watching the employees running about (several had completely sweated through their shirts), as the owner was schmoozing and drinking at the bar. Although the view was beautiful, it hardly seems to warrant paying a very steep bill for poor food, drinks and overworked staff DON'T GO!!
LIke everyone else said, the silken tofu here is cheap and delicious.  Definitely a fan.
I love their tofu pudding with honey and ginger.
Cheese Tudo.  Large sandwiches. The appetizers are great . Cappuccino are also good .service is pretty quick. Place looks like it clean. Try some chicken balls(not anything you are thinking)lol.
Had the jumbo sandwich,  Chinese idli, paper dosa and kusta kachori. Everything was really yummy but loved the Chinese idli. So different too!

Found this little gem on a bike ride. Such a cute little eatery.  Stopped for coffee, but wound up getting breakfast.  The pumpkin pie pancakes sounded (and looked) delicious, but they tasted like plain pancakes.  I think there was pumpkin in them, but they definitely needed some pumpkin spices to seal the deal. The coffee was good, the service, was good and the food was good. They also had free wi-fi. However, the place was very old-fashioned feeling and looking. I would definitely come back. 4 stars!
Great food, great service, really lovely place. Veggie panini was delicious! Will definitely return.

When you eat here, you'll feel like you are eating at someone's cozy house. The food is all homemade. It's like your mom is in the kitchen cooking it rather then some chain eatery chef. They have lots of lunch and dinner specials. If you love a huge breakfast with all the trimmings you can't beat the hungry human platter. The prices are really good too. A nice cozy place for a good priced meal.

Love this place. I'm never unsatisfied. There is indoor and outdoor seating and they have lovely cats that live on the property that are so nice. The food is amazing. I'm vegetarian and my favorite item is the chicken and black bean wrap - they always let me sub the chickens with mushrooms or anything I want. Fries are great. Service is great. Been there for breakfast lunch and dinner. Went here on Valentine's Day and it was great service. The Owners are nice and courteous. They also have great coffee and milkshakes. I just moved and I miss this place so much. I highly recommend trying it out. The servers are great. The last time I went with my bf and he started to drink through his straw and a waitress turned around and said it sounded like there was a crack or hole in it and gave us extras which I thought was thoughtful and good service.

I have been to Chestnut Cafe numerous times over the past two years, and it continues to be my favorite eatery in town. Family-owned with a very comfortable and friendly atmosphere. May get a little crowded on weekends, but definitely worth the wait, if there is a wait. All of the menu items are great, but my favorites are the Buffalo Eggs Benedict, Signature Croissant French Toast, and Mediterranean Chicken dinner.

I had the privilege to dine here for my first time no Floyd Cardoz's last day and had a wonderful lunch - the clam pizza sold me - and knew I wanted to come back. I came back this weekend and fell even more in love. This place somehow achieves the perfect balance of high end food, a more upscale environment matched with exceptional service, but a perfect, comfortable evening. My husband and I split the potato, pancetta, and egg pizza, the burrata (DIVINE!), the shishito peppers, roasted cauliflower and the trout. Our server was fantastic - very friendly and knowledgeable of the menu and made our experience even better. Next time, I'm coming back for the oysters during late night happy hour and something off that delicious dessert menu!

Pro: Just the decor + style of the restaurant. Very spacious, polished + being able to see the kitchen area with its hustle + bustle was great. Con: Sort of out of the way, + parking was a drag the night we went. Prices are a little steep for me.
Great place. Highly recommended. Great service. Good drinks and food. I enjoyed myself.

Seriously Yelp, can we please get half stars? Eli's is definitely more 3.5 stars than it is 3 stars. I really enjoy Eli's as one of my go-to spots..food, drinks, and service are consistently great. Is it a spectacular, mind blowing meal? No. Can I find better food elsewhere? Of course. But they have a wide selection of food that can cater to anyone in your group, prices are fair, and I've never had anything that was bad. It's a great place to meet up after work, watch the game on one of their many TVs, have some drinks on a Saturday night..really, it's good for anything. There's ample seating (including an outdoor patio for the warmer months) and plenty of parking. It can get packed, but the way this place is laid out it never feels cramped. Drinks are strong, food is good, and it won't break the bank. Their signature salad is awesome, and any of their buffalo dishes (buffalo boats, buffalo chicken wrap, buffalo egg rolls, lazy man wings, you get the idea) are delicious as well. It's a solid, reliable spot and I'll continue coming here as long as I live in the area.

Went to Eli's for lunch & had the turkey burgers, but this one was not good. Fries were mushy not crisp & no flavor. I had ordered food to take home which was clearly put in too early. It was the penne vodka which I have seen there as a generous portion when eating in the restaurant. The take home was cold, scant(not much more than a layer of pasta on the bottom of the container), with very little vodka sauce. There was no real flavor.  It was very dry, not tasty, and a huge disappointment. Have had other issues previously...should have known better.  I will not be back. Too many other good places to eat in and around the area. Done, done, done!!!!

Casual, fun, and delicious. They seem to always have a live band where you can relax and enjoy the music while sinking your teeth into some BBQ. I enjoy the ribs, catfish, and collard greens from here and will come back often to get to-go when I'm staying at a nearby hotel. Service is also superb.
5 stars for the Burnt Ends, Shrimp & Grits, Mashed Sweet potatoes and great music.  Wish this place was in my town!

We've been here a number of times and the last two times were not impressive.  We were there on a Saturday night and our server Brett, walked away without taking my drink order (he took everyone else's), then I tried to stop him and he was just gone too fast.  We also weren't given kids menus and I was going to ask for some while ordering my drink but again he flew away.  I swapped out the collard greens for mashed potatoes for my meal and guess what I got?  Collard greens, had to wait for him to come back because again he left before I could open my mouth.  Then the bill, we pay and he doesn't ask if I want a box when I clearly didn't finish my meal.  Brings back the check paid and disappears again.  At this point I look at my husband like "Are you kidding me?"  So then we wait until he's near our table (for someone else) so my husband can ask for a box.  Now, that said we didn't have to be anywhere but if you did this would be a problem, none the less it was annoying there was no apology, and our bill was $80, so I didn't spend $30, I feel the service should have been better.  Not sure I'll be back anytime soon, if at all.

What a warm environment and such a great vibe! We sat at the bar for happy hour and it seemed the place was filled with regulars making conversation, which is always a good sign. The bartenders were friendly and engaging and the cocktails were great! Fried tofu was delicious - light and crispy on the outside and gooey and soft inside.

Great small plates.  The bar is what sets this place apart. They'll make you a custom drink based On what you like!  :) we had the son of a bee sting why is ginger flavored! Yum :). The ricotta is delicious too and so is the "crab" cakes!

I've visited 3 times so far - once for lunch, and twice in the evening. The food was terrific every time. Their veganized ricotta is fantastic; it's a non-dairy version of the ricotta at Barbuzzo. I eat dairy, and both times I've had this dish with non-vegans, and everyone has loved it. The pastas are excellent. I've had the bucatini with veg meatballs and the gnocchi. The tacos are ok. Definitely good, but I've liked the other things a little more. Great cocktails, and there are non-alcoholic options too. I don't know whether they have a new lunch menu, but the time I visited they didn't. I don't think I'd go again for lunch - it feels more like a night-time place. It gets crowded. If you're going for dinner, I suggest making a reservation.
We've been here twice on consecutive Saturdays.  Food was awesome.  I'm a total carnivore.  But this place is great.
Best vegan restaurant I've eaten at in a longggg time. The ricotta is a must.  So yummy.  Also the "meatballs" are delicious. Definitely returning soon.

Charlie may have been a sinner, but his drinks and food are spot on. I live down the street from this lively place and went in for the first time a few days ago. I asked the bartender, Joe, which drink he would recommend and he provided me with a delicious drink that was not on the menu called the Martinez. If you like bourbon, I highly suggest asking for this. My friend and I also ordered the chickpea fries, charred caesar salad and the ricotta dip with bread and everything was delicious. Service was also great. I'll definitely be going back.

This place has been on my list for a little while now, and I'm so glad I finally went! I went for dinner with two friends, and when we got there, we realized they had a happy hour from 4-7. They had half priced cocktails and small plates. The ricotta and the crab cake sliders from the happy hour menu were my favorite. I had the troublemaker drink, it was perfectly refreshing with strawberry and cucumber. We also ordered a few things off the regular menu to try. The chickpea fries were ok, but we really loved the potato croquettes- both had really great dips with them. Service was quick, and everything came out staggered, which was nice.

There really is nothing bad I can say about this restaurant... The food was excellent, the service was excellent, the prices were excellent, even the drinks were excellent! Best Indian food I've ever had! And it is conveniently located right across from the Wellmont Theater. Our friends recommended this place - one of which has pretty bad food allergies and this is one of the restaurants that she can actually eat safely at and really enjoy the food at the same time. We were seeing a show at the Wellmont so it was the perfect location and I was blown away. I plan on going back very soon and many times after!

It took a bit of time to try out this new, bare bones Mexican eatery.  Once we did, though, we determined that, other than some positive flavors...the general experience was lacking anything stand out. First, the menu.  Take your time and look over it all, as we found it confusing.  As vegetarians, and I realize that we are a minority but there are many more of us these days, we always seek out meatless dishes.  There weren't many, that's for sure. We ordered the vegetarian quesadilla and enchilada with mole poblano sauce. No chips or salsa as is complimentary in nearly every similar establishment, but the server asked if we'd like some.  We declined and avoided the up charge. Ten minutes passed and room temperature water was brought to the table. Almost ten minutes later and out comes our food, looking good.  The quesadilla had good flavor and plenty of filling.  It was served with sour cream and a very lime-ey tasting guacamole which was on the tart side of Flavortown. The enchiladas were served with bland rice and good black beans.  Unfortunately, after the first bite of the main star of the plate, it was discovered that there were strips of chicken inside.  A mistake, no big deal, right? We told the server that we made a mistake and didn't notice that the menu showed that there was chicken in the enchilada.  His response?  "It doesn't.  Traditionally enchiladas have chicken in them."  Hmm.  Is that so?  I believe he meant that mole poblano traditionally is made with chicken.  Still, it was our mistake not knowing that, but I'm sure we're not the only ones. Then we asked if the kitchen could prepare the dish with vegetables.  He said he would check, but left the uneaten dish there, in front of us.  Ten (more) minutes later, he appears with a new entree, which tasted good.  The server offered no apology, no refill for the tap water, nothing. While the flavors were standardly fine, there needs to be a clearer menu, on point floor staff, and better ambiance if this place wishes to separate itself from Moe's, Chevy's, etc... ...and they even offer chips and salsa.  No up charge, either.

Arrived here on a saturday night without a reservation but we were graciously seated right away (unlike another place we were turned away from that night). The food tastes truly homemade and fresh. If you are looking for a more typical Italian (i.e., chicken parm, spaghetti/meatballs) you won't find it here. Best meal ive had in a while. Got the most fall apart tender beef on a bed of creamy polenta. I almost licked the dish clean! Hubby got the rabbit which he raved about. Desserts were great. The biscotti were impressive and full of big chocolate chips- looked homemade. One drawback is parking but I guess that's to be expected in the area. I only wish this place was closer to my house!
Warm, inviting and mouth-watering. Could not ask for more.
Delicious fish tacos and guac! Great service, well def be back!
SOME Ting-Wong please. Please is there SOME Ting-Wong? Does any one know if SOME Ting is Wong? I think there is some Ting-Wong here.

My gf came back for the holidays from the west coast and wanted to stop by Ting Wong.  We came for lunch and I ordered the Hong Kong style roasted pork noodles.   The portion was bigger than I remember.  I couldn't finish it myself.  The roasted pork was tasty. We also had the roasted pork in the white flat noodles.  The fried bread in the white flat noodles were very greasy and not pleasant. Again, still cash only.

I was craving roast pork and decided to give this place another try since it was raining cats and dogs and this was the closest roast pork place near where I parked. I ordered a pound of roast pork to go and the cashier asked me to pay before they cut the meat, which I happily obliged, and as I answered  a phone call the cashier took this opportunity to ask me for another dollar without even showing me the meat on the scale. Whatever, it's a dollar and I'll give them the benefit of the doubt. As I get home and excitedly open the lid - I realize that the cut of the meat was crap - AGAIN!!!  I don't expect all belly meat but every piece of the meat that I got was tough and chewy and the skin was stale instead of crackling. Don't hang a whole pig in your window if you don't know how to cut and respect it properly!!

Been coming here for years, and it has quick service, affordable prices, and DELICIOUS food. Also great place to get roast pork or duck take outs. Check out their porridge, roast duck and pork, tomato beef over rice, or any noodle soups. One suggestion is the lighting inside could be a little less dingy and a bit brighter.
The best chicken sandwich on earth. The cheese fries are a phenomenon. For the type of food it is, 5 stars.
I love the taste of the chicken, i stop sometimes for lunch, its a great place for a fast food
Great food and Presentation. Love the Farm to table experience. Look forward to going back soon
Enjoyed everything. Wine delivery available!

Had the hot pot for two and ended up having our leftovers mixed with "risotto". I don't think it was "risotto" but whatever it was, it was DELICIOUS. kind of enjoyed it more than the actual hot pot? though, the tofu was soft and yum. also, def thy that shiso hot paste. it's HOT but good.

Somewhat Japanese fusion food. Food is considered normal Among other Japanese restaurants in nyc. Nothing stands out. Hot pot was ok. Not a fan, I would go somewhere else for it. Other dishes are also soso- not bad. Giving the food 3 stars. Taste is soso and each dish took like 20 mins to come out. No dish stands out in my opinion Service is great and that's why this place receives a 4 star from me instead of 3.

I'll try not to be biased, but boy was this place a huge disappointment and I'm not hard to please. I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 just in case of partial ignorance lol. This place is small, and by small, I mean tiny. If you wanna come here, make a reservation for sure if you can. Walked in and was asked if I had a reservation. I replied no at which point they said "ok, please wait over there." There, being the 3' x 3' waiting area at the entrance where there is hardly any room to "wait" as it was way too cold to be standing outside. It's like a human puzzle game when other people are entering/exiting as you have to shift to just the right positions to allow movement due to how their doors open and close and how confined it was. In addition, when they told us the waiting time we inquired about if we needed to put our names down on a list. The answer was no and that we have to be there at the time they think they will have seats available. Mind you, there were several empty tables which we ended up waiting for to sit at in the end anyway. On to the food.... What we ordered: Monkfish Liver - this was surprisingly pretty good. It's garnished with thinly sliced pork collagen (i think), scallion and black colored roe (don't know from what) in a mildly sweet sauce. Without the garnishes, the liver had a taste resembling that of tuna fish. This wasn't the case the other times I have tried this else where but I enjoyed it despite not normally liking items like this. Atlantic Salmon Carpaccio -  hard to describe the flavors because I can't recall all the ingredients but it was fairly light and appetizing overall. About 8 pieces of salmon with the larger roe eggs atop each, marinating in a puddle of the dressing. No complaints here. Snow Crab Croquette - wasn't really sure what to expect with this one but I wasn't a fan. It had a nice crispy outer layer which tasted pretty good but past that it was downhill. The inside filling resembled watery mash potatoes and had a mild sweetness to it. I don't know if it was my taste buds but I was wondering where the "crab" part of this dish came into play as I tasted nothing close to that. Hakata Tonton Hotpot - this was the biggest disappoint of all. Maybe I wasn't prepared for what to expect but this was certainly nothing close to what I imagined for a hotpot. I was starving and this version consisted of 90% cabbage and chives, 1 maybe 2? dumplings, 1 or 2 slices of pork sirloin, a couple pieces of tofu and a few pieces of pork belly and tonsoku. If you love cabbage and chives then this is the dish for you because that is what you will be filling up on lol. It got old very fast. The broth was pretty good with a bit of spice to it though, i'll give it that. Had to order several more additional meats to get any where close to being fully satisfied. Service was ok. They tend to you well, when they find the time to do so. They will pour your drinks when they see a glass any less than full and assist you in prepping your hotpot. They'll even scoop it into the bowls for you. I'm sure some of their other dishes may be fantastic but from my experience, I doubt I would come here again. Or at the least, not have a high expectation in terms of their hotpot.

Whoever gave this place 4 stars and up needs a check up. #sorrynotsorry. Forget the roach crawling up the wall behind my buddy, forget the hotpot that we ordered (Hakata Tonton Hot Pot ) that came with 90 percent vegetation and 10 percent meat. As my boy said, Chives and cabbage stew. ingredients for the HP - "A specialty of hakata, japan, collagen broth, tofu, dumplings, vegetables, berkshire pork belly and tonsoku. min. 2 persons" There was only 2 dumplings in this pot... really? Seeing as how there was a lot lacking, we decided to order   - Shabu Shabu Pork Sirloin - Shabu Shabu Pork Belly - Pork Tonsoku We had to add all three to the hotpot ( which means that they know they give you barely enough in the dish itself) which makes this 1 expensive hotpot for what it's worth. The broth had a nice and spicy flavor but unfortunately the bad outweighs the good. Dont' get me started on my selection of sake. 40 dollars was the cheapest of bottles  of sake and the price fits the taste. If i had to guess, retail would be under 10 which makes it junk. Disappointing as the mark up for this bottle was def way over priced. Seems like an occurring theme with tonton to give customer less and expect them to pay more. The only positives i can give this place would be the monkfish liver appetizer which was dressed in some type of semi-sweet glazed that added a nice contrast to the rich liver. A close second would be the ginger-ale soda i ordered. Tough choice between the two. Hospitality is almost robotic here as our (mulitple) waitress really didn't understand that much english and kinda just nodded and spoke the general "yes and thank you" notations. Any questions or conversations you would start would be met with the default answers. Expecting anything more would be asinine. Would i come back? I'll let you know when i get that 3rd dumpling in my hotpot.

I was a frequent diner at The Terrace as recently as March 2011 and have to say that this is hands down some of the best food that I have ever had. I have brought family and friends, etc...and was always very pleased with the food and service. Jungle Curry, Terrace Salad, and Basil Fried RIce are among my family's favories. A part of the dining experience, however, is to feel that your privacy is being respected. With that said, the owner of this establishment was arrested for videotaping female patrons without their permission. Please see the following article for details: nhregister.com/articles/… Please use your discretion if you decide to eat here.

Best restaurant in the New Haven area. Chef Amy combines her French-training with old fashioned country thai recipes. Every dish has been special for me, but the Fish and Duck dishes are my favorites.....I go at least twice a week.....thank you Terrace team for all that you do!

The food is some of the best in the area and you can't beat it's price point. The eggplant is made fresh not that frozen crap some other places try to pass off. And the spicy mixed sea food over pasta is amazing plus it's enough to feed four people. I've ordered many things too many to list and it's all good. On my last visit (pictured here) I ordered something I've never had be for and loved it, took the left overs to work the next day.

Super cute date night bar / restaurant! The lighting sets the mood. The food was good. Had the fried pickles, hangar steak and quesadilla. The drinks were weak. And although the waitress was super sweet, she seemed a bit distracted.

I worked around the area before and liked walking over here for lunch. It's a pretty cute cafe and the food isn't super filling, but it's a good enough amount for me when I don't feel like eating a horse. Combo comes with 2 rice balls, choice of miso soup type and a very small side of Japanese pickles or special of the day. The Hawaiian, sukiyaki and unagi rice balls were really good. For miso, I favored the kinoko. Was not a fan of the gnocchi because it tasted more like a rice cake and I'm not into rice cakes, unless it's sweet...Also, wasn't into the Italian rice ball either, but it might have something to do with it being cold while the other ones were warm, flavoring also just wasn't as good as the other ones. This is a good quiet place where you can probably sketch or study and get a light bite to eat. Didn't get to try the drinks but hopefully will next time!
oishi & kauai yuuuum :)

This place is about to be my new go-to spot for lunch.  The lunch combo is a decent deal: $10 for two rice balls, a miso soup, and a salad. Lots of variety, and very fast service- I was getting takeout and must have been in-and-out in 5 min. This would be a super cute spot for a casual date or a solo lunch with a good book.

5 Stars for service, atmosphere and effort with food (although food is definitely more of 3).  We had family in town and need something in this area that was low key and took reservations and Church Publick fit the bill.  We had made the reservation on opentable and forgot to mention we needed a quiet table but when we got there the host was incredibly accommodating and despite it being really busy took me around to see the different options and ultimately recommended one of the booths with curtains in the back.  The booths are spacious and allow you to feel like you are part of the lively action of the place yet still have a conversation.  The staff is incredibly attentive and were happy to go through there impressive beer selection and were very honest about which dishes are better than the other.  The food combinations and presentation is very well thought out and you can tell they are really trying hard to go beyond pub food.  We had the pork chop, 1/2 chicken, and bangers and mash.  All looked fantastic and looked good but flavor was a little too bland for our liking (definitely far from 5 stars).  Nonetheless, given the effort and that this is fairly new place, we are optimistic it will improve and will certainly be back.

Church Publick has a lot of promise including a very good kitchen and menu. The service, unfortunately, was very disappointing so we'll be looking into other options for neighborhoody and family friendly restaurants.

Very good food, great atmosphere. The only thing we didn't love was the potato chips and fondue. We expected a nice bowl of fondue with chips accompanying but it was like a bowl of nachos and not what we expected. Loved the menu generally.

Ordered to have their duck meat loaf dish delivered. The portion was small, but worst of all, the meat loaf was badly over-salted. The greens and some of the other vegetable sides that came with it were pretty terrible as well. For this price and even not for this price, I say yuck! How could Yelp do this to me, I usually love these kinds of places?

Dropped by last weekend for the first time and greatly enjoyed Church Publick. Nice decor with bar seating, booths and upstairs loft seating as well. Great selection of craft brews on draft and yummy (I mean, really yummy) food. The boyfriend ordered the Shaved Brussel Sprout Salad which I helped him devour - and I don't even like brussel sprouts! Mixed with pear, Dorset cheddar, hazelnuts and cider vinaigrette it was a true delight of a salad. Me, the carbo-craver, went for the one of the Grilled Pizzettas - a chicken caesar w/baby arugula and shaved parmesan. Tasty and just right for lunch. Staff was helpful and friendly which added to the pleasant experience of a Sunday afternoon stop at the pub. We would certainly go back to try more of the brews and explore the menu further. This is a nice little place with a good feel and good folks who seem to really enjoy what they do.

Took the 'rents here when they were in town and had a great experience. Nice neighborhood vibe, no wait for a table and great prices. We really enjoyed everything we ordered -- the burratta was a nice balance of creamy cheese, salty anchovies and tapenade on a thick piece of toast and greens. The black rice "surf and turf" was so flavorful with octopus and 12 hour oxtail and a bit of crunch from cilantro sprouts on top. The fried chicken was perfectly crispy on the outside and moist inside and the ham and cheese grits addictive. The blue crab spaghetti was very good as was a special that sort of a summer stew with vegetables and ricotta dumplings I believe. Can't wait to go back!

Simply amazing fried chicken so tender and juicy and melts in your mouth. The mashed potatoes oh boy we got it for our daughter but ended up eating the whole thing. That should say enough. I went simple and got the burger. Can't say that the burger was not good.  next time I will be more adventurous and try something different and yes I did say next time because it was just that good.

NOW! Every so often you come across a hidden gem something like the late-night chicken spot but makes you feel as if your at Martha Stewart Connecticut estate, this restaurant is something Beyoncé should talk about in her next surprise release album. You hear about there's speculation but you don't really know until they let you no and that let me know as soon as that plate came out. 13 hour brazen lamb over a fresh baguette a scoop I'm sorry a dollop of mashed potatoes and some amazingly fresh spinach I've been asking My boyfriend could  we go there since and I won't let up till I get off that G train!!

As a former small business guy I have to say I have ultra respect for business that continue to strive for greatness.  Since Marietta has opened they have tweaked their menu, their cocktails and their wine list in the best possible way.  First few times we went it was good but kind of limiting.  Food we had this afternoon was fantastic.  They now have outdoor seating.  Changes in the wine list were seismic compared to the cocktail/bourbon/beer direction they had.  Our food was great.  Service was great. TV's are gone.  So many things have been fine tuned.  I have to say I'm very happy about every single change that has appeared at Marietta.  I hear that they will soon be open on Monday's and also for lunch which ups our options in the neighborhood. My hat is off to the staff and management for continuing to tweak the Marietta experience for us! ***Also appreciated the music being played at a comfortable level for conversation. I'd give 'em a 5 but I want to go back a couple more times and I will for sure.

This place is really beautiful and clean. Their falafel is fresh with great flavor and they have a nice selection of toppings to put in a pita. The place has so much space to sit that I only wish they had a few more outlets to plug in a laptop. Their Katanchik smoothie with pineapple, orange, kale, banana, dates and almond milk was perfect after the gym. $7.25 seemed pretty expensive for a smoothie, but they really give you a lot.

This is an amazing addition to the UES!  I am so happy I finally went in.  As I was walking on 2nd Ave last week someone from Abaleh was standing outside giving out samples of falafel with tahini.  I thought to myself, if this place is willing to give me a delicious full piece of falafel as a free sample, then I'm willing to give them a shot. We decided to go to Abaleh for lunch today.  As we walked in we were greeted by extremely friendly staff.  They explained how the ordering process worked.  We decided to get falafel in pitas.  The pitas were fresh and looked golden.  The falafel looked extremely fresh and were literally fried right in front of us.  They loaded our pita with hummus lining the inside (what a concept -- a little for every bite).  We were told that with the pita we were able to basically choose as many sides as we wanted that would fit.  (I'm so used to going to places where they charge you for every little addition).   The food was delicious!  The only thing I am upset about is that I hadn't come to Abaleh sooner.  Abaleh was so unbelievably clean and the staff was so helpful and nice. I will definitely be back and maybe even try the smoothies -- they look amazing and were so popular.   This place is a must!  It is definitely the best Mediterranean falafel I have had on the UES.
Delicious and amazing and everyone is super nice

Saw a sign for vegan shawarma which intrigued me.  Walked in and was pleasantly surprised....the food and layout reminded me of israel.  The vegan shawarma was excellent.  The eggplant topping, schug and harissa were superb.  The place was empty inbthe thickbof lunch though and I hope they last!

For my last yelp review... BLACK CRESCENT IS THE JAM. Best new bar / restaurant of 2014. Some people bars take their cocktails to entirely new levels. Reynolds, who runs the bar at Black Crescent, is that man. I've been to all the cocktail joints in NYC and this guy is one of the leaders of the spirit world.  Reynolds starts from scratch reimagining recipes and infusions. He's one crazy friendly long-haired mad man, part scientist, part groover, part grover, part best friend to all. You may know him from Booker & Dax or The Beagle. Try the Broadside cocktail and the Hempen Halter and you're going to find yourself in a really good place. The bell pepper gin cocktail is also awesome, and the best approach is just be open minded and try everything! Food wise, everything I tried was on the money. Apparently, the chef came via New Orleans and Momofuku Ssam, as he already has the food dialed in. The seafood is fresh, complex, and super tasty.  And if you're wanting some beer and wine - oh, they have pairings for that too. For example,  a basque style Oregon-made cider on tap, or some funky red and white wine selections. Food, wine, cocktails... it's all on lockdown in a very warm and welcoming spot. It's kind of like a high end restaurant firing on all cylinders shrunk into a tiny slice of the LES. It's a baller spot, and certainly my favorite of the past year and likely 2014!

Black Crescent is my new favorite bar! The drinks and food are amazing and the service is great. It's easy to become a regular with all the delicious cocktails, wine list and small plates. You feel cozy and welcome the second  you walk in the door. The Peruvian Ceviche is my favorite dish. I've never had anything like it.  The have happy hour cocktails and $1 oysters from 6-8 and $1 oysters again from 12-1 which is great for people who work in the industry. I would definitely recommend to friends and family. You won't regret it!
love dough! their salad and pizza specials are always to die for! never disappoints!

Had a birthday dinner there with a big group. Zucchini chips were awesome and LOVED the pancetta pizza. Had delicious steak with awesome mushrooms and spinach and the Nutella pizza with fresh apples was perfectly crispy and so delicious. Big plus that it's a BYOB. Would definitely go back.

It's okay- not bad, but not particularly great either and we probably wouldn't go back unless there were no better options open. The husband and I tried their rice bowls- he got the chicken Kabab and I got the chicken shawarma. I guess because we were there at the end of the day the meat just seemed kind of blah- it was pre cut in their little steel tubs, and just sitting out. The rice was quite good, but very greasy, so don't expect this to be like a healthy meal option. He roasted eggplant and cauliflower were great, the humus and garlic sauce were actually pretty blah-  for a place that's marketing a Mediterranean chipotle vibe, hummus should be a strong suit... Overall, the ambience of the place was nice and clean, well lit and cheery. The staff is pretty nice as well, tho my particular bowl-maker seemed new and was unsure of what he was doing. If you're looking for something different, give it a try, but don't expect to be blown away. The whole experience was just meh.

Okay, I've been back here a couple of times and I have to say my experience has definitely been better. The pitas I had no longer fell apart, and the customer service is absolutely stellar. Even when I have no idea what the fuck I'm ordering (which is pretty much always), the guy has always been patient and taken the time to explain everything. In fact, I'd say the quality is probably up there with Mamoun's, though obviously you don't get quite the same experience. Still, you could do a lot worse for the money, and I hope they succeed cause they're doing a pretty good job providing a nice, fast, reasonably healthy (I hope?) option for Mediterranean food (am I the only one who has an absolutely awful time spelling that word or what). Keep up the good work!

I had been waiting very eagerly for this place to open since I first heard of it. I rushed out there for lunch with a colleague just days after it open. I was incredibly disappointed. We were seated immediately and did enjoy the decor of the restaurant. They threw down a few broken breadsticks in a plastic package on the table. We ordered drinks (the wine list is impressive) and a few appetizers... 2 of the bruschetta's, which were nothing special, and the olives. The waitress did not come by to take our order until our apps were already near finished and even then, we had to flag her down. She left the menus on our table through the whole meal. After we had finished eating, and had been sitting there for another 10 or 20 minutes, she came by to take dessert orders. We both went with the tiramisu, a complete waste of calories. After we finished, we sat at the table for a good 20 minutes with empty glasses and dishes in front of us, waiting for the waitress to come back. The restaurant cleared out completely and she still walked by us 4 or 5 times before we were able to get her to come give the check. Settling the check took another 10 minutes. The food was decent, but certainly not worth the $50 a person for lunch. The service was awful and the  wait staff even held a brief meeting right next to our table. I would only go back if someone else insisted.

after a few glitches upon opening this place is now moving along.excellent food and a great selection of italian beer and wine. speaking of WHINE i find some negative reviews to be to early to form a correct opinion.all restaurants that just open have their glitches.personally i never visit a new place until a month after opening.i found the food to be pleasurable and the staff was excellent. ty spuntinos
one star is too much for this place bad service expensive and baby plates

First off, the Green Rock is in Port Richmond, not Kensington. Had a great time there tonight with family and friends. The burger was outstanding, the Kenzinger was excellent and the people were awesome. I look forward to many more trips to the Green Rock. One more thing, the fries were the best I've had in awhile.
The poke and loco moco were amazing! Best macaroni salad I've had outside of Hawaii and the owners were very sweet.

after words from friends i finally got to try this authentic hawaiian food , i could go on and on how good the food is , its a must have , very fresh food not a big menu which is fantastic, i went two days straight , kalua pig and cabbage , and the loko moko both AMAZING! Staff is great, im definitely gonna be a regular . great touch with the music.

The worst customer service I've EVER experienced! We ordered at 7pm we called aat 8:30 to find out where it was and we were placed on hold for 15 plus minutes. We then tried to call again and were told our food is on it's way. It wasn't. We called again at 9 when it still didn't arrive and were then finally told they never cooked the order. They knew this was the case when we first called, and didn't seem to care that we had waited over 2 hours for food that was never coming. I will never order from here again.

This place has possibly the WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER!!!! After the delivery took over an hour to never appear, I called to cancel. After speaking with a so called manager i was ensured that my credit card would be refunded for the order. Almost a week later the refund was never processed. When I called  to find out why I never  received the refund another so called manager ( who was completely unapologetic, I might add) tells me that they have been "backed up". How could you not refund a purchase for items a customer never received immediately?!  Its sad that a place who has a great product is missing the key ingredient of customer service. I will never order from this place again. To speak to a nasty employee after I was essentially stolen from, is unacceptable.

Love Greek food and also love seafood dishes. Did my research and found this place on Yelp. I was amazed with all the good reviews here and high average star rating. Was expecting a great dinner at Taverna Kyclades. However I was a bit dissapoited with this place. I was surprised with the food, it had no taste or flavor. Worst I had in long time. I couldn't even finish half of my main course. The service was great, the waiters here are nice and professional, and know their menu well. However the food sucks and it is very overpriced. I got: - Octopodi for $18 - Horiatiki salad for $15 - Sea Scallops for $30

My to go dish at a Greek place has always been souvlaki, but this place is known for their seafood. Came here on a Thursday night, just 3 days ago actually, with a few friends for dinner.  Not everyone from our party was here yet but they still seated us, and it was already pretty busy at 6:30. Our waiter was a nice gentleman who was also attentive, and patient, but he just speaks too fast that I could barely understand him. We were too hungry so we ordered food before the other person from our party showed up. Right after we ordered, late party member finally made it but to our surprise a +1, and we were seated at a table for 4 and a chair on one side. The manager was totally understanding and we were lucky enough to move to the table behind us before the bigger crowd finally came in. We got an order of the octopus and calamari for appetizer. The octopus was one of their highlights here on Yelp, of course! Sooo tender, and the lemony dressing pairs with it sooo well! It was a mountain of fried calamari for a great price, but we all felt like it was more like an Italian style dish, don't get me wrong though, it was good. We had 2 orders of the "Kaklades" Special and a Britzola to share. The "Kaklades" Special is actually a seafood platter with stuffed shrimps, stuffed clams, scallops, a filet of sole, and a huge lobster tail. First, all the seafood on the plate were fresh as you can still taste the sea. Only a few dissapoints in the dish though. I thought the whole dish was actually very bland. Also flaps from the scallops weren't taken off, and the scallops in one of the platter were still half raw. Their stuffing for the shrimps and clams is made with real crabmeat which tasted sweet. Britzola is a ribeye steak, seasoned very well! For the price it was a huge piece of steak. We asked for medium rare and it was a little over, more like medium but that's alright. The fries weren't actually fries, homemade potato chips which half weren't crunchy. Don't forget to save a little room for the complimentary dessert! Don't recall what it was but it was almost like a custard apple pie finished off with crispy phyllo dough. Filling was creamy with a touch of sweet apples plus the crispy dough, the textures and flavors were on point! Mm mmm MMM! Overall, casual atmosphere simply decorated with a touch of white and blue with friendly attentive staff!

I am from Greece and I can confirm that this place has authentic greek food, as good as you can find in Greece. My favorites dishes are: octopus, grilled calamari, shrimps, dips, sausage, lemon potatoes, fried zucchini and galaktompourekto (the dessert they bring at the end).

We had to wait 40 minutes for a table with a reservation.  Food and service were very good but the sound level is unbearable.  You have to yell to be heard across the table.  Granted it has a low ceiling but they do nothing to lower the decibel level.  Even our waitperson said when they get home it takes hours for the sound to get out of their ears.  The sound level will keep  us from coming back.

This was one of the best meals I've had in New York! I had grilled shark with steamed wild greens. Wild greens usually sounds boring to me, but they were so good...like, really really delicious. My only complaint about the entree was that there was a lot of cartilage in the shark** but that just might be the nature of the dish. I also never thought to dip seafood in hummus but it was served with that option and is a great idea. I also really love the interior--it almost feels like you're seaside (if you ignore the buses and taxis outside the window), and even though some of the tables are a bit too close together, there's still enough privacy for you to enjoy your meal with your party. They serve a complimentary dessert at the end which is amazing if you enjoy 'sweet'--as full as I was I devoured all of it. It was essentially a custard with a baklava-like crust and it was truly delicious. Definitely on the expensive side but definitely worth it. **I went back recently, and there were bones in the salmon as well. They also don't serve coffee or other hot drinks, which is how I like to finish my meal. I appreciate a lack of bones, shells, tails, etc. so this (and the lack of my favorite drink) is why I didn't give it the last star.

I was a little hesitant in coming here because I had a terrible meal at the Astoria location. However, I believe in second chances and this place definitely deserved one.
