The food was infinitely better than Astoria's!! Infinitely!! Everything was fresh and had my friends and I wanting more. I highly recommend the grilled octopus and chicken skewer! The octopus had the perfect consistency and wasn't excessively chewy. If we weren't sharing I would have eaten the whole plate myself. The chicken was also unbelievably good. It came in huge chunks so I was expecting it to be dry, but that was not the case at ALL. Mmm... perfectly seasoned, tender, juicy chunks. The grilled onions and peppers it came with were good too. I was able to taste both the vegetables and the nice carcinogenic flakes. The spinach pie was a little too creamy for me so I didn't like it too much. We also had the clams stuffed with crabmeat. I had this over in Astoria and hated it because the crabmeat did not taste anything remotely like crab...or anything for that matter. Here, though, I couldn't get enough. The clams themselves were incredibly small so it was mostly just crabmeat, which is fine by me. The complimentary custard dessert completed a great meal. Great service too. I took off a star because it was way too loud. Having a screamed conversation while dodging flying bits of food is not desirable at dinner. I have come to the conclusion that Astoria simply had a bad night that day, and I will try it again to compare.

COLD....did I mention that it is COLD in there...Take a jacket and expect to wear it. All in all it was OK. The food was ok, the sevice was ok, the timing of the food kind of slow, overall experience ok. It is a chain and like any other chain you get a pretty basic experience as you would at any other. If you are in the mood for Mexican (like we were) this will do it for you, not the best you have ever had (like most things in life) but overall will get the job done.

Delicious Tacos! Blows Chipotle and Qdoba out of the water. Carne Asada (steak) was delicious, but doesn't compare to the deliciousness of Dos Toros' Carnitas (pork)---  juicy, flavorful, shredded pork goodness! Also, note that the Dos Toros' version of the hard taco is not the same as the Taco Bell's version. It's basically a soft corn taco shell pan-fried in a little oil. Yum!

I wish I could give this place 2.5 stars. They don't really deserve 3. We ate there last night. Sort of bland but okay food. I was very disappointed having lived near the more remarkable taqueria in Chapel Hill for 2 years. The carne asada meat was very tasty, but nothing else was remarkable, even interesting or even fully cooked! We had undercooked beans, which we are now paying for. So my recommendation, stay away from their beans. They have strange cheese habits too. With just a little effort, they could make the food worth the $10 or more dollars. I'd rather go to mom and pop's, but next time, I'll hit Chipotle.

Let's just say I'm from the Bay Area and when my buddy (Toro Uno) told me he and his bro were opening up this place I freaked out. This is SO needed in NY. The burritos taste extremely fresh and authentic... like they aren't loaded with random sauces and unnecessary toppings. Highly recommend it.

As luncheon fare goes, this is a perfect place to get your burrito or taco fix, with flavor reminiscent of Bay area taco joints.  Affordable prices, well flavored, and a friendly atmosphere warrants a solid 3.5 stars flat, but a four star on the luncheon scale.   Only a month in business, Do Toros Taqueria will get my repeat lunch business on: a) affordable prices; b) friendly service; c) quality of the staple dishes; and d) the value-add.   The tacos were incredibly simple and well made, and they are not skimpy with their meat helpings (see Chipotle).  I enjoyed the subtle seasoning and the melted cheese on the chicken soft tacos.  Two will be more than enough to fill you up.   The service was incredibly friendly.  I had a chance to speak with the brother proprietors, and they are incredibly friendly and passionate about what they do.  Give people a simple meal at a great price.  Get in and out quickly, or stay and eat, it's all good.   The price is a HUGE plus.  Maybe someone forgot to tell these new proprietors that New York city overcharges on food.  Maybe that's how they do it in the Bay area, but New Yorkers want to pay at least 15 dollars for lunch.  And good quality for that price?  ugh, Dos Toros!  you're doing it all wrong!  8 dollars here will fill you up, if not a little less.  Very nice. . . The value-add here is the use of eco-friendly cups and containers.  They compost them, which is a big act of goodwill in my book.  Not enough people make this effort.   Highly recommended.  Definitely a new add-on to my Under $10 Best Eats in NY.

Such an innocent looking burrito shop, but it is one of the hottest places in the city at the moment.  Everyone is weighing in with their opinions, and the place is, at this writing, number one on Yelp.  So allow me to join the chorus: This is a solid spot for burritos, but it does fall a bit short of a perfect burrito.  I opted for the carnitas burrito with black beans, and I just loved seeing it prepared in front of me.  The rice and beans were pretty good, and the cheese was used in a way that complemented the dish rather than dominate it.  The pork was generous in portion and not overly salty.  The burrito was bursting at the seams with everything they managed to pack in to it.  My only misgiving was that the salsa fresca was not so very good.  Too bad, as I think that would have really tied the burrito together.  Additionally I had a side of chips, but I found these to be kind of stale.  In the future, I will avoid these.  Finally, I love the environmentally friendly approach adopted by Dos Toros and applaud their commitment towards sustainability.  For New York, this is a good burrito stop.
Great Place! Quesedillas are perfect, soft taco shells are the real deal.

This place is hella good.  If you understand the nuance of that statement, you know I know what I am talking about.   For you Bay Area people, this is basically Gordo's or El Far of the East.  I never thought I would live to see the day...

There are a few complaints you will consistently hear from New Yorkers: "It's impossible to catch a cab when you need one." "Pigeons take over the sidewalks and the rats are bigger than small dogs." "Tourists and hipsters are taking over everything." "One hour wait for brunch?  WTF." "There's no good Mexican food in NYC." Dos Toros might be able to help us with that last dilemma.  This place is for sure one of the best Mexican joints in the city.  I found their pork burrito to be really delicious and incredibly filling-- I love how they have a nice layer of sliced jack cheese on their warm tortillas so it's not overwhelming the other flavors.  The beans and rice?  Good.  Salsa?  Good.  The mechanics are the same as Chipotle-- indicate whether you want a burrito, taco, or plato, and pick your toppings as you move down the line.  You know the drill.  Prices are also about the same. (Guac costs extra.) The space is pretty darn small so you'll most likely have to take your food to-go or eat standing up.  The guys who run this place are super friendly so I'm hoping this place succeeds.  And for all those CA folk who complain that this still isn't as good as what they have back on the west coast, why don't you quit your moanin', accept the fact that you're not in CA anymore, and enjoy a good thing when we have it.  Mmmkay? :)
Hands down, best taco I have had in NYC. Juicy meat, generous portions, and tasty toppings.

1 - I'm Mexican (Michoacan) 2 - I was raised since I was 3 years old in Northern CA 3 - I love food.   Even if these guys came from good-Mexican-restaurant-populated Northern CA, they did not bring the food with them.  An honest attempt, this place is a Chipotle Mexican Grill with better ingredients.  Meat was more dry (regular carne asada, pollo) than it should be - which was my biggest qualm.   I've been here in NYC for the last 2 years and have been YEARNING for good Mexican food.  I have yet to find something which I thought was so easy, so simple to make: food for the people, by the people.   Still Dos Toros fails at the attempt...I know why the people here give it great reviews - because of relativity.  They haven't been flooded with the greatness that is Mexican food, properly made.   I need to get some $$$ and try to bring some of my family's cooking here to NYC.

Believe the hype: it's good! Stopped in for lunch last week... long line, but super efficient staff made it better. They were so friendly and professional. Ordered a pollo burrito... WITH guac. Mmmm Mmmm good. Delightfully messy, warm, and full of tastiness. It filled me up and took me out, but left me intent on returning. My dining buddy, a skeptical Berkeley grad, exclaimed that her carnitas burrito was so good it meant she'd return, too. Yay! Kudos also to Dos Toros for using environmentally friendly Greenware and corn-based forks instead of plastic. And, for making the menu cheap-ish. I'd be more willing to give you 5 stars if you shaved a dollar off each burrito/taco/plato, though. But that's just cuz I'm broke. Having said that, I will probably happily be back for more beautiful burrito indulgences. ...but seriously - what is up with all the Californians talking about "authentic" Mexican food? Have they been to Mexico? I realize Cali has a different *kind* of Mexican food than you might get in, say, Mexico City or even San Antonio, TX, but please -- Californian Mexican, while dang delicious, is not "real" Mexican. [edit: it has been pointed out to me that the veggie burritos here are not vegan, in case that is important to you. The rice is cooked in chicken broth. It's not important to me, but I thought it deserved a mention.]

4 stars for a NYC Mexi joint. 3 stars if Dos Toros were in Cali. 2 stars if it were in The Mission or Baja California. This place is better then Chipotle or Baja Fresh but nothing to write home about. I am happy they are here though within a stone's throw of my office. You can't have enough less then $10 lunch options. There is certainly room for improvement though. How bout a salsa bar? Maybe some cup o beans side? Or a soup? Would a small handful of tortilla chips with our burrito's kill ya? If these guys are from SF, let's see some of the SF love. If tiny trucks in LA can have those options, no reason why this place shouldn't.

For NYC, definitely a must for burritos.  They'll even grill it for you, just ask! Go for the carnitas, avoid the chicken unless you like your chicken dry! My loyalties still lie w/ Anna's Taqueria in Boston...wish they would come to NYC already!

i was craving some horchata so i came here because people told me the owners of this place are from the mission. no horchata here! i guess some things got lost in translation. this place really goes the chipotle route with the menu. burritos, tacos, chips, and quesadillas are offered. similar to chipotle, the ingredients here used pretty sustainable. in terms of taste, the carne asada is better, but the fillings are a little more limited. coming from the bay, this place is just average. if you have never been to a california taqueria, this place would probably be 4 stars. but this bay area kid gives it 3

Last night while laying in bed and playing with my.. iPhone (duh what were you thinking?) I came across Dos Toros Taqueria on my home page for Yelp. The reviews seem fairly positive and they claimed they were new. How can a guy say no to tacos and burritos? So I quickly devised a plan on how to get this yummy food in my stomach and hoped and prayed that I would remember in the morning. My plan was simple. Drag the first person I run into to the 4 or 5 train and take it one stop to Union Square and burritos. Then come back later on to buy more and deliver them to the girlfriend for a surprise. What kind of girl wouldn't like being given a long, thick tube of meat? (Zing! Took a page out of Peter D.'s book) My plan went smoothly and before I knew it I was at the nondescript doorway to Dos Toros Taqueria. I got the very satisfying and very tasty Carnitas (pork) Burrito with Guacamole and a small soda. My total came out to $10.50. My friend had the Soft Carne Asada Taco with Guacamole, Chips & Guacamole and Bottled Water for a total of $10.01. The Carnitas and the Carne Asada were perfectly seasoned and tender. The tacos were a tad small and she ended up spending another $4 for one more taco. The decor of this place was somewhat cold in my opinion. The tables were carved out of giant slabs of wood and the seats were crossing straps of leather. There was little color inside other than lots of browns. Color was what I needed today since it was raining and all nasty outdoors. The food here is spot on. Lunch was about 2 hours ago. I think it's about time for me to go back and get more.

I was craving tacos and decided to check out this place after reading all the rave Yelp reviews. It was pretty busy when I got there. I guess it's a quick place to go for NYU students. I glanced at the kitchen and it looked like a dingy ghetto setup. I ordered the crispy tacos and was disappointed that they basically took tiny soft tacos and heated them up with some oil on the oven in front of me. I was like uh ok... I got the carnitas which were a cube-like. It's supposed to be pork that's been cooking for a while, falling off the bones, not meat cubes. Topping wise there wasn't much. They had sour cream, guacamole, and like 2 kinds of salsa.  So 2 crispy tacos and a drink came out to 9 bucks. I was like WTF? I bit the bullet and paid then munched down on my not so crispy tacos. They were soggy and dripping with grease. The carnitas tasted like microwaveable meat cubes . I left feeling ripped off and won't return.  I'll take Chipotle over this place any day.  Why is it so hard to find amazing Mexican food in NYC? Don't believe the hype.

Let me disclaim the above 5 stars by saying that in California I'd give this place 3 or 4. Like so many Bay Area transplants, I've searched actively for a legit mission burrito in NYC, and to little avail (all though I still stand by my previous good review of Los Arcos in Bushwick). That said, for burritos in NYC, this place epitomizes 5 stars, which is to say, "Woohoo! As good as it gets!". This truly is the best burrito in NYC, and I did indeed make exclamations not dissimilar to "Woohoo!" upon consumption. Here's why: From the very first moments of burrito genesis, Dos Toros nails the Bay Area details heretofore unseen in NYC. They pull out a healthy-sized 12" flour tortilla, throw some white cheese on it, and steam it so the cheese melts. Right off the bat, they win. As any experienced burrito-eater knows, the steaming makes the tortilla stretchy (starch + water = glue) and sticky. This is critical not only to the burritos structural integrity, sealing tight the filling inside, but it also enables the tortilla to expand and accommodate a massive amount of filling when properly rolled. And oh, how they fill them! The rice was yellow and spiced, though a little on the bland side. The beans (black or pinto? black.) were on point. The carnitas was regrettably not the crispy-fried gorgeousness that I really missed, but still quite good. So the basics are solid, if not standout. Where Dos Toros really won my heart was in the fixins. The guacamole is only $0.92!!! I can not tell you how much it warms my heart to see guac for less than a dollar. And it's GOOD! It's chunky, flavorful and F-R-E-S-H. Moreover, they heap it on! I counted a solid 5 dollops from a bigass spoon. You get about the same amount (a small mountain range) of the pico de gallo, which is also fantastic and super fresh (but could be spicier). The sour cream and hot sauce, on the other hand, are lightly applied in a criss-cross pattern using a ketchup-style squeeze bottle. This is as it should be. I don't know where people got off thinking that sour cream should be applied in equal proportions to guacamole - that's gross and overkill when you've already got cheese in there. And that's what goes in! No BS like shredded lettuce or olives or broccolli or any of the other countless perversions (nay, abominations!) of the Burrito's true essence that I've had the horror of bearing witness to in NYC. To round things off, they had a full selection of jarritos. A guava one and a burrito with all the fixins ran me about $10. Not bad for all that joy. I wouldn't complain if they added some aguas frescas to the mix, or fresh carrot/orange juice. Salsa bar would also be a great addition. Also, has anyone investigated the chimichanga situation here? Will they fry your burrito? I was so blissed out I forgot to ask. Had a lovely conversation with one of the owners, who rang us up. Nice to see them on the floor, making connections with their patrons. Chips are 2 or 2.50, which I would totally bitch about in California but out here I'll just shut up and eat the best burrito I've had since I last visited my ancestral homeland. The most important part of this review is right here: I ate the whole damn thing! I always stop after the first 2/3s, save the stub for later But I just couldn't help myself! Like a man who has wandered in the desert for many years, I drank deeply at the well of burritos. And I felt great afterward! Not like I was preggers with a food baby; quite the opposite in fact - I felt like I was floating a little as I walked away, fat and happy! In all objectivity, it was far from the best burrito I've ever had (tho the heaps of guacamole were truly something to write home about). If I wanted to be an perfectionist snob I could knock of a star or two or find some irrelevant things to complain about, like the sparse decor and furnishings. But context is everything. And within the realm of cali-style mexican food in NYC, this is the Top of the mf'in Pops. It doesn't get any better than this. Cheers, Dos Toros - I applaud your success where all others have failed, and I can't wait to see where you go from here.

Carnitas taco (crispy): meat tender, juicy, and filled to the brim of the tortilla. Salsa on the other hand was lacking in flavor. Put some more onion and cilantro in there and we can start talking authenic. Making it "picante" wouldn't hurt either. Chicken Quesadilla: chicken are a bit over seasoned and the queso is not what I was expecting. I want "quesadilla," not a crispy tortilla with a slice of cheese. But if you just consider that as a wrap, then good job Dos Toros. Burritos: did not have, but saw someone else ordered it and it was packed like Burro. Looks good for the price. Take that Chipotle! Coming from San Diego, these tacos are wimpy satification. But since they boast "SF taqueria experience," then I guess it's a Nor-Cal sensation. I guess Nor-Cal people are more used to pricey imitation tacos than the rest of us in the Southland.
Being from SF, this place is pretty legit when it comes to mexican food in the east coast. I'd go def go back for my mexican fix.

Since moving away from Santa Barbara I've been craving good Mexican food. Dos Toros is as close as I've come. Your basic assortments of meat (carnitas, carne, pollo), beans, good guac and spicy salsas to shape into burritos, tacos or bowls. The food is good and fresh (it's true, you can taste love). The firs time I ate here for lunch, I went back to pick up dinner to go. For less than $10 you'll leave happy. Limited seating and I heard a whisper of a second location the other day.

Wow-I got the chicken quesadilla and it was the greatest mexican food I've ever had ever. The guacamole was also amazing. It's very small and cute, and my friend said it was like "an authentic Chipotle," and she's right. It's way better, too. Great price, great location, GREAT food.

I have never written a Yelp review but feel compelled to after receiving the worst service and treatment at this restaurant that I have ever received.  The food here is good and I know people that love this place, but the waiter that served us was obnoxious and rude.  He was passive aggressive and made inappropriate comments to our table.  I will never go back to this restaurant, despite my love of interesting Korean food.  Management should consider giving their servers a course on professionalism and what it means to work in the hospitality industry.

chill little place.  great reasonably priced food and decent beer selection.  good date spot and the bar is a good place to grab a beer and some food if you're flying solo.  i usually frequent this spot once or twice a week.
Can't go wrong with this place. Works for brunch, dinner, and dates. Highly recommend the bi bim bap.

It was amazing! We loved it. Appetizer: Crab Dip with crostini. (Real crab meat and so yummy!) Main: House Steak with the House Steak Sauce with a side of garlic roasted broccoli (Amazing) Desert: cheesecake (Heavenly) It seemed like everything we got came with a little surprise! We got bread and butter to start.  Then  the appetizer.   Then they brought around this fantastic salad with beats, greens, pumpkin seeds, and squash-I didn't know I liked beats until today. Then the main meal came and it was melt in your mouth good.  I had the Vermont Ice Cider "Heirloom Blend". Then we got the cheesecake and it came with another surprise! a little donut thing with a crispy crust.  It was SO good. The whole meal was fantastic. Our waiter was pleasant and really attentive!  The whole staff made it a wonderful experience.

Had been hearing about this place even before it opened. Went approximately two weeks after the opening. The starters were outstanding. The issue we had was with the pacing of the meal as well as the overall attitude of the server. There was a certain smugness that we could not escape from. The meal started really well with an appetizer and a salad. We the had to wait 20+ minutes for our main course with no apologies. The presentation of the double rib eye was a bit over the top, especially when we had been waiting so long for it. We could have done without the pageantry in the interest of getting our food in a more timely manner. We ordered coffee which took an eternity to arrive. It arrived at the same time as the check. Considering the priceyness of the tab and the slow service I will not be rushing back any time soon.

To be fair I will give this a second chance. When we dined it was open three weeks. I'm not sure if they are consciously doing a Ruth's Chris theme or it just appears that way, if so, they failed. Everything here is a la carte which in this case detracts from the presentation, a 10 ounce sirloin on a 18 inch dinner plate looks ridiculous. The best french fries that I've had in quite a while other than that everything was fair. "Note service and wait staff were over the top"

Keeping it short but sweet here: Get the Gnocchi Parisian and you won't be disappointed. The roasted parsnips were also amazing. Huzzah for the sustainable, organic and local support from Kennett.  I thought they were reasonably priced. If you feel like you're paying too much, you're paying for quality and potent flavors of food that's in season. The restaurant is casual but romantic, and what felt like a spitting image of Chick's Wine Bar.

I almost gave them 5 stars just because they had 2 of my all time favorite beers on draught that night. Ballast Point Sculpin IPA, and Troeg's Mad Elf. My wife and I sat at the bar and shared "beans on toast". It is a thick slice of toasted Brioche, with Tomato, Braised Butter Beans, topped with a Fried Egg. It was really nice, I haven't had butter beans since I was in Savannah GA. We are both suckers for anything with a runny egg. We then shared the Porchetta Pizza, which is slow roasted pork, farmers cheese, an whipped Lardo., It was fantastic. The texture of the crust combined with the flavors of the pork, and mouth feel of the lardo made for a very enjoyable course. Paired beautifully with my Double IPA. We shared the Chocolate Bark for dessert which had almonds and Vanilla Bourbon Ice Cream accompanying it, it was good but nothing mind blowing. I recommend sitting at the bar, the bartenders were really great and it is a comfortable place to eat and watch the (slumping) Flyers.

I live down the street from Crescent Grill and was anxiously awaiting a restaurant in our neighborhood since there is zero (besides hotel restaurants, but that doesn't count). I had little expectation, and knew that no matter what, that I would patron it since it was in the neighborhood. Well, I was very pleasantly surprised to find that Crescent Grill has it very together. It's a nice looking space, but the owner did his research and has a great staff and a very good chef. I went in on opening day to show support and had some lunch. I sat at the bar and struck up a conversation with the bartender Ryan who showed professionalism and was very friendly. I had the fish tacos which were pretty good. For an opening day, I was impressed how smoothly it all went. A few nights later I returned for a late dinner about 15 minutes before the kitchen was closed. As  a restaurant worker, I know that this can be annoying, but the staff was a pleasure. Ryan the bartender remembered me and made great recommendations. I had the chicken off the lounge menu, and I am not just saying this, but it was one of the best roast chicken dishes I had in a long time. I complimented it and before I knew it, the (very tired) chef made an appearance to chat about the dish and explained how he just got it from the farm that day...which is always a plus to me. The dish was perfect in flavor. The owner chatted with me as well and bought me a glass of wine just for returning. Overall, friendly staff, great food, and lovely service. I will be a regular not only because it's in the neighborhood, but because it's a very good restaurant..so happy it's here. Nice job!

Take it form someone who grew in  with a native Italian grandmother and my mother who learned from her--this is homestyle Italian. Everything on the menu is very good italian. The calzone is huge, tasty, cheesy, with a little mariana sauce on the side.  Pizza-tomato pie also very good. And the true test of any place are the soups--and they do not disappoint. Reasonable prices, too!  And bring your own!
I come here for lunch during work some times. The food is always excellent.

Very good Sushi!  I would highly recommend!  They just opened and we happened to come across them as we were on our way to Cheburger Cheburger in the Mercer Mall (Same shopping center as Shoprite, Chevy's, Hooters, Houlihans, etc).  I like that it is BYO especially since Joe Canal's discount liquor is across the parking lot.  Besides it being hard to find, I will definitely be back.

Stumbled upon this place when the original place we wanted to go to had a long wait. The restaurant had a couple of opened tables but they couldn't seat us because they were all booked. We sat at the bar and the bartender was the one we served us the whole time. That's fine. Now, let's talk about the food for a bit. We couldn't decide what to get so we got spinach feta frittata, chicken and waffles (highly recommended and one of the most popular items), croquettes and Cobb salad to share between three people. I won't comment on the frittata. They're never really impressive to me. Felt like overdone eggs shaped into a triangle. Chicken and waffles. So I had high expectations for it because people from past reviews raved about it. The chicken's color looked nice and brown. The breading was a bit soggy. For fried chicken, there really wasn't much of a "crunch" to it. The chicken felt like it had been fried for a while already because it wasn't even that warm. The waffle that they had under the chicken was nothing special. In fact, it tasted bland and there was, again, no crispy texture to that. It was soft when I put the knife and fork into it. For something people raved about, I thought it was very disappointing. Now, the croquette was breaded and fried pretty nicely. Other than the texture, there wasn't much of a flavor. The Cobb salad should have been an easy dish to make but even that was disappointing. The chicken was cut up into tiny little pieces with scant amount of blue cheese sprinkled on top. The Cobb salad was done with iceberg lettuce. In my opinion, iceberg lettuce should never be used anywhere. The color is too pale, there's zero nutritional value and it's all just water. Overall, not impressed again. I'm sorry but this isn't a place I would revisit.

I live on the same block. Food is mediocre at best but they are the WORST neighbors ever. They have rude, insanely loud drunk ass bridge and tunnel patrons screaming outside until 3am while they blast their cheesy club music all night. Do yourself and our block a favor and go elsewhere.
-awesome crab curry in the made to order menu -buffet has wide variety and good options -food is very spicy for avg Indian food -decent price and good service

I was really excited to hear that there was a place close by that offered a lot of sushi for a good price. However, after my experience I'd never go near Masa Sushi again. I knew that the quality wouldn't be amazing but I did not expect the seaweed to have such an unpleasant taste, which ruined the rolls. They used way too much rice in their rolls, contrary to what previous reviews have said. Sashimi was okay and the fish wasn't old but it definitely wasn't extremely fresh either. The tea I ordered was "brown rice green tea", but it tasted and smelled like old fish. I could barely take a sip and felt nauseous. I'm not sure why it was so awful but it made me skeptical about the rest of the menu. Overall, everything I ordered had an unfortunate taste to it and I felt pretty awful all day after my lunch. I know all you can eat is alluring but don't make my mistake. Spend more on a smaller amount of great sushi in the area from Elements Asia, Mizu, or Peony Pavilion. I'm actually pretty shocked that there are so many good reviews of this place because Masa is not worth it at all.

Didn't have a great experience here Friday night. I showed up at 6:30 to meet friends who had a reservation and were already seated. I politely asked the doorman which way the Library was, and his answer was "The Library is full right now." Well, thank you for that info, but that wasn't an answer to my question. I told him I was joining friends and only then did he point me in the direction. At the first hostess desk I asked if this was the way to The Library, as I was joining my reservation group. Maybe the staff just listens for "The Library," because even though I mentioned my party I was again told "The Library is full." Repeated that I had a reservation and they gestured me in. I found it quite awkward to then walk thru the dining room, but not as awkward as coming to ANOTHER hostess desk, AGAIN being told "The Library is full" and AGAIN repeating my reservation name. As I did, I saw my friends and told the host "I'm with that party." At which point I finally entered The (Full) Library. And saw 4 empty tables. Which stayed empty for the 30 minutes I was there. I don't know if they ever got filled, because we were asked to leave after 30 minutes when we broke their "parties of 6 and under, only" rule. The 3 friends who trickled in after me (all commenting on how many staffers told them the Library was full) brought us to 8 people, and even though we had an empty 2-top next to us and weren't infringing on the space of the group (4 adults & 2 kids) next to us, the host came over to tell us that they made an exception for the 7th person but simply couldn't let us have 8 people at our table. Instead of drawing straws to see which 2 friends should leave, we asked if we could finish our drinks before being shown the door. The host unhappily said "of course" and our check was promptly delivered. As we were leaving we passed thru the crowded outer bar, with groups of people craning their necks to see if a table in the coveted Library had opened up. If only they knew... Shame, too, because my Old Fashioned was great.
Get the Hair Trigger - done. Place is super small and not easy to get to the bar. Okay scene......

Um, yum. Since a bunch of Philly food bloggers have been hyping this place for the past couple months, I was happy to skip breakfast and give it a shot for lunch today. Serious comfort-food goodness. A note on the menu boasted that Bon Appetit had named Paesano's Arista sandwich among the top three meals in America under $10, so I went with that. Roasted pork, long hots, broccoli rabe ... and no regrets. I felt pretty unladylike with juice dripping down to my elbows, but that was a small price to pay (props to the server who saw me struggling and brought extra wet-naps to our table). There were only two vegetarian options (four if you're a veggie who eats fish), so some of my friends might feel slighted here. But if you're down with meat (and aren't on a diet) -- go.
the roasted suckling pig sandwich - amazing.  It is a must-try for anyone that enjoys anything pig.  I will be back many times and eat many more of those sandwiches!

Holy Moly. Don't have much to say other than that. I got the Paesano sandwich, "beef brisket rosted tomato sharp provolone, horseradish mayo, fried egg". While that sounds like (and tastes like) a heart attack in a bun - it's absolute heaven. RUN down to paesano's ASAP. NOW, DO IT. Note: they are cash only.

We came here at 6:55pm not knowing that the place closes at 7.  We've been meaning to go for a while, and it would have sucked if we'd been turned down.  But we weren't!  Even though they were about to close, we were encouraged to pick something anyway and they did not seem irritated by us.  We ordered the vegetarian sandwich with eggplant and and bunch of other stuff.  The sandwiches were good, and they have a cool soda machine with stewart's orange cream soda and root beer, and cherry soda.  The interior is easy on the eyes, it's clean, neat and simple.  Good experience overall.

This place automatically got 4 stars for painting a gigantic orange record with a cow (whose lone spot initially formed the shape of Pennsylvania, but now is, perhaps, Philadelphia?  I'm not sure) listening to a gramophone on the side of a building.  The mural makes me incredibly happy, and, since I live right off of Girard, I get to see it every day.  However, they serve La Colombe, which makes everyone happy except me.  I don't know what my damage is, but I don't like it.  There are very few places that make their espresso to my liking, and no matter where I get it, the coffee is burnt.  Anyway, the mocha that I got here was really strong.  I couldn't taste the chocolate in it at all.  Still, I can tell when a man knows how to make espresso, and this guy did.  So give it a try.  Unless you're me or someone else who doesn't much care for Philly's favorite purveyor of coffee, you'll like it.

Milk Crate has not been open long at all but I have been more than a handful of times already and hung out there for long periods of time.  Its not exactly close to my house I'd say close to  2 miles away, but given the chance to escape rocket cat's douchey clientele is totally worth it.  I have never felt comfortable hanging out in rocket cat, but I feel totally fine hanging around milk crate.  They play good music, the owner is super friendly and nice and there is free wi-fi (ok i don't use the wifi, but maybe someday).  The only downside for me is that it doesn't feel 'broken in' yet.  It kind of has a sterile feeling that I haven't quite put my finger on...is it the furniture, the white walls?  I think its a combination of the two.   All in all Milk Crate is a-ok and has won me over enough to deserve a visit from me on a weekly, or bi weekly basis.  Their coffee is decent and I hear they will soon be serving food products as well.  There is also a record store in the basement, I'm not so much into collecting vinyl anymore, but maybe you are so stop by for a look and happy friendly service.

Great new bar!  Upstairs feels like you are at a classy bar in an episode of Mad Men, downstairs is cozy basement with beautiful wooden bar and booths that have your own personal taps! Food was great too - had the French dip sandwich which was DELICIOUS!  Great place to go for a few drinks with friends and one of the few nice bars in that area.

This place is a home run.  The food is GREAT (not your typical bar food), the staff is friendly and the beer selection is awesome.  It feels like a "bar" should on Park Avenue.  Pouring your own beers downstairs also makes for a fun NY experience!

Nice after work spot.  Good food, great service all within a comfortable atmosphere.  Try the bar downstairs.  Very cozy and enjoyable...especially after pouring your own beer from your personal tap!  Will be back!

I've been to Libertador twice and had a very similar experience both times.  The atmosphere is wonderful, the staff incredibly friendly and warm.  We loved the empanadas and the appetizers, but there's something lacking in the entrees.  The meats are just not that great. I've now tried the steak for two, the lamb, and the steak for one.  Our friends had the mixed grill and said the same thing.  It's ok, just not great.   I would recommend stopping by Libertador for a glass of wine (or two) and a couple appetizers before moving on somewhere else for the main event.

I can truthfully say that Libertador was, all around, one of the best experiences I've had at a restaurant.  From first seating, the staff was friendly, knowledgable and attentive.  Then. . .the food.  Wow.  The steak grill for two was just unbelievable - cooked in part at the table!  And the apple cake?  Yum.  The ambiance was as delicious as the food. Even in a neighborhood with many great restaurants, Libertador stands out.  Truly outstanding.

If LaVa After Dark were a horse, I would shoot it to put it out of its misery. As one of many people who visit LaVa Cafe on a frequent basis, I can't say enough about how toxic this failed endeavor has been for our beloved cafe. I have been going to LaVa pretty regularly for the last two years. It is a cozy, comfortable cafe. You can get a cup of coffee, and if you're there at lunch or dinner, even get a good meal. The staff is great and it feels like one big family. And, as a cafe, it's 5 stars. Heck, I'd give it 6 if I could. But, if you're there at 5:15 on a Thursday, Friday, or Saturday - you become the enemy. Yes, it's true. LaVa After Dark is ruining LaVa Cafe. 5:15 is about the time when an angry woman makes the announcement that all the "studiers" need to vacate. There's nothing worse than being ordered to pack up your stuff and head back to your apartment where your roommate is blasting "Dark Side of the Moon" on full blast in his room on a Thursday after getting off his job making sandwiches at WaWa. Well, I suppose there is. You could be lumped into a demographic based on your possession of a laptop at a coffee shop and then persecuted for it by a shrill unloved shrew - just when you're about to buy another latte! No $3.50 for you, LaVa! After getting a drink with friends at Ten Stone, I walked by LaVa After Dark on my way home just to give it a disdainful stare. And, suddenly, I was overcome by sadness. No, I wasn't pushed out of my go-to cafe for the one-percenters to have their precious candle-lit meal. No, this BYO wasn't filled with rambunctious college kids eager to have a place where they could bring their PBR tall cans and chat. I was pushed out of LaVa Cafe so LaVa After Dark could then proceed to...sit empty. Yes, not a soul to be found! So empty for so long that the staff had congregated and chatted idly, most likely about how big someone's miscalculation had been. And that miscalculation was big. Really big. I mean, when the $3.50 I would have spent on my latte would have made the needle move for the place, you know it's bad. I'm not sure who did such a poor job in the conception of LAD. Poor marketing. Poor menu. Poor communication with its hordes of loyal patrons. But, suddenly I understood that woman's frustration. LAD is failing. You see, that wasn't the only night I've seen this place empty. I walk by it every Thursday, Friday, and Saturday night on my way to Good Karma Cafe, which has become my new go-to spot, and the place is always empty. Really empty. Hear a pin drop empty. So, LAD, I weep for you. When you decide to open your doors again as LaVa Cafe and welcome us "studiers" back with open arms, I'll forgive you. Really. We all make mistakes, and LAD is a doozie. Until then, I'll just have to find some place that doesn't push me out into the cold at 5:15 on a Thursday night. The blustery, merciless cold - into the arms of another coffee shop. We had something, LaVa, we really did. Then, suddenly, I wasn't good enough for you anymore. Enjoy your empty candle lit room as a tear falls into your cold cappuccino. If you look up hoping to see me, I won't be there.

LaVa's hummus is better than Zahav's. There. I said it. Previous commenters seem to really hate the table service idea. I went for dinner the other night and was very impressed by the food and the service. The menu is not extensive, but everything on it sounded like a hit. My friend and I split a red pepper stuffed with rice, veggies and figs (absolutely delicious) and salmon with couscous. Both were perfectly cooked. Both made us keep eating well beyond the point of satiety (portions are a good size). The waitress was attentive without getting in the way, and at the end of the meal we were treated to a dessert from the chef. It was a semolina cake, which I think is a traditional Israeli cake, and man was this thing good. It was like a cross between cornbread and pineapple upside down cake. (OK, that description was completely inadequate.) I can see the controversy about turning this from a cafe by day into a BYO at night. Maybe the chef is just trying out some stuff in preparation for opening a BYO at a different location? I don't know, but I for one am happy to have another BYO option in the neighborhood. I just hope this isn't alienating otherwise loyal clientele who are now going to OCF or Good Karma instead.
La va is our local coffee spot with great food, caffeination and free wifi. The place to go to meet your friends, cheery staff, outdoor seating for you and your pooch too.

I wouldn't come stumbling here without a plan- an escape plan in the shape of a vehicle.  The surrounding businesses didn't look so savory- I believe I spotted a sad-looking strip joint.  Nothing else in the area was open.  However, if you're able to snag a ride, make the trip. I came here on NYE with a group of friends; talk about a #latereview.  I have so many that I'm posting out of order.  It's probably wise to keep your numbers down- the joint is tiny.  From what I remember, the capacity was at a tight 20, tops.  Leave out that one friend who can't stop talking about herself. I definitely ate with my eyes that night, ordering the crab spring rolls, the classic bahn mi, the tomato and garlic rice, and the coconut pudding and a Vietnamese iced coffee.  My new year's resolution is to fatten up to the point of rolling.  It saves me the energy of walking.  The spring rolls were so delicious, definitely a nice twist on the usual pork spring rolls.  The bahn mi flavor was great, but didn't have a lot of filling inside.  The tomato and garlic rice was good to eat as is, not requiring any accompaniments.  I could have done without the coconut pudding- it didn't satisfy my dessert craving and was the only disappointment of my night.  Vietnamese iced coffee is a must whenever I dine at a Vietnamese restaurant- I noticed they used different beans from other places.  The jury is still out on whether I liked it or not.   I also tasted my friends' soup from a special; it had a nice kick though my friend said her mom makes it better and without mushrooms.  I think everyone had an overall great meal here.  I would definitely return to sample the rest of the menu.   Funny shout out to the person who answered the phone.  I called ahead since it was a little less than 2 hrs out from closing time.  I asked approximately how long the wait would be a half hour from the phone call.  His epic answer: "I don't know what the future will be." Bunker tickled my funny bone, but deserves its merit from the food alone- a classic example of how to have an appropriate number of menu options, and how to kick ass on almost everything.  Take notes.

We arrived  at around 6:45 on a Sunday evening and waited about an hour for a table. The wait seemed a bit long even though we put our names down so we went inside to check where we disappointingly found out that groups ahead of us were seated first. They didn't apologize and seated us at the next available table. This was not a good start to the meal. Our party of 4 ordered the crab spring rolls and banh xeo. The spring rolls were good but could barely taste crab in any way. The banh xeo broke apart quite easily and was simply alright. The dipping sauce was also subpar. We ordered the Ca Ri Ga, black angus short ribs, suon nuong ga (pork loin), bo luc loc (angus beef cubes). 3 dishes came almost immediately which was appreciated. However, the short ribs took almost 20 minutes later than the other three dishes. Seriously, how is that even possible? The food itself was alright. The curry had a strong flavor and the roti for dipping was well crisped and flavorful. The angus beef cubes were room temperature, dry and tough. Short ribs were good but the vermicelli was soggy and overdone. The pork loin was not memorable either.  Perhaps should have tried the banh mi which other reviews seem to rave about. Overall, the service was very disappointing. The food certainly was no better than any pho restaurant in chinatown or elmhurst or any other area that you can get viet. The bill also came out to be $110 for 4 which could easily been two meals at a better viet place in ctown. I'm glad we tried it once but we won't be going back.

The food is definitely pretty solid but the service left something to be desired. I'm sure hipster foodies will justify driving to the middle of nowhere, waiting 30-45 minutes, paying a lot, and getting mediocre service. Just wasn't worth it to me to go again since for that, the food better floor me.

Bunker is a hipster Vietnamese joint. My wife and I trekked over an hour to come out here hoping to find some authentic Vietnamese food but what we found was a modern take on Vietnamese food coupled with inefficient service and horrible wait times. We got there around 6:20 pm on a Saturday night and were told that there was a 40 minute wait. Not ideal but there's a market around the corner so we thought we could go waste some time there. We came back around 7pm and were told that our tables weren't ready yet and it may be a while. So we waited.. patiently at first.. but 7:00 pm rolled into 7:30 and then into 8:00pm. By that I was so hungry, I found myself standing by the door and glaring angrily at everyone inside. Finally, after an hour and 40 minute wait, we sat down just after 8:00 pm and got: Cha Ca La Vong: The flounder was cooked perfectly but the flavor was completely off. Turmeric should never be the dominant flavor in anything. I use turmeric in half of my cooking and it never works as the dominant flavor. However it works great when you use it to compliment other flavors. My personal take on this dish is that it would have worked better if it was flavored more with ginger less with turmeric. 3/5 Banh Xeo: Hands down this is the best Banh Xeo I've had tried to date. The crepe was crispy on the outside and runny on the inside. The flavor of the fillings were excellent as well.  While we were eating this, a group of 4 Viet dudes + a token white guy came in and each got their own Banh Xeo. I think this may be the only dish worth getting here. 4.5/5 Braised Duroc ribs: This was on the specials board. I don't think I've had any part of a duroc pig before so I was curious to try this dish. I didn't find anything special about it. They were braised nicely (I mean its spare ribs for Christ's sake, how can you not get this right) but the flavor was underwhelming. I couldn't tell for sure if it was the pig itself or the marinade that made it sweeter. Certainly it was nothing that justified the $17 price tag for me. I'll take my $7 spare ribs at Big Wong's any day. 3/5 I left this place disappointed and somewhat bitter. Their mgmt needs to learn how to turn over a table faster. They are really nice guys but way too laid back. I also think they are expensive as far as Vietnamese food goes. I can get a very decent Banh Mi in Saigon Vietnamese Deli for $4 so why would I wanna come to this hipster joint in the middle of bumblefuck Ridgewood and pay more than double the prices for food that's not even authentic? Makes zero sense to me. Not worth the wait. Not worth the trek. Food: 3.5/5 Ambience: 3/5 Service: 2/5 Value: 2/5
addicted

I lucked up on an absolute GEM... Bun-Ker is absolutely the best Vietnamese food I have ever had. I am not exaggerating. I had the Short Rib Lemongrass Banh Mi. The bread is perfect crispy exterior and soft interior the picked veggies are crisp and don't over power the star of the show the short rib. There are so many flavors bursting and dancing around but it's like a well choreographed musical in your mouth. I'm definitely hooked.

I have been in this place twice and have enjoyed eating at this place.  We ordered ceviche mixto and seco de cabrito (lamb stew) and for dessert picarones( peruvian doughnuts in honey). Everything was great , and I have to say it kind of rivals urubamba. For our second visit, I ordered tallarin verde con milanese de pollo ( chicken milanese with pesto )  and rotisserie chicken; both great. The waiter/ waitresses service could be better ( hope a manager is reading this) attentive but a bit disorganized. I did noticed the B in front of the restaurant and did not get sick or felt sick after I ate the food. Would I be back? Sure.

The food was really good but I had to wait over 45 minutes on Mother's Day of all days when it wasn't even that crowded so if anyone goes here bring a snack because they didn't even bring us snacks until about 5 minutes before the meal finally came out.plus the service just wasn't good at all.

Best of Thai food around, love the sauce and make sure you order the right number of spice level. So far I am to #6 working to #9. Tony is alway helpful to make sure you get what you want. Every week my wife and I are looking forward to visit this little gem. Amazing sauce a must try in any dish. yes drunken noodles is the best around. I dare you to find a better one. Do not share this little secret with too many people, because once you try it, that will be your first inclination.
great food!

I really just thought this place was OK. It's very small, so while we had no problem finding a table on a Thursday night I wonder if that would always be the case. I got the drunken noodle with the mock duck and it wasn't really all that outstanding. But, when they ask you how to rank it for spicy on a scale of 1-10 you should go 2 points down from what you want to say. Trust me on this. The mock duck was a little freaky for me there, I've had it several times before and I've liked it, but there it's just... a little too flavorful you could say. We also go the spring rolls and they were rolled very small so there really wasn't a whole lot inside. Couldn't recommend them. You could see into the kitchen, which made my dining partner a little uncomfortable. As for the service, each interaction seemed to take a little longer than I'd like. The restaurant was overall very cold, which didn't make us feel at ease. They have a good selection of hot teas though! I don't really think I'd need to come back.
First time here, real Thai cuisine. Had basil chicken , with #8 in spicy. Great food with heat. Will be a regular for lunch.

I would give this restaurant between 3- 3.5.  The service has much room for improvement.   Their soups are Super  delicious, the best on a wet and cold day.  The sushi is so so.  It is the service man!

I have been meaning to submit a review for Eatalia and feel bad I haven't done this sooner! I went to dinner with a few friends to Eatalia and consider myself an EXTREMELY picky eater.  I was a little skeptical because I had yet to hear about the place and it's a little off the beaten path.  However, if I would recommend any Italian restaurant in the city, this would be one of them.  I have been to La Viola, Gnocchi, Porcini, Modo Mio, and all of the top Italian restaurants and I can honestly say the food here definitely competes with all of them.   We started with the antipasta and I assure you it was extremely good and had an excellent variety.  Next was the crabcake.  I am extremely picky about crabcakes but this was EXCELLENT! Nice crisp outside and juicy lump crabmeat inside.  Definitely one of the best I have ever had.  From there, I had the Filet Mignon in a Fra Diavalo sauce.  I am sitting here today writing the review while craving their Fra Diavalo sauce.  EXCELLENT! We finished off with the Tiramasu and loved it.  They also definitely get points for the presentation! I think the difference between Eatalia and all of the other Philadelphia Italian BYOBs is that it really conveys that small, intimate setting that you crave when you go to an Italian restaurant.  The owner is waiting on tables, meeting with customers and makes you feel at home.   You feel welcome and are not just "another" customer!  You can definitely tell that they are passionate about what they do!   This is definitely the type of place I see myself going to weekly to have dinner with family & friends.   If you are looking for a diamond in the rough, this is your place!! I'm just upset I didn't know of this place sooner!

Wow! What a wonderful little BYOB in Fishtown. The food, atmosphere and service was outstanding. Dined here on Saturday. The staff was so friendly, as were the other patrons. The food was delicious. The porterhouse was cooked to perfection and was the best I have ever tasted. cannot wait to go back!
I was glad to find such good Mexican food in this area while visiting on business. Commentary chips and salsa fresh. Everything very good. Some interesting dishes incorporating lobster. Great flavors

Found this place on a whim and was so surprised by the food and atmosphere. I ordered the enchilada trio.  Food was piping hot and featured three different enchiladas and sauces. Margarita was expertly prepared. Will definitely be back!
clean. amazing service. quality food. im a fan !

As a vegeterian I found this diamond in the rough.  Their rice noodle vegetable soup is as fresh and tasty as can be.   I found a gem in their menu, vegeterian cracked/diced roll (i believe the name is something close to this, menu item #143).  What a treat and delight.  I have been going their consistenly every week for 2 months, cant get enough.

Overall was a decent dining experience although the service was very slow considering it was a Thursday night and there were only two other small tables in the restaurant. The crispy sweet potato and shrimp was greasey but pretty good. It was my first time eating it so I don't have much to compare it to. The spring rolls were decent. Entrees: 1) Beef pho 2) Sauteed beefs cubes 3) Char-broiled chicken with lemongrass - decent pho. The chicken and beef were decenlty seasoned but were a little tough to chew Dessert: 1) Three bean dessert - my first time trying it, and i thought it was pretty good

Came here a day after getting Viet at a place down in Linden...had been craving more Banh Mi sandwiches and wanted to try some new food as well.   Other reviews are pretty accurate...there are indeed glasses from a Norweigan cruise ship and service wasn't the fastest in the world.  However, our waitress did recommend an awesome shrimp dish (Tom Sa Te), which is shrimp, onions, and diced chilis with a side of rice.  It was pretty salty on its own, but the rice complements it to perfection.  The papaya salad with shrimp was refreshing, but didn't really do it for me.  Banh mi sandwiches were also good but not great..stick to the pork and avoid the saigon style, which consists of Viet cold cuts (tastes almost like a congealed pork served cold).   3.5 stars for the pleasant surprise (Tom Sa Te).

I will have to agree with everyone that the service moves like molasses. The food is very good however. I came here with 2 friends yesterday and we ordered the shrimp in sweep potato nest, the spring rolls, the sauteed beef cubes, a shrimp dish, and some beef dish that was wrapped in grape leaves. The food was delicious. The beef wrapped in grape leaves was ok, it was...interesting. The coconut rice is like a dessert, sweet sticky goodness.

This is "Chinese" food for people who don't know any better. Very average food with the usual suspects on the menu. If you want true authentic Chinese, go to Chengdu 1 on Route 23 (next to Staples). That is the real deal.

Just moved to the area and found this gem!  Wonderful, fresh Chinese food.  Nothing greasy and it all tasted super fresh!  All the veggies were nice and crunchy, and the meat is always clean and tasty.  We haven't dined in yet, but the delivery was great.  I dont see a reason to go anywhere else!
Awesome place, awesome vibe, awesome food. Fairly new, so go before it gets too crowded!

WOW, freakin awesome! I'm writing this review after having just ate from here at work. Yes, they deliver! I def want to come back, to give a 5 star review (a place needs consistency for that top-notch review) because this was my first time here.  After much debate, I decided on the FDNY hero everyone raved about. It was off the hook! Now, the only problem I had is by the time it got to me, the bread was a bit soggy from the vodka sauce. That basically means I just need to go back and have it as soon as it's made.lol.  My co-workers got the healthilicious panini, philly cheesesteak hero, three amigos panini, & NYPD. I tasted the healthilicious and it was delish! My co-worker that got the cheesesteak said it was great (not too greasy like a lot of places), and the other two liked it as well. Ohhhhh my lord how can I forget the nutella milkshake?! We shared a large ($7.50). It's rich and taste just like my lovely jar I can scoop out from and eat directly. ha! Fatty girl status and no shame. I would also like to add that the gentleman on the phone was very friendly. As stated in most of my reviews that I take customer service seriously(including over the phone orders), so that was lovely. Another thing I would like add :  all of the ingredients in my opinion were fresh and tasted good. I would say the average price here is about $8, which to me is to be expected. Shiiiiiit, I rather pay $8 for fresh, just made food than McDonald's any day. Def give this place a shot if you are in the area! Great job Anthony & Son's- you've gained another customer!

The review is for the customer service.. I was helped by the blonde girl who works Saturday's.. She has a terrible attitude, never says thank you. The person who seems to be the owner walks around like he is doing his customers a favor. This is a fairly new place, you would think customer service would be key!! aside from the tweaking of the csr .. Food is always good!!

I guess you could call me a semi-regular. This is not the best place on earth and a lot of things I could make better myself. Do not order latkes or fried matzo. The brisket is very good and the matzo ball soup is outstanding. I often go there for dinner Friday evening as I walk home from Synagogue. Also, the service is very good and very friendly.
When I lived in this area, I would go here often. As far as cart food goes, it's at the top for New York.

This review deals with the King's current setup in his pimped-out royal food truck, which in my opinion is not as efficient as the previous humble food cart.   Broadway in Astoria is full of fine restaurants, representing all of the different ethnic groups that makes Queens the most diverse neighborhood in the world. In the immediate area of the King's royal truck, there's Colombian, Italian, Japanese, Thai, Chinese, Mexican, Brazilian cuisine all within a two block radius. Heck, throw in a good, old Southern Smokehouse for good measure. But the one establishment that consistently draws the crowds is the King of Falafel and Shawarma's food cart, an Astoria staple, that's been occupying the same spot in front of C-Town for as long as most of the newer residents can remember. Regardless of the temperature, or outside weather conditions, the line for the King's food often stretches down the block, breaking formation only when the occasional car wants to enter or leave the C-Town parking lot. The aroma of the food permeates block and whets your appetite for one of the hearty platters or sandwiches on the King's menu. To ease the pain of the wait, one of the staff will come by to distribute the King's signature falafels. The falafels are tasty, crunchy morsels of chickpeas and spices. The only way I can describe them are crunchy taste bombs. To date, I have not eaten a better falafel, and I am an avid fan of street meat. The King sets the bar for the falafels sold in New York City.   Once it's finally your turn, you get to order your food. Assuming you come early enough, you can order the Shawarma, which is delicious, but I guess there's a limited supply. Sometimes when I go at night, it's gone. The one consistent thing that's always available, and I guess is the plate that I am most fit to review is the chicken platter. When it's your turn to order, you state your meat preference and whether you want one of two kinds of rice, yellow or Basmati. I'm not sure which one is more authentic, but I figure I can get yellow rice everywhere, so Basmati it is for me. The King offers a good salad, which lettuce, tomatoes, onions and pickles native to his homeland. The chicken is marinated with spices and is always tender. You get a very generous portion of food. To top it off, you get a falafel on the side. The food is best enjoyed fresh as the falafel experience may be less than optimal when it's trapped with the other food in the container. . There is a small seating area within the C-Town parking lot, but more often than not, I find myself running home, so that I can enjoy the King's food. If it is not apparent already, I am a HUGE fan of this cart. So why only four stars? To be sure, I would rate it 4.5, but since i can't seem to do half stars, 4 is how it stands.  I feel that with the King's enormous success, the experience for the regular customers has suffered a bit. The humble cart "back in the day" (up to about September of 2014), was an efficient assembly line, with the progress of the food prep following an logical order of rice, food, salad, sauce, and payment. Once one man is finished with his part, he passes it down to the next.  While this is likely the same sequence inside the food truck, there's a lot of back and forth inside of the truck. The King, I believe, has started accepting orders for delivery, which furthers delays the wait of those who are actually there on line. Since the truck has arrived, I've been waiting at least twice as long for the food. Yet, I still stand there, despite the cold and/or weather conditions. This is a testament to how good the King is.

These guys are pretty much the best. I've tasted other falafel and shawarma platters, but none have come close. There is usually a line when I go no matter what time or day of the week. Now that they deliver I am definitely taking advantage of that.

Had great lunch; crab and avocado salad was stunning and overflowing with prime clump crab.  Friend had Panini so large he took home half (it came with salad). Groupon made the deal excellent. The service was friendly and kept us informed admitting she made an input error causing delay.  Unsweetened ice tea was real tasty and always refreshed, But for lunch, get a smaller menu to serve quicker  I don't have over an hour every day to leisurely lunch.  Fast casual.  Fratelli's has the food quality; they need to focus.  Too many choices.

went last night, seated very quickly, service was great, waitress had good recommendations. i had the $25 pre-fixe menu, which was a good value, crab cake was good & vodka penne was good. My husband had the Special jumbo diver scallops with mango sauce, which was amazing and cooked perfectly. Had the house wine Pinot Grigio at $7 a glass, great deal. Also, we purchased the $30 yelp gift certificate which made the prices more reasonable, as they are slightly on the higher end. However, i'd prefer this over the Olive Garden across the street from it. All in all, i recommend it!
Meh, it was okay. You've got so many better options in Philly. I wouldn't worry about checking out this one.

I first came here shortly after it opened and have meant to Yelp about it ever since. In lieu of Yelp-ing about it, I have recommended it to everyone that will listen. My mother, my boss, my coworkers, you name it. First, the space is beautifully designed and wonderfully executed. My only complaint is that it can look empty when it's not super busy. That being said, they have a hidden gem on the third floor which is almost criminally underused. Next, the menu. I find the dishes both inspired yet accessible. You aren't forced to take a crazy leap-of-faith, but can branch out and be adventurous if you feel so inclined. Their crudo selection is all delicious. Get all of them. The closest thing I've had to a bad experience was the bone marrow. It was wonderfully done, but very awkward to eat without looking like something off of NatGeo. The service is always friendly, but not stiff. With so many restaurants, the wait staff feels almost robotic, but the servers here seem to genuinely enjoy their job and it shows. They're always very knowledgeable about their menu and willing to make a recommendation. Hopefully this newcomer is here to stay for a while. A good, long while.

Great happy hour! Half off bubbly drinks. Treaty of Paris is honey dew heaven! $1 oysters are great! Friendly and fast service. My new happy hour oyster spot! Also, the spicy maple bacon peanuts are delicious. Salty sweet crunchiness! The duck fat fries are crisp and flavorful, especially when dipped into the aioli sauce. Side note: depending on when you go and how busy it is, the hostess can be rude.

Charred Octopus - baby yukon potatoes, meyer lemon, espelette pepper, black olive vinaigrette Yellowfin Tuna Tartare - roasted red peppers, charred scallions, avocado, pickled cucumbers, spicy aioli Best introduction to raw food I've ever had :P, did not expect tuna to taste so divine! As a restaurant of this price range ($$$), this place is as good as it can get in Philadelphia. Everything about it. The food was excellently prepared, and I would try everything on their menu. I think this is a place everybody should try, at least once - I can't really say much about their food beyond the fact that I think it's perfect. The service is quite attentive and friendly. I was at the bar with a friend. It was a Wednesday night, and unexpectedly not so busy. What a shame! The manager or assistant manager? Ryan greeted us sometime during our meal, introduced himself and that made me quite glad the involvement of management in the restaurant. The bartender was awesome. Easy to strike up a conversation with, and seems quite happy working there. Additionally, the drinks here aren't rushed and are made with attention. The decor makes the place seem smaller than it actually is. Quite dark at night, dimly lit, but enough so that you know where you are. The atmosphere can be quite intimate depending on where you choose to sit, and have 3 floors to the establishment. Definitely on my list of regular places to visit, if the opportunity ever came about.

Really enjoyed my lunch here today. Tried the Roasted Bone Marrow with Garlic Toast, with the Woodford Bourbon Luge, it was very tasty and doing was lots of fun and a photo worthy event. I enjoyed the beefy taste of the bone marrow combined with one of my favorite bourbon's. The service was very friendly. My server fully explained each of my various dishes and offered to help with the Luge. I had the Turkey Bacon BLT which was packed with goodness, turkey and turkey bacon, avocado on a crisp hard roll. I tried some of the Summer squash and chickpea sandwich and really liked the chunky hummus like flavor, thought that since it was grilled the interior would be warm but it was cool , not bad , very tasty. The Duck Fat fries were so good! Crisp and flavorful and when dipped in the Lemon Truffle Aioli , a taste of heaven. Can't wait to try the happy hour for some oysters, fries, and crispy pig ears.

PROS: Good desserts CONS: Overly greasy appetizers and entrees, awkward ambiance Given the plethora of awesome reviews for this place, I'll admit my expectations were sky-high, so I enthusiastically purchased a LivingSocial deal for the restaurant. However, my experience at Pennsylvania 6 was rather disappointing. The Roasted Bone Marrow appetizer was dripping with grease and overflavored with spices, making the individual flavors nearly indistinguishable. The Grilled Asparagus was crunchy and interesting, but also drowned with oil. I enjoyed the Charred Octopus appetizer, which had a soft rather than chewy texture, and the silky Roasted Skate Wing, which was paired with thinly sliced zucchini, but they were both too generously doused in grease. The turning point came at the end of our meal with the desserts. We had the Almond Cake, which was fresh, light, and delicious, paired with strawberries and a creamy scoop of ice cream. The chocolate-y pot de creme with bananas was also pretty good. Overall, the ambiance was awkward. The lights were too bright and the place was decked out in red. It seemed like a weak attempt to set up a classy, retro vibe... which didn't quite work. The food would be decent if it weren't for the lack of oil control!

So I had been meaning to come here for a while now, and since I had no real lunch ideas i figured I would finally give it a try. My first impression walking in was that it was a really sleek, nicely designed place, actually a lot bigger than I expected.  I sat at the bar, where the bartender Tara quickly informed me of the drinks and food she suggested, which was good. Ended up getting the burger, and is when the review goes down. My first issue was the speed it took to get it...there was only one other table (who had already eaten) but it still took close to 20 minutes for a burger, which wouldn't of been too bad had it tasted as good as I hoped it would. Sadly, nothing really about the burger or fries really impressed me...if  anything the burger tasted kind of salty. Also,I ordered the burger medium, and it was definitely more of a medium rare...I'm sorry, but a burger, even in a place like this, should be as well prepared...but maybe it was just an off moment. The meal was almost saved, however, by the crispy pig ear appetizer which was I'm one word...amazing. Imagine fries made of pork...you get the picture.  All in all.it wasn't the worst meal I've had in center city, but for the price, I would suggest Zavino nearby.   I will give one more try though, as there was a seared tuna salad that looked good, and also a roasted bone marrow appetizer I've been dieing to try. Also I heard the rest of the seafood is good, so that'll deserve another visit.

The atmosphere is crisp, friendly and casual with a certain vibe that makes this my new "go to" place especially when the  pre-tense of a fancy restaurant is out of the question.  The food / menu and drink selection have the potential to be a real stand-out.
Seriously? This is what you think the area needs? No, thanks.  Uncomfortable seating, draught menu on some screen I couldn't read, train station atmosphere.
Great artisan beer and spirits list. Like the industrial space. Friendly staff. Had a few appetizers....all were solid.

Nice place.  We sat in the back and drinks and burgers.  The short rib burger was delicious but really under cooked. Fortunately or unfortunately depending how you see it, the beer was so strong that I didn't really care.  I'm looking forward to going when the front doors are open.  So far I'm happy they came to the neighborhood.

I live a 10 minute walk away from Austin Street and the neighborhood has needed a place like this for a while. Great craft beer selection with what seems to be a focus on NY breweries, which I can appreciate. The menu is definitely unique, and nothing like anything else Austin St. Favorites so far are the Picked Pepper Wings and the Sweet Potato Fries that come with some kind of maple syrup dipping sauce. I also really enjoyed the fried pickle and brisket croquet. Service is super friendly, but would love a beer/liquor nerd to talk me through the choices. Great addition to the neighborhood.

Gene, I can actually speak for both Ian and myself as we are former business colleagues. The reason in which i am fully aware of the design and use of the shatterproof glass front entrance is because I work at an architectural firm. We did not have any sort of business contracts with Station House, but we are currently doing work in the Forest Hills area, thus making me well acquainted with its goings on. To be specific we are working on the Continental train station (E,F,M,etc). The station is being made fully ADA-accessible with the addition of three new elevators, one from street level to mezzanine, and two from mezzanine to platforms. Hopefully that is proof enough that I'm not associated business wise with the Station House establishment and that I am speaking only from the viewpoint of a happy customer. The reason for which I responded in such a way to your first post (and I do appreciate the update with a higher rating) is because you don't kick someone when they're down. Although Station House seems to be doing quite well for itself, it is, in fact, a brand new business which barely got up on its feet. From the perspective of someone who only goes by ratings online they might not decide to take the trip to check the place out having seen such (unearned) negative reviews so suddenly. The bar just opened its doors and is probably still figuring out the most profitable times in which to keep their kitchen open.. you can't slander and judge a place for what it "will" be before its even had the chance to be what it is. Perhaps this was just by some coincidence, but a bar (or any similar establishment) that has the largest area for people to gather located in the back, will want all of those people there to be seen from passersby. Would you go into the empty bar or the one that looks like it has something happening? Being that it is also a sports bar with all of its tvs, the higher seating allows patrons who wish to eat something to be able to watch the games as well. As for the bar seating, they certainly aren't the most comfortable I've sat on, but I do actually like the bench seat for two.. never know, could be a good opening to talking to a woman when it's the "only other option." to sit at haha. Also, serving $4 wild turkey shots will certainly attract the wrong crowd. Now I have no idea how old you are, nor am I claiming to assume you older or younger.. but what many people aren't noticing is the growing amount of younger people in the community. Forest Hills is certainly sophisticated... its old money.. but young people. Although, trust me, I enjoy the finer things in life..I'm a young guy and I don't always want to have to sit in a "Whiskey Room" lounge type boring atmosphere to have a good glass of scotch. A young guy with a mature palate is becoming something quite common now. I'm assuming you'd be surprised if you were to find out the new gourmet deli Cucina had its beer list, which totals 105, created by a few guys in their early 20's (don't be, because it was haha). It's for this reason I think the bar is what Forest Hills needs. Station House packs a cool crowd, music I'm a huge fan of, great beer and excellent whiskey all into one. Also, apologies for the b**ch bar comment. - Was having a bad day haha.

Great edition to Forest Hills.  Went here last Friday for Happy Hour and to watch the Knicks game. $5 craft draft beers was great during happy hour.  The place is lively and was just fun watching the Knicks game with good TV coverage.  The food was much more unique than your typical pub or bar fair and everything we had was very good and was fairly priced.  I enjoyed eating things that were a little more unique and having the option of enjoying a good craft beer over your typical run of the mill bud, bluemoon or coors is always welcome.  Steve (owner) and his staff seemed to be pretty on point for the packed Friday night and for opening less than a week.   For those who were disappointed because it was too loud maybe you should think twice before going into a bar with sports on the various screens.  Jack and Nellies on Ascan would probably be more up your alley.  Marking a place low for this reason is like me going to McDonalds and marking it low because it doesn't have fillet Mignon or going into a formal restaurant and marking it low because they have no TVs and I can't watch a game.  Don't mark a place low for what it is.   Station House is a step above your typical bar that carries an awesome selection of craft beers and whiskeys and is a great place to watch a game.  That's what it is and that's what it does well.

I've been wishing for a hip hang out place in forest hills for along time and this is definitely very close to what i wanted. It feels warm, inviting, authentic, and comfortable. The wait staff was friendly, prompt, and enthusiastic! The food was really decent, and the portions were all reasonably large. My only complaint is that their selection of mixed drinks is really limited. They don't carry grapefruit juice, so I couldn't order a greyhound, which in my opinion is just one of those basic bar drinks. But I know, I know, this is more of a beer place, which they had a plenty. My husband who is a beer drinker was very happy. It's more my issue that beer is not my thing. But I'll definitely come back! I had just a great experience here! And I think other people do too since there was a nice lively crowd there. Oh! And I almost forgot to mention. The music was GREAT! Lots of indie rock which I happen to love.

Came into this new spot with my friend the other night. Beer selection is really good and food was above average for a place like this. Our server, she was super cool and attentive; her Spanish accent was really cute that we asked to repeat the special of the day twice just to hear it again :). All in all, I will be back; glad to have this new spot in the area.

Was here last night and we tried the food. We got a couple order of wings which were HUGE! You get the legs and the wings on the plate, and you get 5 of them. So essentially 10 wings. They were good but I had to take half of them home! The truffle fries were also delicious. Going to have to go back AGAIN! because we forgot to order the brownie dessert!

Let me start by stating the fact that I am Cambodian and grew up eating Khmer food all my life. I come from a family that loves our Khmer food. Khmer cuisine is not easy to make.
