A lot of our food starts with a krueng paste that is made by pounding a mix of fresh herbs and spices in a mortar. Let me tell you..if you ever want a good workout for your arm, I suggest you invest in a mortar and pestle and pound you some krueng paste! If you were to ask me what Khmer cuisine is similar to, I wouldn't be able to answer. Although we use similar ingredients as in Thai food and Vietnamese, Khmer cuisine is unique, complex and is on a class of its own. Being that I now live far from my Mom, I am just so glad there's a khmer restaurant I can go to when I miss Mama's cooking. When I go, I like to get the soups. Cambodian soups take a very long time to make. They are complex and flavorful. I also love their prahok kateeh. I've had many prahok kateehs and theirs is one of the best I've ever eaten. Try Khmer Kitchen if you haven't already. You won't be disappointed :)

Delicious, and already one of my top restaurants in Philly. Located in "South Philly", I can't tell if this is a sketchy neighborhood or not.  Place seems fine overall. It's BYOB, though I didn't take full advantage of that when I went. Food is served family style, and they give you HUGE portions.  Two entree dishes should be enough for 3 people, if that gives any sort of guide.  Two entree dishes for two people is wayyyyy too much food. Service is great, very helpful as they know most people don't know Cambodian food that well. Prices are... a little on the higher end for a non-fancy restaurant.  But the food is just so amazing, I can't complain about that. Will DEFINITELY be coming back here often.

Yum!  It was pretty empty on a Sunday night, so getting a table wasn't a problem.  And the pizza was delicious -- better than the pizza on my last several visits to Lucali.  Service was great. It was a bit too dark in there and would have been livelier with more fellow diners, but I will definitely be going back.
Best kind of bar. Unpretentious, cheap, friendly. Come with a group and make friends with Jeff, and you will leave happy. Better than the bro-magnet bars that make up most of South Street Seaport.

Misled by the name, I dropped in for pancakes. They serve crepes. What's a crepe? Apparently a 'skinny pancake'. Sort of a pancake with all the air let out. Not my thing. But then I came back later for a beer. Not only do they have a fantastic selection (Heady Topper, OMG!), but they serve up a damn fine plate of nachos. So to sum up: Crepes ... meh. Beer and nachos ... fantastic. So I'l be back. But probably not for crepes.

Monday morning breakfast with the family.  Sitting outside on the patio,  relaxing and enjoying some great crepes. Had the Atlantic monsieur which is a nice light flaky smoked salmon, eggs, etc.  The crispy apple crepe was very fresh plus the whipped cream :).  The noah's ark was two eggs,  two sugar crepes and two bacon slices.  Had the two hash browns which were a bit like a potato latke.  Great ingredients and good combinations.  My wife,  ex Starbucks batista Daus the coffee is good also.  Packed also on a Mon morning at 9:30!

This place is awesome. I'm an out of towner and had to try it before I left - glad I did. I had the Garlique Chic crepe for lunch which was chicken, pesto, cheddar(?), and roasted red peppers (usually also comes with carmelized onions, but I'm not a huge fan). They really don't skimp on the ingredients, my crepe was STUFFED full of goodness. The lunch-type crepes all come with a tiny salad, which was a nice addition. Wish I had had more time to try out a dessert crepe. My heart was too set on a raspberry maple Creemee that day.

I thought I already wrote a review for Honest Tom's, but apparently I forgot.  No matter. Anyway, in a nutshell, I had the bean burrito and I honestly could not tell you what I was eating.  If I was blindfolded, I would not be able to identify the food at all.  There was no taste.  Not a bad taste, but near absence of any discernible flavor.  I took a swipe of guacamole with my finger to check.  Nope, no flavor at all. I thought maybe I was having a weird day, but my associate picked up the steak and yucca tacos yesterday and said exactly the same thing.  Looks great.  No flavor at all. Weird.

I'm definitely a fan of this place! It's a bit removed from the Penn campus, but it's a reasonable walk, and a good excuse to call it "exercise" while getting there! FOOD: 5/5 I got the Yucca Steak burrito and it was so delicious! For anyone who's had Chipotle before, it's about $1 extra but includes guacamole. The steak is so much better though. It's juicy, fresh, and soft. I've had some pretty bad experiences eating the steak at Chipotle, but the steak here is great! The yucca is an interesting addition. It tasted like potato but it goes well with everything else inside. AMBIANCE: 3/5 Outdoors seating makes it enjoyable. Indoors, there is no air conditioning, so it was a bit of a bummer when we initially sat indoors because it looked like it was going to rain. It's a bit stuffy inside, even with a large, loud fan blowing towards us. Outdoors was great, and everyone seemed to be having a great time. SERVICE: 4/5 Pretty good too. Hassle free ordering, and everything done with on a touchpad by the server with a FourSquare to pay for it. Food came pretty quickly, too.

Went on a Thursday night and met up with seven classmates.  The place was packed.  Wall to wall people and very noisy/loud. If you are heading out and want to talk with friends (vs. shout), this is not the place. Lots of boutique beers that can show up with orange slices: cool if you like that sort of thing.  I'd have given the place "zero stars" but our waitress was terrific.

Malt House was an accidental find when our original plans changed with Bareburger's closure due to renovation and during a walk around the neighborhood , Malt House caught our eye. After seeing the happy hour / rest of menu, we were sold on trying it. Definitely exceeded expectations. All I wanted that day,  was a burger. A good, old fashioned American burger. The angus burger is a bit pricey ($16) but it may have been one of the best burgers I've had and quite possibly the best burger I've had In NYC. The spin Malt House puts on the burger with the jalapeno and the jack cheese is nothing new, but they do it to perfection. The beef was of a great texture and the burger was cooked to a perfect medium, as ordered. The drink specials for happy hour were impressive and I loved their house brews. My girlfriend ordered a bunch of the appetizers from the happy hour menu , and those all came with a world of flavor of their own. Fried pickles were something I still think about, time to time. I hate to talk about décor but I loved it in here. It carried a roadhouse feel with a bit of rustic accents. They have these chairs without backs that look like they'd be incredibly uncomfortable but were actually pleasant to sit on.  Our waitress (Louise, I believe) was friendly, helpful and cheerful. In an authentic way, not in a TGI Friday's cringe-worthy way. I don't know if Malt House would be a 5 star place if you asked anyone else (not everyone is on the quest to find the ultimate burger) , but because I was so enamored by their burger (not to discredit the other items I tried) and their happy hour options, I can't imagine anything less than the best rating for these guys.  I don't live anywhere near the Village but I will make it a point to stop by just for Malt House.

I really enjoyed the Italian Dog I had at Jimmy Buff's. Bread was tasty. Dog's were cooked good. Onions and peppers were fine and I thought the potatoes were (almost) perfect (had the potatoes been seasoned they would have been perfect).

The original Italian hot dog will always be the best. I've been eating at Buffs since I could chew. I have fond memories of the smell when I walked into the old Irvington location with my father for a late night dinner. Of course it's greasy, it's a hot dog topped with fried potatoes. It's the ultimate comfort food. My Mother always knows what I'm talking about when I remind her that it's Tuesday.

Really enjoyed my time here. This was a little bit different of a dining experience than I'm used to; but this was also likely my first Portuguese dining experience. The food was fantastic and abundant. I had the grilled swordfish, which was my first time having swordfish. It was very good, as were the vegetables (plenty of butter!). I was duped into getting the chocolate/peanut butter cake by my dinner companion, but that isn't a complaint. They were a little slow in getting our check; perhaps they were waiting for us to finish our dessert, I'm not sure. There was so much food though, that there was no way that was going to happen.
The quality of food is excellent.  The Portions are very large. Price is reasonable for the service, atmosphere, and quality of food.  It there were more stars, I would give it more.

My husband took me here for my birthday. He knew I was in the mood for Spanish or Portuguese cuisine. I was pleasantly surprised how good the food was. I find most of these restaurants relatively similar so I wasn't expecting this one to be any different.  However, I was wrong. My dh had the rodizio, while I had the clams with pork. It was excellent. Our server went out of his way to make us feel at home. I will definitely return.

OK. I want to start off by saying that this 3 star is for the Rodizio. I came specifically to try the Rodizio.   I was disappointed as my only other Rodizio experience being in "Rio Rodizio" in Myrtle Beach S.C. which was an explosive experience of delicious good cuts of meat. I found the cuts of meat at Solar to be very fatty and skimpy. A lot of slices that were being presented to me were "edge" or "outside" pieces of the roast and when I asked that I have the "next" available inner or 2nd piece that didn't have the outside "crust" on it, I was told they had to cut around the crust first. Who they were saving the inner pieces for I will never know. Another thing, since there is so much pork included in the Rodizio already, I will never understand why they surround the Filet Mignon with Bacon. There are a LOT of people who have stopped eating pork these days. The bacon took away any original flavor of the Filet. Perhaps they should offer an option. I never saw any of these "toppings" people are talking about. OK, so past that disappointment. One daughter with me ordered the Paelha a' Valenciana. The taste was very good. Not as much seafood involved as it should have been. Approx 3 or 4 baby shrimp. I generously give it a 6 out of 10. Another daughter had a chicken dish that came with mashed potatoes and mushrooms. Peito de Frango a' Princesa. This was the best deal on the table. it was enough to feed 3 people , was delicious, and the best price too. Hmm, how do you like that? We had white Sangria..wasn't very alcoholic at all..Good for some preferences. Personally if I drink, I want to drink. If not I would order juice or soda, so why pay for alcohol that you are not getting. The end of dinner for the Rodizio folks came with pineapple slices with a cinnamon coating..pretty pretty darn good. I forgot to mention the rolls at the beginning. they were really good and warm as well. The service was an 8 out of 10, so that is pretty good for these days. I believe I would return, then choose to sit in the room to the left which I didn't know was open on my way in (We had reservations). Just this time I would stay away from the rodizio, or paelha. I think choosing some more subtle dishes would be the answer, like the Peito de Frango. Note; I expected music as stated for Thursday night.. There was none, not even background music. Atmosphere..so-so.

My favorite place to eat in Newark. I could eat their Pad Thai all day every day. Excellent Iced Thai tea. Operated by a great group of people committed to an authentic experience. Cash only! But worth eating at least once a week if you live or work downtown.

I had the basil eggplant with tofu at House of Thai for take out. I would definitely just recommend this restaurant for take out lunch/dinner because the inside is pretty tiny. The food was decent, not the best thai I've had, but not bad by any means. If you live or work in the area its good for a quick bite. They were extremely fast in preparing our order.

Not impressed with overall experience. Came here initially to use free drink coupons we were given on what we found out to be the final days of PBR. Not holding that against this new establishment we gave it a go. Sat at bar, found beer selection to be pretty blah, bartender was not critical enough of choices when asked and said everything was good. This led to some choices we were less than happy with. Nothing wrong with offering tasters first to ensure you enjoy your $7 beer. Burger came out on the well side when ordered medium. The fried chicken sam'wich fell apart on contact and was more bread than I desired. Fries were a bit burnt and of low temperature. This place has some work to do prior to go live if it wants to stick around in this foodie town.
I went in there and bought a bag of burgers for my family. None of us liked them. They were greasy and the Bread was stale.
Went here for the first time. Clean store but highly unorganized. It seems like its their first day so I will try again in the future. I had regular shoe string fries and it was more then $6
Just opened. Fries ROCK. crispy on the outside perfect on the inside. Great toppings. Staff is very friendly too.

Food 4 stars - very good, cooked & seasoned really well Amount of food/price 3 stars - just too expensive for what it is.  I got the frequent frier: small McDonalds size fries with seasoning for 4.25 wouldn't really get me coming back for more. Service 3 stars - the employees were all having a party of their own.  They were very loud and did not help the establish look very professional

I'm a fan.  Solid idea and decent on the execution. All the veggie toppings are free, I think.  So you can actually make a decent meal out of this -- I got one of the speciality potatoes, then realized I could add broccoli, corn, etc on it and it made it worth it.   Service was friendly, a little slow but not bad.  Would come back.

We had a great meal! The salad as very fresh and served with a tasty dressing.  Three of us had the grilled shrimp and it was delicious. Portion sizes were ample.  Condusive to conversation. We definitely would go again. Prices not outrageous!

Firstly, I want to say that I love food! I love shopping for it, cooking it, eating it, and even cleaning up when it's all over. When my wife and I eat at La Slowteria, I get the feeling that they feel the same way about food as I do. Hugo and Stephanie are lovely, warm, welcoming and make us feel like a part of their family. The staff are friendly, relaxed, charming and we never feel "waited on", just taken care of. Honestly, dinner there feels like we just stopped by our best friends' house for a visit, and accidently showed up in the middle of an amazing three course dinner. It's difficult for me to describe the food at La Slowteria, because I have nothing to compare it to. It is definitely NOT like any Mexican food that I have eaten before. Hugo makes interesting, fresh, dishes which contain strange and delicious combinations of flavors and spices that just make us crazy!!! His Habanero sauce is addictive, and his home made, corn tortillas alone are worth the trip to lower Court St. Last night, my wife and I were treated to the nightly special, a green tomato based soup with beans, bacon, beef, fresh cilantro, onions and a lime wedge to squeeze into the bowl. It's the kind of thing that I could go back for day after day! Warm and satisfying comfort food that never feels heavy or over done. We tried to go there twice with our small daughters, but decided that this place was best kept to ourselves. We now use La Slowteria as the perfect excuse to splurge on a babysitter. We are real home bodies, but La Slowteria gets our tired, old butts out of the house, and into a little beach side restaurant on the coast of Mexico, where we can relax and indulge, get away from the pressures of city life, and enjoy good food, cooked with thoughtfulness and passion, that makes us talk about our next visit, even as we are walking out the door. Buen provecho!!!

I'm going to miss Dubuque, I won't lie.  Their truffle burger was one of my favorite things on this planet.  But I dried my tears at Slowteria the other day and I was not disappointed.  Perfectly seasoned and thoughtfully prepared Mexican food!  The homemade, multi-colored, thick, crunchy tortillas will keep you up at night with cravings.  The portions are small and the prices are high, but maybe the impending liquor license will help regulate their food costs? (hint hint, I'm looking at you owners)  One tip on presentation, if you are going to do small portion sizes, get smaller plates.  They bring out a fist-sized meal on a massive, mostly empty plate that makes it look like they gave half your food to someone else.  Also, the coffee cups and other place settings are conspicuously from IKEA.  I'm all about frugal startups.... but come on.  But seriously, try this place.  What they are doing with the food is a-OK.

Went here for brunch today & was very very happy.  The veggie gorditas were delish & my hard-to-please dining companion exclaimed: "these are the best veggie tacos I've ever had"  about his dish.  If you are in a hurry, don't eat here.  Go when you have time to relax & enjoy the care put into a proper home-cooked meal.    Nice array of Mexican wines & fresh juices but really looking forward to them getting a liquor license!   Will go again, 100%.

Dough nuts. Dough...squares? Although a square cut doughnut is something quite new to me, that didn't impact the taste at all. I was in New Haven for an interview and was told that this place was a must try. I was also told that the doughnuts here were gigantic (about the size of my face, if the gestures were to be believed). FALSE. The doughnuts are the size of your average doughnut, although I can't really compare because usually doughnuts are round and wasn't there some theorem in geometry stating that circles have the smallest perimeter and knot energy per equivalent area...? I came early in the morning Sunday, at around 10 AM. The cashier was cheerful enough and walked me through the selection, which consisted of a lot of regular donuts (think plain, sugar glazed, sugar sprinkled, chocolate) and eclairs. However, it was the two I hadn't ever come across that really made this place stand out for me - the butter caramel crunch (which is absolutely amazing; I can't describe it as anything other than caramel taste in a crunchy and not sticky form), and the mounds doughnut (which was a little disappointing, since it just tasted like doughnut with a few stingy drips of chocolate and coconut gratings). The specialty doughnuts were worth the $1.50 price to me...but if you're just in to get a regular glazed doughnut? Try a 7-11 or a supermarket. But it's a homey little place, and offers lots of other things than just donuts. They do soups and sandwiches at a decent (think 6-9 bucks) price. And no, these donuts are not the size of your face. Unless you are a ferret.

Very good doughnuts, especially the "raised" kind-very light and not greasy. Also had a breakfast wrap (first time I had hash browns in a wrap!) and my husband had a sandwich, both good. Our waitress was excellent, too!

As good as it gets!  You'd usually have to trek over to over crowded Astoria for food like this, but finally an authentic Mideastern option for me here in Wburg.  I called in advance to ask if the food was Halaal, and to my jubilation he said "Yes, 100%".  I will be eating here and bringing my friends too. The babaghannoush was described as 'vegetarian heroin' and how accurate a description! High quality ingredients, fresh and flavorful while staying authentic and not gimmicky.  Eat here.
Great space, great food, great everything!

Yes! So happy to have these new neighbors, close to home and my office. First, the food: Great lunch spot. I love cozy places like this with daily specials (like Smile To Go, around the corner), and I especially love if you can get a mix of sides. I got a plate of two sides/salads - red rice and eggplant ratatouille which was excellent, and a fennel salad with mint and orange slices which was very good. I also shared a yummy cookie. The sandwiches looked great and I'll definitely try one soon. Second, the design: Beautiful. They've done a wonderful job decorating this to feel rustic/French countryside. Sitting in the back, away from the street with a beautiful garden outside, is relaxing and peaceful. Third, the staff: So friendly, including the owners/chef and the others working there. The only tiny negative thing I'd say is that it was very hot inside. But they're new, and I'm sure they'll work out the ventilation.

1. the people working are all so friendly and French. it's great. 2. the place smells DELICIOUS. so so good 3. cutest coffee cups, I want to take a whole sleeve home. can I do that? 4. interior is tres cute! super cozy in the back. love the wooden tables and the lighting. idk it's all very adorable 5. coffee is good. their nutty cookie is pretty darn good. I'm not sure what but it was cause I'm not good at differentiating, but it wasn't overwhelming, the chocolate just ooooozes out, and it's the right amount of crunchy on outside and soft on inside. 6. go visit!!!

After reading the reviews online I had to come visit this place and try the well-reviewed nutty choc chip cookie!!! The coffee they serve here I believe is Toby Estate, I got a drip coffee and it was superb, I love the beautiful cups they serve it in, I also adore the milk containers! We sat down the back, a great ambience and cozy place to catch up with friends and relax. Now came the bit I was most excited for- the cookie! The other images look different to the cookie I received.... as  noted in other reviews there are nuts and generous amounts of chocolate- my cookie had plenty of almonds, a few macadamia nuts, however, little/scant amount of chocolate. Msybe it was the one I received....I broke the entire cookie apart to realize it had only 3 pieces of chocolate. I went to the server to ask if this was how it was meant to be, she replied that she was allergic to nuts so she hadn't tried them. At $3.75 +tax  for the cookie I personally believe it is worth missing as is well overpriced. Go for the coffee- maybe you will have better luck with the cookie, or stick to savory! As they have just opened- they maybe still be fine tweaking everything!

Food-delicious, tastes as good as it looks. Perfect blend of fresh and tasty. Menu changes everyday so i definitely will be coming back Service- very friendly and seems as though they put a lot of care into what they serve. Perfect place in soho

This is a great place, I have had lunch here a couple of times.  My favorite is the shrimp in garlic sauce, which is fantastic.  I also has the portabella mushroom appetizer, which has the same sauce as the shrimp and it was surprisingly delicious.  I had the lobster tails and it was not memorable, my companions had the Hake & shrimp with crab meat, they were both excellent.  The potato chips are also fantastic, another reason to visit.  The staff is very friendly and engaging.

My mother's favorite restaurant, she will make ANY excuse to go to Spanish Tavern. her birthday, my birthday, my cousin in Florida's birthday, a birth in the family, a death in the family, we had my grandmother's retirement party downstairs in the private room, a job promotion, a graduation, lower gas prices, ANY EXCUSE & my all time favorite "what's wrong mom?" "I accidentally hit my toe on the edge of the table, if I had a pitcher of sangria from the Spanish Tavern I know it would feel better!" Needless to say, I've been here a lot in the last 5 years. THE PROBLEM for me with coming here is that I do not eat any red meat or sea food so it limits my choices on the menu , but they always have a pitcher of sangria & a delicious chicken entree for me that make's me want to come back for more. Most recently a pistachio crusted chicken breast - WOW it was soo delicious I have to share a photo with you. The staff is friendly, from the moment you walk in the do their best to make you comfortable. They are attentive and personable. The dining room is intimate & elegant. This place is A GEM . DON'T MISS OUT !!
they're over-priced, the menu is deceiving and the food isn't anything special.  don't waste your time.

This is a (mostly) chicken place with one pork dish.  The chicken was moist, portions were generous, and the burritos were fresh. They forgot the bar-b-que sauce for my son's chicken nuggets, which was more annoying because they made a big deal about their sauces, with free samples of different types.

Went here on a Saturday and it was fairly busy. The place isn't all that big so if there's a few people in there, it feels crowded. I ordered a grilled chicken sandwich and my wife had a grilled chicken burrito. The chicken on both was really good with the burrito having some additional spices incorporated. The sandwich was a little messy. The inclusion of the Canadian bacon was interesting as it really didn't add anything to the sandwich. Actually I didn't even notice it was there until I was almost done. My wife liked the burrito and said the rice was very similar to chipotle's rice. We also ordered a side of their fried potato slices (herbed Parmesan garlic). Those where awesome. The employees were all very friendly.
Large portions. The Norwegian Salmon was delicious and the rice was tasty. It was a great experience worth every penny

Not your typical Filipino joint! The menu is fused with malaysian, thai, vietnamese appetizers and entrees...very unique but smart! The food in a word, awesome. Crispy Pata, Crispy Thai Beef, Crispy Adobo Flakes...let's just say anything that starts with crispy in this place is GOOD! They also serve Thai ice tea and Halo-halo, the all-time favorite filipino dessert. For those who have not ever tried filipino food - this is the place to go to in NJ.

Overeaters anonymous. I don't know whether I should be proud to be part of this group or be totally disgusted with myself. Mind you, this only happens to me whenever I eat Filipino food. (or at a buffet -- duh!) Here are the dishes we feasted on: Crispy pata ($16) -- deep fried pork leg. It definitely lived up to its name, I can't get over the crispiness of the pig skin. Dip it in the soy-vinegar sauce and get ready for a fat-fest. Sisig ($17) -- chopped pieces of pork's cheeks/various parts of the pig's head mixed in. This was served with a cracked egg on a sizzling plate. You can taste the sourness of the kalamansi (Philippine Lemon) with salt, pepper and other "secret" spices. Sinigang na baboy ($16) -- pork stewed in a tamarind broth with veggies. The meat was seasoned well but the broth itself could've been more sour, meaning I want my face to pucker up and feel my salivary glands getting activated. Fried tofu ($5) -- crispy triangles of tofu with a sweet-chili dipping sauce. Left too long in the fryer and their sauce is definitely store bought because I use the same thing at home! Siomai ($5.50) -- steamed pork dumplings with mushroooms, carrots and water chestnuts.  It's decent. Molo soup ($5) -- basically siomai in chicken broth. My gf enjoyed this since she was feeling sick. Turon with ube ice cream ($6) -- plantains and jackfruit wrapped in a lumpia wrapper, rolled in brown sugar and deep fried. You can't go wrong with this dessert. Halo-halo ($8) -- literally translated this means "mix-mix". You get this dessert drink and you're supposed to carefully mix this without spilling any of its contents. Takes years of practice! You've got fruit preserves, red beans, rice crispies, flan and coconut slices topped with ice cream. (we had ube, but mango was an option too) The Fiipino dishes were done well even though Pandan describes its menu as Asian fusion because you can see some basic Thai and Chinese dishes in here too. This restaurant is going to be around for a long time since they've tweaked their menu enough to serve their non-Filipino customers as well.  The staff is welcoming and service is friendly. I definitely overate. I asked for second (and third!) helpings. When I thought I couldn't eat any longer, I plucked off the last grain of rice on my plate and asked the server to bag the rest of the food. I was so full from our lunch here that I needed a handsome rugged MAN in his flannel shirt and hard hat to wheelbarrow me out of here. Sadly, he never came.

Terrible service. Gave my drink away at the counter while waiting for my food outside. Kindly asked them for the drink I paid for and only got attitude. Refused to let me speak with the manager. If you act professionally, you shouldn't be afraid to give your name or manager. They need to work on their customer service.

First time here, and I would absolutely come again. Today's special soup (black bean) was great, and the fresh baked rolls were awesome. My wife came yesterday (Sunday) and said she had a great breakfast.

ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE. The food is disgusting. Don't go into place. Stay far away! Very unappetizing. Gave this place a few chances. It takes too long to get your food. Please avoid. Do not waste your time.

First, some pros: the layout of the cafe is really nice, with lots of marble, wide open spaces, and a cool black/white color scheme that gives the interior a chic high-end feel. I think I would enjoy hanging out here to work or relax on a nice day. That being said, I found the waffles rather underwhelming when I visited. Although I didn't try any of their other menu items, the waffle that I had was undercooked, rather small for the price and I even found a hair in it after taking a couple of bites! I've also tried some of their tarts, and although they were better than the waffles, there was nothing to write home about afterward. Overall, this is a welcome addition to the Broadway scene, but it isn't an exemplary restaurant by any means. I have noticed an increase in food quality and a decrease in prices since this place first opened, however. I hope that the upward trend continues, and I will be happy to give this place more stars as it matures!

A piece of Belgium in New Haven. Perfectly recreated with attention to the smallest detail. They serve great dishes scaled up to the American size standards. I tried the omelette and the croque monsieur so far and have been happy with both, not overwhelming with deliciousness but content. The ordering experience left me a bit frustrated though, the cashiers might need an attitude adjustment and some basic human skills like "how may I help you" or "next in line please". Just saying...
Because I enjoy el Sarape so much, I overlook the fact that it currently has a "B" rating from the health dept. Two carnitas tacos, tortilla, three great salsas, Mexican Coke...a standard in my diet.

Let's start with the fact: $20 might for a pork sandwich might seem like a lot especially if you're ordering for two or three people because suddenly you're paying $40-60. But, it's worth it. In the "pignic" you get the roasted pork sandwich, a bag of chips from a Long Island company that are crunchy and delicious, a huge pickle, a drink, a dessert and cole slaw plus some bbq-like sauce for the sandwich. The pork is tender, perfectly roasted and juicy. The onion jam is awesome. I have them leave the mayo off because I"m just not a mayo gal. The sandwich is addicting. To the dark horse of the meal: the cole slaw. I grew up around countless variations of cole slaw in the South: mayo, vinegar, with carrots, no carrots, pepper and detested them all. It was the cabbage, and mayo, that I didn't like. But then I tried Rocket Pig's apple cider vinegar cole slaw, which is, I think, just apple cider vinegar drenched cabbage. It changed my view on white cabbage at the very least. It's simple yet it's refreshing and light. it goes perfectly with the sandwich. Sometimes I take the Memphis BBQ route and put the slaw on the sandwich with the hot sauce. Heaven. The dessert: The first time Mr. F and I went there was this lemon molasses cookie that has stayed in my mind every day since. It hasn't been on offer since that I'm aware although the cookie is usually molasses. That's okay, because where it's at is the hazelnut mousse cookie. Just do it. It's creamy, rich and delectable. I took a pack home to my mom in Tennessee once and she reluctantly shared a bite with my 2 1/2 year old nephew. He's too young to appreciated the bliss that is that cookie. Save one or two for later and have it with a coffee or iced tea. Don't wait until they close. When they run out of pork that's it for the day.

Worst sandwich I've had, in a while. A corner deli would make a more decent sandwich than here. I went here based on the reputation of this place, but unfortunately it is way over rated. I wouldn't give this place a half a star for their food, atmosphere, customer service and pricing. Would not go here for any breakfast.

This place is great. During the week it's best for lunch and dinner. On Sunday they have a brunch menu and they really have some awesome items, check it out. I've never had a bad order from this place. The deserts are all home made and delicious. Check it out!
By far my favorite diner.  Solid food...it is our go to place when we can all agree on one thing.  Love the chocolate milk shakes -- usually get the burger.

Totally recommend this place. My friends and I have come here a bunch of times. Was so excited when they opened up and I keep coming back for more. The tacos, guac and those fries with chipotle mayo are awesome! The service is all ways wonderful!

I went to Rogues Gallery recently and was really impressed with the overhaul to the old TA Flanneries especially the menu.  Trust me, you will not be disappointed with the amazing buffalo wings, burgers, or Mac and cheese I promise.  Great neighbor joint to watch the Phillies.   Also, cozy atmosphere, great location, and fun Friday/Saturday night crowd with a DJ.

I go to cafe renata a lot. Usually when I'm doing laundry, but also whenever I need to take someone to brunch. Renata is AMAZING at brunch. Like, really really incredible. My roommate swears by the waffle rancheros and I personally love the eggs Benedict. And if you can, go for the mimosa carafe. Treat yourself. That said, renata just feels super awkward the rest of the week/day. Coffee and snacks are always good, but the place acts somewhere between a coffee shop and a restaurant and doesn't know which it wants to be. Yeah, I love that I can get a sandwich there. But the atmosphere is like a coffeeshop trying to sell you a steak. It feels a little odd. TL/DR: go for brunch or coffee.

I was excited to get breakfast on a weekday. I went on yelp to see where in the area had open places before 10am. Cafe Renata had OK reviews and we decided to give it a shot. My friend got the Waffle Ranchero. My friend said it was good, but nothing amazing. I tried a bite of this and I agreed. I do think the idea of this was pretty cool. I got the Eggs Benedict... I never had such yucky disgusting poached eggs in my life. First of all, one poached egg was already popped and the yolk was flowing all over my english muffin and to the bottom of my potatoes. Second, the egg white part tasted nastyyyyyyy. It was far beyond than just being bland.. I am tolerable with weird/bad tasting things and will normally try to eat everything b/c I don't like to waste food, but this time I cut out all the egg white out and ate just the english muffin, ham, and the runny yolk. The potatoes were good and I liked how they added sweet potatoes too. Cafe Renata is definitely overpriced considering the taste, and I will not come back here unless a friend says this is the only option..but you know Philly has way too many other places to try out.

Reliable, inexpensive. Perhaps nothing is the best, but everything is very good. I can't quite remember everything I've had here, but I don't remember ever not enjoying a dish. Go and explore for yourself.
checken and dougnuts are not you're run of the mill idea but this place just does it fantastic. service is a little wonky but ya can't win em all! would consider feastin here againLOL

I like the new location because it's big, has plenty of seating where you're not in the way of the line, and a parking lot that makes it a convenient stop for an after-work treat on the way home from the office. The donuts are still warm and amazing, but I wasn't as blown away by the fried chicken. I tried the buttermilk ranch dry rub and the chili garlic glaze. The buttermilk ranch left something to be desired. Upon first bite you can taste the ranch, but it quickly becomes bland and flavorless. The chili garlic was very good, though, and I'll be back to try the other flavors.

So I heard about Federal Donuts and checked it out yesterday. We bought a 1/2 dozen donuts and chicken, our total came to $16.00. Before my husband ordered I told him $9.00 for some chicken is way too expensive but the girl at the counter said they were really big pieces of chicken so he agreed to buy. Ok first the donuts... they were ok we had the warm ones two of each flavor. They are way to sweet topped with sugar so if you have any type of sugar problems this is not the place for you. Now to the chicken.. We opened the box...really 4 pieces of chicken for $9.. 2 drum sticks and 2 small ass thighs. The chicken was alright but it wasn't worth $9. I find this place was over priced and mediocre taste wise. I wont be coming here again.

Hip hip hooray the bar is open, have been there several times and loved it. The staff is amazing could not have been affored better service anywhere. Have to say the food is true comfort all the way round . Please do yourself a favor and try out the newest gem in east passyunk crossing. I promise it's the bomb.

I like the place so far, after about 3 visits.  The decor is gorgeous and the food is pretty good.  However, the beer and wine selection could use some help.  They've been serving Gallo Chardonnay, which to me is very sub-par.  Their beers are better, but still not the full selection I'd like to see  It lacks the microbrews I expect out of a S Philly drinking establishment (although they do carry Dogfish Head 60 minute, so that's good).  That said, I still think this is a nice place to have in the neighborhood and I plan to be a regular!

Ever since I moved up here, Tops Diner has been one of my go-to places, whether it's for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. It's right around the corner from my apartment, so I tend to make multiple stops/pickups a week at times. Still would make the trip even if it wasn't close though...totally worth it! I've tried a good deal of their menu by now and they've pretty much all been winners. If you're in the mood for burgers, try the short rib one...it's my clear favorite of the bunch. Breakfast is my personal comfort food, and their pancakes hit the spot every time. Hell, I even like their salads (which isn't something I typically order when I go out to eat)...although I think they recently cut a couple of my favorites with their new menu slim-down (honey fried chicken salad and BBQ chicken salad were pretty great...so sad). Oh yeah, and definitely do try one of their numerous cheesecake varieties, too. Only issue is that the wait can get pretty long at times, especially weekend mornings. Line is usually out the door.

Great Food, Impressive Portions!! Price is on the higher end for a "Diner", but the quality of food and portion size completely justify it.. Wait is a given here as the place is literally bombarded with people!! Parking is a breeze as well thanks to the rather generous parking spots provided. Must Try!!

I LOVE THIS PLACE!!! I've been coming here about once a week for a year or so. Legit everything is delicious. I believe they just revamped their menu too! Favorite Dishes: Chicken Parm - heavenly Buffola roles - Divine Navajo Chicken Pasta - add shrimp - to die for Check it out, you wont regret it!
Everything is Delicious. I've been here several times! you will not regret it!

Such a great smell comes out of this diner, they have ample parking and seating inside. My first time coming here, inside looks brand spanking new and clean there is a lot of staff. I looked at the breakfast menu and boy do they have choices, in the end I went for George's combo a little bit of everything for ten bucks. Very tasty fresh ingredients and its pretty rare for a dinner to use cage free eggs, tried the turkey bacon it was the best I've ever had-thick cuts and soft unlike regular turkey bacon. Next time I want to try one of there versions of eggs Benedict, prime rib burgers and red velvet pancakes.
Wonderful diner with delicious and vast options and generous portions, friendly service. Will be back!

This is a 4 star place, but a 5 star diner. We went for desserts but everything we saw looked amazing. Portions are generous. The fuzzy bear hard milkshake with Peach Schnapps was amazing. Can't wait to try more.

Since I've been a student in Newark for the past year and a half, I've probably been to Tops about a dozen times.  Each time I go, I come away thinking I ordered the wrong thing.  Not because what I ordered was bad, but because the menu is massive and something else always looks better than what I have.  Its gotten to the point that I don't like going because it takes me so long to decide what to get. I've tried the gyro, the chicken and waffles, the appetizer sampler, the chili, the chicken pot pie, etc.  Everything savory I order is decent/good (with the exception of the chicken pot pie, which is bad). What I really like coming to tops for however, is the cheesecake.  Each piece is massive and exactly the way cheesecake should be (heavy, creamy, and not too sweet). Definitely an upscale diner with pretty good food that you should visit if you're in the area.  Try to avoid weekends, however, since there is always a long wait.

My husband was a little concern as we entered this industrial looking area but as soon as we turned the corner and saw the shiny diner we knew we were in for a great experience. It was very busy but they still got us in within 10 minutes and service was swift and very pleasant. The food was over whelming. So much to choose from and they all sounded amazing. Portions are huge so we split a burger and a salad. I know that sounds boring but they were both memorable. Give it a try, you won't be disappointed!

Tops never disappoints. Such an expansive and varied menu and you can never go wrong from breakfast staples such as omelets and pancakes to diner staples such as cheeseburgers and wraps all the way up to fancier finds like lobster mac and cheese. The cheesecakes and desserts are to die for as well.  Salads are also huge and amazing. Not your typical diner pricing but it's not your typical diner either and I've never had a bill where the meal wasn't worth it. Great for breakfast, dinner, late night rendeveous, or even ordering lunch with the office if you're in the area. My office orders from here all the time but make sure to pass the menu around well in advance especially for newbies since it's a huge menu with so many various options. Also, pick up only sadly no delivery. Full bar ! If you go during busy hours expect a wait especially for weekend breakfast and lunch. Always call ahead to check on the wait if you're in a rush.

Super great, super cute little spot on Carmine. Their food looks delicious, their juices are super wonderful. I would totally go back. I was here late on a Saturday night and it was getting kind of quiet, the employees were obviously cleaning up and let us hang out until they really really needed us to leave. I loved it here and would totally go back and try more stuff.

Had a very cool, open, Cali vibe, which I really liked.  Service was friendly and attentive.  However, the food portions are bizarre.  I ordered the grilled cheese & my pal the chicken paillard.  My sandwich was big and delicious.  His, I couldn't even see his chicken and the portion was stupidly small.  About the same price for both.  My guess is generally this spot is pandering to the model-esque, pretend "vegan" aka I don't like to eat crowd of the West Village, but have a little consistency here.  The decor/furniture is basically saying, "If you're not small, go elsewhere" too.   Likely won't be back,but again, food quality was good and service great.
Delicious food, great people - will definitely be visiting again when we return to NYC. Happy Birthday Leith!!

A surprise sleeper entry for the best burger in Philadelphia list! Business lunch: saw the Angus burger listed and decided to give it a try. The waitress said they pick out the meat specifically for this burger - and boy does it show! Weighty, beefy, big and juicy. Beef-orama flavor. Yes indeed folks, they serve a burger to be proud of. Got the Greek salad as a side rather than fries and was not disappointed. Plentiful, fresh, crumbled feta, diced cucumbers - a real treat. Followed up here next day and tried the lamb gyro. While prepared well and tasty, its on the skimpy side for a gryo - I've had better. Not that this was bad, just not at the same level as the burger. Who woulda' guessed? A big, bad, burger that puts many a philee tavern to shame. I rate it a tie to SPTR's on the burgerlicious scale , but still see SPTR as the overall favorite based on the total package and associated beer selection ;-) Burgerlicious rating = 7

I had lunch at Canal Street today with my co-workers.  We arrived around 12:30 and the place was packed!  Good sign.  The menu featured lots of greek fare (gyros, etc.), salads with feta, various sandwiches and even burgers.  Definitely something for everyone.  The service was quick and courteous, even though they were super busy.  I had the swiss chicken pita sandwich, which I enjoyed.  The salads and the gyros were very popular choices.  Prices are a tad high for lunch, but you get what you pay for.  Everything was fresh and delicious.  I hope to return soon.

The drinks aren't out of this world and kind of over priced. The place tries to hard to look olden and kitschy but it just looks/feels very artificial. I came on a Sunday night and it was very easy to get a table.  The food was pretty good, not your standard greasy bar food (I enjoyed the quinoa salad with kale butternut squash and pomegranate). To me I equate this place to spitzers corner, a rustic looking place which is primarily a bar but has food. I just prefer the atmosphere, crowd, food, and beer section better at spitzers. Sorry.

Really 3.5 stars, but I'll round up.  This is a loud, crowded place right on Houston.  Gets more of a LES crowd than East Village.  The food was alright, the duck confit carbonara was good, but nothing to rush back to get again.  The chicken look pretty good, would get next time.  Beers are a little on the expensive side, but they have a great selection and in full pints.  Overall a good place if you're in the area.

If first impressions are everything, Boulton & Watt has won me over. But before I get into that, two warnings: 1. One of the waiters looks exactly like my ex-coworker. EXACTLY. Creepily so. 2. It is extremely loud in here. If you come in at 8 pm on a Saturday for dinner, it's already going to be 11 pm at a LES bar with two or three bachelorette parties loud in here. It's in a prime location in probably the heaviest drinking neighborhood in the city, so it isn't surprising...it's just worth noting. You're probably only concerned about one of those, but if you can get past the resemblance, you're going to have a good time. They've got the drinks: Despite the volume I'm sure they are doing, the bar made me several excellent cocktails (except the Copper Bullet, which I guess they were out of). They've got the food: The Scotch Egg is as good as any I've ever tasted, and the accompanying Petit Mache salad cuts the richness perfectly. I wasn't allowed to order a burger because APPARENTLY, three burgers in five days is too many. But I definitely wasn't mad about my gorgeous chicken pot pie (although I tasted the blackened brick chicken which almost knocked me over with the flavor). Evidently, they are into the pickling as well. They have almost ten different options (loved the pickled pineapple with the habaneros), each at $5. I must say though, if each jar is $5, you don't need to tell me that it's 3 for $15. I can do most simple math (as long as I have a pen and paper). Tell me how many three jars cost only if you're giving me a bulk discount (which you should). They've got the atmosphere: It's a full-on scene (hence the noise), and people-watching with the aforementioned food and drinks keep me more than happy. To be sure though, things aren't perfect. As with any new place, there were a couple service hiccups, and one of my friends was sorely disappointed with the size of the fish in the fish & chips. All in all though, I'm definitely glad Boulton & Watt is here, especially since Nice Guy Eddie was really, really mean to me. So much so that it made me wonder how he got that name.

Went on a date here last night.....after getting a few drinks elsewhere in the neighborhood, we stumbled upon this gem.  It was about 9pm, the place was jumping and yet we were seating right away.  Our waiter was very nice and quick with our drink order.   We both got the burger and I must say, it was cooked to perfections.  The portion of fries that it came with was a bit on the large side and they appeared to be over seasoned, but they coupled well with the burger.   Overall, great experience. Would love to go back with a group for dinner or drinks.  The windows and the decor were perfect.

What a fantastic gastropub!  It smells lovely the moment you walk in; the decor is fascinating to anyone who appreciates history and design.  The host was kind and welcoming, we had a drink at the bar, then seated by the window when the rest of our party arrived. I thought the bench seat would be uncomfortable but it was fine, and we had a nice view of the entire place from a cosy corner.  It gets quite loud and very crowded, but I can understand why... The location is fab and the food was lovely!  Our table ordered beers, cocktails and wine, the food was just perfect (I ordered the veggie burger with perfectly seasoned chips), and we had the cast-iron chocolate chip cookie to share (comes with whole milk - delicious!).  Our waitress was friendly too - overall, very impressed with service, food quality and ambience.

Holy crap, it's packed here on a Saturday night! And yeah, it's freakin' loud. Primarily, I think this is because most people here are actually eating rather than drinking. A good sign for a gastropub I guess. We weren't here for food though. A friend of a friend was having a birthday party here. Drinks are fairly priced. I like their all-you-can-drink booth in the back.

This place has a lot of potential if they improve their food. Their calamari was decent. However the lobster roll tasted too fishy and the fish and chips was too salty.  Their outdoor garden has a nice atmosphere .But, the food is just not worth coming back.

I'd give it a solid meh. The fish & chips were not great -- fish was really, really dry. French fries were good, but it's hard to eff those up. Service was fairly decent -- they were very friendly but not the most attentive.  I'd go back to try it again when it's not so hot out -- temperature in there was pretty balmy.
Great Great food even tho i have not been here in over 10 years The blue claw crab is the best to order.
Something good

Giving 5 stars !!! Food is outstanding, I've eaten in a different restaurants, from high end to a hole in the wall type . Cooks in this restaurant deserve a special reword.  Sangria won my heart. I've had sangria before, but whatever they do to it ... It's magic!!! We had two pitchers for three of us, and wasn't enough. Not watery at all , refreshing and flavorful with a lot of fresh fruits. Highly recommend this place if you looking for authentic  Portuguese food and not also if you like seafood this is the restaurant for you.

I'm portuguese and I use to highly recommend all of my friends to go here but after the food that I was served last Thursday you can say I will never come back. Went to celebrate my honey's birthday and boy was I disappointed. We started off with the shrimp 7 garlic ( which was the only good thing)  He ordered the Surf & turf (lobster was VERY dry)  I got the Bife a Portuguesa (extremely fatty steak) Just not worth what it is anymore.

Friendly service, good food.  I did not find it quite as delicious as others.  The chicken is crispy, juicy, but very salty.  Not a big problem, but less salt and more seasoning might make it better.  Cornbread quite good, nice and moist.  I'm sure I'll be getting chicken there again at some point.

This was our last meal as a complete family as my in laws are retiring to Asia.  So we decided to go with an all American meal, fried chicken.  Young lady who took our order was courteous and reviewed our order before giving our total which is a lost detail in so many take out restaurants.   Our order was the 16 pc fried chicken, corn bread, mashed potatoes and mac n cheese.   Side dishes were ok.  Although well seasoned,  really nothing more to say.  Pretty standard.  A must order is the corn bread!  Nice, sweet, almost cake like texture! At .59 a pop you can't go wrong here.  The main event, the fried chicken was really good.  Moist, juicy, and fresh.  Breading was not overwhelming and overall well seasoned, although a tad salty.  Pieces were nice and big.  You definitely get good portions here with the exception of the sides.  I would offer a family size on those items.   Overall a positive experience and a good alternative from the chains out there.  A solid 4 stars from me.

this was excellent ! eggplant rollatini was best we ever had -  definitley be back - the owners and chef were very attentive- they  were out of the ahi ttuna special and chef came over and suggested the scallops which were amazing - cooked perfectly served with an awesome arugala pesto really good! nice atmosphere too

Years back this was my go to place, Great food, great service and a busy and fun place - even at lunch. So I was very disappointed when I had a chance to go back and have lunch. Not that it was bad - it was just average. The sole was done well and the service was attentive. the bread was standard fare but we were pleased the staff was happy to offer salad/double vegetable for the meals. I plan to go back as there was me interesting items on the menu to try - but its a bit out of my may and well max and Trumbull Kitchen really pop when you visit - Peppercorns needs to make me want to come back.

I write this sitting at peppercorn grill waiting for my dinner plate to be cleared. My fiancé and I had high hopes for our meal, we had tried peppercorn back in the winter during restaurant week and really enjoyed our experience. We had great food and a great server. A few months back we bought a groupon and tonight was the night to use it. To start we walked in and the host looked us up and down like we didn't belong. And even when he found our reservation he couldn't figure out where to sit us. (Our reservation was at 630 and most tables in the main dining room was empty). He also just pointed us to the table and didn't actually seat us or give us menus. As a matter of fact we got our bread well before our menus. Next was our waitress. She appeared already stressed and again there were maybe 3 other tables seated. She barely acknowledged us throughout our meal and frankly was just a giant sourpuss. One table actually said loud enough for us to hear how bad she was. We were impressed by the specials menu, we had many more options to choose from over their basic menu. We had the antipasto for the table which was delicious, so we had high hopes for our entrees. My fiancé had Chilean sea bass with shrimp and veggies, it was just ok, the description on the menu was better. I took a risk and ordered the cod special with lump crab topping, asparagus and a potato cake. The presentation was nice and that's about it. I suspect my food was victim to the heat lamp as my fish was so overcooked it was dead, buried and the funeral was already over by time it was served to me. It was very disappointing. We were looking forward to a great meal and this really fell short. We passed on desert. We are going to sonic for ice cream where you are greeted and served with a smile ;)

I went with friends on a Monday night. The place is decorated nicely with good atmosphere. The service was pretty good and the staff friendly. I found the menu a bit confusing written half in Italian and half in English. I couldn't pronounce the name of what I wanted to eat and simply had to point to it on the menu like a moron. I had the chicken with mushrooms, seared vegetables and mashed potatoes. It was ok but not great. It seemed that the chicken was a little over cooked, the mushroom crust a little too crusty, the vegetables were bitter and the mashed potatoes somewhat watery. We sat near the front and the constant thumping of the front door closing as people came and went was disconcerting. Would I go back? Nah. I don't mind paying high prices for a good experience but felt Peppercorns came up a little short.

So yummy. So fresh! I came here on Sunday night with my mom and two other friends. Called ahead for the reservation but they don't take any reservation. My friend arrived earlier and put us on waiting list. It was an hour wait! We ordered oyster, cheese, shrimp, mussel, scallops and clam fettuccine.  Everything was so delicious!  Love this restaurant! For sure will come again probably during not busy weekday lunch time to avoid the wait :)

Waited an hour to eat here but it was definitely worth it. Got the fettuccine with clams and it was phenomenal.  The sauce was nice and creamy and the clams were fresh. Pasta was cooked just right. The menu is kind of small, but I guess that works for indecisive people. The portion size is also kinda small, doesn't really get a hungry guy full, but don't let that deter you just get something to eat later if you're still hungry. My friends and I got 3 different kinds of beer that they make and they were all fantastic.  I think I had a summer wheat beer with orange it was really good. Would come back again, but maybe if the wait was 30 minutes or something. I guess a party of 3 is kind of hard to seat though so it could be my fault. Don't forget: get the fettuccine with clams and a beer, can't go wrong.
This is a great place. Hope to come back soon

AMAZING! Amazing food, amazing service! I was somehow able to get a table on a Friday night around 7:30 - no wait! (I was shocked). They do not take reservations. I would guess that the whole place could have 30 patrons, tops. Perfect for small groups of 4 or less. The taps at the bar are labels with letters, and nothing else.  There is a very rustic feel/vibe and the ambiance is further enhanced with the small wooden tables. First, our waiter brought us a little appetizer with roasted red peppers and fish on a crab shell - he told us it was from the kitchen and that they were considering putting it on the menu. I loved the pairing and the seasoning of the peppers. My boyfriend didn't like it as much though. For dinner, we ordered the mussels (an entrée) to split as an appetizer. They were HUGE and so fresh! Instead of being cooked in a white wine sauce they were made with a beer sauce.  They were served with a dish of toasted crustinis - perfect for dipping in that yummy beer sauce. When we finished the mussels, we asked our waiter for some more. Before he came back, another waiter came over and asked us if we wanted more bread.  Very attentive waiters! For dinner my boyfriend had the swordfish and a local beer and I had oysters with wine.  Both were on top of a bed of vegetables that were amazing. We both kept taking bites of each other's meal and could not decide which was better.  Although the portion sizes seemed small, we both left full and had decided we wanted to go back, especially since the menu is always changing. As we got the check, the waiter brought out some whiskey cake. It was super moist and not too whiskey-ish. We both agreed that we could have easily ordered 3 slices. Overall everything that we ordered was amazing, perfectly cooked and well seasoned. I loved that the menu is always changing and that the food is so fresh - there is no freezer! Great date place, especially for the seafood lover. The service was top notch. Our waiter was super attentive but so were the other waiters.  We totally felt like VIP guests but I can tell ever table felt just as special.  I would 100% come back here.
My favorite Oyster place in the city.  They don't take reservations so sometimes it's a bit of a wait, but just head to a bar nearby, the wait is worth it!

Upstate has been on my list to try for one of the longest time. Since it was my treat for 2 of my girlfriends' birthday, I used this opportunity to kill 2 birds with one stone. Upstate is a small restaurant that can serve about 35 customers. My original plan was to get there by 5 in order to grab a table, but one of the birthday girls was extremely late. (FYI-they do not seat you until the whole party is there). But no worries, we decided to just eat at the bar and I couldn't be happier with the result. We were able to chit chat with the owner and he was kind enough to share complimentary chicken pate amuse and tastings to the newest craft beer on tap (I personally loved the ginger one but forgot what it was called). Upstate has a limited menu but everything was very fresh. We ordered maybe half of the dishes from the menu ;) Food wise: 1) Happy Hour Special was 6 oysters + 1 craft beer for $12. We ordered 3 rounds of it and our favorite choice was the tomahawk oysters. 2) Crab cakes were lightly seared to perfection and they weren't as breaded as most places so you can really taste the chunks of crabmeat. 3) The Wild Clams baked in beer were plump and they gave us at least a pound worth of clams. 4) The Scallop Special was my favorite dish for the night. The zucchini, squash, and roasted mushrooms made great sides. 5) Roasted Pollock (in cod family) was also good but the corn they used was absolutely amazing and sweet. 6) The complimentary whiskey cake at the end was delicious too. They even put a birthday candle on it for my friend. 7) Uni was probably my least favorite dish and I wasn't a big fan of the caviars. However, my friends found it interesting. Overall, I had a fantastic time!

Had an amazing experience! Arrived at 445 opened the door, well the greeting was not the nicest, but I am a Chef so I get it. Open is open and closed is closed.... Ok so we sat first only to watch the whole police fill up in 8 minutes flat. This is a wonderful sign! Happy hour special 6 oysters and a beer for 12 dollars. Everything was so fresh and delicious! You can tell there was no re shucking going on here. Fresh, clean, juicy, and plump Oysters. Had a few apps also that were just as good as the oysters, and the Clam Pasta although a little greasy I couldn't stop eating it. All in All Really great spot kudos to you guys for doing a great job!!!!

Me: Two for tonight? Hostess: Oh, we're not taking any more reservations for tonight. Me: It's 5 o clock. Hostess: (Annoying smile) I know. The food is amazing. The oysters make you wanna thank the sea. The wait sucks. The service doesn't. The hostess? Don't even get me started... But hey, it's well worth having to ask her for a table every time you go, that is, if she gives you one... Overall: Good seafood from a southerner that knows it well.

Just fantastic. Maybe an overly glowing impression since i'm coming from the depressing DC food scene but this place was grand. Atmosphere, service, but above all fantastic food. The oysters were incredibly fresh and perfectly shucked - zero residue. Plus the waiter knowledgeably and accurately walked is through the options. Beers were great - as were the wines. Music was great but not intrusive - ditto in the wait staff. Mains were great too - though think my scallops served with variety of squash were slightly better than the fish. We were there on a Saturday so pretty busy but still the wait wasn't more than 10 minutes. Will absolutely go back next time i'm in NY

I would rate it a 3 1/2 actually=)  But since I can't I'm going to round up to 4. Bread that came was good.  The part that was unique is a eggplant tapenade that was quite tasty. Appetizer was calamari fries.  My wife and I thought we would try something different.  It's basically calamari in the shape of a mozzarella stick.  Same breading, calamari is thicker than the rings.  It was slightly over fried.  I prefer the rings which are more lightly breaded. Entrees were a pork chop (bone-in) with long peppers and potatoes.  Pork chop was tender and flavorful.   The long peppers make it spicy with a kick so if you don't like spicy don't get this.  Black linguine had crab and flavorful shrimp with some spinach. The flavoring was good.  I personally like pasta that is adente because the pasta is made with squid ink it does have a softer texture.  So if you're not into that then don't get it.  My wife loved it. Dessert - tiramisu was light and tasty.  Gelato included some flavors I haven't commonly seen  - rice pudding and raspberry chocolate.   Service was good although when the dining room got busy - it started to lag. I would definitely come again - but it is quite pricey.  $100 (w/o tip) includes one app, two entrees, one kids meal, soda/juice and two desserts.

Beija Flor is the best introduction the Brazilian food and live music. Visiting Brazil is on my to do list & one visit to Beija Flor will make you want to apply for your visa right there! I visited the quaint LIC restaurant this past Saturday to see a live samba band performance.  Staff immediately greeted us and were able to accomadate our big group.  Our waitress kindly explained our menu options and even warned of large portion sizes especially the meat platters! (This is carnivore heaven - Carne del Sol appetizer all the way =D) We reviewed the wine list and realized wait we are in Brazil & ordered a round of caipirinhas.  They were tasty and full of sugar but I think they went easy on us. As the band started, a couple people casually samba dance around their tables and with others.  Don't worry this is a judge free zone and anyone who knows anything Brazilian samba can be as lively or lazy as you want. Just have fun.  The musicians then began to give the audience instruments to play and we all made nice additions to band.   Needless to say we had a fantastic time at Beija Flor, Great people (patrons & staff), lively music, delicious food and drinks and warm, cozy atmosphere.  Beija Flor is more than a restuarant; it's a great tourism advertisement for Brazil. If you can't get to Brazil this year, check out Beija Flor. This is as good as it gets! Keep it up :)

With the closing of Da Ciro on Lexington Avenue in NYC, we decided to venture out to Maspeth, NY to Ciro's sister restaurant Forno Pizzeria E Trattoria.  Of course we needed our fix of the amazing Focaccia Robiola, so we picked up some wine and headed to Maspeth.  The Verde family were incredibly welcoming and prepared some wonderful pastas and of course, the incredible Focaccia Robiola.  I am pretty sure I can say they served the best tiramisu I have ever tried in my life!  It's a small, family run restaurant and they make everyone who walks in the door feel like you're part of their family.  It's casual and they don't have a liquor license, so be sure to bring your own.  If you are lucky enough to live close, head over and try Forno right now.  If you're a bit out of town, it's worth the trip!  Can't wait to return.

What a new found treasure; a gem of restaurant with authentic Georgian cuisine on Bleecker St. in the Village! The lunch menu was affordable and with 2 courses plus dessert and soda, it gave me a chance to "sample" some dishes. From the hot cheese stuffed bread to the meat dumplings everything was delicious (all made fresh on the premisis with wonderful ingredients imported from Georgia). The dinning room has a nice decor with fine art and a restful garden as a backdrop.  Great, keep it up, I'll be back for sure. Marty

Last Friday I with another 12 colleges went for lunch to Old Tbilisi Garden. It was absolutely amazing how tremendously people of different preferences and ethnic backgrounds enjoyed the whole experience - outstanding food (both taste and presentation), the décor, which brings you back in time to Old Tbilisi, the atmosphere made of delicate combination of genuine friendliness of the owner and superb level of service of the waiters. We tried and shared quite a few things on the menu: Imeruli, Khinkali, Pxali Trio, Lula Kebab - just to mention a few. And what kind of Georgian cuisine would it be without famous Khachapuri and Shoti?! And, OMG, one was better than the other! There was not a single person who was not raving about the time we had at Old Tbilisi Garden. All of my colleges including myself we'll be very frequent visitors to this place. Thank you for bringing Old Tbilisi with its hospitality and the food meeting the highest demands of the true connoisseurs to downtown Manhattan!

This place is the best!  Georgian food is an experience and the owners are passionate about sharing it.  Everything about this restaurant is quality and the owners are cutting no corners on delivering the very best food at reasonable (for NYC) prices. If trying a cuisine you've never heard of seems a little daunting, just stick with the Khinkali (think dumpling, but better than anything you are used to) and Khachapuri (think delicious warm bread with eggs and cheese and other goodness baked right in).  It's like eating comfort food while trying an entirely new cuisine - delicious through and through. Georgia is also famous for its wines, and now that Old Tbilisi Garden has its liquor license, I can't wait to go back and check out what they have to offer!
Kebabs are delicious!  Highly recommend.  The weather was perfect so we sat in the garden which is cute and charming.  We will be back as soon as they secure their liquor license :)

My wife and I were walking down Bleecker Street on our way to Little Italy during a weekend visit to NYC when we noticed a "sandwich board" picturing what looked like a bread bowl filled with melted cheese and topped with an egg.  Two women were outside looking at the menu, and I asked if they knew the name of the dish.  One of the women said it was "Ajaruli," a Georgian specialty.  (I looked it up at home and some recipes refer to it as "Acharuli.")  First things first, if you ever stumble into Old Tbilisi, order this!  It is possibly the best thing that I have ever eaten.  We sat at the bar.  While waiting for our food, I asked the bartender, Giorgi, to pick out a glass of semi-sweet wine.  His pick was an "Ojaleshi," also from Georgia.  I had never had a wine from Georgia before.  It had a sweet front and a refreshingly dry finish.  (So did the next two glasses.)  It paired very well with the Ajaruli which one of the owners, David, came by to show us how it is traditionally eaten.  He also had us try some therapeutic mineral.  We were also introduced to Vasil, his brother and co-owner.  Everyone was extremely friendly and proud of their culture.  Next time we are in New York, we are heading right to Old Tbilisi.

The people who work there are nice, the food I had was excellent (the turkey meatloaf sandwich), the hot chocolate was delicious, and the decor was interesting. A little off the beaten path, but that just adds to its charm. All in all, a good addition to an already wide selection in North Williamsburg.
Homemade pop tarts.  Nuff said.

A good place to go after taking some pictures of the Brooklyn Bridge. Pros: good food, nice ambiance, great location. Cons: service struggled hardcore. I mean real hardcore. We were asking for forks and water and napkins and refills and the check like it was our last wish and the genie was in a no bullshit mood. Genie why so harsh? All I want is the check to pay you back. Nope.
Nothing to see here. Dive bar, garden variety margaritas, greasy food (the photos speak for themselves)- seems this has been done before... Stay clear of the spicy beer cocktail- yuk.
So so food but excellent service
Amazing!

I'll make this simple...if you're a foodie with an insatiable craving for burgers, go here. If you love Plan B or Max Burger but just aren't in the mood to wait 45 minutes to be seated....go here. If you think Five Guys (which is fine, no offense to them at all) is the best burger you've had....you need to go here. if you think Jake's Wayback Burger is awesome...you're wrong....and go here. Regular menu items are already dynamite...but check the daily specials board for out of this world experimental greatness. I'm talking about things like short rib sliders, the Chicken & Waffle burger (which NEEDS to become a permanent item,) the Slumdog Millionaire, and their oh-so decadent daily dessert items. You will NOT be disappointed.

Great burger joint that I have been going to for 3 years now.  If you like blue cheese like I do get the blue and gold burger, it is very satisfying and love the general atmosphere of the place.  Just fun to be there and the food is great.

Went in 3.9.13. First time NOT ordering a burger, but Matt & Company have stepped their game up. Go here knowing that non burger options aren't dialed in. They are viable and delicious options. I tried the smoked pulled pork sandwich and the cheese/smoked pulled pork/slaw hot dog. Both great. They're their own bacon and are always trying and adding new menu items. They enjoy customer feedback to consistently improve their game.

First time visit. Definitely not a four star Place. When ordering the cashier obviously did not want to answer any questions about the menu. Felt as if my party was not welcome because of the time of day (around 1:30pm). When ordering, they were out of many things, and once again, the cashier was rude about telling me of the other options. When some of my parties food was being brought to the table, the food runner was rude and seemed angry at us for not getting a number for the order yet. She slightly threw the tray towards our table. When it comes to the food, the coffee tastes a little watered down. I understand it won't be as fresh at this time of day, but still... Also, the order was wrong. After the rude customer service I would expect my order to at least be correct. I returned my order and decided to head to Wendy's. At least they have better service there. Don't plan to return.

I sat on a bus for 2 hours and then trekked through the rain for one reason: to enjoy a real Philly cheesesteak for the first time in my life. Rather than taking a cab to Pat's and Geno's, our local tourist guide brought us to Jim's Steaks. Walking up to Jims (a mere 6 blocks that was more of a mere 20), it hits all of the right heart-thumping tourist traps. - Line running out the door (even in the rain) - Signed photos of celebs on the wall - 4+ star review on Yelp - Simple menu - Loud man behind the counter barking for your order "Uh oh," I thought as I crossed my fingers and ordered, "Cheesesteak with whiz and mushrooms, please." Hands flew as the man quickly opened a bun, slathered some cheese whiz on it, and flipped some cooked steak onto the roll before dumping a mountain of onions and then mushrooms atop the growing pile of deliciousness. I paid for that sucker and sprinted upstairs to score a seat at a table. And that's where the beauty of it all began. I bit into the cheesesteak and a huge YUM hit me right in the kisser. Happiness consumed me on the spot, and I was the 2nd (out of the 6 of us) to finish their cheesesteak (losing only to Tim M, who to be fair, was /starving/). While I haven't had other Philly cheesesteaks IN Philly, I'm not sure if I'd be willing to risk trying another place. Jim's makes my taste buds dance, so why risk forcing them to be wallflowers at another mediocre place? 5 stars for Jim's!

I started my cheesesteak experience at Pat's and Geno's and am glad I made my way over to Jim's (don't worry, not all on the same day!).  This location is not very convenient to the city (located in the middle of a West Philly neighborhood), but the cheesesteak was great!  I will probably check out the other location next time and hope for equally good food, but more convenience. The staff was really nice - I had a few out-of-towners with me and the chef very nicely and calmly explained the options and ordering process.  I got the cheesesteak with provolone, onions, sweet peppers, and spicy peppers - yum.  The meat was the most moist of all the cheesesteaks I've had. Two advantages over the other places I've tried: 1) there is indoor seating at a counter (although it's very limited) and 2) the spicy peppers and other condiments were inside rather than sitting out at the curbside in the hot sun.  Not super cheap at ~$7/cheesesteak, but I think that's the going rate and you definitely get better quality here.

My wife and I stopped in on a Wednesday, which is a limited prix fixe menu.  The waiter was dressed a little bit too casual for my preference, but he was friendly and gave good service.  The food was very good.  I had the curried pumpkin soup for an appetizer, my wife had zucchini/cheese (I forget what kind of cheese) fritters.  I thought her fritters would be heavy and greasy, but they were remarkably light - mostly zucchini, not cooked for very long.  I was impressed.  My entre was the wild mushroom risotto, she had free range chicken on wilted spinach with grilled vegetables.  We were both pleased.  For desert, I had a baked apple that was prepared with a cognac and walnut stuffing.  I can't remember what my wife's dessert is called, a little baked pudding sort of thing, but she liked it quite a lot.   I am a cheapskate who likes to go out and likes wine, so I noted that bottles of wine are half price on Thursdays and they have interesting Italian specials for $9.95 on Fridays.  I would be inclined to come back for one of these specials.  All in all, a worthwhile stop.  I'll be back.

We went here to eat the garlic sauce featured on "Best Thing I Ever Ate - Garlic".  In truth this sauce is hugely garlicky, which is OK in its own right, but this sauce is also nearly tasteless otherwise.  No tomato taste, no lively spices.  Also, its consistency is thick and almost pastey.  I ate 2/3s of mine; my partner who loves anything with garlic could only finish 1/3.  To make it all worse, the pasta was over cooked and clearly not homemade.  All in all, this is a low quality Italian restaurant.  You need only look at the bread they serve; it's white bread out of a loaf of Wonderbread (or its equivalent).  Only Italian restaurant I have ever eaten at that did that!

Just what this this culinary mecca needs, still   another Italian/pizza joint. Why won't someone open a nice bistro somewhere nearby? Why?
