After returning to my hometown after living in Brooklyn for the past 20 years, man do I miss great little neighborhood bars and restaurants. This area needs some. Desperately. But instead we get another ancient Trenton transplant. And ancient is a good word to describe this place. The menu is the same as it was 20+ years ago. The same cheesy 1970s bottles of oil and red wine vinegar on the table, an antipasto that still consists of iceberg lettuce, beets (?!!), and little bits of chopped up salami and cheese that look like little dog food kibbles, same as it did in the 80's. The pizza? Eh. Barely decent. It may have a new location, but this place is dated and tired. Which is fitting because while the place was packed, almost everyone in there was 65+.  I guess they're reliving the Papas of their youth. In short, It can't hold a candle to Delorenzos, which actually evolved when they moved to Robbinsville with great and unique modern salads, and the pizza is just worlds better. Sorry Papa. You're living in the past.
Great pizza! Amazing service...I love these guys! I just moved to the area and obviously, I needed a great pizza place that delivers. You can't go wrong.

Do you know how hard it is to get anything other than pizza delivered after 9pm in South Philly? Do you know how mediocre the vast majority of what passes for "Mediterranean" (just say Middle Eastern, you won't get NSA'd) food is in this town? Order delivery, get it quick. Eat at the restaurant, revel in the attentive service. Have a hookah, or don't. Eat the branzino, eat the hummus, hell, eat everything. This is what my memories of the Middle East before the first gulf war taste like.
Just be prepared to return here over and over again. It's cheap, fresh, delicious, spicy, savory, just so damn good. Cucumber salad, the cold noodles, oh hell! Everything is great!!!

Every weekend, we call and hear one of the guys say, "Dusal's--pick up or deliver? What you like?"  While this may not be The Best Pizza in the World, it surely is the best pizza in Kendall Park.  Where are you going to go: Sansone's?  Four Musketeer's?  Please!  Dusal's makes consistently good pizza and fried calimari.

TL;DR:  Good eats. Still working out kinks naturally and expanding the menu, but keep an eye out for them in the coming weeks. Yes, yet another ramen review. I thought I was a snob, but other reviews clearly take it to another level lol. See my previous ramen reviews if you like. If I get around to it, I'll include some NYC places. First, the non-factors but still worth mentioning. - Actual prep time not streamlined as in other places - seemingly in part due to a one-man team. Not the slowest I've experienced, but something I expect to improve over time. - Service is decent and friendly. Whatever. - If you like real menus, this place isn't for you. It's handwritten and fast. Until they set their food choices in stone, I don't expect change soon here. Oh well. - Limited menu at the moment. Just 2 ramens at the moment. Let's hope they are decent. - Decor is acceptable and it's not filthy. But really, who cares? I'm here for the food. - Space/size is smallish, but just right. - They need a noticeable sign and some marketing materials on the store windows. They are very easy to miss if you aren't looking for them. ******  On to the food Broth - I'll be the first to admit shoyu isn't my go-to - I'm accustomed to tonkotsu. Everyone is entitled to their preference. I'm no chef nor do I have any real credentials, but I've had terrible broth before. This was not one of them. When it comes to ramen, not being bad is half the battle. Overall, I liked the flavor of it. Not too salty, maybe slightly on the oily side. Noticeable chicken flavor and hint of ginger. Not as heavy as some heartstoppers I've had, but not as light as the simpler shio broths. Nor is it a flavor bomb with overwhelming garlic and seasoning. In other words, a decent compromise. I finished drinking my broth by the way. But my inexperience/non-preference of shoyu leads to a biased score.  6.75/10. Noodles - The noodles are the curly/wave yellow kind. They are very remniscent of Chinese style noodles. They seem out of place in some ways. Whatever the case, the noodles are tasty and (for the first time ever) are the best part of the ramen experience. Not sure if they are pre-purchased or what he does to the noodles prep-wise, but they really do it for me. Just the right chewiness. They seem to have some good flavor somehow. YMMV   8/10. Cha-shu -  Pork here is good/decent. Thickness is about right, rectangular cuts. Tenderness is good. May need a bit more flavoring/seasoning for my own taste. Needs to be slightly warmer in temperature. Can't say I know much about the charring process - could stand to be more crispy I suppose? Appearance wise, I could care less. Might be too fatty in terms of quantity for the regular diner, but I was ok with it. Standard quantity is 2 slices - no surprises there.         6.5/10 Toppings - Menma, scallion, a sheet of nori, and half egg. Menma was decent. I've had better egg, but not a huge deal to me. 5/10. Price - $9 for a bowl. About on target if you liked your bowl. Maybe knocking it down slightly might change some tunes.   5/10 ****** Would I come back again? Yes. The chef definitely cares and wants to deliver quality product, when he works out logistic issues that are holding him back, I will certainly try it out again. Despite the scathing reviews, this place is far far far from the worst ever. Perhaps the criticisms of consistency in product may have merit, but that will change with time. Bottom line, if you did not have original Ramen Boy, you have not hit the bottom yet in terms of disappointment where I found nothing remarkable about the food. On a side note, chef said tonkotsu broth will be served in the near future, if that's consolation for anyone. Personally, I'd rather they focus on their one shoyu before moving on to other styles (the fixation on tonkotsu is overdone and redundant). Terakawa is still my go-to. They are my vanilla, but sometimes I want chocolate. Hiro is chocolate. Until someone new steps into the arena. @Christopher F and Seema (if you see this): Out of curiosity, which place had the best ramen you've ever had?

This place is so so. Soup is the most important thing for ramen but they pretty much did a bad job. It is like MSG soup and really oily and salty. Noodle itself is just okay. I give two stars bz they are just opened and I will give a shot later after a few months... by that time this place is still the same I don't think I will be back here again..

fluffy words, but very little substance. this place is amateur hour at it's best. first off, if you read their website everything seems very nice and the different menu options are all wonderfully DESCRIBED. then reality hits. the chefs look like college students hired off the street and the food pretty much proves this. the broth is poorly flavored - seems like too much water in the base and a bunch of seasonings dumped in - it's not a very fulfilling experience. the noodles are of cup noodle quality and worse than Nom Nom even. it's also inconsistently plated - sometimes the toppings are on top and sometimes they are smothered by the noodles. the menu is extremely limited and i can see why - the core items (RAMEN) aren't even done right. i shudder to think what "bi-weekly" menu changes will bring - if anything, more inconsistency. service is so-so. not bad, but not great either. noodles took a long time to come out which is a negative considering they aren't that great. decor is extremely simple. it's like a low-rent version of Ramen Boy almost, but too bare for any type of decent ambiance. "industrial" is putting it kindly - this is more like "bare bones". there are much better options in philly bottom line - Ramen Bar, Nom Nom, Terakawa. much too crowded to give this place a second look.

Don't know what the big fuss is about, my first time here, and many more to come. I ordered the vegetable ramen. It was delicious. The right amount of salt, oil, vegetables and other seasonings. The ramen it self was of traditional ramen noodles. Also the ramen was well plated or should I say well bowled? Lol. The hostess and waitress are a pair of very attractive Asian ladies. The were very kind and stayed in eyesight if anything was needed. However, they are latently hungry for a tip. Typical for any hostess or waitress in a new restaurant. 5 stars and well earned!

Best wings in town, especially for the price.  From 5-9 every day the wings are $.40 each, and you can get them in whatever denominations you like.  2 bbq, 3 hot, 9 cajun...sure. I recommend 6 cajun and 6 hot bbq accompanied by switchbacks and football during the winter.  You won't be disappointed. Granted in college the wings were $.10 each....damn you inflation. All of that being said....at the advanced age of anything over 21, I would suggest never staying after 10pm.  First because there are no more wings, and second, it turns into exactly what it should be...a dive college bar with primarily shitty music and girls looking to make mistakes.

This is probably one of the best food places in Burlington, love the wings (our favorite), love the fresh ideas, great soups, outstanding burgers....they have a greek chicken salad wrap that I can't get enough of.... We are never disappointed with the food here, also love the beer choices and the many TV's with whatever sport you'd like to watch. Give it a try !!!! you will be surprised......

I have been really excited to try these dumplings based on the positive reviews here. I finally had a chance today, and I was definitely blown away. First, I got to see Hong make the dumplings I ate to order. I stuck with the chicken/pork because that is my absolute favorite combination. Hong quickly crafted my dumplings (which was so fun to watch) and cooked them perfectly. I put the ginger soy sauce and hot chili oil on mine. The hot chili oil was incredible. It had a good balanced spice with the flavor of the chili shining through. Now the dumplings definitely fell about when I attempted to use a fork. I switched to using my hands, though, and had no issues chomping these down. The flavor of the pork and chicken was accented by some sweet onion, the dumpling was not doughy or undercooked as I've experienced with other restaurant dumplings, and the sauce just brought the entire thing together. I can see these might become an addiction. These are the absolute best dumplings one can buy in Burlington (and really most places for that matter).

Hong's dumplings are amazing!  She has 5 flavors, all of which are absolutely delicious. It's amazing to watch her make them right there on the spot, and the sauces that she has are incredible!   If you're lucky, you'll only have to wait in line a few minutes.

This is a very unique place in Burlington VT. Coming from Seattle, I thought Burlington is not that culturally diverse. I'm definitely surprise to find a food stand serving Chinese dumplings. The dumplings are definitely much better when they are made fresh. I am just amazed how much dumplings she has to make everyday! The fact that you can eat on the street is amazing. She provided various kinds of sauce for you to accent the dumpling flavors. The fact that they are made to order, and Hong is the only person handling everything on the food-stand; I need to give this place a solid 4 stars.

Every yummy Israeli dish you can think of is on the menu: hummus with zatar, bourekas, grilled eggplant and shakshuka ... And everything is *delicious*. What's more, Gila makes you feel right at home like you're sitting in her kitchen. Can't wait to come back :D

FAIL. We placed a largish order that took almost twice as long to be delivered as estimated.  Oh, and about half the items were missing or were the wrong thing. I wanted to like this place, I really did.  And I tend not to judge harshly when a delivery order doesn't arrive as hot or crispy as it should, because maybe it's better when you eat @ the restaurant.   But when the food is super bland - well, can't blame that on delivery.  I ordered a chicken schwarma that came in a falling-apart pita.  The chicken completely lacked flavor (if a street vendor can do it well, shouldn't a restaurant be able to do so, especially if they're charging 2x as much?).  I also ordered a side of grilled eggplant - for $4.50 i got two emaciated slices that look like an extra to put in a sandwich, not a side order.  The chicken schnitzel looks like a sad version of chicken tenders. Gathering from the disappointed sighs emanating from my coworkers, I'd say they're not too pleased with their orders either - well, those that actually got their food.

Don't understand the hype. The "chicken shawarma" is about as unauthentic as it gets. Portions are small. 3 balls of falafel, hummus, and one boureka for 12 dollars you've got to be kidding me. The only thing redeeming is the chef is incredibly friendly. The guy working there however is inattentive and arrogant.

Went to Broccolino with some friends visiting from out of town. We wanted good Italian and we weren't disappointed. The food was great and the service was even better. My friends were happy and we all left stuffed!Good times had by all. Will definitely be going back.

So I came for a pizza and ended up getting a haircut on the side walk...then there was a fb flash mob and I'd say at least 1000 people were there for the opening night. Point is the pizza was good and it had better be at 3.50 a slice;-)

Went to pizza brain with my girlfriend and some friends on opening night. The line was insane but the entertainment was fun. The museum concept is really unique and I'm looking forward to looking around when there's actually room to move. As for the pizza, I had the Jane and it was pretty good. At $3.50 a slice, though, it's pricey for what it is. I think the menu said a full pie is in the $16-18 range which will, unfortunately, lump Pizza Brain into my fancy pants pizza category. Hard to pay that much for a pie when I can get one of the BEST pizza's ever from Franco's for $15, including a tip for the delivery guy. That being said, I'm happy Pizza Brain is in the neighborhood and I will certainly be back to try it again, especially with Little Baby's next door!

I was expecting a stellar experience since I first heard about Pizza Brain, and expectations were surpassed. I've known Brian since before Tim Berners-Lee created the first web page. We were classmates, so the spirit and style of Pizza Brain was not new to me. Nostalgia is a huge part of Pizza Brain. We often view the past as being better than current times. 'They don't make 'em like they used to.' 'The good ol' days.' . . . Pizza Brain takes everything good that we remember about pizza and keeps it alive. The Noid, "Pizza! Pizza!" The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. Pizza Day at school. Pizza Brain has such a large collection of pizza culture that there's bound to be something that touches a personal memory for everyone who goes there. In addition to being a phenomenal celebration of the world's favorite eat-it-with-your-hands food, Pizza Brain serves up slices as well. I had never met dough-slinger Joe Hunter before, so I can honestly give an unbiased review of the pizza despite knowing Brian for multiple decades. I visited with my father and we decided to order a whole pie. We got pepperoni, mushrooms, and carmelized onions on our pie. It's a thin pie whose large slices demand to be folded. The cheese was melty and gooey. The sauce tasted like actual tomatoes instead of thick Spaghetti-Os soup. The pepperoni, mushrooms, and onions just melted in my mouth, and the crust was crispy, chewy, and springy. We didn't have any of the slices that were on-hand, so I can't comment on how they are in single re-heated form. The pie we had was $22.00 so if you can swing it, I highly recommend getting a whole pie so you can experience it at its freshest. It's absolutely worth it. It was even worth the 5 hour drive from Central New York. Don't go alone, bring friends! Pizza is family.

Very innovative and modern. This pizza museum delivers- literally. The walls are covered in age old pizza paraphernalia collected by the owner and the music playing is too cool for school, picked via ipads stuck to the wall. It's really just a fun place to hang out. The pizza was great, but hot enough to burn the roof of my mouth in over eagerness. We tried a pie of the Jane with pepperoni and a slice of the white to try. Both were great. Seating is an issue, but I think one they will take care of very shortly, as they just opened. When they announced my order was ready with a megaphone and a silly voice, I couldn't help but giggle. and the bottled cocacola just TASTES BETTER.

Wow is all I have to say. This place blew my mind with its great care and attention to detail. It is the definition of classy without pretension. My date and I wanted to try as much on the menu as possible, and we did! The staff was friendly, attentive, and not overbearing. We forgot our wine, and they very quietly poured us a couple glasses from their own stock. The bread and homemade butter to start wet my bill. Then came the mussels... oh my the mussels! I honestly have never had them prepared better. They melted in my mouth, just enough sauce, and the flavor was incredible. We had plate after plate of fantastic dishes. The highlight for me was the lamb. It was prepared just rare enough. The last time I tasted lamb so fresh, was when I ate a freshly slaughtered one. No lie... For me, a good peice of lamb is better than any cow steak. We finished with dessert that was just enough to fill my giant belly. The right amount of sweetness combined with bitter rich dark chocolate. This meal was filled with multiple foodgasms.

I cannot possibly say enough good things about the Pickled Heron to fully do it justice. We have had dinner here twice and, each time, the meal was the highlight of our week. The restaurant has been very busy each time we were there, but I imagine it would be slightly easier to get in for a later dinner (after 9pm or so). On our last visit, we were lucky enough to try the head cheese as part of that night's charcuterie plate (along with fois gras & duck confit) which was crispy and delicious. We also ordered a few small plates. I had previously tried the onion soup gratinee and would gladly have ordered it again, but another member of my party beat me to it. Luckily, I got to try the moule frites instead, which were some of the best I've ever eaten. For my entree, I ordered the scallops which cut like butter, yet had an amazing sear. The rest of my party had the Lamb Sirloin and the Black Bass (that nights special), both of which were fantastic. After sharing some deserts (yum!) and finishing off our wine (love the BYOB) we left, discussing how good our meals were and how soon we can make it back to the Pickled Heron.

I came here a couple months ago with my boyfriend and had a pretty good experience. It was a particularly beautiful day and we wanted to sit outside - this place came to mind. We put our name in for the patio outside and were told it would be about 40 minutes. No problem, we went to the bar and ordered a couple drinks (gin and tonics, which came in HUGE water glasses for $8 ... not bad, that was probably 2 drinks anywhere else). In about 5 minutes our table was ready. We hadn't even finished paying for our drinks yet. We sat at a high top table (people try to steal them, so keep an eye out) which had a really nice view of the airport next door. It actually was sunset at the time and it was beautiful, so I can see where they get their name from. We ordered guacamole as an appetizer, then the Sunset burger, and ahi tuna sandwich. Everything was great - burger was thick and cooked perfectly medium rare, as was the ahi. I had a side salad with mine which was pretty underdressed, so you might want to ask for the dressing on the side. Service was a little inattentive, but they were also very busy. We waited quite a while to get refills on our drinks. Between the time discrepancy at the host desk and the inattentive-yet-friendly service, I had to dock a star. However, the food was impressive pub grub and we loved the generous drink portions. Safe to say we'll be back.
In a hurry, this place was close by the gate.  It took a little longer than I was expecting to make the sandwich, but it was REALLY good- A pleasant surprise in the world of airport food

I was kind of surprised to see this small outpost of the same name that I have eaten at while visiting the Disney Marketplace in Orlando. It was opposite my gate at the airport so I decided to pick up a sandwich for the flight. As this is really a "grab and go" spot there are only about 6-8 sandwich options, some pre-made wraps and salads in the fridge, and a few tables. Still, the sandwiches are made fresh and hot, and are as tasty as ever. A great choice to eat rather than fast food type junk. I had the Earl Of Clubs sandwich. Roasted turkey, smoked bacon, lettuce, tomato, sauce, on a soft sandwhich roll. Brought it on the plane which was a good idea as I was stuck waiting on the tarmac for 90 minutes due to bad weather. After an hour I unwrapped it and it was still nice and warm. Delicious! People around me were eyeing it with jealous looks in their eyes. Suckas! Go get your own sandwich!
The sandwich was a good quality. However the waitress was rude and disrespectful. Plus I had to wait 20 minutes for a take out.

What a lovely date night! Had the duck, just phenomenal! Melts in your mouth. The service was very friendly, they truly want you to have an enjoyable experience. Be sure to make reservations - the restaurant is tiny but cozy!
Food was so good!  The Amish Fried Chicken with jalapeno mash was amazing. Excellent tasting menu- Tough area to park in, but worth the trip.

Not sure what other reviewers are talking about, this place is legit. I can see that they are working out kinks (open for less than a week!) but if you like BBQ, go here.  This place is exactly what the area needs. Great, real barbecue available quickly and at a fair price. Went for lunch Weds and then for dinner tonight with my daughters. Yesterday I had a pulled pork sandwich with a corn bread muffin and Mac and cheese. Tonight we got a rib platter as well as a pulled pork platter. Ribs fall apart and have great smoke flavor. Pulled pork is solid. Mac and cheese is really rich and cheesy...a little can go a long way. THe cornbread Is wonderful.fresh and not as thick and sweet as you get at some places. My daughters had some mashed potatoes and said they were good. I also tried a little bit of brisket which was excellent. Finally, we did have some cinnamon apples which were a nice sweet ending to the meal. From the design standpoint, I can see that it can get crowded. They may need to lease the adjacent spot to provide more seating. As time goes by they'll figure out rush times, get staff trained up, etc. The inside is clean and has a nice feel. The staff are friendly and engaged. All in all, this place rocks. Is it Gates in KC or the Salt Lick in Austin? No. But, for legitimate BBQ in central New Jersey, it is ideal.

I stopped by for lunch today at this new place.   I ordered the pulled pork platter with macaroni and cheese and collard greens.   The food was good (especially collard greens) but the portion was a little small for the price.  Service was quick and pleasant.  I will definitely go back to try some different Items.

After reading an article in the newspaper about Funnibonz we decided to try in out. I was not impressed. The meat was cold, the brisket was not tender, they were out of ribs on a Friday night(which I thought was shocking for a BBQ restaurant)& the service was slow which is somewhat understandable since it has not yet been open a month yet. The BBQ sauce is good, but there was not even an aroma of smoking meat or BBQ which was very disappointing. It was just OK but not worth the wait, not sure if I would return.
Very slow service..staff didn't quite seem to know what to do yet.  Chicken was moist, ribs were dry, cinnamon and apples TOO sweet.  May try one more time...

This little gem everyone must try!!!!  What an amazing place to eat at.  The service was excellent as well.  If you eat meat I would absolutely get the merguez lamb sausage dish.  The flavors are phenomenal.  I wish I would have learned about this place sooner.  This place is BYOB.

STICKER SHOCK!!!!!! Three of us came to try the new place down the street for lunch last week.  We had: two Duck Empanadas and two Korean Beef Barbecue Empanadas @ $7.00 each, two Chicken Sausage specials with onions and peppers, described as served on a nice big fresh baked roll, which turned out to be a plain hotdog bun at $12.00 each and a Chicken Panini on soggy multi grain with a tasteless pesto sauce $13.00, three seven ounce drinks in kitchy bottles @ $ 3.00 each for a total of $74.00.  We left shocked, disapointed and hungry!  I told the owner I thought it terrribly expensive for a very average lunch.  I rate this establishment R.P.V.T. (really poor value - tasteless)   By: AJBP (a Jew, Black and Puerto Rican:)
Very nice and interesting food. Great breakfast with music on Saturday.

This is a very cute breakfast restaurant.  Love the decor.  Love the musicians playing outside.  Food is good.  Some items are overpriced (because the portion received is so small; not the price overall) but most items are absolutely worth it. Definitely recommend the avocado, banana sandwich. Not a fan of the Maine lobster sandwich.

Everything about this cafe is outstanding and I really can not stress enough how good I feel when I step foot through that door. You are always greeted with a smile and a friendly hello not to mention the amazing smell of freshly prepared food.  The attention to detail is breathtaking.....it almost feels like you've taken a step back in time when life was much more simple yet elegant. The cafe has the feel of a family heirloom located on the streets of France. The food is prepared with such love and it's a  beautiful thing to know that all of the items on the menu are family recipes and QUALITY ingredients.  If your looking for mediocre, sub-par food for the same price as lets say Panera Bread then you have this place ALL wrong.  This is a classy establishment built and run with with the utmost care.  Overall I would have to say that Le Salbuen is in a league of its own.
The only good here is if your order their chicken in hot oil. But better to eat it at home cause the place looks so old.
This place is wonderful, the owner and his wife courteous and friendly, the food is delicious, we have been customers for 5 years.  The noodles in hot oil are my favorite. Never a bad experience!!

Food taste good but salty. Reason why I would never come here is that nasty owner. I ordered chiken wing two order and mins. Later I canceled one order. The owner yelled at me and giving dirty look until I picked up my order front of the other customers. Please make sure when you receive the receipt that all the items are same amount as shown on the menu. I've got one bad experience. They are very expensive compare to others Chinese restaurant around the areas.

Came here on a Thursday night with my girl for a night out, and so pleasantly surprised! Sushi was so fresh and delicious. The service was amazing, our waitress Ronnie was so sweet and helpful. Loved the atmosphere! Highly recommended!

Staff was extremely personable and pleasant! Environment was inviting, warm and clean. Our server Danielle was beyond accommodating! Drinks and food was prepared quickly and the food was fresh and exceeded expectations.
Great Food and Great Service. Loved the music and the ambiance. I would definitely come back again.
Great service... great food and awesome atmosphere...

Dinner at the Sushi Lounge was delicious!! Sushi was fresh as always!! We love this place. Our server was Monica and she was especially attentive and very friendly. This is not our first time here, we just keep coming back!!

Jason was awesome.  If I opened a restaurant I would have him work there.  Knew all specials, drinks came on time, and he was very friendly.  Angela was also awesome she cleaned the drink I spilled.  I would definitely come back.

Great beer selection and fun burgers and sandwiches. We also like the artichoke dip appetizer. The onion rings are a great side. I would rate 5 stars but the actual meat in the burgers isn't quite on par with Plan B right down the road. All in all though we continue to come back.

Lauren is an exceptionally knowledgeable bartender. She will suggest a few beers on tap which are compatible with the style of beer you like to drink, even if it is not craft beer. If craft beer is not your thing, try a prohibition cocktail. The Aviation is my favorite.

Went there for lunch had the classic burger - it was great. The bar was nicely decorated and everything was very clean.  Are server Lucy was right on the ball supplying extra drinks when needed, She was very pleasant. I would go to prime 16 again for sure.

Great burgers and beer. Staff behind bar is outstanding Mr Brian can make you anything you want or he will come with his own. Kayla and Kari will always take time to make sure you get the beer and special you like. Dont worry dinning room you can always ask Erin or Angela for help!!!
I like the prime 16 great food a lot of beers on tap and great bartenders they are very nice angela and Kayla and always suggest to try different beers wen New ones come on tap

I would give this 5 stars for friendly service alone! The girl at the counter is the nicest person you will ever meet!! So friendly!! I visited a year ago and thought she was having a good day that morning. When I visited recently, she had that same cheery attitude so it must be for real! I had the vegan cheesesteak, which was more like a vegan roast beef club. It wasn't bad, it just wasn't quite what I was expecting. They were very generous with the portion fixings though. They get their vegan baked goods from Vegan Treats every Thursday any time from 12-3pm. They probably get the largest order besides from Gondivas! Love Vegan treats! So I'm happy they get them! It's not in the greatest if neighborhoods and its not very close to center Philly....but I'd rather do than without it

Stopped here for a sweet treat and some coffee. It's a cute corner spot. It was hot as hell in there while ordering. But after we got our goods, we went to the back room and it was nice and cool. The iced chai latte was so good. The chocolate covered cannoli was better than some cannolis I've had in the past. So happy I got that. The peanut butter brownie was also good. Bf got the macchiato and said it was good too. Glad we stopped here.

I found out about this place by browsing the web for the best vegan spots in Philly. This cafe came up again and again and, after checking it out, I can see why. Grindcore is entirely vegan with lower prices than most vegan spots I've been to. I started out with their bottomless coffee. It was brewed to perfection and their creamer options expanded beyond mere soy to rice milk almond milk and coconut milk. Service was helpful and friendly. There's a great seating area in the back with AC, a "radical" library and free wifi. I did some work there and had two more cups of coffee. I finished my visit with a chocolate pb brownie. It was a little oily for my taste but absolutely delicious, especially considering it was entirely vegan. I will be returning to try the cinnamon bun which is apparently very popular! If you like coffee or are a vegan/ vegetarian be sure to check out this spot

In a neighborhood without a lot of options, Grindcorehouse isn't just a rare oasis but manages to serve up fantastic coffee, a great spot to work and incredible staff.  Kick ass salads, coffee to die for and the baristas are incredibly accommodating.  Not to mention the most metal logo I've seen on a coffee joint!  Definitely matches the music in the back room, great for concentrating and getting work done. This would absolutely be a five star review except for one thing - no working AC in the 90 degree heat makes the front of the shop totally unbearable!  Not sure how the staff handles it, honestly.

Went here last night. Great renovation of what used to be a pretty dingy bar. This portion of south street is really improving. The food menu was very interesting, big focus on the apps & sandwiches. I like that it's not trying to be a gastro-pub and restaurant at the same time. We ordered the Nachos, they were fresh cooked and nicely presented. On the downside, the beer list has some strange choices. I mean Corona light? I don't care if it's on draft, I didn't go to a high end bar that boasts about it's beer menu to drink corona available in any dive bar, why not substitute a good light craft beer? I ordered an oyster stout, and it came with a 1"-2" head. It was a good beer, but just badly poured.  It wasn't a huge glass to start, so not only did I feel robbed, it was difficult to drink and enjoy. Hopefully it was a learning curve issue, as it's been open only 2 days, but in a place that focuses on beer, they need to improve pouring it. This place has huge potential, but it's got some way to go in my opinion. Also, apparently not open for lunch, not sure why seen as the food is perfect for a lunch menu.

it's generally frowned upon to review a place that's been in business for less than a week, but the cambridge has done a great job managing its very busy first few days -- and they deserve some credit. sunday dinnertime was packed, but staff was going with the flow. the owner made a point of stopping by our table to chat, and we appreciated the friendly hello when we knew he had a million other things to worry about. beer list is large and varied and looks like it changes often. we only tried a few items off the menu: burrata baguette: liked it, but beware if you're lukewarm about anchovies. they dominate the flavor in this, big time. grilled peach & pecan salad: loved it. probably not large enough for an entree if you're hungry, but a very solid salad. pair it with an app. uncle reuben: great. it's served with salad instead of fries, so you don't feel too gross after inhaling it. additional two cents: i've seen a good bit of online commentary bemoaning the abundance of gastropubs in philly and criticizing the cambridge's opening. i don't get it. business owners are trying to make a living, and as the cambridge has illustrated in its opening days, philadelphians flock to gastropubs (and this particular neighborhood is not one of the pub-saturated ones in the first place). you can't criticize a couple for pursuing a business model that clearly works. this place is going to succeed. i had nothing against tritone, but there's a reason it went under -- and we still have bob & barbara's, which isn't going anywhere. i hope everyone can start making peace with change, because so far, the only thing worth complaining about with the cambridge is the noise level (it is very loud)!

Love the draft list, though I wish they had everything on their list all the time. They have the switch system where if one particular beer runs out, there's a replacement draft for that beer. Even so, there's a great selection. There's plenty of seating, but it fills up quickly. We stood around for a bit before we got a place to sit. The bartenders are quick and would check on you periodically, despite being very busy. Overall, great atmosphere, great beer.
Great service- slow kitchen. Servers were polite and very welcoming- which was needed to make up for the huge wait time to get our food. When it finally came is was ok- but not worth the wait.

Swung by the new Cambridge last night and it was bumpin'! So much so that the wait for a table was almost a half hour. Normally, this wouldn't be a problem and we'd just grab a drink and wait, but I was already well into hangry territory so we opted to grab a bite elsewhere. Afterwards, we returned and were seated at a table right away. We had several drinks and our server was great. The food at the surrounding tables looked awesome, and I was a little regretful that we hadn't just waited before. But I'm sure we'll be back in no time. My only gripe, and I see that it is a common theme in the reviews so far, is the noise. We broke out a decibel measuring app for fun and the reading was very high. But our ears already knew that. I did enjoy the music selection, but I'm hanging on to hope that some sound muffling will take effect soon. Aside from that, the bar/restaurant is gorgeous and I'm really looking forward to hanging out there!

My hubby is Peruvian and is quite critical when it comes to his lomo saltado.  Surprisingly, he loved it. There were no fatty pieces of meat in it and the lomo was tender and flavorful. I ordered the pollo saltado and it was DELICIOUS!!! As our appetizer, we ordered papa huancaina...sauce was good, but the potato was way undercooked (one star off)   The food is a little pricier than most other peruvian restaurants we've frequented, and the portions aren't as big, but the food was good. The staff was very polite and helpful. Angela took my order and she was very helpful and sweet. Will definitely come back for more.

You know that feeling you get when you see something so cute you just want to squeeze it to death or punch it? (no?) Anyway, that's how I felt after every single bite of food at Xixa. I seriously wanted to punch myself in the mouth because it was so good I didn't know what to do with myself. I went with 3 other friends, and instead of doing the tasting menu, we decided to pick 12(?) or so dishes ourselves and share. EVERY SINGLE dish was delicious. There was nothing I didn't like. Alcohol consists of a slightly overwhelming and vast wine list  (server will help you decide),  tequilas & mezcals. Highlights as far as food goes included: Drunken Shrimp (my absolute favorite) Foie gras al pastor Baby Octopus Grilled carrots elote (!!!!!) Guacamole of artichokes Spicy rock shrimp gorditas (this dish had scallions, something I hate. Yet I happily put a crapload in my mouth and didn't give a hoot) Everyone at the table raved about the Fundido (Truffles, cheese, and chorizo). The cheeze/chorizo was absolutely amazing - but I am one of the only people who isn't too fond of truffles. Despite this, I took a huge heaping forkload of the cheese/chorizo and thought I'd cry it was so good. We didn't have time to try a dessert as a reservation was coming in as we were finishing, but we were so stuffed that it was probably a good thing. I'll be back. And I'm taking everyone I know here and if they don't like it, I will question why they are in my life.

In case you got bored of Traif's menu for some reason or if there is a line, then go to Xixa. It's as if Traif was a smoking hot girl and Xixa was her south-of-border identical twin. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu and it has the same tasting menu option as in Traif, $40 gets you 11 courses! (9 savory and 2 sweet). The ambiance is pretty awesome too, a great date spot.

After my second unsuccessful attempt at eating at Traif, I was directed four doors down to Xixa (Traif's new Mexican inspired sister).  The food was incredible and the company was great.  All in all, a great night out. Dishes here are served tapas style.  We each decided to choose a dish to share and a protein for ourselves.  Along with our Carta Blanca, we enjoyed the grilled carrots elote, the fundido with chorizo and truffle oil chips, and the sauteed edamame with arbol chile, lime and garlic.  All of them were fantastic, but I'd choose the carrots if I had to choose a favorite.  From what I've read, this dish seems to be a customer favorite.  In order the pork belly and cheek with a cranberry and corn relish.  One bite in and I finally understood the glory of crispy pork fat.  I would enthusiastically order any of these dishes again. The service was good and speedy, but a little pushy.  If you don't want drinks, good luck.  They give you the drink menu long before they even let you see main menu.  Since we wanted drinks this wasn't a problem for us.  The interior is sleek and modern with hanging rope and lights being the main focal point.  The space is intimately lit and small, but not too tight that I felt uncomfortable.  The bathroom situation is very confusing, but I'll let that slide.

Overall Rating: 4-4.5 Stars. "Do you know what Xixa (pronounced: shkisa) means?" our friendly hostess inquired of us. As two lapsed Jews, wise in the ways of elementary Yiddish, we answered with an emphatic, "Yes." Well, the dear hostess was heartbroken for it appeared as though she had a whole narrative to recount regarding the irony of the name. Truth be told, that's precisely why this destination was chosen. That, combined with the fact that its sister restaurant - Traif -  has treated me well in the past. We had booked a table for 9 p.m. and - having just returned from a softcore pornography exhibit at Die Neue Galerie (oh those German expressionists...) - we needed a palate cleanser sooner rather than later. Enter Xixa. The ambiance is what one would expect from a restaurant of its ilk and - like Traif - candles and dim lighting set the tenor for this simple yet tastefully assembled backdrop for one's eating endeavors. We were here to get down to some serious eating and, though the task was monumental, we are nothing if not brave. After several minutes of deep breathing and transcendental meditation, we were up to the challenge. At least that's what we thought. Apparently Xixa is supposed to embody deconstructed Mexican cuisine, which is my favorite type of Mexican cuisine, as it happens, and so we were in business. This is a tapas-style restaurant and - like Traif - the eater is confronted with several categories of food from which to choose, each dish sounding better than the last. Our charming waiter, John, advised us that 5-6 dishes was the norm for two people and who were we to question his insider knowledge? (Pro tip: 6 dishes = ravenous). We did as we were told and got down to intensive discussions where, at one point, I had cause to recommend resorting to a notepad to ensure we were making the optimal eating decisions. Well, my eating companion was very emphatic in her choices and I had very little say in the matter. -The first thing to pop onto our table was the guacamole of artichokes. While we both agreed that is was really tasty, I don't know whether this was a particularly noteworthy dish. I mean, there are few of us who haven't sought comfort in the warm embrace of a bowl of guacamole after a taxing day, but - compared to the other dishes on the menu - you can safely skip this item. -Next out, there was a dish that entailed foie gras and pork of some variety.The executive summary is that it was a rich and hearty soupy concoction which we took to spooning in earnest. It is not uncommon for me to threaten my eating companions by knocking my knife and fork over while greedily spooning delicious broths into my person and, you'll be pleased to know, that my skills in the art of cutlery distraction and intimidation caused my eating comrade to back away from this dish so I could dabble in earnest. -The next few dishes were a blur of ecstasy and, while there was much moaning and groaning going on at the table (mostly the anguish voiced by my eating companion after having spent three hours in my presence), my "When Harry Met Sally" moments made guest appearances in the cacophony. We had ribs of some variety, which were delightful and duck lettuce wraps which were delicious. For those of you familiar with Traif, you will know that they generally time the arrival of the dishes so that one is not inundated with ungodly quantities of food at a time. We were not so lucky this time, though the professional staff came over to apologize and gave us another glass of wine on the house. I'm no historian, but I believe that worse things have happened than being confronted with five delicious items on one's table concurrently. -The grilled carrots "elote," honey butter, lime crema, coriander, feta were outstanding and, given the opportunity, I would order six plates of that - creamy, sweet, delicious. Order them. Regrettably, the burrata which was stuffed in a sweet pepper was a bit disappointing: while sweet and soft, the burrata got lost in the sweet pepper and resulted in a dish that was rather unexceptional though, by this point, food orgasms had been reached several times already and so there were no hard feelings. It was one of those rare occasions in which there was no room for dessert. At 1 a.m., we had spent 4 hours eating and it is a credit to Xixa that we never felt rushed. Regrettably, there was no room for dessert and, as I lamented not opting for my jeans with an elasticized waistline, we squeezed through the doors. Conclusion: 4/6 of the dishes were outstanding. While Traif limits itself to fewer dishes which are all faultlessly executed, Xixa has gone with greater breadth and, in doing so, misses the mark of perfection in some spots. That said, it is a laid-back setting in which meandering conversations may be enjoyed while excellent cuisine and drink may be consumed. With each dish setting you back approximately $10, it is a perfectly reasonable spot for a wholly exceptional meal.

We went for New Year's Eve for the first time & what a great way to celebrate! If you've ever been to the sister restaurant, Traif, you know you won't be disappointed. The food was delicious & the decor was intimate & unique. The space is small, but cute & cozy. The items on the menu are for sharing, so selecting one from each section of the menu will suffice. The lettuce wraps & the corn tamale were great! We ordered the "steak tacos", which I didn't realize would involve an actual bone to scoop out the marrow. It was greasy & too much on the stomach. Cool concept, but we could've did without it. The salty churros were a great way to end our meal. There is a lot to choose from on the menu. I would go back & would definitely recommend this place to anyone.

There's a HUGE Difference in having a good time and having an AWESOME TIME!.  This was one of the AWESOME TIMES in Queens. I would recommend to come to this place in a big GROUP!. Why?, Here are the reasons: To Try live Octopus (I had the guts to eat it live and it was a very interesting point of view. Pretend like chewing rubber while they were sucking / sticking around inside your mouth) that's how It felt. 1) One order of Sannakji  = Live Octopus with a HUGE Pot of live seafood being cooked in front of us.  If you want to see how big was the size of an octopus, please view the video and see it yourself!. youtube.com/watch?v=41fW… (PS.... There's a staff that will come up to your table and will cut up the seafood into smaller pieces. But basically there was this ENTIRE Octopus, following by the Lobster that was cut in half, it was moving / climbing from the shells and the pot, and the Abalone!!) 2) Watermelon Soju = the size of a empty watermelon filled up with juice and soju.  Refreshing!.  They also have Cucumber Soju, and other regular drinks. 3) Seafood Pa Jeon (pancakes)  = Pretty good, Seafood is FRESH! 4) BBQ Meat! = All kinds, all juicy and tender. 5) Fried Rice = Not just PLAIN fried rice.  Whatever sauce you had leftover from the Seafood Pot (AKA Sannakji) Is mixed with the fried rice. (The staff even Convinced us to add Cheese on top of the Rice).  This was one of the best part of the dinner, it was like a PAELLA!. And by having a large group of people, The manager offered us a complimentary Oysters.  I didn't have it because I was too full.  At the end it came out about $ 35.00 per person (it was 13 of us in the table, view the bill under this link if you don't believe it) yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8… SHOW + DINNER = AWESOME TIME! - Staffs are very friendly and they are very professional enough to take care 30 hungry yelpers - Location is really close to the 7 train station (YOU CITY PEOPLE HAVE TO COME HERE!) --------------------------------------------------­------------------------------------------ PS....This was one of the UYE Yelp events (Thanks Radford and Amy for introducing a great place!) PSS....Watching people eating live Octopus was very entertaining (Radford, Catherine and Tara, I will never look to you the same as I did when we met first time. You guys were SIK!.... In a good way!).

Sik Gaek never fails to entertain me or fill me up with good food!  It's the one place that brings a whole new meaning to playing with your food.  I also have to compliment on the impeccable service. Special thanks to Jenn L, Wing L, and Amy S for introducing me to this place.  It's so good that I've been back twice already. Highlights for this place include: 1) Fresh Live Octopus - the restaurant takes a live octopus and cuts it up into smaller pieces before serving it with 2 different dipping sauces. yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8… My first time at Sik Gaek - I was the LAST person of the group to try this.  Honestly, it's not that scary.  I'm just glad it was NOT live BABY octopus being served. 2) Seafood Hot Pot - this is good for groups to share.   My first visit - we ordered the $75 seafood hot pot - yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8… My second and third visit - we ordered the $100 seafood hot pot - yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8… While both hot pots are similar, the $100 one has more seafood (more conch and a live octopus). After finishing off the hotpot, we opted for the fried rice which contains tobiko flying fish roe.  The fried rice uses the same pot from the seafood hot pot and some of the leftover broth. yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8… For two of the three visits, we ordered Raw Oysters (fresh from Korea). yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8… Both bf and I normally eat our raw oysters with only a squeeze of lemon juice, so that we can taste the natural flavors of the raw oysters.  This particular kind wasn't sweet nor briny.  Both of us had to use the sauce that was provided with the raw oysters to enjoy it.  In our opinion, the flavors of the Korean Raw Oysters - meh... but they were still very fresh, nonetheless. DEFINITELY worth a trip with at least a group of 4 to share.  Bring your cameras so you can take memorable pictures of you & your friends trying live octopus! For those of you that have not been to a Korean place, once you're served food, the servers do not really come around anymore, so you can just drink and enjoy your food.  If you do need service, there is a button on the table that you push to get service. yelp.com/biz_photos/2Bg8…

Decor, service food all awesome.  Laid back stylish vibe, friendly, attentive staff and most importantly everything we had was really good.  The mussels are excellent, gazpacho tasty.  It's also right next door so will be back.  Prices are very reasonable for quality of food..

the husband and i decided to have a friday date night at the bounty. and we're so glad we chose this place. the ambiance - we loved the steady and relaxed vibe. the bar looked awesome and it wasn't too packed which was perfect. the service - friendly people. excellent service. the food - we got the oysters to start which were fresh and yummy. we both ordered the burger which was actually one of the best i've had in nyc. such a great surprise. so juicy and tasty. it went perfectly with the toasted brioche it was in. even the fries that went with the burger were excellent, crisp and well seasoned. we will definitely go back even just for that burger. oh and the dark and stormy was excellent too!

I know this place just opened, but the menu was pretty bland and pedestrian for the prices and the portions.   Yet another eatery done up in the quintessential Williamsburg salvag-chic style...  We ordered the mussels for an appetizer for eight dollars and got eight mussels lined up with no bread.  They were good enough, but can't compare to the 5 Leaves.   Muscles are notoriously inexpensive. So eight mussels for eight dollars better be high concept.    We had noodles with clams for dinner, one of four entrée options. Again, it was nothing to write home about and overpriced.    I won't say this place is bad. It's fun it's a good atmosphere, but there are so so so so so many better places to eat in a half-mile radius....

We had the burger. Great tasty charred meat, great buns, yummy fries. I also had the watermelon summer adult beverage that i forgot the name of hahaha. It was very strong but light and refreshing. now about the burger, I would compare it to the five leaves burger in terms of quality, flavor and satisfying moist meaty deliciousness. Thankfully it is much  less overwhelmingly salty (my bf always orders the burger at five leaves and I Honestly can't eat it without a gallon of water afterwards). I'm so excited we can finally both go get a local burger together without encountering a pretentious staff or too crowded interior. We didn't try anything else off the menu yet, but I'm excited to back back very soon. I will revise this to include a fifth star once they make adding bacon to the burger an option and once we've tried more than half of their menu :)

Considering the price they are charging, I would say that this is a place you would want to go to get a quick, cheap fix for anything you can think of. It is quite typical of a chinese buffet place with a decent selection of items. I am a seafood fan, so I would load up on raw oysters and clams when they have it available. The sushi is OK, but as you would expect, the fish is sliced thinly and necessarily of a high quality. Beyond that, I liked the coconut shrimp and black bean clams. I would avoid most of the carved meat section together with the fried stuff. At the end of the day, you do get what you pay for, but I do like the value you get for it.

The price for lunch and dinner are comparable to other Chinese buffet restaurants, but I find the food at some of the other restaurants better.  They didn't have snow crab legs on the buffet which I thought was usual Chinese buffet fare but not here.  The wait to get in on a Saturday night was horrific!  Granted I expected a wait, but not the chaotic experience I had.  The doorway was completely blocked, and many people didn't know to get a number from the hostess first so they just waited thinking it was a line until some other customer informed them of the process.  Bottom line, I've had better.

You've pissed off the wrong person. I walked in at precisely 4PM. I had a $1.00 off promotional coupon for the lunch buffet from an ad that had both lunch and dinner coupons. It was an hour before I started work, and I was wearing a uniform, so it was plainly apparent that I was a fellow member of the food service industry. Dude:  "No, we serving dinner now." Me: "At 4PM?" Dude: "Yes, dinner start at 3:30." Me: "Well, come on, could you at least do me a favor and give me a dollar off the dinner price? I didn't know that dinner started at 3:30." [this fact is also not posted on the ad that I took the coupon from] Dude: "No, you need the coupon that say dinner." Me: "So you're gonna make me go home to get the other coupon???" Dude: "You need dinner coupon." You gotta be ****ing ****ing me. You entice me to come to your restaurant with a coupon, and then, citing your patently ridiculous policies [who the hell eats dinner at 3:30 PM, Matlock?], deliberately snooker me out of using it? And over a single freakin' dollar?!?! And to do this to a food service worker who was willing to compromise no less? Disgusting behavior. Enjoy your short-lived business tenure in West Hartford.

Absolutely awful. Given the paucity of good steakhouses in N NJ, we have relied on Strip House often, despite marginal service and food. After tonight however, we will not return. Portions are invariably meager and exorbitant, and the quality mediocre. $15 for a wedge salad with 1/16 of a head of lettuce started the debacle (and I should add that we are NYC steakhouse connoisseurs who do not typically balk at the prices at places like Wolfgang's or Porterhouse due to the superb quality). Sides were also crazy small. Shrimp was still slightly frozen. A small $50 ribeye appeared which was tepid and overcooked. The manager (the smarmy bald guy if you are interested) finally attuned himself to the fact that we were unhappy, but rather than try to acknowledge the disparity between quality/quantity and price, he proceeded to challenge us and was over-the-top obnoxious and out of line. Incensed, I lost my appetite for the sizeable remainder of what was left, and asked for the check so we could leave. Never, ever, again....and they just lost a regular, good customer.

Love this place...and would absolutely recommend it for dinner and/or drinks...even for locals.Once inside you dont feel like you are attached to a hotel. Wait and bar staff all so super friendly. Food is amazing. My few pointers for the bar: wish they had an official "drink menu"; St. Germain Liqueur and Ginger Beer.  But the bartenders are so acommodating and always willing to mix you a "mystery" cocktail when they dont have the ingredient you ask for. Will go back often....

Place is fantastic.  Been going since it opened, and have never had a bad experience. Food is always fresh, and very generous portions. Staff is extremely friendly, and very attentive.   This is a byob, so grab your favorite bottle, and be sure to make a reservation on weekends.

Food is good. Service is average. Some items on the menu they didn't have. Sardines were good. dates with blue cheese are very nice. Steamed pulpo - so so. Grilled pulpo is good. Oysters are fresh and good. Sole and surf-n-turf are very good. Veal chop is OK (big ones). NY strip - don't order. Large shrimp are good. We had Portuguese red wine $31/bottle. Very nice. I also can complement on espresso. Flan is standard. One important comment to the owners. Since you have a bar it is important that restaurant guest will be guarded from the noise of the happy bar folks.

Seriously. You guys tell my friend to take off his hat. He was not even wearing a baseball cap or something like that.Mind you this a neighborhood Indian place with casual ambience and clientele. Also there was no sign of a dress code. C'mon guys you are in UES not in TriBeCa. We were about to leave but thought it was impolite, so stayed there for one round of drinks and did not eat. Average drinks with a hefty price tag ,in a pretentious place. Good to take a date but not to hang out with friends
It was the best Indian food i have ever had. The Puri was refreshing and spicy.

The food and service here is great! Decor and ambiance are excellent. A bit on the small side. I don't agree with the two $$ - it's a bit on the pricey side and there are no value specials (no lunch prices and happy hour deal is just okay). Definitely recommend the okra app and cocktails!

Read great reviews on this restaurant via Yelp and decided to give it a try. My fiancé and I came on a Friday night and saw a busy restaurant on the Upper East side which was a good sign to start. We took seats on the outside bench where we started chatting with the owner. He was extremely pleasant and delivered us our first drink while we waited. Once we got inside we were seated at the bar and began our Indian feast. We had the mutton appetizer, shrimp curry which was amazing and the chicken tikka masala. All dishes were extremely tasty and well spiced. My favorite dish was definitely the crispy okra, The atmosphere was really lively and we also enjoyed the hard boiled eggs! Will definitely come back here.

I was visiting Philadelphia and explored this tiny cozy spot on our way back home. We stopped by to try something for dessert after eating the cheese steaks. I must say that they serve the best crepes in the town!!! I have tried several crepes places in the past, as I love crepes but this is certainly the best.  I was impressed by the amazing choices they have in sweet and savory crepes especially the "Ice-cream crepes". I tried the Dark Belgian chocolate crepe with Fresh strawberries and "Honey Honey" Lassi (Honey, vanilla, Levender). Everything was so fresh and flavorful. Owner was very kind and sweet too. She told me that they use "All Natural" stuff. I will try Kashmiri Chai next time as I am too full today. The only con is that they don't have a parking of their own and it's just street parking which could be difficult to find at times.  I'm definitely coming back!!!  Can't wait for my next trip to Philly.

Love this place!  The cheery environement, plus conversation with the owner and chef Liza while she creates her crepes and shakes is a delight.  Had a Gulab (rose and cardamom)  Lassi on my first visit.  It was sensational.  Can't wait to go back to try more items from the menu!

I was in Philadelphia for a show over at World Cafe Live and was in the mood for a savory crepe. Authentic french crepes, with excellent prices. The food was amazing!  It looked beautiful & tasted even better. The atmosphere is relaxed, and the owner is very friendly. The food was prepared quickly. I cannot think of a single thing that wasn't done well! I highly recommend it!

Been there a few times now and each time the food and service has been great. The arepas are fantastic and the drink specials on weeknights (Happy Hour all night Mondays, 2 for 1 mojitos on Tuesdays, $15 sangria pitchers on Wednesdays) are a nice bonus. The manager came by to check in, which was a nice personal touch, and our waitress Alexis was especially attentive, friendly, and fun. Her recommendations were great, and we'll definitely be back again soon. The huge windows looking out onto the East River and the Manhattan skyline make the setting even better!

The view was amazing, the food was delicious and creative, and the staff was very friendly. We were assisted by Alexis who managed to make my first visit to Blend an enjoyable experience. I definitely will be coming again...
The view was the best thing about the restaurant! Definitely won't go back.

The manager Lance, was amazing! Making my daughter's birthday dinner a huge success!!! I can't thank him enough :) He was so so helpful, professional, understanding and kind. I will def come back just to get the service I received from him. The atmosphere and decor is totally superb and exquisite!!!Unreal customer service and delicious food utterly pleased!! Great place for a girls night out, or a date night with your love one :)

I have been here a couple of times and have always had wonderful dinning experiences. My friend's wedding dinner party was held here today. Half of our guest were late by an hour however, the staff were very accommodating. Our server was Alexis and she was very attentive throughout the night. She even inform us of the brunch special that will be starting next week. Being that I'm a Brunch person I'm sure looking forward to it.

The food was amazing, the service was excellent and the atmosphere was just unforgettable. No matter what you order on the menu you will be happy, the apps were amazing, tried a few different ones, but the Mac and cheese and tostadas were two of my favorites. Check it out, great spot.

Blend on the Water definitely has a desirable location. Food was good and prepared well. I didn't like the part that a 20% mandatory gratuity was put on my bill. Especially, since my waitress was not really good at her job. Table was left with dirty dishes for awhile after appetizers were completed. Waited about 15 minutes after meal to be asked if anyone wanted dessert. Then waited 15 minutes after that to receive a check. Lots of down time waiting. Then only for the waitress to get a 15% undeserved  tip. This restaurant does deserve 4 stars. Just can award that with the service given.

Came here for the first time last Friday, to celebrate my dads birthday. The place: LIC.....rite by the water, near the old Pepsi Cola sign. Surrounded by tons of new apartment buildings, that are like super fabulous status. Place itself is real gorgeous, all windows so you see the beautiful nyc skyline. Huge bar, nice size dinning room, and outdoor seating. Dim lighting, Spanish music, chill vibe. The experience.....:::: Roll up to $7 valet parking!! Okay..... well since I'm running late and have a stroller with me, this is pretty convenient, as parking doesn't seem easy around there. Ummmm real quick.....valet is usually free and then you tip! ----Menu has an LED lite in it, super cool! ----Bathrooms are one private bathroom for each, and a community sink outside, not feeling that, caused a line once the place got crowed! Greeted by the hostess and the manager, they directed me to my sis, who was not late and was waiting for me (and my dad, but that's another story). We had to wait a little bit to be seated, I asked the manager how much longer and he seated us rite away. Flip over the high chair and put the car seat in there, apparently they are designed for that...who knew? Manager put the stroller away for us while we ate. Waitress came rite over....let the good times roll........ THE FOOD: We started off with white and red sangria. Both were very yummy! For apps we had tostones nachos, which consist of shredded chicken, guacamole, pico de gallo, queso menonita, and cojita cheese, sooooooooooooo good, crispy tostones (fried plantain) with all this yumminess on top!! We also tried crispy arepas, you get 4 cup like looking things filled with braised short rib, avocado, lime crème, and cilantro, delish! I read in other reviews that you have to try the chorizo mac & cheese, so we did......manchego, cojita, pepper jack cheese, and  chorizo topped with panko crust, soooo creamy, cheesy, gooey, superb!! Very memorable mac! And the last app choice, serrano ham flatbread, cilantro pesto, queso menonita, carmelized onions, and crispy black label serrano ham.....great last choice! They have all kinds of typical Spanish food selections, pernil (roast portk), seafood paella (prawns, scallops, mussels, yellow rice and peppers), they also have a vegetarian choice for this dish, churrasco (skirt steak, yellow rice and beens, with cilantro emulsion), and my choice....pollo a la plancha which is chicken breat, white rice, beans, maduros (I subed for tostones) and lemon butter sauce. I get this dish everywhere, I think blend is my fave!! Lemon butter sauce is seriously amazing, chicken cooked just rite, juicey thick piece of chicken breast. Beans were also pretty slammin! Dessert was melt in your mouth goodness, we had 2 dessert platters. Flan was really good, there chocolate molten....I think was the best I ever had! The service: the manager Lance was so freaking awsum!! We had personalized birthday menu's. Our waitress Elizabeth was also pretty awsum, well she did have fabulous cat eyes so what else can you expect from a gal who knows how to handle a good liquid eyeliner!! Seriously tho, Elizabeth was attentive, polite and was def a big part in making my dads birthday a memorable one!! I want to say a special thank you to Lance, you took such great care of us, my dad and mom were so pleased, they are planning there next visit! Well, we all are!! Really appreciate a manager who cares about what the "people" are saying! SEE YOU SOON LANCE AND SYOY!!

Ate here last Saturday and everything was absolutely perfect. The food was incredible as was the service. My boyfriend and I were a bit late for our reservation, about 20 minutes but the hostess, I think she said her name was Syeda (sp?), was so understanding, so sweet! And that lobster mac and cheese was the best I've ever had. Was a bit of a trek from Harlem but, honestly I'd rather go here than the bougie places in Manhattan.

Great view and good food!  Fun place where you can enjoy the city skyline!  We loved the sangria and the surf and turf recommended by our server, Allesondra.  She was so pretty with a great smile and lots of energy.  We sat  outside and she was pretty busy but always kept that smile and gave us great service!  Definitly will be back!

This place is beautiful. The food was amazing. The manager Lance was so pleasant, welcoming, and helpful. The waitress Genesis did an amazing job. Thank you guys for amazing food and an amazing experience.

Thankfully we got there early.  This place gets crowded on a Saturday night. The service was excellent.  The staff, including the manager were attentive.  I even had a Yelp check in for a free glass of sangria and they decided to give us a free pitcher of sangria and glasses for everyone in our party.  The view is beautiful and we enjoyed our food.  Will be back, but only in the day or early evening to avoid the crowds and long wait times.

Excellent atmosphere and hospitality. To compliment that the food is also good. A must go for adults, but they are kind to the little ones also. Go and enjoy and tell the manager how you feel. No need to look for a manager because they'll periodically come to your take to check on you. Now that's caring about the customer.

I have been here several times with my wife. Every time we have had great food and service. The manager, Lance, always makes us feel welcomed. The mac and cheese is fantastic! We just ate there on 10/9 and again everything was great. Emily was our waitress and she was pleasant and attentive. Again, great service.

Came to NYC for my 21st birthday from Cali and my boyfriend found this restaurant to surprise me, he made a reservation and got seated pretty quickly. Our server was nice. Our food was pretty good. The ambience was very nice and the view was amazing. Really like the vibe there. The manager even came and asked us if the food was okay which was nice. They didn't have the birthday cake shot anymore so that sucked, and my boyfriend had told them to surprise me and sing me happy birthday but they forgot so my boyfriend had to tell them again. Nonetheless very good place and a definite recommend! I will definitely go if I ever return to NYC !

I went back to Blend on Saturday 10/11/14 to give it another try and I really enjoyed it this time, granted I wasn't there for a special occasion so I didn't have certain expectations but the service was great. We were seated right away and the staff was very attentive. As an appetizer we ordered the chorizo mac and cheese. I had the churrasco and my boyfriend had the pernil. It was all really good. I don't recommend their white sangria but I did enjoy their margarita which was only 5 dollars during happy hour. When the manager Lance showed up he brought me and my boyfriend their arepas to try and they were good as well. After this experience I would definitely come back to Blend on the Water. It's a really nice spot. Thank you Lance for everything!

I was a bit iffy about this place bc I heard the place wasn't all that but I beg to differ! It was a slow night and we were seated quickly with a nice city view. I came here for dinner but I also heard they had great drink specials. Steph told us to get sangritas if we wanted something strong and she was right. We had three and we felt nice. We had the arepas and the Majorca corn. The corn was ehhh kind of messy to eat for dinner but the arepas were banging. It had short rib Guac pico de gallo. So good . For dinner I had pernil. The meat was so tender and just fell off the bone. It did need a little bit more seasoning but u can tell that the quality was very good. Next time she told us to try the burger! Will def be back

First time there and all I can say is AMAZING. Me and my bestfriend went at night and just the view itself is breath taking. Our waitress was amazing! She always made sure we were okay and that everything was fine and she took our orders quick. The food came really fast and tasted delicious! The vibe was just perfect. The music wasn't so loud nor low, it was just right. I recommend everyone to try this place. I enjoyed it for my first time and I would definitely return!

I'm sad to see the low ratings here. I suppose I can't disagree completely with other reviewers. Their products do come with a higher pricetag, and they take some time to make, but personally, I don't see either of those things as dealbreakers. I don't mind spending $8 on a superfood smoothie (Nuts About Acai - so stinkin' good!), because it's basically a meal. I'll spend $8 on a delicious & nutritious dinner, and I don't mind waiting a few minutes for it, either. The service is casual, but friendly. Overall, I've never had any complaints, and I always look forward to getting my Eco-fix.

i dont get it,people have to be so mean spirited. Eco bean is probably the best juice/coffee bar i have been too.The smoothie i had was incredible and everything was organic and the price well you get what you pay for.

I stopped in for a smoothie around 8:30am, mid week and there were only a couple other customers there as well. The service was super friendly, willing to make recommendations and wait patiently as I (first time customer) decided what to order. My smoothie was delicious- went for the Almond Buttercup. I have to say the prices are definitely high- I paid almost $10 for a 16oz smoothie + tip.However, this was a special treat for me-not something I will purchase daily. If you're into healthy foods, organic, raw, probiotics, etc etc, this is definitely a fun place to visit to try something new- maybe inspire some at-home smoothie makers. Other reviews knocked the staff for being slow and rude- I did not experience either. I was greeted walking through the door and treated very well. I will definitely go back next time I want to treat myself and give my blender the day off.

My husband & I Just had dinner here and it was fantastic. You can taste  the authenticity in the food. You can tell in every dish we had that it was made fresh on the spot. I love that it is a BYOB too. The owner and staff are very friendly! We will def be back! Must try the guacamole!!!

Matador in Bloomfield is as authentic as it gets when it comes to Mexican food. We went for brunch this past week and sampled a slew of goodies including Tamles (mole and rajas), chilaquiles verde, huevos rancheros, pan con chocolate, and the tacos Al Pastor spicy spork with Pineapple served with onions and cilantro. All of the hot sauces are incredible. The food alone would be enough (their tortillas and chips are homemade) but then you add in the awesome owner that goes by the name "Moose" and his sweet mom who clearly takes pride in her cooking, along with his kids hanging out in the restaurant/helping serve you - you just can't help but fall in love with this spot. Oh and we got some tamale's to go! Moose said they freeze really well. Can't wait to return!
Food here is awesome! Very casual and the host is super nice. Want real Mexican come here. My fiancé and I were pleasantly surprised.
One of the BEST Mexican Restaurants not just in Bloomfield but in my searches all around NJ! Great hospitality and they bring that out in the food... Excellent Job!!

Old school Italian menu but very authentic and lots of fresh specials each night. Very delicious. The decor and music is also really old school, which is not my fave, but definitely fits the menu. Music / decor didn't take away from the experience, but would definitely suggest they change it up or turn the music off!

I do not understand any of the past reviews. This restaurant is awful. I took a date on Saturday night. We were seated promptly the server was good. The food was blah. The sauce was sour, The pasta was over cooked. My girlfriend had a chicken dish it was dry and burnt on the edges. The past reviews must be from friends of the owner. I will not return priced like Manhattan food like Olive garden. Awful!!!!

Amazing food and outstanding service. Il Falco is a very traditional, white tablecloth restaurant where your wine glass is never empty. The atmosphere and menu are very similar to Il Mulino, and the prices are a little more reasonable. Food: Complimentary bruschetta and fried zucchini Seafood stuffed eggplant rollatini appetizer Lobster Ravioli in a pink cream sauce Combination platter: mushroom ravioli with black truffle and homemade parpadelle with sausage/mushroom/tomato basil sauce Dessert: ricotta cheesecake, flourless chocolate cake, and zabaglione combination platter. Will definitely be coming back! Italian food at its finest!

This place was amazing. By far a great fine dining establishment. Went here for my anniversary and they made sure to make us feel super special. The ambiance was nice, very romantic. They also provided a lot of complimentary things from Grappa to bruschetta to zucchini crisps, even a special anniversary chocolate cake with 2 glasses of champagne! Everyone was great and the food was super delicious. I loved everything about it and I loved our waiter and even our bartender Louis for the yummy cocktails. Superb! Worth every penny!

Checked this place out, because it's loved on yelp!!! This place is very nice. The employees are very friendly, the service was very good the glass of water was never empty. They're on top of their game. I had their signature drink raspberry cocktail and it was very delicious, my girlfriend tried it and wanted one as well. Worth checking this place out. The food is fresh and service is great!!!!

Had a really nice brunch here. I called beforehand--about 15 minutes before my party of three wanted to come and they said there should be a table available for me. It was ready and waiting! I got the French Toast with apples and it was divine. One of the top French Toasts ever. I also tried the smoked tile fish sandwich, which was good, but did not go well with the French Toast. It's a cute place with a cozy ambiance. **And they actually do take reservations, as noted below! Very nice!

Could this restaurant be any cozier? The server was eminently accommodating to our every need. We sat at this roomy banquet in the back and chatted the afternoon away. The menu is seasonal, and well prepared. My only criticism is the food needs to be seasoned more carefully.

Really cute little restaurant. Rustic decor with old maps and prints and light fixtures and used wood planks, could easily imagine warping back in time a couple hundred years. Tables tightly spaced. Attentive service. We had gotten Starbucks coffee while we were waiting for our reservation time, and the waiter actually brought us mugs for our outside coffee. Excellent brunch menu - we tried the ricotta pancakes, farm scramble, brioche French toast, and grilled ham and cheese - all delicious. Recommend the spicy margarita - potent.

The Gnocchi Lasagna is awesome! Like nothing I ever had before. I also loved that the owner came right up to me and offered to put parmesan cheese on it and then asked me what I thought about the food. You get a fresh made meal, much better than your typical pizza place for the same price. My new go to spot!
