I stopped in today for lunch.  Upon entering, i was greeted warmly by the staff.  The cashier explained how the quick fixx menu works (chef-prepared items on the front; build-your-own options on the back).  I opted for the orzo salad with grilled veggies and goat cheese.  Tasty!  The veggies are warm and the orzo is chilled, but you can ask them to warm the pasta for you if you prefer.  The salad includes ginger which, at first, i thought would be an odd choice.  But it worked!  I wasn't in love with the grilled romaine, but that's just me. Chris H. ordered the flatbread with bacon and gruyere and i was jealous!  I plan to return to sample all of the flatbread combinations.  Overall, a very pleasant experience.  Great addition to the neighborhood!

My wife recently told me about the opening of Quick Fixx, and I convinced her we should give it a go tonight. The woman who took my order was very pleasant. She told me it would only be about 20 minutes till our food would be delivered, and it couldn't have been more than 10. Our delivery guy was equally friendly. The food was excellent!!! We ordered the Gnocchi Lasagna, the Lancaster PA flatbread, and the Di Carlo salad. My wife and I have never liked gnocchi, but my wife said it sounded good, so we decided to order it. It was cooked perfectly with great flavor. The flatbread was equally delicious, and the greens in the salad were fresh. The salad came with some delicious bread. My only criticism is the caesar dressing left a bit to be desired. It had a slight fishy taste and was fairly heavy. Otherwise, I could not have asked for a better dinner and at a very good price. We will absolutely be going back.

This was a really good place for a super bargain - and it would have been a nice value even if not for our groupon. Chicken satay appetizer was delicious. Being a wuss, the peanut sauce was a bit much for me, but it had good flavor and he lapped up every bite. I enjoyed my drunken noodles with shrimp, although they could have used a bit more flavor over all. They weren't stingy on the ingredients, as they included a perfect balance of non-mushy noodles, tender veggies including carrots, green beans, cabbage, bok choy, onions, and probably a couple things I'm forgetting, and plenty of nicely-cooked shrimp. I'd absolutely order it again. He loved his roasted duck with red curry sauce (although I, once again with the wimpy pallet, could not take the spiciness), which had awesome squash and eggplant julienned over the top.   For a $3 supplement, his rice was replaced by an amazing plate of succulent vegetables. Broccoli, green beans, carrots, mushrooms, cabbage... all perfectly sauteed in just enough garlic and oil. Strange though it may seem, we couldn't stop talking about the veggies. Service was terrific, even though it was just one guy doing everything in the front of the house. We had a reservation but it was unnecessary if you don't have a groupon - empty when we arrived on a Saturday night and at best only 1/2 full. With a couple soft drinks, our total was only around $46 before the groupon was applied. Kind of sad that they don't have more business... maybe it's the location? Worth checking out!
Very good food, excellent drinks and great service! Will definitely come back here and I recommend this place to anyone. Very affordable, you will have a great time. :-)

The food was decent, but the waitstaff is horrendous!!! This was by far the worst service I have ever received. My friends and I were treated so disrespectfully for literally no reason.  I will never be going back. Save your self the aggravation, and pick another spot to eat lunch.

I am a big fan of Indian food and Spice Grill has consistently deliverd good food at a very affordable price.  I had a lunch buffet on Friday 9/9/11 with about 8 of my colleagues. As always, the food and value is excellent.  Ambience is OK and not that great.  Their rice pudding is amazing. Only negative is that clothes smell like Curry due to strong odor from spicy food.  I don't mind, but just want to bring to you everyone's attention.

I love this place The food is so Delicious  The cicilian pizza is the Best in NY and NJ when i have a chance i always Take one to go i really recomend this place is great too for a Red Bull Game is so Close.

My bigest regret in Life? That I don't get back to the Ivy Inn regularly anymore! Okay - so that might be stretching it a bit. But for almost ten years I spent a month every summer in Princeton. The Ivy was an almost nightly affair. Princeton is a pretty buttoned up kind of place, but the Ivy was somewhere I could always go and let it all hang out, so to speak. The price is right on the beer. Justin, Mikey and the rest of the gang that run the place are cool, make you feel right at home and know how to take care of you. What's really nice about the place is that you can find everything you're looking for. If I wanted to just chill out with my friends and colleagues (all a group of professors) at a table and shoot the breeze, it was an excellent place to do it. If I was up for some pool, there's never any shortage of competition and conversation at the pool table. If I needed to tie one on, knock back a few shots and sing karaoke till my voice was hoarse, I had ample opportunity. Seriously though, some of my best memories are from the Ivy. When you want somewhere to go in Princeton that's not like everywhere else, when you want a place where you can just relax, chill out and have fun - the Ivy Inn is the place to do it! I don't think I've ever had more good times, in one place, for so long than being at the IVY Inn!

The indoor seating is OK, but the outside seating it what makes this place! The indoor is a typical dive bar. The outside is a great option for Princeton, inexpensive drinks and casual environment. Great for drinks in the evening in Princeton!

WONDERFUL place that's "real" in the midst of Princeton, NJ. Cheap drinks and the best bartenders around. Always a great crowd that laughs and sings together. Some of my best memories are from that bar! A great alternative to the overly-priced everything else in Princeton!
5 stars because it's mother fucking Dan Delaney. Yeahhhhhhhh Brisket.
The ribs were juicy but somewhat lacking in flavor, while the brisket was a bit on the dry side. Not bad, but nothing great. I definitely want some of whatever the previous reviewers were smoking.

Really?? Are you serious?  We showed up at 6 PM on a Sunday, having pre-ordered 4 lbs of brisket.  After being let in, we stood on line for quite awhile, and eventually asked the manager what the chances were of being seated.  "Slim to none" was not what he said, but implied, in a clearly disinterested  manner.  We left.  Honestly, as long as there are people dumb enough and with enough disposable income (clearly many, as evidenced by the long line as we exited) to stand on line for a pricey piece of meat (which in no way could justify the inconvenience), "buzzy" dumps like this will thrive.  I'd rather go to Blimpie.   (We actually went to a lovely Argentinian restaurant  nearby, with great food, ambiance and service.)

A friend and I dropped by on Friday night when 1/2 lb of brisket that I'd RSVP'ed became available.  We came by around 9:00 and the sign said that they were out of food for the evening, but when I told them I'd reserved my Brisket, Dan came out and was happy to serve us.  He brought us up to the counter, let us sample some of the delicious bark and meat, asked us if we preferred fatty, lean or a combination.  We added on 1/2 lb of ribs and a side of the coleslaw (they were out of the potato salad).  We helped ourselves to some pickles and onions and hot sauce, and grabbed a few plastic utensils.  With the reserve brisket added on it came to a extremely reasonable $30. The food itself was a bit of a mixed bag.  The eponymous brisket is, unsurprisingly, divine.  With little in the way of sauce or seasoning beyond salt and pepper, the unquestioned star of the show is the juicy, fatty beef sliced in long slivers on the tray.  The meat is delicious from any place on the cut, the fattier meat being an tongue-coating indulgence, and the bark being a smoky, salty treat.  They blend well together and with the sides of pickles, onions, and slaw, but the brisket is even better on its own.   The slaw was good, non-traditional.  It lacked a creaminess that I tend to prefer to balance the spice of most places, but seemed unnecessary without a hot barbecue sauce to sit opposite of.  It was crisp, not soggy, and had a bit of a kick of its own that was more than acceptable for a side. The ribs were frankly a disappointment.  For a place that seemingly slow-cooks the brisket into a juicy, meaty pudding (in the best sense of the word), the ribs were fairly dry, and lacked the juicy, slow-cooked texture that was imparted onto the brisket.  The flavors were good, but the cook was fairly inconsistent.  It's understandable why this is not called "rib-town". This is a stripped down BBQ joint at its most skeletal.  Help yourself to a roll of paper towels and hot sauce, and be prepared to share and get your fingers dirty.  You can make yourself a 'sandwich' of sorts by grabbing the brisket with your wonder bread and slopping the pickles, onions, and hot sauce on with it, but its at its best on its own.  If you want fancy table service, this is not the restaurant for you, and yet the atmosphere of the restaurant is one of the things that will keep me coming back.
amazing place,wonderful people and delicious food...all strictly italian!!! a place that New York City was lack of! To try !!!
Amazing place with delicious food and great atmosphere!! Authentic italian coffee and paninis, will be definitely coming back!

One of the best happy hours I have ever seen. Came here with about 6 people and spent at least 2 or 3 hours out back on the 'stoops' which was very reminiscent of all of our younger years drinking on a friend's real stoop -- very fun stuff. Really great service from a burly bearded man who didn't let our glasses stay empty for more than a minute. And just when I thought it couldn't get any better, they built a fire in the fire pit! It was so cozy and fun.  My friends ordered a bunch of appetizers. They seemed to really like the fried jalepeno poppers & spinach dip. I skipped the dip and had one popper that appropriately seared my tongue but it was quickly aided by a nice cold beer. I'll definitely come back and I hope they keep the backyard open in the colder months for many more fires.

I came here just to watch game 7 of the World Series with a friend. We sat at the bar. As it turned out, it was Trivia Night. It was a lot of fun and the host ran it well. After trivia was over, they turned on the sound of the game instead of music. I'm not sure if anyone asked them to do so, but I was very happy about it. We had burgers, which were delicious - above average. Their regular fries were just okay - I will order sweet potato or waffle fries if there is a next time. I chatted with several other customers throughout the night and everyone was friendly. The bartender (Jen), was really nice to us the entire time. She even put away a bag for me which I had left on the bar when I went outside for a cigarette - really good customer service. We had a great time, enjoyed the atmosphere, met some friendly people, enjoyed their burgers and got our asses kicked in trivia. Giants won.

If I could give a million stars I would. But unfortunately this piece of shit yelp only allows me to count to five. As for the food: bomb dot com As for the bar service: bomb dot double com As for the bar tenders: Marshall, he's a hunk of baltimore body and you won't regret talking with him. I also can attest to the fact that he is a trivia goddess. His questions will literally blow your mind. Jen, she is probably the sweetest and most genuine person who can tend to you for 1.5 hours while you satiate your innards with sweet liquor. Overall -- all around great people at this bar. So glad it's in my neighborhood.
Great place to enjoy a great meal! One of my favorite place to eat. Service is always great! Good portions, reasonable prices. Never a bad experience here. Great for families.

Homemade corned beef hash with eggs - my all time favorite diner breakfast.  When I saw that the hash wasn't some over salted canned stuff (which I gladly eat when there's no other option) - I was pretty excited. That alone makes the Galaxy worthy of a visit. The breakfast menu changed since the last time I was here (four years ago). The next time I come in I'll definitely go with one of the new skillets. The all sounded amazing. My wife and I also split a Belgian waffle - no complaints there either. It was served nice and hot with warmed maple syrup. The service here was fantastic too. For breakfast or even some diner food - without a doubt give it a shot.

Great spot to enjoy a drink before or after an event at the Prudential Center. The service can be slow if the place gets really packed, but overall it's a quality establishment. The food is great, especially the pizza and burgers.

I love hockey! I love a great atmosphere and beer as well. Newark is a bit sketchy so I was wary of looking for somewhere to hang out before a Devils game. The bar sits in the shadow of the Prudential Center, so the location is prime before a game. My boyfriend and I sat down at the bar, ordered some beers and a few apps. The wings were great, crispy and spicy. I got the onion rings which had honey drizzled over it with sesame seeds. I would have never guessed to pair these flavors. Wash it down with a cold beer and it's the perfect pre-game ritual. I would love to visit again.

This is without question one of the best sit-down restaurants for lunch or dinner in the area and is absolutely the best pre-game bar/restaurant in Newark. The food is very good. The burgers are delicious, and there's a pulled pork sandwich on the lunch menu (absent from the dinner menu) that's wonderful. The onion rings are a touch too greasy, but the fries are pretty much perfect (try the sour cream and onion fries or the sweet potato fries - both are delicious). Beware, the restaurant becomes completely mobbed before an event at the Prudential Center and service slows down dramatically. Unfortunately, few months after opening they decided to no longer take reservations on game days. So, when considering eating here for dinner unrelated to an event at the Prudential Center, you'd be well served to check the event page anyway to see what crowds you might be competing with.
Yuuuuum simple and Relaxing

So after reading all reviews I was shocked!! I couldn't believe my eyes that people would write such horrible reviews for such a great place. My family celebrated my dad's birthday there yesterday.  It was a party of 8 adults and 3 kids and we had an awesome dinner. I called couple of hours before our arrival to make a reservation and a very nice girl took care of everything. She was very polite and also called me 5 minutes prior to our arrival to make sure that she had to keep the table reserved for us. The place is a small cozy family restaurant which serves outstanding food.  The day before our dinner was scheduled, my brother sent me reviews from Yelp. After reading them, I was very concerned about all those negative feed backs. Then I told to myself, well, people have different tastes and some people are more demanding than others. Let's give it a try. Thanks God I did not pay attention to any of those feed backs. I would make couple of recommendations for those of you considering visiting this place. First of all, about their service and peoples' feedback about it.  Folks...., you have to realize one thing, when you go to a place that is not "Ruth's Chris Steak house" that charges you $80 per person for  someone dancing around your table with a fake smile and kissing your "as..." every 2 seconds, don't expect the same service from a family oriented place. The service was outstanding, the waitress did her best to meet every ones' requests and made sure that we had freshly cooked food, nicely served in  beautifully decorated dishes. In regards to the food, whoever wrote comments about quality of the food, must have been on crack and smoking something prior to coming to this place. Are you kidding me??? The food was delicious. Yes, I have to agree that it took 30 minutes for appetizers to arrive and close to 1 hour for kebab and main dishes to arrive. But folks, everything was fresh, delicious. And even a lot of food was coming prior to main dishes. So, we were not sitting there and starving.  You must realize once thing. This place doesn't serve previously frozen food, which is just shoveled into the microwave to warm it up for needy customers. They cook everything from the scratch, which gives it very fresh taste. We ordered 5 different variety of meat, lamb. It was one of the best lamb I have ever had in my life. And believe me, I have visited several different restaurants that serve meat and none of them were as good as this one. Another thing, when you go to a place that serves authentic food, make sure you at least read about dishes that they serve if you don't know what each dish is.  If you ordering something that takes 1 hour to cook because they serve it fresh, don't expect it on your table in 25 minutes. Order some appetizers and salads while waiting for your dish. So, if you are one of those who like to have a meal on the table 20 minutes after your arrival to the restaurant, you should consider Pizza Hut or Subways. This place doesn't serve macaroni and cheese and chicken nuggets that are ready to eat in 3 minutes. We took half of our food home because we couldn't eat that much any more, and our bill for 8 adults with desert was $300 with tips, which is probably as much as you would pay in a fancy restaurant for a dinner of three. And they let you BYOB without cork fee

I was pretty skeptical about healthy food (pizza) being good but to my amazement the pizza here is very good and it doesn't give me the sluggish feeling after I eat it.  I definitely would recommend the margarita pie with turkey meatball Only reason I did not give a higher rating is because 2 of the 4 times I ordered from here they did not have a shipment of chicken or turkey meatball so I couldn't really order

I had a hankering for Peruvian food, which I hadn't had since I was actually in Peru almost a year ago. So I convinced my coworkers to go to Pio Pio Riko with me. Right off the bat, everyone who works here is friendly. They'll go out of their way to make sure you have everything you need (even pouring your sodas for you). The menu had a lot of Peruvian favorites, including rotisserie chicken, lomo saltado, ceviche, seafood and rice, and salchipapas. We started out with the salchipapas (fries with hot dog slices). Portion sizes were big and the fries were hot, but not very crispy. For my main, I went with the picante de mariscos (mixed seafood in "spicy" Peruvian sauce). I put "spicy" in quotes because it wasn't very spicy (the waitress even asked if I wanted spicy or not spicy, and I definitely said spicy). That said, the seafood was plentiful - crab legs, shrimp, mussels, and squids. The rice came on the side, which I wasn't a fan of; I expected the seafood to be over rice. It was also white rice, which is lame. I also had a 1/4 chicken because I just had to try it. The breast was pretty dry, but the wing was nicely burnt to a crisp and juicy. Glad I didn't go for the whole chicken meal. All in all, it's worth visiting Pio Pio Riko for no other reason than Midtown West sucks for lunch. Prices are reasonable (especially for the portion sizes). Service is quick. Food is okay.

I lived in Miami and visited Peru for business and when it comes to trying to find traditional Peruvian cuisine this is damn good, particularly for the price. Ceviche was very good, lomo saltado was great, but it could use an upgrade in decor. BYOB and cheap and the fact remains my girlfriend is ready to lick the plate.

How do I not even give a star!  We went there to celebrate with my family. Long story short the waiter was DRUNK stole money from us then when I went to the manager to ask the waiter was so rude and abusive.  Let me add that the manager apologized and said he knew he was drunk!  He asked for my # and said someone will call me regarding this.  No one ever called me nor apologized!

The staff was friendly and service good and the food was delicious! The rotisserie chicken was very good! You can order a quarter or 1/2 chicken. We also tried the fish Civiche which was great! One of the best that I have had. The restaurant is small and the noise level high during my lunch. I will definitely go back and try more things but the Ceviche and chicken will be a regular choice.
Great! Everything here was very good, and cheap for this part of town.

The seafood here was good, but the meat was very tough. However the strangest part of the meal was the service.  We were served a dish that was brimming with sauce, and our table was not level.  So when the waitress put the dish down, the sauce started to pour out over the edge.  She gave one wipe of the table with her towel, then just left as the sauce continued to pour out!  We scrambled to scoop things out of the dish and had to ask for a pile of napkins to sop up the sauce. ??

The food is OK, Nothing spectacular.  The reason why Pio Pio Riko gets  one star is because the service is HORRIBLE!!!! I placed an order for delivery and not only did take a 1 hour and 30 minutes to arrive, but when it did arrive I had only recieved half of what was already charged o my credit card. When I called back to notify them that my order was incomplete they assured me that they would return with my complete order. They did return. Only this time they took another hour and 45 Minutes to come back with my completed order. I was a regular at this restaurant but after today I dont think I will be ordering or eating from there again. IF YOU DONT SPEAK SPANISH YOU COULD FORGET ABOUT GOOD SERVICE AT THIS RESTAURANT!
Great breakfast spot (food is not greasy like most places), decent coffee, waitresses are "OK".

Coming here for the past 10 years, I've come to realize that this place is only great for their Banh Mi (Vietnamese hoagie) and their Vietnamese coffee (cafe sua da) which is made STRONG!  Their com, rice platters, are still good, and the pho is decent here, but I would rather go next door to Nam Phuong instead.  Their service is fast, and the prices are the average for vietnamese food, just like the restaurant Nam Phuong next door.  But the food doesn't quite satisfy my hunger.

I used to  love this place. We ate here  all the time.    The last two times that we went, the food was terrible. To add insult to injury, when I brought the poor quality of the food to the manager's attention, he could not have been bothered. Not only did he ignore me, needless to say, he did not take it off the check or compensate me in anyway. I have better things to do with $50 these days Then to spend it for bad food. Accordingly, I will not be back

I came here twice, once with my Japanese friends, once with my very good close friend at night. Sadly 3 of them are all out of Philadelphia now. I thought of writing this as I miss the time.   Both time we enjoyed their place and meal. The servers are very friendly and foods are a lot for a person, but they are all very tasty. It's my favorite happy meal, and it's just very healthy compared to the McDonald's happy meal.

The Tacos Al Pastor are prepared a little differently here than other places I remember.  The pork filling is bright red coated with the Achiote and Chile marinade, and finely chopped rather than sliced.  Served simply with fresh cilantro, onion and a wedge of lime, I couldn't help but add a shot of taco sauce from the green squeeze bottle on the counter. Bold, spicy, fresh, hot and amazing.   A fine taco, A+.

I know it's a chain restaurant, but the service here is really slow. One night we came and there was almost an hour wait to be seated but with tons of empty tables. When we asked the host, he said it was because the kitchen was backed up. We turned around and left. We came the next day but even though we were seated promptly, we waited over 10 min before they asked us what we wanted to drink. Then again it took forever for the food to come. Maybe it was just a fluke because of presidents weekend, but this place is sloooow.

I work nearby and order from OSH all the time.  While the food is good, the service is beyond questionable.  As of late, delivery orders often showed up cold, late, and incomplete.  When we called back to asked for the missing food, the owner would promise to deliver the missing food immediately.  However, our missing sandwiches never shows up.  On three different occasions one of my colleagues would pay for a sandwich and end up starving.  We will NEVER order from this incompetent amateur operation again!

Fantastic sandwiches and wraps.  Pretty good burgers and and soups.  The buffalo chicken cheese steak is a local favorite and for good reason.  It is simply my favorite sandwich in the world.  What makes it really special is the amazing toasted sourdough bread.  When I come home I don't feel like I am home until I have some steak and hoagie.  There is only one drawback to this establishment:  The prices keep getting higher and higher. If the prices were lower this would get 5 stars from me. Delivery service is a big bonus though.

Had an amazing meal there last night. Sat at an awesome table upstairs next to the open windows. Ambiance was great and our sever was fantastic. Beef tartare toast, octopus, and scrambled eggs with roe were all amazing. Formage blanc toast was a bit more sour cream-like than I was expecting and would not order again. Sea bass was solid but not off the charts like other reviewers said. For dessert we had a meringue with rhubarb and basil ice cream that was the perfect end to an awesome meal. Cocktails were also a highlight and the blue heat was the best cocktail I have had in years. Well done Vernick, cannot wait to return!

I went to Vernick with my in-laws for my MIL's bday. We had a reservation for 8:30 but we arrived about ten minutes early and got a drink at the bar. I highly recommend their cocktails - I had the Old Cuban, which is Vernick's take on a mojito. It was one of the best cocktails I have had in a looong time. The bartender was great - quick on service and cheerily answered my FIL's questions about the different types of bitters they use. To start we had a salad- the special (a strawberry goat cheese) which was eh, seemed like a salad you could get anywhere. However, the crispy and creamy mozzarella plate was amazing. I considered snatching it away and hiding in a corner to eat it by myself - Gollum style - but I luckily wasnt quite drunk enough yet to do that. I'm a gluten free vegetarian so I didnt have the peas and bacon on toast, but I was assured it was excellent in a want-to-steal-it-away manner. We also got the grilled icerberg salad, which was great as long as you got a bite of everything on your fork (fig, cheese, etc), otherwise it was just nicely charred lettuce. The chef offered to make me a special plate, which I appreciated. However - and this is the reason I am withholding a star - it wasnt clear from what the waitress described that he was basically going to make me a roasted veggie plate. I was a little disappointed - no rice or anything else - just a plate of veggies. Delicious veggies, but I expected more... The fam loved the whole roasted chicken and fish of the day. Had an excellent dark chocolate cake for dessert (well, I just had the frosting) and without any prompting, the waitress thoughtfully included a candle for the bday. Overall, a very satisfying meal.

Vernick has a great location. We ate on the second floor by the window, so we had a really nice view of Walnut street from up there. Our waiter was very knowledgeable and helpful. He was a little pushy on his favorite wine, but I appreciated that he showed passion for what he was serving. The food was really good. I have gone for just drinks as well, the downstairs bar can be a nice place for a drink as well.

The best thing about this place is the ambience. Sitting upstairs on a warm summer night with the windows open really is quite gorgeous. The food is decent, but for some reason, perhaps it's the dishes we ordered, they all seemed to be near misses. Maryland crab on toast and chicken liver with red onion chutney on toast - Both of these dishes were quite delicious. There's a generous amount of crab and the red onion chutney was delicious on the chicken liver. The little hint of dill on it was nice too. The sourdough bread was good, but slightly burnt. Tuna poke - Very good as well, although the macadamia nuts were not needed. Sea urchin with warm scrambled eggs - The scrambled eggs were deliciously done, and I also love sea urchin. Together they didn't seem to harmonize as much, and everything was just... mushy. Grilled octopus - Again a big fan of octopus, but it came out a little mushy also. I don't like it rubbery, but at the same time... not mushy either. The smoked chili and green tomato was nice. Ginger rice, black trumpet mushrooms, poached egg - Seemed pretty Asian inspired, but the rice was not cooked properly. The flavors were nice though. Pappardelle with braised rabbit - This was a home run dish. The pasta was delicious and the rabbit melt in your mouth. Amish chicken - Very nicely done as well. The chicken was moist and the skin crisp. It was very smoky from the wood oven, which is also nice. Overall I liked the restaurant but perhaps my expectations were a bit high.

Ok this is my favorite place in the city. I went there last week for the first time due to a suggestion from a friend and now I have made reservations for 2 more visits this month. Everything there was delicious. My favorites were the 1. grilled romaine lettuce 2. pea and bacon on toast (this one was surprising because on the menu it doesn't really call to you. but it has the most amazing pea/mint spread. omg) Desserts were a little bit of a let down though I didn't try the pie that all the other reviewers mentioned, so i might go back for that. Service was wonderful. They gave us a couple of little tastings on the house. It was awesome.
Ive been here 3 times now and it has only gotten better. Amazing menu that changes. Great flatbread and best sea food I have had in the city. Pricey but worth it.

I wasn't wowed by Vernick for 1 big reason..my service was struggling.  It could have been a fluke.  I could go through a longggg diatribe about them taking forever to seat us even though there was no line and we had a reze etc but I won't.  I'll spare you.  My main issue is that it took 15 to 20 minutes for our drinks to come out.  On a Saturday night?  That's borderline cruel and indecent punishment.  I know my waitress did not make the drinks so the bartender should get 50 lashes for being the slowest cocktail maker on earth BUT..the server that couldn't was MIA the entire time.  When she finally came back and noticed me drinking another table's cocktail, she got the memo real quick.  She ran right back downstairs to see what was going on with our drinks and promptly brought them to us.  I also took note that there was a manager (or host but I think manager) helping to clean tables off and she was so busy wiping and resetting the tables that she happened to miss my "I'm going to flip a table if I don't get my cocktail" look.  I guess I'm not as fierce as I thought.  Besides the booze issue, the food was excellent so I'll give them another chance..but don't make me wait 15 min for another cocktail Vernick!  You're better than that!

This place is everything I look for in a Jersey diner. Open 24 hours, offers quick service, greasy food, and there is always a table available. Plus, they serve booze. Best item on the menu: pizza fries

Wednesday night are a great night to come and have a drink or 2!!  NO COVER! Kitchen with great food open until 2am!!  Karaokee, cash beer pong tournament, drink and shot specials all night long... the best Wed night party around come check it out!
great drink and food prices also great happy hour prices on food and drinks... i love their wings .  great staff and great place to meet new people

Really great place to hang out, the bartenders are awesome and the drinks are great! I was there for friday happy hour and the free buffet was delicious. I'm definitely going to make this a regular hang out spot.

The pub is the best place in clifton to go if you want to have fun and eat great food...the crowd is always hype and the music will almost always make you wanna get up and dance!! Saturday is the best day to go!!! Def recommend this place to everyone i know!

i have been going to pub46 for the past few years. the pub just keeps getting better. new faces and old friends . people you haven't seen since high school or college. ( the pub has great party and reunion party prices. if your in college monclair state , william paterson or felician college . check out tuesday is $2 bring your own mug. have beer pong on wednesdays. thursday the place is great to meet up at pub 46. go early because gets packed. If your out to watch sports this pub has 28 big flat screen tv s. kitchen open till 2 am. nfl nba nhl mlb ufc wwe ppv . pub46 has tv s everywhere. pool table and video games. on weekends the pub has that local feel of a corner pub. as the night goes on it gets busy with a club twist. if you live in clifton area or bergen passaic essex county you have to check out the pub. njpubs.com for less than $40 you can have a great night out. the place is open till 3 am 7 days a week.
great young atmosphere! always a good time. variety of music and people. great for sports and they have the prettiest/friendliest shot girls!!! everyone come by and get your own positive experience!

I always heard great things about pub but i was optimistic so i finally decided to check it out for myself on a Saturday night and let me tell you it was as advertised the atmosphere was great the bartenders were very uptempo,friendly and most importantly fast. They also have a great menu full of different things, you dont really expect great food at a bar but you should expect it here they have everything from finger foods like chicken fingers to full diners such as chicken parm with pasta (which was great by the way). Also the music was AMAZING! the dj's name was freddie z and hes there every Saturday he played mostly house music as well as classics. But overall you cant help but give this place a perfect rating they nailed every aspect of what a bar should contain and i will deff be going there on a regular basis.

I had a great experience here.  But I was in the company of a very lovely lady so that always helps ;) But seriously... The Sangria here is good; the pitcher is the way to go on this one, though at 25 bucks a pop it's a little much. We had two different bistec dishes and they came out great.  The food was also more reasonably priced so it came out alright in the end.

I have been here 4 times already & i have to say each time i have come in i feel welcomed and pleased with the people who are in the kitchen and who are behind the counter , I have met 3 people there i think their names were Erick , Modesto & Daisy. They are very nice people and they look like they enjoy working there. This place is very pretty. It's based on the Mexican loteria. What an idea!! I loved the artwork. The food is sooooo delicious , makes me lick my fingers! I've had the Carne asada , Camaron and Pollo Taco oh my goodness they are good, the Carne asada burrito is very delicious and not pricey like other places, I've had the bacon , egg , cheese and home fries burrito ,it looked yummy and it also tasted yummy! I loved the sauces as well . I give this place a 5 star rating and i recommend going on a Tuesday why? Because hello! Its Taco Tuesdays. This place will be seeing me more often ;)

I got a burrito with Al Pastor and which was delicious, the hot sauce was excellent and I didn't feel like shit afterwards.  I can easily see myself coming back.  The only issue it was really only big enough for a light dinner... maybe a heavy snack, which is a stretch for an 8 dollar burrito.
best place for quesadillas, and also has horchata, don't miss out!!

I have been hearing alot of buzz about Room 55 which opened in the old Tazzina location. We always love to stay in the neighborhood and give our locals the business. I bought an Amazon local deal figured it was an opportunity to try it. I made a reservation for this evening and told the person who took the reservation that we had a   voucher, no mention about printing it out although I did. We arrived and were greeted by Trevor who seated us. He asked for the voucher right away which I handed to him. He gave us the menu and proceeded to mention that he was a chef and he was helping his good buddy Vinny that night. We looked over the menu and to tell you the truth nothing was making me get too excited. Trevor came to take our order we had to tell him what we would like to drink he didn't ask but proceeded to make a wine suggestion didn't tell us about the Sangria that was being served to other patrons. I ordered the mushroom/asparagus salad and my husband ordered the clams casino appetizer. I must mention that the bread basket which consisted of two flat breads and two slices of white italian bread served with olive oil was pretty pathetic at best. When Trevor took away the bread basket to make room for the appetizers he could have returned with more given the clams casino had a very nice broth great for bread dipping. For the main course I ordered the grouper with a beet salad and beet puree. By far the beets beat out the fish which was covered with two slices of toasted bread. Just ruined the fish by adding bread! Come on with the bread on fish! My husband ordered the perch which was served with spaghetti squash, half of which was hot the other half cold. Trust me for him to comment that it was cold it must have been cold because it is a running joke that I always get cold food. We skipped dessert as I couldn't wait to leave. Btw I took a picture of my view from the table I was sitting at: double doors, and about 10 warning signs an emergency kit and god knows what else. Not appealing to the eye. Sorry to say I will not be recommending or returning any time in the future. Best of luck to you though.

My search for the authentic Chinese restaurant in the Greater New Haven area ended a few nights ago when my family and I dined here.  Felt very assured to enter this restaurant by seeing many Chinese clients, greeted warmly by two waitresses.  Very happy to read the menu of the dishes with freshly prepared food, unlike prepared sauce and precooked fried stuffs you encounter at the American/Psudo-Chinese restuaurants.  The Squid dish, Ginger Scallion Fish, Shrimp Lomain, Scallion Pancake, and Pork Buns were just perfect. We are happy to find this place, thanks to the Yelp, and no longer need to drive to NYC or Boston for the authentic Chinese restuarant, and wonderful Szechuan Food.

Ambiance for outdoor seating on patio is hard to beat anywhere in Philly. Honestly, the place was better when Alex ran it years ago. New owners are nice, but the food (and brunch) is not the same. I still stop by for cheese & desserts to go.

Wedge + Fig was amazing. We sat outside, which was perfect with the heat lamps. You have to walk through a dark alleyway to get to it, though, which was kind of weird. It was amazing once we were actually back there. The French press coffee was delicious and very strong. I should not have had more than a cup. I ordered the Eggs Nola, which were awesome, and everyone I was with seemed to really enjoy their food too. Our waitress persuaded us to get an order of the scones and it was definitely the best choice of the whole meal. Overall, this place was quaint and beautiful and the food was very tasty. You couldn't help but feel happy at a place like this.

Wedge + Fig is a charming Old City destination for anyone looking for a cute brunch spot in Center City. I've been to Wedge + Fig twice recently and left both times feeling satisfied and wanting more. I would give this place a 4.5 if I could, but I'll just round up. A couple of things, in no particular order: + Eggs NOLA puts a cajun twist on a classic eggs, ham + hollandaise, potato, and salad brunch dish. It wasn't until halfway through the meal when I suddenly realized that there were supposed to be cajun flavors in the dish. Nevertheless, still very delicious. + Prices are very reasonable + I went with two other people during my recent visit and we ordered three sandwiches and basically sampled each one. We got the palooka, shackamaxon, and blue figs. They were all really delicious and unique; palooka in particular was perfect. It also had the biggest portion for a marginally higher price. + They have a really cute patio in the back. I would highly recommend it, weather permitting. Getting there requires you to go through a "secret" passageway, which is an adventure in itself! - My only complaint about this place would be that the utensils (specifically the fork) did not seem to be washed carefully. I asked the server to get me a new set. In summary, Wedge + Fig is easily one of my favorite restaurants in the city. I will definitely be back!

Wedge + Fig is a great little place for brunch. The options for breakfast are a bit limited but nonetheless, the food is delicious. I had the Eggs Nola, their take on Eggs Benedict. Perfectly poached egg and hollandaise over cajun spiced ham and a cornbread biscuit, so good! I also got a bite of the bacon lattice mac & cheese and their omelette of the day (chorizo & queso fresco w/ pico de gallo), both were amazing. I love their quaint little outdoor seating area, definitely ask to be seated outside if you're dining here on a beautiful day! Service was also attentive and friendly. I highly recommend this place!
Great atmosphere, music and service. Food 4/5 stars. BYOB also deducts a point! Overall- not bad, maybe ill come back

Went last night for the first time... ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC. The food was amazing and so was the service. I was there with a group of 13 people for a birthday party. The manager / owner (？) was extremely accommodating and helpful and our waitress was wonderful.
Between G Lee's and Super WIngs it is awesomness the pulled pork sandwhich and the jalepenos mac n cheese, is amazing, I will be back.. THIS PLACE Is worth my money
Excellent pulled pork sandwich, great happy hour deals, super awesome staff. I will definitely be going back for more BBQ deliciousness

PHENOMENAL PLACE! Passed by looking for a place to eat and came back here with my friend. Very relaxed ambience and there was live music, too! We were sat immediately, and I ordered a glass of sangria to calm my craving I had all day. Followed that up with the Chicken Skewers (they're small, which is just what I wanted, but they lacked a bit in flavor) and the Waldorf salad. Let me tell you somethin about that salad! Fresh. Crisp. Sweet. Salty. A perfect combination of bits and pieces picked up from God's green Earth culminating in a light, yet plentiful, and very satisfying salad. The Waldorf.

I have a good number of Filipino friends and over the years I've been hearing about Jollibee nonstop. Of course when this Jollibee opened up in Jersey City and I found myself there for work, I had to go and see what the fuss was all about. My coworkers and I got there at about 8:30 PM and there was a huge line that went out the door. Conveniently there is a liquor store right next door, so after a long day at work, my coworkers were able to get some beer to hold them over in line. The line moved relatively quickly considering the amount of people but it still took us about 30 minutes to get from waiting outside to the front of the line. I ordered an Aloha burger, 2 pc chicken w/ a side of fries, peach mango pie, and a buko pandan pearl drink. The bill came out to about $17, which isn't bad considering the amount of food I got. The cashier was friendly and I got my food pretty quickly. The Aloha burger was topped with bacon, (grilled?) pineapple, lettuce, and some kind of special sauce. The beef patty was a little on the dry side, but the moisture of the sauce and pineapple helped a lot. Overall though, the flavors of the burger were great and it is definitely one of the better fast food burgers out there. Even my coworker who claims to be really picky about his burgers thought that the burger was "bangin'." The chicken was quite juicy and was still steaming hot, even after I finished my burger. The chicken didn't have a lot of flavor on it's own but the gravy that it comes with really saved it. The gravy was probably the best part of the whole meal. It was probably one of the best gravies I've ever had. I actually kept some of the gravy to eat with my leftover french fries because it was so good. Speaking of their french fries, they were what you expect good french fries to be: crunchy on the outside and moist on the inside. They had a good flavor on their own, but I only ate so much of it because it was a medium to get gravy into my mouth. The peach mango pie reminded me of a McDonald's apple pie (which I don't really like) but I got it based off a friend's recommendation and seeing a ton of other people at the restaurant eating it.  It was a bit cold for my liking but seeing as how I had eaten a burger, chicken, fries, and savoring every drop of gravy, I'll forgive it. Despite the temperature, I found this to be quite good. I love peaches and mangoes so this pie really did them justice. The buko pandan pearl drink was a coconut flavored smoothie with tapioca pearls. I was not a fan of their tapioca pearls; I don't think they were fully cooked, as the insides were still crunchy. I'm not huge on tapioca pearls to begin with and this really didn't help their cause. The smoothie itself was actually really good and I would get it again, but without the tapioca pearls. Overall, I enjoyed all of the food and I would definitely go there again if I ever find myself in Jersey City. Writing this review is actually making me crave that gravy again.

They're still trying to get into the rhythm of things. The line is always long but I think that in a few months it'll die down. They close at 9 most of the time so if you're planning to head there past 8, you might miss the boat. I had some issues when I went there last night. The ice tea was all water, it took the guy in charge a while to figure out after some people told them. The guy at the registrar gave 2 pieces of chicken instead of 3, missing a spaghetti too so we had to go back to the counter to clear it up, so make sure you got the receipt in case something goes missing! It was 80+ degrees and the fire alarm went off for some reason, the Ube bubble tea's tapioca wasn't fully cooked, it had a hard center which didn't make the experience of eating it that great. The spaghetti is not the typical Italian type, it's sweet and isn't for someone who likes sweet sauce. The chicken was average, not as good as Popeyes or KFC but it's just OK. Yeah, i've experienced better, but I think that after a few more months, they'll get things in order.

Childhood memories of the place give it four stars automatically. Spaghetti joy and chicken joy combo- yum! Halo Halo- yum! Peach Mango Pies- yum! but expensive! (almost $4 for 2) Overpriced jollibee doll for $8- no thanks.  Waiting in line for over an hour- no thanks.  I asked the cashier who took my order if it was always like this.  She said yes.  If you have small children who are impatient, wait a while to take them here. Parking is also very annoying.   I wish there was a drive through.

We've been back again and had the sirloin cheeseburger, steak panini, and grilled cheese. All were excellent, but we esp. love the grilled cheese - Fig bread, cambozola and fontina cheese, with a spiced cherry jam.  Sounds odd, but it is sooo good!
Great food and great service in a trendy setting- absolutely going back.

This restaurant is just what Downtown Hartford needs! It has a clean, updated space right next to the XL Center. The waitress told me the menu will be expanding, as I went there during the first week of opening. I was able to enjoy quality Asian food at affordable prices. I especially love the rice paper spring rolls with shrimp and the wonton soup. The rolls are prepared to order and especially fresh and crisp. The service is outstanding....prompt, polite, and friendly...something I don't find all too easily these days. I also love the cucumber margarita specialty cocktail suggested to me by the owner.

The food was to die for...everything I ordered was interesting, fresh and flavorful. The cocktails were creative and delicious. The service was fantastic...everyone was pleasant and attentive. The design detail of the restaurant gave it a really nice atmosphere...the bathrooms were very clean...plan to come back soon with friends. I would definitely recommend Laetus...this is soon to be the new hot spot!

Last night was my first time trying out Laetus Restaurant & Pho noodle soup & let me tell you I am impressed. The restaurant is a nice addition to downtown hartford - great vibe - great service, staff is very friendly & the food was delicious. The egg rolls were so tasty  and the pho noodle soup dish get 2 thumbs up. My favorite part of the meal was the lychee martini I had - OMG best one Ive ever tasted in my life, the bartenders definitely know what they are doing there. Want to thank everyone there for a great dinner experience. I will be back again soon :) & will definitely recommend this place to my friends & family and anyone who is looking for a great vietnamese dish & the tastiest drinks.... I can't wait to try some of their others.

I was just there for dinner for the first time. The decor was nice, the host was friendly.  She made good suggestions for us, as we were not experts with Thai/Laos food.  The food came out fairly quickly. It tasted delicious, and exactly what I was hoping for. The host did say they were doing new things, so hopefully more people will enjoy it like we did!

Food is excellent, service is just ok- only because it is super slow. I love the panang curry. The lunch specials are excellent too :). I loved cafe de Laos and was really upset when I found out they weren't there but this place is great. The decor also looks much better than before. I'd give it five stars if they could speed it up a bit!

Came here on a whim with a friend who was visiting from Ithaca NY.  We had a wonderful experience!  The food was very flavor and fragrant.  My boyfriend raved that it was the best Pad Thai he ever had - and I especially like how it wasn't so oily like I've seen with other Pad Thai dishes.  We also experimented by trying the Ka Nom Jeen Kang Kai (Green Curry Noodle), which I really enjoyed. On top of all of this, the service was outstanding.  Our server was very pleasant, and you could tell that the manager really cared about your overall experience.

I have been love this place. A very nice people who serve you is one of the biggest sign in this place. The place will take you to an Asian like place. The food is very delicious. The price is very reasonable. The most of all you can order on-line and when it ready you can pick it up. It is very convenient. The website is nicely done. Most of all I totally love this place.

I won't be surprised when Ratchada will soon become a new best place for Thai in South Philly.  I've been here twice this week and has not been disappointed. Their foods are fresh, flavorful, and needless to say DELICIOUS ! I'm eating leftovers of their foods (Green Curry Noodle and Massaman Curry) I ordered from last night right now as I'm writing this review and they still satisfied me.  Yum !!! This place just opened a month ago in December 2012 under new management with an additional new chef from the previously owned Cafe De Laos so those old negative reviews are not reliable. They only have two servers but they always served you with a genuine smile and care despite during busy hours. The ambiance is classy but not pretentious. My boyfriend and I have a pleasantly romantic date here because the beautiful decor and warm ambiance really charmed us. Try their creative and satisfying Laos Samplers appetizer and mouthwatering Thai Tea cheesecake with ice cream ! You wont regret it except maybe on your weight. I would give them a five stars but I figure i should give them four stars so that they'll continue to keep up or eventually might even surpass their current excellent foods !

This place is a GEM!! The food is awesome, nice atmosphere & a super friendly staff. We started our meal with coconut shrimp soup that was so good. It was delicate but had waves of different flavors that would play with your taste buds. Next were Salmon dumplings that were perfectly fried & delicious. The main coarse was Green Curry with chicken & Eggplant stuffed with catfish & red curry sauce over glass noodles, both were terrific. We ended the meal with Thai Tea Cheesecake which was light & yummy. Also this place is a BYOB so you save money on the liquor bill & you can spend it on ordering more of their delicious food!!

this is the best place around... its always peaceful and fun, the food is always amazing!!! i love goin there w friends, its byob and has stuff for the sushi lover in everyone. Then menu has items for nonsushi lovers which makes for a great mixed crowd!

When my 30th birthday rolled around, I knew I wanted some upscale Mexican food. A couple of Best Of lists and a bunch of yelp reviews later, I decided on Toloache. We considered all three locations, but opted for the Village location to be closer to bars after dinner. I'm so happy that we did! The entire experience at Toloache was great, and it ended up being the perfect birthday dinner. The Food: There were three of us, so we opted to share and eat tapas style. We started with the guacamole trio. It is a MUST TRY! Amazing. The price is a bit steep at $24, but I didn't regret it for a second. The Frutas (guac with mango and pomegranate!) and the Rojo were both to die for. We then shared the fish tacos, the quesadilla de huitlacoche y trufas (mushroom and truffles), and the hamachi ceviche. My boyfriend loved the quesadilla, but I thought the ceviche was the winner. Each dish was great though. The Drinks: The margaritas were all excellent, but to really have your mind blown, make sure to order the mezcalita cocktail with grilled pineapple and jalapeño. I wish I had one right now. So good! So good! So good! The Service: The service was the best part. Our server was patient through all of our annoying questions, gave great advice about what to order and once he heard it was my birthday, was sure that he and his servers gave me an appropriately embarrassing and totally fun birthday song and (delicious!) flan dessert. And, before we even mentioned my birthday, the manager Luis stopped by just to make sure that we were enjoying ourselves. My boyfriend made some joke that he enjoyed, which led him to bring us a round of tequila shots on the house. So fun! I will certainly be back! Highly recommended!

We went during Restaurant Week knowing nothing about the place and were pleasantly surprised by how close to perfection it is. Visually it was one of the most beautiful neighborhood spots we have been to - both the bright, warm interior and the view of Thompson Street that was exactly what you expect the Village to look like on a summer night. Food was also visually beautiful but more than that, it was impeccably and creatively prepared (quinoa salad a standout - fish and steak close behind) - Everybody on the staff was friendly (not overly so), competent and extremely attentive in a very natural way - they all genuinely seemed to love what they do and proud of their food and restaurant. It was a totally wonderful experience!

Food is great. Mexican food can be very bland (when it's inauthentic) but this place is anything but. While the food was delicious, it's the service that sets this place apart. The manager walked the restaurant the entire time we were there, greeting guests and taking a genuine interest in their dining experience. For example, we didn't make reservations and so we were sat close to the kitchen (really wasn't bad at all). However, the manager had two complimentary shots of tequila and a free (and mouthwatering) flan for dessert. Great experience from the same owners of Cuba.

Amazing good service.  The food tastes great, especially the pork tacos and mango dessert.  Went to lunch here for restaurant week with co-workers, everyone  was happy.  We all enjoyed the food and white sangria.  The service was exceptional, they were very welcoming and helpful....definitely one of the best experiences I've had at a restaurant in a while.  The non happy hour drinks can get a little pricey.  Looking forward to trying some of there other locations in the city.

Great ambiance, great food/drinks and great service. Can't ask for more than that. Everyone was super nice, the Chef walked around the whole night introducing himself and explaining the dishes to the patrons. I had a group of 6 and everyone loved it. Highlights included - Brussels sprout salad, white bean duck confit, roast lamb, chicken and dessert (Fennel ice cream). Let's get this straight, everything was delish but those were my personal highlights! It's a must go place, you won't regret it!

We just noticed this restaurant had opened the other day and wanted to try it out tonight. The service was great. We sat at the bar by the brick oven which I think might be the best spot in the house. The chef explained all the dishes to us, asked us what we liked, and had many suggestions for food and drinks. The food was amazing. We had hangar steak with a side of the chop salad (kale, brussel sprouts, cabbage and pistachios) which was delicious, as well as the salt trout, which despite it's name wasn't too salty at all. And for dessert, the fennel and molasses ice cream were both unique and tasty. The space is warm and inviting, brick walls and nice simple decor and lighting. We'll definitely be back soon!
Excellent service, trendy ambiance and absolutely delicious food. What are you waiting for, check out this new spot for the foodie in you!!!

Great feel for a neighborhood bar. Walk in and find yourself a table. They have a decent draft beer selection and tasty wings. The clam chowder was really good, especially with big grinds of fresh pepper. Unfortunately, the rest of the menu doesn't seem so good. Stick to the tried and true items and you won't be disappointed.

We started our meal with the following appetizers: Saganaki (Flaming pan fried Greek Graviera) and Octopus Sta Karvouna. The Octopus was literally 2 huge tentacles..it had a nice chewy texture to it. When the Saganaki came out, the waiter lit it on fire so it was literally flaming and then he squeezed lemon to put it out. I thought the presentation of the dish was more impressive than the actual taste but my friend absolutely loved the cheese. We also ordered two bevarages: the sour cherry soda and a fresh peach juice. They were good but nothing too special and in my opinion, not worth the 3.25/ 3.99 price tag. My friend ordered the filet mignon special. It came out in cubes on a stick like a kebob. The meat was nice and tender. I ordered the lamb shish kabob platter with lemon potatoes and salad on the side. Both sides were great. The lamb was a little dry though. All in all it was a great meal. It's sometime a hit of miss when I eat Greek food, but the waitress was really friendly and didn't hesitate to provide recommendations.

The best meal and staff around! I could not have asked for a better meal. If you like Greek food and want to experience a great atmosphere, friendly wait staff and fantastic fresh seafood than this is the place. I visited the Taverna today with my dad and we both opted for an imported fish from greece, char grilled with olive oil, capers, lemon and dill. This simple meal was the best meal I had in a very long time!

The food is beyond delicious, and they're creative with presentation. However, give yourself lots of extra time as service was incredibly slow. Between the octopus appetizer and our main courses, we waited nearly 45 minutes. When taking away our octopus appetizer, he assured us that the food was almost done. In fact, he assured us 3 more times that it was almost done. We were in a nearly empty restaurant (only 1 other table besides us), so it was quite hard to imagine what was taking the chefs/kitchen so long. Our delicious lunch- Octopus! Never before in all my greek restaurant going days have I ever tasted such a soft, succulent and juicy octopus. At close to $19, this platter is very worth it. It comes with red peppers, also delicious, and you must dip it in the lemony/vinaigrette sauce it comes with Bread- comes with your meal, but fresh, hot pita and so good with their olive oil/pepper dip. I also enjoyed the 4 red and green olives that it was served with Spanakopita- if you like spinach and feta, you'll love the way this traditional dish is presented- in a light, flaky pastry! I so enjoyed this, especially the delightful crust. They were definitely not stingy with the ingredients as I could tell each bite was packed with spinach pie Yiouvetsada sti gastra (lamb shank in homemade pasta)- basically, a super tender and juicy lamb shank in spaghetti with sweet sauce. This was filling and pretty delicious, a great choice if you're looking for meat and some comfort food If you're reading the menu here, or on the website, make sure you bring a couple of extra dollars. They've since increased the prices since publishing them. Everything we ordered was about $2-3 more than previously read online.
couscous was no good.

I bought a groupon deal and wish I didn't. The food was subpar. Bagged brown lettuce and a long wait to be seated for nothing. We were one of two couples in the place. The entrees were ok bit not worth paying for. We had to get our own napkins and had to ask for silverware after our food was delivered. They didn't even bring any. And we had to get more napkins. The ranch flavor on the fries was nonexistent. The appetizer was a do it yourself with no silverware to eat it. The only semi exciting part was the movie menu. Would not recommend.

Yesterday we were on our lunch break and decided to try out the Front Street Bistro. Up until then we had only seen movies there.  We sat outside on the sidewalk and ordered ice tea, I had a turkey burger and my friend had  a ceaser salad and salmon. The server checked on us twice as we were enjoying the nice weather. The turkey burger was big and cooked just right. I also has fries with cheddar salt. My friend could not finish her salad so they put it in a box for her to take with her. We are always looking for a new place for lunch. I think we found a nice one. Next week the Capital Grille Mary

Just finished trying Dig Inn for the first time and I was really impressed! Located right on the corner of 28th and Broadway, Dig Inn has an energetic and welcoming vibe as soon as you walk in! The aromas coming out of the kitchen make you salivate while you're in line. To help you stay focused, an employee will explain on how to order and call out any specials available. FYI, the price per dish is based on 1 or 2 scoops of protein, with up to two additional sides. Portion sizes are average, as well as the price. Overall, the food was superb and tasted fresh and packed with flavor! I chose the chicken over brown rice, with cranberry sweet potatoes and a garbanzo bean salad as my two sides. Chicken was surprisingly not over cooked and moist. Looking forward to grabbing lunch here again soon and trying more of their seasonal dishes!
So happy this new location is now open. Great food and fast service. Alethea and Ryan were wonderful and I will be back soon.

I was super impressed by my first visit here.   The salmon, kale, and broccoli salad were top notch and washed down well with the ginger lemonade. The staff were exceptionally helpful and energetic.  The downstairs eating area is quite pleasant and clean.  I'll be back!!!!

My boyfriend and I got lucky and just happened to pass North End Bistro on their opening night and saw people dining al fresco. We had the dog with us, so we asked if he could sit with us if we were outside - and got the OK! (Thumb's up in my book just for that.) You start with a basket of house-made kettle cooked potato chips, instead of bread - YUM. I devoured these in a second! They are thick cut, hearty, crispy chips, seasoned to perfection (for me at least!). The waiter offered to bring more, but we declined for fear we wouldn't be able to finish everything we ordered. We ordered the Lobster Mac 'n Cheese to share as a starter, and ooooh my gosh it was the best lobster mac I've ever had! It had lots of lobster - you could see claw meat! - and there was a slight sweetness to the mac, which was a great complement to the salty, cheesiness of the dish. The texture was spot on too - the pasta shells were slightly al dente, and the hot cheese (not too much!) cooked it just a wee bit more while we enjoyed. There was a nice contrasting crunch factor too - panko maybe? Def will get this again! BF got the Brazilian Lobster Roll for his meal - lobster meat with guac on brioche. This was interesting - it was very good, but I think we just prefer the traditional Maine lobster roll. (It was very big - cut in half like a grilled cheese - so he took the 2nd half home and ate it for lunch the next day - said it was just as good!) I ordered the Pabo burger - NEB's version of a turkey burger on some sort of harvest-y bread bun. It was good, but I was pretty full at this point, so did not finish it. I liked that you could choose between normal or sweet potato fries with no upcharge. I also got a side of charred brussel sprouts with goat cheese and cranberry almond relish. Um, so good! I love brussel sprouts (these aren't fried/crispy ones, they are chewy), and the goat cheese and relish pair so well with it! Didn't have room for dessert, but I'll definitely have to get some next time! We will definitely be back to see what other goodies NEB has on their menu.

Excellent wait staff, great location and atmosphere. Food not so much. We waited an hour for a Reuben I could have prepared better myself and three mediocre fish tacos. I hope the kitchen becomes as good as the front end staff.

AMAZING! The North End Bistro is definitely my new favorite place to dine on dates or with family in the Princeton area.  The staff is extremely friendly, helpful, knowledgeable, and attentive. I ordered the Lobster Roll and was thrilled with how delicious it was.  The wine is locally bought from Hopewell Valley and sold by the bottle (prices range between 20 and 25, GREAT deals).  The menu was very diverse, I can't wait to come back and try everything! There are even plenty of vegetarian options. Overall, my dining experience couldn't be topped. I will be going back with all my friends as often as I can. DELICIOUS! Also, it's incredible that they have a parking lot!! That's almost unheard of in this area and a huge plus for the restaurant in my opinion.

Went for dinner on Sat. night with another couple.  This was my second time at North End Bistro.  We were seated right away outside, which was great since it was a nice night.  The patio atmosphere was relaxing and the outdoor service was excellent.  My only complaint was the table and chairs.  Think camping-style but metal. The chairs were very uncomfortable and the tables were small.  I felt like I couldn't move my chair close enough to the table as I was eating.  Once our entrees arrived, it was very cramped to have two large dinner plates sharing this kiddie-sized table. Food:  We started with the spinach artichoke dip.  This was nothing special - just OK.  Overall, this is something I don't love overall so no surprise there.  The other choices weren't so great so this was the group consensus.  Two of us had the grilled salmon and it was delicious - cooked nicely over some sauteed veggies and potato pancakes.  The other people with us had fish tacos (thoroughly enjoyed) and the lobster mac and cheese - which was delicious. Both times I've eaten here the food and service have been great.  I plan to return and try something else off the menu.
Love this place. Fantastic food, service and atmosphere. The N-Liberties is beyond amazing.

Amazing everything. Don't hesitate. Their French toast, fluffy and full of flavor yet not  overwhelming. The sweet potato Benedict is perfect. Coffee taste sensational. Can't say enough great things. Owner is friendly and makes sure your visit is up to par. Probably one of the best places we've visited for brunch and definitely my fave now.

Depending on the staff you get, your experience can be wildly different.  There are a couple of guys that have been in good spirits each time I've been there, but a weekend younger female barista and the female owner/manager are awful on the regular.  Snarky, disparaging comments, condescending attitudes in response to simple questions.  They seem to have missed the memo that they are in the food service industry and part of that is being professional and courteous.   The first time we were there, we sat down after they showed us our table.  Then we got attitude that we're supposed to order and pay at the counter before sitting down.  Uh, ok.  Duh, stupid customers. Another time, my father got the ice when he asked if he could add toast to his brunch.  Uh, ok. Whatever. Weird but not a deal-ender. The last time, we brought my Pisces Midwestern Minister mother when she was visiting and when the female owner approached and asked my mom how she liked her food, my mom said that she was disappointed in the Eggs Benedict, but that it was ok.  Then my mom got raked over the coals.  The owner pounced on the opportunity, ridiculed my mother, yelled at her.  Super awesome.  The whole restaurant stopped.  We were embarrassed.  We'll never be back. The owner said the meal was on her.  Ha!  You have to pay before you get your meal. Know how the restaurant works before you've ever been there or risk attitude and ridicule.  Other than that it is GREAT!!! (insert glitter and stars and happy faces)

This place just won my best Philly brunch spot award. Sweet potato Benedict was simply awesome - such such good food. Owner was incredibly friendly and helpful, too - rearranging tables from outside so our big group could get seated faster, introducing us to the chef etc. Ambience inside was just OK. Cafe Lift is still better for atmosphere, but the food at la Maude wins hands down.

What a fabulous little place! We are from NYC and were in town for the weekend. SO glad we found this gem on Yelp. The staff are amazingly attentive and friendly and warm. They don't hover - they take care of you. A personal favorite of mine is that the bathroom is SPOTLESS. I even commented on this to the owner, who was there enjoying a coffee with the locals. The food was absolutely delicious. I am a coffee snob and theirs was excellent - served in LARGE mugs. We will absolutely return next time we are in Philly. We had a hard time selecting our food because we both wanted ten different things on the menu. Go!
Love this place! Food is fresh and delicious, and the perfect mix of the French & Lebanese cultures. The chicken salad with hummus is out of site. I eat lunch here 2-3 times a month.
Liked a lot, the sweet potato Benny was really good, and the coffee was excellent, the waffle we got was solid, but unspectacular. We will be back!

****12/13/14 UPDATE**** Keeping it at four stars. I went back for more and forced myself to have the Pho (because upon entering, I was lured and tempted to get a...what could it have been. Grilled beef plate of some sort? Something. It was delicious smelling. I kid you not, I spent about 3 whole minutes going back between wanting to get that over Pho). It's ALMOST all there. They have the cloves, which I appreciate. I can't quite place my finger on it. I'm slightly tempted to say it's missing MSG. But don't hold me to that. I've never made Pho in my life, because truly great Pho is intimidating. The spring rolls were kind of great though. They ALMOST satisfied my craving for whatever the hell I smelled upon entering. ****ORIGINAL**** How I start off any Pho review: Credentials: Asian SoCal Transplant. For those who know, that's pretty legit credentials. That's why when Liza P. said it was good, my mind was at ease. In the very, very rare cases where I go to a Pho place and don't have Pho (I think this is actually the second time in my life), I always try to get a bowl of the broth. Because that will tell you almost you need to know. And honey. That was delicious. I ordered dessert (that was pretty legit as well) and tacked on a bowl of beef broth. I asked if it was possible because it's not technically on the menu, and the waiter gave it to me for free. I love them. I need to go back and actually try the Pho, meat an all, before I can feel comfortable giving them a five, but really, my mind is already at at least a 4.5 based on that broth alone. Also, had a bite of what my friend ordered and that was pretty heavenly as well. COULD THIS BE *THE* PHO PLACE IN NYC?!? Probably.

We have a winner! In a diverse and sordid Vietnamese food scene here in NYC, Ph Vit Nam stands out as easily the biggest, baddest one in the ring. The food smacks of authentic taste, is reasonably priced, an unarguably fresh. I can't wait to come back to try the other stuff on the menu.

Had dinner there yesterday and enjoyed the food. Polite service, helpful advise what to eat, and the food was oh so tasty. Price was acceptable . definitely recommend it.  Who knew you wrap food in lettuce leaves and dip it. What fun that was. A first for me.

Been here twice so far... First time for lunch buffet and it was great. My favorite so far.. Everything was fresh and delicious... My second time I went for dinner and I had my favorite lamb tikka masala.. Delicious.. The drinks were great as well.. This place opened at 6pm and it was packed already.. Everything is super fresh and very tasty.. Best indian food for me so far!!
indian food was really delicious.tendoori chicken was very good.my friends love this place.

Traveling again and hit up yelp for some good local fair. Based on reviews, I tried urban spice. Place was moderately busy when I arrived and prob had 50 or so customers before I left. This was not an issue as the place is big with plenty of servers. The host/waiter was engaging and helpful as I wanted to stray outside my standard main courses (tikki masala, vindaloo, saag...,) after some good questions, he recommended the Kashmiri Gosht Rogan Josh. It was very good, just a little dry and the sauce had some good heat but not overwhelming. Portions were huge and they had Kingfisher, always a plus. Staff was excellent. Had the lamb been more moist, five stars. Would def recommend.

Let me start by saying ambience is fantastic. I've seen some dive Indian joints but this is not among them. Well decorated and lively atmosphere. I came here for lunch buffet and was pleasantly surprised. They had an awesome salad bar and many of the standard lunch items. My only issue was the chicken Masada was a bit dried out. Otherwise, great value and variety. Am interested in coming back again for sure.

I don't know what self respecting establishment would be understaffed during a Friday night dinner service at peak hours.  Our party of 9 had reservations made for  6:45 PM. We placed our orders at 7:00 PM, but did not receive our appetizers until approximately 8:30 PM. Who knew that pouring salt, I MEAN, soup into a bowl took that long? We were there for a total of 3 hours, spending 80% of our time waiting...  AND it was not like there were a lot of people. Each of us made our selection for our three course meal from the prix fixe menu, priced at $30 per person. A deal you may think to yourself as you review the list; however, you should STOP and save yourself from the treacherous experience and long wait. (If you're on the way there now, turn around!!!! You'll thank me later.) Four people from our party (including myself) ordered the filet mignon medium well. We could not fathom the reasoning behind the inconsistency in each of our steaks. The side of spinach (or swamp goop)  tasted like I swallowed an entire pepper shaker. For dessert, I chose the chocolate "lava" cake which was more like an overcooked chocolate cookie. It was a mystery to all of us where the "lava" went. As previously mentioned by other reviewers, the owner was more concerned about his scarf rather than the satisfaction of his customers. He came to our table and asked our opinion regarding the service. We were all honest about how the food lacked quality in preparation and taste, but he was in disbelief and stated that WE probably did not order the steak correctly...  He can be in denial all he wants if his ultimate  plan is to lose his business. To sum it up: FOOD - 0 (Poor in quality unless your preference is burnt and salty.) ENVIRONMENT - 0  (Perhaps dark so you can't see other people's face of disgust or the piece of HAIR served with your steak.) SERVICE - 0 (I don't think I really have to explain myself again.)

Officially the worst place I have ever been to.  I have eaten in third world countries with better service and food then this place.  Oh wait this would mean my food would have come out after 2 hours but it didn't!!! There was one bartender, one waiter for 12 tables and 1 person in the kitchen!! Are your seriously running a business with 3 people? And the kicker the owner was waking around with a scarf doing absolutely nothing.  Not helping the staff, not taking orders, he was sitting at the bar.  When we confronted him he made excuses and walked away.  We literally waited over 2 hours to be served and gave up and left.  Never have I ever left a restaurant due to poor service and lack of getting good but I can add that to my list.  So sad. If I could give it negative stars I would.  Someone please come close this business cause it is simply unacceptable to treat paying customers and staff like this.

1star is too much. This is by far the worst place I have ever been too. Do not waste your money. 2 hours and we still didn't get an appetizer. Only 1 staff and the owner was walking around  with a scarf and not working. Served water with algae and dirt floating in it. They messed up. 8 guys and would have easily sent a few hundred on alcohol.

A poor excuse for a steak house and even a restaurant . I wonder how this place is still open. I actually took my mother here for mother's day for convenience. It was a waste of money. Food was horrible, service was poor , and the cooks walked through the dining room like it was the kitchen. The menu is set up like a big time steak house but the food comes no where close . Just a warning for restaurant week ... stay clear of this establishment.
