I came here during restaurant week. Great service, great wine, and the food was on point! The hanger steak and potatoes was bangin and I'm usually not a fan of steak. Unfortunately it's a little far from where I'm located but if I'm ever near that area again I'd def come back. The waiter who I'm assuming is the owner was mad cool :)

Truffle tater tots? Bacon roasted fingerling potatoes? Sweet potato fries? Max's -- you had me at truffle. What better way to decompress after a most hellish work week than a beer and some good food in the heart of Hartford, CT. The service was excellent, the setting chic, and the menu filled with appealingly delectable choices. Steaks for my compatriots and the chicken for me (paired with pine nuts, squash, tomatoes and chickpeas) -- the food was definitely a highlight of the evening. The beer was a bit of a let down (boo for too hoppy pumpkin ales), and the bread was hard as rock (which was incredibly disappointing in light of the amazing butter it had been served with); however, overall, this place was well worth a try.

As a vegetarian, I don't eat sushi much, but I couldn't pass up a vegan sushi restaurant! I got the spicy mang, and while it was definitely good, it was not spicy. I will be back to try their other options soon.

Vegan or not, you should definitely give these guys a shot.  Their rolls are fantastic, all the ingredients are fresh and bursting with flavor!  The Mighty Mushroom roll was fantastic, as well as their Spicy Mang roll (which apparently is their most popular roll).  Be sure to ask about their monthly special!  Their salads and rice paper wraps also looked very good, but I haven't tried them yet. They also have freshly made juices with no additional sugar.  I've had their watermelon mint lemonade (very nice on a hot summer day) and their blueberry lemonade (which is perfectly tart and has some blueberry pieces in it). I highly recommend this place to anybody looking for something a little bit different.  It is a cozy, but not cramped, place on a relatively quiet piece of 14th St.  A cute place to bring a date for lunch. Last time I went, I met Guy, the owner and executive chef.  We discussed how he got started, and what some of his ideas for the future were.  The man definitely focuses on quality.  They are 100% vegan now, but when they first opened a few items were not vegan.  I asked about what the non-vegan ingredients were, and Guy explained how he used to make his own mayo for some of the rolls' sauces, but with the move toward a 100% vegan menu he experimented with several different types of tofu before finding a good substitute for egg in the mayo.  A little bit of obsessive perfectionism is a great trait in a chef, and I hope this review has convinced you to patronize this restaurant so that they can stay in business and maybe open a location in HK so that I won't have to venture so far!

So I'm a hardcore meat-eater, and was therefore rather skeptical of this place. But my friend swore by it and so one day I went with him. I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised. The sushi looks better than most modern day art, I mean really I felt bad eating it because it was just so pleasing to look at. As for the taste, I've had the spicy mang and the green machine roll; I loved spicy mang! The toasted cayenne sauce is so unbelievable and contributes to the awesome concoction. The green machine was pretty darn tasty as well. My main thing was that maybe its too greeny tasting? I should also mention that this is the first time in my life that I did not use soy sauce on my sushi. This was a small revelation; is soy sauce like the hot sauce of chinese food? Have I been using it all these years to make up for the fact that all sushi I've ever tried tasted exactly the same? As I pondered that, I slowly chewed and enjoyed every second of this unbelievable sushi, and was just so happy. I even felt good after the meal! Also, the venue, though incredibly small, was really thought out and was just very esthetically pleasing. Overall, an experience I will probably repeat tomorrow!

Chris and I enjoyed a lovely meal here this evening, with two delicious drinks (cucumber lemonade and peach..with thyme? basil? sorry!) . I'm usually a huge meat lover or a raw fish addict, but this place is AMAZING! First of all the staff is amazing, very friendly, personable and happy! It is so rare to see happy people who work in this business, and I enjoy having a smile served with my food :) The rolls are like art pieces, very delicate and the flavors explode in your mouth satisfying every inch of your taste bud. For the price, the craftsmanship and the ingredients I will definitely be a regular.   (what a perfect way to help me transition to NYC from Philly)

Let's cut to the chase: I love my meat, but if I could eat at Beyond Sushi everyday, I think I can go vegetarian for at least three months. I had the green machine roll and it was heaven in my mouth. I love textures and color in my food. The cucumber and asparagus added a satisfying crunch. The jalapeno wasabi sauce added the right amount of kick and really highlighted the flavors of the veggies. We also had the pleasure of meeting Guy Vaknin, who was extremely personable. Will definitely be back for more! Tip: NYU students also get 10% off. :)

It's all been said. This place is awesome. Best vegetarian sushi I've ever had and amazing presentation. Even the omnivore boyfriend loved it. The Sweet Tree is my favorite. Just a tip: This is more of a to go place. Counter service and only 3 tables for sit down.

The spicy shroom is delicious. Had a couple of rolls too - beautifully presented, but seriously lacking in flavor. The menu makes promises that the food just doesn't fully deliver. Might go back - but not as impressed as some of the reviewers here.

I NEVER write reviews, so this is saying something. First off, before my friends and I even got our sushi, the girl behind the counter was SUPER nice and gave us the student discount even though we weren't NYU students and we already used our scoutmob coupons. I felt bad that I didn't leave a tip on my card when I first paid because even the service was great! But I will definitely tip the following times I come back! Anyway, so I had the spicy mang and the la fiesta, which were both deeelish!! I tried my friend's sweet tree roll, which was also yummy (i will have to order that next time!). I also tried a piece of the mighty mushroom, which I was contemplating on getting, but glad I didn't because I wasn't too crazy about it. My friends really enjoyed it though. Next time I really wanna try their wraps, particularly the nutty buddy, and the fresh lemonade!! So far, I'm sold! Props to Chef Guy and the amazing staff as well!
Really great addition to the neighborhood although it can get packed. Great atmosphere.

Yeah, this place is not improving with more time open -- for my third visit I went at 7pm on a Monday, the first bartender seemed to lose patience as soon as I asked to see a menu and walked away. I waited a while and then watched as the second bartender filled one of the 14 oz mugs three-quarters full and handed it to me. Too big, overpriced and poorly run so far, but unfortunately, this is the norm for new places in this neighborhood. Radegast crushes this place.

After a sumptuous dinner with his family, Mike and I decided to have a romantic drink or two at Hamilton's.  We had passed by many times before but had never been inside.  The space itself was cozy and dimly-lit with a mermaid motif, so I was instantly enchanted.  I love mermaids. The food looked delicious so we'll have to make another trip there to try the gastropub-like fare.  Mike drank craft beers while I had a delightful riesling.  My wine was comped by our waitress who was wearing an adorable sweater with Laurel and Hardy on it, as I found her missing iPhone in the bathroom.   I would happily return next time we are in the neighborhood.  It was my kind of place and it's always fun to go to cute, neighborhood-y establishments.

Our son recommended this restaurant and it is simply great.  The grilled cheese and tomatoes was delish and my husband had an omelette which he said was equally delish.  The restaurant had a nice European feel.  Coffee was good, and the service very pleasant.  It's a nice local place.

Hamilton's was a pleasant surprise. I have been here a couple of times and haven't had a bad experience. I was excited when I first saw that not only a new restaurant was coming to Windsor Terrace- but also a place to get some drinks! Usually I would have to go to Park Slope or take the walk to Shenanigans but now Hamilton's has saved me from that. The soju cocktails are delicious though a bit pricey (soju is supposed to be a cheap liquor). I am a sucker for the Amante which is jalapeno soju, cilantro, lime and honey. They also have a great selection of beer and wine. The food was also good. I typically go for the Orzo Pasta or Mussels and the Grilled Squid with tapenade. If you just want to drink and maybe pick at a little something I would suggest the Truffle-Cheddar Pretzel. So good! I've only had great service here and considering the neighborhood doesn't offer too much, I'd say this is just as great as any Park Slope or Cobble Hill establishment. Definitely recommend!

Literally stumbled onto this spot after a great East Village brunch and bar crawl.  It's sleek, dark and sexy.  Perfect place to have a discreet cocktail.  The bartender greets you with a menu and chalk.  The walls are devoted to patrons writing down their confessions.  We only stayed for one drink (honestly couldn't drink anymore after the afternoon I had lol), but it was a GREAT cocktail.  Will definitely be back to do a full on tasting, and a better, more comprehensive review.

Stopped by late on a Saturday night over the weekend to eat at the bar. Great ambiance-very relaxed, somewhat sophisticated vibe with modern decor. The bartenders were great and you could tell they take their time when making the drinks with care, which is nice to see because it's a rare sight. They had an array of different liquor but the wine menu was very small. I'm not sure why they call it "new american" as there weren't many choices that would be classified as that. The menu was too eclectic for my taste so I stuck with the chicken entree. It was $22 for 4 tiny bites of chicken which were wrapped in the skin, accompanied by 2 half pieces of white asparagus and 3 tiny potatoes. The asparagus was great, the chicken was not. It seemed undercooked and it wasnt too warm when served. I think it took me all of 4 bites to finish the dish...although I didn't eat all of the chicken. The portions were incredibly small and don't justify the high prices. I won't be eating here again but may stop by the bar for a drink.

Loved the Treemont, atmosphere was great. Server was very knowledgeable and did an excellent job. The food was outstanding and the presentation was perfect. I will definitely be returning. Highly recommend it!

A Philly gem! Dined with friends last evening at The Treemont. We first shared a few small plates...highly recommend the delicious Cherrystone clam ceviche and perfectly prepared Day Boat scallops and Foie Gras. Beef short rib entree was melt in your mouth tender. Don't miss finishing with the Sour cream panna cotta for dessert. Will be back!

Since my first visit (about 14 years ago) this restaurant became one of my family's favorite places. I watched them through the years expending to the left wing and  right wing a few years later, and adding French menu. Than going back to just Thai menu. My kid's favorite of all times was/is Pad Thai. We've brought there friends. We've celebrated there our milestones and we've been eating there every Friday night, sometimes for months. By my opinion their best dishes are: Chicken Satay-intoxicating and deep taste Spring Rolls-small, always cooked to perfection accompanied by intriguing dipping sauce Thai Dumplings-slightly larger than average portions Thai Salad-large portion with peanut sauce, always super fresh Green Papaya Salad-zesty and refreshing Pad Thai-simple and delicious Lard Na-I always order it with the choice of shrimp (tastes better than other choices) Flat Rice Noodles-again with shrimp it tastes better Saute Cashew Nuts-Shrimp or chicken are best choices Mushroom Soup-a bowl of clear soup with mushrooms. It tastes very light and pleasant, but I do not see it in their menu lately. Pan Fried Shrimp-one of chef's specials (might be sometimes too spicy) Fried Red Snapper-Whole fish, very crusty and zesty. It leaves long gingery aftertaste after meal is gone. Vegetarians can have a real fest too with Saute Ginger Vegetables Their Grand Marinier Souffle is a heaven to remember for a long time. Even watching how they pour the chocolate in to the the hole in the middle of souffle and then overflowing is one of a kind experience... ALL desserts are great (if one has any room left at the end of the meal). They also serve Thai iced tea, but I think it is out of the can. Tastes good, though. Once (only once ) I tried frog's legs-unusual strange taste. I got sick after that. May be it was in my head... Ambiance is very pleasant. It used to be more simple with the portraits of the royalty and some art before the renovation. After the renovation it has become much fancier with pretentious Thai art. Since moving out of Montclair a few years ago I switched to take out and it was always good. I highly recommend this place for almost any occasion, but keep in mind-it gets really loud when restaurant is packed.

When a restaurant has the word Yak to describe it, you would assume that there would be more yak dishes to choose from. I was kind of disappointed that there was only 3 dishes that contained yak in it out of the whole menu, the yak momo, the yak tongue (Cheley), and sauteed yak slices (Shapta). We had a groupon and they said that the yak slices were not included in the deal (even though we offered to pay the difference) and they were out of tongue for the day. So we settled for the yak momo's. Yak Momo ($12.95) - Tibetan dumplings that is similar to a Chinese Xiao Long Bao. Inside was seasoned yak meat which was strong in ginger and cilantro taste and the best part was the bit of soup that gushed out when bitten into. The dumpling skin was a little thick and almost bun like. Eating this, you would have thought it was beef. (8/10) yelp.com/biz_photos/hima… Gyuma ($9.95) - A sausage filled with beef blood and ground beef. At first look it might seem a little gross. That's the thought I had when I laid eyes on this dark matter. Taste wise, it wasn't as bold as it looked as it was lacking seasoning but it did have a bloody taste. It was very burger like. When out of the casing, the meat fell apart. (6.5/10) yelp.com/biz_photos/hima… Goat Thali ($12.95) - This was more like a sampler platter of condiments than an entree. The thali only had one small cup of goat meat curry. The other 3 cups consisted of a rice pudding, a chili like dip, and another kind of bean dip. Also they give you some rice and a small piece of crispy bread. Overall not much to eat but you get to try out a palate of flavors. (8/10) yelp.com/biz_photos/hima… This was my first time eating yak not in jerky form and I kind of expected more from it. Maybe I would have enjoyed it more if it wasn't grounded. I did enjoy this cuisine as the food had influences and flavors from cuisines all over Asia. But in the end, it just wasn't something I wanted to have seconds of.

My husband and I live nearby and passed this place a million times without ever thinking of going in.  We purchased a groupon to try it out and it was AMAZING!  Great food, very friendly servers- they did not treat us differently because we had a groupon which sometimes happens.  We will be going back because there is so much on the menu that we have yet to try!  I highly recommend the noodle soups and the friend chicken app...delicious!
The food was great, impeccable atmosphere and service. Very reasonable prices. We really enjoyed watching videos of their homeland on wall mounted TVs . Will come again.

Loved this place and went with hubby for the v-day dinner. Maybe because it was valentine's day and lots customers lured in with groupons, including us, the service was very slow. We waited a very long time to order, and get any food. My suggestion is that they could serve customers some small appetizers to tide us over. Having said that, all the dishes we had were delicious and filling. We got the red snapper, goat with buckwheat, and some assortment on a plate I forgot the name. The videos they played on the big screen were very interesting and showcasing the typically TIbetan life. I learned a lot although I backpacked in Tibet for two weeks years ago.  I definitely recommend checking this place out. All the waiters are very friendly.

If you like Himalayan food, this is the place to go!  Covers himalayan, nepalise, tibetean and indian cuisine as well. Decent ambiance for the area, live music on certain days (really enjoyable), good for families too. The TVs are strategically placed and loop videos of Yaks, their journey thru the Himalayas, and the life they lead.  Again, entertaining. The butter tea was not at all as I imagined. Not delicious in any way, however that was made up for by the meal. Momos are great, the potato and vegetable Himalayan dish was sublime. Overall it's a great place to go on an adventure with a group. Order a bit of everything and enjoy! Plus you'll learn all about the daily lives of Yaks.

A few friends and I met here last night to enjoy flatbread.  We have visited the one in Burlington, VT last year and as such we were very excited to visit this restaurant.  The food and service were absolutely AMAZING!  We ordered a two salads (Evolution Salad and American Flatbread Caesar) and shared them family style.   The table was cleared and we went on to the flatbread. We decided on a small special of the day (chicken and pesto), Medicine Wheel (small), New Vermont Sausage (large) and Pepperoni & Peppers (large.)  Everyone at the table tasted everything and gave solid reviews.  The availability of gluten-free items was important and the Medicine Wheel met the need.  I think the next time we go back we will try making our own flatbread. Quite an extensive beer and wine list including cider (I do not drink beer so wine and cider are very important to me.) Dessert we had the brownie and two locally made ice creams (vanilla and coffee.)  Absolutely delish.   We did not have a chance to sit at the bar but it looked pretty busy and there was a sitting area with ultra comfy chairs to sit in.   I would recommend this for a date night as well as a place for families.   Needless to say I will be back there soon with my appetite.

Nommy! this is the reason why from now on, I will make all my doctor appointments located around Grand Central during lunch -- so I can pick this up on my way back to the office. $13.50 for a large sized Italian "bento-box" with 1 pasta, 1 meat, & 1 veggie. Comes with a drink and bread. Menu changes daily (updated on website), but if you're lucky you may get to try the baked tagiolini with ham... DELICIOUS!

Somewhere between 3 and 4 stars. Baseline: Kati Roll Company in NYC. My favorite there is the Unda Aloo, which is egg and potato in a kati roll. Spice End does a decent job, but the rolls are not quite as good as the place in NYC. The price is about the same as the one in NYC ... except this is Philly. In NYC these prices would be good; in Philly, they are a bit on the high end. One area in which they are lacking is the potato roll. What really makes the potato roll sing is when there's a layer of egg, which costs an extra $1. The chicken tikka roll isn't bad, but it isn't anything special. Bonus: they deliver, and they're open really late (3am or 4am many nights).

very good authentic kati rolls. This is the kind of restaurant that i had been luking for a very long time and found it finally. They have really good quality and authentic kathi rolls. The closest u will get to the ones found on the streets of india.
Poor crowd. Poor management. The food is a copy of the NYC food carts. And it is more expensive than NYC. Lack of seating space. The hot sauce is watered down version of Sriracha.

I ordered the quesadillas.  They were so-so.  Some of the other food looked really good, so I regret having not ordered something else.  The service was good.  The crowd there kind of reminded me of a suburban, mid-range country club, but maybe that's because it was early and there was a sports event on the television.

wow what a find!! wanted a place to have a light meal before going to the theatre. the atmosphere was lively, filled with after-work groups, the wait service quite attentive, BUT the FOOD!!! was the BIG HIT!! having only 45 min., we ordered the bruchetta(yum yum) toasted just right and ooh th goat cheese amid the fresh tomatoes was... well let's i almost hated to share it. then came the "lollipops". they did not skimp out on the meat and oooh wow these i would if i could have everyday..i'd tell you more about them but you have to go enjoy these for yourself. wish this place was in my hometown...you lucky phillie-ites!

What a strange but good place.  I heard about this restaurant solely from Yelp and I definitely would not have found it without it.  Blue Cat is in the back of what appeared to be a closed strip mall.   The interior is charming and romantic.  Our server was great and they have a good wine list.  Everything we had was good also.  My husband got a steak and I got the kafta kabob (randomly enough).  Both entrees were very good, albeit fairly small.  I also thought the hummus and bread to start was a nice touch. I'm not sure I would come back here and I'm not sure why.  There was something slightly off putting about the fact that it was in a deserted strip mall.  It was just a really weird place.  But it was definitely tasty.

My wife and I drove 75 miles to Burlington to a Diana Krall concert at the Flynn Theater, which is very close to this restaurant. I Yelped the area to find a spot for some dinner before the show. Long story short, the Blue Cat was good and bad. The Good: The food was great. Steak and rack of lamb perfectly prepared, great pita and warm hummus, nice Caesar salad, good wine list (a really good Malbec was a hit.) We liked the ambiance, the intimacy and though we sat at the bar, were comfortable and happy. The Bad: We sat down at 6:15 PM and let the server know that we were going to a 7:30 show. We ordered shortly thereafter. at about 6:45, we got the salad. At 7:15, we got our entrees. So - we gulped our delicious and expensive dinners, took some home in a box, and went to the show. Mitigating Factors: We noticed when we were seated that a large party was just ordering when we came in. A small alarm went off in my head, but I thought that an hour would be plenty of time. I was wrong. There was only one stressed-out server, and the kitchen, which is partially visible from the bar displayed no sense of urgency whatsoever. Then I got a bill for close to $100. Conclusion: Mitigating factors or not, not a great experience. For the kind of money being charged, I expected more professionalism, better preparation and faster/better service, even though the food was good. I might go back, but probably not. There are too many other choices within walking distance of the Flynn.

Quick summary, the food here is fine though not exceptional. The price is quite exceptional and the service was very lacking. This restaurant is thinly staffed. This is obvious from entering as there is no host desk. I approached the bar to get a seat. We were seated quickly without issue. The problems started immediately. I think there was probably one waitress staffing the 7 tables available on this Wednesday night. We weren't greeted by the waitress for 5 or more minutes. All of the various procedural elements were late. Drinks, water, bread, entree, etc., were all very late. The Blue Cat's 'bread' offering is a few slices of pita and hummus. Good but skimpy and very late on arrival. Food service was slow. They were out of two of our requests. When food arrived, it didn't include the alteration I had requested (double asparagus, no potatoes). For 29 dollars, I received a good but not exceptional 6 oz steak. I also got the 15 dollar foie gras which was the size of a small cookie. All in all, not worth the cost. Their dessert menu is amazingly skimpy and not worth the wait. Waiting for dessert took especially long. We had the blueberry pie and it was small and the crust is questionable at best. I'm sure you can do better in burlington.

My husband and I also came here for Restaurant Week 2013. Had high hopes, as we've always seen outstanding reviews. I'm not going to talk about the food...it was delicious! What I will share is what the experience was around the food, because I feel that when you're in an expensive restaurant, that is something that should NOT be overlooked. The first thing you'll notice is no table linens...well, ok I say to myself, no big deal. Next, when the friendly waiter asked for our drink order, the two craft beers my husband asked for were out. Okay, so he orders from what they have on hand. I order a glass of prosecco, and we decide on tap water. (hint: this is the wrong choice) Another waitress comes back with two glasses and room-temperature water in an old bottle. No ice. My husband just looks at it and says, "Could they have made it any more obvious that they just ran this under the faucet? We ask for a glass of ice, so again, no big deal. We order our appetizers, and they're delicious. As the waitress takes our empty plates, she puts our food-encrusted silverware back on the bare table. I was pretty surprised at that one. We then wait about 40 minutes for our entrees. Obviously, the service is unpredictable. Now keep in mind, there's no bread served at the table, so while you're waiting, you've got nothing to nosh on. And you're getting pretty hungry seeing and smelling everyone else's food go by. We're by the window...wouldn't it be nice if the view didn't look like Route 22 Springfield with all the car lots? Anyway, it's almost comedic when the food did arrive, and my petit filet is about an inch wide and four inches long. Seriously, this could be a scene from a movie! Well, in all fairness, there was an extremely artistic mashed potatoe swirl alongside the steak. It was at least a hearty tablespoonful, so what the heck am I complaining about? Again, no complaints about the flavor or quality of the food. We receive our dessert rather quickly; my banana bread pudding was okay, my husband said his berry tart was overly tart. So, at this point, I'm noticing how really warm it is in the restaurant. I ask the server about that. He says rather amusingly, "If you think it's hot out here, you should see what the kitchen feels like!".  So glad that we cleared that up...BTW, I work with A/C contractors, and I can say w/o a doubt that this equipment was incorrectly sized for the room. There's no reason for a restaurant with modern comfort equipment to feel as uncomfortable as this did. The price fixe dinner is 30. pp; the restaurant charges a 20% gratuity automatically. With our drinks, and gratuity the bill came to $97. for the two of us. I handed the waiter my credit card; on the non-itemized receipt that came back, there was the $97 charge and below that a line that read TIP: and a straight line next to it to add to the total. I did call the waitress over, just to verify I wasn't going crazy, that I had already paid the tip. She said, rather absentmindedly, "Oh yeah, the machine is doing that. I don't know why", and walked away.  So she's aware of it, yet says nothing when she brings the check?  I think almost everyone out there can relate to this: I know several years ago, my father tipped twice at an expensive family dinner in Manhattan, because this exact same thing happened, and he had been drinking. We always had a bad feeling about that restaurant because of that, and never returned there. So all I can say is that I'm glad we only spent $100 on our dinner. If we had spent twice that (which would be the norm here) I think I really would have been upset. And for the chef/owner: at a minimum, don't you think your customers deserve to be comfortable, and to get fresh silverware between courses? Or is this experience only about you and your food...

I just love this place.  Excellent food.....probably one of the best I've eaten in in NJ.  The cauliflower soup was fabulous!!!  Veal meatballs not to be missed.  A must on any foodie's list.  Just go.....

Good food, excellent service....everyone who works here is warm and friendly. We had the red snapper which was pretty good....I also appreciated the brown rice that came with the entree. We will certainly go back.

A new amazing ,healthy,reasonably priced restaurant. The atmosphere is calming, it's beautiful and tastefully decorated. The staff are sweet as pie. On to the food... Seasoned with love, just enough and the Caribbean influence on the food items make these healthy dishes quite tasty! The stuffed avocado paired with a paradise smoothie is an amazing combo. The hummus is to die for. All around the food is absolutely amazing! A perfect place for vegans and non vegans alike.

Best wine bar/ food/atmosphere in Brooklyn. Adds so much to the fine dining Experiences in Ditmas Park. I love their creative approach to the food they create. I am also glad they added cocktails to the menu. Great addition to an already extensive wine and beer selection.

I love this place. Hard not to like any restaurant that took the place of a shoe repair. But that's not why I like it. I actually like it, for itself. Because it's awesome. The service is my favorite kind, the kind where they make you feel like you're in their home and they're your friends who are bringing food to you. I'm always a fan of a place where servers and bartenders can wear what they like -  as they would if this what their home. That being said, the food is usually fantastic, great place to come with a date or a friend and order a couple apps, some small plates which can be cheese, charcuterie, crostinis, olives, etc. (5 for $30). The music is appropriate and the ambiance is always perfect, combination of cozy, rustic and chic. The mussels I had last night however were just...bad. Very bad. They were tough, not very fresh tasting and way too powerful. Every mouthful felt like drinking seawater...overall bad. I'd give it 5 stars if not for the mussels incident and if the wine selection was slightly larger, but it's still a favorite of mine!

Greek Taverna is a great place if you want to taste authentic greek food. Service is very quick and friendly even when the place is stuffed, and most importantly the food is absolutely amazing. I recommend the melted saganaki cheese for appetizer, chicken gyro with pita for a main dish and kadaif for dessert. I don't mind some noise, it makes the place feel lively and more friendly. In general, the food is wonderful and the service is cool, so I will definetely make many return trips again in the future..

We stop there for late lunch on Saturday. The place was empty but we have very good experience. The staff was pleasant and always willing to help. We ordered Gigantes (Giant Lima Beans) and Grilled calamari for appetizer. Both dishes were very good. As main dishes we ordered Gyro platter and Gyro salad. Not complain everything were very good. The portions were big too. Very good food, very good service.

My boyfriend says mediocre at best for standard american chinese food. I was a little disappointed that the General Tso's chicken didn't come with any broccoli. The portions are magnanumus!! The sauces we were served were okay. Overall the experience was decent and we'll go back, believing that every restaurant (take out or not) deserves three tries...We were told twice to try the ginger beef with string beans. That's the next attempt!

A really fantastic new entry to the Winooski dining scene. It is a tiny space but clean and bright, and the staff are super friendly and helpful. I got the Combo Plate: Kung Pao Shrimp with rice (white or pork fried) and choice of appetizer (I got Crab Rangoon). The dish was nice and hot and chock full off fresh celery, carrots, shrimp and peanuts. The rice portion was wayyyyy too much, but it was good. Three huge Crab Rangoon were included, all for about seven bucks. Can't wait to go back and try something else!

This place absolutely sucked I was very unhappy with the service my waitress was awful, the ribs awful,I don't understand why they get such a good rating for the ribs but they were not tender it will hard. I will never step foot in this place again the only reason why I gave it two stars because I like the tiff in Morris Plains they have good ribs and good service

This place is great. NFL Sunday Ticket. 2 for 1 rack of ribs on Tuesdays. The food is good and the beers are plenty. We absolutely LOVE the corn bread they bring out beforehand. Wife gets soups often and sagebrush are good. I have had burgers, buffalo wrap (excellent), and ribs and they are all things in would get again, but we moved sadly to where there are no more Tiff's near.

I absolutely LOVE Ploy Siam.  The prices are great, the food is delicious!  I have been to many "fancy" restaurants and I would much rather go here.  It is beautiful inside and the staff is amazing!  I am not big on spicy and you can request no spice all the way to super spicy.  Try this place, it is AMAZING!!!

Tapas; just the thought of them brings a smile to my face. As a trained chef interested in authentic Spanish cuisine you can imagine the level of my excitement and curiosity when I learned that there was a tapas bar about a mile away from where I live. My wife and I first visited on a Friday night, we went there for a later dinner. We walked in and were pleasantly surprised at the Mediterranean style atmosphere in the restaurant. There was a very tasteful dining room with elegant tables and dark hardwood chairs, plus there was a very inviting, relaxed bar area. Originally we were going to be sat in the dining room, but because we had come strictly for the tapas, we asked for the bar area. One glance at the menu and I was taken in; this was authentic Spanish tapas: Chorizo Espanol, Piquillos Rellenos de Cordero, Queso de Cabra... I wanted it all. The bartender was our server and he insisted on offering the nights specials, but we decided to start with just four tapas to give them an opportunity to impress me. We ordered the Spanish piquillos peppers stuffed with lamb and a port Shallot reduction, Herb-encrusted goat cheese over marinara sauce and toasted bread, Steak Tartar and  Medallions of roasted pork tenderloin topped with tetilla cheese and Spanish piquillos pepper sauce. The plating was beautiful, the flavors were amazing and I certainly was impressed. So much that we ordered two more tapas before even staying for dessert. The other thing that really impressed me was the level of personal attention that you got from the wait staff. It was so much more than the usual "can I help you". At one point a gentleman had come to the table to top off our wine (without having to ask) and to see if we needed anything else; it turned out to be the owner. By the end of the night we had spent nearly three hours at the Bistro Mediterranean & Tapas Bar. We each had three glasses of wine and we shared six tapas, plus dessert. The bill was very affordable at less than $70. We had an amazing meal, we drank some fantastic wine and we loved it so much we went back the following night for dinner. If you are looking for something outside the box, something simple, something fresh and something delicious, look no further than Bistro Mediterranean & Tapas Bar.
I love love love this place! I think the hubby and I have found our new spot! Service is wonderful, food is delicious, couldn't ask for better in a restaraunt!

Was hoping to try a fun new place for my birthday dinner.  Lesson learned - stick to the favorites.  Some of the dishes showed potential, but for each item we ordered, it just wasn't "right."  The stuffed eggplant, while the sauce was delicious, was rubbery.  The house salad, while the cheese was excellent, the dressing - if there actually was dressing - had zero flavor.  I had the scallop entree, and the scallops were cooked perfectly.  However, instead of risotto per the menu I was served fried risotto cakes which were chewy and slightly greasy.  There was some lobster in the dish, too, but it was rubbery.  The hubby played it safe and ordered fettucine carbonara, but the entire dish was ruined with the heavy flavor of burnt garlic.  Oh, and the service was slow.  On a Monday night. To be fair, the staff was friendly and seemed eager to please.  The complimentary olives and bread were yummy.  The wine ordered by the glass was a generous pour.  Too bad the rest of the meal was sub-par.

This was the best Mexican food I have had in NJ. The owners were great, they stayed open for us after they had just closed. If you ask they will cook everything traditional Mexican style, try the tacos al pastor Mexican style they are made with pineapple just like ones in Mexico City, really real and traditional Mexican, you just have to ask.

*Belgian waffle (I loved the texture of this waffle; it was chewy and fluffy and had a great consistency to it. Some Belgian waffles are too airy and crisp, but this one had substance. Honestly didn't need syrup) *bruschetta omelette (bruschetta, pesto sauce and mozzarella cheese with egg whites and spinach; I loved this!! it was like pizza in an omelette form. the pesto gave this omelette a nice speckled green color; flavors were light and not overpowering; I wish the cheese melted better and was better distributed inside the omelette) *turkey omelette (hearty and comforting; perfectly salted; homefries were pretty good flavor but some of the potatoes were undercooked so they need to watch out for that) This restaurant is a small, cute and cozy place for breakfast and brunch. It's BYOB so make sure to bring your booze. Service is good and attentive. We had to wait 25 minutes for a table on a Sunday morning, so expect a wait on the weekends. The wait is worth it!

I was blown away by this place. They offer a 3 course pre-fixe menu Tuesday-Thursday nights for $39.99, so we went here just for that. The only downfall to that route is you have to sit in the piano room or at the bar. They don't offer the pre-fixe in the main dining room, but depending on where you sit in the piano room or at the bar, you can still get a pretty decent view of the NYC skyline. To start, we went with the baby arugula with dried cranberries, candied pecans, Vermont goat cheese, and maple-balsamic vinaigrette and the soup of heirloom squash and gala apples, infused with cinnamon. Both were really good. I loved the bisque-like consistency of the soup, but the salad could have used a little more goat cheese. For the mains, we went with the grilled salmon with parmesan risotto and lobster sauce. The portion didn't look all that generous, but it was filling. The duck and truffle ravioli with wild mushrooms, diced celery root, carrots and black truffle sauce was banging. Super fresh. For the pre-fixe dessert, they let you pick whatever you want from the regular dessert menu, which has at least 10 options on it. I really wanted the "Grand Chocolate Voila" (Banana Ice Cream, Caramel Bananas, Chocolate, Hot Banana Anglaise Sauce), but having already eaten two bananas and a bunch of chocolate during the day, we went with the mango panna cotta and the orange sake crème brûlée instead. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised by the portions at this place. I was expecting to taste each course and to leave on an empty stomach. But for $40, you get your money's worth. Maria was an outstanding server. At one point, we couldn't decide between two glasses of wine, so she brought both to taste. Definitely an ideal spot for special occasions. If you're getting married and balling out, this is the place to have your reception. My only complaint about this place is the confusion of getting seated. We approached a woman sitting down just as we walked in and told her we had a reservation in the piano room. Rather than taking us there, she pointed to the room. It turns out we were supposed to see the host standing before the main dining room, but she didn't tell us that. So other than looking like idiots for a hot minute, all else was good. I guess the finger pointing and misdirection is not something I expected from a place such as this. Other: -Optional valet parking. -Jackets required for dudes.

Great service with a breath taking view of the New York City skyline. This is a great restaurant from an intimate dinner date to even a small dinner-birthday party. The steak was perfectly cooked and paired with a delicious fresh garlic mashed potato side. I highly recommend this restaurant and also suggest you call ahead and request a table against the large windows in order to appreciate the view.

Special occasion dinner on a budget! As soon as you walk in, there is nothing left to do than to admire the ambiance. The chandelier at the entrance, the decor on the walls, the display of cheeses, wines and desserts were all very exciting. When I walked into the piano room all I saw was a pretty view of the NYC skyline and a smile cracked on my face but I as turned my head to the left , I noticed there was no one playing the piano in the piano room ! Bummer. Our lovely server , Maria , introduced herself and  started the evening with our cocktail orders. I had a Cosmo and my significant other had Manhattan. Pretty standard. No problem here. Moving to the main event - eating! Because this was a pre-fixe dinner I order the following in order: Arugula salad, grilled salmon and orange sake creme brûlée. I enjoyed each and every dish. The grilled salmon was slightly pink but still edible. I thought Parmesan risotto in lobster sauce was a perfect match. It wasn't too heavy to digest. When it came to the arugula salad, it had cranberries, Vermont goat cheese with a balsamic vinaigrette but the special touch were the those candied pecans! It was sweet and rich! The buttery- cinnamon and sugar glaze made the boring arugula salad into an exciting salad! I am going to make this at home, one day! Now dessert, anytime I see crème brûlée on the menu I hate to skip it because of the work involved in making it.  With that said, the orange sake  crème brûlée was was hard to resist and I am glad I ordered it . It was scrumptious! This Orange Crème Brûlée was fresh, rich and delicious. It even had fresh orange slices on the Crème Brûlée as a garnish. And here I was thinking that creme brulee couldn't get any better. Kudos! Another highlight of the night was our server Maria.  She was very professional and pleasant yet unobtrusive. Always had a smile on her face. Why 4 stars? No one playing the piano in the piano room was disappointing.

This is a beautiful and classy looking place.  We had a nice dinner last night but to me there were some flaws.  The seafood appetizer (shared with my husband) was bland and almost watery; at the price of about $22, it was just okay, not a particularly outstanding dish.  The filet mignon, requested cooked pink, was sort of well done on the outside and had a brisket-like taste, not the melt-in-your-mouth feel one wants from a good filet mignon.  Garnishes on all plates were the same: mashed potatoes, haricots verts, and a carrot, nicely done.  The French Pinot Gris we ordered was excellent.  Service was very nice.  At $100. a person, this is a very pricey night out and the food should be a little better than it was.  Just my opinion, obviously, and I would return to Highlawn, but I wouldn't order that seafood appetizer again.
Perhaps my favorite restaurant in NJ Never misses a beat. Wonderful food, wonderful dining room and decor, fantastic staff. Impeccable overall.

My husband took me here for our one year wedding anniversary and it was an amazing night. We were seated by the windows and the views are incredible. We made an early reservation to ensure a great view because we were told we couldn't reserve a table by the windows for a later time. We ordered the Charcuterie Plate and lump crab appetizer which were very good. For dinner we ordered the homemade squid ink spaghetti and 16 ounce 28 day dry-aged sirloin. Both were phenomenal. And to finish off our meal (and ensure a satisfactory food coma), we ordered dessert. My husband got a special with creme brulee and apples with homemade honey and I ordered the chocolate fudge sundae, which was amazingly decadent. The service was lovely, the place was beautiful and the food spectacular. I'm sure we will be back for another special occasion, because while it was expensive, we felt they were fair for the venue.
Good coffee, solid breakfast and lunch choices, and cute ambience.  The food is always tasty and service is always friendly.

OK, this place is just great. Full stop. The atmosphere is really fun and cozy. Great on a cold Fall night. And the food is just delicious. Some of the better Ethiopian I've had. The service is attentive and friendly, and we just had a really nice date night there. Thanks.

I went to Injera a few weeks ago for the first time. Its located on a quiet block behind Abingdon Sq - if you are having trouble finding it google Abingdon Square and just look around. You'll spot it. This is the first Ethiopian place Ive been to where I sat in a fancy chair, was offered cocktails, and hear loud bumpin music. Totally a chic, fancy spot unlike most Ethiopian places I've been to. Despite the weird trappings, it was delicious. The injera was spot on - the vegi combo has a good mix of spicy and flavorful but not too spicy items - my fav was the spicy red lentil lentils for sure. The beets are delicious, so are the potatoes / carrots, as are all the yellow lentils. The combo for two is a fair amount of food for the $$ they charge. Honestly, a good SOLID spot.
Great food, great service

We've been stopping at Baja for over 10 years now for the consistently superb food.  The updated menu has an excellent Baja burger and great fries.   It is the best Mexican food in the area.   (Would have given it 5 stars except that's reserved for the Blue Agave in Pleasanton, CA).

We have been going to Baja's for a few years now and we have found one thing: consistently AMAZING food.  I have read some reviews on here that state that the waitresses don't write things down, that is because they know the menu and what is on it.  So excuuuuuse me if YOU don't know what your little kid ordered.  Read the menu and you will also see when sour cream is NOT included with many of the items.  They ask if you wish for some as MOST people like sour cream with their Mexican food. Anyway, I will get off my soapbox and state one thing.  The food is to die for there.  I will gladly pay $50 for me and my boyfriend to enjoy amazing Mexican food (with leftovers due to the huge portion sizes) and two margaritas, which might I add are the best ones I have had. EVER.   Every winter the place closes for about 6 weeks at which point we go and try other restaurants when we crave that Mexican taste.  Every year we are sorely disappointed and we wait for the minute those doors open again.  We were in there once again tonight and once again, we won't send our friends and loved ones anywhere else.  Nothing in this area beats Baja's.

This is a small hole-in-the-wall  Mexican place right next to a McDonalds that you've probably driven by 20 times. However, their food is pretty good! They have a serve yourself salsa bar with mild and hot salsas and plenty of chips on the table. Before going here, someone commented they don't have bowls and I couldn't think how that mattered until you try scooping up salsa with a chip from a plate...it's hard! I had a bean and cheese burrito for my meal which was relatively inexpensive (compared to some other menu items) but I was surprised it was refried beans mixed with cheese. It tasted good, but I was expecting whole beans, cheese, and possibly a few other ingredients rather than a bean/cheese paste inside.

Went here for lunch with my customers, easy parking, no wait Friday at 130 . I love the salsa bar idea, you have 8 interesting selections ranging from mild to super spicy.  I had cheese enchiladas in a mole, SO yum!!  I don't normally see mole as an option on non-meat dishes so was HAPPY. My lunch cohorts had margs, they looked really good but I had a drive ahead of me. Prices were reasonable, my meal was great. I'd go back.

I love this place!! Great date night place..nice lighting and atmosphere. Small, cozy place, BYO. The staff is great, I've never had a bad experience or bad service. The sushi is so fresh and absolutely delicious. Every specialty roll I've tried has been amazing, even the most interesting flavor combos! My favs: Godzilla, Eternal Sunshine, Pingu. The edmame is perfect, too.

The sushi here was fresh, delicious, and inventive. The customers were really nice- neighborhood folks- all locals- super chill.  Thanks to the next table who let us check out their sushi before we ordered. We got the Godzilla, King Kong, and Ping Pong rolls.  I like the fact that  you can order some rolls that have cucumber wraps with no rice- lighter choice for summer.  Potato crunch in one of the rolls made a great textural change.

Pizza was pretty good but want to mention that the size of the 20 inch pie only consists of 8 regular slices - not sure why the other reviewer said it was so large.  And there certainly could have been more sauce and cheese - had there been I would have given it 4 stars.  Had 2 pies delivered but was disappointed it didn't serve more people.

I ordered from here last night and it was outstanding! I've never had better delivery pizza!  Get the spec and arugula pizza you will not regret it particularly if you get the table 87 salad on the side.
Best pizza I have ever had! Dough was exceptional and am very picky about the thickness/texture and taste of dough. You can't go wrong with any toppings :)

One one the best pizzas I've every had. mushroom and truffle oil pie. Can't wait to go back again. Service was great and very helpful. Great beers on tap. Great looking place with spacious seating but the main reason for the review is amazing food!

Miya's Sushi is more than a restaurant - it's not only one of the friendliest places to visit, it's also where you will find some of the healthiest, most creative, and most delicious food anywhere. Being a regular at Miya's has ruined me for other restaurants. I enjoy a healthy lifestyle, and buy organic, top-of-the-line ingredients to cook at home whenever I can. There are only a handful of restaurants in the Northeast that I trust and love - Miya's is at the top of the list. I always bring out-of-town visitors to Miya's. A friend from DC took one sip of the miso soup, and said, "Oh my God. That's the best miso I've ever had. Oh my God!" I know that when I go there, I will enjoy what is essentially a home-cooked meal. It also happens to be nutrient-rich, sustainable, and unique food cooked and served with love. When you get used to eating food fitting that description, it's easy to sense when other restaurants' offerings don't come close to meeting that standard, and that standard is impossibly high, yet Miya's meets it, and consistently tries to go beyond.  The food there is cutting edge. You don't go to Miya's to get California roll. You go there to eat healthy food that is accessible, delicious and unique. And you'll be eating a lot of stuff that is local. The staff catches some of the seafood. Many of the greens are from Yale Farm. You can't go wrong. Bun and his mom Yoshi care about their product, and they care about their customers. This is not an exaggeration.... the salad there changed my life. I went from feeling obligated to eat salad to craving multiple salads a day. Because it's not practical to eat at Miya's every day, I asked Bun for the recipe. He outlined how to prepare the greens (his mom tears each leafy green into the right size), and how to make the dressing. Now I make it at home and still have it when I go to the restaurant.You won't find a place where the spirit of generosity and caring is as strong. I thank Bun for showing me a different way to eat. Go to Miya's with an open mind. It is one of the most dynamic and original places you will ever experience. You never know, it just might change your life.

Miya's is outstanding!  Not only does it provide excellent food with excellent service but it is also one of the few businesses attempting to align its business with the values of a progressive, just, fun and healthy society!  Just go you'll love it!
Precisely what I don't like about hipsters. It's  good for adventure dinning. I'm surprised the menu doesn't have a myers briggs personality score on each of the things offered.

Love this place! Great concept for a restaurant. A friend brought me knowing I'm not a big sushi person but I'll try anything. I really enjoyed the expierence, the food is creative, the drinks are fun and delicious, dessert is DIVINE! I'm a big dessert person!  Milk and honey roll is great, roll with mushroom and Brie yummy! The best part is the pumkin miso soup, I could eat it all the time!

My family and I are frequent diners at the Country Girl Diner. We LOVE this place. The staff and owner, Kate, are always friendly and inviting, treating locals and out-of-staters with equal hospitality. The atmosphere is a classic diner experience and the food is just amazing. The pancakes are some of, if not, the best I have ever had and they always have some delicious variation like blueberry or strawberry or chocolate chip (great for the kids). My favorite is the V.A.S.T, it is a very filling breakfast served with real VT maple syrup and the coffee is always delicious. My wife loves their waffles and french toast. I highly recommend this place to anyone that I talk to, even though I would love to keep it our little secret, this place deserves as much business as possible. If you have the chance I highly recommend you go.

My wife is loves to go for crab and some of the veggies. There are only a handful of foods that I go for as the rest are typically bad American-Chinese food. Food trays are often empty with an especially long wait for crab and some of the better food. Personally, I find the food at Chef Leu's in Shelburne to be much better.
Good beer from many different countries and really. good buffalo wings.  You can't beat that. I wished the beer were colder and the burgers tastier but this place is solid.

Amazing Food and Great Service! This place is a totally unique experience.  Whether you're interested in authentic South Indian food or a traditional veggie wrap (i recommend #23 - paneer, brie and cucumber, yum!) there is something for everyone here!  So if you're an adventurous eater with a less adventurous dining companion - or having lunch/dinner with a big group, and worried about suiting everyone's tastes (and budget) - this restaurant is absolutely ideal. p.s. Their mango lassi is the best I've ever had  ;o)
Being Southern Indian, its hard to find a good dosa in Philadelphia. These are simply the best dosas I have had in America. Apparently they are opening a couple locations. Super excited.
I will give this place one more try but the potato in my dose was cold.  Maybe baldev should stick with amans in norristown.  I am always disappointed when north Indians try to make a dosa

In Philadelphia there has been a long term dosa deficiency. It was really getting to be a problem to where I would ask Indian strangers on the street hoping they would know where I could find dosa.  Yay!   This place is good and cheap!   They have a ton of vegan an vegetarian options.  Most of the combinations on the menu have cheese (oddly).  I specifically asked if the Dosas were suitable for vegans and he said YES, of course you can leave the cheese off for more authenticity and to suite the vegan in you....  and he went on to tell me that the Grilled veggie 'chicken' may not be, although soy based it also has refined sugars.  Wow-  he knows his stuff! I intend to be back again and again.   yay! yay! yay!  (oh did i mention that it tasted good?)

What can I add to all the superb reviews. Loved the Dosas, Loved the Samosa's, 8 stars for the Vadai,and mouth watering Mango lassi. Sambhar for a $1 is a steal. YESSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS to my new fave, not good at writing but had to do it for splendidly sumptuous meal. Superb prices. Thank you Raveee, the manager for your superb service and my pain in the ass questions.

the great thing about indian food is that even when it's americanized, it's still delicious.  here the dosa, described by our friends as indian crepes, are awesome. the potato masala with veggie "chicken" and spinach dosa was delicious and a nice hint of heat that i wasn't expecting.   the crepe was light and crispy with well seasoned potatoes and "chicken."  they came with a choice of sauces, but mine was so flavorful, i didn't think mine needed much of it.  we also split some mehdu wada which was good and crispy in a sweet and spicy sauce. a definite repeat for a no frills, easy lunch or dinner while in city center.

My girlfriend and I found this restaurant in 2008. We are far from sushi experts but having eaten in no less than 50 sushi restaurants across the US and Asiana House is  in the top 5. The rolls are creative, the fish is fresh and price is fair. It is not a boutique like Oishii in Boston, RA in Scottsdale or Water in Tampa but it provides a clean, casual atmosphere with reliable service and food. We have dinner here at least once each time I come to town (every six weeks) and always leave very happy. They even continue to make a roll for us that was removed from the menu two years ago! For all these reasons I confidently endorse them. They do not take reservations so plan ahead if you are going on a Friday or Saturday night between 6-9pm. PS: remember to tip the sushi chefs.

Just had lunch there, excellent. I have sort do avoided This place, just too many great restaurants and can't go out more than a couple of times a week. We had a bento box, which included chicken teriyaki, tempura, sushi, salad and gyoza, salad and soup (I usually don't have the miso soup, it is just salty warm water, this miso tasted good). Every thing very nicely done, including a sushi boat, wonderful assortment of great sushis. Will go back for sure...

This is my FAVORITE place in hell's kitchen. Every meal here has been nothing less than phenomenal. The wine is fantastic and includes a range of grapes, regions and prices. My favorite dish is the melanzane e caprino although there's not a bad dish on the menu. Meatballs, pear salad, $1 oysters, shrimp and artichoke, charcuterie plate, etc. The service has always been wonderful for me. It is adorably tiny and constantly busy but even so they manage to squeeze me and my boyfriend in with a short wait. It's absolutely worth it to order a glass or bottle and wait for bar/table space for a meal. GO.
Cozy little wine bar. With surprisingly good appetizers. A little pricey. But sometimes it sets just the right kind of mood. Nothing else quite like it in this neighborhood.

Really great food and very reasonable prices! The service was quick and friendly (probably helped that we were just about the only 2 people in there, but still). The portions were large as well! Papaya salad was very well done and the Pad Thai was not heavy at all. Looking forward to trying the rest of their menu. Smaller venue, nothing super fancy, but the food more than makes up for it.

I came here the other day to sit down for dinner, and Barn Joo did not disappoint. I ordered the uni bibimbap and my friend got the duck. The duck was cooked just right - moist, flavorful and juicy. The uni bibimbap was perfectly balanced between all of the items that were in the bowl. There was small bits of kimchi and pickles that gave it a spicy and sour kick and yet not too much so that you couldn't taste the subtle freshness of the uni. Also our waitress was knowledgeable in scotch/whiskey/bourbon and we loved the drinks we got that were suggested by her. Barn Joo is turning out to be one of my new favorite go-to places in the city.

good vibe and food were nice, only the music was too loud for me.  We ordered two drinks, one bimbimbab, one spicy chicken pot with rice, and 1 dozen dollar oysters and the total was only $67! The oysters were very fresh.

*This review is for the bar portion only* - stopped in for an afternoon drink after a morning of shopping on Broadway. Good drink selection - I asked for a Caesar (sorry, Bloody Mary...) and the bartender made a very good one! If we hadn't eaten a while earlier, i would have loved to share a few appetizers in here - the restaurant was beautiful, service was great, and the Bloody Mary was great! (downside, it was $13.) Will definitely go back for food on my next NY visit - the menu board listed some good looking Happy Hour specials!
OMG I LOVE THEIR $1 oysters!!! I always get like 15 and eat them alone LOL. The drinks are strong!!! I only go for happy hour though because their full price menu is not friendly.

Wish we could've tried both the dinner and happy hour menus at the same time but we chose dinner and it was incredible! There were a ton of people there for happy hour, as well, so I look forward to coming back and checking it out. The Ja Chae and the Beef Bibimbap were really really good, and the pumpkin cheesecake was a great way to end the whole dinner :) Awesome looking space and great for both big and small groups, too. Definitely worth checking out if you are in the area and are in the mood for some korean fusion cuisine!

Finally ate here with my partner this evening after wanting to since it opened. Love the decor, love the space (much larger than I anticipated). A bit overpriced and pretentious, but so are most restaurants in NYC. Now let's get into the low rating... First star is gone because of the staff. After being seated, one waiter took our drink orders. A second waiter came back with our drinks, then proceeded to take our food orders. Ordered 3 small plates to share, then one entree each. The waiter then asked "what order would you like these to come out?" I looked at him confused and asked why. He said they serve the food in the order they are completed in the kitchen, and that since I ordered a burger medium-well, it would definitely come out last. I could care less that my entree comes out last (as it should) but I was completely lost as to why I'm being asked what order I want them to come out. Appetizers first, entrees second. Quite the standard practice in most restaurants I've been to. Second star was gone when one of the bus boys started clearing off plates from the appetizers. He grabbed my chopsticks on the wrong end, which were clearly leaning on my plate, and set them aside as if I were going to use it again. No thank you. Third star gone due to the overall idea of the restaurant. I love a good gastropub, but this is overkill. Asian gastropubs should be reflective of the cuisine they are serving in my opinion. Take Jeepney for example. As soon as you walk in you can tell you're in a Filipino restaurant. If I didn't look at the menu before coming to Barn Joo, I'd be totally lost inside this place. Maybe the owners would consider adding some Korean elements to the space. In the end I'm happy I ate here. The food was decent and at least I can say I tried it. In the future, I probably won't come back unless someone else asked me to.

Loved the wheel of fortune! I was bummed that their website bills them as a farm-to-table but the waitress didn't know much about that. Still, everything I ordered was fresh. I've been there twice and would go back - it's also one of the things that's open later around Flatiron. Must-try side dish: The brussels sprouts with barley were amazing (not vegetarian but very amazing).

Chicken thigh wrap, and mashed potatoes :) Place is essentially a take out looking place, though you can eat in. The food is delicious, simple. Pure. Lol hence the name. A great little spot if you want chicken. :)

Came here with Hungry Boy because he told me that everyone been raving about this place. I mean hey, why not, I love chicken anyway. He and everyone was right! The food here are simple, yet very very delicious! We had ordered the chicken burger, which I was skeptical it being too dry. However, that was not the case, the chicken burger was very juicy and flavorful! We've also tried the jalapeno mac and cheese and it was amazing! The mac and cheese was cheesy and the jalapeno taste was just a perfect combination! I would say this is by far the best mac and cheese I've had eaten! We've also gotten their tea, which was very refreshing and natural. Can't wait to go back and try other items on their menu!

Purbird serves the best tasting chicken I've ever eaten. They use Amish raised chicken and the quality is always outstanding. All of their chicken sandwiches are excellent. My favorite dish is the half chicken which is a butterfly with the leg and just melts in your mouth. The sides are all great but what stands out are the mashed potatoes which are probably the best in New York City. It's a small restaurant with a genuinely friendly staff. All dishes are prepared to order and this usually takes about 10 minutes. Their delivery service is prompt and efficient. The only problem is that now if I eat chicken anywhere else I'm disappointed but It never matches Purbird.

I feel Union League is another restaurant that is slightly (ok, majorly) overhyped. Most people dress up to go. The food was good, but not great. I went for Restaurant week for lunch and not only did they only give us bread, entree, and dessert (most restaurants let you choose 2 out of 3 courses or just give you the full 3 course meal), their entree was a bit salty and their bread was a bit sandy. Definitely would not go again, even for special occasions. I'd rather go somewhere with better food and a less stuffy atmosphere.

My girlfriend and I have been lucky enough to have eaten at the Chef's Table twice within the past two months, the most recent of which was this past Saturday. Now, we all know the deal: 1.  It's impossible to get a reservation. 2.  If you happen to get one, they charge you an arm and a leg. 3.  Your arm and leg are payable one week in advance. 4.  No notes. No food pictures (womp womp).   Amidst all these things, all we really want to know is: Is it worth it? In my humble opinion, absolutely YES.   The meal encompasses 15+ courses, many of which are sashimi. I could list each course to map exactly what I had, but I don't think it will be an individual dish that will be most memorable.  What I'll remember is the overall balance, the clean flavors, the pace and progression of the meal, the full spectrum of flavor, the subtlety, the richness, the sights, the smells. Basically -- just delicious. With that said, I do have a few favorite dishes. (i.e. Red Perch in Black Vinegar; Foie Gras/King Crab/Squash Dashi) The wine list is extensive, but not overwhelming. As you'd imagine, vin blanc is king here.  The sommelier recommended a nice bottle at each of my visits, pairing well with both the food and the wallet. The vibe may be slightly intimidating at first, given the aforementioned house rules and the 3* Michelin status, but once the show starts, that goes away pretty quickly. The staff was professional and very friendly, not at all stuffy. As for Chef Ramirez, he is just a cool, down-to-earth guy. He comes off as a little quiet and intense, but will definitely do a few rounds around the room to chat with guests and ask about their meals. And obviously, the dude has skills. Now, assuming you're still interested in eating here, here's what to do:   1. Exercise your re-dial finger. (Reserve.) 2. Save your pennies. (Pay.) 3. Turn off your cell phone and lose the notebook. (Eat.) This is as amazing a dining experience as can be found in New York, or anywhere. I hope to make it back soon.

Tried this place for the first time 2 months ago.  I did feel that the food and service were sub-standard, given their prices.  Never in my wildest dreams did I imagine that any restaurant would provide bad food and service on purpose.  Normally, I would give an establishment the benefit of the doubt, but in this case, there are just way too many allegations, including those of mine.  As Gordon Ramsay says in Hells Kitchen, "Shut it Down!!"

As an Asian American from the Upper West side who ate there six months ago, here is my experience. The food was excellent, just his friendliness was palpable to everyone except our party. And when we asked to take a picture with him he was very rude and just said no and ignored us. We felt disrespected and did not know why. We wondered if it was something we said and or done to deserve this poor treatment but now that this has come to light, it explains everything. We just did not think this type of behavior happen in our own neighborhood in this day in time. To all the non believers and defenders, believe it.

Let me write a longer review that shows I've been here so yelp doesn't delete my review. I was extremely excited to eat here in my short stay in nyc since my friend raved about this place being his favorite.   When you're only in nyc for 4 days and there are several 3 star michelin restaurants to choose from, you expect to have the best experience for the amount of money you pay.  We were able to dine at two 3 star michelin restaurants during our short stay. Le bernardin at first and let's stay they are impeccable with their dishes.  From the service to describing the dishes, they know how to treat a guest.  We even went as far as asking for a kitchen tour which they happily obliged.  Unfortunately, chef Ripert had already left the building. Fast forward to chefs table.  I've heard this is an intimate setting and for dropping hundreds on a meal, you would expect the experience to be intimate.  Ours was anything but that.  Maybes he's not racist but he sure isn't the same with everyone.  He was at the door to greet guests yet he refused to take a picture. He chatted it up with the guests on the sides and sat us dead center.  The ingredients of each plate are only briefly described and  didn't feel sincere.  Some dishes are good but nothing memorable where we wanted to say damn!  You'll definitely be left hungry.  My fiance was already thinking about pizza before we even left.   I'm sure every palate is different as is every experience but in my experience all 3 star michelin restaurants should be held to higher standards and I didn't leave satisfied.  Providence in LA still leaves us thinking about their dishes and they only have 2 stars.

I don't care what people say. And yelp, please don't remove my review as I have dined there and certainly have something to say. Yelp is suppose to be an honest forum where people share opinions and views on their experience. Yes. It was good. Yes. It was impossible to get reservations. Yes. It was Brooklyn which was also a pleasant surprise. But for two people, we paid $1000 and to discover that we were referred to as sh*t people while they seemingly served me leftover meat and robbed of me of my rights as a patron, I cannot give Chefs Table more than a 1 star. Really a huge disappointment.  And if the accusations are true, he should go elsewhere for business. Maybe a place in his own narrow little world. And as I recall, no photos were allowed. And there is always half truth to everything, exaggerated or not.
Celebrated a birthday with couple of friends.  The décor was plain and on the cold side.  Staff acted polite but lukewarm.  Food was pretty good, but not worth the money.

My trip started with a sour note. Food was average, for the price you pay there are better options, but this is not where my gripe is at. I've had one of the worst service I can possibly have. Some staff was friendly and helpful while 2 was extremely extremely rude. My group was well dressed slacks, dressshirt and tie. We were not treated fairly infact one of them ignored us for the entire night while giving other guest their full attention. Even after I flagged one of them he would turn to another guest and ask the other guest if he needed anything as if he was trying to make an excuse to ignore me. I will keep my opinions reserved on here but it did look like some group of guest were treated better than others. On top of that they add 20% on top of my tab. I will not come back.
A solid slice.

Such a lovely night we had! First, the name is fantastic. I just love saying "We're going to Pig & Prince tonight." The restaurant itself is beautiful. Just seriously gorgeous to look at. I love how they turned an old train station into such a fabulous joint. The service, while obviously new and in training, was so eager and willing to please. Our waiter (Hassan) was so friendly and helpful. We were also visited by several hosts and the manager, all of whom asked about our experience. I thought this was very thoughtful of them - they are attentive to the thoughts of their first customers in order to make adjustments early on. Smart! The food itself is really delightful. My salad with roasted tomatoes and house-made croutons was to die for - and I eat a lot of salad, so I really mean it when i say it! The venison was juicy and tender and cooked to medium-rare perfection. The collards and corn bread hush puppies were extra yummy. The bar even made me a Bloody Mary upon request, even though it's not on their menu. The whole experience was really wonderful and we had a great date night because of it. We most certainly are looking forward to coming back. In fact, I'm calling tomorrow to make reservations for our wedding anniversary dinner. I hope this place does well and stays for a long time. I love having it just around the corner!

For diners, great food can elevate a lackluster environment (think an amazing lobster roll at a crappy little lobster pound in Maine, great dim sum in a basement in Chinatown, or even Le Bernardin before its recent makeover) and a unique environment can elivate a lackluster meal (think Tavern on the Green), but it is when high quality and creative food comes together with a unique environment that fireworks fly and diners are treated to an "experience," rather than just a meal.  That is what dining at the Pig & Prince is... an experience. As others have mentioned, the owners have taken an architectural diamond in the rough and made it shine.  No detail was overlooked. Likewise, the food and drink menus (both at the bar and in the main dining area) are, despite the fact that this restaurant just opened last week, highly refined, creative, approachable, and exciting.   My favorites so far: the Cod, the pork belly pizza, the venison, the cured meats (all of them), the mac and cheese fries and pretzel bombs at the bar, and the key lime pie.   On the drink menu: The cucumber drink special and the blitzkrieg are fantastic and I look forward to many more Sorachi Aces served in glasses etched with the P&P logo (another nice touch). With free parking, outstanding food, a liquor license (and fantastic drink menu), and a beautiful space, P&P is a great addition the crowded Montclair dining scene.

I have been to 48 out of the 50 states, 7 of the 13 provinces of canda and easily more than a dozen countries.  One thing I have learned is that you can never judge a restaurant until you've tried the food. Not only is the Pig and Prince beautiful inside the food is absolutely brilliant.  If you are afraid of foie gras or goat's milk cheesecake please stay home.  If you think Chilli's is a good dining experience this is not the place for you.  However if you are looking for 5 star restaurant at Outback prices you have found nirvana. The only thing left to say is if you know your beers their selection is absolutely inspired.  For example they have Brooklyn's Sarachi Ace on tap. Sandnsurf

As soon as we walked through the door we received a great welcoming from staff. We ordered all three courses and all of them were beyond our expectations. We started with the watermelon Sangria then went on to have the salad roll, and galaxy roll, followed by entrees, Sweet Potato Enchiladas, Pad Thai Noodles, and the Laksa Noodle Pot, and to end our already amazing meal we ordered the coconut creme pie (top 5 pies of my life!). None of us were vegetarians and we all completely enjoyed our meals even without meat! We will all be back multiple times and can't wait to share the excitement with more of our friends! For being a new restaurant in Burlington there wasn't a minute that we thought they had just opened. Everything went so smooth. We give this place 5 stars from start to finish... food, drinks, service and ambiance. This place is one of the best new restaurants in Burlington!!

I was very excited to try this restaurant, however it fell short of expectations. The highlight was the service (which was phenomenal,) but otherwise the restaurant was gilded. The experience does not meet the mien, and the food fell short of pretense.

loved this restaurant! friendly and knowledgeable staff, the food arrived quickly and was delicious! i got the greek salad and shared the salad roll with my friend as an appetizer. 5 stars across the board for sure!

A great ambiance, an extremely welcoming and friendly staff, and outstanding food. That's my core impression of Revolution Kitchen from this past Friday night. The place was hopping at about 7:30 on Friday night, but I conveniently found a place at the open bar with my friend, as the table seating was about a 30 minute wait (totally worth it, by the way). I started the night out with some local Lost Nation Saison brew and Pan-Fried Wontons, followed by the Tempeh Reuben Sandwich on Slow Fire Baguette... I think the Wontons, with their almost ragoon-like qualities and texture, would please even some of the pickiest meat eaters. And the Tempeh Reuben? You've got to try it. Pretty full as it were from the mix of goodies, I needed to try one of Debra's homemade desserts: so I caved for the Blueberry Tart made with Almond Flour. I am so happy I did. I highly recommend Revolution Kitchen for anyone looking for a really cool spot and real people.

The bread was burnt. It took 35 minutes to get our drinks. The portions were small and everything was very salty. Impossible to get our water glasses filled. Very confused staff and slow service... needless to say will NOT be going back!

It has been a while since I have been truly impressed by a restaurant, but I honestly was by Agricola. Was there last night with five friends. Our waiter - Darrell - was fantastic. Attentive, but not over bearing, friendly, and extremely knowledgable. Given that they were busy, I expected them to rush us out like most American restaurants, but we were able to enjoy eating, drinking, and catching up with friends. The drinks: bar and wine menu is very good. Some interesting and well-made cocktails on the menu and a nice, but not ridiculous, wine list. We had a very nice Marlborough Pinot Noir.
