Wish we had more time to investigate the bar. Looks very solid. The food: very, very nice. Fresh and original without being pretentious. Our table shared the mushroom flatbread to start which was absolutely delicious.  On Darrell's recommendation, four of us shared the veal shank, which was excellent. Overall: excellent. Truly the first time I have been this impressed by a restaurant in central NJ and I have been to a lot of them. I don't quite believe in giving five stars, as one can never be perfect, but after thinking about our meal at Agricola last night I honestly cannot think of one thing to fault. Go

I think my expectations of this place were super high given the fact that it took me over a month to finally get a table!  The food was good, didn't blow me away but it was tasty! I wish the portions were larger though! The dessert I got DID blow me away....it was the berry cake with the creme fraiche icecream, holy crap! AMAZING!

A new restaurant in the downtown Princeton area that has definitely drawn some attention. A "farm to plate" type restaurant, the chef brings what is currently available from his farm directly to the restaurant. I would definitely give Agricola a solid 3.5 stars with some of the downside being the price/value for the drinks/dishes. The ambience on the day we went for Happy Hour was extremely lively. It was during a March madness game and the open seating bar area was packed (good thing we got there early). The service was excellent with some great recommendations from our waiter. The decor was nice as well. We ordered a variety of their specialty cocktails which ranged in price from about $10-12. The appetizers and dishes that we ordered were good, but for the amount of food provided, it did not justify the price - 3 cod fritters for $12, potato fries for $8, and the strozzapreti pasta for $17. I am interested in coming back to try the full menu in their dining room, especially want to try the braised colorado veal shank.
Great broth, not much MSG. Ice coffee and milk tea are great too. Good portion and price.

** The Pho ** As a longtime pho enthusiast, I've often been a bit disappointed by Manhattan pho, and have long had hopes that outer-borough pho would somehow magically be better.  Thanh Da came on my radar after mentions from several fellow Yelpers, so I made the trek. I had the pho tai and am happy to report that it was pretty good... but sad to report that I did not have that longed-for wow moment, when I first sipped the broth.  The meat was a little chewy, and did not arrive as glaringly rare as I think pho tai beef ideally ought to.  (As for the noodles, I have no idea, someone really ought to school me on what separates the mediocre from the good.) Overall I didn't think this pho tai was in a different or better class than my long-time Chinatown fave Pho Bang, or newcomer Luu's in Kips Bay, with its spicier broth. ** The Other Menu Items ** - Avocado milkshake. Delicious!  Who knew.  Didn't taste a whit of avocado, though. - Bun Bo Hue.  Apparently this is not often on menus so it's the thing to get.  My friend ordered this and loved it.  I had a few sips--very good, very strong flavor, not sure I could have a whole bowl though.   - Chicken Banh Mi.  No good.  Skip it.  Maybe the pork sandwiches are better--the menu offers four or five variations.  The bread was delicious and perfect, and the veggies too, but the chicken was so dry that we imagined they had to work at it, to get it that way, like the owner was in the kitchen all day, tasting it regularly and berating the staff: "still too moist!"  Squirting Sriracha helped some.

Only reason I am giving this place 3 stars is because the bbq pork sandwich was good and thats not saying much because I feel like you can never go wrong with the sandwiches at any Vietnamese restaurant. I had the pork chop rice plate and the pork chop had a charred flavor and wasn't very tasteful by far the worst I have ever had.

After I read the past reviews, I decided to give it a shot and see what's the hot buzz about this place. I was really anticipating the bun rieu, but sadly that section on the menu happened to be out that day I visited(few weeks ago). I knew my mind was set on the house special Banh Mi but I was debating what else to give a try. The lady behind the counter kindly suggested another similar soup vermicelli (seafood). The House Special Banh Mi by far, the BEST I've had so far! I've tried many Banh Mi, especially the popular known ones in Chinatown, Manhattan but boy was I happy to give this place a try. I remember getting cut on my upper inner mouth area by hard crusted bread almost every time after a Banh Mi back in the days from Chinatown shops. But I had no trouble with Thanh Da's! I definitely notice the difference with bread being used and how it was prepared/warmed up. The Banh Mi was just, amazing. The vermicelli w/ seafood, I'll give it 7.5/10 even though I'm typically a seafood lover at heart. Perhaps I was swayed by the thought of not able to try the Bun Rieu. I'll definitely go back to try the Bun Rieu and another Banh Mi Special! (4/5 for now) Oh yeah, I was going to share w/ family members. Ended up having it all to myself, hehe. EDIT: Found time to stop by the place again and picked up Bun Rieu. I think we have a winner!!! (Highly recommend Bun Rieu -- it won't disappoint)

This restaurant is amazing and the best part is its in Ridgewood! The food is great ...I had the chicken which was cooked to perfection.  Friendly staff and great service . I look foward to going back and trying more things on the menu. Cant wait till they get thier liquor licence! What a  great addition to the area!
This place is amazing great food been there twice already gonna make it a weekly thing. Love this place

Pancakes are amazing - food is fresh - get their French press coffee!! So far My friends, family and I have enjoyed all the food we've gotten the last 3 times we are here. I think once they get a liquor license this quiet gem won't be so quiet. Waiter are very nice !! Note to restaurant - please don't loose freshness and cleanliness in the future :)) Otherwise you have a consistent customer

Came here for dinner the decor of the place is nice and the Byob is welcomed. The servers do not come to you so you have to wave them down. They also ignore you throughout the meal. Now for the food. The sushi is over priced. we had sashimi and sushi combination, Kano salad, and chicken and scallop habachi. Bill was 62. Sashimi was ok did not taste too fresh. Sushi was better but too much rice. The California rolls had really overly ripped avocado so that is all you taste. Miso soup was good. The salad that came with the meal choose creamy dressing because their ginger dressing is too pasty does not stick to salad at all. The kani salad is imitation crab meat with vinegar over lettuce. Was not very good and not the type of kani salad I'm used to. 7 for the salad. The habachi was fine no praise but no complaints either. Will try not to return here.

food was not out-of-this-world stellar,, but definitely sits above many other sushi places that I have not enjoyed that much. I enjoy the rolls here whenever I visit; I've yet to try their kitchen foods. the wasabi cheesecake is basically two slices or original cheesecake that is deep fried with tempura batter (a little bit like fried ice cream) and lightly drizzled with wasabi sauce...and I'm glad it was only LIGHTLY drizzled. I'm not a fan of wasabi but I wanted to try it because it was hilarious to see something like wasabi cheesecake on the menu. it was interesting, but wasn't turned on by the melting edges and cold center, but at least I gave something like that a try. service was very accommodating and everybody were friendly. not the best at english, but they suck it up with a smile which I appreciate even through the thick accents.

We were regulars at this restaurant for a little while. However, one night my king crab had a lot of shells in them - I couldn't even eat it. We told the manager but she did nothing but apologize and say next time they would keep a better eye out. Then she told us all she would only charge us for one roll instead of two. I had begrudingly ate one of the rolls so she wasn't doing us any favors. I still paid for what I ate, which was gross. Poor customer service, especially for customers that you know are regulars. Won't go back.

what can i say - I eat a lot of Ramen in NYC area- and  ANI RAMEN was INCREDIBLE- what a treasure!  from the moment we sat down we ate like kings! The gyoza, kimchi, Chashu Don, pork buns- all top notch- the gyoza, might be the best i have had in years!. So fresh and yummy.  The pork in the Chashu Don was tender and melted in  you mouth.  We then had three different ramen: the Ani Ramen, The Mazeman, and the Miso- all were superb. Noodles were firm and fresh and the broth- the real test of a ramen house- was flavorful and complex- AMAZING-.  There was a side dish of three oils- Burnt Garlic ,  Onion  and chili- all tasty and really brought out more layers in the flavor of the ramen.  We also had our son with us and he was over the moon. GO, ENJOY, and KEEP COMING BACK.  WE WILL.

This place is good. Authentic flavors and the service is great!! Must try their  pork buns they are delicious, soft bun and tender pork with an incredible sauce. I had the traditionally Shoyu Ramen and it was so flavorful. The restaurant itself has a great vibe, with great artwork. I'm so glad there is a great ramen place nearby , I would eat here everyday if I could!!

Food was awesome! We started with the Pork Buns and Edamame. The Pork Buns were phenomenal, we ordered two more orders to-go after eating it. The edemame was great too, the addition of chili was a great touch. I had the Ani Ramen, my wife had the Spicy Ramen and the kids shared a Miso Ramen. The kids don't often eat anything other than kiddie meals (nuggets, etc) but they finished the entire bowl of Miso Ramen, and impressive feat for a restaurant. My wife and I couldn't stop sharing eat other's ramen as well. Service was just as amazing as the food. Remember the pork buns that we ordered after the appetizers? Well, we forgot them when we left the place. About a block away later as we were walking to our car, someone from Ani Ramen was yelling "wait...." and running towards us, with two orders of Pork Buns in hand. Can't say enough praise for their service after that.

So good!!!' I went the first week it opened so even at 9:30 pm on a Saturday there was a wait but it was worth it. We sat at the counter instead of waiting fifteen minutes for a table. Pork buns are a must! They're perfect! I had the brothless ramen which has thicker noodles more like what you would find in lomein. It was excellent!!!!!! But it took probably a half an hour before we got our food Overall it's well worth the wait and very affordable. We took home leftovers too!

Definitely one of the best ramen places I've tried. The pork bun itself was great. I pretty much ordered everything in the appetizer section and everything tasted fantastic. I ordered #5 which was the ramen bowl with no broth and just the noodles and the meats. And it was delicious. The only thing that could have been better was to have air conditioning. I believe they said it wasn't working so we just had to deal. The food was too good that we didn't even care for the heat. The food came out pretty quick and the service was great!

Went there with my cousin last night because my friend works there. It is a bit of a drive for me (20-30 mins). We both ordered the Ani Ramen because it was recommended to us (it has to be a signature dish since its from the Ani ramen shop right???) The soup base was amazing - extremely flavorful and the noodles are not starchy either! We also ordered the pork buns - I call it peking duck style - its also nomz. Only complaint was the place is extremely cramped and they are so busy!! But we actually lucked out on a roomy table :)

Ani Ramen House is a great addition to the Montclair restaurant scene. It's totally new. I ordered the shoyu ramen. The broth had great depth of flavor and the the meat was braised perfectly. My friend ordered one of the other soups and we split the lightly pickled vegetable. Absolutely go eat.

We have been eating ramen In Tokyo, Osaka, Hong Kong , New York and in New Jersey Mitsuwa market. We were Looking forward to eat here because close to home, but we were a bit disappointed. 1) tried the house Ramen the soup favor is good but a bit on the heavy side, the pork were tender but on the dry side, the runny egg were cold which is a turn off, noodles too chewy but favor were good. 2) chicken wings were good but too salty, why sprinkle more salt when serving, the wings have been marinated they should just hold off the salt, just sprinkle the chili pepper. 3) House special Salad was just ok, nothing special. 4) the pork don is a bargain for $4, but you are getting bits and pcs of chopped up pork over rice, it was ok for the value.

Pork Buns were good.  Ramen Noodles were average. Wrong order served but insisted we ordered wrong. Receipt showed we ordered right. A quick apology with ' see you again' offered. Disappointing when error was their's and money was ours.  Ok place regardless.  Nothing exceptional

Got the shrimp spring roll - it tasted fresh and yummy. Peanut sauce was addicting and I saved some of it to eat with the pho. Pho was very large portion!! Happy and will return. Only bad thing is that the waiter/only person working the restaurant at the time did NOT speak english well. It was difficult to communicate easily.

I'm from New York where there's a ton of Viet restaurants. I'm really picky when it comes to my pho but this is the best pho, I've ever had. I've also been to Viet restaurants in China. Their beef cube with rice is so tender, it almost melts in your mouth. I didn't know Viet food CAN get better. The beef broth here tastes so fresh, it's to die for. I am still eating as I write this review, that's how good it is. It's so good I had to stop and give them five stars, first time I ever stopped eating to write a review,

Delicious!!! We had the Mexican Ceviche which had shrimp, flounder, red onion, avocado in a tomato and citrus marinade very good! Also we tried the  Venezuelan Arepas excellent served with rice, plantains. Awesome! We will be going back again soon.
It was absolutely delicious!  My only complain would be the actual place, a bit to small and not that conformable.   The staff was friendly and again, the food was different and delicious.

Rubamba has quickly become a favorite of mine, both for takeout and dining in. They recently expanded their space to accommodate more seating, which seems to have worked out quite well. The arepas, both Colombian- and Venezuelan-style, are delicious. I've tried nearly all of the toppings at this point and it's difficult to pick a favorite, but maybe I'd give an edge to the chancho. It does bother me slightly that the price for arepas at their cart outside YNHH is about half of what they charge in the restaurant, but it's still a pretty good deal. They also make a fantastic pollo milanesa sandwich that has never provided me with fewer than two meals, and their tostones are very good if a little on the greasy side. Overall, the positives of Rubamba far outweigh the negatives. Give it a try if you're looking for something a little different than standard New Haven fare.

***IMPORTANT*** The Columbian style arepas are amazing here. I've had the chicken, steak, pulled pork, and fish. My favorites are the steak and chicken (in that order), and they never disappoint. This is actually my favorite food to eat in New Haven. HOWEVER, the prices are totally unjustified. Especially considering that Rubamba has food trucks called Ay Arepa that serve the exact same arepas with the EXACT same quantities for THREE TIMES LESS. For example, a chicken arepa at the food truck costs 5.50 (and since its a truck you don't pay tax) while at the restaurant it costs 13.50 before tax (and this is the cheapest one). That's literally absurd. The only reason this might be the case is that if you eat in at the restaurant you get "free"  chips and salsa. Chips and salsa cost $7.00 if you ordered them off the menu, hence they add about $7 to the food truck prices... But even that is ABSURD. I've been to the restaurant several times before discovering the food truck and I've always gotten take out meaning I didn't get chips and salsa but still paid $15+ for the arepa. After going to the food truck I've become so turned off that I will never be able to go back to the restaurant. If I'm in new haven during lunch time I might go to the truck again, but what the restaurant is doing is ROBBERY. That is all.

Great, great, great!  Some very authentic stuff here.  Try the corn kernels with pine nuts...very good.  The sautéed loofah was perfectly cooked also, with a mild and unassuming sauce which didn't take away from the louffah's wonderful texture.  Service was extremely slow, the ambiance is loud, but the food is spot on!
best Szechuan around! Their chicken and eggplant in five flavor sauce is my favorite, but don't forget the spicy baby wontons. AND they deliver!

A rediscovery of an old favorite! I had to stop by because I was nearby (I normally travel north from my apt. on Saint Marks). Coming here is like traveling to Italy for a moment. (And yes I've been there & am & speak Italian.)  Always delicious. Always authentic. The rule of "Good, fast or cheap?... Pick two." applies. When they're busy, you may have to wait five or ten minutes longer BUT ITS WORTH IT. It's inexpensive & delicious. Support this great local shop.

My wife and I first went to Gaia during a short trip to NYC from Washington D.C. We had heard that getting a table sans reservation could get tricky given the restaurant's seating capacity, so we were completely surprised that we were seated immediately upon arriving. The restaurant wasn't crowded, and I was able to have a lengthy, educational conversation with the owner about limoncello.  Why mention this? Because I didn't see any of the negative attributes that others have ascribed to her. I don't doubt that some people have had unpleasant experiences - it happens everywhere - but I certainly didn't. The second time we went, about six months after our first visit, Gaia was crowded, but the food, still definitely worth the wait. Simple, flavorful, and well-portioned; not to mention VERY reasonably priced!

Wow. This place as rocked my Italian food world. One of the best places I've ever eaten. Every dish has complex, interesting flavors. There is care put into every part of your meal. Love this place. I want to go everyday.

Had this place bookmarked to try. Decided to go with my husband and we were actually told to leave 10 mins ago.  We were exploring the menu and my husband was not familiar with the items. A brunette women of about 5'6 with straight shoulder length hair and an accent said to my husband "this is probably not the food for you, just leave " I was stunned in how rude she was when my husband was simply asking what the words meant in the menu. We left.. Never again

This spot is below ground on Houston so it's easy to miss- but stop by! The food is truly Italian, cooked fresh and delicious (be warned- some dishes are heavy). The place is decorated really cute and cozy- lets in lots of light which is nice.
Good heavens to Betsy!  This place is unreal.  Sassy chef, fantastic food and insane prices.  Just have to remember to bring wine next time.  Jeez Louise!

The manager/bar tender Kyle was very rude to my sister and her gay friend. On separate occasions, he ignored them for hours. When he was confronted with this information, he blatantly lied saying he was overwhelmed with an overcrowded bar. Listen, I'm a deploying soldier and my sister was the one complaining about the show service. The bar seats about 20 people. There were roughly 12 people at the bar at any given time. Give me a break. You are slow because you are slow.

Oh Sea Witch how I love thee! Your wonderful style, fantastic cocktails and amazing staff make you my bar of choice in the Slope. I have introduced many of my friends and they also are now having a love affair with you... I am forever yours

I never really write reviews, but that doesn't mean I don't read them. And when I read reviews that were written for 'a friend' or 'my sister and her gay friend' (which is completely irrelevant, Patrick Y.) I get annoyed. Not only because of a second persons account of a situation (Rebecca S.), but it's clear there are people with just angry slams. I have had my fair share of actually having to wait for a drink for a bit, but I understand that there may be circumstances that one may not control. I will wait a little for a nice, cold craft beer as opposed to buying a dusty bottle at Eagle and waiting for that to chill.   Beyond that, Sea Witch, a tiny little oasis of happiness. You may have to actually respond to a buzzer to get your food, but at least they have food. Delicious food at that. Picking up your food is still better than making it at home. (Get what's happening here?) Andy has made a serene place with the atmosphere that makes you want to stay for hours without people screaming that the other team sucks. Kyle has made it a place that you feel safe and comfortable walking in alone. As a female in 2014, that's pretty crucial. So, stop that hate. People have off days and I will consider the unfounded reviews I have read your bad day. Now get a service industry job and realize that it's hard dealing with most people's bullshit. Nothing but love, Sea Witch.

Heck yeah, Sea Witch! Great beer selection, very fair prices (beer specials! from excellent microbreweries, not standard cheapo yellow stuff), super-friendly staff who seem to really enjoy working here -- those things alone get my thumbs-up. But then... there's more. I am not a "cocktails person," but my ladyfriend is, and she's raved about virtually any cocktail she's ordered when we've been here (and she's also ended up kinda tanked earlier than she expected). Want cheap, tasty sandwiches and other pub grub? You got it, with the kitchen open very late into the night, and even though the food counter is not conjoined to the bar, you can add your food total to your bar tab, no problem, and the kitchen will give you a buzzer so you can keep hanging with your friends until your order is ready. I do like the decor, too, that kinda-nautical-or something theme and especially the backyard. The sandwich board out on the sidewalk refers to their "critically acclaimed backyard" (which I think is great and very funny), and it is an excellent backyard, with big wooden tables, stones and a little faux brook/fountain thing. I don't live around here at all, but when I'm down in this neighborhood, I'm always up for a little Sea Witch. Can't go wrong.

My wife and I went Friday night for dinner and some hookah and we were very disappointed! After we were seated  ( waited 25 minutes for seating), a server brought us some water and took our order.  So far so good, we ordered grape leaves, an eggplant dip and a hookah with a grapefruit bowl. The server that brought out the food never brought us out plates, silverware or napkins, we had to flag down another server for them. He seemed sooooo unmotivated bringing it to us.  Literally dragging his feet!! Now to the food.  Grape leaves we're super bland!!! The dip was good but the pita bread (that I had to ask for) seemed old and like the kind you buy at a super market.  After that we didn't order anything else. They never filled our water. So after finishing the apps we realize we didn't get the hookah we ordered yet.  It had been 50 mins since we ordered.  I asked another server to check on it and he said there was a wait.  I would have liked to know that when I ordered it.  So I asked him to cancel it and bring me the check.  It was never cancelled and after 15 mins more, we got the hookah.  The bowl was an orange not a grapefruit that we ordered.  My wife and I just made the best of it.  We will definitely not be returning here.   Unorganized staff. Bland and old food. Slow and bad service! AND GRATUITY WAS INCLUDED! Ugh. Nightmare. My wife gives them 1 Star!
I loved this place... I would recommend this place to everybody... Awesome experience..

LOVE this place. Perfect for girls night or a date. The service is great; the servers never rush you. Very chill time. The outside is such a nice ambience -- lights and palm trees. Hookah is great and I love the chicken kabob. I never take home left overs but I could not leave my chicken kabob behind. Highly recommended

I've been here many times and had most of the dishes on the menu.  Baba ghannoush, musakaah and falafel are my favorite appetizers, but I've also had their delicious zuppa di clams and mussels and the soujouk  which is quite up to my taste as far as being well spiced. For the main course I would recommend the chicken shawarma and the filet mignon steak as well as the kebabs. The service is good and the hookahs are being maintained continuously with new coals. The service makes the difference versus other similar places: any of their waiters is ready to serve your table whenever you need something, while refilling the water and the hookah maintenance are being done by specialized people, thus allowing the waiters to take care of the main business. After a couple of weeks, I already knew most of the people working there by name. I always end my dinner with turkish coffee and kanafi or baklava. I love this place!
Mediterranea has a relaxed atmosphere with excellent service! We had been going the NYC for hookah but now we have a great local spot to visit. I highly recommend their baklava!
Excellent environment, great service

I came here for their version of cronuts but was told to return around 1pm.  Instead I treated myself to a pistachio croissant and iced coffee.  The fanciest croissant i had before this was just chocolate.  I highly recommend their pastries.  I am looking forward to trying out the other flavors.  Hopefully, i'll be able to finally try out their cronut
Really tasty items here and fresh. Try them out once to be hooked and enjoy the professionalism they show.

Mediterranean pizza -- really, 2 stars for flavor for me.  Four stars for healthfulness.  Averaged to 3 stars. Crust not very tasty and a little argumentative, if you know what I mean.  And I would have loved for the volume of toppings to be increased by at least 25%. I like my healthy food to also be delicious.  This was really just so-so for me.

Popped in off the street on a whim for dinner one evening. I went with camaron, Al pastor and pollo guisado tacos and a carnitas torta. Of the tacos, the camaron was my favorite, though the al pastor was good with a pineapple salsa on top. The torta was a good sized sandwich, and I picked up on occasional spottings of a delicious sauce. Maybe could have used a little more pork, but a solid sandwich.     It was good, basic Mexican food at an ok price. I'd definitely give it a try again to sample more of the menu.

I loved the food at this place! Authentic tacos, and rice & beans also delicious! I'm a big fan and already want to go back- I got two of the carnitas tacos; basically the guy behind the counter told me (you can sit down to eat, but must order at the counter- and that's where the menus are) 1 taco is a light snack, two tacos is a hearty snack and 3 is a full-blown meal. My friends got various other tacos/enchiladas/fruit sodas and everyone loved their meal. Definitely recommend!
WOW.......at at first I wanted to go next door but I'm happy I ate at this place  I recommended to everyone.

This place is actually amazing. Right across from Central Park, the open faced front of the restaurant creates an amazing indoor/outdoor setting. The lighting, music and decor creates an upscale, yet casually comfortable ambiance. Our server Ewa is extremely knowledgeable and personable! The managers were walking around making accommodations and interacting with guests. All in all, a beautiful place with beautifully arranged food and phenomenal staff.

Few restaurants in New York are so well-rounded. Classic and delicious Italian food. You can order off the menu and they will accommodate you without question. I just ordered a classic pesto with roasted garlic, and it was perfect! The complimentary garlic focaccia with tomatoes to start, and bread with olive oil and balsamic, are delicious. I recommend the Portofino salad, Agnolotti Del Magnifico pasta, and Tartufo Gelato for dessert. Also, they have perfectly-sized half-portions--huge plus. Wonderful service, beautiful views into Central Park, and outside sidewalk seating.

We are visiting from California and love this place. Service is excellent. Great place for kids. Food is delicious and fresh. You can make any food requests and they will accommodate. We had Gary as our waiter and he was awesome! The prices are very reasonable.

My family and I went to dinner here last night in celebration of my brother's college graduation. We had never been before and we were very pleased from the moment we walked in. The mod Manhattan décor provided a luxurious appeal, while we passed around glasses of different elegant wines full with depth and balance. The lobster ravioli primavera was, to our surprise as New England vacationers, some of the best we have ever had. This was one of the best meals from start to finish we've had in a while. It's nice to know restaurants still make genuine Italian delicacies.
Shit place. Don't eat here. I can't believe how stupid the people are. I can't believe how rude they are.
Best Greek food in Rutherford hands down The other place wishes they had 1/10 of what these guys can do. Love their gyros and platters Great efficient and fast service.
I guess they stop answering the phone at 8:30 so customers can't place to go orders? Awesome.

MIND BLOWN !!! The Plate for 2 is a steal of a deal ! Under $20 gets you like 3 pounds of meat a big Greek salad and your choice of any side, the good thing is that they let me mix the meats so I got to try they're different meats and they are all mind blowingly delicious! For a side I recommend the baked lemon potatoe wedges! I'm not from the area but I will deff be back for more next week.

This review is only for lunch- as that is the only time I have visited. The inside is large and nice- but if the weather is in your favor, you must sit outside! Gorgeous back patio! I felt poor the moment we pulled into the parking lot, luxury vehicles in every parking spot. Sitting down, all I see are other customers with huge sparkling diamonds, manicures, and designer shoes and handbags. Now I feel poorer. The waiter is quick to seat us and get us menus and drinks. Now I look at the menu, I feel even poorer. I am not a poor person, but I think this place must be for the upper crust of society! I was really surprised that they did not seem to have a lunch menu. I do not want a large (expensive) Italian entree for lunch! I would fall asleep at my desk at work if I ate that! The pizzas looked good, a friend got the mushroom and was happy with it.It looked large and she took almost half of it home. I chose to get the Chop Chop salad. It was good, but not THAT GOOD. The greens were fresh, it was a decent size, but for $17 i feel like I should get more. Another friend got the Tropical salad, with shrimp and avocado. She enjoyed it as well, but we both agreed it was very expensive. The service was great, the atmosphere was lovely, but it just felt a bit overpriced and pretentious to me for a lunch spot. Perhaps dinner is better.

Great restaurant...great atmosphere...great food...great desserts. Restaurant and bathrooms are clean, food comes out quick and hot, staff is friendly and professional. A bit expensive but worth every cent.

Cute I thought when I first saw it. Walked in, friendly stuff. Ordered the salmon tartare (12USD). I was told it was just an appetizer but I still went ahead and ordered it. Was REALLY small! And not only that. Had to look for the salmon. It was an avocado tartare with a bit of salmon!

Had New Year's dinner here and ordered the Yellowtail Crude, which was so fresh and delectable.  My BF had the pork buns and they were tender, juicy and so tasty.  The highlight of the evening was the entrée.  We both got the New Year's special, Filet Mignon with trumpet mushrooms and lemon spinach.  The steak was cooked to perfection and a little bit smokey, the mushrooms added such a good flavor to the dish and the lemon spinach was just an incredible taste combination.  I have since tried to duplicate this at home but it wasn't even close.  One of our new favorite places for sure! Had breakfast here and it was great food as well!

I enjoyed lunch with friends here yesterday.  I ordered the Cuban Sandwich..... because if there's a Cuban on the menu, it must be tasted.  I would rate the sandwich alone 5 out of 5 stars.  Pulled pork was juicy, tender, and delicious.  The fries on the side were also a tasty treat. Everyone was more than satisfied with their meals.  It was also a friends Bday, and he enjoyed some delicious chocolate cake and ice cream!
love this place!! server was soooo friendly and helpful...food was delicious and fresh and the maple cake dessert was to die for! a must try !
Delicious Ethiopian Food... I liked the experience!

This was my first time having Ethiopian food and what a great experience! We went on Friday during Lent when we don't eat meat, so we ordered the vegetarian sampler platter. Everything was very flavorful. I only wish I could have had it with rice instead of injera. The service was also great. I felt like a guest in their home.

Worth walking the extra block or two from your usual hangouts on Court or Smith - it's still new, but the food was excellent, and the vibe is cozy but not too precious. Porkbelly fried rice covered all the salty-sweet-tangy bases, the fries were crisp, etc.   For some reason I also got talked into trying a summertime dessert consisting of watermelon chunks over labne with citrus - each bite burst in your mouth and it might be the most unexpectedly delicious dessert I've had.

I was turned on to this place by a coworker and I've had two wraps there since. First one I had was chicken taco and the second Philly jalepino (my mouth is watering just thinking about them). At first glance it looks like a regular little bar but first bite into one of those wraps and I was sold! The prices aren't too bad considering one wrap is super filling. I haven't gotten the chance to try anything else there yet but I will definitely be going back.

this place is AWESOME!!! u cant beat their prices, i usually get the steak taco wrap...amazing!!! it melts in your mouth, along w a long island iced tea pitcher ( they really make it how it should be), it cant get better than this for their prices!! love love love

i've always liked this place. recently they've overhauled the decor and i think they are confused about what they are trying to be. i haven't really been in there since they became a sports bar-cafe-bistro-smoothie stand but the handful of times i have been in, the prices were reasonable, the food was good and i left full. all-in-all a good spot to stop in for lunch.

While driving down Shelburne Road, looking for a late lunch, and trying to avoid box restaurants, we stopped in at Zen Gardens.  Upon entry, there is a cute koi pond and we were greeted by a young blond hostess.  We were promptly seated and the dining room was pretty much empty.  The menu offers all the traditional American/chinese fare, but they had a separate section for "real" Chinese, offering shredded jellyfish, many clam dishes, etc.  We would have tried it, but we weren't there for dinner.  They also offered an entire menu of "mock" meat for vegetarians.  We ordered the steamed vegetable dumplings and Hot and Sour seafood soup for two.  The hot tea we ordered was a loose jasmine tea, and steeped at our table.  Our soup was brought out first, and was served in cute little bowls, and the pot of soup was served in a metal pot, with a flame below, keeping it bubbling and hot, table side.  The soup wasn't the traditional hot and sour brown, it was a clear broth, with just a few TINY shrimp, and I only had one bite of fish, which was quite fishy.  The only "hot" in the soup was the chili oil, served on the side.  The dumplings were served dim sum style, and had great flavor.  We were warned that the freshly house made ginger dipping sauce was "hot" that day, but it wasn't.  Mostly spicy from raw garlic.  Our server was a nice young man, I even heard him offer another table a sample of soup if they wanted to try it.  I'd say the food itself was average, but the ambiance/decor and presentation make it a nice place for sit down Chinese.  I did leave with a stomach ache, though.  I'd try it again for sure.

Here's the deal with Chinese food. Having grown up in socal, I've been spoiled with authentic Chinese food at cheap prices. When I moved to Vermont, I kept expectations reasonable. Most likely this Chinese restaurant will serve an Americanized version of so called "Chinese food." I expected my food to be doused in soy sauce and MSG. I've eaten at other Chinese places in the area and none of them compare to Zen Garden. Although the location is on Shelburne Road (far from where I live), the food is actually palatable. The inside of the restaurant is actually huge. This isn't your typical sit down Chinese takeout shop. They have comfortable booth seats. So far the dishes I liked are the  Soup Noodle with Pickled Cabbage and Pork (a.k.a. #508), Stewed Beef Soup Noodle (a.k.a. #506), and the pan-fried noodles with chicken (Canto slang =  [gai see chow mein]). Noodle soups are great doing the cold winter months or recovery after a long night of "studying" till wee hours of morning. I was impressed that they served gai see chow mein. Only complaint is they put too much sauce and you don't get enough of the fried noodles which is the whole point of the dish. Disappointed with the portions though. They try to get fancy with flowers on the dishes. Price is not worth it for the scant portions.

When it comes to authentic Chinese food, Burlington is severely lacking. You have your run-of-the-mill greasy Chinese that's on par with Panda Express and then you have Zen Gardens - an oasis of traditional Chinese cuisine in a culinary desert. Once inside, you are first met by a real koi pond - you can't get more Asian than that. But, I did cringe at the sight of an area that could be used to serve a buffet (Chinese buffets are never a good idea). The restaurant itself is huge with an equally large menu to match. A special section is dedicated to traditional Chinese dishes, which homesick individuals like myself can appreciate. Dishes like scallion pancake with beef and the beef stew noodle soup instantly brought up my spirits. They're some of my favorite Chinese comfort foods and are even hard to find where I live back home. The flavor of the scallion pancake was spot on. The pancake itself didn't have any layers and looked like it was just deep-fried, but tasted good nonetheless. The beef stew noodle soup was outstanding. The flavor was great (the spiciness makes it great for a cold Vermont day) and the beef was very tender. On a return trip, I tried the house special lo mein, which was full of greasy goodness. The only thing that tasted a little odd was the shrimp, which might not have been de-veined properly. Sure, it's a little bit expensive (especially for the entrees and specialties), but realize where you are. Think of it as a Vermont tax. I will gladly pay a few extra bucks for a taste of home.
Awful service - left before even being seated.  There was no one there, why did it turn into a 25 minute wait?
The food is fine, but the take out service has been a misery.  They are very disorganized and very late with the food.  Not worth the trouble.

I've tried this place when it first open. I don't remember what I order. Now if it was good I would of went back there. Reading the other reviews here make me think I should try it again. But if I ever go there. I think I rather go to Hoagie Haven.

The hype for Mu Ramen is still alive and well, as I was greeted with a 45-minute wait time when I arrived 15 minutes after opening on the first night of service, a nasty, rainy Monday. I somehow missed out on the pop-up earlier this year when they were operating out of Bricktown Bagels around the corner, so I have been eagerly awaiting the chance to try the much talked about ramen. After grabbing some coffee and a snack at Sweetleaf down the block, we returned right about 45 minutes later to find our seats at the lone communal table waiting for us There are also 6 or 7 seats at the counter to round out the very small space for diners. The two of us ordered pretty much the entire menu, minus the edamame and shishito peppers listed under "Snacks" and the "Mu"ssels under the "Treats" section: - U & I ($15) One of the items I read about from the pop-up that I was most eager to try, this rice bowl with uni, spicy tuna, ikura and a big ball of wasabi on top definitely did not disappoint. So many good flavors and different textures going on in one little bowl make for an incredibly delicious dish. - "Okonomiyaki" ($14) Radically different in composition and flavor from most all Okonomiyaki I've tried (perhaps explaining why it's named in quotation marks on the menu), this was also incredibly good and refreshingly light compared to typical renditions. Consisting of a scallion pancake topped with generous chunks of smoked trout and little balls of tobiko that really popped, along with the requisite bonito, this is another excellent choice to start with. - Tebasaki Gyoza ($14) One of the new dishes to arrive with the re-opening, this consists of two very large deep friend chicken wings stuffed with foie gras and brioche. Like the other starters, this is pretty pricey, but also just as delicious. The really meaty, stuffed parts are obviously especially excellent. I didn't really taste much foie, but the soft brioche with the chicken was great. - Mu Ramen ($18) The namesake ramen has the lightest of the broths, an oxtail and bone marrow base, along with brisket, a half sour pickle, menma and cabbage. The very thin noodles are excellent, and make for a really amazing bowl of ramen, though I prefer the broth to be a bit richer. - Spicy Miso Ramen ($15) with Nitamago (+ $2) This was really incredible, and even better than the Mu Ramen. Made with the heartier pork based soup, this one is topped with scallion, ground pork, menma, corn, sesame and chili oil, and per Heidy's recommendation, we added a perfect seasoned egg to accompany it. The noodles in this one are much thicker, and go well with the generally much more satisfying bowl. If I had to only pick one, I would probably go with this one, though I will definitely be back to try the Tonkotsu 2.0 once they get some new items on the Treats section of the menu to go with it. As you can see from the prices, with the smaller "Treats" priced the same as the bowls of ramen, this place is not cheap, which is especially surprising given the Queens locale that often has gentler prices than the city. Still, it's definitely worth it for the really high quality food in a cozy, lively and fun atmosphere.

I had reservations during the week that the pop up shop closed so I prepared myself to show up on opening day. Indeed, I did and waited almost an hour and a half with my boyfriend. Fortunately, we got seated at the bar so our backs were against the hungry, anxious eyes from waiting patrons. U & I: I love anything uni but this was pretty lackluster. There is basically a spoonful of roe, with two small pieces of uni, on top of a small scoop of sushi rice. It wasn't worth $15. Tonkatsu 2.0: Amazing. It was rich and silky and everything you want your ramen broth to be, without bring overwhelmingly salty. Its name is very fitting as it is the best tonkatsu ramen I've ever had! The chasu almost melted in my mouth. Unfortunately, this wasn't my bowl but I sure will make it mine next time! Spicy miso: I always go for the spicy ramen but I wasn't crazy about Mu Ramen's. The noodles are thick, and a little hard, and almost resemble udon noodles. I didn't really appreciate them and it was too hearty and filling. The broth lacked that appetizing kick I look for. I also wished that it didn't come with grounded meat because I feel like it tends to get lost in the bowl. Mu Ramen is definitely the best ramen joint in Queens and although I'm on the fence of giving a 4 star rating, that Tonkatsu 2.0 has won my admiration.

I've been a fan of Joshua and Heidy Smookler's Mu Ramen since their pop-up* days, and I could not be more excited now that they're finally up and running at a permanent location. In fact I was so excited that I went two days in a row during their soft opening week. Mu's ramen-ya of exposed brick and minimalistic wood is warm and inviting and I love the sculptural design of the industrial pipe lights, geometric block tables, and wavy "noodle" ceiling beams. The restaurant seats just 22 diners at a time, so needless to say, with all the hype surrounding this opening, you should prepare to hunker down for a long wait. Though few, every seat in the house is a good seat, whether you're at the one long communal table with it's own built in succulent zen garden or at the counter bar facing the open kitchen. I typically go straight for the uni when I see it on a menu but since I had the pleasure of trying the U&I (uni, spicy maguro, ikura, sushi rice, sesame, roasted nori, fresh wasabi) during Mu's pop-up days (long story short: It's banging. U want this.) in my recent two visits I tried the newcomers to Mu's small plates menu, each a successful experiment in fusion. The Tebasaki Gyoza was like a mini holiday meal, fried chicken wings stuffed with foie and brioche and served with a plum dipping sauce - I'd choose this over turkey, stuffing and cranberry sauce any day. The "Mu"sels were steamed the classic French way (with shallots/white wine/butter) but accompanied by an addictive Thai chili dipping sauce - such a great combination. The "Okonomiyaki" was my favorite out of the three. The fluffy scallion pancake, topped with smokey shaved bonito and smoked trout, bursts of juiciness from the tobiko, and a mellow foie syrup, made for a perfectly balanced bite of savory and sweet. If only all "pancakes and syrup" tasted like this! I'd previously tried both the Tonkotsu 2.0 and Spicy Miso ramens at Mu, so I decided on the more creative namesake ramen for my first visit to the brick and mortar location. While Japanese ramen is traditionally served with a pork or chicken based broth, the Mu Ramen is beef based: thin springy noodles in an oxtail and bone marrow broth, served with brisket, half sour pickle, menma, and cabbage. The broth was reminiscent of Korean oxtail soup, rich and milky but not heavy. I loved the combination of toppings, especially the thick pieces of corned beef and crunchy cucumbers. I also opted to add an onsen tomago, which at Mu is sous vide and then cracked into your bowl at the table. While the Mu Ramen was good, great even, I had to go back the very next day for the Spicy Miso Ramen, my first love from their pop-up days. I gushed about it when I first had it and I'll gush about it now. This is, hands down, the best spicy miso ramen in NYC: thick chewy noodles in a smokey, mildly spicy red miso/pork broth, topped with corn cut from the cob, ground pork, menma, and sesame and chili oil. This time I opted to add a nitamago, which like the onsen tomago, was also perfectly executed. It's impossible to decide which egg I like better at Mu; I love it all. And with a constantly evolving menu, I want to eat it all. I'm definitely planning on many many repeat visits where I'll do just that. *yelp.com/biz/mu-ramen-lo… **Cash only; parties of 4 or less only ***My 300th Yelp review~ yay!

Been waiting 9 long months for Mu Ramen to open their permanent location and boy is it worth it.   Must get the gyoza.  It's like thanksgiving in one bite.  Love the umeboshi sauce, gives it sweetness, tang and saltiness to balance the richness of the dish. The ramens are spot on.  Deep, complex without being overly salty and fatty.  Still don't know which one I like the best. The decor is really cool too.   Just love this place.

Best ramen in New York. Hands down. Tips: 1) You can make reservations now, same day only, phone lines start at 3pm. 2) You can also try to go before they open at 5:30PM; when I got there around 5:15, there was already a line. 3) Go by yourself or with one other person; there's a 4 person max. 4) Sit at the bar and watch the chefs make your food!!!!!! (only 6 bar seats) Also better lighting for you foodtogs out there. 5) ADD ROASTED CORN AND NITAMAGO! 6) BRING ALL YOUR CASH! I'm already planning my next visit, either solo or with one other person only. Such a small place and long wait due to all the press. Of course it's worth it, though. It's a no frills ramen place that focuses on its noodles. Their broths, man, their broths! Whether you get the beef based one or the pork based one, you can't go wrong. Their appetizers are great and I want to order 2 of the U&I just for myself... I LOVE UNIIIIII. The difference between Mu and Tonkotsu: 1) Mu ramen - signature ramen, beef based with thin noodles 2) Tonkotsu 2.0 - pork based with thin noodles Both are AMAZING. Next time I will try the spicy miso, which has thick noodles (and no, you can't interchange noodles...) lifeonmacro.com/2014/12/… MU-HAHAHAHAHA

I don't always write reviews but when I do...I prefer to write one for Mu Ramen. I am the most ling-teresting man in the world (or at least on this site) because I've had the opportunity and fortune to try all three of Mu's staple ramens - the Mu, Spicy Miso and my personal favorite, the Tonkotsu 2.0. My first experience with Josh and Heidi (the husband and wife team behind Mu) was during Mu's pop-up stages in which my girlfriend and I experienced the prix fixe menu at their apartment. However, I just want to share my experience with the ramen because at the end of the day, the ramen is what matters the most and is nearest and dearest to my heart and stomach. The Tonkotsu 2.0 was ramen romance at first sip. It evoked the feelings of a first date hand holding, a quick peck on the cheeks good night and the undeniable feeling deep down in your stomach that she was the one. To me, the Tonkotsu 2.0 was that special one. It was familiar in the sense that the foundation of the broth tastes like some of the best tonkotsus out there but it really sets itself apart because the broth achieves a porkiness and creaminess without the overbearing fattiness or heaviness. From the first sip to the last gulp, the broth is consistent.... consistently delicious. In my humble opinion, the broth and the noodles make for the best, if not one of the best, ramens in the city. As for the Spicy Miso, it had a nice kick, great full-bodied flavor and was downright tasty. The corn straight off the cob, ground pork and thicker noodles really set it apart. If I was not already engaged to the Tonkotsu 2.0, I could totally see myself succumbing and shacking up to a nice steaming bowl of the Spicy Miso. Fast forward 10 months and several bouts of Tonkotsu 2.0 withdrawal; I was finally reunited after learning that Mu Ramen was finally opened. The Tonkotsu was just as I had remembered and fond memories came rushing back upon tasting it again. I quickly familiarized myself by spooning heaps of the perfectly cooked noodle and broth down my pie hole. I am happy to report that it was still the same wonderful broth I had tasted during Mu's pop-up days. In this crazy and ever changing world, it was comforting and reassuring to know that the Tonkotsu will be a constant in my life from this point on. Did I mention that I love ramen? Well, I love ramen but I what I like even more is food that tells a story. The household ramen, the Mu, pays homage to Josh's Korean/Jewish upbringing as the corned beef/pickled cucumber topping is a riff on corned beef and cabbage and the broth similar to a Korean based ox tail soup. The broth was lighter than the Tonkotsu and the corned beef/cucumber combo was unlike anything I ever had in a ramen. It was undoubtedly delicious but the personal story only makes it that much better.   Moral of this review? Eat more ramen!!!

it's good but it has to do a better job of managing the line. It totally doesn't make sense that you show up when it opens and the wait is 2 hrs. Sorta lukewarm review here: ny.eater.com/2014/12/8/7… I give the apps 2 stars. I much prefer traditional gyoza. the U+I was ok...rice was undercooked or sitting out for too long. I also prefer more squiggly noodles. theirs are silky and thin and straight. Service wasn't bad. They could make much better use of the space in there to accommodate the demand. oh, that sou vide egg is freaking amazing!

Splendid ramenya, definitely lives up to the hype. Visited with a small group -- first piece of advice, SMALL GROUPS ONLY -- and had a really delicious meal: Shared: Shishito Peppers UniPo Okonomiyaki Ramen: Mu Ramen (Beef) Tonkatsu 2.0 All the apps were delicious and very delicate. The flavors on the Okonomiyaki blew us away -- salty, sweet, savory all at once. The ramen lived up to the expectations we've had since before the Pete Wells review in March. The Tonkatsu 2.0 that Wells had really could be considered among the best bowls of ramen in the city, but it was the namesake ramen that really blew us away. I can't recommend this place enough, and I can't wait to go back to try the Tebasaki Gyoza and the Spice Miso Ramen.

U&I Tebaski gyoza Spicy miso ramen Mu ramen AMAZING We have been LIC residents for some time now and are overjoyed that Mu ramen opened up a permanent location - just in time to warm us up for the winter! The ambiance is sophisticated and earthy, with a really cool table that had small succulent gardens in the middle. Their dinnerware was very interesting - wish I could own those too! On to the food -- we were pleasantly surprise on how good it was! We enjoyed both our ramen and starter dishes. We can't wait to come back and try all the whole menu. It's a short walk from our building, and an even shorter walk from the train (7 or G). My favorite thing about the restaurant: the staff was very charming and were very personable! If they weren't so busy, we would probably talk to them for days. The owner told us they were also LIC residents - just across the street from us! We love that this LIC little gem! Thanks for coming to brighten up our neighborhood!

First of all, props to my boyfriend for getting us a reservation. The phone line was tied up at 3pm when they opened, but he finally managed to get through around 4pm and we got an 8:15pm reservation! Beautiful restaurant, great service (you could tell they take pride in their work), and creative menu. I like the place, but don't think I'll be back. A couple comments: -- Not their fault, but for those trekking in from other parts of NYC, the Google Maps location is wrong. They helpfully warned us on the phone at time of reservation that the Yelp location was wrong and to use Google Maps, but that's also wrong. It's on Jackson Ave, just east of 11th St. -- Ordered the U & I uni dish as an appetizer. Good but felt the uni was overpowered by everything else. Also got the foie gras fried chicken wings. Couldn't really taste any foie gras and thought the chicken meat was odd... didn't seem very wing-like. -- I had the Mu ramen and my boyfriend had the spicy miso. I liked it the Mu and it was different. It's a nice, hearty broth. But got too salty by the end. The spicy miso was unique, not really too spicy but flavorful. But can't really say it was better than other ramens. We agreed that we're still Ippudo fans first and foremost.

LIC now has a ramen place to go to without having to cross the bridge or tunnel.  And that is all it is.  Ramen without egg is $16. $2 extra for an egg.  Ordered Mu Ramen and Spicy Miso and was unimpressed.  Had to shell out $2 for egg which comes standard in most, if not, all ramen restaurants in Manhattan or Astoria.   With all due respect to those who give this place a 4/5 star, there are much better value options elsewhere, meaning $12-$15 ramen that tastes closer to Tokyo ramen than westernized food.  Not worth the trip but at least an alternative to Queens/North Brooklyn residents.  For the same price, Ippudo and Momofuku offer more authentic ramen, the same wait time and booze.

First off, can I give a shout out to the amazing attention to detail?? So much thought has been put into the layout, the design, all the way down to the plating of the food and dishes used. Now this could be brushed off as all fluff and no substance in another place. But these seemingly minor details are an merely an extension of Mu Ramen's food - the depth and flavor of the broth, the perfectly paired and cooked noodles, the perfect complements of the condiments. It's these "minor" details that truly distinguish Mu Ramen in a league of its own. Now onto the food: - Chicken wings stuffed with foie gras I would describe how insanely juicy and most and succulent those wings are, but c'mon -  if you're a normal human being, just seeing "chicken wings" and "foie gras" in the same sentence should be enough to make you run to over there right now. - Chicken Ramen I've tried the spicy ramen, the tonkatsu and the chicken and quite honestly, I can't tell you which one I love the most. One of my life's major dilemmas - which of Mu's ramens is your favorite S?? Don't...don't make me choose!! I..can't...do..it...AHHH! In all seriousness though - you can't go wrong with any option. When I ordered the chicken ramen, I was certain nothing could replace my love for Mu's spicy ramen. Upon first bite, I realized that the chicken ramen is mind-blowing. Life-altering. I have always been partial to spicy ramen but after tasting Mu's chicken ramen, my world has been thrown upside down. Now I'm not sure of anything in life anymore. - Truffle topping Although a luxury, not a necessity, if you have some change to spare, I'd recommend it without hesitation. The truffle doesn't have a particular taste; rather, it's an umami agent that heightens the flavors to another level. Do you need it to say it's one of the best bowls of ramen you've ever had in your entire life? No. But let me tell you, the truffle was like ramen deliciousness on steroids. So will I get it again? Hell to the YES! Finally some thoughts on the price: Mu Ramen is priced on the same level as Ippudo and in my opinion, rightfully so. When one goes to Mu, Ippudo, Totto, Ivan, they go for QUALITY. Let's be honest, we can all have some amazing ramen right at home - it's called instant noodles. But obviously, there's a major difference in the quality, taste and experience. So if you're just looking to have a cheap meal, I'd recommend Neoguri or Demae Itcho. If you're looking for something special, go to Mu. You'll be in ramen nirvana for sure.

I consider myself a ramen connoisseur, having eaten ramen all over Japan in Hokkaido, Fukuoka, Fukushima and all over the U.S. and I must say the ramen here is hands down the top 3 ramen experiences I've ever had. I first heard about Mu Ramen through my friends who wouldn't stop talking about it after visiting, so I decided to check it out and see what the hubbub is all about. Upon entering the restaurant, I felt a sense of comfort and well being, now I'm not one to usually spout off hippie metaphysical rants but the decor and aroma of broth really got to me. I ordered the U+I which was amazing with the perfect combination of uni, spicy tuna and rice. The Okonomiyaki was also equally amazing. This was definitely what I needed before slurping up my bowl of spicy miso ramen. The spicy miso was very well balanced betwen the noodles and the broth. The broth....OH MY GOD THE BROTH! It had so much depth that I felt my spoon was more like a submarine than a eating utensil. It becomes apparent when someone puts in a lot of work and passion into their food, and here at Mu Ramen it's obvious. The staff is incredibly friendly and knowledgeable. I will definitely be going back! Oh and those yelpers complaining about the ramen being "expensive" c'mon seriously...do you know how much work is actually put into making good quality ramen like the ones they serve here? Just making the broth takes roughly 20 hours of actively stirring and attention. You are getting what you pay for. I'm usually pretty good about documenting my experiences with pictures but I didn't any this time because I was too busy pigging out on the delicious food.

Mu Ramen was voted #1 ramen in NYC by the New York Times while it was a popup. A few months later, they opened their first real restaurant in Long Island City. I decided to pay a visit as I love ramen and have journeyed all over NYC in search of great ramen. I always say that The Religion of Ramen has different sects -- and whether or not you will like Mu Ramen depends on which sect of The Religion of Ramen you belong to. Do you prefer pork (tonkotsu) or chicken broth? Spicy or regular? Tons of toppings? Thin or thick noodles? More al dente or less? Their appetizers are a mix of standard Japanese fare -- shishito peppers, edamame -- along with more modern appetizers -- foie gras and fruit compote stuffed chicken wings, uni with spicy maguro over rice, and more. I ordered the former; who could read foie gras stuffed chicken wings and say no? It was definitely a very unique experience: juicy, decadent, well-balanced. It was also strange but I enjoyed the adventure. I ordered the Mu Ramen (the classic) along with both renditions of their egg (sous vide as well as seasoned soft-boiled). The seasoned soft-boiled "nitamago" is the traditional egg that comes with ramen, and their version of it was spot on. The yolk was barely set, and the white was seasoned and firm. Their "sous vide" version was a strange sensation to behold as a topping on ramen (a bit too embryonic) but I think it would've pleased modernists (you know who they are, the chemists with rototaps, centrifuges, spherified olives, and so forth). The food was well-executed and delicious but personally I prefer more al dente noodles. The broth had depth and oomph, and at least one server winked at me as I guzzled every last drop of my bowl. Pros: Delicious food Good selection of modern and classic appetizers Modern appetizers are interesting and exhilarating to eat Cons: Some of the items and toppings are a little too modern if you are a purist Noodles are less al dente Only 3 types of ramen Can be pricey, especially if you opt for white truffles as a topping Long wait No alcohol Cash only amendment: One more thing I'd like to add is a point about the service. When I asked for the check, the server was gracious enough to ask me if I didn't enjoy the wings because I only ate about half the appetizer. I was just too full to finish the decadence that it was. But that was a very personal and nice touch!

I am an avid noodle lover. If I didn't hate the idea of having to choose a favorite food, some may say noodles were my favorite food. I had never gotten a chance to taste Mu Ramen when it was a pop-up but as I started paying more attention to the LIC food scene I was avidly following the rumors/news coverage for the highly anticipated opening of its standalone shop. As I didn't exactly want to wait hours in the cold, a friend and I both started avidly calling the reservation number at 3pm and heard busy lines galore! I lost hope around 3:30 but when my friend tried again randomly at 3:45 he managed to snag a reservation for 6:45. So if at first don't succeed, try try again! The interior of the restaurant is very earthy chic (hate myself for using those two adjectives together but you'll agree when you see it...) The walls are wooden and there is a large geometric by asymmetrical wooden table in the center with an open terrarium of sorts in the center. (Terrariums are so hot right now! Perfect for my future food Instagram I thought as I walked in. I wish I were joking...) The right side of the restaurant had some shelves with interesting food related literature. In the back there was an open style kitchen and 5-6 bar seats I believe. We had both done extensive research on the menu before going and were prepared with what we wanted to order. We decided on the U&I  & the Okonomiyaki for appetizers to share, I ordered the Tonkotsu  & he the Spicy Miso. The U&I came out promptly and it lived up to everything I had read about in the press and on yelp. It's awesomely creamy and getting a bite with the maguro, roe, and rice and fresh wasabi all together was just amazing. I actually hadn't had sea urchin in a while before that and it really was the perfect way to rekindle my love. I actually thought the portion (though small) was the perfect amount as an appetizer. We're about to slurp down some very hearty ramen people! I was less impressed with the Okonomiyaki but that could just be because I'm not a general fan of the dish itself. Or any dishes that melt together sweet and savory in fact... I would have to say it's better than any I've had before but I wouldn't order it again. When the two ramen bowls came - I was beyond excited to dig in. One of the chefs came by and freshly squeezed (not sure if this is the right way to describe it) the sousvide egg into my friend's spicy miso. I had what I think was the Seasoned Egg - hard egg whites and soft yolk with my tonkotsu. As we both began eating, we pretty much ceased all conversation other than to say "holy crap this is good". I'm a sucker for a great tonkotsu broth and this one at Mu is probably one of the top I've ever tasted. And this is without any chili powder/chili oil/any other additional seasoning I usually throw in at other places. The Charsu pork was just the right amount of fatty that I didn't hate myself for loving it.  It wasn't too complicated with random ingredients thrown in like many more modern ramen places try to do. I tasted some of my friend's spicy miso broth (before he could finish it all up!) and it also tasted very good. The only thing is I wasn't sure how I felt about the "thicker" more udon like noodles in the spicy one. The noodles in the Tonkotsu were perfect - I would say between thin and medium and just the right amount of chewiness that it had flavor and didn't just melt in your mouth. Mu Ramen - 5 stars. No surprise here. Cash only - and not exactly cheap. Appetizers ran from around 15$ I believe and Ramen from 15-20$ from what I can remember (eggs are extra!). But worth it!

I've been waiting anxiously for Mu to open since enjoying a meal at the pop up. I went there recently with my wife, brother, and friend. We called to make a reservation at 7:30, arrived and were seated at the counter by 7:45. Before we get into the details of the food, let's talk about the service. The only way I can put it is that it felt like I was in the home of the chef. Josh and Heidy made small talks with us and made sure our water was always filled and food was up to their standards. We started out the U & I. After trying this at the pop up and falling in love with it, we couldn't start a meal without this. We also didn't want to share, so we got 4 of them so we could each get our own =) We continued the appetizers with Okonomiyaki(scallion pancake with smoked trout) and a rice porridge infused with Uni and Truffles, extremely rich and delicious. I think this was a temporary special as I don't see it on their website. Onto the ramen...we ordered two of the Spicy Miso and two of the Oxtail Ramen. I was extremely curious to get the Oxtail ramen since this wasn't on their popup menu. I was not disappointed. This broth was so rich and tasty, let's just say despite how full i was from the apps, I managed to slurp up all of the broth. My wife and friend loved their Spicy Miso, though this wasn't a surprise since this was their favorite from the pop-up days. I could type much more, but there isn't much more I can say that hasn't been covered already by the numerous reviews below. I'm happy for LIC and for MU that the transition from pop-up to brick & mortar  was a huge success. I look forward to coming back and trying whatever new apps and ramen Josh can come up with.

We saw the recent NY Times featured article for Mu Ramen and since it's in our next of the woods (Queens) we figured we would check it out. It's not common to find decent Ramen food in this part of the (Long Island) City, however, I am all for avoiding the Manhattan traffic uptown, downtown, eastside or westside to get a good bowl of RAMEN. We came on a Wednesday Dec 3rd and the popularity of this place was obvious. We had to wait about 40 mins for a table for 4 given the place was not big to begin with. Looking at the menu we noticed that prices were about $2-$5 more compared with places we usually go to but after tasting the food, we felt the difference was insignificant. We ordered Tebasaki Gyoza ( TO DIE FOR ), U and I, Mussels, and ramen of choice "MU RAMEN" for myself. - Tebasaki Gyoza - first thing that came to mind.  How the hell you going to stuff foie gras into chicken wings?  But they did it and it was TO DIE FOR!!!!  That foie gras just melted inside my mouth.  Too bad I had to spit out the bones or I would've swallowed that too. - U an I - Uni over rice - wish the bowl was a bit bigger for my appetite but I know my ramen is coming soon so good call on that - Mussels - typical; nothing special except for the soup base which tasted a bit like tom yang - Last but not least, MU RAMEN with the oxtail and creamy, bone marrow soup.  Glad I didn't order another U and I because soup just filled me up with joy.  Broth was hearty and that ramen was AL DENTE. Our waiter/hostess was extremely hospitable and friendly.  Water was always filled.  Everyone had a smile on their face.  Maybe it was that ramen hanging from my lip.  But these small gestures make such a difference in having a positive or negative dining experience. Kudos for their outstanding service at a small casual restaurant.

Finally!!! The wait is over. I've been trying to come here ever since they opened but decided to wait a bit to see what people says. Must say they do live up to the hype but I would give it a 4.7 stars rounding up to 5. My bf and I were lucky. we were able to get a reservation for 2 calling in on a busy fri night. They had time for us at 945. So we went a bit earlier and waited until a little past 10 for us to get seated. We were so hungry atm we ordered immediately. We got seated at the high table area and our server  was really friendly and nice that we had a bit of convo going on. Really like the vibe and ambience here. Not a huge place but they way they have it set up with the huge communal table in the middle really helps. For the two of us we started with the okomomiyaki, and the tebasaki gyoza. I was looking at their picture it looked like some of the gyozas were served with sauces but we didn't get them with it. It was really good and they fried it right before they serve U so the inside was really tender and juicy while the outside remain crispy and hot. I really like it and thought the 2 people's is just about right for the 2 of us. However maybe because we didn't. Had the sauce it came off to be a bit under flavor / blend for me. But def nothing to complain about the quality of it. As for the main course we both got a ramen for each. I had the spicy miso and he had the totally  chicken. Mine was real good and decided to go with the seasoned egg which made it even better. It was the right amount of spice and the soup base was rich enough and not too oily. The noodles were very good as well..as I said before very 'Q' texture. Just about how I like them. For the totally chicken. I was a bit hesitant about this since I've never had a chicken ramen so I told him to try it. And it turns out to be really good! Completely different from what I expect it. The chicken made the soul very rich and 'boney' if you know what I mean..similar to tonkatsu base I feel like, and brings the flavor of the dish out even better. While the ramen noodle they had were the skinny ones and they were good as well. Overall I def recommend trying this interesting dish. Their menu selection is quite small, which is good I think. Our total came down to about 80 with tips. Which I thought was a bit pricey for ramens. Since the appetizers portion are real small. But quality is def outstanding. I would come back again to try their uni!!! Staffs are all very friendly too which made the experience even better!

I'm not even really a ramen lover but I'm definitely coming back. The shishito peppers, gyoza, spicy miso ramen were delicious but OH MY GOODNESS THE U&I...my date and I started off trying to share one but as soon as it came out, we knew we had to order individual portions. So we did. The uni, ikura, tuna, wasabi...it's a divine dish. Next time I'm there, I may order 2 for myself.

Been here twice in the past three days. It's THAT good. Here's the rundown: Tonkotsu Ramen. Not tonkatsu, that's the fried stuff. Anyways, the soup was awesome, very drinkable with juuuuuuust the right amount of salt. Flavor is right at the sweet spot. Noodles are the thin Kyushu style that Hakata Ramen is known for. Menma was great, doesn't have that stinky smell like most other places' (coughippudocough), probably house made. Kikurage is kikurage, it's the same everywhere. My choice of add-on, Onsen Tamago, was a little cold, but that's understandable as they probably had to shock it with ice to stop the cooking process so that it remains gooey. The pork jowl was fatty, tender, not seasoned very much so it doesn't steal the spotlight away from the soup. I would eat a bowl of this ramen every day if I could. Mu Ramen. The broth again is the star of the show. Not overwhelmingly beefy or oily like one would expect from an Asian beef tail soup. Think of it as the beef version of Tonkotsu, nice and mellow, again very drinkable because of the perfect salt level. Seriously can someone just build a pipe that connects their stock pot to my apartment? The cucumber was unusual, but it works well with the soup, surprisingly. Kikurage is kikurage. The shredded cabbage didn't fit in at all, the crunchiness was way too jarring. The noodles were Kyushu style also, and I'm not sure it's the best noodle for this job. The beef brisket was pretty flavorful, I think it was salt-cured like corned beef. However, as good as it was, I don't think it played well with the soup. When I was eating that beef with the broth in my mouth, the two of them were fighting, instead of harmonizing. Maybe some sort of braised beef would work better? Idk Jesus I wrote a lot. I'm almost done I promise. Debasaki Gyoza aka Stuffed Chicken Wings. This one had a few flaws. One, the crust didn't have salt in it, the only source of salt was what the staff sprinkled on before serving. This lead to an unpleasant experience of bites without salt/not enough salt. Two, the Foie Gras didn't really work as the stuffing. It didn't bring much to the table, despite its price point. Three, the meat inside the wings were somewhat pink, probably due to the blood from the Foie. It didn't look all that appetizing. Mu Ramen by no means is your typical New York Ramen joint. The owner is not afraid to take risks and experiment. The first time I was there, a customer sitting next to me expressed his desire to slurp the mussel broth since it was so good. The owner then thought of a way to utilize that broth, by crisping up a ball of rice in a pan and gave it to the customer to soak up the broth. A year from now, all these dishes I described might not even exist in their current form anymore. Mu Ramen is not your run of the mill ramen joint, it's a constantly evolving Pokemon.
Went on the 2nd night of their pop up shop in LIC and it was fantastic. The broth has incredible depth with a slight muskiness to it. Delicious! Buns are to die for...

I really super enjoyed this meal. The scallion pancake was literally a pancake w scallions on top of it. It was sweet and savory. This appetizer wasnt doing it for me, it was trying to be too fancy, and not sure about the price for that tiny loaded pancake. Now the ramen: The mu ramen was creamy and delicious, and had the thinner kind of ramen noodles. The spicy miso was super delicious too, less creamy than the mu but also super flavorful with a nice kick of spice- came w the thicker/square/yellow colored ramen noodles that i love. The only downside was that the ramen itself was 18 bucks, which seems a bit steep for me for ramen, then again, im not a ramen connoisseur. So 32 for a soup and a baby pancake. Anyways, service was super nice. We made reservations for 4 for 10pm at 3pm on the dot, but showed w 7 and they were nice enough to seat us all. Split 4&3, but we were all fed and happy. The owner photobombed our pictures.

Everyone is giving 4 to 5 stars so finally got a chance to go. Don't believe the hype. U&I is great but the ramen and everything else is just okay.  The broth isn't that thick and the taste is sweet.   The pricing is ridiculous. Usually ramen is $12-14. They want $15 and up then plus pricey apps. I don't mind the cash only part but I have to bring a lot of cash to eat there. Lol. Conclusion is just a so so ramen place that is overpriced but getting hype since its in LIC.

New favorite ramen shop right here! We got the U&I, tebasaki gyoza, and "mu"ssels for appetizers. The U&I was a pretty standard but well executed take on kaisen don. The uni was fresh and creamy with no fishy taste, maguro was decent, and ikura was fresh as well, bouncy and not salty, as it should be. The sesame oil flavor came through in the nori as well, but was a good amount and not overpowering. The tebasaki gyoza (fried chicken wings stuffed with foie and brioche) was interesting, exterior was nice and crispy, almost like it was coated with fried cheese. The mussels came with a sauce similar to vietnamese dipping sauce, a nice tangy touch as opposed to the heavy hearty flavors in the rest of the meal. It also came with a fried rice ball stuffed with chorizo to be mixed with the sauce in the bottom of the mussels bowl, which I actually liked better than the mussels themselves. But enough with the appetizers and on to the real star of the meal, the ramen! The mu ramen was probably my favorite. You can taste the oxtail in the broth, and the half sour pickle, which tasted more like a sweet cucumber, stood out a lot as well and gave a nice refreshing contrast. The brisket was okay, but it paled in comparison to the charsiu in the tonkotsu 2.0 ramen, which was moist and tender, falling apart in your mouth. The tonkotsu broth was the most flavorful and creamy that I've had in NYC, amazingly without any miso or MSG (everything is MSG free). The spicy miso ramen came with thick noodles, which I liked better, but the broth was not as unique as the other two. The broth was barely spicy, and the chopped pork wasn't too special, but overall it was still a solid, balanced, tasty bowl of ramen.
