The servers were very friendly and gave an explanation for every dish that came out. Will definitely be coming back, assuming I can call again for 20 minutes to get a reservation (I called 115 times starting 3pm sharp for 20 minutes before I got through to make a reservation, at which point the earliest time available for 3 was 7:15). Definitely make reservations unless you're going alone, as the entire time there were multiple groups of people waiting in line (on a regular Monday night). The appetizers were worth a try, but next time I'll probably go straight for the ramen with extra toppings.

Not surprised to see the success of Mu Ramen ... had the privilege of dining on Chef Smookler's "experimental pop up".  For a guy that is NOT a fan of uni ... U&I was a really generous serving of some fresh and creamy uni.  The ramen I tried was the namesake bowl that started it all.  I know he labors over the flavors of the broth and it really shows.  Rich and flavorful mmmmmm ... the next time I am back in NYC, I will be sure to visit!
We went for burgers on a Sunday night, they were great and the fries were fabulous garnished with rosemary! It's a loud sports bar, but the food is great!

This is a great neighborhood bar and I'm so mad I just recently discovered it given I live so close. There are a ton of positives about this bar - really good bar food with nice variety (burgers, Jameson wings, fries, lobster mac - all great), decent prices and drink specials, friendly service, lots of TVs, two floors with plenty of seating, nice crowd (unlike some more trendy sports bars in the area). This is quickly becoming our go-to bar. You likely won't stumble upon this place given it's location on 28th but it is definitely worth coming by to grab some food/drinks to watch a game. If football (soccer) is your thing, this place is definitely for you.

This bar has plenty of TVs and the staff is great about making sure the game you want to see is showing. Plus their food is great. The caprese salad has fresh mozzarella and amazing balsamic. Their tofu burger is great, rosemary on the fries are great! The grilled veggies are delicious. I would also recommend the guacamole, polenta and steak. Great all around. When the upstairs is open I suggest going up for a little quieter area.
Simplest review yet, kick ass wings, chicken and waffles, great crowd and music.  Thank you Smithfield for making this easy!

Had a great time and solidly tasty food (fries, calamari, and BACON appetizers). Closing Dec. 31, 2013, due to landlord developing the building for other uses...hopefully they will open back up in a new spot!!!

I came here with an open mind not knowing what I was in for. The service is great. Waiter and server have a great and amicable nature! Arugula salad and lobster ravioli are phenomenal. They do not skimp on the lobster. Definitely a hidden gem!

I looked through a number of the reviews here, and it seems like the people who are disappointed are disappointed because of something pertaining to Groupon. I don't have any experience with that, but don't let Groupon deter you. This place is wonderful. La Fourno wasn't my plan tonight. I'd stopped by another Italian restaurant for my birthday late lunch/early dinner with a friend, and it wasn't open until 5. I was really hungry, and my friend said she'd heard La Fourno was good, so we walked down to South Street. We were greeted by two different people coming in and told that we could sit wherever we liked. We ordered the $7 whiskey sours in mason jars, and they were perfect. We both ended up getting the Baked Rigatoni, which was delicious. The sauce was perfect and had just the right amount of kick. The rigatoni were perfectly cooked. There was lots of gooey mozzarella melted on top of it (and ricotta within). The portion size was perfect as well, as was the portion:price ratio. Our waiter was great and checked in on us regularly to see if we needed anything. When we left, we actually joked that we felt like we were getting off of an airplane because a row of employees was essentially in a line and each one told us thank you and to have a good night. So for two of us to each get a mason jar cocktail and baked rigatoni, along with bread and salad, the total bill before tip came to around $40. I thought that was great compared to some other places. I will definitely go back to try some of the other dishes, as well!

Fantastic dinner in the upstairs room at La Fourno Restaurant last night.  Al and his team took wonderful care of us.  Our dinner and appetizers were terrific.  The mozzarella with peppers was very very good and the veal parm lives up to it's best in Philly title.  Our first time in the restaurant but it won't be our last.  Thanks to All the owner for a wonderful night.  Shamus was a fantastic server.  Try this wonderful neighborhood place.  You won't be disappointed.

La Fourno Ristorante Trattoria was amazing.  This was probably one of the best dining experiences I have had in a really long time.  I finished work with a friend and we were looking for someplace to eat on a Sunday night.  It was really by default because we didn't want to walk too far from the car and it was directly across the street.  It wasn't crowded but the ambiance was very quaint and cozy.  Lots of candles and great music.  The staff was excellent and the food was even better.  I ordered the lobster ravioli and she had the chicken Alfredo.  The pasta was fresh and the portion was phenomenal.  We had Italian margaritas which were the best Ive EVER had actually.  I cannot wait to go back.  I agree with some of the other reviews and groupon but that was not my experience at all!
Everything we've tried here so far has been really good.  I was impressed with the breakfast empanadas in particular.  Will be back to try the sandwiches.

I was about to write my review when I saw Stephanie H's review, and mine was going to be pretty similar. I've been to Stocked three times. I really wanted it to do well and succeed - the concept is great, the location is perfect for this neck of the woods, and it's a local young family (or families?) running it, which means I'd rather support it than a chain. However, it's just disappointing. The first time, I had a coffee and a pastry or muffin or something. That was fine, hard to mess up. The second time, my husband and toddler ate in and it was ok. Nothing mindblowing but fine. I do like that it's kid-friendly and there's a play area for children. The space is really dark in the back, kind of depressing. That time, I had the arugula/peach/prosciutto salad. It was decent enough to order again (see below), my husband had a VERY mayonnaise-y BLT and we got a kids meal for my daughter with a grilled cheese sandwich using extra sharp cheddar cheese. Tip: children don't generally like sharp cheddar cheese. Use mild cheddar or even American. I went back with my daughter to grab a quick lunch before running home for her nap. Prepared food should be pretty fast right? I ordered the arugula salad again, a piece of meatloaf, and an iced coffee. I was told that I couldn't be rung up until the meatloaf was weighed. My salad arrived next to the cash register and then the cashier/counter person rung up FIVE orders ahead of me. And by rung up, I mean getting all these people drinks, pastries, bagging everything up, financial transactions, the whole deal. All while my salad sat there sadly. When he'd finished helping everyone else in the free world, he decided to get my meatloaf. Then had to be reminded of my coffee. Meanwhile, people who came in after us were already leaving. When I asked why he helped everyone else before finishing our order, I was told it was "easier for [him] to finish all the other orders before getting to mine". This made no sense whatsoever. I could see helping other people while my salad was being prepared but it sat there, in plain sight, for about 10 minutes while everyone else got served. $25 later ($25??!) we were out of there and on our way. OK, so the saddest part of all: I got home and tucked into my itty bitty $9 salad only to find that it had literally -- LITERALLY -- less than a teaspoon of prosciutto in it. It felt like a bad joke. This place is way too expensive and not nearly dynamic enough to last. Which is sad, because I love local businesses that reflect the neighborhood. And to echo Stephanie, why call it Stocked when everything looks like it's been ransacked? Take a cue from Bklyn Larder (best food, best staff ever) and fill that case with delicious, irresistible things.

Simple, clean and elegant food. . .they really pay attention to the details.  I have been there several times, often by myself but sometimes with a boatload of friends, and I have yet to been disappointed.  The roast pork/broccoli rabe sandwich is the bomb!  My friend loved her arugula, grilled peach salad. . . the proscuitto really was a nice salty contrast to the sweetness of the peaches. All in all, a great addition to the neighborhood and if they get some beer in house, I might have to change my address.
Stopped in to grab a bite and coffee. It's a little pricey, but the quality of ingredients accounts for it. I'll be coming back.

I have three words for you: shrimp.and.grits. Okay, 2 more makes 5 words: french.fries. Possibly the best fries I've ever had. Really really good wine list. All this in a beautiful, lively, windows open wide corner on a Sunday spring afternoon on the LES. It doesn't get much better than that.
Best new place for fried chicken in NYC!!!

Southern comfort on the lower east side. Went for a casual brunch Sunday afternoon. We went around noon and had to wait about ten min for outdoor seating. The drinks were amazing I got mami taylor, if I remember the name correctly and it was great. The best was the chicken and waffles. I am an avid chicken and waffles fan so I don't like just any chicken and waffles. These were an eggs benedict chicken and waffles, the perfect combo of savory and sweat. So yummy. Also with the check they brought us dove dark chocolate so five more points for that. 100% recommend the derby if you want some southern style food and drinks.

Cant beat the quality of food for breakfast or lunch.... Ive made a point to try something new every time I come here, (aside from Fridays which are fully devoted to the best fish taco special I've ever had) and everything has been fresh and delicious. Whenever I have family or friends in town, I take them here even though I'm located closer to the other notable delis that New Haven has to offer. I HIGHLY recommend Zois, and the outside seating is a plus, as the great food draws a large crowd come lunch time.
Great stop for a sandwich when driving north from New York. Delicious freshly made sandwiches which are a meal in themselves. Reasonably priced and obviously a popular lunchtime spot for locals.
Favorite sandwich shop in New Haven. The #25, Cajon pulled  pork, is phenomenal. Try to grab a seat in the back patio during summer days. Limited vegetarian meals.

I love the authenticity of this place! LIC has been missing real Japanese sushi for a long, long time! I love getting a little bit of everything and they daily specials are proof that this establishment cares about its food. It is truly a neighborhood jewel!  They have lunch specials and take out as well! Also have a decent sake!
Finally! A great sushi restaurant in LIC. look no further. They are best in class and take great care in bringing high quality product to the customer. Thank you for coming to LIC.
Finally LIC has a great Japanese restaurant! Great service - great food. No need to get to Midtown east for my sushi fix.

Great atmosphere and surroundings although after a while hearing customer order numbers being called was an obtrusive noise. Food nothing special. Salad greens were from a bag and some were mushy. Stick to drinks only. At least the self-serve style meant I did not have to tip for sub-par food.

I first visited Oaxaca, Mexico, in 1972.  I fell in love with the culture and, especially, the food.  It was so different than the Tex/Mex or California/Mex we were all used to back then.  It was lighter, far more sophisticated, and clearly required more preparation and thought than mere tacos or burritos.  I've returned there often enough to become familiar with the food in Oaxaca, which I still love and now miss, because it has been more difficult in recent years to get there.   If you are looking for authentic Oaxacan cuisine, do not come to the Oaxaca Kitchen in New Haven.   This is not to say that the food is bad, but it is not authentic, despite reviews to the contrary. The Margaritas were expensive ($10) and watery.  Not nearly enough lime or tequila.  Beware of these.  They are 3/4 ice, with salt around the rim.   The Mariscada a la Parrilla Ensalada (seafood salad) was quite good.  The pieces of scallop, shrimp, and teeny-tiny bit of lobster (I think there was only one piece of each) were perfectly cooked  and the dressing was light and flavorful.  But the seafood was overwhelmed by a large pile of arugula, and a few cherry tomatoes, neither of which I have ever encountered in Mexico in more than 20 years of eating there.  Good to eat, but far from authentic.   The mole, on the other hand, was awful:  thick, overspiced, and heavy.  After a few bites the heat of the sauce became overwhelming, not even remotely softened by a little extra chicken broth or sweetened by the traditional chocolate.  And the chicken, which was drowned and nearly obliterated by this heavy sauce, was tasteless and without texture, sort of like spam.  In Mexico, the mole is decorated with a light touch of cilantro, green onion thinly sliced, and white cheese sprinkled over the top.  Not so here.  What was served was just a bowl of monotonous brown stuff, with the chicken/spam hiding underneath all of the sauce. Oaxaca, Mexico has a long culture and tradition of hand made, colorful ceramics.  The serving pieces at the Oaxaca Kitchen in New Haven are 100% white, in rather odd shapes, with no place to set aside a knife or fork.  This will seem petty to anyone not familiar with Mexican dishes, but it is simply a shame that a restaurant claiming authenticity would use dishes like this.  Ditto the loud music. Finally, we had a bad experience with glasses of wine, which were decidedly "corky" (with a mildew smell and taste).  When we complained to the waitress she returned with glasses of a different wine but rather pointedly told us that the bar tender thought the "corky" wine was "fine."  Again, a little disconcerting for a glass of wine, well, let's be honest, 1/3 of a glass of wine, that cost $9.00. It was the evening of Commencement Day.  No doubt the staff, and the chef, were exhausted; and perhaps the ingredients were exhausted, too.  But I found this restaurant noisy, inauthentic, overpriced, and completely unsatisfying.

Great place for upscale Mexican food. The guacamole is great, prepared table-side, and probably the best in New Haven (even factoring Geronimo's). The appetizer tacos are a great deal, but stick with beef or pork. The bistec steak is good as well as the barbacoa. The portions seem a little small until you realize there's a lot of free stuff they can give you like chips, salsa, tortillas, rice, and beans. They don't normally come with the meal unless you ask, which I didn't realize until the second visit.

I would like to write here that I enjoyed great service and food at Oaxaca Kitchen in New Haven, however this is not the case.  My wife and I recently went to the new restaurant for the first time to have a quiet drink and possibly an appetizer or two.  After seating ourselves at the bar we were quickly served complimentary chips and salsa.  After that it was all down hill.  There were no less than three servers and bartenders waiting on customers in the empty place (it was 7 and Memorial Day weekend hence why it was slow).  I watched for 15 minutes while the bartender stocked the bar, filled the ice buckets and chatted with the waitresses.  After about 20 minutes my wife and I decided to leave and go down the street to Geronimo where we received the normal EXCELLENT service there. To add insult to injury I left my keys on the bar at Oaxaca and went back.  A server said that SHE didn't find them and "she was there all night." Then said for us to call in the morning to see if anyone else found them.  HELLO they were my CAR keys, how the heck did she expect we get home?! Having worked in food service I would have asked every server and bartender if they'd found a set of keys.  We even checked back at Geronimo when finally my wife went back into Oaxaca and asked every other person there until the original bartender who never served us came up with them. While I may check the place out again for dinner to try something there this was a very BAD first impression.  Being from East Haven and living here for over 25 years I know the restaurants in the area are very competitive.  Hopefully this place will get its act together.

I went to eat at this place with my friend because i was dying to try it but i couldn't regret it more....It took ten minutes for us to get a menu we raised our hands a couple of time and the hostess who was in front of us kept ignoring us...when we finally got the menu, it took half hour to get a margarita and a coke? seriously  i can understand the food taking long  but a coke????....then an 45 min  later when we finally got our food it was good i can't complain about the food...but the manager personally went and asked every table how everything was except to us? i wonder why? he gave water to the people behind me and even though my glass was empty he didn't bother even asking.....i don't want to say we were treated bad because we were the only hispanics there in that room but i can't find an explanation for it because my money is worth the same as everybody elses......won't be going back there .........

Went to Sabor Peru last week based on the good reviews i read on here. My warning flags should have went up as soon as we walked into an empty place. You could literally hear a pin drop! However, this is never the determining factor, so in i went and sat. We ordered a Ceviche, a causa, a jalea, and tallarines de mariscos. The ceviche was good, the jalea was good. These two dishes were just middle of the road, nothing to write home about. The causa, which is pretty much like a cold mashed potato with different fillings (we had the shrimp). Done right, this simple dish can be delicious. Unfortunately for Sabor Peru, this fell way short of the mark. It was over saturated in mayonnaise which made it hard to eat and very unpleasant on the palet. The "highlight" of the meal were the tallarines, which is pretty much a peruvian lo mein. Again, it was not amazing, just the best dish of the four we were served. I can understand if this is your first time eating Peruvian food and you think it is delicious. The service was good, so i will give them that. However, that is only half the battle. With a little fine tuning, Sabor Peru could really have a prosperous future in Rutherford.

I visited M Wells Dinette today since this is its opening week inside PS1. Knowing that it's likely to be packed with its cultish hipster followers and the fact that the opening coincides with the annual art book festival at PS1, I chose to pay my homage to Hugue Dufour and his gang at an odd afternoon hour. The place was still very crowded and there was a long takeout line. However, don't get fooled. If you are there for dine-in service, just holler at one of the staff and they should be able to seat you right away. The offered menu was shorter than that of the original M Wells but it captures the essence of Dufour's French-Canadian cooking style nonetheless. I suspect the menu will keep growing as the new kitchen staff settles in their cutely designed PS1 space. The new dining space feels a lot like an old school classroom, filled with lines of communal desks and study chairs. Menu is written on big chalkboard on the side walls; and Dufour and his team work right in the front of the room. It almost feels like sitting in a 5th grade classroom only you'd be learning the art of M Wells' culinary creativity. I tried the beef tartar sandwich and hibiscus ice tea for lunch. Everything was fabulous and tasty. The beef tartar was just done right, with a below-market-price tag of $10. The beef was tender and fresh, with just enough dibs of homemade tartar sauce and all together sitting comfortably on fresh sesame brioche bun.  The hibiscus ice tea was brewed to perfection. Service seemed a bit chaotic today but keep in mind that this is its opening week.  I look forward to trying some more dishes in the next few days. Welcome back, M Wells!

Shame on me! I've lived in LIC since 2007 and never made it to the original M Wells. Oh well. Monday was Columbus day and fortunately me and friend both had the day off so we made it over for a late lunch / early dinner. We arrived close to 4pm and I think by then a few items had sold out (certain rows on the chalkboard had been erased). However, we were told that the tuna crudo "just came in" (what does that mean?!) and highly recommended, so we split that, the headcheese terrine, the blood pudding, and the fig tartin. Tuna crudo - SO GOOD! How refreshing to have a fish crudo that actually is not light or citrusy or laced with avocado! I've had some incredible raw fish apps (Marea and La Mar are amongst many that come to mind) and this one is definitely a stand-out. The fish comes in 3 thick slices placed adjacent so it appears as one slab of tuna. First of all, I love the thickness as that sets the tone for the other flavor elements that accompany it. There is some kind of creamy sauce (not spicy mayo), some fried crunchy things (shallots???), every so slightly bitter sprouts, black sesame seeds... you can actually taste how every component balances out the rest of the dish. Hearty and brilliant!! Terrine - points for cool presentation, and nice mix of flavors. Plus I love parmesan crispy things. Blood pudding - good, but my least favorite. Very heavy to eat. Came with a cabbage & bacon slaw and an apple puree. Fig tart - second most delicious thing after the tuna. I liked that the fig topping was not too sweet, not too gooey, and the figs were not cooked so much that they lost their original taste and texture. Flaky tart. Gobbled it up.

I love checking out new restaurants in Astoria and it's surrounding neighborhoods so when Elle P. clued me in on Salt & Fat we made plans to have dinner there over the weekend. Salt & Fat had their grand opening on Friday so imagine our surprise to find that they already had a small crowd waiting for tables on their opening weekend. I guess good news travels fast. The space was very modest, just a small rectangular room with booth seating along one wall and tables for two along the other wall. The walkway down the center of the room was unnecessarily wide so I think there must be a way they can rearrange their tables to get more use out of their space. The decor was simple, clean, and minimalist. Salt & Fat offers a strong, substantial menu of seasonal small plates featuring a globally-influenced American style, bringing to mind a comparison to Traif, Brooklyn's favorite baby last year. When we were seated, our waitress brought us a complimentary starter of POPCORN in a little brown bag along with the menus. yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… The popcorn is popped in bacon fat to give it a little something extra. Mmmm bacon... The two of us shared... YELLOWTAIL (with Italian speck, pickled jalapeño, citrus) - yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… This dish was a great way to start the meal, very refreshing and light. I thought the prosciutto slightly overpowered the fish, so I preferred to pair the yellowtail with the pickled jalapeño and the prosciutto with the grapefruit. SCALLOPS (with roasted carrot purée, truffled golden beets) - yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… I loved the combination of the buttery scallops, sweet carrot purée, and luscious veggies. The only flaw to this dish was that two out of the three scallops were just slightly overdone. BRAISED PORK BELLY TACOS (with pico de gallo, kimchi salsa, queso fresco) - yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… All of the Asian fusion tacos I've previously eaten used a soft tortilla, but to my delight Salt & Fat's taco used a hard shell. Love it! The pork belly was perfectly braised and just fatty enough, and together with the accompanying fillings provided a flavor-packed mouthful. I was also happy to see more of the pickled jalapeño on the side. SHORT RIB BUNS (with pickled cucumber, apricot mustard) - yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… Like the scallops dish, there was a small issue of one of the short ribs being slightly overdone. Other than that, the buns and fillings were very tasty and well-balanced though perhaps not as inspired as some of the other dishes. OXTAIL TERRINE (with caramelized onion purée, roasted mushrooms) - yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… Out of all the yummy dishes we had, this one was my favorite. The oxtail terrine was succulent, and the onion purée had a lovely smokiness that brought out the nutty flavors of the shimeji mushrooms. Each bite was rich, savory bliss. LYCHEE PANNA COTTA (with plum vinegar gastrique, yuzu buttermilk sorbet) - yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… The panna cotta was perfectly creamy. The lychee flavor was bright but not overpowering and went well with the mellow gastrique. The yuzu sorbet provided a welcome tartness though it was on the icy side. Sunnyside is lucky to have this new neighborhood gem. The restaurant was surprisingly on the ball for their third night. Dinner service ran smoothly and the servers were friendly and knowledgeable. Elle and I were especially impressed with their timing. Our dishes were brought to us one by one, the next dish following just minutes after the previous dish was taken away. The Chef de Cuisine (or was it our server?) even arranged our dishes from lightest to heaviest. Little bottles of Biofeel* yogurt drink came with the bill. yelp.com/biz_photos/pZ9s… I grew up with this stuff so I thought it was a cute, nostalgic way to leave one last good impression. I was really impressed and satisfied with Salt & Fat's creative, delicious, and beautifully-presented food. At last Queens has it's own "Traif-like" darling. If only it were located in my part of Queens! *Biofeel (Korean version) AKA Yakult (Japanese version) AKA Yang Le Duo (Chinese version) **Cash only for the first week. ***No alcohol yet.

People seem to think that Salt and Fat is positioning itself to be the vanguard for Brooklyn chic and its presence represents the first sign of the hipster apocalypse in Sunnyside. Even though I'm the sort of traitorous Queens bastard who'd be at the drawbridge throwing a ticker-tape parade for my new Williamsburg overlords, fortunately for Sunnyside lifers and unfortunately of this sole resident who refers to my town as "North Greenpoint" (I don't actually do this, it's just a joke!), Salt and Fat is less a beacon of unrepentant pretension than it is an affordably priced, entry level, fine dining establishment. Okay, so perhaps there were some signs that might furrow some brows. Our MPDG (Manic Pixie Dream Girl for you weirdoes who are not in love with Zooey Deschanel) Asian waitress channeled her inner-Amelie. The ironically casual complimentary bacon fat popcorn was served in adorable mini brown paper bags. And the music selection seemed to be purposefully esoteric unless Dan Deacon and Architecture in Helsinki has more of a Queens following than I think. But before you start asking yourself, "How much more is this poser going to namedrop in this review?" you're in luck because I'm provided with no more ammunition. The décor is wonderful and a stark contrast from Queens Blvd. It was minimal and simple without seeming sterile and it managed to feel homey despite the unclutteredness. Unlike many other restaurants in Queens, visibly absent were any sort of cultural themes. Like the food it served, it was thoroughly New American although my authority on interior design is probably as meaningful as a cat's opinions on cubism. Now before I start describing the meal, contrary to my enthusiasm for watching Top Chef I should warn you that I don't have the most sophisticated of palates, particularly for "New American cuisine". A poster of my personal food pyramid would just be a picture of a platter of Chicken n Rice from the nearest halal cart (no white sauce, extra hot sauce). But not everyone can afford to be a foodie, and this is where Salt and Fat fits a nice niche. While it isn't food cart priced, at $7-$11 for "small plate" dishes, it's a chance to try some more delicate dining at a very reasonable price. Aided by the very helpful wait staff (all two of them), my dining companion and I picked out; -Yellowtail (Italian speck [prosciutto-esque...I had to ask], pickled jalapenos, citrus). I actually wish this had more of a flavor kick to it. I was excited for the pickled jalapeno but barely tasted it since it was sliced thin like how Pauly from Goodfellas cuts garlic in prison. And on the other side of the spectrum, I felt that the prosciutto was a bit heavy-handed and cut too thick to call it a Yellowtail dish. -Scallops (Roasted carrot puree, truffled golden beets). Pretty good, I'm not actually a huge scallop fan, but if I was in a booth and alone, I would have licked that carrot puree and the beets clean off the plate.   -Korean BBQ Wraps (Hanger steak, pickled daikon, seasoned miso). Awesome! And somehow the cheapest dish at $7. Wrapped and lettuce and cooked a perfect medium rare, as someone who usually abstains from beef except for occasions such as these, I refused to eat the other serving for fear of relapse. -Crack and Cheese (fried potato gnocchi, cheese béchamel, bacon, and freebase cocaine). The gnocchi was great. Light and not at all doughy, it had a perfect sort of fry to it. Almost enough to call it a crust but you would never call it that. So, all in all, I had a great meal. Am I now going to turn my nose up against pedestrian food like El Vagabondo Taco Truck a few feet away after having had Salt and Fat? Hell no. But I definitely do appreciate what they have brought to Sunnyside and would recommend the experience to everyone!

How to seduce a foodie Whisper seductive things, such as salt, fat, and bacon. Oh, yeah, that'll get a foodie's mind going and soon moans of anticipation and pleasure will come out. Bring out delectable viands, impeccably prepared. And then your foodie is ready to succumb with an open orifice, all too willing to get stuffed. My friends and I had been drooling with anticipation over Salt & Fat and couldn't wait to go. On opening weekend, Amy S. and I went to try out Salt & Fat. We were NOT disappointed. Salt & Fat is an Asian fusion small plate restaurant. The small plate restaurants had its zenith a few years back, but Salt & Fat demonstrates that this trend is not going away any time soon. Amy and I are both not fans of Asian fusion as we find that the food tends to be terrible, but Asian fusion, when done right, is an incredible symphony of flavors that presents familiar tastes in unexpected ways. For the most part, we were absolutely delighted what we got. We started with a yellowtail sashimi with Italian speck (a type of bacon), pickled jalapeño, and slices of grapefruit and oranges. Very fresh and pleasing to the palate. We both adored the thinly sliced pickled jalapeño as it gave a heat and bite to the fatty yellowtail. I really liked the speck. It had a very luxuriant feel in my mouth and the bright grapefruit cleaned the leftover oily taste. Perfect pairing. Next we had the scallops (3 pieces) with roasted carrot purée and truffled golden beets. One of the pieces, which I ate, was cooked perfectly. The other two were overcooked and were rather chewy and not pleasing. The perfect piece that I had was absolutely orgasmic with the purée and the tiny pieces of beets. Had all three scallops been perfectly cooked, this would have been easily my favorite dish. I think they must have put in some grated ginger with the beets, as golden beets are very sweet and the beets were not overwhelming sweet. I loved how even though the individual pieces were practically microscopic, they still had a toothy bite and were not mushy (so easy to do with tiny pieces). The carrot purée was so creamy and decadent tasting. Although all three have a sweet component to them, this was not a sweet dish. It was balanced to have a sweet feel, but still be a light savory dish. Then we had braised pork belly tacos with pico de gallo, kimchi salsa, and queso fresco. Ah, the Asian taco. Very fatty pork belly (so soft that it was like eating softened butter) that was complemented by a crunchy hard corn shell. You needed a crunchy aspect to this dish, otherwise everything would been the same texture. Next the short rib buns with pickled cucumber and apricot mustard. Delicious short ribs, but I noticed that the edges were overcooked. I would have liked more of the mustard (I barely tasted it). These buns can give Momofuku's buns a run for their money. The favorite dish of the night was the oxtail terrine (with caramelized onion purée, and roasted mushrooms. It was not a pretty dish (geometrically it was very lovely) because it was all different shades of brown. The dark brown square of terrine atop fawn mushrooms with a taupe purée, but the taste was AMAZING!!!!!! The next day, Amy and I couldn't stop talking about the terrine. It was a really tender unctuous meal that made us stop and forget where we were. Heavenly. The mushrooms were perfectly roasted, tender, but still with a toothy give. The onion purée was a wonderful foil to the meat, as the umami flavor was heightened. Lastly, we had the lychee panna cotta with plum vinegar gastrique, and yuzu buttermilk sorbet. After the terrine, which was a heavy and somewhat oily plate, we needed a light, palate cleansing dessert. The lychee panna cotta with the sorbet did the trick. Loved the delicate flavors. It was perfect. We were there on opening weekend and Salt & Fat had been open for three days. Already it had a huge crowd of people. We had to wait about 40 mins for dinner when we showed up because we had mistakingly thought no one knew about this place (and who the heck lives in Sunnyside???). Oh, no, we were so wrong, but being wrong never tasted so good. Even though they had been barely open, already they were serving like pros. Although we ordered the plates randomly, the plates were brought out lightest to heaviest and they were perfectly timed. We were blown away by the service. Each plate was brought out one at a time. As soon as we were done, the plate was whisked away and a couple minutes later, a new one appeared. This type of timing only comes with practice and experience and yet they were able to do on their third day (and with a full house!!!!). The decor is a bit lacking, as it seems slightly sterile, but the wonderful food and great service (and dim lighting) help you overlook whatever slight perceived flaws there may be. Salt & Fat, mmm . . ., more please.

I'll give it a 3.5 for now but it definitely has potential.  It's nice to see a place like this in the neighborhood; Queens needs to step up their game in the food department.  The wait was maybe 5-10 minutes on a Saturday night which was not bad at all.  Staff was very friendly and attentive. And now the food: Yellowtail- Served with Italian speck, pickled jalapenos and citrus; was very fresh and worked well together.   Short Rib buns- I love the bun but thought as  whole they were kind of plain jane.  Didn't taste much of the apricot mustard. Oxtail Terrine- My favorite of the night.  Perfectly cooked, the roasted mushrooms were great and the caramelized onion puree added just the right amount of sweetness to the dish.   Braised Pork Belly Tacos-  This was the item I was most looking forward to.  Wish the pork belly had been crispier.  The kimchi salsa was good but needed a bit more kimchi.   Whole Roasted Branzino- I did not like at all.  The fish was mushy rather than flaky.  Wish the skin had been crispier especially since it was cooked in bacon fat. Complimentary popcorn- Popped in bacon fat you can't go wrong. Rice Krispie (two big squares) with Marshmallow Ice Cream-  The ice cream was good but the treats could have used a bit more marshmallow when they were being  made. The place definitely lives up to the name because salty and fatty is exactly how I felt when I left.  Menu needs a few more items but I'd be back in a few months for another try.

The best part of this place is the friendly and attentive hostess. Our server was TERRIBLE. It took about 20 minutes before anyone came to our table after we were seated. Finally, the server brought over water and then she ran off before we could ask her questions or give her our order. The food is OK. Nothing spectacular and while it is mostly "small plates" I never like spending $50 on dinner and leave hungry. The scallops dish (too small to even be considered a real appetizer) ($10) was the best tasting thing we ordered but it was only 3 small scallops on the plate. There aren't that many choices of menu items and the ones they have is not worth the $.

The Bao is a nice place. Great ambiance. A menu with many options but dishes stereotypically named. In my opinion, if you want to be taken seriously in the culinary world, you have to stop calling stuff "Kung Fu Chicken". The tripe was damn good. Packs a lot of flavor with peanuts, chili, and cilantro. However, if you don't want to take a volcanic dump, you should skip. The xiao long baos were tiny but good. Skin is as thin as a Durex ultra thin condom. One little poke and the bag breaks. Scallion pancakes looked like a crepe pizza. Didn't taste the scallion and wasn't really "fried" enough. Stick to Shanghai manor for the absolute best. The Shanghai pan fried noodles were now the typical "pan fried noodles" that you'd be accustomed to. It's another style with udon like noodles but still extremely good. I'd come back in a heartbeat to try the rest.

The Bao is at a great location (right above  Spot dessert bar)! Compared to typical Shanghai food that you'd find in Chinatown, this restaurant is a mix between traditional and exotic foods, with their Wasabi Xiao Long Bao and Super Spicy Xiao Long bao, which you can't find anywhere else! Really great decor and just an overall awesome atmosphere.

Just opened! I came in today and coming back over the weekend to indulge in my love for the xiao long baos. Really reminds me of my childhood - the meat is firm, the soup is amazingly light, and the skin is just thick enough to keep it all together. I need to try the other main dishes, but I can literally eat 2 dozen of these. The Bao is a welcomed addition to the neighborhood full of food and will become a mainstay in my weekly diet for sure.

The XLB is great.  The skin is very thin yet strong enough to hold all the soup and the very moist juicy meat.  Very creative with their wasabi, very spicy and chocolate XLB.  They have a great selection of some authentic Chinese dishes.  I love the salty egg with bitter melon and the eggplant with lots of spicy hot peppers. An awesome place.  I often go to chinatown or Flushing for XLB, but I would much prefer coming here because the ambience is nice and the restaurant is much cleaner.  I often judge the restaurant's cleaniness by their bathroom.

I am a picky, picky XLB consumer. This place is the best I've had in America -- far better than Joe's Shanghai. The tenderest, thinnest wrapper, but still strong enough that there wasn't issues picking the XLB up. The true test: the bit at the top that sometimes turns out doughy was perfectly cooked. Amazing. In fact, my friend commented that they could probably even use a thicker wrapper and still have it turn out well, and I concur! Now, the true test of XLB is, to me, the wrapper. This place passed with flying colors -- all other complaints (which I will of course list) are minor in comparison. My glass had a weird speck of something floating around -- they replaced it and life moved on. The meat in the XLB was a bit strange in texture; it was slightly flaky and chunky. Not the best filling I've ever had. We ordered the crab XLB, and only half of the XLB came with the roe on top. Finally, the XLB was /expensive/. It came out to 2$ per XLB (though we tipped on the higher side, since we only ordered one item). You'll have to decide for yourself if the price is worth higher quality XLB. UPDATE: The next day, I stopped by again. This time, we ordered both pork and crab XLB. The pork XLB filling is both better and cheaper, so win all around. (I just preferred the texture really.) Unfortunately, we also tried the mushroom soup, which was less of a win. Very strong MSG taste and mostly canned mushrooms. I suspect the way to go here is to go with pork XLB.

All waiters and waitresses here seem a little lost. The lady who took our order forgot to tell us that it takes half an hour to prepare XLB--we planned for a quick grab but spent a lot time waiting. I understand this place is newly open, so waitress' little mistake doesn't really matter. But after dining here, we all got SERIOUS FOOD POISONING. I have never suffered painful bowel like this. We are furious at the food sanitation level.

I wish I had more stars to give but this place was great !! The service was extremely in and attentive and the Decore is cool ... I would recommend the soup dumplings and the fried beef. I would def return !!!
great soup dumploings

I went to this place on a Tuesday night, and the hostess didn't even let me through to dine. I was in a group of five people, but it wasn't busy and I could see empty tables around the restaurant. She made us wait twenty minutes, which I would have  understood if the place would have been packed. We waited, and waited and finally forty minutes later she said oh just twenty minutes please. So we waited and finally left. After an hour I don't think I would come here to eat.I hope this place changed their staff because with service like that I don't know who would want to go.

My new favorite dumpling place. The Kung Fu Steamed Pork Dumplings and the spicy Steamed dumplings are the best! It's like a pop of goodness in your mouth. Pair it with the scallion pancake and you will be in heaven. No liquor license yet so bring your own bottle!

Went in to buy 1/4 lb. of pancetta.  I asked for less than 1/4, but was told that 1/4 lb. was the minimum.. OK with me.  The whole process took about 10 minutes.  When I got home I weighed the pancetta and found it was 3 1/4 oz instead of 4.  The heavy wax paper used to wrap the pancetta weighed the other 3/4 oz.  Shouldn't there be some kind of compensation on the scale to make up for this shortage of product?  I must say, the pancetta was delicious!

Both of the prior two reviews seem weird to me. Look, I came in b/c of the write-up in Serious Eats. Counter guy recommended the roast pork, smoked mozzarella, and wild mushroom sandwich (on foccacia). I get chills just thinking about that sandwich - I can't remember a better sandwich. Looks like a typical Italian deli, except for the blocks of cheese on top of the case, and the prepared food (looks better than the usual). The cheese seems to be well priced, but I'm no cheesemonger. I can tell you that sandwich was amazing, and I'll be back.

As an Italian expat living in NYC I often missed 'authentic' italian food. But not anymore! This deli has the best Italian cold cuts and cheeses in the neighborhood. The panini are delicious. The owner is actually Italian and the guy working behind the counter definitely knows his cheeses.

I've ordered from here pretty consistently since my first time last December. I haven't ordered the spring rolls again, as they really weren't great, but I have ordered the chicken satay many times. I love the peanut sauce and cucumber relish they come with, and the chicken is tender and flavorful. Some satay can get dry, but this chicken is really good. I usually order the drunken noodles with chicken, as they're the best I've found available for delivery in New Haven. (Bangkok Garden's drunken noodles are better, but that place isn't on the campusfood.com site.) Anyway, this time I thought I'd change it up and get the spicy basil chicken, which was a stir fry of chicken, onions, tomatoes, basil, and peppers. It was good, but the sauce was really, really watery. The chicken and veggies were basically in a pool of watery sauce. It tasted ok, but I don't think I'd order it again. Maybe I've found the one decent thing on the menu at this place, in the drunken noodles. I do think this place has a good selection, and the delivery is fast. And they deliver Thai iced tea, so there's that.

I regularly have Thai iced tea, fried rice and drunken noodles here. There can be a bit of a language barrier sometimes. A couple of times after eating here I've felt a bit weird. Best to double-check on all of your ingredients if you're a celiac. Very calming atmosphere! Sitting in this place always makes me feel serene and peaceful. Very nice people, also.

BBQ is not bad at all.  The value is ok, however, there are some good all-you-can-eat rib places, like Big Ed's BBQ, that have better fresh ribs at a better value.  If you are not an all you can eat type, than Famous Dave's is not a bad deal.  Go for the "trash can lid" combo, with a nice mix of everything.  Some of the sides are just ok, but the corn bread muffins are really good (much better than Boston Market.) The sauce is standard, but good.  There are these places all over NJ, so in a pinch, when your not cooking at home for July 4th. or Labor Day, this is a nice option. They used to have good coupons (like they'll pay your toll, if you come over the bridge) but we have not seen those of late.
nice feel to the restaurant.  but $9 for an 8oz mimosa just threw me off this place.

Fresh Salt is very small, but has creative food and a good vibe. Only slightly off the beaten path, Fresh Salt is in an old fish market building. I came with my family on a Saturday night before the nearby outdoor movie (free popcorn, a Men In Black impersonator, fun times). They don't have wait staff after four, so we ordered at the bar and had the food delivered to our table. I had a really solid pork sandwich and enjoyed nibbling on everyone else's food too. Not crowded, not loud. A little outdoor seating is available. Overall a solid choice!

During a lunch break my co-worker and I enjoyed a nice, quick lunch out front of PYT. of course I had to try the Donut Cheesesteak Burger... AMAZING! I am very picky when it comes to food but being from philadelphia I had to try it and enjoyed every bite! Don't forget the delicious fries!! During our lunch we even got the chance to meet the general manager. She was friendly and just as excited as we were for our first visit. She even had our waiter, Bob, bring us each a milkshake on the house! I had the delicous, one-of-a-kind Bacon Peanut Butter Milkshake while my co-worker had the brilliantly decorated Birthday Cake Milkshake! The milkshakes were perfect in thickness, I didn't have to dig for all the goodies at the end either because it came with an extra wide straw! (that all may sound kinky but hey, PYT had my taste buds in a million different directions :) ) CAN'T WAIT TO COME BACK! Thanks for the great dining experience during such a short lunch break!!! OUT DID YOURSELVES!

Stopped here for some post-work beers and food with Mir yesterday evening.  We ordered burgers because it was National Burger Day and Mir thought it would be appropriate.  When the waitress returned, she handed us plates containing ground beef patties sandwiched between two slices of bun and other fixings, with sides of waffle shaped French fries.  You wouldn't think something that is mostly holes could be very dippable, but I suppose everything worked out okay.

The paper towel dispenser dispenses a more than adequate amount of paper towels. Burgers are obviously the best in Philly. I would definitely recommend this place to a friend. Friendly staff and bartenders. Always a rotating bottle/can selection. Adult milkshakes are sublime, had the bacon peanutbutter one, perfectly crafted.
I have eaten here once a month ago. The service was horrible. Waited forever to order, everyone's dishes came out at different times, rude service. I left zero tip, and I have the right to do so.

As a resident of Northern Liberties for the past 4 years, I've been here numerous times and can say the food quality and customer service has degraded significantly since PYT's menu items started gaining publicity/fame for their shock factor.  Years ago, this was a fun place to come in the neighborhood for a guilty/cheat meal.  Over time, it has lost its charm, the dishes are sloppily composed and served, and the food doesn't stand up to the quality of other restaurants you can go to in the area and around Philadelphia.   Beyond the overstated opinions about the customer service (which I can confirm has  been slow and lacking), the crowd here now seems extremely rowdy and immature, and it's impossible to sit in either their indoor or outdoor dining areas without being disrupted or annoyed.  Not that I expect a burger joint to be a classy dining spot, but I think an average level of professionalism should be upheld so you don't attract the wrong type of clientele. As someone who used to brag about this place to non-Philadelphians, I will no longer be bringing my friends here.  PYT has left a bad taste in my mouth and I'm not a proponent of what it's transformed to stand for.

I went to PYT several months back and I'm not typically the kind of person to write a poor review for a restaurant, but after this most recent credit card tip debacle, I will share my PYT horror story as well. We were one of three tables in an entire section assigned to one sever. It took her 30 minutes to even bring water, another 45 minutes for drinks, and I'm not even going to get into how long the wait for food or additional service was. The couple next to us waited almost an hour before they were even given water. The last straw was when our party decided to make things simple and just order PBR's for the table. There were 3 of us, and we waited almost 30 minutes (again, they weren't busy at all) and then our waitress only sets down two beers and walks away quickly while I tried again and again to get her attention. At that point, I went and talked to the manger who acted like a total douche bag and finally said, "I will make this right on your tab I assure you". When we got the tab, he had deducted $3.00 for the missing beer, that's it. At the end of our meal, my girlfriend at the time, who is a GM for a major restaurant, decided that we should let the owner know about how his employees were treating the customers. We asked for the manager's business card and he made us wait 25 minutes at the front desk just to tell us he was out of them. Furthermore, when we asked for his name, HE WOULDN'T EVEN TELL US!!!!! We ended up leaving zero tip for the first times in our lives (we usually tipped EXTREMELY generously, sometimes even 30-40%) but I will tell you what, if they had posted my credit card information and tip, I would have been pissed as well. In closing, poor food, shittier service and a complete refusal to do anything about it. Fuck you PYT, I had the worst service in my entire life when I went to your restaurant and I sincerely hope you close immediately.
This place sucks!!! Horrible food and even more horrible service! I nor anybody I know will ever eat here again. Hope this place goes belly up soon!

Food was ok, service was horrible.   I would never go here again.  Not worth the hassle.   Not sure why you have a wait staff when the customer has to get up for everything.   Next time, just leave me a pitcher of water.  (In town for baseball game)

Unlike some posts from 3,000 miles away, I have actually been here a few times and live within driving distance. The food is good, the drinks made with consistency, and the wait staff are very attentive. There is a wait time though, so be prepared. Very popular place. I always tip generously and have no qualms if they post my receipt. It's a testament to one's character, if you catch my drift.

Not only is the food great, but the entire experience is a lot of fun! Some nights they have djs and often have drink specials, but I usually go just to eat. Their special burger range from unique to an ultimate disaster(in a good way), and that's part of the fun. If you want, they have plain hamburgers. Care to get a little crazy in your food choice, you can get a hamburger covered with cheesesteak and topped with a bun made out of donuts! hahahahaha My favorite burger of all was their great american cookout burger(I think that's what it was called). It had EVERYTHING ON IT. A burger with relish, ketchup, a hot dog, potato salad, chips, and it was amazingly good! They also sell milkshakes that are thick and really good. They're a bit expensive but I can see why due to the thickness and real ingredients. Oh-and if it's an option get tots instead of fries!
The fact that people are posting back reviews because of something the restaurant did is uncalled for. Base it off their delicious food.

The only thing that is consistent with the "PYT" experience is the service.  While I've given this famed establishment several chances, I just can't get over the waits and the disinterested staff.  The special burgers are pretty good, but can't justify the inevitable frustration with the overall experience.
Terrible place to eat. Poor service, lazy staff. I went to eat a burger for lunch and it took a 45mins to get a bacon cheese burger. Unacceptable. I do not recommend and will not return.
I went here with my girlfriend and we had a great time. They have a ton of different alcoholic milkshakes, and the burgers are great.

All the press has reminded me I've never given PYT a review!  I'll keep it brief: -I've always been given excellent service -I've never been shamed for ordering one of their intense veggie burgers (enthusiastically encouraged, in fact!) -Food has been delightful- BF loves every meaty burger he has tried, and I was shocked by how much we liked the fried pickles! -Awesome happy hour deals! Bad service deserves 10% tip.  Less than that is stealing.  And PYT has never, in my experience, warranted less than a 20% tip.  Sorry for jerks, guys.  Keep up the good work :)
The service is awful and the food is a joke. Lackluster food combined with mediocre service is enough to keep me away...do yourself a favor and avoid this place
Best burgers in town! Great service!
Average  food at best. Just cheese and  goo.

Was here on a business trip years ago. The food is ok. Nothing too bad, but nothing to rave about either. When I read an article on the internet about how they publicized a customer's receipt because they were unhappy about the amount tipped, I decided to finally log in to write my review. When I was last here, the service was also atrocious. Slow and and unprovokingly rude. It took over half an hour for my drink to arrive and when I asked for a refill it was met with attitude, for no apparent reason.

My buddy lives right on 3rd street off Girard, so PYT is where we go whenever I'm there. The service isn't spectacular, but the food says it all. I don't have any complaints about the service, but it's a burger, so if I didn't have to wait as long as I had, then I would have 5 stars, but 4 stars should suffice.
Got the PYT Burger, very average, nothing to write home about.  The place was dead, but the music was blaring for some reason.  Lots of good restaurants in the area, I would avoid PYT.

I have only ever enjoyed every experience here. I have gotten a cheeseburger (on 4/20 when they charged $4.20, how considerate), enjoyed their amazing waffle fries many times, gone for their happy hour snacks and had buffalo chicken bites, and eaten the burger of the week Korean chicken scrumptious sandwich. All have been delicious, all have come quickly, and my servers have always been helpful, attentive, and kind. I have also gone here at night time for some beers and they have a wide selection of delicious craft beer at reasonable prices. GO HERE and overlook the silly recent events that are causing some slanderous reviews.

Went here this summer for the first time when my boyfriend came to visit because he loves burgers. Took awhile for anyone to notice we walked in but other than that the service wasn't as bad as I've read in past reviews. The restaurant didn't have very many people in it though. My burger was good but it's kind of far from university city to get to on public transit and not worth going when there are a million burger places to choose from that are way closer.

Made a special trip out here to try and get a straight answer on the food and the service following the dozens of BS reviews recently (both pro and con -- grow up, people)! The Firebird Chicken Sriracha was amazing. This is going to be a new haunt for me whenever I'm in Philly. Service was good, not great, but certainly not like it's being made out to be on here. The kid who waited on me was a bit slow but very courteous and I never felt like I was being kept waiting.

Ok, this place does some crazy things I've never seen any other burger joint dare attempt. Who puts a cupcake IN a shake? This place does. Who coats the whipped cream on a shake with bacon bits? This place does. Who puts chocolate on bacon? This place does. Who uses a DONUT for the bun of a burger? This place does. Overall, most of this stuff sounded disgusting at first, but after my daring guest ordered the donut burger special (which also included chopped Philly cheesesteak and cheezewhiz), I had second thoughts. Undoubtedly, taking just a bite of this burger was the unhealthiest thing I've even consumed, but it was so worth it. The sweetness of the donut blended surprisingly well with the other ingredients. I played it safe and went with the bleu cheese burger and can honestly say it's in my top 3. I loved the potato bun, the crispness of the bacon, the crumbliness of the crumbly bleu and the fact that I asked for my burger medium-rare and it came out accordingly. I'm also a huge fan of the waffle fries and noticed from the pictures on Yelp, the restaurant clearly went through some growing pains before getting to this point. Some of the photos from years past show sad bland potato chips while others show your standard, run-of-the-mill fries, though I can't tell whether they were fresh or frozen. Either way, I applaud the creativity and ballsiness of the menu. The only thing I didn't care for was the service. While the order itself didn't take long to come out, our server (at the bar) wasn't the most attentive. They also have outdoor seating with a very neat fireplace, and a unisex bathroom with more graffiti on the stalls than some murals in Brooklyn.

Wacky little burger spot in Northern Liberties. The Good: Awesome menu creativity! On any given day you might discover anything from a ramen burger to deep-fried lasagna burger, or a peanut-butter-and-jelly burger to a Hot Pocket burger. PYT's star player, though, is definitely the Krispy Kreme slider platter! Beef and chocolate-covered bacon piled onto toasted, sliced Krispy Kreme doughnuts. Mmm! There's nothing else quite like it. The Bad: Execution is hit-or-miss. The beef itself is excellent, but the toppings and sauces sometimes aren't quite flavorful enough. Fried chicken sandwiches are average, and PYT party fries are your run-of-the-mill loaded fries with bacon, cheese, and onions -- tasty, but otherwise unremarkable. Service was particularly slow, considering we were one of only two groups in the whole establishment. If you're feeling adventurous, give PYT a shot -- it's only a SEPTA ride away from Penn.

Just came back from dinner at Chef Mark Simmon's restaurant  KIWIANA.  What a delight!  Every single thing we ordered was delicious.  The restaurant is beautiful and charming with its generous use of woods, vintage wallpaper from New Zealand and friendly + attentive staff.  This was the best meal we've eaten in a very long time.  We can't wait to go back.  Highly recommend!

Ate here last night with some friends and we all loved it! What a welcome addition to the neighborhood! Mark Simmons even came over to our table to chat for a few minutes! I hope it won't be hard to get a reservation in the future. These are the items we had and they were all absolutely delicious: Slow poached baby beets with lavender goats' milk ricotta Horopito and buttermilk fried chicken with kale slaw and truffled honey Manuka- and marmite-braised baby back ribs with squash puree Kiwi Burger - N.Z lamb, fried egg, pickled beet with hand-cut fries Passion fruit and coconut cream caramel with dragon fruit sauce Milo molten cake with pepper berry cream fraiche We will be back soon!

The food here is absolutely incredible.  The chilled corn soup with some sort of spicy oil, plus super fresh avocados and a few kernels of popcorn, is the best summer dish I've had in a while.  But really, what I have to come back for again and again is the fried chicken with the spicy truffle honey.  It's just unreal how good the flavors are in this chicken. Kiwiana also just seems so special -- every detail of the place was chosen by Mark Simmons, the amazing chef.  It has a vintagey feel (down to the 1950s wallpaper), but one that isn't trying too hard -- everything about the place feels genuine and homey.  A wonderful addition to Union Street!

I got the Lox, Stock & Bagel Sliced Salmon Lox, Tomato,  Onions, Capers, Cream Cheese On a Bagel with a side of PJ's mashed potatoes. It was a decent portion but I don't think they give a lot of lox or cream cheese. I asked for extra cream cheese which helped made the bagel less dry. The bagel was toasted which I thought was really good because it's not toasted in most places. The service is kind of slow but they're friendly. I'd be back to try their other dishes. Overall I was pretty satisfied, just wish there was more lox in my bagel!

The staff was incredibly rude and showed no regret for how they treated us. The excuse from the female server was "sorry you're upset", which showed no self awareness on how she treated her customers. Even when one of the people from my group, who has incredible serving experience pointed out her flaws, she got defensive and made it seem like it was our problem. The "manager" was also rude and did not help resolve any issues with our service. The group of the staff all congregated at the front service table where you pay, where they were talking badly about our table for complaining. An extreme sense of arrogance from that place. I would never recommend it. My food was subpar at best.

The service here was, unfortunately, terrible. The server was rude, inattentive, and unprofessional. She seated us at a table for five set with three place settings - fine - but she didn't notice. We had to ask for forks and knives when our food came out. I asked for a fresh water glass (politely!) as mine looked a little dirty and she said nothing, just snatched it and walked away. I did not receive a new glass. She did not ask about our meals, smile once, or even give a friendly greeting, just came after we were done and dropped the check. We wanted to split the bill and she told us that this could not be done - we understood that was not her fault - but she was rude and condescending about how she conveyed this to us. We informed her manager that she had been rude. Moments after he left, she returned to the table to tell us that she was sorry we thought she was rude but that she wasn't rude. She went on to say that we only complained about her because we could not split the bill, which wasn't true, as we had discussed her poor service prior to getting our bill. We were shocked by the unprofessional behaviour displayed by her and her manager. I wouldn't return.

Although PJ's appears to be quintessential college town late night & breakfast diner, this place is definitely lacking in the customer service department. There were some things I did enjoy about PJs. The wooden tables are covered with the carvings of many previous patrons, which leaves a cool vibe and hometown feel. The food itself was good as well and I did quite enjoy my chocolate chip pancakes, eggs and bacon. However, the service itself was terrible. Upon entering we were asked by the manager to wait in a line outside the restaurant for a party of two, midday in 90 plus weather. I told the manager that my wife burned very easily and after walking the main st all morning we'd prefer to wait inside, out of the sun and completely out of the way. He then told us he wouldn't know what order to seat customers in if we didn't wait in line and again motioned for us to go outside. What?! I'm not waiting in line for the club, I'm waiting for some eggs! I've never before been asked, ever, to wait outside when there's plenty of room to stand out of the way inside. Safety and clear transit is one thing; I've been a waiter before and carrying a full tray while dodging people is not fun or safe. But there was plenty of room to stand inside. If other patrons were standing inside because they arrived first, then that is totally fine; we would have waited outside until they were seated to move inside to wait. But to automatically make people wait outside in a line is uncouth. I am even more disappointed if this practice is done purposely to drive up the "hype" of this Princeton staple. The remainder of the service was on par with our initial experience. I understand this is a casual place, but this was over the top. We watched our food, along with many others, sit ready for almost 10 minutes while multiple servers and manager joked around with each other and waiting for what appeared to be the only server working to deliver his plates. We'll certainly never visit PJs ever again.

Terrible service and food and adding to the pain are the expensive rates. I ordered dahi batata puri which costed me $6.38. It took them 20 mins to make a simple appetizer while there were barely any other customers. Now I finally get my dish and what I see is a big plate with the serving size of 4 puris. So basically each puri is $1.59?!Ridiculously expensive! I wouldn't have complained as much if the yogurt they used wasn't old and sour, almost starting to taste bad. When I told the guy at the register, he responded by saying "that's how we serve it". I am never going back to this place. If it was on me I would have given it zero stars.

This is my third horrible experience at this venue. I have ordered pander tikka with gravry for pick up and upon arriving home I came go find out I received dry paneer tikka. Upon calling to ask for clarification I was bluntly told I should have ordered from the menu even though this may be the most commonly ordered item. Also the gentleman receiving the phone told me that because I am Gujarati he assumed I had wanted to get the dry one. I felt this very very offending. Also I was told to bring the product back for a refund otherwise I would not get it. Save your selves the hassle and go elsewhere. This is horrible customer service and ruined my mothers day dinner. So long and I will make sire the whole community I know knows of this issue. Feel free to email me if you have any clarification for low class service on top of subclass division amongst Indians and people. Regards Arpit Gandhi

We had been to Hurry Chutney for a quick lunch. It is one of the self serve place (which should be no surprise if you have lived in NJ long enough). We were on a run and the food came pretty quickly. My husband really liked their dal (lentil curry). The staff was not only friendly they were honest too - I had forgotten my purse there with EVERYTHING in it (yeah dumb of me i know!) - but the owner somehow managed to find me online and connected through linkedin. I got my purse back and sure enough, everything was intact! Totally recommend this place :)
This is a place I'd visit again for lunch, had the hot press pastrami, tasty...

Had lunch here yesterday and tried the hot-pressed turkey & pesto sandwich with melted mozzarella cheese. VERY tasty sandwich. I got sides of balsamic vinaigrette and housemade garlic mayo (which was thin like dressing) and those were great for dipping. The healthy-looking breakfast sandwiches on the board caught my eye, so I stopped in this morning for a bite. I had the Mediterranean Egg Sandwich, which is a "Mediterranean egg" with plum tomatoes, red onions and hummus, served in a warm, soft pita. THIS BREAKFAST SANDWICH WAS TRANSCENDENT! They added a few dashes of hot sauce and that put it over the top. I look forward to going back and adding ham and/or cheese next time. Also tried the iced coffee, which is so-so and which is what prevented me from giving five stars. Their website tagline is "Gourmet Sandwiches & Espresso Bar," and I'd expect better iced coffee from an espresso bar, but I'm learning that most iced coffee in NYC is deplorable, so this so-so coffee isn't all that bad.

Excellent, well-priced Mediterranean food honored with a twist of Spanish delight. I go here almost everyday, whether it's for their specialty cookies, (strawberry shortbread, double chocolate, or date rugelach, or for the Haloumi/zataar hot pressed sandwich (whole wheat). The crunchy tuna is super satisfying on some days, while the breakfast egg, hummus, and olive breakfast feasts 2. Boasting a multiplicity of sandwiches, the sauces at this spectacular venue range from garlic-mayo, date mustard, spicy house or  chimchurri. Targetting a delectable region with a twist, whole wheat pita, baguette and multi-grain breads are always an option.

This place actually has great food for a little lunch place, and the clubs are so great. But I have to give it 2 stars because of my experience today. They close at 3pm, I entered at 2pm and they already had every turned off. If you don't want to be open then change your hours.

We made a reservation for Christmas Eve. We arrived, the place was 60% empty. It smelled like ammonia and/or fish. We waited 5 minutes until waitress slouched over. She was rude and  rolled her eyes at us,  when we asked to be seated away from the door, she explained that they had mapped out their table arrangements earlier in the day and she couldn't be asked to change them even though there were at least 9 other tables and we had a reservation. When we again asked for a better table she refused. This type of attitude is not welcome in the neighborhood. Take it back to Williamsburg, and leave a perfectly nice spot for a restaurant that is interested in being a friendly neighbor with good food.

I've had dinner at Walter's on a few occasions since it opened, and each experience there has been great. Walter's is located on a corner across from Ft. Greene Park, and as you approach the restaurant at night the warm glow of the interior (visible through large windows on both sides) offers an inviting preview of what's inside. The menu feels both classic and up-to-date. Some of the best dishes I've tried: the bibb salad (crisp and delicious. The citrus in the dressing really complements the flavor of the bacon), the Brussels sprouts (awesome, and I don't even usually like hazelnuts -- tasting them prepared like this inspired me to try shredding them at home), the broccoli rabe, the spicy fisherman's stew (definitely the highlight of my first visit) and the lobster salad (I love that it's made with fresh mint). I've also had the bar steak (a frequent go-to order for me when I can't decide what else to get). I like that the emphasis at Walter's is on seafood but you can still get a very good steak, too.   On another occasion I came in solo and sat at the bar after shopping at The Brooklyn Flea. It's nice to see a real-deal, serious bar in Ft. Greene. I ordered the smoked trout, which is served on a wooden board with toast points and a hard-boiled egg. It was a perfect afternoon snack, and I could see it also being great as an appetizer to share. Later a friend wandered in and wanted oysters. I like briny oysters, and she prefers them on the creamier side. The bartender suggested a good mix of both. My favorite touch was the mignonette duo: in addition to a classic mignonette, Walter's also gives you a version made with cilantro, which is a cool update. Service has been very good on each of my visits. The servers are friendly, polite and attentive, and happy to correct any small mistake. Each time I've been in, the manager has stopped by the table at some point to make sure everything is good, even when it's very busy. I haven't made it in for brunch yet, but I'm excited to try it. Walter's is a great addition to the neighborhood!

Walter's has got it so very right. We just had New Years Day brunch there and spent 3 hours sitting at the bar, making friends, and loving every second of our first meal of 2012. We got the huevos rancheros and waffle + fruit and both were absolutely delicious and the perfect amount of food. The decor is the best I've seen in a while and the owner, Danny, and his staff could not be sweeter and more accommodating. Tommy the bartender is especially wonderful and it's a treat to be served by him. Thank you Walter's for coming to our neighborhood and we'll see you again real soon!

Quite possibly the best fried chicken I've ever had. We made a reservation for 4 adults and 2 babies on a Saturday night at 5:30pm. The place was packed by 6pm. What happened to New Yorkers eating at 9pm? Oh, I know... everyone wants to eat at Walter's so they eat early to avoid the REAL chaos at 9pm. Very baby friendly restaurant. They had a nice highchair for our very social 17 month old. The wait staff entertained her each time they walked by. It's pretty loud inside. Definitely more of a "happenin" kinda place. If you're looking for intimate and quiet, then this place isn't for you. All in all, it was a great experience. The only reason I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 is because the food took a VERY long time to come out to us. Sitting almost an hour with a toddler in a restaurant is never ideal.... but that fried chicken was worth the wait.

I love this place for nostalgia almost more than anything else.  Don't get me wrong; Gleaners is still a good cafe.  But there's something about sitting out in the sun with a cup of hot coffee, eating a painkiller (which is a great hangover cure) and watching folk scuttle about the Italian Market that takes me back to 2007.
If Steve McQueen was still alive this is where he would get his coffee.

As a warm-blooded Colombian male... I can't walk by a coffee shop, beans-a-roastin', and not stop on in. Well what a pleasant surprise this lil' gem was. Where do I begin?!! Let's start with the coffee- La Colombe is what they serve here and as I sat and sipped I was transported to my post-doc days on the left bank... And then... I saw the desserts. My chunky aunt always said "eat dessert first" and boy did she ever. But I digress, the pastries here are utterly delectable- tiny muffins, cheese croissants and cookies... Oh the cookies. But the cookie was only the beginning because it was lunchtime and a bagel sandwich called my name, much like one of Odysseus' sirens. But unlike him, I welcomed the call. I ordered an Alder Street Dave, on an everything bagel- score!!! I don't know this Dave or what street he lives on but this sandwich was incredible- almost as incredible as the hot little number that made it for me. Piled high and they even toasted the bagel... Hummus more like yummus! But as I look up from this perfect platter of earthly delights I notice something, actually a few things, and those things are the lovely creatures working at this shop. And let me just say their hiring policy must be no uggo's and no blondes... That's a policy I can get behind! I'm new to this whole Yelp thing, but I thought this place deserved a big thumbs up from Rollie- take it sleazy!
Best place around to get south indian non vegetarian cuisine ... Love the veechu paratha , kothu paratha and kori gassi are my favorites.Everyone should try the place for authentic south indian food.

Delicious-- just writing this review to say the farro salad at Bar Corvo is my favorite thing in the world, and they recreate a version here perfectly! (Makes sense, owned by the same group). Highly recommended. Great space, great food, great addition to the area-- we've been needing a good sandwich place!

Stopped by for a lunch time bite with friends and kids in tow. This was a pleasant addition to a neighborhood that has benefited from well conceived "slow" food outlets. Had the chance to try several sandwich options, soup, and coffee. The duck confit was underwhelming, however the burger, emental grilled cheese, and roasted chicken sandwiches were sublime. All things considered, their coffee is the shining star, drip and espresso were exceptionally brewed and presented. The space is comfortable and bright, service was gracious, and small market is well curated. Welcome to the neighborhood. I look forward to returning.
Excellent vibe, service and food;  I really enjoy this space.

Are the hours correct for this place? I came at around 6:30pm so perhaps that explains why there wasn't much available when I arrived. There were some ribs and meatballs but they were pretty pricey. Luckily, we were told that if we waited an extra 20 minutes, we'd get two roasted chickens straight from the oven (at around $12 ea.). They were so juicy I thought I'd died and gone to heaven. They were stuffed with fresh rosemary and I think brined? Lincoln Station has a lot of potential but I'm confused about the opening/closing times.  Here's to hoping the crinkles smooth with age! All in all, I'm looking forward to coming back here again to supplement my dinners and dinner parties.

This place, tucked away on the edge of Crown Heights, has only been around two months but has a feel that makes it seem it's always been there.  Had amazing lentil soup, served with thickly sliced, toasted bread and a cappuccino done right.  Their menu also includes several heartier options and a variety of side salad/veggie dishes to stay or to take home and enjoy.  They have a large community table, with outlets and free wifi (on weekends it's turned off 1230-330 pm) for laptop users, which is why I'm adding it to my coffee shop list, and smaller two tops around the perimeter of the place. My only suggestion would be to extend their hours beyond 8 PM.  All in all,  If they keep up this level of quality they will certainly be here for many years to come.

I stopped by Lincoln Station one rainy Tuesday when I was playing hooky from work. I'm really glad to see this type of place in the Crown/Prospect Heights area--it reminds me of Choice Market in Clinton Hill, right down to the communal table. The mood is laid back and welcoming. I ordered the cheeseburger with a side of fries and I left satisfied. Service is friendly also. I want to come back for breakfast/lunch, and I'm sure it gets busy on the weekends. Their website and Facebook suggest they hope to stay open later and turn into a beer/spot, which would be amazing.
