Again, normally not in the neighborhood but I visit friends here.  This place is pretty awesome.  It's a roomy deli/cafe with a large center bar table and some tables and seats surrounding it.  Only laptops are allowed at the bar.  They serve whatever is fresh so you'll need to poke your head around to see what they have.  I saw some buttermilk fried chicken in the display fridge and got a piece of that as well as their braise kale and fava bean spread on focaccia sandwich.   The price of the chicken is based on weight so it's always a fair deal.  While the piece of thigh meat I had remained cold, it was absolutely delicious.  They properly drained the oil out so it was still incredibly crispy.  Super good.  The sandwich was only alright.  The bread was top notch but the spread was mediocre.  There was some spice to it which was nice but I felt there was something missing in the flavor profile.  Not exactly sure.  Tasty though. I washed everything down with a coffee which was way better than your normal deli coffee. It's a cute place to get a simple lunch or cater from.  If I lived in the neighborhood, this would definitely be one of my spots.

So Biagetti's is a typical West Haven family-run Italian place. Portions are large and the food is great! Last night was the second time I've come here, and both times the service (or lack thereof) was severely disappointing. First, it does not take 45 minutes to bring out our soup and salads. Really? Second, the waiters completely forgot our appetizers after they claimed we told the "wrong" server our order. The manager simply came over and stated that we told the wrong server our order so it had never been put through. If the manager was made aware of the situation : a) why were our appetizers unable to make it to the kitchen and b) why were we not comped an appetizer? Finally, it took an hour and a half to receive our entrees. Honestly, while the food is good, it is definitely not worth the wait and lack of service to get it. Will be chowing down Italian elsewhere.

I went to a day wedding this past weekend, and I was very impressed at the extent Biagetti's service was to make the day extra special.  Linda, the owner, was responsible for decorating the event.  She has great taste, and made the place look very elegant.  She had touches of details such as chair covers, and fresh flowers for center pieces. Food was delicious.  Our cocktail hour had great fried mozzarella, along with big rings of calamari.  The bar kept up very well to make all guest comfortable.  We had a choice of 6 different entrees for the 3 course dinner. Everyone began with a house salad, followed by a great chicken soup.   Main course was accompanied by mash potatoes, hot garlic rolls, sauteed vegetables, and a pasta with marinara sauce.  I had the veal riccardo, and it was memorable. The portion size is INCREDIBLE may I add! You have to come here hungry or you will not look like you made a dent in your food. Prepare to bring doggy bags home.... Service was delightful, very attentive and caring.  It truly was a wonderful experience, and cannot wait to return!

horrible and unsanitary on all accounts...had a miserable wedding reception there...food gross..my dog would not eat the doggie bags coming home, disgustingly dirty, I used to really love this place...its really really bad now...if the Ct. Dept of health ever walked in this past sunday...this restaurant would have closed on the spot....yes....that bad....ps....check your plates, glasses etc...there are forever loaded with food grime and god knows what else...flies everywhere!!!...bathrooms are smelly, uncleaned, really bad folks....miserable owners, snotty unprofessional staff...this list goes on....better off at American Steak House...really.

Food was ok I mean for the price can't really complain... But as service goes that was terrible don't know how they operate like that ...it seems like either they don't have enough help or there servers just suck

Do not eat here! It took one hour to bring out out food with the wait staff offering no information about what was going on. Lots of wait staff offering no service. No one in the restaurant since it was an off peak time .

I usually appreciate it when servers seem to be delighted to have their customers. But that didn't seem to be the case here. Nevertheless, the five of us liked what we ordered and said we'd come back. So there ya go. I might've given it a 3.5 if possible.

Booze and sandwiches Putting Point Breeze on the map A neighborhood must Got the chance to check out The Sardine a little before the opening, and damn am I glad there's an alternate bar in the Point Breeze area. Meaning an alternate to not going to a bar at all. This place has an awesome atmosphere, very warm and inviting without the glow of a television bathing the whole room. The bar-length mirror reflects the candlelight as well as the street lights and really gives the place a friendly glow. There are a few little accents in the room that really make the whole place feel accessible. The bar is huge, and there's standing room and small rail seats along the whole length of the windows, so plenty of room for any size group. The upstairs looks promising, and should mean the place won't be jammed to the rafters all the time. The beer list is really well put together, with a good mix of local brews. I love talking about beer with people, and the fact that the list is numbered actually made it really easy to reference with out table. Something I hadn't considered previously but actually made a difference. I'm giving the place 5 stars based on the ambiance, setup and beer alone. I can't wait to go back and try all the different sandwiches. It's a staple variety of food in my diet and the whole menu sounds really amazing. I didn't even notice that there's no burger until it was pointed out, because I was so focused on all the other delicious sounding items. The Sardine really has an inviting neighborhood vibe. Couple that with a great selection on the booze and food, and you have a pretty spot on combination of what I'm looking for in a bar.

Aesthetically, the place is perfect. Downstairs is awesome, and upstairs is lit up with string lights. Very nice. In the back, there is a stage for live music (eventually). The beer selection was big and diverse, the server was helpful with beer recommendations, and the beer I had was exactly what I wanted. The food was awesome. I got the Krab cake sandwich with a dill sauce, and it was delicious.The onion rings were exactly what I want out of onion rings--crispy, sweet, and they don't fall apart on you. Salt and Pepper fries were kind of bland. The pork sandwich was good, although the pork itself was a little dry, but tasty nonetheless. We tried the beef stew too. It was flavorful, but very salty. All in all, food was good, beer was great, service was on point and friendly, and the place itself is awesome. I'll be back.
So warmed up about this place. Menu is super cheap and portions are really large. Everything looks so tasty and the decor is well done. Kudos point breeze. Well done!

The main shabu is a good choice for first time meal. However, when I come back next time I'm just going to ala carte. The veggie side that comes with the combo meal is too little and includes things I don't like taro root and squash. You get two lettuce leaves and a handful of spinach. I need more than that for veggies. I would do beef again or the beef with pork. Then a bunch of alacarte bok Choy and spinach. Spicy broth isn't very spicy, but it's spicy if you make your dipping sauce spicy. Next time I'm going to do house broth and have my dipping sauce spicy, both spicy is too much. They are still waiting for their sign so the place is 1023 cherry st., closer to the 11th st side.

I love it!  To my knowledge this is the first shabu-shabu in Philly.  The dining experience was so much  fun.  If your not into cooking your own food and being an active participant this place is not for you.  What makes this place even greater is the single serve shabu.  They have a long U-shaped bar with each seat having their own induction burner.  No more having to share a pot!  It was just a bit odd sitting at the bar if you have a big group, can't really communicate with everyone.  Dear owner(s), please get your sign up ASAP.  It was hard to find this place due to the fogged up window and the lack of signage.  You guys are going to want people to notice your yummy goodness from the outside.  Our group of 5 arrived without reservations on a Saturday night.  They gave us a call within about 30 minutes to return.  Our group was seated at the bar so we each ordered separately.  Since it was our first time, most of us ordered from the main shabu list which included the broth, protein, veggies, and noodles or rice.  You can also add from the a la carte menu or order everything a la carte.  The prices were decent.  Our bill came to about $100.  I suppose since they just opened up that's why they included a 10% off on our bill.   I ordered the seafood shabu.  My choice of broth was spicy.  I asked our waitress how she would rate the spiciness.  She said it wasn't that spicy.  Wrong, it was to the point of coughing.  I like spicy but i also like to taste my broth and food.  It was bearable but i would probably choose either the vegetable or house broth and just add chili oil or chili to it myself.  The flavor of the broth was good though.  My seafood selection included: 3 shrimps, 2 scallops, 4 slices of fish, 3 fish balls, 4 clams, and a small piece of crab with the leg.  The veggies was a good portion but they included a slice of tomato, corn, and i believe it was taro which i did not like so much.  The udon noodles were tasty, if it got cold i just threw it back in the pot.  You also get to choose your own dipping sauce.  The have an asian condiment station which included: soy sauce, scallion, cilantro, chili, chili oil, garlic, and others i can't remember.  All in all, the food was great, the wait staff was attentive, and everyone had fun.  Oh i almost forgot, you will get messy here and that's ok.   This place is definitely a must especially if you've never experienced shabu-shabu before.  We'll definitely be back!

Rolled in on a Tuesday afternoon for one of their $1 taco nights (check their Twitter feed for when they're running the $1 promos; it's not always a weekly thing and they switch up the days of the week) shortly after their 5 PM opening and the place was already starting to fill up. Tacos are normally pretty decently priced (between $1.75-$2.50) so still not too bad without the special. They also do Happy Hour M-Fri from 5-7 (and Sat/Sun 1-3 PM) so double bonus: 1/2 off nachos, $4 house margaritas, $2 drafts, etc. The nachos were off the chain. We got them without meat but if that's your thing, then by all means, load em on up! They had several sauces that you could try which were an excellent compliment to both the nachos (which we had a stare down over the last nacho & eventually decided to call a truce and let it keep it's deliciously crunchy, cheese covered life) and the tacos that arrived swiftly after we'd finished our appetizer. I ordered a carnitas, a fish taco, chicken & a chorizo. The carnitas might have been the best one. Green sauce was killer with the chorizo. The smokier sauce was a perfect compliment to the carnitas. FYI - They're small, 4 inch tacos, not the usual 6 inch - so just knock yourself out and ordered one of everything if you're feeling "loco!"

I've been really excited to try this place because I love mexican and I've heard great things. I've had take-out nachos from here that were absolutely amazing, so I was very much looking forward to the entire experience. I ordered all the standards: margarita, chips & salsa, 1 chorizo & potato taco and 1 chicken burrito. I dont know if it was because we got there later (10:15 ish) or if they were just having an off day, but I was not impressed. The margarita was the only thing that was excellent. Strong yet very tasty (fairlane) We received all of our food in less than 10 minutes (seriously) which worried me a little bit. The chips tasted like day old tostitos and the salsa had way too much cilantro for my taste. The taco was tiny tiny tiny but I suppose that's why they are 1.75 so i'll give them that (even though I've had bigger single tacos for far less) and the burrito consisted of runny, puree beans and hardly any rice. The reason I give this 3 stars instead of 2 is because the service was extremely friendly and the place was very clean. I am willing to give this place another try, an earlier try and hope for the best!

If I had only lied close, I would go here for happy hour every week. So cheep and very good for its price! My friend and I each  got 3 margarittas, 2 tacos, and nachos, and this whole came out to about $25. The drinks we got were strong and good! I loved it! I definitely wanna go back for the nachos too. I was so full but couldn't stop cleaning the plate :)
ive have eaten there only once don't care to much for the food, they use entirely to many spices. some people cant handle to many spices.  only thing that was real good were the drinks.
Short review here, sorry for lack of detail, but don't think this place requires any.  We had a business lunch and the result:  Meh, i'm sure you can find something else that is better.

I went here on a business dinner and thought the food and service were pretty good. I started with the New England Clam Chowder- nothing to write home about. I'm from D.C. but have had better chowder elsewhere. I'm sure there is a better place to get clam chowder in the Hartford area. As far as the entree, I had the stuffed scallops. Now this made my head spin around like the exorcist (in a good way). I've had a lot of scallops, but never stuffed. I highly recommend trying this one out.

Thank god for the small parking lot in the back!! Tried their pizza and it was ok, a bit too much cheese for me. But the Italian Hot Dog is out of this world!!!!!!!! Can't wait to go back for another one! Oh, and the people here are very friendly...
Good steaks and chicken always cooked really well. It's a chain restaurant so I don't expect much but it is still good! I would come back again.

Good service is an essential part of a decent meal. We got great wait service from a very attentive crew and all our requests were handled gladly without condescension. Wifey had a burger and house salad which she enjoyed immensely. I ordered the Outlaw Ribeye, green beans and a sweet potato. My ribeye was cooked to specification and delicious, the green beans were fresh, not overcooked, my sweet potato a nice addition to the meal. The only drawback, not enough steak, I'm jumping from 18 ounce to 24 on the next visit.

Let me preface this by saying I was really excited to see Flat Top open. This stretch of Amsterdam is pretty uninspiring with most places serving up perfunctory American staples to the Columbia crowds. So I was thrilled to see its little twinkling bistro lights and inviting dining room, even if it did look like the design consultant had gone a little overboard on etsy. Unfortunately this is where the good vibes ended. We went for a lateish Sunday brunch and were hustled into the tiny dining room by a bad tempered older waiter who was storming around purposefully but apparently achieving very little. Now I dont mind small dining areas per se. In places like Celeste on the UWS the place is always full to the rafters but the atmosphere is convivial and friendly. The waiter grimly pulled back the table and were squished in next to the other diners. The dining room was freezing (my husband sat in his coat) and had the atmosphere of a train carriage or a dentist's waiting room. I felt as if I was practically sitting on the lap of the people next to us and it was made more absurd when you look around and consider all the dead space around the tables not being used. Some time later we presented with menus and about another ten minutes later asked for drink orders. My husband ordered a coffee. When it arrived another ten minutes later it had a harsh acrid taste, like the coffee was burned. He flagged the waiter down asked for another one. The waiter looked at him incredulously and didnt apologise and brought along another slightly more ok tasting one. My husband ordered a burger and I ordered the bangers and mash. Then we waited, and waited and waited some more. It was particularly aggravating that the people next to us who had arrived quite some time after us were being served their meals ahead of us. I asked the waiter if our food would take much longer. IT'S COMING UP, he practically yelled at me. Then a little while later he stormed back over and asked what we had ordered again suggesting he had probably forgotten to put the order in. By this point we had been there almost an hour. At some point we were given some sort of cheesy scone thing, which where pleasant enough and perhaps staved off some of the hangry rage which was now setting in. At no point did anyone apologise.  I looked over at the plates of bangers and mash the people millimetres away were eating. The sausages looked limp, anaemic and dry. The waiter came over and asked my husband if he'd like more coffee which he declined. "But why? You're paying for it," he said rudely. It was at this point we decided to cut our losses and leave. I've actually never had an experience quite like it. I felt that we were treated with disdain and hostility from the moment we set foot in there and then expected to pay through the nose for the pleasure. It's such a shame as we only live around the corner and it would be lovely to have a nice place to go to. Instead we will continue going to Pisticci were the service is always warm and the food actually arrives and is usually really good.

(This review is 4.5 stars rounded up..) Cozy, romantic ambiance and decor. Very small restaurant, and small menu too, but the quality of their cooking and presentation were all top-notch! I saw the rave reviews on yelp, and I looked at the menu and thought it was a very interesting menu, with different flavors. So I was definitely intrigued by the menu and so, I took my good friend here on the Eve of Thanksgiving for dinner. Apps: She had the 2 mushroom risotto with foam on top, which was cooked very well. Very flavorful dish. I had the Burrata Caprese Salad. First time having Burrata and my reactions were mixed. I liked the creaminess and the texture of the inside, not so much the outside. Combined together with the basil and the cherry tomatoes definitely tasted the best! And later on, after our entrees were finished, being the fatass that I am..I still felt a little hungry, so I ordered their Mussel Special with Bruschetta and Italian Sausage, which we shared. Mussels were clean and cooked perfectly. Broth tasted amazing, and that little bit of heat in it was perfect! Entrees: She had the Scottish Salmon, cooked medium. The piece of fish was thicker than I expected, which was definitely cool. No complaints there. Fish was moist, not dry at all. Skin had a nice crispy taste to it. Served over mash potatoes that weren't too creamy and string beans. I had the Duck Breast, over Blueberry Balsamic Vinaigrette, Blackberries and some pieces of Brie and an arugula salad.. Duck was DELICIOUS! Especially combined with a blackberry and the blueberry vinaigrette. You do not want to miss this..! :D I highly recommend this dish. Dessert: By the time desserts came around, I was feeling sleepy and full. We still had dessert; sharing a peanut butter ice cream, brownies, chocolate syrup and 2 macaroons with strawberry jelly in them. Peanut butter flavored ice cream was creamy and delicious!! Overall, an awesome dinner at Flat Top. I would highly recommend people try this restaurant!
My wife and I have been here twice since it opened and we've been impressed both times.  It's a great addition to the neighborhood!

Flat Top is exactly what so many of us have been waiting for! let's start with the food. the food is top notch and simply so so delicious. the chef seriously knows what he's doing and the flavors of the dishes are unique and perfectly put together. for the yelper below, flat top is now back to serving bone marrow (which is amazing)!!! i ordered their new lamb chop entree last week that is amazing. the lamb is not too gamey, and it goes perfectly with the eggplant stuffed with butternut squash, broccoli rabe, roasted garlic and tomatoes. my husband and i were blown away with this new dish, like all the other entrees we've tried (our favorites are the burger, chicken, bass, and steak). Flat top has become our go-to date night spot. it has such a romantic vibe at night and provides the fine dining experience the area lacks. service is always on point and everyone is very friendly and accommodating. we are always excited to see our server there who never fails to make our experience so great every time. now, onto the coffee and the perfect cafe spot it is during the day time. they serve blue bottle coffee, and for those who don't know it is really the best! i'm obsessed with their iced chicory and their seasonal pumpkin latter is also up there on my list (SO much better than starbucks)! we've also gone a couple time for brunch, which is also really great! the scallion and cheddar cheese biscuits they give us when we sit down is so delicious! im always tempted to ask for one more. love their spinach egg white omelette and bangers and mash! flat top really is the best place in the area and is worth a visit if you haven't been.

Flat Top is high quality food. There is no doubt about that, the food is flawless, well composed, and nicely presented. Even the dipping olive oil is delicious. They have daily specials thats complimented with a really lovely menu. So why the four stars? Well, because Flat Top is the type of place that unless you go the full 3 courses you may end up like we did, buying some papa johns at 11 pm because you are hungry again. And if  you do go the full three courses you may go broke....unless your rich, then its perfect!

Figs is a very nice BYOB restaurant to dine in before visiting the Philadelphia Museum of Art on one of those lazy Sunday mornings.  You can't beat the proximity - a half a block from the museum.  It's a small place but the food is excellent and reasonably priced.  The staff and owner are friendly and go out of their way to make you feel comfortable.  I recommend their crab benedict.

Really nice moroccan/mediterranean fare near the art museum.  friend told me that even though it sounds strange i should try the brie/fig/nut/lavendar appetizer ... and she's right it was great.  whole bronzino was delicious.  nice grown-up feel without the  over-staged trendiness that plagues so many philly restaurants, where the show overwhelms the food. byob

Just came here for dinner tonight, and it was, to be honest, the worst place I've tried in New Jersey. Started off with slow, awkward service followed by weak drinks, and our appetizer was incorrect. Normally, we would have just taken things like this in stride, but our dinner just threw us over the edge. My husband's meat smelled and tasted like mud, and my chicken wrap was filled with wilted lettuce and "salsa verde," which was just chunks of slimy, green pickle/pepper-like things. And, to top it all off, everything was way overpriced, especially for the quality and quantity of food served. We won't be coming back.

Went to Bill's to visit after several years hiatus.  The management has changed and the vibe was horrible. I now understand why there were very few people in the place!! Would not recommend this place at all!! I would suggest you would be more comfortable somewhere/anywhere else :)

Had a lovely birthday dinner here with a small group of friends. Delicious food, nice wine list, good service and great ambiance. Enjoyed a couple of old Aussie classics on the menu - sausage rolls & Oysters Kilpatrick - and also the modern Australian style cuisine. Highly recommended.

Phenomenal- ambiance, food and service. We did the 7 course tasting menu and you def can't go wrong with that- one if us didn't eat meat and hey accommodated it perfectly since the menu is seafood heavy. currant cilantro naan, fluke sashimi, avocado seaweed salad, diver scallops, chicken and veggie lettuce cups, steamed snapper and ice cream. The naan was surprising and unique with the currants and the scallops was heavenly and caramelized perfectly. The lettuce cups had great use of different flavors and the fluke sashimi really was mouthwatering. I appreciated the server introducing each course and actually knowing what it was, and that the chef really knew how to layer unique flavors and ingredients (lily bulb, for example). We started with a round of cocktails, all just as impressive and then when I asked for a glass of sauv Blanc which they don't have our wonderfully charismatic and friendly Aussie server suggested a dry Aussie reisling. I'm typically not a fan but decided everything else they sent us was great so this wouldn't fail, and it didn't. The wine was exactly what I wanted and I was very impressed. He pulled out a Pinot noir suggestion for my sister that was equally as on point. Refreshing to have a server who actually cares about what is on the menu, and capable enough to make those suggestions. Doesn't hurt that he was also one of the nicest servers I've ever had in NYC- just a fun happy guy. The manager, bartender and all the servers were great- seemed to genuinely enjoy working there and what they were serving. We didn't have a reservation but they graciously squeezed us in. You can't go wrong coming here for either a date or dinner with friends.

Pretty amazed at all the good reviews. Maybe we had an off night. Our waiter was so rude it was embarrassing and we thought we had offended him.  He clearly hated his job and the service was shocking. The plates were tiny and we all left there starving and went to eat snacks and dessert after ! Not often you get a bad dining experience in NYC. A real shame as I was entertaining friends from London.
If you're Australian, don't miss it! If you're Alphabetcitian I'm sure I'll see you at the bar. For all the other NYers and tourists - stay out!

I don't know where else you can go and get too much bang for your buck. I had to sit out 3 of the umpteen courses.  No complaints here.  The food is amazing. The service is amazing. The ambiance is amazing.  And yes you do have to stand up and take a tour of the beautiful home if for no other reason but to let the food settle.  It's like a halftime show to make room for the second half of the game or a 7th inning stretch for you baseball fans.  My advice is you may want to fast for 3 days prior to dining at 15 Fox Place and be ready to fall into a food coma as soon as you get home.  Grazie Aunt Kat and the rest of the wonderful family at 15 Fox Place. Can't wait to return!!!

Extremely let down.  I understand this restaurant had just opened 4 days prior but this is a company with other functional restaurants and would assume they know what they are doing. I had been given a copy of the menu from a dear friend since i live in the area and picked out a couple apps and 4 entrees for myself and family (the total check would have come to well over $120) . I called to place the to-go order (its a Friday night) and the woman told me that the to go menus were not yet ready for me to call back mid January!  Since i was holding what i thought was the to-go menu i was very confused and asked the woman again if she meant that no food to go was possible and she replied that was correct that they had yet to even purchase the packaging for making to go food a possibility. She then told me in a very snotty tone of voice that my only option would be to dine in and that the restaurant would be closing shortly making it seem like that was not an option either (even tho when i looked at the clock, it was still open for another half an hour).  I had been very excited to try this new addition to the Carbones restaurant group but cant believe they are not even prepared to handle to-go orders and that the staff act in a way to make me not feel wanted to come in when the restaurant is still open. Over a month to get to-go food service up and running...... Not a good way to start.........

I agree.  This was a big disappointment.  Not only the food but we were there on the night of the Newtown shootings and there was a little man (think he was the manager) who wanted to change the channel to sports because the news was depressing his customers.  Unbelievable.
All of the pasta dishes we had were excellent. Service was great. Good drink menu. Make a reservation because the place gets packed. My only wish is that they were open for lunch on the weekend.

Finding good Italian food in the Hartford area shouldn't be difficult but too often is. Thankfully, Carbone's Kitchen helps narrow the gap between those hard-to-find good Italian joints with their new Bloomfield outpost. Of course, the Carbone's name carries some weight around these parts due to their eponymous Franklin Ave home which has been in business well over a half century now. The new Kitchen is a little less Tony-Soprano-Italian like it's older sibling and more for the kids - a lighter less expensive option that still manages to hit high notes for simple but good Italian food. Prices are on par for a restaurant of this quality but dinner for two can easily be had for under $100 with tip. We tried the Sunday Supper which is is for 3 or more... $24 a piece includes apps, salad, bread, three entrees and dessert... not bad. Will I go back? Of course.

I am in love. Cute, Cozy, awesome fresh salads and pasta, In love with their soft Mozzarella cheese! I cant wait to go back. Lunch was $12 with tax and tip, ni drink included. Come, get two dishes and share ;-) The desserts also looks incredible, so did the Sangria!

FINALLY!! 10+ years of waiting for a decent fast-food Mexican restaurant for a quick, delicious, quality meal, and sure enough, after only 2 days of opening, the place is PACKED.  Good news travels fast...no surprise that quality food has a loyal following.  Welcome to the neighborhood!!!
Best falafel and hummus I've had in the US. Great restaurant!!

Falafels that's not from a truck!  Love the Green Salad (the only salad to come with falafels) and the fried eggplant.  Easy to order at the counter, call your name, and grab your food.  The set-up is nice and inviting.  The staff have been pretty friendly.  Recommended to friends and co-workers.  Gets busy at lunch, be prepared!

This was probably the best sandwiches I've ever had, and the decor was fun. We got the Iraqi Turkey, Lebanese Lamb, and Jamaican Avocado with Turkey. The flavors were tremendous in all of them. The location is off the beaten path, but it worth the short walk from the downtown area. Additionally, it is located next door the Citizen Cider Cidery where they have a tasting flight. Great way to wash down the sandwich.

It took my like 20 minutes to find this place hidden in an office park. I got a sandwich here. I had no idea what it was in this sandwich. Pork and kimchi? It doesn't matter. The sandwich changed my life. I feel like I can jump buildings. I can save lives. I can find love even? That sandwich was the answer to world peace.

My boyfriend and I landed on this place after going to Grounds for Sculpture.  We got there around 6:45 and just beat the rush & reservation crowd.  I was at first slightly dismayed by the prices but after having the deliciously homemade-tasting escarole and bean soup that came with the meal, and the fabulous fresh-baked loaf that came with a wonderfully flavorful olive oil blend, and tasting the main dishes, I decided it was a great deal, especially compared to NYC prices.  The zuppa de pesce (on homemade pasta) was incredible, as was the tilefish special, which came with fresh, local vegetables worked into the dish.  I really loved everything we had -- wonderful flavors abounded -- and look forward to the next time I'm in this area and have an opportunity to go back.

I see that STAR TAVERN PIZZA has finally gone and done it...they have joined many others on my list of good foods gone bad! I have loved this place for fifty years and now it is no longer the same...I no longer have a food reason to visit Jersey anymore....so sad

I've been here 5 times, and every time was great...we usually spilt a meatball parm sandwich for starters, which is amazing, and then go on to a plain pie, also amazing, has to be in my top 3 pizza joints, oh, almost forget to mention the service, it's outstanding, they do "teamwork" style service at this establishment, and every one here is friendly, and quick to take care of their guests, so if you've never been here, it's time to give it a try, it usually gets packed, so expect a wait, but it's worth it for the thin crust goodness you will be devouring shortly, trust me...

Let's get this out there right away..this is not the best pizza in Jersey. Pros: great sauce/cheese ratio which gives the slices a wonderful taste. Cons:  slightly greasy, and the thin crust is not baked well enough, making the slices slightly soggy and too flimsy.It does not have that charred crust which would elevate it to a truly outstanding pizza. Note: these are basically bar sized pies, so order a few. Price: $11.25 for a plain pie. Place is extremely busy, crowded, and noisy.

This is probably the best pizza I've had in a *long* time. It was my perfect style of pizza - thin crust, but not too crunchy and crispy - and the toppings extended all the way to the edge of the pie. We got an original and a White Spinach. My friend and I liked the original best, whereas our significant others liked the Spinach pie better. I thought with the plain cheese pizza, the crust to sauce to cheese ratio was absolutely perfect, and the top was a little oily without being overly greasy. It was really great. The White Spinach pie was interesting but I think I just missed having the tomato sauce on it. The garlic flavor was a little bit overpowering and it sort of tasted like the garlic was from a jar rather than fresh. Of course, I still had a few pieces of it. Beer selection was okay - I had a Shiner Bock that was just alright. It was also in a bottle which I didn't realize when I ordered from their "Specials" chalkboard. The decor inside could use a bit of an update but I suppose that's part of the charm. The prices were fantastic for four of us for dinner.

The salads we had were all really great. Beyond that I wasn't impressed. One waitress covering 15 tables. Charge by the glass for soda refills. Pizza is thin crust but extremely extremely greasy. I'm not a health not but I had to use the napkins to try to dry it out.
Pizza was good .. Fast service .. My first time here .. Music omg can't listen to this kind music ..

This place is great! Expect nothing fancy, and they don't deliver, and you will likely have to wait for a table, but the food is fantastic. Their pizza is thin crust (get it well-done) and last time we tried a pasta dish (cavatelli & broccoli with chicken) and it was fabulous - which I just wasn't expecting to love it as much as I did. The pasta was homemade, and it was just an all-around fantastic dish! We will definitely keep coming back

Taste of Tuscany is a no-frills casual Italian restaurant. I have been coming here for quite some time and truly enjoyed most of the fare. The service is great the staff is super friendly and the food comes out fast. In addition is  a BYOB restaurant, a nice plus. Below are the dishes I recommend: - Pizza Nona's (Grandma) - Rigatoni Vodka - Rigatoni Fiorentina - Chicken Marsala - Chicken Valdostana Buon Appetito

Kim's Sushi is awesome! Great service and great sushi.  Their menu isn't as extensive as other places, but that's OK. It's straight up sushi, no hot entrees.  Once upon a time the original location was in Lincoln Park and named for the owners wife Kim, The current owner (Mr. Kim....strange) worked there.  Then the West Orange location opened with Mr Kim running it. Then he bought it from the original owner, who then closed the Lincoln Park location for some reason.  Anyway, I found them in Lincoln Park and loved it then.  Mr Kim has maintained the great service and food.  Some of my favorites are the creamy salad roll, seared tuna app. and the BEST PHILADELPHIA ROLL ANYWHERE!!!

Sushi isn't always just sushi , it has to be fresh and well prepared to get a wonderful taste in your mouth , well I've been going to Kim's sushi since 2011 and I love the way they treat us is always a great experience and the sushi is just delicious , my wife loves going there cause besides the sushi being amazingly delicious , they're all very friendly and they make you feel like you eating in you're friend's kitchen :) lol , 10 stars for this place . By the way , the prices are very affordable .

This is one of the best sushi in West Orange/Livingston/Caldwell area!  I got Spicy Crazy Eel roll and Lunch Special "F" (Spicy tuna and Spicy salmon rolls) to go and they threw in free salmon pieces :) Their sushi is fresh and I would definitely recommend this place!
Great food and friendly service.  The prices may seem high, but it includes soup and salad and oranges for dessert.

Wow! So crazy seeing all the bad reviews! I totally get that restaurants have their good and bad days, depending on the cooking and wait staff. I'm glad to say that every time I've visited, both have been amazing. The staff has always been attentive and friendly, even on extremely busy Saturday nights. Table side guac is the best I've ever had and the food is always fresh and authentic. They don't pad the plate with rice and beans but instead you get generous amounts of meat, fresh veggies and condiments....guac, guac and more guac! Yum! The prices are decent and the drinks are made a bit strong, but I keep coming back.

I have dined in at Puerto Vallarta twice, and though the food was not spectacular (their rice is incredibly bland and dry), it was adequate. The reason for my 2 star review today is because I ordered dinner from the restaurant through the Silver Spoon Delivery service and received the wrong order. What I ordered was 2 of their chicken burritos (pollo asado). My receipt says burritos on it. But what I got were two trays of fixings for chicken fajitas and fajita wraps. Even if these trays were supposed to be burrito ingredients, they were completely different from the description of the Pollo Asado burritos that I ordered, so either way, they got my order wrong. This, paired with the fact that the delivery came an hour later than it should have, left me very dissatisfied with the food and service I received from Puerto Vallarta today.

Finally came here for dinner. Ordered the Fettuccini Integrali (from the menu - "homemade whole wheat fettuccini with braised chicken, olives, capers, portobello mushroom, and diced tomato sauce") and was sorely disappointed with the chicken in the dish. The chicken was cut into strips and appeared to have been deep fried as the color of the chicken was a uniform gold, and it tasted of fryer oil. The meat was dry and terribly stringy, and completely ruined the dish. And there were no olives. I love olives! Definitely not worth the $17.00 price point. The portion was huge, but the quality of the food was lacking. I'll take quality over quantity any day of the week. Dessert was great. Red Velvet Cupcake with cream cheese frosting and coffee. The cupcake was moist and the frosting, while sweet, wasn't overwhelmingly so. Service was mediocre. I think our waiter forgot about us toward the end of our entrees, or perhaps he was just overwhelmed with tables. We asked for a dessert menu and were waiting forever to order. Then once we were done with our meal, we waited forever for our check. I'll stick to grabbing desserts and bread for carry out. I don't believe I'll have another sit down meal.
Best Indian food in Montclair. Friendly staff. Lively atmosphere. Reasonable prices. Highly recommend.

I have  been coming here for several weeks.  Brick Lane has awesome food!  Raghu, the manager, is always friendly and helpful when helping me chose what to order and describes to me the level of spiciness that is used in the preparation of the food.  All the wait staff is friendly and pleasant and it is a joy to come here for a sit down dinner or take out. Brick Lane has become of my favorite Montclair restaurants!
Really great food and friendly service, but so incredibly LOUD that we will get take-out from now on.

This was such an excellent experience.  The food was amazing.   Came here with a group of 8 and had the opportunity to order a lot of the menu and try a variety of dishes. I swear the garam masala spiced lamb was the best lamb I've ever had.  It just melted in your mouth.  Naan was mouthwatering and the curries were outstanding.  I personally enjoyed  the nigiri korma and the bhuna curries the most. Service is very attentive.   It's BYOB so bring some good wine to enjoy with your meal. Looking forward to trying out one of the NYC locations in the future.

I was hoping to be wowed.... sadly I was not!! The first time we had the lunch special which seemed a decent value for 10$. I ordered the Goan Fish dish and it was clear that the chef has never eaten Goan food, the curry was so far off it would make Chef Cardoz cringe. The food is very heavily laden with spice and fat and perhaps to some, is what exemplifies (British) Indian food. The second time I ordered a mildly spiced Chicken Dhansak for dinner. This dish priced at a whopping18$ consisted of 6 pieces of chicken breast boiled in the lentil dish (that I ate the previous visit) called Dhal Tadka. Unbelievable that they think this would go unnoticed. Jahangir Mehta- HELP!!! The Chicken tikka masala tasted like it was made with Campbells tomato soup. Why is it so hard to find decent indian food??? This place may stay in business for the only reason that the other Indian restaurants around are just so poorly run.

The PJ's expansion into West Windsor was anticipated by no one more than I. I have been a fan of the Princeton location for too many years to mention, and could not wait to try the new, closer, venue. I went on a Wednesday night, around 7. I surprised myself by getting pasta- the linguine vongole. My partner had the penne pecorino, and both were very satisfactory. The vongole had plenty of clams, the penne had plenty of shrimp, and we were both happy with or meal. Of course, we couldn't come without getting pancakes, so we ordered some chocolate chip pancakes for dessert. And here is where the restaurant starts to lose stars. The pancakes were thick. Chewy. Even meaty. I could not have been more disappointed. Moreover, they were simply...meh. Bland. If not for the whipped cream and syrup, they may as well have been mushy cardboard. Another thing that I missed from this location (although, perhaps, this was unavoidable) was the ambiance of the Princeton location. No caved-in tables, no long, family-style tables...it was just a normal restaurant, with normal food. Service was commendable, no problems there. I just can't help comparing the new addition in the chain to the original, and it doesn't stack up.

Eh, avoid this establishment, it is infested with cockroaches! Uno's used to be a good restaurant years ago when ran in a professional manner. I had ordered a large numero uno and found a cockroach hoping around in between the cheese. That should have been the last straw, but yet my children beg to return. We did decide to put this incident behind us, and yet we found a disturbing scent lingering from the kitchen, which smelt like "pot". Absolutely ridiculous, where are the managers cleaning this place up rather than texting on her phone in the lobby?!  Will only visit Franklin Mills location, due to the higher sanitary conditions.

The "locals" ruin this place! But it is a hidden gem when it comes to big sporting events, hardly anyone is here, which makes it easy to get a table. Like I said before,Potential is there for it to become much better.
Worst pizza experience ever, this place is horrible. Order domino's or pizza hut. Is there anywhere in Burlington that has good New York style pizza?

This place is AMAZING!  This locally owned, small business is a great place to find food that you will instantly love for great prices.  I could eat here everyday and not get tired of this place, I certainly would get fat though!  The people working here are very laid back and approachable.  I don't usually eat inside, but it looks like the place could use a little bit of redecorating, but I don't judge because the food is just that good.  I suggest calling and ordering that way because they can get busy and it's not really in a location where you can go shop around and wait for your food at. Things to try off the menu: Garlic knots with cheese Calzones NY style pizza (almost as good as in NYC, almost) Spinach and artichoke dip Subs Brownies

Firebox is probably the one restaurant in Hartford that I looked forward to going to the most.  Why it took me four years to get here, I'm not quite sure.  For the past four years I'd been wanting to check it out after hearing many positive assessments of the food, the ambience ....everything about it really.  I even volunteered weekly right next door at the Kitchen at Billings Forge for several months at one point years ago.  I finally made it here yesterday for dinner. My date and I sat at the large, spacious, beautiful bar.  When we arrived we talked for a moment about the high ceilings, exposed beams and brick, and how it all felt similar to those industrial loft apartments that we both love.  The bartenders were warm and friendly.  We enjoyed our cocktails, a strong Nor'easter for him and a Billing Forge Cocktail for me on our first round.  I also had a Sangria Roja later in the night but I preferred my first cocktail. We took advantage of the Taste of Hartford Summer 2014 deal, three courses for $30 (what a steal!).  We both started with the Duck and Pork Terrine, for the second course he opted for the Fried Eggplant and I went with the Fresh Handmade Pasta, and for the  third and final course we shared the two desserts, a Goat Cheese Panna Cotta and Flourless Chocolate Cake.  Everything was excellent and presented beautifully.  The pasta the highlight for me.  It had been a long while since I'd had a pasta dish that impressed me as much as this one did.  It was tremendous.   With dessert I also had the most perfect decaf cappuccino.  Few things irk me more than when nice restaurants have the ability to do food well but cannot make a good cup of coffee or espresso based beverage.  Since, for some, this is often the last taste of the night if accompanying dessert or even without dessert, it's very important to get it right.  The cappuccino at Firebox was better than many of the ones I've had at specialty coffee shops.  Bravo, Firebox.  Bravo.  You win.   Just one note about service.  As is often the case with Taste of Hartford or other restaurant week menus anywhere, our order was taken in a way in which we gave our selections for each course all at one time.  So, in other words, we made our dessert selections when we chose our first and second courses.  It would appear that they had forgotten we had ordered dessert at all...because we probably finished with our second course around 8:30 or 9...and by 10, when the kitchen was closing, and when the restaurant had cleared out significantly, the dessert still hadn't arrived.  But one reminder and it was whisked out to us immediately. We both used the $6 valet service for parking.  Conveniently, you can pay on the spot, when you leave, or put the charge on the bill.  As instructed, ten minutes before we planned to leave we gave our valet tickets to the bartender (you could give it to the server if you're sitting at a table) and she retrieved our keys for us.  I wasn't sure how that was going to work but I had a few extra singles to tip the valet drivers which proved unnecessary as they were no where to be found when we exited the restaurant and our cars were already parked in spaces of the lot by the restaurant.  I'm not sure if this was customary or if it was because we were leaving so late, but either way, I was happy to see my car there ready to go! Awesome first experience at Firebox.  I look forward to many more!  I'm very happy that I finally made it here.

Went with my mom and sis to the Firebox to have some catch up time with the girls and some good food. We were not let down! The waitress was so friendly and did not rush us. We spent about 3 hours there (by choice!) just talking and enjoying the fantastic food, ambiance, and service. I ordered the cheese plate for an appetizer which was very elegant and creative. My sister teased me for ordering the french fries but put her foot in her mouth (as well as half the bowl of fries) after trying them. By far the BEST fries I have ever had! The duck was delectable, so juicy and cooked medium to perfection just as I requested. My family and I will be returning and we just love how the Firebox is "Farm-to-Table" using only fresh local ingredients. Definitely worth the money and drive.

I've visited Firebox several times, twice for brunch (the most recent trip being today), twice for lunch and once for dinner. This place is absolutely incredible. The decor can best be described as upscale rustic- it is cozy and pretty but not too fancy. They have phenomenal food and an impressive drink menu. The service can be a little slow, but everyone is so nice and the atmosphere is so pleasant that you don't mind hanging out a little longer. However, the staff was very quick to refill our waters so no complaints there. This morning my party & I shared the Melinda Mae cheese plate (which came with crostinis, peach slices, local honey, peanuts, blueberries & pea tendrils) & the pickle jar. Both were delicious. For brunch I had the braised calamari, which was accompanied by sliced heirloom tomatoes, watermelon, fingerling potatoes and a black olive aioli. The calamari was perfectly cooked- not remotely chewy or fishy. I'd also like to note that it was very light and contained no wheat or gluten. Then for dessert (I couldn't help myself- don't judge me), I had the flourless chocolate cake and it was divine. The cake was topped with almond butter and whipped creme fraiche, and there was a strawberry coulis with dark chocolate pieces on the side. It was so delicious that I couldn't even feel guilty! Just for the record, the rest of my party was equally delighted with their meals and desserts. I would highly recommend this place for any meal or for happy hour. My only complaints are the somewhat slow service and their table selection strategies. For the second time, the restaurant was not yet crowded and I was seated directly next to another party. Today we were seated immediately adjacent to a large family party with loud, young children when there were other rooms that could have easily accommodated us. So I'm not sure of what their system is, but it leaves something to be desired. Either way I will definitely return the first chance I get. This is a wonderful spot so don't miss it!

Firebox is the best restaurant in Hartford for local faire, hands-down. Their regularly changing menu safely - but creatively - pulls from various disciplines merging into a wonderful experience. Executive Chef Sean Farrell has yet to disappoint me, and I've gone three times now. The ambiance is a bit stuffy or high class, but I like that. Waiters can be a bit too relaxed sometimes, but that's my toughest critique. Good work Firebox - you're my first favorite restaurant for farm-to-table, and my second overall in Hartford.

This is a fun place that regularly features Ed Fast and Conga Bop, a Latin Jazz group that I really enjoy. They are usually there on the first Wednesday of the month starting sometime in the Fall. The food is good and the ambience is great Very nice crowd who enjoy music and will dance along.

So referring to the store part of Dolce - not the catering/bistro section. Like some others have said - they have a huge Italian selection.  Great overall quality foods.  Staff is a little rude and product is a bit pricey, but the quality and selection EASILY make up for those two factors.   Love the fresh bread selections, pastas and frozen raviolis, pastries, huge Boars Head selection, take home and heat/eat meals, very good sandwiches made to order, and, um, everything else is just great! Its definitely worth going to.

Sat outside, really a nice decadence to the place. Service was top notch, really nice people. Drinks were made well, the food was really something to compliment them about. Anything from the burger, to the steak, was excellent. Expensive, so don't go all urkel when the bill comes and say "did I do that?"

The fluke and moules frites were nice but most of the classic French dishes that i've tried where unable to keep up with the quality that i'd expect form a place with such a professional staff and nicely styled garden. I haven't had brunch here yet but I have a feeling that it might be what they're best at.

Sunday Brunch | Date for Two SUMMARY: Have you ever woken up wanting something rich and delicious to nosh away your hangover OR impress a date? Yes, I assume that's everyone. If needed, Montmartre is classy enough to simultaneously do both for you. In short, the perfect spot for a sunny morning/afternoon bite. HIS: Burger - dry aged beef, bearnaise cheese, spinach [4.5/5.0] This hit the spot on several levels - a sinfully delicious juicy/fatty blend of LaFrieda beef is smothered in a rich layer of cheese up top and spinach on the bottom. I love CRUNCH in my food, and two extremely well-toasted (maybe even too crunchy?!) slices of white toast sandwiched this baby. HERS: Poulet and Pain Perdu - fried chicken, bacon maple syrup and pain au levain [4.0/5.0] I'm a sucker for Southern food, and the flavors of this doesn't stray far from the classic even with the use of sourdough french toast (instead of the usual waffle). With the food we had, cocktails like Elevator Music, Loosey Goosey and Reluctant Debutante, and a back outdoor patio among lush greenery that transported me away from the city, I'm definitely coming back again to this slice of Paris in NY.

The host and service staff are accommodating, personable, and take pride in their work.   Service was the best part of the dining experience.  We felt taken care of by a smart and charismatic team....  with excellent knowledge of food and drink.   Made the meal much more pleasurable.  Thank you! Food, space, location also great.
Probably the only saving grace in Newark. The hostess is wonderful and I am never disappointed. This place is BYOB so feel free to have a great night!

Bought a Groupon and visited the restaurant on 8/15/14. The restaurant was very nice, newly renovated, great atmosphere and the waitress was very sweet and attentive. The Food was delicious and the juices were fresh . I was amazed  how much we received for a Groupon, appetizer, two main courses including salad and drinks(non alcoholic). I would definitely recommend and look forward to attending this restaurant again. :)
In love with the food  great environment,  outstanding customer service, nice workers !!! Highly recommended

Came here with a high school friend of mine that is in New York for brunch. Got there around prime brunch time on a Saturday (around 10/11am) and ended up getting seated pretty easily at the bar. I ended up getting the Sausage gravy smothered chicken sandwich since I wasn't sure what I was going to get. The chicken was well made - juicy, and the sausage gravy was delicious too. Definitely a lot of food, but it's delicious. Decent service. Decent drinks. Think the thing that made me laugh was the California beer tasting. They were definitely all beers I recognized - being from SF.

Here is one of the best restaurant in NYC because the hospitality of staff is sooooooo good than I expected. Thanks to her, I can't forget having a dinner this special day .The day I went to Jacob's pickles is first time America, first time New york city. I would like  to call at this restaurant again if I have an opportunity to go to America!

Where have you been all of my life???? I'm not a fan of chicken with breakfast food but this place has made me a believer. I had the biscuit French toast with a side of chicken and OMG I'm in love. They give you 4 ginormous pieces covered in strawberries and powdered sugar. The biscuit was soft and fluffy inside and ridiculously delicious. My friend swears by their mushroom smothered chicken and it looked delicious, but I wanted breakfast food...I was not disappointed. The only downside was that we were told the wait would be 30 minutes and it ended up being 90 but the food made up for it and it came out pretty quickly

For dinner I suggest making a reservation or be prepared for a short wait. The cocktails are delicious, as was the food! A bit of a snug fit at the dinner table... Elbow to elbow with strangers... But still excellent!

My friend picked this place due to Yelp reviews.  Got seated right away besides being busy with all the hipsters.  It's not tourist spot I'm pretty sure.  Reminds me of some restaurants in the Mission here in SF.   I wanted something light so ended up getting salad with their fried chicken.  Chicken was moist and salad was huge but I managed to finish it.  I also tried their rootbeer I think which was good.  I was hoping their biscuit was warm but not.  It was a good spot but not the real deal soul food.  Good place to hang out with friends for happy hour or catch up.

My mother and I loved this place.  We stopped in a month or two ago and had a fantastic and patient waiter who brought my mom a couple different beers to try before she decided (as a waiter, I know how time consuming diners like her can be).  The food was fried and delicious, definitely a damning find.

Ok... So this was absolutely delicious but holy &@$€ was the portion large... I guess I'm not used to American portions just yet haha not a place to miss if your in the neighbourhood. Ordered a side of pickles that where absolutely delicious, their variety made it hard to pick... If I could I would try and taste them all. I'm a big eater and it was tough, small portion eaters, you might want to split one of their sandwiches haha if you finish it order a second!

To kick off the night, I ordered the Dirty Aphrodite. This was a simple cocktail made with vodka, Dirty Dill Pickle Brine and pickled green beans. The first half was great while the second half got a bit too picklely for me! We started with some appetizers - one of the many perks of dining with a group! The special sour cukes were fantastic and so were the fries. Jacob chatted with our table and sent over some fried pickles. I've never had a corn dog but this reminds me of one. The coating was light and fluffy and not drenched in oil. If you have a chance to speak to the owner, go for it: he is awesome! Out of all the entrees we split, I LOVED the Chicken & Pancakes. It was a knock-out dish. If you're going for a healthy option, don't get the salad - just don't come here! To enjoy the food, you need to indulge a bit...or a lot! The salads were tasty (spinach and wedge) but a bit heavy handed on the dressings. The chicken sandwich was yummy with PLENTY of pickles! The mac and cheese was ENORMOUS. Just ridiculously sized. I wanted to try it but was too full from all the pancakes! This is an AWESOME spot. I didn't even look to see if they have dessert since I couldn't physically move. I had to roll out of there. I imagine whatever is on any menu is delicious here! Also, there is outdoor seating!

Yum! Loved the mac and cheese here. It is absolutely fabulous. The fries were also great and of course, loved the pickle selection. My favorites were the spicy pickles and the green beans. The red beets weren't bad either. The only thing that was disappointing here was the shrimp and grits, and it wasn't even that bad. The grits were great but the shrimp was a bit tough/over-cooked.  Warning--the shrimp come with their heads!

The honey chicken and pickles biscuit sandwich was incredible! And if you're looking for a great selection of domestic beers then this is definitely the place for you. My favorite is the Allagash White (Belgian style, crisp) which is very similar to Blanche de Bruxelles or Blue Moon.  Overall, a phenomenal southern comfort meal just like I'd find back in Texas while looking out onto the streets of NYC. There wasn't one thing I would change about this place; great food, good beer, friendly waitstaff, awesome music, and convenient location. I'll definitely be back!

This place seems to be popular, but I found it to be a total disaster.  First of all, most of the food is terribly greasy, even for foods that are fried.  The tables for 4 are way too small for a party of 4, and to add insult to injury, the service is sloppy and unprofessional. In fact, at the beginning of our meal, the busboy serving knocked over a glass of water, it spilled all over 2 of my dinner guests, and their shopping bags, and all over the floor.  Nobody came by with a mop or extra towels to clean it up, and they had to sit with a puddle of water between them during the entire meal.  One of my guests, who was visiting from Europe, said in a case like that the manager would come over to apologize, and order the mess immediately cleaned up.  Nothing like that occurred.  If you want to impress your out-of-town family or friends do not bring them here, in fact don't go yourself.

Fun place. They actually take your name and number and text you when your table is ready. Why is this concept so foreign to most popular restaurants? Great cocktails and fried pickles. The Brooklyn Gin is awesome. Organic cheese grits mmmmmmm.  All this and a biscuit.

One of my favorite places to eat in the Upper West Side.   If you are a fan of sandwiches on freshly baked biscuits this is the place for you.   Make sure you try one of their 3 root beers on tap - and save room for the fried oreos.   Also if you are looking for brunch this is the best brunch in the UWS.   Bacon, Egg and Cheese on a biscuit????   Yes please... also the french toast is off the charts.

I was visiting from California and decided to try this place out. Best decision EVER! The food was amazing and service was great. The Manager John greeted us and even invited us back for brunch, but our schedules were just too packed. I highly recommend this place and I'm picky.

In a city of thousands of Restaurants, Jacob's Pickles is one that you'll keep coming back to.   From great pickles, to incredible root beer, the best entrees, cheese grits, and amazing desserts it doesn't get any better.   Arrive hangry, because these portion sizes are craZy!   Personal favorite is the chicken bacon egg and cheese biscuit.  Vanilla biscuit pudding for dessert.
The food is worth it when you can skip the wait. Long lines but great chicken-centric dishes with southern style. Craft beers by the growler and solid cocktails. A place to take out of town guests.

This restaurant continues to capture my attention. Has the best food, ambiance, and service. On top of all that this local restaurant has started a program that offers high school student hands on training for those interested in the restaurant business. Jacob's is always a good time and I always leave with a happy tummy.

Great bar, great ambiance, great service, some great biscuits, but meh pickles I loved the setting for a laid back but cool Friday night. The wait was long but we got lucky with a table at the bar. It was hard to resist ordering pickles, given it's their signature. But I was unimpressed. We got the beet, green beans, and standard pickles and they were ohh-k. I generally love pickles, and have had some amazing pickles at the various NYC street fairs, but these were mediocre. The biscuits w various preserves on the other hand were amazing, warm, and perfect. The rootbeer was awesome too, although I must admit all the flavors tasted the same to me. So perhaps a 2 star deduction for mediocre pickles is a bit harsh, but, they are Jacob's PICKLES after all .... Would love to go back.. but not for the pickles
Come here at least twice a week, the taste & freshness of the food is unmatched in the area. It's usually empty since it does not seem the locals have discovered this gem.

Had the spicy ham panini. Was delicious! Great spice level. Be warned, though, it has a lot of cilantro. Luckily I love cilantro. They are a touch disorganized right now (there isn't even a sign out front) but the food is good. I'll be coming back for sure.

Went to this awesome new establishment in the new Standard East Hotel.  Our waiter as just ok but the food was that good that I decided to forgive.  Must haves are the the rotisserie beets and the duck!

The absolute best new restaurant in New York City. Every new restaurant in NYC should use Narcissa as an example in terms of how to plan a menu, design a space, and manage their staff. Every single thing I sampled on the menu during my two dinner experiences here was exceptional. The staff is friendly, informed, professional, and balletic. The space is beautiful. Narcissa does the farm-to-table thing, with a nice, sparkling emphasis on vegetables, without pretension. And I never felt like I was eating a "mission statement." The cocktails are exemplary (and much better than at Cafe Standard, the pretty bar next door with a different cocktail list). Every dish kept outdoing the other one, and this isn't a restaurant to skip dessert. The sundae is the best dessert I've ever had, ever. John Fraser is a talented chef who takes his cooking seriously. Given the open kitchen situation, he might want to tone down laying into his line cooks during the dinner service, but I would come back again and again, and I've recommended it to others, who all loved it as well. I'm grateful it's here. Narcissa, while extremely sophisticated eating, doesn't reflect that on their prices. This is a reasonably priced restaurant, and puts to shame its hotspot brethren like  The Elm or The Dutch or even the (very good) Pearl & Ash, all of which give you less and ask for more.

I want to start this review by saying the carrots Wellington was by far the worst dish we had last night....wtf people???!!! I went for those juicy little raved about bits alone!!! I had a 7:30 rese after many attempts to eat here and thinking at the time of booking both 5:30 and 10:00 seemed like acceptable times to enjoy dinner...not so much. I arrived early and sat at the bar. The bartender was great! I ordered a totally fab drink,  the gentleman farmer...order it, it's like getting your veges and booze all in one shot, the essentials!  We decided that we were digging the bar vibe so we stayed at the bar instead of sitting at a table. Like most hotel restaurants, no matter how cool, they can't dodge that hotel restaurant vibe. We basically wanted to order the entire menu so here's the rundown: 1. Brussels sprouts leaves with greens and things - best salad I've had in forever 2. Long Island fluke crudo broccoli pesto lemon and pine nuts - not a huge fan of crudo and I could have eaten another order...YUM. 3. Poached farm egg quinoa forest mushroom chayote - unbelievably fantastic 4. Rotisserie crisped beets bulgar salad apples creamed horseradish - meh... 5. Carrots Wellington - people, here is where ya let me down....so underwhelmed and disappointed...mushy tasteless carrots surrounded by a croissant ...fail. 6. Roasted hake artichokes clementines - I say you stick with the apps, they were outstanding and the mains were pretty anticlimactic .. 7. Carrot fries - oh I tasted these on the way out as I stopped by my ex lovahs table as he was enjoying dinner with a date...yep, I did that : ) order them The wine list is interesting, we tried the Bebame 2012 Cab Franc/Gamay and although it went well with the food, it's a little light on it's own. The service is great, most of the food, phenomenal so yay, I'm a fan.

4 stars for the garden space. Geez. It was so beautiful and perfect spring weather for brunch under the trees. Romance for 1 please Service was great. They were accommodating of any menu changes Ordered the carrot fries, egg frittata, green juice and the French toast bites. Everything was tasty but the environment really sold it in. We made reservations for a 11a brunch which seems like a magic time for the city

Could be my new favorite place to eat!  We came for Sunday brunch. The decor inside was modern, comfortable, open and welcoming. The menu was phenomenal - never had I had such a hard time choosing what to order! We shared the eggs benedict (because it's usually what I want on a Sunday) and the pork schnitzel. Both were perfection! Both dishes came with salad (as opposed to potatoes, which is a good thing because it's less carbs, less guilt :) )And you know when you can't decide whether to get something salty or sweet for brunch? Problem solved with a side order of French toast bites served with lemon curd and maple syrup - genius! The price was reasonable, actually great for the quality of the food and the warm attentive service. I can't wait to come back to try the many other brunch items on the menu and then come back for dinner too!

Bad news. The experience I had tonight at this restaurant is unprecedented. While most of the food was delicious, the stew was not. It was badly overcooked and when the server asked about our meal, I told him what I just said, honestly and tactfully. He seemed a bit annoyed that I didn't like the dish, but offered to bring us something else. We ordered the steak, which was good. My biggest complaint was the lack of service. We asked for an iced tea on 4 separate occasions to different staff members and couldn't get it until almost the end of our meal. We were given a bad attitude I believe because we chose to share a meal and they didn't like that. They charged us a $6 sharing fee which was never revealed to us when we were ordering. It just showed up on the bill. After the meal was over... We paid the bill in cash. It was $77. We chose not to leave a tip because of the poor service.  Something I had only done once before in my entire life. The server chased us down the street yelling and screaming at us. He said, we were $5 short on the bill. We counted the money carefully and saw the $5 we had put in the pile was missing. I believe he pocketed the $5 claiming he didn't have it.   Still shouting on the street, he threatens to call the police unless we give him the $5 we owe.  I knew we paid it and he was angry that we hadn't tipped him. I told my friend to let him call the police because we did nothing wrong. He proceed to call us the B word, F word and finally called us LESBIANS!  This behavior was the most unprofessional I had ever experienced and blown completely out of proportion. A smarter person would be interested to inquire about what was unpleasant so that they could improve their service in the future.  Instead, he was insulted and bitter that we had opted to not leave a tip for poor service. I know this restaurant has lots of great reviews. But, the snooty attitude and cursing was ridiculous. I think as patrons, we have the right to share a meal. I would not recommend this restaurant.  They turned a birthday celebration among friends into a Jersey Shore episode.

Very good breakfast place.  There were a few "special" items, like the omelettes and the berry pancakes, to make it worth the trip.  I thought the berry pancakes were good.  The first time we went, my companions thought there was too much cheese in their omelettes; the second time we went was better (berry pancakes just as good).  I like to have a little bit of everything, so a combo offer of eggs, hash browns, pancakes, and a choice of meat is usually what I seek.  They don't have that here.  I'll survive, but more combos and more specials would earn 5 stars.  The place does not seat many people, but we've had reasonable luck in getting a seat even mid-Sunday mornings (~9:30).  That's better than some other nearby places.  Maybe the cash-only policy keeps some people away.  As long as you know it going in, I don't see it as a problem.  Cost for 3 adults and a child was reasonable.  The wait for the food was also reasonable.  There aren't many booths, but there's a long counter, so it might be better for those without young kids, or couples.  I prefer this place to another nearby, but the wife usually wins the battle.  Go and enjoy it yourself.
Great food, superb service. This small restaurant is great value for your money and palate :-)
Very nice place although its very small but the food was good.. Also, the food portions were small too! We had chicken tikka masala, pakora, lamp korma, and chicken biryani. Very well made food!

Food was great, service was really good too. Everyone was very courteous. Fantastic vegetarian options, just the right amount of spice. While the portions looked small we had the 3 course meals, and the entres were very filling with the appetizers.
The restaurant itself isnt anything special, but the food is delicious. Definitely worth a try!

found this Indian restaurant with good review and next  my work. decided to give a try after work. staffs are nice , food are good. we got complimentary Mango lassi by moving to next table. will come back again.

This place is awesome! We came to NYC for a week and found this place by accident, and what a pleasurable surprise it was. The meanie isn't huge, with about a dozen entrees and some side dishes it's shorter than most but the food was excellent, service was fast and prompt and the place is clean, cozy and intimate. We tried the chicken curry, Chicken Tika Masala, the Tandoori Chicken Tika and Aloo Gobi Matar entrees along with Pakora and the Vegetable Samosa and all of them where excellent. The dish portions were big but not to big. Definitely a place to visit if you crave some affordable Indian food
Great skirt steak, cheesesteak sandwich and ribs w/cornbread. All followed by delicious desserts!

What can you say about a place that was dedicated to Theresa with everything from the food to the design - they have made her dreams come true! The food is incredible and the staff is courtious and helpful. Breakfast, Lunch, & Dinner NYC style without the city prices - what more can you can ask for!!! Dine in or take out & delivery - AND THEY CATER TOO!!!
Always reliable and good! Mozzarella sticks and curly fries are the best!

Greek Lady is a great place for a relaxed breakfast lunch or dinner at a great price with  filling portions and fast service. I brought my family friends here when they were visiting form out of town because I knew that they would enjoy the may food options Greek Lady offers, as well as the high quality. We had a great time getting brunch there - the food came out quickly and just howe ordered it (I recommend the egg white omelet with veggies and potatoes!) Great experience!
Yum!

Definitely a go-to spot on campus. In fact, going to Greek Lady is somewhat of an initiation ritual when one is accepted into Penn. One of my favorite dishes is the lamb gyro which is simply delicious. It is stacked high with lettuce, tomato, lamb, onion, and just the right amount of tzatziki sauce. Additionally, they put a few french fries inside which serves as a nice surprise in each bite. To accompany the gyro I always order, the crispy, perfectly-seasoned curly fries and what I consider to be the best milk-shake I've ever tasted. The milkshake is made form about a pint of ice cream and just the right amount of milk, making it silky smooth and creamy. Add to that a dollop of their freshly made whip cream and you have heaven in a cup. They satisfy my sweet cravings and in general are a good pick me up after any stressful day. In terms of the service, considering their high demand of orders especially after traditional class time, they are generally quick to serve you. The atmosphere is dependent on what time you go. the place itself is very nice, but on what I call rush-hour times the restaurant can get very noisy; however, I highly recommend Greek Lady as a casual place to hangout and pick up a good, affordable meal with friends.

Just brought a pork avoidant friend here and shared some boiled chicken and mushroom dumplings.  They were so good we also ordered fried ones, which were, as another reviewer describes, very oily but very good.  Like the pork dumplings, the filling is really meaty and flavorful.  Hot & sour soup broth was great again. The sesame pancake with veg had disappointing fillings though.  Mostly shredded carrots, a bit of cucumber, just about no cilantro.  They don't drench the inside of the bread with sauce like the pancake at Vanessa's.  The pancake itself was good still.  Thicker dough and less greasy than I expected.

It has good spicy noodles which is vegetarian...their veggie sesame pancakes are a little odd - fried/baked bread with julienned carrot and cucumber slices and cilantro sandwiched in between two slices. The reason why I didn't give four stars is that the menu is quite limited for vegetarians...no veggie dumplings available. But I thought the service was friendly and my lunch cost $5. Though it is so cheap I don't know if that is good or bad. It is not a dirty establishment at all and those who have written so before prob have a different view on what is clean. It is just a basic dumpling shop.

Delicious. Prosperity Dumpling on Eldridge held the title for best dumpling in NY for me (Yes, I did a study) until this guy showed up around the corner. I've only ever bought the dumplings, and my faves are the boiled. They have them prefrozen but you'd never know the difference. They boil them when you order so be prepared to wait. Love the classic pork and chive and the chicken and cabbage is good too. Highly recommend. -1 star because the sesame pancake isn't usually fresh and the wait can be substantial.

Super dumplings for dirt cheap prices! This is a quintessential hole-in-the-wall, greasy Chinese place. The woman who runs the counter is friendly, but speaks very little English, so stick to the numbering system when ordering. The pork and chive fried dumplings are the best when hot, but their quality drops if they've been sitting out. The fried dumplings are superior when they're fresh, but the steamed dumplings are a little more consistent and a little cheaper. Their stuffed buns are an equally tasty and cheap option, but their Little Juicy Buns (#9) can be a bit tough on the bottom where they are cooked... No innuendo intended in that sentence. Their sesame pancakes are tasty, but greasy and a little dry. Their noodles and fried rice come in large portions for their cheap price. This is my favorite dumpling/Chinese place in Downtown Brooklyn/Polytech area, hands down.

The food is fabulous -  portions good size and appetizers are great  - we usually  have Jessica (our favorite server )pick out 4 appetizers (depending on how many friends go) and make them our meal -- they are all great  - the date appetizer is wonderful.  Thanks Jessica you are the best
