Four of us dined there this evening and I have to say that I've had better greek elsewhere.  We tried most of the appetizers and everyone seems to rave about the octopus.  I thought it was completely overcooked and chewy.  The calamari was tender but way too much breading.  The only things that I thought were great were the hummus and the gyros.  Everything else was forgettable.  We thought the entrees would be better, but again they fell short.  The striped bass was completely bland.  I could've cooked a better meal.  The pastitsio just tasted odd.  I've definitely had better at kanella.  The one entree that I will say was excellent was the rabbit with homemade pasta.  The flavors were spot on. We did let the server know that we didn't enjoy the other entrees.  My friend had two bites of the fish and pastitsio so 90% of the food was left on the plate.  The manager did come over and apologized.  He then said that everyone seems to like the food and that we must be mistaken.  He also said we probably have never tried traditional greek food before.  I was flabbergasted!! I couldn't believe this guy.  I'm in the business and would've never spoken to a guest in the manner that he did.  Needless to say they need serious work on seasoning and customer service!  I will not be back!

You and me, baby, ate nothing but mammals should be the theme song to this place We wandered into the Cannibal during our recent trip to NYC for some afternoon libations with friends. It was around 3 PM and the place was full but luckily a big group was leaving as we walked in. The vibe was really cool; the space is small and we were seated in a high traffic area, but we managed. The TV was playing  a college indoor track & field championship for some reason but nobody was watching the TV anyway It took a while to get through the beer list/Bible. The beer I tried (Captain Lawrence Liquid Gold) was a really refreshing Belgian style ale. If you can't find a beer you like in this long list then you should switch to Zima. After all that drankin' we got hongry so we decided to look at the food menu. The choices are quite interesting (if I ever return I'm trying out that pig's head). We decided to get the country pate and a cookie. No complaints about the pate, the taste and the texture were awesome. The cookie took forever to come out of the kitchen. When we inquired about the status the waiter flipped the dial to "bitchy for no reason" and told us we needed to be patient and the cookie was not ready. We finally got the cookie and we assumed it would be warm and fresh right out of the oven. Not the case. It still was a good cookie (chocolate, molasses, and ginger). Minus 1 star for the diva antics of the waiter but otherwise this place was awesome and it's now on my list of dining destinations in Manhattan.

If you love meat and beer, this is the place for you! Our group ended up sitting in the back patio area under the heat lamps and were a little cold, however we quickly forgot about it once the spicy beef jerky arrived. Chewy and flavorful, these are something you don't want to miss! We ended up ordering a second portion once the first batch disappeared. Ordering family style, we shared the outstanding country pate, the lamb tartare, and the warm, comforting morcilla. These three were probably my favorites of the night. Meaty and full of flavor, these are dishes any carnivore or omnivore should try.

DON"T EXPECT TO FIND RARE BEER HERE EASILY. Beware!  Very poor experience! Was waiting for the release of a somewhat rare beer (KBS), and was told to come back every day, which I did for over a week, during lunch breaks and after work, calling in once a day as well.   In fact, I was there when the shipment came in from the distributor, and again they told me it would be available the next day.  I took time off of work to be there when the store opened, and when I did, the snobby bartender who opened the shop said that even though they weren't reserving bottles, he didn't know me, so he wasn't going to give me a bottle.   Despite the impression that The Cannibal is some sort of VIP club in Gramercy, I am sympathetic to the fact that rare beers are hard to distribute, but I'm very dissapointed that they would keep on telling me to come back, only let me know that I wasn't a preferred customer when the shipment actually arrived.

So 3 stars because the food wasn't as filling or tasty as I was hoping. But if you're rating just the beers 5 MILLION STARS! They have a stunning array of beers in bottles from just about anywhere you could want. It comes in a giant leather bound book much like fancy wine restaurants. Love it. And it's broken down by beer type which I guess everyone does? I prefer it this way as opposed to by region. The bartender was a beer savant. I asked him about two different sour beers and he was all, "GURLFRIEND NAH-UH! I have the best sour beer on tap right now lemme give you a taste." Dude knew his stuff. He also helped our dining guests with their selections and everyone was please. Mind reader. We had the pretzel for an app and as far as pretzels go it was delicious, but I mean. It's a pretzel. A friend ordered the pork cracklin or whatever that stuff is and was delighted. I had the brussels sprouts with ham gremolata and a soft poached egg. They over poach their eggs, which is sad. The center wasn't runny at all. And the sprouts were really just more salt than sprouty, and it was a tiny portion with massive chunks of bread. I was a little disappointed. Friends had the pastrami smoked salmon benedict and again had the same over poached egg, but they said the salmon was delightful. Of course the pigs head cuban is like their signature dish and our friend who ordered it was in heaven. He really had the only dish that looked like it would fill you up. Also, I know we had a really big party (8 people seated at the bar) but it was really odd that all our food came out at different times, even though we ordered together. I found it odd and we all awkwardly started eating while our last member waited until we were almost done before she got served. All-in-all if I wanted a good drink I think I would stop in here again, and maybe order some nibbles. But for a meal I was underwhelmed.

Meat lover's paradise. I couldn't get enough of the beef tartar. The bone marrow was definitely an interesting experience-tasty if you're into that kind of thing. Most delicious meat board, definitely need to pair that with a some cheeses and wine next time. They have an unbelievable beer selection. I've never been much of a beer fan, but I think this place changed my mind on that. I explained what I wanted and the staff selected two impeccable options-Sophie and Sneak Attack. The pigs head looked and smelled amazing-can't wait to try it next time! The lamb looked really great too, just worries that it's very fatty. The cool, knowledgable staff really tops off this great place.

Delish!  Fantastic, fresh, creative tacos in a low-key setting with friendly, neighborhood proprietors.  What more could you ask?!  I've tried several different menu items, including the chicken and chorizo, slow-roasted pork, and -- my favorite -- mahi mahi tacos.  Every item was excellent, served with colorful, flavorful slaws and fixings, and homemade sauces (be sure to try the chipotle--it's hot, smoky awesomeness!).  And get a side of chips and guac!  Also, sit at the big communal table.  It'll make you feel like part of the neighborhood.

Shifty's Tacos opened recently in Brewerytown with a small menu of tacos and a few sides. Order at the counter and you can sit at the tables inside or outside at a sort of wooden bar you can stand at (and bring your pet). Tacos (3 per order) range from $5 to $8 dollars. While we waited outside for our tacos, I drank an Arnold Palmer and snacked on some chips and salsa ($3). I can't recommend either. The tea/lemonade combo was really watery  and the chips didn't taste fresh. Tacos come in trios, I liked that you can do a combo and sample more than one. I picked the tilapia, the fried chicken nugget, and the brisket.  I liked the brisket the least, it was dry- Shifty's would be better off using a fattier cut of beef here. The creamy, spicy sauce on the tilapia was nice, the tilapia itself was decent, but I have had better fish tacos. The chicken, however, was a great taco. The little nuggets were crispy and flavorful, and the cheese and pickled red onions on top worked well. It reminded me of tacos I have had in Texas. So while the chicken taco was the only successful bite of the day for me, the service stood out in a good way. My gluten free friend failed to mention her digestive issues, and her trio was initially presented on flour tortillas. The staff was quick to replace the whole order on corn tortillas for her. (The original order was gifted to me to take home, but I had been drinking a good amount when I dug in to them and can't offer an accurate account of how they tasted.)

If you went the first week or two after they opened and were frustrated by the wait or didn't like what you got- go back. They've figured out a lot of the problems that, I'm sure, inspired a few of the poor reviews. My first two visits would have inspired reviews that weren't great. My last two visits have been great. Great service and food. Order: The Shifty- pulled chicken, chorizo & maduros is an awesome combination of flavors. The Towner- may sound like its from the kids menu but the flavors are awesome and the nuggets are freshly made to order. Trust me. It's good. The Texican- were you going to buy the Ortega box at the grocery store? Stop in for the Texican. You don't have to dirty any dishes, it will save you a cpl dollars and it tastes better than the box. Don't you hate when a place starts out great then the original team leaves or ppl stop caring and it ends up sucking a few months later? This is the opposite. They're getting better. Fairmounters! You have a reason to cross Poplar!

Just fantastic. The period-dressed servers know the menu inside and out. They can provide details on everything from drinks to entrees! They easily worked with our food restrictions (vegan and some allergies), and not one thing was screwed up. The food itself is rich and delicious- everything is quite filling. The drinks are strong (VERY STRONG) and also delicious! Also happened to go there on Thomas Jefferson's birthday- the servers know a ton about the history around as well. highly, HIGHLY recommended.

Pho Hong has the best food ever. #20 with chicken get it I promise you won't be disappointed. So good and always fresh. You have to wait a little longer than anywhere else, there's not usually a lot of waitstaff, I've only seen three at one time. Parking sucks too but other than that the food is well worth it & cheap!!

This place is amazing. The flavors are fresh and bursting and complex and juicy and popping off the plate in your mouth. It's inexpensive and delicious. It can get busy during meal times and it's good to call ahead to check the wait. Bring your own beer or wine.

SOOOO happy this place opened. Great staff, great food and great atmosphere. What a wonderful addition to our neighborhood! Congrats on nailing it! Cant wait for their breakfast and lunch to be extended to dinner!!!!!
I love this place! Great food, lovely decor, and friendly staff. You can't go wrong... Although I kinda wish they were open later. I would love one of their burgers right now.
Food is unremarkable and overpriced. The server objected when I tried to plug in my laptop into the outlet. Who does that?

They've managed to screw up every single thing myself and my friends have ordered while charging us out the nose for it. Its a Greek diner: baklava and or french fries should not be in the "hit or miss" category. Skip it.

This place is great. I went last weekend and I really loved the two starting chutneys. The food was amazing and the waiter were very nice. I really love how the place looks like. It's really a lively and amazing place to go to. I'll defiantly come back for the food and ambiance.

My faith has even restored with tonight's order. My order was correct and the food was excellent. I tried something new today - the chicken tacos. They were fantastic! And for two large tacos, fries and a drink - it was the best $6 deal ever - the best part - $6 is the regular price. My wife loved (as always) her lamb platter and the chicken burger was on point as always. Will be ordering again as everything was good to go!

We were starving and everything we had was AMAZING. We ordered 3 different things and all of it - even the fresh, hot bread - was crazy good. The guy at the counter as so nice and helpful also (thanks, Ali!) Totally go there.

Wow Great combination of atmosphere, food, service and music. Remember not fancy but good cooking. Walk in to the counter , check the menu and place your order . My wife and I ordered a potato stuffed pastry appetizer and hummus. Both were well made and tasty. Presentation was good and amount was plenty. Then came a couple salads to go with our falafel platter and mixed grill (chicken and lamb). Huge, well made and freshly prepared. What a treat. Ate about half and packed up the balance. Give it a try.
Had the lamb chops kabab. It was very good,  larggge portions and price very reasonable. Saw many poeple there with family and friends. The naan is really good.

Thank you for an amazing evening with (i) very delicious food, (ii) a very pretty venue, and (iii) the best service I got for a very long time. (i) We were four girls and ordered three appetizers, Hummus with Falafel, lamb shawarma, something else and I forgot the name, bread and one main dish, the chicken entrée. We also shared three different desserts. The food was very tasty. Everything came at the same time as we asked for and it was definitely enough for all of us. I wish we could have tried even more. (ii) We were lucky and were seated in the backyard. The restaurant itself has a welcoming and fancy but not uptight atmosphere. The tables are arranged in a way that allows you not to overhear every word your neighbor says. (iii) Everybody was extremely helpful and funny but in an annoying or insincere way.No, they were actually very nice and we enjoyed the little chit chat we had. I highly recommend going there, even if this means that I might not get a spot the next time I try to get a reservation.

Recommended by a friend in May. We have now been 8 times for brunch and once for dinner. I have been recommending Bustan to NY friends and they are also now hooked! Everything we have ever had is scrumptious. We always  take our out of town guests (of which we have many) for brunch and they all live the whole experience. Sitting in the garden is lovely and we are usually able to have Omir wait on us which makes the experience even more entertaining! The Chicken DLT, Pastrami Salmon Flatbread and the Crab Benedict are some of our favorites but the Falafel is the best anywhere.  Its our new favorite neighborhood place!!!

Delicous roasted beet salad, bread, hummus with wild mushrooms, and the most perfectly cooked fish I've ever had. My friend can't eat salt and ordered it without it and I, a salt lover, didn't miss it at all! So flavorful with an herb rub, this was the juiciest, most delicious fish ever! Can't wait to return!

I got the lamb terracotta. The lamb was very tender and good. I thought there would be other vegetables to compliment the meat, however it was just a bed of onions and tomatoes. I do not like onions or tomatoes. It came with flat bread over the food, and the flat bread was good. If you do not like onions or tomatoes I would not recommend this. For me the meal was not bad. However, I would not get it again and it was not worth $30.

3.5. Food was mostly very good - a 4+, but the service was...weird.  I've eaten at a lot of restaurants in my life, and this was probably the most and only truly negative experience I've had service-wise, but the food carries it. Came by on a weekend evening for a friend's birthday dinner. Our server was a very friendly, smiley woman who seemed a bit lacking for words. But that's OK, I'm generally pretty adaptable to all kinds of service situations. I've been in the service industry, and I can tell you, it's freaking hard. So I figured she could be new and shy. But she was just...not really around very much. I generally don't blame the server in these kinds of situations, because I figure it's also possible management didn't plan for enough servers given how many patrons there are - and the house was pretty full. Who knows, managing a busy restaurant is probably really challenging. After ordering our cocktails, I happened to be poking around my drink with the included cinnamon stick when this strange, white clumpy mass jumbled its way above the ice. I wasn't really sure what it was - it looked like a cross between feta and a rolled up wad of densely soaked tissue paper. I gotta admit, against my better judgment, I tasted it, but it had no taste.  After a bit of waiting, our server came by. She didn't recognize the object either, and went to ask the bartender. In the end, nobody knew, so she resolved the situation and gave me a new drink. Great. So far, service is slow, but good, and I quickly tried to take my mind off the tasting of the paper cheese thing.  Then our server disappeared again, for a long time. We almost finished our drinks by the time we were able to order our small plates. Anyway, this isn't really about the delays - one can fill it with nice conversation. Fast forward to our four small plates, one for the each of us. One in particular was the octopus dish, and, being a small plate, that gave everyone about two bites.  But it tasted off. We've had seafood of all kinds, including octopus, but our dish tasted a lot like white fish. Actually, kinda like mackerel to be precise, but who knows, I could be wrong and maybe this was a rendition of octopus I've never had before - very possible. But given that 3 of our 4 thought it didn't taste like octopus (the 4th was not sure), the error with the cocktail, and the possible inexperienced server, I was also entertaining the possibility that we got the wrong dish. So why not ask? And thus began bizarro world. Our server was gone for awhile again, and when she finally came, I guess she was overwhelmed with other patrons, so before we could ask our question, she quickly passed another server onto us.  He was not so friendly. Kind of pitbull-ish. We explained our questions about the dish. We were purely looking for confirmation that yes, indeed, that was the right dish, or no, that was the wrong dish. I assume one can do that by recognizing the sauce and plating. His immediate reply was a blunt, "It's all gone. You guys ate it all." Mostly, true, yes. An astute observation. There wasn't much to begin with, but one of us still had a bite of it left. Regardless, not really an answer to our question, though. From there, I received more hostility and defensiveness from him. It began to dawn on me that, in his mind, we were trying to get a free comp on the dish. Which was actually pretty insulting. But I keep all these thoughts to myself. Then he started off on a mini-lecture about how we may not be too familiar with octopus and how it's supposed to taste.  Wow, thanks. That's not condescending. Then another jab about how it's all gone. At this point, I wouldn't be surprised if he flipped us the bird, and now I'm getting kinda agitated, and I try to explain that yes, we've had octopus before. He still hasn't answered if that's the right dish or not, then kind of shrugs and says he'll get our original server for confirmation. She comes by, glances at the dish, and just immediately says, "I'll get the manager." Before I can protest that, no, that's not necessary, she jets off again. Now it's turning into a face-palming situation. The manager shows up, ask what's going on, I tell him we didn't think it was octopus, but that that's okay, we don't really care at this point. It's all gone. I had hoped that would end things and we could resume our nice birthday dinner, but instead he starts his own mini-lecture about how fresh octopus should taste and that they have a special oven (taboon) which brings all the patrons to the yard coming back for more. My brain thinks, "Okay, well I probably wouldn't order it again if that's what it's supposed to taste like" but of course I don't say that. I'm here for dinner, not for a run at the debate team. Finally, he leaves, and we try to forget the awkwardness. Anyway, on a good note, the hummus and lamb meatballs were pretty amazing. The eggplant small plate has a wonderful smokiness to it. Great food generally.

So delicious. Came here for brunch. The menu had a lot if great choices from conventional brunch to very creative spices and sauces. The service was great, everyone was very friendly and helpful. Definitely recommend the pastrami salmon eggs Benedict and the fresh house gelato dessert with fresh made rice Krispy granola, honey, and halva put through a cotton candy machine!

Just got back from Lithos and had to post immediately.  We found this to be a simply stunning restaurant and we had a wonderful experience.  From the moment we walked in until the moment we left, everything was perfect.   We found the food to be very unique, but at the same time authentically Greek.  And not your standard Greek fair authentic too, I'm talking creative and bold while not straying from the root foundations of Greek cuisine.   The decor is very tasteful while there is a warm and lively ambiance.  Considering the fresh selection of fish to choose from, the restaurant is reasonably priced when all is considered.

The only problem with this place is that you spend half the dinner verifying that your'e still in New Jersey.... You're immediately transported to Greece with amazing fair and confident service. The menu provides many classic options each with well thought and perfectly executed additions and twists. You can't go wrong with any of the specials and the fresh fish are made to perfection. The Lithos chips, taramosalata and Feta filled pastry are my favorite starters along with the Greek salad. We've done the Lavraki (Branzino) on a few occasions but consider the short ribs and lamb options as well. DO NOT SKIP desserts. The galaktobourek (spelling?) and walnut cakes alongside the yogurt (honey or various jams accompany) are the go-to... Wine list is brief but offers every option at a perfectly acceptable price.

Perfect date spot... been a few times these are my highlights -Master selection of cheese: Delicious! Great assortment, including my all time fav, Époisses -Rabbit Sausage, Pappardelle: amazing, fresh, interesting mix of flavors that work beautifully together -Pan-Fried Gold Potato Gnocchi: pan frying pasta... uhhhh yes- please and thank you! -Hudson Valley Foie Gras Mousse: the cherry sauce gave this dish a hint of sweetness that was new and exciting for me -Boat Scallops: Awesome! Crispy and delicious! -Lancaster Beef Tartare: Best tartare I've had in a long time.. I love the use of the Crème Fraîche to help balance the saltiness of the tartare
i love the salads and food is also amazing! customer service was great not excellent. but i would still go back here!

Went there on sunday for brunch with my boyfriend and had a bad experience. I had the breakfast burger and it wasn't cooked-raw in the middle, so I ate around it. It wasn't that great, the flavors they were trying to produce were not hitting the target. When I told the manager about my burger being raw they were great about it and even sent us a dessert that was delicious! My boyfriend had the portobello benedict and he said it was pretty good. Unfortunately, we have been feeling pretty sick ever since. It's four days later and we both still do not feel right.

My boyfriend took me to Talulas for my birthday. It was crowded on Monday night, so I recommend making a reservation. The atmosphere is the best part in my opinion. There is a beautiful outdoor space with a living wall and white lights. The outdoor area was full so we sat inside. I was wearing a dress and my boyfriend was wearing a long sleeve button down shirt and both of us were cold because the air was on full blast. The food was pretty darn good. We started with the international cheese plate which was mind blowing. There were cheeses from other countries as well as a few local places which I always enjoy. The cheese plate comes with some honey, berries and walnuts, all were deliscious.  One of the Managers described each cheese and its origins which was nice to get a little history. The hand-torn fresh pasta ribbon dish was really good but nothing super special. The swordfish was done just right with a lovely sauce. They even brought out a small blueberry cake desert for me with a candle for my birthday :) The bloody mary was perfect, and they have craft beers so my boyfriend enjoyed some dogfishhead. I'll definately go back and try to get a seat outdoors. Great place for a special occasion!

Review 400 and my 27th B-Day birthday dinner.....loved it here. This place literally has everything I love in a restaurant. Farm to table, sexy interesting cocktails, beautiful ambiance and top notch service. Food- all amazing but you have to get a cheese board. Cocktails-really any are a great bet. Ambiance-a bit more upscale then we anticipated. We were under dressed. Do it up a bit, I wish I had worn a dress. Service-excellent our waiter knew everything and anything. Great place for a date. One beef-the bathroom is in no way marked. As I got up between courses a woman popped out from what seemed like nowhere and led me to the bathroom door. Bathroom is also unisex. 8 or so private rooms and a common sink. I get that is the trendy space conserving thing to do but I hate putting the seat down at home let alone in public.

Some nights you just feel fancy. On these nights one might call a friend to get a recommendation for dinner. This said friend referred us to Talulahs Garden. What a pretty restaurant ! The entrance is .. A garden, with a gorgeous ambiance and lovely lights that add a sparkle to the night. We were seated immediately without reservations at 10pm on a Saturday night so that was awesome. The menu was a little overwhelming but I went with the risotto with a light truffle. Jill was our server and she made the perfect recommendation ! The meal was out in no more than 15 minutes and while the dish was absolutely gorgeous and tasty, the portion was snack sized at the most. I ended up going to another restaurant to eat a real filling meal.

I have been a frequent customer for lunch and dinner and have never been disappointed! From the greeting by Rich Tullo to expert courteous waiters, Lou s food is delicious! All around the best New Jersey has to offer in high end Italian food!
I love this place! Happy hour rocks! Best mac n cheese ever!

Great location, the cellar is cozy, has a bar & seating/lounge area beside the tables and is just a real good place to enjoy an after work drink... plus the food was absolutely great.  Even better if you can make it for the happy hour as they have great deals for drinks & food!  Overall a winner!!

Went here for a friends birthday and had a great meal.  There was a short wait so started with a drink at the bar.  The ambiance was great and the drink menu was extensive.  However, my party ordered various signature cocktails, and all of them were a bit odd.  Of course I understand the desire to have creative cocktails, but many of the flavors were off putting.  We ordered two macs - the worlds best and the pork belly, meatballs, and kale salad.  YUM!  I think the pork belly macaroni and cheese was my favorite.  We ordered the kale salad to make ourselves feel better about the decadence of the meal, but it was full of candied walnuts and other goodies which probably neglected our efforts.  Overall, a fun vibe and delicious food.  Might be a better place to share some apps than have a sit down dinner.   Will return!

I understand french / modern / fusion food pretty well and have been to plenty of places like this, but never once have I been so beside myself with how much SALT they used. The duck rillettes were nearly inedible with the salt content, as was my other dish. The cooks that night should each have one of their fingers cut off as penance. I am not exaggerating the salt problem, or have a health hangup. It just tasted awful. Service was passable / friendly, but several awkward moments kind of put me in a foul mood. (Don't yell at coworkers next to my table for god's sake... ) My cocktail was quite good at least, and it's a cool venue. Fix the food and you'd have one of the nicest bars outside of NYC.
Very nice ambiance, great decor and beautiful people. However, there is a strong smell of fried food, not ideal when you are just starting your night out...

This place is quite swanky.  I like it as an addition to the Montclair restaurant/bar scene.  I came here for dinner and got the striped bass which was delicious and had a nice mixture of flavors.  For dessert, I had the chocolate mousse, which wasn't the best I've had, but still good nonetheless.  What I was most surprised about is the price of the cocktails here.  I forget the name of the one I had (Fall something), but it was strong enough to give me a buzz and only cost $5.50.  I'll definitely be coming back for happy hour! Also, gotta love those toilets.  Pretty awesome when you're not expecting it.

Liked the ambience of this place but was a bit pretentious (wanna be NYC restaurant ). The pork belly and beet salad were quite good. Fish special was also very good. Skirt steak that my friends had were very tasty as well. Overall a good place to come to in Montclair.
Expensive as hell but the food was great and very eclectic, which was cool. The tables are a bit uncomfortable and the staff sorta forgot about us, but overall an excellent meal choice!
Cool spot to grab some delicious sandwiches. I had the the roast pork sandwich. It was awesome The dudes behind the counter are nice and they take credit cards, which is rare in this neighborhood.

Great addition to the neighborhood! My boyfriend got a cheese steak and fries from there and was very pleased with his meal!  The staff is very friendly (and flirty might I add) with a great sense of humor.   Two comments:   1.  hoping they will expand the menu and perhaps add chicken cheese steaks and maybe a veggie option; 2. add more meat to the sandwich, it was a bit too thin for a cheese steak. otherwise, we'll be back! good luck fellas!
Great cheese steak, as good as any I've had in Philly! Quality meat and sauce, recommend the American cheese. Friendly staff too

a couple of guys from Philly run the place and they do a fine job at making Philly-style steaks, which are hard to come by in NYC. the owners are very nice and even delivered all the way to my apt in Fort Greene (a few neighborhoods over) on Superbowl Sunday.  good steaks. i'll be back for sure.

I haven't had a true Philly Cheesesteak before, so I will not compare my Deliah's experience to an actually Cheesteak. My bf and I shared the cheesesteak with provolone and a side of peppers. The peppers gave it a nice kick and I'm glad we decided to upgrade to provolone. While it was a very tasty sandwich, I think $11 is a bit too pricey. I think many people will try Delilah's at least once and others will save future visits as an indulgence. Delilah's offers delightful sandwiches that satisfy a hungry belly after a day of drinking. If the sandwiches were $8, I could see myself being a regular.

Such a nice surprise to actually get GOOD steak on a Philly Cheesesteak Sandwich.  I am not a cheesesteak lover but my boyfriend hence why we wanted to try this new place. I took a bite just to try and I was empressed.  My chicken sandwich was good but I should have listen to them with the suggestion and put the sauce on it. I ended up putting sauce on it at home and it was just the touch I needed.  I think they have a good thing going here. We will be back.

To all those who say the service is *slow* - perhaps its because you've frequented too many fast food establishments and forgot what it takes to create a home cooked meal!  This place is like "going home".  Grab some appetizers while you wait for "dad" to cook your dinner.  Everything is fresh.  The food is outstanding and if you don't see what you want on the menu - ASK they will make it!  We've had the veal, pasta, seafood, desserts and it's always been the BEST!  The wait staff takes a personal interest in their patrons and treat everyone like they've just come home for a home cooked meal. This place is just a gem!

I've been making dinner with my family on the weekends for years now. Every now and then we treat ourselves to dinner. Marsilios Kitchen was our pick this time. When first walking in you are greeted like family, with a welcoming staff. The decor had just enough balance of today's hip touches with the feeling of Italy. I instantly fell in love with the huge fork and spoon on the back wall. Growing up we had those in our kitchen. Seeing them brought back the great memories of lots of good food and family in the kitchen. Our waitress was a lively lady named Sharon. She was on point with the food and our wants. Their menu is simple but their food is outstanding. I ordered the chicken francaise. Which happens to be my favorite Italian dish. It arrived fashionably on time and smoking hot. The portions were spot on and the quality was wonderful. I was able to finish my whole meal and have room for dessert. Mmmm dessert...Lil' Red Velvet. Layers of red velvet cake and cream cheese. Topped with fresh strawberries and blueberries. And of course I had to order the Nutella Moccaccino. I never order dessert, but the next time I do it will be here. I think after tonight we shall add Marsilios Kitchen to our family dinners. And Sharon to our table. Marsilios Kitchen deserves 5 red hot stars!

I took my family out for dinner at Marsilio's Kitchen this weekend, upon the insistence  of a family friend who had been there for a recent private party.  We were greeted by a smiling hostess and inviting atmosphere. Decor is modern but very warm, hints of Italy throughout and they even have a rustic 'farm table' which could easily seat 10.  Our server Sharon tempted us with the specials of the evening, and was very nice and attentive throughout the meal.  We started with their eggplant rollatini appetizer, which was superb. The marinara is great here. All the entrees came with a house salad which was perfectly fresh and simple, lightly dressed with honey &balsamic. Entrees were piping hot when they came out.  My crabcakes, which were fantastic,  full of crabmeat served over a slaw in a light lemon sauce, were accompanied well by a side of rosemary potato fries. My wife loved their signature chicken cacciatore, and my mother said she was coming back next week to have more braised beef.  Even though we were stuffed, we couldn't pass up an espresso and their 'can't decide' dessert trio, including velvety house-made tiramisu. Prices were good for the food quality and portions were nice.  Overall, we had a great experience.  The whole staff seemed in good spirits and you could tell they enjoy working together. I will definitely have to try one of their specials next time I visit, which will be soon.
Excellent lunch! Service was very friendly and efficient. Bread and cheese on  my salad were both very fresh and tasty and the portions were perfect for lunch!

My experience at Marsilio's Kitchen was excellent to say the least.  The decor is very inviting, and the atmosphere is classy yet casual. The service was top-notch from the second we walked in the door.  We were seated and within minutes were served our drinks and a nice spread of delicious bread.  We had eggplant rollatini for an appetizer.  I am not a huge fan of eggplant, but I have to say it was quite good. For my entree I had the fettucini alfredo with sausage, which was fantastic.  When dessert rolled around I found it quite difficult to decide what I wanted because they all sounded so good.  I decided to try the blackberry gellato, and I was not dissapointed.  Overall we were extremely pleased with the service and the food, especially  the very reasonable prices.  We will definitely be visiting again soon, and I would reccomend the place to anyone.

great little mexican place walking distance from our home.  last time i got the steak tostadas and they were delicious.  price is competitive to even our favorite real mexican places in elmhurst.  very generous proportions.  the 3 tostadas came in a big serving tray so definitely good value for your money.  they even deliver when we're feeling really lazy.
I come here all the time and crave it when I'm away. Great food, great quantities and very reasonable prices. Their spinach burrito sets the standard no other burrito can meet.
In LOVE with their food! esp the chicken avocado salad, quesadillas & guacamole with chips! it's so delicious!

Have frequented the restaurant regularly every other week for the better part of 15 years, yes 15 years. The quality of the dishes have been consistent and very good throughout. The service also has been very good, always with a smile.

Went with really high expectations, but turned out to be huge disappointment. The worst quesadilla and the priciest guacamole dip we have ever had and seen. Ordinary food. It is BYOB, so that might be the only positive for us. Not at all worth for money they charge.

Greatest BBQ ever! Everything from the sides (BBQ Smoked Beans are amazing, creamy Mac & Cheese, slaw and hand cut fries) to the meats themselves are tremendous. Favorites for me are the burnt ends, turkey breast, kielbasa and pulled pork. Bears does a great job with their unique twists on classics, such as Paw Paw's Poutine and the always popular Mac Attack. As a long time member of the Downtown Hartford workforce, Bears has been a great addition to the lunchtime landscape. Get there before noon to avoid the wait and get a table.

Alton Brown and Steven Raichlen are my food gods, and primarily because of the latter, I appreciate all styles of BBQ so I won't go into a merit debate between East Carolina style v Kansas City v Texas, etc. Bear's Smokehouse does a solid job on the way they cook their meat (I've tried both their brisket and their burnt ends) so they stay in contention as a decent BBQ place in the Northeast. As many other reviews have mentioned, the burnt ends are where it's at. Fatty and flavorful all the way! However, as pointed out by Joe C., although the sauce has good flavor, it is WAY too sweet here. When I ordered the Bear Attack with their spicy sauce (cornbread, mac 'n cheese, meat) , they oversauced it and the sweetness didn't help. Then again, I've got a thing about textures, and I don't like stuff once it gets soggy anyway. Maybe I'll ask them to hold the sauce if I ever head back here. I don't even want to imagine how sweet their actual sweet sauce is if their spicy sauce almost gave me a cavity. Mac 'n cheese is very saucy, and the noodles are a bit longer in spiral than normal. I usually prefer some crust on my mac 'n cheese, but this version was very tasty! Collards were okay, but I hit one or two too tough stems there. The cornbread is good and on the sweet side, and the accompanying honey butter just takes it to the next level. Decor consists of lots of wood and clean lodge-like lines in this place. The line is practically out the door for lunch, so you'll want to order those burnt ends earlier in the day and have a friend save seats. Nice clean bathrooms, and a cool little half balcony upstairs seating. A block from the Convention Center.
I haven't been there yet,but hear it's a good bet.

Bear's Smokehouse is the first BBQ joi8nt I have found north of the Mason Dixon line that turns out world class 'Que. It's that good. I found Bear's during a walk through downtown Hartford. I'm glad I did. Bear's is located in what looks like a renovated warehouse, very clean inside and out. Looking at the menu I decided on the 3 meat platter with 2 sides, $17.99. My choices were sliced brisket,pulled pork and burnt ends with sides of baked beans and mac and cheese. To order you stand in line cafeteria style, which is nice because you actually see your meal prepared. since it was mid-afternoon there was no line and I was quickly served. I added a fountain lemonade, paid for my meal and sat down for a feast. Try to find a table next to the meat prep station, it's cool watching giant briskets and pork butts being prepared and placed in the to huge smokers. speaking of  the smokers, 2 Fast Eddy FE750 smokers, these things ring in at about $20k each. Serious stuff. Back to the food, the brisket was perfect, tender, excellent smoke and perfectly trimmed with a nice rub. The pulled pork was just as good, outstanding. The burnt ends while very good lacked a bit of chew, burnt ends should be a bit chewy, a bit caramelized texture, still the flavor was outstanding. The mac and cheese and beans made a great meal perfect. If i had to search for flaws: 1. The lemonade was a bit weak. 2. The Burnt Ends, see above. 3. No beer served. 4. The Bear's website is bad, it really give no clue the menu you will find inside. Still 5 stars, even with these minor flaws. Bear's Smokehouse is the real deal, seek it out and make a point to hit it.

Oh, God, their PIZZA. Their pizza is out of this world. My boyfriend and I live upstairs and we make the long trek down one flight of stairs for the soppressata pizza about once a week. It never gets old. The dough is crunchy and sweet and the rest of the ingredients are just so fresh and bright. The wine on tap is excellent, too. Go here!

I live around the corner, and am so happy to have this new addition to the neighborhood! Not particularly a wine person, but maybe I will start becoming one. Have been here several times for dinner, and have had the pizza and pasta dishes, (which are extremely reasonably priced) and amazingly fresh and delicious (the pesto pizza is my favorite so far). The bread and mozzarella are made fresh in house! Service has always been very good and down to earth, and the vibe is pretty relaxing and nice.

I don't live in Greenpoint. I live in Fort Greene. So Adelina's isn't a place I can walk down the street to. I have to take the train to get there. The G train. Which is more like a caboose. Anyway. My girlfriend and I got off the G at Greenpoint and were bummed to find our friends had mixed up a dinner plan. We were stuck in Greenpoint with nowhere to go and we were arguing. I saw the chalk board outside Adelina's and steered us in to switch up the environment and I'm not going to say that Adelina's is why I drunkenly proposed to her later in the night and why we are getting married - but I'm not going to not say it either. First of all it's dark and nice. You sit on stools like you live there. The bathroom has nice stuff hanging on the wall and yes, I'm the kind of person who judges a place based on their bathroom. My girlfriend - er - fiancee - got a pizza and I had the white bean spread which comes with homemade bread. Amazing. Tangy and nutty. I ate all the bread up and secreted two slices into my bad just like my Dad does so I could eat it on the train for later. The wine comes in these amazing glasses. And by glasses I mean juice glasses. The lady had rose, I had red. A Rhone blend. Such a deal and so delicious. If you know about wine you'll feel stroked, if you don't know about wine you'll feel like you are getting away with it. Then we shared a salad. I had some of her pizza, which is like funnel cake, if funnel cake were pizza. I can't say enough about it. It's a little heavy because it's fried, but when you drink as much wine as we did, it's good to lay a little grease down there. Plus it tastes fresh and the cheese on it isn't heavy like on most pizzas. It's the real stuff. To make a long story short, Adelina's is the kind of place that heals squabbles. The food is great, the bathroom rocks and the people who work there are kind. The place where you look across the bar at the red headed capuchin monkey sitting on the stool in her blue denim dress laughing with her mouth full and you realize that man, you are lucky. You are really lucky. In this dirty city, what more can you ask for? My one complaint is that the thing that closes the bathroom door is a little hard to fasten.

I really love this idea of offering lower prices through wine on tap.  Who wants to pay $13-15 for a glass when you can get a great wine for $8-10? I hope more places in Brooklyn (and Manhattan) think about doing this.  We looked at the menu before we went and the food prices seemed very reasonable, too.  I have to agree with the other reviewers that if you're looking for street pizza than this is not the pizza for you.  If you like more artisan style pizza than definitely try the fried pizza.  It's incredible.  Having Adelina in the neighborhood is a huge plus - a mellow place to grab a glass and a snack.

Despite reading reviews for practically everything I purchase, I'm yet to pay it forward and write a review. So here's to my first!  Shanghai Bun is the newest addition to the Ellsworth shoping center replacing Ganges Indian restaurant.  What a welcome addition!!! I've been there three times over the last three weeks and I don't have a thing to complain about.  Today I had the soup dumplings and just make sure they've cooled down to truly appreciate the experience of a true party in your mouth!  Comfort indeed.    The scallion pancakes is a must and I love the chicken dumplings in the spicy sauce which is a mix of hot oil and peanut sauce.  For entrees, we love the chicken in garlic, the shrimp szechaun, the double sauteed pork was good but spicier than the others, the shaghai rice cakes were great too.  Don't forget to get the VIP card for 10% off (cash only) but worth it..  I had five people over and got 4 mains dishes and 2 apps all under $50 with the card.
AVOID HERE! Food is not clean. The service was terrible. It took us TEN mins to argue with them to let us use two credit cards. This place is terrible. Seriously, AVOID HERE!

Delicious soup buns. Shrimp shumai were different from the ones I get at dim sum places but still tasty. Pan fried pork & chive buns - good, especially the dough. We also had the fish special and szechuan chicken. They were pretty good but not particularly amazing. My friend said the szechuan chicken was not authentic but we probably could have guessed that from where it was on the menu. Both were better than what you would get at typical Americanized Chinese places though. The apps definitely made the meal. I'll be back with more friends next time to sample the rest of them. Service was good and timely for a weekend night dinner. No delivery.

Let me start off by the ambiance of restaurant. Small, cozy, but very noisy place. I almost could not hear colleagues across the table. Waiter well trained and top service. But foods was below average, maybe because my expectation was set higher by all the hypes in review. Plus, I Was the one to bring all my colleagues here for special occasion. Here are Pros Cons Recommendation Monkey Bread: Good 4/5 Barbecued Octopus: 1/5 Im open to new asian fusions, but taste did not blend! Scallops:  2/5 salty as rock salt Bucatini: 2/5 Ive had way better at local store Roasted Duck:  3/5 One of the best we tried. Recommendation: Do not come here for the foods. But just to try the new asian fusion. I would not recommend to friends. For 500$ for party of 4. Hm.. Waste of money, could have gone to somewhere nicer, better, and way fancier.

Best Bite: Carrots, Trout DEC 1,2013 - The early word from Eater on Piora was relatively good, Pete Wells' had provided his semi-endorsement and it was close to my new apartment. Here are my impressions. We dropped by for dinner pretty late on a Friday and immediately noticed the dramatically lit garden backdrop. I don't usually take much notice of the room, but as focal points go, this was one of the more impressive ones I've come across. OK, onto food and drink... First to the table came the barbecued octopus with fermented pepper, basil and pine nuts. I was really looking forward to some strong fermented flavor to contrast with the smokiness of the BBQ, but found only the latter once I tasted it. My guess is the "hot and deeply funky" gochujang was toned down following the NYT review, seeing as that description far from suited my version of the dish. The carrot dish arrived next, complete with plenty of crushed pistachios and yogurt base. It was a mix of carrots that were either (1) cooked in their own juice, (2) pickled or (3) cooked in ham fat if I remember correctly. The mix of all three created great balance and intense carrot flavor that definitely worked for me. Between the appetizers and the entrees, we also wanted to sample the bucatini with dungeness crab, black garlic, maitakes and chili. Our server gladly offered to split a portion, so we each indulged in a buttery, earthy pile of noodles complete with a hint of crab. Very comforting dish that left you wanting more (especially after a 1/2 portion), but will say I didn't pick up any heat on the plate and thought it was a bit shy on the seafood. My entree was an absolutely perfectly cooked square of trout -- crisp top and all -- topped with cauliflower and nduja over what I suspect was a pear and cauliflower puree. Texturally, I was very pleased with the elements for crunch, the flaky fish preparation, and a creamy puree beneath it all. The tastes married well, and it made for a solid dish. The second entree, a juicy slice of duck served alongisde farro and a jujube (a Korean date not to be confused with a gummy) sauce, finished the savory portion of the meal. I would chalk it up as another comforting dish, but without a standout flavor or memorable element. As a diner that wasn't familiar with the jujube, I was hoping a sauce like this one would offer up something stimulating, but instead I think it fell short, only exhibiting a mild sweetness. We ended the night on a satisfying note with dark chocolate tart, fresh raspberries, raspberry sorbet, a yuzu foam and pistachios. The dish made good use of pairing tart fruit and bittersweet chocolate, closing the meal with both freshness and some indulgence. Wrapping Up... Piora was both delicious and unspectacular. Most dishes had a satisfying element whether it was a smoky char, crispy skin or tart sorbet, but in most cases I found myself expecting flavors that were never quite present. I think it's a good sign that the intention behind each ingredient makes the dish concepts really attractive on first read, but my hope is that through some continued tinkering the menu hits its stride and delivers on its potential.

Amazing service and amazing food. The owner personally greeted our table.  We were first served a rich potato soup with truffle oil to taste shortly after a dangerously tasty cocktail called leaves falling.  Rigatoni was cooked to perfection and the duck was to die for!
Great food, great service! One of my favorite spots in NJ!
Great good. Great service at way Bette prices than everything else in NJ. I will return on the regular.

I was born in Bungsar Maternity Hospital, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. I grew up in Bukit Bintang and went to  grade school at the Good Sheperd Convent. I can vouch for authentic Malaysian Cuisine and the quality of food at Penang is as good as it gets! I highly recommend the Satay dishes and Beef Rendang. You have to grow up in Southeast asia to really appreciate the Sambal and Belachan Dishes as this I think is an acquired taste ( a cacophony of pungent, salty,bitter, sour and spicy tastes). The best Char Kway Teow I've tasted was in the Four Season's Resort Beach Restaurant in Pulau Langkawi in idyllic Andaman Sea off the NW Coast of Malaysia. The Penang version comes in a close second! The Hainanese chicken rice is very delicious as well as the ginger and scallion  dish variations. Malaysian Cuisine is a blend between Indian and Chinese Cuisine but less spicy and less greasythan the former and latter respectively. The Service is very cordial and swift. You should all come and enjoy this magnificent place right in our backyard!

Generally the food is good and  spicy at Penang. The quality and attentiveness of the waitstaff leaves much to be desired. A lunch here for 2 runs $50 with tip and for that price one might expect the occasional drink refill.

Absolutely 5 star brisket!! But when I think bbQ I  think ribs, and I wasn't nearly as impressed with their ribs. I'm not really a fan of brisket but this one is just not to be missed. The chicken wasn't anything special either. It wasn't bad but I wouldn't get it again. So in conclusion go there if you want the best brisket ever, even if you don't like it, you will like mighty Quinn's, trust me....

I had the good fortune of being introduced to this place at 4:00 pm on a Tuesday when it was almost completely empty, thus avoiding the dreaded block-long lines I've read so much about.  To start off, I'll admit that barbeque and NYC sound like they're mutually exclusive, sort of a lost food amongst a sea of just about every other culinary category you can think of.  I've had some decent BBQ meals but none that really stand out enough to make an exception, so take that as you will with this review.                           I had the sausage and beans with burnt ends, along with a Hass.  And... it was delicious, a wonderful sweet, tangy, smoky combination in each bite, continuing to satisfy even when I was more than full.  Ordinarily, I expect prices in the city to be high, but $50 for two meals and a beer doesn't exactly make this a go-to spot for every day dining, especially when my portion of meat was only 1/5th of an entire container.  However, in the end it didn't really matter because I left full, satisfied and wanting to come back.  Come to think of it, I should probably just camp out at the end of the block now, just to make sure I get in...

A BBQ place well worth 5 stars. The line wait can be very long, but the food is well worth it. The ribs are amazing, as well as the briskets. The food size is also fantastic, even for the price. This place is incredible and worth a stop if you are near the East Village in Manhattan. Great atmosphere if you can find a place to sit.

I read the great reviews on Yelp about Mighty Quinn's which made me check this place out. When I went there it was around 7:00pm and there wasn't a line or anything but the place was packed. But by the time I left, there was a long line. I heard that the Brisket at Mighty Quinn's was very good so I ordered the brisket. Now before the guy took my order for the brisket, the guy in front of me ordered the half chicken which was HUGE. After seeing how much the guy got for his Half Chicken, I expected at least some what of a good portion for my brisket. But I was wrong!! The portion was very small. For the side dishes, I got the beans (which was a little sweet for my taste) and the vinegar coleslaw. The coleslaw portion was so small that I finished it in 3 bites. The Brisket was tender and moist but I felt that there was nothing very special about it... The food is NOT bad. It was actually quite good but I was just disappointed with the amount of food I got compared to how much I paid. I remember thinking to myself, "With the amount I spent, I could have gotten Chipotle w/ Guac and a drink and would've been much more satisfied". Next time I go there, I will try out that half chicken!
Best brisket I've ever eaten. Brontosaurus Rib was excellent. Hopping place with a cool interior. Good beers on tap. Nice outdoor seating area. Wish they had a location in Wisconsin!
Food was not good at all. Fed the leftovers to my dog and she got sick too. Its hard to find good bbq in NY but this is definitely not it.

Loved the brisket. So far it's the best that I ate in the city. The meat is moist and tender. Great sides and drinks. The prices are fare and it's self serving. Clean and nice place although it's not big. Very good service. I would go there again for sure.
This is the best bbq I've ever had meat is so moist you don't need sauce employees are friendly and helpful.  Do yourself a favor and eat here your taste buds will thank you.
Great place for portuguese food. Atmosphere is nice and can byo. Waitress was great and the bbq chicken and ribs were awesome. A must have!!

Completely in love with this place! They have a great service, very attentive and the food is to die for! I ordered the flan for dessert which is home made and my mouth just waters every time I think of it. I recommend it to all my friends and family and anyone who asks me of a good traditional portuguese restaurant to go to around this area!!!!

I was excited to have Dimitri back after Table 8 closed.  The menu and service was really lovely tonight.  We shared the dates appetizer and had hanger steak entree which was perfect and Black and white sesame crusted tuna..also perferct.  The fudge brownie flight to share really topped it off!             Welcome to Upper Montclair..we will be back many times!

amazing!! we went on a saturday night without reservations so we anticipated waiting at the bar for a bar table to open...we had a cocktail at the bar, great fun atmosphere...the food was soooooo delicoius! loved the cheese plate (and the hot crusty foccacia bread they serve with it)...we split the orichette and the short-rib over polenta- both were sooo great! our waitress was fantastic and so nice! So so excited to go back!!!

Luke's Lobster is a great addition to the neighborhood.  I wouldn't go on an empty stomach, but on a nice warm day this is the place to be.  I tried a lobster roll and a crab roll, and both were quite obviously fresh.  The lack of heavy mayo and butter was refreshing, as the flavor of the shellfish was the main taste.  There is some peppery flavoring on top, which is a nice touch.  The whole place has an underground shacky vibe to it, which is perfectly reasonable.  If you are looking for a simple lobster roll, this is exactly what you will get, no frills, exactly that.  Is it the "best lobster roll ever," as other reviewers have claimed?  No, but I don't think its trying to be.  Their rolls are unpretentious and simple--exactly as a lobster roll should be.

BE STILL, MY HEART! I'm so happy Philly has a Luke's now! I checked out Luke's during its grand opening weekend. I groaned as I walked to Luke's because it was a busy weekend - college graduations all over the city and the Rittenhouse Row Festival - and I was nervous it would be packed. Luckily, no one seemed to be too hungry at 11:15 a.m. The menu is short and sweet and located right next to the register. But I walked in knowing exactly what I wanted - the crab sandwich combo, which comes with chips, a drink, and a pickle. I know, I know, it's Luke's LOBSTER. And yes, the lobster rolls are awesome. I just happen to prefer crab, so if you're like me, I can definitely vouch for the delicious crab option. Grab a friend and split the Noah's Ark - it's a pretty good deal at $38 because you get two half lobster rolls, two half crab rolls, two half shrimp rolls, two pickles, two drinks, and two bags of chips.

I only eat whole lobsters in Maine.  There is no point in eating them anywhere else.  There it is a local food and rather affordable.  You get your hands dirty and you make a real mess.  Lobster roll is a simple sandwich, and is often made to use up left over lobster (Yes, that happens there).  It is NOT a big mayo bomb with celery and various other assorted filler.  It is chunks of lobster on a toasted roll and that is all.   So, if you think that a lobster roll has piles of filler and Hellman's took a dump on it, you will not like this roll.  If you DO like a cup or so of fresh, cooked lobster with just a smear of mayo and a hint of seasoning (I believe it was celery salt) sprinkled on it, you will LOVE this sandwich!  This is, bar none, the absolute best lobster roll I have had outside of Maine.  Period.   I had the combo only because I was intrigued by the Maine sodas they had.  I very seldom drink soda and cannot even remember the last time I had a Coke, regular or Diet.  But these had NO HFCS and had interesting flavors like Maine blueberry, and ginger beer.  I went with the blueberry soda and it was delicious.  Sweet but it had just enough bite to not be cloying.  I also could not remember the last time I had chips but took chips there because they were the Cape Cod brand and kettle cooked. Sure, it is a little on the pricey side (My lunch came to18 and change) and a little small. But it was a delicious sandwich.  Buy one to go and enjoy it with a green salad.

I don't think I can love this place enough. Though I was born in Jersey, I've been in love with New England for years. One of the things I love the most is the freshness of the seafood, and that unlike down here, in NE you get a lobster roll that's barely about the mayo. Luke's is the real deal. Dab of mayo, shake of seasonings, all lobstah. Or shrimp. Or crab. The combo includes chips & a Maine Root Soda, and is even more worth it. The only thing I regretted about my meal was not getting a double order - it's that good. I will be going back, no question. That, and I have a ton of respect for a business that is able to get me in & out the door at lunchtime in 10 minutes, with no issues, on its second day.

Great atmosphere (notwithstanding the line out the door at 12:45pm)  - Philly needed a place like this. But the $2 side of coleslaw was so small I finished it in 2 bites. The lobster roll was excellent but part of the bun was missing. More attention to detail is needed. Quality should not be sacrificed to accommodate the lunch rush.

This is a great lobster roll, and right by Rittenhouse Square. I recommend getting the lobster roll combo (comes with a Maine microbrew root or ginger beer, a cape cod potato chips bag, and a pickle), and taking it to eat in the park. Delicious, and reasonably priced for what you get. I've got the loyalty card (Buy 10 get 1 free), and I'll be back!

I've been wanting to try this place ever since I heard it was taking over the Bonte spot.  Stopped in on an off hour on a Sunday.  I had the half crab, half lobster, not the combo.  It's not on the menu, but I asked if I could do that because I was doing take out and had drinks at home.  Each roll was put in its own hot dog looking container.  When I got home I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of seafood on both sandwiches.  I had to use a fork to eat some of it.  The butter and the spices are a great, simple combination.  My only complaint is that I wish I had more because it was really good and not super filling.  Need to go back with a friend to try one of the big combos.

The food tastes great. I really like the way they set this place up, the look fits the food. I had expected the price to be over $15 given they were serving lobster, but then I was surprised when I saw how small the roll was. However, the sandwich was really tasty and it was only $2 more for a nice soda and chips. All three together made a nice sized meal, even if it looked small on first glance. I would go back.

So, Luke's Lobster is a chain. Also, yes, the rolls are small, and I saw them take them out of a plastic bag on the counter (so they are not fresh).  And yes, the sandwiches are expensive.  But FOCUS, PEOPLE! None of this matters! Go here! Order the lobster roll (and the crab roll--a close second)!  You will not be disappointed. The sandwiches may be small, but they are ALL succulent lobster (or crab) meat, very minimally dressed.  (The shrimp roll was sort of unremarkable, however.) My boyfriend and I spent like a week's worth of grocery money here for lunch on the Saturday before Memorial Day. We ordered the Noah's Ark (two half-rolls of each of lobster, crab and shrimp, two pickles, two drinks and two bags of chips: $38), plus TWO extra lobster rolls. And boy, was it good. Remember that aforementioned, apparently store-bought roll? Well, when slathered in butter and grilled, it turns into a slightly-crispy-on-the- outside, gummy-on-the-inside, perfectly scrumptious vehicle to lift that little pile of delicious lobster meat to your lips! Seriously. So. Good. Other points: The décor was charming, the staff friendly and I loved the bluegrass music playing through lunch.  My only complaint about this place is that the sandwiches are so delicious, you want to sit and enjoy them, but it's a fast food place.  As you eat, there is a line going by your table. There are people waiting to sit down standing next to your table staring at you, waiting for the slightest hint that you will soon abandon your seat. This is a little uncomfortable, esp. if (like we did) you brought a six-pack of beer having heard it was a BYOB and are trying to enjoy a leisurely lunch. I would probably just try to find an off-peak time, since we got there right before the lunch rush. It was just a small blight on an otherwise enjoyable experience.
I have been there for so many time. The food was great.

Sometimes it's a nice feeling to go back to a place that has never changed. I used to come here all the time growing up, I later moved away. Every once in a while I get to stop by and visit this gem. I usually order the chicken Caesar wrap or a Rueben and usually a milk shake. And they still give away the tricolor lollipops that I use to have as a kid. Although it's probably nothing special to any new comers and the staff consists of your typical Jersey waitresses, it's just nice to come back to something that has not changed, that's why I tend to give it that one extra star.

I ordered the Desnuda po-boy and a pint of beer from Desnuda. The Desnuda po-boy and fries plate were delish! Perfectly seasoned and tasty. The sandwich was so packed that I had to use a knife and fork to devour it. As soon as I sat down and even before David knew I was Elite, he promptly greeted me and offered me a carafe of still or sparkling water and asked if I was having dinner. Although he was busy, he took the time to check on me and chat with me. Very friendly and attentive -- how bartenders should be! Great service is very important to me when dining out. Because of David, I will definitely stop by again and try the unique items served on the second floor! David definitely turned around my bad experience two years ago. If you're a seafood (oyster) lover, I highly recommend Desnuda Bar!

I absolutely love this place! Mark, the man behind the bar has a good head on his shoulders. Friendly, sociable and genuinely excited about what he's doing!  We only came in for a cocktail, and stayed for a few more than that. As a bartender, I appreciate the small but well selected liquor selection. Mark knows his products and you can tell he selected each one of them for a specific reason. The lamb looks amazing! I'll have to get it next time. In terms of the space, it's absolutely beautiful! I love it here!

Great decor and ambiance; appropriate for a date for sure. I got the sausage entree; a friend got the rockshrimp appetizer, which seemed like a plate of large cocktail shrimp essentially. Overall the food was fine, but not necessarily memorable. Their wine menu looked fairly varied, but we didn't try any.

This place is great! I got a table because my father has a friend who can get a table. The food was delicious especially the meatballs!  The staff and owner where great! The owner Frankie came up to us and spoke with us for a few minutes and Jimmy Fallon sat at the table next to us! I loved the old school look and the holiday lights that are always at the place. From my understanding the place never changes and always looks the same. The only thing they will add are autographs of athletes, actors, and famous people that are on the walls. I can't comment on price because my fathers friend is a priest and they did not charge us. I highly recommend Rao's and if you have an opportunity to go then drop everything and go!

Coolest place in NY. I am lucky enough to have an "in" so I get to go about twice a year. I have seen some really cool things in this place. Sports stars, politicians, billionaires, models, wall street tycoons, actors,wiseguys all just another night at Raos. The cast of charactors who work there are terrific. Once you are in they treat everyone the same, whether they are famous or not. People check their attitude at the door no matter who they are. The mood in here is great, everyone is there to have a good time and relax. If you are lucky enough to get in remember the table is yours for the night and it is cash only.  There are no menus, but they will make just about anything you want, the food is soooooo good. This is typical meal for a table of four when I go. We start at the bar around 7:00pm have a drink and listen to Nick the vest tell stories. Next step Joe seats us at the booth and goes through the food offerings. It is all family style everyone shares. I usually start with roasted peppers, seafood salad, baked clams, and mozzarella en carozza. Then we have two pastas, a taste of shells in a red sauce and some with garlic and oil with sausage. Next the meatballs, they are insane best in the world!!. Then we go with some lemon chicken, veal parm and sometimes some steak.. Dont be afraid to save some room for cheesecake and homemade ice cream with your anisette and coffee. .

I'm not a foodie, but I know what's good and everything I've had at Biblio has been above and beyond. The Chicken Liver Mousse and French Pork Sausage are sensational, as well as the Mac & Cheese, but I can honestly say that I could point blindly to the menu and be happy with my order. The food, service, and drinks are top notch and the location can't be beat!

We had dinner and a couple drinks at Biblio and this place really deserves the 5 stars. The food is so incredibly good...even the most basic mixed green salad was delicious!  I also had the smoked cauliflower fritti and the red jacket barley.  The cauliflower dish was really good, but the red jacket barley wins.  It's made with vegetables depending on what's fresh at the market, so it won't be the same each time.  I'm vegetarian and there's a lot of things on the menu I'm interested to try next!  I also really want to come here for brunch because that menu looks awesome. I didn't have anything fancy to drink, but the selection of liquor and beers is really on point.  The bartender was quick, friendly, and attentive to all patrons, and the music was perfect for the atmosphere. Can't wait to come back for brunch!

If I have -only one week in NYC I'd eat at Ippudo at least 4-5 times out of 7! That's how friken good the ramen is. Westside is a  little tamer than east side. Food is the same :) awesomely amazing!!!

The only down side of this place is they dont do take out or delivery. I've only been to a few ramen houses but this is the best thus far. We had the pork buns minus the mayo and it was tender and flavorful. I ordered the Akamaru Modern and picked takana (pickled mustard greens) and shigureni (pulled charsu). So delicious. Noodles were fresh and not overcooked. The broth w/ a pork base and a tsp of their spicy pepper paste...flavor w/ a kick. I ended up leaving my bowl empty. Actually, all four of us did. If you are into Ramen, you should really check this place out.

Overhyped and overpriced corporate ramen capitalizing on the annoying ramen craze that has gripped America.  Great, so Ippudo is at the forefront of capitalizing on it worldwide.  The whole experience is mediocre, the staff are for the most part irritating corporate drone imbeciles, and every item on the menu is overpriced by at least 30% of what it should be.   As for the taste of the Ramen itself, it is pedestrian.  If you wait more than 10minutes for a table here, you are out of your mind.

Heard great things about this place.  The food is spectacular.  The pork buns and the chicken buns were delicious.    The staff is extremely friendly and attentive.  We had the hirati milk for dessert.  Nothing I've ever had before but was delicious.  If you want to have dinner there...arrive at 4:30 instead of when it opens (at 5pm) because this place is a packed house by 5:10.

This place is ridiculously amazing. If you want unique ramen this is the place to go. My friend and I went during Ramen King and wee able to sample the specialty ramen that was made for only one night. We had the French Consommé ramen one night and then came back the next night for hotpot ramen. So good. I never eat at one restaurant two nights in a row but we made an exception to this place and even came early to wait in line. It was totally worth it.

This was my first time here. The atmosphere and service was great! I ordered the asparagus as appetizer, which I regreted later. It was not anything special. For noodles, I ordered the akamaru modern with soft boiled eggs for toppings. The broth was average, but the texture of the noodle was perfect. I didn't care for the pork. The only downside is the wait so come early or later in the day.

The buns are to die for, and you cannot go wrong with any of the ramen on the menu. The traditional Japanese service creates a lovely energy around the dining experience. Your water glass will never empty and the service doesn't stop until you are out of the door. It's quite the spot.

Unbelievable.  So. Good.  As a vegetarian, I haven't really been to an upscale ramen place before, but now I will search them out.  I had the Hirata Buns, made with eggplant and eringi (whatever that is).  Crunchy and spicy goodness.  Then I had the Sho-jin ramen (vegan and gluten free).  So well balanced and delicious - unlike anything I've ever tasted.  The carnivores I went with enjoyed their meals as well.  I can't wait to go back!!

Large crowd waiting at the door. We thought we'd have to wait for ages and were told that our wait would be about 20 minutes. However we were shown to our table in less than 10. Excellent service staff, excellent food just as good as the ippudo in Kyoto. Wonderful experience.

Summary: Better waiting space with less wait. Upstairs has less ambiance. All ramen is great.  Get the pork buns. Atmosphere: Ippudo West is similar in atmosphere to East. It's calm, clean and  slightly more high end than your average ramen place. You can take non-exotic eaters here.  You get less of the cheering upstairs. I like the cheering, but if you don't, I'd head up there. The service:  Always good. The turnover is huge here, so you're never really waiting to order. They want you fed, happy, tipping and out. The food:  Same delicious recipes. I didn't notice the difference in food quality when I went last. Some claim East is better.  It's a good quality Ramen. I still prefer Toto ramen, but then I hate the wait there even worse. The pork buns are notably good.  The other appetizers - miso cod, etc are ok.  Hence the 4 stars. It somewhat depends on what you order, how its going to go.

super good, the 1hr wait is worth it, i tried the shishito those are boooooomb !!!!!, the" classic noodles " and a side of "hot chili paste", and for dessert the "millie layer crepes", service is amazing ( hard to find here in 'NY' chefs are always laughing, and making kind a noodle show, I'm coming back

I went in for an early lunch, so I missed the rush but I could definitely see a big wait here. I ordered the eggplant and enoki steamed buns not sure if I would like them, but they are one of the most heavenly things I have every tasked, the vegetables are lightly fried and covered in a sticky, spicy, sweet sauce. It has a piece of iceberg lettuce which adds a nice textural component to the softest lightest buns in the shape of a taco you've ever had. Also the ramen was amazing, I topped it with a soft boiled egg. You need to have the ipudo nigori sake, it's an absolute must. This place is fun atmosphere with everyone shouting japanese phrases whenever food is ready or a customer arrives. Will be going back as soon as possible.

Amazing ramen per usual! I am ramen obsessed and Ippudo is one of my favorite ramen joints in thee entire country! This location was closer to our hotel, so we decided to eat here instead of the one in East Village. We didn't have to wait at all since we arrived at around 11AM on a Friday. However, 15 minutes in and the place was packed! Ordered the Pork Hirata Buns to share and for myself, the Akamaru Modern W/ Nitamago. Simply divine, can't wait to come back the next time I visit!

Not really sure how it gets its reputation unless other NYC ramen shops suck. I come from Seattle where we have US branches of 2 major Japanese ramen chains along with our own home grown chains, and Ippudo simply doesn't measure up with the best. I had the current chef special Cha Cha Cha which came with too high of a noodle to broth ratio and minimal ingredients (couple slices of pork and cabbage with a little bonito flakes). It was all just OK. The pork buns are very nice. Given just OK food and long wait times and high prices, Ippudo may well be one of the best of NYC for locals, but for visitors of the city from places with lots of great ramen choices like Seattle or LA Ippudo is not a destination restaurant.
The ramen is excellent especially the broth and the seasoned egg. The line was terrible. We waited for 90 mins.

Ippudo Westside is my jam.  I've been to both of the Ippudo locations, and I definitely prefer this one - surprisingly so, because I generally hate going to this area of town.  This location is larger and the servers are generally more attentive here.  Plus, they have a bar right up front where you can drink AND eat appetizers while you (undoubtedly) wait for a table. I have eaten many items on the menu here and everything - I mean EVERYTHING - is fantastic.  Thank god I don't live close by, or else I would be getting really, really fat on their food. Some of my favorite appetizers include the Shishito Peppers, the Pork Hirata Buns, and the Ebi & Kani Croquettes.  The yuzu salt that they provide with the Shishito Peppers is off the chain.  I never let them take it away once we've finished our peppers because I like to use it on other items.  I order Shishito Peppers whenever I see them on a menu, but these continue to reign supreme.  The Ebi & Kani Croquettes are good in the way that croquettes are always good.  I like the Asian translation of what I typically feel is a Spanish food - it's just so warm and cheesy and delicious.  How could you go wrong with that?  The Pork Hirata Buns are truly the pièce de résistance.  I crave these.  As I am writing this, my mouth is literally watering.  The pillowy buns filled with crisp lettuce, juicy umami pork (never overly fatty or gritty), and the incredible combination of spicy sauce and mayo....I die.  I may have to go get some today...
