I feel like it should have come with potatoes or a side salad or something because I ate my half in about 4 bites. The bread that came with the scramble however, was really tasty, as was the jam. Unfortunately, the potatoes were pretty bland. Looking around, it seemed that most tables got 2 main dishes and split a third, like the fries. We had tried to order a baked good to start, but despite their advertisement, the baked goods were lacking. They had cookies, brownies, and tarts, but no scones, muffins, etc, so we ended up without anything. The food was definitely well made and the staff was friendly and attentive. I wish the portions were a bit more substantial, but I'll probably be back to try it again!

Very disappointing.  I saw a snippet on the news about this place, they made it sound really hip.  It wasn't.  Also the pictures of their food on their website are totally different from what they serve, very misleading.  The place is small, we waited about 20 minutes to sit.  The waitress took our order, we ordered pancakes, french toast tea and coffee.  My wife got her tea right away, my coffee never came, I had to remind her.  Then she brought the wrong coffee, when I corrected her, her excuse was that she didn't write it down.  Good excuse.  The food we ordered was just average, nothing special, and certainly not worth $30.  But the food we saw looking around at other tables was downright frightening.  Heaping sloppy messes of food covered with goop.  And we didn't see many plates going back empty.  We definitely won't be going back.

Great addition to Bay Ridge! Food is fresh and amazing, pleasant atmosphere, nice staff, good background music. Love coming here for brunch, or just for dinner every once in a while. The Beet Salad with a side of duck is amazing! I think i've tried everything on the breakfast menu and it's all really good stuff (Polenta, Bratwurst, Fried Flatbread, German Sausage Hash, etc...).

Not ready for prime time. French is a difficult language for most. Duck should lead the menu. My duck was flavorless and not warm. The Calamari Salad was petite and less than a fresh catch. The Cornish Hen was flavorful but the size of an appetizer. This place is ideal for young couples exploring atmosphere without a budget concern. I enjoy paying for great food or satisfying  portions, but when both are missing, who wants to order dessert?
Mes Rêves has become my go-to restaurant in the area. Have never had an experience there that was not first-rate.

We were told by a friend that this restaurant had a reputation as the best French restaurant in the Montclair area so we decided to try it out. The decor is pretty and the waitress was very friendly (although a little too familiar and intrusive by the end of the meal) and our opinion of the food was that it was very rich without being particularly flavorful. We ordered the steak frites and a fish entree as well as appetizer salads, and we both felt a bit ill later in the evening from the richness of the food. While it is possible that perhaps the place just had an off night, we won't be going back and continue our search for a favorite French spot.

I was excited to try Stock after having read about it in Philly Magazine and other Yelp reviews.  Considering that half of my friends are vegetarians, it's nice that they had a mushroom/tofu pho on the menu.  We made the hike over from Graduate Hospital to Fishtown on a lazy Sunday evening.  My bf and I could smell the star anise aroma coming from halfway down the block, like my Vietnamese mom and auntie's houses on the weekends. Unfortunately, all in all, I would not recommend Stock or return for their pho dishes.  Given their small menu, you'd think that everything on the menu would be focused and on point.  Boy, were we in for a disappointment.  We ordered the beef pho, mushroom pho and pork sausage banh mi. Beef pho - The bowl was filled with tons of noodles and broth and not much of anything else.  This was called "beef" pho but there were only about 6-8 tiny pieces of beef that I had to fish for in the bowl.  You can't really call this beef pho when there were barely any signs of beef in there.  To make matters worse, the broth/stock tasted like they realized there wasn't enough flavor to it and decided to dump an entire bottle of fish sauce in there.  The broth straight up tasted like a bowl of fish sauce soup.  I sure love my fish sauce (in rice and vermicelli dishes), but a bowl of salty fish sauce soup is not what I came for. Mushroom pho - Again, we received a bowl full of nothing but noodles and broth, with barely any protein.  There were 5 or 6 pieces of thinly sliced tofu.  The broth tasted like shiitake mushrooms and a woody type of mushrooms, which was pleasant.  However, the bowl probably costed them about 50 cents to a dollar to make but they charged $9 per bowl.   Pork sausage banh mi - We actually enjoyed the pork sausage compared to the pho dishes.  However, I would not return for the mediocre $8 banh mi.  The Nhu Y Cafe and Café Cuong banh mi in Bella Vista/Italian Market are much tastier and for $4 per banh mi, you can't go wrong.  Even the much tastier banh mi's in NYC are better priced than they are in Fishtown, Philly. The pho took twice as long as a bowl of pho should take to arrive.  On top of that, we asked for glasses for our drinks.  As our server brought out the glasses,  she must have seen something in one of the glasses.  She stuck her fingers in the glass, wiped whatever was in there off with her fingers and proceeded to hand us the glasses.  The server was a sweet girl, but that's just gross. My bf and I were hoping to bring our vegetarian friends and family here next time.  Unfortunately,  we will not be returning.  We will stick with the authentic Vietnamese restaurants in South Philly and Chinatown for the flavors, amount of actual protein in the pho, proximity to the city and for half the price.
On weekend afternoons they serve a Bahn Mi. By far the best quality of ingredients I have had in a Philly Bahn Mi. We will be back!

i am a yellow man that loves noodle soup- ramen, udon, hand drawn, and of course pho. i was up for the idea of a pho place on girard but i think the place definitely tries a little harder than it needs to.. why wouldn't you just go to a real vietnamese restaurant? the beef noodle soup didn't have much meat in it but tasted just fine.. i don't really see any need to go back, especially since there is a small handful of vietnamese spots on kensington ave that i imagine most locals dont know about- hint hint..

i usually like hipster food but hipster pho is gross - should have listened to my instincts but i had recently had white ramen that i actually liked (i'm usually not into fusion food) so i thought i'd try hipster pho. when you walk in you can tell instantly that it doesn't smell like regular pho - it smells really shroomy.  The broth in the beef pho is kind of bland and really salty at the same time.  the beef pieces in the pho (which is the one thing i thought would probably be better quality than the usually cheaper authentic places) was pretty tough and the flank was fatty (but not a melt in your mouth kind of fatty), the tofu bahn mi was really salty but the french roll it was on was very good. Also - the vietnamese iced coffee had like cardamom in it - they should tell you that on the menu as I would have gotten another drink instead.

I'm not generally one to write a yelp review; however, I had to for this spot!   It's really cool inside - the unbelievable ceiling, the totally random, fun artwork, plus the creepy light fixtures give this place an awesome, hip feel.   The food though - the food is really on point.  I shared a couple of starters with friends.  The chicken liver pate was out of this world.  It's topped with crispy chicken skin! Yes, yes, yes!  We also had the wings - extremely flavorful, not too spicy, and not too heavy.  The Cavatelli was perfection - it's in a nice, light sauce with brocolini.  They top it with breadcrumbs to give it some crunch and a fried egg!  All of the flavors and textures really come together nicely!  And they don't overcook their pasta!!  Delicious! They have a smaller selection of beer and wine, but it all seems to be well thought out and pair nicely with the menu.   The staff is eclectic, welcoming, and really informative. Overall, this was an excellent experience, and Miller's Near and Far would come highly recommended!

I went here on the recommendation of a friend and brought 7 friends from work with me. I think we had almost everything on the menu, every bit of it is worth a review of it's own. The burger may have been the best thing I ever ate - fantastic! I Have to at least mention the octopus as an absolute must have. The service was attentive but not overbearing. I will be returning often. Dreaming about that burger.

Definitely have to go check it out. I came in with a girlfriend of mine and had an awesome time, the space is so cool (i think everyone else has said something similar). We decided to just sit at the bar and the bartender was this hilarious girl who totally made us feel welcome. We weren't planning on eating anything but since we were basically sitting watching the kitchen we decided we had to get at least one thing. THE OCTOPUS IS AMAZING! i'll totally be coming back for a full meal soon.

we came to check out Miller's for a recent double date night with some fellow yelpers. Miller's caught their eye with the high initial reviews, though i must say i was/am very skeptical when the majority of rave reviews for a new place come from yelpers with 1-2 reviews (looks fishy to me...!) anyway, we were here so now you'll get my actual take on the spot which is that it has potential but is way too pricey for what you get. the food rundown: we all got apps and mains. i was the least adventerous of the group getting the wings and the burger. between the table we ordered almost everything on the menu (small menu) and the only standout i remember was the skate entree. portion size varied pretty widely though prices were pretty consistent (too high) across the categories. the cocktail rundown: here i think Miller has some major work to do. cocktails are all priced around $13 but i honestly did not like a single one i tried (vodka pickle martini, earl grey something, and mezcal something... 3 strikes and you're...). my final drink of the night was a glass of prosecco bc i had given up on the cocktails. sad. the service / atmosphere rundown: service was really nice. very friendly and accommodating. they had a slip up with my burger order and the add on  bacon and grilled onions came out ice cold (maybe straight out of the r efrigerator or something). she was quick to fix it and bring me a drink to boot so they get an extra star from me for having good service (meaning they would have gotten a 2 star otherwise). atmosphere is nice for a date night or catch up. not too big or loud. nice bathroom that was kept clean even with a fairly full house. only final gripe is that the seats are very uncomfortable. my friend likened her bench seat to a church pew and said that was the best of the various options she tried when they first arrived. maybe Miller's should look in to cushions if they want people to stay for a while. overall i dont plan on returning and am bummed that we dropped so much money (came out to ~$90pp) for what i thought to be average food and subpar drinks. we still had a really fun night though so all was not lost!

One of the best and cool restaurants in NYC: the high quality of the menu combines with the original setting of the interiors: the kitchen is right behind the bar, so clients can see the chef preparing the meals. I believe this is the only way to make sure that what you are eating is actually good. It is ideal if you want to impress a date or for a brunch with friends. The menu often changes, which is also good so you don't get bored. Still, every time I go to Near and Far, I order the octopus and for sure one of their pasta main courses: gnocchi, cavatelli, whatever is there. It's all primary quality, refined and affordable. Impossible to be disappointed. The selections of wines is also worthy of the best sommelier. And, last but not least, the architecture: the ceiling is made out of square tubes with no ending... A magic trick difficult to explain. It' s actually worth to go to Near and Far just to check it out.

I'm updating my review rather than deleting it because my first impression of this place was awful. Still, I went back. The owner, who was so rude the first two times I went, is actually a nice guy who isn't at all polished. Now that I've gotten to know him as a regular customer, he reminds me of my family from Brooklyn; he's coarse and unapologetically abrupt, but very friendly and well-intentioned. He grew on me. The plain pizza is excellent. I live nearby and usually go in for slices or personal pies. I can't give it five stars because I ordered a large pie with a bunch of toppings and it was pretty much inedible...and that was split with three guys I've seen eat week-old leftovers that smelled up the fridge. I've heard from my neighbors that  the rest of the menu is very good, so maybe I'll give that a shot one night and update again based on that. It would be nice if Yelp offered separate ratings for establishments that are either a bar/restaurant or pizzeria/restaurant, so that you could immediately see which is rated better, without searching through dozens of reviews.

I was very eager to try this restaurant since it opened and I was thrilled with my entire dining experience. I enjoyed the ambiance walking in, which was warm and inviting. We sat in the back of the dining room at a table facing the open kitchen and wood burning stove. The food and wood stove smells were incredible, and it was fun watching the chefs cook. The two of us split the octopus, and lasagna to start, which were incredible and very flavorful. The hot kick was a great compliment to the octopus, and the lasagna portion was generous for two people. We ordered the side of sourdough bread, which came out warm and was perfect to dip in the sauce on the dishes. We also split the pork shoulder, which was so tender and melted in our mouths. I enjoyed my meal with the refreshing Donnie Brusco cocktail. The service was impeccable. I am so happy to have a new favorite local spot. Next visit I'm hoping to grab the table by the window in the front of the restaurant to enjoy the open air with great friends and phenomenal food!
This place is awesome! It still has the same cool, down to earth, vibe that Life had, but with much better food and a much needed renovation! This is definitely my new favorite spot.

Just left there with my wife. What an amazing meal. I have followed Chef David for a while and am so glad he brought it all to Brooklyn. Don't miss this hot new spot. Can't wait to dream about our next trip.

A wonderful and much needed addition to the neighborhood! Went with a group of four girls and we thoroughly enjoyed the market sides-- so many to choose from and so delicious. The garlic mashed potatoes, sautéed kale and quinoa with feta were among our  favorites! Lots of vegetarian and vegan options for my friend too. A must is the Mac N Cheese with roasted cauliflower! The Bartender even made me my favorite drink of a Moscow mule with authentic ginger beer! Our waiter, Grant, was outstanding and so attentive. Couldn't have asked for a better meal especially for the price!

When I heard Life Cafe was closing I was devastated. That is until I heard that the restaurant would only be temporarily closed as it goes through renovations and would shortly be re-opened. Now that it has been reopened I can safely say Im extremely disappointed.   While I must say the new layout and over all atmosphere is a little more laid back and more aesthetically pleasing I cant help but be turned off by the obvious act of gentrification that is happening in my neighborhood. The last thing we need in this area is another stuck up, fancy-schmancy, over priced restaurant/bar. Those are a dime a dozen out here in "East Williamsburg" I also feel a little disgruntled by the homophobic and sexist remarks I over heard among the staff/management. The rosemary fries were good and the sides were reasonably tastey but I noticed the mexican aspect of the restaurant is nearly gone which not only adds to my previous statement about gentrification but also leaves my taste-buds extremely let down. If you insist on checking 983 out I hope your pockets are deep, your taste buds are dull, and that you tip your server well (because they cant get paid nearly enough for the shit Ive seen them having to go through both at Life (some of the staff transfered over) and at 983)

It's too bad that some of the previous reviews were based on what this establishment used to be. Everything has changed.  With the new owners, new menu, new decorum and new philosophy, I rate this restaurant an A+. The staff is friendly, the menu is great, the food is fresh, and the atmosphere is airy and comfortable. I have nothing bad to say about 983 and will continue to go back.

So, I've lived in the area for quite some time, and was a frequenter of Life Cafe as it stood.... I would say that this is a nice new sheen (the renovations look good) - but the gutting of the menu has been a shocker. Basically, the only mention in any articles said that it would be changed slightly - and even mentioned that they'd save the vegetarian options, as well as add new ones. Sadly, this isn't the case. They no longer serve tempeh bacon as a side to be added to everything. They no longer have seitan tacos, now they have grilled vegetable tacos. These are things I suppose I could have put up with (even if myself and my friends were eating the damn things 3x a week) if they didn't try and slide in a "vegetable platter" main. They now have a main dish, that is comprised of your selection of 3 of their "farm market" sides. Interesting? Absolutely fucking not. Making a meal of side dishes is something a vegetarian has to do whilst on holiday in countries that they do not hail from - not something worthy of being called a "main" or even a meal. Fuck off with that. The only addition that was reasonable was the brunch menu that I ate the other day - which was a nice benedict with kale and potato, as well as soyrizo on a breakfast sandwich. I guess you really wanted to ensure that anything but brunch should be avoided - which is disappointing. I have no reason to go here other than breakfast now. Leaving on this note today after my 3rd visit since it's renovations - I had decided I could live with the changes - until - we were approached by our waitress out front of the restaurant because she thought we didn't leave her a tip. We were a table of 6, and 20% gratuity was added to our check. She stuttered and was seemingly rather upset - even though we had paid the gratuity - which leads me to believe one of two things; 1) She expected that her service (which wasn't over the top, just average) was worth more than 20% OR 2) She was unaware that she was tipped based on a mandatory charge Either way, I'm not fucking impressed. If you actually are unhappy with 20% - you simply do not raise a fuss about it, and that would really infuriate me - OR - she's such an awful waitress that she doesn't realize she's charged us 20% because of her restaurant's (and practically every single one in the 5 boroughs) policy. I'd like to say I'm going to return - but I'm not, unless it's for brunch and it will be likely to be a begrudging choice. Thanks for ruining one of my favorite places, assholes!

Bad news Bushwick brunch-heads. 983 blows. I'm seriously disappointed in "Bushwick's Living Room", to the point where I don't think I'll be going back any time soon. My first issue: we asked for whole milk with our coffee. They brought out those little coffee creamers that you get in diners. Frankly, I was offended at this cost-reducing change the new owners implemented. This is north Brooklyn, bro. Gimme a big thing of whole milk on the side of my iced coffee or get out. Also, with my toast they plopped a little packet of diner jelly on the side.. Cheap, and makes me feel like the owner's don't care about their customers. Second issue: Their tofu scramble. I used to eat Life's scramble every weekend. I've had 983's scramble twice now, and each time it was deplorable. Just really bland, like they just threw the ingredients together. I could make something better at home, and for half the price. Third issue: Again, my friend ordered eggs benedict and it came with hollandaise and sriracha sauce. Okay, cool, a nice and balanced, maybe seasoned, hollandaise/sriracha mixture sounds intriguing. Oh, wait. All they do is dump your brunch in hollandaise (no complaints) and then drizzle sriracha on top. The result tastes gross. It's also just lazy on their behalf, in my opinion. All in all, the new owner's seem to think they can get away with cutting costs and being lazy. Unfortunately, it's all too apparent to me and the people I've brunched with at 983 that there is NO love in the place anymore. Pour one out for Life Cafe.... :( EDIT: I take back much of what I said before. the coffee creamer/jelly situation was a temporary one day thing. More over, they've only been open as 983 for a month, that explains the quirks like the gnarly tofu scramble I had. I ordered a veggie burger, vegan, tonight for dinner and when it came with some non vegan ingredients on it, I called the owner and told him how I was feeling about the new place. He was so genuine, so kind, and happy to hear my feedback. He kindly sent me another veggie burger, and a note apologizing. That extra effort makes me feel like a valued customer and I will definitely be going back this weekend for brunch, this time with a new mindset!

Pretty disappointing both times i went.  on my first visit, i had very bland fish tacos (though the club sandwich my friend had was pretty tasty).  Our server didn't check back on us after our food arrived, and it wasn't until i called her over to ask about the brussels sprouts we ordered that she realized she forgot to put them in.   They weren't great when they finally showed up (comped), seasoned with mustard and soy sauce.   I returned for breakfast... service was fantastic this time, but the hash browns lacked any sort of crispness.  Breakfast sandwich was ok with well peppered eggs. I dunno... i really want to like this place, Life used to be a staple until it started to go downhill about a year ago...  but.... Meh.  I've experienced better.

Excellent burgers... We also had the BBQ pulled pork sandwich and was blown away at how good it was... The sweet potato fries lived up to all the reviews and were FANTASTIC!!! The atmosphere is completely authentic and adds to the experience. It truly is a gem of a find!

Had chicken and waffles with a friend this past weekend.  The 2 pieces of chicken were a bit small and more fried than chicken - my plate was covered in the breading when I was done - but the waffles were super light and fluffy.  The waffles were served with a berry, lemon and herb butter - all really good. The service was great.  Our waitress was really friendly and our food came out pretty fast.  We made a reservation for brunch and were seated almost immediately.   I will not be coming back for the chicken and waffles but the rest of the menu and dishes passing our table looked really good, so Ill be back for that!
Had an ish week and have a burning need to be comforted or even waylaid by a sublime Mac and Cheese?  Find your way to Sweet Chick on Ludlow Street. Down home menu with a hipster bar.

I absolutely love this place. Found this place via Yelp because I was looking for comfort food with a group of friends with a short wait time. The menu was absolutely amazing. It was kind of hard to narrow down what I wanted to get because there were so many great choices and everyone that had received their food at nearby tables food looked tasty. I ordered the chicken parmesan which came with a sundried tomato and basil waffle. The chicken was incredible and so was the waffle. I also had the sweet tea. It was sweet but in a non sugary way which was great! The waitress was super nice and joked with the table. Great Customer service. When I called to see the wait time. The guy who answered the phone was super friendly and that made me even more interested in trying out this new restaurant. I never felt rushed and the dessert was great too. Overall it was a good experience with great food .

5 stars for the vegetarian chicken. I couldn't tell the difference. It was amazing. I've been the the Brooklyn location so many times not ordering the chicken because I thought it would be not right like most faux-meats are. This one is perfect. Good job!

Excellent atmosphere. The server was really sweet and friendly and seriously insanely delicious shrimp and grits with well poached egg. And their signature fried chicken and waffles was spot on amazing. Crispy batter and moist chicken. The waffles were well prepared and the choice of three flavored butters (blueberry, Rosemary and lemon honey were all incredible) and also nice to get real maple syrup with it. Overall could not rave enough and can't wait to go back!
Loved loved loved it!!! I had the classic chicken and waffles and it was sooooo good.  I am def going back for more and will try the other things on  the menu. Highly recommend it!

Came here for dinner with a friend. For our appetizer we ordered the crawfish hush puppies. They were excellent! Ordered the special for my entree. It was Indian themed with grilled chicken. The waffle had a great mix of spices. While it was delicious, I wish I had ordered something with fried chicken because my friend ordered the classic fried chicken and waffles and I had food jealously all throughout dinner. I take comfort in the fact that I can go back and order the classic anytime, but who knows when they will serve the same special! Our waiter was beyond friendly! He was really attentive and didn't rush us out the door even after we finished our meals. I will be back for sure- my friend and I have made it a personal goal to try every single chicken/waffle item on that dinner menu!
one word: dessert  !!
Delicious sandwiches with a New Orleans and Southern touch! I tried the Fried Chicket Biscuit sandwich and the Veggie Muffaletta--both scrumptious! Nice guys behind the counter, too.

Have to agree with the other reviews here. 5 stars indeed! The chicken biscuit sandwich is great and probably the best I've had in New York so far. Not too sloppy and both the chicken and biscuit tasted great. I'll be back to sample the rest of their sandwiches soon!
Cheeky Sandwiches was delicious. Fluffy biscuits, creamy gravy & perfectly cooked fried chicken. All cheffed up by a sweet guy with massive guns! Go, eat and enjoy!

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would. Too many mornings I wake up craving their mouth watering chicken biscuit sandwich. Everything is always so fresh, creative & the best coffee in my neighborhood. Not to mention the ever friendly guys working at Cheeky's to make my day!
Very friendly even though I came in close to closing. Sandwiches were made fresh and tasted great! Thank you again you guys! 10/10 would eat here again!

I came here because a lot of my dude friends recommended the chicken biscuit sandwich. I honestly did not like it, i felt that the biscuit was too dry and the sandwich needed more gravy. I like that there was a bit of a crunch from the slaw in the sandwich, not much to say about the chicken. This sandwich left me feeling like i ate a very heavy meal, even after i split my sandwich in half. I would give this a sandwich another go but defiantly need to tell them to give me a little more gravy. and the next time I do go back, I will be trying their beef sandwich also. All these photos on Yelp makes it look amazing. They also have biegnets, 3 for $1. Those are fresh :)

After tasting the chicken sandwich last December I was completely enamored with the textures and taste of the chicken biscuit sandwich. To die for! In fact we tried to revisit several times not knowing that it was going through renovations. Finally when we dropped by recently- we noticed a change. Less batter, less crunch, a biscuit shell less crisp on the outside and soft on the inside, and a lighter tasting sauce. It is by no means a bad sandwich- it's solid-just a noticeable difference in quality. I still appreciate the cozy, down-to-earth, simplistic atmosphere in this little LES joint. There's also something great to be said about the welcoming staff. It did cross my mind that there may be a change in the chef or management or... the remote possibility that our palates have changed within the last year. Despite it all, I will be rolling in some time to taste test the chicken biscuit!

I love this place!!! Whoever gave this place a low rating is crazy. The meat is awesome but I realized it does differ depending on who is behind the counter carving/seasoning it. The first time I went it was great but the second time it was okay because the employee carving did not season the meats so well. What to get: flank steak, chicken and pork sausage, fries, rice and beans are average. Great value for great food!!!!

I haven't written a review in a while.  But I get food here too often so here we go.   This place is pretty freaking awesome.  I speak of the delivery because I never went to this place to sit down and eat.  But anyway the food selection is good.  They have have a bunch of healthy and tasty sandwiches, plates, and salads.   I love the Farmers market, baked tihini with bison meat and veggies over egg whites.  I order this 90% of the time.  Delivery is very quick everything comes within 25mins or just about.   Everything is really affordable, unlike some places that jack up prices for Organic meets and egg whites.  They got themselves a very loyal customer.   Keep up the good work boys and girls!
Great cheap fast tasty

Wednesday all sandwiches on the menu at a $1 Can't pass this up. Value, thoughts of Spain. I'm there. Besides the $1 sandwiches which are considered slider size you can find their sangrias at $2 each. Another great value on Wednesdays. Comes in a beer sized mug tasty, a hint of a soda feel but they do pack a punch. Originally coming here and not knowing the menu layout i actually did think it was soda. After 3 vavoom alcohol hits me hard. Luckily had the sammies to absorb the alcohol. The ones to get i'd say are the pulled pork and veggie style which had mozz and pesto in it. Every other variation seemed to be a salami and Spanish ham variation. The bread is definitely a filler as i was quite stuffed after 5 but at ordering 9 had to skip on the bread later. The bread is quite fresh though. Also go for the sides. The potato wedges or regular fries were fried up well crispy and potatoey in the center. Great dipping sauces with the aioli. I would come back on a non wednesday if in the area as sammies at $2.50 isn't too bad either for a snack. But on Wednesday come early, as i did, order lots, drink hard as when the night goes on the place gets slammed and busy as one of our friends had to wait a hour and 15 min. for his order. We didn't mind the wait as our fries and drinks came first and easily held us through till sammies arrived.
6-7 sandwiches will fill you, avoid the American versions and focus on manchego and Serrano!

This place is a little odd and they do not do a good job of explaining how things work. The staff is poorly trained, VERY poorly trained. They are young, inexperienced, and clueless. This may be an ok spot for NYU students on a budget but for adults who are used to paying for good service, pass on this place.

I found out about this spot from an article at elitedaily.com and decided to swing by on a Wednesday for happy hour (or happy day, actually). Who could resist $1 sandwiches, sides, and drinks?! Located at downtown Manhattan, this spot is great to try something unique. AMBIANCE: A little narrow by the storefront, but other than that, it's great. A couple of 2-seater tables and an indoor patio in the back with a sunroof - don't worry, you'll stay warm enough during the winter. FOOD: Mouth watering. Delicioso. Muy bien. Engraved. Did I just mention engraved? Yes, the bread used for the sandwiches are "engraved" with the 100 Montaditos logo - very cool! I can't even name all the sandwiches we ordered, but you should definitely try all of them. My specific favorites were the pulled pork ones and the salmon with cream cheese! I also highly recommend you try the fries and the dessert sandwiches - specifically the oreo cookie one. This oreo cookie montadito was basically a chocolate bread with whip cream. Yeah, yeah. It sounds simple. But you have no idea how well that whip cream complements the bread until you've taken a bite of this. SERVICE: Well, I'm not sure if waiting 45 minutes for our montaditos is worth losing a star since this food was so delicious. Then again, we did order a lot and it was on a Wednesday.. Once your order is ready, you will hear your name announced on the PA. One complaint I had was that one of the employees at the cash register was extremely rude. I went back up for another order to take out. All your orders (by the numbers according to the menu) are written on a piece of paper and given to them so they can input it into the system. When I was handing my paper, the woman gave me an attitude and said "Okay, you're gonna have to wait." Then she proceeded to have me read everything off the paper as if my handwriting (just NUMB3RS) was illegible. Other than that, everything else was A-OK. COST: $1 on Wednesdays, $1-$3 regular days. Need I say more?
Very tasty and super affordable.  Extensive sandwich combinations to choose from...beverages are OK (sangria consists of wine mixed with soda - affordable option).

Yo Taylor, I'm really happy for you, Imma let you finish but 100 Montaditos has some of the best service of all time. OF ALL TIME! I don't normally give an extra star for service but on a day where I was oddly a klutz, the friendly guys here gave me back my earmuffs which I had forgotten at the counter and also replaced a sangria that had spilled. Top notch. The sandwiches themselves are decent, the tortilla and manchego being meh but the chorizo, shrimp, and chicken+bacon being a lot better. The great thing about this place is you can try a ton of different sandwiches (and drinks) without breaking your wallet.

Context: Two of my Friends and I went to 100 Montaditos for a snack / cheap dinner. The bite size sandwiches are really cute ( it looks fake to me when i first saw it) It was self seating, with the cashier in the front.  You can see the 'chef' making the sandwiches through a clear glass. (which i thought was cool) My friend informed me that it was a chain place from Spain. The selection was huge (hence the name). I wanted to ensure i got the most bang for my buck! The Sandwich prices range from $1 - $3 with Sangria's that cost $3 a cup ( i believe you have the option to buy a pitcher) They also had beer, salad, dessert sandwiches, and fries. A blend between a fast food restaurant and a college bar vibe.   My Meal: I choose around 6 different sandwiches scaling of different prices- $1.00 - $2.00 sandwiches. I thought if i ordered $3 sandwiches, i can throw in a few more dollars and get a real life size sandwich! The filling of the sandwich was delicious- it was fresh and on point. I wanted to ensure i sampled all the bread and a variety of filling ( protein) they had to offer. Positives: Fun to go with a bunch of friends after work (or for college students) that want a snack before dinner. The sauce they offered was good & the staff was really friendly. I actually dropped my sandwich and the lady was nice enough to get me another one. The decor was really chill- with a game showing on the flat screens & random vintage like photos on the wall. They had a really creative ceiling for the seating area where it's adequate heating for the winter but also the chance to open up the top for the clear skies in summer. Howevers: The bread and filling ratio was questionable. The sandwich is two-three bites each. You're practically filling yourself up with more bread then anything. The sangria was like flavored water, and the potato fries/wedges were definitely straight out of a frozen bag. The lady calling out your name had difficulty pronouncing names, which made it really hard for anyone to hear- Trust me, "Molly" became "mul-lie". They really need more coat hangers for the winter. If you're a light weight and want your Sangria to be fruit water- the sangria's here are for you! Overall experience, was not too impressed.   P.S. If you're going to have a see through glass for people to see their sandwiches being made, make sure the "chefs" don't have them look they hate being there. It really throws off the nice Cashier and smiling lady handing you the food. Also if you wanted more water- you constantly had to go the to cashier in the front to ask. I can only imagine how water is so valuable when this place gets  mad busy!

What the.. ... is this really the same place as the Pub right next door? That place where regulars hang outside, drinking pints and saying hello to fellow neighbors as they wander by? Where people are always sittin' at the bar, rootin' on their favorite sports teams? And they have a fancy "Mediterranean Bistro" over here? What the what? Look, I appreciate the effort.  Y'all are wearing your fancy clothes and you have your ambient music and a candle and the nice tablecloths. But just like tryin' to put me in a sweater vest, you just can't make somethin' what it ain't. I came here with a LivingSocial and was more curious than anything. I admit I was surprised to find it trying quite hard to be quite fancy when I knew I was one wall away from a place which could sit comfortably next to the definition of "neighborhood pub" in the dictionary. Don't get me wrong, the food was very good.  I had the duck entree, which I can no longer find on the menu and therefore can't pretend to remember particularly well.  It was good, but not great. My date had the tuna, I believe.  Again, very good, but not spectacular. I tried both and I liked them, but it didn't resonate as anything particularly memorable. It was the sort of meal where you said, "Huh, I'm pretty impressed."  And yet when you look at the prices of the dishes, between 20-28, you expect just a little bit more. With so much competition in the bistro-like fare, you gotta bring your A game. The service was also a tad spotty. I won't say bad, but I will say the time between when I wanted a beer and when that sweet sweet nectar of the gods touched my lips was a little long for my liking. But then, it usually is. Overall I had a good time, and the food is quite good, but I think at that price point, there are better options out there.

One of the best meals I've had with my family. Attentive staff, perfect pacing, and the most beautifully prepared rack of lamb I've had in my life. I cannot express my gratitude enough at finding this treasure in New Haven, and I can't wait to go back.

I'm normally too lazy to write reviews but this restaurant experience compelled me to rave about how great this restaurant is. Also, I never would have found this place without Yelp so I need to pay it forward. I was looking for a moderately priced restaurant with good reviews for food and service in the Chelsea area for my birthday and stumbled upon the Yelp reviews for Porteno. True to the reviews, the food and service was superb and I'm so happy I found this gem for my birthday dinner! My girlfriend, mother, and I shared the pate and octupus salad for appetizers and we were not disappointed. Our server, Natalia, was funny, attentive, and sweet and paired us with a Malbec bottle of wine that was just right for us and didn't break the bank. I had the filet mignon entree, while my mother had the chuleta (porkchop) and my girlfriend had the risotto. My entree was cooked to perfection and my mother had a large, succulent cut of pork chop. My girlfriend enjoyed her risotto but felt it might have benefitted from a little more moistness and cheese. The real gem was the service we received at the restaurant. We were made to feel at home and even kissed Natalia goodbye when we were leaving. I left with a satisfied smile on my face and the perfect birthday night out. I'm excited that I now have a place to recommend to friends looking for a quality dining experience!

Delicious food from Argentina! We had the Grilled Octopus and scallops for appetizers which were amazing. Then for entrees we had the pork chops and filet mignon which were equally as tasteful! The servers were very friendly and helpful. This small dimly lit restaurant is definitely one that I would recommend!

Quick Review 11/2012 This is a hidden spot and thanks to Yelpers i found it and enjoyed it. Food- (selling point) Don't miss out the grilled octopus. MUST HAVE The blood sausage was okay. We ordered the special Rib Eye. I'm a steak person and i'm very picky with my steak. My date wanted it cooked medium (i usually want it medium-rare), but the steak came out perfectly tender. The flavors were amazing! It came with a dip which made it even better. Usually good steak does not require sauce, well this dip didn't ruin the dish at all. I did not enjoy the pork chop. Over cooked, lacked flavors and crisp. Not a bad selection of wine. Service- (negative) The blonde waitress was unpleasant. She seemed snotty, stuck-up, and when she tried to be nice she seemd fake. Even her smile seemed surgically implanted. She is the reason I am taking out 2 stars. Decor- (neutral) Not too impressed but it is dark and it is good for a date. Remember that the restaurant is not that big so you may not have that much privacy.

Excellent addition to the far west Chelsea area!  Really good food, pleasant and casually friendly European service and a charming, intimate room make this a favorite neighborhood restaurant. The branzino was fresh and flavorful. The empanadas had interesting and delicious fillings and the wine list is really good. Great date restaurant, too.

i chose this restaurant because of its proximity to sleep no more. that's it. i can't believe what a lucky find it was! the staff were friendly and fast (and our waitress was argentinian and so proud of the food she was serving, for good reason). and speaking of the food, it was nothing short of awesome. so delicious, perfectly portioned, and so different from the typical food i eat. i really, really enjoyed this meal. the restaurant itself is really nice inside as well. i could see it being a perfect date spot even though i went with a friend. order the calamari salad. yum! the best part: the price.

Wonderful little Argentine gem in a most challenging location. I came here to preface Sleep No More with the SO. Around 6 pm, it's wonderfully quiet and you can grab any seat you like. Our charmingly accented waitress had a bit of spunk and gamely encouraged us to order more booze once she realized we were in for an apps-only dinner. I'm sad to report we didn't have the appetite for an entree (the steak-centric menu will have you salivating, I promise), not wanting to be weighed down during the show, but the smaller dishes we ordered were sensational: -Calimari salad: perfectly seasoned and super fresh, served with avocado and grape tomatoes. -Polenta with blood sausage centerpiece: delicious, though stay away if you're not a fan of blood. It was crispy and easy on the tongue, though. -Empanadas: yummy! (There are 3 types: beef, corn, and spinach. The beef was tops for me, but veggie-heads will enjoy the other two.) Their wine selection is pretty spot on. I tried a Clos de los Siete Bordeaux blend from Michelle Roland (Malbec-heavy) that was a great food wine, and a pure Malbec DOC (Luigi Bosca, I think) that was really good as well. Fans of South American wine will not be disappointed. That being said, go for a bottle, there are some good values. Our new Argentinean friend kept checking up on us, always armed with a bottle of  and giving us liquid encouragement. "Drink here," she said. "It's more expensive at the [Sleep No More] bar." The only thing Porteno has to overcome is the obscure location, but Highline traffic and an already strong following (visually confirmed) will keep it going as a great date restaurant. Can't wait to have a reason to return!
Just an FYI this place does not deliver.

It's funny that everyone always comes back, even though we know how bad the food and service is. Thai Village is the only thai restaurant within walking distance of campus, is great for groups - but we all keep coming back to a restaurant that we know will disappoint us every time. There is no better example of a broken supply-demand chain. I've even tried talking to management - doesn't help that they don't speak English. But whatever conversation we were able to have ultimately ended in them saying they don't really care about the quality they serve and they don't care to improve it. What can we do? The food isn't great or terrible, but they desperately need new management who is dedicated to creating an authentic, delicious and customer-oriented restaurant -- and who can communicate with their customers and take feedback!

Dear Hanover Inn, You REALLY need to add more vegetarian options here. Especially with all the guests from hither & yon coming to stay in town. The place looks lovely but I have had to reschedule 2 dinners now with guests at the College because they could not find anything to eat on your menu. One meatless option just isn't enough in 2013.

Not that good. I'd heard people rave about this place, so I'm pretty disappointed. I had a parma melt. The sauce was overwhelming and not great. If you can't do a parmigiana right then there's not much hope. Very dated interior. Don't they like to spend money on making things look good? Drinks were good and the waitress was lovely, they each earned a star, but I won't be going back and won't recommend it to anyone.

Good hot pot but found a thin sheet of plastic in my food. I could've potentially put it into my hotpot and it would've melted into my broth. I told the waiter and he just offered to take it away. I expected a bit more action from management to remediate the issue.

99 Favor Taste is for about the experience than the food in so many ways. An opulent multi-level dining establishment, dressed in red, black, and gold, provides a feast for both the eyes and the stomach. Dining with fifteen other Yelpers for an UYE (...an Unofficial Yelp Event, for those not familiar with our casual Yelp slang...), some of us were seasoned hot pot consumers, while there were many virgins, such as myself, among the group. For $21.99 per person (prior to tax, tip, and all of those other goodies), we were able to indulge in two hours worth of AYCE hot pot goodness. For our large table of 16, we split eight pots of various broths amongst us. From a menu, we were all able to decide upon various proteins (meats and seafoods) and vegetables to satisfy us. We were also able to get up to the "sauce bar", so to speak, to create customized dipping sauces. I was simple with hoison, sesame oil, and cilnatro in one bowl, and fresh chopped garlic and sesame oil in another, while other table mates of mine definitely got a bit more creative and, literally, spicy. Once the goods were delivered, we dipped, ate, and were extremely merry. Not only was it delicious, but fun and interactive. There were some points of the evening that were a little less than satisfactory. I do feel empathy towards the servers, as, DAMN, it's busy as all hell in there! However, it took multiple waiter requests and a good 20+ minutes before we got our second platter of proteins and vegetables. One patron did not get even the rice he requested three times. Some of the hotplates on the table worked better than others; mine in particular had extremely non-responsive buttons. It was hard to lower temperatures and turn it off. If you're looking for a great communal dinner spot and don't mind breaking the barriers of infection control or possible cross contamination of raw animal products, definitely check this place out!
Friendly service. Reasonable price. Things looked fresh. Definitely will be going back.
Came here with friend on Christmas Eve. Very nice service and good food. Really good seafood for a buffet. Will definitely come again!

This place is awesome! There's so much to chooses from and they give you some very good portions. The inside of the restaurant is cery beautiful. It's a very good price fir all the fiod they give you.
Excellent hot pot place! Great place for an excellent price. Food was good too Good good good good good good good good

Came here for an orphan's Xmas eve. It was perfect. We had the hotpot/BBQ combo and some cava that we byob'd which works nicely with the  buzzy szechuan heat in the "spicy" hotpot broth.  We pounded  the hell out of the duck BBQ as well.  The prawns were juicy as hell and Christy, our server made sure to keep the heads on for us. This is FUN.
Great food and excellent service by Christy. Can tell they are making every effort to make the dining experience enjoyable. Will be back for many times.
I had hotpot there with family and friends on Christmas. It was great! A lot of delicious food.

Great restaurant to try the hot pot! I haven't done much hot pot, but this place is really good, with many soup bases to choose from and all kinds of meat and vegetables and seafood to add- all you can eat! $22 is very worth the price, and the 2 hour wait on a Saturday night is worth it also. I tried most of the vegetables and seafood and they seem quite fresh.

Did the all you can eat hot pot and was pleasantly surprised by the variety and quantity of food (base, veggies, meats, noddles etc) tried the curry, original, spicy and kimchi bases. Only downside was that meats were incredibly fatty. Nice polite wait staff. Would def come back again to try the BBQ

I've heard a lot of good things about this place so I came with high expectations.for me, I think this place is a bit over rated as the lamb and beef here for hotpot is not very fresh. As a hotpot lover, I'm quite disappointed.

I came here with my brother for his birthday (free meal on bdays with ID!). We opted for the ayce BBQ which is $25.99, and I'd recommend that if you love meat. I wouldn't come back here for the bbq just because I'm not a big fan of eating so meat at one sitting. I would come back to try the $21.99 hotpot. You can also do both for $30.99. Overall, I really enjoyed the experience here. The decor is neat, clean, and open, love the high ceiling. Their chairs have mini pillows! My brother and I came at down time so we walked in and got a table w/o reservations. The waitstaff gave us a plastic bag for our jackets- how thoughtful. Our orders were taken via an iPad which I thought was quite neat and the food came quickly. The staff helped us cook all of the meats so we didn't do any cooking on our own. You can choose from many different proteins- beef, pork, chicken, seafood, duck, lamb, as well as vegetables which I'm sure no one chooses.  My favorite meat was the curried chicken. And while the meats were good, I felt they were overly fatty and oily. Ugh, meat overload. Hello to my love handles. The meats did pair well with sauce which there's an area with an array of sauces/seasoning for you to choose from. And me being me, sauce got on my clothes while eating and the waiter quickly gave us wet napkins- I didn't even notice he went to get it. The service was great and we felt attended to. So again, I would come back here but only for the hotpot.

Tried this place for dinner last Friday night. We got a table right away, and it wasn't very crowded, not sure why. This place is great. The decor is awesome- i wanted it to be my house. It would be a good place for a date because it is a romantic ambience. My friends and I split a bunch of stuff. We had the hummus, tzatziki, and some other spread with jalapenos in it, truffled mushrooms, greek salad, the spinach pastry things. They were all delicious. The only thing I didn't love was the flaming cheese. It had a licorice taste. We also got a pitcher of the sangria. I wished it were stronger, it kinda just tasted like juice. Overall, definitely worth trying.
Excellent, the lamb chops are just the best thing you could eat on earth. Came here twice already and I love it. Plus on happy hour the wine is at 4$ !

I was very excited to try Proper West since I really love Manhattan Proper.  I called Friday morning to make reservations for Friday night.  After I said I had a gilt city special, I was told they "may have an event" that night.  We called BS and had another friend call, and not mention the gilt special and got reservations no problem.  So already I was turned off by them.  The four of us got there, sat right away, and the only saving grace of the night was how sweet our server was.  Our appetizers were all ehhh.  Our one meal came out 30 min before the rest of the table, so we had to ask for them to bring us a fresh plate so our one friend wasn't eating a cold dish.  Two of the meals were beyond spicy and not flavorful at all.  We were all severely disappointed and this was not even worth a gilt special.  Stop trying to be so "elite" before you get your own shit together.

Cool little spot to watch a game! Definitely elevated bar food for a game as well. Lots of big screens and a good mix of a higher end restaurant, still being okay with some excited football fans. My friends got steak and the like, which they said was good. I got the truffle Mac and cheese which was pretty bland, but a good side caesar. Service was wonderful, super friendly and attentive. Easy to get a table Sunday night. Give it a shot!
This was a really cool spot to meet up with some coworkers to get some food and drinks while watching the game. Great atmosphere and the staff was nothing but pleasant! Will definitely be back!

A+ = INCREDIBLE FOOD FAIL = INEXCUSABLY BAD SERVICE -- friend and I went here for (what we thought would be) a quick lunch, no wait and was quickly seated at a table in back of main dining room. Went at lunch time, around 1p, on a Tuesday (only one other table was filled and few at the bar) -- we haven't seen each other in years so we were chatting and catching up, then realised 15 minutes passed by and no wait staff has tended to us yet... so when the hostess sat a different table, we asked to place our order with her and apologised our waitress hadn't been over and happily took our food order -- food came out in very reasonable time + looked and smelled ABSOLUTELY SCRUMPTIOUS -- we ate and scarfed the food down it was so good -- as we finished our food, another party was seated next to us and the waitress tended to them, took their order, etc -- we tried to get her attention but she quickly ran off to submit their oder -- we waited another 10 or minutes, we gave up and decided to pay at the bar (no problem with that)

A good bar and grill located right in Midtown, off of the main avenues with a tight menu that hits the spot in so many ways. I recommend the sliders and the Mac and cheese...as well as the NY strip steak. I've been here before and would come here again.

I really like this place! Its very cute and posh and the service is great. A nice spot if you want to watch any game. Its also fun at night, because the music is good! I had the bison burger and it was very tasty. Looking forward to going again to try the other food. Bartender that night was awesome. She really knows her drinks. I had an old fashioned and it was just perfect

This place is everything that you want a Bar-Restaurant to be: * Great service (this one Latina waitress was so nice and prompt) * The burger was perfectly crafted and delicious * The ambience was like something out of a photographers studio with all the "in vogue" photographs of models on the wall * The drinks are practically free! I would most definitely go again.
I went there last night for an event. Had the Bison Mesquite Burger.  It was to die for! Will definitely go again and invite all of my girlfriends.
Swung by for some after work drinks and a small bite. Had the Moscow Mule and Truffle Fries - both were great. I'll definitely be back.

I am truly amazed at the reviews on here. I went in for a quick lunch.  Let me begin by saying, we were there for over an hour and never ate anything.  We ordered 2 sandwiches, one tasted like actual dirt...(not exaggerating) and the other came out totally overcooked.  I returned the one sandwich saying I didn't want anything else, I would just share the burger we ordered. When the second burger came out it was even more cooked than the first. And at that point we had to leave.  Again we never ate lunch.  I will say the server and management were very apologetic and obviously didn't charge us for anything, but at the end of the day it's a restaurant and the food needs to be good...so I don't think we will be going back.

Awful service. The place was empty and we waited 15 minutes for someone to even take our order and then it took nearly an hour for the food to come out. AGAIN there were only 2 other tables I'm the entires place and the waitress didn't seem to care at all. As a waitress myself I try to give credit, but I could not here. Fortunately the burgers were good so that's why I'm giving 2 stars
Awesome place! Great vibe, great food and attentive service. I recommend getting the Mac & cheese and truffle fries - they were all really good. Great spot to start your night!

Definitely my new go-to in Midtown. Great for happy hours (that inevitably head into happy evenings/all-nighters). Service is on point, food superb (the truffle fries are like crack and I love the upscale sports bar feel to it. This is one of those bars I found by chance and now introduce all my friends/clients to - always to good reviews. My only complaint is there are only three Men's toilets, which can lead to lines during the really peak periods. Not something I'm used to! Regardless, love the place and conveniently close to Bryant Park.

Love this place for happy hour and football games! The TVs are bigger than most sports bars, but the atmosphere is classy. I'm having an engagement party in the upstairs section in a few weeks and Mandi is taking care of everything. I haven't had the main dishes yet but I haven't been disappointed by any of the apps! Love the turkey sliders and fries.
This place is just fantastic. Good atmosphere and nice people. Food, you know? Food.
This is my favorite Mexican in the whole city. Amazing frozen margaritas, made from fresh squeezed fruit, and delicious tacos. Especially recommend blackened catfish and the incredible queso.

Gueros is a great little joint in Crown Heights that I love to visit. Being a vegetarian, it can be hard to find good tacos. Is it too much to ask for more than peppers, onions, and rice? Gueros does a great job of having options for everyone, and their happy hour is awesome! $$ off tacos and magaritas and I'm a fan. Watch out, because they can have a huge line, and being small there are minimal places to sit. They are also a little pricey, but what isn't these days? I haven't ordered delivery, but I doubt these would last a trip on a bike/by foot, so I'd suggest going or taking out and devouring quickly!

Service is horrible. When we were seated I had to wait ten minutes to get a high chair for my son.  The waiter never came to check on us ask us for water until we decided to get up and leave.  The menu was unorganized and did not have a lot of choices.  DO NOT GO THERE!

In the People's Republic of West Philly, this is a slice of Nancy Reagan. In dining here for the first time, it feels as if a few Szechuan peppercorns have been heaped on the now defunct Green Garden's previous menu. The beef and chicken quality is uncommonly poor. Seriously. Sub-McNugget for the chicken. Sub-McRib for the beef. That's correct, the McRib is meant to mimic pork. The dumplings, fashioned out of three to four wrappers, are incredibly thick, eviscerating any filling. None of this is hyperbole. What's incredible to me is the margin being made on this food -- it is unthinkable that this type of sickly or manufactured meat product is being rolled for $14 and $18 an entree. Unconscionable. Avoid.
They make very decent doubled cooked port
Great low-key local place in the EV. A good alternative if you are eating alone.

It is a cozy place with really nice people and delicious food!! Don't forget to try their pierogis!! The breakfast sausages and eggs are also amongst the best I have tried in NYC! It is a definite recommendation for everyone, tourist or not!!

I LOVE this place. The owner and the staff are so warm and friendly, and since the place is tiny, it makes it even more cozy. Not ideal for big groups, but great for two or take out. The food is as good (if not better) than Veselka and everything is half price. It is right by my place, and I'm definitely a regular!

A friend and I get together every month or so and sample a new restaurant for breakfast. I have to say none compares to Bella's and we travel all over the state. Bella's is not cheap by any means but worth every penny. Pancakes are great but I have never had anything for breakfast that was not. They also have a very creative menu. Try it..you will love it. The only downfall is it is VERY POPULAR. Plan on waiting...especially on the weekend.

Bella's is absolutely amazing!  We were in town for a college football game against Yale and had already planned to try Bella's before the game (we found it on Yelp).  The game time was at noon, so we arrived at 9:30am Saturday morning, to give ourselves plenty of time.  We were able to get a table for 4 right away (make sure your entire party is present when you enter, or the wait staff will not seat you until everyone has arrived).  I recommend that you go with a group of people that is open to community eating.  We all ordered different entrees so we could have the luxury of trying multiple dishes during a single visit.  We each hit a home run with our selections!!!!!  Shrimp and Grits (the creamiest grits in the world), Creole Catfish and potatoes (seasoned to perfection), Floridian Stuffed French Toast (with plantains and the most delicious drizzle I've ever had), and American Apple Pie (the caramelized green apples and the cheddar cheese was a great new experience atop the thick brioche, with a delicious bourbon maple syrup).  I'm not exaggerating when I say our taste buds sang hallelujah.  The service was amazing as well.  I think out-of-towners are made to feel really special.  We will absolutely return as often as we can.  Oh, and don't forget to try the fresh squeezed orange juice.

OMG is how to describe the meal I had at this small place! The Shan Bang French Toast was to die for. I never had a more deliciously meal! The eggs were fluffy the home fries were well seasoned and on point with flavor! I am so glad for the TV interview on this place I would of never discover such a delicious meal! However the wait was long to get in and even longer to get my meal But worth while!!

From food to drinks to staff it's all top notch!! My Favorite bartender is Luis, the flavors he blends to make it the perfect cocktail.. The end result is nothing short than amazing! Food is very tasty and delicious. I can't wait  to go back!

Rustic Latin Cuisine.....what?? Oh how needed was a place like this on the Upper East Side. OK so they just opened on September 15th and I can't believe its only been such a short period of time. Granted this is their second location, the first being on 46th St on Restaurant Row so they may have had some practice but come on, the Hospitality factor, that's something that has to come naturally you can't fake that, but more on that later. First the location and ambiance, they seem unfazed by the subway construction happening in front of them but we too have gotten use to that. The ambiance is super relaxed and cool with a killer bar and fun double style type of dining areas. The food, yum, cocktails silly good. A Happy Hour full of goodies with food options that am told will be revealed in days. Several visits now with girlfriends and am silly about this Salmon Brulee, yeah that's right, flavor smack with every bite. Had the Pacu Fish Ribs and I don't even know what to say about these cause you just have to try it for yourself. Second visit had the Ribeye Parilla with the seven different sides they tell me change on a regular basis and you know the Argentinian influence is in full effect with meats from Pat LaFrieda I guess they are not playing with quality and it shows. So you have the Brazilian fish ribs, the Peruvian interpretation of ceviches, meats a la Argentina but truly all of Latin and South America seem to be covered on the menu. I now understand the whole Rustic aspect of the name and not just some overly colorful Latin Bistro, a bit classier and at a different level here. After my first visit I actually came across a re-run of Diners Drive Ins and Dives with Guy Fierri and noticed that it featured the Chef Owner Chef Carlos at his other restaurant in Jersey, Quahog's Shack, something like that. Not being certain, on my next visit it was confirmed by the staff that it was the same as he was working the Raw bar and checked up on our enjoying of the drinks we were having. In my nosiness I was also informed that his partner from that location was joining him here and it happens to be Chef Lucas Manteca who happens to be a nominee for the James Beard 2014 Best Chef Mid-Atlantic and my server was super excited telling us that they have tasted some of the new things that will be on the new menu and in their words, it's ridiculous, so now more reasons to keep coming back. yes I will have to bring boyfriend. These 2 will blow away this community that's what we were told so let's see. Am excited. Finally lets talk about service but more than that the general Hospitality that service falls under. I go out to eat often w girlfriends or boyfriend and there is nothing worse than feeling like you are doing the establishment a favor for being there, some, but come on NY, get a clue, you may want to see how these guys do it. From the entering its like your walking into these peoples homes and I've read other reviews around that speak of this, and you do wonder if this is just a show but nooo, it is not. Bartenders warm, informative, engaging, I would hang out with these people. The servers, knowledgeable, excited about the product, attentive and just down right warm but not over bearing as they seem to have been trained properly to read guests accordingly. The table next to us looked like they were in a different personal experience, and the server handled that table as it deserved considering they weren't as fun as we were, just more straight laced. Still we could over hear that table speaking about how wonderful their experience was at the end of their meal and that they must come back.   The Owners, wow, and forget about getting a straight answer as to who they are because there in lies the true humbleness of these folks. The GM Eddie stops by as he was doing with all tables to check on us, we ask if he's the owner because he sure as hell took ownership of this place. We were sure of it with the way he worked the room and his team and the guest, his answer, "no you are the owners, we just keep the doors open for you to enjoy" come on really. This Dude was and is on point and no show about it, the real thing. He comped a dessert at the end of meal as he wanted our opinion on some new ones they were trying out and a finish with a shot of Mezcal, which he took the time to educate us about it and the difference between Tequila and Mezcal which my girlfriend didn't know about nor in that much detail, neither did I. Anyway, you'll know who he is when you visit if not ask for him. And then there is Victor actually one of the Partners, Chef Carlos being the other, warm, sincere, grateful for us being there and as Eddie had said while both of them at our table, "we are grateful to you because you have many choices to dine and you chose US". These two are amazing especially with their banter as to who is the owner both putting it on the other, but you can see the true partnership amongst them.   Wishing the very best.

What a great place with really delicious seafood dishes and even better tequila cocktails.  Went with nine friends and we had a stellar time with Victor, the owner/proprietor, taking good care of us.  The Brazilian seafood stew was a big hit and I loved the lobster.  The decor is beautiful and music/vibe was uplifting.  I'd go back anytime.

If you are in Manhattan, you must try La Pulperia! The warm atmosphere and ambiance of the restaurant makes you want to stay for hours. There was a celebrity at the restaurant when I was dining and every customer was treated with the same warmth and attentiveness by the staff. The chefs creations are brilliant, pulling together flavors that augment and invigorate your palate.  Supplement your meal with one of the unique and amazing cocktails from the bar and you are in for one of the best dining experiences of your life!

Stopped in with my neighbor for a drink and small snack. I love the decor. Reminds me a little of Boqueria down the street. The wide bar (Marble? Zinc?) is just the place to catch up with a friend and soak up the vibe. The prices are on the high end but maybe normal for the hood and factoring in that it's mostly seafood. We ordered three kinds of empanadas ( carne, jamon and squash). They were good with the carne being the best. Wine pours were generous and a Yelp check-in gets a free glass. I plan to go back for the raw bar items and also happy hour specials if I can ever remember to do such practical things. Also noticed a great salad on the menu so will try that too!

The best omelet in Connecticut is the Rajun Cajun, a mix of Jambalaya and cheese in a wonderful omelet. The Home fries are also the best in ct. Coffee is good, I cannot speak for anything else because I do not get anything else. People who downgrade Mo's because of the line should not, you should grade this place on taste and service and nothing else(unless the place is dirty pig stye, which it is not).    Do not go near this place on weekends unless you want to wait, expect to wait and you will not be disappointed.             Now that I think about it I once had this Mexican breakfast a few years ago and it was good also. Pancakes look huge and everyone looks happy.            Service has been spot on every time I have been there. So it is a no brainer---5 stars.    One negative are the booths, if you have a back problem try to sit at the tables because the booths are in need of replacing, I will still give it a 5 but management replace those booths otherwise a 3 or 4 star is on the horizon

Strictly in terms of the breakfast food, this place comes with my highest recommendations.  From fresh fruit-filled pancakes to perfectly seasoned homefries, I've never been disappointed by the offerings.   As far as the ambience/design, the place leaves  a lot to be desired.  To me, there's a bright line between COZY and CRAMPED, this place constitutes the latter.  Both weekends and weekdays draw big breakfast crowds where one should expect a lot of background noise and a feeling that other diners are practically seated at the same table as you. The service is often very quick, though, and the staff is friendly, so the pros far outweigh the cons.  Overall, this is a good place to grab a quick, delicious breakfast at a reasonable price, but it's not really a place to sit back and relax. I think they serve lunch as well, but I've only had their breakfast.

Absolutely awesome. Food, decor, atmosphere, service, management was as good as it gets. That's worth 4 stars in my book. Yet the attention to detail in every one of the above mentioned aspects make it a 5 star experience. I will be back. I highly recommend.

I would've given this place 4 stars if it wasn't for the extremely small portions for very high prices. The ambiance and service was excellent. We were here on Valentine's day so they only had a select variety of dishes to choose from. The appetizer prices were steep - we ordered the calamari as well as the grilled octopus - $15 each for a small portion. For the entree, I ordered the scallops dish. $32 for THREE pieces of scallops. Didn't even come with any potato or bread or vegetables. The scallops were really tender and flavorful. However, $10 for one scallop is really expensive. My fiance ordered the brizola. For $35, the dish comprised of about 8 one-inch strips of steak with a side of potatoes. We left the restaurant hungry which was quite disappointing.

I was in the city and wanted Greek food and my boyfriend and I came here and it was such a great choice. I loved it the mood the food and the service. If you would good feel comfort food this is the spot I recommend this place hands down. Just the drive was bad to come in the city but great

So 9 of us went for dinner to Sonu Da Dhaba... We were greeted and were seated very quickly.. Servers asked us about kids and if we will need elevated seats etc. .. Order was taken fairly quickly.. Bihari Tikka was good .. Chicken Tikka was nothing to write home about .. Tawa Paneer / Tawa Mashroom was oily and deep fried ( no idea why it was called TAWA , maybe just cause it was served on a TAWA ? ) Main course was OK ( 2 veg gravy's and 1 chicken grave ) But by now the restaurant was full and there were only 2 servers , so we had to wait forever to get the check and containers ( about 15 mins or so ).. Overall OK experience !! Oh yes.. they refused to split the check 3 ways .. they said they can accept only 2 cards at most..  that too for a bill of $150 +.. so deducting 1 star!!
Lamb kebabs, chicken lollipops, and more to come!!!
love this hole in the wall! cream chipped beef is amazing! the staff can seem unfriendly sometimes but everyone has their days!
Not only are their plates creative and tasty but they're brought to you by some of best looking ladies in Port Richmond. Mercer is pleasing to the eye and Belly

This is a fast-paced buffet restaurant. Lots of people, vacationists and families visiting. The food, the place, and the service are fine. Its floor service care taker, whose name is Carol is very courteous, efficient and most of all helpful. Try to look for her when you come. Unfortunately, there is one snag...the woman in the counter upon entering is unsavory and unappealing. She spoils the day. Sonny J.

Excellent sushi place. The Miso soup and sushi was delicious. We had the Mayflower  diner (for two). It was nicely presented and very good quality sushi. We been looking for a while for a good sushi place between Somerville and Princeton and now we found what we were looking for. We are already planing our next visit to Midori Sushi III and it very likely we will visit the place regularly. 3/30/2014 - we still love this place, two years after we discovered it.

I've eaten here before with my sister and it was delicious. Open space. The outside is a bit sketch but inside is very nice. I ordered the lunch special 3 rolls for delivery with brown rice instead of white. Total order including delivery fee came to $13.63 which is fantastic! Will order from here again :) and next time, my co workers will be ordering here as well. We work in a hotel and will be recommending this as our main Japanese restaurant of choice.

Worst chicken fingers ever. They were prob sitting around and thrown on the grill for a minute ... They were kind of soggy with char marks from the grill and a weird smoky flavor. How do you mess up chicken fingers? I ordered an they literally came out one minute later. The fries were good and at least I got fast service. The wait staff and atmosphere were fine but I will not return.

Highly recommended crawfish/shellfish boil restaurant! First, the food: 1. Shrimp - JUMBO shrimp, very fresh, super delicious. I had TheBoil Special sauce - sooo good. I've gone to similar restaurants where the sauce is super salty, this is not the case with The Boil. The garlic butter base is to die for. Highly highly recommended! 2. Dungeness crab - super fresh and meaty, YUM. 3. Potato side - if you love potatoes, this is the dish for you. 4. Flan dessert - this was more akin to a cheesecake, very creamy. This was good but a little sweet for my taste. The caramel sauce/juice on the bottom was sweet. 5. Bloody mary - delicious. It was just the right mix of horseradish, tomato juice and vodka. Second, the service: We were there for the 5 o'clock service and admittedly, the food took some time to arrive. However, the service more than made up for it. Instead of getting the brush off, our waitress made sure to come by and let us know what was holding up our food and the ETA. She was fun and made it a great experience. We were a table of 7 and even though we were a larger party, the service was good all-around. Tiip: The line can get very long; make sure to come early and be prepared to wait for a table. It will be worth it!!

Hot damn this place is off the hook crazy AWESOME! I've never had a dining experience quite like this before, or food that required as much work. To put things in perspective, eating a whole lobster is a walk in the park compared to a combo from The Boil. My friend and I arrived around 9pm on a Thursday evening and had no trouble getting a table. As soon as we were seated a waitress came over to tie bibs around our necks. Great. But what came next is what *really* got me excited- plastic gloves. Time to get dirty! We started with the catfish basket and fries. Yummmmm. It's like fish and chips, but better because the batter wasn't as fried and thus the fish wasn't as heavy on my stomach. The fries are equally as satisfying. Served hot, crispy and spicy, they were the perfect accompaniment. For the main event we both got the shrimp and crawfish combo with the boil special sauce, spicy. This is where the fun really began! I'd never had crawfish before so eating these little suckers was quite an ordeal. For newbies like myself, there is a cheat sheet with instructions on how to properly eat a crawfish. As for the shrimp, they too are served whole with everything left on them- the heads, the poopy bottoms, the legs... eeek! I'll admit I had to close my eyes as I worked my way through this behemoth of a bag, but it was worth it. The potatoes, corn and kielbasa were nice touches as well. If you order a combo I suggest ordering more sides to sop up the juice with. Prices are right on point for the freshness and quality of food. Would absolutely recommend this place for groups or a couple of old friends!

Believe the hype! It was my first crawfish experience and definitely won't be my last.
