We ordered  Combo A (crawfish+shrimp) with theboil sauce (A MUST), clams with butter garlic, oyster sliders and soft shell crab basket.  The clams were a little overcooked but still yummy (can't go wrong with garlic butter), oyster sliders decent but probably won't order again @ 3/$12 (for value sake), skip the soft shell crab and just go ahead and get a full order of fries. Next time I will double up on the crawfish order. You know it's good when you're already prepping for a next time. PS- would be icing on the cake if they served garlic bread. Nom on!

What do you get when you cross Chinatown with some finger lickin' crawfish? "Da" Boil, yea heard? New Asians on the block and they're killing it! Came after work to meet up with a friend for dinner around 630ish and let me tell you.. this place was packed within the hour. On the Menu for us was *Half dozen oysters - doesn't tell you what kind but I'd assume something east coast because of the brininess factor. *Oyster Sliders - Fried oyster with slaw & slice of tomato in a potato bun. Perfect drunk food if you're into oysters. Crispy batter with a juicy oyster center combined with sweet slaw makes belly mucho happy. *Combo A - 1 Lb of crawfish & shrimp mixed with corn and sausage (Andouille me thinks?) combined with that killer Boil sauce (garlic butter, ol' bay, lemon pepper). Be ready to get rock a bib and ask for disposable gloves because this dining experience requires a "hands-on" approach. A good fun factor to do as a group but you should def make a reservation if you plan on that route.  Cocktails run 9 dollars and up. Come to the The Boil, leave the white attire at home, kiddies. **cash only

Decor: 4/5 Cozy, clean, contemporary look Washrooms are clean Bar in front, dining room in back Good view of the kitchen from the dining area Service: 4/5 Friendly, with smiles They check on you frequently Water refilled frequently Napkins on request They tied our bibs for us Reservations and credit cards taken for parties of 6 or more, automatic 18% gratuity added (added on top of taxed amount) Two orders were mixed up, not a big deal, we figured it out Food: 4/5 - had combo A, 1lb crawfish, 1lb shrimp for 25$ , comes with pieces of sausage, corn on cob and small potatoes, - you can order individual items by the lb if you don't want the combos - I picked the special boil sauce and "spicy" - spicy was a good amount  if heat for me, I also tried fire and it was good, but after a while all I could taste was pain. - if you're comparing to boiling crab, it comes close but I found boiling crab to have more flavor, more sauce to dip in the bag, and lemons were provided.

Love this place but hated the wait. We arrived around 5:45 on a Saturday, thinking we could just slide on in with our party of two. Nope!  We were told that it was a 2 hour wait but it turned out to be around 30-45 minutes. (FYI, if you have more than 4 people in your party, expect to wait a long time.) Not bad at all. We ended up being seated at the bar which is part of their seating system. So, if you think you will be able to just sit at the bar and wait for your table, you are sorely mistaken. Next up is the food. The food was amazing. It was great portions and came swiftly. We ordered the catfish basket, which was great. It came with a couple pieces of catfish, Cajun fries (which were a bit overcooked), and a great slaw. The catfish was hot, lightly battered and delicious. I can not emphasize how great it was. For our main course, we ordered the 1lb of shrimp and 1lb of crawfish. I got the spicy and my boyfriend got the mild. The spicy was delicious but the heat definitely sneaks up on you. I ended up taking the majority of the food home. My boyfriend definitely enjoyed his because he finished his on site. Let me tell you though, the shrimp are HUGE!!!!! I a m a big fan of shrimp with the heads on and they definitely nailed it with their recipe. By the way, the head of the shrimp is by far the best part of the shrimp. They gave us bibs and gloves but I like to get down and dirty, so I ate sans gloves. To each his/her own. The service at the bar was less desirable but I know that if we sat at the table, we would have been able to get better service. The place does get a little packed so be aware that you may have to stand outside for service. I can not wait to come back and enjoy even more food.

Note: They do not take reservations for parties under 6. So I'd recommend rounding up a group of friends to save yourself the long wait. Oh, and that way they'll accept credit card as a form of payment. I arrived very early and killed time at the bar. The chili margarita was VERY strong. The two bloody Mary's that follow were stellar. I did tell the hostess that my friend wasn't going to arrive until 7:15 (it was 6:03 at the time). The place filled up rather rapidly and smelled amazing. Service was less than stellar. I had to repeat my order a couple of times to the server, and there was a hiccup on our order of fries-- we had to remind them. And we were almost served more shrimp. Granted, it was incredibly busy that night. The crawfish and shrimp combo was superb. The dungeoness crab was also incredible. Your fingers will still get a little ick, but nothing that will prevent you from enjoying your meal. I also picked the special boil sauce, which was spectacular!! Don't skip the dessert. Get one chocolate and one regular creme brulee. They are rich and super satisfying after all the saltiness goodness you just consumed. All in about $146 for the food an several cocktails. The raw oysters were decent too!

This place is jam packed! My friend and I went for something small and then came back here for round two. I recommend coming here at a later time, we got seats in 15 mins as oppose to 30+ mins. (**) I say sit at the bar since the bartenders were really the people who took orders and you can watch the game at the same time. The place was nice with dim lighting. Good for groups, dates, and hang out. I don't recommend coming here just to drink at the bar because there was no room for it. It was mainly occupied by customer who eat. (***) Before I started my meal, the waiter helped us with our bibs and gave us plastic gloves. What came after was all the good stuff which was also in plastic bags. This is where I can truly say "dig in". I had 1LB of the Shrimp and 1LB of the clam with mild sauce and all the spicy they use. It had this thickness of cheese and they used a lot of garlic. It was very salty, but at the same time it taste so good. (***) Service was a bit slow in the beginning since it took us forever to figure out who can take our order, but then it started picking up when our food came. The waiters were like owls, they could spot every empty bag and remove it from your table just like that. I love how the waitress called us "love" whenever we needed something. It works for her so keep it up. When we left the restaurant, the owner would greet us like we were entering. (****)

What a cool place!!  I went with my gf for a girl's night out, and she heard of the place but neither one of us knew what to expect. We got there and it was packed! I'm like, damn it... I'm hungry and there's a line to the host desk and I'll bet the wait will be even longer.  Not so.  I gave my name and we sat in a corner to wait the predicted 25-40 min. to be seated, and we were called in about 15 minutes! Score! We sat down and they wasted no time in getting our orders. The menu is simple enough, with all kinds of seafood goodies, reasonably-priced! We ordered our food spicy, and boy they didn't hold back... whoa! My Blue Moon beer helped to cool my burning lips, and everything was delish! Cudos to the food, but warning - This is NOT an "I'm gonna dress up and eat delicately" kind of place. You get plastic bags of messy shellfish heaven brought to you with a bib and plastic gloves...(although the gloves can be awkward at times, they save the fingers from smelling suspect) It's a go with loved ones and friends, get a little dirty, laugh really loud and enjoy yourself! And you might need a shower after all that shellfish... but it was gooooood going down!

I got here at 6pm and there was already an hour wait.  Lucky it was only 2 of us so I ended up sharing a table.  I was super excited to eat here because my friends been posting pictures up of the food here on Facebook. I love to eat crawfish and crab so that's what I ordered.  The flavor is great. Oh yeah I got the boil special which is a mix of all three sauces and it is delish!  I couldn't get enough to it.  It gets a little tiring eat with your hands after a while but overall the experience is great!  Will definitely go back!

I have never felt the need to make a yelp account to write about my bad experience until my experience at this restaurant today. Every time i go, service and food gets worse. We ended up arriving at the restaurant earlier than the 45 minute wait that they told us for the pick up order.  we got to the the restaurant, the hostess asked us to wait at the bar. We go to the bar and ordered a drink and the bartender tells us to leave the bar because we are taking up space for people who are eating at the restaurant. Donald, the owner, did not care about what was going on. Worst experience ever at a restaurant.

The Food This was the first time I had experienced this style of eating seafood and I'm not sure I would be back again. I ordered the dungeness crab and crawfish combo with the Boil special sauce; garlic butter, lemon pepper and old bay. It came in a bag, we got bibs and gloves. It was like eating seafood out of a garbage bag and given gloves to inspect the contents you were about to eat. The sauce is finger lickingly tasty like all the reviews say but after 1hr 30mins to get through the bag, the smell of the sauce becomes nauseating. The Service The server was really friendly but after we had made our decision, she had totally forgot to mention, there was no lobster for the night...annoying but anyways, the food preparation was really slow, we waited at least 40 mins to get the food - which was strange, you'd think it would be pretty fast to boil seafood and add seasoning?? ? The Verdict Every time you spend money, you are voting for the kind of world you want to live in.  This kind of restaurant is only out to make a profit at the expense of the environment and the people who live in it, like everyone! From the use of plastic cups and foam bowls, eating seafood from a bag felt like eating a bagged aquarium - it totally degrades the privilege of consuming seafood. There is even fine print at the bottom of the menu with a caveat for eating their raw oysters because they are sourced from the Gulf of Mexico and there is a chance of death should you happen to have a poor immune system (no joke!) I suppose sourcing locally farmed oysters is more expensive and the restaurant is willing to put the customer at risk by serving up Gulf of Mexico oysters. After these factors, you start to wonder where they source the rest of their seafood and the impact you are having on the world by consuming this meal. This is a place for people who like to eat to fill their stomach and not for someone who appreciates good wholesome food. If you love seafood and respect the environment, there are better places in New York get fresh and locally sourced seafood than eating here.

Whoa...just whoa.  The Boil is a pretty wild spot that takes no shortcuts with Cajun shellfish, down to the plastic bags they're served in. We came a little drunk, which was a mistake, as you'll need all of your attention and energy to wade through the oily, buttery bags of shells. They outfit you with a big paper bib to catch the splatters of sauces that will inevitably be all over your hands, arms, clothes by the end of the meal.  We started with a few oysters, served in a tin foil dish on ice, and opted for a bag of crawfish and a bag of dungeness crab legs.  The "special sauce" Is butter, old bay, and something else...nom.   The crawfish were overzealous.  I couldn't get anything out of them - seemed like it was all guts and shells, and it's very gory business searching.  The crab legs were definitely a better pick. While it wasn't my cup of tea, it'd be fun for a big group of guys, or as a part of a theme.  Go with someone you're comfortable with, so you don't feel self-conscious ripping the heads off of crustaceans and taking a bath in garlic and butter.

I was very excited when I found out about this restaurant. But I have to say, it really is such a disappointment. It tastes way too much garlicky. It's nowhere near as good as The Boiling Crab. The fact that it's cash only really turns me off because you can easily spend over $50 here and it just doesnt make any sense.

You know what? I like this place. I really do. I would love this place if it weren't cash only (sketch, with an even sketchier atm machine) and the i.n.c.o.n.s.i.s.t.e.n.c.y. The first time I came it was a quiet Sunday night but we came at a time when things were winding down and people sat and chilled before a dreaded Monday morning. We ate at the bar and the service was quite good. The guy at the bar was nice and so were the random waitresses. When the food came it blew me away. Their special sauce was SO GOOD - very flavorful, packed a punch, and definitely went well with the crab, crawfish, and sausage along with the potatoes and corn on the cob. I was thoroughly impressed and vowed to come again. It was so good I had to get another single order of crawfish at 2 pounds so I could get the sausage and extra stuff. Finger lickin good.
Pizza was burned and dry out. First and last time.  It was one of the worst pizzas I've had in a while.  And the place looks like a hole in the wall. Something out of the 60s.
Great food, beautiful decor, friendly staff, reasonable prices and BYOB. Hands down the best oyster appetizers I have ever had.

Villalobos is an excellent Mexican restaurant in the heart of downtown Montclair. Yesterday I ordered the fish & verduras tacos and a margarita (virgin but they are BYOB). The verduras taco was quite tasty. The corn was fresh & crisp and had the right amount of smoke. The fish taco was battered and topped with cole slaw. Their house-made tortillas taste even better than the ones at a typical Mexican food cart. Both accompanying salsa's (salsa verde and regular salsa) were fresh, well seasoned and authentic. I actually ended up ordering the same thing for lunch today along with an order of guacamole that was legit. It's really dangerous working directly next door to them so I'll have to schedule my visits. Adam, the owner, is a great dude. Go, you won't be disappointed!

Checked out this place  on Friday night around 6. Sat at the bar and tried a lot of menu items, as we wanted to a large variety.  Everything seemed really authentic, and contrary to other reviews, service was great.  Water glass was filled promptly, and everyone was eager to help.   The pork belly taco was by far my favorite.  Would highly recommend it! Didn't love the pork rinds or chicken taco (little dry). Had the churro for dessert.  I was not familiar with Mexican chocolate, and found it to be a little bitter. Overall, the ambience was nice, service was good, and food all was authentic.  Like any new place with a menu different from anything else, you will probably not love everything but for sure you will find something you love.  I hope they do well!
Awesome decor great personality, fish tacos were awesome.  Coming back asap with the girlfriend for dinner.

I have been there on several occasions! The staff is wonderful and friendly, my waitress took time out to explain the menu! Now to the food it was absolutely delicious very tasty! The owner came and greeted me and my family and took time out to get to know us!  My waitresses names were named Stephanie and I believe Wendy they were so sweet! Can't wait to go back and have the ribs!
Went back again for dinner with some girlfriends yesterday, we had the sangria it was absolutely delicious!!! would recommend to everyone!

My husband and I stopped in today for the first time, and the food was wonderful! He has the steak and plantains, and I had tilapia and friend green plantains! Since my dad has just been in the same day, he offered us dinner size meals for lunch, and threw in a free piece of tres leches! We also ordered a piece of flan which was delicious and tasted homemade! The owner, Josh went out of his way to make sure our first experience was perfect, and it was! We are very excited to have such a great little restaurant in our neighborhood! We will definitely be going back!

I've been to Yolanda's twice and have not been disappointed. I am cuban American and I felt the food was authentic and my Spouse thinks its better than my mothers. Sorry mom your the bomb when it comes to cooking especially cuban dishes but Yolanda's black beans were better and had more flavor. I plan to go again and again.

My family tries a lot of different food joints, and tend to be very picky about food.  We have had cuban food before and have never been very impressed with other places.  This place changed that.   For appetizers we order garlic shrimp and beef empanadas - both are fantastic!  The garlic shrimp is done perfectly, with a couple of pieces of flattened and toasted slices of bread on the side of it (dip the bread into the garlic shrimp's sauce).  The empanadas de carne are freshly made with an amazing seasoning and perfectly-crisp outer fry to it. Dinner -  I have had the picadillo both times I have been there:  It is AMAZING!!!  I get it on moro ("Special Cuban black rice") and they just compliment each other so well.  My parents have gotten both Pollo Asado and the Cuban Sandwhich.  Both were fantastic.  The chicken falls off the bone and tastes fabulous.  The cuban sandwhich is extremely crisp and freshly made.  The way my dad put it - the last time he had one that good was 30 years ago.   Service - The service is very good; the owner even comes out and touches tables just to make sure everyone is satisfied.  He is a great conversationalist and shows a lot of passion for the business.  He absolutely loves what he does and it shows in the product that comes out of the kitchen.  The rest of the staff makes sure to come out and touch the table to ensure everyone is happy.   Desserts - Tonight is the first night we have had dessert at Yolanda's.  We had both the tres leches and the chocolate flan.  Let me just say I was floored by both!  They were both home-made recipes with the three of us fighting for the last bite!  The tres leches used a rich cake that made it really pop in your mouth with the three milks coming up well on it.  It was not soggy like you find at other restaurants which made it even better.  The chocolate flan was even better!  The flan itself was rich - the texture of it was flawless.   While the place is rather new, it has a very nice aura to it for cuban food.  It could use a little bit of an update in some areas - such as the utilization of a fountain-drink machine; but those are pieces that I believe will come with time.  You definitely have to go in with a little sense of an open mind and looking for something to truly enjoy! I am not sure what else I can say about this place, except you should go try it!  There is eat-in and take out.  Make sure you try it!

Sat at the bar for happy hour (only at the bar) while on a (very quick) work trip to Philadelphia. The $3 vegetable samosa appetizer? Yes! Do not miss it! Two samosas (a little smaller than I usually see, but still delicious) were parked on a bed of Indeblue's channa masala (chickpeas) with a swipe of green chutney and cool yogurt. Indian food heaven... for $3. Even for the small portion, I'd pay the regular $8 non-happy hour. I don't live in Philly and ergo can't return often, so please go eat these samosas for me right now. Honorable mentions: the $5 happy hour ginger-lime-whiskey cocktail. Bartender Sean (?) was helpful, welcoming and knowledgeable. The naan pizza didn't change my life, but it was filling for $5. Live sitar music on Tuesday nights! It was terrific background, but not loud. So glad I randomly Yelped my way to this cozy, classy place!

If you're looking for Indian food that beats the typical hole in the wall places in University City with sub par service and questionable cleanliness, this is the place to go. We came here on Diwali so it was pretty lively inside and I was glad we made a reservation because it was a full house (although usually I've heard you can walk in and get a table). There were a couple of larger tables so it looks like they are good at accommodating large groups (6+). We had a friendly and helpful server, who recommended a few dishes to us. We got 3 appetizers to split among 3 of us: chilled dahi avocado chaat, stuffed long hot peppers, and drums of heaven. All were delicious! For dinner I had the tandoori mixed grill and the lamb chops were some of the best I've ever tasted. I can't wait to go back just to order the lollipop lamb chops. For dessert we split the chocolate sutra. It's not a particularly Indian dish but it was still good. Love the decor inside, not tacky or gaudy looking. It was trendy, sexy, and overall had a great atmosphere. Will definitely be back!

The food here was delicious (definitely order the Spinach chaat), but the service was way off.  We had an early reservation on a Saturday night, and the place was full but not packed yet.  Our drinks and food took forever to come out each time, but one we got them there was a busboy or waiter at our table practically every 5 minutes asking if they could clear anything.  Half of these plates they were asking to clear still had food on them.  We stayed for about an hour and a half which is not a long time for dinner and drinks on a Saturday night, and I couldn't help but feel they were rushing us out to get to the next seating.  I will say that the hosts were extremely nice, but the service stopped there.   I would also say this is a $$$ restaurant, not $$ as Yelp indicates.  The portion sizes are decent, but most entrees are $20+, and you're going to want to try appetizers, too.

This is easily the best Indian food I've had in Philadelphia. I loved that they do a modern reinvention of classic Indian cuisine that still nevertheless remains true to tradition. Must order dishes: 1. Spinach chaat. This was the perfect opener, and I've never had anything quite like it before. The spinach is flash-fried so it's perfectly crispy, and we loved the yogurt and tamarind date chutney together. It was light, but very well-rounded in flavor. 2. Malai kofta bukhara. We ordered this as a side, rather than the entree, so we could try more dishes, but this is something I would order as an entree next time. The creamy cardamom sauce was delicious, and the kofta filled with apricot and cashew was heavenly. 3. Any of the bread selections. Seriously. I especially loved the provencal (garnished with rosemary, thyme, sage, and oregano) because I'm a sucker for truffle oil. We also tried the chicken madras--it was well-flavored, but we didn't find it particularly rave-worthy. Maybe it just didn't stand out in comparison to the other dishes that we loved. (Also completely irrelevant note, but the Williams-Sonoma nerd in me loved the silverware here! Such a unique design that fit in so well with the decor and ambiance of the restaurant.) The service was perfect and attentive. We came relatively late on a Saturday night (around 9:30 PM), and it was surprisingly busy. We were seated right in the middle of the dining room, so it was a little loud at times, but to be fair, we spent a decent amount of meal eating and not a lot of time talking once the dishes came out. The decor was gorgeous. On the whole, can't wait to come back and try the rest of the menu!

When you think of Harrison NJ, you think of amazing Portuguese and Spanish food oh so close to the Ironbound section of Newark. Great Chinese doesn't come to mind. After you go to this restaurant, you will wish more places like this were around. Food:  5 Stars Appetizers: They have the absolute best Chinese Spareribs you will ever have. They are almost dinosaur sized with a beautiful mahogany crust bursting with flavor. The meat is extremely flavorful but what makes their ribs standout is that they brush a honey glaze on them which gives them a candied texture. They are a meal all by themselves. The steamed dumplings are absolutely perfect. You can get pork or vegetable dumplings and you can tell they have been made fresh. The dough has an incredibly soft chewy texture that melts in your mouth. The wonton and hot& sour soups are equally good. The hot and sour will set your mouth on fire. Entrees: They have an outstanding selection of Lo-Mein's which are quite good. It doesn't come out greasy at all and is bursting with flavor. The noodles are cooked properly and the vegetables are fresh The pepper steak is quite good and in their version it is served with tomatoes which add a nice touch. Unlike Chinese takeout, you will find a lot of meat in the dish. They also have a full-service sushi bar which many locals say is top notch. Service: 5 Stars They have an excellent wait staff that will make accommodations if you ask.  Very professional and courteous. You can tell they take pride in their establishment Atmosphere: 5 stars The restaurant is beautiful and elegant. They have dark orange walls with a lot of Chinese decorations that   are accentuated by jade. The booths and tables are very spacious and comfortable. Restaurant is immaculately clean. Conclusion: Chinatown restaurant is one of the top 10 restaurants I have ever been too. The food is delicious and doesn't make your stomach explode with MSG or other takeout garbage. This is high-end high quality Chinese/Japanese cooking that will leave you addicted in a good way. Highly recommended.

I just went here for dinner and had a a spicy tuna roll and shared a chinatown chicken with my daughter. The roll was the standard fare and was above average. The Chinatown chicken was great! I highly recommend this dish. We did not have the horrible service that some others mentioned, the waiter was actually really attentive. Overall, it was a great place that I would definitely visit again.

Finally had a chance to try Chinatown... results are......... drum roll please................................It was fabulous! Absolutely enjoyed the Sushi.. Customer service was amazing. Such great energy starting with the Host, waiter and Chef. It was an pleasant experience. This place is a must go!

The Shopping Bag is our go to place for a burger fix in Burlington. Always freshly ground beef, fresh veggies, and the service is good, for a 1/2 deli 1/2 convenience store. There's no seating or waiting area, just grab and go, but don't let that deter you from trying them out! We first decided to try from hearing of the Scibek, but saw the Cowboy and it's been our favorite. My husband now chooses to have a doughnut on all of his burgers, thanks to Shopping Bag.

There's truly no better Jamaican food truck than Jamaican D's. Sure, it's "slightly hidden" on the Community College of Philadelphia's campus, but the trip is well worth it. Out of all of the food trucks there, their line is twice as long. People will wait as long as necessary just to get their rice and beans only. It's well worth it.

Raised in LA, so I know my Mexican food. Fish tacos are solid. Love the blue corn tortillas (which I think they make in-house). Underwhelmed by the tamales (both pork and shrimp). They were moist but didn't wow me in terms of flavor. The beef tacos were good in terms of flavor and quality, but they came out at room temperature. They were also way too small (you get 3 for about $9)...like c'mon, it doesn't cost THAT much more to make them a regular taco size. The tables are also way too close together, and we had to do that move-the-table-so-we-can-sit-and-leave thing.
Yeah! Finally a local fam. restaurant that serves breakfast all day! The fluffy omelets are their specialty and pancakes are outstanding.
Good breakfast food all day. Been here 2x but they have yet to deliver the toast w breakfast without waiting

There was much "hype" before Chips opened in Wethersfield.  I was excited waiting for it to open. SO as soon as it opened, I was there for Breakfast. I ordered my usual, an egg white cheese omelet but with three speciality pancake (an additional $3.20) instead of potatoes and toast,  The omelet seemed small and the pancakes were good, but not great. And the price was a couple dollars more than what I usually  pay. So I thought the next time I go to CHIPS for an omelet, I would not replace the potatoes and toast with pancakes.  SO that is what I did.  But the omelet was still small and the serving of potatoes was not generous . I tasted better omelets which are bigger and the price more reasonable at several local breakfast. So I debated between three  or four stars and decided on THREE STARS. Service is good and there are plenty of servers.  It is just the size of the omelet and the price which kept me giving it four stars. The restaurant does promote over 40 different kinds of pancakes. TRAVEL KAL
The lamb Gyro was packed with flavor. The waitress was also very friendly and helpful!

We had dinner here last 4/19/2013.  The place is small and cannot accomodate a big group. However, the foods are good.  I ordered chicken with rice and salad and my friend ordered lamb with white rice and salad as well. They served it with freshly baked pita rolls. The waiter was so patient to explain the menus. Foods are delicious and its all worth it.

My friend and I had been waiting for this place to open for some time, so we finally got our chance to try it out when we stopped in for lunch today. As soon as we entered, we realized we were in a special place. The service was attentive and thoughtful from the entrance through ordering and then even after we sat down. The management seems eager to create a friendly and inviting atmosphere for its customers, because we were treated to numerous free samples of things, more than I think I've ever had in a New York restaurant, even a new one. This neighborhood is sorely lacking in decent places to eat, so New York Kimchi is an extremely welcome addition to the scene here. Kam sam nida!

I had lunch here today. I ordered tofu bibimbap. It came with miso soup and a side of kimchi. The food was pretty good. The best part of this place is that they gave out tons of free samples of kimchi, Korean pancakes, Korean pastries and smoothies! The staff here was also very friendly. I'll be back.

Finally a good Korean place to eat in the area!  I stopped by here a couple of times so far, and the place is nicely decorated and looked very clean.  I didn't get to try everything yet, but so far, my favorites are their hamburger and steak sandwich w/ pepper jack cheese.  They're unique in a sense that the meat has the Korean marinated BBQ flavor, which was so good!  On top of that the portions are very generous for the amount of money This is my new favorite place for lunch, and I would highly recommend a visit if you're in the area.

My fiance, his brother and I stopped by for a late lunch at NY Kimchi after meeting with our jeweler just down the street to pick out our wedding bands. We were just looking for something fast to prevent hypoglycemia but were blown away by the selection, cleanliness, service, quality... basically everything.   There was a designated doorman greeting/opening the door for us at the entrance - "Welcome to Kimchi" which was unexpected/a little out of place.  First glance - looked like an ordinary Korean bakery - only to learned that there were many more stations in the back with wide selection of ready to be made hot food. We definitely had a really difficult time deciding - everything looked so amazing and well priced (average $10). Ultimately, we went with short rib burger with fries (only $1 extra!), mandoo guuk, and seafood soon tofu. The ordering process was very simple - give your name + your order, when it's ready they will call you and you pay at the counter - just like any fast food joint. The food came out super fast and we were feasting away in no time. Although the food was served in lightning speed, it did not lose points in quality. Everything was super tasty and fresh. My soon tofu was big enough to serve two - perfect amount of spice, loaded with tofu and seafood! My only complaint - I miss my stone pot and wished I could crack an egg into it! My fiance really loved his mandoo guuk - generous serving of rice cake, perfectly seasoned broth. My soon brother in law's burger - even though I crave burger maybe once a year - after taking a bite, I knew I had to come back to try all the other burgers on the menu. The short rib burger - loaded with fries onion and avocado spread - it was beyond delicious. Even with just one taste - I actually think it might be the best beef burger bite I had in my life (yes better than In-N-Out, shake shack, or whatever best burger places there claim to be). The side order of potato wedges was crispy and well seasoned - such an awesome deal for just $1 more! In addition,  there were samples in every station - baked goods, 9 types of smoothies (yes 9, and the guy didn't mind repeating the selection again and again), 7 types of mochi desserts (all with different fillings - chewy and not overwhelmingly sweet!), kimchi, dumplings, seafood/kimchi pancakes, fish cake - good, cheap food plus more delicious free food? Pardon my lack of self control. A quick light lunch turned into the ultimate indulgence feast - in fact, my soon brother in law asked if my fiance and I can just take him back for every meal for the rest of his stay with us - and I couldn't be happier to oblige to his request.  Only wished NY Kimchi opened a bit earlier in our time in the city - but so happy to have found this place in our last month and a half in the city. Would definitely be back for lunch and dinner!
So delicious!!!  It's really nice and clean looking in there, and lots of really enthusiastic and helpful staff!  Free Samples all around!  Great for lunch! Have to try it out for dinner!

Best meatballs !!!  Best desserts !!!!  Small restuarant with great service and food.  It is expensive but the service and food are excellent.  So you get what you pay for.  Will return for another special ocasion.
You must have the meatballs. Penne with Vodka sauce excellent! Staff is super friendly. Great, great!

Great addition to a neighborhood full of but nothing but Chinese Bakeries and fast foods. Interior decoration can be better bit they seem to be trying. Free wifi, decent menu and price, open fairly late. Cannot complain.

I loved this place, from start to finish!  My fiance and I are currently trying to eat our way through Philadelphia Magazine's top 50 restaurant list. We have about 26 to go. There have been a lot of disappointments on that list (The Farm and Fisherman was the number one disappointment, sadly). However, Fond was WONDERFUL. The service was attentive, the atmosphere was lovely and the food was delicious. My fiance and I shared the lobster risotto (to die for creaminess), foie gras (also to die for), and the tuna crudo (so fresh with a little bit of spice) to start and then had the flank steak and swordfish as entrees. I really liked the flank steak - it was served over risotto and a rich, flavorful sauce. the swordfish was good but couldn't match the flavors in the flank steak dish. For the dessert we ordered the cheese plate and cannolis. I regretted the cheese plate - not impressed by it, but the cannolis were delicious! As other reviewers have said, the olive loaf bread is SO GOOD.  I would definitely go back to this place - they know what they are doing and they do it well.  Fond deserves their place on the top 50 restaurant list!

Nice restaurant priced right. The 7 course tasting is well worth the try. The seating is tight and the restaurant is small but it works. Located on a nice corner where several bar / restaurants are located. As must try. I will be back.

If i could eat here every day, I would (and I wouldn't even get fat because of how healthy the meal is!). What you get here you won't find anywhere in NYC - only in Japan. I love the concept of this restaurant and the peaceful atmosphere of this place. Located on the quieter side of Williamsburg, this is Yuji's (from Yuji Ramen) new restaurant. And what else would you expect from Yuji other than super fresh seafood. Lovely staff & service - I couldn't be more grateful for their love of seafood and to be able to create simple but utterly delicious dishes. My fiance & I had 2 appetizers (because we couldn't decide which one we wanted) and a lunch set each - king mackerel (because we would fight over the mackerel since we both love the fatty flavour). Beside the fact that we were slightly hungover, we both guzzled down the meal and left feeling with a smile & a happy belly. Few tips: - you don't find out what's on the menu until you get there - only appetizers & set lunch available - lunch is usually fish w/ sides + miso soup + brown rice - opens for lunch only I saw on their FB that I missed out on the sashimi appetizer - see! you'll miss out on what you don't know about if you don't go! Can't wait to go back!

It's easy for Yelpers, including myself, to give a buzz-worthy restaurant five stars right out of the gate. We want to be associated with it. We feel ahead of the curve. We take pride in finding a special place. Okonomi is a special place. But truthfully, it's too early to review. Right now, it only serves one menu a day for lunch. It hasn't even opened for dinner yet. There's a reason the New York Times' critic gives his new restaurants a few months to warm up; it's unfair to judge a place, especially an original one like Okonomi, this early. Give it time. Let it find its legs. Then beat it up, or give it its justly deserved star allotment. Having said that, ladies and gentlemen, my hypocrisy: four stars, which accurately represents my perfectly good and refreshingly unique lunch at Okonomi. Enjoy.
Really awesome place! Only 12 seats in the restaurant so it will continue to fill up as it gets more known but really clean, fresh and affordable fish.

I was very impress with everything  here!!! Tacos enchapulinados the best I ever try!!! Service?   I never have a great friendly and professional service all at the same time!! Mg: he make us feel like family!! I will come back soon!! Am so happy to find this place.  It still my hart!!!!
No way, seriously another overrpriced placed w baby portions? Anemic service, cool ambiance and eclectic menu that was different. Overall a miss for me.

12 pretty ladies and a very happy hour ;) I was here with a group of my girlfriends...we sat in the outdoor'ish "patio" space. One sip of that marg and i knew where things were headed. We ordered a few appetizers...the Taco de Suadero (braised brisket) being the fan favorite. Food was good, service was good, bartender was GREAT -funny, entertaining and cute to boot ;) The margs took us down in the best way. After a few of them i could hear the slurs in my friends words and see glasses of water being downed to balance the tipsy. Then the selfies began. We got a little loud i guess. 12 drunk girls on a hot Saturday afternoon, it can get....aggressive. Well turns out some couple didn't really appreciate our funfest reunion, because our waitress asked us to leave :/ (but i get it...we had been there for a few hours and we were pretty wasted) i'd go back (with a smaller group lol) to sample the tequila selection...looked pretty decent!

This was a very cool dining experience, and our server was helpful and knew the menu well. We ate the guacamole with ants (they are ground up so it looks like pepper) and it tasted delicious, slightly nutty.  We also ordered the fried grasshoppers/crickets which were crunchy and had a great mole sauce that was sweet and slightly spicy.  As long as I didn't look at what I was eating it was fine.  Honestly, the texture is really nice, but it seemed that they weren't the most fresh (not that I have ever had crickets before!) and there were a lot of them (a little bowl goes a long way). The tortillas that came with the food were fresh, warm and homemade.  Plus, they were unlimited, and the server kept bringing more back which I loved.  There is nothing worse then restaurants that are stingy with chips/tortillas. The ceviche of the day was also slightly spicy, just as I like things.  However, it was a much smaller plate and we all could have eaten much more but that's typical for ceviche I suppose. One of my absolute favorites was the nopal fries.  With a freshly breaded outer layer, the fries weren't greasy and again the sauce was a wonderful pairing with the fries.   I ate the Pollo de Plaza and couldn't get enough of the sauce (can you tell I'm saucy - and sassy!). It was a large plate but I somehow managed to finish it all, and the string beans were nicely cooked, but slightly crunchy. All and all, the Black Ant is a great, and very unique dining experience.  Highly recommend it, especially if you're with a group of people who are adventuresome and want to try some completely different food!

Delicious food, great service, innovative cocktails, and cool date space. The jerk chicken was exceptional as was the cod cheek tacos - both had great flavor. Guac is very good and unique. Space is well-designed, though they could revisit the weird ant mural on the back wall.

THE.BEST.COCKTAILS.IN.THE.WORLD! thank you Cesar, the best mixologist in the world!!! The moment I sat on his bar with my friend, he was warm, friendly and knew exactly what we wanted!!! I had some churros dessert and some ice cream with strawberry and banana to die for!!! everything was amazing, I'll definitely be back for dinner for sure, but i guess ill sit at the bar, since i LOVE Cesar so much! thank you
Delicious dining experience! The tacos and drinks are outstanding! A very talented owner, magnificent chef, skilled bartenders, and a delightful team altogether.

Great quality and service.  Unfortunately it feels that they are tailored for take out despite having plenty of seating. They wrap your bagels and give you tiny bagel sized paper plates if you ask to sit down. This is not a restaurant that you want to go to with friends and enjoy breakfast together but for a quick bagel, they are the best in town.
They have fast service, the bagels are full of flavor! I love the size of the bagel, it's perfect!!! Coffee it yummy!!! great place to eat in or take out!!! thank you!

I too was a huge fan of Skinner's prior to this place.  That place will hold a dear spot in my heart.  Gone are the booths, the darkness, the cigarette machine (I don't smoke, but it was nostalgic!), the dive feel of the bar.  In are flat screen tvs (I want flat screens at certain bars...this isn't one of them), a "cleaner" feel (how is that a bad thing?  I don't know...but it is in this instance), more modern.   Maybe I'm being picky, but it just didn't feel right here.  It just feels so boring in here now, like every other bar - there's nothing special.  It's like if they made Dirty Franks modern...blasphemous!

Honestly this place was getting a minimum of 3 stars no matter what b/c they served some reediculous good gravy fries; and there is nothing more than this homegrown central jerzee boy likes than a heap of steaming gravy fries..well maybe donuts.  I have not had proper gravy fries in the Filth area. but Mac's took care of that and even threw some short ribs on em. Feefawkingnomeenal. Though they said they could feed 4 people...riiight...try one fat asian face aside from a few that my friends picked off my plate when I wasn't looking    (that's right I don't share..even w/ friends).  Their ham, egg and cheese w/ spicy mustard was shit though.         The bar itself was fine, why r so many people complaining it's no longer a dive? What did u expect when Always Sunny cast bought and remodeled  Skinners? For them to just changed the name and reopen it exactly the same? That would have been a sound business plan. I like a good dive as anyone, but I couldn't imagine eating gravy fries at Frank's or Ray's w/o getting e coli poisoning. Beer selection is pretty good but their only special is 3 dollar Miller Low Lifes which is considered "special" in my book for bad reasons. The bar was  uncomfortably humid and hot considered it was not packed on a Thurs night, but either way Mac's will give me a reason to come to Olde City at night, and that reason is first name "Gravy" and last name "Fries."

We hit Mac's for lunch right before the US vs. Ghana soccer game during the World Cup.  We arrived right before the crowd so we were able to get a table right away.  There was only one waiter working but he was able to handle everything very well and we were not waiting long before he took our order.  I had a chicken cutlet hoagie and my girlfriend had the chicken fingers. Both meals were pretty standard; my hoagie was very large and I could only finish half.  The fries were different; thinly cut and very crispy.  The spicy mayo that accompanied the fries was excellent; I put some on my sandwich too.   It's a small space and filled up quickly prior to the game starting, I could easily see this place becoming packed on a typical drinking night. The place was clean and the décor was simple and functional.  It's located directly across from my office so I'll be adding this to my lunch stop places.

Yes I am a fan of It's Always sunny, but that is not the only reason I enjoy this bar. I have been a few times, and I never go back to bars if I don't like the service. The staff is very friendly and helpful. I went there once on a Saturday night, and the waitress (Ashley) and others tried their best to get me and my large group a table and chairs so we could all sit together. I have been a few times since then and have always gotten the same respect whether it was a big group or a small one.  The food is delicious and not overpriced for what it is worth.  I love the atmosphere and the bathroom is nice and clean. It was hot in there when I was there but from what I hear they have the AC in there fixed now. I love that I don't have to elbow someone to get my beer, or get the bartenders attention. I was there when it was crowded and I still got attention. Really it's just a great bar, especially if you like a place that's laid back and has good food and beer. I would give it many more stars if I could. :)

This restaurant is renovated recently, and the atmosphere is great! I tried many other places, but this place is much better than any sushi place. Above all, service is really satisfying. I went to this place for the first time, and they gave me all kinds of 'on the house' food, like noodle and vegetable pancake. Interesting thing is those foods are on the menu! Great Food, Service, and atmosphere!

Cute shop, good coffee, well trained baristas. That said, the shop is very basic - it's just Stumptown coffee in a tiny space.  There's a definite neighborhood feel, which while nice to see, left me ignored by the barista having a conversation with the two other customers.   With Blue Bottle is a couple blocks away with ample seating (and bathrooms!), don't think I'll be back.

Very cute place, friendly barista, average-priced coffee. I ordered a café au lait and enjoyed it very much. I always love it when cinnamon and cocoa powder are provided as DIY add-ins. I was a little disappointed to find that it was essentially a take-out kiosk, because there are only 3 stools available in terms of seating. I was kind of hoping it would be a nice place to drop by and sit for awhile. Luckily it wasn't too chilly that day, so my friend and I sat on the bench outside in front of the shop.
Stopped in on a cold Saturday afternoon and enjoyed a great cup of drip coffee.  They serve Stumptown.  Highly recommend it.

Stopped in here on a rainy NY day and were thrilled to find this gem. Stumptown being slung and cold brew on tap. Have a small assortment of baked goods but drinks are the specialty. Only about three seats total so don't plan to hang and do work or anything. That being said I will be back!

Great food, atmosphere and music! The last time I went with my family, I spent good money (+$100), expecting to sit and enjoy the band. Right after we payed the bill we were asked if we would be leaving soon... That's the last time I'm going there. They also pour beers an inch below the rim BE CAREFUL... THERE IS NOT A FULL BAR!!!

The Pizza was great.  Their beer selection is a wonderful representation of the local breweries. The place was hopping... the band was great, yet something was missing... our beers all arrived with the appearance someone had taken a good sip out of them...yes the infamous short pour. Not to be deterred we ordered appetizers, and found our waiter was attentive but overworked, we ended up getting our own plates , napkins and silverware.  More beer, (still short) pizza's..ran up a good bill..and then the final straw..no sooner had we paid the bill and the owner swung through and said "will you be leaving soon?" Ouch. Not likely to go back

Meh.  First off call ahead to make sure they are open.  Hours say 11am. Menu says 930.  Other places say 1030.  Sign in window today announced 12. Too much bread.  Breakfast sandwiches are okay.  Zesty was better than Loaded.  With everything prepared to order, I expected more than warmed squash or heated tomato on my egg sandwich.  It was boring. I took the top piece of bread off. Lamb lollies.  Great meat.  Great caramelized pumpkin.  Salad greens were way too bold and did not compliment.   Fish tacos.  Messy presentation.  Overstuffed and messy to eat.  Flavors are fine on the high range, fresh.  But the mid-range, just like on the b-fast sandwiches, was boring.  No acidity to mark the fish.  No pop.  Incomplete.   Having water pitchers on the table makes me think your waitstaff is not capable.  And the tables are too small for that anyway.  Confirmed when I can't get a refill on coffee at brunch.   Regardless of their standards, you feel like you wait too long for food.

Yelp rarely steers me so wrong. After seeing the great reviews for this place, I came for dinner and left hungry and disappointed. As others have said it takes about 35 minutes to get your food. The waiter came and took our uncomplicated order of lamb lollies appetizer, fish tacos and crosti (with prosciutto and cheese). 5 minutes after our order was taken someone came by, who introduced herself as one of the owners, and asked what we ordered, wrote it down, and told us she would check on it. However, she warned that our order would take a while, since they "make everything to order." This explanation annoys me, if you have a slow kitchen, just say that. I don't think you're making me fresh bread for my crosti, or tortillas for my tacos. So what exactly is being "made to order"? My food should be ready in about 10 minutes from a proficient restaurant kitchen, that preps properly for a busy dinner service on the weekend. Also, after one of the owners initially came by, no one else came to our table to tell us how much longer our food would take, I just saw employees looking at our table empty of food and head back to the kitchen. In general if someone from the restaurant tells me they are checking on my order, then provide an update. Otherwise, don't bother telling me you are checking. After we finally got our food, the disappointment continued. The order of fish tacos has lukewarm fish in a lukewarm soft taco shell. The whole bite was a bit bland but edible, and at that point, I was hungry enough to call it a win. The lamb lollies had too much rosemary and were a bit overcooked, but otherwise fine and came with tasty sides. However, the crosti was terrible, it was salty to the point of being inedible, and I tried to eat it, because I was so hungry. But I gave up after two bites. The same woman, one of the owners, checked on us after the food had been cleared off our table, and when I told her about the crosti, she took it off our bill. All in all though, I will definitely not be back.

Heard good things about this place, and I was not disappointed. We started our meal with the lamb lollies and a side of the garlic aioli (just for a little somethin' extra -- it doesn't come with the sauce). The meat was served with dressed arugula, pomegranate seeds and roasted cubes of pumpkin. OMG. First, the meat was fantastically seasoned. The pumpkin was a pocket of sweetness, the arugula provided a bitter contrast and the pomegranate seeds were like crack -- I chased them all down with my fork. I have no idea if this is authentic Aussie cuisine, but my taste buds were plenty pleased. The garlic aioli was not what I expected -- I thought we were going to get a mayonnaise-like sauce, but this was much more traditional -- olive oil steeped with chopped raw garlic. Yum! My dude got an egg sandwich that he said "rocked." He especially liked the slab of cheese that came with it. I ordered the pork sandwich which came with beet matchstick slaw. It was faboo -- but the bread totally overwhelmed the protein. No more boulder baguettes, guys! We also got an order of the fries, which were these logs of wedged potato. They looked good, and their crispy skin was tasty -- but they were raw in the middle. For dessert, we got the Triple T, and sweet, sweet moses, it was the best dessert I've had in recent memory. It was a mishmash of freshly whipped cream and Tim Tam cookies. Order this at least once -- you won't care about the sugar crash later. Ambiance-wise, the Thirsty Koala is a little weird. It looks like a diner, complete with the same mega-bright lighting you'd find in a hospital. That said, it has a snazzy wood-panelled bar area and the bathrooms are really nice. The service was also excellent. I'll be returning -- I want to try a couple more sandwiches and eat that Triple T again!

Awesome food!! We had the lamb lollies as an app which were excellent!! Both meals with steak were full of flavor. They have lots of gluten free options too. They people there were really great there too!!
The fish and chips are great, Im a fan of this place.. And very friendly staff.. try this place

The return trip wasn't as excellent as our first visit, most likely because it was WAY busier (dinner time on a Saturday night).  As other reviewers have said, most of my complaints are probably due to the place being new, and they'll probably work out the kinks as they go along. Since it was so packed, we were given the option of sitting at a table for two (that was right up against another table for two, which would have been as awkward as sitting at a table for 4 with 2 strangers) or the bar.  We didn't really want to sit at the bar, but it was the best option so we settled for it. There were only 2-4 other people at the bar with us, but the bar tender struggled to keep tabs on us once our food came (which was fairly quickly compared to the last visit).  It seemed like maybe he's the guy in charge of tea and coffee for the entire restaurant, so his attention was elsewhere.  He never checked up on us as we ate, never refilled our glasses, and took a very long time to clear our plates after we'd finished.  Another problem with sitting at the bar - there's nowhere to put/hang winter wear.  The stools don't have backs to them, and there are no hooks under the bar top, so when it gets busy and they need all the seats, there's nowhere to put your coat, hat, mittens, and scarf. The food itself was as delicious as ever.  This time I tried a burger with "The Lot", which includes lettuce, tomato, bacon, an egg, a slice of pineapple, caramelized onions, and some kind of beet slaw.  It was incredibly tasty, even if it was a struggle to fit in your mouth and therefore extremely messy.  My girlfriend had the Banjo Patterson jaffle (a repeat order from our last visit) and said it tasted just as good, but was a little cold. THE BOTTOM LINE:  On our return trip, the poor service brought our previous 5 star experience down to a 3 star one.  That being said, the delicious food will surely bring us back a 3rd time.

This place has excellent tacos!!  Perhaps some of the best flavor in NYC and I'm glad they're part of the neighborhood.  Priced right for repeat visits! The staff is really nice.  The ingredients are very fresh.  They are "asian-influenced" flavors and remind me of eating something from a creative Taco Truck.  The place is small but has counter seating. The 2 times I've been there I got take-out.  They prepared it pretty quickly. I live very close to this place and plan to come back often, at least once a week!  My wife loved the flavor too. I've had all the tacos by now: the fish (fresh and crunchy) the beef (tender and sweet) the chicken (smoked, savory and grilled to perfection.)  The Sambal Chicken sandwich had a delicious sauce, but the tacos are the protagonists at this spot. I'm getting hungry again just writing about it.  Glad to stop by again with friends another time.

Amazing place for burgers or tacos. What can I say, its the best burger and taco i've had in a while. I really like the variety of fries too, theres so many different choice. Its small and the price is reasonable. Strongly recommended.

Came here during the mid-day rush so it was packed. Ordered an Original to go. Had order in hand after about 15 minutes. Pretty fast for a completely packed place that's not much larger than a mobile food truck. Got back to the office started to eat lunch. The center was a little undercooked so I brought it back. The guy working the register had it remade for me. Just finished it and all I can say is that the burger was FREAKING AMAZING. If it weren't for the rain today, I seriously think that people would have lined up out the door. Good customer service and even better food? Will definitely be back.
I love this place. Probably the best skirt steak and fish taco they have. It's cheap and affordable and they have a tv to watch basketball games. Definitely recommend coming again.

Although a normal person with a normal sized appetite can walk out of here fully satisfied with a $10 bill, I swear Breakroom's fries, burgers, tacos.... everything on the menu is sprinkled with crack. I found myself consistently looking back at the menu and deciding what I wanted to order next. Please come here prepared to gain a couple pounds or with the plan on having a vigorous gym sesh after because this visit is definitely an indulging one! My friend and I came here on probably one of the coldest days this year so far and the staff was super accommodating with making sure we're warm with hot tea and the space heaters. We ordered the Breakroom fries (must order), the Breakroom burger (must order), fish tacos (must order) and the jalapeno dog (must order). Seriously though, from all the things we ordered.. I've come to the conclusion that you really can't go wrong with anything on their menu. Since they're located only a few blocks away from my work, I can't wait to return and try their other tacos and sandwiches. I'm glad they serve coffee because I'll for sure be needing one so I don't fall asleep at my desk from food coma!

First time trying this place out, was overall pleased with both the level of customer service and menu options they had listed. The staff were attentive and made sure customers were satisfied. Due to an overly busy lunch hour, they ran out of the confit pork belly. I ordered the fish taco, chipotle chicken and steak. All 3 of which were wonderfully seasoned and well portioned. They also offer a large variety of hot sauces, some too hot to even try. The best part was the Breakroom fries, greasy but so worth every bite! I would definitely go back, even for a quick bite before catching the next subway/bus/cab.

Great little place on Baxter street about two stores away from whiskey tavern...has about 8-10 counter seats where you could order and the food comes in around 5-10 minutes..also two seats near the window. Breakroom fries has tater tots, french fries, pork belly, bacon, jalapeno,onions and an egg...prices went up compared to opening week  but still worth the price. Bought the bacon jalapeno hot dog as takeout for my little sister but she ate it before i could take a picture..Would come again!
Damn this shit is so goood. So yummy. Just finished a burger. Want another one. Would have taken photo but ate it too fast.

I'd like to reiterate the words my boyfriend used to succinctly describe some of what we tried here tonight since they accurately reflect my sentiments as well... - Mint lemonade: "Off the CHAIN." - Fish tempura taco: "DUMB good." - Confit pork belly taco: "It's aite. If you fux with pork belly, you're gonna like this." If you guessed that this kid grew up in a hoodish part of Brooklyn on 90s rap, then you are correct. So we ordered the Taco Platter which is a great deal. Comes with 3 tacos for just under $10 and got the skirt steak, confit pork belly, and fish tempura taco. We also got another individual fish taco for $3.45, and we were SO glad we did. The battered catfish was seriously delicious and a must try. Drenched in sauce and topped with slaw and a slice of avocado made it hearty and flavorful. The steak in the skirt steak taco was perfectly cooked and so yummy. I think the pork belly was good, but it wasn't as memorable. I also really liked that they sprinkled green onions on the tacos instead of the traditional cilantro! (I personally don't fux with cilantro.) Everything washed down with a refreshing Mint Lemonade made for a satisfying and wallet-friendly dinner. In terms of environment, this place can get cozy - seats around 10 or 12 on stools around the counter. Love the fact that they have various hot sauces  (Dr. Assburn's, anyone?) and hand sanitizer lined up in front of patrons to conveniently grab. Since their tacos were amazing, I'm definitely excited to come back for their Breakroom burger & fries!

There are few restaurants anywhere, in any state or country, that can hit every single note dead on. And this is really something no one should ever ask of a restaurant: that it be utterly perfect in each way. And yet, somehow, Misery Loves Co. manages to pull this off. Misery is situated in a picturesque small town overlooking a kind of monstrous waterfall, and it is a really quiet, surreal place. Misery is spare and retro, with white walls set off by an open black-hooded kitchen. It is like a location in a dream, the way in dreams things aren't really specific or gaudy or limited to a certain era. My girlfriend and I shared two items for lunch, a chicken liver mousse special and The Vonnegut sandwich. Each was amazing. The chicken liver mousse came with a strawberry onion marmalade, yummy little mustard seeds, and mint leaves (!) The combination of the strawberry and the caramelized onion mixing with the fatty chicken liver and bright mint on top of the crusty bread was inspired. What was most inspired of all, though? The Vonnegut sandwich, which was for both my girlfriend and myself absolutely one of finest sandwiches we have had. It had this thin, crispy layer of pork belly sandwiched under a fried egg that let out this amazing gooey yolk. The sandwich then suddenly became a play on the classic fast food cheeseburger with melty American cheese and thousand island dressing-type spread on the buns. It was just a satisfying, and smart, and ironic sandwich. So yeah, we hit a lot of places when we went to the Burlington area but this is the first restaurant I wanted to write a review for and the first one I think of now when I think of Winooski or of strange waterfalls or soft, white rooms.
Exceptional and creative food. Good drinks as well. Service was alright, but not at a level equal to what we paid/level of food quality.

This place is simply AMAZING! The food is GREAT! The staff is super friendly and nice. The only qualm I have about this place is that it is always busy and super packed (although that is a good thing). If you don't mind taking the food to go, I recommend phoning in an order and just enjoying the food at home or at the park, unless you are ok with waiting for 45 mins to 1 hour.

If I were deciding for or against moving to Vermont, this place would go directly into the "for" column. I was a little bit skeptical when I walked in because the overall look set off my pseudo-Brooklyn bullshit radar. The menu also set a really high bar, evoking both excitement and fear (of failure to deliver). I opted for the nori fries and fish and chips, which did not disappoint. It was one of the most creative and satisfying fish and chips I've had in my life. The kimchi was truly excellent and the fries were delectable. My friends' dishes looked equally delicious, as were their bloody Mary's. Our waitress brought us some unsolicited pastries at the end of the meal to boot. I know where I'll be headed from brunch when I'm back in VT!

Went in for a work lunch today.  It seems they just started working a lunch hour at this particular location.  The food was great!  I had the Salumi Panini which was a bit on the spicy side, loved it.  It did say it comes with either Garlic Fries or a Side Salad, which normally if you don't specify which one you want, you automatically get fries, however we did get the side salad.  The salad tasted fine, but the restaurant was out of fries apparently.  Because of the inconvenience the waiter gave us a free dessert tasting.  I chose the Cannoli Mousse which was fantastic.  I think they have some work to do before their lunch hour is perfected, but they handled things as best they could.  I'll definitely be back in a week or two.

I just had dinner there tonight and what a nightmare This waiter Josh " comes up with this boring pitch That his  mgmt is forcing him to say . Our table was small Me and my wife ordered drinks there was red lip stick on the wine glass! I still can't believe it took 45 minutes for a salad to come out Smh !  This Restaurant has NO NO NO written all over save your money and Just go somewhere else

Went with a co-worker for dinner last night. I had been a fan of Square Peg (the restaurant previously in this spot), and I wanted to check out what had moved in. The decor is fantastic, as is the music. Lots of modern Italian charm and a solid Sinatra soundtrack to go with it. The service was quick and friendly. But of course, it's mostly about the food, isn't?  Co-worker and I had the Orange Cello Cosmopolitan and a margarita of some kind. Neither was particularly great, which was surprising considering the waiter suggested the cosmo. They weren't BAD, but for the price, I wasn't impressed. The bread served was delicious, as was the Mozzarella Fritte. The marinara served with the Mozzarella Fritte was particularly tasty and had a nice zip to it. For the meal, we split the Tortellini Alla Vodka. The tortellini was...odd. It seemed over cooked, but at the same time, the centers of them tasted like flour. The sauce was a bit weak, in terms of flavor. Overall, we both decided we wouldn't order it again. For dessert, we had some kind of chocolate mouse, which was good. For $30 a person (including tip), it wasn't a bad meal. It just wasn't a great meal. We may be coaxed back to try a pizza, which is their self proclaimed specialty. But since all portions are meant for sharing (so said our waiter), my co-worker and I had trouble agreeing on a single pizza we'd both be really into. I wish they had individual portions instead of being all about the "sharing" aspect of each entree.

The restaurant itself is visually appealing. their concept is lost in translation. They say they are a wine bar but don't even use wine glasses. The arrancini was bland and the pasta was very greasy. Service was quick and attentive, but needs better traIning on their products.

We have had dinner three times at SR. The food has been consistently great. Try their salmon. They prepare it medium rare, and it's some of the best I have ever had.  The pasta is never over cooked.  The pizza is among the best in the city.  For the money, this place is a great combination of terrific food and value.

This locations has turned over a few times so were already skeptical about how the experience would be at stella rossa. When we checked in for our reservation we had to wait a few minutes and listen as the hostess, possibly another host, and a waiter or two debated over who was getting seated where. Clearly they were new at this. But I guess that was to be expected at such a new place. We were seated a table in the front, by the windows which was nice. However, the Sinatra singer was very close to us and it was really loud. In fact, the table next to us asked to me moved due to the volume of the guy's singing. Our waiter gave us "recommendations" but really he just listed two items out of every section of the menu which were supposed to be their most popular items. We ordered arancini (very bland and severely under salted and seasoned) and fried mozzarella (seasoned well, but very thick breading and were just ok, but our fault for ordering fried mozzarella anyway) as appetizers. Good news is they came out very fast. Bad news is as I described- so bland. The bread to start was awesome though. For entrees we ordered carbonara (it was VERY greasy), pizza (too much crust and bland- they need salt at this place!), and baked stuffed rigatoni dish- drowning in pepperoni grease. The wine was so expensive, about $12 for a "7oz" pour), and the 1/2 carafe option was such a rip off (about $23). In conclusion, I will never return and I could never recommend this place when there are way better options in the area for dinner. Sadly, that MIGHT even include the Olive Garden.
love this place real Mexican food and the truck they have on fifth even better when its the night

So good! Come support these folks, they make the best tacos. They recently had a fire but their truck is set up outside and is awesome! They need our support! That reviewer who deducted a star because they had a fire - what kind of jerk move is that? This is a small business with hardworking people and great food.

Absolutely delicious! We got 4 tacos and thought each of them were amazing. Does anyone know if they cater out of the truck? I am looking for a taco truck for an event in Queens and would LOVE them to come by and serve their amazing tacos. I saw they catered but we are looking for food trucks. Thank you!

The former reviews, unfortunately, under-exaggerate the power of Lee's Deli's tasty creations. The chicken-cheese steaks are to die for... I repeat: to die for. I cannot adequately depict my experience with Lee's Deli's chicken cheese steak with adjectives. I think 'WOOHOO!' comes close though =) While it may not have the publicity Pat's, Jim's, or Geno's, Lee's Deli impressively appeals to true Philly cheese steak connoisseurs. Those who have experienced the Lee's Deli chicken cheese steaks can nod their heads to my accolades. Whether you are from out of town or a b&r (born and raised) Philadelphian, Lee's Deli has got something--spectacular--to offer. However, one very important perk of Lee's Deli is being heavily ignored by all. Yes; the breakfast platters are phenomenal, the homemade burger is one-of-a-kind, and the chicken cheese steaks stun me every time. But let me say this: Lee's Deli's carrot cake is a real knock-your-socks-off treat! This unique recipe has been commended by several newspapers of Philadelphia as well as the Main Line (suburbs). Lee's Deli's carrot cakes redefine the entire genre of carrot-cake, and flawlessly complement your breakfast, burger, and steak! It honestly does not matter if you dislike carrot cakes, like carrot cakes, detest carrot cakes, or love carrot cakes.  Lee's Deli's WILL convert you to become a carrot cake maniac (It converted me, at least =P). The carrot cakes are UNIVERSAL! Lee's Deli is SECOND TO NONE.

Lee's Deli's carrot cakes are UNREAL and, arguably, the BEST carrot cakes in PHILLY! Unlike many of these reviewers, I frequent Lee's Deli solely to pick up carrot cakes for the week because these treats vanish as soon as they hit the shelves! These cakes are PERFECT. The not-too-sweet cream frosting balances with the moist richness of the cake texture. Each bite hits the buds with tidal waves of flavor. This humble, award-winning recipe transcends your ordinary supermarket-cakes. Whether you have a fierce sweet tooth (like me), or if you are not a carrot-cake fanatic, you are in for an addictive treat. I am absolutely in love with Lee's Deli's carrot cakes! BEWARE: the carrot cake craze is contagious! =)

In 2007, I was deployed to Afghanistan to fight the war. It was incredibly difficult to leave my family, my friends, and my community once more, after returning from Iraq less than a year before. Now, you may be wondering why I'm posting a review for Lee's. Growing up in West Philadelphia, I have been a regular since I was a child. And let me say that Scott, the owner, is a genuinely caring fellow. Last year during Christmas time, while I was stranded at my base in the deserts of the Middle East, Scott sent me an unbelievable surprise: a Lee's signature buffalo chicken cheese steak, barbeque chicken wings, a carrot cake, and letter from the neighborhood. I cannot tell you how much his gesture meant to me; how much it means to me, even now. Yes--the food at Lee's Deli is superb. But--the customer care is unmatched.

Gross!  Looks a lot nicer than it tastes.  I ordered a French dip and it arrived on a round potato roll with no dip.  The waitress didnt know what au jus meant, and the sandwich tasted like the crappiest frozen hamburger cooked in a microwave.  Also, tater tots and a sandwich cost $17.  Avoid this rip off.  Nice on the outside, expensive and unsatisfying on the inside.

Visited the VI recently and it was a great experience. Nice ambience and enough flat screens to watch the game. Looking forward to the football season and watching games. Food and service is definitely better than the surrounding restaurants.

I cant rave enough about this place. I love this place! Everytime we have girls night and go out for dinner or drinks, I suggest this place. The wine is amazing!!!!! The small plates are great. I never had a complaint with the food, but my all time favorite is the cheese and meat plates with the honey, grapes and toasty bread. I seriously have an addiction. Sometimes it can be difficult for seating when busy but its so worth it! I never had a bad server either. My favorite place in WEHA.

So glad we came in here on a Tuesday night for a holiday dinner. The place was packed so we sat at these beautiful marble bars in the back. Vinted is lined with wine stations, offering you a really cool tasting experience. Here, you can order anything from a 1 oz taste to a full glass. We found our server/bartender, I believe his name is Greg, to be super knowledgeable and just really pleasant to talk to. He could talk extensively about craft cocktails, wine and beer to the point that my accompanying booze nerd friends, found themselves listening, for once. Food was fantastic. We ordered crispy pork ribs, with a hint of 5-spice and the perfect skin. Buttered crab legs,  pulled pork tacos rounded it out. Tacos are generally easy, simple, and good. These tacos were delicious. The menu is wide-ranging, the plates are well executed and beautiful. It is on the pricier side, but you are getting a delicious dish. The bartender ended up sending us home with some very hard-to-find craft brews to try. It was a dining experience to remember.

Awesome Caribbean food! Went with Jerk Chicken with Candied Yams, Green Beans, and a decent amount of the homemade hot sauce. My eyes were watering, my mouth was on fire, but I could not stop eating, it was too tasty!

At first I was told it was Jamaican. Now I believe it's Trinidadian. It's a food cart sitting in the middle of Water St. Sometimes you can expect long lines but on average it's relatively quick. They have items from curry goat and ox tail to jerk chicken. Their sides include Mac n cheese, yams, potato salad to collard greens to name a few. Jerk chicken is good but spicy as hell and salty. BBQ chicken is not your typical Southern style BBQ. They make their own sauce which is thinner and more subtle. Their best is probably the curry chicken. It's similar to Chinese curry where it's not too spicy, more salty than it is sweet. Mixed veggies consist of only cabbage and the collard greens are good. Since I try to be healthy, those are my standard choices. I hear the best sides are the yams and Mac n cheese.

Could be worse but definitely could be better.  I wish I could give this 2 1/2 stars because its "ok" but "I've experienced better"... Many TVs, as in 45, so you could see the game wherever you sat.  You do not get seated, you walk in and seat yourself so if you want an up-front table by the big screen get there early.  Menus came quick, drinks were slow, and the meal even slower. The atmosphere is fun and loud (we were here for a Devils viewing party) but friends have said on a non-game night it can be quite dead here.  Felt bad for the waitress who was friendly but way overworked. This place obviously needs to hire more staff for busy nights. After 20 minutes for drinks and ordering it took an additional 80 minutes (yes, that's 8-0)  for our food to arrive- which is just unacceptable. The waitress offered a "sorry, we are so busy tonight" but that was it.   $94 for average food for 4 (sliders, fried fish sandwich, ribs, BBQ combo 4 beers and soda).  They forgot the cole slaw with the sliders, tartar sauce with the fish, and they were out of brisket for the BBQ combo.  Everything came with fries (just average frozen variety) and little plastic containers of ketchup instead of having condiments on the table, so if you wanted more you had to track down your overworked waitress and wait for her to bring some.  The sodas were in fairly small disposable plastic cups with ice making the amount of soda small. No kids menu that I saw, but plenty of kids there for the game.   I don't mean to be too hard on Miami Mikes. The owner is there and it's obvious he loves his job.  Miami Mike's has the opportunity to be the best sports bar around, amazing even, with a little bit of work. More help (waitstaff/kitchen), better fries (think Five Guys), think ahead by ditching the plastic containers of ketchup when you don't have the staff to run condiments to the table. Larger sodas.  Maybe a small kids menu from items already on the menu (sliders, mozz sticks, etc) Funny anecdotes, the menu has listed "McCain fries, Polly-O Mozzarella sticks", etc.  While I understand these are supposedly quality companies, the owner is advertising that he is serving overpriced frozen items that I can buy at ShopRite, which made us not want order those items... and we didn't. But it sure set the expectations low for the fries from the get-go! On a side note, a few Devils Dancers where there for the viewing party, which made the guys happy but the girls themselves looked really unhappy to be there, except when they were "on".  They sat in the corner texting with blank faces.
