Didn't represent the Devils so well I thought. Not sure if we'll be back. If we go again it's not for anything other than apps and beer from the decent beer list on a game day.

The pork chop is substantial and the shrimp okra is delicious.  I really wish I would have taken photos but my friend and I devoured our meals the moment they hit the table.  They give very generous portions.  The place is lovely and quiet.  The service was excellent.  My only complaint was the fact that I was a hot, sweaty mess from riding my bike to Bushwick, and it did not feel like they had their a/c on.  I'd be happy to be a sweaty mess and eat there again.  That's how amazing their food is.

I have eaten many a stellar meal at this establishment since it's opening and now it's time to write a review. Dinner Review: I have had nearly every item on this menu and have had friends and guests come with me to this restaurant numerous times. The response is always unanimous--that the food is completely amazing and unforgettable. Many friends have returned to Falansai because they can't stop thinking about the food. This is a very different type of Vietnamese food from Chinatown or your run-of-the-mill Banh Mi/Pho shop. The food here is from a different region, but no less (if not more) delicious. The emphasis is on the sweet and subtle as opposed to the spicy. Even without the heat, the flavors pack a punch. My husband is obsessed with the Lamb Curry and I can't stop thinking about Mama's ginger chicken. Everything else on the menu is completely scrumptious as well. Even the small vegetable plates are addictive. And as for the reviewer who dumped all over the Shaking beef, he couldn't be more wrong! It is truly incredible. And the papaya salad is NOTHING like a cole slaw. It is made completely fresh and always crunchy. BTW, picky kids eat this food! The decor is simple and calming and the waitstaff is incredibly friendly and accommodating. They also have excellent wine recommendations. Even if you live out of the way, the trip is def worth it! You'll leave stuffed and happy, with no regrets!

Really nice place to go to.  The atmosphere is lovely, the tall ceilings, the blues, the lights, the communal table are relaxing and inviting. The food is very good. The shaken beef is just amazing. And the okra with shrimp was such a wonderful surprise. They are partnering with a sommelier and the wine choices are really good with the food and the staff is very knowledgable and accommodating. If you are in Bushwick, I can't recommend it enough.
Nice bar to go to. .. long beer selection and love the pork belly entrée. . To bad I don't see it on the menu anymore.  Overall, it was a good experience

My husband and I (and sometimes my children as well) frequent this restaurant about once a week.  We love the food here and the service as well.  On the weekends, Daniel waits on us, and knows our orders and preferences by memory.  Everything we have ordered here has always been excellent.  We regularly get the tom yum soop, the chicken lettuce wraps, the red curry, the basil fried rice, and we have had a number of their other dishes as well.  We love the ambience, the service and the food.  Outstanding!!!

I've only had Thai at a few places in Philly, and this was definitely up there as one of the better places I've tried. I usually judge a Thai place on the Pad Kra Pao (basil chicken), and this place was better than average. It wasn't as spicy as I would have liked or expected, given the chili pepper designation on the menu, but then again, I didn't specify a level of spiciness so they probably decided to take it easy on me.  My bf got something that involved "wild boar"-- he loved it and i liked it a lot (I think he's more easily wooed by novelty than I am). The thing that really set this place apart was the service. This is by far the best service I've had in Chinatown and one of the best places I've been to in Philly. The servers were really friendly and helpful without being overwhelming, and they were super sweet even though we had changed our reservation several times. Plus, it's BYO!  I'm sure that the next time a craving for Thai hits, we'll be back.

The food was okay, but the manager was HORRIBLE.  I went with a groupon and I got my money back and I will never return to this place.  The food was decent until desert, which was bad- we got mango and sticky rice and the mango was not even close to ready to eat. It would not have ruined my dining experience but for the managers subsequent behavior. When we sent it back the manager came over and gave us an ultimatum on wasting her mango, which is insane, because it never should have been served. We had already paid and tipped 20% on the bill before the groupon and returned food, and without even looking to check what we had left the manager gave us an ultimatum on tipping.  The food here is average- but definitely not worth giving business to this person.  There are plenty of great Thai places in Philadelphia- you can skip this one.

I discovered this place while visiting Philly on a business trip and my only regret is that I found it the night before I left to go home. Wow this place was great and if I would have known about it earlier in the week, I'd probably have been here a couple times more. Cool restaurant inside with the whole picnic theme. Their menu has a wide selection and they also have the daily specials which change and are displayed in the glass case by the register. I decided on the Sundried Tomato Pesto Turkey pita, the broccoli and sweet potatoes. All were fresh and had great taste. I loved the Sundried Tomato Pesto that they put on the pita; it had a really interesting taste. This place seems to be know as a lunch place but they are perfect for a light dinner as well. Definitely give this place a shot!

The food was bad, the management was rude, they seem to have a tendency  for calling the police on people who complain I watched a man and his family have the cops called on him after he complained about a steak, after the manager told the patron "the meal is free, just do not ever come back here" the man left and the cops showed up just in time to pay the bill from what i could see from what my officer friend said this is not the first time that has happened. frankly this place will just be another failed experiment in the West Essex area. I ordered some of the Asian style food, General Tso to be specific, it was about as good as it would be from any given Chinese place....but cost twice as much. Avoid this place like the plague

I made a reservation on November 10th at 7:30 pm for 2. When I called, the women explained there policy regarding time seated (pretty much to satisfy everyone, they give you 2 hours). Once we got there, the bar & restaurant was filled, but they had our table ready for us. Bread came instantly & waitress came over right away. I only glanced at the menu online (should definitely do this prior to visit. Menu is 42 pages long). Lots of options, so I needed more time to decide. Even with a crowded restaurant, waitress was patient & gave a few suggestions to help out. I just wanted to try everything. So I figured I'd get appetizers as my meal. I went for crab. I had crab won tons, crab spring rolls, & crab cakes (these were excellent). I liked that if you ordered an entree, you get a complementary salad. It was perfect. With all the drinks, appetizers,entrees, deserts, & aperitifs, they meal came to $100 for 2 people. Prices, value, & ambiance are definitely worth it. I will be going back.
First Deli that has made me feel like I'm back in downtown Brookyn. excellent selections whole and fresh. Real Italian deli.
Love you guys!

This is my go-to Italian spot, albeit a tad pricey for a deli, it's the price you pay for authenticity. I've lived in the neighborhood for years, and in order for the novelty to remain, I only have it once in a while. Although, I doubt the novelty will ever wear. Their chicken parm and eggplant parm platters are amazing - I can go without the pasta and just scrape it all up with their fresh breads! They give more sauce than most places, which is just fine with me!

Lives up to the hype, and I rarely say that about anything. Edi & the Wolf is gorgeous, interesting, and the absolutely perfect place to grab dinner on a cold downtown winter night. We sat at the bar and enjoyed the flatbread and spatezle with a dry riesling. I can't wait to come back.

My wife and I went to this restaurant this evening i=based on good reviews on Yelp.  We were underwhelmed. We arrived at 6PM and were the first customers of the evening.  The place was comfortable and the waiter was attentive.  But the jazz music was blaring a loud cacophony of noise that seemed to bother only us. The menu was sparse.  We ordered the freekah salad, cornish hen and wiener schnitzel.  The salad was pleasant with crunchy and chewy grains accompanied by goat cheese.  But the two main dishes were disappointing. They were cooked covered by thin crispy layer of breaded crust which was tasteless.  The hen and the pork were tender but tasteless.  Eating the meats were like chewing on crispy cardboard.  We did not finish eating the two dishes. We lament the delicious wiener schnitzel we ate in the tiny diner in Germantown on East 86th Street some 30 years ago.  Our mouths still salivate from the memory of the flavorful meat and breading, and the wonderful side dishes that accompanied them.  Too bad that street has turned into a shopping district and the diner disappeared years ago.

First let me say I'm a pretty tough grader and maybe this place deserves the 5 stars some have given it--but in my book the perfect restaurant is very rare. This place is very, very good but not perfect. Let's start with the food.  I had an appetizer of pickled vegetables which is actually very thinly sliced (almost shaved) vegies on a bed of well-rinsed kraut and sauced (or probably marinated) in a sweetish, vinegary dressing, not unlike Thai cucumber salad which is something I love.  I found it quite tasty and a nice, light way to start a meal.  Then I had what I came for--the Wiener Schnitzel.  They will do either veal or pork.  I had veal.  It was nice and competently done; nothing to complain about but nothing really special either. What was special were the two sides that come with it:  a German style potato salad (but lighter than most) and what seemed like a cucumber salad sort of thing in what I think was a sour cream-based sauce/dressing.  Both were yummy and appropriate with schnitzel.  I also had a nice desert of a Bavarian custard topped with orange (tangerine?) slices and house coffee that seemed closer to espresso which was fine with me. Now lets talk about service.  I left wondering if they had mistaken me for the Times food critic.  They were that attentive.  I ordered wine by the glass and after I did so, the host asked if I would try another suggestion.  He gave me samples of both what I had ordered and his suggestion to try--his was better and went very well with the meal.  Same deal with desert--I was offered a taste of a suggested Austrian desert wine with my coffee and custard and it was very good so I let them sell me a full glass.  Heck, you only live once. The decor is unique (barn-like rustic)--and be sure to visit the restroom if only to see the "sink" which was apparently made from a very large old pot. When I was there around 6:30 PM on a Thursday, the place was almost empty but by the time I left 3 or 4 more tables were occupied.  In addition, there were a number of people eating, drinking and chatting who seemed like friends of the management.  But at no point would a new arrival have had trouble being seated.

Went with my fiance for dinner! This restaurant is delicious. For those of you who are craving authentic German, Austrian and Czech food, come here! We ordered the sardines. They tasted just like sardines I've had in Germany. And what blew my away was the pickled shaved fennel. I LOVE fennel, and thought it was an act of genius to pickle it. The we got the baby back ribs. My fiance, who was brought up in the South, said they were the best she ever had. "They were the most perfectly cooked baby back ribs I ever had." On to the flatbread. The flat breads here are like mini pizzas. We got one with figs and speck. Delicious. My fiance has been living in a small village in Italy for the past three years. The pizza in this village is AMAZING! And I've never had her say that a NYC pizza was better. Until now. With this flat bread. For our main course we had the schnitzel. It was perfectly cooked and seasoned. But what blew me away was the potato salad! I know, how can I get so excited about potato salad. But it brought me back to a restaurant I ate at in Poland last year. Perfect and bursting with flavor. Edi came to our table a couple of times to ask how we were doing, and Jenna and Kasha were both awesome too, providing great wine advice and stimulating conversation. If you want good food, come here. You won't be disappointed!

best pizza ever had so far extremely recommend. we always go there with my friends. they open until 4 am that's amazing. found nothing wrong with the stuff. they have added more items recently. garlic nuts are amazing.

I travel through Newark airport twice a week and won't be making the mistake of eating at this place again. High prices for low quality food...even for an airport. The lobster roll was sadly small on stale bread and tasted only like green peppers.  Sweet potato chips weren't fresh or hot and had an unexpected and overwhelming curry spice and salt flavor. Lobster BLT was decent, didn't taste like green peppers, but wasn't worth $29 + tip. Couldn't get my water refilled by the staff during my meal. The worst part were the flies and watching the kitchen staff roll the gross garbage out of the front door in clear bags during dinnertime. Gag!

An honor to review one of my hometown favorites! Grew up eating paella marinera here. Just the smell is so nostalgic! The sweetest most friendly staff, lovely ambiance, and the BEST bread and paella. Delicious flavor on the rice and the tender seafood. Also loved the spicy and regular olive oil selection. Didn't have room to get postre, but dessert menu looked very exciting.
They got rid of the Croissant French Toast in favor of that Brioche nonsense, ugh!! Food otherwise is really good!
All was great here. We have a large family and they handled all of our needs very well. The ribs were excellent and so was the home made pasta. Service was very good, too. Thank you, Brix!

I really wanted to like this place. My girlfriend grew up nearby and I make it a point to support local businesses rather than corporate chains. I'm a very loyal diner and regular at many places and am always looking for new restaurants to add to the list. Unfortunately, Brix missed the hitlist and made the *hitlist. When we walked in, our first impression was good. They've recently renovated and have created a kind of low budget, do-it-yourself Gordon Ramsay makeover to the place. However the positive reaction quickly faded as we waited at the empty hostess stand alongside other customers who looked just as confused and annoyed as we did. When we were finally seated, the waitress rudely tossed our menus on the table without even greeting us or telling us it was our table. Sadly, the bad start to the evening only got worse with the food - much worse. Contrary to what the name suggests, this is just a normal Italian restaurant's menu, but with a "tapas" section. As another reviewer below already said, this isn't tapas at all, it's just a collection of appetizers. Nevertheless we decided to stick to the tapas menu since that's what we thought what the restaurant specialized in. The mozzarella and tomato towers (basically a caprese salad stack) simply had no flavor whatsoever. As the first thing I tasted that night, (or didn't taste), it actually made me question whether I had a cold. The seared ahi tuna was completely overdone, practically cooked through, and rubbery. The ribs were just a joke - a plate with four tiny, separate ribs that were clearly not made in house. Imagine precooked ribs from Costco - after 2 nights sitting out on a table. The meatball trio was the only passable dish, which is all I can really say about it - it was hot and edible. However the absolute worst thing I've been served in a very long time was the sausage and broccoli rabe. There was simply no way that the dish had been cooked in the last 72 hours. It tasted like week old leftovers that weren't ever good to begin with. The broccoli was complete mush, the sausage was tough and tasted like a refrigerator, and both were swimming in old, murky olive oil. That was really the common thread among all the food, it was not fresh at all. I don't understand why some restaurants try to cut corners and save time by cooking things in advance, but this place is definitely one of them. Sadly, the service here was just as bad as the food. The place wasn't busy at all, but we waited 10 minutes to be seated, 15 minutes to get our order taken, 10 minutes for our drinks to arrive, and we had to ask for basic things like silverware and plates. The only thing that came out quickly was the food, and it was obviously because most of it was cooked earlier in the week and microwaved to imperfection. After the meal, we waited for over 20 minutes for our waiter to give us the check. We were the last ones in the place, the staff had already began eating at another table, and I had to ask the bartender to find our waiter, which took her another 5 minutes of yelling for him in the back. Unfortunately, while Brix did succeed in renovating the decor, they completely and utterly failed in changing what matters most in a restaurant - the food and service. All in all a completely regrettable and awful dinner experience. One of the few nights I wish we'd gone out for fast food instead. I hear the McRib is back.

Before heading to a cake-tasting event with a friend, we decided we needed something else in our bellies for the evening besides sugar. Fuel hit the spot. There were so many salad choices on the menu that appealed to me, it was hard to decide. I chose the cucumber and tomato salad with white beans, and it was a well-dressed, huge bowl of veggies. Perfect. My friend went with the Ridiculously Delicious Kale Salad, which she enjoyed, but one can only eat so much kale in one sitting, so she didn't quite finish. Besides the salads, the menu looks stellar, and I can't wait to go back and try more.

Fuel has awesome food but HORRIBLE service. I've been there four times and have had awful service three of those times. I don't know about anyone else but I feel like those aren't the best odds... I went for lunch this week with a good friend of mine and it took over an hour to get one serving of chips and guacamole, one salad, and one flat bread. By the time we got our food our lunch break was already up and we had to eat so fast we barely had time to enjoy our food. Not only was the service soooooo slow my friend had to ask 4 times and three different people to get a refill for her water - she probably waited 10 minutes before it was actually filled. When we got our check we waited and waited and finally had to go inside to pay our bill. The restaurant wasn't busy enough to wait that long especially during the lunch hour when people only have a certain amount of time to eat. Quite honestly I don't know if I will be back...

Food was good... I had the grilled veggie wrap, the vegetable and bread was very fresh. I did take out, it was around 6pm it wasn't crowded and I was in and out.. I think they had our food ready in about 10 minutes which is good because I was starving. Oh by the way I had a smoothie it was delicious.. The price is reasonable so this spot is ok with me. I will come back again from time to time when I am in the area

I'm embarrassed that I have not taken the time to review this gem in the past 23 years I've been enjoying pretty much everything on the menu.  Yes, even the vegetarian Reuben (ok, it was on a dare...).  The food never disappoints, whether it is the pastrami, the corned beef, the various homemade soups that change with the season, or their specially-made hot dogs.  And the best part of all is spending a few minutes with the Brummers, who really know how to treat their guests.

This place is a favorite for my coworkers and I to venture to when were craving some especially delicious food and a great old school atmosphere. It's exactly what you think of when you imagine a New Jersey/New York Jewish deli- and I mean that in the best way possible. Family owned and has been around since "before you were born." The sandwiches are out of this world and I plan to make my way through the entire menu. Can't wait to come back again and try the desserts!

Oh man! The world's best pastrami sandwich is found here. A bold statement fully substantiated by the first bite into the "#5." A true old school deli, Hobby's owners and brothers stopped by my girlfriend and my lunch table. For 15 min on a late December Saturday afternoon, Mike introduced us not to just the delicious food chooses we had made but with a fresh baked chocochip cookie, gave us a brief history of this Newark institution and the family that works 13 hours a day, 7 days a week to bring this great food to the downtown area. But let's get back to the important part, the food. The free assortment of pickled vegetables started off our meal. The green tomatoes were my favorite. Chicken noodle matzah ball soup set my girlfriends place, next to her knish served with sour cream. So good! I had the pastrami. Firstly all it's breads are freshly baked on site giving a refreshing crispness my sandwich. A fresh creamy layer of cole slaw coated in between the sandwiches recently made rye bread and the stuffed folds of sliced meat. Each piece of the meal was simple but delectable, honest and authentic to Jewish delis. Although kinda pricey for the area, this place is a gem for those who love a good sandwich or an even better story. I look forward to going back to Hobby's very soon.

We went in to have lattes, which came in tiny mugs for $4!  The place was quiet and the waitress and owner hovered around uncomfortably, the owner even fixed a blind right over my head!  Although it was empty, we felt pressured to finish our lattes and go, since we weren't eating.  I think they need to loosen up a bit in order to fit into the neighborhood.  It's a nice looking space, the menus seem fine, if pricy, but why not have some reasonably priced coffee (including to-go cups), and pastries available for the local pre-brunch crowd? It's all a bit to chi-chi for my taste.  Won't be going back.

This is a rare Gem in Brooklyn!!! It's becoming one of my favorite places to go for fabulous food, wine & good service.  I was there w a girl friend of mine, this Monday, it was a quiet night--which was perfect for my friend & I to have a great conversation.   Foie gras & bone marrow were great (had it the previous time i was here) the traditional French Cassoulet w Duck confit was amazing, the pork belly was yummy, but my favorite was the squid ink pasta! The food was absolutely & fabulously delicious!  Wine was great, and the staff (so courteous & genuinely interesting guys, we had such great conversations bc it was a slower/ more relaxing night!) I highly recommend this restaurant for a great overall experience.   Very Authentic French cuisine, without the pretentious vibe, which made the dining experience even better! Ambiance & music was also very nice --for guys who are looking to pamper an awesome girl, great place to take your date! Though I have to say, I am feeling a little selfish (and want to keep it a secret) bc I don't want this place to become too crowded & snobbish....so conflicted! I have taken away one of the stars bc the service has gone down a bit (I think he was the owner of the restaurant, he was a bit rough/ rude, I thought)   The owner is def NOT as nice as Arran, one of the night servers (he also sometimes works at the bar.)

Stopped in since it's close to where I was staying and empty. Good choice. Breakfast took a bit to arrive but was worth it. Nice, understated decor. Coffee is great here as well. Definitely worth a look.

Classical French Bistro Cuisine presented in a modern, refined yet casual atmosphere. Foie Gras, soupe de poisson, steak frites, escargot, tarte tatin ... These are just a few of the menu offerings we enjoyed on a recent visit. The soup by itself was lacking salt, which allowed the rouille to shine. The palate which relies on salt for flavor sometimes overlooks more subtle tastes. I noticed an herbaceous undertone that was lovely.  Adding a dollop of the pungent garlicky, saffron aioli was the flavorful enhancement the soup needed. It was served on the side with Gruyere and crostini. We tried not to finish it all so we could enjoy some with our frites! The steaks were deliciously prepared, Presented with a your choice of peppercorn or shallot sauce. The fries were crisp and hot. The duck confit was served with lentils that reminded me of the ones my French mother-in-law cooks.  The duck was maybe a bit overly salted but this is a hazard of this type of preparation. The atmosphere was lovely. Dark wood banquets and bistro chairs, accented by candlelight. The slow Monday we dined, there were only a few other guests. The waiter/co-owner was friendly and accommodating. We were put-off by the incongruous rock music that was playing and requested French music, instead. All in all a lovely evening. I would return and recommend to my discerning foodies alike.

I came here on a cold night and was happily comforted by the cozy dining room and delicious food. My buddies and I did the all you can eat+salad/dessert. We ended up trying every single flammie, in addition to the potato and beet salads and the calvados sucree. The gratinee, salmon, and biquette are really special. I'd avoid the provencale because it lacks the flavor that the others have. I've never had Alsatian food before this, but it was a great introduction.  I really want to come back and try their brunch! The service is a bit slow, but it's alright. I kinda got the feeling the waiters were judging my friends and me for eating so gosh darn much, but hey, it's all you can ate and that's exactly what we did. Totally worth it.

I have been looking for a place that makes original tarte flambee, like the ones I ate in Strasbourg years ago. I am glad to say I have found the place and it's 5 minutes away.The tarte are amazing!!! I highly recommend the place, unless you don't like creme fraiche and lardons, but then why are you looking at a restaurant called Tarte Flambee? Reserve ahead, because the seating is limited.

Very cute little restaurant that we found on yelp by accident after looking up Cafe DAlsace (which by the way recently has become very average)...   La Tarte Flambee has only a few tables, its a small but very cozy place.  My husband is familiar with Alsace food and he said it was very authentic and well prepared.  If you enjoy cheese, definitely check them out.  The brunch eggs benedict served over potato pancake with gruyere cheese, very refined hollandaise sause and nice little side salad are a perfect brunch guilty pleasure.  My husband tried the house specialty - tarte flambee and it was also delicious.  Highly recommend....

As the name implies, this little spot focuses on one type of dish and executes it well. You'll find about a dozen variations on the tarte flambee, including a mushroom version, which for me was the obvious choice. The lunch special is a good deal (any tarte plus small salad and a drink).

A true cultural French Alsace experience :D aka the people are really French and speak French (our waiter corrected my bad French).  My bf lives around the corner and I never knew this existed until we saw it for 50% off on ScoutMob- thanks ScoutMob!   Firstly, we came on a Friday around 11am and it was actually pretty busy - the place isn't big; only a few tables so be sure to come early.  I wouldn't come with a group larger than 4-- there was a huge family that came toward the end, and they basically took over the restaurant.  There seems to be only 2 waiters- but both are so attentive, and explain the "Flammy's" in quite detail.  I can't spell the entire spelling - something like Flambeuke. Basically, that's all you get here. It's a really thin crust pizza-like flatbread (THINK REALLY THIN CRUST) with yummy toppings atop.  Try their tradicionalle BIquette, which was thick cut bacon, goat cheese (it wasn't as strongly flavored as others I've had), raw-ish onions, creme friache, with a drizzle of honey.  REALLY REALLY GOOD.  Creamy and salty, with a hint of sweet.  You can get the tradiconelle (the base is the bacon, onion, creme friache) We also tried the Jardin, which is a choice of 3 of veggies- we got leeks, mushroom, and carmelized onions with a choice of French Munster cheese.  Apparently this is a strong Munster- I didn't taste it that much. It was good, but the Biquette was more flavorful. Note the ScoutMob deal is not good for the restaurant's two deals: the lunch special, which is a a Flammy, salad and soda- for some $13. A Flammy itself is $11-13. Definitely filling.  The waiters were very nice about taking our deal, and refilled our coffees. Coffee wasn't anything special, but it came in cute cups. I'd definitely try this again for a different kind of brunch.

First time I tried them I fell in love with their cuisine, worthy of a review! Check them out! you will not leave unhappy nor unsatisfied! The restaurant is cozy and has a nice warm feeling to it, the service is very welcoming and helpful as well, great for dates! :)

I like their food, I LOVE their online ordering option. For over a year I ordered lunch from them once  a week to be delivered, and things went marvelously, tasty food, on-time...ish delivery I've  An hour after my food was due I called to find out what was up, only to be lied to by an employee ("it should be there any minute" when in actuality they had not noticed my order come in so it was not even in process) It took an additional twenty minutes for my food to arrive. I sent their website an email detailing my complaint and received a hasty apology. Maybe I'm just hard to please but that was inadequate.  Were I in their shoes and there was this kind of blatant error, I would have offered something - any little boon. 10% off your next order (that would probably end up being around $2), free 20-ounce beverage on your next order, etc etc. There are any number of very inexpensive options to regain good-will with your customers. On the plus side, my budget's looking a lot better now that I don't order
I love this French Restaurant!

Really nice place. One of our faves in the neighborhood. The long waits at the weekend are a testament to how good it is. The cappuccinos are delicious and so are the croque monsieurs. Service is always quick and efficient.

Excellent eggs benedict! I would give this place 5 stars, however, the service was extremely slow..We waited literally 30+ minutes for our food to come out. The funny thing is that they did not inform us why we had to wait so long..we had to call them over and ask ourselves! The reason why we had to wait so long is because they were making more hollandaise sauce for the eggs benedict. It would've been great if they had told us beforehand... In my opinion, I believe that if customers are dissatisfied, restaurants should give at least some service..Despite the mediocre service I will return for the eggs benedict.

We walked in and there was a super friendly woman who greeted and sat us. The food was great and exactly what you would want and expect from a traditionally French menu and cafe. The cappuccino was so good and the mocha was excellent too.

Yuck yuck yuck.  I get that this place has been around forever, and we heard that they have great pizza, so we decided to try it this afternoon.  We definitely will NOT be going back. The decor was pretty terrible, but I can get past that.  Generally if the food is phenomenal, I don't care what the place looks like.  BUT, the food was garbage, so let's say a little about the interior.  Think old sticky tiles on the floor, old wood panelling, old formica bar with a staff that's probably just as old as the restaurant.  Many of the patrons were also elderly and we could tell they were lifers.  We were told the pizza was great and to also order the "toasties": meatballs.  So we did. The menu also had something called the "Zone" on it: a bunch of cured meats, provolone cheese, wrapped in pizza dough and topped with mozz.  The waitress told us it would take about 30 minutes, so we asked for the meatballs first, then the pizza, then the zone last.  We ordered our drinks and waited. I got my soda, which came without ice and in a very dirty, sticky glass.  Of course I didn't realize this until I drank about half of it.  Looking at it in the light almost made me sick.  Our meatballs came with a size of mustard.  Not what I'm used to but okay.  They didn't taste bad, but also weren't great.  I finally got a glass of water, but for some reason didn't get a straw.  Oh well. The pie came and it looked good, it was piping hot and slightly burned around the edges.  I took a bite and was totally disappointed.  The sauce was kind of salty and the cheese was falling off because there was way too much sauce.  One slice and I was pretty sure I didn't want more.  I like my sauce on the sweet side as most pizza sauce usually is.  This tasted like your standard marinara, nothing special. After that, the "zone" finally came, and that looked good.  One slice and again it was like licking a salt bar or something.  No sauce came with it, and it made sense that it was salty because it was all a bunch of cured meats, but a sweeter sauce to dip it in would've made a huge difference.  After all of that, we were so ready to go. Three beers, one soda, one small pie, and one "zone" and it was over $40.  I hate spending money on crappy food.  I would've been way more satisfied had we gone to Anthony Franco's in Parsippany and it would've been much cheaper. Unless you're a die hard RT fan that's been going there for years, don't waste your time.  The place was jam packed and there was a line of people waiting, and I really don't get why.  We were polite when we asked for our left overs to take home.  They're going in the garbage.

I love the small sausage pie and the sandwiches are very big & delicious. You can't beat the prices and the italian food is home made and enough for two people to share. They have very loyal customers and it gets crowded so prepare to wait for a table. They have a very active bar & you can eat there. My favorite dish is the sausage italian style with potatoes, onions & peppers.
Trios is amazing! Their delivery time was quick and have always been pleased with their customer service. Great job!

The pizza at this place is just absolutely amazing, granted I've only had one or two particular varieties there but hey why mess with a good thing. It is definitely the best pizza I have had in Philadelphia by far. The only negative I can give thus far is that I have seen their newly released menu, and they have raised their prices quite high. I might still spring for it from time to time, but it won't be a regular thing with prices as high as they have now changed to. If you want to split a pie with friends though, this is a great joint to do it at.

We weren't as impressed by Rybread as everyone else. It was packed when we walked in, but the line to order moved fairly quickly. I ordered the Denver (chicken salad) and my bf ordered the San Diego or San Francisco (whichever one has grilled portabellos and eggplant. They don't offer cups of tap water - you have to buy bottles. There's no good place to stand and wait for your food...it is CRAMPED and you are constantly being plowed into. We also noticed that none of the workers were wearing gloves, which REALLY grossed us out (and I'm pretty sure that's against regulations). My bf's sandwich was really, really tiny for the price. Mine was good, I really liked the multigrain bread and the fact that it was light on the mayo. We sat outside and apparently there was an anarchists meeting next to us. It was so awkward...obviously not the restaurant's fault, but we just wanted to eat and scoot as quickly as possible. Overall, it was OK. I don't know if we would go back, particularly because of the lack of gloves (again, ew) and how small the veggie sandwich was for $6.75.

This place is definitely my go to coffee spot in Fairmount.  They have good coffee and awesome sandwiches!!! I usually frequent there for breakfast on the weekends.  The bagels are always so fresh....they remind me of great NY bagels.   My only complaint is that at times there is a wait.  I now usually call ahead so it's ready when I get there.  I would definitely recommend Rybread over Smugshots any day!

only been here for lunch. their ramen special is one of the best deals i've come across in this neighborhood! $17 gets you a wedge salad, a bowl of sushi rice with your choice of topping (scallion, salmon roe, or 2 types of pork), and then a steaming bowl of ramen!! the wasabi broth got my attention first, but it wasn't spicy at ALL . the shiso leaf came across stronger than the wasabi flavor for me! actually, it tasted far too 'healthy' and herbal to satisfy my cravings, but if you're looking for something a little different and lighter than your typical ramen, it's worth a try. also tasted my friends' broths: tonkatsu was rich and tasty, chicken paitan was remarkably similar to totto! all of them had nice firm noodles. on another visit i had the spicy miso, which is definitely my favorite out them all! it had the velvety texture of the tonkatsu broth with the addition of a kick of spice. the extra bowl of rice + topping is nice if you're still hungry.. or like me, someone who just can't leave any food behind. the pork jowl was super fatty and tender -- and they don't skimp on the portions! i think i've been spoiled by the lunch prices so i'm not sure i'll ever order anything else or stop by for dinner... but next time i go, it'll be the seafood ramen for me... and maybe those short rib buns.

great ramen place. sake for $10 a bottle which is great deal the appetizer buns were delicious also. the only knock on this place is that yelp gives u a free asahi if u log in but then u cant use it except for like mon - wed before 7pm. restaurant has nice atmosphere, 2 thumbs up

Claim to Fame is their Ramen, but as with any noodle place, it's the "secret sauce" (or broth in this case) that makes or breaks an establishment. The new owner/chef described how much care and effort it takes to formulate the elixir. In fact, it's stoutly written on their walls..."Up to 120 lbs of pork bones are boiled in a 24" pot at the highest heat for about 24 hours." If  you're on an empty stomach after a night of partying or feeling under the weather, a bowl of hot, spicy Ramen is what Doctors would prescribe. Most of Zutto's reviews are about their Ramen (guilty as charged) but Zutto's sushi shouldn't be remiss. A must to sample is their wild Norwegian salmon with marbling of fat that melts in your mouth! Single? Have a seat at their large communal table and share some. ;)

Zutto offers mediocre sushi, but delicious everything else!  I would return here for the ramen, small plates, and sides, but not the sushi.  If I want good sushi, I go to Nobu Next Door.  The small plates we ordered were outstanding!  I had the "portabella steamed buns" (melted in my mouth), "shishito peppers", "silken tofu" (delicious), "wedge salad" (excellent toasted sesame dressing), and the "Gulf of Mexico" roll (so-so).  I loved the casual, Japanese bar atmosphere and friendly service!  I cannot wait to return for the "portabella steamed buns", yum!!!
Great food, good atmosphere, great service

was debating whether this place deserves 3 or 4 stars.  had the short rib steamed buns which were very good and the chicken paitan ramen which was just decent.  totto ramen beats this place hands down for ramen.  decided on 3 stars because value for your money is only so so.

I think this is going to be my new hot spot!  Good for groups and great vibe & service.  They were very accommodating with the reservation and adding a seat or two last minute.  The food is spot on with the whole Jap Am theme.  By no means this place is fine dining but love the laid back tribeca vibe. If you must have one thing here get the Chuuka Manjuu!!!  I had the Pork Belly and Short Ribs but I think all of them will live up to the hype.  So juicy!  Comes 2 per serving so order accordingly.  Other highlights of the meal Manila Clams Garlic, Spicy Miso, Foie Gras! (we ordered a 2nd since it was that good), Tribeca Spicy Tuna Roll and the Coffee Semifreddo & zeppole donuts!!!  All share-able.  Can order pitchers of beer, sake, etc.   My only little peeve was that they should have served the sushi platter in the beginning of the meal.  Sushi should be treated delicately, by the time we got it towards the end of the meal, we were full of meat, soup, salt, spices, etc. I struggle with writing reviews for places I like since it'll be harder for me to get reservations in the future!  :(

Seeing all of the glowing reviews written for this establishment, my expectations were quite high for this place. Unfortunately, my personal experience here, along with that of roughly half of our party of six, did not reflect the glowing reviews. We shared the short rib, kobe beef, and pork belly steamed buns. Surprisingly, we found that the pork belly was the tastiest amongst the three. Both the short rib and kobe beef had one glaring shortcoming, namely, overcooked, well-done, and dry meat. At $10-12 for two of what are essentially sliders with a different sort of bread, I would have expected the meat to be cooked correctly. Even cooking them medium-well would have been acceptable. Next, the ramen. One of my friends and I both ordered the Wasabi Shoyu Ramen, which the menu specifically marked with an asterisk and an explicit note indicating that it was spicy. We both found our broths to be bland and absolutely not spicy. I had to stir the contents of my dish quite a bit before I was able to detect a hint of wasabi spice towards the end of my meal. In other words, the wasabi seemed to have sunken to the bottom of the bowl. My friend, on the other hand, was not able to detect any spice at all, even after stirring, indicating that wasabi was likely not even present. I would have expected the wasabi to be blended in with the broth prior to serving. But even ignoring that faux pas, it still does not account for why my friend did not have any hint of spice at all. Consistency is obviously not this establishment's forte. If this place did not charge $15-20 for a bowl of ramen, I would probably not be as picky. I would also not be as picky if this establishment were the only one of is kind. However, given that this establishment is located in Manhattan, I would highly recommend that you take the trip to Totto Ramen or Ipuddo instead.

clued into this lunch spot but jacquelyn s.  it really is a deal for $17.  the wedge salad is larger than the side salads you get at most japanese spots.  the rice with choice of topping, i got salmon roe.  it's a nice to have a little in between spoonfuls of ramen goodness.  i haven't admitted in the past that i'm not a huge ramen gal.  i've done the ippudo, and i must say zutto overtakes the more popular outfit.  first off, no lines at lunch and i would say better broth.  i had the hakata classic.  had it with chopped pork and added pork belly for good measure.  needless to say i was stuffed at the end of the meal.  i'll be back to try the sashimi lunch prix fixe.

I had the Hakata Classic Ramen. The ramen serving a little small compared to conventional Japanese servings.  Broth was good, chashu pork a little on the sparse side but soft and well-cooked. The nigirizushi (hand-rolled sushi, not the rolls) was small and overpriced.  The sushi bar was not the freshest quality and the serving sizes, again, smaller than conventional japanese standards. I've spent many many months in Japan and have come to recognize good ramen and good sushi (which is soooo common over there !) Overall, great ramen but would increase the serving sizes by 1/3 to justify the prices charged.    The nigirizushi price should be about $6 for 2pc instead of the $9-10.

Ordered the shishito peppers, which were alright although only 1/4 of them were actually spicy. Was very surprised by the price since it was only listed as $$. Service was very attentive though (although bordering on hovering) and everyone was very pleasant. The fish chips and shrimp were quite good, but go ahead and skip the peppers.

This place opened to the public today and so far, I am impressed. The main bar has a good selection of drinks that I find impressive and delicious. The service at the bar was great and there's seating with a view of the train station and SOPAC. The semi-outdoor seating makes drinking a beer feel worth it. While at the seating area, the waitress came by and served me and my sister bread and the bread was warm. I ended up having an appetizer of artichoke dip and it was delicious. Cooked right and better than most artichoke dip I had. The waitress was new, like the entire staff, but she was attentive and served our food quickly, even with a packed house. Afterwards I ended up going downstairs to a  pub that's part of the restaurant called The Snug and it's small but cozy. There's not that much seating, but they have darts. Overall, I would come back here again. I like the vibe and the service.
A+ in both service and food. The nachos were AWESOME and the drinks were made with fresh squeezed juice! I recommended this as a must visit if in south orange

Very disappointed.  Ate here on opening day.  Entree prices (high $20s/low $30s) were about $5 too high for uninventive ingredients, nonexistent presentation, and bad descriptions on menu.  Amp up the originality of the food and prepare it well at that price point.  Caesar salad had from a mix seeming dressing with cherry tomatoes as garnish (odd), and the tomatoes should have been tossed out the week before because they were no where near fresh. I'd love to have the caliber of restaurant in South Orange they are striving for.  They are just in much need to rethink the menu and approach if they want to achieve it.  For a place with a liquor license, beer on tap selection was humdrum.  I think they are resting on the major renovation work (which is the only positive thing to note) they have done to create a great space and invest in South Orange.  I'd like to see them succeed so I hope they take this review as strong constructive criticism.  Please work out kinks with food (and beer selection), service (which was inexperienced), and rethink price point or amp up the level of entrees and preparation to warrant that price point.  Hoping to re-review higher in future.

Wings are great and they are very accommodating for allergies. They are working out the logistical kinks as any new restaurant must so they can't be judged on that. I will say there was an issue with them losing my credit card the first time I went there and they handled it so professionally and we're so on top of it I was taken back. I go 3-4 days a week for drinks and food.

Went last night and were seated immediately.  Service is friendly if a little hovering.  3 of us had the modernized Shepherd's Pie with beef short ribs, carrots and mashed potatoes - omg it was delicious.  The sole pasta eater was extremely happy too.  Will definitely go back, once I've saved my pennies as the prices are on the high side for this area.

Went on Wednesday 12/18 with a reservation. The restaurant was very busy, but we were seated within two minutes of walking in the door. The ambiance is excellent - very much a Cuban diner feel. It is relaxed with the staff very formal. We had a group of four and found it very easy to relax and enjoy the atmosphere. The food was absolutely delicious - I had the churrasco and it was extremely flavorful and tender. I found myself taking very small bites because I didn't want it to be over. My table also split a few of the small plates, the octopus was my favorite. Super tender and tasty. The mojitos were equally delicious. We split the tres leches (a chocolate version) and the flan. They were fantastic. The food came out quickly The service was exceptional, even with how busy the restaurant was that evening. Our server was Danitza. She was extremely attentive and very knowledgeable about the food. I will definitely ask to be seated in her section next time I go to Rosa Blanca! Overall - an excellent experience and I will definitely be going back often.

Good food, service needs work. My husband and I sat at the counter for a late breakfast/early lunch. We ordered an empindada to start, my husband ordered the El Capitan (chicken sandwich), and I ordered the eggs with corn cakes and grits. My husband's sandwich came out very quickly, even before the empanada. We waited a few minutes before reminding the waiter, who gave us an extra empanada to apologize for the wait. The cheese empanda was delicious, with a decadent center and perfectly fried shell. We waited about 10 minutes, and my food did not come. The bartender said it was on its way, so I told my husband to start  eating his (now half-cold) meal. My husband finished his meal, and my food still did not arrive. I could not catch the bartender's eye, and ended up waiting another 10 minutes for my food, which a waiter had accidentally brought into the dining room. Everything was delicious. My experience was definitely tainted by the fact that I waited a full 40 minutes for scrambled eggs.
Fantastic pork shoulder It reminds me of Miami so much The charming decor is very cool n down to earth , welcoming. The cocktails are great, can't wait to try lunch here. Very soon

We visited Rosa Blanca on the first Saturday night after they opened. Surprisingly, it did not appear to be completely full and the waiter was helpful with recommendations. The restaurant is spacious and has a cool Cuban atmosphere. They have a great drink selection and their signature cocktails are delicious. I was not overly impressed with the food. The empanadas were OK. On the other hand, the croquetas are the one must have. The food here is probably still better than Cuba Libre and can only get better, but for now I'm giving it 4 stars.

Great place! Went for lunch... Staff were very friendly and knowledgable about the menu... The food was soo delicious it speaks for itself!  With the early opening & extensive breakfast food and drink options, as a nurse, I am definitely going to make this a new after work 7a spot :))

I came in here for lunch with some coworkers the Friday after Christmas. I was surprised at how large the space is - the front of the house is set up very cute like a typical diner with seats at the counter and booths, while the back room has tables for larger parties. We all ordered either the Cubano or the Calle Ocho. I wasn't very impressed by the Cubano but I can't say I've had a ton of Cuban food in my life. I just know I've had  way better Cubanos before. The Calle Ocho was better - but the Chorizo had no spice to it. We had to ask for hot sauce to add some kick to the sandwhiches (it was not already on the table). . Prices seemed reasoable to me. Service was great, everyone was welcoming and cheery. We came in at 11:30am and it was definitely packed by the time we left. I will probably go back because I work nearby, but it's not on my list of places I neeeeeeed to go back to in the near future with friends.

I'm gonna be generous and not give this place 2 stars because it just opened. They don't even have a liquor license yet. But as of right now as far as Asian buffets go, this place doesn't have enough food selections. It has the typical concept of sushi, hibachi and Chinese main dishes.  The "piece de resistance" I would say for this place would be their dim sum but alas they only had a small selection...tripe, pink colored chicken feet that needed to be cooked an extra 20 minutes maybe, shumai, egg rolls, noodle roll with shrimp, and pork bun. The flavors weren't a stand out either....just OK. It doesn't have what other Asian buffets have which is a western selection for those that are not really a fan of Asian food. What I didn't like was that I KNOW they were trying to be more classy by putting the main hot dishes in serving plates, but since it wasn't in a typical buffet container like a chafing dish, most of the dishes got cold right away. There needs to be hot water underneath the food to keep it tasting good. Some of those dishes do not taste good cold or in room temperature. I also didn't like that some dishes had preservatives. I wanted to try the hibachi station but the beef had the pink coloring preservative. Why do you need to add that in? I'm not gonna eat it they only have pink colored meat in Chinese take out. Also the chicken feet was pink from the preservatives. Again not appealing. Putting nitrites or nitrates giving food a pink color to make it seem attractive isn't doing the trick. Plus it can lead to a lot of allergic reactions such as urticaria, hives, asthma etc... So as of now as all buffets go this place isn't a stand out for me..and I know my buffets. This place is just OK...so I'm giving it just an OK rating of 3. Improvements can still be made since it just opened recently.

Drove pass it a few times and decided to go in for a try when we were craving sushi. When we walked in, it looked newly renovated from the previous Chinese restaurant it used to be. It was a Saturday night so it was pretty busy and fresh food was continuously being added to the buffet.  The sushi and rolls were good. Not exceptional, but for a buffet it was good. The wide selection of sushi and rolls would please the sushi rookies to the connoisseurs. They even had vegetarian sushi as well. However, there was not enough sashimi. They served 1 piece on one single dish so you'll have to take many dishes with you to satisfy your appetite, but this does prevent those from taking way too much and not being able to finish it. It was just annoying to keep asking "is there more sashimi left?" every time we went up the buffet. The hot dishes were OK, the food did get cold quickly because there was no heating unit to keep it warm; they serve food on pretty white dishes, not the typical buffet style stainless steel pans. The selection included but not limited to pan fried noodles, fish, ribs, dumplings, egg rolls, fried rice, and calms. Dim sum was offered although the selection was small. Traditional Chinese dessert was available as well as different types of soup. A fruit bar was also available with honeydew, watermelon, oranges and cantaloupe. Directly across from the fruit bar is the dessert bar with jello, cookies, cakes, pudding and ice cream (the cookies n cream ice cream was surprisingly very good!) Overall, the meal filled my belly with pretty decent food for a relatively good price. I over looked service and decor because I find buffets to have same style decor and service all around. I left happy and satisfied, what else to look for at an all you can eat sushi/Asian buffet?

This place is nothing to write home about. PROS -Decor is nice. -Price is competitive, but for the same price you could go elsewhere. -Offers hibachi -Clean CONS -Majority of the food isn't labeled. How can you eat something that you cannot identify? And why would they label some things but not others? -Some of the food was not fresh. -No liquor for sale but plenty of bottles behind the counter? I assume they are working on the license? -Minimal variety Probably won't be back. I give it 2 stars because it's fairly new and has time to improve. Me personally...I will drive a few extra miles for better selection.

Very impressed new modern look very reasonable prices food was very good and buffet area was kept clean . Hibachi was a good surprise with all meats and shrimp available bring your appetite and your booze if you want something with dinner . Will defiantly be returning !

Here's the thing: I like Abyssinian, I really do. The food is tasty, although I have very few Ethiopian restaurants to compare it to. Certainly none in the Hartford area. The doro wat is a lovely, wonderfully spiced dish, and the injera bread is something dreams are made of. I've had some excellent experiences but tonight was not one of them. That said, I'll probably never book a reservation for a large party here again. And by large party I only mean 14 people - certainly not unmanageable. Although I called in a reservation days ago, the server only provided a table for 8 people - meaning others had to squeeze in along the way as though they were unexpected guests. Along with the cramped seating, our orders were not taken - instead we were asked to write them down. I think we finally ordered 45 minutes after being seated. My dish was quite delicious - I'll give you that. I just don't know what happened. I've always received prompt, courteous service without a reservation. Tonight's chaotic experience makes me wish I brought my group somewhere else. The restaurant seemed severely understaffed - just one server and one cook. I really want Abyssinian to do well here but this level of service just won't cut it. I live in the neighborhood, I'm sure I'll be back at some point. Just next time, I'll be with a +1 at most.

If you see my reviews of City Steam Brewery or Vito's by the Park, you know that bad service can be a dealbreaker for me. But in those cases, they were medium-to-large restaurants with plenty of servers and only a handful of tables. In those cases, each server was responsible for one or fewer tables and still managed to screw it up. So, while the service was not amazing at Abyssinian when I went for a Yelp event, I feel more compassionate because there was exactly one server on staff. And what nobody has mentioned yet was that we were not the only diners in the place. When I have walked by this restaurant, it usually has only one or two small parties dining mid-week. In addition to our group of 14, there were five or six other parties there at any given time. The woman who was our server was doing the best she could. I never saw her dillydallying, ducking out to play on her phone, heading outside for a smoke. She was constantly in motion. While the table situation (having the right number of seats when a reservation was made) should have been better, that is really the only fault I can find. GIrlfriend was doing the best she could. And I'm just going to take a shot in the dark here, but I'm guessing she had us write down the number of our orders because of a language barrier. Given how often native English speakers mess up my order elsewhere, I can't complain about giving the exact order. I mean, we don't complain when we are asked to do this while ordering sushi, now, do we? I had the vegetarian combo and split it with my date, as we have done there in the past. The quality was on par with what we have had when dining as a mere couple. Some of the vegetables were spicy, some were mild -- as noted on the menu. The cold beets balanced the heat of lentils. We were given a plate of extra teff. We felt that this combo platter was perfectly portioned for two people to share. Other patrons at the time included parties with babies. I think there were three in the small dining room. The restaurant allows this and provides booster chairs, etc. These families were not shunned, as happens in some snooty restaurants Parking is easy with numerous side streets to park upon. I don't find myself in the West End often, but I plan to return here.
Comon people are they paying you to leave reviews . The worst in bloomfield .. All the food is bland and for a place that is slow it's a long wait.....

Nice decor, average food, very good service. My first visit here was for lunch, which was good, but I never wrote a review. My 2nd time was for dinner with a large group. In summary, the food was just average, but I'd go back and probably order more of the small plates next time. Bar: full bar with a good selection of everything. I only had wine, but my friend was very happy with his vodka martini and extra olives (and he loves his martinis) Food: the small plates were better than the dinner. Eggplant tower and polenta fries are good. The antipasto appetizer didn't have as much meat as I would have liked. The vodka rigatoni dinner was good, but too salty for me. That might have been because of all the prosciutto they put in the dish. Normally, I say the more prosciutto, the better. But I think here, it made the dish too salty. I could only eat half at the time; I took the rest home. My husband had the linguini with clam sauce and liked it, but we've had better at authentic Italian restaurants. Dessert: Nice selection of desserts, particularly the dessert drinks. My husband loved the espresso martini. I had a tiramisu, which had a lovely presentation in a martini glass, but it was mostly whipped cream. I could have used more lady fingers and more flavor overall. Service: very good. We had an early dinner reservation, and we were seated right away (actually a little early). The wait staff was very polite and very timely with everything. Decor: very warm and inviting, especially for the holidays. We were tucked away next to a closed off fireplace with a decorated mantle, and floor-to-ceiling windows with a view of a lighted trees. The bar area has nice leather couches and a few TVs.

We went there on New Years Eve, 2013 into 2014. The food took a very long time to arrive. We were there for about two hours total. The table next to us appeared to be favoured by our server. The arrived about a quarter of an hour after us, and had their food a quarter of an hour before us! The food I had, the Sizzling Italian Seasoned Chicken, came without any sizzle at all. In fact, it was cold, burnt, and over-seasoned.  I ended up ordering another dish! Rigatoni alla vodka was my choice. It was drenched in oil and I had no desire to eat it. The place has a very limited menu as well. They had specials that night, but I was refused a normal dinner menu that night. Very unhappy with the food and service, and I have no desire to return there. May have just been a bad night, but I was not happy at all. Prices were ridiculous as well. Over $200 for four people.

Our party of four arrived on time for our 7:00 reservation (Saturday). I was disappointed when we were told it would be "10 minutes".  20 minutes later we were still standing in the bar.  When they did seat us it was in the crowded bar area.  The service was acceptable and the food was pretty good but I don't think I'll be in a hurry to go back. One appetizer, two salads, four main courses, seven drinks + tip =  $230

After years of trolling yelp to steal advice from other people, I finally signed up for an account, just to say how disappointed I am with this place. The lack of good Thai restaurants in Philadelphia is no secret, so when I heard this place was opening 1.5 blocks from my house, I was excited. Lets just say this: even if you're a fan of bland, Americanized Thai food, you'll probably think this place is bland. Even if you explicitly tell them to amp up the spice, it's still bland. I've eaten my fair share of sub-par meals, but this is one of those places that makes you feel like you've been robbed by having to pay for their food.
Bad service,  bland food, and way too loud! Server messed up the order, then lied about it, to top it off we had to ask for check many times. Not coming back, ever.

I have always enjoyed this place until today. I brought in 20 people for a nice dinner and the treatment I got was awful. Waited for over an hour for a table; once we got a table waited for 30 minutes to get menus and get a waiter to pay attention to us. Once we ordered we didn't get our food for over 1 1/2 hours later or drinks which took 45 minutes. I was upset and asked for a manager multiple times. No one ever came!  Finally I went upstairs and met with the owner who basically said," we are so busy if you need to wait 2 hours for your food than you will!" I tried calmly expressing my concerns and the owner and her daughter started to yell and insult me, basically harassing me to leave. I have never been treated in a restaurant like this and I will never go back!! They lost my business and I will tell anyone I know how horrible their service and the bad quality of their overpriced food! It's not worth the money! The food is average the drinks are made with cheap alcohol and the staff is rude and clueless!!

Went for lunch today. Service was impeccable. Staff was friendly, efficient and sandwich was ready in a flash. My friend and I each had the Mensch which was delicious. We also shared an order of crunchy onions which were really good. I recommend this place highly, and would rate Jake's equal to or better than any other sandwich shop in Philly.   Will return for more,  and probably pretty often.

had lunch here yesterday and can still feel my hand-carved pork sandwich nestled in the pit of my belly. this place is good, but whatever you order: only eat half if you have any intention of being productive later in the day. also, try not to wear too much when you go here -- it's hot as balls inside. whoever decided to put milkshakes on the menu was really thinking.

The mensch is a pretty huge and pretty great sandwich that is worth the price! The wasabi ribeye looks like it is probably awesome and I'm going to get that next time. Quick service, plenty of tables,and  good sandwiches can be found at this establishment.  The roll has a great texture and isn't ridiculously tough to the point of absurdity(like some other Philly sandwich places).  The sandwiches are pretty damn large so prepare to take half home for another time.   Bonus points for having sriracha available to tack some kick onto the sandwiches. On the action-movie-parallel-satisfaction scale, this place is Blade Runner.

This is my updated review. We used to love Rizuttos, we would go there for happy hour, dinner, and lunch. However, over the past year or so, it has been on a steady decline... the food isn't nearly as good, the waitstaff not as friendly, bartenders not as personable, and they got rid of the complementary apps at happy hour. Even the bathrooms aren't as well maintained. It's a shame... bring back the Rizuttos from 3 years ago!

My husband and I were celebrating our wedding anniversary. When I mentioned this to Asha, Rizzuto's hostess, she showed us to a very private table near the windows. Asha was so friendly. She checked back with us numerous times during the meal to make sure we were pleased with the service and the food. The service was outstanding. Henry, our waiter, was at our beck and call. He anticipated our needs and was always there to check back with us. Leigh Ann, one of the waitresses, overheard me wonder aloud what appetizer to get. She suggested the tortellini. It was so delicious--succulent and spicy.  Ashley, another of the waitresses, overheard my dilemna about what to order for the main course. She recommended the sweet potato pasta. It was FABULOUS!  I usually leave food on my plate but I ate every bit of that pasta! Both waitresses were friendly and they seemed to smile all the time. John, the manager, stopped by our table several times to make sure all was well. He explained how my main entree was also his favorite. He was charming. Tyler also served us water. He has a wide, easy smile and made sure we had everything we needed. When we left,  Gianna escorted us to the door. What a memorable meal. It was outstanding and the service could not have been better. I highly recommend Rizzuto's in Blue Back Square.
Love the 3 for $20 deal, cheese, meat, veggies...can't beat that. Nice glass of wine for the lady, Peroni for myself. The s'more desert was amazing. Always a great meal at Rizzuto's.

worst pizza ever. I have been to both the west hartford location and the danbury location - the pizza crust was PAPER thin, burnt, and they litterally sprnkled a tablespoon of diced tomatoes on it and called it a margarita, you couldnt even tell if there was cheese on it or if it was just burnt - I will never go here for food again because when I tried to send it back they said that's "how their pizza is"

Pure Fare = actual whole foods prepared with nutrition and deliciousness in mind. All the items on the menu are healthy and won't break the calorie bank. The kale soup I had yesterday was creamy - without cream - and so satisfying that I was shocked to learn that it had 73 calories for what I think was a 12oz portion. 73. Their soups, sandwiches and salads have nutritious ingredients that are hard to find in prepared/takeout foods in Philly like quinoa, wheatberry and tempeh, to name just a few. The coffee is stellar. It's Blue Bottle from SF and is right up there with La Colombe and Illy.   This place has an earthy, casual vibe (albeit with iPads mounted on the wall for you to log into your account and check your Pure Fare nutrition info online, if that's your bag). The seating is limited with a communal bench table and some lovely standing areas along the windows, so it's a place for a quick bite or takeout versus a leisurely lunch. PF is the first place trying to marry food and technology, with their online database of their foods plus everything else you might consume, so you can track your intake of macro and micro nutrients. I don't know if that aspect will catch hold, but it's nice to have the ingredients and nutrition  info proudly displayed on each of their selections. I'm beyond happy that PF has finally opened and didn't disappoint!
I've tried 3 of the salads and they were all awesome.  Good soup too.  And the New Orleans style blue bottle ice coffee takes me back to Cafe du Monde.  Cool vibe in there.

Pure Fare is such an amazing spot. Why? 1) Its healthy 2) Its innovative 3) The food is amazing! In a city where its quite difficult to find healthy food options, PF is a welcome addition. I have been there about 10 times now and I am very impressed with the how consistently amazing the food is. From the soups (roasted cauliflower!!), to the sandwiches (tandoori chicken!) to the salads (chopped kale!), PF literally has great tasting, healthy options for anyone's palate. PF has proven that with healthy food, one does not have to give up taste. Compared to Cosi, Au Bon Pain (which are both revolting), PF wins hands down. My friends said it was a bit pricey, but after having been to Cosi , DiBrunos, Au Bon Pain, etc, PF is in line with the competition. Plus, they source everything locally (so nothing is processed, etc) - there is a premium in that alone. Another really cool aspect to the PF concept is the "My Fare" platform. Any customer can opt in for free and receive a PF card or key fob in store. You can create a My Fare profile on the Pure Fare website - this provides you with a "health snapshot", a kind of personal dashboard that allows you to get more informed on your health, set individual goals and track what you eat. @ PF, everything you buy is automatically and seamlessly sent your My Fare page where it is broken for you (you can see all the nutritional analysis / breakdown of all your purchases @ PF). They also have a database of over 50,000 foods from other brands and chains. You can take a look for yourself @ purefare.com, but this where I think PF is really innovating. By combining food and technology, PF is creating a completely new type of experience for people and this is part of the reason why I come back so much - I know exactly what I am putting into my body. I was talking to one of the owner and they said that they will definitely be adding more features and goodies to the site. This place is going to be huge.. Great, healthy food & technology = amazing. Cant wait to go back!

I was excited to see that another restaurant opened in place of Coaches sport's bar.  Upon arriving I was seated and drink orders were taken right away.  Here's where it goes south, appetizer order was placed along with entree, we knew what we wanted and b/c it was lunch time didn't want to waste any time (12:44p).  Well we sat... and then waited... no appetizer's came up, (1:15pm) no waitstaff came to check, until our glasses were empty.  We were told our meal would be right up, so we said fine we will have it to go, and so we waited some more, by this time it's now 1:30.  It wasn't a large order apps were fried pickles and entree, burger and fries, and grilled chicken sandwich.  Now it's 1:35 and waitstaff is bringing up orders of patrons who walked in 40 minutes after we did.  At this point this is the 3rd time wait staff has assured the meal would be up since 1:15 p.m.   Long story short we walked out, I have to say the water was good, but doesn't merit a 1 star.  Sorry I wouldn't go back, i wish I could have rated the food but just couldn't get beyond the poor service.
Great burger, great service. Other than that, pretty standard east village dining.

Jeremy, what the heck happened to your burgers, man? I first went to Brindle Room about a year and a half ago. I was hungry and in the E. Village. Exhausted from a day out in the sun, I was famished and ordered a burger. OMFG, kapow! BEST DAMN BURGER IN THE GALAXY!! I was astonished at how good it was. I took turns eating a bite and then staring at the burger because I couldn't believe how good it was. I was fairly certain that this was the type of burger that Ron Burgundy would eat if he were in the E. Village. The char was perfect. The patty was crisp in the right places and had punches of sea salt at the perfect time. It was a potent one-two combination and it floored me. The owner and head chef, Jeremy even came out to ask how it was. When I gushed about his burger, he excitedly yelled to the kitchen that I liked the burger. I decided to make Brindle Room my burger place and I visited often. (Fast forward to a year later) Each subsequent visit to Brindle Room has been heart-breaking. What's happened here is what happens too often when a restaurant gets too popular for one item. The demand on the small kitchen shows in the quality of the burger. Each visit after the first saw a decrease in the quality of the burger. The meat was still juicy, but it was missing the care of years past. In fact, Jeremy doesn't seem to be around most of the time. He used to be a staple in the kitchen. Not anymore. The burger has lost all of its char. There is hardly any salt and the burger lacks flavor. It sucks that this happened to such a great food item. Can't we just go back to before NY Times called your burger the best in the City? I liked it when the food was prepared with care. Brindle Room burger, when you're back to the burger I first met, maybe we can try to make this work. Until then, I won't be seeing you any longer. I can only be disappointed so many times. Farewell, sweet deckled prince. Farewell.

I came in here on a hunt - for a delicious brew for myself as well as a gift for some beer lovin' buddies of mine from Denver. I was able to do both in one trip and for a fairly reasonable price. I won't say what I got - gifts being part of the whole thing and all. I can tell you, they were kind of special, very delicious, and not your run of the mill. I could have spent HOURS in there (I did spend an hour actually) browsing and tempting myself with all kinds of goodies. If you aren't a beer person they also have a pretty decent selection of ciders and sour beers as well. If you are looking for a 6 pack they had (on a Monday) 10% off a mixed 6-pack and 20% off of a regular 6-pack.   II'll be back... often.

I didn't think I liked sandwiches....but we all know that that's just not possible. Everyone loves sandwiches. And if you love sandwiches, you'll love The Corner Foodery. The first thing to catch your ear about this Rittenhouse gem is its unparalleled bottled beer selection to carry! We all know good beer carry-outs are a rare bird in uber-liquor-strict PA. But Corner Foodery has a bottle selection that would make any beer snob blush. The local and internationally stocked coolers that guide you from the entrance to the back order counter seem like the stairway to Heaven....and they might as well be. Despite their surprisingly spacious sitting area (the place is at least triple what it appears from the street), I've only had their office catering. These guys NEVER disappoint. Their ingredients are top-notch and their artisan sandwiches would rival any bready bite in the city. My faves are definitely the meatball grinder, the Milstein, and the porchetta, thought you really just can't go wrong with any of their sandwiches. This, THIS is what Philly should be known for--Gourmet, two-handed, chewy-rolled goodness. So put down your soggy cheesesteak and had over to Corner Foodery for a real sandwich (don't forget the long hots). The only problem you might have there is deciding whether you're more impressed by the craft beer or the craft food. I still can't decide...

Our group of six ducked into The Corner Foodery for some pre-gaming action before the Flyers game on Saturday. The set up is half bottle shop, half sit-down eatery. You can pick out bottles to drink there and just pay as you go and enjoy the seating. There are still and bubbly water taps and several TVs scattered around. I was surprised at the ample amount of seating and even more surprised at the lack of people. I think this place is still under the radar, but I can't imagine that it will be for very long. It's not often you can go to a restaurant and drink a beer at the bottle price.   The menu is a mix of sandwiches, salads and snacks that sounds delicious. I'm eager to get back for lunch or dinner sometime soon.

I brought my family in for dinner tonite and we all loved it!  The food was excellent and the place was really comfy.  My wife and I loved all the cool stuff that was hanging on the walls and the beer selection was great.  My kids really liked the pizza which was great because they are very picky about what they eat.  I mean there were no left overs.  I also got to meet the brothers who owned the place who were very funny and friendly.  I recommend every one to try this place out!
I've really enjoyed the pizzas we've had from here.  The crust has a great flavor, and has always been perfectly cooked.  The service has always been very friendly and helpful.  Easy parking.

The food is GREAT, real authentic Taiwanese food. I love their noodles, especially wide noodle. Beef noodle soup (clear broth), noodle with ground pork 7 beans paste sauce, and Chinese style fried chicken noodle/rice are good. They also have pan fried beef bun & pan fried pork dumpling which is hardly to eat in any other restaurants in NJ. I usually order some small dishes, such as seaweed, shredded bean curd, sliced port ears, ....etc to come with my main courses. I also love their deserts, sweet red bean congee & Bubble tea, which I highly recommend.
