From my experience, I went to the restaurant two-three times per week, and I can easily get a place to sit during weekday lunch hours, but in the weekend, I have to wait. The good thing is that I can make the reservation for the party over 6 people. Overall, it is a nice restaurant with great food at decent price.

I was so happy with my first experience one week ago that we decided to go back for dinner again on 8/15/13.  Unfortunately this second experience has made me decided that I will not go back to the restaurant anytime soon.  To make a long story short, no way could a fried chicken leg rice dish took 45 minutes and still not be ready.  The restaurant was way less crowded compare to the first time we were there, and the first time was on a Sunday night!  The waiters were helpless, and we did not even receive an apology.  The wide noodles were so clumpy that I could make better noodles than the chef.  The manager commented after my first review and asked me to contact her if I have any comments.  I emailed her on 8/15 after we came home from dinner....I am still waiting for her response.  Very disgusted!

This is one of the best hand pulled noodle restaurants in the area. I tried Suan La Mien and Zha Jian Mian which were both great. The Suan La Mien is really spicy and a little too salty but is explosive with flavor. I recommend the thin noodles and not the flat ones as only the thin noodles are homemade from when I went when they first opened (It might've changed since then but I'd ask to confirm). The noodles are so chewy and fresh.

There are moments in time when you realize your life has changed for the better. While this may sound like an exaggeration, finding this restaurant is one of those moments in time. When I moved out to the 'burbs, I was a bit sad because I had lived in Hoboken for two years and finally had found a decent, authentic Chinese restaurant. That one happened to be Grand Sichuan in Jersey City (order the tea-smoked duck and the spicy crab if you ever go there). And, the soup dumplings. Then, out to where the air is cleaner and the people are less pushy, I was hopeful. China Chalet was a huge disappointment. Maybe it's authentic, but authentically bad. (Not sure how it gets such high marks on here. Maybe I ordered the wrong stuff.) Having gone to A & J over the weekend, my disappointment in Chinese food options was lifted. This place is solid. I've now tried and enjoyed: * Spicy beef and tendon noodle soup * Clear broth beef noodle soup * Seaweed with bean sprouts and vinegar * Pork chop rice Dishes that could use some improvement: * Sesame pancake with beef inside (don't know the name in English so that's the description) - outside was not crispy. Could have used more beef inside. * Taiwanese-style dumplings - was super excited but then disappointed. Skin is too thick. Inside wasn't juicy enough. Tasted too much like a meatball. Could use more scallion and chive. Wish they also had other types of dumplings. * Ja Jiang Mian - It's a bit too sweet. It's supposed to be somewhat sweet, but the bean paste is also supposed to give it kick. I got it with thin noodles and the noodles were overcooked. BTW, always go with the wide noodle. The thin ones don't seem to hold up as well. Service: Eh. There's been times where we went when it was dead and the serve was questionable. Everyone is nice, it's just they don't seem to be on top of things. Of the 3 times we've been there, 2 times they've forgotten one of our dishes. Not a great batting average. All in all, solid place. Since we found this place, in 4 weeks, we've been there 3 times. Now...if someone just opened a place that offered Taiwanese breakfast: fan tuan, salty soy bean soup, sao bing yuo tiao...I'd be in heaven.

I've been going to bleu sushi since it opened and I must say the quality of fish is great and everyone is so nice and friendly and delivery is always quick. However, with all these positives I only give it 3 stars because now that bleu sushi has been here a while the amount of food you receive for what you pay for is just not equal.   I always order sashimi either as a sashimi appetizer or sashimi chirashi or a la carte.  The sashimi pieces are about half the size as other sushi places but they charge the same price.  This made sense when they had their $1.00 a piece special but now that everything is back to the regular price it's just not worth it.  I will frequent other sushi places that have the same quality but give more for my money like yellowtail sushi or sumo sushi.

I tried this place out because I was looking particularly for sushi and Bleu Sushi had high reviews.  There were two of us and we ordered two of the special rolls and two appetizers to share, yet we left hungry.  We found it ironic that there's a notice on the menu that says "no rip offs" but the sushi rolls are considerably smaller than other sushi places in the area.  The taste was fine and the staff was friendly, though they were running around like chickens with their heads cut off due to a full restaurant.  (You'll need more than two servers for 20+ tables.)  All in all, it wasn't worth the money, but if you're in a pinch, the food is acceptable.

We've been to Bleu a few times now and every time it's been an awesome experience. The staff and owner are extremely friendly and the service is excellent. The fish is the freshest and most tender I've had in the city. The BYOB option really makes the place great and they are happy to provide you with glasses and an opener for any drinks you bring. The ambiance is perfect for any occasion. It's not too dark or too light and the decor/lighting/paint scheme really complements the food and service. This place is great to bring friends. Prices aren't mind-blowing, but they aren't unnecessarily expensive. The fish is high quality and would typically be priced much higher for what you get. The owner has a clear vision of providing guests with high quality sushi at fair prices. Overall, this place is awesome all around and the staff (though some newer than other since the place is relatively new) make your stay much more welcoming.
Extraordinary food and excellent service. Definitely my favorite Japanese restaurant :)
Just had a great dinner with friends after a round of golf. Our Clams were missing a few in our app but the manager quickly handled it with another order and the rest of the food was amazing.

Boyfriend and I just moved to the area and our neighbor highly recommended this place for a special occasion. We chose to go for our anniversary last night. We had a reservation for 7:30PM. It seems to be a challenge to get parking, but that's ok, we found a spot. We went inside to get our table, confirming we had a reservation and we were told it would be a bit longer and we were handed a buzzer. Ok. TWENTY MINUTES go by and we are finally called for our table. "We have a table for you now, but we need it back by 9:20," states the hostess. My jaw dropped! "UMMMMM Ok, I don't think it will take us that long." How rude!?!? After waiting 20 minutes past our reservation time, we get that!?!? Ugh. We were seated in the bar area (how romantic) and we orders some beers and an appetizer. The little necks were good, but I felt over priced. The waiter took our dinner order and then that's pretty much last time we saw him. He didn't serve us anything, other people did. He checked on us once when I was half way through my beer and starting to eat my dinner, we ordered another round. I was done with dinner before another waitress asked us if we needed another round and retrieved the ones we previously ordered at the bar. Yes, the wrack of lamb was the best lamb I have ever had, however, it did not make up for the lousy treatment by the hostess and waiter. Oh yeah, then after we finished dinner it took the waiter 20 minutes to see if we wanted desert... No, it's 9:20 and you need your table back. I don't know where the waiter was all night, but if his neglect was due to waiting too many tables at once, they need to up the staffing. $50 a person for dinner... They can afford more wait staff. We thought about going back for the free BBQ one night, but by the time we got out of there we were done with that place. Never again, despite being five minutes away and the lamb being amazing.

Stage house is a weekly dining option for myself and colleagues.  Whenever we go, we can expect a great meal. The food is always flavorful and if the weather is nice, you must sit on the patio. If you're going for a 3 course meal, I'd recommend the following:     Cocktail:  Jalapeño Margarita     Starter:    Tuna Tartar     Main:       Half Chicken w/mustard sauce     Dessert:   Brownie Sunday The bar is always full, but if you are going for dinner you will always have an enjoyable dining experience. Also, the ambiance is nice for a dinner date, trees wrapped with lights, nice planters, etc. If its nice weather, expect 45-60minute wait.

Does not know how to accommodate guests.  Asked specifically for a corner table for father's birthday, was told yes, then given a table next to other tables.  We have a baby not immunized yet so we needed to be away from other people.  There was a corner table but was for another reservation.  Apparently other patrons were more important than our specific request that was granted over the phone. Go at your own risk. You may not get what you ask for.

Excellent Italian food. Service is wonderful, the servers are very friendly and attentive, and willing to answer questions about the dishes. The desserts are phenomenal, and the pastas are also delicious.

After the terrible experience outlined about, the owner Michele went above and beyond to do the right thing. After likely seeing from the opentable software that we had left after the long wait, he called me to apologize and offered free dinner for 5. That is great customer service and I wish more places would value the experience of the customer in this way. I enjoyed the food (I got pumpkin ravioli app, rack of lamb, and souffle for desert), but likely wouldn't come back as there are plenty of other restaurants in Princeton that I enjoy more. But props to Michele!

Hit or miss. We have been several times, the food has either been absolutely spectacular or below average (even ordering the same dish). Service has always been good and prices are reasonable. Ambience and decor are very appealing. Overall an acceptable choice but nothing special, and better options in the area.

While the food was very tasty, the service left much to be desired. It took forever to have out order taken, we had to ask for water multiple times, and appetizer dishes were left on the table well into the meal.

I came for lunch with my coworkers. Lunch was $10 which is a  pretty good deal. We came around 1:30pm and the waitresses were having lunch so the service wasn't quick. And the salad came without dressing. But pad thai I ordered was pretty good. I will come again.

I liked this place more than the husband, but I have to disagree with a lot of my fellow yelpers on the mac & cheese.  I wasn't feeling it!  Not tasty at all.  My pulled pork sandwich was however, delicious.  Simple and satisfying.  The owner (I'm assuming) was great.  We got a small piece of complementary apple pie and he was asking about what beers we'd like to see on the menu.  I'll definitely be back to try something else on the menu.

Who ever gave this place a 1 should be smacked. I told everyone at the restaurant "THANK YOU! we didn't expect so much juice and flavor" I have never been so happy by a BBQ place. No i'm not from the south, no I'm not a connoisseur, I love to eat, I love flavor. This place made me cry a little. We ordered Mac and Cheese to split and I ended up getting my own lol, String beans, and I had the pulled pork sandwich and my friend had the burnt ends. YES its fatty but it's AMAZING! fat gives it flavor and moister. I appreciate this place for keeping it real and not lean. Corn Bread sucked.... I am a connoisseur of corn bread lol and this corn bread was horrific. Dry, hard as a rock (we even tapped in on the metal trays and it made a clanking sound), but you don't go there for the corn bread, you go for MEAT! Sweet tea i thought could have been sweeter my friend thought it was too sweet, she added water and it was still too sweet, I drank hers and thought it needed to be sweeter so I guess you've got to try it out for youself

I picked up some burgers and sirloin to cook at home.  So far I've cooked the burgers, and they were amazing- juicy and flavorful.  I can't wait to slow cook the sirloin for a great Sunday dinner.  The owner that I spoke with had great suggestions for how to cook the different meats and why- great resource. I would also like to add that the service there is great.  I was stuck waiting for a while for a friend, and the waitress not only offered me water while I waited, but gave me some delicious corn muffins to sample (which were excellent with honey-butter).  Everyone else I interacted with was very friendly and helpful. Overall, I am so excited to have a great source of local, grass-fed meat in Astoria, both for eating in (the prices seemed really reasonable for how they are sourced) and for cooking at home.  What a great combo!  So long, Whole Foods!

I ordered a pulled pork sammich, a side of cornbread and coleslaw. The pulled pork was good - could have been a little warmer. The cornbread was okay. I don't know why people give out these little bite sized muffins. They tend to be dry, not hot, and chewy. I would rather pay more for a higher quality product. The coleslaw was a nice addition. The inside is cute, a little crowded (well, like everywhere else in this city), and the waitstaff was pleasant. The prices were very reasonable.

This place is awesome. I give it five stars because it exceeded my expectations all-around, in terms of decor, quality of food, service and price. Every detail of the decor in the place has been thought out and it works so well.  The place is a butcher shop, yet manages to keep a cozy feel.  In an age where people are quick to label stuff "organic" without even knowing what the word means, it was nice to see that a restaurant owner cares about accountability. I ordered the turkey sandwich.  My sandwich was simple and delicious. The meat was so tasty, it didn't need anything else but the bun and a little mayo.   My boyfriend ordered the "Bob's Burger" which comes with bacon pieces buried inside and it was equally delicious.   The food is simple, and made with high quality meat.  it is well prepared and DELICIOUS. Next time, I will be coming for steaks!  The steaks in the display  looked amazing.  I will be using Butcher bar as my steakhouse from now on.  The meat is a much higher quality meat and it is not as expensive as a pretentious steakhouse. Lastly, I just want to mention the service. Everyone at Butcher Bar was super-friendly and I expect to come here often for a lonnnnggggg time.

Huge disappointment.  Small portions, overpriced.  Ordered the farmers market salad with brisket and applewood smoked bacon added.  Nothing but lettuce, 2 cherry tomatoes, 4 strips of brisket and a tiny sprinkling of bacon.  Just a waste.   The only bright spot, the sweet potatoes I ordered on the side were delicious.

Came in on thursday with my partner to finally check this spot out. We had to wait a bit, which was expected since we dropped by around 830, but the staff was just amazing. To start: -Because of our wait, we were given some corn muffins to munch while our table was getting ready -Once seated, we were given a choice of either chili or beef stew as an extra appetizer on the house (we opted for the stew but were undecided so they gave us a little bit of chili too!) -We declined dessert, but quickly changed our (my) mind when they said that too was on the house Honestly, all of that because of a wait that I didn't mind much. They definitely know how to build up a solid base. As for the food, the burnt ends were solid. The pulled pork was good but oversauced. The brisket was fine, though I may have to give Hill Country and Fette Sau the nod here. The cole slaw was good, not too creamy and a nice citrus note. String beans were probably my least favorite part of the meal. Good food, not great. If not for the amazing service, this would be a solid 3*. It's a fun ambience with great people though, and you have to respect that. Will be back when I'm in the mood for some meat (and hopefully by then they have beer!)

Butcher Bar has it all and will be complete when they get the liquor license. I ate with a bunch of my friends and ordered close to everything on the menu. The highlights were the ribs, brisk, sausage, pulled chichen and mac n cheese. We all treked in from BK and Manhattan which was a quick train ride and very worth it. If you like organic or just awesome food you need to go here asap.

Best ribs I've had in a really long time and possibly ever.  We got takeout from here and while we were waiting they gave us little corn bread muffins to munch on.  It has been open for about a month and one of the co-owners, George, came up to us while we were waiting and gave us a tour of the backyard--not fully functional in the winter but will be great in the warmer months!  We really hope that this place does well because they were super nice and the food was great!  I ordered half a rack and a side of green beans with bacon and I think it came with cole slaw too (it was a few weeks ago, have been meaning to write a review.)  The boyfriend ordered the beef brisket sandwich with baked beans which he said was amazing.  They did a great job with the place but I heard that they have curtains up so that you can't really see inside which I think is a bad move.  It is a casual place with great food and I hope that the curtains don't hinder people from going in. Anyways--can't wait for the summer parties that they'll have with the smoker in the back!!  Would go back more often but I tend to eat healthier.  Oh and they also said that they cater which I'm sure will be great!

I would give this place 10 stars if I could. My partner and I came here last Friday night and we had a fantasitc time.  From the outset our waitress Jennifer was kind and accomodating.  There were not that many folks in on an early Friday evening, so we sat at the window. The food: We both had the philly brisket and everything about it was amazing.  The meat was juicy and tender.  The flavor was truely mouthwatering.  The portion was a generous size.  And the coleslaw was perfectly seasoned, not too much mayo not too much vinegar and a perfectly smooth bite at the end of the bite. Bevarage: They only serve their house made sodas and iced teas and they were both good.  Neither was too sweet or too bubbly. We were also given the apple pie on the house and this pie did not require ice cream to enhance the flavor.  The crust was tasty and filling was delicious. Also, the kind butcher Matt kindly came over to introduce himself as well as generously offered us beef pattys for home.  All in all our experience was fantastic.  They really didn't need to throw in the extras for us to rate it high.  The food honestly speaks for iteself.  If you are looking for a great place to chow down on some tasty meat, then this is the place.

Went to Butcher Bar this weekend for dinner with a friend. We were quickly sat at a table, but the host soon realized that the table had been set aside for a party of four who were waiting. He came back and told us and was very apologetic, so we got up and went out front to wait. No big deal. They apparently have a backyard that isn't open for customers, but the host told us we could wait there if we'd prefer. We were fine out front, so we stayed there. After about five or ten minutes we got a new table. We split corn cakes and honey butter, which were delicious. I also tried the corn cakes with the original bbq sauce they had at the table, which was unusual, but it worked. I also got mac and cheese, which was even better. Perfectly cheesy and creamy. Then, I had the 50/50, a sandwich of half brisket, half pulled pork. It was fantastic. Again, I added the original sauce, which went very well with both meats. All the food was great and I had completely forgotten about the mixup earlier, but they hadn't. One of the butchers, who appeared to be in charge, came over and asked us how our food was and apologized for the inconvenience. He then insisted on giving us something for free to make up for it. We couldn't decide what to get, so he suggested ribs. A few minutes later, another butcher showed up with two ribs. He actually was bringing four, but dropped two. A couple minutes after, the first butcher was back with a plate of pulled pork to make up for the lost ribs. Both were outstanding. I then had a piece of apple pie, which was good, but forgettable. I'll probably skip it next time. Overall, great food, great service. There was an unfortunate mixup at the beginning, but everyone was friendly and they went out of their way to make up for it. I hope to be back very soon.

Holy smokes, can Butcher Bar smoke some amazing meat! Ok, maybe that was cheesy...but not as cheesy as their mouth watering macaroni & cheese! Alright, I promise, no more corny lines. Unless we're talking about Butcher Bar's corn cakes with honey butter. If you can't already tell I'm quite excited about one of Astoria's newest arrivals on the food scene. From the wood paneled walls to the mason jars that their root sodas and sweet tea are served in, Butcher Bar has done it right. I've had the opportunity to enjoy Butcher Bar's pulled pork, brisket, macaroni & cheese, corn cakes with honey butter and coleslaw (can you tell I've made it back a few times?) I have to say I can't complain or recommend improvement on any of these perfectly prepared southern delights. The best part of this barbecue is that it's prepared dry and the sauce is on the table. To tie everything together the service was friendly and on par and our meals were served promptly. I'm a big fan and will be sure to visit Butcher Bar again!

I was born and raised in Austin Texas and I can say without an reservation that the food here, for the most part is excellent. It also costs about 10 times what it does in Texas. Expect to drop at least $30 and pick up a slice of pizza afterwards.

I write this as a Southern transplant (North Carolina) who has been living in NYC for nine years and has spent the better part of the last 3 years enjoying all of the new spots Astoria has to offer and I say without a doubt that Butcher Bar is as top-top-notch as it gets.  The place is very unassuming... we went on a Sunday for lunch because we love to go to any new spot, especially one that is local, organic, etc.  This place did not disappoint in any single fashion.  We got the meal that included 3 meats (you choose... we chose the pulled pork, pulled chicken and burnt ends) and two sides (you choose... we chose the mac-n-cheese and sweet potato wedges) and it was better than we could have ever, ever expected... without a doubt the best BBQ place in NYC- yes, over Dinosaur BBQ, over Blue Smoke, over Brother Jimmys, and any other one you are thinking of.  I would 100% put it up against any BBQ place I know from down south too.  I actually can't wait for people from NC to visit just to take them there to show them that NYC can get BBQ right and this place is IT!  Go here.  It's amazing, and the very idea that this is all hormone-free, grass-fed, local... well that's just enough to push it into the column of perfection.  Everything we had was superb but the one that stands out as "daaaaaaaaaaamn that's good" is the BURNT ENDS... quite possibly the best meat that there is.  The service is so great too... super friendly, attentive, fast, courteous and they make you feel like they are really happy you came to enjoy their amazing new place.  Long story short: we went for lunch and by dinner time, we were looking for the take-out menu they gave us to place an order.  (Sidenote:  you can buy meat here to take home and cook for yourself and while we didn't do this today, we are definitely coming back to do so... the cuts were awesome.) So glad this place is in Astoria... it will quickly become a spot for foodies so I'd go now, before the lines are out the door on the regular.
Aksum has delicious food, friendly staff who give excellent recommendations PLUS it's BYOB. I was really pleased with this place and will definitely be going back.  The soup de jour(s) were AMAZING!

My boyfriend and I had a very average and somewhat disappointing brunch at Aksum last weekend. We ordered orange juice and jasmine tea for drinks. The juice came with ice, which I thought was a little weird, and our waitress forgot about the tea (thankfully we weren't charged for it). We had the grilled calamari topped with marinara sauce and peppers for an appetizer, which was pretty good. The best part of the meal was my shrimp and avocado omelette topped with feta cheese. It was a unique and tasty combination of flavors, but the fried potatoes it came with were unimpressive. Their flavor was very light, and after the first bite, it was gone, so chewing the rest of the potato was like a chore. My boyfriend had a chicken omelette and was also disappointed in how average it was. The place is well decorated with booths and throw pillows and huge windows, which made the restaurant bright and cozy. However, it did get pretty loud with only about half of the tables filled. Aksum looks and sounds good in theory, but our experience just came up short. It wasn't that bad, but it wasn't that great either. Not really sure I will be returning.

The place was awesome.  I would recommend this place to anyone who is looking for a wonderful environment with excellent food.  The hummus is to die for!!!! And the snapper is out of this world and take it from me, I'm a fish person. Although I've never paid a corkage fee (they charge $6.00), it was great that I could bring my favorite wine to eat my dish with.  Despite the charge, there's no way I would've been able to drink my favorite wine  for 1/10th the cost.  BYOA is the bomb!!!!

Aksum is awesome!! I believe it's the best new restaurant in University City in years. The food is amazing and I love meeting new people while enjoying a hookah. I've also been there for brunch which is equally amazing, it's perfect for a date night, entertaining out of town guests (family and friends alike) or just hanging out and enjoying good food. The ambiance is amazing total Center City feel without the congestion of the city I love it and can't wait to be back!!!

My friend & I were looking for a quick bite to eat before hitting the Kipps Bay movie theater.  I tend to be a little picky whenever I "eat out."  I noticed the sign for this place and thought it had a bit of charm to it so we went in.   Tiny spot.   Not necessarily a bad thing.  My friend had a salad (can't remember which) and I had the Works Omlette sandwich.  We didn't eat in as we were cutting it close to showtime.  I took a bit of my sandwich and nearly cried in shock.  It was AMAZING.  Whenever we try a new place we always share the spoils.  Not this time.  She had to wrestle a bite away from me! When I was almost finished, I tripped as I was crossing the street and I screeched  because I was afraid of dropping the crumbs before I could eat them. Great spot.  Can't wait to try the rest of their menu.  Everything looked fresh and smelled fantastic. PS - I had a bite of my friend's salad and almost wolfed it down as well.  Everything was fresh.  Made me re-think my position on never buying salads.

Seriously....not the worst place to get something to eat I guess but definitely not worth my $8.00 for a turkey sandwich. Dunkin Donuts fills the void in my stomach for $3.29 (chicken salad on bagel). I guess its the executives types around here that make 100k+ that dont mind paying through the nose for average food. Sorry Piccolo, I wont be back.
The sandwiches are amazing and the decor is really cute. It can get a bit crowded but definitely worth  getting lunch to go!

Okay, so I'll first say I went in thinking this was going to be bad experience after reading the reviews...most of which was true. We were sat right away and then waited a little while for the waitress to come back...that wasn't so bad since we started on our wine. One took our order, another asked how everything was (once during the 5 course Restaurant Week menu) and another filled waters and cleared plates. The girl clearing plates was wearing a dingy jacket while she did so. I assume she was outside, but take your coat off when it's dirty looking. The food was nothing to rave about. The portabella salad was 1/2 a mushroom on top of spring mix, and then the salad was another portion of spring mix with brusetta, which was tasty, just plain. Three pastas came out, which was probably the best part. I ordered the chicken breast which was served over mashed potatoes. The chicken was thinly sliced which I liked but it wasn't anything that I couldn't have made myself. Dessert could have been skipped, a mousse that was much firmer than any mousse we had ever had. When we asked about the mousse she seemed to have no clue and mentioned nuts on top that no one saw. It was also served with a strawberry dipping sauce (not sure what was supposed to be dipped) and a cream puff pastry.....nothing that great. Over all I would not go back and while it was 5 courses they might want to go with quality over quantity.

The service here was AWFUL.  Granted, it was restaurant week so I understand things are a little hectic but I have never had a worse experience at a restaurant.  When we arrived for our reservation, we had to wait 25 minutes to be seated and due to the restaurant's small space, my boyfriend and I were forced to hover over other guests while they were eating.  We were told our table was actually right behind us because others who were waiting to be seated had sat in our seat. After the other guests were finally seated, we watched the table we were told we would be sitting at, moved.  Right in front of us, they brought a table from the back and placed it where we were originally supposed to be seated.  Two chairs were then dragged inside from the outdoor patio and placed at our table.  We were told our table was ready, without any acknowledge or apology of the half hour wait and the fact that we were sitting in LAWN CHAIRS. I've worked as a hostess and waitress for 8 years and if I had ever made someone sit in a lawn chair in a supposed nice restaurant, I would make sure they received the best service possible from then on.  However, we had no steady waitress, instead our order was taken by the hostess and two out of my 5 courses (two of the remaining three were the same for everyone) were not what I ordered.  With my experience as a waitress I try to be as empathetic as possible however this was just a horrible experience overall.

I work evenings and get done around nine and this is the only place in town that you can get consistently great food at that time of night. Other places may still be open but you are either the only one at the bar or it's very busy but the food is horrible. They have a great variety of small appetizers on the bar menu, which I love. The dinner menu is great also. I had the Salmon on Wednesday and it was out of this world. The oyster selection is really amazing and always taste fresh & incredible. I have had just about everything on the menu here and have truly enjoyed it all. Kind of funny but two of my favorites are the New York and the Grilled 1/2 Chicken. Don't get me wrong the fish is always tasty and cooked perfect but I figured in a Fish house they would have sub-par steak & chicken, definitely not the case! It's almost like they assume people will think that, so they go above and beyond on those items.

Great place love the oysters here. Max burger is great too. It is a little on the pricey side but you get what you pay for right?? Anyway i heard they have good tartare too so i will be revisiting this place very soon.
This place is Great ! I visit this restaurant almost every month and love their food and service. The owner - Kadyr is a great guy, very attentive to all of his clients. Keep up the good work guys!!!
I think people are slightly overrating this place. It's decent. But there are better places in chinatown. Not a five star joint. Really more of a 3.5.
Came here a week ago, soup with beef was really good, also had the pork on the sesame bread also good. Pretty small place, big flavor small prices, a large soup will run you 6 bucks.
The food is amazing.  The drinks are strong. The service always has a smile.  I am always greeted by the owner personally.  What more could one ask for?

I had the nutella and banana crepe with strawberries and I must say it's one of the best crepes I ever had. The place it self is nice and cozy. Not many chairs for sitting and eating but that doesn't seem to be bothering anyone. Can't wait to go back and try their savory crepes.

Hidden Gem of Downtown!!  This place is awesome!  It's a beautiful landmarked building and the inside is gorgeous. Dark wood interior and leather seating on the main floor, two cool bars downstairs and a beautiful dining room upstairs.  Lots of little nooks for quiet dining and a big bar for drinks after if you feel like a hang.  Great food and drinks and the staff couldn't be friendlier.  Just beautiful.

Went last night for the first time and I live in the neighborhood.  Great space, I agree with others.  Food is good, not great and quite expensive.  The cocktails were very good and strong (not watered down).  The overall feel is more of a welcoming club/bar and not a restaurant - it was REALLY loud and all the bar areas (they have several) were packed.  It seems that's what they're striving for.

Outstanding. 4 of us Came in for brunch today. Everything from ambiance &service to food was stellar. Really appreciated their soundtrack of soul & funk classics. We ordered some mezze &pita to start which was delicious. I then got egg"souvlaki" which was a play on a souvlaki sandwich but with egg & Greek sausage wrapped in a warm pita. My guests got lamb burger,octopus,&baked egg dish. All very good. The souvlaki &lamb burger came w smashed fries which I think are treated like tostones as they are fried once, smashed & crisped up in the fryer again. Again really good & unique. Other restaurants in the neighborhood pale in comparison to MP. They should come in & see what modern dining & service is truly about. Will def be back again. Also the bill was really affordable & fair for the quality of food & service we got. Opa!

After all the great Yelp reviews thought it would be a good local place to take a friend from NJ. Unfortunately we didn't get much farther than the door as the two hostesses, who looked barely 21, were less than helpful, had to get their attention from their personal conversation to let them know we were interested in sitting at the bar for drinks. One seat available, we asked if one of the (many) free chairs at the table tops could be moved over to the not at all crowded bar area, to which they barely acknowledged me and said no without even looking. Aren't hostesses supposed to be hospitable? Not here. Too many great places in the area to waste giving this place another chance if that's how they treat potential customers.

I had a list of dishes I was craving, and have to come back again to try them all. What upset me was that Saturday afternoon that I went, they said they did not have the lambshank with orzo available. It looked so good from Yelpers' pictures. We did get the octopus chickpea salad, and the octopus was soft, with a bite (some like it slightly crisp and chewy, but here, it was as if it were massaged and beaten to obtain such tenderness). We then got the scallops that came with capers, spinach, and dried cherries. This was an excellent pairing of flavors, but it would've been perfect if they seared the scallop in the brown butter a tad longer. Then came the Greek paella with shellfish, spicy lamb sausage, and orzo. Don't expect this paella to have the crispy layer of toasted rice on the bottom. It is orzo, after all (so it's more like a seafood pasta than a paella). It was rather like a cioppino/bouillabaisse. Overall, service was excellent, and the room was comfortable. I want to come back for the rabbit dumplings (even though I've had them at Kefi in the UWS).

Honestly, this is hands down the best restaurant in Astoria. The menu is broad and will have something for everyone. Personally, my entree was a special (lamb). It was tender and perfectly salted. The appetizers were also delicious. I had the opportunity to sample a few because I went with a group of 5. Overall, I would highly recommend this place for any occasion.

I first went here in the summer and it was delicious. Finally got to come back here again and still very good. This is a great place for a big group to split a bunch of dishes. Our group of 8 loved everything we ordered which were: - two orders of the trio combo dips: very tasty especially the yogurt - octopus: could have been a bit more tender but liked the unusual combo with chickpeas - mussels: they serve good meaty mussels, came in a slightly spicy red sauce - dumplings: my favorite - almost like a ravioli/gnocci - mixed grill: I'm not a huge meat fan but it's a good variety of chicken, lamb, sausage etc and everyone else loved it - barrel aged feta: another favorite and very well portioned - grandma's meatballs: pretty good, again, I'm not a huge meat eater but everyone loved it. Every dish had lots of pita to go around. Dishes are very well portioned and very affordable. Dessert: brownie was very rich but good. Vanilla ice cream on top was delicious. The space is huge and modern - our table was ready for us (bonus for no waiting for the entire party to be seated) Waitress was very friendly and helpful with recommendations. The one negative is they never seem to be fully stocked with beer and whisky. Both times I've been there, friends have had to go through at least 3 beers or whiskeys before the bar actually had it. Not sure why since the bar is beautiful with a nice line-up of taps (which are clearly empty since they never have anything)

As a renowned "omelet snob" I let server Ashley know that if the egg white omelette with mushroom, spinach, onion and cheese I ordered was terrible, I'd end up on Yelp. Her response "I'm up for challenge." Not only was the omelette superb, Ashley's service was as well.  And it's BYO?! Meet your new brunch spot

I like their food and the atmosphere. My daughter LOVES their fruit smoothies and say they rival her grand pops, which is saying a lot because in her eyes he makes THE BEST smoothies ever. Unfortunately I love pork and prefer pork bacon over any other type of bacon. The service was a tad slow. And I've only ate here twice b/c every other time I've come here it's packed beyond belief.

My fiancé and I took our granddaughter to breakfast because of the great reviews I heard in the past.  The food was lousy! The coffee was lukewarm and the service was worse than the food.  The prices are very expensive for the terrible food served.  The dishes were dirty and the servers act like they don't know what's going on.  The seating is too close - if feels like you are sitting on top of each other - very loud!  I try my best to patronize black owned businesses but when they are not up to par I keep it moving.  I asked a few friends of mine if they had eaten at the Café and they advised that they did and the food was lousy and the prices were expensive.  I could have gotten much more food, better service for less money at IHOP.  Please take all of these constructive criticisms and try to improve on the quality of food and servers.  Thanks, Charmane

I never review on Yelp but felt it necessary to take a moment and start with singing praises to Rose Petals Cafe & Lounge for their outstanding food, quality customer service and owners who really care. This quaint gem of Germantown is the start to some positive change for the area and should be an example of what small businesses in Philadelphia could be all about. Ownership has a story, but more importantly they translate there passion to caring abou there customers, going above and beyond, being a part of the community in many ways, while still serving Amazing fresh, quality food. * I felt the need to mention that some of the other reviews I have read are disheartening, especially knowing that this is a restaurant that has owners and employees that are so humble, pleasant and attentive to their customer base. I suppose some people feel the need to use yelp as a venting space, especially relating to one review stating "they have criminals working for them" simply due to what seems to be a simple credit card pos error. FYI these things happen in chain restaurants all the time, and I don't believe for 1 second they would be stealing from their customers, but again not really the type of dialouge for yelp. I have noticed that Rose Petals continues to become busier and busier, which means the word is spreading so great job guys. Keep up the good work, and remember your not going to please everyone (as yelp has already shown you) but keep true to your mission and vision of this amazing destination as those who really know appreciate your generous efforts. For those who don't I will continue to pray for you as some of the critical comments are unnecessary, but keep patronizing IHOP as that leaves more space on Sunday afternoon for me and my family to enjoy the real stuff!

The sushi was good, but not that great. I've tried sushi at a variety of different establishments, and I was hoping to find a mecca here. After scouring yelp for sushi in the Central / North Jersey area, I affixed my eyes on the dink basement abode known as Ajihei. When my party of 3 got there, we came to the door at 5:56p. We were told to leave immediately, since the restaurant opened in 4 minutes. I thought this was a bit pretentious. We came back 10 minutes later and there was a line out the door! We thought this has to be good sushi. After waiting almost 10 more minutes (the wait staff of 3 had to get "clearance" from the chef / master / owner / sushi-man), we were allowed to sit at a table for 4 at the back. SERVICE: The service stinks. This is partly why I'm giving it two stars. The waiters were rude at the door. When we were finally seated, they never checked on us, filled our water, etc. For a waitstaff of three and only 5-6 tables, you'd think the service would be more attentive. WRONG. Next, the wait staff kept entering the kitchen. It was irritating to have them constantly walking one or two feet past you into the kitchen. They tended to wander around the restaurant and look at tables. When they saw our cups were empty, they kept looking, walking. I'm not sure if they were pretending to act busy, but when you have 3 waiters for 6 tables, and you're not being attended to properly, the service SUCKS. The waiters need to stand in one place. For such a small restaurant in such a dink basement, STOP WALKING AROUND! It's irritating to the people who are eating, especially when you're not attentive! FOOD: The sushi was good, but not that great. The tuna wasn't melt-in-your-mouth. I wasn't expecting toro for the tuna, but it was semi-tough... that was disappointing. The rice was hard, and it was not binding enough to the sushi. The eel sushi was VERY delicious. The other pieces (shrimp, salmon, etc.) were average. I ordered the Chef's special. The miso was powdered; nothing special. The rolls (tuna, oyster) were good. Much better than the sushi pieces. The BEST part of the meal was the goyoza. Our party of three had two orders of it. They were very crispy, fried dumplings served with a soy sauce based dip. The dip was great! It was a combination of soy and some other sauces (TBD). Def. order it! The bill for three people (2x Goyoza, 2x Chef's plate (let the chef choose), 1x Tuna, 1x Oyster, 1x Tempura Rolls) came out to $77. This was INSANE since the sushi was average at best. A snotty wait staff, average sushi, and high price tag turned me off. Ajihei may float your boat if you're into those things... but you may like this Sushi dink.

Very decently sized chirasi bowl, with fresh pieces of fish for just around $20 is really not bad in Princeton! I stopped in with a book while traveling for work, but I'd recommend bringing a friend instead. You don't get signal on your phone, nor is the lightning very bright, so not a solo traveler-friendly place. I'm assuming there's a tiny kitchen, since service took longer than expected, but that could also have been a function of being alone with not much to do. Friendly server staff, though the clientele can get a little rowdy. Tiny seating, so note that carefully!

My guy and I are gluten sensitive and this was our second visit at Mariella's. This visit was simply delicious- we ordered the Portuguese octopus salad with arugula and grilled zucchini- so so good, then my guy had gluten free spaghetti with salmon, capers and olives in a light tomato sauce- scrumptious! And I had the duck breast with figs and cabbage in a red wine reduction and roasted rosemary potatoes. The ambiance is very cozy and romantic. The only thing is the portions are little smaller but it saves the place for desert and you do not feel stuffed. The server - nice Irish young woman- is very attentive. I will definitely go back.

I have been here twice this week, first for dinner and then for a takeout lunch. The food and service are both exquisite. The staff is friendly and attentive, and I found the dishes to be creative and reasonably priced (which is not always a given in oh-so-trendy Brooklyn restaurants). For dinner, we shared the fettucine with duck sausage and mushrooms, and the pancetta-wrapped hake. We also had a side of the rainbow chard and an appetizer of fish (I think it was sable) and fennel. For dessert, we had the brownie soaked in rye. Our server, Bill, also recommended a nice bottle of dolcetto, which paired nicely with all the food. The meal started with an amuse-bouche of olive puff pastry, which was a great way to whet the appetite (and would be great as a full-size croissant for breakfast for us savory fans -- note to the baker!). This place is a bakery first and foremost and the assortment of breads was very fresh, as was the olive oil and the house-made butter. We especially liked the miche, but they were all good. The hake was our favorite of all the dishes. The pancetta was slightly smoky but not too salty and perfectly complemented the fish, which also came with a bit of cauliflower risotto. The fettucine with sausage was a solid, rib-sticking winter dish. The only off note of the evening was the rye in the brownie, which didn't really complement the chocolate. Dinner was relaxed, although that might have been because they were few diners on a winter weeknight. A jazz mix played over the loudspeakers. The manager, Elias, stopped by to see how everything was and answer our questions about the restaurant. I enjoyed the meal so much that I came back the next day to check out their lunch options, which are meager -- just a few sandwiches, salads and a soup of the day. I got the $9 mackerel banh mi (tomato, onion, cucumber, daikon, etc.) to go.. It was delicious -- great smoky flavor. The coffee was nothing special but the array of breads was quite impressive. I tried a sample of the poppyseed cake, which was appropriately moist, unlike most such cakes I have eaten in the past. Alex and Natalie, who were working the lunch shift, were both friendly and even let me peek into the bakery. Overall, this is a fabulous addition to the neighborhood and I can easily envision becoming a regular visitor, Looking forward to how the menu changes with the seasons (and they will win me over for life if they start baking sourdough baguettes).

Was happy to see a new lunch place near work.  But the first time I ordered the duck confit salad to go, I was shocked to see a minuscule serving in the box.  It is not even the equivalent of a side salad on an entree plate...  It wasn't cheap and the size of the portion for what they charge is blatant rip off.  My friend's soup to go also was only a ladle worth in a half filled standard soup cup.  What the heck?!  Will not recommend for lunch take out.  Not sure if its any better eating in.

Visited this new addition to the neighborhood and am impressed. Tried a few of their crepes with a mix of both the salad crepes and sweet crepes. All excellent tasting, light (made with rice flour), and easy to eat (thanks to the innovative cone like structure). Would and will highly recommend this place to everyone I know including the yelp community. A "must try". A++++++

It's very rare that I take the time to write a review about a recent meal; but Eight Turn left such an indelible impression on my taste buds that I felt inclined to share. The crepe was delicious and the woman taking my orders was very accommodating towards my desire to customize the crepe. Everything in this establishment is very well-conceived. The crepe is handed to customers in a paper wrap with perforations which allow you to tear the wrapping as you make progress on the meal. The facility was extremely clean and the employees are inordinately friendly. It's not common to see someone with such a positive disposition in NYC. I strongly recommend everyone try this place for dessert or a quick meal.

Japanese-style cone crepes, I've been waiting for you to arrive for sooooooooooooooooooooo long. Why haven't you come to NYC sooner? As much as I love the established creperies here, they don't usually serve sugar with something called restraint. I had the Matcha Stripe even though I initially had reservations about it. I cringed to imagine how rich a crepe loaded with custard, truffle, chocolate sauce and yogurt would taste, even if it was balanced with berries and pistachios, but I ultimately succumbed to my love for green-tea-flavored anything. You ever had that type of dessert that feels heavenly from the second you take your first nip to the moment you feel it sliding down your throat? Then, when you've regretfully finished the thing, you feel this god-awful oily/sugary residual film in your mouth and at the back of your throat that makes you truly regret eating it in the first place? Well, you definitely won't feel the latter with these. True to their vision, ETC made an amazingly comforting, but delicate dessert with just the right balance of flavors and, most importantly (for me), sugar. I didn't think any single ingredient in the Matcha Stripe, not even the choco sauce or truffles, were overly sweet. And no, it wasn't the custard and yogurt masking the sugar, which brings another point: no component was overpowering the others. Wish I stopped by when they gave complimentary yuzulade. Incidentally, I did try that and the yuzu soda and they are both pretty awesome too! Nice way to wash it all down.

Place used to be good about a yeah ago. Went here recently for lunch and knew i was in trouble when we were the only ones in the place. First off they didn't have any lunch specials. Second we ordered a pie and a chicken parm sandwich. Pizza was so thin and oily you couldn't even hold it like normal pizza. The chicken parm was dry and over cooked. Not terrible but not great either.   Lastly service was not great considering only ones in there. Would not go back when Bruno's is a block away and so much better.

Ordered pizza at 9:45pm.  Pizza never arrived at the hotel.  When I called Vinnies III Pizza at 11:15 pm they said driver was on their way.  In addition they were very rude with a New Jersey take it or leave it attitude so I sent the Pizza back.  Like other individuals customer service is horrible at this place.

This place seriously blew my mind. Aged Cheddar Shortcake, Duck Leg Confit, Trout with Cabbage Tartlet, Cured Pork Belly and Kale & Celery Root Strudel were the highlights. Oh wait, that's everything I ordered. In other words, everything on their menu is AMAZING. Great ambience, friendly staff, beautiful patrons - what you look for in a West Village gem. Oh, and the prices are very reasonable. Too good to be true. Check out the full review here: calimari.tumblr.com/post…

Boloco simply has the best burritos in Burlington. Walking in, the atmosphere is good, but the food is amazing! My two favorites are the Thai and Buffalo burritos, but there are so many different combinations. I like this place better than Bueno y Sano and much better than New World Tortilla, and the service is much better here than either of those places. As long as Boloco keeps making great burritos I will remain a loyal customer!

Great food at an even better price. You really can't beat that combo. I'm a UVM student and I frequently ditch the on-campus dining options so I can take a stroll downtown, sit on Church Street, and enjoy an amazing burrito and nutella shake. Sure, there are probably better options if you're looking for the best sit-down meal in Burlington, but that's not what Boloco excels at. When you walk in, you'll notice the open kitchen right behind the register (the "we've got nothing to hide" atmosphere). I've worked in a café of this style for years- it makes a difference to the customer. Additionally, the service is exceptional and I've had some great interactions with the cashiers. One recommended a new local hip-hop group while another was in my aunt's high school science class (interesting connection). Even better, I've never waited more than 5 minutes for my food! EVEN BETTER, they are open until 10 PM EVERYDAY! One Sunday night when a friend and I were looking for food before a concert, the fact that Boloco was still open at 9 practically made my night (the concert was good too). So, what about the food? I love it. I recommend from experience that you try the Bangkok Thai, Cajun, and Teriyaki burritos. I additionally recommend that you try anything else on the menu because you'll probably like it. I'm boring so I've actually only experienced the nutella shake but next time I'm in there, I'm getting the Jimmy Carter. Boloco is a great place to sit and enjoy said burritos. Indoor seating is comfy and there's AC. Outdoor seating gives you one of the best "people-watching" spots on Church Street. I love going here to eat with my Burlington friends (one of which found the stolen boloco sign in his sublet apartment and returned it- they love him now). Overall, this place is great and often makes my time in Burlington worthwhile.

There are no words that can aptly describe Kamayan Night, but Jeepney is one of the few restaurants in New York City that offers this dining experience. It's based on the Filipino tradition of eating food using one's hands, without the use of any utensils or silverware. I'd long been curious, but put off coordinating the dinner myself given the complexity and requisites for reserving the meal [1]; thankfully, one of my friends took the initiative to do so, and I was more than happy to join in. Our group arrived on the dot, and doing so allowed us to watch the preparation of our meal. A table is covered in long banana leaves, and the food is carefully layered in the center. We'd selected two "appetizers" and three "main courses" in advance, but these items were all plated together and distributed across the table. The garlic rice served as the base, and an array of vegetables and proteins were layered on top; it was an impressively organized presentation, given the mess I was sure would ensue. Before we began our meal, our servers gave us a quick run-through on how best to eat the food, by pressing together the rice and vegetable or protein together between the thumb and subsequent fingers. In the realm of appetizers, the Warm Pinakbet Salad was a solid starter, given the abundance of protein in the other courses. There was a variety of vegetables - roasted kabocha squash, sautéed eggplant,bitter melon, steamed long beans - as well as diced pork belly cooked in a bagoong broth (a salty, fermented shrimp/fish paste) and topped with crispy chicharron. I was fonder of the Banana Ketchup Ribs, which cooked pork ribs in a filipino-inspired dry rub and glazed them in a spicy banana ketchup barbeque sauce. The meat was tender, and the flavor a seamless blend of salty, sweet, and spicy. Our "main courses" included the Menudo, pulled lamb shank marinated in a tomato and kamote purée, which was dotted with chicken liver, carrots, and olives. There was only a hint of gaminess in the meat, and the slight sweetness from the kamote was a smart counter to the heavier flavors. The Inasal na Manok featured a half roasted chicken cooked in lemongrass, calamansi, and achuete (also known as annatto) - a slightly peppery, nutty fruit that's commonly used in Filipino cuisine. And the Dampa Fry (offered at a supplemental charge) featured a whole-fried fish that maintained a crispy, salty skin, but a tender interior. We dug into all of these in excitement, and I was surprised that I was able to maintain some semblance of cleanliness throughout the course of the meal. Dessert was probably the disappointment of the night; the Halo Halo had far too much crushed ice that was solidified in too-large pieces. Thankfully, there was some ube ice cream and a dotting of Rice Crispies across the top, and we were (even more thankfully) given spoons to eat this with. What Jeepney offers, besides a tasty array of Filipino food, is a one-of-a-kind experience. Sure, there's plenty of hassles to coordinate and the price of the meal falls on the higher end of the spectrum [2], but it's a price worth paying. After all, there's no better way of solidifying friendships than by willingly tossing aside all social conventions in front of your dining companions. -- [1] Reservations are taken by phone for Wednesday and Thursday nights, and these spots go quickly. In addition to choosing the menu items and drink options in advance, a 25% deposit (on the expected price of the full meal) is immediately charged on the card. [2] The base price (pre-tax, pre-tip) per person is $50, and supplements, such as certain dishes, rice, and alcohol, can inflate the price dramatically.

Kamayan Night, expect to drop down at least $60 in tax, tips, and drinks, AT LEAST. Do not be a germaphobe, you will be eating with you hands and with your fellow friends. Make a reservation about a month in advanced and come on time.  They will give you about 2 hours to eat until they start giving you a friendly reminder to hurry up and eat your food so they can start setting up for next reservation. Food will be spread on bamboo leaves, our group had chicken, pork belly, sausages, eggplant, bokchoy and rice.  Surprisingly the rice was super flavorfull after being on the bottom of everything and soaked up all the drippings and flavor from the meats. Waiter was super nice, honest and down to earth.   In the end, our party of 10 only had two bowls of the shaved ice Halo to share between everyone.  Our party seriously thought at we should at the very least one bowl for every two person to share.  With the money we were paying, we expected to at least have more bowls of dessert among everyone. Great experience, would I pay $60+ again to eat with my hands? No, just give me a knife and fork and put food on a plate so I can feel civilized and be evolved.

Best Filipino Gastropub I've been to. The food is great, and it's very hipster. I'll be back again if I'm ever in the area. The wait wasn't that bad b/c we went early. Nom Nom Nom. Very enjoyable and cool atmosphere.

More like 3.5 stars. My first experience at Jeepney didn't have me rushing to make a second reservation to come back. Not because the food was terrible but it was pretty pricey for what you were getting. I arrived on a Friday night with two others and with a reservation the wait was not bad.  The vibe is really different as soon as you walk in making it feel like you've been transported to Manila. Our waitress was super friendly and she was really helpful with explaining the menu and making suggestions. We ordered the Sisig tacos, Lumpia, the Bicol Express, Chori burger and the Talangka fried rice and a couple of drinks. All the dishes were solid and we all left super full.  It's worth a try at least once and maybe even for their famous Kamayan night when they lay out food on banana leaves and you eat only with your hands.
Filipino restaurant. Short staffed. I have been waiting for 40 minutes for bicol "express" (lunch special) Food here is pretty good, but I have to give two stars for their very slow service.

What a gem!  Every time one of our Manhattan friends comes to visit, we take them here.  The manager totally gets it, and always gives us a warm welcome.  The bar is usually sprinkled with wise locals, and the servers are incredibly good with any type of patron (i.e. my in-laws loved it, my incredibly snobby dad loved it, and the laid back foodies in us loved it!).  I would HIGHLY recommend this restaurant to anyone in the area!  The food is excellent, and so is the service.   There's a reason the local families fill this place!

My husband and I recently moved to the neighborhood and have driven by this tiny restaurant a million times.  We were really eager to check it out, and when we finally had a chance we were not disappointed!  The owner, Matt, makes you feel right at home and is extremely knowledgable.  They have great wines to go perfectly with your food.  The food is right up there with any of the top Italian restaurants in NYC - freshly made pasta and top notch ingredients.  My husband had the filet mignon and I ordered homemade pasta with vodka sauce.  We left extremely happy, satiated and planning our next visit.  Highly, highly recommended.

A group of us decided to head here for lunch. It seemed to a little slow for being lunchtime but that's better for us right? Well no because the service was lacking. It took close to 5 minutes for someone to come take our drink order and they didn't even ask the last person in our group what she wanted before had to stop him from walking away from our table. Being that it was my first time here I opted for the Rodizio which includes the salad bar and the others opted strictly for the salad bar. Of course these aren't your ordinary salad bars. Well apparently the food warmers must have been malfunctioning or somebody wasn't doing their job because all of the warm food was cold. Upon the return of our waiter, which felt like an eternity, we informed him of the cold food situation. He checked on the situation and confirmed that there in fact was an issue with the warmers. He neglected to ask everyone what they wanted but just brought over a bowl of rice. I mean that was cool but there were much more options at the hot part of the salad bar that everyone wanted to try out. On to the Rodizio. All the meat was good. Seemed to lack the normal saltiness that I've come to expect from the Portuguese meats over the years and I couldn't see the sea salt crystals which explains that. Just so you know they did not charge us for the 2 salad bars so they did attempt to make good. All in all I might have to give this place another shot but not anytime soon since there are a lot of other bonafide options in the area.

OMG SERVICE IS AWFUL... 2nd time and SERVICE has not improved.   I decided to tried it again and I experienced the same problem. We sat at a table by the bar and and the waiter came in quickly got us a round of drinks, after that She never came back.  In fact I noticed her eating at the bar guess lunch break?? who allows their employees to seat at the bar during lunch???  I had to go to the bar I ask for refills.  we were there for 4 hours and we went to the bar 3 times to get drinks.   My coworker asked for a manager and he never showed.  Food is good but the service is AWFUL.  Is the owner aware of all of this service issues? so sad the place is great enough parking its safe, food quality is good, but they lack bus boys and waiters.  Never again

I am hesitant to give Mr. Adams such a dismal rating because the food is really quite good, but the service was so inexcusably bad that it warrants one star. I arrived to a fairly empty bar area on a Saturday evening (around 8:30) and we sat at the side tables by the bar.  I was celebrating my birthday and a group of friends arrived about half an hour after my fiance and I sat down (we had ordered a couple of appetizers and drinks).  This is when things realllly headed south. Our servers came to check on us for food and drinks about once every 45-70 minutes without exaggeration. It took them about an hour to give everyone in our group (~12 people) just silverware and plates! I ordered a glass of white wine, it took 2 hours for them to return with my second glass because "they had to put the bottle in the fridge"...annnnnd because they forgot. These were my only 2 drinks for a 4 hour outing. At one point, my friend asked to speak with the manager, who never showed up.  3 of the 4 servers were all taking break simultaneously and eating at the bar at one point.  The busboy never cleared the plates.  I was so freaking hungry at the end (after the kitchen had mysteriously closed and we finally had one server who came over) that I just asked for a loaf of bread.  Oh and my friends had arranged to have a slice of birthday cake brought over to me but apparently they forgot and 'locked' the kitchen, so not a really happy birthday situation .  I honestly felt like I was on a hidden camera show, the service was so horrifically bad.  Oh and did I mention the bar area was completely dead all night?! Yep.  I have no idea what the service is like in the restaurant part, and I have no desire to ever return to find out.

Went there for the first time since they changed ownership.   The food was OK, the service could have been better. The servers were not very attentive.  Asked several times for different items and they needed to be reminded  The beer prices was NOT bad at all.  4 dollars for a 16 oz IPA.   WILL GO BACK FOR drinks late night.

It's about time someone entered the scene with emphasis on organic, delicious, affordable food! I came here on my lunch break and was pleasantly surprised. Inside the decor is very welcoming, and the staff greeted me at the door, along with the intoxicating aroma of fresh ingredients being cooked to perfection. A coworker of mine ordered the Persampier salad (AMAZING), and I ordered the ginger scallion noodles (also, amazing!). Both of us were really impressed, and the emphasis on ingredients is what sets this place apart. Everything tasted fresh, and the combinations of flavors was truly exceptional.   Beyond the food itself, the actual experience from start to finish was something that I found to be very enjoyable. You are greeted by a very user friendly touch screen interface which shows you the entire menu and the options available to you. However, this is far from overwhelming and allowed expeditious movement of the long line of customers. I was literally in and out in under 10 minutes. Every staff member had a smile on, and was eager to assist anyone. Anyone looking to get a REALLY good meal complete with locally grown fare, great service, and an even better atmosphere should head over to this place. Don't pay attention to the haters below, they clearly missed something! I will definitely make this a staple of my weekly diet, and I can't wait to introduce my entire office to this gem! LONG LIVE HONEYGROW!

the food was delicious.  I had a make your own salad- it was large and had a lot of chicken in it.  the salad dressing (green goddess) was amazing! However- I went at 12.  I didn't need to wait long to place my order- about 5 minutes- BUT then i had to wait 40 minutes FOR A SALAD!!!.  it seemed like the stir-frys were coming out much much faster.  I think they have experienced people working the stir fry lin e(former short order cooks?) but the girls working the salad line were king of pathetic.

This is the first week they are open, but it took them 30 minutes to get my and my friends stir fries out.   Not enough sauce if there's even any on there.  Noodles in one big amalgamated mess.  Shrimp tastes fishy.  It cost $17 for a smoothie (that was good) and a stir fry that I can't even eat.   And in case you get exicted about the pickled cucumber and think it might be Asian pickles that will taste really good in stir fry- be forewarned that they appear to be DILL PICKLES.  Uck.   Oh, and I paid extra for carrots and spinach.  No carrots are in my stir fry and there may be 5 spinach leaves.  Pathetic. ***************EDIT************** I have since returned to honey grow and have had much better experiences.  They seem to have gotten their act together food wise.  Organization wise, it's still a mess in there.  No one should have to wait 10 minutes to pay for their food.

Fast-casual stir fry, falls short of expectations unless you're vegetarian... chicken might as well be sold separately. .. food: C Noodles drown the toppings.  Where is the chicken, or far that matter options for "extra" toppings?  Expect tons, and tons of noodles scantily garnished with your topping of choice, clearly sorted by price.  The vegetables far outnumbered the chicken, and the chicken added up to something like one strip cut in tiny nuggets.  What a joke. .. concept: A Great idea for a place:  awesome venue, touchscreen ordering and a good variety.  Now if the food just lived up to the concept... .. price: D If you're gonna sell noodles by the pound, then let us pay specifically for each topping and portion.  For ~$10 I can get a similar meal with exactly what I want, and how much I want at Chipotle. Needs: - Better portions of toppings - Real portion of meat when you order chicken/beef/seafood - Ordering options for extras

While it is outwardly unassuming (only a small, green sign hangs outside the door that puns "KEEP CALM AND GROW ON"--a nod to their commitment to use fresh, locally-grown ingredients) inside it has real presence. The atmosphere is refreshing: a sleek design reminiscent of Momofuku (crack pie!) with lots of light and a surprisingly tasteful music selection. ( I heard both Al Green AND Smokey Robinson!) The staff was helpful and charming, eager to answer any questions I had without sounding condescending or annoyed. There was a palpable sense of comradery among the workers, which translated into a more pleasant experience for me, as a customer. The food was tasty. I ordered the Spicy Garlic, which was, as the name suggests, spicy, but very dimensional--certainly not overpowering. Paired very well with my orange-banana-lemon smoothie, which was clean and refreshing! Am likely to return on a regular basis.
Fresh, clean, and delicious. Got the honey granola fruit here- so simple yet so good! Special thanks to Sherri- she's so sweet, friendly, and awesome!

Went today for lunch and got the spicy garlic stir fry. I agree with Michelle. WAY too spicy! The spicy sauce killed the dish. There was absolutely no flavor, just spice. And what's more upsetting was that I paid over $10 for a meal I couldn't eat let alone enjoy. My recommendation, either easy up on the spice and add more REAL flavor or put a warning next to the selection telling people this will give you ulcers in your stomach. Doubt I'll go back to this place.
The cannoli are great here and fresh, at least the time that I went. I also have tried their black and white cookies which are huge and cakey, a little too thick in the center though.

Incredible everything with 1981 prices and the family is the best.  Name any other bakery where the police set up traffic cones at least 2x per year, Easter and Christmas, to deal with the pickups...NAME ONE! I've been a lunch regular for 7 years, the best.
The best bakery around!! They have wonderful, fresh bread. I especially LOVE their Napoleons. Noone else makes them the way they do, yum!!!

I must say i'm impressed.  i normally dont like eating asian food outside of chinatown because i never feel like they can do a good enough job, but Saigon Shack proved me wrong.  Though, the prices you pay for in chinatown is still, but if you're looking for some vietnamese pho in the west village, here's the place to go. I had the special spicy pho and man that was good.  delish! totally hit the spot. friend had the duck banh mi and i must say i was disappointed.  i'd be back to try the other phos and vermicelli or rice dishes.  they looked yums while i was eating mine. =D grill pork summer roll - different since it's usually shrimp but solid i shall be back! =D

I wish I didn't have to give this place a perfect review, because the lines keep getting longer, but this place is just delicious.  I've been coming here since Spring 2011, which must have been around the time they opened, and they have stayed great the whole time. The pho is among the best in the city, primarily because of the quality of ingredients.  Sometimes the broth is not crystal clear, which is a downer, but the flavor profile is still the most reliable in the city.  Also, their sandwiches are awesome, and the vermicelli bowls are also spot-on.  Really this is the best you can get for the price. For a perfect meal for two, start with the papaya salad (with Vietnamese chili dressing), and then try the pho and something with pork chops, either a sandwich or a vermicelli bowl.  Share and enjoy!  Note: Pho is hard to share unless you're cool with sharing utensils and having people slurp over the bowl you're eating out of.

Love this place! My girl friends and I come to the city two sometime three times a year for quality girls time and we frequent the Saigon Shack each and every time since we discovered it four years ago! We love it so much we plan where we stay around this place and come back for at least two of our meals if not more!  Can't say enough good things about it. love their fresh drinks, vietnamese coffee, spring rolls, vietnamese sandwiches, pho...the list goes on and on..

Warning: I am of the very strong mentality that no one should ever, EVER, waste stomach space on soup. Then came Pho. For a whopping $8 you can get Saigon Pho, full of flavor and meat! I have been craving it since! Will definitely return! READ ME: if you do happen to have leftovers and don't want to throw them out, there are plenty of homeless people on your way to the subway that i am sure will not mind having some warm soup on these freezing NYC nights.

If you are stuck in the west village and the hankering for banh mi takes over you, this is a good spot to go. Good ratio of bread and filling. They have some options if you want to try the non traditional banh mi.

My husband and I ordered a portion if Veg Spring rolls which was pretty nice ! and a bowl each of Veggie Pho.. Have to say that seeing pieces of red potato in it was totally new to me and they had overloaded the pho with raw onion rings.. Overall I'd say it wasn't half bad but I think I may not come back very often.

I found this spot while waiting for the Halloween parade to start with my teenage goddaughter. I specifally came here for the sandwiches even though most of the yelp reviews talked about "pho" which I had no idea what it was. Most of the customers that evening ordered "pho" which looked like a big bowl of soup with noodles and meat. I kind of wish I would've ordered the "pho" because the sandwiches were just okay. I ordered the chicken and my goddaughter ordered the beef. We shared an order of the sweet potato fries that was delicious but I didn't like the sauce that came with the fries and they didn't have ketchup.  The place was fairly small and stayed pack the entire time we were there. There was a line for people ordering take out and waiting to be seated. I will definitely return just to check out their infamous "pho."

My first experience with Vietnamese food...I was very pleased...The place is cozy...I sat at the bar where seating is a little tight...I ordered the Classic Bhan Mi & Saigon Pho...The sandwich was very good...Bread had great texture and the meats were flavorful...The soup featured sliced beef & meatballs with noodles etc... Overall it was very enjoyable...The broth was tasty...I added Srirachi and Hoisin which enhanced it for me...There was plenty of sliced beef & noodles and it was very filling...The only drawback is the meatballs...They were hard and tasteless...they didn't detract but didn't add anything to the soup...Shrimp Summer Rolls were delicious, very fresh and crisp. Service was excellent...I would definitely go back.

The waitress came over and asked for more tip. What. The. F. Oh did I mention hair in food? "Usually people give 15% tip, this isn't enough" "Are you asking for more tip?" "Yes" "You don't ask for more tip." "..."

It may not be the very best Vietnamese in NYC or world, but I applause SS venturing into the heart of the night life of NoHo and West Village while keeping their food authentic.  So many other restaurants congregate in ethnic neighborhood, leaving more mainstream restaurants just playing with ethnic elements in higher end commercial or residential areas; or ethnic restaurants "Americanize" their food.  Hope this success change the trend for the better.
truly delightful.

Party of ten on our annual Christmas outing. Very disappointing. Limited menu offerings. Entrees mediocre.....not even hot. Lamb overcooked. Service took forever. They have taken deconstruction to be an end in itself rather than an interesting way to present excellent food. Need to rethink some things and get back to great food.

Went to Bartaco last night.  Got there at 9:20 or so on a Thursday night and it was packed!  This is evidently the "bar scene" right now in West Hartford center.  A mixture of young and old (really dude, you're 60 leave that 22 year old girl alone!) and the noise level was very high.  We sat outside which made it bearable but once it gets cold this is going to be a problem for diners.  To some extent if you are sitting inside you will feel like the bar patrons are right on top of you.  To start off, we were seated outside right away, but it took about 10 minutes before anyone came over to help us, and then it wasn't even the person who had our section!  Needless to say this was not a good start.  The drink menu is not extensive, and it is confusing.  If you don't know what some of the liquors that they are using are, you will have no clue...witness my wife who after asking about three different drinks went with a glass of red wine!
