 Don't know what they had on draught as I went with a bottle of Modelo Negro.  We were served a plate of tortilla crips and guacamole which was good, the tortilla crisps were a little salty though.  The guac was good, but not quite up to Besito (which makes it at your table).  We then got a small tray which was plenty for the two of us (and we were really hungry neither of us having eaten since lunch and I'd gone for a work-out).  We had the Baja Fish Taco, Red Snapper and Thai Shrimp tacos and then a chicken tamale and pork tamale.  It came with a side of Chipolte Slaw and Pickled cucumbers.  The tacos were fine, though they go heavy on the cilantro.  I'm personally not a big cilantro fan.  The tamales were okay, not great and a bit dry plus they are pre-made to some extent.  They could've used some type of sauce.  The slaw, very spicy, the cukes a little less so.  Overall the meal with the drinks was $44.  It was okay, but to me this is not a place to go for the food, its for drinks, maybe small plates with those drinks and people watching.  They obviously are still working out the kinks to some extent.  Will we be back?  Maybe but there are a lot of places we like better.  Overall I gave it three stars, its not a 4 and could easily have been a two.

This place was an unexpected surprise and a beaming success on every level. The food was just incredible. I can't explain how generous and personable the staff is. I have a no-salt restriction and Shawn the manager, asked the chef to make many of the dishes for me without added salt. the managers were all incredibly personable and accommodating. They waited on us hand and foot and our server Dina, OMG Dina! was an amazingly funny, bubbly, interesting and lovable person straight out of the best 80's movie ever. She hung out , she talked to us, and was quite possibly one of the coolest waitresses ever. The whole staff was kind and attentive. We were blown away. The ambiance is akin to eating a seaside restaurant, the drinks are made with freshly squeezed fruits, the food is fresh, creative, and generous especially if you get the $33 large plate for two. It is packed with tacos, a huge, fresh Guacamole  (better than any Ive ever had)  cucumber salads, hand cut coleslaw..amazing tamales..it's too much to explain. Just go. Stop everything and go. It will be one of the most fun nights you'll ever have out. The bar crowd is great and the place was packed but because of the high ceiling you never had to raise your voice. The outdoor street diners got to enjoy the warm sun setting on the restaurant and the vibrant streets teaming with late Friday movie goers and diners in the great destination West Harford has turned out to be.

Felt like a big amusement park in Orlando (in a bad way..) Food was somewhat flavorful, drinks were way too small and overpriced as previously stated. But the servers were all horrible, all 25 of them, no smiles, robots, just enough eye contact to walk straight ahead so as to not get your attention, we waited 15 minutes for water refills and beer/cocktail re-orders. I waitered for many years during college years, but we never saw such a morose, pouty, self-loathing staff of servers, albeit all dressed with the same mail order catalog look. Overall, we won't go back and on the way home my wife and daughter were still hungry from the small portions so we stopped at a drive thru.
Did this place shutter? I tried to come last thursday for lunch, and the menu was gone and replaced with the japanese place next door. If not, they need to update their hours.
House of Small Wonder is aptly named.  Cosy, intimate, perfect for breakfast or lunch with a friend or lover, or by oneself.
Very cute, small spot!  Great room. Great food.

When do I ever give a brunch place 5 stars?   I met a fellow Elite for brunch here based on the reviews and the pretty pictures.   The place is so cute!  The seating is semi-cramped but not really that bad for Brooklyn.  It isn't presumptuous either which I find a lot of places around here to be. We both ordered the soup and the double sandwiches.  I had a little cup of corn soup with a mini croissant and parmesan eggs with rosemary and a tiny multigrain bread sandwich with avocado and homemade goat cheese. The food was delightful and we weren't rushed out.   There was not even a line at Noon on a Saturday! The cost was only $20 per person with tip and some coffees. The staff is very friendly and the atmosphere is very bright and lively.   The only complaint I have is not even a complaint.  The restaurant is hard to find because there is no sign and no way to know the location.  It is just shown on the outside as wooden panels on the corner of the block.

Good falalfel sandwich.  Line was a bit daunting today but the flavors tasted very healthy.  I'm not exactly a falafel aficionado (yet) but I had a good lunch.  It's a bit pricer than Pick a Pita but everything does feel a little bit cleaner and healthier if you are into that.  If it were me, I'd probably just go back to Pick a Pita since it's $2 cheaper.   Their packaging is really nice but I'd rather just get a paper wrapper if it meant I could save $2.

Just like I said, I returned to Entree again and guess what? It was all-around great this time! I'd say 4-4.5 stars overall, but since my last review was pretty scathing I want to even them out with a nice, 5 star review for them. It was actually New Year's Eve dinner, and a group of 8 of us dined at Entree. We called beforehand to confirm they'd have an ala carte offering, but when we arrived we only saw a fixed price menu. I asked our server and she said she'd check with the chef, who confirmed we could order ala carte if we wanted. Very nice of her to check and confirm. The food was very good, though a few items were on the salty side. The calamari app ($10) was delish, and many of us enjoyed the seared tuna main dish ($28). What I was really coming back for (besides the food, of course, which I knew was fantastic) was the service. And I can say I was not disappointed. The one waiter who had actually been helpful and nice the first visit was still there, which I was happy about, and our main waitress was very nice and attentive. It was a fairly busy day, and a holiday of course, and I was very happy overall with everything. The waitress did spill a bowl of mussel sauce on one of our group, but I didn't see it or the aftermath so I cant' say how it was handled. Honestly I thought it was somewhat funny to hear about, and clearly a mistake, so hopefully she apologized enough to make up for it. All in all, super pleased that my second trip back was a much improved version of my first. Will absolutely dine here many more times in the future!

The stereotypical NJ diner. Neon signs, cakes, smell of brewing coffee, cramp, noisy, greasy tables and waitresses calling you "honey" and "sweetie". Broadway Diner feels timeless. No one bothered to tell the people and management about the the turn of the century or the invention of the Internet. Food here is good, not spectacular or memorable. Pancake better than most average diners. Other selection is the typical diner cholesterol enhancing choices. This is the diner you go to if the first or second choices have 20+ minute waiting times. Nostalgia aside, the Broadway Diner is your destination. Come here with a group of friends, talk until the sun comes up.

By far the worst diner In jersey food sucks..service is terrible .. Opened a Up a ketchup bottle and there was liquid in the cap the fell all over my food!!! My burger was over cooked and tasted like cardboard the waitress wouldn't stop talking to the table in front of us and wouldn't even look at me wen u wanted to let get know they my burger was over cooked...place smells and not clean will never be back again!!!

Went here for a few after work beers. Stools taken so we sat at a table. Manager gave us some shit that if people want to eat we got to give up the table. And the place was 2/3 empty. Prediction: Place will fail because Manager is a Numbnut......... Just lost 3 good tippin regulars nitwit!

Stowe's Seafood is my one and only seafood place to go. Its super clean, has a simple menu, and everything listed is made impeccably. Soul & heart warming clam chowder soup, cod is cooked to perfection, and the fries are amazing. I love love love this place. It also is non-alcoholic which is a huge plus for me. Location is also amazing! super relaxing favorite place to go for me!

I love this place, it's so great.  A hole in the wall and dive bar feeling but it's wonderful.  Fair priced, don't expect the fine china and it's very much like something you'd find in a vacation town.

You can tell a lot about a seafood shack by how many oyster crackers they give out with their clam chowder. One or two measly oyster cracker bags? Have a heart! I'll be done with that in a few spoonfuls. Then what? Eat my clam chowder with no crackers? How dare you! Stowe's gave us ten bags of oyster crackers. They get it. The most important thing to know about Stowe's is that the lobster roll is $12.50. Yes, that's right. $12.50. Normally, I'd be suspicious of the freshness of such cheap lobster, but Stowe's boldly serves the lobster meat on a simple buttered roll with just a squeeze of lemon. Boom. Nothing to hide. So brazen--I love it! This confident simplicity extends to most of the menu items I tried--the greasy and delectable fried clam boat, the rich and creamy clam chowder, and the fresh cod. Basic seaside shanty food done very well. In seafood joint world, as with strip clubs and casinos, tacky = authentic. This seafood shack is decked out in over-the-top nautical kitsch--brightly colored buoys and plastic fish mounted on the walls, frayed fishing rope wrapped around every beam, and menu offerings scrawled in bright white letters on chalkboards behind the counter. It's perfect. Stowe's is West Haven's buried treasure and I'm so glad I found it.

Well hello there you sexy minx you.  Great spot for a few cocktails with friends.  Nice selection and menu of drinks and food.  Come on a night and you'll be sure to see a local foodie celebrity.   Don't forget to check out the chalkboard bathrooms downstairs.   Oh, and please wash your hands!

Quite possibly one of the best brunch meals I've ever had. Started the meal off with the deviled eggs with Picante seasoning which was delicious and not too mayo based. For our main meal we had one of the steak and eggs and one of the mushroom omelette. Both were amazing dishes that were complimented by some great fingerling potatoes. They also do some really creative brunch drinks.. (Try the Juice Diet !!! You won't be disappointed) Next time I gotta order the poached eggs with asparagus served with table side shaved truffles !!!!

Went for restaurant week with a group of 6. I think if I was rating on just service it would be 5 stars. Some of our party got there late and we kept switching the party size but our waiter was super nice and accommodating. One thing was we wish he told us about the happy hour specials while we were waiting for the rest of our party to arrive to order from the restaurant week menu. With that said the dishes on the menu sounded super cool: corn soup with Hudson valley fois grois, veal cheeks, braided rabbit, espresso creme de pot...everything was so ridiculously salty. All of us agreed and we were downing waters like crazy. Maybe we just went on an off day so with benefit of the doubt I would be willing to give this place another try.
Great great great brunch was fantastic just went yesterday can't be beat Had the funnel cake which isn't really funnel cake but a dressed up French toast it was amazing
Delicious meal! Try the flash grilled Caesar and the trout sandwich. Great service and atmosphere. Would definitely come back. Good find.

Friday night dinner with my wife. Had a 25.00 Restaurant.com certificate so that helped. The fact that the waitress forgot to charge for the wine was good for me! Didn't realize it until we left. They didn't give a regular check only cc receipt. Maybe because of the gift certificate. Food was good. Entree of chicken shrimp and veal was good but could have used another shrimp and maybe larger piece of veal. Wife had wholewheat pasta and shrimp dish that she loved. Very tight quarters with little room between tables. Piano clarinet duo were a nice touch.

My family and I have been dining here since 2001.  Never had a bad experience.  Service, quality and value of food always consistent.  This is a great place with a  warm comfy atmosphere. To customer/yelper Anna A that dined on Feb 3rd, you failed to mention in your review that the chef/owner did take $25 off your bill.  Before you write a review, please be honest.

Me and my friends love this restaurant, especially for lunch. They have authentic Chinese food, fast service (important for short lunch break!), and good price! Our non-Chinese co-workers like to come here as well as Chinese co-workers.

4 stars for overall, 3.8 for the food and 5 stars for services! First off, i really love the name, Chapter One. Intriguing :) Came to Chapter One on a hot Friday evening with my friend. It was actually our backup plan. But it turns out just fine as we would go to the first place, with a even more relaxing environment. Right off the 7th ave south and slightly tuck away on Greenwich street, this airy restaurant is an assuming neighborhood gem: a place you can stop by any night solo or with a good friend, ordering couple snacks and drinks just chill. It was before 7pm so place was not yet filled up. We took the last table that is situated half in-door and half out-door. Perfect for the summer night! Promptly we were served cool water, generously poured wine in the glass. Straight to the most important thing, food. So here we go: - Charred Octopus. This is very good, nice texture and smokiness. Seasoned with confit potato, dried tomato, meyer lemon. the honey mustard oil adds a nice kick to the meaty dish. - Skate bites with napa cabbage ­poblano slaw, jalapeno mayo. This is good but slightly drier than I prefer. My suggestion, lotion up with the jalapeno mayo! Can't miss veggies! We got the baby beets with vadouvan yogurt and cruchny cress. So colorful, almost too cute to eat. But don't hold your folk, cuz this baby beets are so sweet and juicy that you don't want to stop! Since we decided not to have entree, so we added two more small plates: - Beef tartare. Well, since I am not huge fan of meat, I only took a bite. All I can tell you is, it is beef tartare. But I do like how it is presented - square shape of tartare sits between cracker thin and crispy black garlic baguette, dotted with  pickled mustard seed, cress. Eye pleasing! - Smoke trout salad. this is another fave of the night. The fish is not too salty like I found in some other places, subtly smoky. I ordered a glass of crisp sauvignon blanc to go with it. Nice and simple. Most of the ingredients are locally sourced, including the wines. Whites are mostly from New York State, Cali; reds are from Argentina, Chile or Washington. I have to give a bravo to the staff. Our waiter, who I forgot to ask the name, was friendly and attentive. The GM checked on us to see if we enjoying our meal and offered the last round of drinks on the house! We are very happy girls :) Definitely want to come back and check out the brunch!

I walked past Chapter One over the weekend and have been wanting to try ever since, the interior looked really nice, modern and comfortable and the menu looked very interesting. I stopped by with a friend for dinner last night and was very impressed. First of all our server was amazing- very helpful, friendly and attentive. We opted for sharing some starters and sides over a main and were very happy with our choices. We ordered the Charred Octopus, Beef tartare, Skate bites and the Collard Greens. Everything came out very quickly, it was plenty of food to share and very delicious. My favorite part about the whole meal was dessert.. Apple Fritters with salted caramel ice cream- Insane. Will definitely be going back. Very interested to try the brunch menu!

So happy they are here! Great food, friendly staff, healthy food at great prices! Open late. Not many options in this neighborhood other than fast food especially late. Falafel really great, filling, for $3 ! Love the white sauce, I get it on the side for the fries, which are great and super light. I also recommend the chicken kabob, super soft chicken, grilled and seasoned very nicely, comes on a bed of rice with tomato, onion, pita bread, the amazing white sauce, a little green sauce and a little salad of chopped cucumber and tomato.  Really good and filling for $8

I've only been to the newly opened Kabob Shack once, but I was definitely impressed. When I think of Kabobs, falafel, and a shack, I think of Mamoun's. A seedy old hole-in-the-wall with delicious but questionably-sourced food. But this is no shack. Nothing here seems questionable. There's a gorgeously worn-in bench for waiting, one modest  wooden table, and counter stools for a quick bite. The place knows its hood, and appropriately hangs a chalkboard menu and local art, as would be expected in good ole willyB. I wouldn't have been surprised if that chalkboard menu said "Baked organic falafel on whole wheat pita - $6." But this place proves that its decor and menu are signs of caring owners, not hipster magnets. I got a $3 falafel that was filled to the brim and fried potatoes with a delicious jalepeno cheddar dipping sauce. Seriously, I HATE jalepeno, yet I continuously doused my potatoes in them. For the record, I think they used jarred jalepenos so my tongue was spared a burning. What I liked about the falafel sandwich (besides it's deliciousness) is that they put a little bit of red cabbage to brighten it up. It was thoughtful of them to add the gorgeous color to my sandwich, it really does make a visual difference. It's the little things that show me the owners put thought, time, and effort into their business. The only thing I can fault them for is calling it a Shack. It's really more like a cute little establishment. But I guess they couldn't call it Cute Little Kabob Shop.

Affordable Fresh food, great flavor. Luved the chicken gyro. Yummy.. My friends agreed too about their dishes :) Next time I will try the fries. Nice art on display by local artists Kristi Randall and Voodo Fe. Check them out while they are there

Had an absolutely amazing time here. Great service, great food, great drinks. The must orders: Cacio e pepe scrambled eggs (I still have dreams about these) Applewood smoked bacon Truffle mushroom pizza Lasagna (although I didn't like the fact that it was $5 extra PER PERSON. We went in a group of 10 so that's like 50$ more for the table? Seems a little silly) The DIY prosecco tray is amazing! I only took one star off cause their brunch items weren't that extensive to choose from and many options were off limits or at an extra charge. But all in all it's a lovely ambiance, with great food and polite service. Would definitely recommend and return!

Solid place for group brunch. And its one of those places that makes group meals relatively painless, $29 boozy brunch includes a few small tapas plates and pizzas to share.  Their truffle pizza and margherita pizza were pretty good.  Their DIY (Do it yourself) Prosecco tray was also very fun, as we could get creative and make our own drinks.  Would definitely come back.

my friend and i walked past this place while strolling the neighborhood. loved their AYCD and food combo offerings so of course I yelp'd it and bookmarked it for a future sunday boozy brunch visit! not sure if it was the waitress or something else, but our party of 6 had a terrible experience. I made a reservation for 11am. Our waitress (Tessa) reminded us (too frequently) how much time we had left at our table! this is quite possibly the first time EVER i've been told we would be kicked off our table as soon as our 90 mins of drinking was up. She offered to pack up our food (if we weren't finished). Um, thanks? We all got the $29 carafes -- about 3-4 drinks. It's $39 for unlimited/bottomless drinks. Also there is no option to upgrade from a carafe to unlimited -- upsell opportunity! To top it off, the bellinis and mimosas tasted like they had a splash of champagne -- as opposed to a splash of juice (the way all AYCD drinks should be)! However, the food is good here. We got two pizzas (forager and spicy fennel sausage), eggs benedict, frittata, bacon and roasted potatoes. All tasted great! on the fence about coming back to see if the experience changes because i feel like this place has real potential...

Stopped in for a quick bite and drinks with friends. From the moment we came in we were treated to a lovely setting, great service and good food. We chatted-it-up and never felt rushed. Must come back for the brunch - it's apparently something you should not miss!

Pizza for breakfast?   Sotto 13 has great brunch deals that comes at a prefix with drinks that you can make bottomless. Unfortunately Sotto 13 caps your morning drinkfest at 90 minutes but seems to be loosely enforced when it's your birthday. Came here for my big sis' bday, who wanted pizza for brunch and we came to the right place. Mushroom pizza with truffle oil and if you're missing breakfast too much then add an egg on top is delicious, especially to wash it down with your mimosa.   Don't care for pizza in the morning? The prefixes come with classic breakfast dishes.  Get the bacon well done if you like it crispy.  Lamb sausage was a bit too salty for me.  Skirt steak and eggs over a bed of crispy hash browns was on point. Very family style brunch, works perfect for bday brunch because you'll look forward to the siesta after all those mimosas!

More like 4.5 stars. Had a wonderful brunch with my husband here this past weekend.  The dining room with the skylight is beautiful.  You would think it would be hot in there with so much light shining through and the pizza oven nearby, but it was nice and cool the entire time.  We shared the sausage pizza, crab and eggs and opted for the french toast as our dessert.  Everything was delicious!  The pizza was super thin-crust so you have all the yummy pizza flavor without the added extra carbs.  The eggs with crab was creamy and briny with crab flavor -only wish there were more crab meat.  The best part though, was the french toast.  I'm not sure if it's the best french toast we ever had, but it's certainly the best french toast we can remember having this year (my husband and i are not usually into sweets).  i believe there were some eye-rolling to the back of the head involved.   The restaurant has several large tables that are good for large groups and a slightly elevated back dining room area that may be good for semi-private events - it's a bit loud though. Wait staff was efficient and onpoint, can be a little friendlier and personable, but by no means bad at all.  Trendy places like this can oftentime come with some attitude, and we happily did not experience that here.  The only negative is that the Bloody mary was a little weak.  Otherwise, highly recommend to come with a couple of friends so you can share many more plates.  I should imagine this being a great place to take out-of-towners as well.

Great spot for boozy brunch with a fun group where you can stroll over to Meatpacking immediately after for some Sunday rooftop fun.  For the price per person value, the family style food is totally worth it.  You get plenty of food and drinks.  The back area with the open roof/sunlight is also an added plus.

Good is amazing... Service is lacking to say the least. We had the steak and eggs, vege lasagna, and lamb sausage- amazing. The only problem is drinks take 10 minutes to get back to table. I would recommend this place but make sure they are sufficiently staffed prior to booking

I adore this place. I tried planning my birthday here a couple months ago and it turned out it was going to be the same day as their annual pig roast so I wasn't able to reserve a space or set up a "party" per say, but come down early and grab a table, the manager said, and you should be fine. I did and it was a perfect day - buckets of some superb craft beer, awesome barbecue, and being able to be outside in their back garden space on a beautiful August day. The staff is more than accommodating for large groups and everyone was lovely. I have since started to come here on Tuesday nights either before or after my soccer games around the corner and the place has become my new favorite NYC bar.  Both the happy hour bartender and the later evening bartender were knowledgeable and helpful. My boyfriend and I came in for a post-game beer one night and I met up with another friend for a beer and some dinner before a game one night and the food was great. We had a lamb sausage flatbread and a kale salad. Very tasty! I will be continuing to head to this super great bar.

After becoming a Num Pang addict and loving these Vietnamese sandwiches, I figure that I gotta see if anyone else can make a good one. The pork belly sandwich here is great! The only thing I can say is maybe they fall short on the amount of meat in the sandwich, but it is great nonetheless.
Bulgogi was juicy and tender. Have to try the pork belly next time.

I've been working at Elmhurst Hospital and Joju is a godsend! They deliver very quickly (~20 min), are super affordable, and have great food. Disclaimer: I haven't gone to the restaurant, only ordered delivery. So far I've had 3 kinds of Banh Mi (~$5) -- Classic, Bulgogi, and Pork Belly -- and their Kimchi fries. The banh mi are great but could be a little spicier for my taste and perhaps have some more mayo/aioli. The pork belly especially is deliciously fatty and is perfect with the pickled veggies. Also I have found that ordering in the late afternoon, the bread is a little tougher than when I have ordered at lunch time. The kimchi fries are out of this world, covered in not-too-funky kimchi, jalapeños, scallions, and spicy aioli. As for drinks, I've had their classic milk tea and Vietnamese coffee as well, which are solid and hit the spot but not amazing. They do give you a free drink if you buy 5 sandwiches too! Highly recommended.

What wonderful and unique culinary options have been brought to the Elmhurst area from the far east and south east Asia and beyond. As I decipher where to enjoy my next meal, new reviews continue to appear, in the form of new restaurant openings and places that have been established and are in receipt of most favorable reviews. Is this an inside job? How can so many restaurants be so good and so fairly priced, within 2.2 miles of my home and I am just catching this food trend now? But the fact remains, the food on Broadway seemingly concentrated just a few short blocks off Queens Blvd is outstanding. Eating my way around the area, I stopped into JoJu around lunch time to see what the options of Vietnam sandwiches were on the street side, daily chalk board. Upon completion, it was a right-face, forward march into JoJu. Being the bearer of a three star review pains me a little as I know they make wonderful food and people rave about it, but I can not allow prior reviews and thinking change my position. Not that I am throwing JoJu under the bus, but I did not feel an overwhelming experience that the 4.5 stars suggests. ~The crispy chicken wings at $1.00 each were heavily breaded and no dipping sauce accompanied my to go order. ~Pasta with peanut sauce (I am not properly reporting the name of the dish) was out of stock. ~Kakuni pork belly sandwich was enjoyable and for the money ($5.95) an exceptional value. ~Black Milk Tea-Bubble Milk Tea was very interesting but at $2.50, it seemed a touch hogh-perhaps by .50 cents. Overall, I have strong hope that my next meal will be worth an update of strong enjoyment. Service was top shelp from beginning to end and as mentioned in my tip, a runny fried egg adorned my sandwich, free of charge. Reatil value, I do not know.

I would give this place 5 stars but when I came here they RAN OUT OF PORK BELLY! How can they not have it?!?! That part was disappointing, so I got the JoJu Monster. The JoJu Monster is okay in my opinion. It was layered with Viet Ham, headcheese, pate spread and the bbq pork.  I barely tasted the bbq pork was in the sandwich. However, my boyfriend got the Beef Bulgolgi sandwich, and, oh my, that was delicious. This sandwich is off the hook! The sandwich is juicy and very flavorful. It's tastes so good with the pickled veggies inside the sandwich. We both got the extra free egg thanks to Yelp's check in! And I must say the runny egg does make a difference! The Banh Mi fries is probably the best fries I ever had, considering I do not like my fries "covered in things" (it makes the fries all mushy) but the bahn mi fries did not disappoint! It was still crispy even when it was covered with spicy green sauce, picked veggies, spicy mayo and other goodies. Must get if you do decide to go there.
Had the whole wheat penne with a pesto and salmon sauce. It was amazing!!!! My friend had gnocchi with pesto which was also excellent. Great service and nice atmosphere. Have to go back soon!

Having just returned from an extensive trip to Italy and living in the city for a long time, I have to say that Tavola is extraordinary.  I hesitate writing such a lofty review because I need this restaurant to stay just as it is,  fantastic in all regards!  From the beautiful and natural ambiance, to the fine service and most importantly to the authentic and finely prepared food with a sicilian style, Tavola is firing on all cylinders!!  The amazing, wood fired pizza and delicious salads are freshly prepared with the finest ingredients. The entrees are perfect portions also using local and top quality ingredients.  This is the real deal and it is right here in NYC!   Support them but don't overwhelm them.
I'm Italian. Very picky. Therefore I was surprised when I got a pretty good lasagna but their coffee is terrible. Nice ambiance and good people.

Logeant dans ce quartier relativement éloigné de l'animation de Mid Manhattan, ce fut pour nous une véritable surprise de découvrir ce restaurant  au cadre sympathique et à l'accueil chaleureux. La cuisine est digne de la gastronomie italienne et les prix sont  très raisonnables. Happy to give the first opinion written in French with a view to inform a larger public

While our pasta and salmon dishes were tasty, the service was egregious. The waitstaff was uninvested in our dining experience (no check-ins or true service). When we ordered dessert and coffee, the very mediocre coffee (tasted like instant crystals) was delivered, then we waited over 15 minutes for our cannoli to be delivered. Ultimately, because our waiter wasn't paying attention, we had to get up from our table to inquire about it. He swore it was supposed to be on its way -- then it never came. Ultimately, we asked for the check and the waiter told us he had never even put in the dessert order, which is why it hadn't come. No manager ever came over to apologize -- in fact, as we walked out the door, he was outside on his cell phone. Very disappointing for what seemed like a promising establishment. If you're considering eating at Tavola, I'd suggest getting take-out to avoid the service.

After being here three times I actually hesitate to give Tavola even three stars. The place is cute inside, nice homey feel, kind of a mix between a bustling brasserie and a corner neighborhood restaurant. But the food is, in my opinion, really average, and being that we are in Manhattan and not the middle of nowhere, average won't really cut it. The lasagna is good, but the grilled calamari was flavorless, and the pasta with eggplant was kinda dry. But most disappointing about this place is the waitstaff (not busboys - they are super nice and attentive) which is lethargic and uninterested. A few nights ago we waited 15 min to order a drink, then our waiter messed up and brought out one person's entree 10 minutes before the others, so the first person's food was cold. On top of that they stuck us in the corner where we could hardly get anyone's attention - like, waving our arms in the air to flag someone down. Sorry, I'm not directing airplanes tonight, Tavola. The waiters seem to all congregate and have their own happy hour at the end of the bar while their tables fight for their attention. Way too much effort to be a diner here. I give up and will easily find a better spot for dinner next time I'm in the area.

Despite calling in my order 24 hours in advance. when arriving to pick up my pane nero, the new guys at the counter all had no idea what I was talking about and confusingly directed me next door (I walked away, having assumed they had a separate bakery entrance; fortunately the guy in charge caught me and even offered up some EVOO on the way out). This is a unique, substantial, delicious hunk of gluten-y goodness. *$4.50 for a 2.2-pound loaf This brick oven spot near Penn was covered by the WSJ & NYT: "black bread from Sicily, that his grandfather made in Castelvetrano. It's made with tumminia, an ancient wheat flour grown only in that region and said to have been cultivated by the Greeks who settled on the island. The bread is called black because of the darkness of the crust. At Tavola, the sourdough loaves are baked in an oven fueled with olive wood and emerge dense, with an alluring touch of sweetness suggesting cornmeal. They keep well and toast or grill beautifully"

I'm raising my rating here, as more time and subsequent visits have shown that Tavola has developed into a reliable, sometimes great Italian restaurant.  Service has improved and is much more welcoming than it used to be.  They also remember to recite the specials!  I still wish they had a better beer list but oh well, it's an Italian restaurant. The menu has gotten a lot more interesting, especially the appetizers.  I stick mostly to the entrees though.  The shrimp and scallops entree is my go-to; I wish it came with more shrimp and scallops, but they do a great job otherwise.  Well seared scallops and large shrimp in a garlic sauce sort of like a scampi, along with some cherry tomatoes.  Nothing fancy, just simple Italian cooking.  The pizzas are good but not great, although I am a bit more critical when it comes to pizza.  Their market fish--frequently branzino--is served perfectly grilled; I'd recommend it whole.  Their whole wheat penne with salmon is also good even though that is not something I typically order. If you're stuck in Midtown--late at the office, stuck baby sitting tourists, legs broken--you can do a whole lot worse than this for Italian.  Tavola might not be reinventing the wheel but it doesn't have to.  They combine a mix of classics with contemporary Italian cooking to make something well worthwhile.  If you're looking for a go-to for Italian in this area, this should be it.

A couple years ago, I rated this place five stars. Sadly, that's no longer the case. Since being bought a month ago, this place has gone from good to bad to awful. There is no music playing anymore, almost all specialty drinks are gone, the cafe (in a prime location in Center City) now closes at 7 pm, and the espresso is so bitter that I actually threw my mocha away tonight. Touting the politics of your new coffee is irrelevant when it tastes like swill. The last thing Center City needs is another cold, stark coffee house with a generic menu, bad hours, and even worse coffee.
Beef Udon is great! Great prices and service is super quick even during the midtown lunch hours.

Food is good but I want to share my experience about dealing with the manager here, a middle age man with a beard. He was quite rude. He asked us to go to the table next to him because he saw me waving my hand to him telling him table for two, and he response with the v gesture by his hand. Right at the second we got to the table he said table for two over there and point at the table where we we're stand next to when we just got in. So I told him you just asked me to come over and he goes I talked to the other gentlemen and the waitress not talking to you. But how come he saw my and response with the hand gesture of table of two? Why you like to argue with customer so much? As a manager you may just say something nice and make the customers happy again. With this kind of experience, I would not come to this place again, even the food are good here, unless they change this unfriendly manager. Watch out guys

Although I saw the 4 star yelp rating, I was scared to walk in because of the restaurant's exterior.  I trusted in yelp, and was very glad that I did!  The food was cheap, yet good, authentic, and flavorful.  Service was excellent.  While it's not the prettiest restaurant by any means, the food, and prices, definitely make this restaurant worth going to.

Blu is one of NJ"s gems.  Each item on the menu is carefully thought out and expertly prepared.  I have eaten there many times and the experience has been consistently exceptional.  I love that it is a BYOB.  The service has always been very cheerful and accommodating.  If I could change anything, I would put another fish selection on the menu and bring back the olive cake with basil ice cream dessert (YUMMIE!).   Blu is definitely one of Montclair's best.

I've been to Cask a few times and always kinda eh.  There is nothing really appetizing for a vegetarian on the menu - hello, veggie burger!  Cheap and simple.  Sure they have a mac and cheese that you could order without bacon but that is soooo heavy (and fatty) or a pizza but it is so boring in flavor.  I got it once without cheese and it tasted like Wonder Bread.  I, like many other vegetarians I know, like a good brew but I rather choose a place where I can eat AND drink.  Beer selection is amazing but nothing special when you consider the other places in the New Haven and Hamden area where you can also get a good craft brews these days, and eat.  Bartenders and waitstaff are always very friendly, which is nice.  BTW- its kinda weird to get carded at the door.  Makes you feel like "you in da club".  Shouldn't the server be doing this?

I have to agree with Rachel H, about this place. She and I stumbled onto this place during a road trip to Amherst. The staff was super courteous and gracious, and oh yeah, the food rocked! I had a duck soup of some kind that was excellent, I also loved the decor. This will now be a destination place for me the next time I'm in the area.
Delicious food and great service.  Panang curry is a delicious restaurant specialty.  Would definitely recommend to friends!

If you don't have much time to read through a review then here's a quick scorecard: 1) The food here is very good (4.5 stars) 2) The portions are very small (1 star) 3) The pacing is slow (2 stars) 4) Staff is friendly, but due to space constraints may end up bumping into your chair repeatedly (1 star) 5) Pricing is very fair, $55 for a quality 5-course meal (4.5 stars) Overall Contra gets a 3 from me. I'd be interested to see how they develop since they'd only been open for 1.5 months when I visited. The portions are so small that you won't be full after five courses, so if you go to Contra hungry, I'd order bread for $3. (though I'm not sure how much bread they give you). The pacing was quite an issue for me and I started timing the lag between dishes. In between the 1st course and 2nd course it took them 14 minutes. Between the 2nd and 3rd it took 22 minutes. The desserts came out speedily which was nice. Contra chefs don't start cooking your next dish until they clear your plate which I think is somewhat silly. Hopefully they improve the pacing in the future. Overall the quality of the food and the pricing is good enough to make up for the restaurant's shortcomings. If they can work out the kinks with pacing and increase portions by 10-15%, Contra could turn out very good down the line.

The food was delicious, the wine was superb, and I am definitely coming back. I love the spacious dining area and the cozy bar. I've never had chicken that juicy and tender at a restaurant. I couldn't have asked for a better server.

The first time I went to Contra, it was a disaster. I live nearby and had wanted to try it for a long time, but after 90 minutes, my guest and I had only received our first course and were too hungry to wait for the next four. Contra had just opened, kinks were bound to happen, so I gave it another chance. And I am so glad I did!!!!!! The meal was absolutely magical. From the amazing homemade bread (extra $3, and SO worth it!) to the perfectly cooked chicken to the wonderfully unique and delicious desserts, I don't think that I've had any other meal that compares. Because of the slow pacing last time, I told the waitstaff that my guest and I had theater tickets for 8pm, and they did a wonderful job accommodating our tight schedule, getting us out in plenty of time for the show. In short, Contra is an incredible restaurant that is a welcome addition to a slower block on the LES. I can't wait to go back!

Love what this place is offering.  For $55, you get some very well crafted bites of food as part of your 5 courses.  No matter that you are eating chicken, monkfish and vegetables instead of aged beef, lobster and caviar.  The chicken we had was among the most perfectly cooked piece of meat Ive ever eaten any where including Michelin -starred restaurants in France.  The bread was solid and for $3, why not just order it.  one of the two desserts was the rare perfect balance of sweet, textural and acid (the apple graham crumble thing).  A supplemental Mangalista pork dish was a bit fatty, however the pork flavor was nice.  Overall, the chefs are offering you great value and they are paying lots of attention to a la minute cooking.  I imagine with a few more months of experience the Chefs will be able to develop depth of flavor in many of their dishes and fully settle into their culinary style.  At any rate, it was a fun and casual night out and I will return without a doubt.  A great find on the LES

Wow. Really good!!   We had some tuna and salmon rolls and then the Gran Marnier shrimp with the Chilean Sea Bass. The two dishes really complemented each other. More pricey than other Chinese restaurants but worth it. Service was good. Will be back soon

Fairly slow service but the best half-priced sushi around. Go on Tuesdays or Thursdays after 3pm for a 50% discount on all sushi. Two rolls are just around $12 total and taste much better than other Asian restaurants around. Not as much a fan of the rest of their menu. The shrimp tempura rolls are my favorite and definitely worth the price.

I often get boodae jjigae cravings, and this place has hands-down the best boodae jjigae in NY. Unlike other restaurants (kunjip, shilla, etc), HIT actually has boodae jjigae -- not simply the boodae jjigae meats and such added into kimchi jjigae.   It's delicious, and a good portion for $8.95. Try it next time you go!

Now I know why they're a "HIT"!! ^____^ This place on the ground floor inside an office building. You'll find a sign outside that says "Korean Food" with an arrow pointing to the building. Just go inside the building, pass by the doorman and you'll find this really tiny place. I must say they are tiny but have great lunch options of Korean food as well as heroes and sandwiches. I got their Spicy Pork with rice which was $8.95 and didn't expect much as it was a deli. However, when I got back to my office and opened the lunch box, I was surprised to find out that they pack in a great amount of food into that lunch box, I mean A WHOLE LOT. It contained rice, Spicy Pork (A LOT), and came with sides of shredded cabbage salad, macaroni salad, Japchae (Korean vermicelli noodles with veggies) and Soup) For a deli, the place is well-lit and clean with classical music playing in the background, food was decent, and provides friendly service (the cashier girl speaks perfect English and greets regulars by their name). I will definitely return to try other Korean home-made food like Bibimbap, Budae-jjigae, Dakgaejang, and a variety of fried rice dishes!! **CREDIT CARDS ACCEPTED AND NO MINIMUMS!!** **COLLECT 15 COUPONS (THEY GIVE IT TO YOU WHEN YOU PAY) AND GET A FREE MEAL ON THEM!! **

Hidden treasure! Great value for money if you happen to find your way to the back of the lobby of this office building. Especially the Bibimbap is great. Not as good as the real good stuff in K-Town, but for way less than $10, you can't beat the value.

Outside the building is a very small sign pointing to go into an office building. It's questionable and you might keep on walking by. But let curiosity get the best of you. When you walk in, you'll see an opening just behind the guard. Don't stop, just keep on walking through until you're inside a small 10'x10' standing space. The menu is large and clear. As you peruse the menu, you'll see the staff hard at work. HIT has been established here for a little over a year and a half now. When Koreatown is too much to handle, HIT is the perfect spot for some delicious eats. HIT offers a lot of soup dishes. Sometimes it can be hard to handle and some prefer to eat something a little more substantial. The Jeyuk Bokkeum ($8.95), stir-fried pork with vegetables in a spicy chili sauce is one option. It took about 10 minutes to put my order in, but during that time, I was able to make some friendly talk with the staff who are very nice. I was also able to save $1 on my meal by liking them on Facebook and showing it to the girl operating the cash register. When they handed me my bag, I was surprised that it was a hefty ~3 lbs. or so of food. One Styrofoam container included a complimentary clear broth soup with scallions. Clean and tasty with a nice onion flavor. The main plastic container included an assortment of items: - A generous serving of white rice, slightly sticky, topped with black sesame seeds - Slaw with chopped lettuce, carrots, cabbage, red cabbage in a creamy orange dressing. Light and refreshing to the palate. - Jap Chae - very soft sweet potato noodles, similar to cellophane noodles, mixed with carrot slices and scallion. It had a subtle saltiness from the soy sauce and sweetness, that made for a very enjoyable and fresh japchae. - Mac & Cheese - served cold, slightly cheesy slightly cream with a sweet flavor profile. - And then to the main entree: pork stir-fried with onions and carrots, then topped with scallions and sesame seeds. The pork was very tender and flavorful, with a hint of spice. I definitely would have liked the meat to have more heat, especially since the rice, slaw and mac & cheese would have been nice neutralizers to the heat. I was surprised at how fresh and delicious everything was. I was afraid that the food would be stale and old, since it didn't appear to get a lot of turnaround, but I stand corrected. HIT serves some delicious Korean food at very affordable prices. Forget Woorijip, HIT is my new go-to spot for quick Korean lunch food. And don't forget to get your coupon. When you collect 15, your 16th entree is free!

This little gem has been open in Wethersfield since 1982 and I have been coming here since it opened as a kid with my parents and now with my husband as most residents of this town.  It is now in it's second generation of ownership operated by the daughter & her husband.  You will still find her father in the back helping prepare all the food from scratch. No frozen chicken cutlets here!  The family uses the left over grinder rolls to make homemade breadcrumbs for the chicken breasts that they make into chicken cutlets, which they make fresh on a daily basis.   No short cuts here only quality ingredients.  I hear a lot of people make comments that some place they go to makes the best chicken cutlet grinders, but obviously they haven't made it to Wethersfield Pizza yet....once they have they always change their minds. They make Hugh meatballs too! And a really good eggplant cutlet. You can get them just with sauce, with some pasta or on a grinder...hey they will even put them on a pizza too. These grinders are so Huge you almost have to dislocate your jaw to get your mouth around them.   Because of this I usually end up pulling a couple chicken cutlets off my grinder and make chicken parmigiana two days later....but hey I'm not complaining. When you walk in the door here its like your walking into your Italian families home.  They remember their customers and you usually are greeted with a loud friendly HELLO! Yes, if you love overstuffed grinders this is the place.  Order the half.... you'll be lucky if you finish it.  They also make a simple pan style pizza, some nice salads with a homemaid dressing &  some simple italian pasta meals.....but, most people you see coming in order the grinders...you can't go wrong.

Great for pinball, good for classic arcade friendly, unique staff & patrons. Two things hold this back from 5. Arcade game variety & the food. While it is a great ale house and arcade...where it feels disconnected for me is the food. Visited several times since they opened and still leave wishing there was more emphasis placed on the pinball/arcade side of the business rather than their moderately expensive menu. For the price I thinks that there isn't a great value, and TONs of better options close by, perhaps if there was a 'eat and play' combo or something. Long story short. No other place like it in VT to my knowledge. If you have a bit of nerd in you and you like beer you will have trouble not having an epic time @ Tilt.

One of the biggest dining disappointments I've had in Connecticut!  Nothing like its sister restaurant in New Haven, this location features underwhelming food and the absolute worst and slowest service I've encountered lately.  Absolutely won't be coming back.
Simply awful. The potatoes were undercooked, meatballs tasted canned, fish was unfresh, lamb ravioli was gamy.  An enormous disappointment, given Ibiza's otherwise exceptional reputation.  Stay away!
Their dishes are large for tapas. Very delicious too. I definitely plan on going again.

This restaurant fails on every level.   The space is poorly lit and it looks dingy and dirty inside.  The lights that they do have are too bright and not well placed. The service was disinterested and very slow.  The waitress/hostess simply forgot we were waiting for a table.  We waited for about 30 minutes, a table opened up and hostess simply ignored us.  Thankfully the bartender was on the ball and asked us if we still wanted  a table.  As we were waiting at the bar the waitress/hostess was rushing around so much that the there was a hectic, disorganized feel to the operation.     Our food was merely OK.  By OK I mean it was not good, it was not bad.  We had the lobster mac and cheese, a spinach salad and veggie beef soup.  The mac and cheese was heavy on the cheese and light on the lobster.  For $19 I hoped for more lobster.  The salad had far too many onions in it, so many that they overpowered the rest of the flavors.  The soup was WAY too salty.  When I pointed it out to our server she just said "but it was ok, right?"  Well, paying $9 for a small bowl of soup, I would hope the kitchen would shoot for something more than simply "ok" but I guess not. I would not recommend this restaurant under any circumstances short of a complete overhaul.  There is a lot of talk about the fried PB&J.  Trust me, its not worth the trouble of dealing with rest of the operation.

I had high hopes for this place because the mac and cheese looked incredible! Sure it was pricey for cheese and noodles, but it looked like it would be well worth it. It was not. My first impression upon entering the restaurant early on a Monday afternoon was that it was freezing! I am not someone who gets cold easily, but I was shivering. I know it is expensive, but it may be time to turn the heat on. I also noticed that the restaurant as almost completely empty. We were quickly seated and our waitress was very pleasant. My friend and I both ordered the mac and cheese with caramelized onions and bacon with a glass of Malbec. While we were waiting for the food I had the misfortune of having to use the restroom. It was pretty terrible. It looked like the restroom at a dive bar, not a restaurant that charges $13-21 for a dish of mac n cheese. I came back to our table and found that our wine had arrived. My glass was filthy! It was covered in some sort of white dust. My friend also ordered wine, but her glass was passable. I tried to suck it up and drink the wine, but when I noticed the dust floating in the wine (on top of the cork that was also swishing around in there), I decided to ask for another glass. I went to find the waitress and she very very nice about bringing me another glass. There was still a lot of cork in the wine, but the glass was much cleaner. The mac and cheese was extremely thick. I had no idea that it was possible to get mac and cheese that is too cheesy, but it was. I felt like I was eating a block of cheddar. The chunks of bacon were enjoyable, but it didn't seem like there was that much in there. The dish cost $16. It was a lot of food, but it wasn't that large for the price. Regardless, I was definitely full. Overall, the restaurant seems like it could use a major face lift and a little TLC. I paid $25 for my lunch and left wishing that I had gone to Farmhouse.

Came here with my significant other for our anniversary dinner last week! We were really excited because we've never had JBBQ before. Called in a reservation and arrived right on the dot but when we arrived, I guess the hostesses (there were two) were a tad new because they didn't immediately seat us. We were standing there awkwardly for like 2 minutes... And their attempts at blurting out Japanese phrases while the other was talking to us in English, was really weird. When we were finally seated, everyone was staring at us and then also blurted a Japanese phrase to us once we passed the bar. It startled me at first and I was pretty scared. We decided on the Kobe Style course from the menu and began our meal. Our server, David was really nice and helpful for the most part. When our food came out, it was given to us by different servers, although nice, after the first couple of dishes, they stopped telling us what everything was and how to cook it. When it got time to cook our meats, we were unsure of what we had just gotten, and for how long we should cook it for. We even accidentally turned off our burner because the flames scared us and got too big. It wasn't until we finally just asked our server who came around soon after what we should be doing. From there, everything on our end went smooth. When we had cooked everything, our server came and asked us if we were ready for our desert. My SO was, but I wasn't, but we thought it'd be okay to have it sit there on the end of our table while I finished the rest of the cooked meats for the next 5 minutes. I guess not? Before I knew it, a server swooped in and just took my plate away, filled with meats that were cooked but I wasn't finished eating with... T_T" Where are you going?! My eyes followed him in slow motion as he walked away... I sat there in awe, and couldn't mouth out anything. He was super quick, like a ninja.... I guess we had no choice but to start on our desserts... It was smores. Nothing special, but pretty cute for the night. After that, we had just paid and left. Still crying about the steak that was never finished. Would only come back for a special occasion, but the food was pretty good. Really pricey though, so unless there are specials, or we were balling, we'd come back for seconds. Will definitely stalk online for any news about this place though, since we did come in the second week of them opening.

Poor customer service . Booked a table two days ahead and when we arrived they said they couldn't find our reservation in the system (even though I confirmed twice with the guy on the phone) But glad that they still have us seated at the scheduled time. The food is delicious, best beef we have ever had. But the waitress rushed everything the whole time. When we were still grilling the final pieces of beef, our waitress asked us what we wanted for dessert. One minute later, mochi ice cream was served. Another one minute later, she gave us the bill when we hadn't started the dessert yet.   They should definitely improve their service to live up with their name. We expect a Japanese restaurant to have the very high standard of service.

Came here with some friends on a Thursday night. I was a bit late, so when I arrived they had already ordered fried shrimp dumplings which I can't speak for (allergic). I ordered the French fries with cod caviar sauce which was pretty good. The sauce is quite addicting. My friends each ordered a plate of scallop, and a plate of beef. I ordered the Toro beef with shio white soy and New York strip steak in miso. Both cuts of meat were good but I wasn't really a fan of the marinades that I got. The side of sesame oil with sea salt I ordered, along with the table condiments, did not help the beef. I ended up using the cod caviar sauce from my French fries. The sausage fried rice bibimbap we got to share was pretty tasty but it came after we bbq'd. We ended our dinner with three orders of the green tea mille crepe. The portions are huge! We ended up taking our cakes home, but they were delicious along with the ice cream. It was about $50 per person for one cocktail, one appetizer, two plates of bbq protein, one dessert, and a rice to share. Overall, the food was good but a bit pricey. The random Japanese that the staff blurts out can take some getting used to, but our server was great nonetheless.

Came here for dinner last Friday. I called ahead to make reservations, but there was still about a 10 minute wait when we showed up. We were seated in a booth which was a little awkward to get into, and there isn't much leg room because of the grill. Our server was okay... She didn't seem like she had much experience serving though - she couldn't remember what the sauces were on the table, and didn't know what the specials were on the menus. When we asked for suggestions, she kept saying that it was all "personal preference." She turned on our grill, but didn't put enough oil on it since the meats kept sticking to it. We had: 1. Spicy miso chili wings - Very soggy. The wings literally tasted like reheated wings nuked in the microwave. There wasn't much flavor at all. 2. Fried bacon chips - Don't be fooled - it's actually tiny (less than an inch wide) pieces of pork belly, lighted coated and fried. Not what I expected because I thought it would be actual bacon as opposed to pork belly. (I know it's the same thing, just sliced differently. But...it makes a difference...) 3. French fries with cod caviar sauce - this was enjoyable but not many fries. The presentation of the sauce looked like someone was dipping in it previously. (The sauce was splattered around in the vessel.) That made me very paranoid. 4. Kalbi short ribs (in tare sweet soy sauce) -  I did not think this was actual kalbi. It was more like thin strips of a random cut of beef... Sauce was okay. Smaller portion than shown in photo. 5. Yaki shabu (in miso sauce) - flavorless and also smaller portion than shown in photo. 6. Beef Sukiyaki Bibimbap - Rice was too soft and there wasn't much beef. Just tasted like hot pepper paste and rice. The bibimbap was definitely NOT cooked in the dolsot since the edges were not crispy and burnt. They claimed that this was "prepared table side" but really the server just mixes the rice around for you. 7. Scallops - Eh. Nothing special. 8. Asparagus - Did not arrive. 9. Corn - Did not arrive. 10. Mushroom medley - Did not arrive. 11. Sparkling water - Gyu-kaku charged us $8 for a 16 oz bottle of sparkling water. Are you fcking kidding me?!?? Even some of the best BYOs in the city charge $5-$7 for a 32-33 oz bottle. This pretty much pissed me off. The server only asked us how we were enjoying dinner when she brought the meats out. By that point we had only received the fries, wings, and bacon. We eventually had to wave her down to tell her to cancel the veggies since they never arrived and we were basically done our meal. She acted confused and looked at our table trying to find them, then said there must have been a mix up in the kitchen. When we asked for the check, I had to ask her to remove the vegetables and honestly was surprised that she didn't offer to take it off the bill first. Overall, service was below average, and food was extremely mediocre. Don't know if I would come back - such a shame because we had high hopes for this place.
Love this spot... What a great addition to the neighborhood! The oysters are the best in the city and the staff is super-friendly. Will def be back.

Great time at a great place! Staff was very friendly.  Amanda was our server. I recommend her highly.  She was very knowledgeable and helped us w our dinner decisions.  We had the oysters for an app.  Had to try em, they were perfect.  I had the trout, which was delicious and my date had the old bay burger, another solid choice!  Also the drink and wine list were great as we tried drinks from both.  I Will be back!!

Yet another new Mediterranean/falafel joint in the city.  Perhaps it all started with the street carts, monitored and executed by immigrants trying to make a living.  Then someone recognized that there's a needy market out there for this grab-and-eat sandwich, so brick and mortar places started to pop up like daisies.  Once upon a time, you could score a falafel sandwich for just $1.50, but now with all these organic and sustainable messages, you might have to pay $8 and upward nowadays for a decent sandwich.  While there will always be the 'cheap' rendition of the fried chickpea mash and sliced, marinaded meat, if you need a sit down place, you're never far from one.  Hence we have another hummus location.  Well, the title said 'hummus', but unlike the Hummus Place, the star IMHO is the meat.  There are gyro, shawarma, chicken, steak, and taboon (chicken/steak from taboon oven) and only a slight mention of hummus on the menu.  Nevertheless, this place is great for vegans/vegetarians because of all the interesting fill-ins, which unlike Maoz, is assembled by the busy staff behind the counter.  Though they did not go cheap with the fillings.  They really try to stuff the pocket of pita or lavash wrap to the fullness.  Oh and the bread, of course. Everything is baked in house in their taboon oven, roaring continuous to leaven up the doughy casing for your protein. So glad there's even whole wheat pita available! Love that.  I even bought an extra pita (50 cents). There are lots of spaces for eat in.  As they just opened last week, everything looked brand new and clean.  The staff is still learning the rope around the kitchen and not all menu items are available yet. The meal won't be as cheap as the dollar pizza joint a block away, but everything is freshly made, spacious area to dine inside, and just glad it is not another fast food or chain restaurant opened in this space. I look forward to return and try the hummus, but not as an afterthought, but as my main dish.  Hint hint.  Please include a hummus plate option on your menu!

Just ate at a great fast food restaurant in the Chelsea area that opened this week to raves from all the customers I sat next to.  I'm very impressed with their congenial staff and delicious reasonably priced food.  I highly recommend this unique eating experience and can only say if in its first week the lines were out the door this place is a homerun.  Can't wait to come back for lunch.
All I can say is OMG! The food and the staff were amazing! I highly recommend. The meat was tender and fresh. The baked goods were off the chart!!!

I went to Hummus and Pita last week and I absolutely loved it. The service was great and the food was fresh and delicious.  The chicken was tender and tasty and the falafel was perfect. Another great thing about this restaurant is the pita and laffa bread is made on site so it is warm and ready to be filled with their variety of ingredients. If you aren't familiar with the ingredients they are offering you don't have to worry...the staff is extremely friendly and will explain what everything is and even how it is prepared.  Not only is the food great but the restaurant is clean and has an extremely comfortable environment. The only negative thing that I can say about this place is that it is not closer to where I work!
I was in NY for a week., a friend told me about this place. The place was clean, food was awsome and the staff was amazing.. Will good back when in NY!!

Been there 3 times and enjoyed every visit. First I came by myself and was so impressed that next time I invited my family and than couple of our friends. Here is my normal breakdown of my rating: -Food: so far we tried falafels, beef gyro, chicken shawarma, taboon, hummus, salads, Spanish eggplants, Moroccan beans, bourekas and dessert. Everything is handmade to order, so fresh, taste health and delicious. I love home made pitas and laffas, hot and tasty. Every time I bought extra to bring them home for my household enjoyment. Food is very fresh and consistent. I think they have best hummus and shawarma in town. -Décor: very tasteful, cozy, clean and charming. Great inviting atmosphere. It was a real pleasure to have our meal there. -Service: efficient and very hospitable. People are helpful and the manager kept checking up if everything is OK. I found great energy at this new place. -Price point: price is cheap for this variety and quality of food, especially in the city. On behalf of myself, my friends and my family I want to say Thank you, 'Hummus and Pita Co'. Great job! I would recommend going to this restaurant hands down. It is authentic, nice, has fresh, healthy food, grate selection of Mediterranean dishes and every aspect to become one of the most popular places in Chelsea. Try their baklava and almond cookies! I'll be back soon. Anna from New York.

I came in during the lunch hour and i wanted some toppings on my chicken taboon laffa but the guy putting it together was so frustrated over the fact that i requested an extra ''fill it'' on my sandwich he actually sucked his teeth and went on to the next customer like I was nothing. Thank goodness the kind young man at cashier was attentive enough to quickly throw on gloves and easily complete my order as I requested. He even offered me a free freshly made desert as an apology for his coworker's miscue which I've buying everyday since. Despite the rude guy rushing people, My overall experience there gets a strong 4 stars due to that young man's customer first service and the food being delicious and fresh as advertised. However, I must say this place really needs to reconsider some of the people they have working in the front as they have either attitude and/or language barrier problems.

I went with my sister, the vegan.  She thought the food was fresh, healthy, and of good variety.  That's like the highest vegan honor ever!  I thought it was delicious.  Also, there was comfortable seating which is hard to find in New York and especially in this area.
The food was amazing and very comfortable seating.

One of the better hummus places that I ate at. I use to go to Pita Joe on 14th St and 5th Ave before they closed and became something else and I like this place better. Nice space..clean...I agree with the other Yelpers that the staff can be friendly and more helpful when you're ordering.

Where do we start on the story of me vs. The Hummus & Pita Co? If you're into being treated fairly and respectfully at an establishment you choose to spend your money at, please read this. It was love at first sight (as in I'd given it 5 stars). I loved the interior design and the name told me that it must have been designed by someone Israeli (it was, hi, Haim!), and considering that I'm Israeli and love Israeli food (if prepared right), they had me right there. And yes, it looks and feels Chipotle'ish and that's what they're going for, and I love Chipotle, so plus plus and plus again! I fell in love, eyes closed, chewing on my yummy falafel with all the "Fill Its" I wanted because it was the opening week and the staff, not just me, was confused on the proper allotment of these "Fill Its." Could they have picked a better description for these? Yes. Could they have a better designed menu? Yes. Could they have a better layout for the food as to not incur charges that you don't expect at the register? Oh, YES. But I was blinded by my love; I couldn't see the flaws. I chose to ignore them. I ignored one of the owners mean looks in my directions and came back a second time (it's owned by two brothers, one nice and one mean looking Ed Hardy type big biceps evil squinting mean mugging me who refuses to wear the brown uniform everyone else is cause he's a baller? I don't know, but you get where I'm going with this). This time the generosity with the "Fill Its" wasn't there because I happened to have Mr. Ed Hardy helping me out and although he warned me that I'm going above the allotted amount, he still gave me the extra because I didn't understand their menu even on the 2nd time. Third time, I exchanged hellos with the Nice Brother who does wear the brown uniform, while the Mean Brother sat in the corner mean mugging the whole restaurant. Ok, whatevs. I like the food, the tables are made from recycled bowling lanes and it's semi cool. BUT today was the worst restaurant/food experience I've had in 6 years in NYC. I brought two friends from the gym talking up a storm on how good this place is. We worked out; we were hungry; we wanted food. You know like in Chipotle, you get in a line, you watch it being assembled and you're done. I got my food but when asked for a glass of water, which I do get at Chipotle, I was told they don't do that anymore, ahem... ok... my friend #1 got the food, my friend #2 was waiting for her food. I got the falafel platter and didn't get the pita that comes with it. Had to remind them twice, still didn't get it. Ok. We wanted beer. Friend #1 paid for what she thought was everything.  Friend #2 still waiting and waiting. And waiting. When her food finally arrived to the register for her to pick up, we found out from the cashier girl that it wasn't paid for. Ok, misunderstanding, confusion, no biggie right? The cashier didn't hear it and my friend was pulling out her wallet a bit frustrated because it's very disorganized. At this point the Mean Brother comes up and says this: "STOP ABUSING THE GIRL. SHE MADE A MISTAKE," I was a bit confused. Who's abusing who and where is it happening? And then it went major downhill from there with threats of calling the police were yelled out and he literally was trying to kick us out from there. It was the absolute opposite of "the customer is always right" experience, more like "the customer is definitely not right cause I'm the boss here." My friend got upset, understandable, because she was accused of abusing the cashier (she didn't. Gimme a break, it's NYC, if that's abuse I don't know what to call that groping that happens every day on the train) and she didn't get her food on time. She said she wanted to leave the place but we already got our food and the beer was open. He was screaming in the middle of the restaurant in front of the customers and saying "you abused her, she was on the verge of tears" which was astonishing! I tried to resolve this by calming him down, to no avail. The Man should never ever work with customers or even be in that restaurant. His behavior was unspeakable. At some point I thought he was going to get physical with us, 3 women. It seemed like he had so much pent up anger that he just needed to get it out. He refused to refund our money since we couldn't leave our friend outside while we ate and provided no resolution, like "i'm sorry for this misunderstanding, I'll pack up your food to go." The General Manager came out and tried to tell him, "Let me talk to them," but no, Mr. Mean had to tell us "Get out and never come back!" The GM apologized and was a nice guy trying to calm the situation down but the owner, the Big Boss, had to have it his way. If I could give your customer service skills a star, Mr. Meanie, you'd get a big fat 0. I suggest you invest all that money you're making in some anger management classes and train your staff.

We went with our groupon which was expiring that day.  The rules said to make a reservation & we hadn't.  It was a friday night & they were booked.  Nonetheless, they did everything they could to accomodate us & we were able to enjoy a meal. Good Service - friendly staff -  great host!

Went here for Friday night dinner.  We made reservations which was good because it was crowded.  The place is small and tightly packed but once you are seated, you should be good. T ordered the Ginger Scallion Dumplings and I the Jasmine Rice Salad.  The dumplings were very hot but evidently delightful and my salad was fresh and had perfectly pan seared tofu and a delicious curry peanut dressing. For main entrees, T ordered the Jatujak stir-fry and I the Panang Curry with tofu.  WE were both slightly concerned about the portion sizes because they looked rather small.  But by small, I actually mean perfectly sized and once we finished eating, we were both full but not uncomfortable, as so often happens to us when we eat yummy food.  The main courses were very flavorful, although T wanted more spice and I wanted less.   The staff was really nice and they were filling our water like crazy. While everything was tasty and the service was good, there wasn't really anything that stood out about Jasmine Rice.  It is a very solid Thai restaurant and if I happen to be in the area and craving Thai, I will definitely be back but I wouldn't go out of my way to do so.
Love. It. Take out is quick and always hits the spot. Owner is super friendly and if you bite the bullet, the Thai spicy burns in all the right ways. Brown rice is extra though =(

What a fabulous lunch I had there on Monday! From the smiling bartender seating us to the friendly and helpful waitress to the amazing food- great experience. We were in a little bit of a hurry and the service pace was perfect. We ordered off the 10 for 10 specials and they were delicious! I got the flank steak over mashed potatoes and my guests got the Cajun chicken and Italian meatloaf- not a bite left over it was so good. Our server finished off our lunch telling us about the killer happy hour and daily dinner specials and provided us with take home dinner and lunch menus. Highly recommend this restaurant for business or pleasure and we are definitely trying out dinner.
Love the decor, very cute and chic. Service is friendly yet concise, just the way I like it. And of course the food is awesome. Grass-fed beef and perfect medium rare lamb chops? hello.

Few days ago my friend and I decided to find something new, something interesting. The Eddy was the place that we have choosen. And we didn't regret! Situated in the East Village, having just a couple handfuls of tables, with lovely decor. Food and drinks were unexpectedly tasty. That's what we were looking for!

Friendly bartender, server and support staff! The location is superb and the decor is welcoming and homey. Had a great meal with unique twists and turns to the expected. I really enjoyed the fun drink options, salmon rillettes, scallop appetizer, chocolate ice cream and panna cotta desserts. Definitely recommend as a great place for a unique drink or fun menu experience.

Came here for a friends birthday and the 4  of us did the tasting menu. Everything was delicious and definitely worth the price! Waitress was great and drinks were delicious as well. Some stand outs were the scallop crudo, cuttlefish (must get), and gnocchi. Lamb belly was awesome too. Save room for dessert because the cardamom panna cotta is amazing! Will definitely go back.

YUM.  I typically hate overpriced over-thought out food at trendy restaurants but the tasting menu at The Eddy may have changed my mind.  Each dish was more interesting and delicious than the last.  I literally could not pick a favorite.  Great cocktails, great service (even with our party of 8), great atmosphere. Definitely worth my stingy dollars.

Had a great time at The Eddy. Intimate restaurant with a mixologist on hand serving bright and inventive cocktails that fittingly kicked the off the evening for our group. The refreshing bourbon daisy drink arrived in a lovely antique tea cup and my wife's parlor friar beverage was likewise delicious. Executive Chef Brendan's eclectic dishes were skillfully executed with the pillowy gnocci, pickled ramps and char rillette particularly tasty. Overall, a wonderful relaxed evening and we will certainly return soon.
Enjoyed a great night out with friends - JG will do very well!

We dined here, a couple weeks after the grand opening, to see how Jose Garces does 'New American Tapas.' For fans of the slow food movement, JG Domestic strives to use only ingredients that are domestically raised/produced (with exception of a few wines), and the menu's second page lists which ingredients come from which farms. Our waiter mentioned that he thought six people was the perfect number to dine here, because you'd could get a wide range of dishes but everyone could still sample a bit of every dish. Things got very confusing, though, when we tried to figure out just how much to order. Plate sizes are different across the board, and it wasn't easy to tell what dishes were easily share-able... don't be afraid to ask your server. We ended up each getting a main protein entree and a combination of eight 'warm plates' and 'vegetable' dishes to share amongst all of us. Oh, and even though you'll get them no matter what, it's worth mentioning how delicious the dinner rolls were- especially with their terrific butter and apple jelly. Highlights from the small plates: - Lobster Cappuccino: Dumplings in a vanilla consomme, not good for sharing but really wonderful - Heirloom Potato Cassoulet: Cooked with with sausage, shredded cabbage, and cheddar - Keswick Creamery Fondue: if you love cheese (and why wouldn't you?) this was sublime. We were scraping the tiny skillet for the last remnants of fondue I would pass on the Kabocha Squash, the Brussel Sprouts, and the Blue Crab Gratin-- they were rather underwhelming and unsubstantial. I thought all our protein dishes were wonderful, though: - Elk with huckleberry jus (a daily special): It was my first time eating elk and it was sure tasty   - Roased Jidori Chicken: Super moist and flavorful, and a huge portion- enough for two people - Lamb Spareribs with Country Fried Apples: Tender & delicious A nice place for a splurge dinner -some really unique dishes, and great service- but it's a little random to venture out to the Cira Center on a weekend night, and there are other Jose Garces restaurants I'd go to first before coming back again.
