I'd been a fan of Rae, the previous occupant of the Cira Center's ground floor space, and was excited to learn that Jose Garces would be opening a new spot in its place.  I arrived early for a 5:45 reservation and sat at the bar to soak in the atmosphere.  It was around 5 on a Friday and there were lots of people enjoying happy hour.  I ordered a City of New Orleans cocktail which was well-made and a great aperitif.   Once my friend arrived we were seated by the friendly hostess at a table near the open kitchen.  The interior is largely the same as it was when Rae was the name on the door, except with lots more wood and old farm implements to try and give the space a more rustic feel.  "It's like going back to an ex-boyfriend", my friend remarked as she glanced around the room.  Our table must have been right under an air vent because it was a little cold as we were waiting for the server to stop by. Our server was very enthusiastic and explained the menu to us.  I asked about wine pairings and she briefly left to talk to the sommelier.  She returned and recommended a couple of bottles of wine, one was around $150 and the other close to $100.  I was relieved  when she said "If you're thinking about something by the glass..." and she pointed to exactly the wine I had been contemplating.  "We'll take two glasses." We started with a cheese plate which was very good, and the Maine Lobster Cappuccino which was like a bisque with a couple of squash dumplings floating in the broth.  All of the ingredients and wine are sourced from the United States, which is a nice theme.   The server told us that they recommend ordering a meat or fish and a vegetable or two to complement the protein.  So we ordered the Arkansas Wood Oven Rabbit, which was the whole animal special that day, and the brussels sprouts with bacon.  The brussels sprouts were dropped off, but where was the rabbit?  Weren't the vegetables supposed to complement the meat?  Rather than let the brussels sprouts get cold I dug right in.  They were toothy and tender, could have used a bit more crisp, but tasty.   The real star was the whole rabbit.  4 parts; hind legs, rack, loin and front legs were prepared separately and plated together.  My favorite was probably the hind legs.  They were moist and tender and smothered in a delicious brown butter and sage sauce.  All in all JG Domestic has a lot of good things going for it, just need to iron out some service inconsistencies and maybe see about getting that A/C turned down.

The key to this place is in its name "Eatery" We came here for drinks mainly, and that turned out to be a mistake.  The drinks were awful. Steve Laycock, who supposedly is the regular bartender and has had good review, was down in DC this night, so I can't comment on what his stuff tastes like, but whoever was behind the bar was making drinks that tasted awful.  Among the 3 of us we tried 5 of the featured cocktails, passing them around and making strange grimaces at each-other. Non of them were very flavorful, distinguished, or good. However, the cooks at this place saved the night!  The food here was fantastic and very tasty. If we had only ordered food here I would have given it 5 stars. The seasoning and spices, as well as the quality of food used were all top notch. In-summary.  Go for food, this place is great. Just don't order any drinks.
So new for this city. Go and enjoy it all!

Cute little place in the East Village. Food was good but portion size was a little small. We ordered the oysters to start and I was a little surprised it was only three to an order. I do recommend the duck salad, good portion size for dinner or can easily share with 2-3. Drinks were good but a little on the pricy end and nothing too fancy with them. If I'm going to pay $15 I rather go to a speak easy to be perfectly honest.

DINNER REVIEW: I was looking for a place to take my parents/family to dinner that was different from our usual dinner venues. My friend recommended Ducks Eatery so I decided to give it a try. I was definitely skeptical at first because some of the food items were out of the ordinary but I don't usually get to pick the venue so I was really hoping that my suggestion would impress. I made reservations for 8 people the morning of, and was seated by dinnertime without any issues. Considering that it wasn't very spacious, they were able to seat us comfortably, which was a huge plus for me.  My parents, being HUGE food critics, absolutely loved the food here.  We ordered almost half the menu from small plates to entrees to dessert.  Not every dish was big hit, but for the most part 80% of the dishes were delicious. HIGHLY recommended: Crispy Pig Ears, Bone Marrow, Smoked Whole Goat Neck, Smoked Duck and the St. Louis Ribs. Don't forget Beignets for dessert! Recommended: House Pickles, assorted (only if you're into that sorta thing).. and of course, Blue Point Oysters, which were really fresh. (Still not worth the price unless you feel like splurging). Not recommended:  Yakamein Soup and Chicken Wings. Yakamein Soup was just whatever and their chicken wings were below average, a little too much "hickory" for my liking. They were also under-cooked so we had to send it back to re-cook. The ambiance was nice and trendy, a little dark but not enough to bother you. I would've given this place 4.5 stars if it was possible but I left it at 4 stars only because it didn't blow me away.

Whole Curried goat's neck IS the best thing i've eaten all summer. After we all took our first bites of the goat, we all just looked at each other in silence; no one knew the words to express that first bite. Finally my friend said: "Why doesn't all food taste this good?".

There are three reasons why this place is getting four instead of five stars. 1) the servers weren't attentive: - did not offer to refill our waters, we had to wave them down several times - took a long time to get their attention to get our check / boxes for leftovers - didn't check to see how our meals were 2) as hip as this place is, they have no non-dairy milk options 3) the coffee wasn't that good Everything else was amazing. We started with the buttermilk biscuits which were hot, flaky and fresh out of the oven, served with butter and honey. Our food came out quickly, even though our biscuits came out before our friends'. My husband and I then shared the ricotta grits which were in the difficult to achieve "Goldilocks Zone" (not too think, not too runny). It seemed like they were cooked overnight in heavy cream, unlike many places that use water and think that they're not committing a crime against humanity by doing so. The ricotta really amplified the flavor and texture of the grits, too. I ordered the brisket sweet potato hash. It had a little heat, but not too much, and the brisket was tender and pulled apart like it should. The fried eggs that came on top were cooked perfectly, and the sweet potatoes were nice and soft without being mushy. They open the front windows all the way on nice days and have a small patio, which is a welcome addition in NYC. Too bad the servers left so much to be desired.

I've had my fair share of ramen growing up from the pack, but these are certainly NOT from the pack. I went with a friend and we both ordered the Tonkatsu ramen (original) and a takoyaki. The takoyaki was just OK to be honest. It could have been more flavorful and a bit crunchy instead of chewy but the flavor profile was a bit bland so that certainly could have been a bit better. In terms of the ramen though, the noodles are certainly sub par. You can tell that they are not made on site and even if they guarantee fresh noodles, it's not quite good. However, I will commend their absolutely delicious broth. The flavors from this broth were AMAZING. The chashu was also very tender and delicious. Overall, the highlights of this meal was their broth. I could just drink a whole bowl of that (with a lot of water) on the side as well. The ambiance is also very nice and super modern which I like but it fills up quick around 6PM so when my friend and I came at 5:30ish, we were still good for a table. PHEW. Overall, great experience and I will certainly come back again!

So Ramen Bar just opened 2 days ago but I predict that once word spreads, Penn undergrads will swamp this place 24/7. So visit soon, while the wait is still on the magnitude of 10's of minutes. The decor here is pretty classy, as are the serving dishes and such: octagonal vermilion chopsticks, fancy Japanese stoneware noodle bowls. Even the spoon (or rather, wooden ladle) that comes with the ramen is like something straight out of the Edo period, though it makes it a bit difficult to get at the bottom of the bowl. Anyway, about the food. The fried octopus balls are pretty good, though they could do with more octopus and less fried coating. The flavors are nice though. We tried the tonkotsu and shoyu ramens. The tonkotsu was a light yet flavorful milky-colored broth with thinner, smoother, white ramen noodles. The shoyu is a brown broth that is slightly saltier and packs a rich umami punch. The noodles are the thicker, chewier-type yellow ramen, which I think gives it a slight edge over the tonkotsu. The pork is tasty, but the regular $10 bowl only gives you one piece. I'd go with the $12 bowl (charshumen), which gives you 3. I might skip the marinated boiled egg next time, it wasn't that marinated and didn't come whole with a nice runny yolk inside. It seems that their bar and credit card machines aren't up and running yet, and neither are a few of the menu items. No matter, I'm sure they'll work it out in time. On a side note, it's funny and kind of cute that they make their servers greet you Japanese-style with a "irashaimasse!" Overall, this is some tasty ramen served in a pleasant and convenient space, so the slightly higher prices are kinda worth it.

I think I need to go back to try the bar... Been wanting to stop by ever since it opened on campus, but haven't really had the chance to until last week. Came for a late lunch on Sunday and we luckily avoided the wait time everyone has been complaining about. Upon entering, I loved the high ceiling and overall interior of the restaurant. It's very light wood-heavy and the lighting created a nice, chic, modern ambiance. We were quickly seated and decided to place our order. I love asking for opinions of the servers but was unfortunately disappointed when our served didn't know anything about the menu. She told us what was popular, but couldn't really tell us the differences between the many types of ramen on the menu, which I think is kinda a requirement at a ramen restaurant. We decided to go with Tonkotsu Ramen and Tonkotsu Chashumen with an egg. The only difference between them is the number of slices of pork you get (1 v. 3). The ramen came out about 10 minutes later and I will say the presentation was great. Traditionally with ramen, you have all the ingredients layed out on top of the noodles and it was a great display. I also like tasting the broth before going right to the noodles. The broth however was very salty, with a nice, thick layer of oil on top of it. They went great with the noodles I devoured afterwards, but I refused to finish the soup at the end. I also ordered an extra order of noodles ($2 if you're feeling extra hungry) which topped off the meal. I think Ramen Bar is a step in the right direction, diversifying dining options in West Philly. However, I think it still has some things to fix before it becomes a neighborhood staple of mine. It's also very pricey (~$18 for lunch). I'm hoping their bar opens up soon; it could be a nice place to hang out with friends on chill weeknights. Pros: different for the area, great interior, great noodles consistency Cons: pricey, salty/oily broth, inexperienced wait staff

Food was decent, but way too pricey. Further for a quick bowl of ramen, the waitress completely forgot about my table and we had to wait 45 minutes. I gave it a second try, and the same thing happened. Not coming back here again.

I had a craving for Indian cuisine and found this place on yelp . I must say this was the very best I've ever tasted . My date and I equally enjoyed. Its small and intimate perfect one on one conversation.

my husband and i found this amazing restaurant after passing it by for years. we are addicted! the halved chicken and house rice are our favorite takeout. the house salad is enough for 2 as is the mesclun salad. this is our favorite restaurant in parsippany

Visit #1.  *   Stopped in a couple days after it opened for dinner.  Place was crowded but got a seat at the bar.  Nice beer selection but everything was ~$1 more than at similar establishments.  Unfortunately, they didn't have lots of the bottles listed.  Server indicated that maybe by the end of the week they would have them.  I'll give them a pass based on possible delays from the storm but the server at least could have explained that before I tried to order a few. The food was what really dragged this place down for me.  Very little to choose from for a vegetarian so I went with the falafel burger.  The bread was a small hamburger bun you'd get at a supermarket.  There was a little spread on it and some onions but it was tasteless and forgetful.  Came with fries but that's a stretch - maybe a dozen skinny fries like the ones served at McDonalds.  They didn't come with ketchup or any dipping sauce nor was I offered any.  Put this all on an oversized plate and it looked downright laughable.  Probably the worst gastropub meal I've had in the 3 years I've been in Philly. About twenty similar places within walking distance I'd visit before going back. Visit #2.  ****  Better.  Sat at the bar.  Had a couple of nice beers and enjoyed a soup which was actually very good. Visit #3.  **   C'moooon.  I want this place to be good.  Stopped in for happy hour on a Friday evening.  Awesome beers as usual at amazing happy hour prices.  Had two beers and the Brussels sprouts.  Beers were better than the sprouts which were just meh.  Asked to cash out.  Only problem was the management had decided to reboot the computer system in the middle of happy hour so the bartenders were left helpless.  Sat there for a good 20-25 minutes waiting.  Bartenders were apologetic and offered a couple of free tasters.  Could tell they were more frustrated than I was. Overall.  **   Go here for happy hour.  Can't beat it.  Half price on every draft and the lineup normally stacks up with the best in the city.  I still can't recommend the food though.

granted they have been open for a short period of time, there was absolutely nothing good about our experience.   a group of 6 ordered beer and food; the beer order was wrong and delayed for 45 minutes without any apologies or efforts from the staff.  we had to repeatedly ask for our beverages, including water.  the food came out at different times without apologies.  the staff was condescending and defensive.  we are very disappointed because we had high hopes that this would be a new neighborhood favorite.   there is no meal/entree on the menu.  this place is strictly small plates.  the food is not good.  all 6 adults were very disappointed.   there is no reason to eat here.  do not go.

Okay so I watched as they renovated the building and was excited when they finally opened... The building is beautiful and the decor inside is warm and cozy, but seating is kinda cramped and on top of each other. Drinks- The beer & cocktail list is above average, I was overly impressed by the beer list and will definitely go back to do some more drinking! I had an amazing dry cider which was recommended by our server Now onto the food... the food was just okay... My friend and I got a bunch of small plates to share so we could taste a number of the items. We got the mushroom fries, we felt that they needed more cheese and could have been a little crispier. The soup of the day was amazing, very creamy and lots of fresh seafood. The calamari was also amazing and fresh. The brussel sprouts were bland and lacked flavor the idea for them is great but they needed a little extra. The mac & cheese needed to be cheesier. The apple pie desert was very good and fresh and just the right size to finish off our dinner. For the two of us it was about $50, which is acceptable for the amount of food we got. The service was very good also, and they knew the menu which was helpful for our questions. I want to go back to try brunch and to do some more drinking.

overpriced meal for very small portions.  the selection of food is mediocre at best and i honestly thought they brought the child's size for my wife's meal.  if you just want to drink beers, the selection is good.  don't waste your time eating here because you will leave hungry.  the food was ok, nothing spectacular

Went with great expectations; left feeling hungry and disappointed. They created a nice, but noisy, atmosphere at this neighborhood tavern but they fall very short on the food they serve. Neighboring tables also agreed that there just wasn't enough food for the price and we all joked about where we were going from here for a real meal. And the food we had (cod, wings, burger, soup) was all pretty bad. The fries tasted good but are very greasy. All in all it's a shame that the owners didn't consider that people really want something for the money they spend, not big empty plates of tasteless finger food. We live in the neighborhood and we are really sad that this place is so bad. We were hoping for a regular, local go-to pub for a good meal. This ain't it! It might last a while if it were on South street with the parade of tourists but not where it is. People want reasonable FOOD for their money.

I've only been for brunch so can't comment on dinner but was fairly unimpressed. I had the chicken and waffles that was a wimpy piece of chicken on a waffle that looked like it came out of an Eggo package. Bloody Mary tasted like straight watered down tomato juice. My friend got lamb sausage that was pretty good (albeit on the smaller portion size) and the coffee was decent. Granted we were there back on their opening weekend but it will be a while before we go back in the hope they improve.

A classier TGI Friday's with better service and nicer font. What I liked: Burger meat was actual meat versus a puck and correctly cooked to order -- medium rare, which is hard to come by. The burger was not delicious by any definition, but at least it was real. Fries originally came out room temp, I sent them back and they whisked them away without complaint. New batch was fine. Service was very friendly and prompt. What I didn't like: Bartender gave a cheap pour. At least compared to other places in the city. When it's a $14 bourbon, I notice. Bacon I requested was blech. When I say bacon on a burger, what do you visualize? Strips? Yes. Bacon crumble? No. Of course you don't. And neither did I. Burger has no tomato (unless that's an option). This bugs me. Side salad was drenched in two creamy cups of salad dressing and a bucket of salt. 75% less dressing, please. Table by the window (6th street side) sits directly on top of a boiler or generator that vibrates like crazy -- it makes your ears ring and it's like eating on top of a throbbing subway. I mentioned it and the waiter agreed (and said he'd mention it to the manager, which was great). But I was not offered another table and I hoped it would go away. (It didn't.) Barrel House has sort of a super straight, kind of Republican vibe uncharacteristic for the Bella Vista/Queen Village area. Maybe the idea is to give suburbanites a place to go in the city. To the restaurant's credit, it knows who its customer is, because the place was packed. I'll go back, but for food, ambience, drinks, and neighborhood feel, I liked Tapestry far better.

Ok -  it took a few weeks, but wife and I finally got here tonight. I never took the time to read reviews prior to going - so we went on a blank slate. I had no idea until now that there were so many yelpers who had issues w/ BSBH. Love the look of the place from the outside when driving down Bainbridge. Also, major kudos for the revolving door - where do you see a door like that in a neighborhood tap room? No where - way too cool! The huge windows are awesome too! This place lights up the whole corner. The design of the interior is nice and warm. It was about 7pm. Greeted very nicely by hostess as we walked in. The service throughout the whole meal was very good. Granted they weren't that busy on a Monday night, but our server was always coming by our table at just the right time - and she was warm and pleasant. What more could you want? (good food!) Had a pint of the Ithaca Flower Power - good stuff!. Anyway, the problem was the food. We ordered very simply: 1- Pulled pork fries w/ jalapeno and sour cream. The fries were tasty, but needed to be cooked through more - many were limp and close to being soggy. Some folks may like 'em this way, but they could have been crispier. The amount of pork was proper for a $6 dish. The pork itself tasted good or adequate - but I was hoping for it to blow my socks off like the pulled pork tots at The Institute did last winter - I'm still thinking about those tots!  BSBH needs to add a little more love to make their pork above average. 2- The Mussels Puttanesca was a disaster. My wife had to take a pass on them after tasting the 1st one. They were not cooked completely. The shells were fully opened, but the mussels war seriously undercooked. I tried one too - definitely not cooked enough, and very little flavor. My wife said the red sauce wasn't very good either. The grilled bread that came with it looked good, we never tried it. 3- The Greek salad was lame. In hindsight, I wish I had thought to take a photo of it. There's 2 things I have to order in a place that I've never been to if it's on the menu - chicken noodle soup and greek salad. Why? Because those are 2 things that I make real good myself and I'm always looking to see if someone else can make it as good or better. The presentation was nice, but then it was downhill: The greens were spring mix or something similar, not romaine or green/red leaf. That in itself is not a problem, but they were a small pile in the middle of the bowl and soaked limp with dressing that wasn't a good greek salad dressing - it needed more lemon and red wine vinegar.  There were only two small cubes of feta. Are you kidding me? No really! Are you kidding me!! What the ....! The salad is $10 - not a 5 or 6 dollar salad. How do you put less than an ounce of feta in a $10 greek salad? The cut up grape tomatoes are a nice touch and much tastier than regular tomatoes, but there could have been more - it seemed like it was 3 grape tomatoes cut in half. The kalamata olives were cut in half and on the light side too. Also, the cucumbers were few and far between. The only thing there was plenty of was red bell pepper. I was really expecting better things from this kitchen. It's not that I know anything about the chef or owner - but it's clear a ton of money was put into this place. I watched them build it out over the last few months and assumed the owner/investors would make sure the entire food experience was on par with the strong competition in our city from the first day open. With all the excellent dining options in Philly, you can't afford to take a few weeks to work out the kinks. Just sayin'.

Having been here four times since opening day, I figured it's time to write up a nice review of the place.  The first two times I went in were for drinks (opening night and one other time) ... this was before they had implemented a happy hour.  Prices were fair and food wasn't bad, but I was disappointed both times due to the fact that many of the beers they had listed on their vast beer menu were not in stock.  Since it was within the first week or two of their opening, I figured it was just something to chalk up to a new business getting up and running. The third time I went in was for dinner on a Friday evening.  We got seated immediately, despite the fact that the place was packed.  The food was pretty good (I had a quinoa salad and my date had the burger), but the service was lacking.  The waitress brought the wrong beers, our food and drink orders took a really long time to get, and when we actually did need something from the waitress, she was nowhere to be found. My fourth and most recent visit was for their newly instituted happy hour -- one of the best in the city, in my opinion.  They offer half off (yes, 50% off) ALL draft beers (except whatever is in cask) for two hours, which is really an amazing deal.  Since their draft list is always changing and boasts about 15-20 options, you're really getting an opportunity to try out some of the more interesting (and pricey) beers for half off.  I mean, my friend tried an $11 beer for $5.50!  This last visit was the best one so far -- they seem to have more of the kinks worked out now. I'd definitely recommend this place for HH and to try out some really different beers.
Great food and celebrity-watching at this uber-cool spot.

There's a reason they've been around for so long.  Not the fanciest place but you definately get your money's worth.  Just check out the throngs of cops, firefighters, and paramedics waiting online at noon.  This italian sandwich shop is a little off the beaten path yet all these guyus are willing to flock here (I'm one of the above mention guys).  Everything is home made and for $10 you are stuffed.  Try the roast beef/fried eggplant/homemade mozzerella combo or the roast pork special.  If you're in the neighborhood or driving by it is definately worth the stop.

I stopped in here for lunch on a weekday and it was quiet, quick and had a nice vintage saloon feel.... dark but airy too, good service. I had Cary's Salad with a seltzer w. bitters, lime & a dash of simple syrup and it was pretty perfect. I like the vibe here, I'd come back for late night cocktails or draft beer as well.

Waffles here are out of this world a little small but love the different combinations they offer. But their coffee is what I really go for it's the perfect brew I am only here early in the mornings so I must try the rest of the menu I see many more visits in the future.

Being new to the area and in search of a good waffle along with a quality cup of coffee so I wanted to give Grid Iron a shot. Let me tell you I was totally impressed with  the originality and freshness of the waffles and the excellent cup of coffee that me and my wife both enjoyed. I highly recommend a visit to this fine establishment and will be returning there myself.

You can hear the owner badmouthing her staff and customers while seated at your table. The food is overpriced and takes forever. The hours are crazy, who closes at the very time that people are returning from work on the train? The staff is constantly changing so you can't build that small-town relationship with them; something so important in a town like South Orange. While the food is pretty good, it just isn't worth it.
I've been a regular here for years--the food is on point and the drinks are great! I recommend the mint julep. Jessica is fantastic and can make you anything based on the mood you're in--love it!

The wings here are amazing! The fries are crack too. Excellent bar food. The drinks are delicious too. It has become my go to spot. The music can be really loud on Fridays because of the DJ but regardless it is a great vibe. I love it here !

I have been going to this place for years and almost feel bad giving it 3 stars but really nothing special. They have burlesque night on occasion which is interesting, mainly divey feel, good place to just kick it with a friend. Good drink selection, food is average. Convenient location though just blocks away from prudential center and parking usually isn't a problem.

I used to live on Dean Street, but I moved away many years ago.  My friend still lives in the neighborhood and told me about this spot.  I went in and was immediately greeted.  I ordered the 1lb crab platter with potatoes and corn to go.  OMGGGG.  I made a complete pig of myself when I got home.  It was so good.  Everything was cooked to perfection; not oily, not salty, just damn good food.  NOM NOM

LOVE! LOVE! The Crabby Shack! A quaint place - I could see in the Vineyard or Hamptons. The food was so good and very fresh. We had crab legs, crab cakes, crab roll and crab tacos, steamed broccoli, new potatoes and corn - very fresh! Not too over seasoned, just lightly seasoned and tasty, not too salty, the legs were very buttery too!  They crab legs are servedin a plastic bag that they pour this butter sauce in and when you open the bag the butter sauce is in your basket and you can dip the crab meat in it. I can see them adding some shoestrings fries and dipping sauces. (in the future) When I left I was very full and happy. :-) I went with a friend from Maryland and she ordered crab legs and a crab role to go. For dessert they had BCakeShop cupckaes, yummy and the best old fashion banana pudding. I say old fashion because it was just like your mother made it not too over the top, just vanilla pudding, bananas and vanilla wafers. SO good. The decor is classic and the bathroom I want in my home. I will definitely go back! Congrats to the ladies for making this dream a reality! I am waiting on the franchise...Harlem, LI, Hamptons, Vineyard, Philly Baltimore, DC...and the list goes on!

This review is mixed. The food at crabby shack "tastes" good once you get it in your mouth.   But it wasn't the most pleasant experience getting it there. The "platter" is not a platter of food; rather it is a plastic bag full of food all mushed together.  And you have to stick your hand into a plastic bag of hot slop to find your crab. It's a small place, so don't expect a seat at a table if you go during meal time. Eat here if you like crab, but don't order the platter.  They should serve the platter in a more appetizing way.

This place is awesome! I can still smell the amazingness on my fingers!   Let's start with the restaurant itself. When you walk in your warmly greeted. The place is so cute!!! There is not much seating but if your lucky enough to get one I would definitely stop a while and take in the whole experience! Now for the food........... .  .   . Sorry, my mouth was watering. We had 1/2 lbs of shrimp, one crab taco, and two crab rolls. So freaking good. Omg! The food will not disappoint you! I will definitely be back!

OMGeeee!!!!!  I am so glad Fifi and Gwen opened up this wonderful eatery.  Nestled in Crown Heights, it felt like we were by the beach.  I had the Crab BLT w/ Avocado, it was sooooooo delicious.  Buttery, scrumptious bread, filled with sweet crab, avocado, crunchy bacon, lettuce and tomato!!  My mouth is watering right now.....gotta get back to try every single menu item...IJS!!!  Oh, and the price is right y'all.

What a nice little spot!  We were greeted very warmly as soon as we walked through the door. I had the crab taco and hibiscus tea (small items just in case I didn't like the food). Man I tore that taco up! I will be going back to try other items on the menu. I hope business picks up because they are on the far end of Franklin and won't survive if no big buzz is made.
Been here twice now and very pleased both times.  Food was great and you got plenty of it.  You get a lot for your money.  Staff was attentive and friendly.

I saw the reviews and wanted to try something new. This is definitely a new favorite spot for me and my lady. The decor is really nice and has an upscale feel, but it's not pretentious. The owner was very nice and welcoming. He said they have only been open a month so he was still working on getting a credit card machine and liquor license. The food was amazing! If you like salt and fat, you won't be disappointed here. The menu seems to be mostly small plates with tons of quality and flavor. The ribs were fall off the bone and flavorful. The dishes have a touch of Asian spin on them. The complementary dessert was so good. I have never had anything like it. It was some kind of Italian custard (forget the name, but not canoli filling) infused with Jasmin extract. It was so good. I will be coming back more. This place is going to be packed in a few months from now when word gets out about it. Go now to avoid the wait.

Can I just skip straight to the food for once? Truffled calamari. Yes. I love that they use a cornmeal coating rather than the usual breading. And the black truffle flavor really comes through after a few bites. Let some air in while you chew, you'll see what I mean. I was a bit skeptical of the "Rolling Chicken" and was initially enticed by the "black sticky rice." Food came pretty quickly and I dug straight in to the rice. It was good. I was satisfied. What I didn't know is that the real star of that dish was the Brussels sprouts. What? The sprouts were the absolute best I've ever had. The namesake chicken was good too, don't get me wrong. It was juicy and succulent and delicious by all means. But my god, those sprouts. Anyway, I'd skip the chicken lollipops - they were aiiite but not really noteworthy. Very friendly waitstaff, although I suspect someone passed some serious gas while walking by our table (we were the only patrons at the time). Thanks...

5 stars! I have been here a few times for both sit down dinners and for take out and never been disappointed. The staff is very friendly and warm, and the  decor is very nice and inviting. But the best part is the food! I have tried: Appetizers: naan and hummus- above average; truffle calamari- yum! So delicious; charred edamame- deliciously salted edamame that tastes grilled Entrees: both the hanger steak and duck confit- succulent and very flavorful; short ribs- fall-apart tender and perfectly seasoned; Thai saffron rice- very good, best way to describe it is like a Thai version of jambalaya. Dessert: panna cotta- perfect! not too sweet and nice flavor and of course the Thai iced tea is a must try! Will definitely come back here!
Wow! To be continued...after my digestion.   Food coma is priority right now. ;P In the meantime, see my pix.

Since I moved to NY from London, I tried many Thai restaurants in Queens, However I've never found a restaurant which serve decent Pad Tai...as they always put too much Ketchup! This place serves delicious Pad Tai without too much ketchup. I have to try more dishes. This restaurant would be one of my favourite ones.

One of the best Peruvian spots in Jersey. A nice quaint spot that you might just miss if you pass by too quickly. The staff is courteous and friendly. The Lomo is to die for; Ceviche fresh and flavorful. Great apps and desserts. Its BYOB! Yummy :D
Great food!

This place is terrible. The service is absolutely awful. I came here about 2 years ago and can still recall everything that occurred. We had a party of 4, and 2 of us ordered rotisserie chicken- 1 dish was served with cream over the chicken and the other was not. When i asked the waiter why my dish had cream on it, he responded, that the dish was served that way (uhmmm ... my friend's dish did not have cream). He took it back and brought out a "new dish". Upon closer observation, I noticed that he had simply wiped the cream off of the chicken with god knows what. I was disgusted- i imagine it's a health code violation. We immediately asked for the check, paid for our appetizer and LEFT!! My suggestion- STAY AWAY!!!!!
Super restaurant!!!!!!!!

Great happy hour? Check. Delicious Italian food? Double check. Impeccable service? Triple check. Oh and let's not forget that they offer a discount for downtown dwellers! Great incentive for folks who live downtown... we all know how limited our options can be! My only complaint about Salute is probably a result of my wine obsession, but regardless-- I think their wine list is definitely lacking, confusing even. Their list contains a few gems but the rest of it is disappointing, especially for an Italian restaurant. With some more TLC I'm sure that this could improve. Will be back for sure! Nothing but good experiences here.
Really enjoyed the Bolognese! Great ambiance and a very friendly staff.  We also thought the muscles were extremely good.   The price is fair and they offer generous portion. Enjoy!!!

Very friendly and laid-back server. Nice ambiance as well! We ordered the mussels, veggie spring rolls, and the bolognese pasta. We especially liked the mussels and the bolognese pasta! Would definitely recommend this place!
So fresh and everything is from Italy. Share one if you're not that hungry because the panini is pretty big.

Without a doubt, "Outstanding" is one of the best words to describe this little gem. I didn't know what to expect but such amazing paninis from such a small place wasn't at all what I thought it would be. Walking in, it's a small store with paninis being made fast and furious behind the counter. They are 14" long and made with the freshest ingredients I've had in a long time. The bread is so incredibly fresh, the meats and cheeses are awesome and even he arugula tasted like it was just picked. We got three sandwiches for five of us and that worked perfectly. We're staying up by Times Square and we all agreed: we are going out of our way to get lunch here tomorrow. Great food, great staff. Go there. Now!

It's a very good sandwich, fresh and tasty, but unfortunately they don't press or heat the panini, which would've been 5 starts if they did. Otherwise, the bread and cheese with all the cold cuts are very fresh, I had the chicken and I liked it. Be careful, they are huge and one sandwich is enough for two.

Eating a Napoli panino (sandwich) as I type. I literally am astounded that I haven't found Pisillo before now. One of my coworkers recommended it, so we made the trek up to Fulton area to pick up lunch. First, the staff is very friendly. The service was rapido. The small-corner-deli-feel accentuated the feeling that I was back in Italy just getting a bite before continuing the day's explorations. The sandwich itself, as I'm sure you can read from the other reviewers, is enormous. About 14" of fresh Italian bread (crunchy style) with a choice of White, Whole Wheat, or for an additional charge: Ciabatta (add 1.00), Semolina (add .50), Sfilatino (add 1.00). All of the ingredients are Italian products, and the fresh imported bufala mozzarella is to die for. They cut the deli meats fresh on the slicer behind the counter. The size of the panini allow them to be easily shared or made into two meals. That is, if you can stop yourself from eating the second half.

My mother and I visited Dragonfly on a Tuesday afternoon around 5pm. We were shocked after entering the restaurant to find such a beautiful decor considering we knew what the previous restaurant looked like. The dim lights, fancy light shades, and aquariums are a great touch. For appetizers we had the dragonfly wings (teriyaki) and garlic shrimp with toast which were excellent (well seasoned, fresh, and tasty) and well worth the price considering appetizers were half off. For dinner we had the sizzling mongolian beef and the pork chop in green peppercorn sauce. Both meals were fantastic. The beef was fresh and very tender. And the pork chop in peppercorn sauce was great. However, if u have med issues the sauce is a little salty so u may want it on the side. we had a great experience and will definitely come back when they have a live dj and live jazz. we were impressed by the decor, food, and service.

You would think that such a carefully decorated place would have an excellent menu and service to match... unfortunately this is not the case. The menu is over priced and very scattered (not like an Applebees/Fridays selection at all). Although the focus is Asian Fusion, you would expect a more suitable family style menu...especially given it's location. Food quality is alright and the music is really annoying at times (Beatles playing one min and some foreign Asian mountain music the next). Sushi selections are not what I expected either.. want sushi? Take the extra 10 mins to drive further down to Yu-Yee. The management in this place seems like a joke... there was absolutely no structure. Employees were walking around aimlessly and the manager/hostess (dressed in street clothes) walked around with a bowl of food to their faces eating on the floor! The staff joked loudly and conversed with one another across the room. If you plan on trying it out, do it soon because at this rate I see them lasting about as long as the Boulder Creek that used to be there.

I was really looking forward to this place because of the interior/exterior design.  So my family and I went into to check the place out a week after it opened.  Wow.... From the moment you walk in the hosts out on their "just done give a crap" faces on and greet us with a monotonous welcome.   Our server on the other hand was very nice and informative which was probably the only highlight of the restaurant.  So before the food comes out I go to the bathroom and see an employee SHAVE during service.   And he's doing it like its normal.  What kind of training did these foh staff get to be so nonchalant about service.   And as soon as I walk out I see more than half the servers just sitting down and talking right next to the sushi bar.   Now for the food, it was okay.   The garlic chicken was good but the coconut curry was fail.  Bland bland bland.   So if your looking to pay a hefty price for below average hospitality, and most importantly pay for food that is-"i can get better food next-door for a cheaper price" than go for it. But trust me; don't let the decor fool you.   -Coming from a cook.

this place is definitely diverse and beautiful . it is subperb for a family dinner , drinks with friends or even a night out with your significant other . Foodwise, there is a taste for everyone . Anywhere from chicken to steak to sushi to lo mein, red velvet cake and some delicious white chocolate caramel banana fried cheese cakes just to name a few.., you are sure to be delighted. if your bored with the average restaurant scene, go to dragonfly , you won't go wrong. ( prices are reasonable as well)

I recently was on a business trip and was staying at the hotel nexts door, and My coworks and i decided to head over to Dragonfly and grab a bite to eat . And as we walked in the door the decor took our breath away, The host took a lillte a while to greet us but, After they sat us at booth. The server came and made sure our experience was nothing like any other resturant we went too. The sushi and food was amazing had my taste buds in a fenzy... Overall my coworkers and i really enjoyed the resturant .

We picked this spot for a Monday night triple date with friends. Their Monday night special included half off bottles of wine! Thumbs up! However, it did not include Champagnes, sparkling wines, and bottles over $65. The inside setting was very small and cozy, however our 6 person table was pushed right next to the entrance, it was a bit cramped and awkward. But once the wine started flowing, that didn't matter! Very reasonably priced menu, excellent wine selection, and fabulous tasting food kept everyone at the table happy all night. Some of the key items of the evening, the prosciutto wrapped dates, the fontina fondue, and the beef carpaccio .

I want to like it. I like wine, small plates and cozy, intimate restaurants. I had tried to come before and found it impossible without a reservation. I have come here to just have a drink which is awkward at best due to the small amount of actual bar space, we felt like we were in the way and intruding on the dinining experience of those eating. I did however have a lovely cocktail, everyone I was with agreed the drinks were nice, if a little pricey. I finally got in here to eat. We both had wine we enjoyed very much. We started with a cheese plate that I found kind of small and boring. There were only three types of cheese - I would rather have smaller amounts of more kinds. It was accompanied by some kind of mushy grapes (bland standard grocery store variety), toasted bread with nothing on it, a few teeny pickles and a few olives. Meh. We then had brushetta with fig compote and proscuitto  - way too much of the fig, it overpowered the meat entirely (which was left in big pieces that had a tendency to be a bit tough). We also had a  "tramezzini" which was a sandwich of rather tough salmon- again in too big pieces -  with not enough horseradish cream on what I swear was wonder bread with the crusts cut off.  I was also not fond of how close we were seated to other people (Idon't need to hear everyone's business), especially because it wasn't  that busy. I am not sure I would do this again, but they do have some great wine. I like Grenacha and Montepulciano and they are hard to find in a restaurant so I wish the food was more inspiring.

What a gem of a brunch spot! I came at 12:30 on the first Saturday that felt like spring with 2 friends and was surprised to find it nearly empty. It did get filled throughout our meal though so 12:30-1 is a good time to swing by. The decor is tasteful with a laid back ambiance. Our (st. germain glass!) pitcher of bellini was divine- tasted of quality champagne and ripe peaches. Loved the bread basket too, which was filled with slim little mini baguettes. Service was attentive and unintrusive. I had the kobe beef sliders with truffles AND bacon, and mesclun greens- juicy, tender, delicious. It was the perfect portion for a sleepy Saturday afternoon. My friends both loved their dishes as well- black angus beef tartar and the eggs benedict. I really liked their menu, which allows you to choose from both brunch and dinner. It had all your traditional french fare (quiche, 3 kinds of croque monsieur, 4 kinds of eggs benedict), but also other international staples (pancakes, fish and chips, hot dogs). Usually this kind of all-over-the-place menu would be found at your average diner, but somehow they managed to pull it off with skill and finesse. I always appreciate it when a restaurant offers plentiful options without sacrificing quality. An all-around lovely weekend brunch. I will be back!
My favorite Indian place in the Hartford/ West Hartford-area. A must-try!

Went to this restaurant because of Jason's input on the 25th of June and found it satisfying.  I am not a fan of the buffet lunch, but was pleased that the offerings here were well selected and within a range so that they tasted fresh rather than reheated.  The wait staff was conscientious about maintaining the buffet and tending to patrons.  The dining room was busy! I did purchase a Taste of India gift certificate for a discerning friend as I am optimistic that dinner will be a welcome experience... and spiced to our liking.
GREAT first experience!  Excellent service.

We were their the other night after I kept buggin my hubby for Indian food. We usually love this place BUT it seems to have gone downhill. I was really disappointed. It made us both sick. The spice was dead on but it seemed like they just had a "party" and reheated our meals. I ordered the lamb vindaloo which is usually amazing here but it was tough and chewy and the sauce wasn't up to par. Hubby ordered the tandoori mix grill which is usually good and the chicken was dried out and not juicy. The mango Lassi's I raved about last time were being made from a mix now, which really made me mad bc I was really looking forward to it. I also ordered paneer tikka masala the pieces of paneer were so tiny and the sauce was swirly which tells me it was just reheated and not stirred up. The basket of bread which we love was greasy how can Naan bread get so greasy. Well its time to find a new restaurant thats for sure. I mean I understand people have off nights but that was ridiculous. The only good thing that came out of it was the galub jamoon. still yum.

Thanks to Group On/ LS deals, but for which I'd not have known this existed or I might pass on seeing the look and size from outside. It's a great find, probably the best in US so far and have already been there about 5 times in the past 3 months, and would keep going. Tasted food close to home...Pakka andhra spice and style in the southern category. North Indian food is great too and the best Tandoori Chicken...Juicy and Tender while perfectly flavored. We tried Lunch Buffets and A-la-carte menu ordering for dinner and both were excellent. They are open late for Lunch Buffet's, but go in the right time or the food could get stale. I was not aware of Dosa's in lunch buffet as some one mentioned, as we awere not offered any. Wife and Kids love this restaurant, and we have recommended them to a friend for a part catering. Friendly and Cordial service every time.

Came here on Friday night with a soon to expire Groupon. This is really more like 2.5 stars I feel bad going all the way down to 2 though. After seeing the Shrimp Masala picture here on Yelp I knew I needed that........what a let down. Pretty damn small shrimp with no crunch and pretty dry. Man did my heart sink when that place came out. I've only gone out for Indian few a hand full of times, but one of the times I had a shrimp appetizer at Akbar that is on my list of top 10 thing's I've ever eaten. So coming to a new Indian restaurant I kind of couldn't help but to compare the 2 appetizers. I would not order this again. The chips with the 3 sauces were awesome. Tamarind sauce is great and helped save the lame shrimp. Entree's: My girlfriend got a lentil and spinach dish that came out looking like a very thick soup. I got the Lamb Vindaloo that came out looking like a bowl of my parents stew. My girlfriend and I just looked at our food for a minute and started to eat it strait out of the bowls it came in. A minute later the waiter came over and told us to wait for the rice he was bringing out. Ahhhh it all made sense suddenly. So I laid down some white rice. I put some of my Vindaloo on top the rice and a small spoon of the spinach lentil on the side. We asked for a side bowl of the mint chutney sauce that came with the bread earlier and I added this to the top for a cooling contrast in flavor. It kind of served as my Indian Guacamole. It was very delicious. When I ordered the waiter asked if I wanted it spicy or not. I said "Yes, Plenty of spice please" I know they could have made it spicier....oh well. Although my meal was good.....like I said earlier it tasted like my parents stew (After I add hot sauce). That was odd being that my mom is Colombian and my dad Sicilian soooo I don't understand how this Indian dish tasted like my parents cooking. My girlfriend told me to be happy I liked it, but I was kind of thinking about how I could have just hit up the parents for free. $2.50 for the girlfriends Diet Coke can....that's kind of crazy. The Service : At first we had a girl waitress who could answer no questions so she passed off helping us onto a more seasoned gentlemen. My girlfriend and a friend that came with us had been bickering so they were both sitting there all grumpy looking....I was chillin. Awkwardly after the waitress got an earful from the waiter (who I think was the manager) she came over to our table and asked my girlfriend what was wrong? Does she need something or is something missing? .....Our table was empty and we were waiting for our food so I'm not sure what would be missing....just kind of waiting... Oh yea our friend ordered Lamb Kabob's and they came out after my App, but before our entree's. The problem was that the Naan he ordered didn't come out till our entree's did so his meat cooled down significantly. He said it was a bit dry. I don't think I would return without a Groupon or something. Ispice is about 20 Min South of my house,.but 20 Min. North is one of the best dish's I've ever had at Akbar.

My wife and I came here the other night for some wine on tap, and a few nibbles at the bar. The decor is lovely and warm. You can tell these folks care about detail. The staff is inviting and knows their stuff. We enjoyed a few glasses of wine on tap that were fresh and well priced. Their fried pickled veggies are marvelous. An absolutely wonderful addition to this stretch on Fulton. We will return for often thanks to atmosphere, food , and drink.

Three Letters is amazing! And just what the neighborhood ordered. It's casual, but so well curated. Incredibly fine food without being pretentious . The plates they serve on are right out of any 70s truck stop, but the food is so friggin' delicious. I think that the Moules Poutine (french fries, perfectly cooked to a crisp, with mushroom gravy and mussels atop), might be the best winter dish I've had, and is definitely the bane of any kind of low-calorie attempts I may aspire toward. The owner is around and friendly as can be, and explained that the concept is that of a french truck stop, so it's a place to sit back and casually enjoy fine food, without the price shock of hoitey-toitey Manhattan joints. I love going there to cool out and drop 50 bucks on 2 hours of eating, drinking and shaking off the day.

I'm sad to say I'm pretty disappointed with Three Letters. We live just a couple blocks away, so we were eager for it to open. Unfortunately, the cocktails were the highlight of our dinner -- the Rye Devil and Threesco Sour are both very nice, and as a Wisconsin native I love that they have Lakefront beer on tap. Complimentary bread & red onion relish is a nice start -- really good bread. Salade Fevrier was okay...lots of greens with not much else. I didn't find a single piece of squash on the plate, and more pear to balance the bitter chicory would have been nice. No real cheddar flavor in the vinaigrette either, but it was fine. Pate was, again, just okay. Not particularly memorable, and it's weird that it's just served on a plate with greens and nothing else -- though our bartender/server was happy to refill the bread basket. There was also no 'anchovy mustard' as advertised on the menu (unless it's dressing on the cabbage?), so that was disappointing. Moules poutine is heavy on the fries, light on the mussels and mushrooms (or at least I think I found a mushroom or two?), but the gravy is tasty. I wouldn't specifically recommend it, but we definitely finished the plate. The Pork Bourguignonne was where we became seriously disappointed, to the point of feeling misled and a bit ripped off. The pork itself is good -- tender, flavorful, and in a really great sauce -- and I enjoyed the spinach. However, this $17 dish is served on an appetizer-size plate and feels like a child size portion. It is extremely deceptive to list it on the menu as an entree. Maybe it's expensive pork, I don't know, but it's absurd to serve such a small portion, on such a tiny plate, even if you would have to charge a little more for a normal-size dinner portion. Due to it's proximity to our apartment and the great atmosphere and cocktails, we'll definitely give Three Letters another try (or two) before writing it off, but this experience was definitely a disappointment.

My second visit. The first visit was "iffy" at best, but it was their first week and so one has to cut them so slack. Plus, I'm a local resident and wish only the best for new businesses. My second visit wasn't worth much, however. I ordered a drink (the wrong one was delivered) and tried to start my dinner with the soup (one has a choice of clams or chickpeas. I chose the clams. Mistake!) What arrived had a skin on it so thick one could make a handbag and the clams were so dry, there was no earthly way they were fresh. When I sent it back, I was billed for it anyway. Some gentleman (who didn't introduce himself) apologized on the street for it, but made no effort to remedy the situation or refund my money, so what was the point? Did he want to be known as "a nice guy"? I'm sure he is. All the same, it was dreadful and I won't be back.

Nice food. Nice people. Nice atmosphere. A very comfortable yet bustling place. I will return again and again.  (already been 3x) I'm really rooting for this place. Highlights are the lamb, the mussels, the salad and the seitan.

I LOVE their tea...They have a variety of flavored and bubble teas.  The sandwiches are great as well.  The staff is nice and VERY friendly!!  My coworkers and I are regular customers during lunch time since we work nearby.

Nam Nam is a great addition to the neighborhood.  I had the chicken sandwich yesterday and was pleasantly surprised by how tasty it was.  The meat/ cabbage to bread ratio was very balanced and is similar to the ones i've had in chinatown.  Coffee is a good value.   Staff is friendly, the cafe doesn't have an awning/ sign so it can easily be missed.
Excellent food and service.  Great  dining option for this  neighborhood.   Nice and clean environment

The four times I have been there in the last week (for a girl on a budget- that is saying a lot!) have been consistently amazing. The service was very attentive and friendly and the food delicious! Momos are a family favorite. The chow mein is made with handmade noodles and really yummy. The food is milder than Indian food but can be spicy if requested. I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant.

Had dinner at Terre a Terre and the food was awesome!  The artichoke and oregano soup was the best soup I ever had!  So flavorful and creamy with a hint of cheese ... to sum it up HEAVEN!!  My entrée was very good (lamb chops) and the butternut squash that came with it was absolutely delish.  I would highly recommend this restaurant and believe it's definitely one of the Best in Bergen County and am so happy it opened last year.

This is our favorite sushi place in the area!!! We order or eat here at least once a week. Food is always fresh, always consistent, and always delicious!!! The service is so friendly and already know what we like to order ... "Two Tuna salads, one with crunchy and one without" haha we love this place.

We tried Noodles today after hearing so much about it from friends around the country, and getting an invitation for the pre-opening to try out the food.  This is the first one in the Northeast.  The rave reviews were well deserved, as my wife and I thought our dishes were excellent (Japanese Noodles w Steak & a pulled pork dish and noodles), and our kids loved the Mac and Cheese.  All the food was fresh and the service was great. The coca-cola machine was very cool, and mixes almost any combination of drinks you can imagine. Kids loved it. Will definitely make this a frequent destination when we are visiting. Wish we had one closer to our house in Southern CT.  Maybe they'll open one soon.
Good solid experience.  Had an indonesian noodle and it was cheap, fast, and fresh.  High marks for fast food and will go back again.

Just opened working out the bugs Tried to order two Mac and cheese 8+ each one with pulled pork + and then asked to put on side and rang up more Caught the mistake , in the end only got one Mac and cheese Pork is too spiced for a child's pallet Also order steak stroganoff , very strong favors , steak was extremely dry Cucumber and tomato salad ok but tasted like was seasoned and thrown in a bowl setup needs to be bigger One soda machine needs to be rethought Very cool but line feels like I am back in a cafeteria (not good) Overall kids like Mac and cheese , bread was fresh . Eat out 2-4 times per week and I am not sure I would go back. I was really looking foward to this place opening ;(
Fantastic food and service!  Thank you!

Amazing!  When we walked in, we were greeted by a very friendly hostess who didn't make us wait.  Bonus!  The place is rustic and cool looking, casual but I felt fine wearing a dress and heels.  We ordered fish and risotto, both of which were excellent.  The wine was from Spain and the manager or someone who seemed like a manager recommended it.  It was a very pleasant experience from someone living in Chicago, where many restaurants are amazing.  I loved it and I'll be back when I return.

My girlfriend and I were originally thrown off by the table sharing concept because we were both wanting to have a little intimate us time. Once we started ordering and got down to eating, we forgot about all of that and the focus was really on enjoying the delicious meals catered specifically for us. I have a dairy intolerance and Feast handled everything marvelously. The service, food and the experience was excellent!!

A very nice restarant with rustic decor and pleasant and relaxed atmosphere. Everyone from the hostess to the wait staff are exceptionally polite and helpful. My friends and I went there for brunch and enjoyed the starter dishes that were brought to us before we ordered the main dishes all of which were delicious. We were also offered an extensive selection of cocktails which we fully intend to come back for some evening. From reading the other reviews I learned how serious is the management of the restaurant about protecting privacy of its customers even if it may lead to some unpleasant consequences and would like to thank them for the effort. I presume that there are many people who are getting tired of having their meals interrupted by some inconsiderate individuals who can not refrain themselves from talking, texting and snapping pictures with their gadgets with no regard for other people.

Fabulous!......came here for an early "'Mother's Day Brunch"....as to avoid traffic next week.....staff was wonderful and made my 2 little girls and mother feel very special......we had a wonderful table with a lovely view of the lake....buffet selection was incredible....well worth the price......absolutely best eggs benedict I've ever eaten! Will definitely be back.

People rating this restaurant a little lower than average didn't quite seem to make sense to me as I just went there a couple days ago for dinner and had an above average experience. I sat outside where the heaters kept the semi chilly weather at bay and with the excellent scenario out there... The setting, overall mood just had things set up for a great time. Our server was Andrew, who was professional and knowledgable about the menu. Ordering an appetizer, two cocktails and two entree definitely put us at the close 100.00 dollar range overall for the bill.... Which everything tasted delicious but as a big Korean who loves to eat, it was filling but the entree has that fancy pants presentation where you just get a thumb of food when you want a whole handful... But that's just my inner fat boy screaming for some more good tasting food. Pros: - ambience, great outside view - overall great friendly service, I really appreciated how they checked to time the entree. Was still working the appetizer and they didn't rush the entree out whatsoever. Kindly asked actually to time it right with the chef and our completion of the appetizer. - food was delicious 7-8 out of 10 Cons: - Portion control. 'Fine dining'. I would have wished just a bit more for what I paid. I've eaten at some fancy restaurants and paid premium price but were given like 5 course meals that definitely was worth spending the money.... For this I would have expected just a little bit more. - some light outside music would have been nice. Can't remember if there were any inside, but helps with not feeling too exposed to the listening in quiet engaged couple that was sitting at the table behind us,

Took my wife for the brunch buffet a couple months ago on a recommendation from a wealthy co-worker who frequents.  The scenery is gorgeous, like a painting.  The restaurant was packed, and we were sat upstairs relatively quickly. The buffet had everything you'd want; lovely salad and charcuterie, eggs benedict, french toast, a carving station where they make you your own omelette.  Some of the food looked like it was sitting out for too long though.  The coffee was fantastic as were the mini pastries.  Although service overall was friendly, I felt they would have been more attentive for such a place, and the servers looked overdressed and kind of uncomfortable (just my opinion).  However, this was the brunch buffet and I would definitely return to order from their regular brunch menu as my wife and I were too stuffed to stay and walk around their beautiful sculpture gardens.  Overall opinion:  Overpriced, but delicious with a truly unique atmosphere.

Excellent venue for a romantic dinner or to celebrate a birthday or other event.  Menu was a gastronomic feast.   Great service.....warm, friendly and knowledgable.   Unfortunately the fish was farm raised and for this excellent establishment/chef that was a mistake.

Excellent dining experience   We joined friends we had not seen in a long time. After a quick ramble through the Grounds for Sculpture we returned to be seated for dinner. We were greeted warmly and promptly seated upstairs at a corner table with pedestrian views. The quiet disappeared quickly when a large and loud party sat down nearby. Despite that we continued to enjoy conversation with Pat & Ivan.   Our waiter was very well versed in the menu and took the time to help us navigate through it.  The menu included items from across the globe supplemented by supplies provided by local farmers. After ordering drinks, we made our choices. I enjoyed the wonderful Escolar pesce special after sharing a non exciting lobster crepe with my wife. She enjoyed the halibut special while our friends sampled the scallops and salmon entrees. Portion sizes were perfect. We had woofed down several slices of the wonderful French bread before dinner so we were fully sated. Overall we agreed the food was excellent, drinks were enjoyed and coffees and desserts were a nice way to finish up the evening. The ambiance of the restaurant was wonderful. Prices were on the high end but worth it. We all concluded we will be back..

Went for brunch on a Sunday. Offerings were sparse, only a few tables, and they were a disaster - a complete mess. Price is outrageous for what you get. Staff is nice but this doesn't make up for the deficits. $100 would be better spent elsewhere. Very disappointing. Need to step it up Rat's!

Quite charming. Was excited to try this place out since its new in my neighborhood. I stopped in on a late sunday morning solo. Very friendly staff and quickly offered me the lovely table next to the window. Great vibe and the menu has many appetizing options for brunch lunch and dinner... But since it was sunday, i ordered the double decker from the brunch menu. It was pretty good... Only reason I'm giving 4 stars and not 5, is because it wasn't exceptional. The sandwich was a tad on the dry side, but it tasted very fresh. I really enjoyed it here because although it got pretty busy, the staff was attentive and i never felt rushed.

Decided to randomly check out this new place in my hood because I do love all things new and they were open for brunch! Cute, little french place in the upper east side with friendly staff and service. I had an amazingly,refreshing mango margarita that till this day I look back on with fondness. I even tried getting the recipe to recreate it at home but the waitress didn't give it up (I think she lied and didn't know herself). The boy was loving his Bloody Mary and had to stop himself from ordering a pitcher. As far as the food, I had the Frere De Lys Double Decker consisting of two perfectly cooked eggs fried to my liking with some yummy smoked bacon. Bacon makes the world go round I always say. Bread was also perfect in this place. Whether it's the bread used on your sandwich or the table bread, the bread here to say the least, was pretty much the sworn enemy of all the cardio and strength training classes I've been partaking on.  The boy had the Turkey Club sandwich which was equally yummy. Again, perfectly smoked bacon, turkey and of course, bread! They do offer the unlimited typical brunch drink specials here but we passed because we were already hungover. I suggest you take advantage if you do decide to check it out since their cocktails were quite impressive from what I tasted (I could use a pitcher of that mango margarita right now). I plan on checking out their dinner service at some point and maybe steal this really nice drawer they have in back. All in all a cozy little place to brunch and maybe meet a blind date since their bar and decor is kinda sexy.

Someone posted that the steak tartare is no good but I just ate it and... AMAZING. I have eaten a lot of raw beef in my life. Cows flee upon sight of me. This stuff was super good. Also, Zucchini pasta. Good sauce, but more importantly the preparation was fab. Don't expect anything that really tastes all that much like pasta but instead get ready for one of the most awesome zucchini-based dishes since anyone ever thought zucchini could form the basis for a dish. Cocktails were also excellent. Top marks for the Louis XIV. Great atmosphere, and while sitting at the bar I keep seeing people emerge from the underground staircase behind the bar which is frankly hilarious. Will definitely be back!

My new favorite restaurant in the neighborhood. Attentive servers. Had the fig stuffed with goat cheese salad which was fabulous.  My entree was Zucchini Pasta which I've never had it was actually quite good. A perfect summer meal. My friend had the lamb chops and sweet potato.  Both done to perfection.  Flavorful and delicious.
A perfectly wonderful place in the most unexpected of places- good wine, great staff and a delicious Angus beef burger! They even had a homemade mulled wine. Try it!

Queens and Paupers, the new diner/bar right smack in the middle of Queens Plaza, has rapidly established a strong and much welcomed presence in LIC...especially for those of us who have to work in/around this dreary neighborhood! Food (simple and brilliant): Nice to finally have a diner with a breakfast menu that won't give you a chronic disease. The place is always packed for lunch. A pretty affordable and straightforward menu...but don't let the straightforwardness fool you, the food is simply fantastic. It's hard to pick a favorite, but you can never go wrong with their burgers, pancakes, French toast, or any of their omelets. Plus, brunch is served all day! The coffee is solid since its the same owners of Atlas Café next door. Drinks and Happy Hour (Woot!):   Damn good margaritas, muddlers, and martinis. Good wine selection. Happy hour specials practically everyday, and most times its 2-for-1. Nice to finally get a drink in the area that isn't run by a bunch of pretentious hipster mixologists ;) They'll make you pretty much anything your heart desires...within reason. Ambiance (old school): Its like entering a French café but only to be greeted and served by some really friendly Italians :) The booths are ridiculously comfortable and encourage extended happy hours. Off late, they've been hosting a lot of local jazz musicians... who would have thought that a bar in LIC would actually bring in some much needed culture.

Great food and super service -- but why did they have to change their menu? The beet salad is incredible, and the salmon plate is absolutely delicious! So why rock the boat? Even some of NY's super chefs keep their "tried and true" on the menu, year in and year out. Bobby Flay, Thomas Keller, Danny Meyer... all toy with their menu but make sure to retain their signature plates. We order from Taboonette several times a week (sometimes daily). The menu changes are very disappointing and will put a damper on our deliveries.  I hope they consider bringing back some of our faces! Please, please, please...
way better than your average falafel shop. go for the salmon one.
One of my favorite local places for a quick dinner.  Steak dish is amazing.  Very freidnly staff, and clean organized place.  Great neighborhood spot.

Pleasantly surprised by their new Beet Haloumi Salad. It was awesome, in-expensive, tasted great. Fits within my budget for lunch within $10 at Manhattan - which is a rarity outside the franchises (subway etc). Loved the apples and the dressing that came with it. Pro Tip Also get the nice warm pita bread on the side with it for just $0.75 extra and its a nice filling meal in less than $9.

WOW I'm so glad that I finally decided to give this place a try!!! it's been right beside my school this whole time and I have never even went in! Now I'm pretty sure i will be going there very often! This place is adorable! especially with the wood wall decors! both very industrial and rustics! it's very clean and the staffs are very helpful and nice! I actually ordered the salmon, but for some reason, the cashier thought i was getting the Kruveet. I was sad at first when i found out there were no protein in it. BUT I aint even mad..... because IT WAS SO GOOD! SO TASTY!PACKED WITH FLAVORS! I ordered it with quinoa, and it was topped with hummus and tahini spreads. THE FOOD COMPLETELY BLOWED MY MIND BY HOW TASTY IT WAS
New york roll, Godzilla and Fantasy. All excellent. Food is five star, although atmosphere is just typical sushi bar.

This review is based on my delivery order through GrubHub... We ordered 5 rolls online, just standard like Alaska roll, Philly Roll, Spicy Tuna, etc.. and they arrived really quickly. When we opened them up I was shocked at how much there actually was! Each roll was like 7-8 pieces, so they were a little smaller (which I prefer cause you can fit one whole piece in your mouth) and there were a ton of pieces. I only got 2 of the rolls and was full at the 1.5 mark. The roll was fresh and they let me substitute white tuna for regular tuna (if you have never tried white tuna, its glorious!). I didn't even mind paying the $1.00 delivery fee!
good sushi, ok service. could use a little better decor. service was nice, but i would prefer crazy sushi (18th and walnut) over this place. slightly cheaper and better

I can't believe I haven't already rated Barboncino. I first went the November they opened and have loved it since then. The last time I went (April) was the first time the service was a bit lacking, and yes, there can often be a long wait, but it's so, so good.

This is a long overdue blurb of accolades for one of my favorite neighborhood spots. My last visit a few weeks ago I brought in two college pals from Florida and we enjoyed the hip vibe, the attentive and fun bar staff, and some light snacks (I've had most items on the menu, always on point).

Hands down has to be some of the best thin crust pizza I have tasted in Brooklyn! Very fresh and crunchy yet soft! Arugula salad is a great start but good to share since the pizzas are not small!  Brick oven thin pizza! They have a beautiful HUGE BRICK OVEN when you walk in! Only down fall is the long wait on Friday and Saturday nights could easily be longer than an hour because of the small amount of tables but definitely worth the wait they have a nice bar where they get you when your table is ready! Definitely recommend! Tables are candlelit at night.
Chris is the best bartender ever. He's a maverick! He made the tastiest mojito for my friend - we will be back for sure :)

I'm not gonna make stupid claims that just open the flood gates to hater, like; "OMG guys this is the best F***ing pizza in all of NYC"... I'm not gonna do that cuz that's dumb... All I call say is they have great pizza ON A CONSISTENT BASIS, the service is good, the cocktail menu is great and the atmosphere is lovely. I really enjoy coming here, and I think you will too.

Wow. Fantastic. I'm so glad that I was able to fit this stop in on my brief stay in Brooklyn.  This place kicks Roberta's ass! (Sorry Roberta.). The crust is the secret weapon, the one-two punch, the cat's meow.  They figured out how to get the right balance of just enough (carcinogenic) char.  Why do other places feel the need to overdo in that area? The customers are a wonderfully and refreshingly diverse bunch. Love this place.

Dericious pizza! We came on a Saturday afternoon to watch the Brazil vs Netherlands game (they have a bunch of TV's and projectors) for their happy hour ($2 off beers? half off? not sure). There was plenty of seating (although no bar service at the tables - we had to go up and order). I also got the Neopolitan meatball pizza. The sauce was yummy and the crust was good (although a little burnt). Service was excellent. Overall a great place to hang out and enjoy great food!

amazing place inside and out.... its tucked away in a cute spot right off the main street in Princeton and definitely thought it was a plus that they had private parking. it had a really nice romantic ambiance to it and great service from the manager that opened the door for me and my husband to the waitress who gave us the up most care, it was an all around gem of a place to find! yea sure, the food is pricey and you might not get diner sized plates and stuff yourself to the brim food you get amazing tastes and great service for your visit and my husband and i both think that its completely worth it. a nice touch was the owner came up and asked us how our food and night was going and what can we say other that, "great!" and "you have an amazing place!" so please if you're in the near by area you should go to the peacock inn.... you'll have a great time!!

The banh mi here is no where near the REAL banh mis from vietnamese cafes on Washington or Oregon Ave. They do not even use the right bread! I got this speciality pork banh mi (something like barbacoa pork). The sandwich was stuffed with overly salty pork and a bad Asian Fusion slaw. Sorry, but this is not a banh mi. I love banh mis for the crispy baguette and the toppings that have the right balance of sour, spicy, salty, and sweet which Vietnamese dishes are known for. The  banh mi I got here was just salty and the bread was like a regular sub roll. It was 2-3 times the going price for a legit banh mi, too! Looks like I will have to trek to Washington Ave next time or Chinatown. Never getting banh mi here again.

I had a leg and thigh and a large Caesar salad. The chicken was nicely seasoned and properly cooked with the exception of the rubbery skin. The Caesar salad was not a Caesar. It was mixed greens (not a hint of romaine) with tomatoes and cucumbers and some pre packaged croutons. The dressing was atrocious. I'm almost positive it was a bottled product. It was incredibly over salted. I could not finish it. Please make your own Caesar dressing and TASTE IT!
My favorite dinner spot in the area! My family and I visit here often. Great food, service, and atmosphere. The salad bar is amazing, and I recommend any of their salmon dishes.

Had their pizza pie, it was really good. Atmosphere is great at this restaurant, good beer selection as well. Our waiter Joe was unbelievable,  very attentive and approachable.  Our friends come here all the time and now we know why.

Went to the Lobby for lunch last Sunday.  The place looked nice from the outside, but the parking lot was packed. The outdoor seating area, again looked nice, but when we sat down - the tables hadn't been wiped down from the previous guest. The music was very loud, we couldn't hear each other...  The food wasn't bad.

Do NOT order from here via GrubHub or any other delivery service. Twice my order has been cancelled because their "driver was out that day", and today I thought I'd give them one more shot.
