I placed my order via GrubHub at 4:30. I received a phone call ~4:45pm from The Lobby confirming that it was a delivery, not a pick up. I called them at 6pm, still waiting for my food and the manager tells me no one put in the order, but I could wait an additional 30-45 min and they'd put the order in. He seemed confused when I declined and started practically yelling at me that I had to wait for them to cook the food. It took a further 5 minutes for him to shut up and listen that I wanted him to cancel the grub hub order and refund my purchase (which I had prepaid via credit card). Just ridiculous.

Trendy decor. Definitely one of the better styled sports bar/clubs in the area. Indoor and outdoor bar. I was actually pretty pleased with the food. However it's more of a Hooters/Cheeks meets the Elizabeth's ghetto melting pot. Service left much to be desired. Don't go to The Lobby for the ambience. Tons of TV screens if you want to watch a game and baby sit a beer. Bar service is kind of slow and it's obvious the bar maids were not hired for quality or experience.

First time not the last time! We had the fava bean soup,chicken honey and prunes and the lamb couscous all excellent fresh and flavorful . It's like eating home cooking. the chef is the owner and tends to it as you are guests in his home. Sue is helpful and friendly. The place is SMALL so reservations are a must to be safe.

This place deserves a ten star rating I was not a huge fan of moroccan cuisine, let me tell you. I went to a restaurant in the village and the only positive thing I can say is how clean their bathrooms were.So my boyfriend decided to surprise me on Valentines day, I didn't understand where he was taking me since we turned on a residential street, then I saw the awning of "Casablanca Restaurant"; Moroccan cuisine,then I was like oy vey I have to pretend I like this. We were greeted by such a hostess that made me feel like I just walked into my mother's livingroom, it was very homey. The decor made me feel as if I was in a Moroccan livingroom, theres so many great details! So let me tell you about the food, It was amazing, I strongly recommend the tea, from time to time I remember it and wish there was a food fairy that can just wave its wand and serve me the tea I had at Casablanca. Its great to see a chef cook your entree right in front of you, I was pretty disappointed that,that night they didn't have kebobs but thats fine, I had lamb on the bone with couscous it was amazing! So bottomline: I am a huge fan of moroccan cuisine now! And gentleman this is a great place to take your special one to, it will definitely give you bonus points!
The food was out of this world, Sue's suggestions were spot on... You definitely want to make a reservation, but even with a wait its well worth it. Can't wait to come back!!
Yum. This is my favorite pizza place. Sauce / cheese ratio is perfect. Update: Lately something seems different can't put my finger on it but just not the same. Dropped down to 4.
delicious pasta (had the fusilli with sausage, papardelle with sausage - both were excellent)! Don't forget to sit in the back patio.

THANK YOU SO MUCH, PEPE GIALLO! After eloping on the High Line, my husband and 12 guests headed over to this absolutely charming little restaurant where we'd set up reservations 4 days earlier. Making reservations was easy breezy; they were even kind enough to reserve space in the ADORABLE garden courtyard hidden away from the street. Service was top notch! Our server was friendly and boisterous and so patient with our group. The food was fantastic! Simple and rustic Italian with lovely presentation and good portion sizes. They let my bridemaids put up a few silly decorations and even helped us cut and serve our wedding pie! Prices are outstanding given the ambiance and food quality and the prime location in Chelsea. We will DEFINITELY be returning!

Ever since I discovered Pepe Rosso I've been hankering to try out all of their venues... Pepe Verde kept me going for years but then it closed recently (RIP pouring a carafe out for my love of it) and I kept saying "I gotta go try out Pepe Giallo" as it also looked like their most restaurant-y restaurant. Welp, finally got to do that last night and what can I say, it's just as good as all of the other locations and I'm already in tears over the fact that I don't live around the corner so I can go here every night. What a great hometown kind of restaurant, with a decor that provides all of the comforts of that weird italian guy on the corner who you can't tell if he's yelling at you or the voices in his head. The food is fantastic-- just like the other locations, the simplest of things here taste like nirvana and the portions are generous and the prices even more so for the quality. Love love love this damn place. As a native New Yorker I feel like this is one of the few places around that still feels like a real, authentic New York restaurant-- in that all of the food tastes like it's directly from Italy and if that's not enough for you then get out because you're in the wrong city.

I finally got a chance to check out the cheese truck today. With the weather bordering on arctic, I felt it was best to go with something quick with no frills. I ordered a tomato soup and grilled cheese sandwich. The food was ready in less than 3 minutes which was fantastic. (Street food should be quickly prepared.) I rushed back to my apartment, sat down on my couch, and opened everything up. The grilled cheese sandwich looked like an everyday one but after one big bite it was evident that this was the real deal-- I have no clue what kind of cheese they use or how many tablespoons of butter are in between the yummy layers but it was almost perfect (second only to the grilled cheese served at Caseus restaurant). Then I got to the tomato soup. While it was pretty tasty, it wasn't the kind of soup I imagined. It had a very strong tomato taste, a lot like sauce. And there was a bit too much black pepper. I personally like a tomato soup with a creamier, sweeter taste. But still, it was pretty good. Of course I'll visit the truck again and try some of their specials.
Great staff, cool space. And most importantly - wonderful food. As a SoCal native, these taquitos were authentic and delicious. I will be going back!

There's an inherent problem with Taquitoria: With pre-made taquitos that are fried to order, the fillings are already inside the semi-crispy shell. The moisture permeates the shell, and although the outside fries crisp, the inside is kind of mushy. This was true for the beef as well as the bean. For what it's worth, the beans had great texture, and the beef had good flavor. But the overall product was only okay. Service was fine. The people there were very nice and seemed to care about their product. But I left a bit disappointed.

Stopped in to meet up with an old friend, who chose this place having been to the Montclair location. Really great ambience, especially around the holidays. The bartender was super nice. We had some beer and wine and nice and hot fried calamari. It was desolate on a Thursday at happy hour, hope its more crowded otherwise! Check it out if you live nearby.

I came here for dinner with a few friends. My friends and I were not really hungry so we ordered small dishes.  I ordered a Mac&Cheese and my friends ordered fries. It took a while for the food to come out and it wasn't that rushed. The food was average at best. Note: we didn't really try the main dishes. But people around me looked rather satisfied with their food. These service was not the greatest. The waitress didn't come to our table much. She came once to bring water. Every other time my friends and I had to call her to take our orders and bring the check.

Amazing!!! Don't let the size of this place fool you, it's small but but the food packs a punch. This was my first time trying Filipino food. I had the kaldereta backa( it's like beef stew ) the sauce is this light tomato paste with coconut milk, delicious. Not overly sweet.The rice was cooked within coconut and garlic, fantastic. The service was outstanding. She broke down the menu dish by dish. Also we had such a great conversation, even the cook came out to see if we needed anything else and converse with us. In making this a regular spot!

A family-owned joint that serves delish home cooked Filipino dishes. I love this place! So cute! So cozy! Very relaxed ambiance inside with such cute decors. The place is small, they probably have 5 tables inside. The waitress was very knowledgable and enthusiastic about their menu. She was attentive at all times and makes you feel at home. It's like dining at close relatives house. The menu listed was very limited compared to the other Filipino restaurants in the area but the food was really delicious! It features most of the classic Filipino dishes (caldereta, adobo, sinigang, laing etc.) Our orders took awhile to come out but the karaoke sure saved us from being bored. We ordered Dinuguan which was very good. Yum! The Crispy Pata was a while longer so we sang some more karaoke while we wait. All their portions are very generous. The prices are reasonable for such tasty dishes and good service. They have a Salu-Salo (kamayan) on the weekends which they talk highly about but needs a reservation if you ever plan to go. Cash only and BYOB! Awesome place! I would definitely come back!

I opened a yelp account just to give this place a review. This family owned quaint restaurant is fantastic; great food and excellent service. I was here a couple of times with friends. The KAMAYAN Night (eating with your hand) is awesome; consists of three baskets - basket of entrees, basket of noodles and basket of salted duck eggs, tomatoes and mangoes. The Karaoke was so much fun. We had a great time. The second time I was here, my friends & I ordered a la carte. We had Laing, Kalderetang baka (beef stew in tomato sauce), Tinolang Manok (chicken in ginger broth), Fried Milkfish & Sitaw & Kalabasa (long beans & squash). Everything that we had was so good! I particularly liked the Kalderetang baka (Beef stew), it was cooked in perfect softness and the gravy, sooo yummy! Great food, fantastic service and fun!!! We'll definitely go back again with friends!!!

Maybe we caught them on a bad day but quite frankly the food was not all that good. I must say the only dish we enjoyed was the Liang which was unique and very good but the fried milk fish  and beef stew were woefully overcooked and only the sauces provided saved them from being virtually inedible. We also had the Shanghai egg rolls which were gritty and not very good at all and that came with a Japanese sweet chili sauce. That said the service was very good and the people who work there are  very nice. I wasn't crazy about the bad singing and loud karaoke music but I expected that and was willing to deal with it if only the food had been better.

I came to Papa's Kitchen for my birthday, and could not have been more pleased. It's cosy and comfortable, and our group of 15, the largest size they can accommodate, basically had the run of the entire space. The salu-salo sa bilao was ample and incredible--baskets of delicious pork belly and pancit kept getting put out on the table--and the servers were kind enough to periodically clear off our plates so we could keep gorging ourselves (when we weren't singing or running to the bodega next door for more beer). The staff was welcoming and thoughtful, and kept things completely laid-back and convivial. They helped us figure out the karaoke machine, and, completely unannounced, they even brought out a birthday cake! Papa's Kitchen was totally affordable and delicious and FUN, and I couldn't recommend this place more highly.
Every time I've been there, the bread was stale.  Great staff, but what's an Italian deli with stale bread?????

We stayed in the city for my wife birthday . We searched yelp for a great place to eat that was wallet friendly.   We were surprised by the atmosphere.   The food quality was great. Definitely get the spaghetti carbonara and ask them a prosciutto to it!!. We loved it... great find so close to time square
Amazing food and great service.  Melanie was great and really takes care if you.  The calamari was outstanding and you must get the carbonara Melanie style! Soooo good.
Was recommended by daughter. Very reasonable and great food. Convenient location to where we saw a show. Great discount incentive when we checked in on Yelp(10% off bill)

We ate in the bar area.  We stopped in after getting rush tickets to Chicago. We were going to Book or Mormon that evening (which is next door).  We found out from the bartender that we could pre-order intermission drinks, which we availed ourselves of.  We had bruschetta. The server brought from extra bread as a comp. Excellent food and service. Will definitely return when we're in the Times Square area.

A swell place, if a little too loud.  (But I was there when they had a band playing bossa nova, so that was probably the reason for the volume.)  My friend had the burger, which she loved.  I had the vegetariano, because I wanted something simple, and you cannot ever, ever, ever go wrong with rice and beans.  And the yucca fries were perfect.

Tight spot for Cuban food in Brooklyn.  The vibe is upbeat, especially when a live jazz band is performing a few feet from the table.  The room is spacious but very inviting with dim lights barely lighting the dark wood tables long wooden bar to one side.   Food:  Highly recommend the Ropa Vieja and Poncho Pollo!  Both very tasty! Oh and if you love kale and garlic, you have to get the seasonal greens!   Good vibe and delicious Cuban food without breaking the bank is enough to make me a happy customer.  Can't wait to try their brunch!

A cute spot, filled with romantic couples (and blasting rock music). All we had was the Pig Out for two: very satisfying. I know, the $49 charge looks steep, but it's worth every penny. The noodles weren't as warm as I had expected, but they were still tasty. The pork belly was rich and succulent. I wasn't impressed with the other options on their menu, but this dish is very good.

Hands down one of the best meals I've had here in NYC. I've had my eye on Tuome (pronounced Toe-may, since the chef's Asian mother couldn't pronounce Tommy) for quite some time now. The small menu was a little bit of a turn off so it took me a little while to get the urge to check this place out, but I am so glad I did. It seems like the star on the menu here is the pig out for two, but that wasn't that attractive to me and they were out of it anyways by the time we got there around 9. For starters, we shared the octopus and the oxtail spring rolls. These two dishes and the sides were what initially attracted me to come here. The octopus was cooked perfectly, not too chewy or rubbery like many places. The potato foam that the put on at our table was cool to witness and added a great variety of flavor along with the pork xo. Only complaint I had with this dish was that the pork xo was a little too salty for my liking. The oxtail spring rolls came next and these were equally great. The star of the dish was the cumin dipping sauce. It was just too good and we ended up saving it to use on our other dishes. If they bottled that sauce and sold it, I think it would be a huge hit. Next along came our entrees, the scallops and skate, along with a side of the highly praised corn. Honestly, I can't stop thinking about how delicious the scallop dish was. I am always hesitant to get them because they end up being quite boring and bland, but here it was not the case. They were cooked perfectly and served with a flavorful foie gras sauce and carrot purée. The execution of this dish totally blew my taste buds away. Now every time I see scallops on a menu at a different restaurant, I don't even bother because Tuome has set the standards pretty damn high! As for the skate, I had a little bit of my friends and enjoyed it like the rest of the food, especially because cauliflower was incorporated in the dish. The only disappointment I had with this meal was the corn. It was an attractive and flavorful combination of curry, lime, and creme fraiche, but a good amount of the kernels were dried up and chewy, so we weren't really able to enjoy the side dish. Despite that, the rest of the meal was flawless and still earns 5 stars in my book.

NYT and Eater reviews had primed me a good meal; Tuome exceeded the hype those two positive articles provoked.   With good music and tables packed cozily beneath cool light fixtures, ambiance is set nicely for a date or catch-up with a good friend or two.  Not sure I'd choose it for a larger group. Wine list offers a bunch of options in the $45 - $65 range, but enough pretense, let's get to the food: They brought out tiny papaya salads as an amuse bouche, which was a thoughtful and delicious start to the meal. Deviled eggs, with their crunchy exterior, were terrific.  Serving comes with three half-eggs.  We ordered oxtail spring rolls as our other appetizer (two per serving) and they were tasty, but were a clear second-place to the deviled eggs. I almost didn't order the short rib entree because of my dislike of sweet potato, but thankfully went with my gut.  The meat was flavorful and tender and the sweet potato puree was unbelievable.  If they packaged that puree for take-away, they would create an army of Thanksgiving MVPs. The missus ordered the chicken entree, which she said she loved.  (I was too busy ogling our side dishes to taste her meal.)  The corn, with creme fraiche and curry, was a revelation.  The rice, packed with chinese sausage inside a kale leaf, would be the best dish at dozens of comparable restaurants. Believe the hype and bump Tuome way up your restaurant to-try list.

While browsing the NYT, I stumbled upon the review for Tuome which painted a picture of an accountant raised by traditional Chinese parents, who decided to open up his own restaurant after working at Eleven Madison Park. I love stories like these of 8-5 workers who colored inside the lines and then decided to pursue their passion anyways, regardless of the instability, insecurity, and unknown it might give. With a little juggling, we managed to score an 8pm reservation at Tuome. The restaurant facade is how the article describes it, brick walls, but with a little flair. The lighting was dim enough to set a romantic mood, and each table was set with small jars of lavender, tres chic. Amuse bouche was light and a nice slow introduction, (papaya salad). We started with the oxtail spring roll appetizer, and while the essence of bone marrow was not obvious to me, I preferred it that way. Instead the flavors were more in line with the beef itself. The wrapper was fried lightly, without the overpowering oil that encompasses most spring rolls. Of course, we had to try to Pig Out, there really was no other option. I was however surprised with how delicious it was. Each little piece of pork belly was fried with a crispy top and soft and juicy undersurface. I've had my fair share of pork belly, but I've never had pork belly like this.  Surprisingly, I enjoyed the noodles just as much. Each bowl was a large serving of thick, al dente noodles covered in an ode to peanut sauce. We also ordered an obligatory vegetable dish (corn and curry with kaffir lime), which was just as perfectly seasoned as everything else, although it was slightly heavy with the creaminess, but I'm sure some people like it that way. We were extremely full and satisfied. Based on the other reviews, I knew I was going to get a great meal. I will say though that the food had more Southeast Asian flavors than say Chinese flavors. Go into it with an empty belly and you wil be rewarded. What to say yes to: - Early Reservations - Casual but classy attire - Pig Out

Japanese restaurants are becoming prevalent in the area. However, there aren't that many that are authentic. In fact, in most Sushi joints are probably owned by people who does not even speak Japanese. Murasake, (means purple... yes, my date actually looked it up) the most authentic Sushi shop I've dined at in CT. The seafood was very fresh. They offer an extensive variety of sashimi which is very fresh and nicely cut by their Sushi chef (George) They even offer sea urchin and quail eggs. You don't see these kind of exotic options everywhere. The service was good. The interior design of the shop is original. I am impressed by this establishment and will return for more fresh cut sushi!!
Great dinner last night, Lobster and steak sandwiches were great but the sweet potato fries were out of this world! Bronx pale awl also worth a rerun
Excellent food and great place. It's a really charming brunch spot. Really good service and food. The veggie omelette was delicious.

Talk about great food, beer, and service!!! Very cool bar with a great selection of craft beer on draft. The manager greeted us at door and was able to arrange for 8 of us to eat on marathon night. Fun personalities and helpful staff. Burgers cooked perfectly to order and chicken tender and juicy. French fries, especially the sweet potato, are amazing!!! Ciabatta bread a lil too crispy for a sandwich but nice on its own. Clean restaurant. Music at the perfect level. Will definitely return. Thanks for a pleasant meal!

LOUD and almost identical to Valhalla across the street in terms of layout, clientelle, and food/drink selection. It's your typical bar with typical bar food fare, plus an exceptional beer selection. Mixed drinks run $7-9 due to Midtown. Bathrooms are especially nice -- there's even music in there, haha.
An incredible bar and grill masquerading as a pub. The food is exquisite and gourmet. There are a ton of beers on tap, and none of them are Coors Light.

We LOVE LOVE LOVE Alfie's. We first went there two years ago on Thanksgiving week and it was so comfortable and festive inside and the vibe is a lot of fun. We love their food. Salads are full of great chunky and fresh vegetables. Sandwiches are really creative and have ingredients that really compliment each other in unique ways. The fried pickles and the spinach dip are fantastic. We've been there for Brunch as well and the Veggie Omelet is fantastic. We have ordered many items from their menus and we have been pleased with every single thing we've ordered. Go ahead...order anything that sounds good to you. It will be fantastic! Service is wonderful and the decor and ambiance is really fun and comfortable. Thanks to Alfie's! We make sure to go there every time we are in NYC!

Eeh...I think this place is just OK and quite expensive for what it is... It was once japanese, but is now pan-asian cuisine...What's up with this pan-asian trend anyway?..It's like saying pan-American cuisine and serving hamburgers, enchiladas, and whatever Canadians eat... ??? ... The hibachi is just OK - I've had better... The sushi is just OK - I've had better... The entrees are just OK - I've had better... It's like they sacrificed high quality for big selection...Kinda like what the Cheesecake Factory does - they have a menu the size of 'The Iliad' and the food isn't much better than a diner, but much more expensive... I love the specialty places and the independent eateries...But for Chinese, Japanese, Hibachi and Thai, which are vastly different cuisines, there are better places in the area to dine...
Excellent. Eat in take out or delivery very good, Plus BYOB when u eat in a great saver!!!!

Came here tonight with my two girl friends to celebrate of their birthdays it was my first time here and this place definitely lived up to its name. The portion were decent size I ended up taking 1/2 my meal home. We start off with the calamari for appetizer. I had the veal Parm for my entree and we all shared a tiramisu for dessert. I think I just found my favorite Italian restaurant in south philly.

This is by far the freshest and best Italian food ever!  The ambiance and service was impeccable.  We started with fried calamari and caprese salad.  The fried calamari was lightly breaded and fresh.  The caprese salad was not too shabby either, fresh basil, ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella in a balsamic glaze.  I had the bow tie pasta with mushrooms and a basil cream sauce.   Delish! My husband raved about the angel hair with clams and wine.   My daughter had the chicken parmigiana which was a huge thin sliced breaded chicken cutlet with provolone  cheese.  This is a must see in South Philly!  An original landmark and gem that you will remember for years to come.

I enjoyed a wonderful dinner with the Mrs.  Started with the stuffed calamari and shrimp cocktail and the italian antipasto. All were excellent and very tasty.  Then we moved onto the osso buco and my reliable chicken parmigiana. Oh and I forgot to mention the  broccoli rabe, Everything was delicious. The staff was friendly and attentive.  For dessert we had the italian cream cake with rum and the ricotta canoli with chocolate chips. Overall we had a very pleasant dining experience in one of the most authentic italian restaurants in Philadelphia.

Don't know at what restaurant Dana G ate, but I don't think it was this one.  Dante and Luigi's is very clean, pristine tablecloths and sparkling glassware.  As for the food being pseudo-Italian, sorry don't see that either.  I would like to know what she thinks is "legit Italian."
Great food, great service! Past is perfectly al dente! The gravy is top notch and bread is great!

Yay!  My man and I hit the Drinkery tonight, and we were thrilled to have a great dinner, in a great atmosphere at a totally wallet-friendly price point.   I had the veggie burger.  The bread was delish.  The veggie "patty" was flavorful and clearly not of the freezer.  The fries were crazy good, especially the dipping sauce.  I could NOT stop eating the fries and sauce!!! (Thank god my man is well hooked because if this was a first date, he would have thought I was trying to avoid talking to him!)  His dinner was also good, but I'll leave that to him to review. The beer, of course was awesome.  John (bartender and owner) is a bounty of knowledge when it comes to beer.  He told us about his fancy beer engine with such wide-eyed enthusiasm  that he made us both water at the mouth.  He offered up a tasty sample which reminds me: I must explain the awesomeness that is John.  I know John as a bartender first, friend second.  Back in 2005 I started going to the dive and have gone every Tuesday since.  He's a tremendous wit who welcomes you into his bar with a handshake and a warm introduction that leads you to believe that you are long-lost family.  No, I am not exaggerating.  He's a super friendly, funny, smart philly guy.  You'll be happy to enjoy your dinner for all of your own reasons, as well as the satisfaction you'll feel  from supporting this genuinely great guy. Okay, so if for no other reason, hit up the drinkery sometime soon for the pumpkin funnel cake on special.  I asked how long it would last, because when I tell you it was good....words cannot express.   Special desserts are the at the discretion of the chef.  If the funnel cake isn't there anymore, wipe your tears away and order the new dessert.  Odds are it's bangin.

Great neighborhood bar! Good things on tap, and the menu offers up delicious items not seen everyday - Ostrich, Bison, Rabbit, Boar, Duck.  Staff was friendly, jukebox eccletic, and the crowd nice & mellow - actually allowed me to enjoy my date and our discussion. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!! Good to know - they have a 2nd floor that offers additional seating, pool table and more TV's for your viewing pleasure.

Full disclosure 1: When I lived a bit closer to it, the Dive was my second home. Okay, maybe my first. Point is I'm already biased, because I have big hearts for John. Full disclosure 2: This place is about 50 feet from my front door, so I really, really want to like it. Having said that, the beer selection is good, and they actually have decent wine options. I've had the fish and chips, which were great after a few glasses of wine and a ginormous bottle of Brooklyn Local,  and the veggie burger (Not on the same day. I promise.) Veggie burger was great, but messy. The brie, though, is by far my favorite. Yeah, it's a little bright, but given the location's seedy past, I have a hunch the excessive light aims to appease the neighborhood olds. If you've ever seen the crowd that used to hang out here, you'd understand. Upstairs is neat, too. I'm really happy this place is here, and not just because it means I have to walk half as far to get a beer. I hope it stays a while.

Villa Brazil is the perfect place when you are looking for something different and want to try many things. I have been here multiple times and the food is always  fresh. I also love the variety of food and that there are options for everyone; It goes from different vegetables and salads to pasta and even fried fish. The meat options are pretty good too. They have hanger steak, sirloin, skirt steak, chicken, pork loin, sausages, ribs and even chicken hearts among others. I also like that they offer different NATURAL FRUIT juices as well as delicious rich desserts.
This place serves one of the best farofa's. Very flavorful. And good sausages too.
I thought Copacabana's buffet was the best in town, Villa Brasil makes them look foolish.

Met some friends for dinner this week. They all suggested Indian food, and although I had never had it before, I thought it was time to give it a try.  The food was amazing!! The portions were fair and everything tasted very fresh. Although my favorite was the Samosa Chat starter, the Chicken Korma and Garlic Nan were delicious as well. The young man who took our order brought us another starter on the house, the Vegetable Pakora, and we all enjoyed that as well. The restaurant was tidy and clean and the service attentive but not overwhelming. Great place. Will definitely be back.
Wow, this is my new go to Indian place in the area.  I suppose the service was a little spotty, but then again we had a 10 person party. The prawn saag was great!   Bill Lehr aikiacupuncture.net
Cramped space but the heater was on. The service was very good but sort of slow. The food was all very fresh and delicious. The bathroom was through the kitchen but very nice!

Moving to Princeton after several decades in Manhattan is a shock to one's palate, as is adjusting to the dearth of delivery and take out places.  Most of the restaurants range from mediocre to inedible and are overpriced with one notable -- and surpising -- exception: Pizza Star.  This review is for those of you NON-pizza eaters who want fresh, and freshly prepared, homemade food and would never think it possible to find such a thing at the local pizza joint. For example, the Eggplant Parm dinner has eggplant that is neither stringy nor "fishy" tasting but, rather, melts in your mouth and comes with a large helping of (always perfectly) al dente pasta on the side.  The Lasagna is so phenomenal it is hard to imagine that someone was not slaving away in the kitchen hours before it appears on the plate -- perhaps they were.... The Fettucine Alfredo has a very light (Northern Italian style w/butter and good quality parmesan -- not with gobs of cream as in so many American restaurants) and delicately spiced sauce with fresh parsley on top. The pasta dishes remind me of the homecooked food that I received at friends' houses while spending the summer in Florence many years ago; in fact, were Pizza Star to change its name and decor it could easily find success as Princeton's newest Trattoria. And finally, the salads -- all of which are huge and reasonably priced.  The Arugula salad comes with two massive mounds of goat cheese and many good quality olives.  One would pay more in the grocery store just for the goat cheese and olives alone than for the cost of this salad.  All of the salads come with crisp and fresh lettuce -- also not what you'd expect in a pizza place -- and the three optional dressings: Balsamic Vinaigrette, Italian and Ceaser are fabulous -- so much so that we keep the extra and use it for days after our order.  The broccoli sauteed in olive oil and garlic is an excellent side that surpasses anything comparable at Whole Foods and, fortunately, comes unsalted so that you can taper the amount. I rarely write into review services like this, but feel that our family owes it to Pizza Star for helping ease our transition to the constraints of culinary life in Princeton.

Okay this place might be a hidden gem but hopefully not for long! Great burgers and great fries! Quality and taste and for a very good price. Definitely worth checking these guys out - and that's coming from a burger fanatic! Glad I stumbled across this place, will be back soon enough.

Bummed that they were out of veggie burgers, but Report from my friend on the Americano burger was good. had onion rings and shared in the french fries, with sauces, cheese and chipotle. Onion rings are really amazing! Definitely worth your time and dollars.

Excellent food and friendly owners. Jerome puts a lot of love into his dishes and it shows - every detail is paid attention to. Their chicken sandwich is the best I've ever had. Brioche buns are delicious, and the onion rings were amazing, light on breading and super crispy. Will continue to frequent this establishment and hope others follow suit, making this a gem of Rutherford.

First time there..waste of 13 dollars. Got the shrimp tacos. Two small shrimp tacos, they forgot the cheese that the menu listed in the ingredients, I only ate 1 taco, and now I feel nauseous. I think there was something wrong with the shrimp. They were not busy at all it was daytime...and the missing of cheese, in a TACO, was a bummer.

Abridged: Over-priced and all rice. College kids love this place, but students tend to love any food in large portions (they are hungry & broke, after all) Pros: -Large Portions (burrito) -Nice Location Cons: -Burrito was nothing more than rice wrapped in a large tortilla. No flavors. No other noticeable ingredients. -Cramped interior -Didn't appear clean inside (not dirty either...just sort of musty) -Metered Street Parking Only
Decent Mexican food.  Prices were ok, taste was decent but not great, I'd go again.

Was here last week with a party of 4, we sat outside even though it was a bit warm. The outside dining experience was really pretty. Service was great, our waitress was very attentive and gave us suggestions as we had not been here before. Food was very good. Pulled pork was amazing! I am so happy to of found a mexican restaurant close to home.

Jesses is by far the best restaurant in the Upper Valley. The food, service, atmosphere and overall experience is top notch. Sarah in the bar cannot be beat when it comes to mixing drinks and pleasing the crowd- and there is always a great crowd!

After many years my Wife and I had the pleasure of returning to Jesse's Restaurant and Tavern for a meal. With us came my wife's sister and her husband Phil. We had been telling them of this log Restaurant which we found after we had left them after visiting them in Boston ,and drove back through and happened upon it ,great then and even better now, the service, provided by our waitress Amy was exceptional, as was the food  which was cooked to perfection. If you ever get to Hanover NH do yourself a favor have a meal there, you will be pleasantly surprised!!

Vegetarian cuisine at its best.  The sandwich orders are great because you get TWO of them. Love the Chik'n, delicious.   If you're vegetarian or want to eat healthier for take out or just grabbing a quick bite, stop here!   Good prices for good food. And it's actually flatbush ave. bet. clarkson ave. and lenox rd. , clarkson becomes woodruff ave. west of flatbush ave.

Went on a Friday night with my wife, BYOB from a nice wine place across the street. Atmosphere: very nice and cozy. Casual but intimate enough for a date. Clean, with plenty of street parking. Service: We were promptly seated, and our waitress took our wine bottle to open. She ran off with it, and we did not see it again for another 10-15 minutes. She took our order, and we waited about 45-50 minutes for a fish and pasta dish. We were disappointed that the couple sitting next to us (who were seated later than us) not only received bread from their waiter, but were served their entrees before us. Whatever, I can do without bread. Here comes the food (finally). Food: I ordered the smoked salmon linguine. The salmon was really tasty, but the pasta was very overcooked. The pink sauce was water thin, so I could barely taste it at all. Plus I ended up with more sauce on the tablecloth than on my fork.   My wife ordered salmon with pesto sauce. The pesto was delicious, but overcooked. Her side of brussel sprouts were great. She also ordered a side of french fries, which were a huge disappointment. They were cold, bland, and obviously from a frozen bag reheated. The chef was nice enough to sprinkle a little parsley on them to try to convince me otherwise. Overall, a nice place with mediocre service and lackluster food. Will probably not be back anytime soon.

My last review was push down to the bottom because yelp policies of rating. That's why I'm writing again to tell my experience in this awesome place, if you are a lover of traditional Italian food or just homemade food you will be in heaven, besides you will have a great experience, service is great and always on point. Our favorite person there is Jose, he is so approachable and always have the right advice for you. Just two words for you TRY IT.

I have been looking forward to visiting The Dead Rabbit for quite some time now so I am glad to say I can cross this one off "my list". If you hang out with me enough you'll realize that "the list" of places I want to eat in NYC is pretty much never ending... what can I say? I love it! So I came with a party of 4. My fiancé had some family in town staying nearby so I thought it would be a good opportunity to check this place out. It is CRAZY busy in here around happy hour time. I mean it is like impossible to find anywhere to stand or sit really. When you walk in there are stairs right in front of you that lead to the upstairs dining area. There is a guy that stands there and will put your name down on the list if you want to go up. Don't try asking him any information because he definitely is not helpful or talkative for that matter. When we finally got upstairs I was so confused... I thought that upstairs would have the taproom menu but it is actually the parlor that only offers small bites. It doesn't really make sense to me because there was only one table downstairs so why would they offer the big menu for that space? After talking with the waiter we were able to order from that menu as well which made me happy. I ordered the chicken pot pie and it was very tasty but a little bit salty. The portion was ity bity so I was a bit disappointed. We ordered a big bowl of punch and I loved the cute teacups and overall presentation. Not to mention how delicious the cocktail was.. I could have had like 10 more. I wish I remembered the name. He brought us a little sample of it when we first sat down and I was sold. I know it was a punch.... hmmmm. Anyway I like the idea of this place a lot and the cocktails are delicious but I don't think I would go out of my way to make another visit.

Amazing! We had the whiskey sampler flight and our bartender gave us just the right amount of information and attention to help us understand each whiskey. I had a hot whiskey drink (the Clontarf Punch) to warm up and it was delicious. The atmosphere was great, but we were happy we arrived around 5 to get seats and drinks before it was packed because it's a small space and obviously no secret.
Tap Room is awesome. Wood shavings on the floor, great music, excellent aurora. I love this spot and since I work an 80 second walk away I will be sure to be a regular.

Don't let the dark name fool you, the Dead Rabbit is a lively place and a hell of a good time. I especially like the second floor with its old-timey drinks and they have the coolest hand crafted menu that I felt I needed a handlebar mustache to order from. Took all my willpower not to try to steal one for home. The drinks are a bit pricey, but they never disappoint.

Most places in fidi are dead at night. Even those places on Stone Street aren't pippin at 9pm. The Dead Rabbit, however, is crowded, even at 9pm on a week night. There are 2 floors here. The first floor is more casual, you can sit at the bar or stand around. I usually stay in the first floor to wait for a table on the second floor, where you can sit. They will give you an extensive drink menu. I personally recommend looking at the section called "Strong". What's the point of drinking a weak drink? Drink a strng drink for the best bang for your buck. You can also order food. The french fries are decent and so is the cheese platter. If you are hungry, I will recommend eating before you come. The portions here are small and better as an appetizer.

Was rush so I never partook of the eats.  The house Ale is awesome and the surroundings though very small and tight are homey and inviting.  The bride and I are finding an excuse to come back and spend the afternoon.  The train versus the car if you know what I mean.
very poor service.

This is a lovely dining experience, but the food is only average. I've been here twice, once for a birthday celebration and once when my parent's were visiting. The first time I had the prime rib, which is normally something that I LOVE. This prime rib was just ok, it was certainly edible but felt a little tough (even though I ordered it medium.) The second time I got scallops in a sauce, they tasted under seasoned and a bit too fishy, but I normally love scallops so that was surprising. We did get a spinach and crab (or lobster...) dip for an appetizer that was awesome. And I've had the key lime pie as a dessert and that was also good. The staff is really great and the building itself is very cool, especially the bar area. They have an outdoor dining area which I haven't sat in but looks nice for a summer evening. In the future, I will probably only come here for drinks and appetizers, the entrees don't seem to be worth the cost.

I really like the decor of the rooms at Bloomfield Steak & Seafood House. There is also a nice patio area. The food is very good with ample portion sizes. The service good and accomodating (most recent trip involving a group of changing size - started small and people joined throughtout our time there).

The Meatball Shop is the Christian Slater of restaurants except instead of "playing an asshole over and over extremely well," this establishment "makes an awesome meatball over and over extremely well."  I have a great respect for Christian Slater and the Meatball Shop because they have excellent focus on their chosen role in existence. I guess I got lucky, because the place wasn't crowded at all when I had the opportunity to consume here. I had the spicy beef smash and it was great.  The service was quick and courteous.

We were fatty bo batties here on Sunday night. We went in thinking we'd split one ice cream sandwich, and then 15 minutes later had three in front of us. People stared at us it a mocking manner, and i gave them a look that said "so what, i can do what i want, i'm an adult ." We sat at the bar since we weren't getting food and the waitress was so nice. She went through the shpeel and explained the laminated menus where you can check off what you want. It was a great excuse to show of my 4 year old male handwriting and be made fun of. I thought the cookies were delicious, I guess he was dieting or something because he didn't eat them. So I ate his. The waitress recommended the special blueberry yogurt and i said yes. Man got mint and chocolate chip. Mint was super refreshing, but i'm a fatty on the inside so i just care about rich decadence over palette cleansing. We are going back, i demanded it upon leaving. The meatballs look great and the atmosphere is perfect for a casual night out.

There seems to be a very tricky balance of pro's and con's going on here. Pro's: 1. The staff is reasonably friendly. 2. The prices are reasonable. 3. The food is decent.  Slightly interesting. Con's: 1. Over rated. 2. Terribly crowded, which to the shop is a plus. 3. Cramped. 4.  Honestly, if I were judging this solely on what I ordered it would have received a lower rating.  I had the beef meatball with parm sauce.  It was just average. The pork with mushroom sauce was quite nice though.  And the roasted vegetables were quite tasty! Are these better than my mom's?  No way.  But I'd return more if it weren't so hard to get a seat.

Based on all the hullaballoo about The Meatball Shop on the LES, I was pretty sure that instead of Italian bread stuffed with a tasty mix of cheese, garlic and pork, I was gonna find a hip storefront stuffed with scenesters who are too cool for school.  Wrong!  (Well, and a little right about the scenester thing).   This place has AWESOME, fresh, made with care Italian food that really left me impressed.  The pesto sauce (special of the day) was like justblended basil, and the mint ice cream tasted like it was made from mint grown in grandma's garden.   So this place got its gimmick and became a star.  They certainly pull out all of the stops with a menu centered entirely around meatballs.  I loved the many different meatball options and the specials of the day.  Even if you think you don't like meatballs (I mean, who would that  even be anyway?), you probably will after you leave here.  You can get chicken, pork, beef, jambalaya (that was the daily special) and other kinds of meatballs I can't even imagine.  You pick a matching sauce and then you can get the (I really don't wanna say meatball again - it kind of sounds dirty) suckers served as sliders, on a hero, in a sandwich or on top of a pasta side or the greens of the day.  Really, there's kind of something for everyone.   You can also mix and match your homemade fresh ice cream of choice with a homemade crispy cookie (there's peanut butter, chocolate chip, coconut and something else I can't remember) of your choice to make an ice cream sandwich for dessert.  It's imperative that you order this.  It's also fun to use the dry erase marker and menu.  Cute touch. Even the lemonade was great - and maybe I'm only saying this cause the bartender was sweet enough to make us lemonade bellinis, which weren't on the menu, but were a special treat cause we kind of wanted one.   The decor here is super cute and it's a really affordable fun and delicious lunch or dinner.  You probably don't need to hear me say any of this though since The Meatball Shop is so "HOT ON YELP" right now.  I figured I'd through in a penny into our community pool of thoughts.  Enjoy!

Reasons why I like the Meatball Shop 1. The top of their menu says "BALLS" 2. Pork meatballs 3. sliders 4. special Duck meatballs! 5. Ice cream sandwiches with homemade cookies Reasons why I do not like Meatball Shop: 1. 45 minute wait = 75 minute wait 2. no mixing of my balls! My sister and I went here for dinner because I knew anything that combined meatball subs and ice cream sandwiches would be a hit with her.  It was.  However, of course the wait got to us and we were famished by the time we were sat at the bar.  Due to being so hungry, the two of us ordered this massive list of food: one beef meatball sub, one pork "smash" (on a bun) with mozzarella and spicy sauce, one duck slider, one side of vegetables, one side of polenta, one chocolate chip cookie sandwich with vanilla and one with caramel ice cream.  We both also drank a beer to allow something in our bellies while we waited for our food to come.  By the time we were finished we were both so full it was difficult to hold ourselves upright.  I looked at least 7 months pregnant.  It was worth it.

One of NYC's best concept restaurants. It's fun to be given a laminated menu and a sharpie and choose your food.  The flavor combinations of the meatballs, sauces, and sides/ sliders/ heros are fantastic.  They have a good selection of wines and beers too.  The best part is for dessert. You get to choose what homemade ice cream and fresh baked cookie you want for an ice cream sandwich.  It's simply delicious. Enjoy.

As the number 1 Hot on Yelp for a few weeks now, this restaurant easily moved its way to the #1 spot on my list of "to-try-before-i-leave-nyc" in two weeks. Finally decided to go on a Saturday afternoon with my bf, probably around 2 ish for lunch. We waited around 20 minutes, which is pretty average, especially for a place that is so hyped up at the moment. Everything was as delicious as I expected. Balls: beef, spicy pork, chicken, veggie...special was: lamb. Sauces: tomato, spicy meat, mushroom gravy, parm cream..special was: pesto Get it either in a bowl, on sliders, mashed on a roll, or in a hero. We both got the hero, as we figured this was the best deal for your money. Easily the largest option for our hungry selves, and you get a little side salad with it.  My hero was beef meatball in the mushroom gravy with mozzerla cheese. AMAZING. The wheat bread was perfectly toasted, fresh, and the meatballs laid perfectly on it. Bf had spicy pork with spicy meat sauce, which was tasty as well..and not really that spicy, just had a little kick...and I liked mine better :) Salad was just a bed of arugla with some apples and dressing. A nice, light side to the heavier hero. We also split a side of rigatoni, which was al-dente and marinated in a tasty tomato sauce. Pretty standard. Of course we had to try these ice cream sandwiches. I got chocolate chip cookies with vanilla, and he got peanut butter cookies with chocolate ice cream. Cookies were warm and just the right softness. Meatball Shop definitely lived up to the hype, and I've been thinking about going back since! :)

A great afternoon  snack. Got there at 4:30 today and waited only 5 minutes. It was full but thankfully the queue was short!! If you like beef, go for it, you can never go wrong with the ole standard; but if you want more variety, then try the sliders--- pork and chicken at $3 a piece for example for variety of the offerings. Two are good for a tapas style serving with a side dish---if you have a bigger appetite then sample other items off the menu, but be aware that for other sections of the menu, you can choose only one type of meatball, thus I would stick with the sliders. This place is very affordable so it is up to you. For the summer do get the $3 PBR - a Milwaukee special. The wine list looks good and a nice survey of Europe if you are down with that too. Service is good and generally attentive.

Delicious. Arrived at 7pm on Tuesday, waited 35 minutes but had wine at the bar while we waited. It is VERY loud. I had the special meatballs (bolognese) with regular sauce. Salad special was phenomenal. We had a side of polenta -- fantastic -- and then I had the mint ice cream with brownie cookies for dessert. Mint ice cream tasted like I was eating a mint leaf. So good and fresh and creamy.  The noise was a deterrent, but the food was delicious and the wait staff and hostess were lovely.

I LOVE this place.   It is comfortable. It is reasonably priced. It is nicely decorated. The food is good. I tried the pork meatball hero.  WOW! Those are some tasty meatballs!  I was drooling.  The mozzarella was fresh.   My only problem was that the bottom of the sandwich was soggy.  I had considered taking it to go, and I heavily recommend against takeout....It would have been sloppy mess!  Surely there is something they can do to prevent this- I have never seen this before anywhere else I got a meatball parm hero.   The hero was 9 buck and the beer 3 buck.  How can you go wrong?   I sat at the bar, and I thought the bartender was GREAT.  I do not enjoy my meals with snobby or rude attitudes..which is all too frequent in NYC.  This bartender had a smile on her face the entire time, was friendly, happy, helpful, quick, and positive.  That's what I'm talking about.   I really like that the hero comes with a yummy mixed green and apple salad.  It seems most places throw fries as the default, but the salad was wonderful!   I can't WAIT to return to try their other offerings!

The wait was WAAAY too long. We waited over an hour and that's just not cool for a place that sells meatballs. Also, when we were finally seated, my seat was touching the seat of the person behind me (same situation for my bf). Pretty claustrophobic. Not to mention that there doesn't seem to be enough staff at the restaurant because it would take forever for us to get served. We got the special that night that included a pesto sauce that was delicious and redeemed the whole experience in my mind. We tried a bit of everything, sliders, heroes, risotto, and the balls with the focaccia. If I got back, I probably wouldn't order the hero and would just get a bunch of 4 balls w/ focaccia and various sides. The wholewheat hero was just not worth it as a healthier option. I thought the bread tasted awful and ruined the meatball. The ice cream sandwich for dessert was great though. 1 was enough for the two of us to share.

amazing meatballs, great service, but the room is crowded, and waiting 30 minutes for a table here is AGONY.   do yourself a favor and only come with 1 friend, because a group of 3 or more will have to wait for the appropriate number of people to leave the big annoying communal table in the middle.   there is a bar, however, and if you are alone, you can just plop down and order immediately. I had beef balls with mushroom gravy on top of polenta.  solid comfort food option, and appropriate portion sizes for the $

The Meatball Shop has awesome BALLS! I got the Chicken meatballs in a spicy meat sauce with rigatoni on the side and it was phenomenal.  My hot date went with the beef meatballs in the same spicy meat sauce and a beet salad. For Dessert we had the peanut butter cookies with a scoop of Espresso coffee and all I can say is F'n WOW!   All in all I guarantee you'll love their balls and you won't get the shaft with their prices.

Owner #1:  We are opening a shop based mostly on different types of meatballs.  How do we convince people to try us out? Owner #2:  Don't know.  I could just imagine people seeing the name Meatball Shop outside the windows, think subway meatball sandwiches and then pass us by laughing. Owner  #1: Hey, I know.  Instead of having giant letters that says Meatballs, why don't we just have it say BALL.  That will get their attention.  Everyone have a one track mind when they hear that. Owner #2:  Brilliant idea.  How could you possibly pass by a restaurant that have the word BALL on the glass windows outside without stopping to see what it is about? Owner #1:  Yeah.  Once they come in out of curiosity, they will be hooked.  Then they will all go on Yelp and make stupid juvenile ball jokes on the reviews which will catch even more people's attention.  We will be rich.  Bwah ha ha ha ha. At least that is how I imagined the Meatball Shop's owners conversation went when they decided to make the restaurant's actual logo and name so small (and have it slightly blend into the glass door) while the word Ball is so big and bright red in the windows.  If so, luckily for them, they also have the ability to cook some darn good food to keep their customers coming back for more.   Our waitress was all bright, bouncy, and cheerfully helped my dining partner and I through our initial confusion of how to order using their laminated menus and their erasable marker (which actually wouldn't write no matter how hard we tried).  She was also a great help with answering our questions about the different types of meatballs/sauces combination and the available sides. Based on her advice I had: SPICY PORK WITH SPICY MEAT SAUCE SLIDER:  Very large, very tender soft pork meat with a very mild kick of heat between a small soft bun.  I would have loved a bit more of the spicy meat sauce on it but otherwise it was delicious. CLASSIC BEEF MEATBALLS WITH MUSHROOM GRAVY ON TOP OF MARKET GREENS:  I had the pork for the slider so I wanted to try a different kind of meat.  How could you have a meat ball with out trying the classic ingredient of beef?  Again this was very tender, and soft and the mushroom gravy was mildly creamy with thick chunks of mushrooms.  The market greens consists of steamed broccoli, leafy greens, soft beets, and slices of sweet apples all mixed with a very nice, mild vinaigrette that doesn't overpower the taste of the fresh veggies. For the side we had the Rigatoni:  The pasta was very al dente.  The tomato sauce used here disappointingly reminded me a bit of the canned Ragu sauce.  Everything was topped by freshly grated Parmesan.  The dish didn't wow me but it was passable. The dessert.  You basically build your own ice cream sandwich. Choose your type of cookie from their selection and then do the same with the ice cream to make your own combination.  We had brownie with mint.  The brownie portion was buttery soft.  I love my cookies that way. The mint ice cream.  Really refreshing and nice.  It tasted like they had actual fresh mint leaves blended right into the ice cream. Now for the bad portion of the review.  I ordered the sangria.  There was more ice in my glass then there was sangria.  It wasn't very fruity and with so much ice, it tasted very watered down.  I wouldn't recommend getting this.   It was pretty cheap at $6.  Then again, ice cubes aren't that expensive. The strong point of the food here comes from it being made with simple high quality ingredients. Everything tastes very familiar, almost like home cooked meals.  No fancy cooking or exotic ingredients from the dishes that we tried.  Just simple food done right...... but with lots of  balls. **************************************************­***************** Photo of the window with the giant word BALL:  yelp.com/biz_photos/P4hm…

I've had some lucky food convives. The girl who accompanied me to Zenkichi, Megu, and the New Amsterdam Market is one. Doing her better is someone I've taken to places as far and wide as Pulino's, Barney Greengrass, and 15 East. But I think everyone else is trumped by the lady who's been with me to Balthazar, DBGB, and friggin' Momofuku Ko. For our next act, I wanted to shift a bit downscale, and when plan A (Lucali) decided to go and have an electrical failure that night, we had to trudge back onto the F train and settle for something on the LES instead. What place could do in a pinch, could follow up the likes of Keith McNally, Daniel Boulud, David Chang...? Would you believe a restaurant from Daniel Holzman? Well, that's the current culinary zeitgeist: take a chef who's worked in Le Bernadin and San Francisco's highly-regarded SPQR. Let him move into a tiny space on the LES. Make it loud, and light it with energy-wasting dim bulbs. Then find an appropriately homey foodstuff -- make sure it appeals to the drunken crowd -- gussy it up with snazzily-sourced ingredients, devote the menu monomaniacally to said foodstuff... Voila! The Meatball Shop is born. It's a fun spot, to be sure. Doing bustling business, it is loud indeed. Did I miss the memo to remain in recession mode? Because dinner here is cheap enough to have made it onto Time Out NY's list of, well, cheap restaurants for dates. I wasn't with a date; personally, I think the place is just too deafening for romancing. But okay, okay, you don't care about any of that stuff. You just want to know about the meatballs. Well, they come via a slew of delivery vehicles, of which I chose the slider route for maximal variety. Choose any meatball meat, choose any sauce, $3 a pop. For the portion size (each meatball is about the size of a golf ball), it's not as crazy cheap as I'd been led to believe, but certainly not unreasonable. I got the beef in tomato sauce, the spicy pork in spicy meat sauce, and the chicken in parmesan cream sauce. Improbably, the chicken was the best of the bunch, succulent and winningly seasoned. The spicy pork wasn't too spicy-hot, but it hid a surprising amount of juice under its bumpy exterior. The beef was a little lackluster on its own, but I imagine it would have been perfect tossed with some spaghetti (also an option). Each meatball was loosely packed, just the way I like my, uh, balls. Though I did not taste it, my convive's meatball hero, all baguetted and with cheese melted sexily on top, also looked appealing. We shared a roasted beet salad, which was good, but who are we kidding, when was the last time you saw someone really mess up roasted beets? But it was the meal's finisher, ice cream sandwiches, that delivered the knockout punch for me. There are a lot of options, but simplicity usually wins for me where ice cream in concerned: I got a generous scoop of vanilla sandwiched in between two "peanut butter cookies". They really turned out to be more like frozen discs of peanut butter cookie dough -- a messy but brilliant flourish, since they decay along with the ice cream, melting and melding their essence with the creamy vanilla. A perfect dessert for a casual joint like the Meatball Shop. So what could've seemed like a pretty gimmicky place a la K! Pizzacone actually ended up being much closer to Rice to Riches in its pure execution of a simple concept. And it clearly has Rice to Riches-caliber staying power. Good news for all of us. Probability of return with 1 year: 70%

It's so cute and tiny! (That's what she said!)     \              \              \ ,¡||||||¡,    ,¡||||||¡,    ,¡||||||¡,  (      )      (      )      (      ) '\|||||||/'    '\||||||||/'    '\|||||||/' The meatball sliders at The Meatball Shop are adorable. Not only that, but they're delicious too. I tried two of the sliders - the Beef with mushroom sauce and their Special for the day (steak, bacon, and cheddar) with traditional sauce. The sliders are punctured with toothpicks to hold them together - so cute! The flavors of the meatballs? Oh so homey and familiar. That's part of the beauty of The Meatball Shop. The flavors aren't overwhelming, but they still manage to hold their own. It's the kind of food that you could eat every day without feeling sick. All of the meatballs are also super tender and moist. Success! I also sampled the side of rigatoni pasta. It was a little on the al dente side for my preferences. I'd pass on it in lieu of some greens next time. To round out the meal, my dining partner and I split an ice cream sandwich - you select what kind of cookie and ice cream you want to mix. We went with one of the more popular options of a brownie cookie and mint ice cream. Yum! The mint ice cream alone was a little reminiscent of toothpaste, but paired with the soft brownie cookie, it was the perfect ending to a fun dinner. I should mention that you're supposed to mark off the menu with the pens on the table. Mine simply refused to work. I swear it had nothing to do with the alcohol I had just downed before getting there. I swear!!!! When it does work though, it sure helps you remember what you were planning on ordering. I like that because I have the worst short term memory ever. The taste is simple, but still worth eating out for. The fare is also relatively simple, yet slightly elevated than what you might make at home. The overall price is reasonable. If it weren't for the wait, I will definitely be back for more balls. Until something else opens up to catch peoples' eyes, I'll have to stick out the inevitable wait - or send a dining partner ahead to secure a spot on the waiting list. *evil giggle*

The Meatball Shop is very tasty although not the best atmosphere. I would opt for the take-out next time because the restaurant itself is very small and cramped. The food, however, was very good! To start I had the Sangria (definitely recommend) and the Spicy Pork Meatball with Spicy Tomato Sauce which was very tasty. I also had the Hero with Beef Meatballs, Tomato Sauce, Mozzarella Cheese, and White Bread. The Sandwich was great! I absolutely recommend the Hero!

1.5 hrs turned into almost 2.5 hrs of waiting, so they gave us some free pork sliders w marinara. Buns were soft and a little bit sweet. Later they started bringing out peanuts for other waiting customers. We were able to snag 3 seats at the bar, we took them so we could finally sit and take our names off the list for the next group. Not sure if this was the best idea--bartender was not a waiter and did not seem happy to have to serve us. For our meal my boyfriend and I shared the hoagie w beef, mushroom, and provolone on wheat bread. The bread was a little burnt which left a bad taste in my mouth, so I tore the worst parts off. It was really cheesy and good aside from the bread. The sandwich came with a nice arugla and apples salad.  We also had the risotto of the day, chanterelle mushrooms and English peas. First bite reminded me up tuna helper cuz of the peas :/ it was ok, but not great. Only had like 3 mushrooms.  Theresa X only ordered a couple of sliders. She gave me half of her pork slider w parmesan cream cuz she felt it was too salty. Pretty good. Overall it was decent. As a visitor to NY, it's cool to go to these types of fad 1 item restaurants and experience them. Plus it wasn't too expensive-$30 for 2 meals and 1 sweet tea (which was disgustingly sweet not a strong brew, skip it). Now I can say I've tried it and there's no need to go back.

THESE MEATBALLS WILL CHANGE YOUR LIFE. I can not get enough of them. The classic meatball with parmesan cream sauce will make you an addict. I have been 3 times since my first visit 2 weeks ago and insist on bringing everyone and anyone I know here to enjoy the experience. Seating is mostly family style so be prepared to rub elbows with strangers.

I was back in NYC last weekend, and my buddy buddy drag me to The meatball shop. ( I pleated for thai food at Elephant.. but i lost the bet Rock, Pepper Sissor) We waited 45 minutes. for our table. 1. Cuuute Host. 2. Spicy pork with mushroom sauce and provolone = made by hands of god. 3. The meat ball is out of this world. 4. beer selection is ok. TRY Pork ball with parm cream sauce and provolone on white. Spicy pork with classic Tomato sauce chicken meatballs with Parmesan sauce Work it up to everything in the kitchen Platter. I don't even like waiting for tables in Los Angeles, or Chicago Culinary scene.  but NYC is whole different animal. and TMS is great example of that.   I can't wait thill I go back!

I just came here last week with my friend Valerie V. and if you see her review, you should know why I have to top this place off with their final star. We didn't complain about our food taking forever but they still sent over a good looking guy to comp our drinks and dessert. Little did he know he just made the day for two feverishly active yelpers. Food is good, service is spectacular. Attractive men are a plus!

Everyone will come here with a different meatball in mind that they think is THE perfect meatball. And can you blame them? Didn't grandma pass down the meatball recipe down to mom who fed it to you and forever biased your expectations for meatballs??? I feared they would "couture" up meatballs, pull some "new LES" spin on the meatball and serve it over vermicelli. "FUSION, MANNNN. IT'S FUSION." I was pleasantly surprised that they took the traditional meatball and made it as good as it can be made. Traditional and excellent. Where I was even MORE pleasantly surprised was that I loved the VEGGIE meatball the most! The Veggieballs were awesome! Tightly packed lentils under a parmesan cream sauce really threw off my preconception of the meatball. it was meaty yet...veggie. I tried all of the meatballs, as is easy to do here. At 2-3 bucks a meatball its easy to sample the Spicy beef, pork, chicken, veggie and "special" which was a spiced lamb meatball. Sampling them as sliders senza bun is the easiest way. The ambience is awesome, communal benches are the perfect condition for many crossed inappropriate ball comments. Not to mention many TWSS's. While I still remember the old school LES, I only have good things to say about this place and its a positive addition, where many others have failed. I almost forgot to mention how amazing my drink was as well as my two sides! The CUCUMBER MINT LEMONADE was off the hook and perfectly refreshing for a hot humid summer NYC day. The market salad was awesome as well as the beet salad (Veggie of the day). ***3 stars for really good meatballs, and an even better overall dining experience. I enjoyed though I can't say I will be frequenting the meatball shop. I'd have to be jonesing meatballs in order to return. It's the only thing on the menu essentially. Still solid 3 stars and 4 likely on a return visit.

This place is fantastic! We had the roasted veggie wrap, the portobello wrap, and the 'chicken' wrap. All delicious and reasonably priced. For a vegetarian with a non-vegetarian family, everyone still found something to eat. We'll be back!

Know what's surprisingly hard to be? Gluten free vegetarian. Gluten free is not by choice, Vegetarian is. But not here!!! Delicious, healthy gluten free options that don't cost an arm and a leg? YES, PLEASE. And they deliver? I'm in heaven.
Came with a friend of mine for lunch. Had veal Marsala. The veal was tough and thin slices. Serve was ok but not great.  For a quick bite nothing more.

Where do I begin... 8pm reservation, waited 20 minutes, not even an acknowledgement or apology After being seated it took 30 minutes for us to get bread and water Another 20 minutes go by, We get our appetizer, mozzarella and corrozza very good I ordered penne ala vodka, worst I have ever had.  All I could taste was butter.  My wife tried it said the same thing.  This was the very first time I have sent something back in 4 years.   I ordered chicken parm as a replacement.  15 minutes later my new entree comes out with over cooked pasta, and chicken that tasted like it was reheated and a day old at the least.  I'd rather have Olive Garden next time. Not once did anyone come over and ask us how it was, my water was empty more often then full. And if there weren't enough subtle hints for them to save the experience we waited 20 minutes for them to give us the check. The icing on the cake,  when I get home I have someone else's leftovers

I'm really surprised by all these low star reviews. Naunas is a staple for Italian food in the area. If I'm ever craving GOOD Italian food... this is where I go. I've never had the pizza and always make a reservation for the back. The calamari with the different dipping sauces is excellent and the Naunas Chicken is my go to but I also lovee the Lobster Rav. I've never had a bad meal here. And it's a BYO which is always a plus!

This is the most wonderful place! Definitely the best mexican I have had on the East coast. Their carnitas taco is heaven, their fish taco yummy (baja style) and their "special" guacamole with papalo is crazy good. My dining companion loved his torta when we went there for brunch too--the one lack-luster element was the huevos rancheros I ordered, but they weren't bad, they just weren't as amazing as the rest. Also, all the people that work here are great--knowledgeable and efficient.

4 stars easy!!!!!! I missed Bonita but this is even better! It is much more spacious than Bonita and has booths and private tables and not communal dining like Bonita. I hated that! One bad thing about posting pictures on Yelp is people recognize you. A guy kept staring at me and I am the type that does not even recognize celebrities much less someone  whose picture I have seen from Yelp. But then again maybe he was just a pervert. About the food, awesome! Best Mexican corn that I have had in NYC, The last one I had at Cascabel Taqueria  was okay but not as flavorful. The one at Carino had more chili powder on it. Delicious! The Gorditas was delicioso also! The fish tacos taste like they were made in California. The food was clean tasting too. Who would have thought eating head cheese tacos would be so good! (it was a special so they might not have it when you go) The fatty pieces of face pork were succulent, the sweet ramps were fantastic. The tomatillo sauce was so good, you could drink it with a straw! The pink drink in the picture is a watermelon juice. I liked the restaurant itself. It was not freezing cold the way many restaurants are. The doors were open and the summer air was keeping the room cool not ice cold! For me that is a plus! A big huge plus! For me the only negative was the menu is limited. But the specials make up for it. Service was warm and friendly even though they were quite busy. Good Mexican  food in NYC is rare so when I am craving Mexican this is another good option. I am glad we went before it becomes a scene and I think it might. But I will be back for sure!

No stars for this place.  The only reason for the one is that they won't let me warn you without one.   Service was terrible and the food was worse.  I wouldn't even bring the steak that I only took two bites of home to the dogs!  I can't believe I paid for the meal.

I tried Coyote Flaco for the first time last night.  I ordered enchilada suiza and a margarita.  The cook accidentally made me enchiladas with mole sauce.  The waitress recognized the error and asked if I wanted to send it back.  Figuring I was up for something's different, I gave the new dish a try and it was good!  So, it was a happy mistake. This is clearly a family run establishment and felt very homey while enjoying dinner.  I am looking forward to come back during warmer weather to enjoy having dinner out on their patio!

I love this place. So far, I've gotten take out twice from Bosphorus, and I've dined in once with my husband. Both at home and in the restaurant, the food is delicious. The service is spectacular. My husband and I are hoping to go back many, many times in the future to try more of their food and some of our new-found favorites. For reference, we have really enjoyed the following and would get them again: - Eggplant appetizer - Mixed Grill - Chicken Shish - Bosphorus Salad - Kazandibi Both for take-out and dining in, they have the most amazing bread. I really like when the bread is fresh-baked and crusty on the outside, and this is what I got from Bosphorus. Dining in, it comes out warm and goes well with their home-made olive oil. If you eat at home, you have the option of saving some for the next day (because it's still good even then). The only small complaint that I could possibly make is that the avocado in the Bosphorus salad was a bit hard for me, not quite ripe. However, it's important to note that it was so delicious despite this that we finished the entire salad. (I was tempted to lick the plate.) The owner is really nice.  If you're not sure what to get, just ask her. Her recommendations were spot on for us.

Woohoo! As good as it gets! This sentiment that Yelp attaches to a five star rating fits the Bosphorus quiet well.  I came upon this amazing restaurant based on the reviews of other Yelpers.  I was excited to see if the place could really live up to the hype.  I can say for certain that without a shadow of a doubt this place deserves all the high praises it has garnered.  I brought the fam bam on a Saturday evening for a nice dinner and everything was fabulous from the start to finish.  And what a finish I tell you.  I'll talk more about it later but they hit it out of the park.  Let me start with the atmosphere and décor of the restaurant.  It's clean, modern, and has touches of Mediterranean flavor with their use of wood throughout.  It is relatively small for a popular restaurant but it makes it the more intimate.  I highly suggest a reservation especially if you go on a busy night. Let's get to the important part of the review then.  The food was delicious, presented beautifully, and left a memorable imprint on my mind.  I hate it when I visit a place for the first time and I forget what I ordered.  That's just disappointing, but with the Bosphorus I remembered everything that we order from the appetizer to the dessert.  Armed with a 4 year old bottle of wine from my dad's reserve, we started the meal with the cold appetizer sampler which consisted of stuffed grape leaves, hummus, babaganoush, and labneh.  All went awesome with a side of fresh, warm bread.  Then the quintessential Bosphorus salad came next.  I suggest sharing this salad with other people because it is both tall and wide.  Look at the pictures and you'll know what I mean.  The flavor is all there.  It was so delicious, I couldn't get enough of it.  Honestly I was already stuffed after eating the app and salad but alas there was still an entrée to go.  My family ordered three different dishes.  Pops went with the gyro; mother the chicken sauté, and me the lamb shish.  I got to try a little of everything and cross-my-heart they were perfectly cooked and so flavorful.  I don't know how consistent they are but at least on that Saturday night they hit those lil' devils out of the park!  It was like being transported to the Mediterranean with its beautiful landscape, sun-drenched mountains, and deep blue ocean all ready to welcome first-time travelers.  There was so much of the entrée left that we had no choice but to take the leftovers home.  But I wasn't going to leave without dessert.  I had to make sure we got the full meal experience.  So my fam shared an order of baklava and kazan dibi.  Baklava came out warm and gooey, which is the way it's supposed to, and the kazan dibi had the perfect caramelized sugar shell.  It was like a turtle hiding its delicate flavor underneath its shell.  What a great end to a meal! As I said in the beginning it was a great time from start to finish and here is why I placed importance on the finish. When my family and I started heading out towards the door, the waiter who had served us the whole night, dropped what he was doing near the counter, grabbed a box, and opened the door for us, thanked us and bid us a good night.  Then he opened the box and inside it were Ferrero Rocher chocolates for each of us to take.  I have been to many, many restaurants but I can say this was the first time that I've ever seen that level of service.  Teşekkür ederim Bosphorus! We will be back!

This restaurant is located next to the municipal parking right by the Nutley diner. I didn't even know that this place existed, but gosh I want to slap myself for not coming here sooner. The food... Good Lord. My boyfriend and I ate like royalty. We had the grape leaves and the fried calf liver. The grapes leaves were perfect, flavorful, moist. The calf liver was perfectly cooked and not at all metallic tasting or gross, like I've had at other places. Then we ordered the lamb chops and the lamb shish. Each came with potatoes, orzo, quinoa, and yogurt sauce. This is easily the best prepared lamb I have ever had. Succulent, tasty and perfectly cooked. For dessert, I had the milk pudding and my boyfriend had the baklava. Just the right amount of sweet and tasty, paired perfectly with a Turkish tea or coffee. It's also a BYOB. The only thing I could possibly say that was that the service was a tad slow, but that's because it's a husband and wife team and the wife is the front of house.
