Also they ran out of the cream caramel and it takes 25 minutes to make the fried ice cream, so if you want that, order that ahead. The woman, Nora, was apologetic, and extremely friendly. She even asked us what our names were and shook our hands after we checked out. Otherwise, this is a hidden gem that truly deserves the five star rating. It's hard to find a place with great atmosphere, awesome food and a great staff, but you can find it here. So go there. Like seriously.

My husband and I are professional chefs and CIA graduates.  This is an excellent restaurant. The food is fresh, well presented and authentic. Everything is prepared fresh to  order. Service was attentive and the place was immaculate. The atmosphere is very low key, which makes this a good spot for an intimate quiet date night. Also, their online menu only represents a small part of their menu.

This place is amazing. The food is delicious and is very well presented. Every dish is like a work of art. Me and my husband really love this place and have been here today for the second time. The pricing is great too and the service is excellent. If you order a salad, make sure to take a picture before eating it as it's really beautiful! We're Israeli and find the food to be authentic Mediterranean food and very fresh and high quality too. It's a bit hard to find the place, which is a pity. Both google maps and Waze doesn't know the address and points you to the wrong place. We tried going there twice and only on the third attempt were able to find it. ------------------------ IMPORTANT: IT'S NOT IN ON FRANKLIN AVENUE, BUT RATHER PARALLEL TO THAT. MAKE TWO LEFT TURNS TO GET THERE EASILY. ------------------ Don't miss the gem. It's the best restaurant around.

The food is always fresh, hot, and delicious. My favorites are the jalapeños poppers, vegetarian chimichanga, fish tacos! They have vegetarian rice which is a great for us non meat eaters out there!  They serve foxon park which I always appreciate. Yes the place is kinda dingy, and they give you regular napkins, but it's part if the charm. It's a low key place to have delicious food and margaritas!

We tried this restaurant a few months ago and absolutely loved it!  We sat outside and the atmosphere was relaxing.  Service was excellent.  We had the wings for an app which were delicious.  My wife tried the fried chicken and I had the clams and linguini.  The clams were fresh but the chicken was out of this world.  My wife is now obsesssed with this place.  If you want a chill night out in Hamden with great food and a relaxing atmosphere i would highly recommend this place.

We did receive a long letter from the owner explaining the situation. That at least shows that get are aware of the yelp reviews and are trying to be proactive. I still cannot comment on the food as we never ate there and are not sure we will go back any time soon. However I do appreciate the owner getting in touch with me to explain the situation and to be fair it may be bad policy mixed with bad luck.

After making a reservation in advance, the hostess asked us to move to another table because another party had a reservation at our current table in about 20 min.  We hadn't even had time to order dinner yet.  But, we were hungry, so we picked up and moved to a bar table. At that bar table, we found ourselves having to ask the bus boy for ketchup, mustard, the check, etc. because our server was MIA.  Then, as we were waiting for the check, the hostess came to our table for a second time, telling us that she needs the table for yet another reservation, so we need to leave asap.  Who does that?  This woman, and apparently this restaurant.  Sometimes I let poor service slide when the food is great.  However, it was such a problem here that I will not be back, and I really did like their food and drink.

My girlfriend and I have been to Park Central 3 times now and are big fans.   We have sat at the bar twice and have decided that is our favorite atmosphere in the restaurant. I usually judge a bar by whether a place can make a manhattan correctly and this was probably the best I've had in quite some time (also stirred and double strained - not shaken!!). My girlfriend had a drink that I think was called salt and smoke. It was a combo of mezcal, pisco, cucumbers, fresh lemon, and salt - don't quote me on exact ingredients. The drink was phenomenal and all of the cocktails on the list looked very innovative and had a great focus on seasonal ingredients. The draft beer list was refreshing, and you could tell that they spend a good deal of time selecting the choices as nothing was mainstream, but there were good local alternatives. I like to try new things and this is a great place to do that. The only problem seems to be that the majority of the crowd didn't feel the same and was content drinking bud bottles. Changing the local crowd is very hard to do, but I do not think this place is going to hit it's full potential if they cannot get their regulars to try the 'brand' they're going for. To move onto the food some of our favorites after our 3 visits have been: oysters on the shell - they had 2 different kinds to choose from and the bartenders were very familiar. The cucumber mignonette was something different and the oysters were certainly fresh. The fire islands were our favorite! Steak Burger with Jalapeno relish was smokey, savory, and juicy. Fried Chicken was ridiculous and had some kind of truffle honey on it that was addicting. Truffle oil can be overpowering when used in the wrong place but the balance with the sweetness of the honey was just stupid! yum! We have also enjoyed an asian inspired special with udon and a kung pow duck confit leg, which showed just how versatile their chef is. Besides the drinks and food the live music on Saturday nights is great and the service is very homey and warm. There was some acoustic band that was there a few weeks ago playing some americana, blues that made the night. I don't see why Park Central is rated so low on yelp. Maybe the restaurant doesn't quite fit the neighborhood? We go out at least once a week and Park Central is now in our top 3 list of restaurants in New Haven area. Thanks and cya soon!!

We recently went there for valentine's day dinner,  We sat in the bar Food: I had to return the clam chowder which tasted funny & cold.  the salad & main course (surf & turf)  was nothing out of the ordinary, didnt love it. Service: They were out of one of the items in the menu, which no one told us and when i ordered it, they said they are out of it and didnt offer any other cuts or option. No one refilled our wine glasses. The table around  us were cleaned using cleanex, the smell of ammonia is not pleasant while eating food, it kept lingering through out the evening. given that its one of the busiest night, it shouldn't be an excuse for mediocre service & food.   Not going back
This place is great. The "host" staff or method used for seating guests is the only thing off.

I came after work with a few of my friends just to get a drink before going home, and it turned into a "thing." We ordered a few drinks from the bar, and also got a few empanadaas also.. It wasn't the busiest time of the day but still having said that the bartender Ben (apologies if name is wrong) was really cool, and he made every drink the exact same way.. I would absolutely come here again!!

Amazingly delicious drinks-every time! ...Matador, Hemingway... we have tried nearly all of them and really like them! The churrasco is always delicious as are the alitas-we dip the plantain side from the churrasco in the sauce from the wings-yum!. We have been back a dozen times if that is any indication... been a few misses... arepas and guacamole did not live up to how good everything else is...

My friend and I go here after races since he's a regular, and they know him by name. The servers are so funny and constantly joke around with those sitting at the bar. Love the interior since it is more of an upscale diner, which feels cleaner and unique to me. Plus the service tends to be better for these types of places compared to a regular diner, and I grew up in south jersey so I like going to diners :). Regarding food, I have several allergies including dairy, soy and gluten so they happily helped me choose something from the menu. My friend got the empanadas, and I had a bite of his oxtail one, which was SO damn crying on the inside good - crispy, slightly sweet, soft on the inside, delectable meat....I want that recipe. My white egg omelette was cooked well though they got the order wrong the first time. If you check in on Foursquare enough times, you get a free cookie! Can't wait to come here more during triathlon training!!!! Good way to motivate oneself :P.

This is the right place for breakfast or after party "eatsomething".the menu is a mix of Latino traditional plates from different places like Peru Mexico or Cuba.i use to go there after work and my fav is guacamole and quesadillas con pollo.dont forget to ask about the habanero sauce but be careful it will burn your mouth!

I have eaten here 3 times, and each time was worse then the previous. The sushi is not fresh, and the fish in the spicy tuna roll the last time had definitely turned.  The "hot" food from the kitchen was only ever room temperature at best.  Tempura is too heavily breaded, and excessively greasy.  The udon is little more than a bowl of sea water with noodles - way too salty to eat.  The miso is bland, and the salads are wilted and limp. Stay away.

Absolutely wonderful food, plus the chefs are surprisingly artistic in their presentation.  I read one review that said the fish wasn't fresh, and I can only thik they're reviewing the wrong restaurant.  We've gone here at least 4-5 times, and I find it remarkable how fresh the fish is. Great place for singles, families, groups.  I go there with my husband, brother and sister-in-law regularly and have never had a dish that wasn't delicious.  They don't have a liquor license, so we bring our own bottles of saki, and the waitstaff are more than happy to heat and serve.  This helps keep the check very low, which is also very attractive (but I always tip at least 20-25% because the servers who are heating/serving my saki shouldn't get stiffed on gratuity of the liquor). Luv it, can't wait to go back...maybe tonight!

This place is starting to grow on me. Came here a second time and the service was just as good if not slightly better. Food was presented well as usually but I what i did notice is that this place does more filling than rice in their sushi, so you know they're definitely not trying to cheat you out of your money. And any place that wants play Westlife on repeat is thumbs up to me!

We were the first people in this restaurant, which we thought was kind of weird, since it was like 6pm, dinner time. Anyway since the place is BYOB, we brought a bottle of wine, and they promptly opened it up and grabbed our glasses. Service was pretty fast, and the sushi was above average. If I'm in the area I would definitely go again.

Dinner or lunch the sushi portions are gigantic and very fresh. They also have free wifi & plenty of parking in the rear.   Delivery is also quick and food is just the same as eating inside. You can even order online right from their website. Best thing here is that it's BYOB!!!
I stumbled upon this place by accident and it was a great find!! Good food for great prices. It also has a nice atmosphere and setting. The staff is great

Food is 5 stars.  I had a Spaghetti alle vongole. It was so yummy. The portion is generous. Dessert was amazing.  Def will come back next time I am in Brooklyn. The restaurant is small and most people eat here are young couples, some with young kids. Our server was very attentive (considering how busy the restaurant was). Lines gets long so make reservation.

Maybe I was just unlucky.  Food was good. Wine selection was great. Service sucked. We were a group of 7 and to avoid any settlement issues - I gave the card to the waiter.  His snarky comment: "oh you are that guy" - was a red flag to begin.  Later - that same waiter, opens bottles without cutting the foil around the bottle neck.  Yeah - it was busy - but why so sloppy on the etiquette? Pouring wine with spillage, over left, right, over the table.  Yes the space is small - but it just got worse.  Later - the waiter brings fish to one of us, drops the veggie on the floor.  Picks it up, goes to the kitchen - 10 sec later gets back  serves the plate and announces proudly - "I salvaged your meal!".  Oh well - I tipped and all paid over $500 - but I am not going back.

I came here for dinner in Oct. 2012 while visiting a friend who lives in Park Slope. It was a Thursday night so we didn't have a reservation. We walked in and were able to sit at the bar. This is a very quant place but just perfect. We both had wine and the butternut squash ravioli. It was perfection. We loved our meal here. The only downside is how their seating is seat up - you'll likely be sitting right next to others not part of your dining party so be prepared to get cozy! Also, it can get pretty loud. Service was excellent and prices are reasonable.

Delicious. Attentive waitstaff. Lovely dinner! We went on a Saturday night with a reservation, and the place was packed. We ordered buffalo mozzarella with butternut squash and polenta as appetizers - we fought each other for the last bite. The mela salad and shaved brussels sprout salad were both incredible-- I have a feeling I'll crave them and have to go back again soon. The fettucini with duck ragu was so good that I didn't even bother to try my husband's entree of seafood risotto, but he ate every bite. We ordered tiramisu for dessert, which was really good but I was too full by then to really enjoy it. The one thing they could improve upon with the food is the bread they offer before the meal - cold, plain white rolls - although the marinara sauce they bring is pretty tasty. And in terms of ambiance, it could be romantic when it's not packed with people waiting to get a seat, but people standing right behind your table detracts from the mood a bit, since there isn't really a waiting section. We will definitely be going back, maybe on a week night next time!

I made a reservation for 7pm. I got there a couple of minutes early. A group of women showed up after I did, along with the rest of my party. They were a group of three, as were we. The other group who showed up later got sat first. When I brought it up to the hostess she said she was seating us right now. The table she was offering us was one another group had opted to abandon so they wouldn't be near the door. So I made a reservation, showed up early and somehow was offered the worst seat in the house. I left. I won't be back.

My typical stance on Italian food is that it is usually delicious, but almost always overpriced. So (considering my love of cheap food) when given a chance to decide on a cuisine, I'd usually pass on Italian. This place has definitely changed my mind about that! Everything is delicious, and as Danny puts it "I don't know if there's something about how they write their menu, but I want to order everything" (paraphrased, of course). Great service. Everything is fresh. Prices are reasonable. I'll never pass on this place.

I live a good thirty minutes from here but worth the trip. Met some friends here that live nearby and I really enjoyed this place. Fantastic beer selection! The burger was good. waitress was super kind and atmosphere was a plus. Parking is off street so can be tough but not a big deal. .bathrooms were nice and clean. Love the mouthwash dispenser in there. Would love to go back.

Even though we have lived in this area for 5 years we never ventured to this town and now that we have we have been here a few times.  I am lucky we found this place.  The bar itself has a huge selection and drink menu with specials that changes all the time.  Being a vegetarian I was a little stand offish to try the veggie burger here but I did.  For lunch they have a black bean burger taco.  They were amazing.  My boyfriend loves the fish and chips here.  So far we have been here once a week since we found this spot.  The bar is laid back and perfect.

As a beer bar this place gets a perfect score. No place around has the selection they do, which is constantly changing. Prices are what you would expect for some of their less common beers, but worth the cost if you're a beer guy like me. In terms of food, I've never been disappointed either. The service can be poor sometimes (because it's always packed I'm sure), but that is my only complaint. Love this place.

Yes the food is consistent and the beer selection is great but can you over look staff with attitude and waiting forever for your check only to find out they lost your credit card?? We called ahead and were told the wait was 15 to 20 minutes and put our name on the list.  Once we got there we were told it would be 35 minutes.  Our pager went off around that time but when we got to the desk was told there was a miscommunication but would be given the next table. OK, no problem. So we stood right in front of them and watched them proceed to give the next table to another group. When we questioned them we were told "I am not going to explain our system to you". Well, obviously your system doesn't work but moreover, don't lie to me. I said I would be speaking to the manager and she said she was one.  Of course we knew better so we spoke to the main manager while we were endlessly waiting for the check.  Let me say at this point we were pretty happy; the food and drinks were good and the server was very attentive.  After coming back and after waiting yet another 5 minutes for the check to come back, the hostess came up and was saying how dare you say something about me and my people - I'm not charging you for the meal. I wasn't looking for a free meal and wasn't insulting her staff, just her for lying to our faces,  really I just wanted to know where my credit card was. Well,  they had no idea. I had to cancel the card before I left and also left behind my loyalty card.  We used to be really big fans but won't be going back again.

I have been to Cloverleaf a number of times for some Friday happy hours with some co-workers and it hasn't missed once. They have the beers you want to drink plus a zillion you haven't ever heard of. They have quality food, nothing spectacular, but definitely good enough to go for the food. Behind the bar at Cloverleaf, they have a sign saying they are the State's #1 Craft Beer Bar, but also the #2 National Craft Beer Bar. I'm not sure how true this statement is, but with the list of constantly changing craft beers, it's definitely possible. It's almost a game trying to get something so bizarre when you go with your friends. They even have an MBA and PhD program that you have to ask about when you go. Like I said before, the food isn't amazing. I've snacked on cheese fries to chicken tenders to buffalo wings to a burger. It was all good enough to order again. I've mentioned Cloverleaf to some friends and I'm sure I will be back again on a Friday going through my MBA program hoping to complete it soon enough.

So Disappointing. Had a nice cup of drip coffee one morning. Came back for lunch and had an overpriced but reasonably ok carnitas cemitas sandwich. Chips and salsa were fine.  Nice salad.  Aloof service. Got a shot of dark bitter water from the espresso machine.   A few days later I came back for dinner after a long day of hiking and really had a bogus time. Reheated, overpriced and foul tasting rotisserie chicken burnt (fake lemon seasoning tastes like burnt plastic people!).  I have had better for a third of the price from every grocery store hot line.  Absolutely no authentic spices being used in recipes.  Sides were lackluster and confused, pickled mango salad was made with spices that conflicted and may have been old (tasted like rotten garbage).  Elote was steamed corn, probably from frozen and served with a 16th wedge of lemon and a ramekin of butter; where is the chili powder?  Mayo? chihuahua cheese?  Guacamole was inedible, overripe avos, weird dried chilis maybe sundried tomatoes? Poor customer service in an empty restaurant.  Obviously the conversation in the back with the kitchen and register girl was way more important than checking on me and my date or clearing our plates and bringing us the bill.  Bad meals really start to burn when you have to sit and stare at them for ten minutes.  This place is obviously cutting corners and passing the buck to you!  Classic Philly Bullshit.  Can't wait to see what is in the space next month cause I won't be back till it ain't Ynez.

This place has some of the best Mexican food in Philly. Not only that, they are very reasonably priced and extremely friendly. While we were waiting, they offered us a sample of their soup which was super good. Despite being on Washington ave, they have done an excellent job and I'll definitely be back.

This place is between 3 and 4 stars for me....I love its location as I live in the neighborhood and happy to see restaurants like this popping up the area.  I only went there for breakfast.  The space itself was awkward for me, small with chairs placed in locations that made it hard to walk around.  My boyfriend had a chicken breakfast enchilada and I had the veggie version.  I loved my meal but he was not excited at all.  Its hard to fail me on eggs and breakfast....we will definitely be back for lunch or dinner to get a better grasp on whether this place is going to make it or not.  i hope it does!!!

I have been coming to Yoshi Sono for over 10 years and it has continued to be my favorite sushi place in NJ.  Vicky is incredibly sweet and attentive, and the fish is always fresh.  I've never tried the teriyaki or noodles, but whenever I get sushi it is absolutely delicious!  Reasonable prices, great atmosphere, friendly wait staff.  I truly don't understand how this place got bad reviews.  I come here once a week, sometimes for take out, sometimes for dine-in, and I've never had a bad experience.

I went today to get a vegetarian taco salad.  The restaurant really promotes their vegetarian menu.  And while the food looked good, the problem for a vegetarian is that they cook and chops all the meat on the grill, and without removing the large pieces of meat from the grill, he starts cooking the vegetarian food.  I understand no restaurant will completely make the grill spotless before cooking a vegetarian item, but I had chunks of beef and chicken when i got my food.  I feel that at least they should remove all those pieces of meat.  All the Halal carts in NYC do it automatically whenever anyone orders something vegetarian.  I ended up just throwing out my taco salad because there were so many chunks of meat in it.  This was the second time I went with the same result.  I had wanted to give them another try thinking the first time I went was just a bad day.   But I got the same result both times.  The food looks good but it is pointless for a vegetarian to go there if chunks of meat are in your food.  I am someone who usually doesn't mind if my food is cooked near meat, but I had so much beef and chicken chunks it became a little absurd.   If you eat meat, you will probably love this place. The owner is a really nice guy so this is no dig at him.
Great food! Delicious Greek dishes, as well as amazing pizza! Portions are more than enough! The salads are great, I recommend the Bangkok salad or the Bob Marley salad.

This was a go to restaurant when I was living at Drexel. The Bangkok salad with no dressing was my very favorite! The paninis are awesome too. Only thing that sucks is the service. Servers were always rude and unattentive. Really Savas only downfall.

One of South Philadelphia's finest! I recently was in the area and asked a local if she could recommend an Italian place for Dinner her eyes lit up and without hesitation she says Scannichio's!   I wasn't going to question her. She is a local and she is Italian so I took her at her word. Let me say that there is something special about family owned and operated places. It's either "special" because its disorganized and under budgeted,or in this case its special because of supreme personal service, atmosphere, and quality of product.   Very pleased with appetizers. I had the bruschetta not the most difficult thing but all fresh flavors and seasonings. Their is a distinct taste in there Parmesan cheese very good. For dinner I had the best meal I've ever had. "Death sentence last meal good". Had the chicken Saltimbocca with asparagus and pasta (oil and garlic ) Guys I'm not kidding best meal ever. All fresh herbs and seasoning. Distinct taste in the sauces and pasta was perfect. Finished with cannoli and Capp. Will be back soon and often. Strongly recommend.

Much love to the newest eatery on South! Yelptern Enid C and I met for dinner on Monday night and my cobb salad was so delish, I went back a couple days later and ordered it again, to go. Their buttermilk dressing is addictive! Enid's sandwich was enormous and she took half home for another meal. I'm so excited to check out the rest of the menu. This is going to become one of my go-tos. Also, the staff is friendly, the prices are right and the place is super clean. Cute bathroom, too. There is definitely five star potential for Miles Table but since I've only been twice and had the same thing both times, I'll go with a very solid four for now.

I found this place last minute because the place I wanted to go to was closed on Mondays. I mostly picked this place because they have alot of avocados on the menu. This is such a cute place, well decorated and made it feel like you were home. The service was excellent. The cashier and the waiter was super nice and friendly and was very attentive! So you walk in the door, and you walk to the counter, order your food and then they will give you a number. You get to pick your own seat and they will bring your food to you! There is a big board with the menu in the front for you to look at. I had the avocado blt with a side of fries. OMG the sandwich was HUGE! I paid 14$ and it was so worth it, I could only eat a small half. The bread was delicious! The bacon was cooked a little too much, so it was hard and it was hard to bite into the sandwich, but it could also be that I couldn't fit the whole thing in my mouth anyway. The avocado was really good, it was like not mushy like alot of places. My friend had a hot chocolate and miles burger. She finished the whole thing. She liked it. She even said that it wasn't greasy than it looked. (Might just be how the bread looks). I'd totally go back here. In fact, I'm bringing my boyfriend back. :)

My favorite part of Saturday nights is the moment right before I knock back that final shot or beer like "Yeah, definitely going to need The Lot in the morning." The Lot is all you could want when you're body is punishing you for having too much fun the night before.  A heaping pile of scrambled eggs, slightly charred bacon, two fluffy slices of french toast, and some ruby red sliced tomato looks up at you all like "everything is going to be okay, I'm here now." I always steal the brown sugar sour cream my boyfriend gets with his french toast platter.  You would too, if you could.  The lattes are amazing too, and served in giant thick glasses next to the plastic glasses of water that never go empty with the attentive servers fluttering around in a constant blur of activity.  I love the atmosphere: small but not too cramped or loud.  You can hear the action in the kitchen you walk by on your way to the seat, can hear a buzz of conversation happening all around you, but that headache you brought with you won't be bothered much by the level of noise. I have yet to try anything else on the menu, mostly because of how bad of shape I tend to show up in and refuse to trust anything else to revive me like the Lot always does. I'm sure it's great, I've been eyeing up the other entrees over unsuspecting shoulders and it all looks incredible. ***cash only

Brunch.  Saturday at 11:30 am.  Obviously there's going to be a wait, but I at least ask you to please overestimate on the wait time, never underestimate.  Telling me it will be 20 minutes and then it being 50 just makes for an automatically disappointed customer.  I have no problem with waiting, but I would have much rather been told an hour and then walked around the area for a little bit. As for the food, I had the sweet potato hash with sausage, bacon, and eggs.  Delicious.  Everything, especially the sunny-side-up eggs were cooked perfectly.  I like them gooey, so they did good.  I would definitely try this place again, but I hope next time they are better about delivering a proper wait estimation.

We just went to Ant's Pants for dinner and man, it was awesome. We love going to Ant's Pants for breakfast and coffee. -It's the best coffee in the city hands down (take that La Colombe). -The breakfast is delish. My fave's are the brekky platter and the spinach, goat cheese & caramelized onion omelette. -The dinner was so DELICIOUS. It is so wonderful to have another option for dinner in the neighborhood. They said that they can do take out and possibly delivery in the future (yes please!). We had the maple bacon sandwich (YUM!) & the Aussie Burger (my husband said it was one of the best things he's eaten in a long time). We brought our two kids and it couldn't have been more welcoming and inviting. We loved it in the morning, now we love it in the evening! Thank you Ant's Pants for keeping the nabe happy, caffeinated and sated.

I have been to this place two times. The food is decent. However the service is terrible!!! the waiters are the type who are there for show and not to work! My last visit was this saturday, we ordered something light and waited almost an hour! the place was not even full! The couple next to us complained for the long wait too.   They need to hire better trained waiters or people who are there to serve the customers and not just hang out!

You know when you go to place, have an ok meal and then you forget it exists? That is Ants Pants Cafe: forgetable. I don't know why I forgot Ants Pants the first time. I think I enjoyed my food and the service was fine. I think it was that Ants Pants was merely unexceptional. Today, a friend suggested Ants Pants. I thought, "Oh yeah. That place." We wandered over from my job and had a very late brunch. I had two eggs and my friend had a salad. Both plates were good, but nothing struck a chord. There should be something you tell your friends with relish or with venom. There should be something that sticks out about a place. The atmosphere at Ants Pants wreaks of BLAH. I can say that whoever designed Ants Pants is a genius of spatial planning. For a place so small , they smanage to fit 24 seats well enough. But should seating charts spring to mind for where you go for brunch? No. Very Blah.

Went last weekend for the first time and loved it! Had sweet fries and a bacon stack and some great coffee. The waiter was awesome and made great suggestions and kept my coffee filled. Can't wait to go back!

Love Ants Pants! It can be super busy on the weekends and you can end up sitting like right next to someone but it's worth it. Food is always good, coffee is always great (get a latte, there usually is latte art) and the waiter is super friendly and makes sure you're taken good care off. See you again soon Ants!
Excellent dishes, great prices. I highly suggest trying Thai Stories if you enjoy thai food. And for an even better deal try the lunch specials.

The bagels are actually tender ie very fresh. And taste great.  The service is as good as it gets.  And I swear, the lox I had yesterday was the best I have ever had. Ever. This place seems very dedicated to quality.  Very refreshing!

Not only is the Bagel Place superior to all other bagel restaurants in the area I would rate this at the top of my list for all breakfast/lunch restaurants after eating there twice already.  The interior is very unique giving you a feeling of warmth and comfort while having a contemporary flare.  The staff is engaging, friendly, and courteous,  and most importantly...the bagels are delicious!!!  I've had a cinnamon raisin  with walnut cream cheese and I've also had a bagel sandwich which I don't normally order at other shops because the other bagels are always too dense and dry causing the fillings to squish out with each bite.  Not these!  And be sure to try the muffins and the cookies!  So so yummy!  I can't wait to try other items on their menu.

I was skeptical at first based on the location and recent opening of the bagel place. I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious these bagels were. An incredible variety of bagel flavors and baked goods. The staff went out of their way to make my experience here enjoyable. Seriously tasty bagels... And seriously great service. Quite possibly the best bagel in Burlington. I believe in this Place.
Good shit.
The name says it all.. If you Love Bacon, then this place is for you.. Try the Bacon sampler and accompany that with a cold one to wash it down.. Can't go wrong with this place..

EXPERIENCE RUINED BY THE HOST!! I would've given this place all of the stars if it wasn't for Sonny. The food was incredible, our server Antonio was delightful and adorable and the ambiance was stellar...however, the host killed our evening. We unexpectedly had a third join our party of two and completely neglected to accommodate us. He rudely told us he needed the extra chair for a reservation then when we asked for another chair he told us they had none left (with even more of an attitude). Five minutes later he carried a chair out RIGHT IN FRONT OF US to another table. Not ok. All of us work in the industry and would never let that fly. Ever. So my friend had to share her chair with her friend for the remainder of the evening thanks to Sonny! Thank you for making us feel welcome and extra comfortable!! Yeah right...

We live in Hell's Kitchen and are pretty familiar with all of the places. Especially beer/BBQ joints. Food is great. Beer selection is great. I don't partake in the bourbons but know enough to know it is a good selection. I would've given 5-stars because it is just what the neighborhood needed, however the music! I grew up in the 80's but don't want to hear it every time I'm in the place. Especially the Prince, Pat Benetar, Michael Jackson loop I've now heard twice here. Oh well. Place is still great, just hoping for a new Pandora for next time. There will be a next time.

The beer and bacon flight is definitely worth the visit. The smell of bacon when you walk in is absolutely hypnotic! They definitely know how to make good bacon. The service was friendly and prompt, even with the huge crowd they had. However, the main menu itself was nothing special. It was like someone just took regular menu items and said, "Throw bacon on it, and now it's magic! Look! It was a grilled cheese sandwich, but NOW it's a BACON grilled cheese sandwich! It used to be a lobster roll, but now it's a BACON lobster roll!" They put the most effort into the flight of bacon, and the least effort into the actual menu. I could go anywhere else, tell the wait staff to put bacon on what I ordered, and come up with the same menu items. I was expecting a little more creativity than that! I mean, at least make some kind if bacon infused sauce or reduction or something! That being said, the flight of bacon and beer is definitely worth a visit. Go there for that. Hopefully, they'll come up with some more creative menu items, or I fear BarBacon won't be long for the world, which is a shame, as it has great potential as a temple to bacony goodness.
Came here and had their bacon tasting = slices of artisanal bacon on a slab of stone.  You can't beat that.  I will be back for sure!

Bar: Lets start with the cocktails. So good. So many different flavor profiles to explore. I could be wrong, but I dont think any of them are bacon-related. Just delicious cocktails. Bacon: I mean it has bacon in the name so you know everything has bacon. The bacon flight is a must-have. Personally love the jalapeno and pepper-crusted ones the most. Lobster+bacon roll is awesome. Been a couple times with different groups and covered most of the menu with satisfied eaters all around. Service: With the exception of an obviously overwhelmed front-desk person on an ultra crowded night, the service was top notch friendly, helpful and attentive.
I haven't tried a lot of the menu, but it's a fun, casual vibe and the service is great. I'd definitely recommend it for a drink.
Bacon is awesome and drinks are great
Although this place has incredible food, I wasn't thrilled by the atmosphere. It was a little 'corporatey' for me. Decent beer selection and great whiskey, but I was honestly underwhelmed.

I have been dying to try this place ever since it opened.  The name alone is pretty intriguing.  My friend and I came here for drinks after work and had a really good time.  They have a cool drink menu with some unique sounding cocktails.  We tried a few, and were not disappointed.  I ordered the Cobb salad which was really good and my friend had a grilled cheese with bacon and soup.  The food was very good and not too pricey.  Ambiance is pretty casual and they played Motown the whole time we were there, which was awesome.  Service was very quick and the bartender was very attentive.  I would definitely return.

I love going to great cafes and coffee bars to relax, read, write while enjoying good coffee and food. I found the fine grind on Yelp and was happy that I visited. The cafe has a great vibe and was busy with guests when I arrived on a Sunday. It reminded me of a great cafe that I visit whenever I'm home in upstate NY. I ordered a soy latte and the quiche of the day. The latte was delicious as was the quiche. I loved that the quiche was served with a fresh salad and homemade dressing. I was able to sit and enjoy without feeling burdensome and thought the server was friendly. My one complaint was that there was only one server for the entire place. This didn't seem sufficient for the amount of tables and people that were present. I noticed many tables eagerly waiting to be helped or waiting impatiently with their check. Who knows? Maybe someone didn't show up for their shift or maybe it was unusually busy, but the service was the one downfall. I will be back!

The organic coffee of the day was amazing. Had the eggs in a mug with feta and spinach for breakfast, it came out fresh and hot but with only one detectable crumble of fete cheese and maybe 3 baby spinach leaves.  I could have done without hearing the conversation that the employees were having behind the counter, some sort of personal drama. I would go back for the great coffee and perhaps try a pastry.

Rosemary Chicken Wings. Calamari with the San Marzano sauce. Ooooh baby! And that was just the beginning of a fun, cozy night at Carroll Place. This place was packed, not surprising for a Saturday night, so it was a good thing we had reservations. The location is right in the heart of the Village which worked out perfectly for us since we were headed to a comedy show at the Cellar around the corner. The vibe? Casual and warm. The staff? Friendly and helpful. The food? WOW! We started with a few appetizers and since I'd read on Yelp about the wings, it was a must try. So glad we did. Crispy and flavorful and sooooo delish!! The calamari was very good but the marinara sauce was the hero of this dish. The menu consists of "small plates" and main dishes, so you can busy your tastebuds with cheese boards and marinated olives or sliders and various meats. The main dishes of the night for us consisted of the Margherita pizza, the Homemade Pappardelle with braised Pork ragu, the Linguini Vongole and the Homemade Lasagna. Everything was delicious for the most part, but I did feel the pizza was pretty uneventful. Maybe it was because we had the basic pizza as opposed to exploring some of the more interesting ones. But the show stoppers of our meal were the desserts. The warm chocolate cake was gone in an instant. Holy crap it was good. And the Nutella chocolate Calzone was unreal. For the love of all that is holy, GET DESSERT!! I love places like this. Gastro pub atmosphere with amazing food. Carroll Place is a cozy fun restaurant/bar in the heart of the Village with all the right moves. Great food, great ambiance and excellent service.

My wife and I were just passing through the area on our way to dinner with about 2 hours to kill.  The bar was packed when we arrived as it was Saturday night (the night of Santacon in NYC).  We managed to find a spot by the bar and enjoyed some local brew.  Even though the bar was packed, the ladies at the bar were very attentive and friendly.  We shared a small pizza as a snack and it was amazing.  The atmosphere was great as well.  I would highly recommend Carroll Place for both food and drinks.
Had late lunch here.  Food was delish and Happy Hour Prosecco all you can drink!  The meat and cheese board was fabulous and  good prices.   Staff very friendly and attentive and great atmosphere.

the small establishment needs people to eat/drink and clear space so unfortunately no wifi! Egg sandwiches were delicious and service was really friendly. Interesting mix of New Yorkers who are just in the neighborhood + tourists

I wish I was here more than once a week, because it's the best coffee I've had in NYC! As well as the best food. For an Aussie away from home, nothing beats a flat white and vegemite on toast from this awesome, but too small (and now a little too popular) place. Oh, and the staff are the friendliest I've ever met! Thanks guys for always serving the best coffee in town!

Have been there quite a few times.  Always leave feeling satisfied.  Everything I've ordered so far has been yummy.  My favorite is the bo luc lac (Vietnamese beef cubes).  The meat is so tender.  They also have a healthy selection for non-meat eaters.  Can't get enough of the place!

Three things that ticked me off: 1. Waiter was annoyingly impatient whilst we were ordering. When we finished he made a comment that it was a lot of food for three people. We should had taken this opportunity to cancel a couple of items as everything came out unsatisfactory. 2. Appetizer came out after entree & not all entrees came out together either. It seemed as though they just brought out what they finished first, not caring if we each had to sit & watch the other eat for most of the meal. No apologies were made when food was brought out late. 3. The food definitely had a lysol taste to it like everyone else said. Especially the shrimp!   The highly pretentious atmosphere did very little to mask the mediocre service and food.

First of all, the place looks nice - a bit more of an upscale look than most of the other Vietnamese restaurants in the Washington Avenue area.  I actually expected to see a little more of an adventurous menu, fitting to the nice space - but, the menu was very pedestrian - not much different than any othe Vietnamese restaurant. I've read the other reviews - some great, some bad . . . many with comments around a strange taste accompanying the shrimp and other things.  Wow.  I didn't experience that.  I actually experienced VERY little taste at all.  We got the two-person family meal . . . and the soup, which erred on the side of sweet, had two shrimp in it and very little flavor at all.  The fish clay pot was odd - some of the fish was very overcooked, other pieces not so much.  But, the flavor was really lacking - just a cloying sweetness - and, I couldn't actually find anything that resembled the taste of fish in the dish at all.  The spring rolls were average, crispy, but not at all exciting.  The best dish in the meal was the beef - still very much under-seasoned, at least it was cooked nicely and was tender.  The rice was dry.  I've had MUCH better in the same neighborhood. MUCH better. The service - the service just seemed to be all over the place.  Younger and older servers, they seemed to be in a constant state of confusion  - there didn't seem to be any real order to things.  One waiter wanted to take our orders approximately 5 seconds after we got our menus.  The person who actually did take our order and serve most of the food was an older waiter and seemed to be a little less frazzled than the others.  BUT - they brought our check.  Actually they brought TWO checks - leaving one with each of us.  This was odd, since we had not asked for two checks . . .and we soon realized why.  We had been given the processed check AND credit cards of the couple at the table next to us.  The staff never realized their mistake - it was taken care of between us and the other diners.  The staff really seemed clueless. We finally got our check, and after a few attempts to flag someone down, it was finally taken for processing.  This was not a good first impression for a place that I really wanted to like and had been looking forward to visiting. The time to fix this new locale is now - before you build a reputation of being below the par of the rest of the area's offerings.  Because, since you are a little off the beaten path of the other Vietnamese restaurants - you could be easily forgotten.

first and foremost the venue is nice, resembles a more upscale Vietnamese restaurant so I came in expecting a richer taste to Vietnamese cuisine but I left disappointed. It's a tad bit pricier then other Vietnamese restaurants roaming on Washington Avenue yet  more flavorless. the Thai Tea did taste pretty good though, I will give this place 3 stars and maybe give it another try

This place has all the bases covered. The whole place is clean. prepares wear gloves and food prepared in front of you. quality of food is top notch. jalapeno chedar and french toast begals are great. the small pizzas are better than the renouned pizza shops. Boars head meats are very good and fresh. service is very customer centric and friendly. no charge for beverage refills. I rarely go anywhere else to start my day. They just extended their hours until 5 pm on most days and added free wifi.
Some of the best bagels I've had. Always friendly service.
Great food and cool vibe! We had the deviled eggs, mussels and the salmon. The service was friendly and fast. Definitely on my neighborhood favorites!

We came in with a large group and had an amazing meal. The short ribs and the mussels were delicious. The service was friendly and the decor was lovely and thoughtful. Every detail was considered. My friend had the lamb burger, which was also really yummy. They have a great selection of beers on tap, and they introduced me to a new beer that I just love! We had a great experience at Eastwick. Run don't walk to this great new addition to the neighborhood!

So happy to be there on opening night, although the restaurant looked packed on the days leading up to their opening. I was so impressed with everything that hit our table last night. Based on the old location reviews, we were going with a past reviewers star system as follows: the jam, monster jam and the motherfucker. So here you go: Oysters: the jam. i liked them, but I wish I could have tasted more of the oyster. The vinagrette was a bit overwhelming for me. Cornbread: Monster Jam! Not too spicy and super hot in that skillet. Brussel Sprouts: Monster Jam! I have never met a sprout i don't like but these were cooked perfectly. I almost wanted to lick the bowl. Dr. Pepper Ribs: Motherfucker! These were like delicious, like so delicious. Cooked perfectly and the sauce was mucho bueno. Loved it. I had this as my main dish and it was more than enough. Chocolate Bread Pudding: Totally a motherfucker. You have to have this. And as of right now it's the only dessert on the menu, so really..you have to have this. Other things my table enjoyed / Devoured: The Chicken..word was a total motherfucker. The meat was cooked perfectly. The country fried steak and the trout: devoured. I didn't see one last drop on the table of food. The only weird thing was that I ordered two small plates for my entree. Those came first and everyone else's meals came about 20 minutes later. Sort of awkward for them to all sit there and watch me eat and then for me to sit there and watch them eat. Then coming back together to enjoy the bread pudding together. The space is a total motherfucker!

Went opening night, and the house was packed with a celebratory mood.  Got 2 pans of cornbread with bacon and jalapeños for the table.  Four of us agreed if we could only eat one thing for the rest of our lives, it could be Brooklyn Star cornbread!  Entrees on the table: Pork shank, bacon wrapped trout and country fried steak.  It was all incredible.  Not a single mediocre point to the whole meal!

03/10/11 Unfortunately, I never had the opportunity to dine at the original Brooklyn Star before it burnt down.  But when the grand re-opening of its new location on Lorimer Street was stirring up some internet buzz, I couldn't wait to taste chef Joaquin Baca's take on southern comfort food in the 'Burg. Pros: - The ambiance and overall feel of the place is inviting, non-clustered, and very clean.  I would describe the decor as Brooklyn-meets-Georgia. - Southern hospitality was present here.  Staff members were attentive, friendly, and embracing. - The sweet aroma of freshly baked cornbread that traveled through the dining room area was pleasant. - Grilled Quail with quail egg, frisee salad, and roasted fennel was grand.  The combinations of flavors all mixed well and contrasted each one perfectly. Cons: - The Spicy Fried Chicken Wings tasted good, but were ultra soggy.  I believe Hooters produce better wings. - The expeditor could have thought of spacing out our food.  My friend and I ordered a bunch of apps. and they all came at once which made each dish almost impossible to enjoy and/or savor. - Please change the Roasted Veal Marrow Bones to beef marrow bones because it was truly disappointing to expect marrow and not get it with these tiny bones we got served. - You get only three thin slices of overcooked Veal Sweetbreads accompanied with a nicely aromatic broth and kale.  Back to the three thin slices and overcooked part. As you might already know, the biggest part of the restaurant is its food.  Sure, service plays a big role, but it's the food people want to come back for.  The new Brooklyn Star's service hit the bullseye in many ways, but the food aspect needs to be considerably worked on.  I recognize this was it's first day of being re-opened, but, in my opinion, I don't think some of these dishes were acceptable to start with.  Unfortunately, I never had the opportunity to dine at the original Brooklyn Star to give both old and new restaurants a better comparison.  But I'm fortunate enough to admit that I see potential in chef Joaquin Baca's take on southern comfort food in the "Burg. Will Chu "Real Food, Real Wine in The Real World"
Stopped in for a drink today.  The drinks were delicious and reasonable.  The bartenders were great and even introduced themselves...  I'll definitely be back to try the food.

I'm confused how this place has such phenomenal reviews. The staff is great, and the ambience is cute - but the food is bland and nothing exciting. The cornbread with bacon and jalapeños was okay, but I've had better cornbread in a diner. The marrow bones honestly was flavorless. The $76 Rib Eye meal for two was not as much food as you should have gotten for such a price. The potatoes were good, but the cauliflower was dry and the rib eye had so much toppings you couldn't taste the steak, and it just was so bland. Top that off with 3 beers and for a bill of $120 for only 2 people and no dessert - way over priced boring bland food. Won't be going there again!

We passed by early on saturday evening and saw the huge front windows open and the vibe inside looked amazing... we knew we would come back later that evening for some country style food.  After a few drinks and a few more drinks around town we made our way back to the BK Star.   Thank goodness they serve the full menu until 2am!!! We got back there around 1am and were greeted with warm smiles from the staff.  My lady is now obsessed with the Romaine Wedge salad.  We also had the Amazing Mac and Cheese and the Dr. Pepper Ribs to start.  Followed up with the Country Fried Steak , which is unbelievably good - tender meat, crispy breading, and rich milk gravy.   We loved every bite.   Can't wait to go back to our new favorite neighborhood spot - great food, friendly and attentive service, and stays open late!  The Brooklyn Star hits all the right notes for us!

would give this a 3.5 star rating. not that i had a bad meal, but it wasnt amazing and probably is over rated. not to mention that they had something that was listed as a $49 short rib on the menu. it is meant for one person (i asked). i dont think it could be anything other than a massive typo.

My cousin took my husband and I here because she likes their sandwiches. The store is pretty cute located in Burlington and walking distance to Lake Champlain.  It does have a market setup with some grab and go grocery items, but also a sit down section for a bite to eat. My husband ordered a turkey BLT with maple bacon which he said was delicious and I had fish tacos which were fresh and a manageable size. My husband ordered a local beer which has been his favorite so far this vacation, Switchback. I tried a really good root beer, made in New York. They are pretty fast making our made to go orders. Didn't get a creemee from here because I felt I had just the right amount of lunch.

Have eaten here the last two times I stayed at the Loews Hotel in Philly - it's their in-house restaurant, having replaced their prior place "Sole". It is MUCH better than the previous restaurant, in terms of layout, decor, service, and most importantly food. The restaurant is a combination of nouveau American food, along with a full bar & even a bourbon tasting room (hence the name!). I have tried the ahi tuna sandwich (ask for it cooked through if you don't want it raw on the inside with a seared outside) - great aioli & brioche roll; parmesan fries - yumm!; blueberry pancakes - heavenly; egg white fritata with veggies - delicious & a great way to start the day. However, my all time FAVORITE thing to eat here is their cheese plate - served at all 3 meals for $14. It's a selection of 4 small cheese portions, along with honey, fruit, nuts, bread, all served on a wood board. It's delicious & just enough for 2 people to share. Add a glass of wine & you are in heaven. The other reason besides the food that I am giving them 5 stars is that on my last visit I ordered the ahi tuna sandwich for lunch & did not ask them to cook it through (I had it once before & the waiter mentioned to me that it was very rare, so I ordered it more well-cooked, but this time our waiter didn't ask me how to cook it & I forgot). I got it & it was way too rare for my taste. I pushed it around, ate a little bit, but was full on the parmesan fries & cheese plate any way. I didn't complain since the menu does say "seared ahi tuna sandwich", so felt I was partially to blame. However, on the way out of the restaurant, our waiter JOSE came after me & said "I noticed that you didn't eat your sandwich & I'm sorry that you didn't enjoy it". I would like to get you dessert on the house & proceeded to pack up 2 desserts (mini donut holes with a yummy sauce & german chocolate cake) & sent us back to the room with them. What a wonderful touch - a waiter who actually notices when a guest is not fully satisfied, & makes it his business to go out of his way to do something about it. Well, it got even better. The next morning we had breakfast here & of course asked for Jose to wait on us. He was wonderful again, and provided excellent service. Mid-way through breakfast the restaurant manager ALEX came over & said "Thank you so much for giving us another chance to make you happy today. I heard that you were not fully pleased yesterday". I was blown away - this type of service is unheard of even in the highest end places I have dined at. Jose then proceeded to buy my boyfriend's drink (Irish Coffee) on the house. It was an incredible example of how real customer service should be done. Finally, we went to the bar one night during our stay. The bartenders were fun, attentive, & even bought us shots since it was my birthday! All in all this is a great place to eat even if you're not staying in the hotel. I highly recommend it!

I never write reviews but I do come on yelp to look for good spots and find out what people are saying about different places that I would like to try but I felt compelled to give back a little and write about Bank and Bourbon.....Have had meetings in Philly a few times over the last month and someone recommended this place as it was fairly new and a good place to eat.... Been here twice-  lunch once and dinner once....Had outstanding experience both times...Servers were good...coming over to see if we needed anything consistently but never too much to interrupt us.....lunch was really good..had the burger and 2 others had the chicken sandwich and they raved about it..... Dinner I must say was phenomenal.... staff helpful  and they had a guy there to explain all about the bourbon etc..... Usually only order steaks at steak houses so I was hesitant to get it but we ordered a cowboy steak and it rocked....glad we made that call.....atmosphere was nice as well...bar was full and good mix of people....All in all I would say if you are in Philly and looking for a good spot to eat that you haven't tried this would be a good place to check out........

Sat at the beautiful brown marble bar so as not to take up a whole table. The interior is so timelessly glamorous that I was wistfully looking at the window seating.  I could imagine in decades past, the room would be filled smoke and snifter glasses. Was handed the menu for restaurant week and the regular menu. $20 for a three course lunch for restaurant week. Tempting, but I was too curious about their burger. The bartender was very personable. I got the dry aged burger. Oh. My. A little smattering of chopped Poblano peppers, some finely grated cheese, a cute little bun, and the burger itself... The meat was just so full of flavor. I don't think I've ever had a dry aged burger. The bartender says that they do all sorts of dry age and wet age here. (I'd never heard of wet aging, he explained, sounds like marinating or brining for a couple of days to me) my only thing is that the bun was a weird texture, dry and airy. I guess you need something light to counter the meat, and dry but holds together to catch meat juices, but I wasn't a fan. The manager came around to ask about the food. I told her fabulous, but did mention the bun. She looked abashed, and offered to have the bun swapped out, but I think it was more of the type of bread rather than a stale bun, so declined.  The fries were seasoned and crispy. Delicious. Am coming back before restaurant week is out.

The decor looks great! And even though I'm vegan, I've eaten here a number of times and the chefs have created delicious options for me including cavatelli and the tastiest cooked veggies I've had! The others in my party really enjoyed the whole fish they ordered and are definitely looking forward to coming again.

I had lunch for business purposes a few times there over the past months. The food was consistenly delicious and everything I tried so far was amazing. My favorite is their salmon salad and tuna sandwich but the roasted carrot appertizer and the ham/ Prosciutto display are great starters! Every time I went there, the staff was so attentive, pleasant and prompt. A great local "best kept secret" which I think it is likely to become very popular soon.

Excellent food in a very relaxed and comfortable atmosphere. The restaurant's charm is only exceeded by the amazingly delicious food. The rice spiced with carrots, orange peel and raisins challenges your palate and excites all your senses. The kebab platter, a mixture of lamb, beef, fish and chicken had a unique homemade taste to it. I can't wait to go back!!!

Love this place. The food the atmosphere. Amazing. Been here a few times. Unfortunately this review is not for he restaurant but for the hostess. She told me that I didn't hear my name called because "Maybe I should open up my ears". After waiting an hour for a table. And continues to wait afterwards. Not ok to talk to your customer that way.

Oui oui.... Buvette is a superb French bistro ideal for Saturday or Sunday brunch with a loved one. The small intimate setting may be over whelming or even impossible to get into with a large party, considering they do not take reservations. Expect to wait an hour at least As for dining, do not miss the croque Madame or the waffle sandwich, both incredible. Oh and one last thing, rude hostess.

C'est domage et terrible! Long lines and popularity don't a great restaurant make. We found it dreadful. After a month in France in the spring we were looking forward to this "new" spot in the Village. When in NYC we live across the street from Buvette so we were excited to try a new place on the block. Scrambled eggs were overcooked but far worse, full of egg shells. The fruit over the waffle was bitter; the coffee luke warm. I must admit the couples on both sides of our table raved about the food...but then they left most of it on their plates. Go figure. Wait staff should've asked how our food was. But then again, maybe not. Never again.

I don't have many nice things to say about overrated, tourist favorite Buvette.   The service was awful, pretentious, and one of the servers had a fake French accent.  Our seating space was incredibly cramped and uncomfortable.  Our seating consisted of small, backless stools.  Can you think of *any* other NYC restaurant that would have the gall (Gaul, hehe) to ask that of its patrons at these prices?  And what little food we ordered did not fit on the tiniest table I have ever seen in a restaurant/cafe, here or in Paris.   This cafe has not posted a menu for breakfast or any other meal on their website.  However, I can tell you that the menu is short and very limited for breakfast. I did appreciate how buttery and delicious my overpriced Belgian waffle was.  The thought of that microscopic $$$ waffle might inspire me to swing by again should I be in the neighborhood at off hours, alone, unencumbered by coats or bags, with limitless patience, little appetite, a good back, and money to burn.  My companion was less impressed with his eggs. This restaurant also gets credit for our discovery of La Colombe Nizza blend, which really does make an excellent espresso. We did not have to wait for a table because we arrived relatively early on a weekday, but we would have been absolutely furious had we waited for a table only to have this type of experience.  Not sure we will ever go back because there are too many downsides and so little (yet good) food, so little space P.S. - As someone who lived and worked in France for many years, I can confidently say that a claim to being "typically French" is not an excuse for poor service/small portions/uncomfortable seating

No matter what time of the day it is, you can expect to wait for either bar or table seating.  If you come off hours, like we did around 4pm, we only had to wait for 15 min. Portion sizes are on the smaller side but plenty for both of us.  We ordered the tarting with the pesto, it was good but not overwhelmingly satisfying for me.  The mussels on the other hand were the BEST one I've had.  They actually filled almost every single mussel with this breadcrumbs and garlic paste.  I savored every bite and at the end I dipped every single one of the crusty bread into the broth. We had the chocolate mouse for dessert.  Simple and made with quality ingredients.   We made friends with our neighboring table.  Two ladies visiting from Atlanta.  It was great to have a taste of the southern hospitality.  But then the table after them were back to the cold and snobby New Yorkers.  Oh well. The decor, the lighting, the menu made a very whimsical ambiance for me.  Service is on point.  I wish I can linger longer.  I'll be back for brunch!

Food: 4.5 Stars Service: 4 Stars Superb. I came here for brunch with my girlfriend before catching a flight out of La Guardia. They were very helpful with helping me store my luggage and accomodating us pretty quickly. There was a line which you want to be aware of during peak hours. Unlike a different reviewer, I thought it was really unique and cool that they essentially used their door frame and chalk for the waiting list. I seriously doubt people would purposely smudge the names ahead of them just to get ahead in wait time. When we were seated, I will say the tables are pretty close to each other so you'll be packed quite closely. We ordered the: 1. The Croque Madame - which was very tasty, thick and heavy. Although portions looked kinda small at first glance. They're actually quite thick and heavy so you'll be fulfilled after the meal. There was cheese on either side of the bread which was melted in and still hot from the kitchen, which brought out so much flavor from the filling of the sandwich. 2. Waffle Sandwich - my favorite. It came with butter and maple syrup on top, a lot of cheese in the middle, bacon, and I believe an egg as well. Everything just blended together in a beautiful melted mess of sweet, savory, cheesy, crunchy and lightness. I've never had anything like it and would come back again! The menus and decor are also beautiful. Makes you actually feel like you're in a small parisian cafe, but you're in the middle of Manhattan. Highly recommended!
This restaurant is a gem! It's a wonderful, charming French bistro that has great food. It's small and a little cramped but has attentive service and French cuisine that's off the chain!!
Amazing food, fantastic ambiance! If you like the French way of life with smaller plates and great wine you need to go
Here is a simple review. Amazing food, fantastic ambiance! If you like the French way of life with smaller plates and great wine you need to go

Fuck yes. Go here. It's AMAZING. Everything. I got here around 6:15 PM on a Thursday night with the beau and it was already a 30 minute wait.  Glad we stuck around - by the time we left around 8PM, the wait was 1:15 - and lots of people were waiting. We ordered the rabbit (YAS QUEEN), the leeks dish (nicest take on leeks I've ever had), and much more.  Go for the specials. Service is sub-par, beautiful model type who just glare, but that was okay for the delicious food. Hold back on alcohol and you'll be able to eat a lot of stuff for a short bill.
The waffle looks innocent enough from a distance... but when you're done, you'll want 10 more. A+ orange pressé. Breakfast dreams.

Dark and romantic, perfect for a late night get together with an old friend or date. The chicken live pate is amazing, I think I could eat it for the rest of my life. Their wine selection is also really lovely and all prices are very reasonable for the quality of what you get. Anything with prosciutto in it... yum. But really though, can't say enough good things about this place...

went last night for the 1st time. i know nothing about the food or the culture. but i'm learning thanks to a cute turkish man. so he brought me here. its byob. and he had a bottle of a turkish booze called raki.  had lots of food. huge plate of  samplings of traditional fare. such as hummus, stuffed grape leaves, some kind of crazy eggplant and so on. all vegetarian. all super yum. next the meat. it was an assortment of all good things. we ate lamb, chicken and beef.  it was on top of different rices and other stuff. it was friggin fantastic. ended with dessert. have no idea what it was called. it tasted somewhat like rice pudding. i am a fan. shout out to justin the irish waiter and only non turk in the place. he was great. we waited for nothing without him being overbearing. and the owner was a sweetheart to us. he's the kind of guy you want to succeed. he loves his place and the people who go there.the outside seating on a perfect night made the whole experience, amazing. i will def be back. and im dragging everyone with me. i will be spreading the word. side note. that raki stuff? we got tore up. but totally different kind of buzz. had very little sleep and made it to work on time, no hangover. just sayin'.

This is by far one of my favorite restaurants in North Jersey. Authentic food nestled in the heart of Caldwell. The Flamenco dancing is out of this world, as well as every tapas plate you will order. Bring family and friends to Xunta and it will definitely be a night I remember! Oh! And the desserts are to die for!

Decent decor, somewhat romantic. This said, I'm not sure I'd go back. If this was someone's first venture into the restaurant biz, it might make some sense. However, here it is in a nutshell. We had the tapas versions of the following: Spicy potatoes Spinach and chick peas Octopus (boiled BTW) Prawns Scallops Mussels We also ordered the kale salad, which arrived mixed in with the plates of hot food. The kale salad was the best of the plates unfortunately. Absolutely nothing in the above assortment was above average. In fact, I'd suggest that it was all below average. The shrimp, scallops, and mussels were overcooked, and the boiled octopus was odd. Honestly, just pull something out of the freezer and put it on the grill. Service was extremely friendly, but clearly inexperienced. Dessert was ok. The almond pastry was decent, but the other (don't recall the name) arrived with lemon sorbet, don't choose that one...  No espresso or cappucino. Really? Yeah...

Print never disappoints. The chef focuses on local produce, so the menu will change with the seasons. The bar menu needs some updates, but the selections on the restaurant menu are varied and include vegetarian options. The kale salad was great, with apples and toasted pine nuts. Also tried the duck and the pork chop, both were well seasoned and cooked perfectly.

I'd give em 4 stars but the entrees were so mediocre, I just can't. Me and my five dinner guests came for dinner and absolutely loved the decor. We were seated at what we dubbed the Queen's table. It was a giant round table with a high back booth and three plush chairs. We ordered four apps/six entrees and basically shared everything, because we're those girls. Braised Pork Belly: This was the highlight of the apps. Full of flavor, tender yet not overcooked. No complaints at all about the other apps. We took those plates down! Lacinato Kale Salad: Light and crisp. Goat Cheese Gnocchi: YUM! Grilled Octopus: Perfect texture, perfect taste. Yes.   And then the entrees happened. Of note, were the Grassfed Filet: Absolutely melted in your mouth delicious. and the Roasted Cauliflower: Well rounded flavors and textures and well cooked. There was a rabbit on the menu. That was also a winner. Really nice soft texture and great sides. The Pollenta was so rich in flavor but still so airy. Magic. The Seared Black Seabass was pretty boring. And the sides were not very tasty at all. The butternut squash resembled carrots in their hard texture and lack of flavor. Nothing went well together. The Mountain View Farm Crispy Duck was another case of the what-is-this game. The meat was tougher than any bird I've ever eaten. I had to confirm it was duck with the table! Not well flavored either. Drinks menu was great and so were their well priced wine options. I'd go back for apps tapas style and drinks. Skip the entrees; They're so hit or miss.
The gnocchi and the chocolate fan, that is all have to say. To die for!! I love you guys!!

I remember coming here all the time because they are open so late. They are pretty good and have a nice selection of sauce flavors. I always get the spicy version. Sometimes they forget to give you the celery and ranch, but that just means you need to ask them for it.

I was in town for a conference and was looking for a casual place to grab a drink and bite. I of course turned to my fellow Yelpers and found the Cock and Bull, which was super close to my hotel. I walked in and it was a super laid back unpretentious place. I could tell it was perfect for a person alone like me or to go to with a group of friends to grab a drink and watch the game. I ordered a Moscow Mule, which was excellent. For food I got the sliders with fried fish and the curried deviled eggs. The sliders came out piping hot, well seasoned, nice crispy batter, delicious. They were served with fresh, good sized potato wedges. The eggs had a wonderful, but not overpowering curry flavor that was complimented by a slice of cucumber and piece of avocado. The bartender was friendly and attentive, but not bothersome. If I lived/worked nearby I would definitely return!

The best If you are looking for sports on TV in this area, you have found it. The good Pleasant atmosphere. Good service. The meh The food is nothing special.  And over priced because the location is great. Very few options for a vegetarian. Overall Seems like a good place to drink a beer and watch a game.

I actually loved this restaurant! From the moment we stepped in, I loved the cozy pub feel. Now, I've never been to a pub in Great Britain, but I would assume this would be what it is like. It was very warm and welcoming. The bar was well stocked and had a good variety of games on. We wanted to sit down at a table so waited about 10-15 minutes, which wasn't too bad. We were finally seated in the corner of the 2nd floor. Our server greeted us right away and took our order. The menu looked delicious, but I figured I had to go with a classic! We didn't wait too long for our food. When it came I was very pleased. The fish was rather large and there was a decent amount of chips. There were thick and thin and crispy ones, which I loved! The breading on the fish was crispy enough, and the fish didn't taste too "fishy" it was perfect. The servers weren't overly friendly, but they came to check on us throughout our meal. All in all I would definitely come back here on another trip to NYC!

Very good food, good service. The ambiance is not the greatest, but the food more than makes up for it. Definitely the best eatery in the area. Prices are reasonable and the portions are satisfying. The only reason for the withdrawal of the fifth star is the short menu and the fact that the menu is not changed often enough. We are to continue to frequent the place.

The buzz for this place has been fed by hype from "bridge and bridge" people as well as transplants who really really wish they could have lived in "NYC" but had to settle for Philly instead.   Going some place to be seen is sad; it's especially sad when that place serves burgers and shakes.  Being impressed with a long line is a sign you're lacking something in your life. I went, because I wanted to confirm that it was all hype, plus I love me some burgers and shakes. I just wasn't any more impressed by this place than I am by any decent diner that serves milkshakes.  Sorry, kids, you're buying into a slick product again.  But it's OK, because you look cool while doing it. PS:  Doobies has had bowling alley tables since before they were cool, and don't make a big fucking deal about it.

Oh. My. Word. The hour+ time I spent on line waiting for my chance at the famed New York City Shake Shack burger was, without a doubt, worth every hunger-pang inducing second. And I'd do it again. The Shack Burger was perfection.  The shake, dreamy.  The employees, friendly. The ambiance, sleek. Loved it from top to bottom and back again.  Thank you, Shake Shack, for bestowing the best damn burger I've ever eaten upon the City of Brotherly Love.

Certain people I know have been counting this down for months, and for once the opening was just as smoothly operated and worthwhile as you could imagine (take notes, Morgans Pier). Despite the line throughout opening day the customer facing staff appeared upbeat and on the ball.  That counts for something. And the food was spot-on as well.  Having been to locations in DC and NYC the food was just what you want from this place.  Juicy, simple burgers with crisp fries and locally inspired Concretes. Didn't have beer or wine this time but it's nice that the option is there once I inevitably return.  Plus they say sidewalk seating is on the way.  Welcome to Philly, Shake Shack.

OK, so we have all been waiting for this place to open ... and the other day after work, I decided to brave the line and have my first Pennsylvania Shake Shack burger. The food is great, I don't need to say anything about that.  I really don't like the shake sauce they put on their burgers, ask for it on the side ... its weird. What I really wanted to do here is give praise to the staff.  They are the most friendly, most upbeat, most helpful staff of any Philadelphia restaurant ever.  When I arrived yesterday, my girlfriend and I had a long wait.  She was behind me in line, and ordered second to me.  She has a more complicated order, and somehow got it almost immediately.  I had ordered a shake burger and fries ... and waited, and waited, and waited ... The expediter, I believe his name is David, a very nice guy, kept checking in with me, having conversation with me, and doing his best to make sure I was taken care of.  His manager, Noel (i think) came over and chatted with me.  Noel comped my check because I waited almost 15 min after my girlfriend got her food.  He asked me to come back and hoped I will have a good experience. For that kind of excellent staff, I will absolutely come back.  I hope all of you give this place a chance, as they are so busy trying to figure out how to run an efficiently oiled machine. PS the interior is full of recycled materials and environmentally conscious business practices.  I respect this business a lot for that.

I got a double hamburger, fries and a chocolate shake. The fries were very good! Shake was good (I've had many better). Burger was awful! All I added to my burger was ketchup... I'm a purist like that... it was way overly greasy, and tasted very bitter. They didn't ask how I wanted it cooked so I figured I would get it Well to Mid Well... It was on the light end of mid well, which was okay. We didn't wait in line long because it was pouring buckets outside and only waited about 5 minutes... Thank god we didn't wait longer. I don't think I'll be going back there!
