I came to Shake Shack with an open mind.  When they first announced that this site was going to be a Shake Shack, I was admittedly disappointed that another NYC franchise was trying to break into the awesomeness of Philadelphia, but as construction progressed and they planted the vertical garden and made the area much more beautiful than it had been, I wished them well and was anxious to try the new burger place in town.  Today, I finally made it in and tried the SmokeShack and Cheese Fries with a drink for ~$13.  There was nothing stellar about any of the food, and the portion size (tiny greasy burgers) was not worth the cost or the wait in the ridiculously long line, imo.  I will say that the employees are great and friendly and I appreciated that, but as for the restaurant, it's not even in the top three burger restaurants on Sansom Street West of Broad.  I'm in no rush to go back.

The day has come. Finally after years of reading about how awesome Shake Shack in New York is. How the burgers are end all, be all. Only held to the highest standards, using only the finest meat purveyor in all of Meatopia, thee "Nobody beats our meat" Pat LaFrieda  with a custom Shake Shack meat blend. After putting off so many times going to NY to try it. It's finally here. Last year word got out that it was coming to 20th & Sansom st. I hardly could contain my excitement. Most don't get gitty over this shit, but me being the burger slut, I got a meat chubby. That's right a NY icon of burgers is coming to Philly. Shit yea. Excited I was (Yoda-ism). Counting down the months was long indeed. Alas, I got wind just a few weeks ago it was opening June 6th. Instant beef boner. So planning my first visit the Saturday after they open I get a fantastical surprise. A special invite to a private VIP party the night before opening. HUH??? YEAH!!!! Now if I couldn't be more excited, I sure as shit was. Greg at the Shack sends me a email inviting me. You Sir are awesome. HELL YA, my cockles are warmed!   I RSVP'd as fast as possible. Me and all you can eat burgers for free, I can do this. So I cut out of work early to make it down there, It was busy.Yikes. We check in, no problems. Nice. Got our wrist bands, I guess so people couldn't wander in and grub free food. Feeling excited. I walked around for a minute and Greg found me. What a guy. We spoke about some things and answered all my questions with a smile. Super cool dude. You sir are shrine worthy. Now, I need food. I kept looking at the awesome servers hustling around with trays of all the Shack goodies. I stopped one of the servers to try my pink elephant. The Shack Burger. Tears almost welled as the meat approached my mouth. I was almost to nervous to bite it. What if it let me down, there was so much hype built I would feel shitty if it didn't blow me away. The moment drew closer as my hand forced it into my meat-hole. YOUGOTTOBEFRIGGINGKIDDINGME was that redonkulously mind blowing. After inhaling it in 11 seconds I glance around for more. Give me more, lots more. Stat! I figured it might be rough trying to get more food, but I was wrong. The crowds thinned out near the most important spot in the place. The kitchen doors. Me and the wife planted around the prime local as all the servers had to swing by us. One after the other servers kept the food train flowing. The meat was so perfectly seasoned with salt & pepper and had that perfect crust. The LaFrieda custom blend  of beef for the Shack was tear worthy. Not sure of the fat ratio but the beef blend is chuck, brisket and sirloin. The patties range around 4 to 5oz of heaven. Mr. Lafrieda if I could hug you I would. A great big beefy hug you meat genius. Bravo! The meat party all rested on a super soft slightly sweet Martin's potato roll. Roll retention was in check. I dug how the cheese beautifully blanketed the meat like a long winters slumber. All the toppings were crazy fresh, and the bacon was crisp and sublime. I though for sure some of the many burgers flying out the the kitchen wouldn't be consistent, I was so wrong, but happy as shit. The kitchen staff blew me away of how well it handled the mob of hungry grubbers. I can't leave the potato out of this. The Shack was rocking old school crinkle cut fries, which were nicely crisp and salted just right, but I have to implore you to get them with the most ass slapping smooth cheese sauce I've ever tasted. Hows blended cheddar & American cheeses to coat the fries with. Huh? Only the most perfect topping, Fuck ketchup. As if I needed more meat, I had to try the Hot dog which  was sourced from Vienna hotdogs. I was so full from eating four burgers, but I had to do it. Shoving the wiener in my face had to be done. Hey, not that one. What a nice grill char to it,but the Chicago toppings really set it off. It too rested on a potato bun, nice choice keeping it all together nicely. Loved it. Custard. Let me say it again, AHHHH custard. So smooth and velvety. I was told the butterfat content was high and you could tell. I couldn't even think of any others that came close. All the mix ins were good, but the Liberty Shell was the winner. Wow Wee. I was surprised of how well it all came together. Second fav was the Rittenhouse 2. As if my ass needed more sweet I couldn't resist washing down my custard with a chocolate shake. Pig I am, so what. The staff was beyond awesome and they were so on point, it was amazing. With the throngs of people they were super friendly and always had a smile on. I had asked a few of them for certain things and was promptly brought it. I would expect this service at a fine dining restaurant but was shocked to find it here. Another kudos for the Shack.

I was super exited to hear a shake shack was opening in Philly. Having partake in their wares during my trips in NYC a few times before. But there is no reason that every time I walk by SS people are lined up outside as if Kate Upton was giving free lap dances next to the ketchup dispenser. I digress...in my opinion the burgers are pretty decent and I personally am a pretty big fan of the shakes especially the racially harmonious black and white.  The fries are a skip for me.. I personally think SS should send one of their fifty minions they have scurrying around the kitchen down to 5 guys and get some proper fries. Could you get a better burger?..most definately and a better milk shake?...maybe, but both at the same place? Not in Philly bub. PS if you say Bobby's Burger Palace..I will hunt you down and remove your tongue with my bare hands.

I did the whole Shake Shack thing this past weekend because Philadelphia thinks their cool now because they have this place. Nothing like waiting in a long line for underwhelming food. I mean it is a burger and shake, you can't really mess it up, unless you have your customers wait 25mins in line and then over charge them. Unfortunately, I knew this was going to be the case but just had to check it out. Ever hear of an oldie that is being resurrected, Gino's. Check them out: ginosgiant.com, not some hipster joint from NY making philadelphia yups feel important, but it is very good! I don't think I will be back to shake shack, nor do I understand the fanatical Yelp reviews. Yelp should incorporate some sort of factor into their filter to prevent trendy disappointments like this from happening

Eh. I can't say I'm impressed. I've been here twice.   What I am pleased by is the "C-Line", reserved specifically for those ordering dessert (and looking to get in and out quickly, of course). On their second night of business, I got a Philadelphia Pretzel concrete. It was OK; but only that--OK. The custard was pretty good, but it was not wait 2 hours in line down 20th street good. (Mind you, I didn't wait that long. Again: the C-Line!). The pretzel bits were terrible! Is it actually pretzel? Whatever it was tasted stale and bland. I'm also pleased at the availability of Draught Root Beer. I purchased this on a later visit. As a non-drinker, I'm always happy when a bar/restaurant puts a root beer on tap which could easily be taken up by another beer. However, they charge $2.65 for a "Regular" which equates to about 12 ounces. It's a bit steep, if you ask me. Especially if you add ice. One thing that my girlfriend noticed was the odd pricing for concretes: If you order a "half" (which is plenty big for one person) a pre-made one is $4.25. Keep in mind their pre-made super-gourmet ones have 3 or 4 "add-ins". If you do a "design your own", which starts at $3.25 for a half, mix-ins are $0.55 each. When you add only two, you're spending more than the 4 mix-in predetermined concretes. If you want 4, you're spending $5.45 vs. $4.25. Okay, sure it's only $1.20 - cry me a river, right? I'd say it's a bit discouraging for those that want to be adventurous and create their own! Overall, I'd agree with the Yelp suggestion for 2 stars: "Meh. I've experienced better."

Really? I waited an hour for this?? The burger was small and mediocre, the fries had enough salt kill you and the shake was tiny. There are so many better places to eat in Philadelphia. Proof that crowd sourcing doesn't work.

I'm a huge fan of this chain, but I guess I was spoiled with the original in NYC. Maybe they were having an off day, but they were still pretty packed at 11 pm on a thursday. I ducked in RIGHT before closing and still had to wait a good 20 minutes for a cheeseburger and fries. That's to be expected because it is a new opening of a hallowed institution. FINE. But, yo. The burger was kind of flavorful and somewhat juicy, but it was well done. It was way over cooked. They need to retrain the chefs to keep the maximum amount of juicy. I have yet to try my favorite Shack Stack there, it was way too heavy for an 11 pm meal. Maybe one day when the hype dies down. Soon my friend, soon.

My husband and I have eaten lunch there twice, both times after seeing the line at the Chipotle's next door.   On the basis of the food alone, I'd rate 3-4 stars.  However there are other issues.  Observations: 1.  I'm quite literate, have a grad school degree, but had one hell of a time parsing the food options displayed on the wall at the front of the restaurant in order to choose something to order.   The layout and combinations made my head want to explode. 2.  The music was too loud, particularly at the front of the restaurant where you wait in line to order (probably contributed to the feeling of my head wanting to explode). . Although Chipotle's does this too, this is a really BAD feature, one that shouldn't be copied.    The kids may not mind this, but for my middle-aged ears, the sound levels made me want to leave.  If I wasn't absolutely ravenous at the time, I would have left before ordering. 3.  Ordered large veggies & tofu (both times, with different sauces).   Veggies and tofu were good, rice was way too abundant.  In the future (if we return) would probably order small plate instead of large and order extra vegetables to get the ratio of protein/vegetables/rice to where I'd prefer.   4.  Waited quite a while for our order on the most recent trip.   It seemed like the server was overwhelmed.  We got our order after the cashier left her post and jumped in to help get orders to tables.

I surprised by the bad reviews as well. The place has a variety of selections. I have taken some food out, mostly seafood and I felt like I was robbing the place based on the great quality of seafood that  I chose. I think  one's experience depends on the time of day her or she goes there. For example, during dinner time, they put out a lot of crab legs and it goes quickly! They had to keep on putting out more. I'm going to have an event there and I've ask them to make sure that the food is hot, which was my only complaint the second time I had been there. They did say  that they will make sure that the food is hot.  I think the second time it wasn't hot was that all the food was gone and since it wasn't extremely busy, they didn't bring out more food quickly. I'll send another update.

This place is horrible... I was sick for 2 days I had gotten food poisoning from them I will never ever eat chinese or there again :( it was horrible!!! PLZ call the health people and get this place fixed or shut down!!!

I stopped by this place to purchase fish and chips. First let me say they do have fresh fish which looked amazing.  I may come back and purchase fresh fish. As for the take out, I came with a coupon to get 15% off.  I ordered the fish and chips and was told that the fish & chips was a special and not applicable for the coupon.  (The fish and chips is a special which is on the standard menu?) Anyway, in about two minutes they gave me my order and I drive a total two minutes home. When I got home I open the box to find the fish was just barely cooked and soaked in grease.  There was no time for anything to drain and it was soggy, greasy and completely tasteless.  There was no seasoning what so ever. After two bites, my mouth coated with grease, I could not continue.  It was by far the worst fish I have ever tasted. I normally do not write bad reviews but this was not a good experience.  I may choose to buy fresh fish but never cooked fish again!

I was amazed and delighted by high end, fresh food in a cool vintage looking pub - they have a separate dining room, a game room with shuffleboard! and a cool bar with a famous legendary "death seat" where 3 bar patrons died in the sixties (at different times)...It's funny. But the food was really good - and I write about food for a newspaper. The burger was made from very high quality fresh beef (not frozen) and the owner whipped up a baked ziti with roasted garlic, sausage, prosciutto and no ricotta which was wonderful. Going to check out the live music this weekend - I'm hooked! Diane Lilli

I've never wrote a review before, but felt it was necessary for this restaurant.  We will NOT return....sub par food and costly for what you get.  We visited Alla Spina on the Friday of opening week. My boyfriend and I are HUGE fans of Marc Vetri restaurants (Vetri, Amis) and thought the concept of an Italian gastropub was incredible.  While the concept is still incredible, the food is very lack luster.  We were not going there looking for food like Vetri or Amis, but expected better food than what was served.... Our table had the following dishes: House made pretzel with beer cheese Veal riblets Pig pot pie Swordfish BLT Mortadella hot dog Italian lasagna Oysters Aside from the amazing oysters and the swordfish BLT, the rest of the dishes were absent of flavor (except for the flavor of salt).  I've had better beer cheese at a no-name hole-in-the-wall pub.  The veal riblets had NO meat on them.  We were literally trying to pick strands of meat off the fatty bones.  My guess is there was approximately 1 teaspoon full of meat on the bones of the $14 dish.  The pig pot pie crust was good, but the filling was destroyed by an excessive use of salt.  We took a few bites of the lasagna and then noticed the meat looked very undercooked; needless to say, both of us were sick last night.   The Italian beer selection is great, but seems a bit pricey when a 12 oz beer costs $10-14 on average. I would suggest having some kind of beer specials to help draw more people in, because I can tell you the food will not.   Our tab was $200+ and I still left there hungry.   Our party of 4 all agreed that we would not return for the food, but might consider going back for a drink.

Checked out Alla Spina with a bunch of friends Friday night. We had the best table in the house: it was on the second floor and overlooked the dining room! As one of my dining companions commented, "This does not feel like Philadelphia." And it certainly didn't. The lay-out of the restaurant is very open, very hip and very approachable. It was hopping on a rainy Friday, which I think says a lot. Most city-dwellers would need to take a cab to Alla Spina, but by the packed tables and bars, they clearly think it is worth it. The menu was written by a man, for a man with a lot of meat, fried foods and cheese. That said, the girls at the table did not go hungry. Our table tried many different appetizers and a few entrees. Highlights included the grilled cheese, the prosciutto, the crispelle, the lasagna, the soft pretzels and the pot pie. The boys seemed to love the pig tail, the oysters and the fried chicken. Our server was really great, making sure that the 30-week preggo lady (me) had a constant supply of cranberry and seltzer and also checked on us constantly. You can also send the kitchen a six pack of beer for 10 dollars, which we did, and he let me ring the bell to signal this. I think the ambience of Alla Spina is pretty great. If I go back, I am going to get a grilled cheese and not share.

So the wait was a bit long and subsequently the service a bit chaotic. The baked oysters were very good. And the beers very interesting (and good). It was their first week, so perhaps worth a second shot. If you're in that neighborhood, I think Route 6 is better.

I think this place would have better reviews if the name Vetri was  NOT attached to it.  Take away all the Vetri expectations and the place lives up to its intentions, which is a casual gastropub with great food. I loved it, and will definitely be back.  Bartenders were great, and the company surrounding the bar really gave you that CHEERS kinda feeling.

So happy to have this new pub in the neighborhood!!!  Hubby and I tried it out Sat evening...ended up sitting outside...shared three of the small plates and then had the fried chicken and grilled cheese.  All good and our waitress, Julia, was fantastic!!  We will be repeat customers.

I have been to this Vetri Family restaurant on 2 occasion, implemented 2 different styles of ordering and sharing with members in my party. I have been very pleased with the food, wine and beer. Very well executed and inventive food choices. Service and food were top notch on both occasions. I highly recommend this restaurant.

My wife and I had lunch there using a Groupon the she got a while back. I'm glad we finally went as the the food was quite good. The only Chinese we ever eat is take-out so this seemed like a nice change. We still played it safe thought. She ordered General Tso's Chicken and I ordered Sesame Chicken, both from the dinner menu. Since I don't know what REAL Chinese food tastes like, I can say that this was way better than any take-out. The service was very good, although our waiter could have smiled once or twice. The presentation was also done really well. We'll go back again.
Great food.  A bit expensive.  Nice service.  Good location.

Fornino is a fantastic spot, tucked away on the coast of brooklyn. While the walk there might not be so scenic, you will be surprised to see a beautiful public park area in active development and a large quiet rooftop with plenty of seating and an incredible waterfront view of manhattan once you arrive.
Nice people who work here; excellent home-cooked food; I would highly recommend this Thai restaurant.
Very very good. Very fresh ingredients. If you in the mood for Thai, come here!

So my date took me here a month ago.. We won't go on a date again ( ssstttttr) But I will be back to this lovely place. I love restaurant that have great food. Fresh and great quality, expert chef! Thank you for being so close too See you soon my dear

We've been to Woody's quite a few times and always leave feeling very satisfied. I'm one of those strange people who likes their dogs naked, so a good quality dog is important. Woody's has top quality dogs and delicious toasted buns. My husband, on the other hand, is a true adventurer - he likes them all but his favorites are the Deputy Dog and the Underdog. Woody's is a great place for us to meet for lunch.

Last night (6/27/11) my wife brought home baklava from there. She told me they had a sign that read. "Best Baklava." That sign knows things. Trust it always. I swear there was almost a flavor of really good pizza dough in there. It was the best baklava I've had. It came in small cubes (my wife tells me its $0.50 a cube) so sharing it was easy and not messy. My wife should stop by here after work more often.

Came here for my morning Chai!  I am impressed with this place since it used to be a DHL shipping facility back in the day.  Now located next to a nail saloon and dry cleaner.  It has seating, open windows and brand new everything. It was slightly less expense than a Starbucks and I really like the loyalty card, buy 10 drinks get 11th one free. However, I did not try any of the baked goods, they looked fresh.  I think it's ashame the location is not open on weekends, it would probably get a fair amount of business due to the high traffic location of being in a residential spot.  I'm sure since the other location has good reviews, this one will do well too.  Hoping to stop by and try some other treats soon.

Illy coffee (served at four Financier and two Manon outposts) is no longer the only decent coffee brand name in Fidi, as Intelligentsia has arrived on the scene via the nicely appointed Blue Spoon. The prices here for smooth, strong, high quality Intelligentsia coffee and tea are also lower than at many competing shops, including those offering inferior product.  Neatly arrayed fresh pastries from Balthazar and Ceci-Cela are enticing in their display case, and gourmet lunch items are  also available. All sandwiches are served on crusty Balthazar Ciabatta bread, and the roasted turkey sandwich with mixed greens and plum tomato was very fresh and generous in size for the price. Service is very efficient--there is none of the line out the door business from the Cedar Street Financier or tomfoolery among baristas at other chains.

I was excited to see a Thai place in SO and I will say it wasn't bad but it wasnt' great. I feel the menu is too sushi based and doesn't offer many thai options. The portions are small too and can be bigger. The price point is okay. I wouldn't say I won't go again but I feel they can offer more selections on the thai food side, I felt the menu was all sushi etc. The atmosphere was nice, they did a nice job decoration
so so yummy!!! went for lunch......amazing.  will return!!!  super good lunch deals!  If you know me, you know I love nothing more than a CHEAP LUNCH!

I couldn't disagree with the other review more. I too am stoked to have a place across the street from me. But after sampling the crispy pig ears, bone marrow, and steak frites, I was very happy. The cocktails seem to want to be speakeasy. But may need some tweaking. I sat at the communal table and within 15 minutes found myself chatting with blonde, twin doctors. So overall, I had a good time. I look forward to many nights of stumbling back across Moyemensing.

Awesome place! Great food & great beer/cocktails. Lots of cheap but high quality food and very different kinds of dishes too (lamb neck gravy/ pork ear lettuce wraps are what I got..sooo good) definitely recommend this place for any occasion.

The bad reviews are a little concerning to me because I've been here twice and have enjoyed it both times.  I live around the corner and am ecstatic that there is some place I can grab a beer and some decent food.  Don't get me wrong, the Brew House is great but The Industry is within stumbling distance, especially on a weeknight after a long day of work.  The beer selection is well rounded and the space is really nice.  I have not had any problems with excess noise, but  I realize I'm in a bar!  There is still much on the menu to try but I have had a few appetizers, salads, and sides and have not been disappointed.  Hopefully, the reviews start to change a bit and The Industry can flourish here.

Man ooh man did I want to love this place! Like everyone else I've been anticipating its opening.  I'll make this review short and sweet: -decor: pretty decent. Love the ceilings. -service: average at best -drinks: good beer menu and mixed drinks -food: eeehhhhh.  Had the burger it is was not that good. bun was stale, cheese was cold and burger was room temp.  General Tso wings sucked! The Mexican corn was ok. But for 4$ no way! Its corn! The menu looks SO odd and not yummy at all (hence why I played it safe with a burger). I was disappointed the good ol' guys at good dog couldn't even get a burger right. As far as everything else on the menu Nothing looked appetizing at all.  I To be fair I'll try it again some night. Hopefully they get their act together by then.
I enjoy the food here and their service is great always. The waiters or waitresses are always good with answering questions on the menu. The prices on the menu is okay.  Great place e to dine.

This is my favorite buffet place in the Princeton area. They have a good variety of food and the food is more authentic than place like PF Chang. The person who complained about the sugary goo, well what does walnut and shrimp is suppose to taste like? The people who complain does not know what Chinese food is suppose to be. Come on American people go to PF Chang and Tiger Noodle. When you look in look at what kind of people are in there. There are a lot of Asian there. So think people! More Asian = good Chinese food. And who goes to PF Chang and Tiger Noodle?  Enough said. One thing I do not eat the American food there and I would not eat the dim sum section. It's just a waste of time. They have Peking Duck there, you're not going to find this in PF Chang & Tiger Noodle and yes Peking Duck is very greasy.

Cool atmosphere, amazing selection of whiskey, great educational flights, a little pricey compared to what I am used to but seems fair given compared to other local places for scotch. Don't let the relationship with Ri Ra scare you off.
The 5 stars are for the scotch collection and 200 open bottles whisky.

My husband loves whiskey so we had to stop for a drink after seeing this place on Church St. The bar is dark, with wood paneling and leather seats--very masculine and cool. They had a great cocktail menu (which changes seasonally) and a list of local beers. However, where The Whiskey Room really shines is their whiskey list; our waitress dropped off a book of whiskey selections (with descriptions) from all over the globe. With our drinks, we enjoyed a cheese and cracker plate made up of a selection of local cheeses. All in all, a great experience although a bit pricey.
Great liquor collection. Could beef up the beer selection. They definitely should dim the lights more  - it's too bright.

Found this place quite by accident - awesome choice of whiskeys, scotch, bourbons & ryes, and Ger the bartender was entertaining and a great mixologist. Had the sliders and daily bread off the menu - very good...highly recommended.

The food and soups are very fresh and high quality.  The platters are small and a bit overpriced.  They are served in a foil pan which is impossible to eat pilaf from.   The shawarmas are delicious but could use more meat to make them a decent value.  The menu is not the easiest to navigate, it is reminiscent of Lilly's step 1, step 2....  I will definitely be going back again and again.

Glad I found this place! When we first walked in, I have to admit, I got a little scared. Three table of ppl literally just looked right up at us... Got seated and lady walks over ready to take our order... Umm.. Menu please?I guess they know we're not their regular~!!! Lol.. Almost every review i read and saw pictures of, was the Bun Bo Hue... So... Two please... Large for the hubby, regular for me =) It was out of this world.. The broth even smelled different!! Smelled like a homemade pot of soup... Filled with lots of beef, even for my regular size bowl... They were a little stingy on the jalepeno, we only got two pieces... Overall, this place was good and I would be back to try their other stuff =)

I can't believe I've lived 5 minutes from this place for 2 years and didn't know it was there.  The service was on point and the manager was really nice.  I had a coupon for $25 off, but, really, it wasn't needed.  The food was very reasonably priced and the portions were huge.  We had calamari, a turkey club (which I brought the other half for lunch today) and the steak skewers.  Everything tasted great and our server was so helpful.  They had a happy hour for $4 cocktails which was a plus.  I will definitely be back.  They finally gave me a reason to hang out on Roosevelt Island.

I love this place. Living on Roosevelt Island doesn't give you too many options when it comes to eating out or ordering in, so it help that all the restaurants here are good. But this one is the best. They have the best sweet potato fries ever, and the Taco Burger may well be the best burger I've ever had. We eat here (or order in) at least 3 times a month.

I was very excited about you, Fare. And then a little bummed about the reviews going into it.  I was expecting fussy, what with the so heavily emphasized ORGANIC! ARTISNAL! etc and got very yummy straightforward food. Came with a good friend whom I hadn't seen in a while, which may have not been the best plan because it was a little noisy to really catch up, though we were in the center of the dining room, which may have had something to do with it. Service was fine, nothing spectacular. Lovely to have a 1/2 liter wine option for the two of us (the Torrontes was delish). I had the beet salad and crab cake app, my friend the chicken thighs. The highlight was certainly the crab cake - so good. Prices were decent, and the food was satisfying to the palate and the belly. I was pleasantly surprised, and will definitely be back.

I went here twice in one week I liked it so much.  If you don't feel like cooking and don't want to eat unhealthy this is a great place.  The cocktails are delicious and the food is very reasonably priced.  Get the avocado crab cakes and thank me later.  Can't wait to go back here.

The food here was perfectly described by "Meh".  It was not bad, but decidedly not good.  The onion soup was maybe actually bad.  It was watery and lacking flavor but was at least offset by a decent piece of grilled cheese (but really how hard is it to make good grilled cheese?).  Across the board the food looked good, was well presented, but lacked in completeness.  The flavors in each dish were not carefully considered at all, or if they were, unsuccessfully.  This place has potential if a talented chef were brought in to revamp the menu.

Fine dining comes to Fairmount. I must admit, I was somewhat expecting a super pretentious place given the culinary point of view of this place: all organic, local, blah blah blah. I appreciate that stuff but I generally associate it with experiences like the first episode of Portlandia... "the chicken's name was Colin, here are his papers". With that being said, I couldn't have been more off-base. We sat outside and enjoyed a lovely Friday evening meal that was all vegetarian. And a word about that: with the exception of Belgian Cafe and Mugshots, there is no vegetarian food in the neighborhood. But I digress... The plates we had were awesome: the cashew cheese, pink peppercorn salad; the baby artichokes; and the bbq seitan. Nut cheeses are awesome. The cashew cheese at Fare is a perfect example. It was slightly salty, very creamy, and perfectly seasoned with crushed pink peppercorns. It came with sprouts and oranges. Delicious. The artichokes were nice because they were savory and slightly garlicy with whole cloves of roasted garlic. A nice balance to the sweet salad. Finally, the seitan was insanely good. How do you get burnt ends like on a beef brisket on wheat gluten? Well they figured it out. It was so good! and the spicy sauce was a nice touch, I just wish there was more of it. Washed down with a half liter of Argentinian white wine was great. And that wine held up to the spicy bbq and the garlic in the artichokes. Good addition to a neighborhood that already holds its own in the restaurant landscape.

Dined here last night with a group of friends for my bday.  Having read the reviews here prior, I would say most were pretty on par with our experience. The ambiance is lovely.  It's whimsically charming with a calming essence.  The filtered (and free) sparkling water that came in delightful glass bottles was a hit and very refreshing!  The bread basket with hummus was also really good.  It had a good hint of garlic, without being overpowering.  We took a bit to order and the waitress was patient and answered any questions we had.   I started with the ginger beets and arugula salad.  The beets were firm and fresh and the added walnut chutney was full of flavor.  The goat cheese ricotta was smooth and creamy.  Everything blended together well and my taste buds were in bliss.  The artichoke app was also full of intense flavor.  The artichokes were fresh and soft, and the romano cheese cheese and peas came together nicely.  Last was the avocado crabcake.  It was filled with lump pieces of crab and avocado and the breading was not overpowering or deep fried like some I've had in the past.  The kicker was the sweet chili sauce that had me craving more.  Definitely recommend!  It can be made as an app or entree.  Also can be prepared gluten free for anyone with an intolerance.   Another thing that we were a fan of?  The salt and pepper shakers... instead of twisting to grind, you press down on a button and it was quite fun! The only part that was lacking for us was the dessert.  I had the apple crisp and while I wouldn't say I didn't enjoy it, it felt more like a breakfast of oats and apples than a savory end of the meal treat.   Great food, scene, and service.  I'll be back and grateful for this new addition to the neighborhood.

Fantastic newish restaurant. Had the Pork Chop and my husband had the chicken thighs. The food was amazing. I loved that everything was sustainable. The cocktails and beer list was thoughtful and delicious. Service was great. Possibly one of the best meals I've had all year. Definitely check it out!
There once was a restaurant named Fare. Organically made food was their flare. The confit duck tasted dry. We wanted to cry. Next time I think we'll go elsewhere.

Terrible! This place is way overpriced with poor quality and poor service. I purchased $52.72 worth of food, WTH was I thinking. At the time when I placed my order I had asked if the chicken was grilled? Not once but 3 different times and I was told "Yes" all three times by the server. The only offer a roasted chicken option that must sit in a liquid for hours through out the day. The pesto pasta was extremely bland and the margarita pizza ($23) was soggy and bland. This pizza has to be one of the worst in the area. As for the salads greens, I asked for the dressing on the side to prevent the greens from softening, instead they though it would be ok to dump the wet chicken over the top. The store manager was on a personal call the entire time, and when I did have a chance to explain about the grill chicken, "Jimmy" the store manager replied with an attitude like I was disturbing his personal call  "What would you like me to do, we only serve roasted chicken". This was my first and only visit. What a disappointment!

GREAT PIZZA! This is authentic brick oven pizza. It was Very good. We walked in and were told to take a seat wherever we would like. I was surprised that they served beer and wine. The Beer selection was not much, but i assume they will get more beer as business continues to increase. We ordered the medium Pie, with Devil's hot sauce and Sausage. The pie was more than enough for 2 people who had a large appetite. There were several TV's set up, and one had the Devils game on, which was appropriate. The ambiance was nice: had the feel of a pizzeria but also a decent place to sit and have a nice dinner. I did not try anything except the Pizza, but that is def. the highlight of Mercato. There was only one waitress working, and several patrons, so service wasn't the fastest, but the waitress was attentive and very nice, and nothing was delayed too long. From reading other people's reviews, I think people are going a bit too crazy over the "price". While there are plenty of "cheap" places all throughout the great city of Newark, this was priced just fine for a downtown establishment with a very nice setting and close to the Prudential Center and NJPAC. We ordered a medium pizza, which was enough to feed probably 3 adults, a few beers, and it came to 43.00 which is about the price of a casual dinner out. There are a few good pizzeria style places in downtown Newark, but most close around 3, and the pizza is not as good or authentically brick over italian as this one. Will be coming back! Try it!

I work in Newark and pass this place everyday going to and from my office.  I went on Yelp and read some"Not so great" reviews and was a little worried.  I finally stopped in about 3 weeks ago for lunch and let me tell you these people could not be more wrong.  The service was amazing, the food was delicious, and the prices are very resonable for the amount of food you get.  Needless to say i have been back a few times since then and have had the same GREAT experience every time.  I highly recommend this place and am looking forward to going back again soon.
Amazing Pizza...Amazing Service...I will definately be going back soon!

Went to a show at the Prudential Center and most of the other restaurants in the areas had long lines. We were able to get a table without any issue. We ordered a regular tomato pie and we ordered a medium pie with mushroom. I'm used to very good pizza (NYC and Brooklyn) and I wasn't too impressed with Mercato. The sauce was bland and the pies needed some sort of additional flavoring. Somewhat disappointed but the food was enough to satisfy a group of 5. The waitstaff was very slow. One of my party members got a soda and was only able to get a refill once since the waitress never came over.

I ate lunch at Mercato on Friday after Christmas, the pizza is cooked in a big coal fired oven and was awesome.  The atmosphere is great, pleasant staff and the Pannini  I had was also very good. I would recommend this place to anyone for lunch or before a show at the Prudential Center or anytime really. Go try it out, you will love it.
Just went there tonight before Devil's game.  Had the pepperoni pizza it was great.  Right next to Prudential Center so great for pre game meal.

Great new addition to the small world of Mexican food venus in Burlington. They make a great tongue taco as well as the other tacos I have tasted. They should also recieve an A+ on the make over of the old diner without losing any of the orginal charm.

If the rating alone was solely based on aesthetics and how well planned out the theme of the restaurant was, they would receive a 5 star. Food  + Value = " 2 1/2 star"    5 dollar tacos will leave you hungry and your wallet empty . A normal complete meal for the average person would be 4 Tacos in addition to maybe a side order of chips w/salsa. Total price for one person would be 20 dollars easy.. Sorry but that is expensive for tacos that are just average. The sauces that I tried were average and nothing special. The Salsa Verde was notable and there best condiment from what I had tried. I base my judgment more upon the food and value than anything else. If you want the best Mexican in my opinion, go to at Aztlan Foods. Next to Green Mtn Coffee Roasters Outlet in Waterbury, VT. 8 dollars buys you a Giant Burrito that screams flavor with each and every bite.

In terms of aesthetics, they did a fantastic job; bar looks great, tables, even the toilet had been decorated, which was a riot. Hooks on the underside of the bar for handbags would be a very welcome addition. As for their tacos- the flavours in the fillings were great, but the tortillas were very difficult to roll. Their texture seems as though they had been microwaved and unfortunately, in the time it took to consume one taco, the second tortilla was impossible to eat- very tough and chewy. I ended up jettisoning it in favor of making a kind of loaded nacho. If the tortilla issue is taken care of, I'd definitely go again, as the tongue and pork were both very good.

I must say I expected more because I love the Farmhouse so much. I didn't love the decor/menu style, but that isn't a big deal. The guac/salsa were expensive and bland. My margarita was amazing and our waitress was superb. The carnitas and pescado tacos were delicious.. no complaints there. The pollo and camote were boring in comparison. Next time I will skip the guac and head right for the tacos!
Nothing about this place is impressive.  The food was mediocre..well it sucked. thats about all I remember.  Won't go back.

Best Burgers around! No joke! Was one of my secret places in Newark for a burger and a beer but now everyone knows about it. I go out of my way because they have honest hearty manly burgers. They have made me spoiled. I want one now....
The soy garlic chicken wing is a must have.  And the jasmine green bubble tea.

Best Chinese food outside of Chinatown. My favorite egg rolls and fried rice dishes in the city. Good, fast service and they offer both take-out as well as delivery. Decent prices and a great go-to for Chinese takeout.

I can only say with a lot of excitement that another reviewer who said that sip for sip and bite for bite this is the Upper Valley's best cafe was very right!   I've been coming here at least once if not twice per week in the last two years and I cannot commend this place enough. The service is OUTSTANDING. Reed, Danielle and May are very friendly, remember customers by name and even remember customers' beverage preferences which is a great touch. They also make great coffees.  Which brings me to...coffees. This place makes the best coffees west of Italy and Turkey!  Whether you want a delicious expresso or an authentic Turkish coffee (including the Turkish delight), Tuckerbox will not disappoint. Not only is this place a great choice for a coffee break, it is also an awesome choice for lunches and dinners!  I regularly take the kebab salad because it is both extremely delicious and healthy (juicy kebab freshly prepared, with fresh salad, a delicious dressing and some yummy yogurt based sauce).   For dinner, the meze platter will wet your appetite and any of the kebabs will leave you happily full!  Ask for the Turkish red - a delight! Also ask for Vural, the owner. You'll very likely find him very involved, either in the kitchen or talking to customers. He's a great guy with a service attitude and friendliness that is fully aligned with that of Tuckerbox's overall feel!   I will miss this place a lot as I leave the upper valley!  I hope it stays as charming as it is now.
Super cute cafe, great atmosphere... But the food was SO slow to arrive (others were complaining, asking where their food was). Food was nice enough, but not worth the money or wait.
Cool restaurant, good draft beers, and pickles are good. Besides that it was just ok. Food was nothing special. Brisket bark wasn't full of flavor like it's supposed to.

Beef rib is delicious, but why cant you just get half pound of it? They cut it off the bone and serve it with the bone but ain't like anyone is gonna eat the bone...so I think half pound of beef rib should be an option! The pulled pork is good. The sauces are good. UNFORTUNATELY, the sides are really mediocre in comparison. The beans were drenched in the sauce. The collard greens were subpar--not much flavor, kind of one-dimensional even with the added pork. We got a small in both and we didn't finish either of these. The cornbread was bland, although the honey on top was a nice touch. I'm knocking off a lot of stars though because the SERVICE WAS BAD. They were unfortunately out of brisket, and there was someone in line that asked the server when the brisket would be ready. The server said he didnt know, that it could be as quick as "5 minutes" or as long as "45 minutes." The customer then inquired if the server could ask someone in the back for a more accurate timeframe as he was interested in getting some brisket to-go after dining in. The server, visibly annoyed by the customer's further inquiry, didnt even bother to ask the pitmaster and implied that asking would be pointless/a hassle because the pitmaster would have to weigh the meat or something. He didn't sound apologetic or sympathetic to the customer. First of all, if the wait could potentially be as quick as "5 minutes," you should get your hiney to the back and ask. What's the harm? The customer wants to buy more food, and REFUSING to SIMPLY CHECK how long til the next batch of brisket comes out is a SLAP IN THE FACE to that customer. Plus, the line is pretty long (we were there on a Saturday a little before 2pm), so if indeed the wait potentially was going to be as quick as 5 minutes, then the customer could've had others go in front of him til the brisket came out. Seriously, train your middle-aged hipster-wannabe servers correctly with some proper restaurant manners. As for my own order, I think they charged me an extra $13 or so. We got the beef rib ($25), 1/2 lb pulled pork ($11), 2 small sides ($8) and 1 cornbread ($3). The total was a little less than $65. That doesn't add up. Unfortunately, we didn't realize this until we drove off, so we weren't able to bring it up. I guess 13 bucks is no big deal in the end, but considering the aforementioned incident, it annoyed me. In addition to training your servers to abide by some degree of service to the customers, please train your servers to do their math correctly. The meats were good. Certainly better than a lot of the other places around town. But if you have CR*P service and start overcharging people for things they didn't buy, that's not gonna do ANY good for the business... EDIT: I was just informed that the beef ribs were $25/pound with it usually being 1.5 to 2 lbs. We asked specifically for a pound. You know how you go to Whole Foods, ask for a pound of salmon, they weigh it at 1.1 pounds and ask hey, is that alright? Yeahhhhh, you guys should really do that so that the customer knows how much they're paying beforehand. Again, CUSTOMER SERVICE, FOLKS...it can make or break a business.

I'll make this short: food was good. I had the pulled pork sandwich but for some reason they throw a dainty amount on a thick hard roll. I'm not being picky, this roll is about 4-5 inches thick making it more of a roll with a slight pork flavor vs a pulled pork sandwich. I ended up eating it off the roll and eating the roll as a side. Also, as others reviews state, service ain't too good. And, their ordering system straight sucks. Hey owners! Do something about it! Having one line with annoyed workers isn't good. By the time you get your food you already have a bad taste in your mouth. Are two lines and a little speed in service too much to ask for? I also had the Mac and cheese which was good. Basically this comes down to them losing business due to service and  ordering system. I honestly may not go back. The food is good but not worth the experience. ( and please use better bread on with your sandwiches. The meat should be the focus, not the stiff, chewy bread.)

Pretty expensive for such cheap meats. $14 for a 1/2 pound of brisket is asking a WHOLE lot. I really don't care if you're smoking it for mass amounts of hours. I shouldn't be paying for a miniscule amount of sub par brisket at that price. These downtown trendy bbq places get away with this. It's pretty unfortunate that I heard such good things about this place, only to be left still hungry and my wallet empty. The dry rub is pretty basic, with a hell of a lot of black pepper. Kind of over compensating if you ask me. This is just another brooklyn bbq spot that will accommodate the tourists off the water taxi, or the hipsters of bumblefuck who know next to nothing about food.

Fun, laid back atmosphere with plenty of room to sit, although it does get crowded quickly on weekends. Get a few things to try, but make sure you prioritize the moist (fatty) BRISKET. Go light on the pork belly. Side dishes are fantastic--I thought the collards were particularly good, but the beans and mac n cheese were great too. Key Lime Pie dessert was disappointing. Great beer selection. Will be back for more.

Seriously shitty atmosphere & waaaay over priced. I payed for top of the line meat and literally got all fat. Just because it marinates for a long time does not make the fat disappear. Absolutely gross.

Having grown up in Texas (yup, I'm pulling that card), something just rubbed me the wrong way about this place. -decor is just trying way too hard...like I could see it on Portlandia -comically slow service -so-so brisket -overpriced -no wonderbread/fixins - what Texan would honestly want some artisanal bread w/bbq? -$6 key lime "pie" was a freakin' tartelette (what is this...a pie for ants?!)...didn't even taste good To make things worse, THEY WERE OUT OF SHINER BOCK (SERIOUSLY?!?!? YOU HAD ONE JOB). Not even Lonestar as a backup beer...so sad. If you're looking for something more authentic with an even better price point, I highly recommend Mable's...they carry not only Shiner, but Shiner Seasonal (RUBY REDBIRD, my friends). It feels more like a place back home than Hometown did.

Was totally excited to dine here after reading a spread on Hometown in Thrillest. But I have to tell you I was sincerely and truthfully disappointed. The line was terribly slow for starters, we went midday on a weekday so the place wasn't packed. They were just slow for no reason. Then the prices. $25.00 a pound for beef ribs, $12.00 per half pound for spare ribs. And the outrageous prices for the meats go on. But regardless of the that ominous warning, we pushed on and ordered beef ribs, spare ribs and brisket sandwiches. A side if Mac and cheese, baked beans, and greens. The beans and collards were mediocre at best. But the Mac and cheese is fabulous, some of he best I have ever had. Too bad this isn't a Mac n Cheese restaurant. The BBQ, well it is NOT WORTH THE PRICE. The dry rubs and sauces were great, the meats were dry. Ribs were all dry and tough. The brisket was dry, and they don't give enough meat in the sandwiches to offset all the bread in the buns.... Sauce to the rescue!!! Friends I was literally at a block party in BK, where the main host smoked up some of the best brisket and ribs I've had in my entire life. And that was a back yard smoker the size of a hot dog vendors cart in the city. Smoked over night and cooked to perfection in someone's yard..... What's HOMETOWNS EXCUSE? Another thing that turned me off to this place was the site of them throwing out food. The carver literally was cutting brisket and ribs, weighing out of the pieces for orders. Then in front of our faces they were throwing out ribs, chunks of meats... Big pieces not scraps. Wasteful and sad when Meals on Wheels, and City Harvest exist. When asked why are they throwing out food? He simply chuckled and lied, "Oh, those are scraps we make our beans with". Then shortly after he proceeded to throw out scraps of paper, plastic and trash in the same trash can as those "beans destined scraps". This is just another well dressed and advertised hipster hole. Shoot go to "Brother Jimmys", at least you get what you pay for there. Or better yet, do it yourself. They get 2 stars from me for 2 reasons. Mac N Cheese was excellent, and they have free refills on soft drinks... sadly they do not offer sweet tea! BBQ and no sweet tea... W T F! Go for the Mac and that's all.

OMG.  I thought places like Plenty only existed in my dreams.... Went here last night for the first time and the service was outstanding! We were offered multiple samples of various sides, just because! (or maybe I was drooling more than I noticed).   Their MAC and CHEESE is too die for!! No, let me be more specific: It's literally the best mac and cheese I've ever had! (Good thing my mom has no idea what yelp is....blasphemy.)  Oh, and just because the service is amazing, they actually went to the back to get us the hot, fresh batch of mac and cheese : )   Also had the cauliflower with pesto....amazing!  Husband got shredded bbq pork which he said was delicious; I can only attest that the whipped sweet potatoes (w/madras curry) and the HOMEADE CORNBREAD were also five stars!  It's obvious they've prepared their foods to go and specially constructed them to still have moisture when reheated....cornbread was moist and sweet and nothing was even close to dry after reheating.   Bottom Line:  We finished our meal feeling like we'd just eaten out at one of our favorite byos, except that we got way more food and only spent $20 for both of us!  I am officially declaring myself a (soon to be) regular!
Good food, however, I had to wait for over a hour for a table even though I had a reservation... Disappointing

It is very rare an owner of a  restaurant greets you with a hand shake on arrival. For a Tuesday night the place was rather crowded, a good sign. ( 15-20 seat area) a few outside. We sat outside (7 people) Warm bread with garlic and olive oil  was very tasty. Apps were very clean and  simple, very fresh. Salad and sides were not overdone, again very clean. All sauces were "light" slightly sweater and creamier than the usual over salted acidic red sauces. The service was rather attentive, to the point . Very simple menu. We ordered several veal and chicken dishes all tasted uniquely different.       I will say this ...Anyone who gives a one star pathetic ego filled pretentious review should be banned forever ! You can always eat some fake "charcuterie" from that place next to the shannon rose!

This place was packed on Wednesday night. The restaurant is very cozy, but I had the pleasure of being seated on the outdoor patio. The meal started with a bread basket, which came with a nice oil based dipping sauce with garlic, herbs, and cheese. We opted not to get an appetizer to save room for the nutella pizza I kept hearing about. The menu is fairly extensive and I opted for the fusili with creamy artichoke and sausage. The food was excellent. The creamy artichoke sauce was flavorful, the fusili was cooked perfectly al dente, and the sausage had the perfect amount of herbs in it. Now, I knocked off a star solely because the service I got was pretty terrible, and because of that poor service, I did not get to order the nutella pizza. I'm actually even tempted to knock off two stars because it was pretty frustrating that I could not get my waitress' attention. She came to the table to bring take our orders, bring drinks, and bring food. She did not check on us once until she was clearing the plates. She did not keep our drinks filled. And most importantly, we were not able to get the nutella pizza because the chef had left for the night and she didn't think to offer us the chance to order dessert. It was all the more frustrating to see the other waiters being friendly with other patrons, providing excellent service at adjacent tables, while I sat there waiting to be served. Next time, I'll have to try to get an earlier  reservation or hope for a different waiter/waitress.

A very good Italian restaurant!  We went on a Thursday night and it was crowded.  Reservations are highly advisable!   The owner is very amicable and makes for a pleasant dining experience.  The pizza here is delicious!

I ran about 1.5 miles in uncomfortably tight jeans to get here in time before they closed. Turns out they close at 3:30pm instead of 3pm like I thought so I didn't even need to run, but it was so worth it. The texture of chang fen was perfect. Very soft, steaming hot, and mixed with your choice of topping and scallions. I tried the corn, beef, and dried shrimp kinds. Favorite was the dried shrimp since it was the saltiest. They also have sweet soy sauce and peanut sauce you can put on your rice rolls. They also sell bottles of packaged soy milk for $1. It's not as freshly made as they sell in the soymilk/dou hua specific stands but goes great with the rice rolls and at least it's not the gross American kind of soy milk. If you get a chance watch the lady make the rice rolls. She spreads the rice batter thinly onto a metal sheet with the toppings and sticks it in a large box shaped steamer. It's pretty cool to watch. Definitely coming back to get more rice rolls and try their other kinds as well. Also want to try their dou hua later on.

I passed by this place for years and I never knew they sold rice noddles.  I am kicking myself for it now because of all the potential rice noddles I missed because of it. What I don't like about this place is that there is no order.  There is a open door and an open window stall.  People seem to line up at both places and order like crazy. The noddles were are really good because the workers steam them right there.  What even better is that they allow you to put on the sauce so you can get it exactly the way you want.  I ended up with a little too much sauce that made a mess with my jacket. For 1.25 it is one of the cheapest options left for a good meal.  If you want more add on then that is going to cost more but I like to stick with the basics. This is literal a hole in the wall.  There is no seating or even eating inside.  You just buy and you walk away eating.

I have been craving cheung fan, lately, and I'm so happy that I found Sun Hing Lung Co.  I used to go to the prep school that is next to this place, and I never knew that you can just get it right there.  When I was younger, I would always go to the cart in front of the Hong Kong Supermarket on Allen St before the supermarket burned down (now it's a Mariott Hotel).   Anyways, Sun Hing Lung Co. is different than the other carts or other places that serve cheung fan because they make it fresh.  I don't mean a fresh batch that they put in the steamer, I mean a fresh batch right from the liquefied mixture to solid cheung fan.  I had the roast pork cheung fan, the pork cheung fan, and the mixed vegetable cheung fan.  I liked the mixed vegetable more than the pork because of the cilantro and the corn (my favorite vegetables).   Another good thing is that they allow you to mixed your sauce.  This is a big plus because I never seem to get enough sauce in my cheung fan.  Don't ask for the cups because I think the sauce is different.  I used one and I think it's just soy sauce, not the one you put in cheung fan.
Very average food....not a great Buffet spread....the curries tasted bland....Desserts were just ok....small place so service was not an issue...

Good Indian food..little pricy. Buffet spread is very average. Service was good. My fav has to be chicken Biriyani and Shrimp Pakora...little oily thou..! Restaurant on the whole is not noticeable and easy to miss it in the strip mall. Definitely a place to try out if you are looking for some Indian Food..!

0 FUCKING STARS FUCK THIS PLACE MY GOD!!!!!!!!!! ITS 3 am and I am still thinking about how fucking shit this establishment is... Jesus H Christ....First off the Service was absolute shit it took 30 minutes to get a fucking beer, which they got wrong.  Next they proceeded to serve me and my father shit food, which mine was cold and my father said his sucked too... I told the waitress my food was cold and she got the manager and he asked if i wanted a new plate (fuck off)...The manager blamed it on being busy, this PLACE IS MANAGED BY 12 YEAR OLDS.....Overall a horrible experience and I usually dont do this but this place is exceptionally SHITTY!  I dont understand how a restaurant that is this terrible could still be in business but i assume its just another shitty corporate restaurant that cuts corners for profit.....WORST DINING EXPERIENCE EVER!!!! FUCK THIS PLACE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

The Good: Perfect dive bar with cheap beers and proper shots Great bartenders and friendly staff Games a plenty -perfect Sunday football spot. The Bad: Expect a dive bar with dive bar food, dive bar clientele and dive bar prices and you won't find anything bad about this place.  If you're looking for craft cocktails and pork belly, go back to 2010.

cheap drinks, big place,plenty of room to rock out & they take debit without a min. thank god, i never carry cash on me! ive come here just to see a few local bands on certain nights, its always pakced and filled with sloppy people. its usually a fun time, and they have cheap drinks! get your booty down here!

I went here on 2/15/13 and I'll be honest I didn't have coffee, so mums the word on coffee. I did have a a French Dip burger (I believe that's the name) with the onion rings, cheese and BBQ sauce. The burger was great I would go back just for that burger. That said there were some temperature issues, I ordered medium rare and got medium and the rest of my table ordered their burgers medium and got well done. With that said, the burgers were still very good (the reason we didn't send it back.) The wait staff was great and very accommodating! Its BYOB folks! Come on!!! Were are you gonna bring your own beer/wine and have a great burger at the same time? Oh yeah that one shop on the corner of nowhere. Anyway they had live entertainment, it was open mic so that could either be a great thing or a bad thing depending on who's on the mic. We had the fortune of having a gentleman with a great voice and an acoustic guitar, so it worked in our favor. All in All folks give this place a shot and you just might like it. For me and my family we were very happy and will go back again.

They care how they're doing and it shows -- they spare the expense to buy fine ingredients such as real, balsamic vinegar, and if they get a suggestion, it gets tested and can be likely found on the menu soon after.  You can tell they have fun with recipes and take risks.  I cannot wait to go to have my family to their Sunday brunch and score major points.

I love hand rolls. They're my favourite form of sushi. This is like a hand roll on steroids and is about the best thing I could ask for after a brutal weekend gym class. I went with a build-your-own and got the chicken katsu on white rice and seaweed wrap with spicy gochujang, spring mix, carrots, cucumber, asparagus, and crunchy shallots. I died and went to hand roll fusion heaven. It was really, really delicious. I am docking 1 star for lack of low-fat protein options. There is chicken and shrimp - both fried, plus flank steak and salmon. I would have liked a grilled chicken option. I will say that the chicken katsu was a good choice in terms of the amount of protein you get. Two large chicken pieces was more than enough to make this a filling meal. I will be back on many a sunny Saturday in the future! This is also a great option for dining in the parks nearby - very portable and easy to eat. Service was friendly and fast!

Hai street is hot stuff! On an evening visit we had fortunate timing.  There was no line when we ordered, but by the time we were halfway through our rolls the line was backed up to the door. My beau and I each ordered a roll, he opted to "go zilla" for additional protein leaving us both satisfied with our meals.   Like Christine B. mentioned, the hand rolls are messy. Just picture trying to eat a burrito that wasn't tucked in at the ends and you'll get an idea of how messy it can get. Regardless, it was a delicious mess! My portobello mushrooms with spicy gochujan sauce, asparagus, carrots, cucumbers, and cabbage brown rice roll hit the spot. Everything was fresh and well seasoned. This healthy no-msg meal cost us $20, including a box o' water & chips with wasabi guac. Will be back to try both rice and salad bowls. For those who haven't been, it's definitely more of a takeout place, with some counters but no chairs. Special thanks to the friendly guy behind the counter who complimented my Peter Pilotto dress & hooked us up with a delicious dinner.

I was the very first person in line on free lunch day and I'm sitting at my desk now having Hai Street for a second time. I absolutely love this whole idea - it's completely different from anything else you would find, and that makes me think Hai Street will be here to stay. First time, I had the Crunch roll which was amazing and fresh! I've got the Sumo Steak now (added the spicy mayo because I loved it on the last roll) and also some tempura corn. Ummm whose idea was tempura corn?? High five for that! The Sumo Steak is super yummy as well, with the spicy mayo giving it that extra kick I wanted. It is definitely more on the expensive side for just a roll, but I think the quality of ingredients speak to that. My roll and corn was around $12. Definitely not an amount of money I'd spend on lunch every day, but it's a nice treat from time to time. Best of luck to Hai Street, hope you guys continue to do well!

I, like many a foobooz reader and  self diagnosed "foodie" awaited this opening with anticipation, then decided against going on free sushirito day, tried and failed to go the next day (12:30- line was down the block, ain't nobody got time for that) and finally succeeded last week. And man. Was. It. Awesome. Pro tips: -No line at 11:45. Yes line at 12:30. -byo water bottle and save a few bucks on their weird carton water, you're not eating there anyway. -they don't actually cap you at 4 ingredients in the build your own. - grab some napkins. I was very happy (ecstatic and full) with my: -brown rice, salmon tataki, spicy mayo, cucumber, papaya salad (little bit of a kick to it), spring mix, asparagus, and fried shallots ( just enough crunch) sushirito. I'm still thinking about it. I feel like it was kind of healthy too? And it kept me full for the rest of the day until my next meal adventure. Service was quick and friendly. Docked one star because for $9 I do find them a bit on the pricy side. I'll be back though. Because Burrito. Sized. Sushi. (Clarification: not like chipotle sized burrito cus that's nuts, normal smallish burrito size.)

This place is what it is. They're offering delicious sushi burritos, a concept I have not seen before. The thing is - 1) I think you should get a little more for what you pay for and 2) its a little hard to eat. For the price at $8 a roll, you should get more that just a piece of salmon and some veggies. The portion size leads this to be more of a snack than a lunch. Also, it's rolled and cut in paper, rather than foil. This makes it a lot harder to eat. Overall, this is a nice concept that's definitely unique. However, the amount of food you get for $8 isn't nearly enough to feed me for lunch. I'll probably pass.

A pretty interesting concept. Think a gigantic sushi roll that isn't cut into 6 - 8 pieces. Sort of like a Japanese burrito.  We ordered the salmon one and the shrimp tempura one. I thought the salmon was better, I liked the Chinese veggies and wasabi guac that was on it. I went at 2pm, I was in and out in 5 mins. (I've heard the line can get long)  definitely something to try once and I would go back if I was in the mood.  Also, the lemonade was horrible, jus sayin

Dropped by this interesting place last night. It's kind of American style sushi. Everything is for your own selection. I love their idea of making the Japanese sushi into a fast food, however, It doesn't taste as good as the authentic sushi. Their rolls taste just like salad with some rice. I am a sushi fan, I don't want to be mean about the taste of their sushi rolls, their rolls actually taste good, simply not taste like sushi.

PROS: Fresh ingredients, interesting concept, tasty CONS: Pricey for lunch Spending close to $10 for a tasty but small salmon sushi-rito (or a large salmon sushi roll, depending on how you look at it) is not a bad deal. At a normal sushi restaurant, you'd likely order a much smaller sushi roll for around the same price. But burrito-fying the concept of sushi leads consumers (me) to associate lower quality to the roll on a subconscious level, I think. You get a higher quality and higher-priced NORI-wrapped Asian burrito, in contrast to the cheaper, larger, carb-intense Chipotle burrito. If you have some extra money to burn and a small appetite, definitely hit this place up!

Nice place, but... slow, food took an hour plus for 3 people. The plates were a good size and nicely put together.  The pasta special had one small piece of mushroom and no tomatoes.  The waitress was nice and the beer was cold. This is not a place to go if you are in a hurry.

We just had dinner here and thought it was great. I loved the spare ribs and hot and sour soup, my daughter liked the udon noodles, and we all enjoyed the steamed vegetables and tofu.  Beautiful, comfortable place and pleasant, attentive staff...they even gave us free ice cream for Christmas eve.

Great place to grab any meal! I love the option of having breakfast throughout the day. Their mozzarella grill cheese with tomato and bacon is delicious! At $4.95 you can't go wrong. I never have to wait long to be seated, and the staff is always friendly. It's a great place to eat with the family   and not empty out your wallet. It's has the feel of a mom and pop restaurant with all the bells and whistles from a chain restaurant.
The chicken burrito I just had made me wish for the first time in 9 months I was pregnant for a longer period of time to justify eating 3 more...
Very clean and welcoming. Superb mole sauce. Reasonably priced. Parking across street behind kinkos in yellow striped spaces.

It is probably one of the best Mexican places in the area and reminds me of the amazing mexican food I got used to in CA. Do try their Carne Lengua burrito which comes with rice and  a yummy corn bread. I would have given it a five star if their service matched their food!
So fun if you're looking for a throwback to the diners you used to go to with your great-grandmother. They even have a jello flavor of the day!

Classic American "Diner Food" in a non-diner setting. Convenient location at the junction of I-89 and I-91 in White River Jct. VT. Booths and tables, air conditioned. I've eaten here a number times and it's always been very good. Prices are reasonable and portions are generous. They are open until 2:00pm and do breakfast all day as well as very good classic American lunches. Sandwiches and burgers, french fries and onion rings, as well as stomach stuffing hot specials with homemade mashed potatoes and gravy. They also offer cakes and pies for dessert. The decor is nothing fancy, but it's clean and the service is friendly and down-home. Clientele is a mix of locals including many seniors (a testament to the low prices) and people passing through the bus stop next door. A very good place for families with a good kid's menu and good folks all around. Today I had poached eggs on their homemade corn beef hash which was REALLY good. They have daily specials and soups as well.

If it's good enough for TV then it's good enough for me, that's what I thought. It was my first time at George's and of course I had to order the famous TNT. I love tripe and I've never had beef tongue, so why not! My first bite into the sandwich was bland and disappointing, and so was the second bite. But the meats were tender and worthy of the fine hoagie roll that housed the sandwich. After taking the TNT home, emptying the contents into a bowl, and sprinkling it with salt and pepper, the hoagie became tasty and flavorful.

I have been here twice and love the food. My first visit I got a roast pork sandwich and the meat was tender as well as delicious. My second visit I had a meatball sandwich which was probably on par with my own grandmother's homemade meatballs. Also a friendly staff who makes you feel at home.
I work in Hanover so I was thrilled when they opened, something new and I'm in love with this place! Everything's so fresh and unique! Five stars all the way! Keep up the hard work!

Service is a bit slow but the food is excellent. Absolutely worth the wait. Probably the best noodles that you will get in Hanover. The restaurant is clean and the workers behind the counter are friendly and helpful. Very pleasant experience, highly recommend going here if you're not in a rush
This Mexican restaurant is very good especially for delivery. Clean. Authentic. Good flavors. The portions could be a bit bigger but that's ok.

My first experience at BLVD was at the chef, Carlos', birthday. My wife and I were traveling from out of town and wandered in, unannounced, at about 10pm. We happened to have a friend, Louis, from Harlem Haberdashery down the block, attending the party, so we were invited to stay. The owners offered us sangria, on the house, as well as some birthday cake. We were introduced to everybody and felt very welcomed at this intimate event of friends and family. The hospitality was incredible. The next time I came here was for brunch. I had the jumbo shrimp and grits, with jalapeños and bacon. It was out of this world good. The shrimp were cooked to perfection, and the grits were creamy, cheesy, nicely spiced with the jalapeños, and the bacon was the cherry on top to bring it all together. Did I mention they bring complimentary biscuits to your table as well? Now I have. Thanks again to the wonderful owners and staff, you've got a good thing going here.

I went to the old Blvd Bistro when it first opened, and although the food was great, the owner's attitude was not at all, and I didn't go back.  Until a gf dragged me there last Sunday for brunch . . . and I LOST. MY. MIND, the food was so good.  She'd had the grits, eggs & bacon two weeks before, and couldn't stop thinking about them since!! The new owner & chef hails from Natchez, Mississippi, and is FABULOUS! The food is scrumptious! Southern-inspired but never heavy or greasy, everything on the menu is to die for delicious.  Making home fries light and fluffy is no mean feat, but somehow Carlos' kitchen delivers! The table next to us had the fried chicken and biscuit sandwich, and raved, too.  I opted for the banana bread pudding for dessert, and my oh MY -- oh MY!!! DIVINE. It is a small space and could be better configured, especially the outdoor seating, which is communal and wedges you together like sardines, hence the one star deduction, but that's just me being persnickety. The staff is accommodating and adorable, too.  The new Blvd Bistro gets two thumbs up!
Great food...Awesome beer selection..our server was on point...clean, fresh...nice outdoor deck for drinks

Egan's is a classic case of too much hype too quickly, and not enough control on quality. The positives: 1. Nice selection of beers, and a few house-made brews, as well as a respectable wine list and whisky list. 2. Clean and well maintained dining room and bar, and as a bonus a patio in back - perfect for a relaxed Sunday afternoon. 3. The chocolate brioche pudding. 4. The chocolate brioche pudding. Seriously, it's crystal meth in a cup. Now for the negatives: The service is rather hit or miss.  There are nights at Egan's where even fully packed the service is calm, friendly and efficient, and other nights when it is brusque and shoddy even when the crowds thin. The food lacks consistency.  I have had one of their signature pizza's - called a Mia Hamm topped with spinach, bacon, egg and a parmesan sauce - where everything is cooked perfectly.  I've also had to send it back because the eggs were still raw.  The oysters are rarely cleaned properly, which the couple times when I've mentioned this (once to an older gentleman in a suit I took for one of the owners), I was met with scorn and derision about not knowing how to eat an oyster. The major different between a good experience at Egan's and a bad one seems to be the general mood of the kitchen and wait staff.  When everything is humming along, there is camaraderie amongst the staff.  But on nights with poor food and service, there seemed always to be squabbles between employees.

I am new to the area just having moved here from south Jersey, and I've been checking out the local joints.  I'm also new to Yelp and thought it fitting that Egan & Sons be my first review since it has been the best experience I've had in Montclair.  I've been there three times so far and each time has been stellar, which is why I can't understand all these posts about bad service.  Seems to me like a neighboring establishment might be trying to make them look bad. The first time I went there I sat at the bar and I must say, kudos on the beer selection.  Impressive.  My bartender was Jeff.  He was great.  Somehow, between loading beer and cleaning glasses, he still found enough time to make sure my glass never got below a quarter full before checking on me.  Also impressive considering it was during a World Cup game and the place was busy and I wasn't his only customer.  Plus, he was knowledgeable about sports which came in handy because I don't follow soccer. The second time, I came in for dinner and sat at the bar again.  I don't recall the name of the bartender that served us this time, but he had a very heavy accent and I couldn't always understand him.  He was very friendly though, and he understood us as we got everything we ordered the way we ordered it and we never had to wait for a new drink.  The food there is great.  If you're a steak lover then I recommend the New York Strip.  Another one of my party had the Ahi Tuna which looks as good as it tastes.  The only thing I didn't care for was the wings, which everyone on here seems to love.  They seemed over cooked. The third time my party sat at a table in the front of the place at one of the bar tables.  I can't pronounce the name of our server, but it was something with an S.  She was very engaging and did a great job.  She kept checking on us throughout the meal.  My New York Strip was cooked perfectly (again).  My girlfriend had the scallops and she though they were phenomenal.  Her sister had the mussels and shared them with me because the portion was so large, she couldn't handle it herself.  They were great.  So good I asked for bread to soak up the sauce they were served in. This place is great.  I only gave it four stars because I want it to one up my previous experiences, which will be no easy task.  I will be coming back here again and again.  It has been nothing but a good time for me.

Agreed.  Jeff is the man Joey G..  I love Stew and Matt, but Jeff is a great new addition to the bar.  He was waiting on me during one of the world cup games when he wasn't there as a bartender, but the other bartenders were busy.  That's the kind of service I come to Egans for.

I love this place! Every time I go here I have a great experience.  The food is great and they have a great bar! They have a lounge upstairs thats a nice chill spot after the fact.  And they also have an outside deck thats great to hang out on and enjoy the night air. Definitely a place I tell people about.
hands down best sushi I ever had...yankee roll is to die for....food is fresh..unbeleivable....perfect resturant for a date...family...my favorite resturent of all time

Went here for Sunday brunch and we had a wonderful time. The outdoor seating was lovely, the server was great, and the food was a classic brunch. The menu is limited, but my partner and I were both happy with our meals. I ordered the belgian waffle and he had the western omelet. Kite & Key is a great option to get a hearty brunch before heading out to the art museums.
