Great Food, Reasonable Prices, and Chimay on Tap, does it get any better?  Amazing French Onion Soup, a nice variety of salads made better by adding grilled chicken.  I love the Steak sandwich with Chimmichurri sauce and the burger is a safe bet.  Never had a meal I didn't like.  I jokingly refer to it as the Winchester (Shaun of the Dead reference) because I spend a bit too much time there.

People familiar with the other location of Go Go Curry will see similarities in this new location. More of a hole-in-the-wall than the 38th street location, Thompson only has four square tables, which can seat about 8-12 people at any given moment. Though, in nice weather, most people simply order to go and eat in Washington Square Park. Despite being fast food-ish, Go Go Curry is not actually a quick stop, especially with its constant flow of customers and only two sets of hands handling the kitchen and cash register. Useful facts: single size serving of any curry is only $5 for the rest of March. Opens at 11:55am. Cash only until they get their machine.

A very welcome addition to my neighborhood. The food is cheap, good, and filling (though probably not the healthiest for you). The curry comes with a topping (like katsu, shrimp, sausage, etc.; or more than one if you choose to add toppings), rice, and a bit of shredded cabbage on the side. In addition to the curries, they sell a variety of Arizona Iced Tea drinks to wash it all down. The single serving size is filling enough for most, and is also only $5 for the rest of the month of March. They also give out free toppings coupons often, and have various deals throughout each month, so check for deals (especially on the 5th, 15th, and 25th of every month). I've been twice so far (once on opening day, and on a sunday afternoon for takeout) and have always found service to be pleasant as well-- the waitress/server inside is ALWAYS cheerful and smiley, which makes for a happy customer :D Interior is a bit small though-- I believe there are only 10 seats or so, but I don't think they are often too packed. Maybe a bit dangerous that I live so close, as I foresee myself coming often... But so far both my tummy and wallet are happy, so that's good enough for me.

Yum!  I had never heard of Japanese curry, be prepared, it is not like Indian or Thai curry really at all.  But it's pretty yummy.  Quick and friendly service, lot's of Japanese people were eating there when I went, which is usually a good sign.  I feel like $7.50 isn't that great a price for such low brow fare/atmosphere, especially in this neighborhood where there are a lot of great really cheap options.  But this is good stuff, I'll definitely be back. I got the chicken curry, it's rice with some curry sauce on top, topped with a large piece of breaded fried chicken.  They also have hot sauce at the table that is a nice addition.  Next time I will try one of the "toppings".   Warning, there are no vegetarian options here because the curry sauce has pork in it.
Love the pizza here! It's real pizza and that means greasy goodness! The cheesy garlic bread is good too. It has some spice to it!

My in-laws live next to this place.  I always wanted to go.  I just went starting a few months back.  I've eaten there at least 4-5 times since.  I seem to always want their pizza when visiting the in-laws.  Great ratio traditional pizza and specialty pizzas.  Family owned and operated.  Super clean.  They got Tartufo for dessert FYI. I dont have to ask for them to keep it in a few minutes longer cuz it comes out just perfect with a hint of crisposity.  My go - to for pizza in Rutherford and there's a few good pizza spots in those parts for sure.  Good. Fresh. Pizza. Great Specialty Slices Selection. Lots of tables and a TV.

Do yourself a favor; spare yourself from the excruciatingly long wait and eat somewhere else!!!!!!  In my 37 years on this planet, I have never had a more unpleasant dining experience.  Unfortunately, I cannot comment on the food, because the staff was SO off the charts rude, that we never ate.  After waiting an absurd hour and a half to be seated (Really?  For a burger joint??), including an hour just to get into the outdoor bar area for a beer, my wife and I and the couple that we were out with finally sat down at a booth.  We were immediately "greeted" by a waitress who was as unpleasant as the wait was long, and basically told us to hold our questions until she was ready to take our order.   After an unpleasant exchange with both our server and the manager, we got up and left - even after waiting nearly two hours to sit down.   This place is the new fad in B-town, and will burn out like most others within a year or so, especially if they continue to treat people the way we were treated.  It doesn't matter how good your food and beer list is if your treat your customers like sh*t!

Excellent weeknight dining experience.  The Vermont cheese selections are fairly straight forward but delicious.  The quinoa salad with rhubarb compote was absolutely divine for an appetizer.  All in all good food at a low cost.  Will eat there many times over the next year!

I'm not sure what all the fuss is about. The cheddar ale soup was mediocre.  The chicken wing special was inedible due to way too much pepper and vinegar in the Buffalo sauce.  The mac and cheese was decent.  The beer battered fish was blanketed. The service was adequate. The wait was too long for the overall experience. We'll skip it next visit to Burlington.

The 4 star is for a beer nerds paradise and selection of Vermont cheeses.  The food is only ok although mostly locally sourced.  Over rated food. BUT...beer nerds...they have Hill Farmstead on draft...Lawsons on draft...and often Heady Topper.  A book of rare bottles.  And many other rare taps like a 2 year barrel aged Meat Whistle by Magic Hat. Just go and sample beers.
I think everyone who works here is just about the nicest, ever! Excellent food and drinks. Would definitely come back if I'm in the area again.

This was pretty great. Spruce tip IPA was lively. The foie gras was more like a taurine than what I was hoping for, but good none the less. The bone marrow wasn't served how I was wanting either, it came spread on toast. It was tasty however. The cornmeal dusted fried oysters with house Kim chi were lovely. Two trips in two days, partly because they didn't have heady topper the first day, so we had to go back. All in all I love the concept of local farm to table and Vermont has a lot of stuff to pick from.

In the beginning of Barbuzzo....got 5 stars, but IMHO Marcie Turney and Valerie Safran have expanded where Barbuzzo and their other restaurants have taken a hit in the quality...3 out of 5! That's the problem with star chefs and their restaurant empires...becomes about the $$! BUT make no mistake it is still very decent!!! Barbuzzo's Sheep's milk ricotta and the beet/kale sale is amazing but has been down downsized portion wise over time and the grilled bread for the sheep's milk ricotta appetizer was over crisp...burnt! I love sitting at the counter and watching the chefs make it happen...the expediter gets 4 out of 5 stars, but he needs to be more type A for the details! The gentleman making the pizzas was such a hard worker, but the Uovo pizza was not as good as the original version 4 years ago, it was still tasty though...but it did not have that perfection that it used to have....Marcie and Valerie.....what's happening?

Yum, yum, yum!  I love it here.  I came here a few times with friends and it's always been consistent each and every time.  I love consistency when it comes to quality of service, attentiveness to your table whether it's refill your glass, dropped silverware, etc. and the speedy delivery of your food, Barbuzzo aces in all categories.   I normally get a smorgasboard of food when I come here since I can never decide what I want.  Their pizzas never let down with all fresh ingredients, they have great pasta and salads here.  I don't think I ever ordered anything sub par as you can figure out by now, I over order since everything is go good! For dessert be sure to try their salted caramel cup... it is to die for, literally it has the salty and sweet combo that you'd think you died and went to heaven. If it doesn't kill you it'll make you stronger, right? So give me another round.

One of our favorites. The space is small, so you will be sitting close to your neighbors. We loved the sheep's milk ricotta, the farro salad and the two specials we had (shrimp and paparadelle and braised short rib). Don't strike us down, but we thought the Budino was just "good". Great drinks, and the overall value is great for the level of food. The service was efficient and friendly.
Great service, love the sugar snap pea salad, only tiny complaint is some items are a little difficult to eat or cut... definitely want to try again :)

I came here for lunch. Sat at the bar! It has a great selection of drinks and a great menu! I had one pizza for myself... I was stuffed! It was the pizza with pear and some sort of meat, I can't remember. They could stand to cut the pizza in smaller slices. I was making a mess! The server was friendly and knowledgable. Cozy place... Casual.

Easily the best wood fired pizza in the city, side by side w vetris pizza in fairmount. The beet and kale salad is terrific perfectly done! Meatballs delicious and filled with cheese and deliciousness. As an italian whos family makes their own pizza from scratch at home this is a bug complement. Bravo
I've eating there 3 times now. Nothing matches the first experience. The second time was not great and the 3rd was good but not great. I would still recommend it if you can get reservations.

As a vegetarian, I'm forever in search of a desire-worthy antipasti plate and Barbuzzo delivers. They do a buzzing weekday lunch, and can get you in and out quickly if you don't have time for unlimited people-watching at the front table. Sitting at the bar is a fun experience for solo diners, as you can literally watch the fare being prepared right in front of you. The atmosphere is hip and the servers are young and friendly. The cocktails are delicious, but so are the house made juices and non-alcoholic spritzers.

My last stop in Philly was for dinner here, which is a Mediterranean place. The interiors were calming with an attractive, sophisticated ambiance. Because is a tight place, make sure to make reservations. The service was great and the food was as expected, not at all a disappointment. The good part, at least in my opinion, was that they brought out the pizzas individually right as it was done and did not wait for all of our food to be made, so we just started eating whatever was on the table! Each pizza we got was shareable. We ordered three pizzas between us four and also the butternut squash arancini as a small plate. Butternut squash arancini- Fell in love with the walnut-basil pesto. It was amazeRISOTTOBALLS. Uovo pizza- the eggs on the pizza were actually a little overwhelming but surprisingly tastes really good. The secret sauce definitely adds to the amazing taste. Margherita pizza- One of the best ones I've had. I was able to taste each ingredient and could definitely say it had the right amount of everything. Girasole pizza- Really good, but compared to the other two, a little less special. The best part is the warmth of the buffalo mozzarella that just sort of melts in your mouth. Highly recommended if you are looking for a nice place for dinner!

As a vegetarian, I'm forever in search of a desire-worthy antipasti plate and Barbuzzo delivers. They do a buzzing weekday lunch, and can get you in and out quickly if you don't have time for unlimited people-watching at the front table. Sitting at the bar is a fun experience for solo diners, as you can literally watch the fare being prepared right in front of you. The atmosphere is hip and the servers are young and friendly. The cocktails are delicious, but so are the house made juices and non-alcoholic spritzers.
Have eaten  there several  times with different groups and have always had a great meal with good service. this restaurant stands out.I enjoyed every part of my meal at Barbuzzo.
Dimly lit, but excellent food and drink. Went with the a meat lovers pizza and the branzino entry. Highly recommend this place but you might need a flash light to see the menu!
Have to make it back to this place! Everything was great. The meal wasn't cheap but it was well worth the expense.

Great ambiance, and great food! Came here with some friends that made a reservation(smart idea). Place was pretty packed, but the ambiance made it really cozy despite it being pretty tight! You might end up sitting here for a bit since the entire vibe is so chilled! Staff: Pretty friendly and helped us out with the menu! Food: I personally went with the 'Margherita Pizza.' It was pretty good nothing spectacular, but with the spicy oil it gave it a nice kick! The Uovo pizza was also a favorite at our table. Overall the pizza was good, just be prepared to share! Try it!

I was super excited to try Barbuzzo, and it was great as expected, but just shy of 5 stars for me.  I don't think you can go wrong w/ the 13th street corridor to which they have made a culinary focal point, and I would definitely try Barbuzzo again after I finally get to Lolita. NOTE:  Just received an email for their new upstairs space and it looks pretty rad..

Omg if your a foodie and love food this place is amazing!!! I will def be back I was in love with everything I got and the blood orange drink was also amazing!!!! Great service and an amazing atmosphere ... I have nothing negative to say ... It is a MUST that U eat here

Amazing Mediterranean food! The quality and flavors of every single dish will blow you away. What I particularly love about this place is the freshness of its ingredients and the combinations they make.  Definitely highly recommended looking for amazing, well-made food!

Short and skinny: Barbuzzo turns out a top-notch dining experience, from top to bottom. The good: 1. Food is fantastic. Started off with the sheep's milk ricotta-- was buttery and the balsamic/ olive oil dressing really complimented it nicely. Went with the Girasole pizza and Clams & Chorizo for our main dishes; the pizza had nice balance and flavor, though was really runny (only blip, and not sure why it was falling apart because the crust was perfection). The clams, well they deserve their own sentence: so, so, so good and served up in a heaping portion. Oh, and the dessert...the dessert... salted caramel budino. This was, bar none, the best dessert I have ever had. Just get it. We took an additional one to go (and considered stopping by for a couple more before heading back to NY-- we'll be back) 2. Decor was really interesting. Had a little farmhouse aesthetic going on with some barrel-themed light fixtures and big barn doors for contrast. Dig it. 3. Service was impeccable. Everyone was bringing their A-game. Waitress even took the time to have a 5-minute convo at the end of the meal to key us into Philly's nightlife (her recommendations did not disappoint, particularly the Ranstead Room and Franklin Mortgage & Investment Co.). The bad: 1. Nada. Not a blemish to be spoken of, excluding the pizza needing a little more crunch. The unexpected: 1. Clumsy me managed to spill a cocktail and a healthy portion of ice all over myself (turned bright red). Was promptly cleaned up and I ordered a beer. The waitress came back with a beer and... my previous drink, filled precisely to the point at which it was spilled. I was super impressed and taken back by that level of detail. Like I said-- service was impeccable.
Meh. But a slightly above average Meh. At least it's better than the places around city center.
Had a cheesesteak with the works.  Bun was awesome and the cheesesteak as a whole was really good. Fries were good as well.  Nice little place.
Everything I ate had a perfect taste. I took the filet mignon with fries, they were excelent and for desert i took the classic creme brulee and it was the best i've had in a long time.
Great food - little pricy but biggest issue was VERY LOUD - overly loud. Too hard to conduct a conversation. Had the Panzini- delish.

Sea Fire Grill is a fine upscale New York restaurant, with a good menu and wine list, excellent service, and very good fresh food.  While we had to stand waiting 15 minutes before we could be seated on a Thursday night, the staff were apologetic and the table was fine.  Nice ambiance to the restaurant.  The food was very good, but not exactly memorable.  Overall, a good experience, and a great place for an expense account dinner.

I am a frequent customer to the Sea Fire Grill with my father. We love the fresh seafood and apps! The staff is super friendly. The bartenders Ben and Madison are always so attentive. This place deserves five stars!
Really liked this place amazing apps, entrees are really good. It seemed like everyone at Seafire knew what they were doing from out waiter nick to management, only complaint it's pretty noisy.
The happy hour $1.50 oyster deal is amazing

Everything was pleasant, foods, service to atmosphere but nothing to excite about. Like most said, perfectly executed and decent thus not so exciting. My blackened trout with a guacamole sauce(?) and lightly seared tuna cubes were fun and fresh. Our memorable dish was Lobster Mac & Cheese. It was delicious. Macaroni was cooked perfectly al dente rather than too soft. The texture coming from the bread crumbs on the top made it even better. Our group didn't said anything bad about their dishes and what were exciting. The service was efficient. Our attentively smiling waiter that liked small talks without disturbing us was professional. I thought most of the servers were Italian with their accent. They thought us how to say thank you in their language "faleminderit". Is that Albanian?

I like the Happy Hour here. It's near home & has good $3 draft beers on tap, along with $5 glasses of house white or red wine & $5 house martinis like a Cosmo, Lemondrop, etc. It also boasts a delicious Cucumber martini. The small plates, which are available on the standard dinner menu, but half priced for smaller portions during Happy Hour, are delicious. My favorite is the Roasted Eggplant Timbale, which has sun-dried tomatoes,spinach, Alouette cheese, marinara & buffalo Mozzarella. Friends & I usually get about 3 plates of different small plates & share. It's a great way to get a little bit of everything . The people who frequent this Happy Hour are a friendly crowd. The bar staff are great & really helpful. What more could I ask for!

Stopped in here for dinner on a business trip with a colleague.  Waited for a space at the bar for a long time and then suddenly had the choice of 2 tables.  Weird, but happy to sit in a giant booth.  Had great cold beer on tap and a delicious goat cheese and pear pizza.  Would definitely would go again.  (Next time with a more adventurous diner who would order something more interesting to share - he got a margherita pizza which he said was great.)

I love this place, the food is great for being all vegetarian! Its a great and healthy option for lunch or dinner.  I have eaten more at the Rittenhouse location and frequently go to pickup a meal before work.  Their "chicken" ranch sandwich is great and hits the spot.  Definitely a recommendation for a quick meal or meal on the go that is healthy and incredibly tasty!

My new favorite place in University City! I went here twice today. Once for lunch, and once for dinner. Was not disappointed either time. This is a great place to go for fast vegan food. Whether you're a plant or meat eater, you will like this place. I saw a LOT of happy faces (and it was super crowded.) What I had: Quinoa chili (a special for the season) Pumpkin Shake (also a seasonal special) Ziggy Burger Udon Noodle Salad Green lemonade I LOVED my Ziggy burger. Whatever they put in that "special" sauce truly is special. I like the way they wrap the burgers up, so when you eat them nothing runs down your arm or gets messy. Not greasy in the least, just delicious and filling. The salad was also filling and is perfect for dinner - not too light, not too heavy. Just right. The service here is excellent. I even saw the owner for a bit making her rounds. They have desserts here! Brownies, shakes, cupcakes...didn't have any yet, but I'm sure I'll get around to it. The interior of this new location is beautiful. Lots of plants hanging on the wall, which I loved. Sure, it's busy, but it's a great place to eat. We never waited more than 8 minutes for our food despite how many people were in there, which was excellent. They are very organized here and seem to really have things together. I'm sure impressed. I also love that all of their plastic ware and packaging is compostable! The green lemonade was super tasty - there's kale in it. I would have never thought to put kale in lemonade before, but it was a good combination. Everything inside is clean, too. Oh, and it's great that the tomatoes were SO red and juicy! Lots of organic ingredients. This means the food is...ehhhh kinda pricy. A burger here is $8.50 and it doesn't come with fries. They're separate. It's kind of expensive to eat here, but you figure you're getting top quality ingredients so it's worth it. We picked up a side asian salad for my boyfriend's tortoise for dinner and she loved it, hahaha!

Found this relatively new place, thanks to you helpful Philly Yelpers, thanks! The place has a clean, simple look, with a long communal table in the middle and two seaters on each side. Step up to the counter to view the menu of vegetarian options, and the drinks menu is to the right of the cashier. The Udon Noodle Salad was good. It's seared spicy tofu chicken ("toficken"?) served with Udon noodles with Arugla. At first glance, I thought "I should get some Sriracha for this", but the toficken itself was seasoned well enough that no additional seasoning was needed! It was also probably the healthiest thing I ate on my weekend trip to Philly. I got a Carrot Ginger lemonade and wasn't wowed by it. I got kinda jealous of the people walking out with Green Smoothies "Groothies" and the "Five Dollar Shake" looked really good too. I love HipCityVeg and now this and the Rittenhouse Square location are on my radar for when I return!

I seriously love this place. My first time there was a week or so ago and I'm in love. The atmosphere there is really friendly and upbeat. Also, the employees there are super nice. They can answer and questions and if you're sitting down some even give you your food! Now on to the food. SO DELICIOUS!!! I got the buffalo bella and it was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. My friend got the chick'n fajita wrap and I tried it and that was also sooooo good! I also had the Asian side salad, which is also really good. I personally would have liked a tad bit more dressing, but i didn't bother to ask because I still loved it. For dessert we got banana whips. Awesome and refreshing.

This is my third try to pass the filter and get the good news out about Russet. I'll keep trying until I make it. Russet is that good!  Probably one of our top five meals in the last 35 years. My wife and I made different choices for each course and neither of us could decide whose was better. .For 1st course we had umbrian-style flatbread (surprisingly wonderful) and beet & blue cheese ravioli (who knew that combination could taste so good); for 2nd course suckling pork leg (too good to be true) and striped bass (cooked just right); for dessert chocolate ginger tart (you have to try this) and hazelnut praline mille-feuille (equally great).

Russet is where its at.  I have known of Andrew Wood and have had the fortune of tasting his food in the past.  My wife and I just celeberated our 5th wedding anniversay this past weekend and had a reservation for Sunday night that we highly inticipated.  In the past when I was over excited about something I leave dissapointed.  This was not the case. First of all BYO which I do not know for how long but its a great way to free up some money to order more FOOD. My wife started with the mortadella tortellini I could stop writing here.  It may be the best app I have every had.  So Savory and the pistachio gave it a perfect crucn. I had the stuffed cabbage.  Really cool combo of Shrimp and blood orange For Dinner My Wife went scallops and I braised beef shoulder.  Both fantastic. Tried three desserts (It was a special occasion) loved all three cinnamon ice cream stood out if I was made to pick one. Overall very cool concept, atmosphere and the chef is the man.

This place will make you feel like you've transported far out of East Hartford and into a sleek Manhattan lounge! How it opened in East Hartford is beyond me. I heard this was a new place to catch sports, so went for the World Cup. Man! Incredible experience. Food was quick and tasty, they have like literally 50 beers to choose from and so many different food items to choose from. I started snacking on the Parmesan Truffle fries which were so good that I actually ordered a Milano chicken panini (also with truffle fries) in addition. Back to the World Cup - this is definitely the place to come for sports they have this INSANE sound system that broadcasts the game live on a whole bunch of screens that the bartender told me are specifically designed for watching sports. The picture quality was amazing! I'm planning on being there this weekend for the World Cup finals and looking forward to another great experience!
Amazing Fresh Food! Beer Selection is outstanding. This will be my new go to spot. I had the Pizza and the Pasta was amazing you can tell its the real deal Will be back soon.

Awesome place! Saw a write-up in the local paper, and it's only a 5 minute drive from my house, so thought I would check it out. Not disappointed! The servers were very personable- shout outs to Sebastian and Judd. The focaccia bread that was brought to the table was fantastic. Our food was great as well- I had a southwest chicken wrap and the Mrs. had a chicken panini. Looking forward to going back to try out some of the more traditional Italian fare! Also, can't forget the delicious gelato that came with strawberry and a lemony biscotti which was a nice compliment to it. The presentation was also quite nice!

I've ordered from Nolita twice now on GrubHub.  Good delivery time and it is delicious.  As someone who works in Hartford, it doesn't always seem like there are a lot of good delivery choices.  Thank you Nolita for delivering to downtown Hartford.   I've had the Bowery Burger and Truffle Fries - delicious!  Can't wait to try more items!

Its awesome the food is great always fresh and new and the customer service is excellent the test is excellent and very good  pizza with excellent test and price. this is my third time visit and i recommended to all that dont scar due to the new place but i promise that you never disappointed once you try

OMG - This place blew us away!! We only tried it because I had a Living Social deal. (I mean, who wants to go to a restaurant you've never heard of attached to a hotel in East Hartford, of all places?) But boy, am I glad I did, because this is our new favorite restaurant! Fabulous soup, unbelievable foccacia, and homemade pappardelle bolognese to die for! We are going back next week for our anniversary. This chef is brilliant.

Went yesterday with a wedding party.  I have to say that it was one of the most pleasant time at a restaurant I have had in a long time.  The staff was quick to seat us, The server was funny, and the food was out of this world.  I had the seared scallops with truffle potato and it tasted so fresh.  The management stopped by the table to see if we enjoyed everything,  Great bar as well.  Do yourself a favor and try it out,  Few places still have what it takes but Nolita Restorante  has it.

Had the great pleasure of meeting David (chef) last night as my friend and I were sitting outside. Super friendly, loved talking about his Thanksgiving Balls and how people love to eat his balls. I only wish there wasn't as much focus on canned beer and more focus on a larger draft list. I will definitely be back! They still don't accept credit cards, so cash only for now

This is a fairly new establishment in Northern Liberties.  I stopped in the other day for food and drinks and was pleased with the experience.  It's primarily a beer bar (And they have a good selection of that.  Also, the people at the table next to me ordered canned beer and the can came with a nifty handle!), but I was in a wine mood and opted for that.  The wine was decent and reasonably priced, but keep in mind, it's not a wine bar, so no fancy stuff.  The food was excellent.  I ordered the lamb sliders and they were delicious.  Service was very good too.  When I mentioned that I had a dairy allergy, they were very reassuring and accommodating.  I will definitely be returning.

I was pretty stoked to check out the Blind Pig. I really was. I saw chorizo quesadillas on their menu and read a little about their Thanksgiving Balls and it was on. I grabbed a friend and made a spontaneous stop here after work. I honestly believe there is good here. Seriously. I was unfortunately denied it during this visit. We sat at the bar. Things started out okay. We got beers and the beginnings of some banter with the bartender. We ordered two apps, they arrived, we went to work. A party of four young men arrived and took residence at an adjacent part of the bar. The bartender went into salutation and introduction mode with the newly arrived party. His level of enthusiasm and vigor was notably greater than that with which he greeted us. Hmmm....It soon became apparent why. He had been expecting these fellows. They were there to meet and discuss business, the details of which I didn't particularly gain nor did I care to. From what little conversation was inescapably overheard, the genesis of some potential endeavor among the quintet was evident. Interested in a couple of entree orders for the night dear sir, or must I wave you down and beg? Ever notice the sound an empty can makes when it is set upon a solid surface? It's unmistakeable. Surely you'll ask me if I need another beer after fifteen minutes. No? Twenty maybe? From the moment those gentlemen arrived, we were essentially ignored for the remainder of our stay. I got the perfunctory "How is it?" when I was finishing my sandwich and itching to settle up and leave, but that was it. Enough harping for a moment: Location: Aces, of course. Outdoor seating. Inside: Looks great. Dark woods. Looks comfy and clean. I can attest to the presence of a baby-changing table in at least one of the two bathrooms. You don't see that every day. Beers: The can thing is alright, Percy Street pulls it off to a degree. I struggled a bit with my choices here, I'm not gonna lie. But hey, a couple of Sixpoints and a bevy of IPAs keeps most of the public happy, right? There was a really nice Brown Ale on tap. Good stuff. Food: The chorizo quesadillas were the best part of my meal. They were great. I would have (and should have) asked for a second order. Thanksgiving Balls? I'll give them an 'A' for creativity, but they're really no big deal. You can't really taste the turkey. It's more like a spherical knish than anything else. All potato. It's going to be one of those things people have to just say they've had it....like a Jim's steak. I had the Cubano sandwich. Eh. I've had so many mediocre Cuban sandwiches, what's one more? It wasn't bad, per se, but it wasn't great. It was solely perceived hunger and will which got me through the second half of it. My buddy had the lamb sliders. I didn't try them. They looked good. He said they were. All in all, the food was okay. You can readily find the equivalent in many other places. As I said earlier, I know there is good here, like Luke Skywalker gazing upon his sinister father with hope. I don't doubt some of the more positive reviews. The thing that killed it for us on this occasion was the service. I'm easy to please and I never expect to be treated like royalty, but bartender-dude totally fucked us. We finished our apps and were looking to order entrees and sat ignored. We had to excuse him from his conversation more than once to get beers. The kitchen signaled twice that our food was ready, someone else eventually wound up bringing it out. The bartender looked surprised when he saw us with our entrees with a body language and expression that read, "oh wow, I must have missed that..." (Yes, he was the one running food to the bar. He brought us our apps and the other bar-seated patrons their entrees.) All the while, he's less than four feet away from us making nice with his new friends. We didn't once get his name, nor he ours. I hope they're not pinning their success on those Thanksgiving Balls, I saw an awful lot of "Balls"-related merchandise for sale behind the bar. Lots of luck gentlemen and/or ladies. I realize we probably got the short end of the stick, but give enough people that kind of service and you truly are blind. How fattened this pig ever becomes we'll just wait and see. P.S. - The bill came handwritten on one of those pads like the ones waitresses use at a diner instead of on an itemized, computer-printed receipt. Odd. Whatever.....next!

Just outstanding! Dinner at Lucky Lou's was nothing short of an amazing experience. The staff was friendly and professional, the menu diverse and exciting, and you can't beat the beautiful Old Wethersfield location. We sat in the quaint bar for a few of the signature happy hour cocktails, then relaxed on the extensive and beautifully lit patio to enjoy what their menu had to offer. From the delicious calamari appetizer to the steak special (perfectly prepared and executed!) we were thrilled with the entire experience. In a word, we felt "pampered." Can't wait to go back and feel like a part of the Lucky Lou's family again! Thanks again to all who made our night so special :)

Another visit to Lucky Lou's. Food was spectacular, service was very attentive and our meal was delightful. The food is always full of flavor and great quality. Specials are always worth it! We had a great time with our family and the crowd was also great. Every time I visit this place the owner does such a great job making sure we're all happy and interacts with his customers. Great guy! I have recommended this place to many people even from the Fairfield county area. You must go!

It is more than just "being Lucky" when you dine out a "Lucky Lou's". The quaint and cozy ambiance, warm staff and incredible menu takes tremendous thought, talent and outstanding cuisines that puts this dining experience "over the top". We were escorted cheerfully into an enchanting room putting us immediately into a relaxed, warm state. Melissa, the friendly waitress, made you feel right at home..like you always knew her! She brought out delicious appetizers such as steak medallions and caprase on bread rounds that were mouth watering and delightful. I ordered the delicate steak pieces served over scrumptious garlic mashed potatoes in a mushroom sauce. It was one of the best meals I have ever had! My husband fully enjoyed his elegant salmon dish and everyone just moaned with delight over their selections! I would highly recommend this restaurant for an exceptional night out experience. Truly, one of the best places to be. I can't wait to visit Wethersfield, CN again! To thank our dear niece and hubby for this wonderful dinner treat, we sent them a gift certificate so that they may enjoy their own special night at Lucky Lou's! Still drooling! Lori G.

I really don't have enough good things to say about this place, but here's the short version of why Lucky Lou's is one of my favorite restaurants in the area. For starters, the food is amazing. I can really appreciate that just about everything on the menu is made from scratch, it really feels as if I'm eating a home cooked meal! I can't stand it when I'm dining out and, for example, my steak is noticeably one of those cuts of meat that have been frozen, thawed, grilled and delivered to me as my "meal". Not at Lucky Lou's. I've always been able to tell the difference between frozen or fresh meat and produce. I notice that the quality and freshness of the food they use is outstanding. Some of my favorites off the menu: (Appetizers) Dirty Wings, Spinach Artichoke Dip or their "Dips" (a variety of different dips from various parts of the world, served with fresh pita bread). (Entrees) Baked Stuffed Shrimp, The Russell burger, Stonington Sea Scallops, Chicken Arugula. I can't forget to mention that if you're looking for a great happy hour spot, their happy hour specials are definitely something worth checking out. I've brought friends, family and coworkers here, and I feel comfortable recommending this restaurant because I've never had anyone tell me I steered them wrong. The food is great, the staff are wonderful and to top it all off the establishment itself is gorgeous. I've come to a baby shower here, multiple work dinners and an engagement party. The owner and his staff always do a fabulous job making any event I attended a  great experience for all of the guests. All that being said, I definitely give this place 5 stars!

The first time we ate at Lucky Lou's, I wasn't a fan. While I loved the atmosphere (Old Wethersfield is such a charming place to enjoy outdoor seating!), every dish we ordered tasted "off" somehow. We went back a few months later and my faith in Lucky Lou's was restored! I ordered the soup of the day, the delicious bruschetta, some sort of espresso martini, and a cappuccino. I will definitely be back in the summertime for the atmosphere, the appetizers, and drinks with friends.
Pretty good happy hour, I got the taste of Colombia dish which was good. Would eat here again.
This is my fav happy hour place sun-wed happy hour all day thur-sat till 5 best service ever I love everyone here
It used to be good The food is decent but the service went to hell  arrogant, low class thugs now serve you Very disappointed long time customer Mike T

Came here for a late dinner and was very satisfied. Started with a mango pineapple margarita which was pretty good but then I had a coconut margarita OMG it was the best (I will be back for that) the sweet corn appetizer was yummy as well. I chose the plantain crusted chicken for an entree.. Lots of flavor no complaints... Our server Natasha was awesome went through a lot of popular items on the menu she was very nice... Overall great meal... I will be back next week!
The food here is ALWAYS amazing!!!!! Our server Natasha was AWESOME!!!! Great service!!!!!!

This place is a great hit for Latin cuisine, might I add it is located in Park Slope. I absolutely recommend this place for it's bandeja paisa, pollo de rellenos, and mango margaritas. Thumbs up! Great service.
Great drinks, food and service. I will definitely be back natasha is a great server and rook great care of my kids

Every time I come here, it is a great experience- friendliest, great spirited group of individuals I have ever come across. I am here quite often, but hey...if it ain't broke don't fix it. In my opinion, it is fairly easy to find a bar/restaurant with good drinks but consistency on the other hand is very rare. With that being said, Nicole, Miguel and Fred are five star bartenders. That is all... I will see myself out.

My boyfriend and I were in the mood for Latin food, so he suggested we check out Bogota Latin Bistro. That was the best restaurant choice he EVER made!! There was sooo much to choose from we couldn't decide. Our server, Denise T., helped out A LOT in that department! She was pleasant, attentive, and suggested the Arroz Con Pollo, Colombian Platter, and the Sangrita...and everything was AMAZING!! We will DEFINITELY BE BACK!!!
Great service from Doris, she was super friendly and helpful! The food was incredible--especially the goat cheese empanada and the arroz com pollo. Delicious mango margarita as well!

So, I had dinner with three friends on a Tuesday night. The fish tacos were great, very tasty. The frozen margaritas hit the spot on a 90 degree humid day, I had strawberry.  The banana bread pudding dessert was to die for; it had a great caramel sauce, enough for every bite. And we had the most engaging and amazing server, Natasha from BROOKLYN!, I can't wait to go back again. I might try the brunch here next time.

Ok. The first time I can't to bogota was a yr ago and I have been hooked ever since. I love this place. Great food, great service and most of all great environment. I've been to many places and this place definitely has amazing customer service. When it comes to the drinks they are the best. Miguel, Fred, Tyler and Nicole are the best behind the bar. They rock :-D

Had great drinks and a delicious steak empanada. Great service from a lovely bartender Nicole, who shares my hometown of Silver Spring, MD! She had great drink recommendations and let me try Aguardiente which was awesome! Overall great experience. Two thumbs up!

Went for brunch...Excellent food, fun, lively atmosphere, and generally authentic (with a few twists) Latin food (particularly Colombian). The bunuelos were tasty, but a bit hard on the outside for my taste. Whatever the dipping sauce was: nice. Colombian breakfast: yummy. All the components worked well together although the eggs were a tad dry. Migas de Arepa: Interesting combination, and so so so good. Definitely recommended if you want a hearty but not heavy brunch meal that's going to give you a variety of flavors.

Consistently great! I've been going to Bogota for several years now, and brunch, dinner or happy hour the food is always very tasty and affordable, the drinks are well composed and the service is great. Perhaps more importantly is that they have maintained a clean kitchen and an A health rating. You can't go wrong with the empanada sampler and skinny mojito. They make an awesome kale salad too. No it's not especially Colombian, but I'd say the dishes include a cross-section of South American and Caribbean flavors with some obligatory trendy stuff that is meant to appeal to hipsters and the health conscious. This place gets 5 stars for giving a good time and a great meal each and every time I've been there.

I absolutely love Bogota! I have dined here a few times over the past few years and it gets better every time! Every dish I have ordered is great. The last 2 dishes I ordered was the Paella and one of the specials, the Fried chicken. Both were delicious! The fried chicken was so crispy and juicy. You have to dip the chicken in the honey, it makes it so much better. I love the mojitos, I have to get one every time I go. Maragritas are also very good. Who can beat all day happy hour Monday - Wednesdays? We had Catleen as our server and she was awesome!! She was nice, attentive and friendly. We had a very late dinner so we had a chance to talk to Catleen since she didn't have a lot of other tables. She had us laughing the entire time! Over all I love this restaurant. I never have to wait long for a table or for my food. Food and drinks are always delicious. We definitely hope to be catching Catleen on another one of her shifts. She was a fantastic server and made dinner so much more enjoyable.

I finally was able to try Green Chicpea for lunch the other day. Im really and glad that they're on Halsey St. to bring variety and healthier options to the mix of restaurants in the area. Let's face it, the Mac and cheese and slammin' Caribbean food are great, I wish I could eat it everyday, but my metabolism isn't one of a 16 year old athlete. Im a visual person, so when I reviewed the menu a couple of times before going, I was a little overwhelmed. There were so many options, so much customization which I like, but it involves me knowing exactly what I like and I what I know first. Thankfully the actual ordering process when my coworkers and I got there was easy enough since everything was in sight. Naturally the foodie in me picked the platter; it has the most amount of options; plenty of things for me try and sample for my first experience. I got the falafel, spicy tabouli, hummus, and tomato cucumber salad. I had asked for the tahini sauce and the Harissa hot sauce on the side. With the platter came a whole pita too which I wasn't expecting. For $7.95 you can't beat it. Everything was fresh and flavorful. The Spicy Tabouli had some round heat from the diced jalapeños. The Falafel balls were crunchy on the exterior, soft and flavorful on the interior. The Harissa hot sauce and pita?!?! Phenomenal!  The freshest pita in my life; a minute before fully done, soft and pillow-y! The Harissa just a flavorful kick! You will definitely see a few more check-ins from me!

Great addition to Halsey Street. Family owned restaurant that has prior restaurant experience that did it right. Consistently great and fresh. Love the falafel pita sandwiches. It is kosher and has lots of vegetarian options.

me and my lady friend had bunna cafe food ..  as a vegan pop up.. we both agreed that food has a lot of heart in it and it was very very very good. and we decided to get more squishy sour pancake because it was so great to soak up the savory goodness. We had a wonderful time and we were both so pleased to have a vegan alternative that didn't try to be a meat product.. the servers that served us our food were not utterly incompetent ..

I've gotten food from them many times when they were a pop-up and have gone to their restaurant location once now too.  I would really like to support them b/c they are vegan (although the owners, apparently, are not even vegetarian, just making a buck off people eating veg*n in BK).  From the other reviews on here, it's clear that they have some supporters.  At the same time, a reality check is in order. Each and every time I have gotten food from them, the portions have been insultingly small.  I thought the portions were bad when they were a pop-up before, but my lunch there recently was even smaller.  At most, the 4-item plate was two tablespoons each of the 4 vegetables.  It was an appetizer at best.  Even in terms of flavor, they are 4 compared to 5 for Queen of Sheba and 4.5 for Awash.  My girlfriend confirms the portions are simply ridiculous, and she points out the extremely low cost of the ingredients used.  I also noticed they skimped on the heat because everyone eating there had their jackets on.  Guess it's all business.  Rather than looking to satisfy their veg brothers and sisters like a fellow veg*n might do, they are just regular business people looking to upsell while keeping costs low . If you want the "eshi" feeling they use to promote themselves, at least plan to get a "feast for two" all for yourself.

So yummy I could probably eat  a three person platter by myself. This is vegetarian, which incase you don't know means, there is no meat. Oh man it is so good who cares. Heads up the food can pack a kick (piquant). With the feast for 3 you get everything, you may want some extra injera (the spongy bread), we got some. There were three of us, and yes it's enough for three. We also shared an order of Lentil Sambusa, which tasted great, but the order could use a third piece (standard is two pieces). I actually ate the cilantro sauce, it was really hot, cause it had jalapeno. It was hot but refreshing, mmm. It was cold out, we had some Shai tea (yes Shai, like "If I ever fall in love"), instead of chai. Very delightful, raw/brown? sugar cubes provided, not needed, the cinnamon adds a nice sweet note. And finally we (3 of us) shared a dessert, I don't remember the name but it was something like a baklava with a coffee flavor. Interesting, but I'd focus on the not sweet food next time. Fantastic to have Bunna in one location so it can be enjoyed by many, many times over.

I was sad to see Mama Joys go but so so happy for Bunna to come in. They do a great lunch and dinner combo where you can get 4 (lunch) or 5( dinner) options all on one piece of injera bread. The seasonal special right now is a sweet pumpkin that is delicious. It's hard to pick a favorite hence I usually combo. There's a feast option too where you get to try all of them. It's a cute spot, everyone is really nice. I like to get take out and order a coffee to drink while I'm waiting. They roast the coffee in the restaurant and its a cool process. I really dig this place. If you come in a group it sometimes takes a while so I would order quickly and keep in mind you may be hanging out for 20-30 depending on the size of the order but it's a nice ambience to hang in. They play really good music too. I came in once just asking to buy some of the bread on it's own and the owner just gave it to me for free. I had to hassle him to tip him for it. Really great place.
the only cuban restaurant in little old kearney :) great food tho i love their empanadas.

A great new addition to the Bed-Stuy/Clinton Hill Neighborhood. Daily specials including traditional handmade gnocchi and homemade Lasagna. Great presentation, great Traditional Italian food done Right! Their regular menu features a modest variety of Crosstini, Antipasti, and Insalate. Good for vegetarians; I recommend the Bruschetta and the cheese plate! The prices are just right, you cannot find a better deal in Brooklyn for homemade Traditional Italian food, made Fresh! The decor is rustic and warm. Full of Southern Italian charm (as the name suggests, SUD means south in Italian). Staff is Italian too! The storefront is subtle... A true diamond in the rough.

Last night I went to SUD with a couple of friends, what a treat!  The Lasagna with pork ragu was delightful and the Lasagna with vegetables & bechamel was to die for.  Also the homemade gnocchi with walnut and pesto was the best we had ever had.  The best tiramisu ever!  BYOB.

SUD = fantastic! First of all, I have to say, freakin a gnocchis.  THE BEST GNOCCHI I have ever had in my life (don't tell my dad), and I grew up eating gnocchis (a gnocchi connoisseur if you will).  They were incredibly soft and melted in your mouth.  Also, the sauce was a gorgonzola cream sauce, so it had just enough punch, but didn't overwhelm the pasta.  So delicious. We also got the cheese plate, which was very well done.  They gave us three different cheeses and each was paired with something that complimented it well. The interior is beautiful - warm, dimmed, exposed bulbs, and a few, interesting chachkis.  It says, "Hey!  I'm an Italian restaurant, and I don't need to put Italian crap all over the place to make the diners realize it, because they aren't stupid, and they can remember where they are eating". Understandable that they don't have their wine license yet, BYOB is a nice substitution.  Free, never ending bread, as well as free olives, and complimentary ice cream because they lacked a desert list.  Really friendly, sweet service.   The only reason it doesn't get 5 stars yet is that at the end of the dinner, they forgot about us and all the other customers, and never brought anyone their checks.  We all had to ask.  I didn't mind the extra time at the table, but some of the other patrons looked cranky .  So it's sorta the service's fault, but I'm more upset at the stupid snobby-looking hipsters that were annoying me with their crankiness, sitting at the table across from us. EAT HERE.

Had dinner at Sud. Cozy ambience and helpful nice staff. Gnocchi were fabolous, light and fluffy, cooked to perfection. Next time I want to try the lasagna: it looked beautiful and smelled so goood! Remember: BYOB for now.

Sud is a great find worth looking for.  The food is authentic Italian with homemade pasta and homemade sauces.  I've been there twice and had the ragu lasagna both times because it is so delicious.  Tried the other dishes from friends I was with and enjoyed all of them.  The atmosphere is soft and relaxing.  The Tiramisu, my favorite dessert, is wonderful.  Is there ever such a thing as "too rich?"
The burgers,soup, desert's and service were absolutely top shelf.! We had a delightful experience.!! Very reasonable, you just can't go wrong. We will certainly be back.
amazing, inventive food, great personable staff and beautiful decor.  Will definitely bring my friends back!

I am trying not to start my review with WOW, so K-Bang.  I am usually one for not stepping outside the box but the food was outstanding!  The lamb, rabbit (oh so yummy) and desert were a reason for me to go back again.   Service was great, the were prompt but not overbearing and it made for a very nice relaxed evening.  But go there for AMAZING food. There was not a dish, and we order a lot of them (party of 7) and did not have a single one that was not eaten down to the glazing on the dishes.

Just got back from this hidden spot, which was highly recommended by some friends.  The dishes are thoughtfully composed and tasty.  No complaints except for the damn hipster service.  The host was especially great upon entry, but the waitress just stopped coming to our table.  To the point that a different server had to stand in and offer us desert/check.  She just kicked back and texted all night.   New code to live by...hipster service = reduced tip.

Pretty decent local bar right off of Main Street, Sharky's is set up well with a ring of flat panels around the main dining area for easy sports viewing.  The food options are the definition of bar standards, including pretty good wings - definitely not the place to get a salad probably. Beer options are pretty generic, with the craftiest option being Cricket Hill East Coast Lager.  The place itself is pretty bright and looks a lot nicer on the inside than on the outside, don't let that deceive you. Keep a look out for the monkey - when you see it, you'll hit yourself for not seeing it immediately.

We, my family of 4, gave Sharkey's two tries.  Once when they first opened and once this week.  The first time they didn't even put my daughter's cheese burger order in.  So she go no food on that visit except what we gave her from our plates.  The food was blah at best. The second and most recent time they messed up two of our 4 meals.  Upon returning with corrected meals the food on the plate was a mix of over cooked and cold.  We've eaten burgers and fillet mignon sliders and sandwiches and chicken wings, frankly I'm afraid to order any fish.   It does smell of cleaner when you walk in the door.  There are hardly any people in there at lunch time and I can see why.  Not a good value for the money.  There are better places to eat in Boonton.  We tried to give you the benefit of of the doubt, but you haven't improved.

WOWZA!!! Went here last night with my boyfriend. It was the last night of a valid coupon I received in the mail. We were seated pretty promptly, we ordered drinks right away. They are not skimpy with the alcohol, however... they were pricey drinks. We were astonished at the many options on the menu.. there is something for everyone on there. We opted to go with the coupon for the "clambake". It is a Wednesday special every week for 25.95, but with our coupon it was 19.99. SO  WORTH THE MONEY!!! We started with a "sharky-tizer" called fire cracker calamari. The portion was large and delicious. Spicy....lots of sauce on it, my only complaint was that some of the rings were a bit chewy.. but not enough to mar my opinion... delish. The entree came out a bit quickly for my liking. However, we managed. Because the offer was so good, we ordered two clambakes... one is definitely sufficient to share amongst 2 people. The clambake contains: 1 1/4 lobster, 1 lb of king crab legs, 1/4 pound (6+) pretty large shrimp that were very easy to peel as they sliced and de-veined the bugger before it arrives to your table, 1 dozen steamers, some mussels, a small chunk of corn and baked potato. This amazing large wooden bowl is accompanied by a large white vat of delicious butter and a small, very small amount of cocktail sauce that tasted more like a bloody mary. Really delicious... We didn't eat all of our seafood as WOW it was a lot of food, so we did not order coffee drinks or dessert, but they had some awesome options. Atmosphere is a little loud and on Wednesday they have karaoke in the main dining room... it was too loud and annoying. We had to keep asking them to turn down the speakers as there were maybe 20 people in the whole place and we were sat right under the speaker, which came in about 15 minutes after we were sat. Definitely will be back though, tonight... leftovers.... surf and turf. ENJOY!

Sharkey's in booton is a great place to watch a game and eat some wings with friends.  Lively atmosphere and plenty of TV's.  Their wings are by far the best I have ever eaten.  I highly recommend the blackened wings.  I also like how they serve blue cheese stuffed olives with their martinis.  Not the classiest place but overall a fun time.  Will definately go again.

Cute little place with reasonable prices! I highly recommend their Thai entrees (the shrimp curry and pad Thai were great!) but I wasn't too blown away by their sushi/sashimi (I had the lunch special). Good place for a quick, tasty lunch!

First off, because my theory is that half the guys on here are just looking for decent date spots, this is an excellent first date spot. It's very small, it's not loud, and it's relatively classy at a very decent price; if you're like me and worry more about first-date logistics than the date itself, this is perfect. Plus, not that this is news, but girls love sushi. And you can get a big plate and share it with her, and it's a whole thing, and there are plenty of bars around so it's a solid jump-off point. Duh. Moving on. Only four stars because the sushi is good, not great - agree with other reviews saying the simpler, cheaper rolls are better than the specialty selection. Service is excellent, and ignore earlier reviews mentioning BYOB - you can get beer and wine there now. Looking forward to going back!

I went here with my brother and a friend on a whim because we were at Top Hops around the corner and wanted a place to bring out newly filled growlers of beer. Not only is this place BYO (a rarity in this city), but their happy hour is amazing. We arrived around 6 on a Friday and place was pretty quiet. We ordered a bunch of rolls from their happy hour specials and a plate of sashimi with rice (only $19 for 18 pieces!!) and the bill was only $56. It was more than enough for me and two guys. The food was fresh and the service was great. We will be back!

My favorite thing about Zest was the ambience. It's small and cozy but it doesn't feel cramped or overcrowded. I suggest making a reservation though because they seem to give priority to those who have reservations. The sushi is good and the staff is friendly. The Happy Hour menu is definitely worth checking out--everything (appetizers, sushi, drinks) is only $3. Even when it's not Happy Hour, the prices are reasonable. Your wallet won't feel a thing.
My friend and I each brought a bottle of wine and each drank a bottle of wine.  The Snow Mountain sushi was awesome.

Good sushi (I enjoyed the mixed veggie roll and california rolls) and attentive service. If you check in here on Yelp, you can get a free bowl of edamame. Economical prices! The $6 sake was bigger than we expected and was tasty!

This was my 2nd visit to Euro Lounge. My first time there I was charged a ridiculous $10 cover, but this time there wasn't one so I'm adding a star just for that.  It's ultimately a diner with a dancefloor, so I really don't know where they get off charging a cover - especially $10. I mean, if they really need to charge one to make $ then make it $5. It's literally a restaurant with a bar/dancefloor area in the back. People were still sitting down having dinner in the restaurant area at 11pm when we got there, which I found a little odd, but whatever.   Anyway, it's not the best club (diner with a dancefloor) you'll find, but it does the trick if you just want to stay local, have some drinks and listen to music/dance. It also helps if you're with a fun group of people. If not you'll probably have a miserable time. Just watching the regulars that go here (I'm assuming they're regulars) is a good time in itself. It's a very mixed crowd of guido guys in super tight Affliction-esque t-shirts, Latina's wearing super tight cocktail dresses who shouldn't be wearing super tight anything, slutty drunk white girls also in super tight dresses and old men.  My favorite was the man who had to be in his late 60's/early 70's in the droopy pleated khakis and wife beater busting out moves on the dancefloor like nothing I have ever seen. He provided much needed entertainment for the night for my friends and I, so that was much appreciated. The drinks weren't overly expensive, but weren't cheap either. The bartender was making them pretty strong, so they were well worth the money. Is this the best place? No, not at all. Would I go back? Yes, I sure would (if there wasn't a cover).

Great food! Especially the big fish for two, the pink snapper is very tasty and fresh and the lamb chops are delicious. Generous portions. Pleasant atmosphere and the waiters are very attentive and friendly. If your looking for great Greek food this is the place to go.

I love this place!!! First if all bc food is so yummy and sending of all its not to far n everyone loves it.  I love gyros, I feel like instead of eating road size food,  this restaurant provides high quality,  clean n healthy food. Everytime I go here I try doesn't variety of good. Ones I got gyros or chicken pita sandwich, salad wIth gyri or chicken etc. I m betty picky about meat. I dont like chewy meat but this restaurant makes it perfect.  Their shredded gyro are awesome,  soft n yummy, tasty,  delicious that you won't stop eating.   I remember I went to the ones in hoboken n hated the meat. It was cherry n grosser but in its greek to me in Clifton they make it perfect everything's.   Overall service was good too. Waiter came too take out pretty,  have us change back.. and ask if hows everything going or wee need something else. I think ill deff go back again. Unlike some other restaurant I would live to go here:)

The minute I step into the joint I am already greeted with a free sausage sample. The place smells like sausage, onions, and pure awesomeness. Everyone there is friendly and accommodating. It's a great place to get a quick, 1400 calorie lunch. Weeeeeee!

I would have never known that there was anything here besides a WalMart and Home Depot if Nando F didn't tell me about this must try italian sausage vendor here. It only took me a day to make my way here to try it for myself. Since I'm a big sausage parm sandwich fan, making this place my first meal of the day was an easy choice. There was only one other person there besides myself, so the service was really quick, and the person making what was ordered was talkative and friendly. While i was deciding what to order, without asking he cut a 2" piece of sweet sausage and handed it to me on a toothpick to try. If i wasn't sure by then, it was a good way to help me decide. With all types of sandwiches on the menu, and bacon on the grill, i went with a mix of hot and sweet sausage with spicy mustard and grilled onions/peppers. A huge sandwich, hot, served on a seriously good roll. The sandwich combo came with a bag of chips and a can of soda for $8.50. I can't say enough about how good this sandwich was. Grilled perfectly and it had more than enough onions and peppers on it. So good that I'm trying to figure out how to conveniently make my way here next week. The fact that one of his soda choices was one of my favorites but rarely found Fresca has me looking forward to my next meal here.

Best Thai food this side of the pacific and the best I've had outside of Thailand.    We've been going here for years and have never been disappointed.  The food is delicious, it's one of the few restaurants that will actually prepare a spicy meal on request, and it's a BYO, what else do you need?  Just be warned, even their "mild" dishes are fairly spicy and their "Thai spicy" is the spiciest food I've ever had at a restaurant in this country. The restaurant is a very casual dine-in restaurant with prompt service and a relaxed atmosphere.   My only regret is that I finished my meal and now have to sit by as my wife enjoys her amazing leftovers.

I travel a lot for work and I try Thai any where I can find it. Sometimes I get lucky and its pretty good. Sometimes I get home and have to go right to Mie Thai to make the world right again. The spice levels are not for the novice. All you need to say is mild and you're good to go. I've gone up and down the menu here and its just amazing. Try this place and I'm certain you will be quite happy.

OK so I was going to go for Korean BBQ tonight, but opted for some Good Ole American BBQ.  Its  was a Sunday night around 7:00pm.  The place was packed and I was worried we weren't going to get a seat.    No Worries though you walk in through the courtyard and into the dining room.   Where you wait in line to order your BBQ by the pound at the counter.   The wait wasn't long bout 5 minutes or so. The BBQ meats are  kept in the hot display case at the counter.  They were offering Brisket, Short ribs on the Bone, Pulled Pork, Sausage, Ribs, Pork Belly, & Chicken.   I went for a 1/2 pound of brisket, 1/2 pound of pork belly, 1 sausage link, 2 short ribs, and went for a side of Baked Beans and potato Salad.   People's palettes are different from one to another.  I enjoy my Brisket on the fatty and juicy side and this brisket did not disappoint, so tender and juicy, just how I like it.  If you prefer a leaner cut, just ask the meat carver to get you a leaner cut of brisket. The Short ribs were first class ultra tender and were falling off the bone.  The sausage link was alright nothing that blew me out of the water.   The Show Stopper was the Pork Belly which was like tasting heaven.  The flavor bomb with each bite was out of this world.    The pork belly was very fatty and the rub on it amplified it to another level. The potato salad was perfect and dressed in a tart mustard vinegar base.  The beans were tasty also with a hint of burnt ends from the brisket and the beans were AL dente.   They did have a broccoli  salad I will have to try next time.  After you get your order you seat yourself and grab your silverware at the water station.  They use real forks and knives so this adds a little class to the dining experience.   Your food is served on sheet trays with a parchment paper lining.  I wish they labeled their BBQ sauce they have 3 sauces, Vinegar, House, and Spicy.  Vinegar I'm sure had some apple cider vinegar base to it.  House BBQ sauce was tart and tangy, Ketchup base I'm sure with some brown sugar or molasses.  The spicy sauce was a different it didn't have a good viscosity to it, very thick like a Oriental Hoisin sauce and it wasn't spicy at all.   The service was attentive they have a bus person roaming and they come to your table to clear the table for you.  We saw our bus person like 4 times during the dinner.   My friend was upset that the BBQ was $76.00 between the 2 of us.  He was paying so he was shocked to see such a high price for BBQ.  Note they use Black Angus Beef, Berkshire Pork, Duroc Pork, and they source out meats that are free of hormones and antibiotics.   Put into consideration it's a Steve Starr Restaurant your going to pay for quality.  BBQ is a food that should be savored once in a while.  Not every week it's too rich of a food group to do that. I used to work in a BBQ joint as a cook & manager so the BBQ stacked up pretty good.   I had a chance to speak  to Joe C. the owner after dinner.    We talked bout the woods he uses to smoke his meats.  He uses oak which burns hard and longer and mixes in some fruit woods to balance out the smoke.  Very cool and laid back guy and he was down from Brooklyn for the week to make sure everything was on point.   If I were to come back I would just do a slice of this and a slice of that.  The music  they were playing was modern and had a good hipster vibe to it.  The ambiance was very industrial farmhouse chic.

Well, this is absolutely a great addition to the neighborhood. The feel of this place was great. It was casual with open outdoor space yet it still feel cozy. I went with some BBQ lovers so lucky for me, I had the opportunity to sample a lot. I think my favorite had to be the pork ribs. They were juicy on the inside with a killer crust of flavor on the outside. I totally loved these. Second, the pork belly. This was great. It was fatty and cooked perfectly but not too fatty. Third, the hot Italian sausage. Wow, I loved this one. Hot and juicy and snapped when you cut it! My only semi disappointment was the pulled pork. I really liked it but it wasn't the best I've ever had. That being said, I would definitely order it again, it would just come further down on my list. With any great BBQ place, comes lots of sauces and these sauces were also delicious. Half way through, I found my perfect blend of sauces, a little of their BBQ sauce, mixed with some sort of liquid smokey sauce. Excellent. It came out to be a perfect smokey/sweet sauce of tastiness. Can't wait to get back!

Believe it. I have been a couple times, although a couple of meats have been perfect one trip and just okay on another (pork belly and brisket), the pulled pork has been spot on, and the short rib is a thing of beauty. Get your Fred Flintstone on and go try this place. Don't forget, you don't have to order a whole pound, so take 1/4 lb tastes of things or share with friends. Don't miss the beer and whiskey either.

I am only giving Fette Sau one star for the atmosphere. My boyfriend and I walked in and were impressed and could not wait to eat and dig in but as soon as we walked up to the amusement park style roped off line to order our meals, our smiles started to turn down. We were looking at the board (which seems to be the latest corny trend in all the new places in Fishtown) and the guy behind the counter rudely said, "Are you going to order or what?" So we kind of felt rush even low no one else was in line. The female cashier kind of had an attitude, too and only smiled when she handed over our credit card slip to sign. I looked down and noticed a huge tip jar. It made me feel like I was at Dunkin Donuts but at least they are polite and do not rush you. So, with the cafeteria tray in hand, I went to the bar to get 2 glasses of wine and stood waiting for at least minutes as the bartender talked to friends. (there was only about 10 people at the bar and I was ignored by both bartenders) Meanwhile, my boyfriend had to go collect paper plates and utensils. Luckily they weren't busy, but my thought was "What if there were no open tables? Where do we go with our trays?" Then we started to eat and didn't finish anything, except for the wine. The chicken and brisket were dry so we tried adding the sauce which didn't improve the taste. So we tried our sides, potato salad, sauerkraut and baked beans and I wasn't impressed with any of them but I was especially disappointed in the baked beans. They were extremely spicy and I can not do spicy, I literally had an allergic reaction the next day, it was horrible. Maybe I am just use to my family's real German cooking. We left hungry and we both felt sick. I hope this place changes. I love Steven Starr, I have always enjoyed all of his other establishments but I just don't understand why his people are handling his places differently in Fishtown; why do they not have servers? We only spent $75 but when I go out for dinner, I am sorry but I do not want to get up to get another paper plate or drinks at the bar. I believe it is extremely tacky and I hope they figure it out.

I really don't get some of the reviews.  The food and service are great, all while being one of Steven Starr's most reasonably priced establishments.  A quarter pound of brisket, sausage, broccoli salad, and ginger ale only cost $14!   The guy cutting the brisket was nice enough to ask what kind of cut I wanted(an end or middle), and the cashier explained everything on their menu and was very nice.   The brisket was perfectly cooked.  The sausage was good, but not my personal taste.  The broccoli salad was really good.  Can't wait to go back.  I wish they were open during weekdays for lunch since I live across the street!

I loved the space, the concept, the communal tables, the outdoor heat lamps but the food left something to be desired. I did not like any of the three BBQ sauce options. I really actually hated one of them. And that's hard to do to a sauce lover like myself. The meats also were a 3/5 for BBQ standards. The ribs were no good and I heard the same about the brisket. The chicken, sausage and pulled pork were all fine. The pulled pork was really enhanced by the vinegar sauce. I think that I might like it more as drunk food so perhaps I'll put this on the end-of-the-night list in the future. In fact, that's the reason why I didn't give it a 2.  Maybe they should consider staying open past 12 on Fridays and Saturdays.

We went to Fette Sau  for dinner this weekend for my boyfriend's birthday.  We had a great time and loved it!  The meats were so delicious and I'm usually disappointed in baked beans at BBQ joints...but these didn't disappoint and were so filling!  The pork ribs and pork belly were amazing, but this place is pricey so be prepared.   We loved the atmosphere, I had one of the cocktails at the bar and it was really tasty!  Everyone was really nice and I have absolutely no complaints.  I'll definitely be back.

I'm consistently satisfied when I come here. Great food at very reasonable prices. Wait staff is terrific.  Favorite dish is the tilapia. Only neg is the food comes out slow, but why be in a rush all the time anyway.
love the fresh food - awesome service and what a nice looking place! will be back and will tell my friends! I like the breakfast menu and the fruit and veggies aren't canned, thank god.

I had dinner at Parker & Quinn for the second time last week and it was a great time again. The service is attentive without being too pushy, they were friendly and gave us plenty of time to mull over the menu. The food came out SO quick, I was quite impressed because it was executed to perfection. Although the wine list is not the most extensive we enjoyed the wines we selected, a Cabernet and a Malbec.  We had the tagliatelle with lamb ragu- I don't like lamb but I loved this pasta dish; beef meatballs - they were tasty but firmer than how I'd like mine prepared; steak, broccoli rabe, and mashed potatoes were all great. Our servers were wonderful, George was funny and made a wonderful recommendation for dessert - the salted caramel cheese cake- delicious! If you're a cheese cake fan do not pass on this treat. This is a wonderful place with a lively scene, delicious food and top notch service. There is also a beautiful roof top for those summer nights- definitely visit the Refinery Rooftop in the warmer months. Will be back!

The food was great, served piping hot by an attentive waitstaff, and it's located inside a very nice hotel, with which it has shared restrooms. They are nicely finished. Good perk. The wine and beer selection is strong and the interior decor and furnishings carefully appointed.

The restaurant is quite well decorated with a very warm atmosphere. The service is not as prompt but once they see you they're quite nice and knowledgeable. Most importantly, the food is great, no complains at all. As far as the menu goes, we were there for brunch and you cold find the usual items for an American brunch, although there was too many variants of the steak & eggs. A bit more variety would have been appreciated. This is also a restaurant that can easily accommodate children , although there were less high chairs then we expected but we could all fit in a booth. Overall, great experience, strongly recommend it and we'll definitely return!

Stumbled upon P&Q walking through Refinery Hotel. This place is clearly bumpin' on the weekend which is always the greenlight for me when I'm scoping out the city! Large order of pappardelle- mushrooms porcini, cooked with white wine/herb/garlic. The size of the small order could be considered a side, so if you're looking to make this a meal, size up kid! The table next to us ordered a bunch of sandwiches and fries- couldn't stop my salivation. The fries are awesome and I highly recommend getting some to share. Between the pasta, hanger steak (two thumbs up!) and fries, we were stuffed. The menu is American fare of much-better-than-average comfort food. The staff is very busy but it's the friendliest service I can remember when visiting the city! The whole atmosphere of the restaurant is cool: the hip portraits and lighting help make the most of this space!

After an extensive Yelp search in our hotel on the raining Saturday evening this past weekend, my husband and I decided on Parker & Quinn. The decor paired with the set up of the high top tables and round booths gave us a good impression of what was ahead. The drinks were delightfully prepared, refreshing (old fashion and fleur de lis), and paired well with the lamb meatballs which were nothing short of delectable. For our meals, my husband chose the short ribs that were accompanied by root vegetables and mashed potatoes and I ordered the quinoa salad with a hanger steak. After our food arrived, I quickly took one bite as I was so eager to try the beautifully presented plate. The words out of my mouth were, "This is one of the best things I've ever tasted." My husband was just as satisfied with his meal as well. My hanger steak, cooked well, was still juicy, tender, and could be sliced with a butter knife. I made sure not to leave a speck on my plate and would have licked it clean had that been appropriate at the time. My list of "Best Meals I've Ever Consumed" is now a short, yet well-deserved, list of two (P&Q accompanied by Kimo's in Maui). My husband and I left there completely satisfied with everything from the atmosphere, wait staff, managers, and, most definitely, the food. Although we won't be able to visit as often as we'd like, we're not too far away in Boston and will make Parker & Quinn a must-visit whenever we're in the city.
I love this place! i've been here a bunch of times and everything on the menu is delicious! all the ceviches are off da hook!

Lamb Shanks were bland, fatty and gross. Apple Crisp was raw.... like not fully baked. I gagged literally. Seafood dish ws pretty good, but they put these vinegar onions all over it that made it soggy. the point of deep frying and breading is for it to have that texture. Why ruin it by making it soggy. Altogether after spending $80, I actually ate maybe a fifth of the food I purchased. The yellow plantains and the rice. The read was unedible. No wonder the place was a ghost town when I walked in. I would suggest you walk around. In park slope there is too much to choose from to overpay for nasty food.

Surfish brought back memories. College study abroad, getting tipsy before technically legal memories that made me "WOW" at the power of its remarkable food.
