The shy-girl pleasant service that I experienced here wasn't bad either. But eating in a backyard with not-so-comfy seating didn't do much for my appreciation of the ambience. I kept thinking during the meal that perhaps one day I'll make it back to Perú, to visit my host family. But if I don't, at least I can save the airfare, while I reminisce over the sometimes elegant tapas at Surfish. Fried oysters with tuna were deliciously moist and flavorful in every bite. Ceviche mixto was everything I expected and even tastier: tart and oniony. Even the plantains and homemade tortilla chips served with an amazing yellow sauce reminded me of an authentic home cooked meal.  Especially the sauce!

First off very long wait.. Very tight spaces .. They pick up the phone and have you waiting 15 to never answer at all for reservations .. Food was overall good .. Cerviche sampler amazing .. paella was below average .. Very upset about that.. But in general good experience .. Not a romantic spot..

I've been on a great dining streak lately and Surfish Peruvian Bistro continues the (hopefully) ongoing trend. I haven't eaten a lot of Peruvian food so I can't vouch for the authenticity of the dishes, but if this is what Peruvian food tastes like I will certainly make it a mission to try more. We celebrated Father's day a day early with lunch at this restaurant. There was a little hiccup with the brunch menu not being available. No worries though, since our meal was very good. Instead, we ordered a bunch of plates off the tapas menu. Crispy oysters, beet salad, mahi taquitos, chicharron sliders, shrimp tamale, ribs ... if it sounds like a lot of food that's cause it was. I left the restaurant ready for a food coma. My favorites of the day were the crispy oysters and the chicharron sliders. Both were absolutely delicious. The ribs were my least favorite. The meat was very tender but didn't pack the punch of flavor I was hoping for. Also worth mentioning is the house made drink of purple corn (I can't find the name on their menu). It's a sweet drink that is similar to sangria but with the warm spice of cinnamon and no alcohol. Well at least I'm pretty sure there's no alcohol - it was hard to get an answer from the waitstaff. One waitress couldn't say. Finally our waitress confirmed that there was no alcohol.   Dessert was equally delicious. The chocolate souffle was amazing and had a warm chocolate sauce in the center. It also came with some ice cream studded with peanuts.--- simple touches like this can make a meal go from good to great. All in all Surfish went on the list of places to revisit soon.

Great, creative options. I absolutely love this place. Their rolls are so delicious and filling, and the price isn't too bad. BYOB too, so you can't go wrong with that. The owner is really kind, and he's happy to give recommendations if needed.

Want a totally weird sushi place. Bam!  this is it. What to expect: not enough wasabi, and a charge for $1 for more wasabi a waitress that forgets your edamame and then your soup salmon rolls that may not be salmon, unclear to me still The good: BYOB fin

I used to love their food, where they were located on Bay Ave, right next Brookside Park.  But now, there is always a Dissapointing factor, every time i order from them. Normally i order the "Linguini Garlic & Oil", which is always good, but i always have to mention in the comment section: "make sure the sauce does not leak".  When i don't make that suggestion, the bag is always soaked in oil.  One time i choose to add Brocoli to the dish, & noticed there was a a lot of water in the container.  So it is obvious that the cook did not strain the brocoli before adding it to the pasta.  Because as we all know: "Oil & Water don't mix".  Then today i ordered "Rigatoni Bolognese", but the pasta's texture was pasty, under-cooked. Just reminds me, "why did give them another chance", & the pizza isn't so great either.

I have been ordering from here for about 2+ years and sad to say it has consistently gotten worse. Dine in is fine. Ordering for delivery is a problem, food is sometimes cold/soggy. They got my order wrong once and I called (nicely) and the man at the front desk caught an attitude with me. I went in the other night (placed the order for pick up) and the nice girl asked me if I wanted anything else. I did, and the guy at front desk glared at me like I just ruined his life. If you want to dine in, go for it, although there are better italian places around here. For take out, only do it under desperate situations and take a 50/50 chance that it will come late, cold or wrong altogether.

I have never written a review about any place but this place really ticked me off with their service.  Let me just Say NEVER CALL and ORDER HERE. Now I have only been here once before.  I called to make an order; a lady who spoke good English picked up and handed the phone to a guy who could barely speak English.  I told him what I wanted and I ask him to repeat so I know he got he says "yes Yes" and hangs up.  So I go there as soon as I can since I was on my lunch break, so when I get there to pick it up, everything that I got was wrong.  They wasted half an hour and they still get it wrong two more times while I am there.  So decided to leave and the owner runs towards me and tells me sorry and I will give you free food.  Well so I wait another half hour and she gives me Thai iced tea for free and I ended up paying for rest.  She says I meant free iced tea.  I don't mind paying; just give me what I ordered. I don't understand why they are in business if they can't speak English.  Be careful when you decide to make an order here.  I would never wish this kind of experience on anyone.

I have dined at Stone Hearth 3 times now- we are from Westville and frequent the restaurants there- and I must say it's got some room for improvement.  It's not totally bad but there are a few suggestions they need to heed before we become regulars: 1.  The Staff- many of the wait staff and the bartender seem either socially inept or are feining a snootiness that doesnt sit well with my family or friends.  You dont have to tell me your life story, but dont be a stepford wife (robot) either. 2.  The portions are smallish, but that's fine.  I think the pricing is a bit steeper than it should be for the size and taste of the food. 3. Drink prices arent cheap so dont go there if you intend on having a few w your dinner or 2 of you will be well over $100. 4. The so-called tables for 2 (there are 2 or 3 of them) in the dining area are not suitable for normal sized adults. Very cramped and uncomfortable, especially for the price you're paying.  When i remarked to the waitress about it, she did not offer another table, though many were open. 5. Lastly, the Manager seems nice but in 3 trips there for dinner, he's never come over to see how everything was, etc which to me is a major mistake in a new restaurant. We havent given up yet on Stone Hearth  but we will think twice before bringing other famliy and friends there.

I'm surprised at the negative comments. I too have been to Stone Hearth 3 times. I've found the waitstaff extremely friendly and especially warm to children. The Thai slaw salad is great, as us the trout and pizzas. Butterscotch pudding is amazing. My kids now ask to go. Nice wine list. Service is a bit slow but I chalk that up to working through the opening weeks.

Ate here tonight and thought everything was fantastic. The menu was creative, extensive, and I thought the portions were more than satisfying. The atmosphere was inviting and the space was well planned. I will continue to eat here often and plan to tell others to do the same! I think it's a much needed addition to the westville village.

This place is pretty good. The modern style layout makes for a nice ambiance. & their menu has a great variety of selections, a lot of which are health-conscious. I especially love the paleo options. All of the salads sounded awesome, I couldn't even decide on one. But my friend got the shredded cabbage with cashews and scallions in a spicy Thai peanut sauce & added grilled chicken (which she said was awesome- juicy and flavorful- perfect for a salad topper). Her only complaint was that it could have had more dressing. (She is known to put extra dressing on her salads so it may be just enough for some of you). She also got the butternut squash soup which could have been thicker (that's what she said ;-) lol) but no really, it was a little too watery and needed some added salt & pepper for flavor. The Caprese appetizer was fresh and fantastic with burratta cheese and pretty good sized tomatoes, mescaline greens and a little evoo. It was the perfect light and tasty start to my dinner   I had meatballs over spaghetti squash (paleo!) with tomato sauce. It was OK. I like the idea of the spaghetti squash as a healthy alternative and the sauce was nice & sweet but it could have been better. The meatballs were slightly dry; however, it was all still edible and enjoyable so it really wasn't that bad. I guess I'm just used to grandmas sauce and meatballs (can't beat that).   All in all, this place is a relaxing restaurant with friendly staff. I would definitely recommend it if you're looking to try something new!

I am from the Hartford area, and rarely make it to New Haven. However, after attending the Stone Hearth soft opening night, I knew I would have to make a return trip! After a surprisingly easy trip from Hartford (no more than 40 minutes, tops!), my group of three was seated at a spacious booth. It was a beautiful Sunday morning, and we were delighted to see that our booth had sliding windows next to us! The electrical outlets at each booth are also a plus. The service was excellent, and the chefs accommodated our request for egg white frittatas. The Lorraine frittata uses Gruyere cheese, yum! The group also shared a few breakfast pizzas (something I would have never thought of, but loved!) and the AMAZING rice krispy coated french toast with nutella and whipped cream. We practically fought over the last piece of the french toast! There is something for everyone - lighter options for the health conscious and decadent items "From the Grill" for those treating themselves. Brunch is served Saturdays and Sundays from 9am-3pm, and I highly recommend. See you soon, Stone Hearth! ... and I will definitely be requesting the Georgia Peach cocktail from opening night.
Chiken Parm pizza is the bomb...nuff said.

I always thought Mays was an underrated deli but looking back its like night and day compared to what 19 degrees has done. This place now gets 5 stars for cleanliness as I'm guessing the lack there of at Mays ultimately led to its demise. As for the sandwiches the new menu has a nice variety of classic deli sandwiches as well as more pre-crafted items such as paninis. Overall the menu is eerily similar to Palm Gourmet but that's good company to be with  They use boar heads meats (+1) and the ingredients are always fresh. The Jewish hoagie with Russian dressing would be what I go with most often but I have yet to make a disappointing order and I eat here at least once a week. The prices lean on the high side for the quantity and the speed of service can be slow but this is a fantastic lunch option in the graduate hospital area. Recently they have been closed on multiple occasions with a sign in the window related to a liquor license, I guess this review will have to be continued......

Best pizza in Connecticut. Seriously. I have been coming here for years and if you like thin crust pizza, you will fall in love with Harry's. In late summer, try the amazing fresh tomato basil. They have several good beers on tap.
Great food. One of a kind burger interesting presentation.
a calzone and a hamburger had a love child.  it is here, and it is delicious

Me and my husband went to this place desperately looking for food at 1030pm and we were pleasantly surprised by the pizza and penne all vodka. They made it fresh and perfectly. Such great hospitality on the owners part with making our food fresh and the sauce was perfect. I would go back to this place on a normal visit not hunting for food late night. Excellent service! Excellent food!

If I could give two sets of ratings I'd give 3 stars for menu options and 4 for service. The waitress seemed to wait just on us. The tempura was perfect (as rated by others), but rolls left more to be desired. Very simple, tiny and low variety. Not great for kids.

I've lived in Tokyo for 3 years and have only had a handful of meals that compared to Wajima. We had the misoshiru, agedashidofu, spicy tuna roll, and sukiyaki. The misoshiru was delicious--fantastic lacquerware and was "roastier" than the standard fare you get a lot of times. The agedashidofu was also delicious. Perfectly cooked and just the right amount for 2 people. The spicy tuna was also fantastic, everything down to the pickle ginger tasted fresh and homemade. The sukiyaki was the biggest hit with us, as the broth and quality of every ingredient was above anything we've had in New York. Lastly, the service was impeccable. Everything down to how the beer was poured was precise, and we couldn't have been more delighted.

-Service 4 stars -Don't come here for maki (tons of rice, little fish, little flavor)  (i.e., even their "spicy" rolls were pretty bland) -Their green tea ice cream was not offered fried and had a substantial amount of ice in it -If you want basic fish, this place is probably fine (as I did see a bunch of Japanese looking folks there...:) )

Food is decent, but more often than not the order is screwed up. When you order the pulled pork, expect to get large chunks of pork, not the real deal.  I called and asked what the story was after the second time it happened, thinking they'd changed the recipe or something. Whoever I spoke with said that the person who pulls the pork simply didn't do it right, and was glad to know of the problem. Next week I ordered the pulled pork again and received again just large chunks of pork - not "pulled."  Disturbing that they are so un concerned with getting right the food that leaves their kitchen. I've been burned for the last time.

This is a great little neighborhood store.  The sandwiches are great.  The meats are good.  But, unfortunately, you really do pay extra for the convenience.  I think I spent about $14 on a sandwich, a little thing of macaroni salad and a drink.  Based on the prices, I would have to call this  place UnFairChild's Market.  :P  No, in all fairness, they're okay.  I suppose the quality is there to warrant the price.  Three stars, coulda been four, but I've been given those out a little too frequently, gotta tighten up on that.

I ordered six sandwiches to pick up and called an hour ahead.  Was told they were busy and they'd try to have it ready.  When I got there to pick it up there were three people in various places behind a large counter and one other customer.  I moved to two places where people were working and no one helped me.  I watched the other customer go to one end of the counter to pay for her coffee so I followed her and stood behind her.  After she paid the woman behind the counter walked away.  A few minutes later she came back and just looked at me so I said I was there to pick up an order.  About 5 minutes later it was done.  I just felt like a second class citizen or something.  The food was good though absolutely no extras and I would say the portion size was very small for the prices.  I feel like I can find food equal to or better quality with far more pleasant service.  Really disappointing.

Although pricey, sandwiches at Fairchild's are worth every penny. I typically opt for the turkey on country white, but the ham and brie is also delicious. Also am a fan of their rotating craft beer selection.

Overall, Sushi on Chapel offers a mediocre sushi experience. The menu itself is moderately extensive, with a range of classic, specialty, and vegetarian rolls. The type of rice used (mountain rice made with red bean) adds a unique touch and color to the sushi itself, but provides little in terms of taste and texture. The fish in the roll was fresh and and plentiful, but oftentimes overpowered by the copious sauces used on many of the specialty rolls- a shame, given the fact that the specialty rolls are on the pricier side, often ranging from $15- $18. Furthermore, look out for the ambiguous recipe wording, as the sauces listed on the menu are not specified. One of the rolls I ordered had wasabi sauce on it, which I was unaware of upon ordering. If one has food allergies, you may want to be extra cautious when placing your order.

Ate here once before; food was unimpressive, but I'm a sucker for Chicken Pad-Thai and I was willing to give it another chance. (They'd apparently never heard of Cilantro or lime/lemon juice...LOL)...but who knows! Every cook is different, I'll give it another shot! Bought a Groupon to come here for $12.50 for $25 worth of Thai food. As per the agreement, I showed them the document BEFORE being sat down for dinner, and I adhered to the terms of the agreement. At the end of the meal; KNOWING that I wanted to use a groupon, they came and told me that they weren't accepting it- but wouldn't clearly explain why? Terms were 2 people, $12.50 for $25; I ordered two entrees plus drinks- ate one, my date picked at hers, and we asked for it to go. They said only *I* ate, so therefore they wouldn't accept it. Bill was well over the $25- and now they didn't accept the Groupon. Chattered at me in broken English; and were completely unseeing of any point of view but their own- I have never had to FIGHT to redeem a Groupon before. Not only did Groupon hear it from me, but I'm smoking this place on TripAdvisor, Yelp, Yahoo local, you name it. This is NOT how you win customers. Almost all of my YELP! Reviews are good ones; this is one of the few AWFUL ones.

My girlfriend and I frequent this place a lot, as it is close to Drexel campus, and we love it! The owner, James, is a very personable guy.  The food is delicious, and the prices are reasonable.  You have the option of buying a 6 pack and mixing different drinks just in case you want to try something new, which I think is a great idea. In addition to the food being delicious, I like the customer service.  I ordered a pizza and they accidentally put bacon on it (I don't eat pork).  While we waited for another pizza to be made, the owner provided us with drinks on the house. I recommend this place if you're in the area.
Very nice and intimate setting ... Great for group or on a date. Id say this is a local hotspot ! There scallops and chicken cous cous is delicious.  must go!
3 stars. 5th oldest tavern in NYC (Irish bar). Ordered a burger which was OK.
Good atmosphere. loved the hooka. Food was so-so. the rice need a bit more spices (not sure if that is a afgan trait) lamb kebab is a must have, loved it.

Food is okay at best and overpriced. My sister had a Groupon that she had to use, so we decided to go for dinner. I had been a couple of years ago for lunch and really enjoyed it, so I figured I'd have the same experience. We ordered the vegetarian samosas and garlic shrimp for appetizers. The samosas were delicious, however, the shrimp was rather undercooked for my taste. The sauce the shrimp came in was flavorful. We got five rather small shrimp in the order of garlic shrimp for $12 - WAY OVERPRICED. We then ordered a half order of tandoori chicken ($14), my sister ordered a lamb dish ($22) and an order of garlic naan ($4). The maître de/server said that we might want to order rice since it didn't come with it, so we did. My tandoori chicken was two drumsticks with a small portion of shredded lettuce, two carrot slices and two cucumber slices (let me say that again: two chicken drumsticks for $14.) The chicken lacked much flavor, but was juicy. My sister's lamb dish was more sauce than anything else. It consisted of four small pieces of lamb (I'd say the size of a standard meatball) and a bunch of vegetables. Pretty disappointing for $22. The garlic naan was delicious and there were four triangles of it. So by this point, we had easily blown through our Groupon, but thought maybe we'd get some dessert. $6 for ice cream. No thanks. So we left. It's a shame because I love Indian food. The restaurant is never going to survive if they keep the food at the prices they are at now. The server must have asked us half a dozen times if we were really enjoying ourselves. My guess is that he's the owner or manager and doesn't seem many return customers. Needless to say, I won't be going back anytime soon. Definitely wasn't the same great experience I had a couple of years back.

Stopped in for a drink and app before the HSO show at The Bushnell. Knew nothing about it and didn't read other reviews until mid way through our time there. Staff was friendly enough but with the exception of one young man named Sam, not very skilled. They have a well stocked bar but our waiter/bartender didn't know how to even begin making a Gray Goose dirty martini. They then changed us $12 for a drink I practically made for myself. The vegetable samosa were excellent as was the garlic naan.  The chicken 65, which at our favorite Panjabi Tadka in Springfield is crisp and spicy, was soggy and flavorless. Our first order of chili shrimp was so undercooked that we sent it back....The chef promptly made a new order which was cooked properly but hadn't been fully shelled. Too many great places to settle for a $70, 2 star quality experience. We won't be back.

Named after a river which runs through both France and Italy, Roia offers a menu with selections from the cuisines of both countries.  Originally the ballroom of the New Haven landmark Hotel Taft, the space has received  an elegant update,  with a few missteps.  There are no soft surfaces, so the room is very noisy.  It's almost impossible to hear someone speaking across the table and the racket is deafening.  Anyone in the dining room who is seated facing the comfortable and intimate bar area also gets a dramatic view of people using a large sink located at the entrance to the restrooms.   The menu itself is rather basic - steak frites, chicken liver mousse, or duck confit from the French side and a few pastas from the Italian side.  Prices are rather high for the food served.   Deserts, however, were uniformly excellent, and since portion sizes are small, you should have plenty of room.

Delicious doesn't even begin to describe the dining experience at Roia!  As someone with a gluten intolerance, the server was informed and if she wasn't sure about something, she went to the chef and asked!  Almost everything I wanted was gluten free!  From the appertif to dessert, the server was knowledgable and helpful!  The char was deliciously prepared with just the right amount of flavor and texture!  Devine is the way to describe the whole experience!  It's a great date night location!  Also, my husband is very tall, so we sat in a booth, which was very comfortable!  I can't wait to go back!

We ventured out of Manhattan to visit some friends and had dinner here during Roia's opening week. We really loved everything about it. The space is beautiful, and the food was delicious. If I lived closer I would definitely be a frequent visitor!

We happened by during their grand opening about a week ago, and there samples were amazing! We decide to come back soon for dinner. We were not disappointed. In fact, I would say the dinner was even beat than the food at the opening. The staff was friendly and very knowledge about the menu. We had a number of appetizers including the sweet shrimp and the raw fluke. Melt in you mouth good and filled with flavor. I had the whole fish for my main course, and it was outstanding. It was just perfectly done. Dessert was just as good, and they make their own sorbert and gelato. We will return here to dine often.
Ok, I live in Brooklyn and drove to New Haven for the opening of this restaurant to meet friends.  It was a lovely experience.  I will plan to venture again to Roia for an encore.
Really good food. Had the brick chicken. The pesto mashed potatoes were the best part so damn good. Ambience is cool. My waiter sucked but every one else seemed to get good service. Highly recommend.
Fried pickles - wow, the best thing ever. Great place, love the vibe, everyone is really cool. I'm coming back for sure.

So there I was, late night in NYC having just hopped off my inbound flight, and I was very much in need of a place to watch the NCAA tournament. Enter: Brickyard Gastropub. Mission accomplished, but there's room for improvement. Star 1: How was the service and atmosphere? Very, very good. This is where BG shines, with a cozy yet sports enthused crowd that'll have you enticed into whatever event happens to be on even if you're a neutral. Service is fast and friendly, and the location is ideal depending on your needs. Star Granted. Star 2: How were the portions relative to the cost? Even in NYC, my appropriate range for a good burger falls between $10.00 and $15.00, and BG just misses the cut. Yes, my bison burger was priced starting at $15.00, but the second I added a bit of bacon and some grilled onions, we were now at $17.00, or $20.00 after tax and tip. Had this been world's biggest burger? Fine, but it wasn't. Have a look - yelp.com/user_local_phot… No Star Granted.   Stars 3 and 4: How was the food? Meh. It was okay. A look at the picture is enough to tell you that the bun, lettuce, tomato and onions were standard, and while Bison can be challenging in that it tends to dry out so easily, this was a sub-standard burger. The patty, while of suitable size, had no independent flavor cooked in, and when you rely on mediocre toppings for flavor, you end up with a mediocre burger. I'll give it to BG when it comes to the truffle fries and the beer selection, but I've simply had better, and cheaper, burgers in NYC. Single Star Granted.   Star 5: Would you eat here every day if you could? A great atmosphere, but I've experienced much better food. No Star Granted.

My wife and I met up with friends to have dinner at this restaurant. This is a new location for this chain and we had never been to Brio. Out first impressions were very good as the place had a warm feel to it. We did have to wait about 20 minutes longer than our reservation we had made. It is a new location and this was not unexpected. Once we sat down, the waitress came over very quickly and asked us if we were ready. This was maybe three minutes after sitting down. We wanted to order minestrone soup as it was a very cold outside. The waitress came back to us and said they were all out. That was a bunch of crap! Once we got our food, the fish my wife and I ordered was just overlooked and dry. It was also freezing in the restaurant and we were not alone. Looking around many others had there coats on. It is also a pricy restaurant for the quality they provide. I may give them another chance one day and update my review but a very poor first impression.

My friend and I were trying to decide where to go, and since I love Italian food, we thought we would give this place a try on a sat night.  keep in mind they had only been open for 3 weeks.  we made a reservation for 745pm, and thank god you can beause there were so many ppl there!  it doesn't help that it's in a mall.  we got there right on time, but ended up waiting 35 minutes to be seated - apparently they forgot about us.  the manager said that we would get a free drink or entrée - my friend took them up on the drink.   we ordered right away, and my dish was salmon with sweet potatoes and spinach.  and my friend got their sausage flatbread (which they had passed around while we were waiting rather genius move if you ask me).  Well the bad luck didn't end there.  so when my meal came, the side of veggies I got was so peppery I had to send it back.  then after another 10 min they arrived.  when we got the bill, the drink and side of veggies were not comped.  the manager cam over and said it was all taken care of - meaning they comped our entire dinner and said they didn't want us to never come back due to this experience.  thanks to their generosity, I will be back at least 1 more time.  also, they have a 400 calorie and under menu, which is always nice and exactly what I ordered from.

Ate here on a Monday night, around 7pm.  We had tried to dine here once in the summer last year, but it was simply too hot inside for comfort and we left without ordering.  We came back on a cool spring night, excited to try this place because we heard great things and it is close to our home. The atmosphere here is pleasant and the staff was very attentive. But the food... the food here was simply not good, especially considering the prices.  The bread served before dinner was cold and unremarkable.  The calamari was not exactly cold, but certainly not hot, although the mediocre temperature reflected the flavor of the dish. My entree was the Arrabiata, "chicken chunks" in a spicy wine-lemon sauce.  While the chicken was adequately cooked, it was not hot at all.  The lukewarm chicken and sauce made for a disappointing pairing.  The only hot item on my plate was the mashed potatoes, which were pretty tasty.  My wife ordered the salmon with quinoa and barely.  The salmon was overcooked, and I don't know how else to describe the flavor of the barley other than "off-putting". Again, I thought the staff here was great, but there is much better italian food in Montclair.  I do not believe I will be dining here again.

I've been here twice and both times food was great and service was excellent! Second time we went we forgot our wine (it's a BYO), but don't worry our server gave us a wine menu and had the local liquor store deliver our wine right to the table!!! How awesome is that!!! I recommend getting their Filet Mignon or pasta dish with crumbled sausage. Both dishes were delicious!! Will def keep going back!

Another great Montclair BYOB!!!  Start off with the arancino, a pan fried rice ball in a delicious sauce.  My wife and I had a pizza which was very good but we kept hearing all the tables around us rave about their homemade pastas.  Definitely getting a pasta next time; if you want some upscale good old Italian comfort food; Salute is the place for you.
Artichoke dip is a must try for everyone! Great atmosphere, very friendly staff. Perfect for a date or a place to relax with girls!

This place is such a great hole in the wall. It has an amazing, unpretentious vibe and is the kind of place where I would sit all day, periodically getting up to order either another (homemade) snack or meal or another beer or even some dessert and coffee. They have it all - it's all fresh and it's all homemade and most importantly, tasty. I will definitely come back.

This is such a fun place! Great atmosphere and neat environment with decor and good music. The food was very tasty. We waited in line for about 20 minutes on a Sunday morning while we were deciding what to order. Order at the counter and food is brought to the table with a little self service involved. Very friendly and attentive workers. I had the Baja fish tacos and they were solid! They didn't skimp on the fish and the flavor was great. I also had sweet potato fries and tried some of the egg asparagus tacos which were also good. Definitely a fun breakfast/brunch joint and I am sure there are other gems on the menu!!

Excellent place to grab breakfast/brunch and catch up with a friend. How it works: You get in line to order at the counter, let the host find you a table, grab your freshly brewed latte (which is yum), and wait for your food to arrive! I ordered the french toast, which seemed pretty popular. It arrived with a heaping pile of strawberries, blueberries, and banana slices on top, and four fluffy but eggy slices of thick bread. Definitely hit the spot. The wait can get a little bit long, but there's always a table just opening up for you. Chill, laid-back atmosphere, and lots of ROOM! You don't ever feel crowded here. Free refills on your coffee, and super friendly staff in general. I'll be back!

Really great scene! Gray dog has a fantastic happy hour wine special, half off bottles of wine! It's amazing. I can't speak to the quality of the food, other than that the sweet potato fries were divine. The resteraunt/bar itself is very very cozy- a great place to go with friends after work. the decor is nice, but they only have one bathroom, which can be annoying. All in all, I would definitely recommend!

Was recommended to pop in here for breakfast, wondered through Little Italy to get here - wasn't disappointed. For a week day, it was relaxed and cosy. We queued up, ordered food and sat down at table. Grey Dog breakfast was plenty and looked yummy. I had Breakfast Quesidilla - very yummy and delicious, would highly recommend. Lots of choices. Friends said coffee/cappucino was good too.

Great place to grab quick breakfast or lunch with friends, chat, and hang out.  I had the brie and turkey sandwich (one of the most popular items), raspberry ice tea, and to die for apple pie (I don't even like apple pie but it was gooey in a good way).

There's definitely never been food this good in a diner before. Celebrity chef Amanda Freitag has reopened the iconic Empire Diner in Chelsea, serving playful and creative takes on classic comfort foods, which were all delicious. It was completely packed when we arrived at about 7 PM on the first Saturday they were open. We were quoted a wait time of 45 minutes, and they have that excellent system here where they take your number and text you when the table is ready so you don't have to sit around in the restaurant waiting. Just 20 minutes later, I was excited to get the text and we made our way in and got seated in a nice cozy booth right behind Geoffrey Zakarian. Chef Freitag was also walking around the place chatting with customers and being really cool during what looked to be a really hectic time. There are a ton of great choices on the menu, so we did our best to try as much as possible: - Buffalo Skate Wings ($11) This was one of the tastiest bites of the meal. Instead of chicken, this comes with 3 deliciously flaky, soft pieces of crispy skate smothered in buffalo sauce, served on top of a pile of a very flavorful mix of creme fraiche, carrots, and celery. Just like buffalo wings, the cool carrots and celery provide a very refreshing taste to go with the hot and heavy buffalo taste. - Happy Waitress ($9) I got this mostly because of the intriguing name, and it turned out to be really delicious. Verging more toward the breakfast end of the offerings, the waiter described this as something like eggs benedict. It consists of a poached egg, ham and cheddar cheese on top of brioche bread. The cheese is like the hollandaise sauce you get in an eggs benedict, only this was way tastier. It's a shame they don't give you any bread, which would have been amazing to soak up all that great sauce - they missed a great opportunity here to make some kind of housemade saltines or melba toast like they give you in bread baskets at divey diners. - Matzoh Ball Marrow Soup ($9) This was a delicious take on matzoh ball soup. It comes with one nice and dense, excellent ball perched atop the bone with the marrow. There is also a good amount of poached chicken in the soup, making for a much richer, more flavorful broth than the typical plain chicken stock you get with some of these soups. I think my grandma's matzoh balls may have had the edge on these, but these were up there with some of the better ones I've had in non-Jewish restaurants. - Empire Burger ($16) This was an excellent burger. The fries looked almost like diner fries, which was troubling, but they tasted way better. They were extremely crispy with a nice amount of salt, and nice and hot. The best part of the burger was probably the fluffy brioche bun, which also stood up well against the juicy patty and the special sauce. - Pork on Pork Chop ($21) This was excellent. The first pork in the dish name refers to a generous sprinkling of pancetta on top of the second pork, which is a massively thick pork chop. The crispy bacon combined with the soft, tender chop makes for a great bite. Combined with the super buttery sauce and the kale and beans underneath, it is the perfect bite. Seriously, that sauce is really buttery. If you can't take a rich sauce, this might send you over the edge, but I loved it and thought it went well with the inherently drier consistency of the large pork chop. - Brooklyn Blackout Cake ($10) On to dessert, these were some of the best desserts I've had in any restaurant in recent memory. The problem with nice places is that the dessert often isn't sweet enough, since fancy people like more refined and subtle flavors. Not me though - I like feeling a cavity form as I bite into a piece of cake. This large piece of devil's food cake was super rich and sweet. It comes with a little cool dollop of cream, which is a good complement to the very decadent chocolatey cake. - Black-N-White Cheesecake ($9) This was even better than the rich blackout cake, and was just as beautiful as it was delicious. The perfect cylinder of cheesecake is divided in half, with the vanilla portion on the top and the chocolate portion on the bottom, with two great mini black and white cookies adorning the plate. This was some ridiculously tasty cheesecake, and was even richer than the other cake, and I would have to go with this one if I could only choose one dessert. But why would you ever only choose one? - Homemade Cookies ($6) These say "to stay or to go" on the menu, so in an effort to not look as obese, we ordered them to go, even though I clearly ate them immediately once I got home. You get 3 different kinds of cookies, with 3 of each, and they are pretty good, but don't come close to the awesome cakes. Service was a little shaky, but I don't mind considering they just opened and the food was so good. I am surprised they intend on keeping such a nice place open 24/7, but I would love to come back and see how it goes. Next time, pancakes for dinner.

While browsing New Businesses in Yelp, Empire Diner appeared on top of the list. I quickly realized this is Celebrity Chef Amanda Freitag's restaurant after reading Mike C's review. My wife loves the Chopped show on Food Network and also a huge fan of Amanda Freitag, so I decided to take her to Empire Diner without telling her it is Amanda's restaurant. At 5:35pm on Friday evening, we were greeted by a friendly staff and immediately seated at the far left corner of the dining room which is very cozy and intimate. While heading to our table, my wife got a glimpse of Executive Chef Amanda in the kitchen. She got excited and immediately starstruck. :) We ordered the Empire burger and Pork on pork chop with crispy pancetta, cranberry beans, and kale. The brioche bun on the burger was so soft and chewy and the meat was well seasoned and juicy. The pork chop was tender and cooked with perfect crust. While writing this, I am already planning more visits. The food and service were great and the best part is able to hear Amanda firing up the dishes from where we were seated. In person, Amanda is just as nice and approachable as what we see her on the Chopped show.
Sat at bar (albeit end) for about 10 min without so much as a greeting from the bar tender, so we left. Love Amanda. Guessing this is not what she would expect.

I have eaten twice at the Empire Diner the past two weeks and have found the food to be for the most part excellent.  The skirt steak with smashed fried potatoes, parsley-butter sauce is cooked to perfection and is as tender as you would ever want it.  The onion soup with bagel croutons exhibits terrific beef broth, the right amount of Gruyère cheese and soft onions, delicious.  The chicken dish on the menu should never change, as on consecutive weeks one of my dining companions ordered this succulent white meat with a crunchy crust and a ricotta dip with roasted baby carrots, perfection.  The Pork chop is served boneless and as I started to cut in with the butter knife in the middle the pork chop cut so easily that it was almost redundant to use the sharp steak knife as this thick chop was cooked perfectly with no fat and served with cranberry beans and a bit of sauteed kale.  The donuts are served hot and tasty with a caramel sauce.  Now for the only peeves, $4 for a cola is a bit high, but the beer and wines are marginly higher, with an excellent selection and the prices of the food are gentle, so the diner has to make money somehow...  The patty melt is delicious, but serving it with Terra chips is not the right fit.  The French fries are not bad, just not outstanding, they need to be double fried or seasoned a bit more and some of the other desserts are mediocre or just below the delivery of the rest of the menu.  One final note, the servers and front of the house is extremely nice and professional.  It is also a pleasure to see Chef Amanda Frietag at the pass through directing her first restaurant, after all the above review would not be possible.  She is a talent and as even tempered a talent as any chef in America.

Had dinner here last night. The Happy Waitress was the highlight of the meal. Both the actual waitress and the dish named after her. Also very good were the Brussel sprouts and the cauliflower. To top it all off, the cocktails were fab-u-lous. I'm normally not a mixed drink kinda guy but these were out of this world. Try the martini with the pickles vegetables. It's like a Bloody Mary.... For grown ups.

The best grilled cheese and tomato sandwich I have had since my mother's growing up. It was extremely crowded when we went around 10pm on Friday night but the energy was great. The bartender was a class act. He asked what I liked, I said Vodka, Ginger and lime then he proceeds to make his version of a Moscow Mule. It was exceptional. The Hubby and I have decided to try and return for brunch because we think they will make killer french toast.  This is an old school diner with a 4-star food menu in that they enhance the basic american cuisine. Pinkies Up!

Damon's was recommended to me by a few people so recently myself and two friends checked it out. It's located in the space formerly occupied by West Wings just over the Hartford Line from West Hartford. The outside of the bld is nothing to write home about...it's much nicer inside. It has a Buffalo Wild Wings vibe but it's nicer decor. There are tv's at every booth and all over the perimeter of the place. The good: While we didn't drink anything (it was early for us) there was a huge beer selection on tap. We ordered the potato skins and we liked them very much. Simple, fresh, good. The bad: My order of the slider appetizer (one buffalo chicken, one pulled pork, one bacon cheeseburger) was lamely presented on a plain plate. No fries with it...no garnish. I actually had one chicken and two porks. All 3 were SUPER dry. The chicken was leathery too. My friend ordered the BLT which looked fantastic aside from the completely brown slices of avocado on it. The fries that came with the sandwiches had nice potential but were limp and overly browned. The worst part(s):My other friend ordered the Monte Cristo and it was batter dipped and deep fried. I had a bite and it was like a sponge of oil. It was really bad but if you picked through it the ham, turkey and cheese were of decent and tasty quality. They should explain that it's deep fried on the menu because when the waiter asked my friend if she wanted to wrap up her sammich, she said "no thanks, I wasn't expecting it to be deep fried" and the waiter said "everyone says that." I think there's room for improvement. All said and done--the menu has promise, and the atmosphere on a quiet Sunday afternoon for lunch was right, but the food wasn't great.

I've been there 4 times in the first 2 months of it's inception. The menu is already being revamped which I always think is a mistake that quickly. I've always sat at the bar and had good service. I would like the 2 bartenders to decide if the are taking a side each or if they are both servicing EVERYBODY. Last time my friend and I DID have to wait a long time to place an order. The two girls were NOT busy- they just were confused on who was working where. No big deal. There will be growing pains and we will be back. GO Yankees!
I've only had their drip coffee, very disappointing. I can't speak to their espresso drinks.

Went for dinner on a Friday night. I had to change my reservations several times due to a delay in part of our party arriving in town, but they were SUPER accomodating. When you first walk in the music is so so loud!! We were seated along the bar area, but asked to move closer to the back where it was just a bit quieter. We got the steak springrolls as an appetizer and they were DELICIOUS! I had the lobster rolls for dinner and they were equally delicious. I believe everyone else in my party was pleased with their meals as well. Even though it's loud, they have a nice vibe and great food.

This was the second time I came here, more for drinks this time rather than to eat. Started with a regular drink that I knew, prior to looking for one on the drink menu. I got some cocktail in a martini glass with a slice of cucumber. Pardon me for not remembering the name, but it was refreshing and delicious! Tried some cocktails of my friends', and they were also very good, but I stuck with my choice and got another one of the same. At that point we started to get hungry and ordered some sliders and lobster rolls. Very satisfying food just as the last time I was there. Then ordered some more cocktails, all more delicious (exponentially :) at this point. Chatted, laughed... Bottom line, with a drink menu like theirs there is no way you will not have a good time!!

I recently went back to Ivy Bar for a friend's birthday  and tried the new spring/summer cocktails and appetizers. The new drinks are so light and fresh and perfectly pair with the new seasonal menu. The lobster spring rolls were so good I ordered TWO!

A little off the beaten path, but worth going out of the way!  My new staple, its a great spot to meet up with friends for a casual, no frills kind of night which often isn't easy to find in New York.  Great drinks, reasonably priced and the staff is friendly and always suggesting creative new cocktails not on the menu. Side note: if you love the wall decor as much as I do, it was hand painted (not wallpaper).  I am obsessed!

Good food, nice staff, great service, cute decor. I honestly recommend this place to everyone. Its a nice place to bring a few people to hang out and a lot of people go on dates here. They also host a lot of free events (which is how i discovered it) so check it out next time. I even met the owner and he recommended other good restaurants and dishes to try in the area. I love the udon and dragon roll sushi but I sometimes stop by JUST for the Mochi ice cream, it is soooooooo good. Never had a bad dish or bad experience here. Just to emphasize how nice they are, I sat on their seats outside one hot day because I was so hot and tired and the waiter came out and offered me a glass of water! 5 stars for not only being a good quality restaurant, but for being decent people. UPDATE: Zento is still one of my favorite regular places to visit. You get to know the staff very well and the owner often comes down and mingles with the guests. They frequently hold events here and it is just a lively place to be at.

Delicious food with affordable menu! Casual yet high-end, sophisticated atmosphere. A friendly, knowledgeable, professional staff. Zento's is a wonderful dining experience! Great place to meet friends and drink, eat, hang-out for hours!!!
Pretty slow service, gets pretty crowded and cluster around evening hours, but great food! :)

I'm inherently suspicious of restaurants that constantly run deals on every one of those daily deal sites imaginable. Either they're in such bad shape that they're desperate to get anybody in the door, or they've inflated their prices so much that the deal just re-sets the prices back to normal. Zento seems to fall into that latter category. The sushi was good, but you can't honestly call Zento a sushi bar. The food is all prepared in a kitchen somewhere in the basement of the place. The service was solid. I'm not sure what else I can say. It was a good meal, but not anything that blew my mind.

The food was ok not great. I expected better from a tasting special. We used the groupon special and the portions were small which was reasonable for the $60 it costed for 2 people. The service was not great. I understand that the business picked up after our appetizer was served but not once did the server ask us how the food was or how everything was going. He was quicker  The miso mussel soup was decent and the fish appetizer was not cold enough for it to taste great. The calamari salad was good. The sushi was mediocre, nothing special. The dessert was mochi and tofu cheesecake which the mochi was ok but the tofu cheesecake was not good , I think the wooden made the cheesecake taste funny. Also there is a corking fee.  Overall I was not impressed with the food or the service. I don't plan on coming back.

I have never written a review of restaurant but the worst service I have ever experienced inspired me to do so.  I have worked in the restaurant business for about 20 years and while I know it can be annoying when people use coupons and vouchers, there is absolutely no need to be obnoxiously rude about it which our waiter was.  I purchased the 7 course tasting menu deal on Living Social because while my son loves good food, he tends to inhale it so I don't always love spending a fortune on a meal for him.  We made a reservation but were seated in the bar area even though there were multiple open tables in the dining room available.  Our waiter sat at the bar watching us for about 10 minutes before approaching the table and when he did, he said "tasting menu, can I get your coupon?"  He never asked if we wanted a drink or anything else when he greeted us or at any point during our meal.  I do not eat meat and I asked if I could substitute and his reply in an extremely snarky, condescending tone was "no, it is a chef's tasting menu", the only thing he left out was "duh" which he obviously thinking.  I have have ordered many tasting menus at many restaurants and have never been denied a substitution for a dietary restriction.  Even if this restaurant does not substitute, had he been civil about it, I would have skipped that course without complaint.  When he presented each course, he barely grunted what we were eating.  When my son ordered a soda, it sat at the bar for so long while our waiter watched TV,  half the ice in the glass had melted and he had to drain the glass before pouring his soda in.  At the end of our meal, our waiter dropped the check immediately after dropping dessert without asking if we wanted anything else, which we might have had he not been so rude.  I have experienced incompetent service on many occasions and it has been tolerable because at least the service was civil.  This server was clearly capable but acted as if he were doing us a favor by bringing us the food we paid for.  I have never been tempted to not leave gratuity in my life but I came very close tonight.  I typically would have tipped on the value of the meal and not what I purchased it for but I could not bring myself to do that either.  I ended up compromising and tipped on the price of the Living Social voucher plus what we spent on additional food and drinks.  As for the food, it was solid but had it's ups and downs.  The Miso soup, calamari salad and dessert were very good, the carpaccio and sashimi were excellent.  The crab cake was not great, it was fishy tasting and had a lot of shells in it.  We ordered an additional tempura lobster roll which was fine but not exciting.  I really wanted to and fully expected to love this place.  Overall, the food was good, the prices were reasonable but the service made the experience miserable.
Walnut meringue Hungarian sweet roll - get it now and get hooked!;) love their bike bread delivery around town.

Great open loft space with plenty of tables and leather couches. Massive outlets everywhere but Wifi is slow and a bit pricey. Staff is great with a nice variety on the menu. Don't go in unless you have a MAC Book.
It was a Sunday night. They were 15 mins to close but still made the best food I had that day. Great and friendly service as well.
Its incredible the taste and the quality of the steaks, you cant imagine, first time i tasted i was introduce to a new level of steaks.

Its incredible the taste and the quality of the steaks, you cant imagine, first time i tasted i was introduce to a new level of steaks. i recommend this ALOOOTTT!!! Dont forget to ask for the special sauce!!
Sitting in here eating a grill cheese sharp cheddar with green apple and prosciutto.  Omg. I think this may be the best grill cheese ever. Very excited about this place and love the decor.
Perfect comfort food for a cold rainy day in NY, and at a reasonable price. Best, it was no problem to get a table at lunchtime. Thai 51 dumplings were delicious, pad see ew was solid.
Great food, great service, good selection, good prices, Thai spaghetti with lobster tail the best!

This place used to be Thai 51 which I really liked, too! Anyways, it was pretty packed during lunch, but they do have good lunch deals!  I got the beef drunken noodles and two spring rolls for $9.  I loved the lil' pot they put the noodles in too, and they were yummmy!  Ask for some hot sauce for some extra spice!

Small place with exceptional food.  I had the Bangkok Noodle and my son had the Pad Thai (his first Thai experience and he loved it).  This was the best meal I've had in NYC. If I had to find one complaint, it would be that the writing on the menu is extremely small, making it difficult to read in the dim light.  However, the quality and taste of the food are amazing. This was a last minute find on Yelp since it was just a block from our hotel.  So glad we found this place.  I will be back on my next NYC visit.

Excellent tasting food, and will now be my go to for Midtown East Asian takeout.  I ordered three items from here for pickup.  All were delicious, affordable, and quickly prepared.  The staff was friendly and I look forward to going back or ordering takeout again to try more of their expansive menu.  Highly recommend the King's Rama dish - the peanut sauce and flavor was on point.

I ordered take out from them - curry puffs and bangkok noodles with tofu. Being a fan of Thai cuisine, I have tried many a Thai restaurants, and I would say they were very middle of the road. The curry puffs were a little sweet. The bangkok noodles were ordered spicy, which they were. The tofu was not fried, but sauted, and could have used some more veggies. There was nothing wrong with the food, but it was not great. Cannot comment on the decor or service. Being in NYC, I'll try a different Thai place next time I want Thai food.
Food was okay.,but a little sweet for my taste. Drinks were too sweet. 1 of the female staff wasn't very friendly.

I came here with my dad about a week ago. It was freezing outside and we could not wait to eat something hot. Right away I ordered a veggie tom yum soup ($4) and veggie dumplings. For my entree I decided to go with the green tofu curry. I asked her if they can do both veggies and tofu and she said it is extra $2 meanwhile the  tofu/veg and shrimp curry cost the same.. Weird. Right after we ordered it started to get REALLY HOT. Like I was down to my tank top and almost sweating. They must have put the heat on 90 because it was unbearable. They did turn it down but the fact that I ordered hot food didn't help. The veggie dumplings were very yummy. There are 6 in an order and they are bite sized. The soup was good but it was small and I wish it was spicier. I have had better tom yum soups. The green curry with tofu was AMAZING. I love how they use sliced bamboo shoots to almost feel like noodles. It was spicy and really hot in temperature which is just how I like my food. My dad ordered some shrimp veggie dish that came In some kind of rice paper bowl. It was amazing as well. The only thing that bothered me is that the dishes were extremely small. They do come with rice but it is nothing special, a little dry. My dad had a creme brûlée for dessert and he really enjoyed it though I wouldn't really say it was authentic.. Will 100% be back. They also give 10% off if you check in

I've always liked Thai food but it's never outstanding in my opinion. It's just a yummy dish usually that I occasionally am in the mood for. However I think this place's Thai food does a good job of leaving an impression on you. I loved the Drunk Man noodles a lot. Only problem was I didn't expect it to be so darn spicy - I nearly died and the waitresses here do not keep their third eye on your water cup unlike some places so I had to ask multiple times. But yeah, Drunk Man noodles were delicious.

10% off your entire bill with a yelp check-in! Try to remember this because I forgot about it when it came time to pay the bill; whoops. I had the Chicken Pad Woon Sen and I really loved it. It was flavorful and very filling. My friends ordered the chicken green curry and the chicken pad see ew. The pad see ew was a bit too sweet for my liking. The green curry was delicious, a tad sweet and a bit spicy. The over all space of this restaurant has a very cozy feel to it. It is very small and it would be smart to call ahead of time and make a reservation. My table was ready as soon as I got there; and my party and I arrived 15 minutes early. It's not a place where you'd take a group of 15, maybe 4-6 at most.

My visit to this restaurant yesterday managed to effectively ruin my appetite. I was there with 5 friends and we took up three small tables. There was a small line waiting so the waitresses kept pushing us to order faster. After doing so they said that we had not ordered enough as they wanted each one of us to order one of the lunch specials. One waitress declared that she would give us 15 minutes to eat. When they brought out my soup it was filled half way in an obvious attempt to kick us out quickly. They also "forgot" our drinks. The food (especially the pad Thai) made me wish that they had saved some of their sweetness for their staff. Being a group of teenage girls DOES NOT mean that they can treat us less than other paying guests.

Ordered shrimp pad thai at 11:30 a.m., given a 15-minute wait time. Arrived at 11:50, food not ready, order-taker answers the phone and talks for a few minutes. Charges me full price because it's take-out (half-price noodles and rice is their weekday lunch special). Takes my money and tells me to sit down - as if I weren't on a schedule? Goes to the kitchen, comes back twice to assist a table of customers, and finally comes out with my order. I get back to work and there is no napkin or fork in the bag. Guess he thought I would eat with my fingers or something. The dish was good. Medium spicy was plenty hot, and I do like spicy dishes. The shrimp were about one inch in size and not proportional to the amount of noodles or the price ($10.65). If I'm paying half price, sure, give me 6-8 little shrimp. Otherwise, use bigger shrimp or put in more. Not sure I would bother again, as they didn't really bother themselves for me.

Amazing prices, amazing food, wonderful staff, long hours, good location. Only problem is no dining room and only takes cash. Which is probably a good thing because I would no broke and eat three meals there. And they have food that meet three meals. It's next to my work so super convenient. Today I had a falafel pita sandwich. It was INCREDIBLE. I'm unsure if I'm just starving, but I'm pretty sure it's the best falafel I've had in the states. Usually I get some soup or another. They're all good. All of them. I haven't had a gyro yet, but I bet it'll be killer. I'll let you know. Anyway, since there are no Mediterranean food trucks around here, so this place is the next best thing. Go here if you're hungry and want a good deal. And carry around cash like some sort of caveman.

I was just visiting Burlington a few weeks ago for their annual Jazz festival. Manhattan Pizza is right at the end of church street. i sat outside for hours sipping on great VT made beers. I could hear all the great music, without being in a huge crowd. They have a great seating area outside. I tried the cheezy garlic bread, and they were right, ITS HUGE! The people were very nice, the atmosphere was casual and relaxed. The bartender was great, the food was great, all in all i would say if your're in Burlington, dont go to any other pizza place until you try this one first

This place was awesome! i was just in town visiting a few friends and we all went out for dinner and some drinks one night. we liked it so much we went there every night of my stay (3 days). The bar staff was so wonderful and helpful, especially for a first timer to Burlington, VT. I had a nice conversation with the bartender about what do around town. The food was great and ready fast. They had something like 20 beers on tap, most of them all Micro Brews from VT. If youre a beer lover, you will LOVE this place. I would and will go back to this place every time i come to the town. Best Place Around.

The food was a step above duck food and the owners (i assume they were the owners) were big a$$holes. I couldn't stand to work there the way they talked about the workers and patrons. Food should be enjoyable. This place wasn't.
Fast, easy, delicious, and knowledgable. I'm celiac and felt completely at ease enjoying the healthiest "fast food" lunch I've ever had. Yummy!

For what they offer they are really good. We had mahi curry and creamy soup. Both tasty delicious. They have few tables . Most people take out. They has this Brooklyn hipster vibe and food philosophy in the place and the food. Most foods even in places that advertise themselves as healthy taste taste to some degree unhealthy salty. No exception here! I find the food a bit salty. Above what level of being considered healthy. But it could be just me. If you want a quick fix of reliable, not over priced food in there area with no frills , this is the place.
This place is just what the neighborhood needs. The Balkan Burger was delicious. Eggplant Provie had tons of flavor. Easy to order. Friendly service.

Not sure how I feel about this place, the food wasn't that bad, but I felt like my loco moco (moco means snot in Spanish btw) been served on a jailhouse tray or a disposable airplane tray. Overall, it wasn't bad, the service was friendly, and there were plenty of healthy options. Fresh? Not sure, but their outer space cooker heats it up nicely!
Came here for dinner, sat outside on the patio. BYOB. Great food, decent service considering they were running in and out. Nice setup. Quiet. Recommended.

Philadelphia's Gay bars can be cliquey and exclusive, even though it's Philadelphia and the gay population is fairly small. The atmosphere also promotes a certain pressure to be "on" whenever" you're out. You must be dressed well and on the prowl and sporting a bubbly mood. The Venture Inn damands none of this. It's dark, caters to a mature crowd who only want some peace, a drink and conversation. Socially, it is an oasis from the rest of Philly's gay scene. The bartenders are attentive, good natured and pour a good drink. The food is less than stellar and the price doesn't merit it, but no place is perfect.

So I was super pumped to try this place since it was sold to me as Japanese Soul Food. But I'm guessing it wasn't the traditional soul food I was thinking of (i.e. fried chicken, ribs, mac n' cheese, etc.) and more so along the lines of Japanese comfort food. It's a small place and definitely reminded me of Japan but when I tasted the Kara-age...I just wasn't impressed. It was just OK. I was over at Jin Ramen earlier that day and tried the boneless fried chicken, which was super delicious. My other friends really liked their food so maybe I just didn't order the right thing. If there's a next time, I'll try the Chicken Nanban.

The ramen here was so yummy. It was exactly what I needed for lunch to kill my hangover. I got the miso and it made me so so happy! The noodles were nice and chewy, the broth was rich and flavorful, the egg was a nice touch. I just wish the pork was a little more tender, though the flavor was great. The chef/owner (? i think) came out to ask my opinion about my ramen and seemed like such a nice guy. I'll definitely be back.

Let's face it, Philly is severely lacking in the ramen department.  And by lacking, what I really mean is that it doesn't really exist. Enter: Nom Nom Ramen.  For ramen lovers out there then, this restaurant should be somewhat of a nice surprise.  Except that it's really not all that.  It's not terrible, but i certainly wouldn't characterize this as good ramen. The broth is mediocre and lacks depth of flavor.  The noodles are even worse - it's like they threw in spaghetti noodles and called it ramen. The char sui is flavored fine but is a little tough. Since there's really no other ramen joints, it might satisfy your ramen craving.  But don't expect something you'd get in LA or NYC.

Had my first lunch at Nom Nom today with my daughter.  We both had the Shiro with a poached (actually a soft boiled) egg.  It was very good!  Other people have complained the noodles were too al dente, but we thought they were just right.  The broth was flavorful and not overly salty.  The pork belly was not as tender or as smoky as Ramen Boy's, but also not as fatty.  We got there at 11:45 to beat the crowds and easily secured a booth, though it did fill up quickly as the lunch hour got underway.  The soup was ready in about five minutes and at less than $9 for a large, I felt it was good value. Service was very friendly.  The K-pop was a fun element!  WIll try the spicy miso next time!  All in all, cheaper, better and closer (for me, at least) than Ramen Boy!

Whenever I crave ramen, I would get my fix in Edgewater or NYC... but considering the distance and my laziness, I'd rather stay home. Just when I was about to lay in bed, I suddenly remembered news of a ramen joint opening up in center city. Might as well try it out, right? I ordered a bowl of karai with egg. Compared to other places I've gotten ramen, Nom Nom simply isn't the same. It's all about the type of noodles and broth... Noodles were different and on the tough side. It's not like the type of noodles I would encounter whenever I order ramen. the broth here lacked oomph and seemed kind of boring. It didn't taste spicy to me at all. The pieces of pork weren't bad, though. Aside from that, the staff were very friendly. One of the kitchen staffs said hello to me as I paid for my meal. Compared to Philly's standards, I guess the ramen here isn't bad? I think the prices are a bit on the high side.... But if you want the real deal, venture to NY or northern Jersey.

Decent ramen in center city. The environment is pretty casual and you order and pick your own seating, no service whatsoever. Cash only, so remember to bring cash. Went there with a friend on a weekday evening and had to wait a bit to be seated. Overall, I would say the food is decent. We ordered the spicy ramen Karai but it wasn't all that spicy. The noodles were on the thicker side. I have to agree with the other comments that the portions are not on the generous side and it is pricey for what you get. The portions were small and even with the added portions, the meat and broth seem to be little. I would go back when I want to get ramen but do not want to go to NYC but that would be pretty much it, not so much for the restaurant.
We had the spicy ramen here. It was heavenly. I was worried it wouldn't be open because it says "good for lunch," but it was open for dinner too.

we came here on a weekday afternoon. they are still in their soft opening phase so they were only serving the first 50 I believe. The sitting area is very clean and simple, it was really cozy for lunch or catching up with friends, but I wouldn't come here with a date, it too simple, unless that's what you are looking for. This is a place that could easily become a regular spot, unfortunately too far from where I lived. We got the regular sized Shoyu & Karai ramen and pork buns. The Shoyu is a soy sauce tonkotsu broth served with pork belly, fishcake, bamboo, kikurage mushrooms, scallions & seaweed. I loved it! It was not salty at all (which some soy sauced ramen does) and it was flavorful but not overwhelming.  Karai is their only spicy broth, have the same ingredients as Shoyu with "nom nom sauce" drizzled on top. I only tasted the broth. To me, its the kind of spice where it starts off burning slowly and then grows in your mouth. Not a real big fan of spiciness, so to me, it was HOT spicy. To my friend, who loves spice said it was just right. The pork bun can be worked on a little bit more. I think it didn't taste as crispy as it should. It could have been more tasty. Over all, I liked it and I will definitely return for some more!

I was just in here for the first time tonight and walked right back out. I was by myself and although the restaurant was less than half full, the hostess wanted to stick me at this strange table in the window that looked like it was there for decoration, certainly not for eating. When I gave her a surprised look, she volunteered that they would certainly clean it up for me (since it was covered in dust). I don't know what was wrong with the many empty tables that were empty in the actual restaurant. I told her not to bother and I walked out. I drove over to Lalibela, which is where I go with my husband and kids about once a week. (Since they were at an event, I decided to venture away from the tried and true. Big mistake.) Lalibela had a line out the door so I guess their food, as well as their service and attitude, is better. I'll be sticking with Lalibela from now on.

I've been to Walia several times now and can confidently say it's my favorite Ethiopian spot in North Jersey. I've had much of the food on the menu and all of it has been great so the only way I'll get through this review is to list my favorites. On the appetizers side I'm a fan is the Yetimatim Fit (diced tomatoes, jalapeño peppers, onions mixed with Injera and seasoned with olive oil and lemon) and Sambusa (Pastry shells filled with chopped prime beef or lentils mixed with onions, scallions, garlic and Jalapeño pepper and herbs). With the Sambusa I'm partial to the beef. That remind me, Walia has great options for meat-a-tarians and vegetarians.   On the entree side, I always prefer lamb if I could get it and Walia delivers on that.  My favorite is the Lega Tibs (Sautéed Lamb cubes with Ethiopian spices and cooked with onions, tomatoes, garlic and seasoned butter).  It truly is delicious!   I usually eat here with a group of people and we eat family style where everything comes out on a shared plate. It's a great way to try everything Walia has to offer and traditional at that. I wouldn't call myself a coffee drinker by any stretch but I make an exception for the coffee here since the aroma alone is enough to get me to change my mind. It is truly delicious and shouldn't be missed. It's a BYOB which in my mind is always a good thing since many places over charge for wine where by the glass basically costs the same as you can purchase the entire bottle in the real world. With that in mind, I recommend finding a good honey wine to complement the authentic experience you will no doubt get here.

This place is AWESOME. The service is quick and attentive, and they were unbelievably accommodating to my gluten intolerance. Unlike other places that require 24 hour notice to make gf injera (made with teff rather than wheat), Walia will make fresh gluten free injera as long as you call about an hour before you plan to arrive. The gluten free version costs an extra dollar, but it's totally worth it. The food is delicious. We ordered the meat combination for two, and the serving size was perfect. We were stuffed and happy by the end :-) HIGHLY recommend.

So the fun of korean bbq, is meeting with your friends and having conversations while cooking the meet. Not at this place! The waitress stood over our grill while preparing the meat, sternly moderating the garnishes (so as you do not eat them before the meal is ready). Then she rations out the meat around the table. Really? really? we as a whole can not decide what we want to eat? Seriously? We ate in silence... it was not FUN

I went here with a few friends and I was not impressed.  While the food was decent, my major problem was the lady that helped us.  And by "helped" I mean didn't let us enjoy our food and wouldn't leave us alone. I understand that a little help is needed for people that have never done Korean BBQ, but I really didn't appreciate having some random lady piling food on my plate. I am fully capable of picking what I want to eat when I want to eat it.  And yes, we were a party of 4 white people and 2 asian people, but maybe ask first before deciding that we had no idea what we were doing. If I ever desire to have Korean BBQ again while in Parsippany, I will go to Hwang Bu Ja instead.

Worst dining experience in a long time. Enough to write a review. From start to finish: Disorganized, not particularly friendly staff. A mumbled 'what are you ordering?' and cashier girl walking away while I am in the midst of ordering. Do we sit, can we sit, do you bring us our food...? Unclear. I guess you get brought the food. Backyard is pretty. Food. Came without silverware, firstly. The waiter cheerfully brought us some upon request. My order was put under the wrong person's name, so the disoriented gentleman was wandering around for some time, calling another woman's name. Food arrived, with portions fit for an anorexic bird. $10 for a few chopped beets and a cold over easy egg???? Absolutely ludicrous. $10 for a piece of toast with a scrambled egg on top of it and two asparagus??? Insulting. Then, finding random bits of pork in my meal. I am a vegetarian. After bussing our own table, I let the person at the front know this. She stared blankly at me as I repeated 'there was meat in my meal. No, not BEET, MEAT'. "Oh, like bacon?" "Yes, like bacon". "Oh, I guess they didn't write that on the board...." WHAT?!?!?! That is the reply? Firstly, NO, secondly, if there was supposed to be bacon, the 5 nubbins of pork I pushed to the side of my plate would be a paltry amount to claim that the dish comes with bacon. No apology, nothing. I left hungry, and pissed off. I should have trusted my gut and stuck with new local business that are welcoming and community oriented, like Express Yourself Barista. That is what Bushwick is about.

I would literally eat here everyday if I could. Everything I've ever had here has been spot on. Every time I order take out I get extra green sauce and put it on everything I eat for a week. I have also fallen in love with their guava and cheese empanadas. I dream about my meals here.

Best Sophie's Location! Love the Shrimp with Garlic Sauce & Grilled Chicken with Yellow Rice and Green Plantains! Get extra green sauce! Sophie's is a saving grace for the expensive TriBeCa area. Though, Sophie's is not consider cheap but it's a lot of food for 2 meals. It is most affordable considering the neighborhood it is in. My favorite dishes mentioned above is about $11 to $13 after tax. Shrimp with Garlic Sauce - Shrimps are marinated with this orange garlic sauce. The flavor is so rich and the shrimps are marinated very well. Though, the shrimps are not jumbo-sized but it's a decent size and it's a generous amount of shrimp (always more than 10, when I count it!). The semi-thick sauce goes great with their yellow rice. Their rice is flavorful to begin with and not dry at all! Though, it does have a strong garlic aroma and taste - probably not a good idea to eat it during lunch without your mouthwash! I highly recommend this dish! Grilled Chicken with two sides. This is part of their daily specials. Very generous with three large pieces of chicken breast. (You can get the Spicy Grilled Chicken breasts if you like spicy - trust me, it's spicy!) The chicken breasts are grilled to perfection, never burnt anywhere. It's tender and moist, most of the time. There has been a few times it was a bit dry. The grilled chicken breasts are seasoned well so every bite was exciting! The best thing about Sophie's is the green sauce that comes with everything you order! It is the best green sauce, ever! The spicy level tickles my tongue but not overwhelming. Sophie's make their own green sauce so it's very fresh! Great food, friendly, & quick service at this particular location. A definite 5-Stars in my book!

Amazing food, great service with friendly staff, and the sushi is all very fresh. Plus you can't beat their prices! Their regular rolls are 50% off and their specialty rolls are usually some percentage off. Definitely recommend the shrimp tempura roll - still hot when they bring it out! Even on weeknights it gets pretty crowded. It's in a mini-strip mall and there's usually parking in the small lot next to it, but street parking is also fine. Whenever I visit a friend in Bloomfield we always head there for dinner!
Sushi is very good and a very detail menu which help to pick some awesome rolls. I love the staff very help full and great deal for the sushi

best tacos ever wait staff awesome.  super friendly. but the food is incredible, everything tastes so fresh. i always leave feeling full but not weighed down.  i have never had anything i didnt love from this place but you definitely can't go wrong with tacos.  The chicken and el pastor are my favs but they are all delicious. ive never had a problem with them mixing and matching tacos too.   do yourself a favor and dont miss out on the home made beverages at the counter.  A rice drink and a jimaica (hibiscuss flower tea) make regular appearances and both are well worth it.

My go to Mexican in south Philly. I would have give 5 stars, but they are so slow that its hurts! I passed by there and order for pickup, I waited almost an hour for fish taco's and quesadilla.. but its was SO worth it. when I ordered delivery it was even worse.. but again - worth it. everything is fresh and the food is delicious and flavorful. Its inexpensive, their chips and salsa are great, its byob and their portions are huge. what there not to love?

Unbelievable I came to this Turkish Restourant with my family I was surprise about quality of the food and service it was so tasty food we had lamb Doner chicken Doner with rice and hummus lentil soup it came with fantastic Turkish style warm bread and they gave us free Turkish tea very authentic style tea and they have clean restroom i recommend if you are in that area try there food

First, just wanted to say that the food here is great and I really wanted to give at least four stars because of the generous check in offer, but when I was there the service was lackluster and slow.
