Came here around 8 pm after a dance class and there just happened to be a seat open and noticed the check in offer, so I took advantage of that sat down and ordered. The place is a little cramped, but has around 7 tables that can fit twos and fours. The tables topped with the clear hard plastic cover, but the person who cleaned the table didn't do a good job because of leftover scraps. So I ordered a lamb shish kebab wrap and the lamb meat was very fresh and not too game-y. Also, the check-in offer is amazing because the dessert portion is huge and it's pretty tasty. You can either get baklava, rice pudding, or almond pudding. The reason why I'm only giving 3 stars was because service was way too slow. From getting my order, dessert, check, and food, everything was too slow. I had to be proactive is getting the things I need. Also, I finished half my wrap wondering why it wasn't really flavored. Then, my waiter said he forgot to give me the sauces that came with it... He was nice, but he seemed to be dazing off or something. Literally asked for dessert and check, which could have definitely been done at least within 3 minutes (considering there weren't any other customers he needed to tend), but it took more than 10.

Great find! Upon entering, we first noticed how beautifully the place is decorated. We had a lovely table for 6 by the window and we were first greeted at our table by the chef, who happens to be the owner's son. The food was delicious--we all enjoyed what we had ordered! They also can make many of the menu options gluten-free, as is indicated on the menu. While we were eating, the owner, Dominic, came over to our table; we enjoyed chatting with him hearing his stories about when he worked at the Helmsley Palace Hotel in NYC. Very warm, friendly staff and great food. We'll be back for sure!
Excellent food, staff was very attentive.  I really enjoyed my experience here and will be back again.
Wonderful place!!!! Dishes are always fresh and the fish never over cooked.  Save room for the awesome Italian Cheese Cake!

What a perfect place to plan a birthday celebration! Mario, of course, was fantastic JUST like the yelp reviews said. He was very accommodating and helpful in planning the menu and timing of the SURPRISE party for my boyfriend. The food was amazing, but mostly the homemade spaghetti was a HUGE HIT! Everyone was raving about this hidden gem. I'm so glad for planning my boyfriends 29th birthday party here. 27 people came out (we pretty much had the whole place to ourselves) and it was the most fun and intimate dinner party ever!!!!

What a great place and delicious meal!  The owner Mario makes you feel at home from the beginning. The ambiance is very nice. The food (pasta, etc) is all made from scratch and is delicious. Great variety as well. They have a parking lot too where they valet for free. I had a the veal chop special that was amazing. Period. Homemade wine was delicious and appetizers and desserts following suit. They were also very accommodating to food requests, saying, and I quote, "sure thing, just tell me what you want and we'll make it for you just like you like it, we can do anything you want" to one of our party who had specific food needs. Very reasonably priced for the level of food you get. I will definitely go back here and highly recommend it to anyone looking for legit Italian food!

Right off the bat we had reservations for 8pm and were told rather rudely by the hostess/waiter/owner Mario we might have to wait about 20-30 minutes I was not happy I asked if we could wait at the bar and was no it was occupied with someone eating there. This restaurant is really small and we had to wait by the front door the alternative was waiting outside in the freezing cold. Mario came back about 10 minutes later and offered a small table by the bar that had become available we accepted just to get out of the front door. We were offered the specials but never asked if we wanted drinks so I had to flag someone down to place a drink order. I ordered the stuff clams and for the entree the fruiti di mare which were good my fiancée ordered the mozzarella and the pasta with sausage and broccoli which she really didn't  care for. We needed to flag someone down for just about everything drinks, desserts and the check so overall the food was ok but not worth the hassle of having to grab someone just to get basic service. This establishment would be served with just hiring a real waiter and letting Mario go to an office hopefully off site and let someone who knows what they are doing to manage the front of the house.

I went on opening night, and except for the wait, which was expected, everything was awesome. Great service. Have to get that out of the way- my water was refilled frequently, I was checked on for my beer without the server being obnoxious... perfect (thanks Evan!). The food came out in a reasonable time, considering how busy it was. The food was delish. Got the margherita pizza (foreign to me as I'm Texan), and the meatballs. Holy crap those meatballs are AWESOME! The owner told us that they were unfortunately not his recipe, but a grandmother's recipe. I say, no prob. Makes for delicious. You have to try them- they're only $11. As far as the pizza, it's reasonable prices as the pizzas are about 12" and they have a really interesting selection (cheeseburger to mac n'cheese to gahlic) and this includes red/white sauce. So basically you can get away with one pizza for 2 people, and get a side order if one of you is especially hungry. They also have a tasty looking selection of entrees/salads other than pizza. And nothing is over $20, as far as I can recall. Their beer selectiom is pretty nice, I just hope it rotates. I got a Brooklyn Chocolate Stout and SO got an Allagash White, so basically some solid contenders. I hope this place does great, and I'll be back when it's not opening night to try some more of their interesting pizza combinations.

We decided to go to Birra last night since we usually spend months listening to friends tell us about the new places they've eaten while we just say, "Yeah! We keep meaning to go there..."  So we wanted to get in on the Birra thing from the ground floor, considering it's only a hop skip and a jump away. When we first walked in, the owner greeted us but then turned and was gone, delivering pizzas to a table.  We stood awkwardly for a few minutes, not knowing whether to seat ourselves or to wait, until finally someone came around.  Ok, so not the greatest welcome.  Once we sat down though, the servers were very friendly and attentive. The beer list I thought was totally adequate for a pizza place, and the prices were in line with the other neighborhood drinking spots.  Of course, considering the place is called "Birra" the beer selection wasn't nearly as extensive as, say, POPE, but they had plenty of good choices.   We ordered the porchetta panini, which was tasty but not amazing.  We also ordered the gaahlic pizza, which was pretty damn good.  Perfect crust.  I'm not normally big into fancy thin crust pizzas, but this was definitely delicious.  Again, prices were very reasonable, considering I tend to be pretty cheap. Now for the bad news.  This place is WAY too small for what it's trying to do.  There's cozy and then there's just plain cramped, and this place is cramped.  We sat at a table on the far side of the restaurant, my husband sat on the wall side and we squished the table into him as far as we could, and I pulled my chair in as far as I could, but still my chair got kicked almost every single time anyone walked past behind me, which was about a hundred times.  The servers are whooshing by everywhere and have to constantly duck in and out between the tables to let people pass through the teeny aisle between the tables and the bar.  The bar seems way too big for the room or something, and add people and bulky coats to the mix, and it feels uncomfortably tight.   Unfortunately that could be the big drawback of this place, because being bumped and kicked all over the place really made for an unrelaxing dinner.  We kind of just had one beer, ate quickly and then left.   Another thing is the (what I consider) unnecessary presence of three huge TVs.  This isn't really the type of place that I would expect to have a bunch of TVs, and it made for a weird mix of upscale and sports bar.  More importantly I think it made it feel less cozy and even more cramped. I'm not giving up on Birra, because there were lots more delicious looking options on the menu, but I think next time we'll try sitting at the bar for a little more breathing room.

A little late on this review but.... I went on opening night to Birra.  I had read about it on Foobooz and some other blogs and didn't have anything to do that night so I figured I would check it out.  I feel like I was one of the only people there that didn't know the owner Gordon, however, I was still treated like royalty. Now it was opening night so I am sure everyone was on their best behavior...but the staff were super nice and everyone seemed like they really wanted to know your opinions.   We figured that the house specialty seemed to be the pizza, so we ordered 2 pizzas and split them.  We wanted one red and one white so we went with the Gaaahlic and the Mac N Cheese. Both were very good but I think I liked the Mac N Cheese more.  The Gaaahlic was very sweet which was unexpected and both good and bad.  Good in that it was different and interesting...but personally I do not like my pizza to be sweet at all so I was not a huge fan of that. It was also annoying that about 5 people in the restaurant came up and asked what we ordered and when we told them they all said the same cheesy line "oh be glad you are both eating that because it will give you really bad garlic breath."  Yea no shit, I ordered a pizza called Gaaahlic, I didn't think my breath would smell like roses. Anyway, back to the pizza.  The Mac N Cheese was VERY good. I liked the fact that it was not super greasy or too cheesy and the breadcrumbs added the perfect touch. My only complaint about this restaurant is its size.  The strip of tables leading up to the bathroom is way too narrow., it is almost impossible for more than one person to squeeze in there at one time.  Otherwise it was enjoyable and I will definitely be back.

Birra - good to have another fun selection on passyunk ave. Mussels were very good   Odd layout prevents you from taking in the whole scene.  Pizza ingredients and crust were great. Lacked flavor though which seems odd. Red pizza sauce is bland. Service was very good and apple cherry cobbler-sweet- in a good way. I'll try Birra again.  But $10  for glass of (so-so)wine, really?

Its a stylish gastro pizza pub ala Stella, their white pizzas has creme fraiche (giggle) and they offer truffle oil among their many toppings (eye roll).  I guess the pizza is NY style, small and crisp. The dining room is cramped and the chair legs and bar stools flare out which means getting around or dining is tight and jostly.  We saw many well behaved babies last night and it was pretty loud in there, poor servers have to practically yell. I did not see TVs, but I hear there are 3. Their beer selection is good/great and a dining companion who'd been to Italy liked their selection of Italian beers. A recent write up said their "scampi shrimp" was the "best shrimp EVER." I found them overcooked, greasy and steep at $18. I would not get them again, I would not recommend them and on return visits i will avoid all the small plates, except maybe salad. Pizzas comes in one size and start at $6, toppings extra. Family style small plates also available. Based on our experience I view this place a cramped and stylish a small step up from the perfectly good pizza and beer across the street. Amazing, that a new place can make any other place on P'shunk seem open and airy. Lastly, the menus has punctuation issues where a "-" is used both to connect 2 ideas "oompaloompa pizza - red pizza with orange meatballs" and as comma in the list of toppings "basil - garlic" Does that mean they have basil AND also garlic or that basil/garlic mixed together is one topping? Style over substance.

We stopped by here for a quick, no-thrills bite to eat one night. Bueno Y Sano had friendly service, good prices, and good food. I don't see myself specifically seeking it out in the future, but if you're looking for a quick, decent, fresh burrito, it's worth the stop. I had the Spicy Chipotle Chicken burrito, which wasn't very spicy. The flavor was good, but not anything exceptional. And to the reviewer (Christopher B.) that docked them a star for not having table service: really? It seems to me that type of service would not be a good fit for this eatery.

Just saw the guy (black shirt and glasses) drop pizza in the garbage by mistake, grab it bare handed and throw it in the stove to serve customers. I brought it to his attention and he just shrugged his shoulders. Absolutely terrible and unacceptable. I walked right out.
Usually pretty good but left me on hold for 7 minutes then hung up without me placing an order. Rather unprofessional

Although we have eaten in D'Italia a number of times, this is my first review. A party of four dined here on Black Friday evening. After being seated, it took a good few minutes before our waitress approached the table, despite the fact that they were not at all busy. Other than that delay, the service was prompt and very business-like. Despite the fact that we were not negatively impacted, the (abundant) staff seemed more interested in socializing than serving. In any case, three of our entrees were served with a fresh and nicely presented salad; dressings were good. Hot, delicious rolls accompanied the meal, and were nicely browned. Meals ranged from a simple chicken panini, to stuffed rigatoni with shrimp, linguini with sausage, and stuffed shells (hot sausage on the side). All were very well-prepared, and the hot sausage was definitely "hot"! The ricotta filling of the shells was hot and velvety. All entrees were well-received and thoroughly enjoyed. Portions were generous, and the balance of two entrees were taken home. As a result, we did pass up the desserts. While I used to jokingly refer to D'Italia as a "glorified pizzeria", the consistently high quality food preparation defies that nickname. Good Italian fare will certainly be found in this BYOB establishment. Ample off-street parking, comfortable decor, and casual dress make this a place to go for good quality food when you want to get out, but not dress. The only thing I might suggest, is that the wait staff be encouraged to display a bit more warmth and friendliness, as befits an Italian restaurant. D'Italia merits a solid four-stars, and is well-recommended.

There used to be a couple of branch locations of Uncle Willie's closer to where I live that have subsequently closed due to a tough economy. Thankfully this location is still in business, and is well worth the drive. I have never had a bad meal from here, and over the years I do believe I've sampled everything their menu has to offer. Top notch barbecue that would make you swear you actually were south of the Mason-Dixon line.

We were in the area looking at our puppy and we used yelp to find a good place to eat around here. We saw 4 and a 1/2 stars and said lets try this. Upon arriving even the restaurant looked questionable, but we said lets try it, it might be really good. This good was the worst food we've ever had. Big disappointment! I thought by the reviews it would be much better than this. We had the pulled pork with mash potatoes and Mac n cheese everything was gross and cold. Honestly fast food would've been better!

I've been back 3 times since writing my original review and every time it has been wonderful. Becoming my favorite nice restaurant in New York- I love the lunch soups! And the service is by far some of the best I've ever received. Will always make time for a visit here when I'm in the city.
Good

Beautiful interiors and food to go with that! The service was exceptional - my silverware was changed without my realizing! Seamless. The zucchini soup is delicious - with ribbons of zucchini infused with citrus. Cheers!

Went there today for RW but end up choosing the 42 dollars 2 course option instead of the regular 25 dollars 3 course option, the portions were reasonable for a "fancy" restaurant let's put that way and I had the caviar for appetizer and the halibut fish for entree both were fantastic, I had halibut many times and today I definitely had one of the best if not the best halibut ever. Caviar was great too. Staff was so informative and friendly, great option for RW or for any special occasion. Highly recommended.

Went with a friend during restaurant week. Three courses were just enough for us as girls. I ordered chicken as the main course. The chicken was specially handled with crispy and juicy tastes. Elegant environment! Great service! Btw, I like that I need to dress up to meal (;

1.  The restaurant is exceptionally clean. 2.  The service was excellent (we went on a Thursday night).  They were prompt, fast, and helpful. 3.  My husband and I ordered the hummus to start.  It was clearly from scratch, as were the pitas.  Delicious.  We shared the mixed grill and all the meats were seasoned well and cooked perfectly.  The rice was good and the cucumber dip was tasty as well.  We had seen another patron order this dessert (it sounds like galactoboutyka?) It's like baklava stuffed with custard..  we usually skip dessert but this looked too good to pass up..  we were so glad we tried it because it was awesome.   We will definitely be back!
I've always been a satisfied customer at Murphy's.

Fantastic restaurant:   excellent service, great food, super ambience!  I had the Butternut Squash & Ricotta Cheese ravioli - OMG, I haven't been this excited about a meal in a long, long time.  The flavors and textures within this dish are not to be believed.  Hold on to your knife and fork, your taste buds are in for a terrific ride!!!

Happy hour deals can't be beaten.  Half priced wines are a steal on M, W, and F.  Baked goat cheese marinara is worthy of licking out of the bowl.  The Fri night live music makes you think you're in a real college town.   Stick with happy hour, wines, and frequent the bar.  This is always a good detour in Princeton.

My husband and I love Salt Creek Grill. the food is great, the servers are always attentive, and the atmosphere is casual and nice. The restaurant always smells amazing from the wood fire grill, and there are fireplaces and comfy seating outside.   The bar is a fun place for happy hour from work, and the restaurant itself is a great place for lunch or dinner.   My go to is either the House salad with grilled chicken, or the salmon dinner.  My husband loves the ribs and both of us love the fries! If you are in Princeton, this is a great place to have lunch or dinner.

My husband and I recently went to Salt Creek Grille in Princeton with some other couples on our 'without kids' night out. Our server Heather was excellent and impressed us all by remembering all our special orders without taking notes! Our food was delicious and Heather was very attentive to our table. I recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for delicious food, great drinks and great service!

This is such a cool restaurant. I just love the ambiance of it. Beautiful architecture and a nice mood in general. Sometimes they have nice music. The food is very unique and delicious. I recommend the brisket sandwich and the  roasted squash and ricotta ravioli. Also the pork chop is great if you go for dinner. I had my engagement party here as well and everyone loved it. We frequent this restaurant.

After a 3 year long hiatus I found myself here with my family for Easter dinner. Our large party of 8 was seated comfortably in the main dinning area. The only issue I had was 2 people from our party were about 15 mins late and they would not seat us until the the whole party was present. This rule is dumb. The 6 of us sat around the lobby area waiting when we could have sat down and started ordering drinks. Good thing they have a lovely waiting area and outside seating. At first, we were disappointed to find the regular menu was not available and we could only order from the Easter Dinner special menu available for that night only. We were pleasantly surprised with the menu selection, though it was limited. We ordered a table full of apps and each of us a entree. Everything was delicious. Everything. The staff was attentive. There was no live band playing which made the atmosphere more enjoyable (the acoustics in this building are horrible). Im hoping that my next visit will be as enjoyable and the food equally as good. Otherwise, I'll see you next Easter SCG.

I HAD a reservation for 6 people and wanted to increase it to 7 people.. I received a comment of they needed to "ask" if that was possible.. for 1 person?!?!? then I was instructed that I needed to change my dining time to 45 min later to accommodate 1 extra person.. just 1... I canceled the reservation.. asked to speak with the manager, that never got on the phone.. I will NEVER dine there.. and will deter all who suggest it..

Whether you're looking for a nice dinner for date night or looking for something different for a night out with friends this place does the trick. Food is delicious and if you want to try something other than a  plain old beer or vodka club ask for bartenders Steph or Jackie, they know what they're doing!

Not impressed. Service was actually ok but the food left much to be desired so more of a comment to the chef. Not bothered about price but dude... Get your act together. The ravioli was tasteless or worse - sweet.

We had trouble finding a dinner spot near our hotel and stumbled into Salt Creek Grille.  We were very pleasantly surprised.  We were a bit concerned when we seemed to be shuffled off to the back dinning room and told that the main dinning room was full since there seemed to be some table available - not sure what that was about.  Nevertheless, we had access to the full menu and best of all we had a great waiter - Marc.  Marc was very attentive and accommodating.  His goal was clear, to make sure we had as best an experience as possible.  The menu selection was not huge but more than adequate and the food was very tasty.  The tuna burger was super.

Went here for happy hour with some work colleagues last night . Place was pretty crowed but we managed to get what ended up being private seating outside! Drinks were great, apps too! Out waiter Marc was fantastic ! Very attentive as well as funny ! We will be going back soon and hope we are lucky enough to get Marc as our waiter again
I love the atmosphere and my wine glass was always full! Thanks so much Scott, my friends and I will be back again soon!

What a great place. Take something relatively simple, like the chicken finger, and turn it into something awesome. I really only have one complaint about Sticky's Finger Joint, and that would be the pricing, which is a little on the expensive side. Regardless, I have no problem shelling out the required cash for some of their delicious chicken fingers. The wasabi fingers are out of this world. So good. Also, the staff there is incredibly friendly and hospitable, which only adds to the greatness. Give this place a try immediately.
Fantastic local merchant. Food was excellent as was the service.  The owner introduced himself, and quite frankly made the experience. I would definitely return, and recommend it to friends.
Pretty delicious. I had the Bada Bing, which was off the charts. I thought the price was a little expensive when I ordered, but the food was pretty gourmet, and I left feeling happy and satisfied.
Overpriced.  Food was not good.  Owner was arrogant and rude.  Felt bad for the staff.
Don't bother!  Over-priced & mediocre food, with a crazy manager to boot.

I was really excited to come here, so much that I brought 3 co-workers. The food is good, but not good enough that poor management is completely overlooked. They were out of every variety of coleslaw except for some sub-par bruschetta, and also out of green bean fries at 1:00 on a thursday afternoon. Forgot our drinks, credit card machine was down... Whatever, this can be overlooked - I open up my box of 3 chicken strips, there were 2 and a little crumb. Getting a little frustrated at this point I asked for them to bring me the 3 strips that I ordered - dude comes out of the kitchen, tells me something about how the chicken is free-range and really expensive and refuses to do anything about me being unhappy. Here's the deal dude - if you're doing a crap job of keeping your business basics together, at least appease the customers so they can leave happy. I won't come back to your restaurant not because the food isn't good, it's because you're a douche bag that told me about how the chicken is organic and expensive instead of just fixing the problem. Your rusty tables left orange marks all over my pants.

You could give me a million years to come up with a name for a chicken strip place and it wouldn't be as good as the one they decided on. Sticky's is so much more than a clever title though. Their fingers really will make you wet. (your mouth water that is) With flavors like salted caramel pretzel, wasabi, and the Bada Bing! which is basically a mozzarella stick with chicken stuffed inside it's the best strip experience I've ever had in my life. The staff is mostly cute and friendly girls and although it's not a bar, it's more fun than most I've ever been to. I won't go into specifics, but if you know what I'm talking about then you know what I'm talking about. Go to Sticky's or miss out on the experience of a lifetime.

Very creative... I liked salted caramel finger. It had everything, salt, sweet and meat (chicken). It could be dinner and dessert in one. Next, I remembered was wasabi...? It had Furikake, a savoury condiment in an individual sachet and sprinkle over rice, on it. The concept reminded me of JapaDog in East VIllage, anything everything on a hotdog. SFJ also put anything, everything on chicken strips. The small condiments were tasty and interesting but it was confusing which works which and most of the chicken was nicely well seasoned. I think I saw this place on Foodnetwork with Bobby Flay. He was helping this business to start...??

You wouldn't think much of the little shop if you walked past it but what waits inside is a delicious surprise!  Quality chicken and a number of tasty recipes. Most of them seem familiar but each has its own unique twist. My favs would be the Buffalo or Maple (aka chicken'n'waffles). Had the tempura green beans and sweet potato fries, also great and tried a number of the dipping sauces w/ the popcorn chicken, to many sauces to list but all were great. All in all fun and affordable spot for the Village/NYU.

My favorite place in Princeton! The relaxed eastern ambience combined with the friendliness of the owners make this place feel like a home away from home. You can come here any time of the day to work, drink tea, catch up with friends, listen to music, or play board games. Other highlights include free WiFi and a variety of seating areas - from cozy floor cushions to spacious wooden and glass tables in the back perfect for working or studying, to small two person tables ideal for catching up with friends. The food and teas/coffees are great (and definitely NOT overpriced) and the owners take extra care to make sure everything is perfect. If not (which is very rare), they will often bring a new meal free of charge. The ingredients are fresh and healthy - the owners make most of the food in the kitchen, and gather ingredients from around the world. The food is vegetarian, and while I am not vegetarian, I have loved all of the items so far. Customer service is amazing 5 star - extremely personal and accomodating, all the items are brought right out to your table, often by the owners themselves, inifinitely better than Starbucks or Small World. While some reviewers have complained that the teas take longer to make, that's only because of the care needed to freshly brew certain varieties of tea - if you're in a hurry, just ask which drinks are made faster. The owners are also very welcoming of feedback and actually make changes based on customer suggestions. In addition, Infini-T is not just a tea house, they also have many items for sale - Turkish coffee cups, scarves, spices, and other items gathered from around the world. The furniture is also imported from around the world. On many Friday nights, they have live music, making sure to incorporate a range of styles - jazz, country, folk, more exotic styles as well. Recently, they even had a bellydancing show. Everyone who I have brought to Infini-T has loved it and many have become regulars. I am here several evening per week and highly recommend it.

A great place to relax, chat, enjoy. Excellent selection of teas, fantastic decor. Highly recommended. Will make you feel traveling in exotic places while staying in the core of Princeton. Lovely place

Dinner on Saturday night was great! Grabbing a couple delicious margaritas at the bar during happy hour was a great way to start---strong, delicious, inexpensive, and fast!! Dinner was very good, though nothing to rave about. Atmosphere was fun and intimate and the service was great! I'd absolutely return--on a busy weekend night or on a weekday. There are lots of bars  nearby as well-good find!!

This review is for there Brunch: Came here on a group brunch birthday party. Had a great time. Drinks were free flowing for 2 hours. Included blended margaritas, mimosas and bloody marys. Food was a bit limited for the group (it was 10 people) but I understand they had to have a set menu for such a large group. Would definitely return.

Fonda was a treat! We came in with a party of 6 on a sunday evening. As I was checking in on Yelp with my gf we found out we just won a free dessert which was of course exciting! We ordered a duck dish and guacamole for apps which were both served promptly and were delicious. They beer menu met my needs with many of my south american favorites such as Tecate, Bohemia, Pacifico amongst others. I ordered the pulled pork entree with Yucatan which was incredibly juicy and flavorful topped with a hot pepper which may qualify as the hottest I ever tasted. Our waiter was very nice to deal with and very attentive . The decor and environment is hip and friendly and the bar was hopping with a fun but respectable crowd. A great group destination!

The atmosphere is very nice, the appetizers were great (we had the guacamole and the melted cheese - yum!) and so was the desert (tres leches). However, our entrees left a bit to be desired (enchiladas suizas, pechuga relleno) - a bit more bland than expected after the appetizers and superb margaritas. We will definitely give this place another shot!

I have visited many Portuguese restaurants in Newark and so far this is the worst. We had a Groupon and called ahead to reserve as requested.  Our table was waiting for us (one point) but after that it went straight downhill. Our waitress greeted us and we informed her of our Groupon.  She explained it to us very nicely and then told us it would be 45 minutes so you may want to order appetizers and showed us where they were on the menu. When you come hungry for a 7:30 PM dinner that is not what you want to hear.  45 minutes.  So of course now we are ordering appetizers and upping the bill.   We ordered a stuffed shrimp, fried calamari and stuffed mushroom all tapas size.  We were served our sangria and waited and waited and waited.  about 30 minutes later I said "we ordered the appetizers to hold us over for the meal, now they are going to arrive WITH the meal"   The usual apologies and they arrived.  All three were mediocre at best and one had to be returned and taken off the bill because the shrimp was not cooked.  After you got through the breading and toppings it was grey!  This shrimp was so tiny it was ridiculous and you can't even cook it thoroughly?  Waitress apologized and took it off the bill.  The other two extremely mediocre. Dinner arrives about right    At least 45 minutes or more.  It was a Paella for four.  The entire meal was overcooked, dried out, the rice was sticky and although I am not a paella expert I can just say it was pretty bad.  Two of our guests have had it many times and stated they would never come back here again. Dessert -  no thanks, we'll go elsewhere.  Left feeling very ripped off and disappointed.  From what I can see the reviews are all over the chart on this place so I can only believe that there are good and bad nights for this place, but there are too many other great places in Newark where the food is good every visit. Sangria - not bad Food - Bad Service - decent Wait Time - Bad Lesson Learned - Check back here at Yelp before buying Groupons

I have to agree with a lot of the other reviews about the service, or rather the lack of it.  We were here on Thursday night and the restaurant was not all that busy; there were four of us--two with a groupon ordered the paella and the other two ordered off the menu.  We also ordered a couple of appetizers; in all, not that difficult of an order for an experienced staff to handle, yet when the meals came the paella came first (after about an hour), the second order off the menu came 10 minutes later, and mine never came.  When I complained to the waiter (about 5 minutes later), I was told it would only be a few minutes more; 20 minutes later he showed up with a dish that presumed to be a tapa that had nothing to do with my order (ironically, my order was one of their daily specials, so I can't imagine it was that hard to convey to the kitchen staff).  At that time it was nearly 40 minutes since the paella came, so I told him to forget it; 10 minutes later (now nearly an hour after the first entrée was served), the manager came by the table and asked if something was wrong.  When I told him, he said that he could have my dish for me in 10 minutes (where was this speedy prep when it was ordered or after I asked for it again), but didn't buy it and told him to forget it, everyone had already finished eating.  We ordered the dessert (I needed to get something in my stomach after the wine) and were not charged for it (although I don't know if that was intentional or a waiter error), and the waiter also apologized and said he was removing the mandatory 20% gratuity (of course, I still tipped on what we received). My guess is that the waiter was new and didn't understand English well enough to take the order (although we took pains to point out everything on the menu), but the way it was handled was pretty ridiculous, culminating in the manager offering to get me my dinner after everyone finished.  Even on a busy night this would be unforgivable, but on a Thursday when many tables were empty (and perhaps rightfully so) it was unbelievable. The food, from what I tasted (a little paella and some appetizers) was pretty good, but certainly no better than many of the other restaurants in the area.  Parking is on the street, but generally available within a couple of blocks. All in all, if you are planning a dinner in Newark, try one of the many other Portuguese restaurants along Ferry and the adjoining streets.  Even with a groupon, this place is no bargain and is not worth the trip.

Vietnamese sandwiches never get old especially when they are close to home :) There are a few Vietnamese sandwiches shops near my apartment and it is always a challenge to find a new one that could outdo the other. Xe May does it for me. It took over a Bodywork parlor that used to occupy the same space and transformed it into a cute, woody and modern Vietnamese sandwich shop. The menu handwritten on the blackboard states that the sandwiches here are meant to be unrivaled and unique. I ordered the SuperClub Classic for lunch special, which includes a full sandwich, any drink you want and a bag of cookie or chip. I ordered the SuperClub Class sandwich, which is BBQ pork, pate  with pickles and cilantro and spicy mayo inside the lightly toasted baguette. It is a huge sandwich and the BBQ pork is thinly sliced and sweet. It is more like a smoked honey glazed ham than traditional shredded pork. However, the new interpretation is surely delicious! The pickle and cilantro really compliment the flavor and texture of the pork well. I am definitely coming back for more as the price in the area is unbeatable and the flavor is outstanding! next one I am going to try is lamb :)
Great place to eat! The lamb curry sandwich was delicious excellent blend of flavors. Very satisfying meal. The overall vibe of the shop was very warm and homely. Definitely will come back again!

What's so great about Vietnamese sandwiches? They're inexpensive and they're damn delicious. Xe May recently opened in East Village and it instantly stands out. The staff is friendly, the decor is refreshing, and I love the creative naming of their sandwiches, which are all names of motorcycles. The first time I went, I was recommended the Super Cub Classic, which is a sandwich made of BBQ Pork, Headcheese, Pork Roll, and Pate. This was excellent. The second time I went, I had the Hog, which I liked even more. This is made of Grilled Pork, Scallion Oil, and Fried Shallots, and it was absolutely scrumptious. That grilled pork was so very juicy and the scallion oil and fried shallots really completed the flavouring. My friend recommended that I try the Lam'bretta next time - yes, it's a lamb sandwich. I can't wait to go back.

4 1/2 Stars. Finally a Vietnamese banh mi place I can write home about. I mean, literally. I just wrote an excited email to my parents about this gem on St. Marks. They'll be happy to know that I'm not "starving" anymore (typical Asian parent fear - although how anyone can starve in New York City with the abundance of great food options is beyond me). Alright, weird fact about me: I hate bread. I find most breads to be boring; I am much more interested in the contents between the bread. Xe May's bread? GOOD! Crunchy, buttery, and dare I say a little savory? I've only tried the Hog and the Sidecar, but I am eager to come back and try the rest of the menu. The "Hog": grilled pork, scallion oil, fried shallots ($6) The sandwich was so good that I basically forced myself to keep eating even after I was full. Which obviously led me to change into stretchy pants (thank goodness for take out). I ate half of the sandwich, took a break, had a second wind and finished the other half. The pork was very well seasoned and of course the topping of shaved pickled carrots, cilantro, and peppers balanced the sandwich nicely. The Sidecar: grilled beefsteak, pineapple chutney ($6.50) I had a few bites of Brian M.'s sandwich because he kept "Mmmming" the whole time we were eating. Once again, the meat was well seasoned and the pineapple chutney's acidity paired with the creamy mayo spread on the bread was saliva inducing. Definitely something to "Mmmmm" about. Don't forget to make the cheesy "I'm enjoying my food oh so much" face that all the people on the Food Network love to do. I plan on coming back and trying the more traditional Super Cub Classic - pate and headcheese, yum. Don't forget to have them stamp your customer card. You get a cute girl on a motorcycle stamp (Xe May means motorcycle) for every $6 you spend. You get a free sandwich after the 10th stamp. Totally doable.

Not your typical banh mi as it's more fusion-ish but it was still pretty good. Only gripe would be the bun but I quickly forgot about it after feasting on the insides. And I got the chicken and the first sandwich. Forget what it's called. The summer rolls were also solid. The dude at the counter also reminds me of Eddie Huang, except friendlier and minus the ghetto. De la ghetto. Still makes me laugh. Definitely gotta try the tacos.
Always great food chicken fried chicken  or Ruben with steak fries they have alot of old candies  you can't find  anymore.great store for shopping

Stopped here on busy Saturday night for a relatively good meal.  Very crowded and as this is a chain, you can go in one of these restaurants all over America and have basically the same decor.  First there is the porch selling all kinds of rocking chairs, church benches, then is the country store in the entrance where you can buy all kinds of knick knacks, clothes, novelties, etc.  This is also where they take your name for the tables and lead you into the restaurant.   The restaurant carries on the rustic country store decor theme.  After being quickly seated near a window, the host gave us cutlery and menus.  Our waitress (looked like the server to table ratio was very high) came right over for our drink orders.  These were delivered quickly to our table and then we placed our food orders.  The menu is really a lot of comfort food and I ordered breaded shrimp and got 3 sides (usually you get two).   If I had timed placing our order and then getting the food I would say maybe ten minutes.  It seemed a tad long but only cause I was starving.  The food was good, average portions and really filled me up.  I could hardly finish my meal. Oh, least I forget....we also got a basket of corn bread and regular rolls with butter.  The rolls were piping hot, causing the butter to melt when put on the rolls. We did not get dessert as we were stuffed at that point.

It was very crowded but passed the time shopping in the country store where you can buy all kinds of knick knacks, and old fashion candy and beverages.  It has a rustic country decor and AMAZING pancakes!

Food is always the same so no complaints there. Had a server today that may have been new so he was a little hesitant. But overall a great family breakfast place. If you're planning on going on a weekend expect to wait but check out all the cool things in the country store.

Warm and cozy interior.  TV's were great to catch the games.  Service was spot on!!Awesome grilled pizza, yeah I said it!!  Shared one with my girlfriend, a hint of truffle oil was a nice touch on the mushrooms pizza.  She had the cranberry salad with a tofu burger added to it, not my taste but she loved it!  I had the filet on the bone, tender and juicy, could have cut it with a butter knife.  We split a berry parfait for dessert, nice finish to the evening.  We will be back for sure.

Lovely spot. Overly hyped ... we hard time getting reservations through open table for the time we wanted, but the restaurant wasn't filled at all on a Saturday evening. I arrived a few minutes early and the awkward hostess had me waiting till the exam time of our reservation, but the restaurant was hardly packed! Pleasant waitress with good knowledge of the menu. Allergy and gluten free accommodating with several menu items that are gluten free as listed and several more that could be slightly altered to be safe. Food was really quite delicious. Drinks were inconsistent but tasty. Will be back!

Kids pros- They were nice enough to put my husband, myself and the baby with the stroller in a an area away from the rest of the people in case the baby cried, also with enough room to place the stroller next to us. All that despite the fact that it was restaurant week! They have a super clean family room to change your baby. Kids cons-Elevator for the stroller was broken, no kids menu, although there are some very healthy options that could work for them such as the Brussels sprouts. If you go without kids: If you are a big fan of kale salad you will fall in love with theirs. If  you never fancied kale, it is your best shot to like it! It comes with some hazelnuts to die for and you can request some salmon on it to make it a an entree. Very creative cocktails! ONE OF MY TOP CHOICES FOR NEW HAVEN!

Love that they're happy hour goes until 8PM, even on a friday. As someone who is never out of work int time for happy hours, this was such a treat. Plus, you can even get specialty cocktails at happy hour, which is super awesome. Oysters on the halfshell were delectable, love west coast oysters. Pumpkin Gnochhi was so good, that my dining partner ordered another serving of it. Oh and the lamb sliders were fabulous. Love the decor in this place too, felt like a kitchen/reading room. Can only assume the Whitman then is attributed to Walt. Will definitely try this place again

So where do I start.....this place was so laid back. My boyfriend and I went after a friend recommended it....we got to sit in their backyard which was so peaceful. It was the perfect start to our date night. We had several happy hour specials which were awesome. The sever was good she was the only waitress for the back area and did a good job on checking on everyone. The food is AMAZING!! Their huge on organic local foods including their ketchup!! I have recommended this place to other couples price is great too!!!

This is a hidden gem... Amazing food, reasonable price and very nice decor...I am glad i found this restaurant today...  The front exterior of restaurant doesn't seem impressive as inside but once you walk inside you will be surprised.. Why you wait an hour at Penelope? I was not impressed with their foods at all....
Great food (we had the aged steak and the roasted chicken), the service was very friendly. We'll go again!

Nothing to exciting...food is ok in general...we were a group of 4....and apparently this was a little much for our waitress bc she continuously forgot about us.....in general will never come back thank god there are so any other options in NYC

This place was solid. Not too many options on the menu but definitely good choices. The service was friendly and our waitress had suggestions, which I liked! It just didn't blow me away. An excellent Bloody Mary though. Get one of those.

I have lived in the area for a few years and found this spot last week. A group of us sat at the bar and we had a great time with the bartenders, a girl and an Irish guy who were so funny and made us laugh all night! We had planned to just go for one drink for happy hour and ended up staying all night! We had a great time with some regulars too, who made us feel very welcomed! Happy Hour goes till 8, which is so great and rare! Get the Nocturnal cocktail! It is a gin and tea martini! Amazing! We had the fried pickles, lamb sliders, and 1.50 oysters. The decor is incredible. I am a designer myself and it is so obvious how well planned out the lighting and decor is. This place is definitely a hidden gem in Murray hill! Can't wait to go back and try their brunch menu out! I think they have live music on Wednesday and Thursday too in their speakeasy.

I got a reservation for brunch on Sunday. And it was not very crowded, so I think without reservation you can still get a table shortly. The brunch menu is concise, so it's easy to decide what you want. We got egg Benedict, which was cooked perfectly. The lamb slider is fine, not as good as I expected. Salad is fresh. Decor and ambiance are great. Just wish the service could be faster. Overall , I still recommend this place for hang-out with friends.

This place just opened and looks very cool on the inside. A great mix of Cafe / Bar / Food.  The menu is a good mix of breakfast and sandwiches, with a mini menu of bar snacks. Friendly staff from what I can tell on my first visit. I got the salad with feta / green beans / avocado and raspberries. It's good! I am looking forward to trying more of the menu. Pertinent info: I believe the bartender said they open at 8am. They serve food till 10 on thurs/friday/saturday but are open as a bar "until 2 or 4"   I am super stoked this spot is right around the corner from my new place, was starting to get down on the lack of food options after leaving Greenpoint's many many restaurants.

Holy god that was good! My WIfe and I had dinner last Friday at Skytown, a new cafe/bar that just opened a couple of weeks ago. Very nicely done interior with a warm and welcoming atmosphere, friendly and attentive staff, and a really nice overall vibe. Had a couple of interesting beers (the IPA was outstanding!) and a sip of some sort of amazing lemonade cocktail with fresh blueberries that I think the bartender invented right on the spot...if I hadn't been driving later that night I might still be there drinking them! But the food- holy cow. We shared a lamb sausage sandwich and a roasted yellow beet sandwich that was simply and astoundingly good. The beet slices were perfectly cooked and seasoned, and somehow magically I could taste all of the individual flavors of the various fresh greens inside the sandwich. The bread was crispy on the outside, and chewy/yeasty tasting on the inside- just the way I like it. Add in some amazing roasted potato slices and several very tasty dipping sauces, and this was a memorably delicious dinner. Their food artistry and the care they put into selecting and preparing their dishes is evident throughout- very highly recommended.

I was disappointed when Calliope closed but very happy with what replaced it.  There are three things that I really liked about Contrada: 1 - Service is fantastic.  My friend and I sat at the bar and were perfectly waited on by a very personable bartender.  The manager also checked up on us and was very warm and welcoming.   2 - Food was great.  We started with the Oysters, at $1 an oyster how could we not? I had the squash salad and a pasta dish.  Delicious.  My friend had the Tomato salad and the steak, he finished both before I could try them. 3 - They solved the noise problem that plagued Calliope.  The manager explained that they hired a contractor that specializes in room acoustics.  He was definitely successful. Biggest knock - a couple of "bro-ish" groups on bachelor parties came in, were obnoxious, had some shots but thankfully didn't linger.  That's likely less a restaurant issue rather the neighborhood on Saturday nights.   -H

I would without a doubt give this place a five star rating if it wasn't for the fact that it took kind of long to get the food to the table but omg was the food delicious when it arrived! Some of the best dishes I had this summer. We were 5 people and ordered 2 dishes each to share (our waiter recommended that and it was the perfect amount). Can really recommend The octopus and the skid witch was awesome, also really good steak! They have a big table in the middle of the restaurant that I recon will fit ~20 something people that would be perfect if your celebrating your birthday out with friends and family Literally the only thing I can complain about is the time it took to get the food, witch was way to long but the staff offered bread and took orders for drinks so we were not totally forgotten ;)

Verjus was a great find. The food was excellent; portions were just right, the ingredients were appropriate for the each dish, and I left having had a satisfying meal. The atmosphere is elegant and warm, the waitstaff caring, though not particularly attentive. The average price per entree is around $33, it's a great special occasion place.  If you want a nice dinner, I highly recommend Verjus.
Black Dragon roll was Sam's favorite. Mine was Mt Fuji roll and Fashion Roll. The service is Sooooo disjointed though.

Very nice place! Fantastic food and excellent service ! Must try it..I had lot of sushi in NYC, we were passing by and decided to try it... It's definitely worth to try... Sashimi are fresh, dishes are very creative ... They seriously put lot of lobster in the lobster Roll... Highly recommended ...

Mike and Rob accommodated my family for three hours on a Saturday afternoon with very short notice.  We had 20/25 in the front lounge for snacks.  The service was excellent, the finger food and fruit salad was highly praised by family members from far and near.  Several took menus and plan on returning for happy hour, dinner, breakfast, etc.  Our appreciation is beyond measure.

We ordered a spread including wings, calamari,  mussels, palenta, and flatbread. From 4:30-6:30 they offer an Adult Happy Meal including a burger, fries and beer.  Overall solid food, service and atmosphere with live music at night.
Excellent, fresh tasty food.  The homemade veggie burger is great!

Great atmosphere at this place- low key yet hip.  Super nice and helpful waitstaff from the hostess to the waiter to all of the servers and clearers!  I went here with my tween daughters and the eldest (picky eater) said it was the best restaurant she's ever eaten at. She even tried - and loved! - the watermelon gazpacho. Her personal fav was the candied bacon. I'd also recommend the pickles, the avocado appetizer, the Burke n Bag (dessert) and the amazing donuts. Yes the skirt steak was delicious -- but I have to say the apps and the desserts stole the show!

We are New Yorkers and I was looking forward to eating here during restaurant week. Unfortunately, it seems the restaurant either deliberately overbooks the tables or doesn't know how to manage/honor reservations. This is not something you would expect in what is supposed to be a sophisticated New York restaurant. We had an 8:15 reservation and arrived at 8:05. The hostess said to check back again at 8:15 for our table. So at 8:15 we inquired again and were told it would be another 10-15 minutes. We told them we needed to pick our son up at the bus station, so we could wait a few minutes but didn't have too much extra time. At 8:30 we asked again and they offered us some complimentary champagne and said the table was still not ready. I noticed that there were several other parties who were being told similar stories and had made reservations that were not honored.  At 8:45 we were told our table would be next.  By 8:55 when our table was still not ready and we were out of time, we left. Wound up having felafel across the street at Olympic Pita. If you're in the mood for felafel and shwarma, Olympic Pita was great. The waitress was nice and the food was yummy. Wish I could say the same about David Burke fabrick but I doubt I'll get the chance to go back again. If you can't run your restaurant properly in New York, it won't last.

Made reservation through OpenTable for 7:30 on a Thursday night.  When I checked in the hostess told me it would be a long wait for a table. When I asked why there would be such a long wait she 'found' a table right away. The food was delicious but the service suffered. The restaurant staff seems inexperienced and stressed out. They had gross fruit flies that kept bothering us throughout the meal. I've been a waitress before and it just seemed like bad Management.  Thank goodness the food made up for it. Avocado panna cotta was hands down the best thing I've had in a long time. My husband got the octopus tacos and loved it.  I hope the restaurant gets its act together.

Their lobster bisque was disgusting. It tasted like tomato broth with shrimp dumplings.  There was no creaminess to it at all, and the menu did not state that it was so watery (versus the usual creamy bisques).  The cost of that was overpriced for that brothy disappointment. And, yes, I ate it all.  There's no way I'd throw that money down the drain. The salmon was delicious, crispy on the outside, and succulent.  The chickpea fries were a hit.  Definitely overpriced, but at least they tasted good.  At the end of the day, this place was all hype. Service is good.  They were very nice about getting my order in before the kitchen closed.

Last Wednesday a friend and myself visited fabrick before a play we were greeted immediately by 2 very friendly hostesses that brought us right over to this really quaint spot overlooking the whole restaurant. We were then greeted by our server Marc and he introduced us to the sommelier who recommended a wonderful Rioja based on our tastes. Marc then went through the menu with us and actually got us to change our minds from a few appetizers and entrees to adding a mid-course of the David Burke burger that he said was made from brisket which sounded great so we were sold. Btw it was an absolutely fantastic burger and perfect for a mid-course. The lobster dumplings were sooooo delicious I wanted more but I lost that battle because of the amount of food that we had ordered. The entrees came out, the scallops with fresh horseradish was fantastic the beets added great texture and a sweetness that off set the horseradish what a great combination of flavors We also decided on the lamb and rib combo which struck me as an unusual combination but the savory lamb just melted in your mouth and then you had the sweet, spicy sauciness to the ribs WOW. This was a meal to remember and to add to all this the wine selection was a fantastic match to all aspects of the meal Marc you definitely made this a memorable night with your suggestions thank you. I don't want to leave out the general manager which jumped at the chance to get me some extra fresh horseradish for me because I told her I love horseradish Thank you all that were involved in making this a spectacular evening. I look forward to coming back soon.

What an experience! I enjoyed an amazing lunch at David Burke's new restaurant! It is a foodie's dream! The octopus tacos alone are a reason to return. My salmon entree was fine but the chick pea fries are what really made the meal. It was VERY expensive so I caution people to save this for a special occasion and not an everyday meal.
Absolutely fabulous... The presentation was beautiful, the food is to die for, the atmosphere is chic, and the service is perfection. Must try the candied bacon and the red snapper ceviche!

Delicious from start to finish! Had dinner there last night and I am really impressed! First off, our server was fantastic and attentive.  He suggested many dishes for us to try and he was not kidding about how good they are.  We had the 1  burrata salad, which was so refreshing 2. Red Snapper ceviche, WOW! must have, the chef brought it out to us himself and told us it's his best creation thus far 3. Octopus Angry tacos, so tasty, 4. Shrimp Angry tacos, good, but if you like octopus, I'd go with those, 5. Grilled skirt steak, tender and tasty, and the cheese fritters are sinfully good 6. Pork Shoulder Rigatoni, Oh em gee, it's all I want to eat ever again, forever! The general manager then brought out some desserts to make up for our long wait for a table which was so nice and thoughtful of him! Standouts were the melba donuts and the napoleon, YUM!! Everything was delicious, the long wait was totally worth it, service was impeccable, and I'll definitely be back.

Visited today again, this time for dinner and drinks - amazing experience of excellent food and great service. Candied bacon was a surprise of taste and creativity; skin and bones... let me not spoil it by describing - it will be another interesting dish to try. Tuna sashimi were too salty for my taste, but were loved by my companions and their presentation was amazing.

Finally found a great place to get Chinese food.  While the place is a little dumpy, the food (honey pork and chicken) was damn good.  It's also pretty cheap at $6 for a rice plate that has tons of meat on it.

Cool concept just the food is really overpriced the "rolls" of sushi are only 4 small pieces and they don't taste really flavorful i must say and the rolls that don't have fish in them as in the Chicken Teriyaki roll taste fishy very unpleasant. That wasn't gonna break it or make it for me until me and a few friends ordered cocktails and I wasn't sure who they had making the drinks but it was bad your better off ordering the sake. My waitress was nice at first but as it got busier she seemed less caring about my table which i consider really rude. On a positive note they sure know how to make bubble tea they are really good!

The service is what really was the poop of the night because they were unattentive and didn't want to give us our checks and didn't want to give us bread. The bread thing usually wouldn't be a problem because I'm kinda carb-phobic (it's the way I was brought up?!), but we were soooo hungry. We're like pleaseee give us some bread. I digress. I don't know how we found this place, but it is damn good. I got the combo ribs and half chicken with rice and beans. I'm sooo obsessed with rice and beans since I came back from the Dominican Republic last summer. It was damn good except for the random olives in there. Bleh! There was so much meat on the plate that my old 20 year old self could eat it all, but now that I'm old and wrinkly, there was like 3 meals on my plate for me. The meat was so good and salty. I don't think this is the kind of place where you need BBQ sauce, but they have it if you realllyy want it. For the amount of food and deliciousness I got - $12 is totally worth it.

Don't gooooo. Me and my husband went there for lunch, and it was horrible!!! Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else. Im still trying to get the coal taste out of my mouth, and the disgusting smell off my hands.

We got a groupon and went to dinner last night for bbq and what a pleasant surprise! I had the bbq combo platter which has ribs, pulled pork, chicken bbq, and brisket. It also comes with a corn bread and two sides. Everything on the plate was DELICIOUS. The ribs were tender and juicy. The pulled pork was so flavorful and the brisket I couldn't get enough. My husband ordered steak medium rare and it came perfectly the way he wanted. The sweet potato fries were excellent and the collard greens were close enough to what we had in Charleston. The waitress was very attentive and helpful. We didn't need to use any of the bbq sauces there because everything was so flavorful already. Overall it was a great experience. Even my 18 month old loved the ribs and the fries. Would definitely recommend to friends.
Excellent food and service! Very nice environment!

Great food! It's our weekly go to restaurant for when we are not in a mood to have dinner at home. The place is small and cozy but the food is awesome. We have tried most everything on the menu and everything is delicious. The service is always fast and quick with a friendly smile. Portions are great.

Popped in a couple nights ago - I was so excited to see a place like this open up on East Girard and I wasn't disappointed in the least. My partner and I ordered an order of grape leaves and a lamb gyro to split - both excellent: fresh tasting, nice portions, and excellent tazaki (which tends to be the litmus test by which we judge such restaurants). The owners were incredibly kind and when we complimented their new restaurant and our dinner, the owner asked us to please tell just one person about the place. Hopefully more than one person will be swayed to pop in and welcome them to the neighborhood.

Great addition to Fishtown. Gyros were delicious and tasted extremely fresh - meat was very moist. Additionally, the owners are just lovely. Hopefully more people will find out this place is here and will support it.

Always on the search for new and innovative cocktails, and this is definitely the place!  My new favorite place to sit and snack at the bar (with a bar called Madam Geneva) next door... and my new go-to date night spot with about four different places to eat, all with a different vibe.   Went again for dinner with a bunch of friends and probably ordered everything that was on the menu.  I'd never typically order chicken, but it's maybe one of the best dish that we had all night.  I ordered the pork chop and it was cooked perfectly, and the steaks were AMAZING.  And everything has a really creative twist to it. Really nice staff, reasonably priced for huge portions, and dangerous that it's so close to where I live.

We were passing through NY recently for my husband's 30th birthday and a few friends recommended this new restaurant near their apartment. He wanted to go somewhere else but I am so glad we convinced him to try something new. The venue is beautiful, and the food delicious - simple food, done well, and with a little twist (eg the carrot, ginger and lemon soup is enlivened by toasted chilli marshmallow). The best thing, for me, was the cocktails. They even make their own whiskey! Try the chocolate souffle with S+P whiskey - you'll want seconds. We will definitely be back!

I'm a sucker for horses, so I liked the premise before I ever walked in. Fortunately, the design delivers in the best possible way. I felt relaxed and happy. Love the simple space and the rustic references. Even better, love the food! My favorite were the mushroom pot and the lemon carrot soup topped with a marshmallow, if only because they were such a happy surprise. I also had the burger which was decadent and delicious. Plus, the waiter was kind enough to ask the mixologist to prepare me a special mocktail, since I wasn't drinking that night. Looking forward to my next visit!

I wish I was allowed to swear on here, because I don't know how to express my absolutely awesome experience here without using some forceful expressions. As I showed up with my girlfriend for our 9PM reservation we were greeted warmly and seated promptly without a fuss, even though the restaurant was pretty busy and bustling at this point. We started with a mini seafood tower that wasn't very mini at all, and absolutely delish. Some other reviewer wrote about the shrimp, and they are that good. Next up: rib-eye for two. Probably one of the best pieces of steak I've had in a long time. Sides were also really good, but were kind of left in the wake of the the main dishes. There was this cauliflower gratin though, which was good enough on its own as maybe an appetizer or so. We skipped dessert this time, but our server caught that me and my girlfriend was celebrating a promotion, and discreetly brought over two glasses of sparkling dessert wine on the house. How's that for attentive service? I am hard pressed for negatives; it is a cool bar scene, but even if it looked busy over at the bar, our table in the back room was quiet and secluded. This one of my new favorite spots, and I think it is great either for a date, or maybe a medium sized group of foodie carnivores? F%^k yeah!

Went there last night with a party of five for a birthday.  Most of the dinner went fine -- we ordered the housemade pot with mushrooms, the mini seafood towers,  and a plate of pork and pickles.  We enjoyed the starters and we excited for our main courses.  Four out of five arrived, the burger was missing -- at first they said it was on its way.  Then the waiter came back and said he was sorry it was not here and it would be two minutes and he hadn't put it in.  Then the floor manager came over to personally apologize for it not being at the table but 'how is everything else.'  The apologies were all very nice -- albeit disingenuous and no one made an effort to offer something (even a plate to share) while we waited for the burger.  Finally the burger arrived and it was rare -- barely cooked.  The order originally should have been medium, and it was clear they were rushing to get it out before the other mains were gone.  We sent it back because we didn't want it anymore.  The waiter just said, 'Sorry,' not offering up anything else or even a comp drink.  That was a big bummer.  Also, the remainder of us sat with our empty plates in front of us for a good ten minutes before anyone offered to remove them.  The waiter offered us dessert but first said, 'Aside from my mistake with the burger, how was everything?'  Ugh.  We ordered dessert, the donuts and the boozy ice cream and three out of five ordered coffee.  The coffee arrived after the dessert was finished.  In fact, we were wondering if it would arrive at all.  In summary: We spent $500, margaritas cost $19 per -- we had to ask the waiter to remove the burger from our bill, nothing was comped due to the burger flub.  In fact, while the waiter and floor manager  emphatically apologize (mind you, we were all going with the flow and no one was rude or impatient) it was annoying when nothing was offered to make up for their error.  That goes a long way.   We will never return to Saxon + Parole, in spite of some of us enjoying the food.  We will also not recommend it as a place to go.  Do not waste your money.  It's overpriced and the service is superficial.

The mushroom pot was to die for. We had to contain ourselves from licking the pot... seriously.  Cool ambience. Loud, but you can hear yourselves talk. Good, unique drinks.  Service needs to get their rhythm being a new restaurant, but that will come. Good for Gluten Free as well.

Here's the Deal... If you're from the area, you definitely know Diamonds.  They've had a long successful history in W. Trenton area.   This newest location does not disappoint.  While the location tucked away in a strip mall, it still delivers quality meals. They have innovative specials daily and the service is always knowledgeable and friendly.  They also have a nice bar area & high tables if you're looking for something a little more casual.

This is the kind of place where you scratch your head and wonder why they are doing so well in this location, but I guess it's because there are SO MANY PEOPLE that every other restaurant is full.  Seriously, there are what, 20 restaurants all up and down Church St.?   Anyways, what dropped this one from A-OK to 2 stars is the fries (soggy) and the cheese steak (dry and rather tasteless).  The fish and chips was all brown with a plastic container of tartar sauce.  Plastic, ugh.  No cole slaw, not even some forlorn parsley to make it look palatable.  It was palatable, but you had to close your eyes. The beer, Long Trail IPA on tap, was rather "light", but that's our fault for making that choice. Service was ok, but all in all, you can do a lot better on Church St.

WORST RESTAURANT ON CHURCH ST.   This place is severely overpriced and the food is just subpar for Church St. I mean how often is one disappointed with a simple slice of pizza? Not often, but you will be EVERY time at Kens. If by some act of god they make a decent slice, its still going to be outrageously expensive.   First off, it comes to $3.05 for one simple slice of CHEESE pizza. The owners are delusional if they think they are making slices of culinary gold, because they most definitely are not - its just regular damn pizza.   Secondly, they have absolutely NO CLUE how to grill up a legitimate philly cheesesteak - never in my long life of eating phillys have I ever been so disappointed - I had to throw mine away after two bites. They bake their sandwich roast beef in the oven instead of grilling up a legit cheese steak...blasphemy if you ask me.   Third, and maybe most important, is that both the employees and the owner are very rude. I've only had one experience at Kens and I promise I will never return. I witnessed the owner's fowl mouth, the staffs general rudeness, and the cooks disregard for overall cleanliness.  Also for some reason they have crammed an absurd amount of tables into their small outside eating area so you cant even comfortably enjoy a meal without feeling like you're sharing it with 10 other people.

We had a fabulous experience. I had walked by with a friend and we decided that our next dinner would be there - just because it looked cosy and lovely through the window. We were not disappointed! The food was excellent and we were well taken care of by the staff. I'll definitely return!!

Went to Wallflower last night with a group of 4 (including myself). The cozy ambiance at Wallflower is extremely welcoming - especially when the staff is very friendly, attentive, accommodating. etc. Service is VERY good here. We did the a la carte menu and our entrees were the Loup de Mer, Sea Scallops, Barley Risotto and the Pork Tenderloin.. all delicious, and filling. The food here is all about quality. Between the 4 of us we tried 2 different cocktails each, and even had Xavier Herit bring out something he crafted that wasn't on the menu. Definitely recommend and will definitely be going back.

Went for dinner on our anniversary.  Had the tasting menu, so got to sample pretty much everything on the menu.  Food is great, but the overall dining experience was wanting.  For a $260+ bill for a couple, one is looking for more of a fine dining experience (I mean white table cloth and everything else that goes with it) than what Wallflower presents.  The staff seemed in a great hurry to turn you over (not unusual in NYC, but not at this price point), and very matter of fact.  No sooner did you put your fork down at the end of a course, that the wait staff was there to clear the plate with a perfunctory "How was everything", followed by a "Great", irrespective of what you had to say.  The chairs are not comfortable so even if you planned on a relaxing evening, it is hard to achieve that.  The tables are very small - hard to ensure that you don't knock off either your silver, or your water glass or your wine glass.  The walls are bare, making for a high decibel level, probably remnants of its predecessor entity.  I think the owners need to decide how they want to position this - probably qualifies for a more casual, eat-and-get-going kind of an experience, in which case needs to be priced accordingly.  Would still recommend the place once though, just for the food, which was outstanding.

What can I say, this place is just amazing.   We were there mainly for the cocktails, and boy, were we impressed.  I had the Arlay Sour and it was so refreshing!  The chamomoile infused gin with lavender bitters was exactly what I needed to cool down from the Sunday heat.  I was so into my own drink that I forgot to try what my friends ordered, but they loved it. We also had the country pate which was so smooth and delicious.  And the coffee and chocolate pot de creme for dessert was decadent without being too sweet. The staff is attentive, very knowledgeable, and super friendly.  It's the perfect dinner date spot or a cute place to grab drinks with some friends.  Wallflower can be easily overlooked from the outside, but that adds to its unpretentious charm.   Will definitely be back for dinner and more drinks.

Previously, I would have given Reservoir a 5 star rating.  The place is usually packed and their pizza is truly great.  The reason why it's 3 stars is that  we got take-out a few days ago, and the pizza and the chicken parm sandwiches were great, but the rest of the food (Italian sub, chicken Marsala, and pasta w/ meat sauce) were all just average.  The chicken Marsala was overcooked and the sauce a bit thin and it didn't stick to the chicken at all... just overlooked dry chicken in thin sauce w/ a few shrooms.  The pasta was over overcooked and mushy, and the meat sauce wasnt as good as it usually is.  And the sliced tomatoes on the Italian sub weren't ripe... They were mostly green, which is a no-no, especially this time of year.  When I got home w/ the take out order ( even though the waitress said she checked and everything was there, the Italian sub was missing and I had to go back a second time.  Although the staff is usually friendly I had to wait the second time to get the sub they forgot, ( even though it was ready) and wait while they seated other customers, and they definitely could have had a better attitude about giving me food that I already paid for and had to drive back a second time to get (but they did give me 2 meatballs on the side, for free, when I complained about it).  Perhaps it was just a bad night.  I'll go back again sometime b/c 9 out of 10 times, I've really loved Reservoir and would have previously given it 4 or 5 stars... and the pizza definitely still rocks.

This restaurant is one of our favorites in New Jersey! Their Pizza is the best!! The flavor of the crust is absolutely delicious! We always order the Tony Salad for two- if you like meat and cheese- you will not be disappointed. The meatballs are tasty for side dish or an appetizer. Dinner we split Chicken Savoy and Penne A La Jake along with Sauteed Spinach. We give this restaurant 5 stars!! A perfect neighborhood spot. It is great quality Italian food, family style portions and very inexpensive! We also love BYOB! When we bring friends from out of town- they are just as happy as we are! Check it Out! PS- talk to the people in the restaurant, you will find that they are all loyal customers who have been customers for years and they all have their own "favorite dishes."

Let me start by saying that if I could give this place no stars, I would.  First, the place is dirty and very out dated and the wait staff looked bothered and annoyed at our very presence.  We were seated at a very wobbly table in front of a closet, which the staff needed access to (one waitress even pulled out a windex bottle and started spraying a rag right next to us while we were eating). We had to wait 15 minutes before anyone came over to even ask for our drink order, while everyone that works there starred at us and the owner sat at the next table stuffing his face.   Not to mention the large pizza that came out to the dinning room for the entire staff, including kitchen workers, which brought the entire restaurant to a halt while everyone sat at the tables and ate.  I appreciate the owner feeding his staff, but I feel that was better suited for inside the kitchen and not in the dining room with paying customers.                    I would normally say that most of these things could be over looked IF the food is good, but sadly it was one of the worst meals I have ever had. I even got sick afterwards.  The fried calamari was so bland and tasted like freezer burn and the mussels weren't taste fresh and were drenched in a very greasy sauce.  My husband's entree was some chicken dish that was swimming in some nasty brown sauce with rubbery and hard to eat chicken.  My linguini and clams in white sauce was both greasy and bland at the same time.  It had clams that weren't cleaned and were crunchy to the bite, huge chunks of garlic and an entire bottle of dried parsley that seemed like the cook was trying to compensate for flavor.  Needless to say that while the portions were huge, it doesn't make up for the terrible food.  That was our first and only trip to that restaurant.
I really loved the food over there, yummy yum yum said my 3 yr old daughter (miss crunch roll) and the service was great.

Good sushi! The Saturday night special "Dancing Roll" was delicious, as were the Cy-Tuna and STC rolls. The wasabi was super fresh! Service was very good, and we enjoyed the cute decor. Music could be improved, but overall an enjoyable evening. So happy to see sushi near Graduate Hospital!

5 stars for a few reasons: 1) The first sushi place serving high-grade fish in graduate Hospital (finally!) 2) Service was attentive and quick- waitresses were very attentive and grateful for our patronage.  My water was probably refilled every time I took a sip.  Sushi chefs were professional and also welcoming. 3) And of course, sushi was great!  We got the Dancing sushi special, Cy-Tuna, Kabajo, and Veggie Roll.  Fish was fresh (waitress informed us that the tuna just came in and was fresh), rice was well seasoned and rolled properly.  Wasabi and seaweed salad were both fresh.   Lunch deal looks good and reasonably-priced.  Found my new go-to sushi joint!
