Exceptional place. The atmosphere is casual. The foot is well priced, $14 for a rack of ribs, with rice and salad, and the pork ribs are great and have a sweet marinade. the beef ribs are fine, but not as good. If you're looking for ribs in Newark, try this place.

Bunch of my friends and I, decided to grab Mexican for dinner. We spotted Jolie's.  It looked nice and the ambiance seemed fitting from the outside. We startedd the night with drinks. I ordered a strawberry mojito and to my surprise it was pretty good. Well, I can't say the same towards the food, nothing special and extremely overpriced. The gratitude was a whopping 20% and the waiter dared to ask more as if 20% isn't pushing it. Definitely a place you go once and never go again!

Good atmosphere. Open restaurant - meaning they had outdoor seating and had two doors which allowed the nice cool summer night air flow in. I only ate their oysters and their dessert which was kinda blah but my friends ordered the all you can eat mussels that comes with fries and choices of three different sauces. They are all three heaping of it! I was full from another restaurant. I had a bite of another friend's French beef tartar and that was good too. Surprisingly none of us actually ordered the Mexican dishes so we can't judge on the "cantina" factor of the restaurant. It's very clean. They also have guac made in front of you, sad that I already ate avocados twice today.
love the food, so simple and great!!! the waitress can be nicer..:0

I usually dislike eating Italian out.  Despite not being Italian myself, I find that I am a competent enough cook that what I make at home usually far outshines the slapped-together fare found at most Italian places.  This place, along with Vetri and Modo Mio, are starting to make me change my mind.  There is no way I could create gnocchi as air light as the ones I had at Ulivo.  Every part of the meal was simple, but outstandingly well prepared by a chef who was a craftsman.  Highly recommend.
Great food, friendly service, quaint and quirky atmosphere, free wifi, what else could you really ask for?  The borscht is delicious. For cookies, go for the sea salt shortbread.

Yum yums for me! Ah...this place is so good. It's so different from the different places I've been trying in Jersey City. Actually, about a year ago when I was looking for an apartment, I wandered into here and got a cottage cheese cookie. It was yummy then and it is damn yummy now! It's got a crunchy exterior with a nice, soft and delicious interior. The sea salt shortbread cookie is a bit salty for me, but to each their own. Unfortunately for my tummy, they ran out of pilaf that day. I'll be back. So I got the veal dumplings and a spicy lamb steak sandwich instead. The veal dumplings are like tiny tortellinis and a bit bland, but with their scallion soy sauce - it's soooo good. The spicy lamb steak sandwich is damn good too. There is no gamey-ness to it, but you could still taste the lamb and the peppers and onions were so good and fresh. Lamb samosa? You guessed it! SO GOOD. The filling is so good and the pastry is not oily at all, but my only problem is that some of the pastry was a bit undercooked and the filling was a little cold because they had to reheat it. Still good though! :) I'll be back for you lamb pilaf - just wait for meee!

Cozy little place and friendly service. The Spicy Lamb Sandwich & the Veal Dumplings are DELICIOUS! Everything is made fresh daily, on the spot. They were out of Lamb Pilaf and the Cottage Cheese Cookies by the afternoon, but I'll definitely be going back to try some...along with the Samosas and Cheesecake!
Been awhile since i have been in this area, well worth the visit...loved the quaint place with really excellent food..I ordered the lamb samoas, properly seasoned, very satisfying..will visit again!

Yuck, keep looking We stopped here after coming back from NYC. We had a 20% off coupon and figured what the heck.  You needed to show the coupon before ordering which we did,  upon receiving the bill low and behold the 20% ws NOT taken off.   We had french onion soup which came out lukewarm. The glasses and silverware were dirty. Each glass and piece of silverware had pieces of some sort of hard substance on them. I can only imagine what was on the inside of the glasses. The draft beer was skunky, which is ususally caused by not having the lines cleaned out on a schedule. The dinners did not come out at he same time. One was brought to the table 10 minutes after the others. The ribeye steak was tough. The cajun spiced shrimp was not cajun spiced, it was regular Fridays shrimp.
Food is good but it comes out super slow.... Super super slow...........

Came here for an Easter brunch and was surprised to learn that it was an Easter buffet. The food was outstanding--oysters, clams, prime rib, eggs benedict, parfait, omelettes--it all tasted high-quality.  The only downside was that it was difficult to access the food because of the amount of people funneled through one room, but I think the food is consistently good here and it is not recognized as such, for whatever reason.  I hope that more people give them a chance.
The lobster roll is chock full of big chunks of yummy fresh lobster. You can really taste the freshness and it makes all the difference. I am coming back for the lobster dinner for my birthday. Yum!

I would like to thank the event known as the Prospect Park Food Truck Rally for presenting the Red Hook Lobster Pound Truck to my list of culinary delights.  That Maine Style lobster roll was the truth! The bun, the lobster, the pickle, the mayo, the texture, the crunch factor, the presentation, the taste.....OMG!!  I wanted to make a u-turn in one way traffic just to get another one!  Next on the list....Connecticut Style!  As a matter of fact, damn the truck, I'm heading to the spot....uh, huh that's right!!!

My god.  That was delicious.  Not sure which I like better in the war of Maine- vs. Connecticut-style.  I got both. Maine is cool, creamy, and singing with flavor.  Good for a hot summer day, and probably the better choice for takeout. Connecticut is savory, buttery bliss, enhancing the flavor of the meat, and the perfect complement to the toasted JJ Nissen's roll. And the whoopie pie for dessert almost steals the show...

I went to the Brooklyn Flea and was determined to try the infamous Lobster Roll. Man, I was so disappointed. I should have gotten a hot one, instead I got it cold and I did not like it one bit. It was just OK. It was also tiny for $15... I went to McDonald's right after.

Came here to try a lobster roll as I had only tried Luke's Lobster Roll in the LES and wanted to compare the two. My boyfriend and I split the hot lobster roll. The lobster was good and they were very generous with the amount in the sandwich (more so than at Luke's). It was served with a pickle and a bag of chips. Although it was buttery, the flavor was OK, not as great as Luke's... maybe this is because the hot roll is prepared with butter and does not have the homemade mayo. Would come back if in the area and would try the cold lobster roll!
Great selection of Belgium beers and great and friendly staff.Meet some great people for Belgium there as well.

I had a funny experience in this restaurant about two weeks ago. A couple behind me was engaged in a fight; they were highly intoxicated. They were throwing around mussels (it was mussels night!) and one of them hit me in the head. I told the bartender on duty and he did nothing about it. I would have given them four stars had they had a bouncer there that night. In general, I love their food. Their staff during the week is excellent, especially the girl with the dreadlocks who happens to be one of the best employees they have. I can also rate their meatloaf: one of the best in the city!

This is a good neighborhood spot.  I stopped in for lunch on a Saturday after running errands all morning.  Good beers, good food, and good prices. Bartender was very friendly and the service was quick.  I'll have to come here again on a Sunday for football.  Lots of TVs and good NFL specials.

I'm glad we stopped by For Pete's Sake early yesterday evening. I read the yelp reviews and thought since we were in the neighborhood - getting a new hairdo from John at Europa salon on Front St (a really great experience) - we'd stop by. At 5:30 on a Fri. the outside tables were all taken, with more people waiting inside at the bar for a seat outside. I think I know why - good cold fresh selection of beers, I had Alagash, C had her usual g&t. Looked at the menu and found it really interesting. So we stayed at the (friendly) bar and We shared the 3 kinds of hummus with lots of pita bread. It was good,  although not as garlicky as I was looking for. Then ordered a hamburger with carmelized onions and goat cheese. Hamburger was cooked perfectly atop a fresh brioche (?) roll with a side of their good although slightly greasy fries but all was delicious. Bar staff was friendly and efficient. Nice mix of young and old, executives and grunt workers. When we left about 7 - outside was still crowded and so was the inside bar.  I'll go back to try some of the other menu items, and bring my pooch and sit outside.

To my taste, the best pie in Brooklyn -- which is saying something. Super thin crispy crust charred just right by the coal buring oven. Perfect amount of cheese with lots of fresh basil on the margherita. Some may find the sauce a bit sweet but it worked well for me. They have a friendly staff that takes pride in their pies (as they should) and a very pleasant dining room with Italian crooner music piped. BYOB is a plus as there is a great wine shop just steps away.
Great food, best thin crust pizza ever!

Really amazing! As a resident of Brooklyn Heights, good and affordable food is hard to come by.  Thank goodness Table 87 has opted to pick up the slack! More than just mouth watering pizza, their salads are delicious and the service is a delight. Hopefully I will be coming to this place for years!
Great Pizza...Great for delivery and eat in! We get the margarita pie, and a salad their Panini's are great too! Great Staff!

This Pizza is definitely on the same level as the heavyweights of NYC pizza.  If you don't feel like standing in line at Grimaldi's or trekking to Midwood for DiFara, come here and enjoy a top notch slice at the counter or sit in the back for a whole pie.

Went to Table 87 for the first time last night and it was great!  We were seated right away, and the staff was really friendly.  I love the open kitchen in the back so you can watch them cook your food - it makes your meal a little more interactive!  We tried the Table 87 House Salad (house-made mozzarella, roasted red peppers, mixed greens, balsamic vinaigrette). was very generous and it was only $8!  We then split a Margherita pizza (added fresh mushrooms) and the linguini with clam sauce.  The freshness of the ingredients was truly stellar.  The sauce on both the pizza and pasta was just as I like it - simple, fresh, tomato flavor.  The pizza crust was a good balance of chew and crunch, the house made mozzarella on the pizza bubbled and browned on the edges.  The mushrooms were sliced just the right size so they frizzled up in the coal oven.  Topped with lots of fresh basil, it was delicious.  The clams in the pasta were SUPER fresh and served in-shell which I like. The pasta portion was perfect (not overwhelming) and the sauce was stellar.  They bring you jars of roasted chili peppers in oil, and roasted garlic cloves, which you can add as you see fit - a nice touch.  When this place has their liquor license they will be rocking and rolling!  It's a nice unpretentious, affordable, fresh and delicious and uncomplicated Italian spot.  Worth the walk the extra block down Atlantic, past Red Gravy, to try it out!

First bite I took was of the lemon chicken, which is a five-star worthy street meat if ever I've tasted one! Sadly, everything went downhill from there. Merguez was essentially raw, and the beef was inedible (as in burned, fatty, stringy, and acrid tasting). The kofta was o.k. but nothing mind blowing, and the sauces were average. Were it not for the lemon chicken and the flavorful onion chutney-esque side dish thrown into the mix for apparent funsies, I'd say au revoir to this truck. But I'll come back someday for the smiling service and--you guessed it--the poultry.
Great !

This truck is on Park and 51st, usually only on Wednesdays until about 3:30 p.m. One of my favorite trucks, with some of the better Mediterranean food. My favorite dish from here is beef with couscous and Casablanca sauce some veggies and potatoes is very tasty. They also have dishes with fish. A platter runs for about $9, and the size is decent.

My favorite spot, here everyday, literally multiple times throughout the day. Love the staff coolest people, super sweet & I'm not taking about their baked goods...yet. Their bakery is insane. I've tried it all, you haven't had nothing until you've walked in my shoes... Lemon bread, banana bread, corn muffins, pecan cookies, bundt cake muffin, brownies, chocolate chunk chip something. The list goes on duh! Love, Soy latte & americano

I went here with a friend on a Monday night. It's a BYOB restaurant so I was excited to bring in a bottle of wine. As for Sushi California, the place is pretty decent. I would recommend it for a first or second date because it's sushi (good for a date) and the place is pretty enough without being stuffy. We ordered the loveboat, or rather the "boat", for us and we enjoyed the experience. I wished the spicy rolls were a bit spicier because I didn't think it was spicy enough. The staff are super nice.

Best sushi place in the area. My boyfriend and I go there regularly. The blonde girl that works there is absolutely ADORABLE and I'm glad they finally got her some other servers to help! The sushi is FANTASTIC!!! I get the green hulk roll every time I go, and with a little extra spicy mayo, there's no better or more delicious roll anywhere. Customers for life!!!

I almost wish I didn't discover this place- because boxed pasta will never be the same. We found out during a walk in Little Italy (aka trying to walk off a Paesano's food coma) and realized we had nothing planned for dinner. The refrigerated section was a carb/pasta lover's dream come true- multiple varieties of different pastas, recommendations for sauces to go with said pastas, and Italian dinner specialties that are already premade. After a few minutes of discussing what we should get, we noticed a sign that for $24 you can get two packages of the lobster ravioli and a sauce of your choice. As we were walking towards the counter to pay, we also grabbed a loaf of fresh bread. All I can say is wow- the pasta was fresh, the sauce was amazing (go with the Rosa sauce - you will not be disappointed)  and fed us for 2 meals. Each package came with either 16 or 20 ravioli- a hearty portion per package compared to going out to a restaurant and getting 4-5 lobster raviolis for $20 and you could taste the lobster in each bite. They had a ton of gnocchi varieties there as well which I can't wait to go back and try. If you happen to be walking around the Italian Market area definitely stop in- and if your not in the area, find an excuse to go .
Very good food. Service quick however not the friendliest staff. They were not rude just not friendly. Took 20 minutes to get bill. That drives me crazy but food was really good

I lived next to B4 for a year and was always hesitant because it looked so empty all the time. My girlfriends and I finally decided to try it out and it was amazing! The service was efficient, the food was amazing and the atmosphere was relaxing and fun. I'm not sure why this place stays empty - people should flock here. We got the waffles/fried chicken, gravy and biscuits, omelette, and the farmers breakfast, side of (thick!) bacon, sticky buns, donuts, excellent bloody marys and mimosas. I'll definitely be coming back.

Made an Opentable reservation for a Saturday night here for dinner. When we arrived we were greeted very cordially and given a choice of tables in two areas. We chose a table by the window. Shortly after we arrived, water was served in "jar glasses" A sliced "mini loaf" of bread arrived with a plate of salt and one with olive oil in which there were a collection of fantastic herbs. B4 got off to a good start. Our waiter took our drink order and informed us of the daily specials including their price. Our waiter informed us that the Fish special included corn and despite liking the type of fish being offered, my dining partner passed on the special due to the corn. However, B4 is extremely accommodating to special requests so it is probable that the corn could have be eliminated or something else substituted if requested.  My dining partner ordered a Gin and Tonic which was excellent. Our waiter was extremely knowledgeable about the menu and informed me that the Apple Curry Soup was made with nuts, so I avoided it. We ordered our appetizers;  the Orange Fennel & Jicama Arugula Salad w/Honey Chili Vinaigrette  and Strawberry and  Spinach Salad w/Warm Bacon Dressing & Candied Pecans. We chose the Seared Salmon w/ Israeli Couscous  Feta Salad and Seared Sea Scallops w/Cauliflower Purée & Cucumber Dill Drizzle as our entrees. Our waiter did not ask how I wanted my salmon cooked (usually I prefer medium rare) so I assumed that the chef would prepare it appropriately. The appetizer salads were both excellent although the optional "fresh pepper" was overpowering coarsely ground peppercorns so if you get "fresh pepper" here go lightly on it. Then our entrees arrived. My dining partner's scallop entree was excellent but it included a considerable amount of corn accompaniment that was NOT mentioned in the menu description. My dining partner specifically avoided ordering the daily special due to corn and chose a dish that ended up having corn as well. My salmon entree was admittedly good but, it arrived medium well, certainly not the way most professional chefs would prepare salmon. It was good, however, so I kept it. My dining partner chose the chocolate brownie with candied bacon and hazelnut gelato for dessert. I had a taste and while everything was excellent, the combination of candied (pork) bacon and chocolate brownie just didn't work for me. Fortunately, my dining partner loved it.  The decor feels like a theatrical set with different color brick walls throughout, fascinating photographs in the front room and large paintings of food in the back dining room. Service was extremely friendly and accomodating. When we were about to leave, the hostess apologized for the behavior of the child at the table adjacent to ours. Actually, as we told her, he was not disruptive at all and there was no need for an apology. (There were several open tables available and if he had been disruptive, we would have notified the hostess and she would have moved us to a different table). It's a tough call between 3 and 4 stars for this restaurant. I really want to give it 3 1/2. But, I certainly would return, so I'll give it 4, mostly because of how hard they try to please, and see how things are on my next visit. It's not really a destination place, more of a neighborhood gem that needs a little bit of polishing.

Stumbled across B4 one night. Immediately Loved it. Great decor, plenty of seating, friendly and knowledgeable staff (which can be hard to find these days).  Enjoyed every meal we have had there, namely the drinks, sweet potato fries, seared ahi tuna nachos, salmon, pizzas. Looking forward to trying more of the menu!

Pretty good food, great waitress, dreadful hostess. I came for a birthday dinner with 7 of my friends.  I made reservations for 7pm.  At 7:02pm the waitress calls me and asks where I am.  I told her I was down the block.  When I got to the restaurant, there was literally 2 people in the restaurant.  I didn't understand the urgency on her part to get me and my party to the restaurant.  My friends were late and for 20 minutes, she kept pestering me.  Basically, she rushed us during our meal because she had booked another party after us.  We spent over $400 there, and if she can't do her job to schedule reservations, don't blame us.   I will never come here again and will tell my friends again.  Disgusting hostess.

They said god created the world in 6 days well thankfully you don't have to wait that long for your food. Great service & hospitality. Amazing dishes, desserts & drinks! Try the pasta w shrimp it's really good. The pizzas are fresh & tasty and don't forget to finish your meal with the Baby Jesus. If you like cocktails ask for the Gringo.....no not the blonde guy smiling all the time with the beard, I mean the drink! God bless America!

Ventura is o so. We were most impressed. Especially after all these great reviews   The first thing we encountered upon arriving was "do you have an reservation" We came early and it was only less than half full. This kind if attitude don't work on Queens Blvd. sorry... I had the pasta with the red beats thinking it was a main course as was listed on the menu? It was so small a portion it barely qualified for an appetizers and it was barely lukewarm. The wine served here by the glass is terrible overpriced. Hugs...
Went here for drinks and dessert last night. Very friendly servers, awesome sticky toffee pudding and nice wine list. Going to go back for dinner, absolutely want to try the salad and pasta.

I give this place a very big thumbs up. Service was excellent. They know the menu very well and know what to recommend (and it's not just the most expensive thing). Small but cozy. We had Nadine who is more of a hostess but pays very close attention to all of the tables. Overall a fantastic experience.

The other reviews weren't lying. This place deserves a 10! A true Creole gem. You don't find many places like this and thank God I don't have to travel to NYC to get here. Long to short: excellent location, excellent decor, authentic Creole food, authentic Haitian service, great Haitian music, more than reasonable prices. It's a 10 all the way. Coming back here isn't a question.

Wow! What a great little place! This small and rustic Haitian restaurant made me feel like it wasn't the middle of winter in Montclair NJ. The staff was helpful and attentive. They reduced the spiciness of my friends entree and explained the menu. We had the sampler as an appetizer. Haitian caviar (eggplant on a plantain with some goat cheese on top), spicy fried fritters and spinach empanadas. So so good. I had the shrimp estufee and it was delicious! The place is BYOB. We paired the meal with a Spanish Rioja and it was perfect for cutting the heat. For desert, we had a sweet potato concoction. It looked like pumpernickel bread soaked in a vanilla sauce and vanilla bean ice cream. It was so good. We even met the owner, Ron and he told us all about the place, food and Haiti. Great place!

I've lived in this neighborhood for years and for whatever reason never ventured into Ichiban. Monte Alban, Abyssinian, Tisane & The Half Door? Yes. All of the above - just never this addition to my usual West End lineup. At least in terms of sushi, I wasn't missing much. After walking to CVS for a few things with my boyfriend, we impulsively decided we didn't feel like cooking and ducked into Ichiban on the way home. The interior is decent enough - dark wood, sushi bar, and service was okay - a little slow. I started with an avocado sesame salad, which was extremely generous with the avocado (like an entire avocado sliced on top) and flavorful dressing. Nick's bibimbap  came as another highlight although the kimchee was lackluster (he likes it spicy and stankyyyyyyy) and the egg was too fried so the yolk couldn't mix in with the other meal accoutrements. My sushi was as bland as could be, despite the Paradise Roll sounding quite good. Salmon & tuna coated with mango....except the mango was drenched in this creepy, flavorless mango-colored goo and a squiggle of mayo. I had to scrape it all off. Overall, I might eventually return to try some non-sushi dishes, but probably no time soon.

The chicken satay tacos with spicy are amazing! I feel like the combination and amount of chicken, peanut sauce, lettuce, tomato and spicy stuff is perfect. If you were put three of these on a plate in a fancy restaurant and charged $18, I would still be going back. It's that good. It takes me nearly 30 minutes just to walk from my office and back otherwise I would be here way more often! It's also a bonus that the guy that runs the truck is seriously one of the nicest people I've ever come across in the food business-even if it's crazy busy around lunch time, he is pleasant. Not that it really has an effect on the food, but it's nice to buy from someone like this! Can't wait to try one of these iced teas next time

I'm so happy I found this place! I was craving fish & chips after a dance rehearsal and typed "fish & chips" into yelp... so unassuming, I was worried it would be a little too high end but after peeking in the window it looked so warm, cozy, intimate, the lighting was perfect-- I walked in and the hostess was so sweet and accommodating. I had dinner by myself at a bar table watching the Devils game.... the level of the music was perfect too btw...The beer selection was intimidating.. I didn't even know where to begin.. I ended up choosing a Scottish beer called Belhaven Lager, it was delicious! Initially I was going to order the fish & chips since that's what I came there for, but immediately upon looking at the menu I saw a fried fish sandwich in some kind of buttery roll or something I forget exactly, but I went with it--- I was sooo glad I did! You guys this sandwich was incredible! I was going to stay and have another beer and was sooo tempted to try the deviled eggs I had seen on the menu... the table next to me ordered them and they looked so good. My phone was dead so I decided I should probably just go home... I'll definitely go back there  ASAP and will tell everyone I know! Service was excellent as well (working in the industry myself I really appreciate this!) 5 stars :o)

Went again last night, to meet up with some of the ladies and we had a fab time.  Unf the yummy toasts are off the menu at the mo, but cheese plate and chips did me just fine. And the staff are splendid, even the owner was lovely.

I had an hour to kill on a Sunday afternoon before getting my ride to JFK, and the clock had just struck beer:30.   Here's to Yelp for directing me to this bar, which had only opened a couple weeks before, and was right around the corner from my hotel.  The Shakespeare is in the basement of a building and I would have otherwise totally missed it. The Shakespeare was pretty empty then, so I talked for a bit with the bartender (named Lee, I think), who recently arrived from San Diego.  The San Diego beers on the menu (several Stone products, above and beyond the now-ubiquitous IPA) made me happy.  Lee was kind enough to introduce me to a couple other people he knew there, then I was off to the airport. So two months later, I find myself in the same hotel, and you'll never guess where I go once a day during my stay.  Weekday and weekend evenings the bar packs, but the servers were still attentive and the beer list had expanded even more. Only downside is that cell service does not exist in much of the bar area, but it's good for you to go without that for an hour every now and then.  You may twitch like your methadone scrip ran out, but you'll get by, boys and girls. A friendly neighborhood place with great beers -- yep, I'll be back, and repeatedly on my next visit too.   And for those of you familiar with the Shakespeare in San Diego (yelp.com/biz/shakespeare…), you'll find its NYC namesake to be cleaner and newer, albiet lacking the old fish-n-chips smell and patios.  And I think you'll be able to live with that.
Really fantastic. Excellent execution, definitely going here again. If you don't want to spend too much and you're looking for some great food in the East Village, this should be on your list.

Average south East Asian food. Came with a friend who is thai and another friend who has lived in Hong Kong/ Malaysia/Singapore. Had the nasi Lemak, pad Mao and pad thai. The Pad thai, as with most places in New York, is completely inauthentic- too sweet, noodles not fresh, too gummy and chicken sort of bland. Nasi Lemak was also not as good as dedicated Malay restaurants I've been to in Queens. The pad ke Mao was quite good... Noodles were well cooked and spice level was strong but not overpowering. The servers did not seem familiar with the names of the dishes and we had to point them out on the menu. The appetizer for one of us came almost 10 mins before the appetizers for the other 2 of us. Same with the entree- my entree came and got cold by the time my friends got their entrees. Nothing amazing and I would argue not particularly authentic. At this point, would say it's worth the trek to queens for more authentic food of this genre.
Sunday afternoon lunch - great menu with choices for everyone. Great appetizers and entrees with terrific flavor and decent prices.

Deliciously flavorful Southeast Asian food! This is the sit-down restaurant, just to be clear (since some pictures are of the food cart). The manager or owner is also very nice. It could be better heated so it's pretty cold in there these days, but great prices for delicious food.
I have never had a savory crepe before and fell in love after I had my first one. They have so many different combinations and types of crepes. For $5 you will walk away satisfied every single time!

Good food at a good price. I end up eating here at least every other week for lunch or dinner. The line is always long during lunch and it has to be one of if not the most popular lunch truck on campus. I have had a few problems from time to time - forgotten/mixed up veggies in the crepe, filling still cool, etc. but never anything too terrible. I would definitely recommend it as all those I have introduced to it have loved it.

I have been going to The Creperie since my first year at Temple and even after having graduated, I continue to go when I'm in the area. Being in college meant eating like a college student...on a budget! At The Creperie you can't go wrong when it comes to getting a meal on a budget! It used to be $5 for a savory crepe plus a bottle drink, but has bumped it to $5.25. Still a deal for a fulfilling meal. The line is usually long but if you grab their # and call ahead of time you can avoid that long wait. I usually go with the Southwestern savory  crepe with everything on it! The portion that you get is well worth the money =) The guys that work there are pretty nice too. No complaints here!

Food is ok- greasy Americanized Chinese. Service is never its strength. We've been there once in a while for many years but did not notice until last Friday that the lady owner does not greet or smile at people of her own color... Well i feel disgusting after I saw the huge contrast. Will never go back.

We waited an hour for the food.  We did not leave a tip, needless to day.  The waitress then had the nerve to chase us out to our car, demanding a tip, and started arguing with my husband, in front of guests who were seated in our car who we had from out of town.  Based on reading the other reviews, I guess the wait staff is family and won't be fired for giving such atrocious service.  Bill and Harry's down route 10 eastbound has very good Chinese takeout with no attitude..  I will never go into this place again.

You know you enjoy a restaurant when you start making plans for your next visit. The only reason I dropped a star was because my meatballs were a little cold and the sole disappointment in an otherwise excellent meal. Service was A++

Solid food. 4 small plates definitely enough for two people-- the fried artichoke was a delight, the octopus was...decent but perhaps not so mindblowing as all of the reviews led me to believe. The ricotta gnocchi, though, was on point (and rich as all getout). They also had a really good halloumi special-- wish they hadn't taken the plates before I could have sopped up all the delicious tomato sauce with their great pita, though! Has revisiting value. I think. Going to try other things than the octopus, anyway.

I can't believe it has taken me this long to write a review. amazing, amazing mediterranean food. this place does not take reservations but do not be fooled, I have never had to wait more than 8-10 minutes at both brunch and dinner times, so don't walk away. It is worth the stay. This place is great for dates and great for small groups. I have eaten here for both occasions. I would go into all the food,that I love but I have to say having been here for brunch a number of times and dinner, it's worth giving anything a shot on this menu because I have never been disappointed.
Good food.  Terrible service and attitude.  They added tip to my ticket - after I signed the card slip.  Find a restaurant where they appreciate customers.

Trusty Yelp sent me here.  My friend and I wanted to ride our bikes somewhere in West Village for a late lunch.  So i looked up places with 2 $ signs and a 4 or higher rating.  I made a list of 4 places and my friend choose here ...sooo happy she did.  Cute place, great ambiance, friendly service and customers.  The table net to us was regulars and suggested the octopus salad, saying the octopus was the best they've had in the city.  Hands down I agree.

Came here for dinner and got seated right away. Service was great. Food was delish. We ordered the seafood platter, tacos, octopus and fried artichokes. For dessert we had the Molton chocolate. Nice atmosphere and seating outside (weather permitting). Would go back and try the chicken tangine.

A few months after I moved to New York, SeriousEats.com told me to get pumped about Taim, a West Village staple, opening a larger shop on the corner of Spring and Mulberry. As a Midwesterner with little falafel experience under my belt, I can't explain the love at first sight feelings that came over me reading the menu for the very first time. It's coming up on two years and it's safe to say that no single operation in all of New York City has recieved more of my business than Taim. Even more fascinating, the only time I've left home with intentions to visit Taim was that first time. I don't even live in Manhattan anymore and I still find myself scarfing down a falafel sandwich in the window facing DeSalvio Playground like a criminal at least once a week. GO GREEN. Yeah, I'm a sucker for spicy foods and I'll admit that the falafel rookie in me badly wanted to go with the harissa option at first. Hype said the green was the winner and "they ain't neva lie." In lieu of an adjective-filled description of the components, I'll simply say the green falafel sandwich is excellent. Trying other things on the  menu in subsequent visits proved to me that the quality is consistent in all of Taim's offerings but nothing on their menu, and perhaps in all of NYC, is a perfect as their green falafel sandwich. Did I just make that claim? Hearing "the best (fill in the blank)" from the mouths of New Yorkers lacking the courage to try something that hasn't been praised by thier sheepish friends has fueled my culinary explorations. Tasting Taim's falafel created a ton of work for me. Now I had to try all of NYC's cult falafel shops in order to defend my claim that Taim was "the best." Am I now here to tell you that after buffing my falafel credentials, Taim is in fact superior to all else? Nah. The truth is that I stopped caring. Even if I found a superior sandwich, I'd still bow to the name that is Taim for creating what I consider a perfect food. I know how tough it is, but we have to give up the list mentality. No comparison can change my opinon on Taim's green falafel and it shouldn't change yours. You're about to eat something truly special. That's worth celebrating.
I would give five stars if you were open later.  This is the best falafel in the eastern United States.
This is consistently the best falafel I've ever had. Just get the falafel sandwich with "everything" and you will be rewarded, every time! I love Taim!

5 Stars for 5 Guys! I'm a huge fan of In-N-Out too but this place is different.  For starters, you can eat all the peanuts you want while you wait for your order (it's really not that long of a wait), don't like burgers? Order a hot dog (although I haven't seen anyone eat one yet)! Don't eat meat? Oder a grilled cheese sandwich! And let's not forget their oh so generous portions of fries.  No matter what size you order (regular or large) it always overflows from the cup to the paper bag!  5 Guys' burgers have a backyard cooked on a grill taste... nice and "homey". Yum! Yum! Don't forget: - Order the burgers that don't say "Little" in front of it and you                         get two patties instead of one.                       - Free re-fills on drinks!                       - Leave a note on their bulletin board... I may just take a picture of it :)

Mood cafe is a must go place!! I saw the reviews and wanted to try once, then found to be one of the best chaat places. Indian chaats modified with papdi,cut  fruits and chutneys. Dont expect to see typical chaat here, instead try out different flavourful new combinations. Also I was shocked to see 60 types of Lassi!! OMG just awesome. I had Samosa chaat, Almond pistachio lassi and my hubby had Panjabi chaat, original lassi. Everything was delicious, worth five stars. Owner is really courteous and talkative, it was almost closing time and still he took time to talk with us. I cant wait to visit this place again.

I really love that they make vegan lassis! Mint and honey has been my favorite combination so far. Very excellent on a hot day with some spicy chaat. This has to be the friendliest cafe in all of Philly. The gentleman behind the counter is so patient to explain the different items to customers who are out of their element. Love it! He's always cheerful (but not in a sleazy way) and accommodating.

I love Mood Cafe! Hasan not only makes all his chaats with care, he takes the time to interact with all his customers. If the food alone isn't enough to put you in a good mood, he definitely will. I've tried several varieties of chaat and while it's true that the differences between each variety are pretty small, no matter which kind you get you'll have a different experience in every bite. Sometimes you get a bit of fresh fruit, sometimes you get the creaminess of the yogurt, sometimes the punch of hot sauce...and all with those delicious little crunchy bits. Chaat is like the perfect food for people with short attention spans (like me). The lassis are also delicious; fig is my favorite. If I lived or worked closer, I'd be there all the time!

Came here with a girl. Ordered some lassi's and a veggie chaat. I loved the rose and mango lassi drinks (smoothies). The chaat was interesting with some strong spicy flavors even though it was on the lower end of the spiciness level but I really enjoyed it. Very healthy choices and Hasan was very helpful, friendly and very generous. Something you do not find a whole lot of, so I appreciated that about this place. There's only enough seats (along the storefront window) for about 4 people + chairs and they bring out the outdoor patio tables and chairs in May (after winter) so it'd be nice to eat outdoors. This place did seem like an order-to-go spot. Saw a lot of people come in and take their orders to-go. I'd definitely go back and try out the other lassi's. It does contain yogurt so if you're lactose intolerant, you might want to take that into consideration. Also, this is not just a vegetarian/vegan spot, though that is what they primarily have, they also serve certain chaat dishes with different kinds of meats. It's neighborhood street parking here so it's best if you took pub transportation or if you're close enough, walk (it didn't seem too ghetto). Oh yeah, West Philly. Parking: Street Price: $4-$8 Wait: 5 mins after ordering
If the meals were $90 instead of $9, this guy would be a 3-star Michelin chef. Don't let the cheap prices and unassuming location fool you.
Great thin crust pizzas. Average price beer. Fair prices overall.

Stopped in for a quick breakfast on a Thursday morning. I was third in line and there were two other guests waiting on their order at a table. Only 1 person appeared to be working the kitchen and the register so the wait was a bit longer than expected. The coffee was really good- bean and leaf. The raspberry croissant on the other hand was out of this world!  By far the best I've ever had.

This is my boyfriend and I's favorite Asian cuisine restaurant in town. He is vegan and I am vegetarian so finding a place to eat out can be tricky. HJ House has multiple options and the staff is open with ingredients and more than willing to alter meals to accommodate. They have lots of ramen dishes, sushi, various salads, and tempura. Their tempura is awesome! They substitute all veggies for us with their tempura dish, using even mushrooms and avocados (which is unbelievably tasty!). My personal favorite is the Fruit Rolls, which is a sushi roll with fruit on top and a fruit sauce. It is SO good! I especially like the mango one. The best part of HJ is that the price is great for the food you get. We recently got four appetizers and two meals and the shebang only came to $26.50. Highly recommended!!

Beware! Once you come here, you will be hooked and probably do everything in your power to come back. The 6.50 All-Veg.special is worth every penny.  Ask for the Roti if they are not including it.  It should come with some yoghurt and chili sauce, as well.  Sometimes they even have cucumber and red onion.   It's great, authentic Punjabi Vegetarian food.  The Spinach dish in particular is so tasty, can be a little salty, but you will definitely be satisfied.   Also try the pickled spicy Mango on the bar, it's tart and just a little spicy.  mmmmmmmm..

Spicy and authentic. My favorites are the spinach broccoli mustard green mix and the paneer with peas. There isn't any seating and they don't serve meat but the favors are strong and very filling. The people here are pretty friendly and the food isn't nearly as greasy as Cuisine of Pakistan.

Okay . . . so I eat here more than any other place. . . without doubt. Top quality food, all vegetarian and authentic Indian. Flavorsome and cheap. It's super casual . . . you can stand around and eat in or get take away. There is no dining as such, it's standing room only. This place is not for a first date. . . or any date. However if its quality Indian food you are looking for, that is what you shall find. I like a platter to go. Or often I just duck in for a small bowl of chickpeas and rice (Chana Masala) and eat it there. This place is frequented by taxi drivers, stopping to get tea, dinner and have some Indian chats. I like the sweet rice. . . ask for sweet rice.
Summary based on 1 dinner: --decent food --very inexpensive --friendly service --stand up only dining unless you take away --good alternative to the pricey restaurants in the area, so extra *
This place is great and now I stink.
Excellent food and service. Best calamari I ever had.

What a pleasant evening.  The staff were all so pleasant and attentive. The food is really terrific. They had live music which I was afraid would be too loud, but it just made the experience more special.  You can tell that the owners really care and try to make everyone have the best experience.  Prices are great too and it's BYOB. Top notch all the way.

The BF took me here for our Friday night dates and I must say props to him for finding a delicious restaurant that I haven't heard of or been to yet! ;) I was always biased against restaurants in Theater District/Restaurant Row only because there are a lot of touristy places with gimmicks and not so great food. This place is definitely none of those things! We started with some delicious and creative drinks. I had the La Pulperia which changes seasonally and my bf a whiskey drink that was infused with berries. They both were very refreshing and had the right amount of alcohol in them! Then we split the lobster taquitos, the pappardelle and the fish ribs. The lobster taquitos are mini crispy tacos that just melt in your mouth. Although I didn't think the amount of lobster warranted the $19 price tag, it was very flavorful and yummy. The pappardelle was outstanding! We loved the handmade pasta and the short ribs had the perfect hint of wine. The fish ribs were very interesting. I've never heard of the dish before. The portion size is very large. The dish came with 4 or 5 slabs of white fish with the bones in smothered in BBQ sauce. The "ribs" were a bit hard to eat as the bones are no where as big as beef or pork ribs so you had to pick them out as you ate the fish. Other than putting in a bit of effort and not looking so graceful (not recommended on a first date!), the fish and BBQ sauce itself was great and worked well together! For dessert we had the chocolate tamale. I wasn't a huge fan as the dessert had a weird grainy texture to it but my bf seemed to like it. The dulce de leche ice cream that it came with was on point. Definitely a great date spot with top notch food! We also got a free shot of tequila to boot! :D

Food was great, and service was even better. I made a reservation on line, but for some reason, the reservation wasn't on their system. They understood and were able to find room for us on a Friday night, when all tables were taken, and the line was long outside. We shared different ceviches and especially loved the salmon tartare. We had good wine with our food and closed the evening with an awesome tres leches. Fue una noche espectacular, gracias!!!

Came here for a dinner with colleagues while traveling on business to NYC. We had a set menu, so I can't base my review on the menu/selection. But in terms of food, service and drinks, I'd give this place about a 3.5 if I could. If I was basing my review on cocktails and appetizers, I'd give it a full 5 stars. I had a really delicious spicy margarita that I wish I could figure out how to recreate at home. It had just the right amount of sweet, spicy and fresh flavor to give me the kick and the refreshment I was looking for. And the appetizers - from the fresh guacamole to the empanadas, were all really yummy. For dinner, I had fhe "fish ribs" which sounded very interesting and yummy, but left a lot to be desired... I guess I should have realized that anything called "ribs" would have bones, but I never expected to be served fish full of bones at a restaurant. Unfortunately, though, that was what it was... and it tasted good but was very difficult to eat and avoid bones. I'll certainly be sure to avoid anything called "fish ribs" for the rest of my life :) Dessert went back to yummy - there was a really good pound cake soaked in some sort of vanilla liquid with berries on the side that I couldn't stop eating!! I'd go back here to try other things and hopefully add another star or two to my review. My advice if you haven't been here before: don't order fish ribs!
Amazing place for seafood! A hidden gem in NY's Hells Kitchen... And Victor was amazing!!!!! Best service ever :)

Did not really feel welcome.  I feel for the "craft beer" bait. I soon realized they had only 5 subpar craft beers. Felt creepy and although they were not busy not even the bartender said,  "Hello." Will never return.  Note. .. I had one beer & left so cannot speak to the food.

My friend and I had a wonderful time here! We were actually walking by, on our way to dinner reservations. The bar area seemed so welcoming, that we stopped in for just a glass of wine. (that's what we thought!) We ended up canceling our dinner reservations and stayed here! The atmosphere, staff, clientele, wine and food are great! The staff was so friendly and attentive, especially the bartender, Jacque. We really enjoyed his company while sitting at the bar. So much great food in NYC. The atmosphere and staff really sets Baker & Co. apart! I am from out of town, but visit the city often. Baker & Co. is now on my favorite list for NYC. Can't wait to go back!

Great addition to the neighborhood. Clean, minimalist decor with a very cool wooden bar with a slated wooden ceiling. Food is good. Portion sizes are a bit on the small side for the price point. Salt cod hash could use more cod. Good flavor but not enough fish. Eggs were poached perfectly. Sage pancakes were very good. The dates and apricot sausage were a great accompaniment, but they could have offered a bit more syrup. Coffee was very good. Same quality you get from their other restaurant, Milk Bar on Vanderbuilt. Overall a very nice meal, but definitely room for improvement. Owner, Alex, is very friendly but his staff can be a bit cold.
Food was good. Friendly. The wait wasn't too bad given it was Sunday and everyone and his Uncle was looking for somewhere to brunch.

Buffalo wings were quite good. 'Gnarly' heat was just right, wings were meaty and tasted fresh, and the price point (~$11ish for a dozen wings and a bottle of water) was reasonable.   Based on my inaugural visit, they may be the best wings in Maplewood/South Orange. My one quibble was the blue cheese and carrots/celery portions were a tad small for a dozen wings. But I'd definitely go back. Edited to add: I went back and the wings weren't as good. They were okay but a bit gristly and burned. April 14: Edited to add: I've been disappointed the past two times I've been there, including tonight. Both times the wings were underdone, and tonight the heat was weak too. bleah, I may be done with this place.

The best Italian restaurant in New Jersey.  I traveled to Italy and since returning it has been hard finding a restaurant that matches the caliber of food I enjoyed in Rome.  Gennaro's in Princeton offers unique AUTHENTIC Italian dishes  that reminded me of the exquisite meals I enjoyed in Italy. The "Gennaro's Greens" is by far the best appitzer I have ever had in my entire life.  No restaurant has managed to make eggplant as delectable as Gennaro's.  Every dish I try is better than the last! And the desserts?! I cannot think of a better way to top off your meal than with a cannoli or a chocolate dipped strawberry!    The service is extraordinary and the owner is by far the most inviting person I have ever met in a place of business.  If you're looking for an intimate restaurant that has legitimate AUTHENTIC Italian dishes, Gennaro's is definitely a place I would suggest. ..absolutely worth the hour drive I make to get there twice a month!

Went with my girlfriend for a nice romantic dinner while i was visiting her at Princeton University. At first we were sat in the middle of the room (kind of awkward), but as soon as the large party taking up all of the back tables left, the owner immediately came out to ask us if we wanted to move so it was less noisy and more cozy...and that was before we even got the food, the service alone is enough to warrant at least 4 stars! I ordered the Greens Gennaro -- FANTASTIC, little bits of sausage and prosciutto and italian greens sauteed together with some oil and sprinkled with cheese, simply amazing My girlfriend ordered some penne pasta with chicken, tomatoes, peas, mushrooms and a balsamic cream sauce (that was no where near TOO creamy) - this was also fantastic, it wasnt over sauced and didnt need too much because of all the tomatoes in there adding their own juices to the already delectable mix I ordered the veal Osso Buco that was a special that night  with saffron risotto - this was SUPERB, fell right off the bone as Osso Buco should, had just the right fat content and was so soft it melted in my mouth - and as is proper they even provided me with the mini fork in the bone to scrape the marrow out afterward (delish) If you're in Princeton and have not been here - you're missing out This is now going to be a regular spot whenever I'm out visiting my girlfriend

I had the most amazing time, I did not want the night to end!. It was my first time dining at Gennaro's, but it will not be my last! The food and hospitality was the best I've seen. We were greeted by Gennaro himself and were seated  in a very warm, inviting table. I loved everything about the restaurant and would recommend it to everyone! It was the best date I've ever had!

Our waiter was friendly and the food was VERY VERY GOOD! We ordered the guacamole and chips. Chips tasted fresh and hot, and the guacamole tasted very fresh as well. The pork carnitas tacos were very moist and flavorful. I had the margaritas and mojitos and those were good as well. Finally my sister and I finished everything off with a guava mango cheesecake and that was probably one of the best cheesecakes I've ever had. I really liked the theme/decor of the restaurant as well. A bit dark, but didn't mind it. I was about to give Lucha Cartel a four, however, the service was a little slow and it wasn't even busy. Also, I asked for the pork carnitas taco on the happy hour menu but ended up getting charged for the regular priced pork carnitas taco. But, I had a good time and enjoyed some excellent food so I am still giving Lucha Cartel a FIVE! Yay. I highly recommend!

Yummy,  solid Mexican Food with really friendly bartenders. It is a casual, but well executed food in a funky and bright space. The Luchador Skate board decks that recreate a scene of the last supper is rad. I have been here a number of times and it serves a great go-to in Old City: Super happy hour deals, comfort food to dig into pre-movie at the Ritz, Salsa dancing on Tuesday nights for those of us who are just learning and a fun spot to grab a drink at the bar and get a snack. I am a big fan of the quesadillas and guacamole which comes piled high in a stone bowl. I have had some really good soups of the specials along with some hearty meat dishes too.

Wow! First off let me just say the service was outstanding. A couple of friends and I went out this past saturday night for a couple of drinks and some food. The food was absolutely acceptional and the place was bumpin'. I got the carne asada burrito. YUM! Our bartenders name was Evan and not only could he make the most delicious off the wall drinks but boy was he a handsome devil. I definitely recommend this place as one of the finer restaurants to hit up in the old city area.

Having visited Lucha Cartel for dinner and drinks a number of times, I have to say the owners of National Mechanics have done it again. Lucha has one of the best Happy Hours in the neighborhood. With friendly service and perfect $5 margaritas it's hard not to over indulge. I've also never been disappointed by anything I've ordered from the menu to soak up said margaritas.

What would I do without Juniper!? It's by far my favorite place in the neighborhood and gets better every time. Everything here is good...EVERYTHING. If it's your first time, definitely go for the pulled pork. It'll change your life. The owners are also super nice and friendly. This place is becoming one of my staples in Williamsburg. Do yourself a favor and go!

The food is amazing here. I recently moved to Brooklyn; I started researching some local burger places and Junipers caught my eye. The place is surprisingly small for all the hype it has received on Yelp, but the food doesn't disappoint. The menu only consists of a handful of items, but everything on the menu is delicious. Each dish is executed perfectly and presented in a very artistic manner. My personal favorites are the baked mac and cheese (for 7 dollars it makes a great lunch) and the grilled burger. The spicy fries are not spicy, but I find them to be seasoned perfectly. The sweet potatoes fries also add a nice change of pace. Also if you get two entrees you can get a free appetizer for mentioning Yelp. The atmosphere is very friendly.  I have experienced anywhere from a 15-40 minute wait since Tom is the only one in the kitchen. It really depends on how busy it is. In this part of the town, business usually picks up after 8. Tom usually comes out after your meal to ask you personally how you liked it. You can tell this is a restaurant that strives to satisfy their customers.

JUNIPER IS AWESOME, Bytches. The restaurant is super laid back and simple, which is cool, because I'm so super double guns cocked sick-n-tired of restaurants trying so hard with their little lights, and fancy random objects from World War 2. I don't wanna eat somewhere with the same cluttered atmosphere as my grandpa's garage (but I HEART YOU GRAAAANPY). So when it comes to restaurants AND men, I'm going to avoid both complicated and vegetarian (i.e. short on meat) from here on out. Juniper is super easy going. Cool like a Polar Bear's toe nail (oh hyell, there she go again... )... which is good, because you can be there with friends and actually have comfortable conversation, like if you want to get with the girls and talk about how your ex-boyfriend Aerius is a super selfish creep, and doesn't know how to love another human being (not just me, but also his parents, and I should probably say "living creatures", because he treats his ferret like sh*t and had like 3 goldfish die. The food is the best part. I mean, you can totally have a cool vibe at your place, but if the food is lame, then you're lame. Great burger!

West Coast meets East Coast, a definite must try for burger lovers! My co-workers and I had the opportunity to be among the first guests for the California based, Umami Burger pre-opening event earlier today in New York. We started out with the house pickle plate, which included green beans (a bit spicy), beets, cucumbers, pickles, okras and and unfamiliar vegetable my taste buds just couldn't get a hold of. They had just the right crunch and not too sour. There was also a hint of cloves and cinnamon on some of them.   I was able to sample four of the eight burgers on the menu. The Original, The Greenbird, the Hatch Burger and my favorite, the Truffle Burger. Our waitress recommended we try the burgers medium rare, which is also the way the chef recommends them. They were perfect but I still recommend you get them just the way you want them. We also sampled the Make 'em manly fries and the sweet potato fries. I definitely recommend the Make 'em manly to compliment the Truffle Burger. The sweet potato fries had a touch of cinnamon which I don't really think was necessary. I will definitely be back to sample more and to grab a cocktail or two.
I waited 2 years to have the Truffle burger again and OMG is was so worth the wait. Followed by the Market cocktail I was pretty much in BURGER HEAVEN & I will def be there again by this weekend.

Went to Umami Burger for lunch today.  5 stars.  Bang.  Right there. Got there right around noon and there was no wait for a 2-top.  We sat down, ordered a nice cold beer, and perused the menu.  After the helpful waitress pointed out several options and explained how they make their burgers, we settled on an original Umami Burger and a Truffle Burger, thinking we'd split them and get half of one each (this proved to be an excellent decision).  Also threw in an order of fries "truffled". In short, both burgers were the bomb.  I liked the truffle burger a bit more, but man, both of them were just awesome.  I'm not one to get caught up in hype, but this got me. Fries were decent enough.  Nothing super special but enjoyed the truffle cheese on them. For dessert I had the Cookie Ice Cream Sandwich thing and it was pretty good.  Didn't love it but it was good enough for something sweet to end the meal. Burgers alone elevate this to 5 stars no problem, despite the fries and dessert that were probably more in the 4 range. Go.

Had an awesome lunch yesterday at the grand opening of Umami Burger NYC.  Came by with some co-workers, and we shared about half the menu - the Truffle Burger was the standout winner with the Hatch Burger coming in a close second.  Be sure to try any of the fries so you can mix-and-match with the four dipping sauces.  Also, don't forget to save room for dessert - ice cream sandwiches from The Good Batch were the perfect ending to our meal.  Will definitely be back to try out the rest of the menu!

Loving this burger...and especially the fries!! Went with a couple friends and got to try a bunch of burgers. The Truffle Burger and Green Chili one were the all stars! Everything from the rich toppings to the flavorful burger meat, to the moist buns are awesome! Also, as a pickle lover, the pickle plate is pretty delicious - the standouts are the pickled green beans (both flavors)! Oh, and you cant miss the manly fries. I dont event like cheese fries and these are awesome! The dipping sauces for them are the icing on the cake! It is just a fun spot with creative burgers and a really sweet staff!

What  can I say that hasn't already been said? They have a pretty cute wait list system - you put your name down and receive a link where you can see how long you've been waiting and what the current wait time is. Then they text you when the table is ready. Yesterday around dinner, the wait was 2 1/2 hours but I'm sure it's just because it's the second day after opening. I got the truffle burger and truffle fries and they were both delicious. The meat was just perfectly done, the bun was just the right balance between soft and soggy. I got the Field Recordings wine and it was brilliant. The staff are also super nice and honest about their recommendations. Overall, one of those experiences that leave me blissful.

First off, I must say that I have great friends that waited 1.5+ hours while I was at work. This eliminated the wait factor for me. One could argue that this took away from the experience. I would argue that I didn't stand on line for 1.5+ hours. The service was great right off the bat. Our server introduced the beverages and highlighted the food items by tying their West coast roots to this location's NY/Chelsea-specific twist. Drinks were ordered along with 2 orders of truffle fries and an order of the cheesy tater-tots (off the menu). Portions on apps were good considering the price.  We ordered another portion of the tater-tots (testament to how good they were rather than sub-par portion). Burgers were ordered. My party didn't deviate far from what we heard were the essentials. Truffle burgers and manly burgers all around. My manly burger did taste manly with large chunks of bacon a opposed to strips (because that's how men do). The burgers are cooked medium rare here. I don't know too many people who get their burgers medium rare, but the quality of meat here is top notch. Any other temperature and you lose the melt-in-your mouth factor. The burger was very good. I've had more satisfying burgers, but flavors-wise, this was top 3. The bun to meat ratio was a little off, but Umami made sure that we knew they were aware of the problem and getting ahead of it. (More on that in a sec) Our server came around with a third order of truffle fries, on the house. I assume that the fries are constantly being made and when a batch sits for a certain amount of time, they just give them away. Who am I to question their process? I got free fries. After finishing up, we received our bill, which reflected that all the burgers were half-price. Giggling like naughty schoolgirls, we immediately paid the bill before asking what the deal was. Apparently the batch of buns they were using at the moment were bigger than they liked (thus off-setting the bun to meat ratio). What I appreciated was their humble-approach. No flashing signs or demands for high-fives for lowering our check. Just a pleasant surprise to top off a great experience. Bottomline if tl;dr - Great burgers, sides and service. Probably not worth a ridiculous wait, but they're opening upstairs seating and 2 more locations in NY soon. Wait a month for the hype to die down unless you enjoy waiting on line for 2 hrs wondering if this will be worth it. Four stars for food. Five stars for service.

I came here on a Monday night at around 715pm and the host said it was going to be about a 1hr 45min wait for a table for 2.  What?! Are you crazy?!  Well, good thing is they'll take your number and text you when your table is ready.  So you can roam around the area.  I came back about an hr and a half later and they still said it was going to be about another 30 mins, but we got seated in 15 mins.  I think because we checked back in, they allowed us sit earlier.  Yay! So onto the food! Truffle Beet Salad - Nice and refreshing salad.  Totally tasted the truffle in it.  It was good.  I liked it. Umami Burger (the original) - Very flavorful, but i felt it was too much going on that i didn't realize i was eating a burger.  It didn't have any of the meaty taste i was looking for. Truffle Burger - This was a little lighter than the umami burger.  Had the meat taste i was looking for, but didn't have that much flavor.  I also didn't really taste the truffle.  =[ Truffle Fries with cheese - meh.  not that truffle-ly either.  the truffle beet salad had the most truffle flavor Also! my server was terrible.  I normally don't talk much about the service, but she was terrible that I have to say something.  She took forever to get us things and we had to ask multiple times and left empty plates at our table! Hope you guys have a better experience! Overall, it was ok.  Wouldn't say it was the best burger i've had and it def didn't satisfy my burger craving.  and for the wait, ehhhh.

Waited 3 hours for this place, only thing good about that was I didn't have to stand in line, they put you on a waitlist and text you when you are around 15-30 minutes away from being called. Ordered the truffle burger, came out a bit smaller then I expected x: the server had told us it would be medium rare but I believe mine came out rare..kept falling apart as I was eating it. Truffle fries are only good hot and they are a bit soggy. Fried pickles = not worth it. Its basically a dollar a piece and its so thick that if you don't eat it in one bite the rest of the breading just falls off. 21 U-club because I have never tried a bloody mary I'm not quite sure how its supposed to taste but I believe it was too garlicky. Margarita Peached was good came with a fresh piece of peach but at the price of 12 dollars a cocktail I would think it would be a bit stronger, same for the 21 U-club. Overall the meal wasn't bad for two people (two appetizers, burgers and drinks) but for a burger joint this place is a little overpriced (60+)

Went here last night at 7pm to put my name in. I was quoted 2.5-3 hours, but it ended up being about 2 hours and 15 minutes until I got the text my table was ready. We were sat and a very nice waitress explained how everything worked and even shot the shit with us for awhile which I appreciated given how busy they currently are. We asked a lot of questions which she was very helpful with... FYI they don't have any of the "off-menu" specialties yet. I told her I had a question for her and if she wasn't able to fulfill it my life would be ruined (ok I was being dramatic, but i only had a green juice for lunch in anticipation of this moment and it was 9:15pm at this point). Could they pleaseeeeeeeee make me the truffle burger with a veggie patty since I am a pescatarian? She gently told me no because the veggie burger itself had so much "umami" flavor already the chefs won't do it. I was actually disappointed at this point, because the veggie burger did not sound appetizing to me. "Soyrizo" is not my ideal topping and everyone knows the key to ordering a good veggie burger is to replace whatever their best burger is with a veggie patty. But, she let me know, the chefs will put a portobello in place of burger. I was not happy about this.. I don't like straight mushrooms as my patty... But starving, delusional, and having no other options I trusted her (as she said she trusts the chefs who say its the closest to the consistency of a burger patty). Fine just bring me my wine. Things come out quickly here--they don't have heat lamps in their kitchens, so you're food is never warming waiting for your side dish. This means fries tend to come out first... Just munch slowly until your burger joins. No problem for me. We ordered two rounds of truffle fries (yum!!), fried pickle spears (I don't eat these, but my bf said they were not so great), cheesy tots (good, though not exactly "cheesy," more shredded potatos deep fried), and the questionable mushroom burger and a manly burger. OMG. My life is changed thinking about this mushroom burger and how I looked down upon it. The flavor of the mushroom was incredible, very tender and juicy. I read many reviews before going to Umami in which people stated their truffle burgers were not "truffley," thinking to myself wtf does that mean? how could it not be filled with truffle deliciousness? But it's not and I don't care. It's just gooey and delicious and I am dreaming about it now as I detox. I let my server know that I doubted her in the beginning but she was SO RIGHT. She thanked me for my honesty. Sorry I'm not sorry. They are still working out some service issues, so we got our fried pickles and cheesy tots for free which helped ease the blow of the bill. Just wait a few weeks and go experience this incredible burger for yourself!!!!!!!!!!!

Manly burger was excellent, the original was pretty good but nothing to get worked up about. NOT worth a mid-day wait of almost 40 minutes. And and and - there were empty tables the ENTIRE TIME while the staff kept us waiting, on the theory that someone they were holding tables for would show up. Some tables were open long enough for us to have ordered, eaten and left. Service was fairly quick once we were finally seated, though the food seemed to take a while to arrive. The burgers and hot sides were lukewarm. Not even hot. We ordered the burgers medium rare, and they were clearly rare. I would go back for the manly burger, but not if there was a wait. Hey, Umami? Keeping people who are waiting with money in hand cooling their heels to preserve empty tables for idiots who may not bother to show up is a lousy idea.

Came at around 3 on a weekday, ended up waiting about half an hour. Umami was definitely good, and has a different enough vibe from most NY burger places that I can understand the hype. Is it fully warranted? Not sure. I had the original burger without the bun--I know, but a medical procedure I had earlier in the summer keeps me from being able to actively bite into things, so I figured that it would be easier to fork-and-knife it without the bun. It ended up coming protein style (lettuce wrap) which I ignored straight for the meat. I think I would have enjoyed the mixing of flavors more had I been able to eat the burger like a sandwich, so I'd definitely be willing to try again once my mouth has more mobility. The meat was flavorful, albeit essentially raw (but that is medium-rare, I suppose), the grilled tomato and parmesan delicious. There weren't very many mushrooms and onions. Overall, a solid burger, but not the best I've tasted. We ordered a variety of sides, namely the truffle fries and smashed potatoes. The smashed potatoes were very good with the garlic aoli, though they resemble hashbrowns more than the potato mash we were expecting. Truffle fries were delicious but didn't taste very much like truffle--more a nice savory, salty cheese. I also had the 21-U cocktail (bloody mary) which was very good. I'll be back once the line dies down, but I don't think I'll be waiting two hours to eat dinner here anytime soon. There are many equivalent burgers in NY.

Eh it was okay. It's a good burger, but doesn't live up to the hype. I got the duck burger and truffle fries. My main squeeze got the 'trust us' which ended up being the truffle burger, sweet potato fries, and a beer which I forget the name of. We also got the ginger ice cream sandwich was really delicious.

We came at 5:30 on a weekday and had to wait about 10 minutes because according to the hostess, "I just seated someone in the same section and the waitstaff won't be able to handle both parties sitting at once". I should have realized what was to come. The staff here is obviously very inexperienced. After we sat down, we saw people waiting to be seated for long periods of time. We counted and there were 6 tables empty in the downstairs area (there is definitely an upstairs area that I've seen when I ate at the restaurant that was here prior but I'm not sure what they do with that area).  The food takes a very long time to come out. After getting our food 45 minutes later, I had to ask 3 different people for ketchup before I just got up and went to get it myself from the bar. In instances like this, you have to blame the management and those running the restaurant because they are the ones responsible for ensuring that they have a proper waitstaff that are competent. The food is fine. I had the truffle burger and was only able to finish 1/2 of it because it is just very heavy. My friend had the hatch burger and said it was just fine also. I would definitely not come back here because the service is seriously lacking. In a city like NY where you have plenty of people who are career servers, you should have much better staffing. I also would not come back because they make people wait hours even though they have empty tables in order to create some kind of sense of demand.

Heard about Umami Burger a few months ago and was crushed to find out they were based in LA. So, imagine my excitement when I passed by 6th avenue and saw this!! Obviously I made it my mission to eat here and I did. Thankfully I waited 5-7 minutes, sat at the bar, ordered the truffle burger and a brew to wash it down with. It was good, no it was really really good. Definitely a burger I would happily plunk down $12 for. What I didn't get was that they didn't do "add-ons". Someone next to me wanted a bunch of stuff on their burger and staff said they would bring it out on the plate instead of putting it on the actual burger. I thought that was odd, but I still enjoyed my tasty burger. Get the burger medium rare, like they suggest. It is moist, juicy and oh sooooo damn good. Truffle burger, you are forever in my heart.

One word: exquisite. This popular west coast burger chain recently opened here, and I've only ever heard good things about them. So I decided to come check this place out on a Saturday, in between meal rushes (around 3:00 PM or so). The wait was about an hour (they told us that it would be an hour and a half, so that was nice). Went with three other friends. All the beers they had on tap were unique. Maybe I'm not the best beer guy yet (just turned 21! D:) but I've never heard of any of these before. I went for a Bronx Summer Ale, and it was great. We got an order of truffle cheese fries, sweet potato fries, and onion rings for the table to start out. Let me just say this: the house ketchup is amazing. It has a perfect texture, with a sweetness lightly playing with the savory flavor of the tomato. It was definitely the best ketchup I've ever had. It complemented all of the starters well, and I found myself dipping more into the ketchup than the other specialty sauces they offered. We happily munched away, and when the burgers finally came out, it was like the commencement of something grand. The buns had a large U seared into them. I personally got a truffle burger. First bite - absolutely perfect. The meat was cooked perfectly medium rare, and apparently had been ground from good quality steak meat.. The custom bun's sweetness and truffle sauce's savory flavor complemented the lightly seasoned meat perfectly. After a few bites, I added some more of that superb ketchup onto the burger, and it was even better. The service was great. They had an automatic texting app set up so that you can leave your name and go chill around the area for a bit (maybe check out the library across the street!). The hostess and the waitress were both super chill and nice, and we never were in want of water or anything. They had no problem splitting the check after we fumbled around with cash and cards for a few minutes, haha. Definitely go. Worth the wait.
Great burger. Make sure you get on the list thought as the wait can get incredibly long (3-hr wait tonight for two).

I've been to the one in santa Monica, which i really liked it. In my opinion, I think umami burgers in Cali tastes better. I tried the original burger at this place, the cheese is kinda hard, it could of been better. but overall, I like this new umami burger place.

I had the pleasure of experiencing Umami Burger when they were vending at GoogaMooga, and knew I'd have to come back when they opened a permanent NY location. And it did not disappoint! It was a Tuesday afternoon during lunchtime, and there was a bit of a line. We gave our name/number to the hostess and she punched it into her iPad. Then I received a text with a link to their online tracker that tells you how long you've been waiting. Super cool. Anyway, they quoted us 15-20 minutes, but it was 13 (that tracker sure comes in useful). The system also sends you a text a few minutes before you're read to be seated. We sat down quickly and ordered some Mexican Sprites (with real sugar!). My friend and I split two burgers and a side of regular shoestring fries. We had the Truffle burger (of course) and the Umami burger, but medium rare. The caramelized onions in the Umami burger were tasty and the parmesan crisps gave it a nice texture. Couldn't really taste the mushrooms though. The Truffle burger was what I had at Googa, and it was every bit as good as I remembered. So much flavor (umami flavor, I suppose) and the melted cheese was just the icing on the cake (or cheese on the burger). And for about $12 a pop, you can't really go wrong. They're not skimping on quality or size either. You get three spoons full of dipping sauces. The garlic aioli was very garlicky. The Diablo hot sauce was actually spicy. But I think my favorite was the jalapeno ranch, which had just the right amount of kick. The decor is cool (and what my friend said was very California). Lots of wall art and neon signs. Reminded me of the "after" shot on an episode of Restaurant Impossible. If you're a deprived East coaster like me and want a good burger, definitely stop by Umami!

Happiness without having to buy a plane ticket to Los Angeles. Manly Burgers, Strange Concoctions + More The last time I tasted an Umami Buger I was in Hollywood. Trust me if U-Mami made a burger like this you'd still be living at home. Thanks for coming out east guys! Love the different options. Appreciate the unique drink menu. Don't just get the truffle burger, they're all good. Is it worth the wait? If it's that big of a deal you could always hire a Task Rabbit to wait in line. I prefer to dine at the bar, but it can still be quite a long time since this spot is pretty new. These guys aren't going anywhere so I won't be in a hurry to come back, but I look forward to my next visit when I'm craving a burger or missing So Cal. The Scene: Casual, Burger lovers Destination Rating: 6 Date Rating: 4 Hob Nob Potential: TBD Strong Suggestion: Definitely save room for dessert.
